wikis.title: Original Naruto anime gets four brand-new episodes for 20th anniversary
wikis.summary: Anime News Network reports that the Naruto TV anime will air four brand-new episodes starting in September, with earlier episodes rerunning in Japan from July.
wikis.body:
- Posted 2023-03-09 by Rafael Antonio Pineda (Anime News Network), sourced to the Naruto anime's official website.
- The official website announced on Thursday that the Naruto television anime will air four "brand-new" episodes starting in September to celebrate its 20th anniversary. The anime debuted in October 2002.
- Selected earlier episodes will rerun in Japan beginning in July.
- Studio Pierrot began streaming a "Road of Naruto" video in October, condensing 20 years of anime history into 10 minutes with brand new animation footage. The Boruto anime's Twitter account revealed three new visuals in October for the anniversary.
- Background: the Naruto TV anime aired from 2002 to 2007; Naruto Shippuden premiered in 2007 and ended in 2017.
- Boruto: Naruto Next Generations manga (Ukyo Kodachi, Mikio Ikemoto) launched in Weekly Shonen Jump in May 2016, moved to V Jump in July 2019; Masashi Kishimoto took over as writer in November 2020. The Boruto TV anime premiered in April 2017; Part I ends March 26, with a Part II green-lit.

wikis.title: Naruto manga and anime franchise (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto manga (1999 to 2014) and its anime, films, games and reception, including the postponed 20th-anniversary anime episodes.
wikis.body:
- Manga by Masashi Kishimoto in Weekly Shonen Jump, September 21, 1999 to November 10, 2014; 700 chapters, 72 volumes; 250 million copies in circulation.
- Anime: Naruto (October 3, 2002 to February 8, 2007, 220 episodes) and Naruto: Shippuden (February 15, 2007 to March 23, 2017), by Pierrot and Aniplex.
- Four "brand-new" episodes for the anime's 20th anniversary were originally scheduled for September 3, 2023 but, per the article, were postponed to a later date in August 2023.
- Franchise also includes 11 films, 12 OVAs, novels, video games and a planned live-action film; continues in Boruto.

wikis.title: Naruto: manga, plot, production, anime, films, games and reception
wikis.summary: Main body of the Wikipedia article on Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto: plot, development, media adaptations, sales and critical response.
wikis.body:
- Naruto is a Japanese manga by Masashi Kishimoto about Naruto Uzumaki, a socially isolated ninja who dreams of becoming Hokage; Part I is volumes 1 to 27, Part II volumes 28 to 72. Based on Kishimoto's one-shots Karakuri (1995) and Naruto (1997).
- Serialized in Weekly Shonen Jump from September 21, 1999 to November 10, 2014; 700 chapters in 72 tankobon volumes (March 3, 2000 to February 4, 2015). Chapters 1 to 238 are Part I, 239 to 244 a Kakashi gaiden, 245 to 700 Part II (after a 2 and a half year gap). Viz Media licensed it for North America.
- Development: an early concept had Naruto as a chef; Godzilla inspired the tailed-beast mythology.
- Anime: first series directed by Hayato Date, produced by Pierrot and Aniplex, TV Tokyo, October 3, 2002 to February 8, 2007, 220 episodes (first 135 adapt Part I, remaining 85 original). Naruto: Shippuden ran February 15, 2007 to March 23, 2017. "A series of four 'brand-new' episodes, to commemorate the original anime's 20th anniversary, were originally scheduled to premiere on September 3, 2023; however, in August of that same year, it was announced that the episodes would be postponed to a later date."
- Also 11 theatrical films and 12 OVAs; a live-action film announced by Lionsgate in July 2015, with Tasha Huo announced as scriptwriter on November 27, 2023. Video games mostly fighting games; the first, Naruto: Konoha Ninpocho, released March 27, 2003 for WonderSwan Color.
- Sales: 250 million copies in circulation across 46 countries and regions; volume 28 was the top-selling manga volume of 2008 in North America; volume 7 won a Quill Award in 2006.
- Critics praised characters, storylines and action, though some felt the fights slowed the story.

wikis.title: Classroom of the Elite: overview, plot and light novel volumes
wikis.summary: First half of the Wikipedia article: the light novel series, its premise, publishers and manga adaptations, with volume lists.
wikis.body:
- Light novel series by Shogo Kinugasa, illustrated by Shunsaku Tomose, published by Media Factory under MF Bunko J. Year 1: May 2015 to September 2019 (eleven volumes plus three short story volumes, May 25, 2015 to September 25, 2019); Year 2 (2-nensei-hen): January 2020 to November 2024; Year 3 (3-nensei-hen): began March 2025. Seven Seas Entertainment licensed it in English and on February 17, 2021 announced a new version of volume seven after localization omitted several paragraphs.
- Premise: at the government-established Tokyo Metropolitan Advanced Nurturing School, students in Classes A to D compete over three years; graduating Class A members are said to be promised their chosen career path or further education. Protagonist Kiyotaka Ayanokoji is in Class D with Suzune Horikita and Kikyo Kushida.
- Manga: Yuyu Ichino's adaptation began in Monthly Comic Alive on January 27, 2016, twelve tankobon volumes as of February 22, 2022 (Seven Seas volume 1 in February 2022); Shia Sasane's manga of the sequel novels began in December 2021.
- Anime overview: Lerche produced seasons in July to September 2017, July to September 2022, January to March 2024 and April to June 2026; "a fifth season has been announced".
- Sales: over 10.8 million copies in circulation.

wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Aka Akasaka's manga Kaguya-sama: Love Is War and its anime, live-action, novel and spin-off adaptations, including the announced finale film.
wikis.body:
- Japanese manga by Aka Akasaka, published by Shueisha (English: Viz Media). Serialized in Miracle Jump (May 19, 2015 to January 19, 2016), then Weekly Young Jump (March 24, 2016 to November 2, 2022); 281 chapters in 28 volumes (first March 18, 2016, last December 19, 2022).
- Premise: student council president Miyuki Shirogane and vice president Kaguya Shinomiya at Shuchiin Academy are too proud to confess, believing whoever does so first "loses"; halfway through the series they confess and the focus shifts to advancing the relationship.
- Anime: 12-episode TV series by A-1 Pictures (2019); 12-episode second season Love Is War? (2020); OVA (2021); 13-episode third season Ultra Romantic (2022); film The First Kiss That Never Ends (December 2022); TV special The Stairway to Adulthood (2025). An anime film serving as the story's conclusion, "The Final Chapter", with an original story by Aka Akasaka, "was announced" (no date given).
- Live action: film premiered September 6, 2019 (Sho Hirano, Kanna Hashimoto; director Hayato Kawai); sequel Kaguya-sama Final announced January 6, 2021, premiered August 20, 2021.
- Spin-offs: Dojin-ban manga by Shinta Sakayama (June 14, 2018 to June 25, 2020, 4 volumes); yonkoma Kaguya-sama o Kataritai by G3 Ida (July 26, 2018 to November 2, 2022, 8 volumes); two novels by Juichiro Hitsujiyama (September 19, 2018; November 17, 2023).
- Sales and awards: over 22 million copies in circulation by December 2022; 65th Shogakukan Manga Award (general category, 2020); third Next Manga Award (2017); ranked 50th in TV Asahi's Manga Sosenkyo 2021.
- Viz announced the license at San Diego Comic-Con on July 20, 2017. Akasaka's Oshi no Ko began in the same magazine April 23, 2020.
- Akasaka's stated inspirations: character names from The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter; School Rumble and Death Note-style mind battles cited.

wikis.title: Marriagetoxin: overview, plot, characters and manga volumes
wikis.summary: Opening of the Wikipedia article: the manga's premise, its cast, the Shonen Jump+ serialization and early volume summaries.
wikis.body:
- Marriagetoxin is a Japanese web manga written by Joumyaku and illustrated by Mizuki Yoda, serialized in Shueisha's Shonen Jump+ app and website since April 2022, with 18 tankobon volumes as of July 2026. Viz Media licensed it in English (as Marriage Toxin). A Bones Film anime aired April to June 2026; a second season "is set to premiere in January 2027".
- Plot: Hikaru Gero, of the Poison Clan of assassins, is told to marry and produce an heir or his younger sister will be forced to bear one. He asks assassination target Mei Kinosaki, a cross-dressing marriage swindler, to marry him; Kinosaki declines but agrees to coach him on dating.
- Voices: Hikaru Gero - Haruki Ishiya (anime), Ethan Gallardo (English); Mei Kinosaki - Shion Wakayama (anime), Brittney Karbowski (English). Other cast includes Kyoko Himekawa (thief, Anna Nagase), Shiori Ureshino, Akari Gero (Hikaru's sister), Piichi Nakagawa, and Masters of the Beast, Bug, Needle, Spear, Bear, Wind-Wheel and Ghost families.
- Manga: announced by Shueisha on April 11, 2022; weekly free serialization began April 20, 2022, with simultaneous English release on Manga Plus. Viz announced its license in June 2023; Viz volume 1 released January 2, 2024 (Japanese volume 1 then, volume 2 on November 4, 2022 and volume 3 on February 3, 2023 in Japan).
- Early volumes cover the Himekawa rescue against Water Master Ushio, and Gero's bodyguard job for Shiori Ureshino against Sound Master Naruko.

wikis.title: Marriagetoxin: later volumes, anime series, episodes and reception
wikis.summary: Rest of the Wikipedia article: anime adaptation details, episode summaries and critical reception.
wikis.body:
- Anime: announced October 1, 2025; produced by Bones Film, directed by Motonobu Hori, series composition/scripts by Kimiko Ueno, character design and chief animation director Kohei Tokuoka, music by Taisei Iwasaki and Yuma Yamaguchi.
- Aired April 7 to June 30, 2026 on the new Ka-Anival!! block on Kansai TV, Fuji TV and affiliates; 13 episodes. Opening "Kill or Kiss" by Yurina Hirate; ending "Shake Na Baby" by AKASAKI. Streamed by Crunchyroll; Muse Communication licensed it in Southeast Asia.
- A second season was announced after the final episode, set for January 2027 on the same block.
- Episode 1 (April 7, 2026), "The Poison Master's Search for a Bride": Hikaru is hired to poison Mei, then instead offers to spare Mei in return for matchmaking. Later episodes air weekly (ep. 2 April 14, ep. 3 April 21, ep. 4 April 28) and adapt the Himekawa and Ureshino arcs.
- Reception: nominated for the Next Manga Award (Best Web Manga) in June 2022, ranked eighth of 50 nominees; fifth in Nationwide Publishers Recommended Comics of 2023. Recommended by Koyoharu Gotouge and Gege Akutami. First volume reviewed positively for art and action; ANN's Lucas DeRuyter called it a shoo-in for best new manga of the year in his year-end retrospective.

wikis.title: Re:Monster: overview, plot, characters, novels, manga and anime
wikis.summary: Main body of the Wikipedia article on the Re:Monster light novel series, its manga, and the Studio Deen anime.
wikis.body:
- Re:Monster is a Japanese light novel series by Kogitsune Kanekiru, illustrated by Yamaada, serialized online from May 2011 to 2018 on Shosetsuka ni Naro; AlphaPolis published nine main volumes, a side story volume and an extra volume between August 2012 and August 2017. Licensed in North America by Hanashi Media (novel) and Seven Seas Entertainment (manga).
- Sequel light novel Re:Monster: Ankoku Tairiku-hen (illustrator Naji Yanagida) began with AlphaPolis in July 2018, five volumes released so far.
- Plot: Tomokui Kanata, murdered by a lustful woman, is reincarnated among goblins as Gobrou, retaining his memories and the ability to absorb the powers of anything he eats; he becomes strongest of his tribe and leader of the mercenary group Parabellum.
- Characters (Japanese / English voices): Gobrou - Takuya Sato / Sean Letourneau; Gobkichi - Kenta Hosoda / Reagan Murdock; Gobmi - Ai Kakuma / Kate Bristol; Gobe ("E") - Kana Ueda / Jill Harris; Hobsei - Aya Yamane / Mikaela Krantz.
- Manga: art by Haruyoshi Kobayakawa, serialized on AlphaPolis' manga site since March 2014, 13 tankobon volumes; licensed by Seven Seas.
- Anime: announced September 19, 2023; animated by Studio Deen, produced by Genco; director Takayuki Inagaki, series composition Hiroshi Yamaguchi, character design Junichi Takaoka, music Go Sakabe. Aired April 5 to June 21, 2024 on Tokyo MX and other networks. Opening "Into the Fire" by Chansung and AK-69 feat. Changmin; ending "Sadame" by Everdream. Crunchyroll streamed worldwide outside East Asia; Muse Communication licensed South and Southeast Asia.
- A second season was announced September 25, 2025 and, per the intro, "will be aired in April to June 2027".

wikis.title: The Summer Hikaru Died: plot, characters, production, manga and anime
wikis.summary: First half of the Wikipedia article: premise, cast, how Mokumokuren created the manga, serialization details and the 2025 anime adaptation.
wikis.body:
- Manga written and illustrated by Mokumokuren, serialized on Kadokawa Shoten's Young Ace Up website since August 31, 2021; nine tankobon volumes as of June 2026; "set to end with its 51st chapter on October 20, 2026". Yen Press announced its English license in September 2022.
- Plot: Yoshiki Tsujinaka's childhood friend Hikaru Indou is fatally injured hiking in the mountains and is consumed by an eldritch being that takes his body and memories yet remains a separate entity; Yoshiki stays with "Hikaru" despite other eldritch beings and hunters.
- Production: conceived while Mokumokuren studied for high school entrance exams; began posting drawings on Twitter in January 2021, then approached by the Young Ace Up editors. The manga is described by the author as "coming-of-age horror" with queer themes, never serialized as boys' love. Setting is a fictional town in Mie Prefecture, with some characters speaking Mie dialect.
- Anime: announced May 24, 2024; produced by Cypic, directed by Ryohei Takeshita (also series composition); Yuichi Takahashi chief animation director and character design. Aired July 6 to September 28, 2025 on Nippon TV and affiliates. Opening "Saikai" by Vaundy; ending "Anata wa Kaibutsu" by Tooboe. Netflix streams globally; Abema streams it in Japan. A second season was announced after the first season's final episode.
- The first volume sold 200,000 copies in three months.

wikis.title: The Summer Hikaru Died: final episodes, stage play, reception and awards
wikis.summary: Second half of the Wikipedia article: episodes 10 to 12 summaries, the stage play, sales figures and awards.
wikis.body:
- Episodes: ep. 10 "Truth" aired September 14, 2025; ep. 11 "Indo's Sin" September 21, 2025; ep. 12 "Its Place" September 28, 2025 (directed by Ryohei Takeshita). Ep. 11 explains the Indo family's past sin of sacrificing heads to a mountain god; ep. 12 has Hikaru admit the real Hikaru is dead, and he and Yoshiki reconcile.
- Stage play: announced September 19, 2025; ran at Kinokuniya Hall, Tokyo, January 9 to 18, 2026; Sotaro Fujii directing and writing, Mikihito Sano composing.
- Manga reception: 11th in web manga at the 2022 Next Manga Award; topped Kono Manga ga Sugoi! 2023 (male readers); nominated for the 16th Manga Taisho; 2024 Eisner nominations (Best U.S. Edition of International Material - Asia; Best Writer/Artist); Harvey Award nominations in 2024 and 2025; won the American Manga Awards Best Continuing Manga Series in 2026 after nominations in 2024 and 2025.
- Circulation: 200,000 (first volume, three months), 550,000 (October 2022), 1.4 million (June 2023), 1.9 million (December 2023), 2.1 million (May 24, 2024), 3 million (November 4, 2024), 3.5 million (July 4, 2025), 4 million (September 26, 2025), 4.5 million (December 26, 2025), 5 million (June 1, 2026).
- Anime awards: won IGN Awards Best Anime Series (2025); nominated for 10th Crunchyroll Anime Awards (Anime of the Year, Best New Series, Best Director and others), 12th Anime Trending Awards, Japan Expo Awards, 31st Manga Barcelona Awards, 21st AnimaniA Awards, Music Awards Japan.

wikis.summary: Overview of the Medaka Kuroiwa Is Impervious to My Charms manga by Ran Kuze, its characters, publication details, anime production and sales.

- English: Kodansha USA; first digital volume March 8, 2022; print announced at Anime Expo 2022 for Q2 2023 (volume 1 print June 20, 2023).
- Plot: queen bee Mona Kawai wants the new transfer student Medaka Kuroiwa, who glares at her, to fall for her but falls for him instead; Medaka is a monk-in-training forbidden by his temple masters from falling in love. Other girls join as rivals or friends.
- Main characters: Medaka Kuroiwa, Mona Kawai (from Osaka, Kansai dialect when flustered), Tsubomi Haruno, Asahi Shonan (basketball star), Tomo Namba (Mona's childhood friend), Minami Shirahama, Shou Kobayakawa, Yuzuru Kido, Anri Shinagawa.
- Anime: announced May 13, 2024; SynergySP, directed by Yoshiaki Okumura, scripts Kazuyuki Fudeyasu, character design Mayumi Watanabe, music Akiyuki Tateyama. Aired January 7 to March 25, 2025 on TV Tokyo and affiliates, 12 episodes; Crunchyroll streamed. Opening "Ame Tokimeki Koi Moyo" by AyaFubuMi; endings "Kyunapi" (Kaori Maeda) and "Is this love?" (Rikako Aida).

wikis.title: Premise, characters and manga details
wikis.summary: Plot, main characters and publication information for the Wistoria: Wand and Sword manga by Fujino Omori and Toshi Aoi.
wikis.body:
- Manga by Fujino Omori, illustrated by Toshi Aoi; Kodansha's Bessatsu Shonen Magazine from December 9, 2020; 16 volumes as of August 2026; English Kodansha USA. Light novel "Grimo Acta" by Omori (illustrated by Yuunagi, SB Creative GA Bunko) from July 14, 2024, 2 volumes; English Yen Press.
- Anime summary: Actas and BN Pictures; season 1 July to September 2024, season 2 April to June 2026, "A third season has been announced." 24 episodes.
- Premise: an invasion from the sky nearly destroyed the world; five mages cast a barrier atop the tower Mercedes Caulis. Will Serfort, sixth-year student at Rigarden Magical Academy with no magic aptitude but strong swordsmanship, seeks to reunite with childhood friend Elfaria Albis Serfort, the youngest Magia Vander. He later discovers an ability called "Wis" that absorbs magic into his sword.
- Characters include Will, Kiki (carbuncle familiar), Elfaria (Ice Faction), and classmate Colette Loire.

wikis.title: FOMC meeting calendars and information (2021-2027)
wikis.summary: Federal Reserve page listing FOMC meeting dates with links to statements, minutes and projection materials, including the 2026 schedule.
wikis.body:
- The FOMC holds eight regularly scheduled meetings a year and other meetings as needed. Minutes of regular meetings are released three weeks after the policy decision. Committee membership changes at the first regularly scheduled meeting of the year.
- Meetings marked * are associated with a Summary of Economic Projections.
- 2026 meetings: January 27-28; March 17-18*; April 28-29; June 16-17*; July 28-29; September 15-16*; October 27-28; December 8-9*.
- 2026 minutes release dates: Jan meeting Feb 18; Mar Apr 8; Apr May 20; Jun Jul 8; Jul Aug 19, 2026. The September 15-16 meeting lists statement, implementation note, press conference and projection materials but no minutes yet; October and December list nothing yet.
- 2025 meetings: Jan 28-29; Mar 18-19*; May 6-7; Jun 17-18*; Jul 29-30; Aug 22 (notation vote, Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy); Sep 16-17*; Oct 28-29; Dec 9-10*. Minutes for 2025 released between Feb 19, 2025 and Dec 30, 2025.
- Earlier years (2024 back to 2021) are also listed; the page also has a 2027 tab.
- The page also describes the FOMC's annual FOIA report.

wikis.title: FOMC statement of September 16, 2026
wikis.summary: Federal Reserve press release announcing a 12-0 FOMC vote to raise the federal funds target range by 1/4 point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent.
wikis.body:
- Released September 16, 2026 at 2:00 p.m. EDT; approved by a 12 - 0 vote.
- The Committee "decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate." It continues its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system.
- Economy: activity expanding at a solid pace; uncertainty elevated owing in part to geopolitical developments; domestic spending resilient; productivity growth strong; capital investment robust; job gains have kept pace with the workforce and unemployment has changed little.
- Inflation "remains elevated. Today's policy action will support a timelier return to the Committee's 2 percent goal. The Committee will deliver price stability."
- Implementation Note issued September 16, 2026.

wikis.title: September 2026 Fed dot plot and rate hike (Bondsavvy)
wikis.summary: Bondsavvy blog post (updated September 16, 2026) on the September 2026 Fed dot plot, the quarter-point hike, Warsh's press conference, projections and effects on bond and money market yields.
wikis.body:
- Posted by Steve Shaw, updated September 16, 2026.
- On September 16 the Fed published a dot plot projecting a fed funds target range of 4.00% to 4.25% at yearend 2026 and 2027. With the day's quarter-point hike (to 3.75%-4.00%), the plot implies one-half point of total 2026 increases. In the March dot plot, participants had projected one-half point of cuts across 2026 and 2027. The Fed's last prior move was a cut in December 2025 to 3.50%-3.75%.
- Dots: 18 for 2026 and 2027, 17 for 2028 and 2029; Fed chair Kevin Warsh does not provide dots. For yearend 2026, 12 participants projected a quarter-point above the current range and four projected two additional quarter-point hikes. For 2027 there were four outliers projecting cuts; the other 14 projected 4.00%-4.25% or 4.25%-4.50%.
- Cumulative change vs current range at yearend 2026/2027/2028: +50bp 4/8/0; +25bp 12/6/4; unchanged 2/0/5; -25bp 0/3/3; -50bp 0/0/1; -75bp 0/1/4.
- Median yearend range: Sept 2026 plot 4.00%-4.25% (2026 and 2027); June 2026 plot 3.75%-4.00% and 3.50%-3.75%; March 2026 plot 3.25%-3.50% and 3.00%-3.25%.
- Projections (SEP): PCE inflation to fall from 3.7% at yearend 2026 to 2.3% at yearend 2027; versus March, 2026 PCE inflation projection up 1 point to 3.7% and 2026 unemployment down 30bp to 4.1%; real GDP growth largely unchanged.
- Press conference: Warsh spoke after the 2:00pm ET statement raising the range by 25bp to 3.75%-4.00%.
- Market figures: Vanguard VMFXX 7-day yield 3.63%, expected to rise to about 3.88% over the next several weeks; VMFXX is a $378 billion fund. Two-year Apple bonds YTM 4.71%; twenty-year over 6%; RTX two-year bond 5.09%. 2- and 20-year Treasury yields closed at 4.74% and 5.39%.
- The author says the dot plot "is not a 'plan'" and can change; the piece promotes Bondsavvy's bond strategy.

- Series by Takumi Yanai: web novel on Arcadia April 2006 to June 2009; AlphaPolis print from April 12, 2010; five main plus five side volumes; sequel Gate Season 2: Jieitai Kano Umi nite, Kaku Tatakaeri from July/August 2017 (five volumes to November 30, 2020); prequel Gate: Zero (two volumes, December 31, 2021 to August 31, 2022). Hanashi Media began publishing the English novels on March 25, 2026.
- Plot: a portal appears in Ginza, Tokyo; the JSDF repels the invaders and passes through the Gate; reserve officer Yōji Itami investigates the Special Region.
- Manga: seven series; Satoru Sao's began July 30, 2011 (28 volumes); Gate: Zero manga from March 13, 2024; Season 2 manga from February 27, 2026.
- Anime (2015): A-1 Pictures, director Takahiko Kyōgoku; first 12 episodes July 4 to September 18, 2015, second half January 9 to March 26, 2016; Sentai Filmworks in North America.
- Sequel anime: "announced on July 4, 2025"; Kasagi Labo, Oshi and Genco; animated by Studio M2, director Tōru Takahashi, series composition Tatsuhiko Urahata, character design Shigeru Fujita, music Yoshiaki Fujisawa; "set to premiere in 2027."
- Reception: over 4.2 million copies in Japan by June 2017 and over 6 million by May 2021; the anime was produced in collaboration with the JSDF Tokyo Provincial Cooperation Office, and a JSDF recruitment campaign used the characters as mascots.

wikis.title: SK8 the Infinity (anime series)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the original Bones skateboarding anime SK∞ (2021), its plot, production, 12 episodes, OVA, manga, stage plays and the announced second season.
wikis.body:
- Original anime by Bones, directed by Hiroko Utsumi, scripts by Ichirō Ōkouchi, character design and chief animation director Michinori Chiba, music Ryō Takahashi. Announced September 20, 2020; aired January 10 to April 4, 2021, on ABC and TV Asahi's Animazing!!! block; 12 episodes. Opening "Paradise" by Rude-α, ending "Infinity" by Yuuri.
- Plot: in Okinawa, hardcore skaters race in the secret midnight competition "S" down an abandoned mine road. Sophomore Reki takes Canadian transfer student Langa, a former snowboarder, to S, drawing him into skateboarding; the arc includes challenges ("beefs") against Shadow, Miya, Adam (founder of S), a tournament, and a final race between Langa and Adam.
- Production: Studio No Border (founder Thomas Romain) designed the skateboards so they could work in real life; Juliette Mercier did most designs; decals by Ayumi Kakei, Loic Locatelli and Romain; five artists worked on the series. Moves inspired by real skaters (Miya's style resembles Rodney Mullen's).
- Follow-ups: new project announced July 4, 2021; revealed August 14, 2022 as a second season plus OVA, with main staff returning. The four-episode OVA SK8 the Infinity Extra Part (Bones Film) released in Japan March 19, 2025, after a theatrical screening on January 24 that year. The article says a second season is being produced.
- Licensing: Aniplex of America outside Asia (Funimation, AnimeLab, Wakanim); Muse Communication in Southeast Asia (Bilibili, Animax Asia); Funimation made a SimulDub.
- Manga: SK8 Chill Out! by Toriyasu (Young Ace Up, Jan 11 to Sep 20, 2021); adaptation by Kazuto Kōjima on BookLive! from March 5, 2021.
- Stage plays announced July 4, 2021: SK8 Part 1 ran December 2-12, 2021; Part 2 (January 15-24, 2022) was canceled after a staff member tested positive for COVID-19.

wikis.title: Fed rate decision September 2026: benchmark hiked to 3.75%-4.00% (Raisin)
wikis.summary: Raisin explainer (last updated September 16, 2026) on the FOMC's unanimous 25bp hike and what it means for savings accounts and CDs.
wikis.body:
- Last updated September 16, 2026; written by Clarke Bowling of Raisin.
- On September 16, 2026 the FOMC voted unanimously (12-0) to raise the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00% (previously 3.50%-3.75%; "Effective Sept. 17, 2026"). The page says recent inflation data stayed elevated above the 2% target, with persistent pressure in energy and consumer price measures.
- Statement released at 2:00 p.m. ET; economic activity described as expanding at a solid pace. The Committee reiterated its commitment to returning inflation to 2%, with policy decisions data-dependent into the final quarter.
- Savings effects (per Raisin): variable high-yield savings APYs typically track increases upward within 1 to 2 weeks; partner banks usually update HYSA and CD offers within 3 to 10 business days; a 25bp rise does not always mean CD yields rise exactly 0.25%. National average savings rate cited: 0.38% as of August 2026.
- The rest is promotion of Raisin's savings and CD marketplace (FDIC/NCUA insurance up to $250,000) and general disclaimers.

wikis.title: Sword Art Online light novel series: overview, plot, adaptations and reception
wikis.summary: Main text of the Wikipedia article on Reki Kawahara's Sword Art Online light novels, their spin-offs, anime seasons, films (including one set for 2028), games and reception.
wikis.body:
## Series
- Japanese light novel series by Reki Kawahara, illustrated by abec; web novel 2002-2008, then ASCII Media Works' Dengeki Bunko from April 10, 2009 (29 volumes as of April 10, 2026); English by Yen Press.
- Spin-offs: Sword Art Online: Progressive (from October 10, 2012, 9 volumes), Alternative: Gun Gale Online, Girls' Ops. "30 million copies in circulation" by 2024.
- Arcs: Sword Art Online, Alfheim Online, Gun Gale Online (volumes 1-8); Alicization (volumes 9-18); Moon Cradle (19-20); Unital Ring began in volume 21 (December 7, 2018), the first arc not based on the web novel.
- Plot: in 2022 the VRMMORPG Sword Art Online launches; on November 6, 10,000 players are trapped and told they must beat all 100 floors of Aincrad; Kazuto "Kirito" Kirigaya plays alone as a "beater".

## Anime
- Season 1: Aniplex and Genco, A-1 Pictures, director Tomohiko Ito, music Yuki Kajiura; July 7 to December 22, 2012. Extra Edition special December 31, 2013; Sword Art Online II premiered July 5, 2014.
- Alternative: Gun Gale Online (3Hz) April 2018; Alicization October 6, 2018 to March 30, 2019, War of Underworld from October 12, 2019, second half rescheduled by COVID-19 to July 11 to September 19, 2020.

## Films
- Ordinal Scale: February 18, 2017 (Japan), March 9, 2017 (US). Progressive: Aria of a Starless Night: October 30, 2021. Progressive: Scherzo of Deep Night: delayed from September 10, 2022 to October 22, 2022.
- Sword Art Online the Movie: Integral Domain, an original film following Alicization: War of Underworld, announced by Aniplex and "scheduled to premiere in 2028".

## Games
- First console game Infinity Moment (PSP, March 14, 2013); console games sold over 10 million units by March 2026.

## Reception
- Top-selling light novel series of 2012 (Oricon); 20 million in print by 2017, 26 million by 2021. Ranked first in Kono Light Novel ga Sugoi! 2012 and 2013; best of the 2010s and hall of fame in 2020.
- Praised for premise, world building and Kirito-Asuna bond; criticized for pacing, deus ex machina resolutions and treatment of female characters.
- Removals: Sword Art Online II listed among 38 titles banned in China (June 12, 2015); seven manga titles removed from Books Kinokuniya Australia in July 2020.

wikis.title: Sentenced to Be a Hero: series, setting, media and anime
wikis.summary: First part of the Wikipedia article on the Sentenced to Be a Hero light novel series, covering its setting, plot, characters, light novel and manga releases and the Studio Kai anime with its announced second season.
wikis.body:
- Japanese light novel series by Rocket Shōkai, illustrated by Mephisto. Web novel on Kakuyomu from October 2020; ASCII Media Works' Dengeki no Shin Bungei imprint from September 2021 (eight volumes as of January 17, 2026; a ninth listed for October 16, 2026); Yen Press licenses it in English (first volume August 22, 2023).
- Setting: humanity fights demonic faeries; "Heroes" are convicted criminals forcibly resurrected after each death; "Goddesses" are living weapons. Being a Hero is seen as a harsher punishment than execution.
- Plot: Xylo Forbartz, a former Holy Knight commander who killed his corrupted goddess, is sentenced to be a Hero and leads Penal Hero Unit 9004; he meets the sword goddess Teoritta and works to find out why he was set up, supervised by Holy Knight commander Patausche Kivia.
- Manga: Natsumi Inoue, Dengeki Comic Regulus from March 25, 2022; two volumes as of April 26, 2024; Yen Press to release volumes from June 23, 2026 (announced December 2025); digital English on BookWalker.
- Anime: announced at the Dengeki Bunko 30th anniversary event in July 2023; Studio Kai, directed by Hiroyuki Takashima, series composition Kenta Ihara, characters Takeshi Noda, music Shunsuke Takizawa. Initially scheduled for October 2025, delayed to improve quality; premiered at Comic Fiesta on December 21, 2025 and aired January 3 to March 26, 2026 on Tokyo MX and others. Opening "Kill the Noise" by Spyair. Crunchyroll streams; Medialink licensed it on Ani-One Asia's YouTube channel.
- "A second season was announced at the AnimeJapan event on March 28, 2026."

wikis.body:

- Video game: a project titled Sentenced to Be a Hero: Game of the Goddess was announced at AnimeJapan alongside the second season on March 28, 2026.
- Reception: in the 2023 Kono Light Novel ga Sugoi! guidebook the series ranked third in the tankobon category.
- See also: Scum of the Brave (also by Rocket Shōkai).

wikis.title: Spice and Wolf (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia overview of the Spice and Wolf light novel series by Isuna Hasekura and its manga, anime (2008, 2009, and a 2024 remake with a second season set for 2027), games and reception.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Japanese light novel series by Isuna Hasekura, illustrated by Jū Ayakura; ASCII Media Works has published 24 volumes since February 2006 under Dengeki Bunko, plus 13 volumes of the spin-off Wolf and Parchment since September 2016. Yen Press licenses it in English.
- Story: Kraft Lawrence, a 25-year-old traveling merchant, finds the wolf-deity Holo (over 600 years old) in his wagon and takes her north toward her homeland Yoitsu; the plot focuses on economics and trade. Mainichi Shimbun called it a "unique fantasy".
- Sales: over 3.5 million copies by December 2009; over 5 million by October 2020.

## Adaptations
- Manga: illustrated by Keito Koume, Dengeki Maoh, September 27, 2007 to December 27, 2017, 16 volumes.
- First anime: 12 episodes January to March 2008 (studio Imagin), OVA May 2008; second season Spice and Wolf II, 12 episodes July 9 to September 24, 2009 (Brain's Base and Marvy Jack), plus a 2009 OVA. Funimation released both in English.
- Two Nintendo DS visual novels (June 2008, September 2009); Spice and Wolf VR (2019, Spicy Tails).

## 2024 series
- Announced February 25, 2022 for the novel's 15-year anniversary; a remake titled Spice and Wolf: Merchant Meets the Wise Wolf, produced by Passione, directed by Hijiri Sanpei, music by Kevin Penkin, with Fukuyama and Koshimizu returning as Lawrence and Holo.
- Aired April 2 to September 24, 2024 on TV Tokyo and affiliates; Crunchyroll streamed outside Asia; in March 2024 Netflix announced streaming in select Asian regions.
- "Following the finale of the first season, a second season was announced. It is set to premiere in 2027."

## Reception
- Ranked in Kono Light Novel ga Sugoi! first in 2007 and fifth in 2008 and 2009; Holo won Best Female Character in 2007. ANN's Michael Basile called the 2008 anime an "incredibly fascinating and captivating work".

wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the South Korean web novel Tomb Raider King by Sanji Jiksong, its webtoon, its 2026 Studio EEK anime ("aeni") and the announced sequel.
wikis.body:
## Work
- South Korean web novel by Sanji Jiksong, serialized on KakaoPage from November 1, 2016; English release by Wuxiaworld December 14, 2019 to May 22, 2021.
- Plot: tombs containing power-granting relics are appearing worldwide; tomb raider Seo Joo-Heon returns 15 years into the past to steal all the tombs before anyone else and take revenge on those who betrayed him.
- Main characters: Seo Joo-Heon, Irene Holton, Lee Seol-Ah, Yoo Jae-Ha, Oh Seug-Woo, Julian Miller, Chloe Laurent, Ilya Volgof, Im Hae Jin.

## Webtoon
- Launched on KakaoPage June 30, 2019 (illustrator 3B2S, Redice Studio); first season concluded January 30, 2023, second season February 9 to March 27, 2023 (412th chapter). Twelve collected volumes as of August 2024. English on Tapas; Yen Press (Ize Press imprint, announced at Anime Expo 2022) has published in North America since November 22, 2022.

## 2026 anime
- Announced at Anime Expo 2024; produced by Studio EEK, directed by Woo Seung-wook, character designer Lee Hyun-joung, music Kim Ju-young; 12 episodes.
- Premiered July 9, 2026 on Aniplus (South Korea) and, as a Japanese dub titled King of Grave Robbery, on Fuji TV's B8station block; also Kansai TV, Tokai TV, BS Fuji, UHB. Episode 12 listed for September 30, 2026 (episode 11 September 16, 2026).
- Opening "Show Down" and ending "To Be Continued" both by QWER. Crunchyroll streams it, including an English dub; Medialink licensed it in Southeast Asia.
- Voices: Seo Joo-Heon - Hwang Chang-young / Yoshimasa Hosoya (Japanese) / Monty Thompson (English); Irene Holton - Lee Yuri / Saori Hayami / Natalie Van Sistine; Yoo Jae-Ha - Shim Ki-hyuk / Miyu Irino / Tyler Viator.

## Other
- May 29, 2025 collaboration with the mobile idle RPG "Max Level Idle".
- Sequel: "In July 2026, Kakao announced a sequel titled Tomb Raider King: End Line", set after Joo-Heon's wedding with Irene, also written by Sanji Jiksong.

wikis.title: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba - The Movie: Infinity Castle (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 2025 Ufotable film adapting the Infinity Castle arc, the first of a trilogy, covering production, release, box office records and awards.
wikis.body:
## Film
- 2025 Japanese animated dark fantasy action film directed by Haruo Sotozaki, produced by Ufotable; music by Yuki Kajiura and Go Shiina; running time 155 minutes; budget $20 million; box office $793.5 million.
- Adapts the "Infinity Castle" arc of Koyoharu Gotouge's manga; a direct sequel to the fourth anime season, following Mugen Train (2020), To the Swordsmith Village (2023) and To the Hashira Training (2024). It follows the Demon Slayer Corps' climactic battle against Muzan Kibutsuji and the remaining Upper Ranks.
- It is "the first film of a trilogy announced in June 2024, immediately following the airing of the fourth season's finale". Production of this first installment took three and a half years, beginning in early 2022 while the Entertainment District Arc was still airing.

## Release
- Japan: July 18, 2025 (Aniplex and Toho). Crunchyroll via Sony Pictures Releasing in select Asian countries in August, all other territories the following month.
- Blu-ray and DVD in Japan on July 29 (2026); in July 2026 at the film's Anime Expo panel it was announced Crunchyroll streams the film on July 28.

## Box office
- Japan opening day: ¥1.64 billion (US$11.11 million), 1.15 million admissions, a record; three-day total ¥5.52 billion (US$37.42 million), 3.84 million admissions, biggest opening weekend in Japanese cinema; fastest to reach ¥10 billion; ¥40.24 billion in Japan as of July 2026.
- Worldwide $793 million, seventh-highest-grossing film of 2025; US opening weekend $70 million (record for an international film and for an R-rated animated film); China US$96 million total. Highest-grossing Japanese film and highest-grossing R-rated animated film.

## Reception
- Positive reviews for action and visuals, some criticism of pacing. Won Best Animation Film at the 49th Japan Academy Film Prize and a record seven awards including Film of the Year at the 10th Crunchyroll Anime Awards.

wikis.title: Claude Opus 5.1 release date: leaks versus what shipped (CellCog tracker)
wikis.summary: CellCog blog tracker (published 30 August 2026, updated 14 September 2026) saying Opus 5.1 and Sonnet 5.1 were not announced, and tracing the rumor to community readings of two test strings.
wikis.body:
- By Nitish Garg (CellCog), 30 August 2026, updated 14 September 2026. A living tracker of rumor versus official statements.
- Status as of August 30, 2026: no announcement, model card, API identifier, pricing page or benchmark for Opus 5.1 or Sonnet 5.1. Anthropic's docs list claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5 and claude-fable-5 as current. Official pricing: Opus 5 $5 input / $25 output per million tokens; Sonnet 5 $2 and $10.
- Origin of the names: test strings claude-marshmallow-eap and claude-melon-eap circulated in screenshots August 21 to 24; a claude-marshmallow-ht-eap sighting on August 21 reportedly showed API traffic with fallback to Opus 4.8 on some requests. The strings never contained "opus", "sonnet" or "5.1"; commentators inferred the names on August 24. A developer reportedly found the plain marshmallow and melon strings produced no verifiable first-party output.
- Contested map: majority reads Marshmallow as an Opus successor and Melon as Sonnet; others read Melon as a new Haiku; a minority reads Marshmallow as Fable-class. Testers claim neither reaches Fable 5.
- Rumored window was "late August", which slipped; early September speculated, based on one precedent: a claude-honeycomb-eap string reportedly surfaced about two weeks before Opus 5 shipped on July 24, 2026.
- From August 27, Reddit threads reported Opus 5 suddenly improved and speculated about stealth A/B testing; the page says a checkpoint swap or routing/system-prompt changes explain it equally well.
- September 14 update: one X account claims Opus 5 in Claude Code is being served by a newer model it calls "Opus 5.2"; no identifier or traffic report backs it.
- Watchlist: an API identifier, instruction-following/verbosity changes, token efficiency, what Melon is, pricing (point releases have historically held tier pricing).

wikis.summary: Wikipedia overview of Yukinobu Tatsu's Dandadan manga and its anime seasons, stage play, sales and awards, including a third season set for 2027.
wikis.body:
- Japanese web manga by Yukinobu Tatsu, serialized in Shueisha's Shonen Jump+ since April 6, 2021; 25 tankobon volumes as of September 2026 (first volume August 4, 2021). English: Manga Plus, Viz Media's Shonen Jump site; Viz print licence announced February 2022, first volume October 11, 2022.
- Plot: Momo Ayase (believes in ghosts) and Ken "Okarun" Takakura (believes in aliens) bet on who is right; Momo gains psychic abilities, Okarun is possessed by a spirit; they fight yokai and aliens. Later Momo is afflicted by a curse and loses most memories when it lifts.
- Tatsu previously assisted on Chainsaw Man and Hell's Paradise: Jigokuraku; serialization was approved in Q2 2020 and he delayed starting until both had concluded.
- Anime (Science Saru): season 1, 12 episodes, directed by Fuga Yamashiro, aired October 4 to December 20, 2024. Season 2, 12 episodes, directed by Abel Gongora with Yamashiro co-directing, aired July 4 to September 19, 2025. "After the airing of the second-season finale, a third season was announced... set to premiere in 2027."
- Films: Dan Da Dan: First Encounter (2024), Dan Da Dan: Evil Eye (2025).
- Stage play announced April 6, 2026 (director Imagine Ito, writer Shinjiro Kameda, music Ryo Konishi): August 26 to September 3, 2026 at Nippon Seinenkan Hall, Tokyo; September 11-13 at Sky Theater MBS, Osaka.
- Sales: over 3.2 million copies in circulation by November 2023, over 10 million by March 2025.
- Awards: won Best Shonen at the 31st Spanish Manga Barcelona Awards (2025); won the 71st Shogakukan Manga Award in 2026; Next Manga Award 2021 second place; Manga Taisho 2022 seventh.

- Season 3: announced August 2022; directed by Shinpei Nagai; aired October 12 to December 28, 2025, with a season-2 recap special on October 5. "The second cours of the season is set to premiere in 2027." Streams on Hulu (U.S.), Disney+ (Canada), Crunchyroll (Europe and Middle East).
- Live-action film: announced April 21, 2020 by Sony's Columbia Pictures; Justin Lin named director June 13, 2022; in April 2024 Dan Harmon and Heather Anne Campbell reportedly hired to rewrite the script.
- Reception: season 2 got mixed reviews (animation drop after the studio change); "The third season received overwhelmingly negative reviews" (Game Rant cited on subpar art, animation and direction).

- Updated Sep 3, 2026 by the Anna AI model and API research team. Opus 5.1 is described as the "community name" for an anticipated incremental upgrade to Claude Opus 5. No official Anthropic announcement, model card or API listing as of late August 2026.
- Leaks: identifiers claude-marshmallow-eap (often mapped to Opus 5.1) and claude-melon-eap (mapped to Sonnet 5.1, or possibly Haiku-class) appeared mid-to-late August 2026 in developer tools and Discord. Early anecdotal reports: neither reaches Fable 5; Marshmallow beats Melon and may feel better than Opus 5 in conversation and consistency; heavy thinking-token use; strength in 3D/spatial tasks.
- Opus 5 baseline: released July 24, 2026; $5 per million input / $25 output tokens (same as Opus 4.8); 1-million-token context, up to 128k output tokens, adaptive thinking, effort controls; marketed as "a thoughtful and proactive model that comes close to the frontier intelligence of Claude Fable 5 at half the price". Reported Frontier-Bench v0.1 about 43.3%. Available on Claude apps, the API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud and Microsoft platforms.
- Other prices: Fable 5 / Mythos 5 $10 / $50; Sonnet 5 roughly $2-$3 / $10-$15.
- Cadence cited: Opus 4.8 in May, Fable/Mythos 5 and Sonnet 5 in June, Opus 5 in July. The Honeycomb EAP to Opus 5 gap was roughly two to three weeks, implying a window of late August into September 2026.
- Late-August reports: an August 28 window for Fable 5.1 / Opus 5.1 slipped; one widely circulated (unverified) view placed Fable 5.1 around August 31 and Opus 5.1 around September 5.
- Expected price: unconfirmed, but continuity at $5/$25 is expected.
- The page also promotes CometAPI as a unified gateway to Claude models.

wikis.title: Dragon Ball Super Beerus premiere, streaming and English dub update (Geekdom podcast)
wikis.summary: Geekdom episode covering a V-Jump scan for Dragon Ball Super Beerus, its October 11 premiere time and where it streams, plus expectations for an English dub.
wikis.body:
- Episode published September 16, 2026 (14 min), Geekdom podcast. Host's framing: a V-Jump two-page spread about "Dragon Ball Super Beerus", the enhanced edition of the first three Dragon Ball Super arcs (Battle of Gods, Revival of Frieza, Champa), all under one title, with Akira Toriyama credited.
- Premiere: "starts on October the 11th at 23:15" in Japan (11:15 p.m. JST), on Fuji TV first, as Dragon Ball Daima did. Episodes about average anime length (23-30 minutes with commercials).
- Streaming: about 15 minutes after broadcast on Amazon Prime Video (Japan; host says access outside Japan needs a VPN) and U-Next; about 45 minutes to an hour after broadcast on Crunchyroll with subtitles. Host says Toei is trying to put it on as many platforms as possible; may be on Hulu (existing Dragon Ball deal); nothing known about Netflix.
- English dub: host says it is "coming" and expects an announcement and dub trailer "any day now"; believes returning voices such as Jason Douglas (Beerus) and Ian Sinclair (Whis); does not think it will be simul-dubbed but hopes it is close to Daima's pace. These are the host's expectations, not confirmed.
- Scan text: Beerus is described as a "God of Destruction" whose only possible rival is the "God of the Saiyans"; opening and ending song names were revealed in the trailer; a QR code links to the trailer.

wikis.title: Chainsaw Man: manga, adaptations, sales and reception
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article covering Tatsuki Fujimoto's Chainsaw Man manga: premise, plot, production, media adaptations, sales figures and critical reception.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Japanese manga by Tatsuki Fujimoto, published by Shueisha. Part 1 ("Public Safety Arc") ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from December 3, 2018 to December 14, 2020; part 2 ("School Arc") ran in Shonen Jump+ from July 13, 2022 to March 25, 2026. 24 tankobon volumes, March 4, 2019 to June 4, 2026. Viz Media publishes in English (first volume October 6, 2020; 21 volumes released as of June 2, 2026); Manga Plus carries it digitally from January 2019.
- Set in the late 1990s in an alternative timeline where the Soviet Union still exists; Devils are born from human fears. Denji fuses with Pochita, the Chainsaw Devil, and joins Public Safety Devil Hunters led by Makima; part 2 follows student Asa Mitaka, who contracts with the War Devil Yoru.
## Production
- Fujimoto always intended to serialize in Weekly Shonen Jump, inspired by the 1974 film The Texas Chain Saw Massacre; he called the series a "copycat of Dorohedoro and Jujutsu Kaisen".
## Adaptations and media
- 12-episode anime by MAPPA on TV Tokyo, October 12 to December 28, 2022.
- Film Chainsaw Man - The Movie: Reze Arc premiered in Japan September 19, 2025.
- Sequel anime Chainsaw Man - Assassins Arc announced at Jump Festa '26 on December 21, 2025.
- Novel Chainsaw Man: Buddy Stories (Sakaku Hishikawa; Viz release July 25, 2023).
- Stage plays: Chainsaw Man The Stage (Tokyo Sept 16-Oct 1, Kyoto Oct 6-9, 2023); Reze Arc stage set for Tokyo July 25-August 2, 2026 and Kyoto August 7-12, 2026.
- Games: free browser game August 4, 2023; smartphone game announced June 19, 2026 at MAPPA's 15th anniversary livestream; BanG Dream! collaboration December 15-25, 2024.
- Other: Universal Studios Japan attraction September 6-November 4, 2024; The Loop event (Crunchyroll and Three Ten Merchandising) August 22-October 18 at Westfield Topanga Mall, announced August 2, 2026.
## Sales and awards
- Over 36 million copies in circulation by June 2026 (3 million by August 2020). 66th Shogakukan Manga Award (shonen) in 2021; Harvey Award Best Manga 2021 to 2023. Top of Kono Manga ga Sugoi! 2021 list. Best-selling manga series in the US in 2022 per NPD BookScan.
## Reception
- Generally well received by critics (e.g. ANN's James Beckett gave volume 1 a B+; Sequential Tart 9/10; Anime UK News 6/10); art and graphic violence discussed at length.

wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Gege Akutami's Jujutsu Kaisen manga: setting, plot, production, manga/novels/anime/games/stage plays, and sales figures.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Manga by Gege Akutami, serialized in Weekly Shonen Jump from March 5, 2018 to September 30, 2024; 30 tankobon volumes (July 4, 2018 to December 25, 2024). Sequel to Akutami's Tokyo Metropolitan Curse Technical School (Jump Giga, April 28 to July 28, 2017), retitled Jujutsu Kaisen 0.
- Premise: high schooler Yuji Itadori joins Jujutsu Sorcerers after swallowing a finger and becoming host to the Curse Ryomen Sukuna. Plot summary covers the Shibuya incident, Kenjaku's Culling Games and Yuji's defeat of Sukuna.
## Production
- The serialization committee approved it unanimously (per editor Hiroyuki Nakano). Influences named: Neon Genesis Evangelion, Yoshihiro Togashi (Hunter x Hunter), Tite Kubo. Hiatus June 9, 2021, resumed August 2, 2021.
## Media
- English: Manga Plus from January 2019; Viz Media print, 30 volumes from December 3, 2019 to May 12, 2026.
- Spin-off manga Jujutsu Kaisen Modulo (with Yuji Iwasaki), September 8, 2025 to March 9, 2026. Two novels by Ballad Kitaguni (May 1, 2019; January 4, 2020); a spin-off novel by Yumeaki Hirayama announced September 2025.
- Anime by MAPPA: season 1 (24 episodes, October 3, 2020 to March 27, 2021); prequel film Jujutsu Kaisen 0 (December 24, 2021); season 2 (23 episodes, July 6 to December 28, 2023); season 3 The Culling Game: Part 1 (12 episodes, January 9 to March 27, 2026); a fourth season, The Culling Game: Part 2, announced after the season 3 finale.
- Games: Phantom Parade (released November 21, 2023, internationally November 7, 2024); Cursed Clash (February 2, 2024); Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton announced June 9, 2026, originally for 2026, later delayed to 2027; collaborations with PUBG Mobile, Fortnite, others.
- Stage plays (2022, 2023-24, 2025; a Shibuya Incident play set for Tokyo November 14-23 and Osaka November 28-29, 2026); Universal Studios Japan attractions (September 16, 2022 to July 2, 2023); exhibitions through 2026; McDonald's sauce tie-in July 9, 2024; The Loop event August 22 to October 18 (announced August 2, 2026).
## Sales
- Over 150 million copies in circulation by December 2025 (10 million by October 2020, 100 million by September 2024). Best-selling manga series in 2021 with over 30 million copies sold.

wikis.title: Stuttgart 21 rail and urban development project
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Stuttgart 21, the Stuttgart underground through-station and rail project, covering its costs, delays, funding, protests and the 2011 referendum.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Stuttgart 21 is "a major railway and urban development project in Stuttgart, Germany, that is replacing the surface railway lines with tunnels". Core: a renewed underground Stuttgart Hauptbahnhof among some 57 km of new railways, including ~30 km of tunnels and 25 km of high-speed lines.
- The 16-track surface terminus is to be replaced by an underground through-station with only 8 platforms, at right angles to the existing building. Parts of the historic Bonatzbau, platforms and approach tracks are to be demolished and the land sold for urban development.
- Includes the Filder Tunnel and a new Filder station serving the airport, Messe and Filderstadt; connects to the Wendlingen-Ulm high-speed line, which opened in late 2022. Carriage sidings move to Untertürkheim.

## Timeline and costs
- Officially announced April 1994; construction began 2 February 2010.
- Finance agreement signed 2 April 2009; on 23 November 2009 construction was announced for February 2010 on condition costs do not exceed EUR 4.5 billion.
- 19 July 2007 funding: DB EUR 1,115 million, Baden-Württemberg EUR 685 million, Federal Government EUR 500 million, on a EUR 2.8 billion estimate with up to EUR 1 billion of overrun provision.
- March 2013 estimate EUR 6.5 billion (previously EUR 4.5 billion in 2009); March 2022 Deutsche Bahn estimate EUR 9.15 billion.
- Opening: expected December 2025 in 2019 (delayed from an initial 2019 estimate); in 2024 delayed to December 2026; in 2025 the December 2026 date was canceled, "officially due to technical issues with the new signaling system". "By June 2026, a Deutsche Bahn audit found the 2026 commissioning date to be unrealistic. The new Stuttgart Hauptbahnhof is scheduled to open in December 2031, with associated works to be delivered in phases between 2027 and 2033." Total costs "had also risen by EUR 3 billion to EUR 14.5 billion".

## Opposition
- Weekly Monday demonstrations since fall 2009; more than 50,000 demonstrated on 1 October 2010 (also stated as an estimated 100,000).
- "Black Thursday", 30 September 2010: hundreds injured when police used water cannon, pepper spray and batons; Dietrich Wagner permanently lost his eyesight.
- Critics cite the Schlossgarten park, the Bonatzbau heritage and cost; some critics suggested costs might rise to EUR 18.7 billion.
- Referendum 27 November 2011: 58.89% No (2,160,411) vs 41.11% Yes (1,507,961), turnout 48.3%; construction continues. A "yes" vote would have meant pulling out of funding.
- Politics: Greens gained a council majority in Stuttgart in June 2009; the March 2011 state election produced a Green-SPD coalition.

wikis.title: Railway Gazette: Stuttgart 21 delayed again
wikis.summary: February 2026 Railway Gazette feature on DB cancelling the partial 2026 opening of Stuttgart 21, the review it commissioned, and the project's cost and controversy.
wikis.body:
By Tony Streeter, February 15 2026 (from the February 2026 issue).

## Delay
- DB cancelled plans for a partial opening in 2026 and commissioned a further review; the project "may not deliver its intended benefits until at least 2032".
- In November (2025) DB announced it had identified "risks" to opening the 420 m underground station in 2026 and much of the project, notably the pilot phase of the DKS digital resignalling project (Digital Knoten Stuttgart, launched 2020, ETCS Level 2 for S-Bahn). No new date was announced.
- Visiting Stuttgart in December, new DB Chief Executive Evelyn Palla launched an internal investigation. A new date is not expected until mid-2026 at the earliest; observers suggest some trains could use the facilities during 2027.

## Cost and history
- Agreed in principle in 1994 at EUR 2.5bn, to complete by 2008; works began 2010; ~EUR 4bn by 2009; completion pushed to 2019. Recent estimates put final cost at "more than EUR 11bn".
- DB lost a key court case on sharing overruns (rejected 2024); on August 5 2025 Baden-Württemberg's Administrative Court refused DB an appeal.

## Scope
- 16 terminal platforms replaced by eight through tracks; ~100 ha of land freed for two new districts; about 100 km of new track, 11 tunnels (56 km combined bore), 42 bridges; new Flughafen Fernbahnhof airport station via the Fildertunnel; extra S-Bahn station at Mittnachstraße.
- Promoters expect ~10 million passengers per year to benefit. Planned December 2026 times: Hbf-airport 6 min (from 27), Stuttgart-Ulm 64 to 41 min.
- Wendlingen-Ulm (59.6 km) opened December 2022. In July 2025 DB had expected all long-distance and about half of regional trains rerouted from the December 2026 timetable change, remaining regional services in 2027.
- Pfaffensteig tunnel: 10.8 km, two single-track bores, airport to Mönchsbrunnen near Böblingen; alliance agreement signed November 2023; completion not envisaged until 2032.

## Criticism
- Environmental damage, cost and partial demolition of the Bonatz-Bau (north and south wings removed). Winfried Kretschmann called Germany's image on railways "highly precarious". A citizens' initiative just failed to reach 20,000 signatures. Stuttgart dropped legal proceedings on reuse of railway land in December 2025.

wikis.title: Chūō Shinkansen maglev line (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on JR Central's under-construction Tokyo-Nagoya-Osaka maglev line, covering its delayed opening dates, cost, route and the Shizuoka dispute.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Maglev line under construction from Shinagawa (Tokyo) to Nagoya, with plans to extend to Osaka; owner JR Central; stock L0 Series; operating speed 505 km/h. Tokyo-Nagoya 285.6 km (about 90% in tunnels), Tokyo-Osaka 438.0 km. Expected journey times: 40 minutes Tokyo-Nagoya, 67 minutes Tokyo-Osaka.
- Intermediate stations on the first section: Sagamihara, Kōfu, Iida, Nakatsugawa; later Mie, Nara, Osaka.
- Government permission to proceed granted 27 May 2011; MLIT approved Plan C on 31 October 2014; construction began 17 December 2014. Cost "over ¥9 trillion" (about $82 billion USD), up from 5.1 trillion yen estimated in 2007.
- A 42.8 km Yamanashi test track (opened 1997) is used; public 500 km/h rides began in 2014.

## Opening dates
- Tokyo-Nagoya: originally 2027; in 2024 JR Central President Shunsuke Niwa said 2027 was impossible and it would not open until at least 2034; then "in 2025, it was further pushed back to no earlier than 2035". The infobox says "No earlier than 2035".
- Nagoya-Osaka: planned as late as 2045, moved to as early as 2037 after a government loan; infobox says "No earlier than 2037".
- The page carries an "update needed" notice dated February 2026.

## Shizuoka dispute
- Shizuoka Prefecture denied permission for construction in June 2020 over Ōi River water concerns (a section of about 9 km); JR Central said 2027 was "difficult".
- Governor Heita Kawakatsu resigned 2 April 2024; Yasutomo Suzuki won the 26 May 2024 by-election; preliminary work approved as of October 2024.
- January 2026: Suzuki and Niwa signed an agreement for JR to compensate for water resources. 26 March 2026: the prefecture's special committee approved all 28 environmental measures; a vice governor said construction could begin by the end of 2026. 7 July 2026: Suzuki announced he would finalize the agreement on 18 July, which "would allow JR Central to begin the maglev service as early as 2036".
- 27 October 2021: two construction workers died in a work tunnel wall collapse.

## Other
- Fares estimated about 700 yen above Tokaido Shinkansen for Tokyo-Nagoya and about 1,000 yen for Tokyo-Osaka.

wikis.title: Chuo Shinkansen completion delayed until 2034 (Railway Gazette)
wikis.summary: April 2024 Railway Gazette report that JR Central no longer expects Tokyo-Nagoya maglev service in 2027 because tunnel work in Shizuoka has not begun.
wikis.body:
Published April 25 2024.
- Central Japan Railway announced at the end of March (2024), after a March 29 transport ministry meeting, that it no longer expects to start Tokyo-Nagoya superconducting maglev service in 2027.
- President Shunsuke Niwa: "we cannot project a new opening date"; "we cannot estimate a new starting year because we have no idea when we can begin work on tunnel construction within Shizuoka Prefecture." Excavating and fitting out the tunnel "is expected to take at least 10 years". The article text itself gives no 2034 date (2034 appears only in the headline).
- Cause: Shizuoka prefectural government refused to allow work on nearly 9 km of tunnel, fearing effects on the Oi River water volume. Kyodo News reported late 2023 that a JR Central dam proposal had been accepted, but a MLIT report in December raised concerns about damage to the Minami Alps ecology.
- On December 14 (2023) JR Central said it would change the scheduled completion year from "2027" to "on or after 2027".

wikis.title: IGN: GTA 6 delayed again until November 19, 2026

wikis.body:
By Rebekah Valentine, updated Nov 7, 2025.
- Grand Theft Auto VI "has been delayed until November 19, 2026", announced by Rockstar as part of Take-Two's second-quarter earnings. Take-Two said it was "giving the team some additional time to finish the game with the high level of polish players expect and deserve."
- Previously announced for fall 2025, then delayed to May 2026.
- Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick: "We've had more time to develop the title... We are grateful that it is still within the same fiscal year." He said players should not expect changes to the cadence of GTA Online updates.
- The prior week Take-Two fired dozens of employees alleging "gross misconduct"; the employees say it was for union-organising chats. They protested at Rockstar North and Take-Two's UK offices.

wikis.title: TheGamer: GTA 6 delay reportedly about polish, game said to be content complete
wikis.summary: TheGamer report that the GTA 6 delay to November 2026 is reportedly for optimisation, with discussion of the layoffs and studio morale.
wikis.body:
By James Lucas, published Nov 7, 2025.
- Rockstar announced it was delaying GTA 6 again to November 2026. Reporter Reece 'Kiwi Talkz' Reilly said the game is "content complete" and remaining work is optimisation "to prevent a Cyberpunk [2077] scenario"; he doubted insider claims of a delay to 2027 or a messy state.
- Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick told IGN "more time was required to polish" and said he is "highly confident on the new date", though he said the same earlier in the year.
- Layoffs were not blamed: Reilly said developers were told of the delay "well before the union layoffs"; Jason Schreier said the delay was announced because Take-Two reported earnings that day. Reilly noted about 6,000 employees work at Rockstar.
- The IWGB called the layoffs "ruthless" union busting; an anonymous employee on GTA Forums said "morale in the studio is at rock bottom" and alleged refusal of union representation in disciplinary meetings. Schreier said this could lead to missed deadlines later.
- Listed release date: November 19, 2026.

wikis.title: Tesla Roadster (second generation) (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Tesla's upcoming second-generation Roadster: specifications, claimed performance, price, and the history of repeated delays including an October 1 launch event tease.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Upcoming battery-electric four-seater (2+2) sports car from Tesla, Inc.; production "yet to commence"; designer Franz von Holzhausen. Tri-motor all-wheel drive (one front, two rear motors), 200 kWh battery, claimed range 620 mi (1,000 km), Supercharger V3 at >350 kW.
- Claimed performance: 0-60 mph in 1.9 seconds (Musk earlier said 2.1 s base; 1.1 s with rocket thruster option); 0-1/4 mile 8.88 s; top speed above 250 mph. In February 2024 Musk said the design goal was 0-60 mph in under one second. Torque at the wheels stated as 7,400 lb-ft.
- Unveiled as a concept on November 16, 2017 at the Tesla Semi event; originally set to start production in 2020 with 10,000 units.
- Price: base model listed at $200,000, Founder's Series (first 1,000) $250,000; pre-orders required a $50,000 deposit.
- June 2018: "SpaceX option package" of about ten cold gas thrusters proposed. August 2025: patent filed for ground effect technology.

## Production date slips
- 2020 (Nov 2017 announcement) -> 2022 (Jan 2021) -> 2023 (Sept 2021) -> hoped 2024 (May 2023) -> 2025 (Feb and Oct 2024).
- November 2025 shareholder meeting: Musk said the production version would be unveiled April 1, 2026, with production 12 to 18 months later; the lead says Musk said production would begin in 2027.
- "On September 12, 2026, Tesla teased a 'Go for launch' event on social media, to take place in Waco, Texas on October 1."

## Analysis
- Bloomberg NEF analyst Salim Morsy doubted the 200 kWh battery was physically possible in 2017; a Carnegie Mellon professor found the 1.9 s claim reasonable given estimated battery weight of 1,836 pounds (833 kg).

wikis.title: Electrek: Tesla delays Roadster demo to April 1, production to 2027/28
wikis.summary: Electrek report on Musk's November 2025 shareholder-meeting statement pushing the Roadster 2 unveiling to April 1, 2026 and production 12-18 months later.
wikis.body:
By Jameson Dow, Nov 6 2025.
- At Tesla's shareholder meeting Musk said the Roadster 2 "product unveil... will be very different than what we've shown previously", with the demo "tentatively" on April 1 of next year: "I have some deniability because I can say I was just kidding." Production "probably about 12-18 months after that."
- The week before, Musk had said a demo was coming at the end of the year and that the car would have "crazier" tech than all James Bond vehicles combined.
- Founders' Series reservation holders ($250,000 paid for the last 8 years) would be invited to the demo.
- Electrek's reading: reveal delayed at least 3 months; production start at least April 2027 or as late as October 2027, so likely 2028 availability, 11 years after first unveiling. A job listing for a "concept development" engineer suggests even 2027 may be optimistic.
- Originally unveiled 2017 for a 2020 release. Electrek notes Tesla patented a "fan car" grip system.

wikis.title: Yahoo Finance: TSLA on track for worst week as Roadster demo slips again
wikis.summary: June 5, 2026 report that Tesla reportedly postponed the Roadster public demo to August or later, with Tesla shares down 5%.
wikis.body:
By Anan Ashraf, June 5, 2026.
- Tesla shares (TSLA) fell 5% on Friday after reports (The Information, citing four people) that the Roadster public demo was postponed to "August or later"; the unveiling is expected in Texas.
- Musk had said the unveil would be April 1; he later said on X it was pushed to later in May or early June, with no updates since.
- November 2025: at the shareholder meeting Musk said the demo would be April 1, 2026 and production would start in the first half of 2027; he picked April 1 for "deniability".
- Stock on track for its worst week since June 2025.
- Musk has said Tesla is working with SpaceX so the Roadster could reach 0-60 mph in under a second (initial estimate 1.9 seconds). Per The Information, Tesla plans a limited-edition SpaceX version plus a scaled-down version; the SpaceX version was presented to Musk in late April. Musk called the hover time "classified" and said "If safety is your #1 goal, don't buy the Roadster."
- Tesla has not launched a new vehicle since Cybertruck deliveries began in late November 2023. The second-gen Roadster was announced November 2017 with deliveries slated for 2020.

wikis.title: BepiColombo (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the ESA/JAXA BepiColombo Mercury mission, with its 2024 thruster issue delaying arrival to November 2026 and the planned orbit-insertion schedule.
wikis.body:
## Mission
- Joint ESA/JAXA mission to Mercury with two orbiters: the Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO, ESA) and Mio (Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, JAXA). Cruise stack also included the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) and the MOSIF sunshield.
- Launched 20 October 2018, 01:45 UTC on Ariane 5 ECA (VA245) from Kourou. Estimated cost in 2017: EUR 1.65 billion (US$1.86 billion).
- Cruise used solar electric propulsion and nine gravity assists: Earth April 2020, Venus October 2020 and August 2021, six Mercury flybys (1 Oct 2021, 23 Jun 2022, 19 Jun 2023, 4 Sep 2024, 1 Dec 2024, 8 Jan 2025).

## Delay
- Originally expected to enter orbit in December 2025 (5 December 2025). On 15 May 2024 ESA reported an issue stopping the thrusters from operating at full power (during a 26 April 2024 manoeuvre); on 2 September 2024 ESA said a revised trajectory adds 11 months, moving arrival to November 2026.

## Arrival schedule (as of September 2026)
- 15 June 2026: solar electric propulsion switched off for the last time. 3 September 2026: MTM separated, starting the Mercury Arrival Phase.
- 21 November 2026: Mercury orbit insertion (planned; "weakly captured" in polar orbit); 10 December 2026: Mio reaches science orbit and detaches from MPO (planned); early 2027: MPO reaches science orbit; April 2028 end of nominal mission (one year of science, possible one-year extension to December 2029).
- Orbits: MPO 480 x 1,500 km; Mio 590 x 11,640 km.

## Spacecraft
- MTM 2,615 kg incl. 1,400 kg xenon; four QinetiQ T6 ion thrusters, max combined thrust 290 mN. MPO 1,150 kg with 11 instruments; Mio 285 kg with 5 instrument groups. Operated from Darmstadt, Germany; Cebreros (Spain) 35 m ground station.
- Named after Giuseppe "Bepi" Colombo (1920-1984); "Mio" means waterway in Japanese.

wikis.title: ESA BepiColombo factsheet
wikis.summary: ESA factsheet on the BepiColombo Mercury mission with spacecraft masses, journey milestones through the planned November 2026 orbit entry, and instruments.
wikis.body:
- Joint ESA/JAXA mission; ESA provides MPO, the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) and Mio's sunshield MOSIF; JAXA provides Mio (MMO). Named for Giuseppe (Bepi) Colombo (1920-84). Over 35 European companies plus US and Japan teams contributed.
- Launch 20 October 2018 on Ariane 5 (dates listed "19/20 October 2018"). Launch mass 4100 kg incl. 1400 kg propellant, 1230 kg MPO (85 kg science payload), 255 kg MMO (45 kg payload). Composite 3.9 x 3.6 x 6.3 m.
- Journey milestones: Earth flyby 10 April 2020; Venus 15 October 2020 and 11 August 2021; Mercury flybys 1 Oct 2021, 23 Jun 2022, 19 Jun 2023, 4 Sep 2024, 1 Dec 2024, 8 Jan 2025; MTM separates 3 September 2026; MPO+Mio enter Mercury orbit 21 November 2026; MPO and Mio separate 9-10 December 2026; science operations start April 2027.
- MPO has 11 instruments (BELA, ISA, MPO-MAG, MERTIS, MGNS, MIXS, MORE, PHEBUS, SERENA, SIMBIO-SYS, SIXS); Mio has 5 (MGF, MPPE, PWI, MSASI, MDM).
- Third mission to visit Mercury, second to enter orbit after NASA's Messenger (2011-2015); Mariner 10 flew by three times 1974-75. Mercury's day (noon to noon) is 176 Earth days, year 88 days.

wikis.title: ESA: Fourth Mercury flyby begins BepiColombo's new trajectory
wikis.summary: ESA article dated 02/09/2024 explaining how a thruster power glitch pushed Mercury arrival from December 2025 to November 2026 and previewing the 4 September 2024 flyby.
wikis.body:
Dated 02/09/2024.
- Teams spent four months on a glitch that stopped BepiColombo's thrusters operating at full power; the mission is "still on track" with a new trajectory.
- Cause: from April 2024, unexpected electric currents between the MTM's solar array and the power unit meant less power for electric propulsion. Mission Manager Santa Martinez: the MTM's thrusters "will remain operating below the minimum thrust required for an insertion into orbit around Mercury in December 2025."
- New trajectory (from ESA's Flight Dynamics team): "BepiColombo is now expected to arrive at Mercury in November 2026." Fourth flyby on 4 September (closest approach 21:48 UTC) at 165 km altitude, about 35 km closer than originally planned; fifth (December 2024) and sixth (January 2025) flybys go ahead as planned. MTM fires thrusters September to October 2024.
- Science is expected to be unaffected: 16 instruments across two orbiters; ten could operate during the flyby. First images expected released 5 September; first science results 13 September.

wikis.title: ESA: BepiColombo turns off solar electric propulsion for Mercury arrival
wikis.summary: ESA article dated 24/06/2026 reporting that BepiColombo's solar electric propulsion shut down for the last time on 15 June 2026, starting the arrival phase.
wikis.body:
Dated 24/06/2026.
- At 15:24 CEST on 15 June 2026 the four QinetiQ T6 solar electric thrusters in the MTM completed their final thrust arc, ending the eight-year cruise phase (nine planetary flybys: one Earth, two Venus, six Mercury).
- Next: MTM separation on 3 September 2026, on a "ballistic" trajectory; then MPO's chemical propulsion adjusts the trajectory before the Mercury orbit insertion manoeuvre on 21 November, guides the craft to Mio's deployment orbit in early December, and lowers MPO into science orbit "by March 2027".
- Lead SEP thruster engineer Neil Wallace met the team at ESOC in Darmstadt to review lessons learned.

wikis.title: Melbourne Airport railway station (planned)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the planned elevated Melbourne Airport station, its delays to 2033 and the dispute with the airport operator.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Proposed station on the planned Melbourne Airport railway line, at Arrival Drive, Tullamarine, near Terminal 4.
- Status: planned premium station; 2 platforms, 2 tracks; owner VicTrack (projected), operator Metro Trains Melbourne (projected).
- Opening: 2033 (planned). Initially scheduled to open in 2029; now expected from 2033.
- Connects with the Metro Tunnel; trains would travel via Sunshine, Melbourne CBD stations, and the Pakenham and Cranbourne lines (limited express services via Town Hall).

## Delays and dispute
- Early 2023: media reports suggested a delay.
- May 2023: the state government confirmed contracting would be paused until a major Commonwealth infrastructure pipeline review finished. November 2023: the federal government reaffirmed its matching $5 billion commitment.
- September 2022: state announced an elevated station near the terminals rather than underground (quicker, cheaper, less disruptive). Airport operator APAC objected, wanting it underground to suit terminal expansion and Suburban Rail Loop connectivity.
- May 2023: then Deputy Premier Jacinta Allan said slow negotiations over airport land caused delays.
- April 2024: federal government appointed an independent mediator.
- May 2024: Treasurer Tim Pallas confirmed in the state budget a delay of at least four years, completion 2033 at the earliest.
- July 2024: Melbourne Airport confirmed it would work with the government on an above-ground station; the negotiation time caused the four-year delay to 2033.
- Proposed site between Terminals 3 and 4 above inbound roads, with elevated walkways to Terminals 3 and 4.

## Transport links
Bus routes 478, 479, 482 (CDC Melbourne), SmartBus 901 (Kinetic Melbourne), and four SkyBus express services.

wikis.title: Vietnam's US$67 billion high-speed rail construction start moved to late 2027
wikis.summary: Travel And Tour World article (10 Sep 2026) reporting Vietnam's North-South high-speed railway construction target moved to December 2027, with route and specification details.
wikis.body:
## Timeline change
- Vietnam moved the launch of the North-South high-speed railway to late 2027, "setting back the launch ... by about a year".
- The government originally planned to begin construction in 2027 but later attempted to accelerate; the target start is now December 2027.
- Ministry of Construction: progress slower than anticipated "due to objective reasons"; it instructed agencies to prepare detailed implementation plans (site clearance, consultancy selection, technical surveys, feasibility study, construction planning).

## Project facts
- Estimated investment around US$67.34 billion; length approx. 1,541 km; Hanoi (Ngoc Hoi Station) to Ho Chi Minh City (Thu Thiem Station); double track; 15 provinces and cities.
- Designed speed up to 350 km/h; expected journey about 5.5 hours versus about 30 hours by rail currently.
- Ticketing systems and fares not yet announced; construction has not started.

wikis.title: Vietnam timeline for the $67 billion North-South high-speed railway
wikis.summary: VietnamNet article (20 May 2026) giving the project's specifications, cost, and schedule from feasibility study to groundbreaking and 2035 completion.
wikis.body:
## Schedule
- Expected to complete feasibility study procedures and break ground between Q4 2026 and Q4 2028.
- Substantially completed by 2035.
- Land clearance split into independent provincial projects, targeted complete by Q4 2028.
- Consultant selection for the feasibility study expected to begin June 2026; interim feasibility report due by June 2027.
- National Assembly has approved the investment policy (per Thang Long Project Management Board, Ministry of Construction).

## Specifications
- About 1,541 km, Ngoc Hoi Station (Hanoi) to Thu Thiem Station (Ho Chi Minh City), through 15 provinces and cities.
- New double-track standard gauge (1,435 mm), up to 350 kph, axle load 22.5 tonnes; 23 passenger stations, five freight stations; electrified.
- Primarily passenger, also dual-use for defense and security, and freight when necessary.
- A Front-End Engineering Design (FEED) replaces the conventional basic design.
- Preliminary investment over VND1.7 quadrillion, about USD67.34 billion.
- Deputy Minister of Construction Bui Xuan Dung spoke at a consultancy roadshow.
