- NEV: low-speed vehicle certified for roads with limits of 45mph (72km/h) or less. Zero is a two-seater, side-by-side, fully enclosed (unlike Renault Twizy, GEM, golf carts).
- 4kW (5.3hp) motor, 6kWh lithium-ion battery: 55 miles (89km) range, 4.5 hours charge at 110V. Zero+ with 8.3kWh pack: 85 miles (137km), six hours. Weight 877lbs (398kg) or 904lbs (410kg).
- Founder Marcus Li: "85 clean miles at only $1, assuming 12c/kWh"; about 350MPGe; aluminum chassis; 40 percent smaller than a Smart Car. No self-driving; Li believes autonomy will worsen traffic.
- Not eligible for IRS credit; California Air Resources Board in contact about a $1,000 rebate.
- Eli tooling up; hopes to deliver first vehicles in early 2019. MSRP $10,900, with discounts for preorders.

wikis.title: First Eli Zero Neighborhood Electric Vehicles go into production
wikis.summary: New Atlas reports the Sept 24, 2021 start of the first production run of the Eli Zero NEV with European partners.
wikis.body:
- Sept 24, 2021 (Paul Ridden): Los Angeles-based Eli Electric Vehicles announced the Zero in 2018; an initial production run has now started with manufacturing partners in Europe.
- NEV: top speed 25 mph (40 km/h); Eli says legal on most roads with a 35-mph limit.
- Changes from the 2018 prototype: 72-V architecture (was 48 V), power steering and braking, reversing camera, dual-beam LED headlight, redesigned chassis.
- 4-kW rear-drive motor; 5.8-kWh or 8-kWh battery for 50 or 70 miles (80/112 km). Size 88.6 x 54.3 x 62.5 in; 23.6-ft turning circle; aluminum chassis; 160 liters trunk; 7-inch digital dash; tilting sunroof; two of three configurations have hot/cold AC.
- Homologated late 2020; production-ready earlier in 2021. Shipments to first European distributors expected in the coming weeks; US launch planned "in the near future".
- Second equity crowdfunding on StartEngine launched; first closed July 30 with nearly US$1.4 million from over 1,500 investors.

wikis.title: NASA pays the price of a massive, expensive rocket (SLS delay)
wikis.summary: Ars Technica's May 12, 2017 analysis of why NASA's Space Launch System is likely at least three years late and over budget.
wikis.body:
- May 12, 2017 (Eric Berger). NASA's acting administrator Robert Lightfoot and human spaceflight chief William Gerstenmaier announced completion of a study on adding crew to the first SLS launch (after Trump advisers asked NASA to consider a splashy first-term achievement).
- Result: technically feasible but would cost $600 million to $900 million above the existing budget and would not appreciably advance long-term deep-space goals. Lightfoot: "We're in this for the long haul."
- SLS was born in the 2010 authorization bill signed Oct 11, 2010, mandating launch of the rocket and Orion by December 31, 2016; that slipped to 2017, then to a September-November 2018 target. NASA now says not before 2019 and needs one or two months to finalize; Ars heard from two sources November 2019 for the uncrewed launch.
- Cost: about $10 billion through next year. A 2011 Booz Allen Hamilton analysis warned of "unjustified cost reductions"; the President's budget typically offered about $1.3 billion a year while Congress appropriated $2 billion for SLS. Senators such as Richard Shelby (Alabama, home of Marshall Space Flight Center) backed the program.
- Gerstenmaier, asked why the deadline is missed by up to three years: "I don't know", pointing to the complexity of the work.

wikis.title: NASA confirms first flight of Space Launch System will slip to 2019
wikis.summary: Spaceflight Now, April 28, 2017, on a GAO report and NASA's agreement that the SLS/Orion EM-1 flight will slip from November 2018 into 2019.
wikis.body:
- April 28, 2017 (Stephen Clark): NASA's top human spaceflight official says the maiden SLS flight will slip from November 2018 to some time in 2019, per a GAO report published Thursday.
- Problems named by GAO: missed delivery date of the European-made Orion service module, welding snags in the SLS core stage due to low weld strength, and a tornado at the Michoud Assembly Facility in New Orleans on Feb. 7.
- Bill Gerstenmaier: "maintaining a November 2018 launch readiness date is not in the best interest of the program, and we are in the process of establishing a new target in 2019." Schedule assessment to be completed by Sept. 30.
- GAO urged NASA to tell Congress about the new schedule and delay cost before the 2018 budget; concerns over low cost reserves.
- EM-1: uncrewed lunar orbit trip lasting more than three weeks; Trump administration directed in February a study of adding crew. EM-2 (2021-2023) currently the first piloted mission.
- NASA inspector general (April 13): by end of FY2018 (Sept. 30, 2018) $23 billion spent on SLS, Orion and ground systems, $15 billion since 2012.

wikis.title: NASA reconfirms 2019 for first Space Launch System launch
wikis.summary: The Register, Nov 9, 2017, on NASA's schedule review keeping EM-1 for December 2019 while admitting it could run late.
wikis.body:
- Published Nov 9, 2017 (Richard Chirgwin): NASA reconfirmed it hopes to stage the first SLS and Orion flight (EM-1) in December 2019, but conceded it could run late; earlier assessment said crewed missions wait until at least 2020.
- Review considered building the core stage for the first time, issues with Orion's first European service module, and tornado damage at Michoud in New Orleans.
- Administrator Robert Lightfoot: "several of the key risks identified have not been actually realised".
- EM-1 costs within 15 per cent of budget, ground systems slightly above. More than 100 Orion parts use additive manufacturing.
- "SLS has completed welding on all the major structures for the mission"; a "green run" test (all four RS-25 engines firing) is coming.

wikis.title: Apple's modular Mac Pro may not ship until 2019 (MacRumors)
wikis.summary: MacRumors on April 6, 2017 relaying OSnews claims about why Apple began a modular Mac Pro and how long it might take.
wikis.body:
- April 6, 2017 (Juli Clover): Apple executives that week announced a revamped high-end modular Mac Pro, set for release sometime after 2017; no date given.
- OSnews' Thom Holwerda, citing sources: the Mac Pro was in limbo; negative reaction to the Touch Bar MacBook Pro, a surge of orders for older MacBook Pros, reaction to the LG 5K display and "constant negativity" from pros led Apple to "double down on professional users."
- The decision came "in recent months" with development starting "only a few weeks ago"; Holwerda expects late 2018 at the earliest, more likely early 2019.
- Holwerda also believes Apple is working on MacBook Pro models without Touch Bar and iPad Pro-as-Cintiq-style tablet pairing.
- Apple says the modular design allows regular hardware updates, VR and high-end cinema editing support, and an Apple-branded pro display.

wikis.title: Apple says modular Mac Pro is a 2019 product; Pro Workflow Team formed
wikis.summary: AppleInsider, April 5, 2018, on Apple declaring the redesigned Mac Pro will ship in 2019 and disclosing a new pro engineering group.
wikis.body:
- April 5, 2018 (Roger Fingas): the Mac Pro hadn't had a major update since 2013. The redesigned modular Mac Pro, teased April 2017, won't ship until 2019.
- Tom Boger (senior director of Mac hardware product marketing, to TechCrunch): "the Mac Pro is a 2019 product. It's not something for this year." Told now because pros may be weighing an iMac Pro versus waiting.
- Phil Schiller confirmed work on a standalone monitor. New Pro Workflow Team led by John Ternus works with engineers and hires full-time and contracted artists (visual effects, video editing, 3D animation, music production) to find workflow bottlenecks; effort includes external GPU technology.
- Apple denied any change in roadmap; Ternus: "I don't think that the timeline has fundamentally changed"; modular approach remains the focus, though "the iMac form factor or the MacBook Pros can be exceptionally good tools."

wikis.title: Apple's $5,999 Mac Pro goes on sale Dec. 10, 2019
wikis.summary: CNBC, Dec 9, 2019, on Apple taking orders for the new Mac Pro starting at $5,999.
wikis.body:
- Published Mon, Dec 9 2019 (Todd Haselton): Apple confirmed to CNBC it will begin taking orders for the new Mac Pro on Tuesday, Dec. 10, starting at $5,999. First announced in June at its developer conference; in mid-November Apple said it would launch in December.
- No display included; the 6K Pro Display XDR starts at $4,999, so an all-in system costs "more than $10,000", likely much more with upgrades.
- Aimed at audio and video professionals, not regular consumers.
- Assembled in Austin, Texas, after Apple won tariff relief on some components imported from China; the only computer Apple manufactures in the US. Tim Cook (September statement): "The Mac Pro is Apple's most powerful computer ever and we're proud to be building it in Austin." The previous model was assembled in Texas by contract manufacturer Flex.

wikis.title: Audi and Nvidia working on fully autonomous car for 2020
wikis.summary: MacRumors, Jan 5, 2017, on the CES announcement of an Audi-Nvidia partnership for a self-driving car by 2020.
wikis.body:
- Announced Wednesday (Jan 4, 2017) at CES in Las Vegas: Audi and Nvidia to bring a fully self-driving car to the consumer market by 2020, using Nvidia's AI car computing platform.
- Nvidia CEO Jen-Hsun Huang: "Nvidia is pioneering the use of deep learning AI to revolutionize transportation."
- Audi's Q7 Piloted Driving Concept with Nvidia Drive PX 2; after four days of "training" vehicles reportedly drive a complex road course without pre-mapped routes.
- Partnership nearly a decade old, originally graphics chips for virtual cockpit and navigation. Audi to expand testing on public roads in California and select states in 2018.
- Nvidia has partnerships with over 80 automakers and suppliers; introduced Xavier AI system on a chip in September.
- Context: Apple reportedly shelved its electric car for now and works on a self-driving software platform.

wikis.title: NVIDIA and Audi partner to put AI car on the road by 2020 (press release)
wikis.summary: NVIDIA's Jan 4, 2017 CES press release announcing collaboration with Audi on AI cars starting in 2020.
wikis.body:
- Las Vegas, CES, Jan 4, 2017: NVIDIA and Audi announced collaboration to put advanced AI cars on the road "starting in 2020". Announced at the opening keynote by NVIDIA CEO Jen-Hsun Huang with Audi of America President Scott Keogh.
- First phase focuses on NVIDIA DRIVE PX, an AI platform using trained neural networks.
- CES demo: Audi Q7 piloted driving concept with DRIVE PX 2 and DriveWorks software, using NVIDIA PilotNet; riders sit in back with no one at the wheel; course with varied surfaces and a simulated construction detour.
- Partnership began seven years earlier at CES, producing Audi MMI navigation and virtual cockpit. In coming months Audi rolls out the new A8, "the world's first Level 3 automated vehicle" with Traffic Jam Pilot powered by zFAS integrating NVIDIA hardware and software.

wikis.title: Nvidia and Audi aim to bring a self-driving AI car to market by 2020 (TechCrunch)
wikis.summary: TechCrunch, Jan 4, 2017, on Nvidia's Audi partnership targeting Level 4 autonomy by 2020.
wikis.body:
- Jan 4, 2017 (Darrell Etherington): Nvidia announced several new autonomous-car partners; Audi the biggest. Work together for 10 years; aim is Level 4 autonomy (full self-driving with manual options) by 2020.
- Audi test car at CES: a Q7 with onboard AI trained for only four days yet driving itself competently. Huang: skill "not end of this year, not end of next year – right now."
- System based on Nvidia's new Xavier computing platform, plus an AI-based Co-Pilot for interim autonomy (facial recognition, gaze tracking).
- TechCrunch: possibly the most substantial claim yet of a firm timeline for highly automated driving.

wikis.title: Volkswagen unveils the I.D. concept, a long-range EV due in 2020
wikis.summary: Ars Technica, Sep 28, 2016, on VW's I.D. electric concept shown at the Paris Motor Show, with 250-300 mile range and self-driving from 2025.
wikis.body:
- Sep 28, 2016 (Jonathan M. Gitlin): at the Paris Motor Show VW revealed the I.D. concept, a battery EV VW says goes into production in 2020, positioned parallel to the Golf with similar dimensions.
- 125kW motor; range 250 to 375 miles (400 to 600km) per the text (headline says 250-300 miles). First car on VW Group's Modular Electric Drive (MEB) platform.
- Self-driving mode available from 2025; steering wheel recesses into the dash in automated mode.
- Background: after the diesel scandal VW's board decided electrification was the future; VW forecast 20 to 25 percent of 2025 sales to be EVs.

wikis.title: Amazon launches solar energy initiative on fulfillment center rooftops
wikis.summary: Amazon's 2 March 2017 press release announcing rooftop solar on 50 fulfillment and sortation centers globally by 2020, starting with 15+ US sites in 2017.
wikis.body:
- Announced March 2, 2017 (Seattle, Business Wire; NASDAQ: AMZN).
- Plan: large-scale solar on rooftops of more than 15 fulfillment and sortation centers in the U.S. in 2017, and solar on 50 fulfillment and sortation centers globally by 2020.
- Initial projects due by end of 2017 will generate up to 41 MW, at facilities in California, New Jersey, Maryland, Nevada and Delaware.
- A solar installation could generate as much as 80 percent of a single facility's annual energy needs. Patterson, California: panels cover more than three-quarters of the 1.1 million square foot rooftop and will power the hundreds of Amazon Robotics units.
- Dave Clark (SVP Worldwide Operations): "By diversifying our energy portfolio, we can keep business costs low and pass along further savings to customers."
- Other renewable projects: largest wind farm to date in Texas; wind and solar farms in Indiana, North Carolina, Ohio and Virginia feeding the grid that powers AWS data centers. Announced or under construction projects total 3.6 million MW of renewable energy. Amazon was the leading corporate purchaser of renewable energy in the US in 2016, per the 2017 State of Green Business report.
- Career Choice program expanded to fund NABCEP certification for associates (40 to 80 hours of PV design, OSHA training and hands-on installation). Kara Hurst (Director, Worldwide Sustainability) quoted.

wikis.title: Einride launches prototype of driverless electric truck T-Pod
wikis.summary: Interesting Engineering, 5 July 2017, on Einride's full-scale T-Pod electric autonomous truck prototype and its planned Gothenburg-Helsingborg route.
wikis.body:
- Einride, a Scandinavian startup, released a full-scale prototype of its T-Pod, a fully electric truck meant to replace small heavy-duty fossil-fuel trucks on short trips.
- Range 124 miles; the article gives a "20kWh capacity" (TechCrunch's version of the same story says 200 kWh).
- No driver's cab; also has a remote-control mechanism adding "human flexibility and decision-making".
- Plan: 200 vehicles moving goods between Gothenburg and Helsingborg, Sweden, by 2020. Network capacity up to 2,000,000 pallets per year. Each truck fits 15 standard pallets. Einride claims the network may grow across Sweden faster if trucks work well.
- Company is also building the remote control center and charging stations along routes.
- The prototype is not exactly what will reach roads; the charging system is yet to debut a larger battery capacity. First production trucks "expected to be delivered later this year".
- CEO Robert Falck quoted on accepting change and putting the T-pod system into practice.
- Context: Volvo self-steering trucks; Tesla Semi unveil set for September (Musk tweet, April 13, 2017).

wikis.title: Einride's T-Pod self-driving transport EV gets a full-scale prototype
wikis.summary: TechCrunch, 4 July 2017: Einride built a full-scale prototype of its remote-operated electric autonomous T-Pod truck.
wikis.body:
- Swedish startup Einride built a full-scale prototype of the T-Pod, an electric autonomous transport vehicle it hopes will eventually replace smaller heavy-duty trucks; remote control operation, 200 kWh energy capacity, maximum range around 124 miles.
- Designed without a crew cabin for remote human operation and driverless functioning.
- First service: route between Gothenburg and Helsingborg, Sweden, by 2020 with 200 T-Pods, outfitted with charging stations.
- Network can move up to 2,000,000 pallets per year, which Einride says has roughly the CO2 emissions equivalent of 400,000 passenger cars over the same distance.
- Einride says it might expand the route earlier than planned given client demand.
- Remote control adds "human flexibility and decision-making"; one driver able to control multiple T-Pods at once.
- Byline Darrell Etherington, July 4, 2017.

wikis.title: Einride unveils T-pod autonomous electric truck prototype
wikis.summary: Designboom, 5 July 2017, on Einride's first full-scale T-pod prototype, its specs and planned Swedish route.
wikis.body:
- Swedish company Einride unveiled its first full-scale prototype of the autonomous electric truck 'T-pod'; it can also be remotely controlled by drivers.
- Carries 15 pallets 124 miles on a single charge with zero emissions; the article says each pod is "23 feet (7 meters) in length". Windows and seating removed, simple box form. Einride is developing compatible charging stations.
- Will run between Gothenburg and Helsingborg, Sweden; the first active system will cover 2,000,000 pallets per year, which "corresponds to 400,000 passenger cars on the same route".
- Claimed benefits: emission-free, noise-reduced trucks, workers on standard schedules closer to home, improved road safety, new jobs, more cost-efficient transport.
- Filip Lilja, COO: big long-haul truck makers "keep building bigger trucks to increase efficiency, which ultimately means even more emissions".
- Published Jul 05, 2017 (Hollie Smith).

wikis.title: Tesla Gigafactory to produce three times the original 35 GWh plan by 2020
wikis.summary: NextBigFuture summary of Tesla's January 4, 2017 Gigafactory investor handout on tripling planned capacity to 105 GWh cells and 150 GWh packs.
wikis.body:
- Original plan for Gigafactory 1: 35 GWh of battery cells and 50 GWh of packs. Tesla now plans that capacity for 2018 and will triple it to 105 GWh of cells and 150 GWh of packs for full production around 2020.
- GF1 will produce cells, battery packs, energy storage products and vehicle components. Phase 2 construction (underway) supports 35 GWh cells / 50 GWh packs annually; cell capacity is said to exceed 2013 total global lithium-ion cell production of all other manufacturers combined and to support about 500,000 cars.
- Goals: supply cells for high-volume programs such as Model 3, Powerwall 2 and Powerpack 2; lower capital cost per GWh and cost per kWh.
- All-electric, no fossil fuels consumed directly; 100% sustainable energy via a 70 MW rooftop solar array (~7x larger than the largest installed today) plus ground solar. Closed-loop water system re-circulates about 1.5 million liters (80% reduction in fresh water). On-site recycling facility under construction.
- Partnership with Panasonic (relationship began 2006); tax abatement agreements with the State of Nevada and Storey County; a German manufacturer began making cell cans on site.
- Cost levers named: in-house design/build, higher production density, domesticated production to reduce tariffs, supply-chain re-engineering, improved cell design (2170 vs 18650).
- Page dated January 10, 2017 (by Brian Wang).

wikis.title: Adobe will kill off Flash by 2020
wikis.summary: Interesting Engineering, 26 July 2017, on Adobe's plan to end Flash Player updates and distribution at the end of 2020.
wikis.body:
- Adobe plans to remove support for Flash by the end of 2020. Quote: "We will stop updating and distributing the Flash Player at the end of 2020 and encourage content creators to migrate any existing Flash content to these new open format."
- Chrome, Microsoft Edge and Safari have already pulled the plug (per the article). Microsoft will pull the plug by 2019; Google will phase it out over the next few years with no declared timeline; Mozilla says Firefox users can choose per site and it will look to abandon Flash around 2020; Apple is on board for 2020 (Safari requires per-site approval; optional download on Mac).
- Reasons: HTML5, canvas and WebGL are well implemented; Flash seen as a security risk and battery drain.
- Concern: large amounts of rich web content will be inaccessible after 2020; hope Adobe builds a full-fidelity player using canvas or JavaScript, otherwise archives may be lost.
- Published Jul 26, 2017 (Jessica Miley).

wikis.title: Adobe: Flash and the future of interactive content
wikis.summary: Adobe's 25 July 2017 blog post announcing it will end-of-life Flash, stopping updates and distribution of Flash Player at the end of 2020.
wikis.body:
- As open standards (HTML5, WebGL, WebAssembly) matured they now provide capabilities plugins pioneered; browser vendors are integrating plugin capabilities and deprecating plugins.
- With partners Apple, Facebook, Google, Microsoft and Mozilla, Adobe is "planning to end-of-life Flash": "we will stop updating and distributing the Flash Player at the end of 2020" and encourages creators to migrate content to open formats.
- Adobe remains committed to supporting Flash through 2020: regular security patches, OS and browser compatibility, features as needed on major OS's and browsers that currently support it.
- Plans to "move more aggressively to EOL Flash in certain geographies where unlicensed and outdated versions of Flash Player are being distributed".
- Continues contributing to HTML5 and the WebAssembly Community Group; keeps Adobe Animate (HTML5 animation) and Premiere Pro.
- Page date 2017-07-25.

wikis.title: Adobe's Flash end of life scheduled for 2020 (TechTarget news roundup)
wikis.summary: TechTarget 28 July 2017 roundup covering Adobe's Flash end-of-life date plus Microsoft's bug bounty expansion and Kaspersky Free.
wikis.body:
- Adobe said Flash end of life will occur at the end of 2020; it will "stop updating and distributing the Flash Player at the end of 2020". Working with Apple, Facebook, Google, Microsoft and Mozilla; will keep patching on Windows, Mac OS and Linux until then.
- Background: decline began in 2010 when Steve Jobs kept Flash off iPhones, iPods and iPads for security reasons (citing a Symantec report). Google's Anthony Laforge: three years ago over 80% of Chrome daily desktop users visited sites with Flash; "Today only 17%". Adobe first released Flash Player in 1996; in 2015 it began using HTML5 for a web animation tool.
- Also in roundup: Microsoft launching its Windows Bounty Program on July 26, 2017 (covers Windows Insider Preview features, Hyper-V, mitigation bypass, Windows Defender Application Guard, Edge; payouts $500 to $250,000, highest for critical Hyper-V remote code execution; no time limit). Kaspersky Free antivirus to roll out globally over the next few months with "bare essentials" features.
- Published 28 Jul 2017 (Madelyn Bacon).

wikis.title: TSMC dedicates over 300 R&D staff to 3nm process
wikis.summary: HEXUS, 6 October 2016: TSMC reportedly assigns 300-400 R&D staff to 3nm development, citing CTimes.
wikis.body:
- Per a CTimes News report, TSMC has allocated between 300 and 400 R&D staff to develop its 3nm process, to "break the limitation of Moore's law".
- Background: TSMC started work on 5nm in December 2015; target launch H1 2020.
- Dr. Mark Liu (President and Co-CEO) said the tool would be three-dimensional stacked architecture technology, and that TSMC has established "the complete ecosystems with the intellectual property, automation solutions and equipment providers"; aims to make Taiwan "the strongest fortress in the global semiconductor industry".
- Liu has already earmarked the 3nm R&D staff to move on to 1nm process development.
- Posted 6 October 2016 (Mark Tyson).

wikis.title: Intel introduces XMM 8000 series 5G modems
wikis.summary: HEXUS, 17 November 2017: Intel launched its XMM 8000 series 5G modems and the XMM 7660 LTE modem.
wikis.body:
- Intel launched the XMM 8000 series the day before (article dated 17 November 2017), following Qualcomm's Snapdragon X50 "a month ago".
- XMM 8000 is Intel's first family of commercial 5G multi-mode modems, operating in sub-6GHz and millimetre wave bands. Hopes for design wins in PC, phones and vehicles.
- First product: XMM 8060; supports 5G non-standalone and standalone NR plus 2G, 3G (including CDMA) and 4G. Expected in devices from mid-2019, ahead of wide-scale 5G deployment "the following year".
- Intel plans Wi-Fi 802.11ax (Gigabit Wi-Fi) starting in 2018.
- XMM 7660: LTE modem, Cat-19, up to 1.6 gigabits per second, MIMO, carrier aggregation; due in devices from 2019.

wikis.title: 5G will have 'fastest ever' global rollout (Ericsson Mobility Report 2018)
wikis.summary: TechRadar, 27 November 2018, reporting Ericsson's forecast that 5G will reach 1.5 billion subscriptions and 40% population coverage by 2024.
wikis.body:
- Per the Ericsson 2018 Mobility Report, 5G will have the fastest global rollout of any generational mobile technology: subscriptions expected to reach 1.5 billion and networks covering 40 per cent of the world's population by 2024.
- The first 5G network has gone live in the U.S., with Verizon offering Fixed Wireless Access broadband to several major cities; other operators in North America, Europe and Asia are preparing launches "in the next few months".
- Ericsson predicts a "strong" line-up of 5G devices by Q2 2019, with more advanced, power-efficient smartphones thanks to second-generation chipsets later in the year.
- Fredrik Jejdling (Ericsson): coverage build-out and subscription uptake projected to be faster than previous generations; cellular IoT continues to grow strongly.
- Europe risks falling behind: only 29 per cent of the continent will have adopted 5G by 2024, versus 43 per cent in Japan, South Korea and China, and 55 per cent in the US.
- Published 27 November 2018 (Steve McCaskill).

wikis.title: Dubai to add the world's first rotating skyscraper by 2020
wikis.summary: Interesting Engineering, 19 March 2017, on architect David Fisher's Dynamic Tower planned for Dubai with completion expected in 2020.
wikis.body:
- The "Dynamic Tower" is expected to be completed in 2020, per the article; it describes "80-story-high rotating condos each costing a whopping $30 million" (and calls it a "42-meter skyscraper").
- Architect David Fisher (Israeli-Italian); first proposed in 2008; "first building designed in four dimensions".
- Each apartment rotates 360 degrees independently; residents can program it to follow the sun; voice-activated control of position and speed.
- Stationary core houses an elevator.
- Power: two-foot gap between floors houses 79 wind turbines; UAE hopes to produce 7% of electricity from renewables by 2020.
- First prefabricated skyscraper: 40 factory-built modules per floor, hung from the core.
- Published Mar 19, 2017 (Huseyin Kilic).

wikis.title: Dynamic Tower (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on David Fisher's cancelled 420 m, 80-floor rotating skyscraper planned for the UAE, never built.
wikis.body:
- Also called the rotating tower or Da Vinci Tower; a cancelled 420 m (1,378 ft), 80-floor moving skyscraper by architect David Fisher; status "Never built"; developer Dynamic Architecture; cost AED 1.2 billion, $330 million.
- Each floor designed to rotate independently, max 6 m (20 ft) per minute, one full rotation in 180 minutes. Compared to Suite Vollard (2001, Brazil).
- Proposed as the first prefabricated skyscraper, 40 factory-built modules per floor; Fisher said 90% could be factory-built, cutting cost and workers and taking 30% less time than a normal skyscraper. Core provides a patented clean-water connection based on aircraft mid-air refuelling technology.
- Powered by wind turbines between floors (up to 1,200,000 kWh a year each) and solar panels; surplus enough for five other similar buildings.
- Timeline: 2008 Fisher expected completion in 2010; 2009, late 2011; Fisher did not say where it would be built; February 2009 National Geographic reported Dubai, apartments USD 3 million to 30 million, 1,100+ prospective buyers on a waiting list. Fisher acknowledged he had never built a skyscraper. "By 2019, construction had not started, and there has been no official announcement of the building site."

wikis.title: Dubai's rotating Dynamic Tower proposal is back
wikis.summary: Archinect, 3 Feb 2016: Dynamic Group says an 80-storey rotating tower will stand in Dubai by 2020 if all goes to plan.
wikis.body:
- Dynamic Group told Archinect an 80-storey 'Dynamic Tower' will be standing in Dubai by 2020 "if everything goes to plan".
- Would be the world's first skyscraper of separate rotating floors attached to a central column, with luxury apartments; residents control rotation speed and direction by voice activation (quoted from whatson.ae).
- Proposed in 2008 by architect David Fisher; aims for 420m, which would make it the second tallest building in Dubai and second tallest residential tower in the world behind New York's 432 Park Avenue (425.5m).
- Article by Alexander Walter, Feb 3, 2016.

wikis.title: World's first ropeless multi-directional elevator to be installed in Berlin
wikis.summary: Interesting Engineering, 26 June 2017, on thyssenkrupp's Multi elevator and its first installation in Berlin's East Side Tower.
wikis.body:
- ThyssenKrupp will install the world's first rope-free multi-directional elevator in Berlin, Germany "this year". Multi cabins travel up, down and sideways on a track like a metro; each cabin is powered individually by linear induction motors; horizontal moves via rotating track sections. Uses maglev technology.
- Cabins smaller and slower than traditional but multiple cabins mean short waits. Reduces peak power demand by up to 60%.
- Markus Jetter (head of research): "Buildings are becoming like vertical cities, and they need a flexible transport system similar to a metro". Cable elevators were invented in 1854. Antony Wood (CTBUH) says it could transform tall-building design.
- First full version goes into OVG Real Estate's East Side Tower in Berlin: 140 meters, office high-rise, "expected completion in 2020".
- Published Jun 26, 2017 (Jessica Miley).

wikis.title: thyssenkrupp Elevator wins German Design Award for MULTI cabin
wikis.summary: thyssenkrupp press release, 23 Oct 2017: the MULTI elevator cabin won the German Design Award 2018 in the category Buildings and Elements.
wikis.body:
- Press item dated 2017-10-23. The MULTI cabin design won the German Design Award 2018, category "Buildings and Elements"; the prize is to be presented in Germany on February 9, 2018.
- Design concept by the Junior Professorship in Industrial Design Engineering at TU Dresden; lighting concept and interface by agency neongrau; cabin built by Composyst GmbH. Displayed in the lobby of the thyssenkrupp test tower at Rottweil, Germany.
- MULTI is described as the world's first ropeless, sideways-moving elevator, "currently still being tested".
- Transparent lightweight cabin made from carbon fibers ("as strong as steel, but weighs a third less than alloy"). Carbon parts weigh 150 kg versus about 500 kg for a comparable stainless steel cabin.
- Operating panel has a circular display showing horizontal and circular travel directions.

wikis.title: ThyssenKrupp unveils the world's first sideways-moving elevator system, Multi
wikis.summary: Dezeen, 12 July 2017, on ThyssenKrupp's rope-less Multi elevator installed in a test tower in Rottweil, Germany.
wikis.body:
- Multi, developed by ThyssenKrupp, installed in a purpose-built test tower (246 m tall, Rottweil, Germany) across three shafts. Multiple magnetised cabins on an electromagnetic track move sideways as well as up and down, using linear motor technology from the Transrapid maglev train; exchanger mechanisms like railway switches guide the cars.
- Antony Wood (CTBUH): "the biggest development in the elevator industry since the invention of the safety elevator some 165 years ago."
- First unveiled in 2014. Company claims up to 50 per cent higher transport capacity and up to 60 per cent lower peak power demand. Fewer, smaller shafts can increase usable building area by up to 25 per cent; elevator-escalator footprints can occupy up to 40 per cent of high-rise floor space.
- Andreas Schierenbeck (chairman): "a genuine game-changer".
- OVG Real Estate is the first customer, planning it for the new East Side Tower in Berlin, touted as the world's most sustainable office building.
- Dated 12 July 2017 (Ali Morris).

wikis.title: Construction of Jeddah Tower resumes after years-long hiatus
wikis.summary: CNN, 3 Oct 2024: work on Saudi Arabia's 1,000 m Jeddah Tower has resumed almost seven years after it halted, now scheduled to finish in 2028.
wikis.body:
- Construction of the 1,000-meter (3,280-foot) Jeddah Tower resumed nearly seven years after stopping amid Saudi Arabia's anti-corruption purge. At a Wednesday ceremony the developer, Jeddah Economic Company (JEC), announced completion is now scheduled for 2028.
- It was around a third complete when in 2017 key figures, including chairmen of main contractor Saudi Binladen Group and co-financier Kingdom Holding, were detained. Work came to a standstill in early 2018; Covid-19 also reportedly delayed resumption.
- Prince Alwaleed bin Talal attended and posted "We're back." Bakr bin Laden, reportedly released in 2021, whose family firm has been rehired to complete construction.
- New contract worth 7.2 billion riyal ($1.9 billion), about 1.1 billion riyal ($290 million) already paid for completed work. 63 of 157 stories built.
- Formerly Kingdom Tower; broke ground in 2013, initially expected completion 2020; will stand more than 500 feet above the Burj Khalifa. Office, retail and residential space.
- Published Oct 3, 2024 (Oscar Holland).

wikis.title: Kingdom Holding resumes construction of Jeddah Tower
wikis.summary: World Construction Network (via Yahoo Finance), 21 Jan 2025: Kingdom Holding restarted Jeddah Tower with a ceremonial concrete pour.
wikis.body:
- Kingdom Holding Company (KHC) restarted construction of the Jeddah Tower, Saudi Arabia, with the ceremonial pouring of concrete, attended by chair Prince Al-Waleed bin Talal and CEO Talal Al-Maiman.
- Construction began in 2013 and was halted in early 2018 following the anticorruption campaign led by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.
- Set to be the world's tallest building, height "exceeding more than 1,000m". Bin Talal said it is expected to cost more than SR100bn ($26.6bn). Will include residential units, commercial spaces, a Four Seasons-branded hotel and an observation deck.
- October 2024: KHC announced subsidiary Jeddah Economic Company signed an agreement with Saudi Binladin Group to resume construction, valued at SR7.2bn, construction set to take 42 months.
- Aligned with Saudi Vision 2030. Dated January 21, 2025.

wikis.title: Apple confirms plans for Iowa data center and up to $100M community fund
wikis.summary: MacRumors, 24 Aug 2017: Apple announced a $1.3 billion, 400,000 sq ft data center in Waukee, Iowa.
wikis.body:
- Apple announced plans to build a 400,000-square-foot data center in Waukee, Iowa, providing backend infrastructure for App Store, Siri, Apple Music, iMessage and other services in North America. Investment $1.3 billion; over 550 construction and operations jobs in the Des Moines area.
- Up to $100 million to a new Public Improvement Fund managed by the City of Waukee (parks, libraries, recreational spaces, infrastructure).
- Runs entirely on renewable energy from day one; Apple to invest with local partners in wind and other renewables.
- Construction expected to start early next year (2018), online in 2020.
- Reportedly, Iowa's Economic Development Authority approved $208 million in state and local tax breaks for two data centers near Des Moines; Apple will reportedly buy 2,000 acres. First reported by The Des Moines Register.
- Quotes from Tim Cook and Governor Kim Reynolds. Dated August 24, 2017 (Joe Rossignol).

wikis.title: Apple's next US data center will be built in Iowa
wikis.summary: Apple press release, 24 Aug 2017: a $1.3 billion, 400,000 sq ft renewable-powered data center in Waukee, Iowa.
wikis.body:
- Apple announced a 400,000-square-foot data center in Waukee, Iowa, to serve North American users of iMessage, Siri, the App Store, Apple Music and other services; runs entirely on renewable energy from day one.
- $1.3 billion investment creating over 550 construction and operations jobs in the Des Moines area; up to $100 million contributed to a new Public Improvement Fund managed by the City of Waukee. First project: the Waukee Youth Sports Campus (greenhouse, playground, fishing pier, fields).
- Apple has pledged 100 percent renewable energy globally and reached it in the US and 23 other countries. Tim Cook: Apple is responsible for 2 million jobs in all 50 states and more than 10,000 in Iowa.
- "Construction on the data center is expected to start early next year and Apple plans to bring it online in 2020."
- Last year Apple spent over $50 billion with more than 9,000 US suppliers; US developers have earned over $16 billion in App Store sales since 2008.

wikis.title: Apple confirms $1.3B Iowa data center, operations to start in 2020
wikis.summary: AppleInsider, 24 Aug 2017, on Apple's Waukee data center announcement with added detail on the fund's pace, jobs and incentives.
wikis.body:
- Apple confirmed a $1.3 billion, 400,000 sq ft data center in Waukee, Iowa, near Des Moines, for Siri, iMessage and the App Store, plus up to $100 million for a Public Improvement Fund; entirely renewable power.
- AppleInsider notes the fund will take time to reach $100 million as Apple pays in "about $1 million per year", and that although over 550 construction and operations jobs are cited, "it's likely that just 50 of those will be permanent" (the site's assessment).
- Apple is receiving some $213 million in incentives from state and local government. Construction should start in early 2018, online by 2020.
- Tim Cook to appear in Des Moines and visit students at the Waukee Innovation and Learning Center with Governor Kim Reynolds.
- First fund project: Waukee Youth Sports Campus. Dated Aug 24, 2017 (Roger Fingas).

wikis.title: Suzhou Zhongnan Center (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the stalled 499.2 m, 103-floor Suzhou Zhongnan Center, which replaced an abandoned 729 m design.
wikis.body:
- Stalled 499.2 m (1,638 ft), 103-floor mixed-use (hotel, office, residential) tower in Suzhou Industrial Park, Jiangsu, China; developer/owner Zhongnan Group; architects Gensler and East China Architectural Design. Status "On-hold"; construction started 2020; estimated completion 2028.
- Original design: 729 m, 137 floors, 93 elevators; proposed 2011, construction began 2014, halted 2015, abandoned. It would have been the second tallest building in the world.
- Plans were scrapped in 2019 in compliance with China's ban on buildings over 500 m. New design revealed 2019 (inspired by traditional Suzhou patterns), construction started less than a year later.
- Mid-2022, when construction had reached ground level, work halted due to the owner Zhongnan's financial difficulties. "As of 2026, the tower remains incomplete and no news of it resuming construction has been announced."

wikis.title: Suzhou Zhongnan Center on The Skyscraper Center
wikis.summary: CTBUH Skyscraper Center database entry for Suzhou Zhongnan Center, with limited public facts.
wikis.body:
- Suzhou Zhongnan Center, Suzhou, China; address Xing Zhou Road. Redesign that replaced the previous Suzhou Zhongnan Center project.
- Height 499.2 m / 1,638 ft; 103 floors; function residential / hotel / office.
- Images credited to Zhongnan Group. Further data is restricted to CVU members; the page's status field shows only the list of possible statuses, so the current status is not stated in the text.

wikis.title: Microsoft's next-gen Xbox will arrive in 2020
wikis.summary: Thurrott.com, 12 June 2018: Brad Sams reports, from viewed internal content, that Microsoft plans a next Xbox codenamed Scarlett in 2020.
wikis.body:
- Brad Sams was tipped off that the next-generation Xbox is codenamed "Scarlett" and viewed content highlighting several unannounced Microsoft products coming in the next two years; he verified it as authentic.
- Microsoft is planning the next Xbox release for 2020, and describes Scarlett as a family of devices, so multiple hardware pieces may come that year.
- Unknown: whether it is a brand new set of devices or a more powerful, backward-compatible Xbox One. His expectation: support for current-gen games, more advanced features, possible alignment with upcoming game-streaming services.
- Hedge: "As with any leak this far out, timing and plans can change."
- Published Jun 12, 2018.

wikis.title: Phil Spencer confirms a next-generation Xbox is in development (E3 2018)
wikis.summary: Pocket-lint reports that Xbox chief Phil Spencer said at Microsoft's E3 2018 press conference that the next Xbox is in development, alongside a hinted cloud streaming service.
wikis.body:
- Xbox chief Phil Spencer teased a new Xbox console during Microsoft's E3 2018 press conference, claiming that the "next Xbox" is in development.
- Microsoft had only recently released the "world's most powerful console", the 4K HDR-enabled Xbox One X.
- Spencer was keen to stress the Xbox One is to be replaced in the "near(ish) future", amid many rumours of a PlayStation 5 to be released in the next couple of years.
- The article says what spec is planned is "anyone's guess"; the one sure thing is that the console will keep the name Xbox.
- Also hinted at: a new cloud gaming service. Spencer revealed Microsoft is working on cloud streaming technology to bring console-style games to multiple platforms, including mobile.
- Sony already has a similar service, PS Now, but is reducing the number of platforms it is available on. The article notes cloud game streaming is not proven, since services such as OnLive have fallen by the wayside.
- Published Jun 10, 2018 by Rik Henderson.

wikis.title: Xbox Project Scarlett unveiled as Xbox Series X
wikis.summary: Gematsu relays Microsoft's announcement at The Game Awards 2019 that Project Scarlett is named Xbox Series X, due holiday 2020.
wikis.body:
- Microsoft announced Xbox Series X, the official name for Project Scarlett, at The Game Awards 2019; it will launch in "holiday 2020". Posted Dec 12 2019.
- Microsoft calls it "our fastest, most powerful console ever", with four times the processing power of Xbox One X; it supports both vertical and horizontal orientation.
- A new Xbox Wireless Controller was also unveiled: refined size and shape, a new Share button for screenshots and clips, and a d-pad derived from the Xbox Elite Series 2 controller.
- Senua's Saga: Hellblade II (Ninja Theory) was unveiled, with in-engine footage, built to use the full power of Series X.
- Technical claims: 4K at 60 fps with possibility of up to 120 fps, Variable Refresh Rate (VRR), 8K capability; custom processor using AMD Zen 2 and next-generation RDNA; hardware-accelerated ray tracing; Variable Rate Shading (VRS); next-generation SSD to "virtually eliminate load times"; Auto Low Latency Mode (ALLM) and Dynamic Latency Input (DLI).
- Designed for a future in the cloud.
- Backward compatibility: thousands of games across four generations, all Xbox One accessories, and Xbox Game Pass available at launch.

wikis.title: Microsoft announces Xbox Series X, arriving Holiday 2020
wikis.summary: GSMArena's report on the Xbox Series X announcement, its claimed specs, design and backward compatibility.
wikis.body:
- Announced 13 December 2019 (GSMArena post): Xbox Series X, previously Project Scarlett, is Microsoft's fourth major console and will be available Holiday 2020; successor to Xbox One and Xbox One X.
- Design: vertical, monolithic; Microsoft says it can be placed horizontally. Front has a vertical disc slot with eject button and a USB-A port; a glowing Xbox logo at top left.
- Hardware: AMD CPU on Zen 2 and GPU on RDNA; integrated flash storage for faster loading.
- Claims: 4x the performance of Xbox One X; 4K at 60 fps consistent or 120 fps in some cases; 8K output, though the author says actual rendering will likely stay at 4K.
- Features: VRR, VRS, ALLM (HDMI 2.1), Dynamic Latency Input for developers.
- A Senua's Saga: Hellblade II trailer showed in-engine 4K footage; the author cautions in-engine is not real-time in-game footage.
- Backward compatibility with all three previous Xbox generations; cloud gaming support. More details possibly at E3 2020.

wikis.title: Apple plans new UK headquarters at Battersea Power Station
wikis.summary: MacRumors reports, via the Evening Standard, that Apple will consolidate 1,400 London employees into a new campus at Battersea Power Station expected in 2021.
wikis.body:
- Apple is building a new London campus in Battersea Power Station, moving 1,400 employees from eight London locations. Predicted opening "sometime in 2021".
- Apple is leasing 500,000 square feet, among its largest offices outside US campuses; about 40 percent of total office space, room for 3,000 employees. Top six floors of the former boiler house around a central atrium.
- Apple's official European headquarters is said to remain in Cork, Ireland, where 4,000 employees work.
- The 42-acre site is being restored after 33 years abandoned; also planned: three floors of shops, 253 apartments, a 2,000-seat auditorium and cinemas, designed by Wilkinson Eyre. First apartment tenants as early as December; shops and restaurants spring 2017.
- Apple statement: looking forward to the 2021 opening of "our new London campus". Until then it keeps offices including Hanover Street and James Street.
- Published Wednesday September 28, 2016.

wikis.title: Apple UK to move into a new London campus in 2021
wikis.summary: TechCrunch reports Apple will consolidate eight London offices into a campus at Battersea Power Station in 2021.
wikis.body:
- Apple plans to consolidate its London offices into a single campus in 2021, inside the Battersea Power Station redevelopment zone (news broken by the Evening Standard).
- Apple statement: "We are looking forward to opening Apple's new London campus at The Battersea Power Station in 2021. 1,400 Apple employees from existing offices around London will relocate..."
- Eight Apple sites are to be consolidated, including near its Regent Street store and above Covent Garden.
- Apple rents the top six floors of the former boiler house, the largest office tenant, about 500,000 sq ft or 40 per cent of the total office space.
- Cork, Ireland site accommodates 6,000 staff per this article; the new US HQ is specced for 13,000 in 2.8M sqft.
- The station was decommissioned in 1983; the latest redevelopment is a 9BN pound project backed by Malaysian investors, ongoing since 2012, with a new metro station and 581 promised affordable units (later moved off the main site, and criticised).
- Published 28 September 2016 by Natasha Lomas.

wikis.title: Apple opening a new UK headquarters at Battersea Power Station
wikis.summary: The Apple Post summarizes Apple's plan to merge its eight London offices into Battersea Power Station by 2021.
wikis.body:
- Apple plans a new UK headquarters in Battersea Power Station with room for up to 3,000 employees in 500,000 sq ft of office space, merging all eight existing London offices; expected to open in 2021.
- Mayor of London Sadiq Khan said he was "delighted", calling it "a further sign that London is open to the biggest brands in the world".
- Main European offices remain in Cork, Ireland, employing 4,000.
- Apple quote: "It's a great opportunity to have our entire team working and collaborating in one location while supporting the renovation of a neighbourhood rich with history."
- Described as one of the biggest single office deals in London outside the City and Docklands in two decades.
- Posted 28/09/2016 by Tom Sykes.

wikis.title: NASA closer to an ultra-quiet supersonic passenger jet
wikis.summary: Interesting Engineering reports NASA and Lockheed Martin's quiet supersonic demo plane moving to a bid stage, with a $390 million five-year budget.
wikis.body:
- NASA announced last year it was designing the aircraft with Lockheed Martin; in June 2017 the team did wind tunnel testing of the initial demo, and NASA is now ready to accept bids for building a larger "real-world" version.
- Aim: reduce the sonic boom to a hum, which Lockheed says is akin to the sound inside a luxury car on a highway. Concorde's noise was 90 dBa.
- Flies up to 55,000 feet at supersonic speeds; two engines; could cut New York to Los Angeles from 6 to 3 hours.
- Cost to NASA: $390 million USD over five years; first year funded in the 2018 budget draft.
- NASA plans to share the design with other US fabricators; Peter Coen: "That's going to make it possible for companies to offer competitive products in the future." Boom Technology and Aerion are expected to be interested.
- Other obstacles: carbon emissions (NASA funded an MIT study), airport noise (GE working on engine sound), and legislation that banned the Concorde. NASA plans six test flights over populated areas beginning in 2022.
- Published Jul 25, 2017 by Jessica Miley.

wikis.title: NASA's X-59 makes its historic first flight
wikis.summary: NASA image article on the X-59 quiet supersonic aircraft's first flight on Oct. 28, 2025.
wikis.body:
- The X-59 took off Oct. 28, 2025 at 11:14 a.m. EDT from Lockheed Martin Skunk Works in Palmdale, California, flew 67 minutes, and landed at NASA's Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California.
- NASA test pilot Nils Larson flew to about 12,000 feet at an approximate top speed of 230 mph, "precisely as planned". Landing gear stayed down the whole flight, common for first flights of experimental aircraft.
- Next: test flights at higher altitudes and supersonic speeds, to ensure it meets performance and safety expectations, as part of the Quesst mission.
- Quesst aims to usher in "a new age of quiet supersonic flight".
- Published Nov 20, 2025 (Kristen Hatfield).

wikis.title: NASA's X-59 supersonic demonstrator makes first test flight
wikis.summary: AIN headline and teaser: the X-59 achieved first flight on Oct. 28, 2025, topping 254 knots (only teaser text was retrievable).
wikis.body:
- The X-59 demonstrator achieved its first flight on Oct. 28, 2025 (photo credit Lockheed Martin).
- Subhead: "Supersonic demonstrator topped 254 knots in first test".
- Byline Hanneke Weitering, October 28, 2025. Article body not available in the retrieved text.

wikis.title: Volkswagen confirms electric Microbus return in 2022
wikis.summary: Interesting Engineering reports Volkswagen confirmed at Pebble Beach that a fully electric Microbus will be built and launched in 2022.
wikis.body:
- Volkswagen confirmed at the Pebble Beach Concours D'Elegance in Monterey, California that the microbus will be back in 2022 as a fully electric vehicle.
- CEO Dr. Herbert Diess: after presentations at Detroit and Geneva, customers wrote "please build this car"; "The Microbus has long been part of the California lifestyle. Now we're bringing it back by reinventing it as an electric vehicle."
- Known details: fully electric powertrain, batteries expected in the floor, drive components small to maximize interior space; compact commercial van style with SUV comfort and space; a cargo version; Level three autonomous driving expected as standard across the range.
- It will follow the production version of the I.D. hatchback concept, expected in 2021.
- Background: the original microbus (Transporter/Kombi) was released in 1950, second VW model after the Type 1 (Beetle); the article mentions VW's 2015 emissions scandal.
- Published Aug 22, 2017 by Jessica Miley.

wikis.title: World premiere of the production Volkswagen ID. Buzz and ID. Buzz Cargo
wikis.summary: Volkswagen press release of 03/09/22 for the world premiere of the ID. Buzz and ID. Buzz Cargo, with battery, charging, software, design and launch details.
wikis.body:
- World premiere in Hamburg, press release dated 03/09/22 (Wolfsburg/Hanover). Header note: vehicles are near-production concept cars and have not gone on sale yet.
- Market launch: "this autumn in Europe"; advance orders possible in some countries in May. Europe's first all-electric bus and transporter range; built by Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles in Hanover; based on the Modular Electric Drive Kit (MEB).
- Space: five persons and 1,121 litres of luggage; the Cargo takes two euro pallets.
- Battery/drive: 77 kWh net (82 kWh gross), 150 kW motor driving the rear axle; AC charging at 11 kW; DC up to 170 kW, 5 to 80% in about 30 minutes; Plug & Charge (ISO 15118) planned; bidirectional Vehicle-to-Home charging via a special DC wall box.
- Assistance: Car2X, Front Assist standard, Lane Assist in the MPV; optional Travel Assist with swarm data (partially automated driving, assisted lane-changing on the motorway); Memory Function for automated parking on a saved route.
- Sustainability: manufacture and shipping carbon-neutral footprint; recycled synthetic materials, interior free of real leather. ID. Buzz to be used in MOIA ridepooling.
- Design: Jozef Kaban ties it to the T1 (1950s), short overhangs, V-shaped front panel, optional two-tone paint.
- Quote (Ralf Brandstaetter): "The ID. Buzz is a genuine icon for the electric era."

wikis.title: Volkswagen presents the ID. BUZZ concept at NAIAS 2017 Detroit
wikis.summary: Volkswagen press release (01/09/17) presenting the ID. BUZZ electric MPV concept with up to 600 km range and eight seats.
wikis.body:
- Presented at the North American International Auto Show (NAIAS) in Detroit; press release dated 01/09/17. Described as the microbus of the new age; brand claim "We make the future real."
- Dr Herbert Diess: by 2025 VW wants to sell one million electric cars per year; from 2020 the I.D. family launches, "affordable for millions, not just to millionaires".
- Concept: up to 600 km NEDC range, up to eight seats, all-wheel drive with 275 kW / 374 PS (150 kW motors front and rear), 0-100 km/h in 5 seconds, top speed limited to 160 km/h; 150 kW charging gives 80 percent in around 30 minutes; also inductive charging.
- Dimensions: 4,942 mm long, 1,976 mm wide, 1,963 mm high, 3,300 mm wheelbase; based on extended MEB XL platform.
- Fully automated "I.D. Pilot" mode (envisaged as of 2025): steering wheel retracts; sensors include laser scanners, radar, cameras; AR head-up display, removable tablet, touch-sensitive steering wheel.
- Unveiled four months earlier: the compact I.D. at the Paris Motor Show, launching as of 2020.

wikis.title: France aims for driverless high-speed trains by 2023
wikis.summary: Interesting Engineering on SNCF's 'drone trains' project: a freight prototype by 2019 and passenger service by 2023.
wikis.body:
- Government-owned SNCF has a "drone trains" project. The first prototype is pitched for 2019 (article prints "219"), first hauling cargo; passenger service around 2023 between Paris and the south-east of France.
- Trains look ordinary but carry external sensors that detect obstacles and apply automatic braking. A driver stays on board to supervise.
- Meant to make station operations more efficient by eliminating "tedious manoeuvres of setting up in stations before departure".
- Matthieu Chabanel (SNCF adjoint director) compared it to aircraft autopilot.
- SNCF believes it could scale up speed and regularity around Paris. Mentions the partially automated London metro line and Lille Metro.
- Published Jun 22, 2017 by Jessica Miley.

wikis.title: SNCF to run high-speed driverless trains by 2023
wikis.summary: RailwayPro on SNCF's plan to be the first to run driverless high-speed commercial trains, trials from 2019 and service from 2023.
wikis.body:
- SNCF CEO Guillaume Pepy told Le Figaro: "We will become the first in the world to put into service an autonomous train on a high-speed commercial rail line."
- Trials begin in 2019; driverless high-speed trains could run starting 2023, operating like airplane autopilot with a driver on board to supervise and handle unexpected events.
- By 2019 SNCF hopes to test a prototype, only on freight trains.
- Driverless trains are common on metros (about 50 km/h, mainly in tunnels). SNCF says the aim is not saving personnel costs but more effective service and more TGVs on the tracks.
- Dated June 19, 2017.

wikis.title: France announces driverless high-speed trains by 2023 (CGTN)
wikis.summary: CGTN reports SNCF's plan for autonomous TGV trains by 2023 with trials from 2019 and up to 25 percent more trains Paris-Lyon.
wikis.body:
- SNCF announced on Friday it is developing autonomous "drone trains" for its high-speed TGV lines by 2023, with initial trials in 2019.
- Goal: increase speed and frequency; per FranceInfo, 25 percent more trains between Paris and Lyon and time between trains cut from 180 seconds to 108 seconds.
- External sensors detect obstacles and brake automatically; conductors will ride along for a while in case of emergencies. Passenger services expected 2023.
- Guillaume Pepy told Le Figaro SNCF would be the first operator in the world to run automated high-speed trains if it succeeds.
- Published 2017-06-18 by Guo Meiping.

wikis.title: PlayStation VR2 review (IGN)
wikis.summary: IGN's review of PlayStation VR2 calling it a generational leap at $549.99, held back mainly by game selection.
wikis.body:
- By Gabriel Moss, updated Sep 12, 2024. Verdict: "a quantum leap in console VR gaming"; console VR leads in "just about every category... except available games".
- Price $549.99. Specs: HDR OLED, two 2,000 x 2,040 per-eye panels at up to 120 Hz, 110-degree field of view, built-in tracking cameras (four), eye tracking, two Sense controllers with adaptive triggers and haptic feedback.
- Compared: HP Reverb G2 (dual 2,160 x 2,160 LCD, 90 Hz, 98-degree FOV, no HDR); Meta Quest Pro costs three times as much. Requires a PS5 via a single 4.5 m USB-C cable.
- Setup: firmware update, calibration of controllers, eye tracking and lens spacing; room scan; guardian walls. Passthrough button; IPD slider.
- Sense controllers: battery lasts around four to five hours per charge. Games mentioned: Horizon Call of the Mountain, Star Wars: Tales from the Galaxy's Edge, Tetris Effect: Connected.
- Quotes the 2016 PlayStation VR review, Score 8.5.

wikis.title: PlayStation VR2 launches February 22, 2023 at $549.99
wikis.summary: PlayStation.Blog announcement of the PS VR2 launch date, prices, bundle, pre-orders and specs.
wikis.body:
- Posted November 2, 2022 by Isabelle Tomatis (Sony Interactive Entertainment): PlayStation VR2 launches February 22, 2023; pre-orders begin November 15 (registration from the announcement day).
- Prices (RRP): PS VR2 $549.99 / EUR 599.99 / GBP 529.99 / JPY 74,980 (headset, Sense controllers, stereo headphones); Horizon Call of the Mountain bundle $599.99 / EUR 649.99 / GBP 569.99 / JPY 79,980; Sense controller charging station $49.99 / EUR 49.99 / GBP 39.99 / JPY 5,480.
- Initial pre-orders in US, UK, France, Germany, Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg solely via direct.playstation.com; orders ship throughout launch week.
- Features: headset feedback, eye tracking, 3D audio, adaptive triggers and haptics; 4000 x 2040 HDR (2000 x 2040 per eye), OLED; slimmer and lighter than the previous headset, integrated vent, lens adjustment dial.
- "More than 20 titles at launch".

wikis.title: PlayStation VR2 review (NPR): strong foundation, questionable future
wikis.summary: NPR's James Delahoussaye praises PS VR2's screens and comfort but doubts its game library and price.
wikis.body:
- Published Feb 21, 2023. Horizon Call of the Mountain is the flagship launch title (launching Wednesday alongside PS VR2), a contained, almost on-rails experience of maybe 6-7 hours.
- Praise: "easily the best screens I've seen in a VR headset" (OLED); eye tracking for menus and foveated rendering; headset haptics; easy setup; comfortable, glasses-friendly.
- Criticism: tethered to PS5; of launch titles only Call of the Mountain is truly made-for-PS VR2, others ported (Resident Evil Village and Gran Turismo 7 get VR updates); Sony says 100+ games in the works, most likely ports; price over $500. Suggests a Meta Quest 2 or upcoming Quest 3 for newcomers.
- Concern: hard to imagine PS VR2 selling well enough to inspire costly new third-party VR games.

wikis.title: Demon Slayer season 3 (Swordsmith Village arc) guide
wikis.summary: GamesRadar+ guide to Demon Slayer season 3: finale date, episode-by-episode story recap, cast, theme songs and where to watch.
wikis.body:
- Last updated 12 June 2023 (Bradley Russell). The season 3 finale is an extended episode airing Sunday, June 18 on Crunchyroll and Funimation at 10:45 AM Pacific / 1:45 PM Eastern (6:45 PM UK), possibly 45-60 minutes and likely setting up season 4.
- Season 3 is the Swordsmith Village Arc, covering manga chapters 98-127, around 11-12 episodes.
- Story: Tanjiro recovers at Hashira HQ; Muzan sends Upper Rank demons Gyokko and Hantengu; Tanjiro and Nezuko go to Swordsmith Village to repair his sword and meet the Love Hashira (Mitsuri Kanroji) and Mist Hashira (Muichiro Tokito); Kotetsu helps Tanjiro; Hantengu splits into personas (joy, anger, pleasure, sorrow; Karaku, Sekido); Genya helps; Muichiro defeats Gyokko; Mitsuri fights.
- Cast (Japanese): Tanjiro (Natsuki Hanae), Zenitsu (Hiro Shimono), Inosuke (Yoshitsugu Matsuoka), Nezuko (Akari Kitou), Muichiro (Kengo Kawashini), Mitsuri (Kana Hazawa), Kotetsu (Ayumu Murase), Hantengu (Toshio Furukawa), Gyokko (Kousuke Toriumi), Kokushibo, Akaza, Doma, Nakime, Muzan (Toshihiko Seki).
- OP "Kizuna no Kiseki" and ED "Koikogare" by Man With a Mission and Milet.
- Streams on Crunchyroll and Funimation; English dub weekly on Sundays; Netflix has seasons 1-2 in some territories.

wikis.title: Demon Slayer Swordsmith Village Arc: April 2023 premiere and March US movie release
wikis.summary: Epicstream (Dec 12, 2022) on the season 3 broadcast date and a US/Canada cinema release of a compilation movie in March 2023.
wikis.body:
- Aniplex of America and Crunchyroll announced details via the official website. Confirmed: the Swordsmith Village arc is a TV anime series, not a feature film; premieres April 2023 on Fuji TV in Japan; streaming not yet confirmed but Crunchyroll is likely.
- The cinema release is a movie cut combining Entertainment District arc episodes 10 and 11 plus the first Swordsmith Village episode.
- Premiere at the Orpheum Theatre in downtown Los Angeles on February 18, 2023, attended by Natsuki Hanae, Aniplex producer Yuma Takahashi and OP singer Aimer; tickets on Ticketmaster.com from January 7, 2023.
- US and Canada select cinemas: March 3, 2023, as part of the "Kimetsu no Yaiba -To the Swordsmith Village- World Tour": Tokyo, Los Angeles, Paris, Berlin, Mexico City, Seoul, Taipei.
- Published Dec 12, 2022 by Nicolo Manaloto.

wikis.title: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba season 3 (Swordsmith Village Arc)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the third anime season: 11 episodes aired April 9 to June 18, 2023 on Fuji Television, adapting manga chapters 98-127.
wikis.body:
- 11 episodes; original network Fuji Television; aired April 9 - June 18, 2023. Based on Koyoharu Gotouge's manga; adapts volumes 12-15 (chapters 98-127). Announced at the end of season 2's finale.
- Directed by Haruo Sotozaki; character designs and chief animation director Akira Matsushima; animation by Ufotable; main cast returned.
- Story: Tanjiro and Nezuko travel to Swordsmith Village and join Mist Hashira Muichiro Tokito and Love Hashira Mitsuri Kanroji, with Genya Shinazugawa, to defend the village from two attacking Upper Rank demons.
- Music: opening "Kizuna no Kiseki" (Miracle of Bonds), ending "Koi Kogare" (Yearning), both by Man with a Mission and Milet; insert "Kamado Nezuko no Uta" by Go Shiina featuring Nami Nakagawa in the finale.
- On February 3, 2023, a compilation film "To the Swordsmith Village" (final two Entertainment District episodes plus an advance screening of the first Swordsmith Village episode) premiered in Japan.
- Aniplex of America licensed it outside Asia and streamed it on Crunchyroll, which began an English dub on May 28, 2023; in July 2024 at San Diego Comic-Con it was announced the dub would air on Adult Swim's Toonami, August 11 to October 20, 2024.

wikis.title: Demon Slayer Swordsmith Village Arc trailer reveals April 9 premiere
wikis.summary: Anime News Network (2023-03-01): TV anime premieres April 9 on Fuji TV with a one-hour special; also world tour screening box office.
wikis.body:
- The official Twitter account announced on Wednesday (posted 2023-03-01) that the Swordsmith Village Arc TV anime premieres April 9 at 11:55 p.m. JST on Fuji TV with a one-hour special (the embedded tweet says 11:15 p.m.); a second promo video and key visual were posted, previewing OP "Kizuna no Kiseki" by MAN WITH A MISSION and milet.
- Director Haruo Sotozaki, character designer/chief animation director Akira Matsushima, studio ufotable and main cast return. Two Entertainment District Arc specials air April 1 and April 8.
- "World Tour Screenings" opened February 3 in 418 theaters in Japan (MX4D, 4DX, Dolby Cinema from February 25), with Entertainment District episodes 10-11 and the first Swordsmith Village episode. It will screen in North America on Friday, in over 95 countries and territories. It ranked #1 opening weekend: 813,000 tickets, 1,158,765,410 yen (about US$8.75 million) in three days; cumulative 2.26 million tickets and 3,190,289,400 yen (about US$23.42 million).
- Background: TV anime first premiered April 2019; Mugen Train film October 2020; manga launched February 2016 in Weekly Shonen Jump, ended May 2020, 23 volumes.

wikis.title: Where to buy The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom (Polygon deals guide)
wikis.summary: Polygon's Aug 3, 2023 buying guide for Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, its retail options, collector's edition and Zelda Switch OLED.
wikis.body:
- Published Aug 3, 2023 by Alice Jovanee. Polygon calls the game "nothing short of a triumph"; a massive sequel to Breath of the Wild.
- Digital via Nintendo eShop; physical copies from Amazon, GameStop or Best Buy; Amazon typically $5 to $10 off (sometimes more).
- $129.99 collector's deluxe edition: unavailable at MSRP from retailers; since the May 2023 debut it returned briefly then sold out again.
- Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom Switch OLED: $359.99 (same as other limited-edition consoles), without the game; functionally identical to the Switch OLED that debuted October 2021 (7-inch 720p OLED, 64 GB), with runic Joy-Con and dock; Dbrand's unofficial "Clone of the Kingdom" skins as a cheaper alternative.

wikis.title: Breath of the Wild sequel titled Tears of the Kingdom, out May 12, 2023
wikis.summary: IGN (Sep 13, 2022) on the Nintendo Direct reveal of the title The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom and its May 12, 2023 date.
wikis.body:
- The BotW sequel is officially The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, out May 12, 2023, revealed in a Nintendo Direct trailer.
- Trailer: exploration, new stasis powers, shattered Hyrule; skydiving off floating islands, a boulder floating into the air, climbing tree roots, a stone bird that may be used to fly.
- Press release: "In addition to the vast lands of Hyrule, the latest entry... will take you up into the skies and an expanded world that goes beyond that!"
- Originally expected in 2022 and delayed to 2023; series producer Eiji Aonuma: "the entire development team is continuing to work diligently on this game, so please wait a while longer."
- By Joe Skrebels; developer Nintendo EPD.

wikis.title: Zelda BotW sequel officially releasing May 2023 as Tears of the Kingdom
wikis.summary: VGC (13th Sep 2022) reports Nintendo named the sequel Tears of the Kingdom with a May 12, 2023 release date.
wikis.body:
- Nintendo revealed the name Tears of the Kingdom and a May 12, 2023 release date. Nintendo: "...will take you up into the skies and an expanded world that goes beyond that."
- History: announced June 2019 (Link and Zelda trailer); June 2021 trailer confirmed 2022; later delayed to Spring 2023. A spokesperson said the title was withheld because it contained hints about the plot.
- Reportedly grew from DLC ideas for the first Switch game. Patents suggest new powers focused on verticality (passing upward through solid objects, changing position while free-falling). Nintendo suggested a darker tone.
- The 2019 trailer showed a cavern under Hyrule Castle and a mummified corpse coming to life.
- Posted by Andy Robinson.

wikis.title: Street Fighter 6 release date, features and modes (PCGamesN)
wikis.summary: PCGamesN guide (updated June 5, 2023) to Street Fighter 6: June 2, 2023 release, platforms, World Tour, Battle Hub, controls and crossplay.
wikis.body:
- Released June 2, 2023 on PC, Xbox Series X/S, PS4 and PS5; date revealed at The Game Awards 2022; not on Xbox Game Pass. Updated June 5, 2023 (Christian Vaz).
- A Capcom showcase on April 20 covered World Tour mode, DLC plans and a demo with Ryu and Luke. Crossplay between PlayStation, Xbox and PC, which can be disabled.
- Full cast revealed at TGS 2022. Story takes place after Street Fighter 3: Third Strike per Capcom's Twitter.
- World Tour: single-player, roam Metro City as a custom fighter, starting at Buckler Security with coach Luke; Battle Hub: online lobby with arcade cabinets (Game Center with Capcom classics), Event Counter, Body Shop.
- Modern Control Type simplifies special moves to a single button.
- Focus on single-player after Street Fighter 5's criticism for lack of content.

wikis.title: Street Fighter 6 sells over 1 million units worldwide (Capcom press release)
wikis.summary: Capcom's June 7, 2023 release: Street Fighter 6 passed 1 million units and the series passed 50 million cumulative.
wikis.body:
- June 7, 2023 (Capcom, Osaka): Street Fighter 6 sold over 1 million units worldwide; series cumulative sales pass 50 million units.
- First Street Fighter arcade game 1987; Street Fighter II in 1991; more than 35 years old. SF6 launches seven years after the previous title.
- New features: World Tour Mode (avatar), Battle Hub, varied controller input options, improved audio accessibility settings; "broad acclaim".
- Esports: over $2 million (approx. 260 million yen at $1 = 130 yen) prize money for Capcom Pro Tour 2023, of which $1 million to the champion, largest-ever.
- Release date June 2, 2023 on PS5, PS4, Xbox Series X|S, PC.

wikis.title: Street Fighter 6 (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Capcom's 2023 fighting game: release, gameplay systems, modes and sales.
wikis.body:
- 2023 fighting game by Capcom (director Takayuki Nakayama), seventh main Street Fighter entry after Street Fighter V (2016). Released June 2, 2023 on PS4, PS5, Windows, Xbox Series X/S; arcade version Street Fighter 6 Type Arcade published by Taito in Japan December 14, 2023; Years 1-2 Fighters Edition plus Nintendo Switch 2 version June 5, 2025.
- RE Engine, cross-platform play, rollback netcode, real-time commentary, "2.5D" style.
- Critical acclaim for its open world, control options, characters, gameplay, graphics and voice acting; story received minor criticism. "As of June 2026, the game has sold over 7 million units worldwide."
- Gameplay: Drive Gauge (five techniques, Burnout state when depleted); control types Classic (six-button), Modern (four-button), and offline-only Dynamic; Super Art levels and Critical Art.
- Modes: Fighting Ground, World Tour (single-player, Metro City and fictional Nayshall; no further updates after season three), Battle Hub (online lobby). May 2026 update added avatar battle modes.

wikis.title: Diablo 4 launches June 6, 2023 (Polygon)
wikis.summary: Polygon (Dec 8, 2022): Blizzard confirmed at The Game Awards 2022 that Diablo 4 launches June 6 with pre-order early access.
wikis.body:
- Blizzard confirmed at The Game Awards 2022 that Diablo 4 launches June 6 (2023) on PS4, PS5, Windows PC, Xbox One and Xbox Series X. Pre-order gives early access. Sequel to 2012's Diablo 3.
- New trailer showed the open world of Sanctuary; designers call it the game's "newest character"; a "far cry from the brighter, cheerier art style of Diablo 3".
- First announced at BlizzCon 2019, expected 2022; pushed out by staff turnover and the 2021 harassment claims. The Washington Post reported a studio bracing for "crunch" ahead of the June deadline set by Activision leadership.
- By Owen S. Good, published Dec 8, 2022.

wikis.title: Diablo IV arrives June 6th, 2023 (Engadget)
wikis.summary: Engadget (Dec 8, 2022): Blizzard confirmed Diablo IV's June 6th, 2023 release; story centers on Lilith.
wikis.body:
- Blizzard confirmed Diablo IV on June 6th, 2023, "after more than a decade" since the last desktop Diablo. Public beta due early next year.
- Promises new classes, familiar mechanics such as skill trees, more tactical depth, and a story about fighting the banished Lilith, Daughter of Hatred.
- Blizzard has promised no pay-to-win microtransactions: only cosmetics and season passes; no auction house. Pre-purchase gives Open Beta Early Access.
- By Jon Fingas, Dec. 8, 2022.

wikis.title: Diablo IV launches June 6, 2023 (Gematsu)
wikis.summary: Gematsu (Dec 8 2022): Diablo IV launch date, platforms, world/classes and digital editions at $69.99/$89.99/$99.99.
wikis.body:
- Launches June 6, 2023 on PS5, Xbox Series, PS4, Xbox One and PC via Battle.net.
- Story: Lilith and Inarius created Sanctuary; decades after Diablo III: Reaper of Souls they are enemies at war. Five classes: Druid, Rogue, Sorceress, Barbarian, Necromancer. Zones: Fractured Peaks, Scosglen, Hawezar, Dry Steppes, Kehjistan (Caldeum). Over 140 dungeons, World Bosses, Strongholds; endgame Helltide, Nightmare Dungeons, Paragon Board, Whispers of the Dead, Fields of Hatred.
- Digital pre-purchase: Standard $69.99 (Open Beta Early Access plus items), Deluxe $89.99 (up to four days early access, Battle Pass unlock), Ultimate $99.99 (accelerated Battle Pass with 20 Tier Skips).
- Posted Dec 8 2022 by Sal Romano.

wikis.title: Diablo 4 is coming June 6, 2023 (PC Gamer)
wikis.summary: PC Gamer (9 December 2022): Diablo 4 arrives June 6, 2023 with pre-orders and early access, standard edition $70.
wikis.body:
- Announced at The Game Awards: Diablo 4 arrives on PC June 6, 2023, three years after announcement; also PS4, PS5, Xbox One and Xbox Series X simultaneously. Pre-order grants some early access.
- Trailer follows the BlizzCon 2019 announcement trailer: Tyrael and holy soldiers versus Lilith's demons.
- Standard edition $70, Ultimate $100; editions: Standard (Open Beta Early Access, Light Bearer Mount, cosmetic items in other Blizzard games), Deluxe (up to 4 days early access, Battle Pass unlock, mount armor), Ultimate (accelerated Battle Pass with 20 Tier Skips, emote).
- Tyler Colp's preview: "the Diablo I've been waiting for". By Evan Lahti, 9 December 2022.

wikis.title: Sphere Las Vegas: facts, design and opening
wikis.summary: 1 OAK Las Vegas guide (May 8, 2026) to Sphere: size, cost, opening on September 29, 2023, and design.
wikis.body:
- Sphere Las Vegas: 366 feet tall, 516 feet wide, "world's largest spherical structure"; exterior Exosphere with 580,000 sq ft of programmable LED; interior 16K wraparound LED display; area 875,000 sq ft; dome weight over 13,000 tons.
- Cost $2.3 billion, more than the $1.9 billion Allegiant Stadium. Seats about 18,600, up to 20,000 for some events.
- Opened September 29, 2023 with U2: UV Achtung Baby Live at Sphere; soft debut on Independence Day 2023 with exterior visuals. Estimated completion was 2021, delayed by supply chains and working conditions.
- Address 255 Sands Ave, Las Vegas, NV 89169; owner Sphere Entertainment Co.; joint partnership of Las Vegas Sands Corporation and MSG from 2018; Sands contributed the 18-acre site.

wikis.title: MSG Sphere president Lucas Watson on U2 and booking plans (Jan 2023)
wikis.summary: Las Vegas Review-Journal column reporting Lucas Watson's Preview Las Vegas remarks: no U2 confirmation, 4-6 residency headliners a year, and an 18,600 capacity.
wikis.body:
- Source: Las Vegas Review-Journal "Kats!" column by John Katsilometes, January 23, 2023 (updated January 25, 2023).
- Lucas Watson, president of MSG Sphere, spoke at Preview Las Vegas (Vegas Chamber's annual economic forecast) at the Las Vegas Convention Center West Hall on Monday, Jan. 23, 2023.
- He sidestepped questions about U2 opening The Sphere "this September"; the column says the band's opening dates are being reviewed, pending progress on the $2.18 billion construction project.
- Watson: "We'll have announcements about artists and tickets for sale, soon."
- Between four and six residency headliners are to play at The Sphere every year, each roughly 10 to 12 shows, "depending on their availability and scheduling".
- Josephine Vaccarello has been promoted to lead all MSG Sphere bookings.
- A theatrical, "multisensory" presentation with fewer live performers and more cinematic technology, "just for The Sphere", is to play regularly; it is being developed at the venue's Burbank prototype and the columnist expects it to anchor programming.
- Total capacity is given as 18,600, up from the previous 17,500.
- Other items in the column: Live Nation's Joe Berchtold is reported to blame bots for the Taylor Swift presale problems ahead of a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing (Sen. Dick Durbin); Garth Brooks, due to open a Colosseum residency in May, is expected to back the testimony.

wikis.title: U2 announces first dates at the Las Vegas Sphere (April 2023)
wikis.summary: USA Today report on U2's five fall 2023 opening dates at MSG Sphere and The Edge's comments on the venue's sound and screen.
wikis.body:
- Source: USA Today, Bryan Alexander, April 24, 2023 (updated April 25, 2023).
- U2 announced five fall dates for "U2: UV Achtung Baby Live at Sphere", opening the roughly $2 billion venue beginning Sept. 29. First concerts in four years for the band, without Larry Mullen Jr. (per a linked story).
- Venue figures: 17,600 seats (article's wording; also cited as a full capacity of 20,000 fans); 366 feet tall and 516 feet wide, described as the world's largest spherical structure; 160,000 square-foot 16K screen wrapping up, over and around the seats; more than 160,000 speakers; 4D effects including scents, temperature changes and wind.
- The Edge, 61: "This is light-years ahead of anything else out there... a quantum leap forward for the sensory impacts of a rock'n'roll concert."
- U2 has rehearsed with the technology for nine months and is finishing the album "Songs of Surrender"; The Edge: "There is some jeopardy here."
- Presale begins April 27 with priority for verified U2 fans, before the Friday Ticketmaster release; The Edge acknowledges "recent ticket sales issues".
- USA Today toured the Sphere staging ground in Burbank, California.

wikis.title: Hudson Yards progress report (amNewYork, January 2015)
wikis.summary: amNY update on construction, towers, tenants and public spaces at Hudson Yards, New York's largest private real estate development.
wikis.body:
- Source: amNewYork by Winnie McCroy, posted January 29, 2015.
