- 797B (spring 2002, first units in service October 2002): 345 t (380 short tons) payload, engine from net 2,394 kW to 2,513 kW, top speed 68 km/h (42 mph).
- 797F (introduced at MINExpo September 2008, full production late 2009): 400 short tons payload; Cat C175-20 ACERT 20-cylinder engine, gross 4,000 hp (net 3,793 hp); same 68 km/h top speed.
- Before 2008 the Liebherr T 282B (2004) was the only 400 short ton truck.

## Technical
- Mechanical drive (diesel-electric considered in 1997 and not developed). Original engine: Cat 3524B, two 12-cylinder 3512B blocks coupled, 106 L displacement. Seven-speed planetary transmission.
- Tires: Michelin 59/80R63 XDR, 4.028 m tall, 5,300 kg each; six per truck at about US$42,500 per tire in 2009.

## Manufacture, cost, life
- Components made at seven facilities in North America and shipped to the customer site: engine (Lafayette, Indiana), transmission (East Peoria), axles (Winston-Salem), cab (Joliet; 40 hours each), dump body (Monterrey, Mexico), castings (Attica, Indiana; Amite City, Louisiana).
- One truck needs 12 to 13 semi-trailer loads; final assembly at the site takes seven mechanics working three shifts for 20 days, plus 7 to 10 days for the dump body. It cannot be driven on public roads between sites.
- Price approximately US$5,000,000 (another listing US$3,400,000). Frame service life estimated at twenty years.
- Competitors at 400 short tons: Liebherr T 282 B, Bucyrus MT6300AC, Caterpillar's own 798AC (diesel-electric); BelAZ 75710 carries 500 short tons, the largest.

wikis.title: Carnival Vista cruise ship (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Carnival Vista, lead ship of Carnival's Vista class, built by Fincantieri and delivered April 2016.
wikis.body:
- Cruise ship operated by Carnival Cruise Line (owner Carnival Corporation & plc); lead ship of the Vista class (also Carnival Horizon, Carnival Panorama, Costa Venezia, Costa Firenze). Built by Fincantieri, Monfalcone, Italy; ordered 2012; cost US$780 million; yard number 6242.
- Timeline: first steel cut late February 2014; laid down October 14, 2014; launched June 25, 2015; sea trials completed March 2016; delivered April 28, 2016; maiden voyage May 1, 2016 from Trieste (13-day Europe cruise ending in Barcelona). Christened in New York City by godmother Miss USA 2016 Deshauna Barber.
- Specs: 133,596 GT; length 323.63 m; beam 37.2 m (48.34 m max); draught 8.55 m; 15 decks; diesel-electric with two ABB Azipod XO units; 18 knots; capacity 3,934 double occupancy (4,977 max); crew 1,450. Largest ship in Carnival's fleet by gross tonnage until Carnival Horizon (2018).
- Home ports: Mediterranean season May-October 2016, Miami from November 2016, Galveston from September 2018; Port Canaveral planned November 2023.
- Incidents: August 28, 2016 wake damaged Marina del Nettuno harbor near Messina; June 2019 three cruises cancelled over Azipod problems, repaired using heavy-lift ship BOKA Vanguard as a floating dry dock; July 2019 temporary power loss in the Gulf of Mexico; 28 November 2019 bus crash in Belize with seven passengers (two deaths, five injuries); propulsion issues reported again August 2024. New livery in 2024.

wikis.title: Carnival Vista at Fincantieri
wikis.summary: Fincantieri's product page for Carnival Vista: delivery, features, dimensions and cabin counts.
wikis.body:
- Delivered at the Monfalcone shipyard in April 2016 for Carnival Cruise Line; Panamanian flag; the thirteenth ship Fincantieri built for Carnival Cruise Line and the largest; "The Most Innovative Cruise Ship Ever" (page heading).
- Features: IMAX 3D cinema, 5D theater, onboard craft brewery, open-air cycling track 45 m above the sea, WaterWorks water park with a 137-metre spiral slide, Havana Area themed zone. Built to the "Safe Return to Port" standard, with an exhaust gas cleaning system.
- Data: 133,596 GRT; length overall 323 m; beam moulded 37.2 m; design draught 8.25 m; service speed 18.0 kn, max 22.6 kn; Lloyd's Register class.
- Cabins: 1,967 passenger cabins (8 penthouse suites, 49 suites, 873 balcony, 74 window, 709 standard inside, 215 window deluxe + family, 25 fully ADA); 785 crew cabins; max persons on board 6,448.
- Machinery: two pods of 16,500 kW; 2 x 16,800 kW MAN 14V48/60CR and 3 x 9,600 kW MAN 8L48/60CR generators; total installed electrical power 62,400 kW.

wikis.title: MV Paul R. Tregurtha lake freighter (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 1,013.5 ft Great Lakes bulk freighter Paul R. Tregurtha, current 'Queen of the Lakes', its construction, records and groundings.
wikis.body:
- Great Lakes bulk carrier; the current "Queen of the Lakes" (unofficial title for the longest active vessel on the Great Lakes); flagship of Interlake Steamship Company. Launched as MV William J. De Lancey; last of the thirteen "thousand footers" and the last vessel built at American Ship Building's Lorain, Ohio yard. Nicknames "The Big Paul", "Fancy De Lancey".
- Specs: 1,013.5 ft (308.9 m); beam 105 ft; depth 56 ft; 36,360 GT; two MaK 6M43C diesels of 8,160 HP each; 15.5 knots; capacity 68,000 long tons iron ore or 63,616 long tons coal.
- Built under a 1979 Interlake contract for Republic Steel; designed also for executive passenger transport (full air conditioning, elevators). Keel laid 12 July 1979 (Toledo), launched 4 February 1981, christened 25 April 1981, maiden voyage 10 May 1981 from Lorain to Silver Bay, Minnesota (55,944 long tons of pellets). Self-unloader: 260-ft boom, 10,000 long tons of ore per hour.
- Renamed Paul R. Tregurtha on May 23, 1990 at Sturgeon Bay, Wisconsin, after Interlake's Vice Chairman.
- Records: 63,007 long tons load at Escanaba (7 August 1982); lower-lakes record 50,239 net tons of coal from Ashtabula; carried the most cargo through the Soo Locks in the 2001 season (3,004,957 long tons).
- Captain Mitch Hallin died in his cabin on May 3, 2002, aged 55. Winter 2004: mid-winter coal run to Algoma Steel with icebreaker help. 2008: cracked bow plating in ice, repaired at Fraser Shipyards, Superior.
- Groundings: 15 August 2012 in the St. Marys River with 62,000 tons of coal, refloated August 19 with help of the Coast Guard and two tugs; 20 September 2014 in Duluth Harbor Basin.

wikis.title: M/V Paul R. Tregurtha at Interlake Steamship
wikis.summary: Interlake Steamship fleet page for its flagship M/V Paul R. Tregurtha, the longest ship on the Great Lakes.
wikis.body:
- Statistics: carrying capacity 68,000 gross tons; overall length 1,013.5 ft; built 1981; hull depth 56.0 ft; beam 105.0 ft; engine horsepower 17,120.
- Interlake's flagship, "the longest ship on the Great Lakes"; carries up to 68,000 gross tons of taconite pellets or 71,000 net tons of coal; her unloading system and 260-foot boom empty her five cargo holds in about eight hours.
- Built by American Ship Building Company at Lorain, Ohio, in 1981 as William J. DeLancey; renamed in 1990 for Interlake's Vice Chairman of the Board.
- "Queen of the Lakes" since entering service in 1981; has an elevator and luxurious owner's accommodations, earning the nickname "Fancy DeLancey". Built for approximately $60 million.

wikis.title: When each airline took delivery of its first Airbus A380
wikis.summary: Simple Flying article (29 Sep 2021) listing the delivery date of each airline's first A380 and what became of each fleet.
wikis.body:
Published Sep 29, 2021. Opens by saying the A380's exit from many fleets was hastened by the pandemic while more carriers bring it back out of storage.

## First deliveries, in order
- Singapore Airlines: first of 24 delivered October 15, 2007; first revenue flight (9V-SKA) October 25, 2007, SQ380 Singapore-Sydney, seats sold via charity auction from $560 to $100,380. 9V-SKA left the fleet in June 2017 and is stored at Tarbes Lourdes; 12 remaining A380s being brought out of storage.
- Emirates: first on July 28, 2008; 119 in fleet, three more expected, final delivery in November 2021; 123 total incl. one retired February 2020.
- Qantas: first on September 19, 2008 (VH-OQA, Toulouse); plans to bring back half of its remaining ten by 2022 and the rest by 2024.
- Air France: first of ten in October 2009 (first European carrier), first revenue flight November 23; entire fleet retired (last flight March 23, 2020; farewell scenic flight June 26).
- Lufthansa: first of 12 on May 19, 2010; fleet retired, CEO Carsten Spohr said it does not fit future plans.
- Korean Air: May 24, 2011 (407-seat three-class layout; ten in total, last July 2014). China Southern: October 14, 2011 (five in total; only Chinese operator; last February 2013).
- Malaysia Airlines: May 29, 2012 (six; the sixth in March 2013 was the 100th A380 built; put up for sale). Thai Airways: September 27, 2012 (six; reports it will retire all).
- British Airways: July 4, 2013 (12 total; still flying).
- Asiana: May 26, 2014 (six; last December 2016). Qatar Airways: September 17, 2014 (ten; impaired). Etihad: December 16, 2014 (ten, last May 2017; all retired).
- All Nippon Airways: smallest customer, three aircraft in special liveries; first arrived March 14th, 2019, normally intended for Hawaii services.

wikis.title: Maasvlakte 2 extension officially opened for shipping
wikis.summary: Dutch Water Sector news item (23 May 2013) on the 22 May 2013 opening of the Port of Rotterdam's Maasvlakte 2, built EUR 150 million under estimate.
wikis.body:
- Dutch infrastructure minister Melanie Schultz van Haegen officially opened Maasvlakte 2 for shipping on 22 May 2013: "The port is growing 20 percent larger, and the container capacity has doubled."
- In 2008 PUMA (50/50 joint venture of Boskalis and Van Oord) began creating 2,000 hectares of new port zone with 20 m deep basins. Sea defenses completed July 2012. Two container terminals were scheduled to be ready by end of 2014.
- Cost: 2006 estimate EUR 1.7 billion for the first phase; now about EUR 1.55 billion, "150 million euro less expensive than estimated"; the EUR 200 million contingency untouched (CEO Hans Smits).
- Reasons: thorough preparation with almost no legal delay; contract forms allowing optimisation; a half-open block dam and cobble beach instead of a solid dike; a narrow canal to the Yangtzehaven for the E.ON cooling water instead of an expensive structure; risk split where only storm sand loss from waves above 6.75 m for over 3 hours (about once in 10 years) fell to the Port Authority.

wikis.title: Maasvlakte 2 (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Maasvlakte 2, the reclaimed-land extension of the Port of Rotterdam opened on 22 May 2013.
wikis.body:
- Major Dutch civil engineering project building a new port on reclaimed land adjoining the Maasvlakte; about 2000 hectares reclaimed behind a 4 km dike, about 1000 hectares for port-related industries. The biggest Dutch civil engineering project since the Delta Works.
- Area opened on 22 May 2013. APM Terminals and Rotterdam World Gateway (RWG) began building terminals in 2012; the APM terminal opened in April 2015.
- RWG is the main competitor for ECT; its terminal has a 20-metre deep dock and its own railroad station, capable of 2.35 million containers annually. The Eurogeul was widened for the extra traffic.
- Uses Europoort's transport links; directly connected to the Betuwe Route.

wikis.title: Paris Metro begins operations on Line 1, 19 June 1900
wikis.summary: EarthSky 'This date in science' note on the opening of the Paris Metro's Line 1 on June 19, 1900.
wikis.body:
- On June 19, 1900 the subway system in Paris began operations on Line 1 after two years of construction that involved tearing up several streets.
- It was France's first subway system and was said to symbolize a country in the forefront technologically.
- Construction was decided in 1898 to connect sites for the 1900 Paris Exposition Universelle (World Fair). Streets were dug up; "Complaints flooded in, and there was widespread opposition to the project."
- The opening was delayed by several weeks due to a general strike. Line 1 quickly became popular enough to justify more lines.
- It was part of a worldwide subway building boom: Boston, Chicago, Philadelphia, Berlin and Hamburg were built between 1900 and 1910.
- Today the system is mostly underground, 214 km (133 mi) long with 303 stations (62 transfer stations); said to be Europe's second busiest metro after Moscow.
- As of 2010, Line 1 carries 225 million passengers annually through 25 stations over 10.3 miles (16.6 km) of track, and now includes driverless trains.
- Operator: RATP Group, state-owned.

wikis.title: First German Quadriga Eurofighter Typhoon maiden flight at Manching
wikis.summary: Aviation News report that Airbus flew the first Eurofighter built under Germany's Quadriga programme on 14 July 2026.
wikis.body:
- Airbus Defence and Space conducted the maiden flight of the first Eurofighter Typhoon built under Germany's Quadriga programme.
- Single-seat aircraft serial 34+02 (c/n GS0114) departed from the Military Air Systems Centre in Manching on 14 July 2026; production test flight lasted approximately one hour.
- The flight demonstrates assembly-line readiness and paves the way for acceptance testing by the German Luftwaffe.
- Quadriga order: 38 Eurofighter Typhoons (30 single-seat, eight twin-seat), to replace the Luftwaffe's ageing Tranche 1 fleet.
- Aircraft are Tranche 4 configuration with new radar technology, upgraded software and enhanced electronic warfare suites.
- Michael Schoellhorn, CEO of Airbus Defence and Space: "This new order is further proof of the Eurofighter's importance to the German air force..."
- Airbus will focus on delivery of the remaining 37 aircraft.

wikis.title: Mjøstårnet, wooden tower in Brumunddal, Norway
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 18-storey timber Mjøstårnet, completed March 2019 and formerly the world's tallest wooden building.
wikis.body:
- 18-storey mixed-use building in Brumunddal, Norway, completed in March 2019; 85.4 m (280 ft) tall. Officially the world's tallest wooden building at completion, until surpassed by Ascent MKE in August 2022.
- Named after Norway's biggest lake, Mjøsa.
- Combined floor area around 11,300 m2; hotel, apartments, offices, restaurant, common areas; adjacent first-floor extension (about 4,700 m2, also wood) has a swimming pool.
- Designed by Voll Arkitekter for AB Invest; timber structures by Moelven Limtre (glued laminated timber load-bearing structure; cross laminated timber for stairwells, elevator shafts, balconies).
- Considered an all-timber structure; concrete slabs used on the top seven floors for comfort and acoustics.
- Next tallest: the 84 m, 24-storey HoHo Tower in Vienna, a timber-concrete composite per CTBUH.
- Sumitomo Forestry proposes the W350 Project, a 350 m, 70-floor tower for its 350th anniversary in 2041.

wikis.title: Frankfurt Airport Terminal 3: first Sky Line vehicle presented
wikis.summary: Fraport press release on the first Siemens-built vehicle for the Sky Line people mover linking Terminal 3 to existing terminals.
wikis.body:
- The first of 12 Sky Line vehicles, supplied from Siemens Mobility's factory in Vienna, was presented at Frankfurt Airport by Fraport CEO Dr. Stefan Schulte. First test trips are scheduled to take place in 2023.
- The driverless system supplements the existing system between Terminals 1 and 2 and can carry up to 4,000 persons an hour in each direction; runs fully automatically around the clock.
- Each vehicle has two permanently linked cars (11 m long, 2.8 m wide, 15 t each); one car of each vehicle is reserved for non-Schengen travelers.
- Vehicles have many folding seats and special grab bars; they run on angled wheels around a guide rail on a concrete surface. Based on Siemens' Val solution (also at Bangkok and Paris airports).
- Max Bögl group builds much of the 5.6 km route (work since July 2019, on schedule): mostly on columns at 14 m height; 310 prestressed and reinforced concrete sections up to 60 m long and up to 200 t.
- Travel from the long-distance and regional train stations to Terminal 3's main building takes eight minutes; vehicles run every two minutes, 365 days a year. Regular operation to begin on time for the planned inauguration of Terminal 3.

wikis.title: 2019 Lamborghini Huracán EVO launch
wikis.summary: Lamborghini's presentation of the Huracán EVO V10 super sports car, republished by ConceptCarz.
wikis.body:
- Sant'Agata Bolognese 07/01/2019: Automobili Lamborghini presents the Huracán EVO, based on the Huracán Performante with new vehicle dynamics control and aerodynamics.
- 5.2 l naturally-aspirated V10: 640 hp (470 kW) at 8,000 rpm, 600 Nm at 6,500 rpm; dry weight 1,422 kg (2.22 kg/hp); 0-100 km/h in 2.9 s, 0-200 km/h in 9.0 s; 100-0 km/h braking in 31.9 m; top speed over 325 km/h.
- New Lamborghini Dinamica Veicolo Integrata (LDVI) central processing unit with predictive "feed forward logic"; LPI 2.0 inertial platform; rear-wheel steering, torque vectoring and enhanced all-wheel drive; drive modes STRADA, SPORT, CORSA.
- New aerodynamics: front splitter with integrated wing, integrated rear spoiler, high-mounted twin exhaust outlets; downforce and aerodynamic efficiency improved more than five times over the first-generation Huracán.
- 8.4" HMI capacitive touchscreen with Apple CarPlay; optional dual-camera telemetry.
- Shown in Arancio Xanto; 20" Aesir rims with Pirelli P Zero tires.
- First customer deliveries in spring 2019. Suggested retail prices: UK GBP 165,256 (excl. taxes); USA USD 261,274 (excl. taxes/GST); China RMB 3,298,100 (taxes included); Japan YEN 29,843,274 (excl. taxes).
- Quote from Stefano Domenicali, Chairman and CEO: "The Huracán EVO is the very definition of evolution".

wikis.title: Frankfurt Airport Terminal 3 press kit: inauguration set for April 22, 2026
wikis.summary: Fraport press kit on the new Terminal 3, with an October 8, 2025 release announcing the April 22, 2026 inauguration plus a facts list.
wikis.body:
- October 8, 2025 release: Fraport AG will officially inaugurate Terminal 3 on April 22, 2026, after passing official inspections including fire protection.
- Final work: 21 security check lanes with CT scanners, food and shopping areas, baggage handling tests. Test operation on 21 days between January 27 and April 16, 2026 with around 8,000 test passengers.
- Groundbreaking was October 5, 2015; footprint 176,000 square meters. Initial configuration with Piers G (Schengen and non-Schengen), H (Schengen) and J (non-Schengen): capacity up to 19 million passengers a year. An optional fourth pier K would raise capacity to 25 million.
- Investment about four billion euros. Built by Fraport Ausbau Süd GmbH (FAS); technical director Harald Rohr said it was delivered "on schedule and on budget" despite the pandemic, the war in Ukraine and supply chain disruptions.
- Parking structure with 8,500 spaces. The Sky Line people mover links Terminal 3 to existing infrastructure; eight minutes between Terminals 1 and 3.
- All 57 airlines now at Terminal 2 will move to Terminal 3 in four phases between mid-April and early June.
- CEO Dr. Stefan Schulte: "We held the groundbreaking ceremony for Terminal 3 ten years ago..."

wikis.title: Bell 429 GlobalRanger light twin helicopter
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the Bell 429, its development, certification in 2009, design and operators.
wikis.body:
- Light twin-engine helicopter developed by Bell Helicopter with Korea Aerospace Industries (and Mitsui Bussan Aerospace of Japan). Prototype first flew February 27, 2007; type certification from Transport Canada on July 1, 2009, FAA by July 7, 2009, EASA announced September 24, 2009. Single-pilot IFR, Category A.
- Development driven by the EMS industry; the Bell 427's cabin was too small for a litter. Uses Bell's MAPL modular airframe concept. Certification originally planned for late 2007 but delayed by parts and material shortages.
- Over 301 letters of intent by June 2009. Launch customer Air Methods Corporation; first aircraft delivered July 7, 2009 at Mirabel, Quebec.
- Design: four-blade composite rotor with swept tips; cabin volume 204 ft3 (5.8 m3); glass cockpit with three-axis autopilot; skids standard, retractable wheels optional; can operate with one engine inoperative.
- By July 2018, 325 aircraft had flown 330,000 hours in 42 countries. Number built 500 (July 2024). In production 2007-present.
- Operators include Canadian Coast Guard (16), Swedish Police Authority (9), Royal Australian Navy (historical), Delaware State Police (4), plus many police, medical and government users.

wikis.title: Porsche Taycan production start at Zuffenhausen
wikis.summary: Porsche press release (06/09/2019) on opening the new Taycan production facility, with production of customer cars starting 9 September 2019.
wikis.body:
- After a construction period of less than 48 months, Porsche opens a new production facility for its first all-electric sports car at Zuffenhausen. Production of first customer vehicles begins as scheduled on 9 September 2019.
- Albrecht Reimold (Executive Board, Production and Logistics): "It was a deliberate decision to build the Taycan in Zuffenhausen".
- Production is to be CO2-neutral; electricity from renewable sources, biogas heat, electric logistics vehicles, paint-shop waste heat use, green roofs.
- New body shop, paint shop, electric motor and component plant, assembly hall. 35,000 tonnes of steel; 170,000 square metres of buildings.
- Construction began end of 2015 after the September 2015 Mission E concept presentation; old buildings cleared May 2016. 21 preliminary projects and more than 5,000 employee relocations. Assembly building height limited to 38 m; the pit is 25 m deep with 240,000 cubic meters of earth moved.
- 130 companies and suppliers involved; 10,000 site passes, 530 containers, 3 km fencing, 35 km power cables, 4 km of new road within the plant.

wikis.title: MSC Meraviglia delivered by STX France, 31 May 2017
wikis.summary: MSC Cruises press release on taking delivery of MSC Meraviglia at Saint-Nazaire.
wikis.body:
- 31 May 2017, STX France shipyard, Saint-Nazaire: MSC Cruises took delivery of MSC Meraviglia; flag ceremony attended by French President Emmanuel Macron.
- 171,598 GRT, guest capacity 5,714; 315 m long, 43 m wide, 65 m high; up to 22.7 knots. Biggest ship ever built by a European ship owner and the largest to enter service in 2017; 13th ship in the MSC fleet.
- Nine million man-hours over three years; 1,700 workers per month (over 3,000 at peak), 400+ suppliers. One of six new ships due 2017-2020; four built by STX France. Total investment at STX France 2003-2020 estimated over 7 billion euros.
- Christening in Le Havre on June 3; inaugural season in the Western Mediterranean; first regular 7-night itinerary from Genoa on 11 June (Naples, Messina, Valletta, Barcelona, Marseille).
- Godmother: Zoe Africa Vago. Executive Chairman Pierfrancesco Vago and STX France CEO Laurent Castaing quoted.

wikis.title: History of the Rocky Mountaineer luxury train
wikis.summary: Destinology blog on how Rocky Mountaineer began in 1990 and grew, with timeline and FAQs.
wikis.body:
- First journey departed 7th June 1990 with 72 passengers through the Canadian Rockies; the first season sold out.
- Background: the Canadian Pacific Railway completed the first transcontinental line in 1885; passenger rail declined in the 1980s; Expo 86 in Vancouver sparked interest in Western Canada.
- Concept: daylight-only travel, overnight hotel stays in mountain towns, glass-domed carriages, fine dining on board.
- Early 1990s routes linked Vancouver with Jasper, Banff and Lake Louise. GoldLeaf Service (bi-level glass dome coaches) introduced in 1995; SilverLeaf is single-level with meals at the seat.
- 2021: first US route, Rockies to the Red Rocks, Denver to Moab.
- Timeline: 1986 Expo 86; 1990 launch; 1995 GoldLeaf; 2000s growth; 2021 USA expansion. Described as privately owned, based in Vancouver.

wikis.title: Allseas pipelay vessel Solitaire
wikis.summary: Allseas fleet page for Solitaire, one of the world's most advanced pipelay vessels.
wikis.body:
- Launched 1998 (per the page); S-lay technology and dynamic positioning; 1050-tonne pipe holding capacity; installed pipelines to record depth of 2775 metres.
- Pipe cargo capacity 22,000 tonnes; double-joint welding; laid 5 km of concrete-coated 48-inch pipe in 24 hours.
- Installed over 13,000 km of pipeline worldwide; first vessel to install a subsea pipeline north of the Arctic Circle.
- Projects listed: Chevron Anchor export pipelines (2023, Gulf of Mexico), Whale Oil & Gas export pipelines (18-inch, 2023), Southeast Gateway Pipeline (2024, with Lorelay).

wikis.title: Solitaire (1971 ship), Allseas pipe-laying vessel
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Solitaire, a bulk carrier launched 1971 as Trentwood and converted into a pipe-laying ship.
wikis.body:
- Launched 17 December 1971 by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Hiroshima (completed 1972) as bulk carrier Trentwood; IMO 7129049; registered in Valletta, Malta from 2015.
- 300 m long, beam 40.6 m, 59,193 tonnage, 129,479 DWT; 8x Wartsila 6R46B, 51.50 MW; 14.5 kn; crew 420.
- At conversion the world's largest pipe-laying ship; pipe capacity 22,000 tonnes; lay speed more than 9 km a day. Owned by the Allseas Group.
- Allseas acquired Trentwood in 1992; conversion contract with Sembawang Shipyards terminated in 1995; converted at Swan Hunter, Tyneside. First pipe laid 1999 on Statoil's Europipe project. Settlement of the Solitaire arbitration with Sembcorp in 2006.
- 2006: laid 10-inch pipeline at 2,775 m depth and 24-inch at 2,550 m in the Gulf of Mexico. Laid the Nord Stream 2 pipeline in the Baltic in 2019-2020, among other ships.

wikis.title: Renzo Piano's Genoa San Giorgio bridge opens
wikis.summary: ArchDaily news of the new Polcevera viaduct in Genoa opening to traffic on August 5, 2020.
wikis.body:
- Genova San Giorgio, designed by Renzo Piano, replaces the Morandi Bridge; open to traffic starting August 5, 2020, two years after the collapse that claimed 43 lives.
- The Morandi Bridge (built 1967) was about one kilometre long, 45 m above ground; on 14 August 2018 one of three pylons collapsed with about 200 m of road. Piano offered to donate the design.
- New viaduct: 1,067 m, 19 spans, 40 m high, 18 pylons; cost 202 million euros; two rows of solar panels to meet 95% of its energy needs. Built without pausing during the pandemic.

wikis.title: Genoa San Giorgio Bridge by Renzo Piano opens
wikis.summary: Dezeen report on the opening of Renzo Piano's replacement for the collapsed Morandi Bridge.
wikis.body:
- 1,100 m motorway bridge over the Polcevera river inaugurated by the Italian prime minister almost two years after the Morandi Bridge collapse on 14 August 2018 (43 killed). Built in less than two years with round-the-clock construction.
- Deck supported by 18 reinforced concrete piers, 50 m apart (100 m in the central section), elliptical section; steel and concrete deck with seismic isolation devices; underside curved like a ship's hull; light-coloured steel.
- Metal fins, photovoltaic panels powering lighting, 2.5 m protective glass barrier; sensors (accelerometers, extensometers, velocimeters, inclinometers) and rail robots for monitoring and cleaning panels.
- Credits: Renzo Piano concept; Italferr technical project; Pergenova ScpA general contractor; Rina Consulting; iGuzzini lighting. Morandi bridge was a concrete cable-stayed bridge completed in 1967.

wikis.title: LKAB moves Hjalmar Lundbohmsgården in Kiruna
wikis.summary: LKAB press invitation for the September 26, 2017 relocation of the heritage building Hjalmar Lundbohmsgården to Luossavaara.
wikis.body:
- Tuesday September 26 (2017): sixth of eight heritage buildings moved from the mining-affected zone; Hjalmar Lundbohmsgården goes to the foot of Luossavaara mountain (new address Lottens Erikssons gata 34).
- Seven buildings go to Luossavaara (about 20,000 m2 prepared); the Länsmansbostaden goes to the new urban core. Already moved: three bläckhornshus buildings, Ingenjörsvillan, Arbetarbostaden B5.
- Built 1895, LKAB's second building; home and office of first president Hjalmar Lundbohm until 1920. Dismantled and moved in three sections due to extensions.
- Press tour 26 September from 08:30 at LKAB's administration office; relocation and "Move Walk" begin 10:00; contractor PEAB. Project manager Tjabba Nordanfjäll quoted.

wikis.title: Semco Maritime to prepare West Bollsta rig for Norway
wikis.summary: Offshore Engineer report that Seadrill hired Semco Maritime to prepare the West Bollsta drilling rig, with PSA non-conformities pending.
wikis.body:
- Seadrill hired Semco Maritime to prepare the newbuild West Bollsta rig for the Norwegian Continental Shelf; work at Hanøytangen near Bergen expected from mid-February 2020, employing around 100 people.
- Rig starts a 10-well contract with Lundin Norway in Q2 2020; firm contract until early 2022 with options for close to one year more.
- Harsh environment semi-submersible based on Moss Maritime CS60, owned by Northern Ocean Ltd, operated by Seadrill; built at Hyundai Heavy Industries in 2019; currently at anchor near Tenerife.
- Yard has Northern Europe's largest operating dry-dock (125x125x17 m).
- It has yet to receive an Acknowledgment of Compliance; on January 22 the PSA Norway identified seven "non-conformities" (electrical facilities, technical safety, maintenance management), giving Seadrill until February 7 to report.

wikis.title: Northern Drilling exercises option on Bollsta Dolphin semi-submersible
wikis.summary: Splash247 report (Dec 21, 2017) that Northern Drilling took up an HHI option for the Bollsta Dolphin rig at $400m.
wikis.body:
- John Fredriksen's rig investment company Northern Drilling exercised its option at Hyundai Heavy Industries (HHI) for semi-submersible Bollsta Dolphin.
- Contract price $400m; Fredriksen's Seatankers originally secured the option when it settled a dispute between Seadrill and the yard over the West Mira.
- Ordered originally by Fred. Olsen Energy in 2012; cancelled in 2015 citing delays. Now set to be delivered in January 2019.
- Northern Drilling "will continue to pursue its strategy of opportunistically acquiring distressed drilling assets."

wikis.title: Norwegian Cruise Line takes delivery of Norwegian Epic
wikis.summary: Cruise Industry News (June 17, 2010) on NCL accepting Norwegian Epic from STX France and its inaugural schedule.
wikis.body:
- June 17, 2010: NCL accepted delivery of Norwegian Epic from STX France SA; 153,000 gross tons, the largest ship ever constructed in St. Nazaire.
- CEO Kevin Sheehan: "more than 20 dining options and a wide range of accommodations including the largest suite complex at sea"; more than four years of development and construction.
- Departs St. Nazaire for Rotterdam, then two-day inaugural cruise; June 21 one-night preview to Southampton; June 24 seven-day transatlantic to New York arriving July 1.
- Christened by Reba McEntire on July 2; host venue for Macy's 4th of July Fireworks (July 4); arrives Miami July 7.
- From July 10: alternating seven-day Eastern and Western Caribbean from Miami through April 30, 2011; then Western Mediterranean from Barcelona May-October 2011.

wikis.title: Diego Della Valle marks first part of Colosseum restoration
wikis.summary: WWD article (July 1, 2016) on the Tod's-funded Colosseum restoration milestone event and an interview with Della Valle.
wikis.body:
- The first part of the Colosseum restoration, started September 2013, has been completed; event July 1, 2016 hosted by Diego Della Valle (chairman and CEO of Tod's Group) with Italian Prime Minister Matteo Renzi.
- In 2010 Della Valle pledged 25 million euros ($27.6 million); 10 million euros spent so far. 31 arches restored (143,640 sq ft) plus 109,620 sq ft of travertine, new gates, a recovered gladiator bas-relief. Restoration expected to finish in four or five years, "between 2020 and 2022".
- Della Valle: the color "has returned to white pink"; foundation "Amici del Colosseo"; plans night lighting from July 2 and school trips; a service center planned near the monument.
- He cites Fendi (Trevi Fountain), Bulgari (Spanish Steps) and Renzo Rosso (Ponte di Rialto) as other private restorations. Says "Noi Italiani" project is not political.

wikis.title: MV Stena Britannica ferry
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the Stena Line RoPax ferry on the Harwich to Hook of Holland route.
wikis.body:
- RoPax cruiseferry built by Wadan Yards, Wismar (yard 164); laid down 17 December 2008, launched 7 June 2009, completed 2010, maiden voyage 9 October 2010. Owner Stena Ropax Ltd, operator Stena Line; route Harwich - Hook of Holland; IMO 9419175.
- 64,039 GT, 240 m long, 32 m beam, 12 decks; four MAN diesels totalling 33.6 MW; 22 knots; 1,200 passengers, 538 cabins, 230 cars / 5,500 lane meters; crew 85. Sister of Stena Hollandica.
- Ordered 2006 (RoPax 55) at about EUR 400 million; order temporarily withdrawn then reinstated with a 6% (about EUR 24 million) price cut. Naming ceremony 19 October 2010 at Harwich.
- January 2018 fire on a refrigerated lorry did not breach the lorry decks; back in service three days later.
- Featured in Mighty Ships season 4, episode 4 (first aired 16 October 2011); a bow door locking pin problem forced upper-ramp loading for 72 hours / six crossings.

wikis.title: United Parcel Service (UPS): company overview and history
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on UPS, founded 1907, covering history, acquisitions, and Worldport and other facilities.
wikis.body:
- UPS (NYSE: UPS), founded August 28, 1907 in Seattle by James E. Casey as the American Messenger Company; HQ Sandy Springs, Georgia; CEO Carol B. Tomé; revenue US$88.7 billion (2025); c. 460,000 employees (2026).
- Names: Merchants Parcel Delivery (1913-1919); United Parcel Service from 1919 (Oakland expansion). Air service 1929 (ended in the Depression), resumed 1953 as Blue Label Air.
- Milestones: 1975 all 48 contiguous states and Canada; 1985 Next Day Air; 1988 UPS Airlines; 1994 UPS.com; 1997 Teamsters walkout of 16 days; IPO November 10, 1999 (largest of the 20th century); Mail Boxes Etc. bought 2001 (The UPS Store 2003); Overnite bought 2005 for US$1.25 billion; 100th anniversary August 28, 2007.
- TNT Express bid ($6.8 billion, March 2012) fell through in January 2013 after European Commission blocking. 2019 FAA approval for drones. 2021 UPS Freight sold to TFI International for $800 million. Acquisitions: Roadie (2021), Delivery Solutions (2022), Bomi Group (2022), MNX and Happy Returns (2023). Estafeta deal terminated September 17, 2025. 12,000 job cuts announced January 2024; 48,000 jobs reduced in 2025. Reducing Amazon volume in 2025.
- Worldport in Louisville: 290 aircraft, 20,000+ employees, 5.2 million sq ft, 115 packages per second (416,000 per hour). Five regional air hubs (Ontario CA, Dallas, Rockford, Philadelphia, Atlanta); European hub at Cologne Bonn.

wikis.title: UPS Worldport expansion at Louisville
wikis.summary: PARCEL Industry article (July 13 2009) on UPS's roughly $1 billion Worldport hub expansion.
wikis.body:
- UPS began a $1 billion expansion of Worldport in 2006 to raise sorting capacity about 37% to 416,000 packages per hour (from 304,000); adds two aircraft load/unload wings; footprint up 1.2 million sq ft to 5.2 million sq ft.
- Phased project complete by June 2010 (May 2010 in another line); first operational phase opens August 2009. Construction cost about $600 million anticipated economic impact; UPS exceeded commitment of 20 percent of contracts to minority and women owned businesses.
- Earlier expansion more than doubled the hub from about 2 million to 4 million sq ft and sort capacity from 215,000 to 304,000 per hour. Design allows up to half a million per hour.
- Largest fully automated package handling facility in the world: 130 aircraft daily, average 1.2 million packages a day, record 2.5 million on Peak Day.
- History: September 1982 Next Day Air; April 1999 Hub 2000 begins; phases open September 2000, July 2001, September 2002; May 2006 new expansion announced.

wikis.title: Munich Airport (MUC): overview, history, terminals
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Munich Airport covering its opening in 1992, terminals, satellite, runways and traffic figures.
wikis.body:
- Munich Airport (Flughafen München "Franz Josef Strauß"; IATA MUC, ICAO EDDM), 28.5 km northeast of Munich near Freising; opened 17 May 1992 as Munich-Riem closed 16 May 1992. Second-busiest in Germany and eleventh-busiest in Europe (41.6 million passengers in 2024); 2025: 43,394,442 passengers, 337,438 movements, 339,671 t cargo. Hub for Lufthansa.
- Passenger traffic more than doubled 1995-2006; over 40 million first in 2015; 2018: 46.2 million passengers, 266 destinations. Terminal 2 opened June 2003 for Lufthansa and Star Alliance partners, run by a joint venture (Flughafen München 60%, Lufthansa 40%).
- Terminal 2 Satellite: EUR 650 million (60/40 split), approved 2010, construction from 2012, inaugurated 22 April 2016, open to passengers 26 April 2016; 609 m long, 125,000 m2, 52 gates, 27 stands. In March 2026 an eastward pier expansion was announced for 2035, adding up to 10 million passengers capacity.
- Site 1,575 hectares; two parallel 4,000 m runways (08R/26L, 08L/26R); a third runway remains subject to political and legal debate. About 30,000 parking spaces. Munich Airport Center, Hilton hotel (opened 1994), Visitors Park.

wikis.title: Skytrax 5-Star rating for Munich Airport
wikis.summary: Skytrax page certifying Munich Airport as a 5-Star airport, with rating categories.
wikis.body:
- Munich Airport is certified as a 5-Star Airport for facilities, comfort, cleanliness, shopping, food & beverages, staff service and security / immigration.
- Skytrax says: "Munich is one of just two 5-Star Airports in Europe" and a second hub for Lufthansa. Two terminals around the Airport Centre; mostly comfortable and efficient, "however, baggage delivery times can be slow". Most connecting flights occur in Terminal 2.
- The page lists rating categories for Terminal 1, Terminal 2, Terminal 2 Satellite and the Airport Centre (no scores in the text).

wikis.title: Crystal Serenity cruise ship
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Crystal Cruises' Crystal Serenity, built 2003 and known for the 2016 Northwest Passage voyage.
wikis.body:
- Cruise ship owned by Crystal Cruises; built by Chantiers de l'Atlantique, St. Nazaire; ordered 7 November 2000, launched 10 August 2002, completed 30 June 2003, christened 3 July 2003 by Dame Julie Andrews in Southampton; maiden voyage 7 July 2003 (14-day round trip from Southampton). Cost US$350 million.
- 68,870 GT, 250 m long, 32.2 m beam, 13 decks; diesel-electric; 21 knots service; 1,040 passengers, crew 655. Owners: Genting Hong Kong (2003-2022), A&K Travel Group Ltd (2022-present).
- First world cruise began 14 January 2004 (106 days, Los Angeles to New York). Redesign at Lloyd Werft Bremerhaven emerged November 2018.
- Largest cruise ship ever to navigate the Northwest Passage: from 10 August 2016, Vancouver to New York, 28 days, 1,700 passengers and crew.
- Passenger Lee "Mama Lee" Wachtstetter lived aboard full-time (10 years by 2018), about US$170k a year.

wikis.title: Olympia Looping travelling roller coaster
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Olympia Looping, the largest portable roller coaster, which debuted at Oktoberfest in 1989.
wikis.body:
- Portable steel roller coaster (also Munich Looping) owned by R. Barth und Sohn Schaustellerbetriebe KG; designed by Anton Schwarzkopf and Werner Stengel, built by BHS. Opened September 17, 1989 at Oktoberfest.
- Largest portable roller coaster in the world and the only one with five inversions; five vertical loops resembling the Olympic rings.
- 34 m lift, 30 m drop, 1,250 m track, 84 km/h, up to 5.2 g, 1:45 duration; height restriction 130-195 cm. Structure weighs 900 metric tonnes and needs 85 m by 36 m.
- Appears as Munich Looping at London's Hyde Park Winter Wonderland since 2016. Design name was Fünfer Looping.
- In December 2024 Wiener Prater announced the coaster would close there on August 24, 2025 for a new theatre set to open in 2027.

wikis.title: 2019 International Swimming League
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the inaugural ISL season, eight teams, six meets and a Las Vegas Final Match won by Energy Standard.
wikis.body:
- Inaugural edition, 5 October - 21 December 2019; eight teams (men and women); budget $20 million. Energy Standard won the regular season and the Final Match at Mandalay Bay, Las Vegas (20-21 December). Season MVP Sarah Sjöström; Finals MVP Caeleb Dressel.
- Meets: Indianapolis (5-6 Oct), Naples (12-13 Oct), Lewisville (19-20 Oct), Budapest (26-27 Oct), College Park (15-16 Nov), London (23-24 Nov), then the Final Match. 37 races per match.
- Teams: Cali Condors, DC Trident, LA Current, New York Breakers (American); Energy Standard, London Roar, Iron, Aqua Centurions (European).
- Final Match: Energy Standard 453.5, London Roar 444, Cali Condors 415.5, LA Current 318. Regular season: Energy Standard 1499.5, London Roar 1448.5, Cali Condors 1437, LA Current 1360, Iron 1196.5, DC Trident 975, Aqua Centurions 957.5, NY Breakers 886.

wikis.title: MS Ocean Endeavour expedition cruise ship
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on MS Ocean Endeavour, built in Poland in 1981 and now an expedition ship.
wikis.body:
- Built 1981 by Stocznia Szczecinska in Szczecin, Poland (launched 17 April 1981); names: Konstantin Simonov (1982-1996), Francesca (1996-2001), The Iris (2001-2010), Kristina Katarina (2010-2014), Ocean Endeavour (2014-). IMO 7625811.
- 12,907 GT, 137.61 m long, 199 passengers, crew 90-100, 15 knots; cruise ship since 1 December 2004. Sold and renamed Ocean Endeavour on 8 January 2014.
- Operates Canada east coast, Greenland and Canadian Arctic (Adventure Canada) in northern summer and Antarctica from Ushuaia (Intrepid Travel and Chimu Adventures).
- Latest deployment: with NATO to house troops in Greenland as a floating barracks "after geo political concerns in 2026". On 5 September 2019 Adventure Canada passengers visited the wreck of the Erebus.

wikis.title: Volvo's Ghent truck plant: first CO2-free vehicle plant
wikis.summary: Volvo Group press release of 2007-09-20 saying its Ghent, Belgium truck plant is the world's first completely CO2-free vehicle plant.
wikis.body:
- Press release dated 2007-09-20 (AB Volvo): the Volvo Group "can now present the first vehicle plant in the world that is completely free from carbon dioxide (CO2)", Volvo Trucks' plant in Ghent, Belgium.
- Fits the EU goal of cutting CO2 emissions 20% in Europe by 2020.
- CEO Leif Johansson: "Our ambition is to make all our plants CO2-free plants and Ghent is the first."
- Ghent: three wind power plants built on site cover half the plant's electricity; the rest is certified green energy from Electrabel.
- A new pellet-fired biomass plant supplies 70% of heating; solar cells on the roof provide energy for the combustion process; the remaining 30% comes from an oil-fired boiler converted to burn bio oil.
- Ghent produces 35,000 trucks a year and has 2,500 employees.
- Tuve, Sweden plant was decided in 2005 to become CO2-free (planning and environmental permit application in progress); Umeå, Sweden plant is also being transformed.

wikis.title: Volvo heritage page: world's first CO2-free vehicle plant in Ghent
wikis.summary: Volvo Group heritage article on the 2007 Ghent truck plant becoming the world's first CO2-free vehicle plant, with background on Volvo's environmental work.
wikis.body:
- In September 2007 politicians and industry representatives visited Volvo's Ghent, Belgium truck plant; lights were not turned on because roof windows and light interiors gave enough daylight.
- Volvo Trucks made the Ghent plant emissions-free in 2007, partly powered by on-site wind power plants and a bio-oil-fired boiler, the rest from certified sustainable sources.
- The plant "currently produces more than 40,000 trucks per year"; it is a key manufacturing hub and recently became home to Volvo's first battery array assembly plant.
- Background: Volvo's first environmental declaration was made at the UN Conference on the Human Environment, Stockholm, June 1972; the Volvo Environment Prize was founded in 1990 with an initial 20 million Swedish kronor.
- Volvo works towards Paris Agreement climate goals with validated science-based targets.

wikis.title: ARC Independence (formerly MV Faust) car carrier
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the ro-ro car carrier Faust, built 2007 and re-flagged in 2019 as ARC Independence.
wikis.body:
- Built by Daewoo Shipbuilding & Marine Engineering, South Korea, for Wallenius Lines, Sweden; launched 24 February 2007, completed 2007; operated by Wallenius Wilhelmsen Logistics.
- Sailed under the Swedish flag for just over twelve years; re-flagged into the United States Merchant Marine in October 2019 under the name ARC Independence.
- Type: car carrier; 71,583 GT, 33,546 NT, 30,383 DWT; length 227.8 m, beam 32.26 m, height 51.98 m; draft 9.5 m design, 11.3 m maximum.
- 13 decks (5 movable); stern quarter and side ramps; B&W 7S60MC-C engine, single shaft; crew 15.
- Capacity: 8,000 cars (RT-43) or 3,484 cars and 468 buses.
- IMO 9332925; call sign SLKQ; status in service.

wikis.title: MV Faust ro-ro car carrier (Marine Insight)
wikis.summary: Marine Insight overview of MV Faust, described as one of the biggest car carrier ships.
wikis.body:
- Described as owned and operated by Wilhelmsen Logistics; registered in Sweden; built in South Korea by Daewoo; "in operation since the past five years".
- Specs given: about 228 m long, about 33 m wide, GRT over 71,000 tonnes, DWT over 30,000 tonnes, draught almost 12 m, speed up to 21 knots, deck space almost 70,000 square metres.
- Carries about 8,000 cars or a mix of cars, lorries and motor coaches; loading ramps at the stern and starboard side.
- Complies with maritime environmental rules (ballast and bilge water); Lloyd's Register awarded it a 'Green Passport' classification.

wikis.title: Emma Mærsk container ship
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Emma Mærsk, the first E-class container ship of A.P. Møller-Mærsk, launched in 2006 as the largest container ship then built.
wikis.body:
- Built at Odense Steel Shipyard, Denmark; laid down 20 January 2006, launched 18 May 2006, acquired 31 August 2006. Named 12 August 2006 after Mærsk Mc-Kinney Møller's late wife, Emma. Maiden voyage from Aarhus on 8 September 2006, reaching Singapore 1 October 2006.
- In June 2006 welding work caused a fire in the superstructure, delaying completion by six to seven weeks.
- Specs: 170,794 GT, 156,907 DWT; length 397 m, beam 56 m, draught 16.02 m; speed 25.5 knots; crew 13 (room for 30). Engine: Wärtsilä 14RT-Flex96c, 80.08 MW, described as the world's largest single diesel unit (2,300 tonnes).
- Capacity: officially about 11,000 TEU by Maersk's 14-tonne method, or 14,770 TEU by the standard definition; estimates 13,500 to 15,200 TEU. Sister ship Ebba Mærsk set a record of 15,011 TEU in May 2010.
- 1 February 2013: a damaged stern thruster let water flood the ship in the Suez Canal; she went to Port Said to offload 13,500 containers, then to Palermo (arrived 25 February), returning to service in August 2013 after a DKK 250 million (roughly US$44.5 million) repair. Not in danger of sinking.
- 2011: National Bank of Denmark issued a 20 DKK coin for her; 2008 featured on Mighty Ships.
- Exhaust heat recovery gives 8.5 MW, about 12% of main engine output. On 21 February 2011 Maersk ordered ten Triple E class ships (18,000 containers) from Daewoo.

wikis.title: MSC Divina cruise ship
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on MSC Cruises' Fantasia-class ship MSC Divina, built 2010-2012 at Saint-Nazaire.
wikis.body:
- Third of four Fantasia-class ships; 139,072 GT (text also says 139,400); length 333.33 m; 3,502 passengers in 1,539 cabins; crew 1,388; cost $550 million. Built by STX Europe/Chantiers de l'Atlantique, Saint-Nazaire; designed by De Jorio Design International.
- Originally MSC Fantastica; renamed to honour Sophia Loren, who christened her (infobox 19 May 2012; text says delivered 19 May 2012 at Marseille and christened 26 May 2012). Maiden voyage began 27 May 2012 in the Mediterranean; the Venice entrance drew protests over pollution and wake concerns.
- Diesel-electric: five Wärtsilä engines, 71,400 kW total; two GE electric motors of 21,850 kW each; speed about 23 knots.
- Late 2013 repositioned to Miami, first MSC ship serving North America; hosted the Holy Ship! festival January 2014 to February 2016; year-round programme ended Spring 2019, now seasonal in the Caribbean.
- Incident: 18 June 2014 a passenger jumped overboard.

wikis.title: MSC Divina officially delivered
wikis.summary: Offshore Energy report of the 19 May 2012 delivery of cruise ship MSC Divina to MSC Cruises at STX France, Saint-Nazaire.
wikis.body:
- On Saturday 19 May 2012 in Saint-Nazaire, France, MSC Divina was officially delivered to MSC Cruises at the STX France yard; Laurent Castaing (STX France) handed her to owner Gianluigi Aponte, who gave command to Captain Giuliano Bossi.
- CEO Pierfrancesco Vago: the 12th addition to the fleet, third Fantasia-class ship, dedicated to Sophia Loren. Each Fantasia-class ship represents 5 million working hours and an average investment of 550 million euros, over 70% benefiting the French economy.
- Castaing: MSC Divina is the 11th MSC ship built by the yard in just over 10 years; sister ship MSC Preziosa under construction will be the 12th.
- Specs: 333 m long, 38 m wide, about 140,000 tonnes, 4,345 guests, up to 23 knots; designed by De Jorio Design International; 30,000 sq m of public areas including the Garden Pool and Galaxy restaurant.
- After the ceremony she began a pre-christening cruise.

wikis.title: Port Waratah $270 million shiploader investment
wikis.summary: Port Waratah Coal Services announcement (6 May 2025) of a roughly $270 million programme to replace and extend the life of Kooragang Terminal shiploaders.
wikis.body:
- Dated 06 May 2025: Port Waratah Coal Services committed to a capital programme of approximately $270 million so Kooragang Terminal meets demand beyond 2030.
- A new shiploader at Kooragang's K4 berth replaces original Shiploader 7.08 (operating since 1984); expected to enter operations in 2028.
- Life-extension works on the other two shiploaders (commissioned in the 1990s): the first begins July 2025 with a four-month outage of Shiploader 7.09; further outages over the next four years including 7.10.
- CEO Hennie du Plooy commented; an asset assessment completed in 2023 recommended the programme.
- Contracts for the new shiploader and the 7.09 works are with Civmec Construction and Engineering.

wikis.title: Jumbo Fairplayer DP2 heavy lift crane vessel
wikis.summary: Jumbo Maritime vessel page for the DP2 heavy lift crane vessel Fairplayer.
wikis.body:
- Fairplayer has an exceptionally large, flush working deck and a multi-level cargo hold for adding modular components.
- Specs listed: deadweight 13,278 t; free deck space 3,100 sqm; speed 17 knots; cranes 2 x 900 t SWL, combined 1,800 t.
- Part of Jumbo's fleet alongside Jumbo Javelin (also DP2); serves shipping and offshore markets.

wikis.title: Tumut Hydroelectric Power Stations
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the Tumut 1, 2 and 3 hydroelectric power stations of the Snowy Mountains Scheme, New South Wales.
wikis.body:
- Located in the Snowy Mountains Scheme, NSW, Australia; owner/operator Snowy Hydro; Tumut Pond reservoir 52,793 ML.
- Tumut 1: commissioned 1959, 4 turbines, 330 MW, 847 GWh annual generation, hydraulic head 292.6 m.
- Tumut 2: commissioned 1962, 286.4 MW.
- Tumut 3: commissioned 1973, pumped-storage, 6 turbines plus 3 pump-generators, 1,800 MW (pumps 600 MW), head 150.9 m, Talbingo Reservoir 921,400 ML with Jounama Pondage below (43,500 ML).

wikis.title: Tumut 3 power station opened 23 October 1972
wikis.summary: Canberra Times report on the opening of Tumut 3, the last Snowy Mountains scheme project.
wikis.body:
- Governor-General Sir Paul Hasluck opened Tumut 3 near Talbingo on a Saturday (23 October 1972), 23 years after the scheme's official opening on 17 October 1949 by Sir William McKell.
- Tumut 3, scheduled for completion late next year or early 1974, cost $170 million; first pump storage scheme in the southern hemisphere.
- Whole scheme: 16 large dams, more than 90 miles of tunnels, seven power stations, a pumping station, about 50 miles of aqueducts, about $800 million total.
- About 1,500 guests watched Hasluck close a switch starting No 1 generator. Minister Sir Reginald Swartz said it was completed within original time and cost estimates. Staff peaked at 7,300 in 1959.

wikis.title: Angkor Wat: origins, history and rediscovery
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Angkor Wat, the Khmer temple complex in Siem Reap, Cambodia, built by Suryavarman II in the early 12th century (this part covers the overview, name and history).
wikis.body:
- Vaishnava Hindu and later Theravada Buddhist temple complex in Siem Reap, Cambodia, "the largest religious complex in the world"; site 162.6 hectares, max height 65 m; UNESCO World Heritage Site (Angkor) designated 1992; more than 2.5 million visitors every year; appears on the Cambodian national flag.
- Commissioned by Suryavarman II (ruled 1113 to c. 1150) as a state temple to Vishnu in Yaśodharapura; construction commenced 1122 CE and was completed 1150 CE (intro says between 1113 and 1150). Generally considered intended as his mausoleum; work ceased after his death leaving some bas-relief unfinished. Oriented west, unlike most Angkorian temples.
- Name means "Temple City" or "City of Temples"; original name likely Vrah Viṣṇuloka. Modern analyses suggest a resident population of 3,000 to 4,300.
- 1178: Angkor sacked by the Chams; Jayavarman VII restored the empire, built Angkor Thom and the Bayon; Angkor Wat gradually converted to Buddhism, predominantly Theravada from the late 13th century. Never completely abandoned; Khmer empire fell to Ayutthaya in 1431.
- 17th century: Japanese pilgrims settled; Ukondayu Kazufusa celebrated Khmer New Year there in 1632.
- Rediscovery: Portuguese friar António da Madalena visited in 1586; Henri Mouhot popularised it in the West after 1860 (published 1864).
- Restoration coordinated by ICC-Angkor (established 1993 under UNESCO) with France, Japan, India, Germany, the US, South Korea, China and Italy.

wikis.title: Opening of the new hop extraction plant in St. Johann
wikis.summary: BarthHaas press item on the ceremonial opening (31 October 2022) of the CO2 hop extraction plant at St. Johann, Bavaria.
wikis.body:
- Ceremony 31 October 2022 (published 4 November 2022) for the CO2 extraction plant at St. Johann, described as the world's largest hop processing plant; commissioned September 2020 but the celebration was postponed due to the pandemic. Guests included Bavarian Minister President Markus Söder and Hubert Aiwanger.
- About 65 million euros invested; about 190 employees; joint venture of BarthHaas and the HVG Hop Processing Cooperative.
- Each season the site processes around 33,000 t of raw hops (60 varieties from 16 growing regions), about 26% of the world's harvest, supplying breweries in 100 countries. Eleven hectares; storage for 11,000 t raw hops and 23,500 t finished product.
- CO2 extraction processes around 33% of capacity; extract is up to 3-fold concentrated, needs about 25% less storage volume; CO2 compressed to 500 bar supercritical; method used at St. Johann since the mid-1980s replacing alcohol and hot water.

wikis.title: World's largest hops extraction plant goes into operation
wikis.summary: inside.beer report (8 October 2020) on BarthHaas and HVG starting the new hop extraction plant at St. Johann, Germany.
wikis.body:
- Reported 8 October 2020: the plant is "slowly" started up; a 60/40 joint venture of BarthHaas and hop cooperative HVG, investing more than EUR 60 million.
- Previously Hopfenveredlung St. Johann had a pelletising plant plus a CO2 extraction plant (formerly Nateco2) in nearby Wolnzach; hop extraction moves entirely to St. Johann, and the Wolnzach plant will be used for coffee, algae or vegetable proteins.
- Groundbreaking was October 2018; around a quarter of the world's hops will be processed at St. Johann.
- Regine Barth: "This enables us to effectively implement our vision of processing everything from raw hops to hop pellets and extract at one location."

wikis.title: Oasis of the Seas cruise ship
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Royal Caribbean's Oasis of the Seas, first of the Oasis class, delivered in 2009.
wikis.body:
- Ordered 6 February 2006 as "Project Genesis"; built by STX Europe Turku Shipyard, Finland; original cost US$1.4 billion; laid down 12 November 2007; float-out 21 November 2008; completed 28 October 2009; named 30 November 2009 (seven "godmothers", charity sailing for Make-A-Wish); maiden voyage 5 December 2009.
- 226,838 GT; length 361.8 m; max beam 64.9 m; 16 passenger decks; 24.5 knots; capacity 5,606 passengers double occupancy, 6,699 maximum; crew 2,181 as of 2019. Three 20 MW ABB Azipods.
- Largest passenger ship until surpassed by Allure of the Seas by 50 mm; Oasis class later surpassed in 2024 by the Icon class. Sisters: Allure (Dec 2010), Harmony (May 2016), Symphony (Apr 2018), Wonder (Mar 2022), Utopia (Jul 2024).
- 31 October 2009 passed under the Great Belt Fixed Link (65 m clearance) with less than 60 cm to spare, using retracted funnels. Arrived Port Everglades 13 November 2009.
- Refits: minor winter 2011; drydock October 2014 (main dining room split into three); amplification 24 November 2019. As of November 2024 sails from Port Everglades and Cape Liberty (Bayonne).

wikis.title: Oasis of the Seas debut (Royal Caribbean Blog)
wikis.summary: Royal Caribbean Blog history piece on Oasis of the Seas, whose maiden voyage on 5 December 2009 made her the world's largest cruise ship.
wikis.body:
- Updated 5 December 2025; maiden voyage 5 December 2009. Previously Liberty of the Seas was largest; Oasis was more than 40 percent larger at 225,282 tons, accommodating 5,400 passengers.
- Project name "Project Genesis"; split-superstructure design opened the rear for the Boardwalk and Central Park (12,000 plants); first ship with seven "neighborhoods"; four pools, two with beach-like sloped entries.
- The Aquatheater hosts water ballet and diving shows (dives from up to 72 feet); a full Broadway show, "Hairspray", was performed.
- At launch: 25 restaurants and 37 bars; 9 specialty restaurants ($4.95 at Johnny Rockets to $75 for Chef's Table); 150 Central Park offered a ten-course tasting menu for $35.

wikis.title: 50 years of Opel's Dudenhofen test centre
wikis.summary: autohaus.de/dpa report (9 September 2016) on Opel's 50-year-old test centre in Rodgau-Dudenhofen.
wikis.body:
- Published 09.09.2016: Opel's test centre in Rodgau-Dudenhofen near Frankfurt celebrates its 50th anniversary; Opel has already invested about 30 million euros and a further double-digit million sum is to follow by 2020.
- Chief tester Matthias Schollmaier: "We will in future also test cars completely without drivers here. But we cannot do without people."
- Autonomous driving and electromobility are already present on the fenced-off site; the battery car Ampera-E, announced for 2017, is adapted for the European market there; prototypes and camouflaged models are tested.
- Many tests can be simulated, but a human must judge how the technology works.

wikis.title: Cadbury's Chocolate Factory, Claremont, Tasmania
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Cadbury's Claremont factory in Tasmania, opened 21 October 1921 as Cadbury's first expansion outside the UK.
wikis.body:
- Founded 21 October 1921 by Cadbury-Fry-Pascall Ltd at 100 Cadbury Road, Claremont, Tasmania; now owned by Mondelez International (bought Cadbury in 2010).
- Site chosen after a January 1920 visit: 246-acre (100 ha) peninsula, cheap hydro electricity from the Hydro Electric Commission, cool climate, fresh dairy supply; 8.0 km water frontage inspired the phrase "By mountain and sea".
- Construction began 1920: white ferro-concrete, 9,200 cubic metres, about 22,000 tonnes; six rectangular blocks. Forty workers from Birmingham and Bristol relocated to train staff. First shipment left 8 April 1922 for Sydney. A three-storey building was added in 1939 (£A 40,000).
- Cadbury's Estate modelled on Bournville: housing, shops, sport facilities, school, Friends meeting house, parkland with purple benches.
- Workforce fell from 1,100 in 1960 to 450 in 2018. Produces Dairy Milk blocks, Caramello Koala and Freddo bars. Visitor facilities closed in 2015 over health and safety concerns; in 2025 an application was lodged for a $150 million chocolate-themed tourism development next to the site.

wikis.title: Tropical Islands Resort, Brandenburg
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Tropical Islands Resort, an indoor water park in a former airship hangar in Brandenburg, Germany, opened 19 December 2004.
wikis.body:
- Indoor tropical water park at the former Brand-Briesen Airfield, Krausnick/Halbe, Brandenburg, 50 km from Berlin's southern boundary; described as the largest indoor water park in the world; owner Parques Reunidos; opened 19 December 2004; max capacity 8,200 visitors per day; about 600 staff.
- Housed in the Aerium hangar built by Cargolifter AG: 360 m long, 210 m wide, 107 m high, cost EUR 78 million, 5.5 million m3; commissioned November 2000, but the CL160 airship was never built; Cargolifter went bankrupt in mid-2002.
- Bought by Malaysian corporation Tanjong on 11 June 2003 for EUR 17.5 million (EUR 10 million subsidy from Brandenburg); building permit 2 February 2004.
- Interior kept at 26 C and about 64% humidity, open every day. Areas: Tropical Village, Rainforest (about 50,000 plants, 600 species), Tropical Sea (140 m pool), Bali Lagoon, Amazonia outdoor area.
- 4,000 m2 play area 2007; sauna/spa 2007 (largest tropical sauna complex in Europe, designs inspired by Angkor Wat and Elephanta); campsite 2008.
- Break-even needs 1.25 million visitors a year; 2005 loss EUR 10-20 million; about 600,000 visitors by October 2006.

wikis.title: Tropical Islands: history of the giant hangar (No Tourist Info)
wikis.summary: Blog post on why the CargoLifter airship hangar in Brandenburg became the Tropical Islands resort.
wikis.body:
- Tropical Islands is inside a former hangar of CargoLifter AG, about 60 km south of Berlin; opened 2004. Figures given: over 66,000 sq m indoors, about 1.2 million visitors a year, up to 6,000 guests at once, 26 C year round.
- CargoLifter's late-1990s vision was moving heavy cargo by airship; the company filed for bankruptcy in 2002 (lack of investors, rising costs).
- 2003: a Malaysian investor bought the hangar with support of the state of Brandenburg; the hall was transformed in under a year. Early problems: plants would not grow, little daylight; a UV-permeable membrane was later installed.
- The site was a Luftwaffe airfield from 1938, later a Soviet base and an East German airport.
- Today includes beach, lagoon, rainforest, hotels, camping and holiday homes. Author is a Berliner; personal anecdotes omitted.

wikis.title: Peregrino Field, Campos Basin, Brazil
wikis.summary: Offshore Technology project profile (13 April 2010) of Statoil's Peregrino heavy-oil field offshore Brazil.
wikis.body:
- Located in Campos Basin, 85 km offshore Brazil (block BM-C-7), water depth 100 m; owner/operator Statoil; first production April 2011, expected to continue until 2040.
- Statoil acquired 100% in 2007 (originally with Anadarko); in May 2010 sold a 40% stake to Sinochem.
- Recoverable reserves estimated 300 to 600 million barrels of heavy oil. Development in three phases with 60 wells; Phase I has 37 wells (30 producers). April 2011 discovery: Peregrino south well found a 130 m oil column.
- FPSO by Maersk FPSOs with BW Offshore submerged turret production system (ten mooring lines, 15 risers); two wellhead platforms A and B installed by heavy lift vessel Hermod (completed March 2010).
- Contracts: Subsea 7 flexible risers (May 2007); Aker Solutions mooring installation (July 2009); FMC Technologies $30m wellheads/trees (June 2009); Wood Group $60m five-year maintenance (September 2009).

wikis.title: FPSO Peregrino: billion dollar beauty (Safety4Sea)
wikis.summary: SAFETY4SEA article (23 August 2012, source ABB) on the FPSO Peregrino oil production ship and ABB's electrical and automation role.
wikis.body:
- Converted from a VLCC to an FPSO for more than $1 billion; completed April 2011 after three years, then A.P. Moller-Maersk Group's biggest single-vessel investment; recently acquired by Statoil.
- Capacity: 100,000 barrels of oil per day, 350,000 barrels of liquid, 7.3 million standard cubic feet of gas; storage 1.6 million barrels (16 days of production); accommodation for 100 staff; 15 topside modules and two production trains.
- Docked permanently at the Peregrino field, 85 km off Brazil, 5 km from two wellhead platforms; oil is 2,300 m below the seabed and so thick it needs submersible pumps and heated flowlines.
- ABB was main automation and main electrical contractor (System 800xA platform, power distribution down to submersible pumps).
- Named one of Offshore magazine's 'top five offshore projects' for 2011.

wikis.title: Cristobal Colon dredger (Marine Insight)
wikis.summary: Marine Insight profile (25 July 2011) of Jan De Nul's trailing suction hopper dredger Cristobal Colon, described as the largest and most high-tech dredger in the world.
wikis.body:
- Belgian company Jan De Nul's flagship dredger; hopper capacity given as 46000 (source says square metres) - nearly 40% more than Vasco da Gama, its closest peer.
- Dredging depth 155 m; electric submerged pumps of 6,500 kW each; two suction pipes of 1,300 mm; electric discharge pumps of 8,000 kW each; suction pipes adjustable to three depths.
- Specs: 223 m long, 41 m broad, draught 15.15 m, deadweight 78,000 tons, 18 knots, accommodation for 46 people.
- Another vessel of similar capacity, Liev Eiriksson, has been ordered.

wikis.title: Emsflower 20 years in Emsbüren and 14-hectare greenhouse expansion
wikis.summary: FloralDaily report on Emsflower celebrating 20 years at Emsbüren, Germany, and opening a 14-hectare greenhouse expansion.
wikis.body:
- Emsflower held a jubilee day for 20 years at Emsbüren with more than 700 customers, suppliers and growers, introducing the newly completed 14-hectare expansion; 3.5 km tour.
- History: Jan Kuipers founded Kwekerij Kuipers in De Lutte, Netherlands, in 1954; Bennie Kuipers joined 1977; construction in Emsbüren began 2003 (Tom and Bart Kuipers, now managing directors, joined); renamed Emsflower in March 2006.
- Cuttings from a facility in Modjo, Ethiopia (pelargonium, osteospermum, chrysanthemum, lavender, bidens) are grown on in Emsbüren; strawberries are also produced there.
- Three greenhouses in the new facility are dedicated to breeding; a small water-based lettuce trial is underway.
- About 330 permanent staff in Europe plus seasonal workers.

wikis.title: Emsflower 14 ha expansion launched (HortiDaily)
wikis.summary: HortiDaily report on the 14-hectare expansion of Emsflower, Europe's largest nursery for pot and bedding plants, in Emsbüren, Germany.
wikis.body:
- Expansion covers 14 hectares: 12.5 ha cultivation and 1.5 ha warehousing, corridors and operational areas; focus on capacity for potted and bedding plants, with a combination greenhouse allowing crops including tomatoes.
- Spokesperson Erwin Savenije: "If this complex operates as expected, we might explore commercial lettuce cultivation on water or even year-round cultivation of various fruits and vegetables."
- Havecon Kassenbouw was given the assignment; engineering drawings being finalised while foundation work progresses; drainage systems next, then steel construction. The Voorwinden Group has started pouring concrete for the foundation.

wikis.title: 40 Jahre Marzahn (Tagesspiegel, paywalled teaser)
wikis.summary: Tagesspiegel article of 8 July 2017 on 40 years of the Marzahn prefab housing estate in Berlin; only the opening is visible.
wikis.body:
- Headline: "Europas größte Plattensammlung" (Europe's largest panel collection); standfirst: during construction people lived in a "Schlammwüste" (mud desert) but enjoyed the modern flats; the former GDR showcase district is becoming more popular again.
- Founding myth: a concrete slab on Allee der Kosmonauten bears the outline of Peter Zeise, a worker of an assembly brigade said to have given the signal 40 years ago. The first slab was set in the fields on 8 July 1977.
- Rest is paywalled.

wikis.title: WBS 70 panel housing type (East Germany)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on WBS 70, the slab-construction housing series built in the GDR.
wikis.body:
- Wohnungsbauserie 70, developed in the early 1970s by the German Academy of Architecture and TU Dresden. First block built in Neubrandenburg in 1973 (now a monument).
- Of about 1.52 million slab-construction dwellings built to 1990, WBS 70 accounts for up to 42 percent.
- Technical: 6.00 m x 6.00 m grid; depth 10.8, 12.0 or 14.4 m; floor height 2.80 m (3.30 m for WBS 70/G); 5, 6 or 11 storeys; three-layer outer wall; interior bathrooms.
- Museum in Berlin-Hellersdorf (Hellersdorfer Strasse 179) with a 61 sq m three-room flat; DDR Museum Berlin has a five-room replica. In the 1990s WBS 70 microdistricts were built in Russia (Chaykovsky, Polazna, Izhevsk).

wikis.title: Madrid-Barcelona high-speed rail line
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 621 km AVE line between Madrid and Barcelona, opened in full on 20 February 2008.
wikis.body:
- 621 km (620.9 km to Barcelona; 748.9 km to Figueres) standard-gauge double track, 25 kV 50 Hz, owned by Adif; operators Renfe (AVE, Avlo), Ouigo, Iryo. Designed for 350 km/h; operating speed 300 km/h; ridership 4.4 million (2019). Madrid to Barcelona in 2 h 30.
- First phase Madrid-Zaragoza-Lleida commercial service began 11 October 2003 at 200 km/h; 250 km/h on 19 May 2006, 280 km/h on 16 October 2006, Camp de Tarragona from 18 December 2006, 300 km/h from 7 May 2007. Full line opened February 2008 (inaugurated 20 February 2008). Before it, the trip took more than six hours.
- 310 km/h on a 60 km section from 11 December 2011, reduced back to 300 km/h on 17 August 2016 because ballast stones rose and damaged trains.
- By end of 2017 the line had taken 63% of traffic, mostly from aircraft; in 2007 Madrid-Barcelona was the world's busiest air route with 971 scheduled flights a week.
- Criticism: a 23 June 2004 KPMG report cited over-hasty works; the Barcelona tunnel passes metres from Sagrada Família's foundations. July 2006 Siemens Velaro test hit 403.7 km/h.
- Extension to Figueres-Vilafant opened 9 January 2013 (131 km Barcelona-Figueres section), linking to the French TGV network; Figueres-Perpignan section 44.4 km with the 8.3 km Perthus Tunnel, completed February 2009.

wikis.title: Great Wall of China (HISTORY)
wikis.summary: HISTORY.com article on the Great Wall of China, its Qin origins and Ming-era construction.
wikis.body:
- Series of walls and fortifications totalling more than 13,000 miles in northern China; conceived by Qin Shi Huang in the third century B.C. to prevent incursions by nomads; beginnings traced to the fifth century B.C.
- Around 220 B.C. Qin Shi Huang had earlier walls joined into one system of more than 10,000 li; general Meng Tian directed the work using soldiers, convicts and commoners; "as many as 400,000 people died" during construction.
- Most of the wall as it exists today was built under the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644); most extensive section began around 1474; the Ming wall ran from the Yalu River (Liaoning) to the Taolai River (Gansu). Six major passes near Beijing were heavily garrisoned.
- Mid-17th century: the Manchus broke through, ending the Ming. UNESCO World Heritage site in 1987; the claim that it is visible from space has been refuted by NASA. Badaling (43 miles / 70 km northwest of Beijing) was rebuilt in the late 1950s.

wikis.title: Qin dynasty: origins, unification and collapse
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article (part 1 of 2) on China's first imperial dynasty (221-206 BC), covering the state of Qin's rise, unification under Qin Shi Huang, and its collapse.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- First imperial dynasty of China, 221-206 BC; capital Xianyang; emperors Qin Shi Huang (221-210 BC) and Qin Er Shi (210-207 BC). Named for the state of Qin, a Zhou fief. Its 14-year existence was the shortest of any major dynasty in Chinese history; the Han dynasty largely continued its military and administrative practices, so Qin is credited as originator of the imperial system that lasted until the Xinhai Revolution in 1911.
- Reforms: standardisation of currency, weights, measures and the writing system; large projects using hundreds of thousands of peasants and convicts, including connecting northern walls (later the Great Wall), a national road system, and the Mausoleum of Qin Shi Huang with the Terracotta Army. Area about 2,300,000 km2 in 220 BC.
## Origins (9th century BC - 230 BC)
- Per the Shiji, Feizi was granted the settlement of Qin in the 9th century BC; Duke Xiang helped escort the Zhou court in 770 BC and Qin became a major vassal state. Shang Yang introduced military reforms 359-338 BC (executed 338) and helped build the capital Xianyang. The Guanzhong homeland gave fertile land and mountain protection; the Wei River canal was built in 246 BC.
## Unification (230-221 BC)
- Conquests: Han (capital Xinzheng, 230 BC), Zhao (surrendered 228), Yan (226), Wei (Daliang, 225), Chu (surrendered 223), then Qi (Linzi, 221 BC). King Zheng took the title Shi Huangdi, "First Emperor", and had non-Qin weapons melted into twelve statues.
## Expansion
- 215 BC: campaign under Meng Tian against the Xiongnu in the Ordos; 214 BC: about 500,000 men sent south against the Baiyue, losing over 100,000 men in the first attempt but building a canal; later conquered the Guangzhou coast and moved over 100,000 prisoners and exiles to colonise it.
## Collapse (210-206 BC)
- Three assassination attempts on Qin Shi Huang (227 BC Jing Ke; two around 218 BC). He died in 210 BC seeking an elixir of immortality. Zhao Gao and Li Si altered his will, forcing eldest son Fusu to suicide and enthroning Huhai as Qin Er Shi, who executed ministers, raised taxes and continued building; revolts followed. Li Si was executed; Zhao Gao forced Qin Er Shi to suicide; Ziying executed Zhao Gao, and surrendered to Liu Bang in 207 BC (and was executed shortly after). Xianyang was destroyed in 206 BC; Liu Bang founded the Han.

wikis.title: Tokaido Shinkansen: overview, history and infrastructure
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article (part 1 of 2) on JR Central's Tokyo-Shin-Osaka high-speed line, opened 1 October 1964, covering its history, route, signalling and stations.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- High-speed rail line between Tokyo and Shin-Osaka, 515.4 km, 17 stations, owned and operated by JR Central. Opened October 1, 1964, shortly before the 1964 Tokyo Olympics; described as the first railway in the world built for regular operation above 200 km/h. Operation passed from JNR to JR Central at privatization in 1987 (April 1, 1987).
- Services: Nozomi, Hikari, Kodama; all trains are 16-car; max speed 285 km/h; fastest Tokyo-Shin-Osaka 2 h 21 min. Rolling stock N700A and N700S.
- Ridership: 168 million passengers in fiscal 2024, about 460,000 per day, 383 services a day on average. The March 2026 timetable permits up to 13 Nozomi per hour; JR Central says the line can handle up to 18 trains per hour.
- 2000: designated an ASME/IEEE Historic Mechanical Engineering Landmark and IEEE Milestone.
## History
- Late 1930s: government proposed a standard-gauge "bullet train" line Tokyo-Shimonoseki, halted in WWII; some tunnels reused. JNR feasibility committee May 1956; Cabinet approval December 1958; construction authorized April 1959, begun April 20, 1959 at the New Tanna Tunnel. JNR president Shinji Sogo and chief engineer Hideo Shima backed a new standard-gauge line; the initial cost estimate was too low and both resigned before completion.
- World Bank lent JNR US$80 million on May 2, 1961 (about 15 percent of project cost), repaid in 1981.
- Opening 1964: Hikari took four hours, Kodama five; trains designed for 210 km/h ran at 200 km/h at first; from Nov 1, 1965 210 km/h schedules cut Hikari to 3 h 10 min.
- JNR era: 16-car Hikari 1969, Kodama 1972; San'yo Shinkansen to Okayama (March 1972) and Hakata (March 1975); 100 series 1985; 220 km/h in Nov 1986 (2 h 56 min).
- JR Central era: 300 series and Nozomi from March 14, 1992 (270 km/h, 2 h 30 min); Shinagawa platforms opened October 1, 2003; N700 in 2007 (2 h 25 min); 285 km/h from March 14, 2015; 700 series left service March 2020; N700S in commercial service July 1, 2020. JR Central plans Grade of Automation 2 operation on some services around 2028.
## Infrastructure
- Route 515.4 km (fare operating distance 552.6 km); double-track, standard gauge, fully grade-separated; 25 kV 60 Hz AC with frequency-converter substations east of the Fuji River; curves about 2,500 m radius; gradients up to 2%; mostly ballasted track.
- Civil works: about 276.7 km earthworks (54%), 170.1 km bridges and viaducts (33%), 68.6 km tunnels (13%).
- Signalling: cab signalling; analog ATC-1 replaced by digital ATC-NS in March 2006; COMTRAC traffic control from the General Control Center in Tokyo with a second backup center.
- 17 passenger stations; six served by every train: Tokyo, Shinagawa, Shin-Yokohama, Nagoya, Kyoto, Shin-Osaka.

wikis.title: Shinkansen and the Legacy of Tokyo 1964 (Japan House London event)
wikis.summary: Event page for a Japan House London talk, with the Central Japan Railway Company, on the Tokaido Shinkansen and how the 1964 Olympics reshaped Tokyo.
wikis.body:
- Japan House London, in partnership with the Central Japan Railway Company, looks at how the 1964 Olympics reshaped the urban fabric of Tokyo.
- The Tōkaidō 'New Main Line' (Shinkansen) was inaugurated on 1 October 1964, just 10 days before the opening of the Tokyo 1964 Olympic Games, and was viewed by many as a symbol of Japan's post-war modernization.
- The 'Series 0' Shinkansen was the first train in the world to operate commercially at a top speed of 210 kph. It was dubbed the 'bullet train' for its speed and the aerodynamic shape of its nose. It connected Tokyo to Osaka in 4 hours instead of the 6 hours 30 minutes of a conventional express.
- Speakers: Ueno Naoyuki (General Manager, Central Japan Railway Company's London office) on the history and development of the Shinkansen; Professor Roderick Smith (Emeritus Professor of Railway Engineering, Imperial College London) in conversation.
- Part of the programme around the exhibition *Tokyo 1964: Designing Tomorrow*. Models of the Series 0 and of the Series N700S (in service since 1 July 2020) were on display, the latter in The Shop until 7 November 2021.
- The event was livestreamed on Zoom, Facebook, YouTube and LinkedIn, with a recording to follow.
- Venue: 101-111 Kensington High Street, London.

wikis.title: Great Pyramid of Giza: overview, purpose, attribution to Khufu and age
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article (part 1 of 3) on the Great Pyramid of Giza, Khufu's tomb, covering its dimensions, purpose, evidence tying it to Khufu and dating estimates.
wikis.body:
## Overview
