- Largest Egyptian pyramid, in the Giza complex, Egypt; tomb of Pharaoh Khufu (Cheops), Fourth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom; built c. 2600 BC over about 26 years. Oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World and the only one largely intact. Ancient name Akhet Khufu ("Khufu's Horizon"); Hemiunu, Khufu's vizier, is "believed by some" to be the architect. Part of the UNESCO site "Memphis and its Necropolis" (inscribed 1979).
- Height originally 146.6 m (481 ft; 280 cubits), now 138.5 m after most of the white limestone casing was removed; base about 230.3 m (440 cubits); volume roughly 2.6 million m3; slope 51°50'40". Tallest human-made structure for more than 3,700 years (c. 2600 BC to 1221 AD).
- About 2.3 million large blocks weighing 6 million tonnes; local Giza limestone, white Tura limestone for casing, Aswan granite up to 80 tonnes for the King's Chamber. Three known chambers (unfinished bedrock chamber, Queen's Chamber, King's Chamber with granite sarcophagus). No consensus on exact construction techniques.
- Complex: two mortuary temples with a causeway, family tombs including three queens' pyramids, a satellite pyramid, five buried solar barques.
## Attribution to Khufu
- Historically attributed via Herodotus and Diodorus Siculus. In 1837 four relieving chambers above the King's Chamber were found with red-paint work-gang graffiti including Khufu's name. Boat pits found 1954 (Khufu ship), with Djedefre's cartouche on covering blocks. The Diary of Merer, found 2013 at Wadi al-Jarf, documents shipping Tura limestone to Akhet Khufu under Ankhhaf.
- Likely looted as early as the First Intermediate Period; Al-Maqrizi (1364-1442) reports Arab accounts of finds inside.
## Age
- About 4,600 years old, dated via Khufu's chronology and by radiocarbon dating. Modern estimates of Khufu's first regnal year range from 1266 BC (Greaves, 1646) to 4235 BC (Mariette, 1867); Ramsey et al. (2010) give 2613-2577 BC.

wikis.title: LC-130H Skibird lands on freshwater ice in Canada for the first time
wikis.summary: The Aviationist report that a 109th Airlift Wing LC-130H landed on a frozen lake at Parsons Lake, Northwest Territories, during Operation Nanook-Nunalivut on 5 March 2025.
wikis.body:
- On Mar. 5, 2025, an LC-130H Hercules of the 109th Airlift Wing (New York Air National Guard) landed on a frozen lake during Operation Nanook-Nunalivut in Inuvik, Canada: the first time in the unit's history its ski-equipped Hercules touched down on fresh water ice.
- The LC-130H is described as the largest tactical aircraft in the world capable of landing on snow and ice using skis. Only 10 operational LC-130s are in U.S. Air Force service, all operated by the 109th since first fielded in 1984; it is the only ski-equipped US military aircraft capable of large-scale airlift in Antarctica, the Arctic and other extreme cold-weather environments.
- Maj. Joseph Shanahan (ski landing control officer) and team searched over 25,000 miles of ice along the Northwest Territories coast and found none met the requirements, so they moved inland and found Parsons Lake.
- The Polar Camp Skiway Team (airmen from the 109th, 123rd and 133rd Airlift Wings) built the ski landing area in one day, then groomed it from sunrise to sunset every day.
- Royal Canadian Air Force support: CC-138 Twin Otters (440 Transport Squadron), CH-147F Chinooks (450 Tactical Helicopter Squadron), CH-146 Griffons (430 Tactical Helicopter Squadron) and 417th Combat Support Squadron. Seventeen flights moved 23,000 pounds of cargo and personnel to the camp.
- The 109th flew eight missions during the operation, including resupply and carrying Twin Otter spare parts from Yellowknife to Inuvik.
- The article notes recent U.S.-Canada tensions and says whether such joint drills continue "remains to be seen".

wikis.title: 109th Airlift Wing (New York Air National Guard)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the New York Air National Guard unit at Stratton ANGB that flies ski-equipped LC-130H Hercules to support Arctic and Antarctic operations.
wikis.body:
- Unit of the New York Air National Guard at Stratton Air National Guard Base, Schenectady, New York; gained by Air Mobility Command if federalized.
- Mission: airlift for the National Science Foundation's South Pole research program with LC-130H Hercules on wheel-ski gear, as part of Operation Deep Freeze; "the only unit in the world to fly these aircraft"; operates 5 LC-130 (per the article). Also supported Operation Enduring Freedom and domestic disaster relief.
- Units: 109th Operations Group, 139th Airlift Squadron, 139th Aeromedical Evacuation Squadron, Maintenance, Mission Support and Medical Groups.
## History
- Activated 1 May 1956 as the 109th Fighter Group (Air Defense); became a Tactical Fighter Group in 1958; redesignated 109th Air Transport Group (Heavy) on 2 January 1960 with C-97 Stratofreighters; 109th Military Airlift Group 1966.
- After C-97 retirement in 1971 became a Tactical Airlift Group with eight C-130A. First major mission June 1972 relief after Tropical Storm Agnes.
- ski-equipped LC-130s flew National Science Foundation missions to Antarctica since 1988; Greenland DEW Line resupply ended with a last flight to DYE-3 in December 1989. In Oct 1984 C-130Ds were replaced by eight C-130H, four ski-equipped.
- 20 February 1998: responsibility for US Antarctic Program airlift passed from Navy squadron VXE-6 to the 109th at Christchurch, New Zealand; it set up a forward location at Williams Field on the Ross Ice Shelf. Oct 1999: aided rescue of Dr. Jerri Nielsen from the South Pole station.
- 21st century: 49 personnel to Ground Zero within 24 hours of 9/11; 139th Expeditionary Airlift Squadron to Afghanistan June 2007; a 2005 BRAC proposal to move four C-130H was not enacted.
- 2011-2012 season: six LC-130H flew 359 missions between McMurdo and eighteen inland destinations, over seven million pounds of cargo and fuel and more than 1,600 passengers. 2013-14: seven LC-130s on the ice, 479 Guardsmen deployed.
- 2023: transported US National Guard and Canadian Reserve troops in a joint tactical insertion exercise off the coast of Canada.

wikis.title: A timeline of Stonehenge (English Heritage)
wikis.summary: English Heritage timeline of Stonehenge's history from Mesolithic posts (8500-7000 BC) to the 2013 new visitor centre.
wikis.body:
- Stonehenge was first built about 5,000 years ago in the Neolithic; by about 2500 BC larger stones arrived, starting over 800 years of building and alteration into the Bronze Age.
## Timeline
- **8500-7000 BC:** Mesolithic posts, like totem poles, raised by hunter-gatherers north-west of the site.
- **3500 BC:** Early farming communities build ritual monuments north of the site: a causewayed enclosure at Robin Hood's Ball, two cursus monuments, long barrows.
- **3000 BC:** First Stonehenge, an earthwork enclosure about 100 m across with a circular ditch and two banks and a ring of 56 timber or stone posts; used as a cremation cemetery for several hundred years. The Preseli Hills (Wales) bluestones, over 150 miles (250 km) away, "may have arrived around this time".
- **2500 BC:** Over 80 large sarsens brought from the Marlborough Downs, 15 miles (25 km) away, raised in two concentric arrangements; bluestones set in a double arc between them.
- **2400 BC:** Beaker culture people arrive; graves include the Amesbury Archer, the richest grave of the time.
- **2300-2200 BC:** Central bluestones rearranged into a circle and inner oval; the earthwork Avenue links Stonehenge to the river Avon.
- **2100-1500 BC:** Hundreds of burial mounds, the densest concentration in Britain; two rings of pits dug around the sarsen circle.
- **1750-1500 BC:** Over 100 carvings of axeheads and a few daggers on four sarsens.
- **700 BC:** Vespasian's Camp hillfort built about a mile east.
- **AD 43 - early 5th century:** Roman objects left at the site.
- **14th-19th centuries:** growing interest from writers and antiquarians; monument deteriorates and some stones fall.
- **1897:** Ministry of Defence buys a large area of Salisbury Plain, including a First World War airfield.
- **1901-64:** restoration campaigns, starting with Sir Edmund Antrobus re-erecting the leaning tallest trilithon in 1901.
- **1918:** Cecil Chubb, who bought it three years earlier from the Antrobus family, gives Stonehenge to the nation.
- **2013:** the nearby road is closed and a new visitor centre built 2 km away.

wikis.title: Martin JRM Mars Hawaii Mars retires to the BC Aviation Museum (The Aviationist)
wikis.summary: The Aviationist's account of the Hawaii Mars flying boat's final flight on 11 August 2024 to the British Columbia Aviation Museum, with history of the JRM Mars.
wikis.body:
- Hawaii Mars II, one of only two surviving Martin JRM Mars flying boats, retired on Aug. 11, 2024 after "well over 78 years", flying to the British Columbia Aviation Museum in Sidney, Vancouver Island, escorted by 9 CT-114 Tutors of the Snowbirds.
- After landing in the bay, on Aug. 14, 2024 it was to be winched up a Coast Guard ramp for de-watering, then moved to the museum Aug. 19-23; a closed display until the official opening scheduled for Sep. 28, when visitors can enter.
- History: the JRM Mars was created in 1938 in response to a US Navy request for a long-range ocean patrol flying boat, the largest Allied flying boat of WWII. Development delays made it obsolete by 1942-43, prompting conversion to a cargo transport; first delivery June 1945; the order for 20 was cut to 7 airframes.
- Hawaii Mars (actually II; the first sank in Chesapeake Bay days after delivery on Aug. 5, 1945) was delivered as the sixth Mars on Apr. 23, 1946, withdrawn 1956, sold 1959, and converted to a firefighter with cargo-bay water tanks. Registration C-FLYL, flown for FIFT, FTI and the Coulson Group.
- In 55 years of firefighting it dropped over 50 million gallons of water, which Coulson says is more than any other single firefighting aircraft. No firefighting since 2015.
- Marianas Mars was lost in a 1961 crash; Caroline Mars was damaged beyond repair in Typhoon Freda in 1962. The last two were acquired by Coulson in 2007 and based at Sproat Lake, BC. Philippine Mars (C-FLYK), repainted in US Navy markings, awaited transfer to the Pima Air and Space Museum in Arizona later in 2024.
- Context: the retirement comes amid retirement of the first ShinMaywa US-2, further shrinking the number of large flying boats operating.

wikis.title: Hawaii Mars makes final flight to the BC Aviation Museum (Skies Mag)
wikis.summary: Skies Mag report on the Hawaii Mars waterbomber's last flight on 11 August 2024 to Patricia Bay and its planned display at the BC Aviation Museum.
wikis.body:
- The Hawaii Mars, a 1945 Martin Mars waterbomber and one of only two remaining in the world, flew its last flight on Sunday, Aug. 11, 2024, to the BC Aviation Museum in North Saanich, B.C. Thousands gathered at Patricia Bay.
- Last active firefighting season 2015; maintained by Coulson Aviation since. 120 feet long, 200-foot wingspan, described as the largest waterbomber in the world, able to drop more than 25,000 litres of water per run. Museum display commemorates its "50-year legacy" in Canadian forest firefighting.
- Lifted off from Sproat Lake at 3:20 p.m. local time after a goodbye flyover with the Coulson family aboard; pilots Peter Killin and Rick Matthews; route via Comox, Nanaimo and Croften, where nine Snowbirds jets joined. Arrived at Pat Bay about 7 p.m.; the museum's YouTube livestream had over 110,000 views at publication.
- Removal from the water planned Aug. 14, 3-7 p.m., by Nickel Brothers Moving, the BC Aviation Museum, Coulson Aviation and Cold Water Divers, winched up a Coast Guard ramp (the ramp used in 1960 to convert it into a water bomber), then moved on a heavy-haul trailer.
- Grand opening of the display slated for Sept. 28, with a planned "open experience" letting visitors explore inside and sit at the controls.

wikis.title: Frank R. Bowerman Landfill, Orange County, California
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the landfill in the Santa Ana Mountains, opened 1990, and its landfill-gas-to-LNG project.
wikis.body:
- Located in the western Santa Ana Mountains, Orange County, California, between Limestone Canyon Regional Park and State Route 241. Opened in 1990.
- One of the largest landfills in California and the ninth largest in the United States; an estimated 31 million tons of waste.
- Named after Professor Frank R. Bowerman, former director of environmental engineering programs at the University of Southern California; he was also a technical consultant to the film Soylent Green.
- Site of what the article calls the world's first commercial landfill gas to liquid natural gas project, the Bowerman Landfill Project, built by Prometheus Energy (Redmond, Washington) and Montauk Energy.

wikis.title: Manchester Plant (Kellogg's factory, Stretford)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Kellogg's Manchester Plant in Stretford: construction in 1937-38, history, visits, incidents and production figures.
wikis.body:
- Large food factory in Stretford, North West England, making Kellogg's cereals; during WWII the largest food factory in Europe. Completed 1938, inaugurated 24 May 1938 (Empire Day); tenant The Kellogg Company of Great Britain.
- Site chosen for proximity to the Manchester Ship Canal by managing director Harry McEvoy. Construction started 17 June 1937 on the new Barton Dock Estate; built in ten months; cost given as £250,000 at start and £500,000 for the five-floor site at opening; seven acres. Granary stored 500,000 tons; raw materials from the British Empire, white corn from South Africa.
- Opened by a woman from Edwinstowe, Nottinghamshire, chosen in April 1938 from around five thousand applicants.
- By 1960 making 1.25 million boxes a day. Another production site in north Wales opened 28 April 1978. Around 300 redundancies in 1981 due to automation. The 60 ft illuminated K sign switched on 24 November 1981. By the late 1980s the factory was seven times larger, and the second-largest breakfast cereal factory in the world.
- Visits: Prince Philip 14 June 1963; Prince of Wales 22 May 1974; Margaret Thatcher 15 January 1982. Documentaries by Channel 5 (2020), BBC Two (2016), Channel 4 (2015, 2022).
- Incidents: gas explosion 15 July 1950; worker killed 11 August 1955; large fire 22 October 1967 with 150 firemen; 1,400 workers struck in May 1977, back after a ten-week strike on 9 September 1979 with an £8.50 a week rise.
- Production: about 200 tonnes of corn a day from Argentina, ~10 tonnes of Corn Flakes an hour; 150 tonnes of Arborio rice a day from Italy and Spain; a million packets of cereal a day; 21,000 tonnes of Coco Pops a year. December 2005: contract for a 5 MW CHP unit.

wikis.title: Exhibition celebrates Kellogg's Trafford Park legacy (Trafford Council)
wikis.summary: Trafford Council news item on an exhibition at Trafford Local Studies & Archives Centre marking the Kellogg's Trafford Park factory ahead of its closure.
wikis.body:
- Exhibition of nearly 90 years of Kellogg's history in Trafford, at Trafford Local Studies & Archives Centre, Sale; open until August (final date TBC).
- Over 100 items across nine decades, from construction in 1938 to the present: model vans, vintage promotional material, a plaque for King Charles' last visit in 2023, a large Tony the Tiger cut-out, and items from a time capsule unearthed earlier this year.
- Developed with Kellogg's factory colleagues.
- The factory is closing "for the final time later this year"; Kellogg's is moving manufacturing from Trafford to its Wrexham site. The closure is due to the plant's layout, "not suitable for modern manufacturing" with a large amount of redundant space.
- Quotes from plant director Tim McKnight and a council spokesperson: "For nearly 90 years the plant has been a major local employer".

wikis.title: H. J. Heinz factory, Kitt Green, Wigan
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the Heinz plant at Kitt Green, Wigan, opened 21 May 1959 and described as Heinz's largest facility in the world.
wikis.body:
- Food plant at Kitt Green, Orrell, Wigan, Greater Manchester; owned by H. J. Heinz Company; 55 acres (22 ha). One of the largest food processing plants in Europe and Heinz's largest in the world; over one billion cans a year.
- Background: Heinz varieties first sold in Fortnum & Mason in 1886; first UK production facility at Harlesden in the 1920s; a former munitions factory at Standish near Wigan taken over in 1946. Heinz Ltd grew sixfold 1945-1956.
- Site chosen for access to agriculture, water, skilled labour and transport links (Liverpool Docks).
- Opened 21 May 1959 by the Lord Chancellor, Earl of Kilmuir; visited by Queen Elizabeth The Queen Mother on 24 June 1959.
- By the 1980s about 3,000 employees and converted to high-speed automation. Ketchup production moved to Holland after Harlesden closed in 2000. A 140 tonnes/hour steam plant installed 2005.
- 50th anniversary in 2009 with a visit by Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip, who opened a new packaging hall. 2013: listed by Discovery Channel among the world's top five manufacturing units.
- As of 2019: 850 employees; 1.5-3 million cans of Heinz Baked Beans a day; over 1.3 billion cans a year (about 383 thousand tonnes). £113.6 million invested between the 2015 Kraft merger and August 2018, incl. £20 million for filling and packing.
- January 2021: Kraft Heinz began freight-train trials to the Wigan distribution centre to cut carbon footprint.

wikis.title: Heinz factory marks 50 years with visit from the Queen (Reliable Plant)
wikis.summary: 2009 news item on the Queen and Duke of Edinburgh visiting the Heinz Kitt Green factory near Wigan on 21 May to mark its 50th anniversary.
wikis.body:
- The Queen and the Duke of Edinburgh visited the Heinz Beanz factory at Kitt Green near Wigan on May 21 to mark 50 years since its official opening on May 21, 1959.
- The factory makes more than 1 billion cans a year and 1.5 million cans of Heinz Beanz every day; largest food processing plant in Europe and Heinz's largest worldwide.
- They opened and started a new packing operation: a robotic line for automatic handling of "dollies", wheeled sales units that go directly into supermarket aisles, for Heinz Beanz, Cream of Tomato Soup and Heinz Spaghetti. It follows a series of multi-million pound investments in the packaging hall over 10 years (multi-pack unit, shrink wrapping).
- Opened 1959 by the Lord Chancellor, Viscount Kilmuir; Queen Elizabeth The Queen Mother visited June 24, 1959.
- Heinz Europe's Scott O'Hara: the 57 years of the Queen's reign matches Heinz's "57". Heinz also marked 140 years since its first product (grated horseradish, 1869); UK sales began at Fortnum & Mason in 1886.
- The "57 Varieties" slogan: Henry Heinz saw a shoe advert on a New York train in 1896; company now has more than 5,700 products.

wikis.title: Tallest telescopic crane: Liebherr LTM 11200-9.1 (Guinness World Records)
wikis.summary: Guinness World Records entry naming the Liebherr LTM 11200-9.1 as the largest/tallest telescopic crane, with a 100 m boom.
wikis.body:
- Record holder: Liebherr LTM 11200-9.1, dated 2007.
- Maximum boom length 100 metres (328 ft); the boom has eight nested steel tube sections that extend like a mariner's telescope.
- The 100-ton boom is truck-mounted and can lift 1,200 tons.
- Powered by a six-cylinder 240 kW engine, separate from the 500 kW engine driving the 20-metre, nine-axle carrier vehicle.
- Page notes that records change daily and comments may relate to previous holders.

wikis.title: Liebherr LTM 11200-9.1 mobile crane product page
wikis.summary: Liebherr product page for the nine-axle LTM 11200-9.1 all-terrain crane with specifications.
wikis.body:
- Described as combining the maximum lifting capacity of a Liebherr all-terrain crane with the longest telescopic boom in the world; lattice extensions are available.
- 9-axle chassis with active, speed-dependent rear-axle steering; Y-guying on the telescopic boom significantly increases lifting capacities.
- Described as ideal for erecting wind turbines, with setup times significantly shorter than lattice boom cranes.
- Specs: max load 1,200 t (at radius 2.50 m); telescopic boom 18.30 m up to 100 m; max hoist height 188 m; max radius 136.0 m; lattice jib 6.50 m up to 126.00 m; 9 axles, drive 18 x 8 x 18; driving speed 75 km/h; total ballast 202 t.
- Engines: drive engine 8-cylinder diesel, 505 kW; crane engine 6-cylinder diesel, 300 kW. HVO fuel option shown.

wikis.title: Symphony of the Seas (Royal Caribbean Oasis-class cruise ship)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Royal Caribbean's Symphony of the Seas, the fourth Oasis-class ship and the world's largest cruise ship from March 2018 to January 2022.
wikis.body:
- Oasis-class ship owned and operated by Royal Caribbean International; built by Chantiers de l'Atlantique, Saint-Nazaire, France; ordered 9 May 2014; cost US$1.35 billion (2016); registered Nassau, Bahamas; home port PortMiami.
- Keel laid 29 October 2015; floated out 9 June 2017; sea trials 15-18 February 2018; delivered/completed 23 March 2018; first passenger cruise 31 March 2018; maiden voyage 7 April 2018 (week-long Mediterranean); moved to PortMiami in November 2018 (arrived 9 November). Christened in Miami in November 2018; sponsors ("Godfamily") Alexa Vega, Carlos Pena Jr. and their 23-month-old son Ocean, the first family ship sponsor in the industry.
- World's largest cruise ship March 2018-January 2022: 228,081 GT, surpassing Harmony of the Seas and later surpassed by Wonder of the Seas in 2022.
- Specs: length 361.8 m (infobox; text also says 361.011 m); beam 47.448 m waterline, 66 m max; height 72.5 m; draught 9.322 m; 18 decks (16 for guests); 5,518 passengers double occupancy, 6,680 max; crew 2,200; 22 restaurants, 4 pools, 2,759 cabins; cruising speed 22 knots. About 30 m longer than Nimitz-class carriers.
- Power: three Wärtsilä 16V46D and three 12V46D diesel sets; three 20 MW ABB Azipods; four 5.5 MW bow thrusters. Design needs 85 MW versus the 100 MW normal for Oasis-class; LED/fluorescent lighting, a 2 MW steam turbine for waste heat, and an air-bubble hull lubrication system.
- Facilities: children's water park, basketball court, ice-skating rink, a 10-deck zip line, 1,400-seat theater, aquatic theater, two 43-foot rock-climbing walls, a park with over 20,000 tropical plants.
- COVID-19: services suspended in 2020; a 27-year-old housekeeping crew member evacuated March 2020 died in April 2020; family sued. Channel 4's Billion Pound Cruise (2020) filmed on board.
- Incidents: Jan 2019 guest jumped overboard in Nassau as a stunt, survived and banned; Aug 2019 an Australian passenger died after going overboard; Oct 29, 2023 a passenger overboard was rescued.

wikis.title: 30-metre lengthening for TT-Line's PETER PAN (Shippax)
wikis.summary: Short Shippax teaser (paywalled) saying TT-Line's PETER PAN will be lengthened by close to 30 metres at German Dry Docks in Bremerhaven in early 2018.
wikis.body:
- In early 2018 TT-Line will send its 2001-built PETER PAN to German Dry Docks in Bremerhaven for a close to 30-metre lengthening, increasing cargo intake by almost 25%.
- The ship will be cut in two just in front of the twin scrubber-equipped funnels.
- Published 5 Oct 2017. The rest of the article is behind a login.

wikis.title: TT-Line to have its ro-pax PETER PAN lengthened (Ferry Shipping News)
wikis.summary: Brief news item: TT-Line will lengthen ro-pax PETER PAN by 30 m at German Drydocks in Bremerhaven in early 2018, with a new bow.
wikis.body:
- TT-Line, operating ferries between Sweden, Germany and Poland, decided to lengthen PETER PAN by 30 m.
- In early 2018 the ro-pax goes to Bremerhaven where German Drydocks will do the work; the vessel also gets a new bow with improved fuel consumption characteristics.
- The process will take two months.

wikis.title: ORBIS Flying Eye Hospital three-week program in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia (2011)
wikis.summary: ORBIS press release on its June 19 - July 7, 2011 skills-exchange program aboard the DC-10 Flying Eye Hospital in Ulaanbaatar, supported by Alcon.
wikis.body:
- ORBIS and volunteer eye care specialists completed a three-week program in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia (June 19 - July 7, 2011) aboard the Flying Eye Hospital, a DC-10 aircraft. Supported by Alcon Inc. Release dated July 5, 2011.
- Sixth ORBIS Flying Eye Hospital mission in Mongolia. Invited by the Mongolian Ophthalmic Association; hosted by "Hospital Number One" and the "Mother and Child Hospital".
- Blindness context (WHO): North-East Asia prevalence estimated at 1.4%; adult cataract and glaucoma together more than two-thirds of the country's blindness; cornea conditions 7.2% of adult blindness.
- Training covered ophthalmologists, biomedical engineers, anesthesiologists and nurses: pediatric cataract and strabismus, glaucoma, cornea, medical retina, phacoemulsification cataract surgery, ocular oncology. Skills transferred to more than 300 local eye care professionals via hands-on surgical training, live demonstrations, lectures and workshops. Alcon engineers volunteered to help maintain ophthalmic equipment.
- Alcon has partnered with ORBIS for more than 30 years and is a global sponsor. Quotes from Sara Woodward (Alcon) and Barbara A. DeBuono, MD, MPH (ORBIS President and CEO).
- WHO figures cited: more than 39 million blind people worldwide, 90% in the developing world; about 80% of blindness could be prevented or cured.

wikis.title: Inside the Orbis Flying Eye Hospital MD-10 (Key.Aero teaser)
wikis.summary: Paywalled Key.Aero feature teaser on Orbis's third-generation Flying Eye Hospital, a former FedEx MD-10, returning to service after COVID-19.
wikis.body:
- Orbis International is poised to return its third-generation Flying Eye Hospital to the skies, in a former FedEx MD-10 combining flight and sight operations.
- Since 1982 the non-profit has fought preventable blindness using a trio of McDonnell Douglas types. COVID-19 halted the flying schedule and replaced field operations with virtual training; the New York-headquartered organisation was "cautiously optimistic" of soon resuming in-person work "from South America in the west to Indonesia in the east".
- The current MD-10 (N330AU) is an operating theatre and teaching hospital, served by paid staff and a network of 400 volunteers within a faculty, training eye surgeons worldwide; it teaches local ophthalmologists the latest techniques rather than just visiting and operating.
- Rest of the article is subscriber-only. Originally published in Aviation News Magazine.

wikis.title: Santa Maria della Salute, Venice
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the Baroque plague church at the Punta della Dogana in Venice: its 1630 vow, design by Longhena, art and influence.
wikis.body:
- Roman Catholic church and minor basilica at the Punta della Dogana, Dorsoduro, Venice, between the Grand Canal and the Giudecca Canal. Parish of the Gesuati; "the most recent of the so-called plague churches".
- Infobox: consecrated 1681; groundbreaking 1631; completed 1687; architect Baldassare Longhena; Baroque; length 70 m (230 ft), width 47 m (154 ft); Istrian stone and marmorino; Archdiocese of Venice.
## History
- Summer 1630: plague hit Venice and until 1631 "killed nearly a third of the population": 46,000 in the city, some 94,000 in the lagoons.
- Prayers and processions had failed; on October 22, 1630 the Venetian Senate decreed a new church, dedicated to the Virgin Mary, echoing Palladio's Redentore after the 1575-76 plague.
- Site chosen from eight candidates; the Somascan Fathers were invited to administer it.
- Design competition: 11 submissions, two reached the final round. Longhena (26 years old) won; the Senate voted 66 in favor, 29 against, two abstentions. He described a rotunda "in the shape of a crown". Completed 1681, the year before his death.
- A yearly Senate visit was decided. On November 21, the Feast of the Presentation of the Virgin (Festa della Madonna della Salute), officials parade from San Marco, crossing the Grand Canal on a pontoon bridge; "still a major event in Venice".
- The end of the plague was attributed to an icon of the Virgin brought to Venice in 1670 by Francesco Morosini from Candia.
## Building and art
- Vast octagonal building with two domes and two bell towers, on a platform of 1,000,000 wooden piles. Statue of the Virgin atop the pediment; facade figures include St George, St Theodore, the Evangelists, Prophets, Judith.
- Interior octagonal with eight radiating chapels; Marian symbolism (dome = her crown, eight sides = eight points of her star).
- Altars: Luca Giordano scenes; Titian's The Descent of the Holy Spirit; high altar by Longhena with a 12th/13th-century Byzantine Madonna and Child (Panagia Mesopantitissa) from Candia in 1669; statuary The Queen of Heaven expelling the Plague (1670) by Josse de Corte.
- Sacristy: Tintoretto's Marriage at Cana (1561) and several Titian works.
## Influence
- Dome emblematic of the skyline; depicted by Canaletto, Turner, Monet, Sargent, Guardi. Modeled on it: shrine in Gostyn (1675-1728), Rotunda of Xewkija in Gozo, Malta, Basilica on the Holy Mountain, Glogowko. Coordinates 45.43083 N, 12.33444 E.

wikis.title: Santa Maria della Salute and the Festa della Madonna della Salute
wikis.summary: Blog post by a Venice local on the 1630 plague origins of the Salute church and how the November 21 holiday is celebrated today.
wikis.body:
- Post dated November 25, 2019 (also shows June 6, 2021), by "allaboutvenice".
- Church on the south side of the entrance to the Grand Canal near Punta della Dogana, central to the Festa della Madonna della Salute on the 21st of November.
## Origins
- Bubonic plague returned in A.D. 1630; the author says it came from inland: Mantua ambassadors were quarantined on San Servolo but Venetian officials still met them.
- Within a month the streets were "practically covered with dead bodies"; the Doge and the Patriarch died.
- Autumn 1630: three days and three nights of procession to the Virgin; the disease then slowed. Doge Nicolo Contarini vowed a church (as with the Redentore); he died in April 1631.
- Building took some 50 years; consecrated 21 November 1687 (per the post). A temporary bridge is built from San Marco to Dorsoduro each year, like the Redentore bridge to Giudecca.
- Author's view: the plague likely slowed naturally (immunity, winter fleas); it was over in November 1631 with a little less than 50,000 dead, one-third of the population.
## The holiday today
- April 25 is both Liberation Day and St Mark's day, so by law Venice chose the Festa della Salute as its local holiday instead; schools and jobs are free.
- Candle stands outside; visitors light a candle for the Virgin. Street food, sweets, chocolate, cotton candy, mulled wine, street artists, balloons.
- Late November is low season; many come from Mestre, Marghera, Rovigo, Conegliano, Pordenone. No fireworks or regatta unlike the Redentore: "an ordinary village feast in Venice".

wikis.title: How the Mack Rides Rocking Boat works (Mission Bermudes, Futuroscope)
wikis.summary: Coaster101 article dated Jun 16, 2025 explaining the first Mack Rides Rocking Boat ride, Mission Bermudes at Futuroscope.
wikis.body:
- By Nick Weisenberger, Jun 16, 2025. French theme park Futuroscope "is set to debut one of the most innovative rides of the year": the first Mack Rides Rocking Boat.
- The boat floats freely like a real boat while also negotiating large roller-coaster drops.
- The first video revealing the concept was posted five years earlier.
- Per the patent, a flexible connection system links the floating boat to an undercarriage chassis: pivoting arms let the boat sway and rock, while it follows the guide rail underneath. The coaster track runs the entire ride, so boat position is always controlled and it cannot capsize.
- A drive system (the author assumes LSMs) moves the chassis forwards and backwards; track switches change direction.
- The track can be completely hidden underwater, making the layout unpredictable; it briefly emerges before submerging again.
- "Mission Bermudes officially opens on June 28th." The author speculates the system would suit a Creature From The Black Lagoon or JAWS ride.

wikis.title: Futuroscope Mission Bermudes announcement
wikis.summary: Lift Hills and Thrills news post saying the Mack Rides Rocking Boat ride Mission Bermudes was set for a mid 2025 opening.
wikis.body:
- Headline: "Futuroscope Mission Bermudes Set for Mid 2025 Opening" (posted "2 years ago" relative to capture).
- A new Mack Rides boat ride; prototype system named the Rocking Boat, giving a controlled rocking motion that can handle tight turns, sudden movements and steep climbs, combining a water ride with coaster thrills.
- 10 people sit in each boat. The experience lasts 10 minutes, starting peaceful then more intense, combining indoor and outdoor scenes; construction images suggest rocky terrain and jungle scenes.
- Includes steep slopes, a vertical lift and a 15 metre plunge.
- Family-friendly; minimum height 1.1 metres.
- Described as the world's first rocking boat attraction from Mack Rides.

wikis.title: Carr's (British biscuit and cracker maker)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Carr's of Carlisle: founded 1831, ownership changes, royal warrant loss and factory floods.
wikis.body:
- British biscuit and cracker maker headquartered in Carlisle; founded 1831 by Jonathan Dodgson Carr; currently owned by Pladis Global through United Biscuits; marketed in the US by Kellogg's.
- 1831: small bakery and biscuit factory in Carlisle, Cumberland; royal warrant in 1841. Within 15 years "it had become Britain's largest baking business".
- Both mill and bakery (vertical integration); bread by night, biscuits by day; biscuits loosely based on dry ship biscuits, kept crisp in tins and shipped by canal and railway.
- Carr protested against the Corn Laws. Carr died 1884; by 1885 the firm made 128 varieties of biscuit with 1000 workers.
- 1894 registered as Carr and Co. Ltd.; private again in 1908. Carrs Flour Mills Limited incorporated on acquiring the flour-milling assets.
- Part of Cavenham Foods 1964-1972, then sold to United Biscuits (with Wright's Biscuits and Kemps) for $10 million. United Biscuits sold to Turkish-based Yildiz Holding in 2014; in 2016 all UB brands combined with Yildiz's snack brands to form pladis.
- Since 1972 the factory is part of United Biscuits; officially McVitie's, "still known locally as Carr's". Carr's Group PLC (flour, agriculture, light engineering) sold its flour-milling division to Whitworths Holdings Ltd in 2016.
- March 2012: Carr's Table Water Biscuits lost its royal warrant due to "changing tastes"; Carr's licensed the City of Carlisle coat of arms for packaging instead.
- Floods at the Caldewgate factory: 2005 (two months' production lost; £1 million government grant); 6 December 2015 (levels above five feet), damaged brick ovens, causing shortages; works closed for a month and production resumed gradually in spring 2016.
- Family member Capt. Richard Carr MBE was decorated for escape attempts from Italian and German POW camps in WWII.

wikis.title: Oshkosh Truck Corporation 10-K for fiscal 2003: business overview
wikis.summary: Opening part of Oshkosh Truck Corporation's annual report for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2003, describing the company, its acquisitions, contracts and strengths.
wikis.body:
- Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2003 (commission file 1-31371); Oshkosh Truck Corporation, Wisconsin, P.O. Box 2566, Oshkosh, WI; common stock on the NYSE. Forward-looking statements speak as of November 26, 2003.
- Share splits adjusted: two-for-one on August 13, 2003 and three-for-two on August 19, 1999.
## The company
- "A leading designer, manufacturer and marketer of a broad range of specialty commercial, fire and emergency and military trucks" under the Oshkosh and Pierce trademarks; truck bodies under McNeilus, MTM, Revolution, Medtec, Geesink and Norba; compactors under Geesink Kiggen.
- Oshkosh began business in 1917, an early pioneer of four-wheel drive. In 1981 it won the first HEMTT contract from the US Department of Defense.
- Since a 1996 strategic initiative, sales rose from $413 million (fiscal 1996) to $1,926 million (fiscal 2003); earnings per share from a loss of $.01 to $2.16.
- Acquisitions: Pierce (fire trucks), September 1996; Nova Quintech, December 1997; McNeilus (concrete mixers, refuse bodies), February 1998; Kewaunee, November 1999; Viking, April 2000; Medtec (ambulances), October 2000; certain TEMCO assets, March 2001; Geesink Norba Group (European refuse bodies), July 2001.
- Customer financing via Oshkosh Capital and the Oshkosh/McNeilus Financial Services Partnership.
## Defense
- MTVR contract for the U.S. Marine Corps awarded December 1998: expected total sales up to $1.1 billion from fiscal 2000 through fiscal 2005; fiscal 2004 sales expected about $167 million.
- First contract outside the US: wheeled tankers for the U.K. Ministry of Defence valued at about 145 million British Sterling ($241 million) over three years from fiscal 2005.
## Strengths and strategy
- Strong market positions, extensive distribution, flexible manufacturing, diversified products, quality (ISO 9001; Pierce certified to ISO 9001:2000 in August 2002, McNeilus in July 2003), and proprietary components (ALL-STEER, TAK-4, Sky-Arm, Hercules and Husky foam, Command Zone, Auto Reach arm, SmartPak, ProPulse hybrid drive). Exclusive license for the Revolution composite concrete mixer drum in the Americas.
- Stated risk factors include the launch of the Revolution drum, defense truck procurement outcomes, cyclical commercial and fire markets, and government spending. (This page is part 1 of 5 of the filing; later parts not summarized.)

wikis.title: Pierce Manufacturing timeline, 1913-2026
wikis.summary: Company history timeline of Pierce Manufacturing (Appleton, WI): founding in 1913, fire apparatus products, ownership by Oshkosh, and milestones to 2026.
wikis.body:
## Founding and growth
- 1913: founded as Auto Body Works by Humphrey and Dudley Pierce in Appleton, WI, in a converted church. 1917: incorporated; built truck bodies on Model T Ford chassis; 11 employees by year end.
- 1920: Dudley H. Pierce became president. 1927: Eugene L. Pierce joined; entered specialized utility bodies. 1939: first fire trucks (pumper on Ford chassis).
- After WWII: own line of fire apparatus. c.1950: products branded Pierce. 1954: Eugene became president. 1956-57: Darley mid-ship pumps allowed sales beyond home region.
- 1958-59: the Snorkel (articulating boom and platform) contracted with Pitman Manufacturing's Art Moore; first Snorkel built 1959 for Elwood, Indiana; discontinued 1997.
- 1960: Doug Ogilvie president; renamed Pierce Auto Body Works, Inc.; sales topped $1 million; van and beverage bodies dropped. 1969: renamed Pierce Manufacturing, Inc.
- 1970-71: new 62,000 sq ft Highway 41 facility in Appleton. 1975: first export order, Saudi Arabia, 700 large rescue trucks, trailers and Snorkels; one of the top three fire apparatus makers.
- 1988: 75th anniversary; utility vehicles discontinued to focus on fire apparatus. 1989: Ogilvie retired after 41 years.
- 1996: became a subsidiary of Oshkosh Truck Corporation. 1998: first and only single-source custom fire apparatus maker with ISO 9001 certification.
## Products and firsts
- 1979: Pierce Arrow, first custom cab-forward all-aluminum cab. 1982: ground-up Arrow production (chassis, cab, body); Arrow production ended in 2023. 1984 Dash (first custom tilt cab); 1985 Lance split-tilt cab (ten seats); 1992 Saber; 1995 Quantum (in production until 2023); 1999 T-300 with Kenworth; 2000 Enforcer and 10,000th custom fire truck.
- 2001: TAK-4 independent front suspension. 2003: side roll protection with IMMI. 2006: PS6 seat, Velocity chassis with frontal airbags. 2007: first electronic stability control in the fire industry; PUC (Pierce Ultimate Configuration). 2011: Dash CF (discontinued 2016).
- 2015: Ascendant 107' steel ladder; 2017 Ascendant class of aerials (five configurations); 2019 Ultra Highrise Pumper pumping up to 420 meters (1,378 feet); 2021 PACCAR MX-13 engine (up to 510 hp).
- 2021: Pierce Volterra electric platform, "the first electric fire truck in service in North America" with a patented parallel-electric drivetrain.
## Later milestones
- 2010: first fire apparatus sale in China (Nanjing, Jiangsu Province Fire Bureau); by 2011 over 100 Pierce and Oshkosh airport vehicles sold in China.
- 2012: 27,023 custom chassis and 51,600 trucks built. 2013: 100th anniversary open house drew over 12,000 people; Wisconsin governor declared July 13, 2013 "Pierce Manufacturing Day"; first 9-11 Memorial Stair Climb at Lambeau Field (July 14, 2013, 561 participants, 343 firefighters honored).
- 2017: CARE carcinogen awareness partnership with the Firefighter Cancer Support Network. 2021: ownership interest in Boise Mobile Equipment. 2022: Oshkosh acquired Maxi-Metal Inc. (Quebec).
- 2025: over 500,000 square feet added across Wisconsin, Florida and Tennessee. Presidents: Jim Johnson 2010-2023; Bob Schulz 2023-2025; Marty Bass 2026-present.

wikis.title: Edda Freya construction vessel launched at Kleven
wikis.summary: Offshore Energy news item dated August 17, 2015 on the launch of Ostensjo Rederi's 150 m cable-laying and construction vessel Edda Freya.
wikis.body:
- Edda Freya, Ostensjo Rederi's new offshore construction vessel, was launched on Saturday, August 15 (2015) at the Kleven yard in Norway.
- 150 m long, designed for cable laying, offshore construction and IMR operations; SALT 304 design; 149.8 m long, 27 m wide, 2,300 m2 total deck space.
- To work for Deep Ocean after outfitting and delivery in February 2016, offshore Norway on a project with Statoil and Wintershall.
- Siemens BlueDrive PlusC propulsion control (fuel saving) and DP3 positioning; Greater North Sea market.
- Mission equipment: 150T dual tensioner vertical lay system, 3000 ton carousel below deck; 600 ton active heave compensated knuckle boom main crane with extended reach; accommodation for 140 persons.

wikis.title: Edda Freya vessel (DeepOcean)
wikis.summary: DeepOcean vessel page describing the diesel-electric hybrid construction vessel Edda Freya and its specification.
wikis.body:
- Edda Freya is described as "a state of the art construction vessel" with an environmentally friendly, fuel-saving diesel-electric hybrid propulsion system, designed for cable laying, offshore construction and IMR, with redundancy, maneuverability and station keeping.
- 2,300 m2 deck space; 400 T AHC offshore crane lifting 600 T in double-fall mode; 70 T AHC crane that can be moved to a secondary position; Huisman 15 T dual tensioner VLS over the main moonpool; quick reel mobilisation; skidding system for modules; two moonpool launch and recovery systems for WROVs; 3000 T carousel below deck.
- Siemens BlueDrive PlusC (with Ostensjo Rederi): variable rotational speed, optimal generator operation plus battery system to reduce fuel, NOx, CO2 and methane; selective catalytic reduction further reduces emissions.
- Specification sheet: battery hybrid vessel, DP3, ROV system ready for remote operations, 2,300 m2 deck, 400/600 Te AHC crane, 70 Te AHC crane, 150 Te VLS, 3,000 Te carousel, 2 WROVs in hangar, Siemens BlueDrive PlusC reducing yearly fuel consumption by 15 - 20%, accommodation for 140 persons, helideck.

wikis.title: Siam Park (Tenerife) water park
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Siam Park, the Thai-themed water park in Costa Adeje, Tenerife: history, rides, technical details and awards.
wikis.body:
- Water park in Costa Adeje, Tenerife, Canary Islands; Siamese (Thai) theme; opened by the Princess of Thailand Maha Chakri Sirindhorn. Principal owner Loro Parque (Wolfgang Kiessling and son Christoph). A second park is planned for Gran Canaria. Area 18.5 ha.
- Construction began 2004, cost 52 million euros (US$58.7 million). Originally to open in May 2007 but delayed; opened September 15, 2008. 25 Thai-themed buildings, "the largest collection of Thai-themed buildings outside Thailand".
- Rides (ProSlide unless noted): Vulcano (BehemothBowl 60), The Dragon (Tornado 60, 20 m funnel), Wave Palace (Murphys Waves; 3.3 m waves, "the highest of any wave pool in the World"), Naga Racer, The Giant, Tower of Power, Mai Thai River ("world's longest lazy river", 8 m elevation), Jungle Snakes, Lost City, Mekong Rapids, Kinnaree (2012, 200 m), Singha (2015, 18 m/s), Patong Rapids (2018), Coco Beach Wave Pool (Nov 2018), Saifa (2023 dual race water coaster).
- Built on a hill so slides follow terrain; water heated to 25 C (77 F); desalination plant on site desalinates 700 cubic meters of sea water per day; used water recycled for plants; first natural gas plant in the Canary Islands.
- Awards: Tripadvisor Travellers' Choice World's Best Waterpark 2014-2022; World's Best Amusement Park 2023.

wikis.title: Boeing delivers first 747-8 Freighter to Cargolux
wikis.summary: Boeing press release of Oct 12, 2011 on the delivery of the first 747-8 Freighter to launch customer Cargolux.
wikis.body:
- EVERETT, Wash., Oct. 12, 2011: Cargolux took delivery of the first Boeing 747-8 Freighter at the Everett delivery center; the plane then flew to Seattle-Tacoma International Airport to load cargo for its first revenue flight to Luxembourg.
- Initial orders announced in November 2005 by Boeing, Cargolux and Nippon Cargo Airlines. Delivery came nearly 18 years after Cargolux received the first 747-400 Freighter.
- Quotes: Jim Albaugh (Boeing Commercial Airplanes): "Queen of the Skies for the 21st Century". Frank Reimen (Cargolux CEO) and Elizabeth Lund (747 program) also quoted.
- Cargolux ordered 13 747-8 Freighters in total: a 10-airplane launch order in 2005 and three more in 2007. Eight customers have ordered 75 in total.
- Specs: double-digit improvements in fuel burn, operating cost and emissions; 16 percent more revenue cargo volume (seven additional pallets); maximum structural payload 147.6 tons (133.9 metric tonnes); nose-door loading; 10-foot (3-m) high pallets; 9.9 pounds per cubic foot (159 kg/m3) density; interlining with the 777 Freighter.
- GEnx-2B67 engines with composite fan case and blades.

wikis.title: First 747-8F delivery to Cargolux, 11 years on
wikis.summary: Simple Flying article (Oct 12, 2022) recalling the Oct 12, 2011 delivery of the first Boeing 747-8F to Cargolux and the type's background.
wikis.body:
- Published Oct 12, 2022 by Mark Finlay. On October 12, 2011 Boeing handed over the first 747-8F to Luxembourg-based Cargolux.
- The delivery ended a month-long disagreement over the order: Cargolux was unhappy with the performance of the General Electric GEnx-2B engines. CEO Frank Reiman (as quoted by Flight Global): "I am pleased that we have reached an agreement on the contractual issues."
- Cargolux: founded in Luxembourg in 1970 by Luxair, Loftleidir and Salen Shipping Group; began with a Canadair CL-44; ordered Boeing 747s in 1978 (first in 1979). September 2011: Qatar Airways bought a 35% stake (Luxair had 43.4%), later sold to the Government of Luxembourg then a Chinese investment company. Fleet per ch-aviation: 6 747-400ERFs, 9 747-400FSCDs, 14 747-8Fs.
- 747-8: introduced November 14, 2005, forecast production run of 300; freighter first flew February 8, 2010; passenger version March 20, 2011. World's longest airliner (250 feet) until the 777X in 2020. 747-8F carries 308,000 pounds 4,120 nautical miles; passenger version 467 passengers 7,790 nautical miles.
- As of May 2022 orders: 107 747-8Fs and 48 passenger versions. Last 747-8 due to Atlas Air before end of 2022, ending 747 assembly.

wikis.title: Mall of America: overview, planning, opening and ownership dispute
wikis.summary: First part of the Wikipedia article on Mall of America in Bloomington, Minnesota: size, development, 1992 opening, the Triple Five v. Simon lawsuit and early-2000s changes.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Super-regional mall and entertainment complex in Bloomington, Minnesota; opened August 1992 on the former Metropolitan Stadium site; "the largest mall in the United States", largest in the Western Hemisphere and 12th largest in the world.
- Developed by Triple Five Group (Ghermezian family) with Melvin Simon & Associates and TIAA-CREF. As of September 2025, about 32 million visit annually, 80% from Minnesota, Wisconsin, Iowa, Nebraska, the Dakotas, Illinois and Ohio.
- Gross floor area 5,689,000 sq ft (528,500 m2), 129 acres; gross leasable area 2,869,000 sq ft. More than 520 stores on three levels (fourth on south and east), four anchor department stores, four zones. Common areas are unheated; heat comes from skylights, lighting and people.
## Planning and construction (1982-1992)
- Metropolitan Stadium demolished January 1985 (78 acres). Triple Five proposed the Minnesota International Center (scrapped), selected in 1986; the revised plan had over 400 stores and an indoor theme park (Fantasyworld, later Knott's Camp Snoopy). Approved 1987.
- Architects: Jerde Partnership, KKE Architects, HGA. Groundbreaking June 14, 1989; cost about $650 million; Bloomington invested over $100 million in infrastructure.
## Opening and 1990s
- Grand opening August 11, 1992 with 330 stores and 10,000 employees; anchors Nordstrom, Macy's, Bloomingdale's, Sears; first Lego Store; at least 150,000 visitors at opening. The Theatres at Mall of America opened August 14, 1992 with 14 screens.
- 42 million annual visitors by 1997 (per article). Underwater World aquarium opened 1996, bankrupt 1998, became Underwater Adventures in 2000.
## Ownership lawsuit
- January 1999: Simon acquired TIAA's 27.5% stake without notifying Triple Five; Triple Five sued October 29, 1999. September 2003 ruling by Judge Paul A. Magnuson for the Ghermezians ("worst kind of self-dealing and subterfuge"); Simon forced to sell its stake at $81.4 million. November 3, 2006: Ghermezians gained full control by spending $1 billion for Simon's remaining shares.
## 2000s
- 10th anniversary August 2002, about 40 million visitors annually; IKEA opened August 2004; smoking banned 2004; fourth floor largely vacant by 2005 after Fat Tuesday, Gators, Planet Hollywood (left 2003) and Jillian's (closed August 2005). January 9, 2006: talks with Cedar Fair over the Peanuts branding broke down.

wikis.title: MV Tonsberg ro-ro ship
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on MV Tonsberg, a Wilh. Wilhelmsen ro-ro ship that was the world's largest when built, with specifications and history.
wikis.body:
- Roll-on/roll-off ship owned by Wilh. Wilhelmsen; "when built, it was the largest RORO ship in the world". Builder Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Nagasaki, Japan; launched 2 October 2010; IMO 9515383; Malta flag.
- Size: 265 m (869 ft) overall, 32.26 m wide, 11 m draught, 46 m air draught; 76,500 gt (infobox 75,251 GT, 41,820 DWT). Capacity 5,990 cars, 5-7% higher than Mark IV ro-ro ships.
- Decks: six fixed and three hoistable (4B, 6, 8); main deck loads up to 7.1 m high; total deck space 50,335 m2, cargo volume 138,000 m3; stern ramp 12 m wide, 505 tonnes.
- Design: improved hull uses 15-20% less fuel per unit of cargo; double bottom.
- Propulsion: 7-cylinder MAN B&W engine derated from 22,890 kW to 20,100 kW MCR at 108 rpm (normal in service 18,090 kW), 7.3 m six-bladed propeller, two 2,500 kW Kawasaki thrusters; service speed 20.25 knots.
- History: fourth Wilhelmsen ship named Tonsberg (Wilhelmsen founded in Tonsberg in 1861); built as the 150th anniversary of the line coincided; first of four "Mark V" ships built 2010-2011; second, Parsifal, delivered September 2011.
- June 2012: awarded "Ship of the Year 2011" by the Japan Society of Naval Architects and Ocean Engineers.

wikis.title: HDMS Absalon (F341) Danish frigate
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the Royal Danish Navy's Absalon, its specifications, and its service including Somali counter-piracy operations.
wikis.body:
- Lead ship of the two-ship Absalon class (sister Esbern Snare) of the Royal Danish Navy; ordered November 2001, built by Odense Staalskibsvaerft, laid down 28 November 2003, launched 25 February 2004, commissioned 19 October 2004; full operational status 2007; home port Frederikshavn.
- Originally pennant L16, a "flexible support ship"; reclassified as an ASW frigate in October 2020.
- Specs: 6,300 tonnes, 137.6 m long, 19.5 m beam, 6.3 m draft; 2 x MTU 8000 M70 diesels (22,300 bhp); 24 knots; range 9,000 nmi at 15 kn; complement 169; large ro-ro deck; aft helicopter deck with 2 x EH-101 or Westland Lynx.
- Armament includes a 127 mm Mk 45 gun, VLS for up to 36 ESSM/Sea Sparrow, 8-16 Harpoon Block II, two 35 mm Millennium CIWS, MU90 torpedoes, Stingers.
- Counter-piracy from 2008 as flagship of the Danish Task Group leading Task Force 150: September 2008 capture of 10 pirates (later freed); 3 December 2008 rescued a skiff in the Gulf of Aden; reportedly capturing 88 of the 250 pirates detained; 16 March 2009 with TCG Giresun prevented capture of MV Diamond Falcon; mission ended 1 April 2009 with over 80 captured.
- 5 February 2010 helped rescue crew of Ariella; 1 March 2010 reportedly sank a pirate mother ship; 7 January 2012 boarded a mother ship freeing 14 Iranian and Pakistani fishermen.
- 30 November 2015: to be moved to the Mediterranean at Turkey's NATO request. 7-13 May 2022: Exercise Mjolner 2022 in the Arctic. Featured on the Mighty Ships TV programme.

wikis.title: Pirelli P Zero: 40 years of records and innovation
wikis.summary: Pirelli article on the P Zero tyre's 1985 debut on the Lancia Delta S4 Stradale, its design idea, notable cars and recent developments.
wikis.body:
- Article (page date 04/02/2025 as shown) says the P Zero turns 40; first appeared in 1985 on the Lancia Delta S4 Stradale, an evolution of Pirelli's Lancia Delta S4 Group B experience.
- It began the Ultra High Performance (UHP) tyre category. Across four generations it has "over 3.000 homologations" from car makers.
- Anecdote: Miki Biasion's Delta S4 at the Sanremo rally used P Zero road tyres for transfers, kept them on a slippery rain-hit stage and won ahead of competitors on racing tyres.
- Design idea (engineer Mario Mezzanotte, building on the 1976 P7, first low-profile tyre): three "souls" in one tread - inner shoulder grooved like wet racing tyres, outer shoulder like slicks, central section like intermediates.
- Name: "P" for Pirelli plus "Zero" for a new beginning. The first generation equipped the Ferrari F40 (1987); other cars listed include Ferrari 512 Testarossa and LaFerrari, Lamborghini Countach/Diablo/Murcielago/Aventador, McLaren MP4-12C and P1, Pagani Zonda/Huayra/Utopia, Aston Martin, Porsche 911/Cayenne/Macan.
- 2019: the Elect package for EV and plug-in hybrids debuted on a P Zero. 2023: P Zero E, the first UHP tyre with at least 55% biological or recycled materials and a "triple A" European label rating.
- Range is split into variants by vehicle, use and season (summer, winter, all season); marked the start of Pirelli's "Perfect Fit" strategy.

wikis.title: Ford Germany (Ford-Werke GmbH)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Ford's German subsidiary: Berlin and Cologne origins, WWII forced labour, later model range and German sales.
wikis.body:
- Ford-Werke GmbH, headquartered in Cologne; fully owned subsidiary of Ford Motor Company; two plants (Cologne and Saarlouis); founded August 18, 1925 by Henry Ford; 28,842 employees (2009).
## History
- 1912 parts operation in Hamburg; Ford Motor Company AG entered in the Berlin register on 18 August 1925. First German-assembled Model T on 1 April 1926 in Berlin's Westhafen; 1,177 Model Ts in 1926, 2,594 in 1927; Model A assembly from 20 August 1928.
- After GM bought 80% of Opel in March 1929, Ford decided on a full factory in Cologne (170,000 m2 site, beside the Rhine, made available by mayor Konrad Adenauer). Foundation stone 2 October 1930; cost 12 million marks; Berlin assembly ended 15 April 1931; first Cologne Ford (a Model A truck) on 4 May 1931.
- Models: Ford Koln (1933, 2,453 built), Rheinland, Eifel (61,495 built 1935-1940), Taunus from 1939. Ford became Germany's fourth-largest automaker in 1938.
- Renamed Ford-Werke in 1939. In WWII built trucks, Maultier half-tracks and V-2 rocket turbines; production restarted May 1945; US government paid $1.1 million for bomb damage. Car production restarted late 1948 with the Taunus.
- 1965 Transit and 1968 Escort mark European integration; Ford Europe created 1967.
## Forced labour
- Ford-Werke used slave laborers in WWII, "although not required to do so by the Nazi regime". Elsa Iwanowa filed a class action on March 4, 1998; dismissed 1999. Ford's December 2001 study said US headquarters had no control; in March 2000 Ford agreed to contribute $13 million to the restitution fund.
## Other
- October 2004: Aston Martin engine plant (12,500 m2, up to 5,000 engines a year) inside the Niehl plant. Tagline "Eine Idee weiter".
- German sales: 2012 206,128 units (6.70%); 2011 230,939 (7.31%); 2010 198,156 (6.79%); 2009 290,620 (7.63%). Current range (January 2026): Kuga, Puma, Explorer EV, Mustang Mach-E, Mustang, Tourneo Connect, Transit, Ranger.

wikis.title: Albvorland Tunnel breakthrough by TBM WANDA
wikis.summary: Implenia press release on 29 October 2019 marking the southern-tube breakthrough of the Albvorland Tunnel on the Stuttgart-Ulm line.
wikis.body:
- Wendlingen am Neckar (DE), 29 October 2019: Implenia, commissioned by Deutsche Bahn, is building the 8-kilometre Albvorland Tunnel, a key section of the new 60-kilometre railway line between Stuttgart and Ulm.
- Tunnel boring machine (TBM) WANDA broke through in the southern tube, ending Implenia's drilling on both tubes. TBM Sybille had broken through in the northern tube in August 2019.
- WANDA is 137 m long, weighs 2,300 tonnes, and dug for almost exactly two years. Implenia installed 3,989 tubbing rings; advance averaged 15 m a day, peak 32 m. Tubbing segments were made in a factory set up near the site.
- It ends mechanical drilling at the last major tunnel on the new Stuttgart-Ulm line; Implenia calls it one of the ten longest railway tunnels in Germany (Erwin Scherer, Global Head Tunnelling).
- Deutsche Bahn's Thorsten Krenz: line designed for 250 km/h; with Stuttgart 21 the Stuttgart-Ulm journey will be almost halved to around half an hour; about 61 km of tunnel dug under often-difficult geological conditions.

wikis.title: Calheta III hydropower plant commissioned in Madeira
wikis.summary: Gamesa Electric news item (2020-09-17) on commissioning two generators for the 37.5 MW Calheta III plant in Madeira.
wikis.body:
- Gamesa Electric commissioned two horizontal generators (2 x 18.75 MW, 37.5 MW total) for Calheta III hydropower plant, in the municipalities of Calheta and Ponta do Sol, Madeira (Portugal).
- Part of the plan to get 50% of yearly electricity consumption on the island from renewable sources; developed with EU funding and complemented by wind and PV plants.
- Triples the previous plant's hydroelectric capacity; connected to a network serving more than 130,000 consumers and about 800 renewable producers.
- Upgrades bring a net increase of 79.3 GWh of renewable electricity. Two diesel generators guard against blackout if a generator fails.

wikis.title: CMA CGM JACQUES SAADE delivered by CSTC and Hudong-Zhonghua
wikis.summary: CSTC news item (released 2020-10-10) on the delivery of the first LNG-powered 23,000 TEU container ship to CMA CGM.
wikis.body:
- On September 22nd, CSTC and Hudong-Zhonghua named and delivered the world's first LNG-propelled 23,000 TEU container vessel, CMA CGM JACQUES SAADE, to CMA CGM at Changxing shipbuilding base, Shanghai.
- Ship: 400 m long, 61 m wide, 16 m draught; main engine is the W12X92DF dual-fuel engine from WinGD (a CSSC subsidiary), described as the world's largest of its kind.
- Claimed emissions cuts: 99% sulfur oxides and fine particles, 85% nitrogen oxides, 20% less CO2.
- Named after CMA CGM's founder; regarded as the group's "flagship"; framed under the "One Belt and One Road" initiative.

wikis.title: CMA CGM JACQUES SAADE with Wartsila solutions
wikis.summary: Wartsila news release (15 October 2020) on the delivered LNG-powered 23,000 TEU CMA CGM JACQUES SAADE and the Wartsila equipment aboard.
wikis.body:
- CMA CGM JACQUES SAADE is the first 23,000 TEU container vessel powered by LNG, first in a series of nine; 400 m long; built at CSSC Hudong Zhonghua Shipbuilding, China; delivered 22 September 2020.
- Wartsila orders for equipment began in early 2018.
- Wartsila supply: fuel gas supply system, Nacos Platinum integrated automation control, Propulsion Control system, sewage treatment plant, seals and bearings; Wartsila 34DF dual-fuel engines for auxiliary power.
- The fuel gas system has the Operational Performance Improvement and Monitoring (Operim) system giving real-time data.
- Quote (Denis Herve, Wartsila Marine Power): delivery "marks a further step in the shipping sector's efforts to decarbonise its operations."

wikis.title: Samso, the renewable energy island (UN Global Climate Action Awards 2023)
wikis.summary: UNFCCC profile of Denmark's Samso municipality as a 2023 Climate Leader that moved from fossil fuels to renewable energy.
wikis.body:
- Samso has completely transformed its energy system from fossil fuels to renewables, "the world's first renewable energy island"; results include becoming carbon negative and 100% local ownership of renewable investments.
- Samso Energy Academy (mandated by the municipality) does capacity building, knowledge exchange, study visits, workshops and leadership programmes.
- Annual CO2 emissions reduced close to zero via 11 on-shore and 10 off-shore wind turbines, 4 biomass district-heating plants, solar panels and electric vehicles; 100% net annual balance of renewable energy.
- Renewed ambition: completely carbon-free by 2030 (no fossil fuel), extending renewable electricity to heating and road transport and replacing fossil fuel in sea transport with local biogas or electricity; ahead of Denmark's and the EU's 2030 goals.

wikis.title: The island where everyone owns the wind (Samso)
wikis.summary: Andrew Wear excerpt (25 December 2020) on how community-owned renewables made Danish Samso island carbon negative.
wikis.body:
- Samso, off Denmark's Jutland Peninsula, is a farming community; all its electricity comes from community-owned wind turbines and biomass boilers burning local straw meet 70 percent of heating needs. Each of its 3,724 residents emits an average of negative-3.7 tons of greenhouse gas per year.
- Denmark ranks second (behind Sweden) on the Climate Change Performance Index, has halved per capita emissions, and has committed to 100 percent renewable electricity by 2030.
- Background: in 1997 the island's abattoir closed (100 jobs lost). The Danish government launched a competition for a Danish Renewable Energy Island; Samso won in 1998, beating three other islands and a peninsula. The prize funded a coordinator for a ten-year plan; Soren Hermansen, now director of the Samso Energy Academy, took the role.
- Government wanted civic participation and new ways of organizing, financing and owning existing technology.
- Excerpt from "Solved! How Other Countries Have Cracked the World's Biggest Problems and We Can Too".

wikis.title: Gorona del Viento hydro-wind plant, El Hierro
wikis.summary: Article on the Gorona del Viento wind and pumped-hydro plant powering El Hierro, with its records and CO2 savings.
wikis.body:
- Hydro-wind system on El Hierro (Canary Islands), inaugurated June 27, 2014, aiming at energy self-sufficiency. Wind farm: five turbines, 11.5 MW; surplus wind pumps water to an upper reservoir, released for hydro power when there is no wind.
- January 25 to February 12, 2018: 18 consecutive days on 100% renewable energy; 1974 hours renewable-only that year. In Q1 2018 it produced 60% more energy than demanded, allowing the Llanos Blancos diesel plant to be offline for long periods.
- Prevented more than approx. 30,000 tons of CO2 since starting; in 2021 it met demand with 100% renewables for 1,328 hours, cutting diesel by 6,000 tons; avoids importing 43,000 barrels of oil a year.
- Share of demand covered: 19.2% in 2015, 40.7% in 2016, 46.5% in 2017.

wikis.title: Gorona del Viento wind-pumped hydro power station (official site)
wikis.summary: Company homepage describing how the El Hierro wind-pumped hydro station works and its component specifications.
wikis.body:
- Gorona del Viento El Hierro, S.A. operates the Wind-Pumped Hydro Power Station of El Hierro to supply the island with electricity from wind and water; the wind farm can fully meet the island's demand.
- Surplus wind energy pumps water from a lower to an upper reservoir; stored water generates power when wind is inadequate.
- Pumping: two 1,500 kW pumps and six 500 kW pumps, 6 MW total. Lower reservoir 150,000 m3 near Llanos Blancos. Turbines: four Pelton turbines totalling 11.3 MW. Two pipelines approx. 3 km long, 0.80 m diameter. Upper reservoir 380,000 m3 in the La Caldera crater at 700 m altitude, lined with polymer sheets. Wind farm: five Enercon E-70 turbines of 2.3 MW each, 11.5 MW total.

wikis.title: Porsche Leipzig factory and electromobility
wikis.summary: Porsche Newsroom page on the fifth Leipzig factory expansion for the electric Macan and its history.
wikis.body:
- Porsche invested some 600 million euros in the fifth expansion after deciding to build the second-generation, electric Macan in Leipzig (new body construction facility, axle preassembly, new 'marriage' process, paint shop and logistics). The line can build petrol, hybrid and all-electric cars. Ramp-up of the electric Macan began in 2024.
- Earlier extensions: 2004 (Carrera GT area), 2009 (Panamera hall and logistics centre), fourth step for second-generation Panamera from 2016. Full factory in 2013 for first-gen Macan.
- Total investment since founding in 2000: around 1.9 billion euros. Around 550 Macan and Panamera per day in three shifts; more than two million cars since production started in 2002. 738,503 Cayenne built 2002-2017; Carrera GT limited to 1,270 units (2003-2006).
- Net carbon neutral since 2021; 'Lean & Green Management Award' 2021; Kearney 'Factory of the Year' 2023.

wikis.title: Czech Republic extends JAS 39 Gripen lease with Sweden
wikis.summary: Army Recognition news (3 Sep 2024) that the Czech Republic signed on August 31, 2024 to extend its Gripen lease beyond 2027 until F-35As arrive.
wikis.body:
- On August 31, 2024 the Czech Republic signed an agreement with Sweden extending the lease of 14 Gripens (12 single-seat, two two-seat) beyond 2027 until the F-35A arrives, expected to begin in 2031.
- Gripens delivered 2005, based at Caslav Air Base, initially an interim solution.
- Swedish Defence Minister Pal Jonson: "defense cooperation between Sweden and the Czech Republic will further intensify to the benefit of both parties." Includes joint training with the CV90, which the Czech Republic is considering acquiring.
- Czech Parliament ratified purchase of 24 F-35A in September 2023. Lion Effort exercise held at Caslav in May with over 150 personnel from Hungary, Sweden, Thailand and Brazil.

wikis.title: Czech Republic considering Gripen lease extension to 2035
wikis.summary: The Aviationist (April 12, 2025): Czech MoD evaluating a Saab offer to extend 12 Gripen C/Ds from 2027 to 2035.
wikis.body:
- Czech MoD statement of Apr. 8, 2025: evaluating a new Saab proposal extending the JAS39 Gripen C/D lease from 2027 to 2035, worth 16.65 billion CZK ($732 million), for 12 of 14 aircraft (10 single-seat, two dual-seat). A first offer did not meet expectations and was renegotiated; MoD cites "significant financial savings".
- Czech Air Force will include F-35s in airspace protection gradually from 2031; first F-35A expected 2031, deliveries completed 2035. MoU for 24 F-35As signed Jan. 2024.
- Original 2004 10-year lease with FMV and Saab worth 19.65 billion CZK ($867 million) for 14 Gripens, later extended to 2027. Air Force commander Maj. Gen. Petr Cepelka called the offer "acceptable"; a draft contract might go to government for signing.

wikis.title: Le Commandant Charcot (Ponant icebreaking cruise ship)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article (raw wikitext) on the French icebreaking cruise ship Le Commandant Charcot; only infobox data readable in the text.
wikis.body:
- Cost listed: 2.7 billion (NOK, per VARD press). Laid down December 2018; launched March 2020; completed July 2021 (delivered by Vard Group); status in service; IMO 9846249.
- Cruise ship, 31,283 GT, length 150 m, beam 28.3 m, draught 10 m. Ice class Polar Class 2; BV Icebreaker 3 (bow), Icebreaker 4 (stern).
- Power: 4 x Wartsila 14V31DF (7,700 kW each), 2 x Wartsila 10V31DF (5,500 kW each); 5 MWh batteries. Described as the first electric hybrid cruise icebreaker with LNG propulsion, ordered by PONANT from VARD.

wikis.title: Le Commandant Charcot reaches the geographic North Pole
wikis.summary: Cruise Industry News (September 13, 2021): Ponant ship Le Commandant Charcot reached the North Pole on Sept. 6.
wikis.body:
- Le Commandant Charcot, Ponant's first hybrid electric polar exploration ship, reached the geographic North Pole on Sept. 6 at 10:38 a.m., per a press release.
- Captain Etienne Garcia was at the helm with Captain Marchesseau beside him.
- Described as the first French ship to reach the North Pole and the first LNG-propelled ship to reach it.
- Garcia: "I am hugely proud to have been at the helm of the very first French ship to reach the geographic North Pole."

wikis.title: Deep Dive Dubai, the world deepest diving pool
wikis.summary: CNBC Travel (13 July 2021): Deep Dive Dubai opened July 7 as the world deepest diving pool, with a sunken city attraction.
wikis.body:
- Deep Dive Dubai opened July 7, 10 days after Guinness World Records named it the world's deepest diving pool. Indoor pool nearly 200 feet (196-foot vertical pool) deep, almost 3.7 million gallons; holds the water of six Olympic-sized pools.
- Contains a "sunken city" with graffiti, crumbling facades, a Marilyn Monroe portrait, an apartment building, library and arcade with Pac-Man, foosball and pool table.
- Open to ages 10 and older, including first-time divers. Beginners dive to 40 feet; certified divers can explore the whole pool, and free dive on a fixed ascent line.
- 156 lights; water at 86 degrees Fahrenheit; no living marine life.
- Bookings by invitation only at first; public bookings later in July, prices from 800 UAE dirhams ($218). Will Smith's Instagram post got over 3 million likes in four days.

wikis.title: Eiffel Tower: overview, origin and artists protest (Wikipedia, part 1)
wikis.summary: First part of the Wikipedia article on the Eiffel Tower: description, records, design origin, contract, and the protest against it.
wikis.body:
- Lattice tower on the Champ de Mars, Paris, named after Gustave Eiffel, whose company built it 1887 to 1889 as the centrepiece of the 1889 World's Fair marking the centennial of the French Revolution. Nickname "La dame de fer". 5,889,000 visitors in 2022; 6.91 million ascended in 2015. Monument historique 1964; UNESCO World Heritage Site part 1991.
- 330 m (1,083 ft) tall, base 125 m per side; tallest human-made structure in the world for 41 years until the Chrysler Building (1930); 1957 aerial made it 11 m taller than the Chrysler. Top platform 276 m; over 300 steps to first level and again to second.
- Infobox dates: construction start 28 January 1887, completed 31 March 1889, opened 15 May 1889; architect Stephen Sauvestre, engineers Maurice Koechlin and Emile Nouguier.
- Origin: Koechlin's sketch in May 1884; Eiffel bought the patent; presented 30 March 1885. Contract 8 January 1887 granted 1.5 million francs toward an estimated 6.5 million; Eiffel got commercial income during the exhibition and 20 years. CIC bank helped finance; article ties CIC to loans to Haiti's National Bank.
- 14 February 1887 "Artists against the Eiffel Tower" petition (Committee of Three Hundred led by Charles Garnier); Eiffel compared the tower to the pyramids.

wikis.title: Eiffel Tower opens in Paris, March 31, 1889
wikis.summary: HISTORY.com entry on the dedication of the Eiffel Tower on March 31, 1889.
wikis.body:
- March 31, 1889: dedicated in a ceremony presided over by Gustave Eiffel, with French Prime Minister Pierre Tirard and 200 construction workers.
- Built for the 1889 international exposition honoring the centenary of the French Revolution; chosen from more than 100 designs; open-lattice wrought-iron, almost 1,000 feet, then the world's tallest man-made structure. Completed under budget in just two years; only one worker died.
- 984 feet tall on four masonry piers, three platforms with observation decks. Otis Elevator Company designed the glass-cage elevators, not complete by March 31, so Eiffel climbed the stairs and raised a French tricolor; fireworks from the second platform.
- Exposition opened in early May. Tallest until the Chrysler Building in 1930. Nearly demolished in 1909 when the 20-year land lease expired, saved by its value as a radio antenna.

wikis.title: Seven Stars in Kyushu luxury excursion train
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the JR Kyushu Seven Stars in Kyushu sleeper excursion train: design, formation, routes, history.
wikis.body:
- Deluxe sleeping car excursion train run by JR Kyushu since October 2013; first service 15 October 2013; designed under industrial designer Eiji Mitooka; name from Kyushu's seven prefectures and seven coaches.
- DF200-7000 diesel locomotive built by Kawasaki Heavy Industries (Kobe), maroon livery, completed July 2013 (delivered 2 July 2013); coaches built by Hitachi (Kudamatsu) and JR Kyushu Kokura Works; operating speed 100 km/h.
- Formation: five sleeping cars, lounge car (piano, bar, observation), dining car; capacity 28 passengers; rear car has two deluxe suites. Cost approximately 3 billion yen. Some suites have porcelain bathrooms designed by Sakaida Kakiemon XIV.
- Routes from Hakata: 2-day (Hakata, Nagasaki; Aso, Yufuin, Hakata) and 4-day circular tours.

wikis.title: SCHEUERLE SPMT turns 40
wikis.summary: TII press release on the 40th anniversary of the SCHEUERLE Self-Propelled Modular Transporter, launched in 1983.
wikis.body:
- In 1983 Scheuerle Fahrzeugfabrik (now TII SCHEUERLE) developed and launched the Self-Propelled Modular Transporter (SPMT); the name SPMT itself originally came from TII SCHEUERLE.
- Several 10,000 SCHEUERLE SPMT axle lines are in use worldwide; "the global standard".
- The idea came from the needs of long-time customer Mammoet; module width 2,430 millimetres so it fits a standard container (flat rack) and can travel on motorways.
- Series named: SPMT InterCombi SPE, K24, K25 SPE. Loads moved: luxury yachts, industrial plants weighing thousands of tonnes, mining-vehicle components, offshore wind turbines, complete hotels, historical cultural assets.
- Quote (Dr Gerald Karch, CEO of the TII Group): customers' needs for functionality, cost-effectiveness, safety and efficiency are the incentive.

wikis.title: Self-propelled modular transporter (SPMT)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on SPMTs: what they are, specifications and history.
wikis.body:
- A platform heavy hauler with a large array of wheels, upgraded from the hydraulic modular trailer; carries bridge sections, refinery equipment, cranes, spacecraft, entire buildings and oil platforms. Used to replace bridge spans in the US, Europe, Asia and Canada.
- Grid of computer-controlled axles (usually 2 across, 4-8 along); each individually controllable, swivels 270 degrees (some 360). Loaded speed often under 1 mile per hour (1.6 km/h). Multiple SPMTs can be linked and run from one control panel.
- History: 1935 Gothaer Wagonfabrik motorized model of the Culemeyer trailer (32 ton load capacity); first modern modular units in the 1970s; early 1980s Mammoet set module width 2.44 m (ISO container flatrack) and added 360 degree steering, commissioned Scheuerle; deliveries started 1983 (4-axle, 6-axle, power pack).
- 2016: ESTA published the first SPMT best practice guide addressing trailers tipping over. Shipbuilders use SPMTs instead of gantry cranes for ship sections.

wikis.title: Meyer Werft delivers Norwegian Breakaway
wikis.summary: Meyer Werft press release (25 April 2013) on delivery of the 146,600 GT Norwegian Breakaway to Norwegian Cruise Line.
wikis.body:
- Bremerhaven/Papenburg, 25 April 2013: NCL took delivery of Norwegian Breakaway (146,600 GT) after an 18-month build; first of two Breakaway class ships (sister Norwegian Getaway to launch in Miami February 1, 2014). Yard number S.678.
- Features: The Waterfront, 678 Ocean Place, largest aqua park and ropes course at sea, first salt room in a spa; approx. 75% outside staterooms, solo staterooms, The Haven by Norwegian.
- Diesel-electric pod drive; support from Federal Ministry of Economics and Technology and Lower Saxony for innovation aid.
- Main particulars: 324.00 m overall, 39.7 m breadth, 18 decks, draught 8.30 m, engine output 62,400 kW, propulsion 35,000 kW, 21.5 kn.
- Route: Bremerhaven to Rotterdam, transatlantic from Southampton to New York (naming ceremony); 12 May 2013 to Bermuda for seven-day cruises.

wikis.title: Norwegian Breakaway (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on NCL cruise ship Norwegian Breakaway: naming, construction, design, service and incidents.
wikis.body:
- Ordered 17 August 2011; built by Meyer Werft, Papenburg; steel cut/laid down 21 September 2011; launched 30 April 2013 (per infobox); godmothers The Rockettes; delivered to NCL 25 April 2013; IMO 9606912.
- Named through a public contest (Kimberly Powell); announced 14 September 2011. With Norwegian Getaway, first two ships of Project Breakaway.
- 146,600 GT (infobox 145,655 GT), 325.64 m, capacity 3,963 passengers, 1,604 staterooms and 350 suites; ninth largest cruise ship by gross tonnage at launch; 21.5 kn; two ABB Azipods.
- Homeported at New York Passenger Ship Terminal (Bermuda cruises May-September, Bahamas/Florida October-April); leaving New York from late 2018 for New Orleans, Miami early 2019, Port Canaveral November 2019.
- Onboard: Ocean Blue restaurant by Geoffrey Zakarian, Second City comedy club, hull art by Peter Max. Incidents listed: 17 September 2013 balcony fall; 3 February 2014 child drowned in pool.

wikis.title: Claas Axion 960 Cemos wins Sustainable Tractor of the Year 2021
wikis.summary: HeavyQuip (January 8, 2021): the Claas Axion 960 Cemos won the Sustainable Tractor of the Year 2021 title.
wikis.body:
- Jury of 26 specialist agricultural journalists from 25 countries picked the Claas Axion 960 Cemos from 18 finalists (17 others); second time the Sustainable TotY has been awarded. The ceremony was virtual for the first time due to the corona pandemic.
- Jury: Cemos system and tyre pressure optimization give "remarkable fuel saving" and efficient performance.
- Claas introduced the Stage V Axion 900 series in September 2020, optionally equipped or retrofitted with Claas Ctic tyre inflation and self-learning Cemos for tractors. Cemos received the DLG approved label for fuel savings of up to 16.8 percent and 16.3 percent productivity increase (DLG test report 7096).

wikis.title: Claas Axion tractor (Wikipedia stub)
wikis.summary: Short Wikipedia stub on the Claas Axion tractor built at the former Renault tractor plant in Le Mans.
wikis.body:
