At first glance one might dismiss Shonan Bakusozoku as a generic 1980's anime. But to do so would be to overlook an extremely influential, fun and downright enlightening series. Eguchi Yousuke is the second generation leader of the small, but infamous Shonan Bakusozoku bikers. The series revolves around ... the lives of Eguchi and the entire Bakusozoku gang, in and out of school. In doing so Shonan Bakusozoku maintains a great balance between the comedy, romance, and drama that make up the average high school student's life. However, whereas most high school hobbies include sports or the arts, Eguchi and company sport pompadours, customized gakuran (school uniforms) and ride especially loud motorcycles. While this hobby affords it's own series of unique conflicts and adventures, it's not to say there's nothing normal about the Bakusozoku's lives- they have jobs, girlfriends and belong to school clubs (Eguchi is president of the school's embroidery club). As for the technical aspects, Shonan Bakusosoku shines in every category. The production values are surprisingly high. The animation is slick and beautiful, especially considering its 1986 release date. The rock soundtrack pops and fits the subject matter and time period perfectly. Though the voice acting is great, some of the high school students' adult voice actors take some getting used to. But these are tough, sometimes bearded and mustached students, so how can anyone complain? It may be worth noting that each episode runs about an hour long, usually combining two stories from the manga. So although Shonan Bakusozoku will take a little more time than the average 22 minute episode, it's well worth it. Perhaps Shonan Bakusosoku's greatest strength lies in its depiction of Japan's bosozoku and yanki subcultures. In the book "Kamikaze Bikers," Ikuya Sato argues that Japanese bosozoku and yanki were not the extreme menace that the Japanese media had portrayed them to be. He concludes that most were in it for fun, friendship and as a last hurrah before settling into adulthood. If Mr. Sato is right, Shonan Bakusozoku is an extremely accurate portrayal of these subcultures. The series creates a sense of the youthful lust for fun, style and recklessness. Unlike some of its successors, Shonan Bakusozoku never limits its focus to the exploits of its bike gangs. Instead, it presents various aspects of the gang members' personal lives throughout the series. The characters are high schoolers in a bike gang, not simply bike gang members. The result is a multidimensional experience, offering insight into rare aspects of Japanese culture- far more so than any of its successors. Although almost forgotten in Japan and nearly non-existent overseas, Shonan Bakusozoku's influence cannot be denied. If Crows is the "Yanki Bible," then Shonan Bakusosoku must be... the Yanki Bible's Bible? Bottom line is it's a must see for anyone interested in the Japanese yanki, bosozoku or delinquent subcultures. And considering the genre's renewed popularity, there is a huge audience just waiting to check it out. Reviewer’s Rating: 8 What did you think of this review? A love letter to high school and youth with almost every episode having some deeper themes about what it means to be a man, to grow up, and to live. It's lighthearted and laidback for the most part but takes itself seriously. It's not so much a comedy as a pure slice of life, just segments of the lives of these budding adults as they live their final year in high school. Manly guys doing quite manly things, coming into their own, yet still being kids. If you're struggling to ... find it, Inka-Subs is the one who has done the fan subs of the bluray. It's a teenage drama that really encapsulates and oozes the 80's, visually it's one of my favorites due to how much it feels like a painting of a 60's diner come to life with 80's stylings. It starts strong and largely only gets better in its visual styling. It's got that incredible use of contrast and color in all of the best ways. It'll punch you with nostalgia, even if you've never had any about the period or never lived through it. It's one of those that really just paints the period so well. The only episode I can call weak is episode 10, which has some quite painful Engrish in it and is the least developed plot wise. If you want a very genuine, ernest slice of life, of 18 year old rock-n-rollers and grease monkeys set to 1980's Japan, this is your show. Reviewer’s Rating: 10 What did you think of this review? I don’t write reviews all that often so please excuse the amateur quality of this review, I just wanted to talk about this classic series as it doesn’t seem to have much attention on MAL. I was very lucky to stumble upon this series when I did. As it appears that just a few months ago someone by the name of Inka-subs actually took the time to subtitle all 12 episodes of this anime's beautifully clean-looking blue ray. I’ve seen almost all the pre-2000s ... delinquent anime/OVAs available with English translations, so I think I have a good sense of what aspects I enjoyed of Shounan Bakusouzoku compared to other Delinquent shows that were likely influenced by this series. Animation: 10 For one the artwork is phenomenal all the background shots can honestly be put into a gif and posted to an anime aesthetics account on Twitter. The Blu-ray wiped away the grimy VHS rip look I usually would see watching a show of this level of obscurity and age. The animation looks clean and fluid for the time this was made holding up today despite the show being over 35 years old. Characters 8: All the characters in this are really likable each having a bit of their own arc character growth arc sprinkled in throughout the series. All the characters look fairly unique with different hairstyles and body types which is nice because in other Delinquent shows such as “BeBop High school” all the characters had the same body build, hair, and Gakurans I couldn’t tell who was who. I also have to give the girls in this series a shout-out as they are more confident in themselves than in other shows I’ve seen making them more like a part of the team rather than an annoying damsel in distress. Story: 8 The storylines in each episode were much more engaging than some of the other delinquent shows I’ve seen typically in most delinquent shows the plot goes as follows, “Bad guy from different school does bad things so let’s go beat them up” sure this anime still has that in most episodes plot lines. However, the episodes like that usually have a B plot to explore other character's daily life or backgrounds so it’s not so stale. Music: 9 The show spares no expense when it comes to music. Each episode has two unique songs in them that fit the scene they play in. The majority of songs played sound super 80s which if you're a fan of Japanese 80s pop this shows right up your alley. ## Synopsis
In the far reaches of the dark and frozen universe, nine enormous dragon corpses were tied with an ancient bronze coffin. It seems that they were set there since the birth of the universe. Such an astonishing scene was captured by a space probe floating in outer space. Nine dragons and the mysterious bronze coffin made people wonder whether they came back to ancient times or just reached the other shore of the universe. A giant mythical world was unfolded, where immortality gradually appeared and paranormal events continuously occurred. Countless people started to find their own paths in such a mythical realm. Their passion was like a turbulent ocean wave that would never cease. The heat in their blood was like erupting volcanoes. Their desire for power and immortality dragged them down to the chasm without knowing it. Thirty-three classmates held a reunion after graduating. Their friendship was tested, as the bronze coffin took them away from earth and arrived on another unknown planet. The desire for living forced them to follow the path of the ancient gods. Entering a new world of cultivation, will any of them reach immortality, or will they all die along the way?

They're all together quite funny, and I think the thing that was enjoyable to me about them is that they really helped me to let go of the series once I had finished it. It lets you go back into the world of these characters without having to rewatch the entire series. Not to mention, you actually get to see some stuff that you wouldn't get to see in the series (like Kuroko laughing). Other than that, though, it's just lighthearted, good fun to watch. The ... movie's version of bloopers was pretty awesome just because you got to see the Generation of Miracles being funny together, which is something new. For example, there's a blooper with Kise and Aomine that I love. Obviously, there's no character development or anything that benefits the story, but it does lighten up some of the more intense moments of the anime, so it's nice to be able to let go of some of that tension. If you wanna watch it, go ahead. It's fun at the very least. Reviewer’s Rating: 10 What did you think of this review? The characters are now confronted with an American team, which includes two other child prodigies. It has been made as antagonistic as it could have been done at all. In that sense, also a 1: 1 copy of "Hawk" from Hajime no Ippo as the main antagonist. As a closing film, it wasn't bad, it had momentum and a subtle closing ceremony for the characters and their new paths. ... However, this whole movie felt completely forced and like an oversized Ova episode. Just the fact that the final opponents were terribly meaningless and the whole reason for their duel was a badly provoked joke. You should either have chosen a different plot or at least somehow connected it to the series. There was another character over the course of the second season who was significantly better than a potential antagonist. There is nothing to complain about in terms of optics and animation. The game had a certain dynamic, fluid animation and was good enough for the eyes. And that has been the biggest problem with the whole Kuroko no Basket anime for the most part. It's subtle as a sports title and can entertain, but it's mostly just something for the eye. The series ultimately lacked a lot of character, detail, and atmosphere. Nonetheless, you can definitely watch the anime as long as you let yourself be put off. Reviewer’s Rating: 5 What did you think of this review? ## Synopsis
Pokémon are marvelous creatures that come in a variety of types and sizes, with abilities, powers, and personalities as diverse as they are numerous. Doctor Yukinari Ookido has dedicated his life to studying these fascinating beings, that can be caught, trained, traded, and battled against each other. There's only so much he can do from his lab though. With this in mind, Ookido entrusts two young boys with a Pokémon of their own and a computerized encyclopedia to catalog them. One of them, Green, is brash, passionate, slightly arrogant, and Doctor Ookido's own nephew. The other boy, Red, is equally passionate, and filled with a wide-eyed, mildly naive sense of wonder. Pokémon: The Origin follows Red in his journey through the region of Kanto in his attempt to complete his "Pokédex" by capturing and cataloging all the Pokémon that exist. Along the way he'll discover there's more to himself and his goals than he originally thought. Red will have to put both himself and his Pokémon to the test in special Gyms whose leaders are steps along the way to the Pokémon League, in order to challenge the Elite Four and become a Pokémon League Champion. Aside from his goals to become a Champion, Red has other problems brewing. There are others who capture and train Pokémon for more sinister reasons, with the infamous criminal organization Team Rocket being one of them. If Red can defeat them, fellow trainers, his rival Green, and wild Pokémon all through Kanto, he just may fulfill his own dream, and Doctor Ookido's as well.

## Synopsis
Following NERV's failed attempt to retrieve the Spears of Longinus and carry out the Human Instrumentality Project, the destruction caused by the Fourth Impact has been largely averted. In a state of disarray, Shinji Ikari, Asuka Langley Shikinami, and Rei Ayanami travel to Village 3—a survivor settlement free from Earth's ruination. There, Shinji slowly comes to terms with his past, developing an entirely different life from his days as an Evangelion pilot. Meanwhile, NERV makes preparations to continue the Instrumentality Project by means of a new Impact. When WILLE's main aerial battleship arrives at the village, Shinji decides to board, believing that he can help by piloting an Evangelion. As new secrets are uncovered and a battle between WILLE and NERV approaches, the future of Earth hangs in the balance. Can Shinji save humanity and the rest of the world one last time? [Written by MAL Rewrite]

## Background
Shin Evangelion Movie:|| has earned a franchise record of 10.22 billion yen (92.7 million USD) and debuted at No. 1 at the Japanese box office. Additionally, it won the Animation of the Year award in the Film category at the Tokyo Anime Award Festival in 2022. The film was released internationally on August 13, 2021, via the Amazon Prime Video streaming service. The film has been dubbed in 10 languages: Chinese, English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Latin American Spanish, and Peninsular Spanish.

wikis.title: Who will win the 2026 midterms? Polls and prediction-market odds (Sept. 16, 2026)
wikis.summary: USA Today Network article giving polling averages and Polymarket and Kalshi odds for control of Congress in the Nov. 3, 2026 midterms.
wikis.body:
- Byline Maria Francis, USA TODAY NETWORK; updated Sept. 16, 2026, 1:51 p.m. ET.
- Election Day: Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, deciding control of Congress plus gubernatorial, state legislative and local races. Republicans defend House and Senate majorities; Democrats look to capitalize on the president's party historically losing ground.
- RealClearPolling generic ballot average: Democrats 50.2%, Republicans 41.6%. This week's YouGov poll: 44% Democratic, 39% Republican, 17% undecided/other/not voting.
- Polymarket: 88% Democratic House win, 59% Democratic Senate win, 59% Democratic sweep, 11% Republican sweep.
- Kalshi: 54% Democratic sweep of both chambers, 87% Democratic House, 55% Democratic Senate.
- Odds "reflect polling and odds as of Wednesday, September 16, 2026" and are constantly changing.
- Trump has promoted proposed $5,000 dividend checks, which would likely have a smoother path if Republicans keep both chambers.
- Hakeem Jeffries on impeachment: "we haven't ruled anything in and we haven't ruled anything out"; Jamie Raskin said Democrats "will not hesitate" to use impeachment if necessary.

wikis.title: When Will Bitcoin Price Bottom Out? Benjamin Cowen Predicts (Apr 15, 2026)
wikis.summary: Yahoo Finance/BeInCrypto article where Benjamin Cowen expects a Bitcoin cycle bottom around October 2026.
wikis.body:
- Kamina Bashir, April 15, 2026. Bitcoin has shown resilience amid the US-Iran war, "climbing over 12% since February 28".
- Cowen (CEO of Into The Cryptoverse, former NASA researcher) told BeInCrypto: "The base case has to just simply be that it'll bottom when the other two cycles bottom, which is about a year after the top most likely scenario is October of 2026." Bitcoin topped within one week of when earlier cycles peaked.
- A bottom as early as May would need a massive capitulation event well below what midterm years typically produce; while 2026 year-to-date ROI stays within one standard deviation of prior midterm years, he sees no reason to change the October thesis.
- Joao Wedson (Alphractal): cycle top came 534 days after the April 2024 halving; bottom could come 912 to 922 days after, i.e. late September or early October 2026. CryptoQuant models: bottom between June and December 2026, September through November most probable.
- Cowen also notes this cycle topped on apathy, not euphoria.

wikis.title: Bitcoin analyst predicts price could fall to $40,000, bottom in late 2026 (KuCoin flash, 2026-06-24)
wikis.summary: KuCoin news flash relaying Bitcoinsistemi: Benjamin Cowen sees a $40,000 area and a cycle bottom around October-November 2026.
wikis.body:
- Release time 2026/06/24 17:53:40; source Bitcoinsistemi. Summary cites weak altcoins, low retail interest, a bearish fear and greed index, Bitcoin dominance, and a strong U.S. Dollar Index.
- Benjamin Cowen, founder of Into The Cryptoverse, says Bitcoin has not yet reached its ultimate bottom; based on the "4-year cycle", the macro bottom comes about a year after the peak, and the most likely major bottom is around October 2026.
- He says this cycle peaked on "apathy rather than enthusiasm", so the expected altcoin rally did not materialize; it most resembles 2019 and money stays Bitcoin-dominated.
- Downside target: the $40,000 region, where Realized Price and Balanced Price converge. Bottom in Q4 2026, around October-November.
- A strong US Dollar Index (DXY) pressures risk assets. Quote: "Bears sound smart, but bulls win the money." "This is not investment advice."

wikis.title: List of Apple media events, 1984 to September 2008 (Wikipedia, part 1)
wikis.summary: First part of Wikipedia's list of Apple Inc. media events, running from the 1984 Macintosh event through WWDC 2008 and the September 2008 special event, with products announced at each.
wikis.body:
Intro: Apple announces major products through press conferences (minor updates via Newsroom press releases); agendas are usually secret; events are streamed live and replays since 2007 are on the "Apple Events" podcast. Venues named include Moscone West, Yerba Buena Center for the Arts, Bill Graham Civic Auditorium, Flint Center, McEnery Convention Center, Steve Jobs Theater, Brooklyn Academy of Music; online-only 2020-March 2022, online and in-person since June 2022. The list is flagged incomplete.

## 1984-1999
- Macintosh event (Jan 24, 1984) at the Flint Center; Apple II Forever event (April 1984) introduced the Apple IIc.
- WWDC runs annually from May 1990; WWDC 1991 showed QuickTime; WWDC 1995 focused on Copland, "never released".
- Jan 7, 1997: Gil Amelio announced NeXT technology integration. 1998: Apple Studio Display (first LCD desktop monitor); May 1998 original iMac at the Flint Center.
- 1999: Power Macintosh G3 (Jan 5), iBook (July 21), PowerPC G4, Power Mac G4 and 22-inch Cinema Display (Seybold), iMac DV and iMovie (Oct 5).

## 2000-2006
- Macworld Jan 5, 2000: Aqua and Quartz; Mac OS X 10.0 to ship January 2001 (actually March 2001); Jobs made full-time CEO. July 19, 2000: Power Mac G4 Cube.
- Oct 23, 2001: first iPod. Jan 7, 2002: iMac G4 (first LCD iMac). 2003: 17-inch PowerBook G4, Power Mac G5, Panther. 2004: iPod Mini, iTunes Music Store to Europe, iPod Photo/U2 edition.
- 2005: iPod Shuffle, Mac Mini; Jobs said 4.5 million iPods sold in the 2004 holiday quarter vs 733,000 a year earlier; WWDC 2005 announced the move to Intel x86; Sept 7: iPod Nano and Motorola ROKR; Kanye West performance.
- Jan 10, 2006: first Intel-based iMac and MacBook Pro. Feb 28: iPod Hi-Fi. WWDC 2006: Mac Pro; Leopard previews. Sept 12, 2006 "It's Showtime": Apple TV.

## 2007-2008
- Jan 9, 2007 (Macworld, Moscone West): iPhone introduced ($499 4GB, $599 8GB with 2-year contract; Cingular exclusive; ship in June); Apple Computer, Inc. renamed Apple Inc.; Apple TV at $299; 2 billion songs sold on iTunes.
- WWDC 2007 (June 11-15): iPhone release dates. Aug 7, 2007: aluminum iMac. Sept 5, 2007 "The Beat Goes On": iPod touch, third-gen iPod nano; iPhone 8GB drops from $599 to $399.
- Jan 16, 2008: MacBook Air ($1799), Time Capsule, iTunes movie rentals ($2.99-$3.99), Apple TV "Take 2" at $229; 4 million iPhones sold in 200 days. March 6, 2008: iPhone SDK. WWDC 2008 (June 9-13): App Store, iPhone 3G, iPhone OS 2.0, Snow Leopard, MobileMe. Sept 9, 2008 special event follows (text truncated here).

wikis.title: NVIDIA unveils GeForce GTX 780 Ti (press release)
wikis.summary: NVIDIA press release of November 6, 2013 introducing the GeForce GTX 780 Ti, available now from $699.
wikis.body:
- Dated November 6, 2013, Santa Clara. NVIDIA introduced the GeForce GTX 780 Ti, claimed "unquestionably the fastest gaming GPU in the world", aimed at extreme-resolution gaming in Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag, Call of Duty: Ghosts and Batman: Arkham Origins.
- Kepler architecture; dedicated frame metering hardware; supports G-SYNC; 25 percent more cores than the GTX 780; 7Gbps onboard memory; GPU Boost 2.0; "almost 21 percent faster on average" than the original GTX 780. Design: aluminum cover, LED-backlit GeForce GTX logo, clear polycarbonate window.

wikis.title: TechRadar review of the Nvidia GeForce GTX 780 Ti
wikis.summary: TechRadar review (8 November 2013) finding the GTX 780 Ti the fastest single GPU but only slightly ahead of AMD's Radeon R9 290X at stock and best justified by its overclocking.
wikis.body:
- By Dave James, published 8 November 2013. Verdict pros: takes performance crown, more desirable than AMD R9s, overclocking gives a decent boost. Cons: still priced out of reach of most; performance gain doesn't equal the price premium.
- First card with the full GK 110 chip: 2,880 CUDA cores in fifteen SMX modules (the Titan had 2,688 across fourteen).
- Stock results (avg FPS, min in brackets): Company of Heroes 2: 780 Ti 25 (12), R9 290X 29 (15), Titan 25 (12), R9 290 27 (14). Total War: Rome II: 37 (12), 36 (13), 33 (12), 34 (11). Metro: Last Light: 28 (14), 26 (13), 24 (13), 25 (13).
- Overclocked Heaven 4.0: 780 Ti 49.2 (21.5) vs R9 290X 36.7 (18.5). GPU temperature at 100%: 83C vs 95C (290X), Titan 80C, R9 290 93C. Peak platform power: 340W vs 383W (290X), Titan 300W, R9 290 347W.
- The 780 Ti is "another GBP 100/$160-odd more expensive" than the 290X; reviewer "underwhelmed" at stock. Overclocked sample hit a minimum of 16%, sometimes over 22%, staying at 83C.
- Still says the R9 290 (non-X) keeps the top of its shopping list on price/performance; the Radeons lack the desirability of the 780 Ti.

wikis.title: SimCity (2013 video game): gameplay, development and launch problems (Wikipedia, part 1)
wikis.summary: First part of the Wikipedia article on Maxis' 2013 SimCity reboot covering gameplay, the GlassBox engine, audio, development and the troubled always-online launch.
wikis.body:
- SimCity: city-building game by Maxis Emeryville, published by Electronic Arts; reboot, first major installment since SimCity 4 a decade earlier. Windows release NA March 5, 2013 (EU/AU/JP March 7 per the infobox, UK March 8); macOS August 29, 2013. Engine GlassBox; composer Chris Tilton; designers Ocean Quigley and Stone Librande. Last game by Maxis Emeryville before the studio's closure in 2015.
- Gameplay: curved, non-orthogonal roads; roads carry water, power and sewage and road density sets building density; streets 24 m wide, avenues 48 m; single zone type per residential/commercial/industrial; finite resources; region of connected cities that trade, share services and build "great works"; specialisations (manufacturing, tourism, education); simulated global economy for resource prices; UI inspired by Google Maps and infographics.
- Multiplayer/online: first full online play since SimCity 2000 Network Edition (1996); requires EA's Origin login even in single-player; at release a constant internet connection was required until a patch added an offline single-player mode; outages longer than 19 minutes lose game state (per a Kotaku editor).
- Development: leaked concept art via GameStar; announced March 6, 2012 at GDC; trailers at E3 2012; closed betas January and February 2013. GlassBox uses agents (water, power, workers) with animations tied directly to agent activity; citizens go to the first job/home they find. Maxis published its mod policy January 9, 2014 (re-skinning and buildings allowed, not gameplay changes). Audio synced to the simulation; music synchronised to 120 BPM.
- Editions: standard, Limited Edition (Heroes & Villains, Plumbob Park DLC), Origin-exclusive Digital Deluxe.
- Launch: severe server outages, long loads, disconnections and lost saves; publications called it "disastrous", compared to Diablo III's launch; Amazon.com temporarily withdrew the download version. Reviewers said the game was "unplayably broken" at launch. GlassBox issues included traffic taking the shortest route.

- Specs: Intel Core i7-4702HQ (up to 3.2 GHz), Nvidia Quadro K1100M with 2GB GDDR5, up to 16GB memory, 15.6" UltraSharp QHD+ (3200 x 1800) or FHD (1920 x 1080) display, 18mm (0.71") aluminum and carbon fiber frame, 4.15 lb (1.88 kg), up to 10 hours 6 minutes battery with Optimus, Windows 8.1 Pro or Windows 7 Professional 64-bit.
- Update 10/23/13: the release wrongly said both an mSATA port and 2.5" bay were for storage; the mSATA slot is used for the Intel AC 7260 WiFi/BT card and storage is a 2.5" bay plus an NGFF half mini slot.
- Press release claims: thinnest and lightest 15-inch true mobile workstation; up to 1.5TB storage; five-finger multi-touch Gorilla NBT Glass; four USB PowerPorts; optional D3000 USB 3.0 dock; a 31.5" UltraSharp 32 4K monitor "coming later this fall"; tuned for Adobe, Autodesk, Avid, Dassault, PTC and Siemens software.
- Quotes from Jon Peddie, Sandeep Gupte (NVIDIA), Andy Rhodes (Dell), and users at Freeman, Autodesk and Appalachian State.

wikis.title: Tom's Hardware: Nexus 5 will arrive at T-Mobile November 14
wikis.summary: Tom's Hardware, 10 November 2013: the 16GB Nexus 5 heads to T-Mobile USA November 14 for $42 down plus $17 a month over 24 months ($450 total), vs $350 at Google.
wikis.body:
- Published 10 November 2013 by Jane McEntegart, citing Engadget. The Nexus 5 launched "just last week" and is only available via the Google Play Store.
- T-Mobile will sell only the 16GB model; $42 up front and $17 per month over 24 months, $450 in all vs $350 from Google.
- Specs listed: LG-made; 4.95-inch 1920x1080 display; quad-core Snapdragon 800 at 2.3 GHz; 2GB RAM; up to 32GB storage; 8-megapixel camera with OIS and 1.3-megapixel front camera; 4G/LTE; dual band WiFi; wireless charging; 2300 mAh battery. Google calls it the slimmest, fastest Nexus phone yet.

wikis.title: Nexus 5 coming to T-Mobile November 14th for $450
wikis.summary: Engadget, Nov. 8, 2013: T-Mobile will sell the 16GB Nexus 5 online November 14th and in stores November 20th at $450 total.
wikis.body:
- The Nexus 5 launched on Halloween through the Google Play Store only and sold out quickly.
- T-Mobile will offer the 16GB version online on November 14th and in stores on the 20th.
- Google sells it for $350; T-Mobile's option costs an extra $100 ($450): $42 down and $17 per month for 24 months.
- T-Mobile is not discussing plans (if any) for the 32GB version, which stays Play Store only.

wikis.title: LG Nexus 5 now available on T-Mobile US (GSMArena)
wikis.summary: GSMArena news of 14 November 2013 saying the Nexus 5 reached T-Mobile US that day, almost a week ahead of leaks, at $449.99 or $41.99 plus 24 payments of $17.
wikis.body:
- 14 November 2013: the LG Nexus 5 hits T-Mobile in the US "today", "almost a week ahead of what some leaks suggested".
- Price: $449.99 outright, or $41.99 up front then $17 for 24 months, adding up to the same total. Leasing needs a T-Mobile contract but can be exited after the device is paid in full. Not as good a bargain as the Play Store.
- Its only advantage, per the article: speed, since the Google Play store "is really unable to catch up with demand".
- Also: Verizon started selling the 5" BlackBerry Z30 exclusively at $199.99 with a two-year deal, or $549.99 upfront month to month.

wikis.title: PlayStation Killzone page returned an error
wikis.summary: The us.playstation.com Killzone PS4 page returned only an error reference, no game content.
wikis.body: The URL (us.playstation.com/ps4/games/kill-zone-ps4.html) returned "An error occurred while processing your request" with an Akamai reference number. No information about Killzone was retrieved.

wikis.title: Killzone Shadow Fall (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Guerrilla Games' 2013 PlayStation 4 launch shooter Killzone Shadow Fall: gameplay, setting, plot, release and reception.
wikis.body:
- 2013 first-person shooter by Guerrilla Games, published by Sony Computer Entertainment for PlayStation 4; director Steven ter Heide; composers Tyler Bates and Lorn; new Decima engine. Sixth installment of the Killzone series. Released 15 November 2013 (NA, PS4 launch title) and 29 November 2013 (EU).
- Set 30 years after Killzone 3; player is Lucas Kellan, a "Shadow Marshal". After "The Terracide" on Helghan, Helghast refugees live on Vekta behind "The Wall".
- Gameplay: more open-ended, stealth-capable levels; the OWL drone (attack/stun, zip line, shield, hack/scan); LSR44 rail-gun-like rifle; Echo joins in the second half. Multiplayer shipped with 10 maps, custom "Warzones", three classes (Assault, Scout, Support); 4-player co-op arrived with the Intercept expansion on 24 June 2014.
- Plot (year 2370): Kellan's father Michael is killed; Kellan becomes a Shadow Marshal under Sinclair; a bio-weapon by Dr. Hillary Massar, the Black Hand led by Vladko Tyran, Jorhan Stahl; Echo (Visari's daughter) helps Kellan; they descend to Helghan to stop Stahl.
- Reception: "mixed reception overall"; praise for visuals and multiplayer, criticism of single-player and lack of innovation. As of January 2014 it sold over 2.1 million copies, the first PS4 game past a million. Online servers shut down 12 August 2022.

wikis.title: Game Informer review of Killzone: Shadow Fall (PS4)
wikis.summary: Game Informer's Nov 15, 2013 review (score 8) calling Killzone: Shadow Fall a beautiful but unsurprising PS4 launch shooter.
wikis.body:
- Review by Dan Ryckert, Nov 15, 2013; reviewed on PlayStation 4. Publisher Sony Computer Entertainment, developer Guerrilla Games, release November 15, 2013, rated Mature. Score: 8.
- Setting: 30 years after earlier Killzone games; Vektan forces and the Helghast in a tense standoff; Helghan refugees live in slums outside Vekta City. Missions in the city and beyond the wall; environments include train stations, refugee camps and space; occasional vehicle and stealth sections.
- The OWL drone, controlled with the PS4 touchpad, has attack, shield, hack and zipline functions and is praised as more useful than allies in other shooters.
- Campaign lasts 8-10 hours; collectibles and intel drops; criticised sections are a free-fall through a collapsing city and a stealth area, neither with the OWL.
- Multiplayer: progression focused on challenges rather than XP grinding (over 1,500 challenges); Warzone mode shifts objectives within a match; Run n' Gun gives everyone an assault rifle and limited health. Fun but "don't highlight anything that hasn't been seen before".
- Verdict: "a competent shooter", "may not be the most innovative title", "one of the top stars of the PlayStation 4's launch lineup"; best gameplay in the series and a graphical showcase. Subscores: graphics stunning, sound passable, playability manageable, replay moderately high.

wikis.title: Nokia Lumia 2520 tablet available on November 22nd (Windows Experience Blog)
wikis.summary: Windows Experience Blog post of November 15, 2013 by Brandon LeBlanc on the Lumia 2520 Windows RT tablet going on sale November 22nd via AT&T.
wikis.body:
- Availability: starting November 22nd; black only from AT&T at $399.99 with a two-year agreement, or $199.99 with a two-year agreement when bundled with a Lumia 925, 1020 or 1520 Windows Phone. Pre-order from the Microsoft Store is mentioned.
- Hardware: 10.1-inch full HD display with ClearBlack technology (outdoor readability); weighs 22 ounces; up to 11 hours battery life; 6.7 megapixel rear camera with ZEISS optics; 32GB storage with microSD slot.
- Software: Windows RT 8.1 with Microsoft Office 2013 RT.
- Nokia-exclusive experiences: Nokia Storyteller (compiles pictures from Facebook, SkyDrive, Picasa, Flickr and Lumia phones into a timeline; Lumia Share app connects via NFC), Nokia Video Director, Nokia Music with Mix Radio, HERE Maps with offline support, and the Dragon's Adventure app made with DreamWorks Animation ("How to Train Your Dragon" themed).
- Nokia Power Keyboard: up to 5 additional hours of battery, touch pad, 2 full USB ports; sold separately for $149, in black and red.

wikis.title: Nokia Lumia 2520 reaches AT&T November 22nd for $400 on contract

wikis.body:
- AT&T will release the Lumia 2520 on November 22nd for $400 with a two-year data contract; black only.

wikis.title: LA Auto Show confirms 22 world debuts for 2013 (press release)
wikis.summary: Los Angeles Auto Show press release of Oct. 9, 2013 confirming 22 world debuts during Press Days, 56 vehicle debuts in all, November 19-21, 2013.
wikis.body:

- World debuts named: NISMO JUKE RS and a NISMO Concept (Nissan); four Mercedes-Benz models alongside North American introductions of the GLA 250 and S63; two new Porsche world debuts in addition to the Macan. Also global introductions from BMW, Chevrolet, Ford, Honda, Hyundai, Jaguar, Land Rover, MINI, Subaru and Toyota.
- North American debuts: BMW 4 Series Coupe, i8, i3, 5 Series Sedan and 5 Series Gran Turismo. US introductions include Jaguar C-X17, Cadillac Escalade, a Nissan high performance model, three Volkswagen vehicles including the e-Golf, and five from Audi.
- Trends: more than two dozen green vehicles; nearly 20 luxury debuts (BMW, Maserati, Mercedes-Benz); 12 planned concept cars from Jaguar, Mercedes-Benz, Subaru, Volkswagen and Volvo, plus the Cadillac Elmiraj concept.
- Quote from LA Auto Show President Lisa Kaz on Los Angeles as a media hub and car buying market.

wikis.title: Motor Authority: 22 world debuts confirmed for 2013 Los Angeles Auto Show
wikis.summary: Motor Authority article of October 9, 2013 previewing the 22 confirmed world debuts for the Los Angeles Auto Show starting November 20.
wikis.body:

- Porsche: 2015 Macan small SUV, plus two other models (one likely the 2014 911 Turbo Cabriolet).

- Press days begin 20 (November).

wikis.title: Sea-level rise and wave exposure on reef island dynamics in the Solomon Islands (Environmental Research Letters)
wikis.summary: Open-access paper (published 6 May 2016) by Albert et al. using 1947-2014 imagery of 33 Solomon Islands reef islands to show five vanished and six severely eroded, with wave exposure amplifying sea-level rise.
wikis.body:
- Authors: Simon Albert, Javier X Leon, Alistair R Grinham, John A Church, Badin R Gibbes, Colin D Woodroffe (University of Queensland, Sunshine Coast, CSIRO, Wollongong). Environ. Res. Lett. 11 054011; received 21 January 2016, accepted 19 April 2016, published 6 May 2016.
- Abstract: 33 islands, aerial/satellite imagery 1947 to 2014 plus local knowledge; five vegetated reef islands vanished and six more have severe shoreline recession; recession at two sites destroyed villages that existed since at least 1935, leading to relocations; recession rates are substantially higher where wave energy is high, indicating a synergistic interaction between sea-level rise and waves.
- Context: Solomon Islands over 1000 predominantly volcanic islands, population 560,000 over 28,000 km2; sea level rose 3 mm/yr since 1950 and 7-10 mm/yr since 1994.
- Methods: Isabel (20 reef islands) and Roviana Lagoon (12), plus Nuatambu and Mararo communities; 1947-1962 aerial photos, 2002 Ikonos, 2011 and 2014 Quickbird/Worldview-2 imagery; vegetation edge as shoreline proxy; centroid analysis; bomb-pulse radiocarbon dating of trees; CAWCR wave hindcast 1980-2009.
- Results: five of twenty Isabel islands totally eroded (Kale, Rapita, Rehana, Kakatina, Zollies, per the table; Kale 48,890 m2 to 0), six more declined over 20%; Hetaheta lost 62%, Sogomou 55%, Nuatambu village area 51%. Isabel loss rates rose from 0.1% per year (1947-1962) to 0.5% (1962-2002) to 1.9% (2002-2014); Roviana averaged about 0.1% with no change; Roviana islands were mixed (six grew slightly, six declined slightly). Ten houses at Nuatambu lost to the sea 2011-2014. Wave energy flux at Isabel was twenty-fold higher than Roviana.

wikis.title: Sea-level rise has claimed five whole islands in the Pacific (The Conversation)
wikis.summary: The Conversation article of May 6, 2016 reporting the first scientific evidence that five Solomon Islands reef islands were lost to sea-level rise and wave-driven erosion.
wikis.body:
- Published May 6, 2016. At least five reef islands in the remote Solomon Islands have been lost completely and six more severely eroded; the lost islands were one to five hectares with dense tropical vegetation at least 300 years old.
- Nuatambu Island (25 families) lost more than half its habitable area; 11 houses washed into the sea since 2011.
- First scientific evidence, published in Environmental Research Letters.
- Solomon Islands sea level has risen 7-10 mm per year since 1993, almost three times the global average of 3 mm per year (partly natural variability). Earlier studies were in areas with 3-5 mm per year.
- Method: 33 reef islands studied using aerial and satellite imagery 1947-2015, local traditional knowledge, radiocarbon dating of trees, sea-level records and wave models.
- Wave energy matters: 12 islands in a low-wave-energy area saw little change; of 21 exposed to higher wave energy, five disappeared and six eroded substantially.
- Human impact: ad hoc relocations, some communities returning to inland ancestral sites; chief Sirilo Sutaroti (94) of the Paurata tribe moved to a hilltop. Taro, capital of Choiseul Province, is set to become the first provincial capital in the world to relocate residents and services due to sea-level rise.
- Melchior Mataki (National Disaster Council) calls for support from partners and the Green Climate Fund. The Solomon Islands recently joined 11 other small Pacific nations in signing the Paris climate agreement.

wikis.title: Five Solomon Islands reef islands lost to rising seas (Common Dreams)
wikis.summary: Common Dreams report of an Environmental Research Letters study finding five Solomon Islands islands submerged by sea level rise and erosion.
wikis.body:
- Byline Nadia Prupis, 10 May 2016.
- Five Pacific islands, part of the Solomon Islands archipelago and above water as recently as 2014, were "swallowed by rising seas and coastal erosion"; Australian researchers call it the first confirmation of what climate change will bring. The islands were uninhabited.
- Six further islands have "severe shoreline recession", forcing settlements, some existing since at least 1935, to flee.
- Study published "last week" in Environmental Research Letters used aerial and satellite images dating back to 1947 across 33 islands; at least 11 islands in the northern region have totally disappeared or are severely eroding.
- Lead author Dr. Simon Albert (University of Queensland) told AFP that sea level rise in the Solomons is almost three times the global average.
- The five lost islands were one to five hectares (roughly two to 12 acres) with dense tropical vegetation at least 300 years old.
- Rates were higher where wave energy is high, indicating "a synergistic interaction between sea-level rise and waves". Researchers say these rates match what much of the Pacific can expect in the second half of the century in all but the lowest-emission scenarios.
- Relocated families used their own limited resources with little to no government or international climate fund help; communities of hundreds were fragmented.
- Melchior Mataki, chair of the Solomon Islands' Natural Disaster Council, called for support from partners and the Green Climate Fund, including nationally driven scientific studies.
- The Solomon Islands were among 175 nations that signed the Paris climate agreement in New York "last month".

wikis.title: Five Pacific islands lost to sea level rise (Mongabay)
wikis.summary: Mongabay's 2016 report on a study finding five Solomon Islands reef islands lost and six severely eroded.
wikis.body:
- Mike Gaworecki, 10 May 2016.
- Study published "last week" in Environmental Research Letters: five reef islands in the Solomon Islands completely lost to sea-level rise and coastal erosion, six more severely eroded; "believed to be the first scientific evidence" of climate impacts on Pacific islands.
- Australian team led by University of Queensland scientists used aerial and satellite imagery of 33 islands from 1947 to 2014 plus local traditional knowledge.
- "Shoreline recession at two sites has destroyed villages that have existed since at least 1935, leading to community relocations."
- Lost islands ranged one to five hectares with vegetation at least 300 years old. Nuatambu Island, home to 25 families, lost more than half its habitable area, with 11 houses washed into the sea since 2011.
- Taro, capital of Choiseul Province, "is set to become the first provincial capital in the world to relocate residents and services" due to sea-level rise.
- Earlier studies finding islands keep pace covered areas with 3-5 mm/year rise (global average about 3 mm/year); the Solomons have risen almost three times the global average, about 7-10 mm/year since 1993, partly natural variability.
- Erosion was higher in high wave energy areas ("synergistic interaction"). Researchers say many Pacific areas will see similar rates in the second half of the century in all but the lowest-emission scenarios.
- Many communities relocated inland ad hoc with no support from local government or international climate funds.

wikis.title: AMD Kaveri APU details and release date
wikis.summary: HEXUS news item, 13 November 2013, on AMD announcing Kaveri APU availability from 14 January and headline specs.
wikis.body:
- By Mark Tyson, 13 November 2013. AMD announced at the APU13 developers conference in San Jose, California that the desktop Kaveri APU will be at retail from 14 January, a week after CES2014.
- Headline figure 856 GFLOPS, on the flagship A10-7850K: 4 compute cores (two Steamroller modules) at 3.7GHz, GPU at 720MHz with 8 GCN 1.1 compute units (512 cores, similar to a Radeon HD 7750).
- Made on 28nm by GlobalFoundries. Heterogeneous system architecture: CPU and GPU share memory via hUMA.
- Steamroller cores tweaked for power, loop behaviour and floating point; L2 cache dynamically sized by power mode. Supports AMD Mantle API and TrueAudio; compatible with desktop FM2+ boards; laptop chips to follow later in the year.
- Pricing expected at CES in early January.
- Reader comments note Intel at 14nm vs AMD at 28nm and question a Steamroller FX line.

wikis.title: AMD Kaveri desktops set for January 14, more at CES 2014
wikis.summary: TechRadar news, 12 November 2013, on AMD confirming Kaveri desktop APUs from 14 January 2014 and what Kaveri is.
wikis.body:
- By Michelle Fitzsimmons, 12 November 2013. At the APU13 Developer Summit AMD said "Kaveri" will arrive in 2014 in desktops (FM2+ socket boards), notebooks, embedded systems and servers.
- After FM2+ motherboards ship to customers later this year (Senior VP Lisa Su said this is on track), Kaveri arrives in customer desktops starting 14 January 2014.
- More details due at CES 2014, "the big coming out party for Kaveri" per a 7 November phone briefing; TechRadar expects (unconfirmed) a pre-CES tech day.
- Kaveri is AMD's third-gen performance APU and first with heterogeneous system architecture (HSA) features; supports TrueAudio and Mantle. A10-7850K: four "Steamroller" cores, eight Graphics Core Next cores (512 cores), GPU 720MHz, CPU 3.7GHz; GPU takes almost 50% of the die. AMD says HSA unlocks 856 GFlops across CPU and GPU.
- hUMA makes the GPU a "first-class citizen" for memory access; heterogeneous queuing lets CPU and GPU dispatch work via queues rather than through the OS. AMD claimed first uniform visibility of the entire memory space for both.
- Pricing unknown; John Taylor said a single Kaveri APU costs less than a competitor's CPU plus GPU.
- Demo: Battlefield 4 at 1080 x 1920 on Kaveri (A10-7850K) vs an Intel Core i7 4470K with Nvidia GeForce GT630, Kaveri running nearly double the frames per second.

wikis.title: Nokia X and Nokia X+ Android phones announced
wikis.summary: GSMArena news, 24 February 2014, on Nokia's first Android-app-running phones, the Nokia X and X+ (with XL), at MWC 2014.
wikis.body:
- 24 February 2014 (MWC 2014): Nokia announced its first Android-app-running smartphones, the Nokia X and Nokia X+.
- 4" 800x480 IPS LCD (233ppi), 1GHz dual-core Qualcomm Snapdragon 8225 (X, X+ and XL), 512MB RAM (X+ and XL get 768MB), 4GB storage, microSD up to 32GB.
- 3MP fixed-focus rear camera, 129 g, 1500mAh battery: 10.5 hours 3G talk time, 17 days standby, up to 26 hours music, 8.4 hours video.
- Nokia Glance Screen; swipe right shows installed apps, another swipe reaches fastlane. Tiles resizable like Windows Phone 8 UI.
- No Google Play Services or Play Store; Stephen Elop highlighted the Nokia store and the Yandex Store for apps.
- Nokia and Microsoft apps preloaded.

wikis.title: GSMArena Mobile World Congress 2014 coverage index
wikis.summary: Index of GSMArena's articles and hands-ons from MWC 2014, held 23-27 February 2014.
wikis.body:
Coverage index dated 23-27 February 2014 listing headlines by maker:
- Nokia: Nokia X and X+ (Android), Android-powered Nokia XL "official, costs EUR109", Nokia 220 at EUR29, Asha 230, Lumia Icon hands-on.
- Samsung: Galaxy S5 with 5.1-inch screen, Tizen-based Gear 2 and Gear 2 Neo, Gear Fit, Exynos 5422 Octa and 5260 Hexa.

- HTC Desire 816 and 610; Huawei thinnest 7-inch tablet, Talkband B1, Ascend G6, MediaPad; Asus PadFone Infinity 2 and mini; Alcatel Idol 2 range; HP Slate Voicetab; ZTE Firefox OS phones (Open C, Open II) and Grand Memo II LTE; Acer Liquid E3/Z4; BlackBerry Z3 and Q20; Lenovo S-Series and Yoga Tablet 10 HD+.
- Misc: Windows Phone 8.1 update due in spring; HTC One awarded Best Smartphone and iPad Air best tablet; Qualcomm Snapdragon 801, 610, 615; MediaTek MT6732 64-bit LTE chipset; Blackphone, YotaPhone, Oppo R1.

wikis.title: Nokia introduces its first Android-powered smartphones at MWC 2014
wikis.summary: HardwareZone/Yahoo Singapore, 24 February 2014, on Nokia X, X+ and XL with prices and features.
wikis.body:
- 24 February 2014, Mobile World Congress: Nokia announced Nokia X, a family (X, X+, XL) running Android apps, Microsoft services and Nokia experiences, with a Lumia-inspired tile UI and the Fastlane screen.
- Apps from the Nokia Store, more than a dozen third-party stores, and sideloading. Includes HERE Maps with offline maps and turn-by-turn navigation, and Nokia MixRadio.
- Microsoft services: free OneDrive storage; one month of Skype Unlimited World Subscription in select markets (landlines in 60+ countries, mobiles in eight).
- Nokia X: 4-inch IPS display, 3MP camera. X+ has more memory and storage. XL: 5-inch display, 2MP front camera, 5MP autofocus camera with flash. All use a Qualcomm Snapdragon dual-core and support dual SIM.
- Availability: Nokia X immediately from EUR89 (APAC, Europe, India, Latin America, Middle East, Africa); X+ and XL from early Q2 2014 at EUR99 and EUR109.

wikis.title: Tesla Model S gets free titanium and aluminum underbody armor
wikis.summary: Ars Technica, 28 March 2014, on Tesla adding a three-part underbody shield to the Model S at no cost.
wikis.body:
- Lee Hutchinson, 28 March 2014. Elon Musk posted on Medium that all Model S vehicles built after 6 March 2014 have added titanium and aluminum underbody armor to protect the battery enclosure from puncture and reduce fire risk.
- Musk noted only two Tesla fires resulted from road accidents (one at 110 mph into and through a concrete wall) versus hundreds of thousands of gasoline vehicle fires last year.
- Three parts: a hollow aluminum bar to deflect, a titanium plate to absorb impacts, and an angled aluminum extrusion to make the car "ramp up and over" objects.
- Musk posted GIFs of the system destroying a concrete block, brushing aside a three-ball steel trailer hitch, and pulverizing an alternator.
- Negligible effect on range and handling; no sticker price increase. Existing owners can have it installed free, or automatically at next service.

wikis.title: Tesla offers Model S owners a titanium/aluminum underbody plate
wikis.summary: Electrek, 28 March 2014, on Tesla's triple underbody shield announced by Elon Musk on Medium, retrofitted free.
wikis.body:
- Seth Weintraub, 28 Mar 2014. Musk announced on Medium a triple underbody shield for the Model S, free to current owners; motivated by the two highly publicized fires, both involving punctured battery protective plates.
- Quote: "we felt it was important to bring this risk down to virtually zero to give Model S owners complete peace of mind."
- All cars with bodies manufactured from 6 March have it; Tesla service retrofits free on request or at scheduled service.
- Shield 1: rounded hollow aluminum bar that deflects objects or forces a hard object such as a three-ball tow hitch upward well forward of the battery pack (piercing plastic aeroshield and front trunk liner but leaving the car driveable). Shield 2: titanium plate protecting front underbody components. Shield 3: shallow-angle solid aluminum extrusion that absorbs energy and makes the car ramp up and over incompressible objects.
- Purely voluntary, not required by regulation; cost borne by Tesla. Electrek suggests it may help the NHTSA clear those fires.

wikis.title: Titanium underbody shield and aluminum deflector plates added to Tesla Model S
wikis.summary: Techaeris, 28 March 2014, reproducing Tesla's statement on the triple underbody shield added to the Model S.
wikis.body:
- Alex Hernandez, 28 March 2014. New titanium underbody shields and aluminium deflector plates installed on all Model S vehicles manufactured since 6 March 2014; the article reproduces Elon Musk's statement.
- Statement: two 2013 collisions caused underbody damage and fires, and got more headlines than "the other 200,000 gasoline car fires" in North America last year. Occupants walked away; a steel and ceramic firewall protects the passenger compartment. Fire odds "roughly 1 in 8,000 vehicles, are five times lower than those of an average gasoline car". A software update months earlier raised default highway ground clearance.
- Triple shield fitted from bodies made 6 March; free retrofit on request or at scheduled service. 152 vehicle-level tests: shields prevented any damage that could cause a fire or penetrate the existing quarter inch of ballistic-grade aluminum armor plate.
- The Mexico fire followed a 110 mph impact with a roundabout, a concrete curbwall, and an eight-foot concrete wall.
- Three shields: hollow aluminum bar (deflects, or forces a three-ball tow hitch to pike upward), titanium plate, shallow-angle solid aluminum extrusion (ramp up and over).
- Shields have a 0.1 percent impact on range, no effect on ride or handling, no discernible drag or lift change in wind tunnel testing. Musk: "zero deaths or serious, permanent injuries since our vehicles went into production six years ago".

wikis.title: DirectX and OpenGL may soon allow low-level hardware access
wikis.summary: Tom's Hardware, 26 February 2014, on GDC 2014 session text suggesting DirectX and OpenGL are answering AMD's Mantle.
wikis.body:
- Niels Broekhuijsen, 26 February 2014. AMD's just-released Mantle prompted apparent responses from the Khronos group (OpenGL) and Microsoft (DirectX), per GDC catalogue text spotted by Neogaf user "Dictator93".
- Direct3D session: future changes will allow "an unprecedented level of hardware control and reduced CPU rendering overhead across a broad ecosystem of hardware". DirectX has been the game developer platform "for nearly 20 years"; developers asked to get "even closer to the metal".
- OpenGL sponsored session: Graham Sellers (AMD), Tim Foley (Intel), Cass Everitt and John McDonald (NVIDIA) on cutting driver overhead "by up to 10x or more", applicable to all major vendors, with open source demos.
- "When these changes are coming, how effective they'll be, or how widely-adopted they'll be all remains to be seen"; more expected at GDC 2014.

wikis.title: DirectX and OpenGL catching up with Mantle at GDC 2014
wikis.summary: DSOGaming, 26 February 2014, on GDC 2014 session abstracts showing Direct3D and OpenGL adding low-level access to cut draw overhead.
wikis.body:
- John Papadopoulos, 26 February 2014. Per GDC slideshows, both DirectX and OpenGL will offer low-level access to reduce draw overhead, seen as performance gains on older CPUs. Nvidia had not commented on supporting Mantle (AMD's API).
- Quoted Direct3D session: future improvements allowing "an unprecedented level of hardware control and reduced CPU rendering overhead across a broad ecosystem of hardware"; DirectX "for nearly 20 years" the platform for game developers, asked to get "closer to the metal".
- Quoted OpenGL session: Graham Sellers (AMD), Tim Foley (Intel), Cass Everitt and John McDonald (NVIDIA) to present techniques reducing driver overhead "by up to 10x or more", across vendors and platforms, with open source demos.
- Unknown when first games will use them; author wonders whether Microsoft will make DX12 (or the low-level version) exclusive to Windows 8. Spotted by NeoGAF member 'Dictator93'.

wikis.title: DirectX 12 and a new OpenGL to challenge AMD Mantle coming at GDC?
wikis.summary: PC Perspective, 26 February 2014 (updated 27 February), on GDC session listings hinting at low-overhead DirectX and OpenGL.
wikis.body:
- Ryan Shrout, 26 Feb 2014; credit to The Tech Report. Session details for next month's Game Developers Conference in San Francisco suggest DirectX and OpenGL will announce changes to compete with Mantle, recently released with the Battlefield 4 patch.
- Sessions quoted: "DirectX: Evolving Microsoft's Graphics Platform" ("closer to the metal"), "DirectX: Direct3D Futures" (reduced CPU rendering overhead) and "Approaching Zero Driver Overhead in OpenGL" (Sellers/AMD, Foley/Intel, Everitt and McDonald/NVIDIA; up to 10x or more).
- Author speculates an updated DirectX 12 with similar features would shift the market and make it "hard to see anyone really sticking with the AMD-only route"; if DX12 doesn't address overhead like Mantle "all bets are off". BF4 keeps Mantle support, as will Thief (update pending).
- OpenGL description hints at methods lowering overhead without custom APIs or DX12; possibly new vendor modules or an OpenGL revision.
- Open questions: whether the new DirectX satisfies developers, how AMD reacts, Microsoft's DX12 timeframe, whether NVIDIA is relieved of pressure to build its own API.
- UPDATE 2/27/14: AMD statement says it supports lower-level APIs; "industry experts expect this to take some time", developers can use Mantle immediately, and AMD will share its API's future at GDC.

wikis.title: Ars Technica review: Diablo III Reaper of Souls
wikis.summary: Ars Technica review (28 March 2014) arguing the Reaper of Souls expansion and patches turn Diablo III into the game it wanted to be.
wikis.body:
- Rowan Kaiser, 28 Mar 2014. Expansion details: developer Blizzard, publisher Activision/Blizzard; Windows, Mac, Xbox 360, PS3, PS4; release 25 March 2014 (console versions later); $39.99, requires base Diablo III.
- Thesis: after two years of play and patching, Diablo III "is a raid simulator": a fight-chaos-loot loop every five to 10 minutes with one to four characters.
- The Auction House (real-money and gold) is gone and its removal "cannot be overstated". The loot generator now heavily weights drops toward the player's class, so each drop seems useful.
- New Crusader class ("smash-tastic"); moment-to-moment play praised; target stays locked while the mouse button is held; multiple health "cushions" prevent quick deaths.
- Adventure mode drops the plot and most geographical progression: "bounties" and Nephalem Rifts. Difficulty is now player-chosen (Normal, Hard, Expert, Master and so on) instead of Normal-Nightmare-Hell-Inferno. Within two days of launch the author had friends with level 70 Crusaders from Adventure mode.
- Fifth act centred on the fallen angel Malthael: a medieval European city, a swamp, and Pandemonium; better boss fights. Story "still excessively self-serious", with one major unresolved plotline leaving room for further expansions.
- Author says Torchlight II may beat it as an RPG and Path of Exile as competitive play, but for simple playing "Diablo III is currently unbeatable". Verdict: "Reaper Of Souls is the redemption of Diablo III".

wikis.title: Diablo III: Reaper of Souls release date March 25, 2014
wikis.summary: Engadget, 19 December 2013, on the Blizzard Store listing a 25 March 2014 release date for the Reaper of Souls expansion.
wikis.body:
- Adam Holisky, Dec. 19, 2013. The Blizzard Store listed the digital pre-order of Diablo 3's first expansion, Reaper of Souls, with a release date of March 25, 2014.
- A beta was running, opt-in via a Battle.net account page; impressions "generally favorable".
- A paid expansion, but a pre-expansion patch would give non-buyers many new systems.
- Update: Blizzard investigating pre-order issues affecting some live accounts.

wikis.title: Diablo III Reaper of Souls out March 25, 2014
wikis.summary: Game Informer, 19 December 2013, on the release date, editions and prices of the Diablo III expansion.
wikis.body:
- Mike Futter, Dec 19, 2013. Diablo III's first expansion Reaper of Souls releases March 25, 2014, with the Crusader class, a loot system revamp and new end-game content; pre-purchase in physical and digital versions.
- Standard edition $39.99. Digital deluxe $59.99: exclusive helm and transmogrification recipes, spectral hound pet, three more character slots, a treasure goblin pet for World of Warcraft, StarCraft II crusader portrait and Malthael decals.
- Physical collector's edition $79.99: all deluxe bonuses plus hardcover art book, two-disc blu-ray and behind-the-scenes DVD set, and a Malthael mouse pad.
- No release date announced for the PlayStation 4 version, the Ultimate Evil Edition, which includes Reaper of Souls content and lets PS3 players move characters over. Source: Blizzard.

wikis.title: Nadella announces Office for iPad at public debut
wikis.summary: Fortune, 27 March 2014, on Satya Nadella's first public press conference as Microsoft CEO announcing Word, Excel and PowerPoint for iPad.
wikis.body:
- JP Mangalindan, March 27, 2014. In his first public press conference as CEO, Satya Nadella announced iPad versions of Word, Excel and PowerPoint, "available today".
- Nadella: "Today's briefing is all about giving you the first step on a journey"; vision of a "critical intersection of mobile and cloud", platform-agnostic and developer-friendly.
- Julia White (General Manager) demoed touch-friendly UI with features such as Word's Ribbon.
- Freemium: free to download, view and present; an Office 365 subscription is required to edit. White: "This is just the beginning."
- Announced 52 days after Nadella replaced Steve Ballmer. Office accounted for 90% of revenues of the business division last fiscal year. John Case (VP Marketing): aim to turn Office into "a first-class cloud service".

wikis.title: Microsoft unveils Office for iPad in big mobile move
wikis.summary: NBC News, 27 March 2014, on Nadella's first public event launching Office for iPad and his mobile-first push.
wikis.body:
- March 27, 2014 (updated 3:58 PM EDT). Nadella unveiled Office for iPad at his first public event, in San Francisco; Word, Excel and PowerPoint available from 11 p.m. PT Thursday in Apple's App Store.
- Free for Office 365 subscribers (Office 365 starts at $70 per year); non-subscribers get a read-only version.
- Julia White said it is "definitely not the Windows app ported to the iPad"; tablet features include a numeric keyboard in Excel and a touch "laser pointer" in PowerPoint.
- Tim Cook tweeted: "Welcome to the #iPad and @AppStore! @satyanadella and Office for iPad". Box CEO Aaron Levie: "Better late than never."
- Nadella (52 days in) also introduced a "personal" Office 365 for $70 per year on one device (vs $100 annually for a premium five-device subscription). Office Mobile for iPhone launched last June; OneNote for Mac earlier in March.
- Build begins April 2, where a Windows update is expected; rumors include new Nokia devices, a Surface mini tablet and a Siri rival called "Cortana".

wikis.title: Microsoft Office for the iPad is (finally) here
wikis.summary: TIME, 27 March 2014, on Microsoft launching Word, Excel and PowerPoint for iPad at Satya Nadella's first public event as CEO.
wikis.body:
- Harry McCracken, MAR 27, 2014. Office for iPad announced at a San Francisco press conference on Microsoft's cloud and mobile strategy, Nadella's first public appearance since replacing Steve Ballmer; apps available from 2PM ET.
- Word, Excel, PowerPoint; OneNote already had a free iPad edition. Not feature-complete replicas of the Windows versions but "considerably richer" than minimum viable ones: Word edits charts in place and supports collaborative editing with redlined changes and threaded comments; touch-friendly Ribbon. Files save to OneDrive by default.
- Not sold stand-alone: free to view files and display PowerPoint; creating and editing needs Office 365, from $70 per year. This positions it as a complement to Windows Office, not directly competing with Apple's iWork (Pages, Numbers, Keynote).
- Author had believed Microsoft would wait for a touch-centric "Metro" Office for Windows 8; that version was acknowledged earlier but unmentioned at the event.
- Assessment: not game-changing; biggest benefit may be file compatibility/formatting fidelity.

wikis.title: Qualcomm Snapdragon 805 performance preview (page 1)
wikis.summary: Tom's Hardware preview (31 July 2014) whose captured page introduces the Snapdragon 805's architecture, memory bandwidth and Krait 450 CPU; the benchmark pages are not captured.
wikis.body:
- Matt Humrick, 31 July 2014. Eight-page article; only page 1 ("Snapdragon Becomes Snappier") is captured (later pages cover GPU/4K, test methodology, CPU/web/GPU/GPGPU results, and a conclusion titled "The 805 Extends Snapdragon's Performance Advantage").
- Background: Snapdragon powers over 1350 announced or available devices; per Strategy Analytics, more than half of smartphone SoC revenue in Q3 2013. Started in 2008 with Snapdragon S1 (Adreno 200, Scorpion CPU, 65 nm, up to 1 GHz). 2013 brought Krait and Snapdragon 400/600/800; the 800 has Adreno 330 (450 MHz) and Krait 400 quad-core up to 2.26 GHz. Snapdragon 801: GPU 578 MHz, CPU up to 2.45 GHz, ISP 465 MHz (vs 320 in 800).
- Snapdragon 805: Krait 450 CPU, Gobi 9x35 modem (up to 300 Mb/s LTE Advanced CAT6), improved ISP, Adreno 420 GPU; reps call it the first commercially available mobile SoC supporting 4K viewing.
- Krait 450 is the last Krait and last high-end 32-bit Qualcomm SoC; a new 64-bit ARMv8 CPU architecture comes with Snapdragon 810 in 2015. Four cores, 4 KB + 4 KB L0, 16 KB + 16 KB L1, shared 2 MB L2; 28 nm HPm process like Krait 400; peak frequency up from 2.45 to 2.65 GHz. Krait: 11-stage pipeline, fetch/decode three instructions per clock, execute four in parallel, 40-entry reorder buffer; Apple Cyclone is six-wide with 192 micro-ops.
- Memory: 32-bit quad-channel bus with LPDDR3-800, 25.6 GB/s peak: twice Snapdragon 800 (12.8 GB/s) and about 70% more than 801 (14.9 GB/s); reserved for the Adreno 420 GPU.
- Reader comments (54) discuss 64-bit, Tegra K1 absence and chart scaling.

wikis.title: Nokia Lumia 930, 630 and 635 announced at Build 2014
wikis.summary: Microsoft Devices Blog, 2 April 2014, on Stephen Elop announcing three Lumia phones with Windows Phone 8.1 and update plans.
wikis.body:
- April 2, 2014, at Microsoft's Build Developer Conference 2014: Stephen Elop announced Nokia Lumia 930 (flagship), Lumia 630 (most affordable, first dual-SIM Lumia) and Lumia 635 (4G/LTE), all with Windows Phone 8.1, in bright orange, bright green, bright yellow, black and white.
- Lumia 930: 20MP PureView camera with ZEISS optics and OIS; Rich Recording; Living Images; 2.2GHz Snapdragon quad-core, 2GB RAM; four microphones; Dolby Surround; 5-inch 1080p ClearBlack (441ppi); LTE-ready; 2420 mAh battery; wireless charging. Rolling out globally in June (Europe, Asia, India, Middle East) from $599 before taxes and subsidies.
- Lumia 630/635: quad-core Snapdragon, 4.5-inch ClearBlack screen, Nokia Camera, HERE maps, free MixRadio, and new SensorCore low-power motion sensing with Bing Health and Fitness (SDK piloted with select partners). Lumia 630 expected in May starting in Asia, Russia, China, India and Europe, from $159 single-SIM and $169 dual-SIM; Lumia 635 from $189, broadly available including the US "starting this summer".
- Windows Phone 8.1 comes as an over-the-air update starting this summer for all Lumia Windows Phone 8 phones (including 1520, 1020, 520): LiveTiles, Word Flow keyboard, Action Center, Cortana (starting in the US), enterprise pack. A Lumia Cyan update bundles 8.1 with new Lumia features (camera roll, Creative Studio, Nokia Storyteller). Imaging SDK 1.2 BETA available that day at developer.nokia.com.

wikis.title: Nokia Lumia 930, 630 and 635 are first Windows Phone 8.1 handsets
wikis.summary: Silicon UK, 3 April 2014, on Nokia's three Lumia phones running Windows Phone 8.1 with prices and specs.
wikis.body:
- Steve McCaskill, April 3, 2014. Nokia showed the first three phones running Windows Phone 8.1 and said all existing Nokia Windows Phone 8 handsets will eventually receive the update, packaged with Nokia features such as Sensorcore, through an OTA update called Lumia Cyan.
- Lumia 930, the "flagship embodiment" of 8.1: 2.2 GHz quad-core Qualcomm Snapdragon 800, 2GB RAM, 32GB storage, no MicroSD but 7GB OneDrive cloud storage; metal and polycarbonate casing; five-inch Clearblack full HD; 20MP PureView camera with Zeiss optics; Qi wireless charging; LTE and NFC. $599 (GBP360), June.
- Lumia 630 (single- and dual-SIM) and 635 (4G): 1.2GHz Snapdragon 400 quad-core, 512MB RAM, 8GB storage expandable up to 128GB via MicroSD, 5MP cameras, 4.5-inch full HD displays; colours orange, bright green, bright yellow, white, black. HERE Maps, Office, Nokia Camera and Mix Radio. Lumia 635 $189 (GBP115) this summer; Lumia 630 $159 (GBP95) single-SIM, $169 (GBP100) dual-SIM in May.
- Windows Phone 8.1 adds new live tile settings, Cortana and enterprise mobility options. Stephen Elop is quoted on "the best of Lumia and the best of Microsoft".

wikis.title: Windows 8.1 Update arrives April 8, mouse and keyboard friendly
wikis.summary: Ars Technica, 2 April 2014, on Microsoft announcing an April 8 release for the Windows 8.1 Update and its mouse/keyboard-oriented changes.
wikis.body:
- Andrew Cunningham, Apr 2, 2014. At Build in San Francisco Microsoft set a release date: the Windows 8.1 Update (formerly Update 1) arrives via Windows Update for all Windows 8.1 users on April 8, Patch Tuesday. It had leaked, downloadable from Microsoft's servers for a couple of days early last month.
- Changes for mouse and keyboard users: full-screen Modern apps can be pinned to the desktop taskbar and the taskbar works inside Modern apps; new PC settings tile plus dedicated power and search buttons on the Start screen; systems without touchscreens boot to the desktop by default.
- Criticism: the changes make the interface less consistent and won't satisfy people who want nothing to do with the Start screen and Modern apps; bigger changes may wait for the next Windows version, possibly discussed later at Build.
- Tuned to run well on devices with 1GB RAM and 16GB storage (about half the current minimum), to let OEMs cut low-end Windows tablet prices.
- The update was about 700MB when downloaded last month; Windows 8 users must first install 8.1 from the Windows Store.

wikis.title: Microsoft shows off Windows 8.1 Update 1
wikis.summary: TechCrunch, 2 April 2014, brief note on Microsoft demoing Windows 8.1 Update 1 at Build with an April 8 rollout.
wikis.body:
- Alex Wilhelm, 9:34 AM PDT, April 2, 2014. Microsoft showed Windows 8.1 Update 1 at Build; the tweaks help the OS work better with traditional inputs; rollout begins via Windows Update on April 8th.
- Non-touch devices will boot to the desktop; Metro apps can be pinned to the desktop taskbar; improved app closing. Internet Explorer 11 gets an update supporting legacy line-of-business applications.
- The update was broadly leaked through a registry tweak earlier this year, so its feature set was unsurprising. Further coverage promised.

wikis.title: Microsoft unveils Windows 8.1 Update 1: new features (Fox News / Digital Trends)
wikis.summary: Fox News republication (Digital Trends), 2 April 2014, listing Windows 8.1 Update 1 changes announced at Build 2014.
wikis.body:
- By Digital Trends, published April 2, 2014, updated November 4, 2015. At Build 2014 Microsoft detailed Windows 8.1 Update 1, the first significant Windows update since October, a free update for Windows 8 and 8.1 users on April 8 (Patch Tuesday).
- Boot and resume straight to the classic desktop, bypassing the Modern UI.
- Taskbar: Windows Store apps work on the desktop taskbar; a new taskbar button opens the Windows Store; the taskbar is reachable in Modern apps by moving the pointer to the bottom of the screen.
- Start screen: dedicated Power and Search buttons (power off without the Charms menu); newly installed Modern apps labelled "New"; right-click opens a drop-down menu instead of the bottom bar.
- "a minor refresh as opposed to a dramatic makeover". Minimum requirements drop to 1GB RAM and 16GB storage.

wikis.title: World's largest solar array, Agua Caliente, set for 290 megawatts
wikis.summary: Scientific American, 9 May 2014, on the completion of the Agua Caliente photovoltaic plant in Arizona.
wikis.body:
- Roni Jacobson, May 9, 2014 (correction noted 5/9/14). Agua Caliente, the largest photovoltaic solar facility in the world, was completed "last week" in Arizona between Yuma and Phoenix: more than five million panels spanning the equivalent of two Central Parks, generating 290 megawatts, enough for 230,000 California homes at peak capacity. Article opens by citing a White House climate report released Tuesday.
- Four years earlier the largest US solar facility produced 20 megawatts. Total cost $1.8 billion; received a "million-dollar loan" from the DoE Loan Programs Office (per the text), under the "SunShot" initiative. Peter Davidson (DoE): "Solar has completely arrived as a competitive energy resource."
- Owned by NRG Energy with MidAmerican Solar; operated and maintained for NRG by First Solar (Tempe, Ariz.), using thin-film panels. NRG sells the power to Pacific Gas & Electric for 25 years. California law requires utilities to get 33 percent from renewables by 2020.
- It probably will not hold the record long (e.g. Antelope Valley Solar Ranch One in the Mojave). Solar is 1 percent of US energy production, the fastest-growing sector (NREL's Robert Margolis).
- Downsides: hard to maintain and, per some environmental groups, displaces wildlife; many California legislators prefer small-scale plants nearer users. Extra panels let the control system compensate for cloud cover (John Karam, NRG Solar).

wikis.title: Agua Caliente Solar Project, Arizona
wikis.summary: Power Technology project profile of the 290MW Agua Caliente photovoltaic plant in Yuma County, Arizona.
wikis.body:
- Power Technology project page dated May 2 2014 (author Krishna).
- 290MW photovoltaic plant in east Yuma County, Arizona, US; annual output 626.2GWh; estimated investment $1.8bn.
- Construction started 2010; completed April 2014. Developed in two phases.
- Owners: NRG Energy and MidAmerican Energy Holdings; developer First Solar. Described as "currently the world's biggest photovoltaic solar power plant".
- Originally initiated by NextLight Renewable Power, acquired by First Solar on 12 July 2010. NRG Energy acquired the project from First Solar in August 2011; MidAmerican bought a 49% stake in January 2012.
- More than five million thin-film cadmium telluride PV modules; 400 SMA Sunny Central inverter units.
- Serves around 225,000 average homes and will cut 5.5 million metric tonnes of CO2 annually.
- Pacific Gas & Electric (PG&E) buys all output under a 25 year power purchase agreement.
- Named 'Project of the Year' by Excellence in Renewable Energy awards in February 2012.
- Built on previously disturbed agricultural land at White Wing Ranch, chosen for solar resource and proximity to the Hassayampa-North Gila 500kV transmission line, so little new transmission was needed.
- Related project mentioned: Topaz Solar Farm, California (550MW, under construction).

wikis.title: DOE/EA-1797: Agua Caliente Solar Project environmental assessment
wikis.summary: US Department of Energy page for the environmental assessment of a federal loan guarantee for the 290MW Agua Caliente solar project in Yuma County, Arizona.
wikis.body:
- DOE/EA-1797 analyses the potential environmental impacts of providing a federal loan guarantee to Agua Caliente Solar, LLC.
- The loan guarantee is for construction and operation of a 290 megawatt gross output photovoltaic solar power project and an associated interconnection transmission line, Yuma County, Arizona.
- Documents listed for download: Finding of No Significant Impact, and the Final Environmental Assessment (contents not included in the page text).

wikis.title: Windows Store refresh makes it easier to find apps
wikis.summary: Windows Experience Blog post (13 May 2014, Brandon LeBlanc) describing a Windows 8.1 Store update with a persistent navigation bar, collections and featured titles.
wikis.body:
- Published May 13, 2014 by Brandon LeBlanc on the Windows Experience Blog.
- Follows the Windows 8.1 Update released the previous month, which let users pin Store apps to the taskbar (Store pinned by default).
- The new update focuses on Store enhancements based on customer feedback, rolling out that day.
- Changes listed:
  1. Persistent navigation bar with Top charts, Categories and Collections (previously needed a swipe or right-click); Account info still accessible.
  2. Collections on the Store landing page, curated by a team of experts, e.g. a Getting Started Collection and theme collections (music, travel, sports) plus Red Stripe Deals, where 6 top apps and games are discounted at least 50% each week.
  3. Multiple Featured titles grouped on the landing page.
- The text is cut off after item 3.

wikis.title: Windows 8.1 Store and Windows Update client improvements: May 13, 2014
wikis.summary: Microsoft Support article listing the Windows Store and Windows Update features enabled by the May 13, 2014 update for Windows 8.1, RT 8.1 and Server 2012 R2.
wikis.body:
- Applies to Windows 8.1 (Enterprise, Pro), Windows RT 8.1 and Windows Server 2012 R2 editions. The update has a prerequisite.
- Store features: persistent navigation bar at the top (Top Free, Top Paid, Top Grossing, Best Rated, Picks for You, Collections, account info); more prominent app collections and a new Collections page; a few collections on the home page and in search results; "Install All" for certain collections.
- Universal apps badge for apps bought once and usable on both Windows 8.1 and Windows Phone 8.1.
- Discount info shown on home page, search results, lists and description pages; promotional pricing and expiry next to the Buy button.
- App description page: larger screenshots, universal apps and hardware requirements identified, improved post-acquisition recommendations, privacy shortcut in the charms.
- Hardware targeting filters touch-required apps out of the live tile, Spotlight and "Picks for You" on non-touch PCs; a warning shows when selecting one.
- Windows Update: integrates with SleepStudy for diagnostics; improved performance, resiliency and authenticated proxy support.
- Obtainable via Windows Update.

wikis.title: Google Glass open beta for any US resident, with IHS teardown
wikis.summary: HEXUS article (14 May 2014) on Google Glass going on sale to any US resident for $1,500 and IHS's teardown cost estimate.
wikis.body:
- By Mark Tyson, 14 May 2014.
- A month earlier Google let any US resident buy Glass for one day; now it is moving "to a more open beta" for US residents, while stocks last. Aim: expand the number of 'Explorers'.
- Price stays $1,500. The finalised consumer version is "expected to go on sale towards the end of this year".
- Teardown.com earlier put components, manufacturing and testing at about $80. IHS estimates a BOM of $132.47 plus $20 manufacturing, a base total of $152.47.
- IHS's Andrew Rassweiler: most of the cost is non-material (non-recurring engineering, software and platform development, tooling); Glass "feels like a prototype" with many off-the-shelf components and mature ICs such as the 45nm TI OMAP4430 apps processor.

wikis.title: Google launches Glass open beta at $1,500
wikis.summary: The Next Web article (13 May 2014, Emil Protalinski) reporting that anyone in the US can buy the Glass Explorer Edition for $1,500.
wikis.body:
- Published May 13, 2014.
- Google opened Glass to all in the US: the Explorer edition is on sale at google.com/glass for $1,500 with no invite needed.
- Less than a week earlier Google said it was accelerating "new ways to expand the program in the weeks and months ahead". The wider consumer launch is "still slated for later this year".
- The article suggests the earlier one-day sale went well enough to justify a broader test.
- Google also posted a thank-you video to early Explorer members.

wikis.title: Google shatters the Glass ceiling
wikis.summary: Fortune article (14 May 2014, Laura Lorenzetti) on Google selling Glass to anyone in the US for $1,500.
wikis.body:
- Anyone in the US with $1,500 can buy Google Glass, per a Google blog post. Follows last month's one-day sale; the company said it nearly ran out of stock due to "overwhelming" interest and has rebuilt inventory.
- Glass remains in beta; a consumer version is expected later this year.
- The Explorers program began about two years earlier to refine the hardware and software.
- Buyers choose colour, earbud type and frame style, including prescription lens and sunglass options.
- A linked story says the cost to make Glass is just $152.47.

wikis.title: Watch Dogs confirmed for 27th May launch, except Wii U
wikis.summary: HEXUS news (7 March 2014) on Ubisoft confirming a 27 May release date for Watch Dogs on all platforms but Wii U.
wikis.body:
- By Mark Tyson, 7 March 2014.
- Ubisoft confirmed the date via the Watch Dogs Twitter feed: "The Watch_Dogs release date has been confirmed. Resuming Transmissions".
- Release 27 May (2014) for PC, Xbox 360, Xbox One, PlayStation 3 and PlayStation 4. No date for Wii U; Polygon reports a senior producer said a 2014 Wii U ship date is still a "possibility".
- Originally expected as a launch title on next-gen consoles before Christmas, it was delayed to spring so the team could "polish and fine tune every detail"; Ubisoft called it a "tough decision". The delay may have irked Sony, which had prepared a Watch Dogs PS4 bundle.
- Story trailer leaked on Xbox.com. Protagonist Aiden Pearce was a hacker and thief; he discovered something he was "never meant to see" and payback follows.

wikis.title: Ubisoft Confirm Watch Dogs Release Date
wikis.summary: Vortez news (6 March 2014, Tim Harmer) on Ubisoft's official announcement of the 27 May 2014 Watch Dogs release.
wikis.body:
