- Posted 06.03.2014. Ubisoft officially announced the date after a leak on XBOX.com earlier that day: 27th May 2014.
- Setting: a future Chicago run by a Central Operating System; player is Aiden Pierce (spelling per this page).
- Platforms: PC, PS3, PS4, Xbox 360, Xbox One. Pre-order prices start from 32.99 (currency symbol garbled), with special editions.
- Author advises waiting on reviews. Related stories cover an earlier delay announcement (16.10.2013).

wikis.title: Watch Dogs (video game): overview and gameplay
wikis.summary: First part of the Wikipedia article on Ubisoft's 2014 action-adventure Watch Dogs, covering its overview, release, reception and gameplay.
wikis.body:
- 2014 action-adventure game developed by Ubisoft Montreal, published by Ubisoft; first in the Watch Dogs series. Director Jonathan Morin, producer Dominic Guay, writer Kevin Shortt, composer Brian Reitzell (infused with krautrock). Third-person, single-player plus online multiplayer for up to eight players.
- Release dates: May 27, 2014 worldwide for Windows, PS3, PS4, Xbox 360, Xbox One; Wii U on November 18, 2014 (NA), November 20 (AU), November 21 (EU); Stadia December 9, 2020.
- Set in a fictionalized Chicago in 2013; grey hat hacker and vigilante Aiden Pearce seeks revenge after his niece is killed in a botched assassination attempt.
- Development began in 2009 and ran over five years, with more than a thousand people across Ubisoft studios. Field research in Chicago; hacking features made with Kaspersky Lab; control system based on SCADA. Announced June 2012.
- Reception: "generally favorable"; praise for gameplay, mission and open-world design, combat, hacking; criticism of technical issues, graphics discrepancy between marketing and the real game, plot and protagonist.
- Sales: record biggest first-day sales of a Ubisoft game and biggest UK new-IP launch at the time; over 10 million copies shipped. Sequels: Watch Dogs 2 (November 2016), Watch Dogs: Legion (October 2020).
- Gameplay: Aiden uses a smartphone to control trains and traffic lights, infiltrate security systems, jam phones, view pedestrians' data and empty bank accounts. Open-world Chicago with day-night cycle and dynamic weather. Weapons include an extensible truncheon, handguns, shotguns, sniper rifles, machine guns, grenade launchers; lethal and non-lethal approaches. Vehicles include motorcycles, muscle cars, SUVs, speedboats. Radio has about fifty songs. Reputation system, skill tree, minigames, QR code and audio log collectibles, ctOS towers unlock map icons and side missions.

wikis.title: Ubisoft reveals Watch Dogs release date (press release)
wikis.summary: Ubisoft press release (London, 6 March 2014) announcing Watch Dogs' worldwide release on 27 May 2014.
wikis.body:
- Posted 6 Mar 2014. Watch Dogs to release worldwide on May 27, 2014; Wii U version "at a later date".
- Players take the role of Aiden Pearce, a vigilante who hacks Chicago's central operating system (ctOS) via smartphone.
- Geoffroy Sardin (EMEA SVP Sales and Marketing, Ubisoft): extra time for the dev team "will be more than worth the wait".
- PS3 and PS4 buyers get exclusive access to 60 minutes of additional gameplay via PlayStation Network; Michael Pattison (VP Third Party Relations, SCEE) calls PlayStation a preferred destination.
- Platforms: PS4, PS3, Xbox One, Xbox 360, Windows PC.

wikis.title: 2014 24 Hours of Le Mans: overview, results and pre-race context
wikis.summary: First part of the Wikipedia article on the 82nd 24 Hours of Le Mans (11-15 June 2014), covering the result summary, schedule, standings and circuit changes.
wikis.body:
- 82nd 24 Hours of Le Mans, held 11 to 15 June 2014 (race 14-15 June) at the Circuit de la Sarthe, organised by the ACO; third round of eight in the 2014 FIA World Endurance Championship. About 263,000 spectators, the largest crowd since 1989. Schedule moved forward one week to avoid clashes with other series.
- Overall winner: Audi R18 e-tron quattro of Marcel Fassler, Andre Lotterer, Benoit Treluyer (their third win as a trio after 2011 and 2012), Audi's thirteenth win since 1999. Toyota TS040 Hybrid led half the distance before stopping; Audi's Kristensen/Gene/di Grassi finished second, three laps back after turbocharger replacements; Davidson/Buemi/Lapierre's Toyota third.
- LMP1-L: Rebellion-Toyota of Heidfeld, Beche, Prost, sole finisher. LMP2: Jota Sport Zytek-Nissan (Dolan, Turvey, Tincknell) ahead of TDS Racing Ligier-Nissan by less than a lap. LMGTE Pro: AF Corse Ferrari 458 Italia (Bruni, Fisichella, Vilander). LMGTE Am: Aston Martin Racing (Heinemeier Hansson, Poulsen, Thiim).
- Championship after the race: Davidson/Lapierre/Buemi lead drivers with 80 points; Fassler/Treluyer/Lotterer second on 60; Toyota's manufacturers' lead over Audi cut to one point, Porsche third, five races left.
- Pre-race: Toyota led the drivers' standings on 50 points and the manufacturers' on 84 (48 points ahead of second-placed Porsche; third-placed Audi had 28); Toyota had won the previous two races.
- Circuit and rules: after Allan Simonsen's death in the 2013 race, Tertre Rouge re-profiled, new barriers and tyre walls, bigger Corvette run-off, Tecpro barriers at Porsche curves, kerbs at the second Ford chicane. New "slow zone" system (60 km/h, GPS-monitored) allows marshal intervention without a full safety car. Rookies and drivers absent five years need half-day simulator training.

wikis.title: 2014 24 Hours of Le Mans by the numbers
wikis.summary: FIA WEC news item (17/06/2014) summarising records and podium statistics from the 2014 Le Mans 24 Hours by class.
wikis.body:
- Dated 17/06/2014.
- LMP1: Audi Sport Team Joest's Fassler, Lotterer, Treluyer won their third Le Mans in four years; Audi's 13th overall victory in 15 years, sixth consecutive win, the last six with TDI diesel technology; Michelin's 17th consecutive overall win. Marc Gene (late switch back to Audi) scored his fourth overall podium; Lucas di Grassi a second podium. Tom Kristensen missed a 10th overall win after turbo problems on the No.1 car but took his 14th podium including nine wins. Toyota's second consecutive podium; first at Le Mans for Nicolas Lapierre. Rebellion Racing's R-One finished fourth (Heidfeld, Prost, Beche), exceeding its aim of finishing.
- LMP2: JOTA Sport (Simon Dolan, Oliver Turvey, Harry Tincknell) won on debut; second consecutive Nissan-engined podium sweep; Dunlop's third consecutive class sweep and fourth consecutive LMP2 win. Thiriet by TDS Racing's Ligier took the marque's first podium in 39 years; Alpine's first since the 1978 overall win. Matt McMurry (Caterham/Greaves) became the youngest driver to start and finish, age 16.
- LMGTE Pro: AF Corse (Bruni, Vilander, Fisichella) second class win together, third podium together; third class win for Bruni (first in 2008). Porsche 911 RSR podium second year running.
- LMGTE Am: No.95 Aston Martin Racing Vantage V8, all-Danish crew, won in memory of 2013 team mate Allan Simonsen; Kristian Poulsen second class win, Nicki Thiim won on debut. Proton Competition Porsche No.88 (Ried, al Qubaisi, Bachler) third... first podium for all three.

wikis.title: Le Mans 2014 - Audi, the 13th
wikis.summary: ACO report (15/06/2014) on the 2014 24 Hours of Le Mans, with a record crowd of 263,300 and Audi's 13th win.
wikis.body:
- Dated 15/06/2014. Record attendance of 263,300.
- LMP1: after 90 minutes a downpour on the Mulsanne Straight caused accidents affecting the No.3 Audi (Bonanomi) and slowed the No.8 Toyota (Lapierre). The No.7 Toyota had nearly a lap lead at halfway before stopping at Arnage with electrical trouble (Nakajima: "It tears my heart out"). The No.1 Audi (Kristensen, di Grassi, Gene) then stopped with turbo issues. Porsche led on its return to the top class, with a close Webber/Lotterer battle, but retired with mechanical issues two hours from the finish.
- Winner: No.2 Audi of Fassler-Lotterer-Treluyer, third for the trio and Audi's 13th; No.1 Audi second three laps back; Toyota third (Davidson-Lapierre-Buemi); Rebellion fourth. Gene was called in to replace Loic Duval after a Wednesday accident.
- LMP2: Zytek-Nissan (Dolan-Tincknell-Turvey) won, fifth overall; Turvey was called up Thursday to replace Gene. Ligier (Badey-Thiriet-Gommendy) second; Alpine third.
- LMGTE Pro: No.51 AF Corse Ferrari (Bruni, Vilander, Fisichella) won, second time for the trio after 2012; Corvette C7.R debuted, No.74 a lap behind; Aston Martin No.97 retired in the 18th hour after setting fastest lap 3:53.763; Porsche No.92 third.
- LMGTE Am: No.95 Aston Martin (Poulsen, Heinemeier Hansson, Thiim) three laps ahead of Proton Porsche No.88 and AF Corse Ferrari No.61.

wikis.title: Civilization Revolution sequel coming to iOS next week
wikis.summary: Ars Technica (23 June 2014, Kyle Orland) on 2K and Firaxis announcing a Civilization Revolution sequel for iOS on July 2.
wikis.body:
- 2K Games and Firaxis announced the long-requested sequel arrives on iOS "next Wednesday, July 2" (2014). Consoles are left out as 2K takes a mobile focus.
- Few details; promo shots show leaders like Winston Churchill and Abraham Lincoln. The game will "stay true to the series": wage war, conduct diplomacy, discover technologies, build the most powerful empire.
- No price announced, but it is "launching as a premium title".
- Original Civilization Revolution was a console-friendly version of the PC series, first on Xbox 360, PS3 and Nintendo (text cut off).

wikis.title: 2K launches Civilization Revolution 2 for iOS
wikis.summary: MacRumors (2 July 2014, Richard Padilla) reporting the App Store launch of Civilization Revolution 2 at $14.99.
wikis.body:
- Wednesday July 2, 2014: Civilization Revolution 2 launched on the App Store; turn-based like the first title.
- Features: new units (Aircraft Carriers, Jet Fighters, Special Forces); new tech (Lasers, Modern Medicine, Information Technology); new buildings/wonders (Nuclear Power Plant, The Red Cross, Silicon Valley); enhanced 3D graphics; Scenario Mode challenges.
- 2K says it is the first in the series developed exclusively for mobile devices.
- Price $14.99; original Civilization Revolution for iOS is $2.99. 2K will release Civilization: Beyond Earth on Mac in the fall.

wikis.title: A new Civilization Revolution game on the block
wikis.summary: TIME (2 July 2014, Matt Peckham) on the low-key launch of Civilization Revolution 2 for iOS at $15.
wikis.body:
- Sequel to 2008's Civilization Revolution, available on iOS App Store for about $15, with an Android version to follow "later this year". Little pre-release press.
- Author says Firaxis designed the original (consoles first, then mobile and DS); 2K China handled the iOS port and appears to be behind the sequel, known mostly for ports.
- 2K's standalone Civilization Revolution site does not mention the game. Compatibility: iPhone 4S+, iPad 2+, iPad Mini 1+, iPod Touch 5.
- Features: new units (Aircraft Carriers, Jet Fighters, SpecOps Infantry), tech (Lasers, Medicine, Information Tech), buildings/wonders (Nuclear Power Plant, Red Cross, Silicon Valley), 3D graphics (originals were 2D), scenario challenges.

wikis.title: 'Sailor Moon Crystal' trailer and July 5 air date
wikis.summary: HuffPost (5 June 2014, Sara Roncero-Menendez) on the trailer and final air date for the Sailor Moon reboot.
wikis.body:
- Published Jun 5, 2014 (updated Dec 6, 2017).
- "Sailor Moon Crystal", a reboot of the 1992 Japanese animated series, has a final air date after a brief delay: to air in Japan on July 5 and simulcast worldwide. It premieres 22 years after the original.
- Trailer shows Usagi Tsukino getting ready for school, then transforming into Sailor Moon and introducing the Sailor Scouts.
- Animation closely mirrors the original manga; some fans dislike the "expressionless" faces.
- New music from pop group Momoiro Clover Z and the return of voice actress Kotono Mitsuishi as Sailor Moon, both praised by most fans.

wikis.title: Sailor Moon Crystal to premiere on Neon Alley and Hulu on July 5, 2014
wikis.summary: Viz Media press release (19 June 2014) reposted by Anime Herald announcing simultaneous North American streaming of Sailor Moon Crystal.
wikis.body:
- Anime Herald post by Samantha Ferreira, June 19, 2014; source Viz Media, San Francisco.
- Sailor Moon Crystal premieres July 5 on Hulu and Neon Alley, simultaneous with the Japanese streaming premiere; free streaming episodes. Subtitled episodes then arrive on the first and third Saturday of each month.
- Rated 'TV-PG'; based on Naoko Takeuchi's manga (published in North America by Kodansha); Usagi Tsukino searches for fellow Sailor Guardians and the Legendary Silver Crystal to stop Queen Beryl.
- Neon Alley is Viz's free streaming destination; also on ad-supported Hulu and Hulu Plus on devices like Xbox One, PS3/PS4, Roku, Chromecast, mobile.
- Charlene Ingram (Senior Manager, Animation Marketing): "More than two decades after it first captivated millions of fans... returns in a big way". Viz uploaded a translated trailer to YouTube.

wikis.title: Pretty Guardian Sailor Moon Crystal (ONA 2014) - Anime News Network entry
wikis.summary: ANN encyclopedia entry for Sailor Moon Crystal with plot, ratings, episode count, air dates and theme songs.
wikis.body:
- Listed as ONA 2014; alternate retelling of Sailor Moon (TV). Sequels: Crystal ONA 2015, Season III (TV 2016), Eternal (movie), Cosmos the Movie. (c) Naoko Takeuchi / PNP / Kodansha / Toei Animation.
- Genres: action, drama, magic, romance; themes: aliens, magical girl, monsters, past-life, reincarnation, sentai. Objectionable content: mild.
- Plot: Usagi Tsukino, a second-year middle school girl, meets talking cat Luna and learns she can transform into Sailor Moon; she must find the Illusionary Silver Crystal and other guardians to protect the Moon Princess, facing enemies sent by Queen Beryl.
- Ratings: 270 ratings; arithmetic mean 6.059 (Decent), weighted mean 5.981, Bayesian estimate 6.045; rank #1637 of 10504 by seen-by count (730 users).
- 13 episodes. Vintage: 2014-07-05 to 2015-01-03; other airings include Hulu English dub 2015-11-20 to 2016-02-05 (USA), Netflix US/Canada 2021-07-01, Netflix Brazil 2022-03-01.
- Opening "MOON PRIDE!" by Momoiro Clover Z; ending "Gekko" (Moon Rainbow) by Momoiro Clover Z.

wikis.title: Rumor: Windows 9 may be revealed next week
wikis.summary: Tom's Hardware (10 July 2014, Kevin Parrish) reporting a WZor rumor that Microsoft may discuss Windows 9 'Threshold' at WPC 2014.
wikis.body:
- Published 10 July 2014. Rumor from Russian Windows leaker WZor: Microsoft may talk about Windows 9 "Threshold" at the Worldwide Partner Conference 2014 "next week", and introduce Windows 8.1 Update 2, supposedly released by mid-August.
- Previously reported: a Windows 9 preview expected "later this fall", full retail release in Q2 or Q3 of 2015. Update 2 would be the last major Windows 8 update.
- Rumored heavy advertising focused on the return of the Start Button and Menu.
- Rumored new activation: users log into Microsoft Store to activate rather than use a resalable key; new hardware installs require "detaching" the old installation; activating the same distribution on three PCs with one license would cancel activation after three days. WZor's use of the word "rent" prompts speculation about subscriptions; Office 2013 already offers $9.99 per month.
- Author frames all this as rumor.

wikis.title: Microsoft recognizes top-performing Dynamics partners at WPC 2014
wikis.summary: Microsoft press release (15 July 2014) listing 2014 Microsoft Dynamics Partner of the Year award winners at the Worldwide Partner Conference in Washington, D.C.
wikis.body:
- Dated July 15, 2014; awards presented at WPC 2014 in Washington, D.C. the previous day.
- Neil Holloway (corporate VP, MBS Sales & Partners): each year Microsoft honors select Dynamics partners for exemplary performance.
- Hitachi Solutions America Ltd. named Microsoft Dynamics Global Outstanding Reseller of the Year; Incadea GmbH and To-Increase BV named Global Outstanding ISVs.
- 13 regional reseller awards and nine regional ISV awards. Reseller winners include Hands-On Management (Asia Pacific), ADXSTUDIO (Canada), GMCS Verex (CEE), Shanghai Wicresoft and Shenzen Huaxu (Greater China), ISATECH (France), KUMAvision (Germany), Acxiom Consulting (India), Hitachi Solutions Ltd. (Japan), Fesworld (Latin America), AccTech System (MEA), eBECS (UK), mcaConnect (US), HSO International (Western Europe). ISV list not captured.
- Criteria: sales performance, technological expertise, customer satisfaction, feedback from Microsoft team members.

wikis.title: Washington, DC welcomes Microsoft's 2014 Worldwide Partner Conference
wikis.summary: Destination DC press release (9 July 2014) on Microsoft's WPC held in Washington, DC, July 13-17.
wikis.body:
- July 9, 2014, from Destination DC. WPC runs July 13-17 with 16,000+ partners and employees (headline says 15K+) from nearly all 50 states and more than 150 countries; estimated $29 million for the local economy.
- Held at the Walter E. Washington Convention Center; last hosted in DC in 2010. Quotes from Mayor Vincent C. Gray, Elliott L. Ferguson (Destination DC) and Gregory A. O'Dell (Events DC).
- DC cites more than $8.5 billion in development since 2010. Remote registration at Reagan National Airport is new; a block party is planned.
- Monday and Wednesday vision keynotes at the Verizon Center feature new CEO Satya Nadella, addressing partners for the first time since taking the role in February.
- WPC is described as celebrating partners' achievements, networking and previewing products.

wikis.title: Kinect v2 comes to the PC on July 15 for $199
wikis.summary: Ars Technica (5 June 2014, Sam Machkovech) on the Microsoft Store listing of Kinect for Windows v2 at $199, releasing July 15.
wikis.body:
- Jun 5, 2014. Microsoft Store listed the Kinect for Windows v2 Sensor at $199 for pre-order, release July 15, hours after Xbox One controller drivers for Windows appeared.
- Listing says it is "intended for use with the Kinect for Windows software development kit 2.0", suggesting a developer target. SDK requires a "separate license" with no price announced; supported Windows versions not stated.
- PC edition includes four microphones and two visual sensors like the Xbox One edition; interface to PCs not specified (Xbox One version has a proprietary connector; original Kinect for PC needed USB 2.0 and power cable).
- Release date and price for the standalone Xbox One Kinect v2 not yet finalized; Kinect will soon no longer be in every Xbox One system.

wikis.title: Microsoft starts shipping Kinect for Windows v2 and releases SDK 2.0 preview
wikis.summary: The Next Web (15 July 2014) on shipment of the $199 Kinect for Windows v2 sensor and the free SDK 2.0 public preview.
wikis.body:
- July 15, 2014: shipping began at $199 with free SDK 2.0 public preview downloadable from Microsoft.com. Microsoft said "thousands" of sensors went to developers, more in coming weeks.
- Sensor: ultra wide-angle 1080p HD depth camera, RGB video ~30 fps, can detect being off balance and monitor heart rate.
- Sensor improvements: tracks up to six skeletons (two before) with 25 joints each (20 before); higher depth fidelity; 1080p colour; active infrared for seeing in the dark and lighting-independent view, IR and colour at once; wider field of view.
- SDK 2.0: improved hand and joint orientation; Unity support for Windows Store apps; Kinect Studio recording/playback; Gesture Builder for custom machine-learning gestures.

wikis.title: New Kinect for Windows available for $199, shipping July 15
wikis.summary: TechCrunch (7 July 2014, Darrell Etherington) on pre-orders opening for Kinect for Windows v2.
wikis.body:
- July 7, 2014. Microsoft previewed availability in June; now pre-orderable for $199 on its website, shipping July 15.
- Based on the Xbox One Kinect; meant for developers building gesture-based software on Windows. Hardware is ready for Kinect for Windows SDK 2.0, but ships without bundled software; "not intended as a consumer device just yet".
- Author expects a limited audience; Microsoft has dropped the requirement to bundle Kinect with new Xbox One consoles. Suggested as a solid, affordable option for robotic vision and gesture projects.

wikis.title: Continental supplies world's first turbocharger with aluminum turbine housing
wikis.summary: Continental press release (15 July 2014) on series production of a water-cooled aluminum turbine housing turbocharger in the MINI's three-cylinder engine.
wikis.body:
- July 15, 2014, Auburn Hills, Mich. Continental's turbocharger with water-cooled aluminum turbine housing entered series production, the first of its kind in a car, in the MINI Hatch three-cylinder gasoline engine (1.5l, 100kW).
- Weight cut by nearly 30% versus a conventional turbocharger, with cost and system benefits. Wolfgang Breuer (Head, Engine Systems BU): "Aluminum in a turbocharger designed for cars is a real milestone."
- Continental's first turbocharger entered series production in 2011 in a 1.0l engine.
- Double-walled housing with a coolant jacket keeps external surface at most 248 degrees F and internal at most 662 degrees F; electric wastegate actuator speeds catalytic converter heat-up; reduced catalyst thermal load.
- Turbocharger is a fixed part of the exhaust manifold; developed with BMW Group from the simulation phase. Steel-housing variants fit the same base engine for high-performance and hot-country exports.

wikis.title: Microsoft merges Windows Store and Windows Phone developer resources, adds 21 payout markets
wikis.summary: The Next Web, July 16, 2014: Microsoft unified its Windows Store and Windows Phone developer resources into one Dev Center site and added 21 payout markets.
wikis.body:
- Published July 16, 2014 (The Next Web, by Emil Protalinski).
- Microsoft merged the online developer resources (education materials, guidance, code samples, reference documentation) for Windows Store and Windows Phone into a single Windows Dev Center at dev.windows.com for phone, tablet and PC.
- Follows the merging of Windows Store and Windows Phone developer accounts in November 2013 and the rollout of universal Windows apps in April 2014.
- Unified documentation, available in 11 languages (German, English, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese).
- Code samples continue to be published in the MSDN code gallery but are reachable from one Dev Center page.
- Windows Store and Windows Phone developer forums merged; dashboard forums combined, technical forums stay specialized per form factor. Dashboards stay separate; users choose Windows or Windows Phone first and switch in the left-hand navigation.
- 21 new payout markets for paid apps on both stores: Albania, Antigua and Barbuda, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Botswana, Comoros, Dominica, Fiji Islands, Georgia, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Mauritius, Monaco, Mongolia, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, Tajikistan, Tonga, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan.
- Microsoft says this brings the count to 149 markets where developers can earn revenue via paid apps or in-app purchase. In-app purchase is the fastest growing revenue model, over 30% of Windows payout and nearly 50 percent of Windows Phone developer payout.
- Developers can start submitting Kinect-powered apps to the Windows Store later this year; a new SDK preview was released the day before.

wikis.title: Microsoft to cut workforce by 18,000, first 13,000 now
wikis.summary: TechCrunch, July 17, 2014: Nadella announced 18,000 job cuts over the next year, 13,000 of them in a first wave, with 12,500 tied to Nokia.
wikis.body:
- TechCrunch, Darrell Etherington, 5:14 AM PDT, July 17, 2014.
- Microsoft announced layoffs of 18,000 employees over the next year, following a company email from CEO Satya Nadella the week before.
- 12,500 of the cuts come from "streamlining" acquired Nokia assets ("work toward synergies and strategic alignment on Nokia Devices and Services is expected to account for 12,500 jobs"). Microsoft brought on around 25,000 Nokia employees in the devices and services acquisition.
- 13,000 positions are being actively downsized in the first wave; the "vast majority" of those affected get notice over the next six months.
- Cuts include "fewer layers of management" and a flatter organization; Nokia device teams roll into Microsoft, ending Nokia X Android-based designs in favor of low-cost Lumia hardware running Windows Phone.
- Affected employees receive severance and transition assistance; Nadella to host an internal Q&A the next day.
- For comparison the article notes Google laid off around 6,000 from Motorola before selling it to Lenovo.

wikis.title: Microsoft to cut 18,000 jobs worldwide
wikis.summary: Al Jazeera, July 18, 2014: Microsoft announced its biggest layoffs, 18,000 jobs (14 percent of workforce), including about 12,500 from Nokia.
wikis.body:
- Published 18 Jul 2014 (Al Jazeera, Reuters/AP), announced on Thursday.
- Biggest layoffs in Microsoft's 39-year history: 18,000 jobs worldwide, 14 percent of the workforce, about twice analysts' estimates. Previous biggest cut: about 5,800 jobs in 2009.
- About 12,500 jobs tied to the Nokia unit, nearly half of the 28,000 employees Microsoft took on in April. Afterward, headcount is about 109,000, still about 10,000 more than before the Nokia acquisition.
- Nadella's public email: changes needed to "become more agile and move faster"; seen as a pivot away from Ballmer's strategy of making its own devices. Microsoft will largely abandon low-price Nokia Asha phones and reverse Nokia's February Android "X" line; Nokia to focus solely on Windows Phone.
- Cuts by place: about 1,350 Seattle-area workers around Redmond, 1,800 in Hungary, nearly 370 in San Diego, 1,100 in Finland.
- Closing Xbox Entertainment Studios (two-year-old, Santa Monica, original video content).
- Expected charges of $1.1bn to $1.6bn over the next four quarters, largely severance; on track for the $600m annual savings target within 18 months of the deal closing.

wikis.title: Microsoft announces OneDrive storage increase: 15 GB free, 1 TB with Office 365
wikis.summary: Microsoft 365 Blog, June 23, 2014: OneDrive free storage rises to 15 GB, Office 365 subscriptions include 1 TB, and paid storage prices drop.
wikis.body:
- Microsoft 365 Blog, June 23, 2014, by the Microsoft 365 Marketing Team (Omar Shahine, Group Program Manager, OneDrive.com).
- OneDrive free storage goes to 15 GB, up from 7 GB; "3 out of 4 people have less than 15 GB of files stored on their PC".
- All versions of Office 365 get 1 TB of OneDrive: Office 365 Home ($9.99/mo) 1 TB per person for up to 5 people; Office 365 Personal ($6.99/mo) and University ($79.99/4yr) 1 TB per subscription. Follows April announcement that OneDrive for Business customers get 1 TB per person.
- Standalone monthly storage prices cut by over 70%: $1.99 for 100 GB (previously $7.49) and $3.99 for 200 GB (previously $11.49). Changes take effect "in the next month"; current subscribers are moved automatically.

wikis.title: Microsoft raises free OneDrive storage to 15GB (HotHardware)
wikis.summary: HotHardware, July 30, 2014: free OneDrive accounts were bumped from 7GB to 15GB, matching Google Drive.
wikis.body:
- HotHardware, Rob Williams, Wednesday, July 30, 2014.
- Microsoft rolled out the upgrade to free OneDrive accounts but was only then emailing users. New sign-ups previously got 7GB; now 15GB, matching Google Drive. Dropbox offers 2GB, up to 18GB via referrals.
- Author notes 15GB is less than the 25GB the service originally gave free.
- Follows the decision to give Office 365 subscribers 1,000GB of cloud storage.
- Users can check their total on the OneDrive website, bottom-left corner.

wikis.title: Samsung 105-inch curved 4K UHD TV opens for pre-order (HEXUS)
wikis.summary: HEXUS, 23 July 2014: Samsung priced its 105-inch curved UHD TV and opened pre-orders.
wikis.body:
- HEXUS, Mark Tyson, 23 July 2014.
- Samsung's 105-inch Curved UHD TV, first unveiled at CES 2014 in January, is available to pre-order at $199,999.99 per the article's text, while the same article also states "$120K" and "US$120,000" (about GBP 70,300; possibly upwards of GBP 90K including tax in the UK). The figures are inconsistent in the source.
- 5120x2160 resolution, 11 million pixels, 21:9 aspect ratio, made to order with a metal frame and wood-finish back; UHD Dimming, Precision Blacks, Quad Screen Multi-Link, UHD Upscaling, Samsung Smart TV.
- "Samsung Elite Service": field engineers demonstrate and optimise the set. Delivery about 12 weeks; pre-orders open that week; non-US price and availability not yet disclosed.
- Quote from Joe Stinziano, executive vice president, Samsung Electronics America.

wikis.title: Samsung curved 105-inch 4K TV costs $120,000 (Engadget)
wikis.summary: Engadget, July 22, 2014: Samsung put its curved 105-inch UN105S9W 4K TV up for pre-order at $120,000.
wikis.body:
- Engadget, Dana Wollman, July 22, 2014.
- The Samsung UN105S9W was at CES described as the "world's first, largest and most curved 105-inch curved UHD TV". Now on pre-order at $120,000 (the URL slug says 129,000).
- 5,120 x 2,160 resolution, 21:9 aspect ratio; a visit from a Samsung "Field Engineer" to explain features; Smart TV with four-quadrant screen split.

wikis.title: Samsung 105-inch curved 4K UHD TV priced at $119,999.99 (Tech Times)
wikis.summary: Tech Times, July 25, 2014: Samsung set the UN105S9W price at $119,999.99, made to order with about a 12-week wait.
wikis.body:
- Tech Times, Aaron Mamiit, Jul 25 2014.
- Price $119,999.99; UN105S9W (originally named 105U9500), made to order, not bulk built.
- UHD Dimming, Precision Black, Quad Screen mode (four smaller HD screens), 21:9 aspect ratio, 5,120 by 2,160 (over 11 million pixels).
- About 12-week wait; "Samsung Elite Service" field engineers with delivery. Optional wall mount and Evolution Kit (software/hardware upgrades). Uses Samsung Smart Hub (e.g. Netflix).
- Line of curved UHD TVs first announced January at CES 2014 in Las Vegas; quote from Hyun Suk Kim, vice president for visual display business.

wikis.title: Nvidia Shield Tablet puts gaming first (New Atlas)
wikis.summary: New Atlas, July 22, 2014: Nvidia announced the Shield Tablet, an Android gaming tablet with Tegra K1, an optional controller and case, from US$299.
wikis.body:
- New Atlas, Chris Wood, July 22, 2014.
- Nvidia Shield Tablet: Android, powered by Nvidia Tegra K1 (192 graphics cores, Kepler architecture, called by Nvidia "the world's most advanced mobile processor"); runs Unreal Engine 4; can locally stream PC games.
- Display: 8-inch IPS LCD, 1920 x 1200, 283 ppi. Front-facing speakers with PureAudio and dual-bass reflex. microSD slot up to 128 GB. 5 MP camera, WiFi a/b/g/n, LTE option.
- Built-in gameplay recording and streaming via Twitch; Grid Cloud Streaming for users in Northern California; Console Mode to connect to a big screen (details unclear at the time).
- Optional controller: ultra-low latency over WiFi Direct, first gamepad for both Android and PC games; up to four controllers per tablet.
- DirectStylus 2 bundled (first GPU-accelerated stylus) with the Dabbler app; the article thought it fits poorly with a gaming-first approach. Hinged cover with kick-stand sold separately.
- Pre-order available, release scheduled (at least by Amazon) July 29; 16 and 32 GB configurations starting at US$299.

wikis.title: Nvidia Shield Tablet (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the Nvidia Shield Tablet, an Android gaming tablet released July 29, 2014 and discontinued in 2018.
wikis.body:
- Gaming tablet by Nvidia, released July 29, 2014 (USA/CAN) and August 14, 2014 (EU); lifespan 2014-2018. Nvidia's second portable gaming device using Android; controller is separate (up to four wireless).
- Intro price US$299 (16 GB WiFi only), US$399 (32 GB + 4G LTE), US$199 for the Shield K1 (16 GB WiFi only).
- Specs: Tegra K1, 4x Cortex-A15 2.2 GHz, 2 GB DDR3L, 16-32 GB flash plus microSDXC up to 200 GB, 8-inch 1920x1200 (283 ppi) IPS, 5 MP front and back cameras, 5197 mAh battery, Android 4.4.2 KitKat upgradable to Android 7.0 Nougat. Weight 390 g (356 g for Shield K1).
- November 2015: refreshed and renamed Shield Tablet K1, price reduced to $200 (comes without charger or stylus). August 2016: Nvidia cancelled a hardware upgrade; speculated reason is conflict with the Nintendo Switch. Mid-2017 no longer for retail on Nvidia's site; mid-2018 officially discontinued.
- Software: OTA 2.0 with Android 5.0 Lollipop on November 18, 2014; Android 6.0 Marshmallow February 1, 2016; OTA 5.0 with Android 7.0 Nougat on February 9, 2017 (K1 also got Nougat February 9, 2017 and Vulkan support in OTA 1.2, April 13, 2016).
- July 31, 2015: recall to replace devices sold between July 2014 and July 2015 due to overheating that posed a fire hazard.
- Reception: Android Central's Andrew Martonik praised speakers and Twitch streaming; downsides were weight (390 g vs Nexus 7's 290 g) and price ($299-$399, controller $59, cover $39).

wikis.title: NVIDIA launches SHIELD tablet and wireless controller (press release)
wikis.summary: NVIDIA press release, July 22, 2014, launching the SHIELD tablet (Tegra K1) and SHIELD wireless controller.
wikis.body:
- NVIDIA newsroom, Santa Clara, July 22, 2014.
- SHIELD tablet: Tegra K1 (192 GPU cores), 8-inch full HD display, front-facing speakers with PureAudio and dual-ported bass-reflex, optional cover that doubles as stand, optional LTE. Quote from Jen-Hsun Huang, co-founder and CEO.
- Claimed firsts: PC game streaming with GameStream from GeForce GTX PCs; GRID cloud gaming beta (Northern California owners); ShadowPlay with Twitch (5MP front camera); Console Mode (native 1080p on TVs).
- SHIELD wireless controller: ultra-low latency Wi-Fi Direct, up to four controllers, headset jack, touch pad, volume control, voice command.
- DirectStylus 2: twice as responsive as predecessor, GPU-accelerated 3D painting, Dabbler app.
- Preloaded with SHIELD Hub and Trine 2: Complete Story; full Google Play access.
- Pricing: 16 and 32GB, Wi-Fi or Wi-Fi+LTE, MicroSD up to 128GB, from $299; controller $59; cover $39. Preorders open in the United States, Canada and select European countries.

wikis.title: NVIDIA SHIELD Tablet coming July 29th (ABI Research)
wikis.summary: ABI Research blog, July 22, 2014: SHIELD Tablet US release July 29, Europe August 14, priced $299 and $399.
wikis.body:
- ABI Research, July 22, 2014.
- US release July 29; first Nvidia gaming end-to-end product to ship outside North America (August 14 in Europe, later in 2014 elsewhere).
- $299 for 16 GB Wi-Fi and $399 for 32 GB Wi-Fi + LTE (compatible with AT&T and T-Mobile, no carrier certifications announced). Priced competitively with premium 8" tablets.
- Specs listed: Tegra K1 (192 core Kepler GPU, 2.2 GHz quad-core A15), 2GB RAM, 8-inch 1920x1200 IPS, stereo speakers, 5MP front and rear cameras, mini HDMI 1.4b (4K at 30fps), microSD to 128GB, Bluetooth 4.0, GPS, integrated stylus, 19.75 WHr battery (up to 10 hours HD video), 13.7 ounces (0.36" thick), native Twitch.
- Wireless controller $59 over Wi-Fi Direct; also works with SHIELD Portable (which cannot serve as a controller for the tablet). Supports GameStream and GRID.
- Author view: the tablet will appeal to a wider audience than the portable; the controller lacks motion controls.

wikis.title: 15-inch mid 2014 Retina MacBook Pro benchmark (MacRumors)
wikis.summary: MacRumors, July 29, 2014: Geekbench result shows the refreshed entry 15-inch Retina MacBook Pro about 8 percent faster than the 2013 model.
wikis.body:
- MacRumors, Juli Clover, Tuesday July 29, 2014.
- Geekbench 3: entry-level 15-inch is eight percent faster than the entry 2013 model and two percent slower than the mid-level 2013 model. Single-core 3050 (vs 2811), multi-core 11586 (vs 10730).
- New Haswell processors: 13-inch 2.6 and 2.8 GHz dual-core (BTO 3.0 GHz); 15-inch 2.2 and 2.5 GHz quad-core (BTO 2.8 GHz). 13-inch now 8 GB RAM standard (up to 16 GB); 15-inch 16 GB standard.
- High-end 15-inch got a $100 price cut; 1 TB flash option on both sizes. Article calls Haswell a stopgap until Broadwell "next year". Available that day.

wikis.title: Apple updates MacBook Pro with Retina display (press release)
wikis.summary: Apple press release, July 29, 2014: faster processors, doubled entry memory, and a lower starting price for the top 15-inch.
wikis.body:
- Apple, Cupertino, July 29, 2014.
- 13-inch Retina: dual-core Core i5 up to 2.8 GHz, 8GB memory (up from 4GB); starts $1,299 (2.6 GHz, 128GB), $1,499 (256GB), $1,799 (2.8 GHz, 512GB). Options to 3.0 GHz i7, 16GB, 1TB flash.
- 15-inch Retina: quad-core i7 2.2 GHz, 16GB (up from 8GB), 256GB at $1,999; 2.5 GHz, 512GB, Iris Pro and GeForce GT 750M at $2,499 (new lower starting price for top-of-the-line). Options to 2.8 GHz and 1TB.
- Non-Retina 13-inch MacBook Pro price lowered $100 to $1,099 (2.5 GHz i5, 4GB, 500GB HDD).
- OS X Yosemite to be a free download this fall. Quote from Philip Schiller. Available today through Apple Online Store, retail stores and authorized resellers.

wikis.title: Apple MacBook Pro with Retina display gets faster processors and more memory (The Next Web)
wikis.summary: The Next Web, July 29, 2014: Apple refreshed the Retina MacBook Pro lineup with better internals.
wikis.body:
- The Next Web, Nick Summers, July 29, 2014.
- Outside unchanged; specs bumped. 13-inch starts $1,299 with 2.6GHz dual-core Core i5 and 8GB; +$200 for 256GB flash from 128GB; further $300 adds 2.8GHz i5.
- Entry 15-inch starts $1,999 with 2.2GHz quad-core Core i7 and 16GB; $2,499 model has 2.5GHz chip and 512GB flash instead of 256GB.
- Refresh described as unsurprising with OS X Yosemite approaching.

wikis.title: Philips SlimStyle BR30 LED bulb (CNET)
wikis.summary: CNET, May 28, 2014: Philips SlimStyle BR30 LED at $12.97 from July, compared with Cree, EcoSmart and TCP bulbs.
wikis.body:
- CNET, Ry Crist, May 28, 2014.
- Philips SlimStyle BR30 follows the flat SlimStyle A19; flat design removes the aluminum heat sink, making it lighter (3.6 ounces vs 5-6 ounces) and cheaper to make. Available starting in July at $12.97.
- 9.5W, 650 lumens, 2,700 K, 68 lumens/watt, CRI 80, 25,000 hours, dimmable, 10-year warranty; Energy Star listed as "Yes" in the table.
- Comparison (all 650 lumens): Cree $19.97 (9.5W, 10-year warranty), EcoSmart $15.97 (10W, 5-year), TCP $13.99 (12W, not dimmable, 3-year). Cree is $7 more than SlimStyle; article expects Cree may cut prices.
- BR = "bulging reflector"; 30 = diameter in eighths of an inch; used for recessed spot/flood fixtures.

wikis.title: Philips SlimStyle BR30 LED flood hands-on (SlashGear)
wikis.summary: SlashGear, May 28, 2014: hands-on with the 9.5W Philips SlimStyle BR30, RRP $12.97, on sale online in July and stores in August.
wikis.body:
- SlashGear, Chris Davies, May 28, 2014.
- SlimStyle BR30 drops the heatsink; large frosted top, plastic support stem. 9.5W, 60W-equivalent, 2700K, 650 lumens, 85-percent less power, up to $152 lifetime savings (per Philips).
- Going through ENERGY STAR testing; the original SlimStyle got approved in April and fell below $2 in some states with utility subsidies.
- Online sales in July, stores the following month, RRP $12.97.

wikis.title: Philips releases 650-lumen SlimStyle LED lamp (LED professional)
wikis.summary: LED professional, Jun 04, 2014: Philips released the SlimStyle BR30 floodlight at $12.97 MSRP.
wikis.body:
- LED professional, Jun 04, 2014.
- 9.5W, 650 lumens, Luxeon mid-power LEDs from the Philips Lumileds facility in San Jose, California; dimmable; 85 percent lower energy use, estimated $152 savings over bulb life; 25 times longer than average incandescent floodlight.
- Online July, retail August 2014 in the US; submitted for ENERGY STAR testing. MSRP $12.97.
- Quote from Bruno Biasiotta, CEO and president, Philips Lighting Americas, on affordability and rebate programs.

wikis.title: Philips SlimStyle BR30 LED floodlight for $13 (CleanTechnica)
wikis.summary: CleanTechnica, June 4, 2014: Philips SlimStyle BR30 at $12.97 with 650 lumens at 9.5 watts, 68 lm/W.
wikis.body:
- CleanTechnica, Nicholas Brown, June 4, 2014.
- 9.5W, 650 lumens (60W incandescent or 15W CFL equivalent), 68 lumens per watt vs CFL 45-60 and incandescent 12-18; average LED 45-100 lm/W.
- Flat surface conducts heat, no aluminium heat sink. 85% less energy, est. $152 savings, dimming, 25 times longer than average incandescent. Submitted for ENERGY STAR testing.
- Available online July, retail August.

wikis.title: Wellograph announces Windows Phone 8.1 app for its wellness watch
wikis.summary: Marketwired via Yahoo Finance UK, May 1, 2014: Wellograph watch to work with Windows Phone 8.1 when it ships in July.
wikis.body:
- Marketwired, Los Angeles, May 1, 2014.
- Wellograph, Inc. says its "world's first premium wellness watch with a sapphire crystal display" will be compatible with Windows Phone 8.1 at its July 2014 ship date, with an official app alongside iOS and Android apps. Preorders just opened.
- The watch is stand-alone; the app uses Live Tiles (steps, exercise score) and syncs over Bluetooth. Features integrated heart rate monitor, activity tracker, pedometer, running watch.
- Quotes: Nick Warnock, president of Wellograph ("first fitness tracking device dedicated to Windows Phone users"); Todd Brix, general manager, Windows Apps and Store, Microsoft.
- Preorders for classic Silver Satin and limited edition Black Chrome (first 10,000 orders only).

wikis.title: Wellograph smartwatch fully compatible with Windows Phone (All About Windows Phone)
wikis.summary: All About Windows Phone, May 2, 2014: the $350 sapphire-crystal Wellograph smartwatch will support Windows Phone 8.1 from July.
wikis.body:
- Steve Litchfield, 7:57 UTC, May 2nd 2014, sourcing MarketWatch.
- The $350 smartwatch, shipping in July, will be compatible with Windows Phone 8.1; the company says it is "committed" to the platform. Official app for Windows Phone 8.1 with Live Tiles, syncing over Bluetooth; heart rate monitor, activity tracker, pedometer, running watch.
- Preorders open for Silver Satin and limited Black Chrome (first 10,000 orders).
- Author speculation: since all sensors are in the watch and no host phone is needed, integration may be easier.

wikis.title: Open-air fish market coming to San Diego (NBC 7)
wikis.summary: NBC 7 San Diego, July 16, 2014 (updated July 19): an open-air fish market opens Aug. 2, 2014 at the Tuna Harbor Pier.
wikis.body:
- NBC 7 San Diego, Vanessa Herrera and Monica Garske; published July 16, 2014, updated July 19, 2014.
- From Aug. 2, 2014 the Dockside Fish Market at the Downtown Waterfront opens at Fish Harbor Pier near Tuna Harbor between the USS Midway Museum and Seaport Village, every Saturday 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. for "the next year or so".
- Spearheaded by County Supervisor Greg Cox, announced Wednesday; compared with Seattle's Pike Place Market. Fishing boats unload fish, lobster, urchins, crab; fishermen pay a vendor fee not yet set.
- Cox: gives fishermen a higher price than wholesale and a bargain for residents. Partner Zachary Roach says his father has caught rock crab for 20 years without a wholesale price change.
- A proposal to promote the market goes to the Board of Supervisors at a July 29 meeting.

wikis.title: Local fishermen land a dockside market in San Diego (Voice of San Diego)
wikis.summary: Voice of San Diego, July 16, 2014: permits issued for the Tuna Harbor Dockside Market opening Aug. 2 at Fish Harbor Pier.
wikis.body:
- Voice of San Diego, Clare Leschin-Hoar, July 16, 2014 (page updated March 15, 2022).
- Less than one month after an earlier story, County Supervisor Greg Cox and Port Chairman Bob Nelson announced Wednesday that permits were issued; the market opens Aug. 2 at Fish Harbor Pier.
- Peter Halmay (sea urchin diver, president of the San Diego Fishermen's Working Group): "For about a year they told us it couldn't be done... within two weeks it was done." Fishermen had sold from a docked boat.
- Fishermen fell in a regulatory gap (not classifiable as a farmers market) so could not get County Department of Environmental Health permits; now solved with county and Port permits.
- Cox cites health benefits: Americans eat under 15 pounds of seafood a year (vs nearly 70 poultry, 100 beef); supports LiveWell San Diego. Correction: the initiative is countywide, not a city program.
- Halmay: goal is to "sell the idea that fishing exists in San Diego".

wikis.title: Tuna Harbor Dockside Market grand opening in San Diego
wikis.summary: A photo blog post reporting the grand opening of the Tuna Harbor Dockside Market, a Saturday fresh-seafood market on San Diego's Embarcadero, dated 2014-08-02.
wikis.body:
- The new Tuna Harbor Dockside Market had its grand opening on the Embarcadero "this morning" (URL dated 2014/08/02).
- Open Saturdays from 8 to 1 on the pier adjacent to Tuna Harbor, between Seaport Village and the USS Midway Museum.
- Described as San Diego's attempt to recreate Seattle's Pike Place Fish Market and San Francisco's Fisherman's Wharf; "a modest but very popular beginning".
- Tables and tanks of fresh fish and invertebrates caught locally by fishermen from the nearby fleet.
- Catch that morning: stone crab, box crab, sea urchins, top snail, kellet's whelks, black cod, ling cod, rock fish, sand dabs, bluefin, yellowfin, yellowtail, sheepshead and octopus.
- The author writes, "According to what I read on the internet", that the market is produced by the San Diego Fishermen's Working Group, established in 2010 to promote commercial fishing in San Diego, with assistance from the Port of San Diego.
- A large line of customers formed before opening; the author thinks "they'll need more fish".
- Photos show County Supervisor Greg Cox checking a tank of crabs, fish sold to the public, a fisherman removing catch from ice, and TV reporters waiting.
- Author: Richard Schulte, blog Cool San Diego Sights!

wikis.title: Visual Studio 2013 Update 3 adds mixed-case menu option
wikis.summary: Ars Technica article (Aug 4, 2014) on Visual Studio 2013 Update 3, whose headline feature is a Title Case option for the ALL CAPS menu bar.
wikis.body:
- Published Aug 4, 2014 by Ars Staff.
- Microsoft released Visual Studio 2013 Update 3 "today", a mix of bug fixes and new capabilities.
- New features: memory usage profiler expanded to support .NET applications using WPF and native Win32 applications; CodeLens support for git repositories (work items and change history in the editor); better debugging for Windows Store apps on multimonitor systems.
- Other Microsoft updates the same day: Windows Phone 8.1 Update preview now available on all phones in the developer preview program (emulator images updated); Azure SDK updated to version 2.4 with better support for Azure-hosted virtual machines; preview of "Multi-device Hybrid Apps" (HTML5 smartphone and tablet apps using Cordova) upgraded, needed if the VS update is installed, with wider OS support including Windows 7.
- The "big upgrade": an option to make menu bar text Title Case instead of ALL CAPS, with the setting roaming to any machine signed in with the same Microsoft Account.

wikis.title: VS2013 Update 3 Continues Refinements (InfoQ)
wikis.summary: InfoQ news item (Aug 07, 2014) summarising the Visual Studio 2013 Update 3 release: CodeLens for Git, Code Maps, memory tool, menu case option and simpler deployment.
wikis.body:
- By Jeff Martin, Aug 07, 2014.
- Microsoft released Update 3 for Visual Studio 2013; the RTM designation means it is safe to use in production. Available as web-based and standalone installers, or via the Notification menu inside VS2013.
- VS2013 Ultimate: CodeLens now works with any Git repository (previously only TFS-based repositories); a revised Code Maps tool can generate maps from DLLs, has better zoom tools and colour-coding of relationships.
- The Memory Usage Tool (debuted in VS2013, previously Windows Store and Windows Phone apps only) now supports WPF and Win32 applications.
- The JSON editor from Update 2 gains formatting and brace matching.
- The menu capitalization issue from VS2012 (previously a registry key) is now configurable under Tools | Options | Environment | General.
- Deployment simplified: no Microsoft Deployment Agent required on each target machine; supports on-premises and Windows Azure targets; Windows PowerShell, PowerShell Desired State Configuration and Chef supported.
- Refers readers to the official Microsoft announcement and release notes.

wikis.title: Visual Studio 2013 Update 3 RTM Available (Visual Studio Blog)
wikis.summary: Official Visual Studio Team blog post (August 4th, 2014) announcing Update 3 RTM and listing its features and related releases.
wikis.body:
- Posted August 4th, 2014 by the Visual Studio Team: "Today we released Update 3 for Visual Studio 2013". Download the update or full versions of Ultimate, Premium, Professional, Windows Express, Web Express and Desktop Express with Update 3 included.
- CodeLens (Ultimate): shows authors and changes for files in Git repositories; work item indicators when Git is used with TFS work item tracking.
- Code Map: coloured links; drag and drop binaries from File Explorer into a directed graph.
- x86 debugging for .NET Native apps; managed memory dump analysis gains Go to Definition and Find All References.
- CPU Usage tool: navigate from a Call Tree function to its definition. Memory Usage tool: support for Win32 and WPF applications (.NET 4.0 and up on Windows 8.1) and forcing garbage collections in managed apps.
- Notification Hub: badge turns yellow when an update is available and now toggles the hub.
- ALL CAPS: a Tools Options setting under General Environment lets users choose menu bar styling; the setting roams across devices.
- Testing: customizable test plans and suites, work item history for suites, enhanced security, cloud-based load testing with Application Insights.
- Release Management: deploy to on-premises or Windows Azure environments without a Microsoft Deployment Agent; PowerShell, PowerShell DSC, and Chef (for non-Windows servers).
- Graphics Analyzer: analyse graphics frames and see the impact of shader changes without re-running the app.
- WebJobs tooling for Azure WebJobs (continuous, triggered or scheduled); two-factor authentication in One ASP.NET templates.
- Application Insights included; account setup possible without a Visual Studio Online account.
- Related releases: Multi-Device Hybrid Apps CTP 2.0 (not compatible with CTP 1.0 and 1.1; minimum edition Professional); Azure SDK 2.4 RTM; IntelliTrace Stand-alone Collector.

wikis.title: Windows 8.1 Update 2 reportedly to land August 12
wikis.summary: CNET report (July 21, 2014) that a leak claims Windows 8.1 Update 2 arrives on August 12, with Microsoft declining comment.
wikis.body:
- By Lance Whitney, July 21, 2014.
- Leaked information from Russian site PCPortal.org.ru pegs August 12 as the date for Windows 8.1 Update 2, per Neowin; "the report can't be confirmed", though Neowin considers it authentic based on prior information.
- In April, sources told ZDNet's Mary Jo Foley that Update 2 could arrive in August. Patch Tuesday is typically the second Tuesday of the month, so August 12 seems logical.
- A Microsoft spokesperson told CNET the company had nothing to share.
- In April Microsoft released a Windows 8.1 update with a Start screen Power button and the ability to pin Windows 8 apps to the taskbar.
- The leaked description says the August update includes new features, but previous reports suggest it will be minor (bug fixes and stability tweaks).
- Microsoft initially planned to bring back the Start menu in Update 2 but "apparently changed its mind" and now intends to revive it in what could be Windows 9, aka Threshold, "slated for release in April 2015".

wikis.title: Windows 8.1 Update 2 is here but a letdown (How-To Geek)
wikis.summary: How-To Geek article (Aug 20, 2014) saying the August Update (formerly Update 2), released August 12, adds little and the Start menu was pushed to Windows 9.
wikis.body:
- By Chris Hoffman, published Aug 20, 2014.
- The update formerly called Windows 8.1 Update 2, now the "August Update" (KB 2975719), was released August 12; the author calls it "a small update that barely adds anything".
- Windows 8.1 Update 1 was renamed "Windows 8.1 Update"; it made non-touch PCs boot to desktop by default and added a Start screen power icon.
- At BUILD (April 2014) Microsoft announced a returning Start menu and windowed Store apps; sources told The Verge it would return in August as part of the second update. Microsoft later decided not to release it for 8.1; it is now slated for Windows Threshold, "probably" called Windows 9, scheduled for Spring 2015.
- The author speculates about why (cynically, an upgrade fee). Cost figures cited: $119 to upgrade Windows 7 to 8.1; Windows 8 upgrades were $40 temporarily. Mary Jo Foley and others reported rumors Windows 9 could be free to 8/8.1 users; no pricing announced.
- Microsoft's blog says it will use the monthly update process for more frequent improvements.
- Included in the August Update per Microsoft: Precision Touchpad improvements (disable touchpad while a mouse is connected, right-click, double-tap to drag) and Miracast Receive support (APIs for developers); the list continues beyond the text read.

wikis.title: Microsoft ends Windows 8.1 Update 2 and renames Patch Tuesday
wikis.summary: The Register (Aug 5, 2014) reports Microsoft's blog said no second big Windows 8.1 update will ship, with monthly updates bringing features and Patch Tuesday renamed Update Tuesday.
wikis.body:
- By Neil McAllister, published 5 Aug 2014.
- Microsoft's Brandon LeBlanc blogged that instead of "waiting for months and bundling together a bunch of improvements into a larger update as we did for the Windows 8.1 Update", customers can expect the existing monthly update process to deliver "more frequent improvements along with the security updates normally provided as part of 'Update Tuesday'".
- Patch Tuesday is renamed "Update Tuesday", meaning new features may arrive alongside patches. Examples given: the Windows Store Refresh in May and the June OneDrive update.
- The next Update Tuesday, August 12, will include three new feature bundles: touchpad settings (keep touchpad active with a mouse connected, choose whether right-clicks are allowed, enable drag by double-tap); APIs letting Windows devices act as Miracast receivers; fewer password prompts for SharePoint Online.
- The approach applies to Windows Server 2012 too.
- The new Start Menu teased since Build in April: "latest scuttlebutt" says it is on hold until sometime in 2015, possibly until "Threshold", widely expected to ship as Windows 9.

wikis.title: Amazon Local Register mobile card reader vs Square and PayPal
wikis.summary: Ars Technica (Aug 13, 2014) on Amazon's Local Register card reader and app, its low fees compared with Square and PayPal, and its lack of EMV.
wikis.body:
- By Megan Geuss, Aug 13, 2014.
- Amazon announced Local Register, a mobile card reader and app for merchants to swipe cards; similar to Square and PayPal magnetic-stripe readers.
- Reader costs $10. Customers registering before October 31 pay 1.75 percent on swiped transactions until January 1, 2016. Otherwise 2.5 percent per swipe and 2.75 percent for manually keyed purchases. The first $10 in fees is credited back.
- Comparison: Square 2.75 percent and PayPal 2.7 percent on swipes; both 3.5 percent + $0.15 for keyed transactions; both readers free on registration.
- Square: "We've long been focused on building a complete register service for local businesses." PayPal: "Payments isn't just about the swipe, it's the experience."
- EMV: on October 15, 2015 most major card companies shift fraud liability to merchants without EMV readers. Amazon said the reader "does not have EMV capability". Square announced an EMV reader earlier that summer; PayPal has one marketed to Europe.
- Amazon says data from Local Register customers will not be used for any purpose other than fraud protection and risk management for Local Register.

wikis.title: Amazon press release: Introducing Amazon Local Register
wikis.summary: Amazon's Aug. 13, 2014 press release announcing Local Register, a $10 card reader and free mobile app with a promotional 1.75 percent swipe rate.
wikis.body:
- Dated August 13, 2014, Seattle (Business Wire). Amazon announced Amazon Local Register, a secure card reader and mobile app for local businesses to accept credit and debit cards from a smartphone or tablet.
- Quote from Matt Swann, Vice President of Amazon Local Commerce: making payments "so easy and inexpensive that it no longer gets in the way of a business owner".
- Sign up in three steps: create account at localregister.amazon.com, buy a $10 card reader, download the free app (Amazon Appstore, Apple App Store, Google Play).
- Reader available that day with Free Two-Day Shipping on Amazon.com; from August 19 at Staples retail locations nationwide.
- Compatible with Apple devices running iOS7, Kindle Fire tablets, select Android smartphones, and "coming soon" to the Fire phone.
- Rates: sign up before October 31 for 1.75 percent per swipe until January 1, 2016; afterwards a flat 2.5 percent on swiped transactions. No hidden fees, no long-term contracts. First $10 in fees credited back to recoup the reader cost.
- Funds deposited to a bank account within one business day, or spent on Amazon.com within minutes.
- Also: dedicated phone and email customer support (Mayday button for Kindle Fire HDX owners), stabilized reader that limits swivel, in-app business reporting, compatible accessories (cash drawers, receipt printers, cases, stands).

wikis.title: Amazon launches iOS-compatible Local Register card reader (MacRumors)
wikis.summary: MacRumors (Aug 13, 2014) short news item on Amazon Local Register, a card reader competing with Square and PayPal Here at a 1.75% rate until January 2016.
wikis.body:
- By Richard Padilla, Wednesday August 13, 2014.
- Amazon launched Local Register, an iOS-compatible reader to compete with Square Reader and PayPal Here. Anti-swivel design and Amazon payments integration; accepts Visa, MasterCard, American Express and Discover.
- Special flat rate of 1.75% per swipe until January 2016.
- The companion iOS app lets users add items and discounts, track cash transactions, add staff accounts, change tax rates; connects with cases, stands, receipt printers and cash drawers.
- Reader available for $10 through Amazon's website; app on the App Store.
- Reader comments (not the article) include praise for Square's next-day deposits and scepticism of Amazon; these are commenters' opinions.

wikis.title: Amazon announces Local Register mobile card reader (Washington Post)
wikis.summary: Very short Washington Post item (Aug 13, 2014) saying Amazon unveiled Local Register, a headphone-jack card reader; only the opening paragraphs were captured.
wikis.body:
- By Hayley Tsukayama, August 13, 2014 (The Switch).
- Amazon announced Wednesday "Amazon Local Register", a physical credit card reader that plugs into a smartphone or tablet's headphone jack.
- Stores using it can use the same payment-processing system Amazon uses for its own online transactions. Sign-ups start Wednesday.
- The captured text ends after this intro; no fees or other details are given.

wikis.title: Diablo 3 for Xbox One to get 1080p in day one patch
wikis.summary: Ubergizmo (08/07/2014) reports Diablo 3 on Xbox One ships at 900p but will run at 1080p and 60 fps after a day one patch, with release on August 19.
wikis.body:
- By Tyler Lee, 08/07/2014.
- Diablo 3 for Xbox One will ship and play at 900p, but a day one patch will raise it to 1080p.
- Spokesperson quote: "We've now confirmed that following a day one patch, the Xbox One version of UEE will run at full HD 1080p resolution and 60 frames per second (up from 900p, 60 fps)."
- Previously suggested to be possible because Microsoft unbundled Kinect, freeing processing power.
- Would match the PlayStation 4 version's graphics quality. Size of the patch not stated.
- Release "pegged" for the 19th of August.
- Saved characters can reportedly be transferred from PlayStation 3 or Xbox 360 to the newer consoles.

wikis.title: A Closer Look at Diablo III: Ultimate Evil Edition (Xbox Wire)
wikis.summary: Xbox Wire post (August 19, 2014) previewing Diablo III: Ultimate Evil Edition, launching the next day on Xbox One and Xbox 360.
wikis.body:
- By Xbox Wire Staff, August 19, 2014. The game "launches tomorrow" on Xbox One and Xbox 360; described as the definitive version of Blizzard's Diablo III.
- Includes all existing Diablo III content and a four-player co-op mode, playable offline or online.
- New console control scheme: left analog stick for direct movement, right stick for a directional dodge, instead of point-and-click.
- The Xbox One version runs in 1080p HD.
- Includes the Reaper of Souls expansion: adventure mode, new Crusader class, new areas and bounties.
- Launch day copies include a code for Infernal Pauldrons shoulder plates ("Wearable at level 1", bonuses to Vitality, Life per Second and Cooldown Reduction, usable for transmogrification).
- Streamlined from PC: no Battle.net account needed, offline play allowed, no real-money auction house, loot drops tweaked to be more relevant.
- Saves can be ported from Xbox 360 to Xbox One.

wikis.title: Report: Haswell-E, X99 and DDR4 to arrive August 29
wikis.summary: Tom's Hardware (15 August 2014) rumour, sourced to Hermitage Akihabara, that Intel's Haswell-E CPUs, X99 motherboards and DDR4 launch on Friday August 29.
wikis.body:
- By Niels Broekhuijsen, published 15 August 2014. Framed as a rumour ("This is still a rumor").
- Japanese site Hermitage Akihabara posted the release date; originally expected mid-September. Official availability "possibly" Friday, August 29; other product releases also point to end of August.
- Three CPUs expected, with rumoured specs:
  - Core i7-5820K: 6 cores/12 threads, 3.3 GHz, 15 MB L3, 28 PCIe lanes, 140 W, expected price $400.
  - Core i7-5930K: 6/12, 3.5 GHz, 15 MB L3, 40 lanes, 140 W, $600.
  - Core i7-5960X: 8/16, 3.0 GHz, 20 MB L3, 40 lanes, 140 W, $1000+.
- Comes after a "flood of X99 motherboard reveals".

wikis.title: Intel reportedly launching Haswell-E and X99 on August 29th (TechSpot)
wikis.summary: TechSpot (August 15, 2014) reports Intel will launch Haswell-E CPUs, X99 chipset and DDR4 on August 29th, with three CPUs and their expected prices.
wikis.body:
- By Tim Schiesser, August 15, 2014. "According to a recent report", Intel will launch Haswell-E alongside X99 on August 29th; not just a paper launch, with CPUs, X99 motherboards and DDR4 RAM all reportedly available on the day.
- Three CPUs:
  - Core i7-5960X (flagship): 8 cores/16 threads, 3.0 GHz, 20 MB L3, expected to cost more than $1,000.
  - Core i7-5930K: 6 cores/12 threads, 3.5 GHz, 15 MB L3, "upwards of $500".
  - Core i7-5820K: six cores; other specs unrevealed (possibly 3.3 GHz and 15 MB L3); expected $350 to $450.
- X99 is the first consumer platform supporting DDR4. X99 boards seen at Computex in June had USB 3.1, SATA Express and many PCIe channels.

wikis.title: Xbox One to launch in Japan on September 4
wikis.summary: Ars Technica (Apr 23, 2014) on Microsoft Japan's announcement that Xbox One launches in Japan September 4, with 48 registered publishers and a light game list.
wikis.body:
- By Sam Machkovech, Apr 23, 2014.
- Microsoft Japan announced the Xbox One will launch in Japan on September 4, nearly 10 months after North America and Europe.
- 48 companies listed as registered publishers, including FromSoftware, Level-5, Atlus, Electronic Arts, Bethesda and Ubisoft.
- First-party games: Forza Motorsport 5, Dead Rising 3, Ryse: Son of Rome (2013 launch titles), plus upcoming Sunset Overdrive and a tentatively titled "Halo for Xbox One" (unclear whether Halo 5, a Halo 2 anniversary edition or another; not Halo: Spartan Assault).
- Few JRPGs: Kingdom Hearts III, Final Fantasy XV, D4 and Metal Gear Solid V's two releases; Japan-friendly first-party games so far are D4 and Crimson Dragon.
- No prices or dates for games and no mention of media apps. The author says Sony's 10-month lead should keep Microsoft at the bottom of Japan's sales stats (author's view).

wikis.title: Xbox One sells fewer than 24,000 units in Japan (Time)
wikis.summary: Time (SEP 10, 2014) reports Famitsu figures of 23,562 Xbox One units sold in Japan in the first four days from September 4-7, compared with other consoles' launches.
wikis.body:
- By Matt Peckham, SEP 10, 2014. Per Famitsu, the Xbox One sold 23,562 units in Japan during September 4-7.
- Comparisons: Xbox 360 (Dec 2005) 62,135 in half as many days; original Xbox (Feb 2002) 123,929 in launch weekend; PlayStation 4 322,083 in first two days (Nov 2013); Wii U 308,570 in first two days (Nov 2012); PlayStation 2 best ever at 630,552 in launch weekend.
- Original Xbox sold fewer than half a million in Japan over its life; Xbox 360 "north of 1.6 million"; Wii U passed the Xbox 360 in Japan last February.
- Software: Titanfall 22,416, Kinect Sports Rivals 14,191, Dead Rising 3 7,330.
- Worldwide: 5 million Xbox One at last check in April; launching in 29 new markets that month.
- Upcoming titles mentioned: Halo: The Master Chief Collection, Forza Horizon 2, Sunset Overdrive, Ori and the Blind Forest ("not yet a lock for 2014"). Quote of Aaron Greenberg on reluctance to publish sales figures is not captured.

wikis.title: Xbox One launch didn't ignite Japan: 23K consoles sold (Engadget)
wikis.summary: Engadget (Sept. 10, 2014) on Famitsu data showing 23,562 Xbox One units sold in Japan in the opening week, with launch comparisons and a Microsoft Japan executive quote.
wikis.body:
- By Sinan Kubba, Sept. 10, 2014. Famitsu recorded 23,562 Xbox One units from Thursday September 4 to Sunday September 7.
- Comparisons: Xbox 360 62,135 over two days; original Xbox 123,929 in opening weekend (more than five times Xbox One); PS4 about 322,000 in two days; Wii U about 308,000 launch weekend (2012); PS2 best ever at 630,552.
- Software: Titanfall bundle helped Respawn's shooter reach 22,416; Kinect Sports Rivals 14,191; Dead Rising 3 7,330.
- Launched seven months after the PS4 and nearly two years after the Wii U. Microsoft held a launch event but photos emerged of empty queue lines near midnight.
- In 2013 Microsoft Japan CEO Yasuyuki Higuchi said the console "is geared toward a western lifestyle" and releasing it "as is would be difficult".
- Global: up to 5 million shipped as of April 2014, after more than a million in its first 24 hours in the West.

wikis.title: Broadcom BCM4358 combo chip doubles Wi-Fi performance (press release)
wikis.summary: Broadcom press release (Sept. 3, 2014) announcing the BCM4358 802.11ac 2x2 MIMO Wi-Fi and Bluetooth combo chip for high-end smartphones and tablets.
wikis.body:
- Irvine, Calif., Sept. 3, 2014 (PRNewswire). Broadcom Corporation (NASDAQ: BRCM) announced the BCM4358, described as the industry's most powerful 5G WiFi (802.11ac) 2x2 MIMO combo chip for mobile devices; second-generation 2x2 MIMO combo.
- Claims: 650 Mbps Wi-Fi data throughput, 50 percent better coexistence with Bluetooth, downloads two times faster, indoor location accuracy down to one meter. Consumers spend an average of 4-5 hours a day on Wi-Fi (ABI Research, August 2014).
- Key features: 867 Mbps PHY rate on 80MHz channel; low power PCIe host interface for WLAN, UART for Bluetooth; Android, Windows and Chrome support; integrated PA, LNA and TR switch; transmit beamforming and LDPC; RTT-based indoor location; TurboQAM for the highest 2.4 GHz data rate; first to enable Angle-of-Arrival direction finding on a smartphone.
- Quotes: David Recker (Broadcom Senior Director, Wireless Connectivity) and Philip Solis (Research Director, ABI Research).
- Availability: "now in production and will be shipping in mobile devices available in Q3 2014."

wikis.title: Broadcom aims to double Wi-Fi performance for smartphones and tablets (VentureBeat)
wikis.summary: VentureBeat (September 3, 2014) report on Broadcom's BCM4358 Wi-Fi and Bluetooth combo chip, which Broadcom says will double wireless performance in high-end devices.
wikis.body:
- By Dean Takahashi, 5:00 am PT, September 3, 2014.
- Broadcom unveiled the BCM4358 Wi-Fi and Bluetooth combo chip which it says will double wireless networking performance for high-end phones and tablets; "Or so the company hopes."
- Broadcom says it will be the highest-performing 5G 802.11ac combo chip available when it debuts in the third quarter; second-generation 2x2 MIMO.
- Bluetooth coexists with existing wireless devices; Wi-Fi can deliver accurate indoor location. Consumers spend an estimated four to five hours a day on Wi-Fi; videos download twice as fast with less lag.
- Quotes from David Recker (Broadcom) and Philip Solis (ABI Research), same as in the press release. The captured text ends at "More".

wikis.title: TechCrunch Disrupt Hackathon: get your tickets
wikis.summary: TechCrunch (July 28, 2014) post with details and ticket information for the Disrupt SF 2014 Hackathon on September 6-7 at Pier 48.
wikis.body:
- By Jeffery Bennett, 2:00 PM PDT, July 28, 2014.
- The Disrupt Hackathon kicks off TechCrunch Disrupt. Starts Saturday, September 6th at 12:30pm; hackers have "24-hours(ish)" to build a working concept, then teams get exactly one minute to present.
- Location: Pier 48. Hacking begins Sat. Sept 6th at 12:30pm; presentations begin Sun. Sept. 7th at 11:00am. API workshops planned.
- Tickets released in batches of 250 via Eventbrite; first batch available.
- Competitors traditionally got free Disrupt tickets; this year only the top 75 teams, as rated by judges, will receive tickets (later corrected in a September 6 post, see that article).
- Reasons to enter listed: exposure, time (food and Red Bull provided), and meeting other developers and VCs.

wikis.title: The Disrupt SF Hackathon has begun
wikis.summary: TechCrunch (September 6, 2014) note that the Disrupt SF hackathon kicked off at Pier 48, with corrected rules for earning Disrupt tickets.
wikis.body:
- By Anthony Ha, 3:20 PM PDT, September 6, 2014.
- The hackathon just kicked off; tables at Pier 48 (Disrupt's new, bigger home) are full of coders. Teams have "a little less than 24 hours" to build products and prototypes and present them the next morning for prizes, rated by judges.
- Some teams travelled from as far as Berlin (interviews in a video by Jordan Crook and Anthony Ha).
- Ticket rules: (1) team needs a 3 or above from the judges; (2) each judge rates each team 1-5, averaged; (3) advancing teams get two tickets per team to Disrupt SF; (4) each team nominates the two recipients on Challenge Post before presentations.
- Editor's note: an earlier version wrongly said 75 tickets would be given as prizes.
- Tickets to Disrupt SF are still available for purchase.

wikis.title: Full agenda for TechCrunch Disrupt SF 2014
wikis.summary: TechCrunch (August 28, 2014) announcement of the full agenda for Disrupt SF, September 6-10, 2014 at Pier 48, with speaker lists and a day-by-day schedule for September 8-10.
wikis.body:
- By Susan Hobbs, 11:12 AM PDT, August 28, 2014. Disrupt hits San Francisco September 6-10 at its new home, Pier 48; five days.
- Named speakers: Peter Thiel, Vinod Khosla, Laura Arrillaga-Andreessen; Brian Chesky, Elizabeth Holmes, Scott Dietzen; Mark Cuban (Dallas Mavericks owner); Marc Benioff with Michael Arrington; Dan Gilbert (Quicken Loans, Cleveland Cavaliers) on rebuilding Detroit; Max Levchin, Daphne Koller, Julia and Kevin Hartz; Ev Williams and Walter Isaacson; Sean Rad; Emmett Shear and Kevin Lin (Twitch); Liam Casey. "A few more surprises to come".
- Hackathon: 24-hour event starting Saturday, September 6, teams present on the Disrupt stage Sunday. Startup Alley and Hardware Alley host hundreds of startups.
- Startup Battlefield winner gets the Disrupt Cup and a $50,000 prize.
- Tickets: 300 student tickets; early-bird until September 1, after which price jumps $1,000; free Hackathon tickets "sold out" but free tickets to see presentations available.
- Schedule highlights: Mon Sept 8 - Travis Kalanick (Uber) fireside chat 9:05am, Max Levchin, Mark Cuban, Elizabeth Holmes, Ev Williams and Walter Isaacson, Peter Thiel "Zero to One" at 2:00pm, Startup Battlefield sessions One-Three (Automate, Accelerate, Activate); after party by New Relic at Mighty, 119 Utah Street.
- Tue Sept 9 - Dan Gilbert, Eventbrite's Hartzes, Marc Benioff at 11:00am, Vinod Khosla, Ryan Hoover (Product Hunt), Brian Chesky at 2:00pm, Battlefield sessions Four-Six (Streamline, Transform, Extend); after party at Public Works, 161 Erie Street.
- Wed Sept 10 - Daphne Koller, Sean Rad (Tinder), "Game of Drones", Dave Morin (Path), digital medicine and "The Convenience Economy" panels, Gil Penchina and Naval Ravikant; further items follow beyond the text read.
- Wed Sept 10 afternoon: Startup Battlefield Finals 3:00pm-5:00pm (judges include Roelof Botha, David Lee, John Lilly, Marissa Mayer, Keith Rabois, Kevin Rose), cocktail reception hosted by Live Journal, Closing Awards Ceremony 5:30pm, after party at Mezzanine, 444 Jessie Street.

wikis.title: Bloomberg also claims September 9 debut for Apple's wearable (MacRumors)
wikis.summary: MacRumors (August 28, 2014) says Bloomberg seconds Re/code's report that Apple will unveil its wearable device alongside the iPhone 6 at a September 9 event.
wikis.body:
- By Juli Clover, Thursday August 28, 2014.
- Re/code reported the day before that Apple would introduce its wearable device alongside the iPhone 6; Bloomberg now seconds it, pointing to a simultaneous debut of two iPhones and a wearable at Apple's September 9 event.
- Per Re/code, Apple had originally planned an October event for the wearable but changed plans. Bloomberg speculates the joint debut may limit expectations, positioning it as an iPhone accessory (contrast: iPad got its own event in 2010).
- Event location: Flint Center at De Anza College, where the original Macintosh was introduced thirty years ago and the first iMac in 1998; Apple is building a massive structure on site, purpose unclear.
- Tim Cook promised "really great stuff" in new product categories; Eddy Cue called it the "best product pipeline" in 25 years.
- Likely unveiled several months before consumer availability; lack of leaks suggests it is not yet in production.
- Rumoured (no images seen): commonly called the iWatch; focus on health and fitness sensors (steps, sleep, heart rate), multiple sizes and price points, tight integration with iPhone and iOS 8 Health app.
- Page sidebar and comments (2026 stories, reader remarks) are unrelated to the article.

wikis.title: Apple unveils iPhone 6, iPhone 6 Plus, Apple Watch (CBS News)
wikis.summary: CBS News (updated September 9, 2014) report on Apple's event introducing the iPhone 6 and 6 Plus, Apple Pay and the Apple Watch, with prices and dates.
wikis.body:
- By Alain Sherter, updated September 9, 2014. Apple introduced two new iPhones, its Apple Watch and a mobile payment system at an event at the Flint Center (Cupertino), presented by Philip Schiller and Tim Cook; started late.
- iPhone 6: 4.7-inch screen, over 1 million pixels; iPhone 6 Plus: 5.5-inch, over 2 million pixels; aluminum body, curved glass front; camera with image stabilization.
- Availability: Sept. 19; pre-orders begin Sept. 12. With two-year contract: iPhone 6 $199 (16GB), $299 (64GB), $399 (128GB); iPhone 6 Plus $299 (16GB), $399 (64GB), $499 (128GB).
- Apple Pay: uses NFC; Cook said Americans make roughly 200 million payments per day; partners American Express, Mastercard, Visa; works at more than 220,000 retailers; also McDonald's, Disney, Target, Subway, Whole Foods.
- Apple Watch: six interchangeable bands; stainless steel, aluminum or 18K gold; priced at $349; navigated by tapping, swiping and a crown; works with iPhone 5, 5c, 5s and 6; available "early next year". Cook: "the most personal device we've ever created."
- IHS's Ian Fogg: a first-generation device in a "bold, expensive and risky" new category.
- Context: recent launches seen as incremental; the watch is the first product developed entirely under Cook. HealthKit is mentioned; the text is cut off after that.

wikis.title: MacRumors live coverage of Apple's September 2014 iPhone and iWatch event
wikis.summary: Live blog (September 9, 2014) of Apple's Flint Center event: iPhone 6 and 6 Plus, Apple Pay, Apple Watch and a free U2 album, in reverse chronological order.
wikis.body:
- By Jordan Golson, Tuesday September 9, 2014. Event at the Flint Center for the Performing Arts, Cupertino, 10:00 AM PT / 1:00 PM ET; live stream on Apple's website and Apple TV. Blog ends 12:01 pm "The keynote is concluded."
- **iPhone 6 / 6 Plus (10:30-10:41 am):** Panorama up to 43 megapixels; Focus Pixels autofocus; optical image stabilization on the 6 Plus only; 1080p video at 30 and 60fps, slo-mo at 240fps (up from 120fps on the 5s); front camera f2.2 letting in 81% more light; time-lapse. Colours Gold, Silver, Space Gray. With two-year contract: iPhone 6 $199/$299/$399; 6 Plus $299/$399/$499 (16/64/128GB); iPhone 5s from $99, 5c 8GB $0. Preorder September 12 in US and 8 other countries.
- **Apple Pay (10:44-10:56 am):** Tim Cook: "We spend $12 billion in credit and debit transactions per day in the US". Uses NFC and Touch ID with Secure Element; card number not stored or shared; works with 220,000 US merchants and Amex, Mastercard, Visa, 83% of credit card purchases; launches in US "next month", free with iOS 8.
- **Apple Watch (10:57-11:44 am):** named "Apple Watch"; digital crown, force-sensing display, S1 chip, heart-rate sensors, haptic feedback; six straps, two sizes; three collections (Apple Watch, Sport, Edition, the latter in 18K gold); Digital Touch, Siri, Glances, Maps, Photos; activity rings (Move, Exercise, Stand) and workout app; WatchKit for third-party apps; needs iPhone (5, 5c, 5s, 6, 6 Plus). "Apple Watch starts at $349." Available "early 2015".
- **U2 (11:44-11:57 am):** U2 performed; album "Songs of Innocence" free to every iTunes customer in 119 countries starting immediately, exclusive through October 13.
- Closing thanks to Apple staff including Craig Federighi, Eddy Cue, Jony Ive, Jeff Williams.

wikis.title: DisplayPort 1.3 spec finalized, bringing Retina iMacs and 5K displays closer (MacRumors)
wikis.summary: MacRumors (September 15, 2014) on VESA's release of DisplayPort 1.3, with 32.4 Gbps bandwidth enabling single-cable 5K displays, in the context of Dell's 5K display and rumoured Apple Retina products.
wikis.body:
- By Eric Slivka, Monday September 15, 2014 (via 9to5Mac).
- Dell announced an upcoming 5120 x 2880 "5K" display, equivalent to a Retina 27-inch iMac or Apple Thunderbolt Display; Apple rumored to be launching its own later that year.
- VESA officially released DisplayPort 1.3: 50 percent more bandwidth, 32.4 Gbps, or 25.92 Gbps of uncompressed video data after overhead.
- Enables 5K (5120 x 2880) over a single DisplayPort cable without compression, and two 4K UHD (3840 x 2160) monitors over one connection via Multi-Stream, using VESA Coordinated Video Timing.
