- DisplayPort 1.2a already supported uncompressed 4K; 5K was difficult. Connectivity bottlenecks are described as one factor slowing Apple's Retina iMacs/displays; DisplayPort 1.3 will "presumably" be built into future Thunderbolt implementations.
- Reader comments (opinions) worry about needing a new Mac Pro to drive such a display.

wikis.title: VESA releases the DisplayPort 1.3 standard
wikis.summary: VESA press release (15 September 2014) announcing DisplayPort 1.3 with 32.4 Gbps maximum link bandwidth.
wikis.body:
- Newark, CA (15 September 2014): the Video Electronics Standards Association (VESA) announced release of the DisplayPort 1.3 audio/video standard, an update to DisplayPort 1.2a.
- Max link bandwidth rises to 32.4 Gbps: four lanes at 8.1 Gbps/lane, "a 50% increase from the previous version". After transport overhead it carries 25.92 Gbps of uncompressed video data.
- Enables 5K monitors (5120 x 2880) over a single cable without compression, and two 4K UHD monitors (3840 x 2160 each) through one connection via Multi-Stream and VESA Coordinated Video Timing.
- Keeps video conversion to VGA, DVI and HDMI; adds HDCP 2.2 and HDMI 2.0 with CEC; adds 4:2:0 pixel structure, which "enables support for future 8K x 4K displays".
- Two lanes can drive a single UHD monitor at 60Hz and 24-bit color, leaving two lanes for other data such as SuperSpeed USB as allowed in DockPort. DisplayPort is the A/V transport used by DockPort, Thunderbolt and other multi-function interfaces.
- Quote from VESA Board Chair Alan Kobayashi (MegaChips Technology America): the enhancements "will facilitate both higher resolution displays, as well as easier integration of DisplayPort into multi-protocol data transports".
- The standard is offered to VESA members without any license fee.

wikis.title: KitGuru on VESA DisplayPort 1.3 spec release
wikis.summary: KitGuru news article (16 September 2014) reporting VESA's DisplayPort 1.3 release, with 8K support and 4K at 120Hz in the headline.
wikis.body:
- Published September 16, 2014 by Anton Shilov; says VESA "on Monday released the DisplayPort 1.3 standard".
- Max link bandwidth 32.4Gb/s, four lanes at 8.1Gb/s each. Supports 5K (5120*2880) over one cable without compression, and two 4K (3840*2160) monitors via Multi-Stream with VESA Coordinated Video Timing.
- Adds 4:2:0 pixel structure enabling future 8K*4K (7680*4320) displays; supports HDCP 2.2 and HDMI 2.0 with CEC.
- 8.1 Gbps per lane can drive a single UHD monitor at 60Hz and 24-bit color over two lanes, leaving two for other data such as SuperSpeed USB (DockPort).
- Quote from VESA board head Alan Kobayashi about higher resolution displays and easier multi-protocol integration.
- KitGuru says it "remains to be seen" when graphics cards and DP1.3 monitors arrive; it is "logical to expect" GPUs with DP 1.3 sometime next year with new UHD displays, and mass adoption "will take some time".

wikis.title: iPhone 6 said to launch Friday September 19 in 32 GB and 64 GB
wikis.summary: MacRumors report (25 June 2014) citing Tencent that Apple would launch the 4.7-inch iPhone 6 on Friday, September 19, in 32GB and 64GB variants.
wikis.body:
- MacRumors, Wednesday June 25, 2014, by Richard Padilla.
- Per a report from Chinese portal Tencent citing inside sources, Apple "will look to launch" the 4.7-inch iPhone 6 on Friday, September 19. German carrier Deutsche Telekom was reported to be telling customers a similar date.
- Reported capacities and prices: 32GB at 5,288 yuan ($846) and 64GB at 6,288 yuan ($1008), suggesting Apple "may" launch without a 16GB model. 5,288 yuan is the current 16GB iPhone 5s price in China; 32GB iPhone 5s is 6,088 yuan.
- Article notes a September launch matches the past two iPhone launches and Apple typically launches on a Friday. A Bloomberg report claimed the 5.5-inch and 4.7-inch versions may launch simultaneously, though earlier reports said battery and display issues would hold up the larger one.
- Expected features: larger display, thinner design, faster A8 processor, improved camera (5.5-inch model exclusively with optical image stabilization).
- Reader comments (not article facts) mostly ask for a 128GB option.

wikis.title: Apple announces iPhone 6 and iPhone 6 Plus
wikis.summary: Apple press release (9 September 2014) announcing iPhone 6 and 6 Plus with 4.7-inch and 5.5-inch displays, A8 chip, cameras, Apple Pay, and US pricing.
wikis.body:
- Cupertino, September 9, 2014: Apple announced iPhone 6 (4.7-inch, 1334 x 750, "38 percent more viewing area than iPhone 5s") and iPhone 6 Plus (5.5-inch, 1920 x 1080, 88 percent more viewing area, nearly three times the pixels). Anodized aluminum unibody, "thinnest ever".
- A8 chip with second generation 64-bit desktop-class architecture; Metal graphics in iOS 8; M8 motion coprocessor with new barometer.
- Cameras: new iSight sensor with Focus Pixels; optical image stabilization on iPhone 6 Plus only; 1080p at up to 60fps, slo-mo at 240fps; FaceTime HD camera captures over 80 percent more light, f/2.2 aperture.
- Connectivity: LTE up to 150 Mbps, VoLTE, Wi-Fi calling, up to 20 LTE bands, 802.11ac Wi-Fi up to 433 Mbps, Bluetooth 4.0.
- Apple Pay: pay in stores by holding the phone near a contactless reader with a finger on Touch ID; payment info kept in a Secure Element. Available to US customers as a free iOS 8 update "this October".
- iOS 8 free update starting Wednesday, September 17; more than 4,000 new APIs; App Store has more than 1.3 million apps in 155 countries.
- Pricing (US, two-year contract): iPhone 6 $199 (16GB), $299 (64GB), $399 (128GB, new). iPhone 6 Plus $299, $399, $499. Colors gold, silver, space gray. iPhone 5s $99 (16GB) / $149 (32GB); iPhone 5c 8GB free.
- Cases: leather $45 (iPhone 6) / $49 (6 Plus); silicone $35 / $39.
- Pre-orders begin Friday, September 12; availability Friday, September 19 in US, Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Hong Kong, Japan, Puerto Rico, Singapore and UK.
- Quote from Tim Cook: "the biggest advancements in iPhone history".

wikis.title: iPhone 6 and 6 Plus (Wikipedia, part 1): history, specifications, reception and issues
wikis.summary: First half of the Wikipedia article on the iPhone 6 and 6 Plus covering their release, hardware and software, reviews, and early hardware issues such as Bendgate.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Eighth-generation iPhones by Apple, succeeding the iPhone 5, 5c and 5s. Unveiled at the Flint Center for Performing Arts in Cupertino on September 9, 2014; pre-orders began September 12; released September 19, 2014 (US$199 for iPhone 6, US$299 for 6 Plus, starting prices).
- 4.7-inch and 5.5-inch displays, faster processor, upgraded cameras, improved LTE and Wi-Fi, NFC-based mobile payments. Replaced as flagship by iPhone 6s/6s Plus on September 9, 2015. Article says the iPhone 6 "sold extremely well", becoming the best-selling iPhone model and "the most successful smartphone to date".
- Supported iOS 8 through 12 before being dropped by iOS 13 (Apple announced in June 2019).
- Release dates in the infobox: Sept 19, 2014 (US, UK, Canada, France, Germany, Australia, Hong Kong, Singapore, Japan, Puerto Rico and others); Sept 26 (25 countries); October 17 (China, India, Monaco) and further waves through October and November 2014.

## History
- Reports from January 2014 suggested larger 4.7 and 5.5-inch models after Apple's loss of smartphone share to larger-display makers; earlier iPhones had 3.5-inch (up to 4s) then 4-inch displays.
- In China Apple said it could not release on the 19th, citing "details which are not ready"; local media reported it lacked Ministry of Industry and Information Technology approval.
- August 2015: replacement program for some early 6 Plus models with potentially faulty cameras (blurry photos).
- Sept 9, 2015: 6/6 Plus moved to mid-range; 128 GB versions and gold discontinued; 16/64 GB silver and space gray cut in price.
- June 2016: potential China sales ban alleged by Shenzhen Baili over a design patent.
- Sept 7, 2016: discontinued in most markets when iPhone 7 announced (iPhone SE had been released March 31, 2016). February 2017: iPhone 6 relaunched with 32 GB storage (Asia first, US in May, Canada July 2017).

## Specifications
- Design: glass front curved at edges, aluminum unibody back with two plastic antenna strips; gold, silver, space gray. Thickness 6.9 mm (6) and 7.1 mm (6 Plus). Side button moved from top to side.
- Displays: "Retina HD", iPhone 6 4.7-inch 1334x750 (326 ppi), 6 Plus 5.5-inch 1920x1080 (401 ppi); dual-domain pixels.
- Batteries: 6.91 Wh (1,810 mAh) and 11.1 Wh (2,915 mAh), not user-replaceable.
- Chips: Apple A8 and M8 coprocessor with barometer. Phil Schiller said A8 gives 25% more CPU and 50% more graphics performance than the 5s.
- Connectivity: LTE Advanced, over 20 bands, up to 150 Mbit/s, VoLTE; 802.11ac up to 433 Mbit/s; Wi-Fi calling; NFC initially used exclusively for Apple Pay.
- Camera: 1080p at 30/60 fps, 720p slow-mo at 120/240 fps; phase detection autofocus; optical image stabilization on 6 Plus only, photos only (off during video); protruding lens; front camera 1.3 MP with f/2.2, burst and HDR.
- Software: iOS 8 preloaded; "Reachability" double-tap gesture added.

## Reception
- Positive reviews. Re/code: "the best smartphone you can buy". TechRadar praised design, battery and camera; criticised plastic antenna strips, lower display resolution than rivals, and price. The Verge: "good, even great, but there's little about it that's truly ambitious". Engadget panned the 6 Plus grip but praised OIS. Forbes criticised lack of 2160p video.

## Issues
- Bendgate: chassis bending under pressure; Apple said it had received only nine complaints and that bending from regular use is "extremely rare". In May 2018 court documents showed Apple's internal tests found the 6 was 3.3 times and the 6 Plus 7.2 times more likely to bend than the 5s.
- Hair ripping (9to5Mac, October 3, 2014): users complained the glass/aluminum seam caught hair.
- Flash storage performance complaints on larger capacity models, 6 Plus camera problems, and "error 53" are also listed as issues.

wikis.title: Apple: iPhone 6 pre-orders top four million in 24 hours
wikis.summary: Apple press release (15 September 2014) reporting record iPhone 6/6 Plus pre-orders of over four million in the first 24 hours and launch dates.
wikis.body:
- Cupertino, September 15, 2014: "over four million" pre-orders in the first 24 hours, a record for Apple. Demand exceeds initial pre-order supply; many pre-orders "scheduled to be delivered in October".
- Walk-in supply on Friday, September 19 at 8:00 a.m. local time at Apple retail stores; also from AT&T, Sprint, T-Mobile, Verizon Wireless, other carriers and select resellers.
- Launch September 19 in US, Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Hong Kong, Japan, Puerto Rico, Singapore and UK; in more than 20 additional countries on Friday, September 26 (including Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, Ireland, Italy, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, UAE and others).
- US pricing with two-year contract: iPhone 6 $199 (16GB), $299 (64GB), $399 (128GB); iPhone 6 Plus $299, $399, $499. Gold, silver, space gray. Free Personal Setup in Apple retail stores.
- Restates specs: 4.7-inch and 5.5-inch Retina HD displays, A8 chip, iOS 8, Apple Pay.
- Tim Cook quote: pre-orders "set a new record for Apple".

wikis.title: Tim Cook: iPhone 6 will trigger 'the mother of all upgrades'
wikis.summary: MacRumors (9 September 2014) on Tim Cook's Wall Street Journal interview after the iPhone 6 event.
wikis.body:
- MacRumors, Tuesday September 9, 2014, by Richard Padilla.
- In a WSJ interview after the media event, Tim Cook said Apple expects iPhone 6 and 6 Plus to trigger "the mother of all upgrades", and expects Android users to consider switching, saying the phones are "appreciably better in every single way".
- On Apple Pay: "classic Apple" in taking a complex problem and making it simple; "Yes, there is going to be some economic benefit".
- On Apple Watch: the byproduct of deep thinking about every aspect of the product, possible because of collaboration among hardware, software and services teams, which he believes will differentiate it from other smartwatches with "tepid sales".
- Launch September 19, pre-orders from Friday, September 12. iPhone 6: 16/64/128 GB at $199/$299/$399; iPhone 6 Plus: $299/$399/$499.

wikis.title: Huge crowds greet Apple's iPhone 6 launch (MacDailyNews)
wikis.summary: MacDailyNews (19 September 2014) excerpting a Wall Street Journal report on iPhone 6 and 6 Plus launch-day queues, starting in Australia, and pricing.
wikis.body:
- Posted Friday, September 19, 2014. Quotes WSJ reporters Daniel Stacey and Ross Kelly.
- Apple began sales Friday with consumers in Australia first globally; veterans said queues were "the longest" outside Sydney's Apple store, "highlighting strong initial demand".
- WSJ: screen upgrade, better battery life, faster processor and improved camera expected to drive demand; Tim Cook had said he expects the "mother of all upgrades".
- Pricing: base price of the most-expensive model raised by $100. iPhone 6 starts at $649 without contract (same as the iPhone 5S a year earlier); iPhone 6 Plus $749 without contract, the most expensive iPhone Apple has sold.
- Apple's US online store waiting time: iPhone 6 Plus three-to-four weeks; iPhone 6 seven to 10 business days. Apple set aside supplies for in-store buyers on Friday.
- Related links: a report of long lines in Asia and Europe, an iFixit teardown of the 6 Plus, and Larry Ellison stepping down as Oracle CEO (only as neighbouring headlines). Reader comments (not article facts) describe queues in Basingstoke UK (about 200), NYC 14th St and Fifth Avenue.

wikis.title: Apple: first weekend iPhone 6 sales top 10 million
wikis.summary: Apple press release (22 September 2014) announcing over 10 million iPhone 6 and 6 Plus sold in three days, a record.
wikis.body:
- Cupertino, September 22, 2014: Apple sold "over 10 million" new iPhone 6 and iPhone 6 Plus models, "a new record", three days after the September 19 launch.
- Available in US, Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Hong Kong, Japan, Puerto Rico, Singapore and UK; more than 20 additional countries on September 26; 115 countries by the end of the year.
- Tim Cook: sales "exceeded our expectations", "our best launch ever, shattering all previous sell-through records by a large margin"; "we could have sold many more iPhones with greater supply".
- US pricing with two-year contract: iPhone 6 $199 / $299 / $399 (16/64/128GB); iPhone 6 Plus $299 / $399 / $499. Gold, silver, space gray. Retailers include AT&T, Sprint, T-Mobile, Verizon, Best Buy, Radio Shack, Target, Walmart.
- Free Personal Setup and free iOS 8 workshops at Apple retail stores. Apple Pay to arrive as a free iOS 8 update in the US "this October".

wikis.title: Tom's Hardware Tech Industry news listing (no Tesla article)
wikis.summary: The fetched page is a Tom's Hardware Tech Industry section listing of headlines dated August-September 2026, not the Tesla Model S software update article named in the URL.
wikis.body:
- The URL slug refers to a Tesla Model S software update, but the captured text is the Tom's Hardware "Tech Industry" category index page. It contains no text about Tesla or a Model S update.
- It lists headlines only, with bylines and dates (mostly 17-19 September 2026, older ones back to May 2026), grouped under Artificial Intelligence, Big Tech, Cryptocurrency and Cybersecurity. Examples: "Intel suspends bug bounty program that paid up to $100,000 per flaw" (19 September 26); "Nvidia revenue tops $96 billion as memory commitments soar to $160 billion" (27 August 26); "Apple eyes Nvidia NVLink to power its new custom M8 Ultra AI servers" (17 September 26).
- No facts about the intended Tesla topic can be taken from this source.

wikis.title: Tesla Model S software v6.0 adds calendar and traffic navigation (Engadget)
wikis.summary: Engadget (19 September 2014) on Tesla's version 6.0 Model S update with calendar sync, traffic-based navigation and remote start.
wikis.body:
- Engadget, by Dana Wollman, Sept. 19, 2014. Tesla released the "(previously leaked)" version 6.0 of the Model S software; the article says most changelog updates are minor bug fixes and major feature updates are rare.
- Built-in calendar syncing with your smartphone: daily view on the in-car display; tap an event with a location for driving directions.
- Traffic-based navigation: monitors real-time traffic using data from other Tesla drivers and gives a pop-up if it thinks you should take a faster route.
- Remote start using your phone, useful if you forgot the key fob.
- Smaller tweaks: location-based air suspension remembers where you chose high ride heights; car nickname in the app; power management setting to enter energy saving mode at night.
- Quote from Elon Musk on Twitter: the calendar app with tap to nav and traffic predictor "will radically improve how the car adapts to the owner over time".
- Update available now; requires latest Android/iOS app.

wikis.title: Tesla Model S Software v6.0 now available (CleanTechnica)
wikis.summary: CleanTechnica (23 September 2014) summarising Tesla's Software v6.0 over-the-air update features for the Model S.
wikis.body:
- CleanTechnica, September 23, 2014, by James Ayre. Software v6.0 arrived over the air with more personalization options.
- Traffic-Based Navigation (BETA): route suggestions and estimated travel times from real-time traffic, updated dynamically, using traffic data shared by other Tesla vehicles.
- Commute Advice: monitors traffic before a weekday commute and shows a pop-up on the 17-inch touchscreen when a faster route is available.
- Calendar (BETA): syncs with smartphone for a large in-car daily schedule; tap an event to get route directions.
- Remote Start: start the Model S from the Tesla mobile app; password required for each use.
- Location-Based Air Suspension: remembers where high ride heights were selected and adjusts automatically (needs air suspension).
- Name Your Car: nickname appears in the mobile app and the About Your Tesla section.
- Power Management: energy saving mode at night; option for the app to connect immediately while saving power.

wikis.title: Xbox One to launch in China September 23 (Xbox Wire)
wikis.summary: Xbox Wire post (30 July 2014) announcing Microsoft and BesTV will launch Xbox One in China on September 23 from ¥3,699 RMB.
wikis.body:
- Xbox Wire Staff, July 30, 2014: Microsoft and BesTV announced Xbox One launches in China on September 23 starting at ¥3,699 RMB. It is "the first gaming and entertainment console approved for sale in China", coinciding with the Shanghai Free Trade Zone one-year anniversary.
- Games: more than 25 developers building more than 70 games. Prices ¥99-¥249 RMB (e.g. Forza Motorsport 5 at ¥249). Day-one Microsoft Studios titles: Forza Motorsport 5, Kinect Sports Rivals, Powerstar Golf, Zoo Tycoon, Max: The Curse of Brotherhood; later Sunset Overdrive and Halo: The Master Chief Collection. Twelve large developers (EA, Ubisoft, 2K) and thirteen Chinese developers (Neverwinter Online from Perfect World, Gamebar, Yingpei; Snail Games, NetEase, Tencent in development). Neverwinter Online Xbox One-only for six months after launch.
- Entertainment via BesTV: hundreds of thousands of hours of movies, sports, documentaries, TV; two free movies per month; English Premier League free for the first year; Xbox Fitness library including Tai Chi; local apps (Tencent QQ Music, Douban FM, GameFY, Karaoke Master).
- Every console includes: Powerstar Golf and Neverwinter Online (Special Edition Pack), BesTV experience, free Xbox Live Gold through March 2015, localized Chinese interface and payment methods, two-year warranty and local support. Xbox Live Gold subscriptions ¥199 RMB.
- ID@Xbox program launches in China that day; two innovation centers (first in Shanghai) planned with BesTV, Microsoft and local government.
- Quotes: Yusuf Mehdi (Microsoft) "honored that Xbox One is the first console approved for sale in China"; Zhang Dazhong (Shanghai Media Group / E-Home Entertainment); Robert Xiao (Perfect World); Enwei Xie (general manager, Xbox China).

wikis.title: Intel preparing new Xeon E5 v3 processors for potential Mac Pro upgrade (MacRumors)
wikis.summary: MacRumors (14 August 2014) on Intel's Xeon E5 v3 'Grantley' chips and AMD FirePro cards as possible parts of a first Mac Pro update.
wikis.body:
- MacRumors, Thursday August 14, 2014, by Eric Slivka. The redesigned Mac Pro started shipping in the last days of 2013; shortages persisted for months; shipping reached "within 24 hours" two months earlier.
- Intel's "Grantley" Xeon E5 v3 chips are "nearly ready to ship" as successors to the "Romley" Xeon E5 v2 used in the Mac Pro. Intel began shipping some E5 v3 to server makers in July; wide availability "reportedly set for September".
- Top-end: the 2.7 GHz 12-core E5-2697 v2 is succeeded by the 2.6 GHz 14-core E5-2697 v3 (higher thermal rating); E5-269x v3 range spans 12 to 18 cores.
- E5-1600 series: 4-core 3.7 GHz E5-1620 v2 -> 3.5 GHz E5-1620 v3 or 3.7 GHz E5-1630 v3; 6-core E5-1650 v2 -> 3.5 GHz E5-1650 v3; 8-core 3.0 GHz E5-1680 v2 -> 3.2 GHz E5-1680 v3. All new chips support DDR4-2133 memory and have higher thermal ratings.
- Graphics: Apple's D300/D500/D700 roughly equate to AMD W7000/W8000/W9000; AMD introduced four new FirePro cards that week including the W7100. Per the article's comparison, each level has at least doubled VRAM and added 40% more stream processors.
- Timing of a Mac Pro update "remains unclear"; an upgrade in September is unlikely given Apple's iPhone focus; the article says late this year or early next year seems possible.

wikis.title: Intel unveils Xeon E5 v3 processors with up to 18 cores (KitGuru)
wikis.summary: KitGuru (9 September 2014) on Intel's launch of Haswell-based Xeon E5 2600/1600 v3 server processors and the Grantley platform.
wikis.body:
- KitGuru, Anton Shilov, September 9, 2014: Intel "on Monday" rolled out Xeon E5 2600/1600 v3 processors on the "Haswell" micro-architecture, with up to 18 cores per chip and quad-channel DDR4 memory controllers; new C612 platform code-named "Grantley".
- Up to three times higher performance than predecessors "in select cases". Platform extras: QuickAssist server adapter (hardware crypto acceleration and compression), Intel Ethernet XL710 40GbE adapter, DDR4 memory, Intel P3700-series SSDs.
- Specs: 4-18 cores (with or without Hyper-Threading), up to 45MB L3 cache, 55W-160W TDP; AVX2 doubles vector integer width to 256 bits (up to 1.9 times gains); AES-NI.
- Pricing (per 1000 units): E5-2600 v3 family 26 parts, $213 to $2702; E5-1600 v3 workstation family six parts, $295 to $1723.
- Partners ready to ship 65 servers, over 77 new systems in coming months, 250 machines in development.
- Quote from Diane Bryant (Intel Data Center Group) on data-center re-architecture.

wikis.title: BioLite smashes Kickstarter goal, raising over $1 million for BaseCamp
wikis.summary: BioLite press release (16 June 2014) on its BaseCamp wood stove Kickstarter raising $1,032,443 against a $45,000 goal.
wikis.body:
- Brooklyn, NY, June 16, 2014: the BaseCamp campaign raised $1,032,443 against an original goal of $45,000. The 32-day campaign ended "yesterday on Father's Day" with 3785 backers, the "67th most successful campaign in Kickstarter history". 3,244 backers pledged at the $299 level (BaseCamp plus a special-edition carrying case). A stretch goal (accessory chosen with backers) was met at $750,000 with three days to go.
- Product: wood/biomass-fuelled stove for groups that converts heat into electricity; 5 watts for charging devices, "twice the power of the CampStove"; can charge tablets; stores power; LED dashboard; flexible USB LED light; one-touch grill-to-boil lever; side feed; foldable legs.
- Specs: weight 20 lbs; 15" high (legs folded), 23" extended; 21" wide; 13.25" diameter cooktop fits eight large burgers. MSRP $299. Available September 2014.
- Quotes from Erica Rosen (Director of Marketing) and Jonathan Cedar (co-founder and CEO): "first crowd-funded product"; HomeStove-inspired product for the outdoor market.
- About BioLite: founded 2009 by Jonathan Cedar and Alec Drummond, headquartered in Brooklyn, NY.

wikis.title: BioLite BaseCamp: electricity from fire (Engineering.com)
wikis.summary: Engineering.com (10 June 2014) on BioLite's Kickstarter campaign for the BaseCamp stove that cooks and generates electricity.
wikis.body:
- Engineering.com, Jun 10, 2014, by Tom Spendlove. BioLite was in the "end stages" of a Kickstarter campaign for BaseCamp, after funding the CampStove there in 2012. The campaign had "already blown by its $45,000 goal with a week left".
- A thermoelectric generator turns fire heat into electricity; some powers a fan for combustion, the rest charges devices. Power pack generates up to 5 Watts and can store power; estimate: thirty minutes of charging gives five hours of talk time. Heat can be spread as a grill or concentrated for boiling.
- BioLite works on outdoor recreation and emerging markets; says smoky cooking fires kill more people than AIDS and malaria combined; four generations of stove prototypes since 2009; sells in Ghana, Uganda and India; 25 professionals.
- Prototyping complete, production tooling in process; stoves "expected to ship in October 2014".

wikis.title: Xbox One standalone Kinect sensor available in October (Xbox Wire)
wikis.summary: Xbox Wire post (27 August 2014) confirming a standalone Kinect for Xbox One from October 7 at $149.99 with Dance Central Spotlight.
wikis.body:
- Xbox Wire Staff, August 27, 2014. Beginning October 7, fans can buy a standalone Kinect sensor for Xbox One. It comes with Dance Central Spotlight (Harmonix, digital download, 10 tracks) and will be at retailers for $149.99.
- Context: since the new $399 Xbox One option (without Kinect) launched, Xbox One sales "double[d]", and demand for Xbox One with Kinect also increased.
- Kinect features listed: voice and gesture controls, biometric sign-in, instant personalization, QR code scanning; games such as Kinect Sports Rivals, Dead Rising 3, Project Spark; "billions of voice commands since launch"; commands "Xbox On", "Xbox Broadcast", "Xbox Record That"; Twitch, Game DVR, Bing voice search, Skype video calls, TV/set-top control via voice and HDMI-In ("Xbox watch ESPN").
- Purchase options: with Kinect, without Kinect for $399, bundled with games like Madden NFL 15 or Sunset Overdrive, or adding the standalone Kinect later.

wikis.title: iPhone 6 said to launch Tuesday October 14 (MacRumors)
wikis.summary: MacRumors (31 July 2014) reporting a source's claim that Apple may launch the iPhone 6 on Tuesday, October 14, after a September 16 media event.
wikis.body:
- MacRumors, Thursday July 31, 2014, by Richard Padilla. Apple "may be planning" to launch iPhone 6 on Tuesday, October 14, per a source citing an internal Apple Retail Store meeting where a senior Store Leader called October 14 an "immense" day and said the whole month would be very busy.
- Apple is also said to be planning a media event on Tuesday, September 16, a month before launch. A report the previous week claimed a mid-September iPhone 6/iOS 8 event followed by an October event for the iWatch, OS X Yosemite, new iPads and Macs.
- A Tuesday launch would break from past years (Fridays); the source says "high customer demand" and ample supply from a large production effort motivate an earlier-in-week start.
- Unknown whether an October release would include both 4.7-inch and 5.5-inch versions; production issues reportedly plague the larger one, which might come later in the year or 2015.
- Update: Apple's financial projections and earnings-call statements "strongly point toward" an iPhone 6 launch before the quarter ends on September 27.

wikis.title: TechRadar: iPhone 6 release date may fall on October 14
wikis.summary: TechRadar (31 July 2014) relaying MacRumors' report of a September 16 iPhone 6 event and a tentative October 14 on-sale date.
wikis.body:
- TechRadar, JR Bookwalter, 31 July 2014. MacRumors reported Apple "may be planning" to reveal iPhone 6 at a media event on Tuesday, September 16, with October 14 tentatively as on-sale date.
- Source: an unnamed attendee of an "internal Apple Retail Store meeting" where a senior Store Leader called that day "immense".
- Article notes every iPhone launch since 2007 has been on a Friday while October 14 is a Tuesday; the only explanation was "high customer demand" driving unprecedented production for "an ample supply".
- A separate report described a mid-September event for iPhone 6 and iOS 8 and an October event for OS X 10.10 Yosemite, Mac and iPad refreshes and possibly the "mythical iWatch".
- Conflicting reports questioned whether 4.7-inch and 5.5-inch models could launch together, with the larger possibly delayed by production issues.

wikis.title: Christian Post: iPhone 6 rumors of September 16 unveiling, October 14 availability
wikis.summary: Christian Post (2 August 2014) summarising a MacRumors report and analyst comments on iPhone 6 timing and sapphire glass.
wikis.body:
- Christian Post, Arvin Donguines, Saturday, August 02, 2014. Per a MacRumors report "if true", Apple plans a mid-September event to present the iPhone 6 and iOS 8 but not roll out the device until October 14, 2014.
- AppleInsider noted Oct. 14 is a Tuesday and Apple traditionally releases on Fridays, and that a month between unveiling and release is questionable since Apple usually releases about a week after unveiling.
- LEDinside (Trendforce) analysts said they had not noticed a spike in sapphire glass orders, suggesting Apple may not be in a hurry for a September rollout; they said sapphire cover glass "remains missing from the picture", components would need to ship to OEMs in June 2014 for a September launch, and a sapphire iPhone would be in limited volumes because of lower ingot yield rates.
- Rumored specs: Apple A8, NFC for mobile payments, Touch ID, improved camera; colors silver, gold and space gray like the iPhone 5S.

wikis.title: Killer Instinct: Season 2 launches October 15 on Xbox One (Xbox Wire video page)
wikis.summary: Xbox Wire video page (premiered October 14, 2014) announcing the global launch of Killer Instinct: Season 2 on Xbox One on October 15 with packs and prices.
wikis.body:
- Video page, premiered October 14, 2014, 4:12 runtime. Microsoft Studios and Iron Galaxy announce global launch of Killer Instinct: Season 2 on Wednesday, Oct. 15, exclusively on Xbox One.
- Story: "The Rise of Ultratech"; ARIA, Ultratech's CEO, unleashes creations including two classic arcade characters.
- Features: eight new characters (TJ Combo and Maya, joined by Riptor and Cinder; also a Babylonian sorcerer, an avenging ghost, a war golem); new interface; Season 1 cast rebalanced with new moves; "aerial recapture", Air Breakers and Air Counter-Breakers; new progression system with per-character levels and "Fight Challenges". As in Season 1, the game is a free download with a free rotating character weekly; Season 1 owners get updates automatically.
- Launch week free character: TJ Combo. Maya wields daggers "Temperance" and "Vengeance".
- Purchase: Ultra Edition $39.99/£34.99/€39.99 (all eight fighters, remaining six monthly from November, 16 accessory sets, eight costumes by Kevin Bayliss, and Killer Instinct 2 Classic, a port of the 1996 arcade game with 1000 Gamerscore). Combo Breaker Pack $19.99/£16.99/€19.99 (all eight fighters, TJ Combo and Maya on launch day). Individual characters $4.99/£3.99/€4.99.

wikis.title: Gematsu: Killer Instinct Season 2 release date set
wikis.summary: Gematsu (12 August 2014) reporting Killer Instinct: Season 2 launches on Xbox One October 15, with edition prices.
wikis.body:
- Gematsu, Sal Romano, Aug 12 2014: Microsoft and Iron Galaxy Studios announced at Gamescom that Killer Instinct: Season 2 launches for Xbox One on October 15. Microsoft also confirmed Killer Instinct 2 Classic.
- Starts with new fighters TJ Combo and Maya; enhanced game modes and revamped interface.
- $39.99 "Ultra Edition": eight fighters (one added each month), select costumes and accessory packs, and Killer Instinct 2 Classic. $19.99 "Combo Breaker Pack": eight fighters starting with TJ Combo and Maya, one added monthly. Additional fighters $4.99 each.
- Pre-purchasing the Ultra Edition between September 23 and October 14 gets TJ Combo early.

wikis.title: Killer Instinct Season 2 release date and pricing
wikis.summary: Game Rant report that Killer Instinct Season 2 starts October 15, 2014 on Xbox One, with edition prices, pre-order bonus and roster details.
wikis.body:
- Published Aug 12, 2014 by Ben Kendrick; source is a post on the Killer Instinct official (Ultra Combo) forums by Microsoft and Iron Galaxy, announced around Gamescom 2014.
- Background: first announced at E3 2013; Xbox One exclusive by Double Helix Games, sold as quasi-free-to-play (one free fighter each month to test, buy characters a la carte, or buy the full season). In nine months Double Helix delivered eight fighters (Jago, Sabrewulf, Glacius, Thunder, Sadira, Black Orchid, Spinal, Fulgore). After Amazon purchased Double Helix, Microsoft handed development to Iron Galaxy (Divekick).
- Season 2 starts **October 15, 2014**. Eight fighters, starting with TJ Combo and Maya at launch, one new fighter added each month, plus costume/accessory packs and Killer Instinct 2 Classic (arcade port with full multiplayer over Xbox Live).
- **Ultra Edition**: $39.99 / 34.99 pounds / 39.99 euro; all eight fighters, select costumes and accessory packs, KI2 Classic, Content Early Access.
- **Combo Breaker**: $19.99 / 16.99 pounds / 19.99 euro; eight fighters only (no add-ons or KI2 Classic).
- Individual Season 2 fighters: $4.99 / 3.99 pounds / 4.99 euro each.
- Pre-order incentive: Ultra Edition purchases between September 23rd and October 14th get early access to TJ Combo and Killer Instinct 2 Classic.
- Article speculation (not confirmed): remaining six spots might include Cinder (already teased), Riptor, Kim Wu, Tusk, Eyedol, Gargos. The franchise produced 15 characters (including bosses) before the Xbox One relaunch.

wikis.title: Civilization: Beyond Earth October release date announced
wikis.summary: HEXUS news post (4 July 2014) saying 2K Games set Civilization: Beyond Earth for 24 October on PC, Mac and Linux, with a pre-order Exoplanets Map Pack.
wikis.body:
- By Mark Tyson, 4 July 2014. 2K Games officially announced release on Windows PC, Mac and Linux on **24th October**, priced at 27 pounds (US$50).
- Latest game in Sid Meier's turn-based strategy series, described as the spiritual successor to 1999's Alpha Centauri; first announced at PAX in April. Explores the future of mankind on an alien world; players lead factions with contrasting cultures; nonlinear technology progression and a quest system to unlock resources and upgrades.
- Pre-order bonus (per PC Gamer): Exoplanets Map Pack of six maps "inspired by real exoplanets": Kepler 186f (lush forest, one of the oldest known Earth-like planets), Rigil Khantoris Bb (arid continental), Tau Ceti d (seas and archipelagos), Mu Arae f (tidally locked, desert and frozen sides), 82 Eridani e (scarce water, tectonic forces), Eta Vulpeculae b (unknown terrain).
- An E3 walkthrough video was released by 2K: Will Miller, lead game designer at Firaxis Games, shows eight minutes of gameplay.

wikis.title: Civilization: Beyond Earth launches October 24, 2014
wikis.summary: Engadget (July 3, 2014) reports Firaxis and 2K set Civilization: Beyond Earth for October 24 on PC, with a free Exoplanets Map Pack for pre-orders.
wikis.body:
- By Mike Suszek, July 3, 2014. Firaxis Games announced Civilization: Beyond Earth will launch **October 24, 2014** globally for Windows PC; suggested retail price $49.99; not yet rated by the ESRB.
- Pre-order at participating retailers gets the Exoplanets Map Pack (six custom maps inspired by real exoplanets): Kepler 186f, Rigil Khantoris Bb, Tau Ceti d, Mu Arae f, 82 Eridani e, Eta Vulpeculae b.
- First announced at PAX East in April; a spiritual successor to Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri (per Firaxis at E3 the previous month); inspired by sci-fi authors such as Isaac Asimov and Arthur C. Clarke.
- Press release (New York, July 3, 2014, 2K and Firaxis): new science fiction-themed entry; first time players lead factions divided by contrasting cultures; new gameplay includes nonlinear technology progression through the Tech Web, a new Orbital Layer, and a Quest system unlocking details about the alien world plus resources and upgrades.

wikis.title: Hands on with the Microsoft DT-903 Qi wireless charger
wikis.summary: Windows Central (4 September 2014) hands-on video article about Microsoft's smart DT-903 Qi charging pad for Lumia phones, on sale in October for 59 Euro / 59 USD.
wikis.body:
- By Daniel Rubino, published 4 September 2014. Next-gen Qi charger from Nokia's line, "now under Microsoft".
- Features: Qi wireless charging, NFC "tap-to-pair", Bluetooth 4.0. Phone pairs via NFC then keeps a Bluetooth connection; the pad pings the Lumia for battery info when nearby.
- LED behaviour: if battery is below 30% the pad "breathes" with a slowly pulsing LED; placing the phone gives a constant glow matching the pad colour (green, orange or white); glow shuts off when fully charged; a quick double pulse signals a missed call or text.
- Brightness set low/medium/high or off at night; notifications optional.
- Larger than predecessors, better for Lumia Icon, Lumia 930 and Lumia 1520.
- Price/date: on sale in **October** for 59 Euro / 59 USD.
- Recently announced Lumia 830 and Lumia 735 with replaceable Qi charging covers can use it; Lumia Denim firmware and Windows Phone 8.1.1 are needed for the advanced features.

wikis.title: ITPro Today merger notice (original DT-903 article gone)
wikis.summary: The URL now shows an Informa TechTarget notice that ITPro Today has merged into TechTarget; the DT-903 charger article is not present.
wikis.body: The page fetched is an editor's note by Nick Martin (published 06 Apr 2026): ITPro Today, Network Computing and IoT World Today merged with Informa TechTarget as of September 2025, and old URLs may no longer be supported. The original article about the DT-903 Nokia wireless charging plate from Microsoft (per the URL slug "new-dt-903-nokia-wireless-charging-plate-now-available-from-microsoft") was not retrieved; the rest is unrelated site navigation and headlines.

wikis.title: Nokia DT-903 glowing wireless charging plate
wikis.summary: Engadget (Sept. 4, 2014) short news item on Nokia's Wireless Charging Plate DT-903, which glows for missed calls or low battery and costs $59, arriving next month.
wikis.body:
- By Steve Dent, Sept. 4, 2014. Nokia's Wireless Charging Plate (DT-903) is a Qi charger with lights and Bluetooth connectivity.
- Pair it to the phone when off the charger; it glows for missed calls and texts, or a battery below 30 percent. Lights are tinted to match the green, orange or white colour options and pulse in different patterns per notification.
- Charges phones or tablets wirelessly; requires a Qi-enabled Lumia with Windows Phone 8.1.1 and Bluetooth 4.0.
- Price $59; "should arrive next month" (October 2014).

wikis.title: iPad Air 2 rumored for October 2014 launch
wikis.summary: MacRumors (September 22, 2014) reports a Commercial Times rumor that iPad Air 2 launches in October while the Retina iPad mini may come in early 2015.
wikis.body:
- Monday September 22, 2014, by Juli Clover. Per Taiwan's Commercial Times, Apple plans to introduce the next-generation iPad Air in October; it enters production in September and ships next month.
- Commercial Times also suggests the next-generation Retina iPad mini might not launch alongside it, coming in early 2015, with the 12.9-inch iPad Pro in the second quarter of 2015. MacRumors notes there was no prior indication of separate launch timelines; earlier rumors said both would launch together at an October event.
- A rumored October 21 media event was shot down by The Loop's Jim Dalrymple, who did not rule out another October date. Bloomberg reportedly said the iPad Air 2 is in production and the Retina iPad mini 2 is entering production soon.
- Both expected to get an A8 processor, camera improvements and Touch ID; iPad Air 2 may gain an anti-reflective screen coating and gold, silver and space gray colours.
- Reader comments were joking or wish-list remarks (name, Touch ID, 2 GB RAM).

wikis.title: Apple introduces iPad Air 2 and iPad mini 3
wikis.summary: Apple press release (October 16, 2014) announcing iPad Air 2, 6.1 mm thin with A8X and Touch ID, plus iPad mini 3, with prices and availability.
wikis.body:
- Cupertino, October 16, 2014. iPad Air 2: 6.1 mm thin, under a pound, improved fully-laminated Retina display with anti-reflective coating (reduces glare by 56 percent over the previous iPad Air), gold/silver/space gray. iPad Air 2 and iPad mini 3 add Touch ID and Apple Pay within apps (Apple Pay only available in the US).
- Philip Schiller: iPad runs "more than 675,000 apps specifically designed for it"; iPad Air 2 is "the thinnest tablet in the world".
- A8X chip: 40 percent better CPU and 2.5 times the graphics performance of iPad Air, up to 10-hour battery; M8 motion coprocessor with new barometer. Metal graphics in iOS 8.
- Cameras: 8MP iSight (panorama, time-lapse, slo-mo, 1080p); FaceTime HD captures over 80 percent more light, burst mode, HDR.
- Connectivity: 802.11ac MIMO Wi-Fi, 2.8x Wi-Fi performance, up to 866 Mbps; more LTE bands, up to 50 percent faster cellular. Ships with iOS 8.1 (Continuity, Handoff).
- iPad mini line: iPad mini 3 (Touch ID); iPad mini with Retina display renamed iPad mini 2 from $299; iPad mini from $249; iPad Air from $399 (16GB Wi-Fi).
- Availability: online order from Friday, October 17 in 29 countries and territories; in stores later the following week (US, Australia, Canada, China Wi-Fi only, Germany, Japan, UK and others); more countries through end of October.
- US prices: iPad Air 2 Wi-Fi $499 (16GB), $599 (64GB), $699 (128GB); Wi-Fi + Cellular $629, $729, $829. iPad mini 3 Wi-Fi $399 (16GB), $499 (64GB), $599 (128GB); Wi-Fi + Cellular $529, $629, $729.
- Accessories: Smart Covers $39 (seven colours); iPad Air 2 Smart Cases leather $79; iPad mini Smart Cases $69.

wikis.title: Far Cry 4 announced by Ubisoft
wikis.summary: HEXUS news post (16 May 2014) on Ubisoft confirming Far Cry 4 for November 2014 across PC and consoles, set in the Himalayan region of Kyrat.
wikis.body:
- By Mark Tyson, 16 May 2014. Ubisoft confirmed Far Cry 4 for PC, PS4, Xbox One, PS3 and Xbox 360 in November.
- Developed by Ubisoft Montreal with Red Storm Entertainment, Ubisoft Toronto, Ubisoft Shanghai and Ubisoft Kiev. Set in the Himalayan region of Kyrat, "an untamed region currently ruled by a despotic self-appointed king". Open world with wildlife, crafting, weapons and vehicles.
- Dan Hay, Executive Producer: "Following the success of Far Cry 3, we wanted to take the franchise to the next level..."
- Pre-order gets the Limited Edition at no extra cost: three extra single-player missions ("Monkey Around With Hurk") and Hurk's 'Impaler' harpoon gun.
- Release dates: UK 21st November; other EMEA 20th Nov; US 18th Nov. Gameplay premiere online from 9th June, coinciding with E3.

wikis.title: Far Cry 4 arrives November 18th
wikis.summary: Engadget (May 15, 2014) on Ubisoft revealing Far Cry 4 for November 18 in the US on PC, PS4, Xbox One, PS3 and Xbox 360.
wikis.body:
- By Alexis Santos, May 15, 2014. Revealed during talk of Ubisoft's 2014 financials.
- Ubisoft Montreal, with Red Storm and Ubisoft's Toronto, Kiev and Shanghai studios; release November 18th in the US and November 20th in Europe, the Middle East and Africa on PC, PS4, Xbox One, PS3, Xbox 360.
- Players roam the mountainous terrain of Kyrat, a Himalayan region with a "despotic self-appointed king".
- Pre-order gets a free upgrade to the Limited Edition: three single-player missions "Hurk's Redemption" plus Hurk's harpoon gun.
- Ubisoft's goal is for Far Cry 4 to be one of the top 10 best-selling games of 2014; more at E3.

wikis.title: Far Cry 4 (2014 video game) - Wikipedia article
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Ubisoft Montreal's 2014 first-person shooter Far Cry 4: gameplay, plot, development, release and downloadable content.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- 2014 first-person shooter developed by Ubisoft Montreal, published by Ubisoft; fourth main Far Cry game, successor to Far Cry 3 (2012). Engine: Dunia 2 (upgraded). Platforms: PS3, PS4, Windows, Xbox 360, Xbox One. Released **November 18, 2014**. Directors Alex Hutchinson and Patrik Mechė; composer Cliff Martinez; writers Mark Thompson, Li Kuo, Lucien Soulban.
- Set in fictional Himalayan country Kyrat; Ajay Ghale (Kyrati-American) is caught in a civil war between the Royal Army under king Pagan Min (voiced by Troy Baker) and the rebel Golden Path. Mostly positive reviews (praise for open world, visuals, soundtrack, characters; some disliked the story and similarity to the predecessor). Sold over 10 million units by March 2020. Spin-off Far Cry Primal (February 2016); Far Cry 5 (March 2018).

## Gameplay
- Open world, stealth or assault, weapons including bows, flamethrower and rocket launchers; digital camera to mark enemies; ride elephants; vehicles including the "Buzzer" autogyro, wingsuits, grappling hooks; tiger companion in Shangri-La segments as Kalinag.
- Map split into North and South Kyrat; bell towers liberated to open the map; outposts and four fortresses become fast-travel points. RPG elements: The Tiger and The Elephant skill sets, karma, Arena mode.
- Multiplayer: two-player co-op "Guns for Hire"; asymmetric competitive "Battles of Kyrat" (Rakshasa vs Golden Path; modes Outpost, Propaganda, Demon Mask); Map Editor. Competitive multiplayer support for the Map Editor was added February 3, 2015.

## Plot and endings
- Ajay returns to scatter his mother Ishwari's ashes; helps the Golden Path against Pagan Min's governors De Pleur, Noore Najjar and Yuma Lau; must choose between commanders Sabal and Amita. Multiple endings, including an early Easter-egg ending; the final state of Kyrat depends on who leads the Golden Path (Amita: authoritarian drug state; Sabal: patriarchal theocracy).

## Development
- Started late 2012 after Assassin's Creed III shipped. Montreal did the campaign, Toronto the Shangri-La segments, Red Storm the competitive multiplayer, Shanghai hunting missions, Kyiv the PC version. Team dropped a planned direct Far Cry 3 sequel after four days. Kyrat blends India, Nepal and Tibet; the team visited Nepal; the civil war was inspired by the Nepalese Civil War; Pagan Min's pink costume inspired by Japanese films Brother and Ichi the Killer. Only Willis and Hurk return from Far Cry 3.

## Release
- Hinted June 2013; setting leaked March 2014; announced May 15, 2014; gameplay shown at E3 2014. Cover art drew accusations of racism; Hutchinson responded. Limited Edition (free for pre-orders, extra missions and Impaler Harpoon Gun); Kyrat Edition collector's box; season pass; companion app Arena Master.
- DLC: Escape From Durgesh Prison (January 13, 2015), Hurk Deluxe Pack (January 28, 2015), Overrun (February 10, 2015 consoles / February 12 PC), Valley of the Yetis (March 10, 2015 NA / March 11 Europe). Available on Amazon Luna November 23, 2020. A surprise patch on April 29, 2025 added 60fps on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S.
- Reception: Metacritic PS4 85/100, Xbox One 82/100; individual scores e.g. Destructoid 9/10, Eurogamer 8/10, Game Informer 8.75/10. The second part of the source is mostly citation lists.

wikis.title: Qualcomm buys Wilocity for tri-band Wi-Fi
wikis.summary: Ars Technica (Jul 3, 2014) on Qualcomm completing its purchase of 60GHz WiGig startup Wilocity to build tri-band Wi-Fi platforms.
wikis.body:
- By Jon Brodkin, Jul 3, 2014. Qualcomm purchased Wilocity, which makes 60GHz "WiGig" (802.11ad) chips, and will combine them with its own Wi-Fi chips into a tri-band platform (2.4, 5 and 60GHz).
- Qualcomm announced "yesterday" it completed the purchase; financial terms not disclosed; rumors in May reported a price of $300 million. Qualcomm Atheros had invested in Wilocity since 2008.
- 60GHz is easily blocked, so sender and receiver must be in the same room. WiGig is technically capable of 7Gbps (Wilocity's early chips reached 4.6 Gbps); Wilocity is expected to ship a 4.6Gbps smartphone chip this year. 802.11ac (5GHz) can exceed a gigabit per second.
- Initial tri-band platform: reference design based on the Snapdragon 810, "the world's first mobile platform designed to support WiGig", expected to ship in the first half of 2015. Dell released a wireless dock using Wilocity chips (laptop to USB storage and up to two monitors).
- Netgear's "Nighthawk X6 AC3200 Tri-Band WiFi Router" claims 3.2Gbps combined throughput but uses one 2.4GHz and two 5GHz bands, no 60GHz; Qualcomm-based routers should beat it, "although not until next year".

wikis.title: Qualcomm Zeroth platform and Snapdragon 820 at MWC 2015
wikis.summary: Qualcomm press release (March 2, 2015) previewing the Zeroth cognitive computing platform and the Snapdragon 820 with Kryo CPU at MWC 2015.
wikis.body:
- Barcelona, March 2, 2015. Qualcomm Technologies (QTI) will preview next-generation mobile experiences at MWC 2015 using Zeroth, its "first cognitive computing platform designed to enhance on-device user experience".
- Zeroth will be optimized for premium devices based on the Snapdragon 820 processor, built on a FinFET process and introducing the custom 64-bit Kryo CPU. Snapdragon 820 "is expected to begin sampling in the second half of 2015".
- Cristiano Amon: devices will "learn and adapt to the needs of the user"; Zeroth intelligence will scale across automobiles, wearables, smartphones and client computing.
- Capabilities: visual perception, intelligent connectivity, intuitive security (behavioral analysis against malware), always-on awareness, immersive multimedia (dynamic audio adapting to head movement), speech and audio recognition, natural device interactions (gestures, expressions, faces).
- Demo at the QTI booth, Fira Gran Via, Hall 3, Booth 3E10.

wikis.title: California smartphone kill-switch law signed
wikis.summary: MacRumors (August 25, 2014) reports California's SB-962 requiring smartphone kill switches by July 2015 was signed into law.
wikis.body:
- By Juli Clover, Monday August 25, 2014. Governor Jerry Brown signed SB-962, introduced in February, approved by the Assembly in early August, then passed by the Senate.
- Requires smartphones sold in California to include software or hardware that renders the device inoperable to an unauthorized user if lost or stolen; must survive a hard reset or OS downgrade, prevent reactivation on a wireless network except by the authorized user, be installed during initial setup, and be reversible by the authorized user. Effective **July 2015**.
- Co-sponsored by San Francisco DA George Gascon and state Senator Mark Leno. Leno: "California has just put smartphone thieves on notice."
- Article says Apple's Activation Lock (iOS 7) likely fulfills the law; the law will likely affect makers like Samsung and Microsoft. A federal Smartphone Theft Prevention Act might follow. Only Minnesota and California then had such laws; in April Apple, Google, Samsung, Nokia and major carriers agreed to add anti-theft tools to phones made after July 2015.
- Comments were mixed; some sarcastic.

wikis.title: SB 962 smartphone kill switch bill: legislative history and signing
wikis.summary: Consumer Federation of California post (August 26, 2014) tracking SB 962's votes and arguments until Governor Brown signed it on August 25.
wikis.body:
- Signed by Gov. Jerry Brown Aug. 25, 2014. SB 962 (Leno) applies to smartphones manufactured after July 1, 2015 and sold in California.
- Timeline: introduced Feb. 6; Senate Energy, Utility & Communications committee 6-2-3 (April 1); Senate floor failed 19-17-4 on April 24 (21 needed), reconsideration granted 37-0-3, passed 26-8-6 on May 8; Assembly Business, Professions & Consumer Protection 11-3-0 (June 17), Utilities & Commerce 9-5-1 (June 23); Assembly floor 53-20-6 (Aug. 7); Senate concurred Aug. 11.
- Requires manufacturers to equip smartphones with an owner-activatable kill switch, reversible if the phone is recovered.
- Opposition: AT&T and other telecom companies. Claims cited: SF DA George Gascon says phone theft creates a $30 billion a year replacement market plus $8 billion theft insurance; an industry email showed major US carriers refused to market a Samsung phone with a kill switch; Consumer Reports: over 3.1 million Americans lost smartphones to theft in 2013, double 2012; Gascon: two-thirds of SF robberies involved phones or tablets, up from half; telecom donated nearly $1.4 million to state senators (Maplight via LA Times).
- Every statewide law enforcement organization supports it, per Leno's office.

wikis.title: California smartphone kill switch bill signed into law
wikis.summary: VentureBeat (August 25, 2014) reports California SB 962 requiring a kill switch on smartphones sold in the state was signed.
wikis.body:
- By Gregory Ferenstein, 9:14 pm PT, August 25, 2014. California will require any smartphone sold in the state to include a "kill switch" rendering it useless to thieves. Smartphones accounted for over 40% of thefts in 2012 (per the article).
- Bill text quoted: "Any smartphone that is manufactured on or after July 1, 2015, and sold in California after that date, shall include a technological solution at the time of sale, to be provided by the manufacturer or operating system provider, that, once initiated and successfully communicated to the smartphone, can render the essential features of the smartphone inoperable to an unauthorized user when the smartphone is not in the possession of an authorized user."
- Outside California, industry lobbies and wireless companies are teaming up on voluntary kill switch standards. A joint California and New York government report found anti-theft features have an impact; Apple products saw a 38% drop in robberies in the six months after it introduced a kill switch feature.
- Open question whether states or manufacturers will drive anti-theft features.

wikis.title: BioLite 2016 line at Summer Outdoor Retailer 2015
wikis.summary: BioLite press release (August 4, 2015) on new PowerLight Mini, SolarPanel 5/5+ and CookStove shown at Outdoor Retailer Summer Market.
wikis.body:
- Brooklyn, NY, August 4, 2015 (SNEWS page updated May 16, 2017; original Aug 5, 2015). BioLite shows its Spring 2016 additions at booth #BR539 (Ballroom).
- **PowerLight Mini** (MSRP $44.95): credit card-sized rechargeable lantern and power bank, 135 lumens, edge-lit, 1300mAh battery.
- **SolarPanel 5** ($59.95) and **5+** ($79.95): first solar products; 5 watts monocrystalline, onboard battery in the 5+; "Optimized Sun System" sun dial and 360-degree kickstand; weighs 12 ounces. CEO Jonathan Cedar: users on average get 30-40% less power than possible from misalignment.
- **CookStove** (MSRP $99.95): streamlined CampStove, up to 30 hours of clean burning from a rechargeable powerpack.
- BioLite's product line doubles in 2016. Company founded 2009 by Jonathan Cedar and Alec Drummond, HQ Brooklyn.

wikis.title: biem Butter Sprayer V2 product website
wikis.summary: Home page of the biem butter sprayer, a rechargeable handheld device that sprays real butter using heat and air, marketed as seen on ABC's Shark Tank.
wikis.body:
- Marketing page for the "Biem Butter Sprayer V2"; "As seen on ABC's Shark Tank".
- Features: no chemical or artificial propellants, "just heat and air"; store in refrigerator or on counter; faster and easier than spreading with a knife; does not overheat the butter to melt; uses any real butter stick; automatic shut off; easy to use and clean; patent pending nozzle designed to prevent clogging.
- Suggested uses: toast (use half as much butter), popcorn without sogginess, natural non-stick cooking spray, muffin pans, grilled cheese, vegetables, basting turkey or chicken, garlic bread, steaks, pasta, pancakes.
- Specifications: weight approx 1.5 lb, height approx 10 in, width approx 2.4 in; high density rechargeable battery pack. No price on the page.

wikis.title: biem butter sprayer launch press release
wikis.summary: Brevda, Inc. press release (March 1, 2016) introducing the biem, a handheld sprayer that turns a stick of real butter into a spray, available for pre-order from March 1.
wikis.body:
- Austin, Texas, March 1, 2016. Brevda, Inc. introduces the biem butter sprayer: touch-controlled, motion-detecting (accelerometer turns it on/off by position), no chemical propellants, patent-pending non-clogging nozzle; only uses the butter needed and leaves the rest of the stick un-melted.
- Claims: cuts an estimated 50 percent of calories vs. spreading with a knife; in consumer testing no participants could distinguish toast with half the butter. Can also spray coconut oil, olive oil or other oils. High-density rechargeable battery; store in fridge or at room temperature; self-cleaning with water, a drop of soap and a button push.
- Creator Doug Foreman (44 years in the food business, founder of Beanitos in 2010 and Guiltless Gourmet in 1989). Brevda was founded in 2014, privately held, named after his sons Dalton, Evan and Brycen; two years of development. Pre-order at www.BiemSpray.com beginning March 1.

wikis.title: The Gadgeteer on the biem Butter Sprayer Kickstarter
wikis.summary: The Gadgeteer (March 28, 2016) news post on the biem Butter Sprayer's Kickstarter, over $200,000 pledged against a $42,000 goal.
wikis.body:
- By Lex Baer, March 28, 2016. Pronounced "beem" (sprays a "beam" of butter); creator Doug Foreman.
- Kickstarter had 5 days left, about 1,500 backers, over $200,000 pledged against a $42,000 goal; basic pledge $129.
- Insert a whole stick of butter into the canister-shaped device, press a button; it melts only what is needed, can sit on the counter or in the fridge, is easy to clean, and can use oils.
- Uses listed: popcorn, corn, toast, grilled cheese, vegetables, pancakes, waffles, non-stick pans, basting, garlic bread. Reader comments are minor.

wikis.title: NORML California marijuana laws and penalties
wikis.summary: NORML's table and explanations of California's marijuana possession, sale, cultivation, concentrate and paraphernalia penalties after Proposition 64.
wikis.body:
- Prop 64 (Adult Use Marijuana Act) permits adults over 21 not in the medical program to grow up to six plants and possess up to one ounce (28.5 g) of flower and up to 8 g of concentrates; took effect **November 9, 2016**; also licenses commercial production and sales.
- Possession: up to 28.5 g flower: no penalty. More than 28.5 g: misdemeanor, up to 6 months, $500. 28.5 g or less on school grounds (18+): misdemeanor, 10 days, $500. Under 18: infraction (up to 8 hours drug counseling and/or 40 hours community service).
- Intent to distribute: any amount misdemeanor, 6 months, $500. Gifting up to 28.5 g without compensation: no penalty. Unlicensed sale or delivery: misdemeanor, up to 6 months and $500.
- Cultivation: up to 6 plants no penalty; 6 plants or more misdemeanor, 6 months, $500.
- Concentrates: up to 8 g no penalty; more than 8 g misdemeanor, 6 months, $500. Unauthorized manufacture: misdemeanor, 6 months, $500; manufacture using chemical extraction such as butane: fine up to $50,000 and 3-7 years (H&S Code 11379.6(a)).
- Paraphernalia: simple possession no penalty; sale/delivery/manufacture with intent: misdemeanor, 15 days to 6 months, up to $500; delivery to a minor at least 3 years younger: up to 1 year, $1,000.
- Page notes expungement legislation exists, medical marijuana laws exist, and drugged driving is criminalized.

wikis.title: California Proposition 64 (2016) marijuana legalization - Ballotpedia overview, design and campaign finance
wikis.summary: Ballotpedia article on the approved November 8, 2016 initiative legalizing adult recreational marijuana in California; this part covers results, design, taxes, ballot text and campaign finance.
wikis.body:
- Initiated state statute on the Nov 8, 2016 ballot ("Adult Use of Marijuana Act"); approved: Yes 7,979,041 (57.13%), No 5,987,020 (42.87%).
- Yes = legalize recreational marijuana for age 21+ under state law with sales and cultivation taxes.
- Before: medical marijuana legalized by Proposition 215 (1996); both remained illegal federally. Effective dates: November 9, 2016 (possession, cultivation, use); January 1, 2018 (sale and taxation).
- Design: up to 28.5 g marijuana and 8 g concentrate; up to six plants in a locked private home; smoking allowed in private homes or licensed on-site businesses, not while driving or in public; no sales within 600 feet of schools, day care or youth centers; no large-scale licenses for five years. Bureau of Medical Cannabis Regulation renamed Bureau of Marijuana Control. Local governments can restrict or ban businesses. Resentencing eligibility for prior convictions.
- Taxes: cultivation tax $9.25 per ounce of flowers and $2.75 per ounce of leaves; 15 percent retail excise tax; inflation-adjusted from 2020. Revenue to a California Marijuana Tax Fund: $2 million/year to UC San Diego Center for Medical Cannabis Research; $10 million/year for 11 years for university research; $3 million/year for five years to CHP for impairment protocols; grants rising $10 million a year to $50 million in 2022; remainder 60% youth programs, 20% environmental damage, 20% DUI reduction and health grants. Ballot label fiscal impact: additional tax revenue from "high hundreds of millions of dollars to over $1 billion annually"; criminal justice savings of tens of millions.
- Campaign: Yes raised $26.5 million (seven committees) vs $1.1 million opposed (two committees), about 12-to-1; LA Times, SF Chronicle and California Democratic Party endorsed, California Republican Party opposed; polls 51-60 percent, average about 56. Largest support committees: Yes on 64 ($12.1M), New Approach PAC ($7.4M), Drug Policy Action ($4.5M).

wikis.title: Californians vote to legalize marijuana with Prop 64
wikis.summary: CBS San Francisco/AP (November 8, 2016) election-night report that California voters passed Proposition 64 legalizing recreational marijuana.
wikis.body:
- November 8, 2016. Edison Research exit poll for AP and networks: Prop 64 passing 55 to 45 percent. Adults over 21 can possess up to an ounce and grow six plants.
- Massachusetts and Nevada also voted to legalize recreational use; Arkansas, Florida and North Dakota approved medical measures (Florida backed by 71 percent); Montana voted on easing its medical law. Florida and Arkansas became the first southern states with full medical programs; 25 other states had them.
- Rob Kampia (Marijuana Policy Project): "These votes send a clear message to federal officials that it's time to stop arresting and incarcerating marijuana users."
- If all yes votes prevailed, more than 23 percent of the US population would live in recreational states; existing jurisdictions (Alaska, Colorado, Oregon, Washington, DC) had under 6 percent. Marijuana remains federally prohibited.

wikis.title: Global renewable energy investment fell in 2016 while capacity rose
wikis.summary: Ars Technica (Apr 10, 2017) on a UN/Frankfurt School/BNEF report: $241.6 billion invested in renewables in 2016 added 138.5 GW.
wikis.body:
- By Megan Geuss, Apr 10, 2017. Investment about $241.6 billion in 2016, down 23 percent from 2015, but capacity added was 138.5 GW, up nine percent from 127.5 GW in 2015 (wind, solar, biomass and waste-to-energy, geothermal, small hydro, marine). Falling solar PV and wind prices explain much of it.
- Renewables' share of global energy rose from 10.3 to 11.3 percent; renewables prevented an estimated 1.7 gigatonnes of CO2 in 2016; CO2 in January 2017 was 406.1ppm, up 3.6 ppm year on year.
- Renewables were 55 percent of new capacity, highest in the report's 11-year history; investors spent about twice as much on renewables as fossil-related energy. Excludes hydro above 50MW, storage, smart grid.
- Slowdown in China, Japan and emerging markets; Europe up three percent, offshore wind up 53 percent.
- Michael Liebreich (BNEF): unsubsidized wind and solar can be the lowest cost new power in an increasing number of countries "sometimes by a factor of two"; authorities "may have to subsidize natural gas plants".

wikis.title: BloombergNEF Insights landing page (no press release content)
wikis.summary: The fetched page is BloombergNEF's generic Insights index, not the 2016 renewable energy investment press release the URL suggests.
wikis.body:
- The page is the BNEF "Insights" hub: it describes access to perspectives on the energy transition from BNEF experts through research reports and analysis.
- Topic areas listed: Clean Energy, Clean Transport, Commodities, Data Centers, Finance, Industry and Buildings, Nature and Agriculture.
- Flagship reports listed: Climatescope, NetZero Pathfinders, Electric Vehicle Outlook, Transition Metals Outlook, Energy Transition Investment Trends, New Energy Outlook.
- Also promotes the "Switched On" podcast, BNEF events, a monthly newsletter, and freely available Climate Week and COP public research.
- The page contains no text about global renewable energy investment in 2016 or any figures.

wikis.title: NORML: Nevada marijuana legalization status
wikis.summary: NORML's state summary of Nevada's adult-use cannabis law, including possession limits, home grow, and penalties.
wikis.body:
- Status: Legalized; became law in 2017.
- Adult-use possession limits: flower 2.5 oz; concentrate .25 oz.
- Home cultivation: yes, up to six plants.
- State-licensed retailers operational: yes. Delivery: yes.
- THC limits on commercially available products: no.
- Edibles serving size limits: 10 mg per serving, 100 mg per package.
- Employment protections for off-the-job consumption: yes; under a 2019 law it is "unlawful for any employer in to fail or refuse to hire a prospective employee because th. prospective employee submitted to a screening test and the results of the screening test indicate the presence of marijuana."
- Expungement/sealing of past convictions: yes, by written request to the court for marijuana-specific activities since decriminalized or legalized.
- Per se traffic safety limits: no.
- Public consumption: smoking cannabis in public is subject to a fine of up to $600.
- Information source listed: Cannabis Compliance Board, State of Nevada.

wikis.title: Nevada Question 2 recreational marijuana explainer
wikis.summary: A Las Vegas defense law firm blog explaining what Nevada's Question 2 (2016) allowed and prohibited for adults 21 and over.
wikis.body:
- Posted January 1, 2024 (page date), by attorney Michael Becker of Las Vegas Defense Group; written as of Question 2's passage.
- On November 8, 2016, Nevada voters approved Question 2, the Regulation and Taxation of Marijuana Act. Effective January 1, 2017, adults 21+ may legally buy and use recreational marijuana.
- Retail sales: the page says it is likely to be "at least another year" before non-medical sales; the state must enact regulations before January 1, 2018, then businesses need licenses. Medical users can keep buying from licensed businesses (NRS 453A unchanged).
- Possession: up to 2.5 ounces of marijuana or up to one-fourth ounce of concentrate. Exceeding it is a misdemeanor (up to 24 hours community service, victim impact panel, and/or evaluation).
- Use: legal in a private home if the owner permits (HOAs may restrict). Still illegal in public, while driving, at schools, and at correctional facilities. Employers and governments may restrict use; still illegal on federal property (courthouses, National Parks, airports, military bases such as Nellis AFB).
- Growing: adults living more than 25 miles from a retail marijuana store may grow up to six plants in a locked area not visible from public; max 12 plants per residence; no chemical extraction.
- 15% excise tax on wholesale marijuana sales, paid by licensed cultivators.
- Minors: falsely claiming to be 21 is a misdemeanor; entering a retail store under 21 can bring a fine up to $500; giving marijuana to under-21s is a misdemeanor, and a gross misdemeanor (up to one year in jail) if the person is under 18.
- Other states legalizing in the 2016 election: California, Maine, Massachusetts, joining Washington, Oregon, Alaska, Colorado. Nevada is described as one of eight states where recreational use is or will soon be legal.

wikis.title: Nevada Question 2 (2016) marijuana legalization initiative: aftermath, results, design and ballot text
wikis.summary: Ballotpedia's article on Nevada's Question 2, approved November 8, 2016, covering the 2017 licensing and distributor fights, election results, initiative design and ballot text.
wikis.body:
## Basics
- Election date November 8, 2016; indirect initiated state statute, citizen origin; approved. A yes vote supported legalizing recreational use of one ounce or less of marijuana by individuals 21 and over.
- Took effect January 1, 2017. Legal sales began July 1, 2017.
- Result: Yes 602,463 (54.47%); No 503,644 (45.53%).

## Aftermath
- The initiative was designed to legalize sales on January 1, 2018; in May 2017 the Nevada Department of Taxation approved regulations letting licensed medical marijuana facilities in good standing start sales July 1, 2017.
- Question 2 gave wholesale liquor dealers exclusive distribution rights for 18 months. The Independent Alcohol Distributors of Nevada (IADON) won an injunction on May 30, 2017 against a regulation letting medical facilities distribute; Judge James Wilson extended it June 20, 2017.
- A week after sales began the Department said sales exceeded expectations at the 47 licensed retail stores and stores were running low on stock. Gov. Brian Sandoval (R) issued a statement of emergency on July 7, 2017. Nevada Tax Commission unanimously passed a regulation July 13, 2017 allowing licences to medical facilities if alcohol wholesalers alone would cause a shortage.
- August 10, 2017: Department found too few alcohol wholesalers interested. August 11: Judge James Russell halted non-alcohol licences; August 17 he lifted the restraining order; August 29 the Tax Commission approved the plan. September 1 IADON appealed; September 14 the Nevada Supreme Court issued an injunction, kept after October 3, 2017 oral arguments (already-issued licences not invalidated). November 28, 2018: the Supreme Court dismissed the case as the 18-month period had passed.

## Overview and design
- Before Question 2, recreational use was illegal; medical marijuana was legalized by Question 9 in 2000. Marijuana remained illegal under federal law in 2016.
- Campaigns: Yes on 2 raised $4.3 million; No on 2 $3.8 million. Largest donors: Marijuana Policy Project (support), casino mogul Sheldon Adelson (opposition). Las Vegas Review-Journal endorsed in 2014, opposed in June 2016. Polls showed about 51 percent support before the election.
- Users: 21+, one ounce or less of marijuana or one-eighth ounce or less of concentrate; up to six plants in a locked enclosed area.
- Sellers: Department of Taxation regulates; for the first 18 months only registered medical marijuana establishments could apply for store, production and cultivation licences, and only wholesale liquor dealers for distributor licences. No establishments within 1,000 feet of a school or 300 feet of a community facility.
- Store caps by county population: over 700,000 (Clark County) up to 80; 100,000-700,000 (Washoe) up to 20; 55,000-100,000 up to 4; under 55,000 up to 2.
- Tax: 15 percent excise tax on wholesale sales by cultivation facilities; annual licence fees $3,300 to $30,000; one-time $5,000 application fee; revenue first covers costs then goes to the State Distributive School Account.
- Penalties/limits preserved: impaired driving, sales to under 21, use on school or corrections grounds, workplace bans; new penalties for public-view cultivation, public or moving-vehicle smoking, giving to under-21s.
- The fiscal note states financial impact "cannot be determined".
- Table of contents also lists sections on support, opposition, finance, polls and background (not covered in the text read).

wikis.title: BioLite CampStove 2 announcement (Digital Trends)
wikis.summary: Digital Trends news item on BioLite's CampStove 2, a wood-burning stove with improved power output, shipping at $130.
wikis.body:
- Article by Kraig Becker, published April 21, 2022 (as shown on the page).
- The original CampStove (2012) burns sticks, twigs and leaves and converts flame heat into battery power to charge devices.
- CampStove 2 packs down to about the same size, weighs the same (2.2 pounds), and is compatible with the KettlePot and Portable Grill. New: sturdier legs, new mesh body design, a modified fire chamber for a new heat probe.
- BioLite says it produces 50 percent more energy than the original, charging its removable 2600 mAh battery faster and powering a four-speed fan.
- LED dashboard shows battery power, fan speed and heat. Ships with a FlexLight USB lamp.
- "Began shipping on Wednesday" with a new CoffeePress ($15) that works with the KettlePot. Stove price $130, same as the original.

wikis.title: BioLite CampStove 2 announcement (New Atlas)
wikis.summary: New Atlas report that BioLite's CampStove 2 adds a 2,600 mAh battery, 3 W thermoelectric output and an LED dashboard for US$130.
wikis.body:
- Article by Nick Lavars, March 02, 2017.
- Almost seven years after the original wooden stove, BioLite gave the CampStove a makeover. It still runs purely on wood.
- Captures wasted heat via a thermoelectric generator; new integrated 2,600 mAh battery stores power for later; charged via Micro USB; thermoelectrics upgraded to 3 W of continuous power.
- New LED dashboard shows available power, fire strength and fan levels in real time. Fan speeds doubled from two to four.
- Weighs the same as its predecessor, 2.06 lbs (935g). Price US$130 (same as before). Works with the KettlePot and Portable Grill. Available now through BioLite's website.
- A reader comment questions how much the 3 W output can really charge.

wikis.title: BioLite CampStove 2 update (Field Mag)
wikis.summary: Field Mag report that BioLite's CampStove 2 gets a design refresh, an onboard battery and up to 50% more electricity output for $130.
wikis.body:
- Published 03-01-2017, updated 10-03-2018 (as shown on the page).
- Brooklyn-based "social enterprise" BioLite launched the CampStove four years earlier; CampStove 2 follows an equal number of years of feedback.
- Still a smokeless wood-burning portable stove; updated thermoelectric design generates up to 50% more electricity.
- Weighs the same as the first generation; now has an onboard battery storing electricity for later (previously power could only be used as produced).
- Updated LED display shows fan speed, power output and fire strength.
- Compatible with the BioLite Grill and KettlePot with new CoffeePress.
- Price: $130 from BioLite.

wikis.title: Kaneka 26%+ efficiency silicon solar cell (Ars Technica)
wikis.summary: Ars Technica on Kaneka Corporation's heterojunction back-contact silicon solar cell reaching 26.3 percent, later 26.6 percent, efficiency.
wikis.body:
- By Megan Geuss, Mar 22, 2017. Researchers at Japanese chemical manufacturer Kaneka Corporation, funded by Japan's NEDO, built a cell with 26.3 percent photo conversion, beating the previous record of 25.6 percent.
- After submitting to Nature Energy they optimized it to 26.6 percent, recognized by NREL.
- Silicon cells have a theoretical limit of 29 percent; low-20-percent is considered very good for commercial panels.
- Cell: 180.4 cm2, thin-film heterojunction, low-resistance electrodes at the rear, front coated with amorphous silicon and an anti-reflective layer.
- Loss estimates: 0.5 percent resistive, 1 percent optical, 1.2 percent extrinsic recombination.
- Made with "industrial applicable" processes such as plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD). The authors note "further work is required before the individual cells can be assembled into a commercially available solar panel."
- Per IEEE Spectrum, Kaneka will keep working with NEDO to bring levelized cost to $0.06 per kilowatt-hour by 2030.
- Panasonic uses heterojunctions and will likely use it in cells for Tesla at the Solar City plant in Buffalo. Paper: Nature Energy, 2017, DOI 10.1038/nenergy.2017.32.

wikis.title: Kaneka solar cell record efficiency (GIGAZINE)
wikis.summary: GIGAZINE summary of Kaneka's Nature Energy paper on a 26.6% efficient silicon solar cell certified by NREL.
wikis.body:
- Mar 24, 2017. Osaka-based Kaneka Corporation's paper in Nature Energy reports a solar cell with 26.6% conversion efficiency, certified by NREL.
- Theoretical limit of silicon cells is assumed to be 29%; commercial panels are mostly 20% or less.
- Kaneka announced 26.3% in September 2016, exceeding the previous record of 25.6%; after submitting the paper it reached 26.6%.
- Kaneka did not mass-produce the cell; the team said "It takes time to use the new solar cell for commercial solar panels".
- Kaneka will continue research to lower cost to $0.06 per kilowatt hour (about 6.67 yen) by 2030. Solar energy demand is estimated to be over 20% by 2050.
- Cell title: silicon heterojunction with interdigitated back contacts, over 26% efficiency.

wikis.title: Dell UltraSharp 32 Ultra HD 8K (P3218K) on sale
wikis.summary: HEXUS news that Dell's 31.5-inch UltraSharp 8K monitor P3218K is available to buy in the US at $4999.
wikis.body:
- By Mark Tyson, 24 March 2017. Dell first showed the monitor at CES 2017.
- 31.5-inch diagonal P3218K; 7680 x 4320 at 60Hz (over 33 million pixels, equal to 4x 4K or 16x FHD). IPS LED backlight, 6ms grey-to-grey response.
- Aimed at photography, videography, architecture, engineering. Dell PremierColor, 10-bit panel with 1.07 billion colours: 100 per cent Adobe RGB, 100 per cent sRGB, 100 per cent Rec. 709, 98 per cent DCI-P3.
- Aluminium build, borderless (InfinityEdge), flicker free, low blue light; stand with tilt, swivel, pivot; VESA mounting optional.
- Ports: power, 2x DisplayPort in, audio line-out, USB 3 upstream, four USB downstream (one BC1.2 charging).
- Available online in the US at $4999; not seen on Dell UK. 3 year warranty.

wikis.title: Dell UP3218K UltraSharp 32-inch 8K monitor goes on sale (GSMArena)
wikis.summary: GSMArena news that Dell's UP3218K 8K monitor is available for purchase at $5,000 with an April 17 ship date.
wikis.body:
- By Himanshu, 24 March 2017.
- The UP3218K UltraSharp 32-inch is now available; as promised at its CES announcement it carries a $5,000 price tag. The listing shows a shipment date of April 17.
- 8K is 7680x4320 pixels, approximately 33 megapixels: four times 4K and 16 times 1080p.
- Supports 1.07 billion colors and 100% coverage of Adobe RGB and sRGB.

wikis.title: Comcast gigabit cable in 15 cities by early 2017 (Ars Technica)
wikis.summary: Ars Technica report that Comcast's gigabit cable is sold in four US markets with 11 more due by early 2017.
wikis.body:
- By Jon Brodkin, Nov 2, 2016.
- Gigabit cable is on sale in Atlanta, Chicago, Nashville and Detroit (connected the day before); Miami was previously promised before the end of 2016.
