But it will also be local, and we who travel this route every day are most relieved. We welcome it because it will relieve congestion, improve safety and drainage, and help in so many ways."
- Commissioner Robert Vaughn: "In addition to mobility improvements, we're also improving bicycle and pedestrian paths helping to accommodate all modes of transportation."

## More information

- Project updates and alerts at mymobility35.org. Media contact Jeff Barker, 512-870-7585.

wikis.title: Austin Transit Partnership selects Austin Rail Constructors for Austin Light Rail
wikis.summary: Press release announcing that ATP's board picked Austin Rail Constructors as construction contractor for Austin Light Rail, with the procurement details and the system's planned size.
wikis.body:
## The selection

- "Austin Transit Partnership, the local government corporation charged with implementing Austin's first light rail system, has selected Austin Rail Constructors (ARC) as the construction contractor for Austin Light Rail, marking another major step toward beginning construction in 2027."
- "The ATP Board's approval of ARC at the Feb. 18 meeting enables ATP to begin pre-construction activities and advance final design for Austin Light Rail under the first phase of what will be a multibillion-dollar contract."
- Dateline: AUSTIN, Texas, Feb. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/. News provided by Austin Transit Partnership.

## Austin Rail Constructors

- "ARC - a joint venture between nationally and locally recognized firms Stacy Witbeck and Sundt Construction - will help shape and build the design and construction of nearly every aspect of the system, including the transitway, tracks, systems, stations, bridges, traffic signals, utilities, drainage structures and streetscape improvements."
- The team's experience includes "McKalla Station, Austin-Bergstrom International Airport and national rail projects in Arizona, Hawaii and Utah", with "several Texas-based contractors represented within ARC's subcontractor team."
- "ARC was identified as the highest-ranked firm following a rigorous, competitive procurement process that evaluated elements including firms' experience, personnel qualifications, technical approach and design innovation."

## Procurement

- "ATP completed the procurement in approximately one year, faster than many comparable mega projects nationwide."
- Before formal solicitations, ATP ran a Request for Information process and hosted "Connect & Build" industry networking events for small and local businesses.
- "As design advances and construction are authorized, ARC will competitively bid portions of the work, creating opportunities for local and statewide businesses, including subcontractors, material suppliers, specialty contractors and small businesses."
- "The design-build model ATP has chosen to employ brings the final construction partner on board sooner in the project with the goal of earlier alignment, preventing costly change orders and future construction delays. In the coming year, ATP will work with ARC, providing current designs and feedback collected from the community."

## The system

- "Austin's first light rail system will feature 15 stations along a nearly 10-mile alignment and consist of all-electric trains running every 5-10 minutes throughout most of the day. Austin Light Rail is designed to be fully expandable for future extensions."

## Quotes

- ATP CEO Greg Canally: "This is a big, important milestone for Austin Light Rail... with this contract now in place, we are on track to begin construction in 2027. Not only is Austin getting this major transit project, but we are also creating thousands of jobs and economic opportunity here in Texas."
- Austin Rail Constructors Project Manager Armando Tiscareño: "Austin Rail Constructors is ready to deliver light rail for Austin. We're bringing together the best local builders and designers alongside international experts."
- Austin Mayor Kirk Watson: "Austin is building the transportation system our growing city demands. Selecting a construction partner is a major step forward in delivering the voter-mandated transit system and will provide infrastructure careers for thousands in our region."

wikis.title: Journey With AUS: Austin-Bergstrom airport expansion and development program
wikis.summary: Austin-Bergstrom International Airport's program page for Journey With AUS, listing each near-term, long-term, airfield and completed project in the multi-year expansion with its phase, timeline and budget.
wikis.body:
## The program

- "Journey With AUS is Austin-Bergstrom International Airport's multi-year airport expansion, development and improvement program."
- Vision: "Meet the current and future needs of our growing region while staying true to our roots and elevating the passenger journey with an authentic Austin and Central Texas experience."
- "The program's overall scope and budget are currently in development."
- Funding: airport cash reserves, current and future airport revenues, future revenue bond proceeds, and Federal Aviation Administration grants. "No local Austin taxpayer dollars will be used to fund the program." Elsewhere the page says all projects are funded by airport revenue bonds, revenue from rent and fees charged to airlines and other tenants, passenger facility charges and FAA grants.
- Environmental review: after reviewing the Final Environmental Assessment, the FAA approved on July 22, 2022 an environmental Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI)/Record of Decision for the proposed Journey With AUS projects.
- The page notes construction activities in the terminal may be noticeable to passengers, and offers a Speaker's Bureau and a program map ("project size and scope are subject to change").

## Near-term improvements

- **Atrium Infill** — in construction, estimated completion 2026, approximately $30 million.
- **West Gate Expansion** — in the build phase, estimated completion 2026, approximately $165 million.
- **Concourse M** — in design, construction estimated to begin summer 2026.

## Long-term expansion and development

- **Concourse B & Tunnel** — in design, estimated to open in the early 2030s; Austin City Council authorized $72 million for engineering and architectural services and $1.031 billion for pre-construction and construction services.
- **Parking** — Yellow Garage broke ground February 2025, expected to open to the traveling public by early 2027 ($15 million engineering/architectural, $250 million pre-construction and construction); Surface Parking Phase 1 opened with Economy Lot H in late 2024, Phases 2 and 3 in design ($8 million authorized for Phase 1 construction services).
- **New Arrivals & Departures Hall** — in design, estimated to open in the early 2030s; $45 million authorized for engineering and architectural services and $820 million for pre-construction and construction services.

## Airfield, utility and infrastructure projects

- **New Midfield Taxiways** — in the build phase, estimated completion 2027; $26.7 million for engineering and architectural services and $320 million for pre-construction and construction services.
- **New Central Utility Plant** — in design, construction estimated to begin in 2027; $162 million authorized for design and construction services.
- **Utility Infrastructure Campus-Wide (UICW)** — expanding or enhancing existing and newly proposed utilities including electrical power distribution and electrical system, storm drainage, water quality pond/de-icing pond, detention pond, hydronic piping, IT/telecommunications duct banks and other utility extensions. Currently in design; construction estimated to start in 2026. $10 million for engineering and architectural services and $120 million for pre-construction and construction services.
- **Integrated Baggage Handling System** — will span from the New Arrivals and Departures Hall to the new Concourse B & Tunnel, approximately five miles of conveyor belts interfacing with the existing Outbound Baggage Handling System that screens 4,000 bags an hour. Currently in design; planned to open at the same time as the Concourse B & Tunnel and the New Arrivals & Departures Hall. Budget approximately $300 million.

## New facilities and completed projects

- **International Arrivals Improvements** — an additional 20,600 square feet added for passenger queuing, new baggage carousels, office space for Customs and Border Protection and more booths to process customers; new bag carousels can transition between international and domestic arrivals. Completed in 2025. Budget approximately $241 million, which includes the new Outbound Baggage Handling System, West Infill, International Arrivals Improvements and other related projects.
- **New Outbound Baggage Handling System** — a centralized baggage processing system for departing checked bags "to meet the demand of 30 million annual passengers," with checked luggage travelling across 1.5 miles of conveyor belts and processing 4,000 bags per hour. Completed in 2025; same approximately $241 million combined budget.
- **West Infill** — a renovation of the existing Barbara Jordan Terminal from the back edge of the existing concourse to the existing terminal curbside roadway, adding over 75,000 square feet over the baggage claim, apron, concourse, mezzanine and roof levels, and including Checkpoint 4, a new four-lane checkpoint with space for up to eight total lanes pending TSA requirements. TSA checkpoint improvements have been completed at all 4 checkpoints and new Computed Tomography (CT) scanners for carry-on items installed; additional lanes were added to Checkpoints 2 West and 2 East to offset the closure of Checkpoint 3 during construction. Completed in 2026; same approximately $241 million combined budget.
- **New Airline Fuel Facility** — a second airplane fuel facility "to have enough fuel supply on hand to meet the projected demand increase of 3% to 5% annually over the next ten years." Substantially completed; the facility began operations in 2024.
- **Vacant Building Removal** — 30+ unused and vacant buildings removed on the south side of the airport property to make room for future development; completed in 2023.
- **Terminal Restroom Refresh Project** — cosmetic refresh (new fixtures, fresh paint, new sink countertops, new mirrors) of restrooms on both east and west sides of the Barbara Jordan Terminal food court; completed in 2023.
- **New TSA Security Checkpoint** — in 2021 Austin Aviation partnered with the TSA to open a new checkpoint addressing "the record-breaking growth in airline and passenger activity the airport experienced shortly after COVID-19 vaccines became available and travel bans were lifted." The checkpoint opened in December 2021 and is currently used by TSA as a General Screening Checkpoint.

wikis.title: Atrium Infill
wikis.summary: A near-term project adding about 12,000 square feet of concourse-level floor plate to the Barbara Jordan Terminal by filling in open space above baggage claim.
wikis.body:
- The Atrium Infill project "will add more square feet to the terminal for security screening, bag check and passenger processing by filling in existing open space above baggage claim."
- It will add approximately 12,000 square feet of concourse level floor plate to the Barbara Jordan Terminal. The elevated slab will be constructed while the existing vertical circulation is kept in place.
- Includes all required signage and wayfinding, special system upgrades, and fire-life-safety improvements, plus upgrades to mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems as needed. "The suspended slab will likely require enhancements to the existing structural capacity."
- The project will also study a mezzanine level infill and provide a report with findings and recommendations.
- Timeline: currently in the construction phase; estimated to be completed in 2026.
- Budget: total estimated cost approximately $30 million.

wikis.title: West Gate Expansion
wikis.summary: An 84,500 gross square foot expansion over three levels adding three gates, new amenities and a mezzanine with an outdoor balcony.
wikis.body:
- Addition of 84,500 gross sq ft over three levels — 30,000 sq ft on the concourse level including a new third-level mezzanine and apron-level airline support space for new passenger amenities.
- Scope also includes replacement of 12 current gate boarding bridges and creation of three new gates to offset gate closures during future expansion projects.
- New features: five new waiting seating areas; three new gates; dining areas for new concessionaires; additional restrooms; playscape; meditation/quiet room; family and nursing rooms; pet relief room; a new mezzanine with a public outdoor balcony and indoor seated viewing area over the concourse.
- Timeline: currently in the build phase; estimated to be completed in 2026.
- Budget: total estimated cost approximately $165 million.

wikis.title: Concourse M
wikis.summary: A midfield facility on the west side of the airfield adding six gates to maintain capacity while the main terminal is remodeled and Concourse B is built.
wikis.body:
- A midfield facility located on the west side of the airfield that will add six gates allowing for six narrow body aircraft: four contact gates and two walk out gates.
- Concourse M "will operate separately from the Barbara Jordan Terminal and help maintain airline operations and passenger capacity while the main Barbara Jordan Terminal gates are remodeled and the new 26-gate Concourse B is built."
- Features: restrooms including a family restroom, and passenger amenities including a nursing room; grab-and-go concessions; 37,537 square feet for airlines to board and deplane passengers; shuttle buses to and from the Barbara Jordan Terminal; public WiFi; pet relief area.
- Timeline: currently in the design phase; construction estimated to begin in summer 2026.

wikis.title: Concourse B & Tunnel
wikis.summary: A new 26-gate midfield concourse with a subgrade tunnel to the Barbara Jordan Terminal, estimated to open in the early 2030s.
wikis.body:
- The project will design and build a new 26-gate midfield concourse "to meet the airport's long-term passenger activity level demand."
- It includes all passenger and tenant spaces, passenger boarding bridges, baggage handling system expansion, apron support spaces, back of the house, baggage makeup, tug and other support spaces, and all related aircraft apron expansion and underground utilities, including in-pavement hydrant fueling system.
- "Concourse B will be home to Southwest Airlines as the Concourse B anchor tenant with 18 gates, United Airlines with 5 gates, and 3 gates will be available for domestic common use."
- It also includes construction of a new subgrade tunnel connecting the Barbara Jordan Terminal with Concourse B, with the capability of expanding to a new Concourse C. The tunnel will incorporate a passenger conveyance system "to assist with passenger movement and capacity for a future Automated People Mover (passenger train) corridor."
- Timeline: currently in the design phase; Concourse B is estimated to open in the early 2030s.
- Budget: Austin City Council authorized $72 million for engineering and architectural services and $1.031 billion for pre-construction and construction services.
- Renderings shown are pre-design conceptual; "final design specifications and features subject to change."

wikis.title: Parking: Yellow Garage and surface lots
wikis.summary: A new 7,000-space Yellow Garage north of the Blue Garage plus a phased surface parking lot of about 1,400 spaces.
wikis.body:
**Yellow Garage**

- AUS will construct a new 7,000 space, multi-level garage north of the existing Blue Garage, including intelligent parking systems, revenue control and roadway realignment.
- The Yellow Garage broke ground in February 2025.
- "The completion of the Yellow Garage will allow teams to move forward with the Red Garage closure to make way for the new Barbara Jordan Terminal Arrivals and Departures Hall expansion." The project is expected to open to the traveling public by early 2027.
- Budget: Austin City Council authorized $15 million for engineering and architectural services and $250 million for pre-construction and construction services.

**Surface Parking**

- A surface parking lot designed and built in three phases to support long-term passenger growth; once complete the lot will include approximately 1,400 spaces, with revenue control, lighting, line marking, drainage improvements and new shuttle bus shelters.
- Phase 1 opened with Economy Lot H in late 2024. Phases 2 and 3 are currently in the design phase.
- Budget: Austin City Council authorized $8 million for Phase 1 construction services.

wikis.title: New Arrivals & Departures Hall
wikis.summary: A new hall replacing the Red Garage and Presidential Boulevard curbside, with expanded ticketing, a centralized TSA checkpoint and a new baggage claim hall.
wikis.body:
- The project will design and build a new Arrivals & Departures (A & D) Hall where the Red Garage and current drop off and pick up lanes on Presidential Boulevard are located.
- It will include new expanded ticketing and check-in areas, a new centralized TSA security checkpoint, amenities such as new concessions, a mobility lounge and meet and greet area, and a new expanded baggage claim hall.
- It includes a redesigned curbside experience "that will reduce congestion and improve passenger and vehicle flow as well as support future growth," and adds a new pedestrian bridge connecting parking garages and the Rental Car Facility.
- Enabling projects will include removal of the existing Red Garage and associated roadways and utilities.
- Timeline: currently in the design phase; estimated to open in the early 2030s.
- Budget: Austin City Council authorized $45 million for engineering and architectural services and $820 million for pre-construction and construction services.

wikis.title: New Midfield Taxiways
wikis.summary: Two new concrete parallel midfield taxiways connecting the east and west sides of the airfield, needed to build Concourse B.
wikis.body:
- In order to build the new 26-gate Concourse B, AUS will construct two new concrete parallel midfield taxiways — "paths for aircraft that connect between the runway, the terminal, and other airfield facilities."
- The new midfield taxiways will connect the east and west side of the airfield and provide access to the existing maintenance ramp.
- Features: two miles of 2 new parallel taxiways plus several smaller connector taxiways to support Concourse B and future concourses; two bridges under taxiways for airfield support services; airfield lighting, signage and a new taxi route for low-visibility conditions; enhancements to security fencing; a new reclaimed water bulk refilling station; pavement recycling, building demolition, utility relocation and drainage improvements; roadway changes and a new parking lot on the south side of airport property.
- Timeline: currently in the build phase; estimated to be completed in 2027.
- Budget: Austin City Council authorized $26.7 million for engineering and architectural services and $320 million for pre-construction and construction services.

wikis.title: New Central Utility Plant
wikis.summary: A new Central Utility Plant with chilled water thermal energy storage to heat and cool the expanding airport, with construction estimated to begin in 2027.
wikis.body:
- The project will design, construct and commission a new Central Utility Plant (CUP) and associated chilled water thermal energy storage (TES) "to reliably cool and heat the airport as we continue to expand."
- The new CUP includes new chilled and hot water hydronic piping to the existing Barbara Jordan Terminal, as well as chillers, cooling towers, pumps, control systems and utility connections.
- Timeline: currently in the design phase; construction estimated to begin in 2027.
- Budget: Austin City Council authorized $162 million for design and construction services.

wikis.title: The Portal (Downtown Rail Extension), San Francisco
wikis.summary: TJPA project page for The Portal, the Downtown Rail Extension bringing Caltrain and future California High-Speed Rail into the Salesforce Transit Center, with its design and funding status.
wikis.body:
## What it is

- The Portal, also known as the Downtown Rail Extension project, is described by the Transbay Joint Powers Authority (TJPA) as "a transformational infrastructure investment, delivering on the decades-long promise of bringing communities closer, reducing climate change impacts, and providing Bay Area residents with better access to jobs, housing, and economic opportunities."
- The project "has been over 30 years in the making" as part of the TJPA's vision to deliver seamless transportation service through its multimodal six-level transit hub, the Salesforce Transit Center, in downtown San Francisco.
- The Portal will extend Caltrain service from Fourth and King Street and ultimately bring the California High-Speed Rail system to the Salesforce Transit Center, in downtown San Francisco, and connect 11 transit systems.
- Delivery of The Portal is part of the long-term vision of the TJPA's Transbay Program, created in 2001.

## Project status

- **Design:** TJPA has completed the 30% design of The Portal, which has an anticipated revenue service date of 2035, funding dependent.
- **Federal program:** The Portal is in the Federal Transit Administration's Capital Investment Grants Program (FTA CIG) Engineering phase as of May 2024; it completed the Project Development phase in December 2021.
- **Priority status:** Endorsed as a Tier 1 project in the Metropolitan Transportation Commission's Plan Bay Area 2050 and recognized as a Federal SAFETEA-LU Project of National and Regional Significance.
- **Environmental:** The Transbay Transit Center Program, including The Portal project, is environmentally cleared pursuant to the requirements of the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), and their implementing regulations.

The page links to further material including a factsheet, a Portal Monthly Report, FTA Project Management Oversight Reports, a project schedule and construction updates.

wikis.title: UCSF Health Helen Diller Hospital at Parnassus Heights
wikis.summary: UCSF Real Estate project page for the new 15-story UCSF Health Helen Diller Hospital being built at the Parnassus Heights campus, with its schedule, preparatory work and construction hours.
wikis.body:
## The project

- UCSF is constructing the UCSF Health Helen Diller Hospital "to serve the city with world-class care for the next century."
- The hospital is 15 stories, at the Parnassus Heights campus, built on the former Langley Porter Psychiatric Hospital (LPPH) site.
- Construction runs through 2029, with the new hospital expected to open in 2030. Expected project completion date is given as 2030.
- The hospital is part of the Comprehensive Parnassus Heights Plan.

## Preparatory work

- Beginning February 2022 through April 2027, 20 Site Make Ready (SMR) and 12 Hospital Make Ready (HMR) major projects are required to prepare for construction of the new hospital building at Parnassus Heights.
- Impacts of this work are being communicated to UCSF faculty, staff, learners, patients, visitors and the community.

## Construction hours

- 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday
- 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday for noisy work
- 5 to 8 p.m. Monday through Friday - extended hours
- 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Saturday - extended hours
- 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Saturday for noisy work
- 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Sunday - extended hours
- Construction may occur outside regular hours with prior review by UCSF Community & Government Relations.

The page notes a video of a second tower crane installation at the HDH site and a latest Parnassus Heights monthly construction update.

wikis.title: Groundbreaking of the $2.6 billion SFO Terminal 3 West Modernization
wikis.summary: Turner Construction insight announcing the groundbreaking of the Terminal 3 West Modernization at San Francisco International Airport, with the project's scope, temporary passenger corridors, sustainability goals and opening dates.
wikis.body:
## Groundbreaking

- Turner, along with design-build partners Gensler and TEF, announced the groundbreaking of the Terminal 3 West Modernization project at San Francisco International Airport (SFO).
- Turner will lead the $2.6 billion transformation of the terminal, "which will result in a modern, world-class facility."

## Scope

- A 200,000 square foot expansion of Terminal 3.
- 650,000 square feet of renovation.
- A new six-story building that will house airline lounges and operational office space.
- Cutting-edge amenities, expanded concessions and enhanced security features; a redesigned check-in area, improved baggage handling systems and a more intuitive wayfinding experience; advanced technology systems aimed at streamlining airport operations and enhancing passenger flow.

## Temporary passenger corridors

- Turner is constructing temporary corridors to reroute passengers safely around the construction zone; prefabricated interim passenger corridors are being installed "to facilitate passenger safety and comfort."
- This "one and done" process was planned to reduce the complexities of multiple moves of the corridors over the project's duration.
- The 1,000-foot West Corridor and 400-foot East Corridor were fabricated as 11 modules at a nearby air cargo yard to avoid disruption to travelers, then transported across the airfield over 11 consecutive nights.

## Sustainability

- The terminal will incorporate energy-efficient systems, water-saving fixtures and materials sourced from sustainable suppliers.
- The project aims to achieve LEED Platinum certification.

## Schedule

- The expansion portion of the project is scheduled to open in the fall of 2027, with the eastern addition side of Terminal 3 opening in 2029.

## Quotes

- Tina Smith, Construction Executive at Turner: "This project represents not only a significant investment in the future of air travel but also in our commitment to building sustainably... Our team is dedicated to creating a terminal that not only meets the highest standards of efficiency and comfort but also serves as a model for environmental stewardship in the aviation industry."
- Nino Adamo, Turner's Vice President & General Manager: "This groundbreaking marks a milestone in our longstanding partnership with SFO... this project is an opportunity to showcase our expertise in delivering large-scale, complex projects that align with our values of innovation, quality, and sustainability."

wikis.title: Light rail to Federal Way begins service (Federal Way Link Extension)
wikis.summary: Sound Transit news release announcing the opening of the Federal Way Link Extension, a nearly 8-mile 1 Line extension with three new stations in South King County, plus its cost, funding and station details.
wikis.body:
## The opening

- "Starting today, new Link light rail service to Federal Way begins," allowing passengers to travel the region while avoiding congestion.
- The nearly 8-mile 1 Line extension adds options to travel between Seattle, Sea-Tac Airport and Federal Way and includes three new stations — Kent Des Moines, Star Lake and Federal Way Downtown — as well as two new parking structures and a parking addition in Federal Way.
- This is the fifth light rail extension in the past three years for Sound Transit; the others were T Line service to Hilltop, the 2 Line between South Bellevue and Redmond Technology stations, the Lynnwood extension into Snohomish County, and the 2 Line extension to Downtown Redmond.
- Voters approved the Federal Way extension in 2008 as part of the Sound Transit 2 ballot measure. The project broke ground in summer 2020.

## Cost and funding

- Kiewit was the design-builder.
- Funding for the $2.5 billion project includes a $790 million federal grant agreement from the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) and a $629.5 million low-interest loan from the U.S. Department of Transportation.

## Stations

- **Kent Des Moines** — elevated, just southwest of I-5 at the SR516 exit; serves Highline College and future affordable housing to be constructed adjacent to the stations; includes a parking garage with approximately 500 new spaces as part of the project.
- **Star Lake** — on the west side of I-5 just north of South 272nd; serves surrounding neighborhoods and features a 1,105-stall parking garage.
- **Federal Way Downtown** — elevated, at the Federal Way Transit Center, "one of the busiest transit centers in the region," with connections to local and regional service; serves the Federal Way Performing Arts and Events Center and local businesses; additional housing is expected on surplus property adjacent to the station; a garage addition added 341 parking spaces to the 1,224 already in use.

## What comes next

- The Crosslake Connection, spanning the 2 Line across Lake Washington into Seattle, is expected in 2026.
- A new Pinehurst Station at NE 130th Street in Seattle is expected to open in 2026; it was part of the ST3 ballot measure.

## Quotes

- Sound Transit Board Chair and Snohomish County Executive Dave Somers: "The debut of the Federal Way Link Extension marks yet another progress milestone for Sound Transit and the region. This extension brings Link that much closer to connecting all three counties of the Puget Sound region."
- U.S. Senator Patty Murray said she is "proud to have helped steer over a billion dollars in federal investment toward this project."
- Congresswoman Marilyn Strickland (WA-10): "Nine years in the making, extending this service to our growing region is a critical step toward a Tacoma Dome Station and completion of our vision for ST3."
- King County Executive and Sound Transit Board Member Girmay Zahilay noted "the 2-line across Lake Washington nears completion in 2026."
- Sound Transit Board Member and King County Councilmember Pete von Reichbauer said that "as our region prepares for FIFA next year, light rail will put South King County on the map as a destination."
- Sound Transit CEO Dow Constantine said the team "overcame the challenges of the Great Recession and Covid pandemic during the life of this project, while still finishing hundreds of millions of dollars under budget."
- State Rep. Jake Fey, chair of the state House Transportation Committee, and U.S. Senator Maria Cantwell also spoke.

wikis.title: Memorial Stadium redevelopment at Seattle Center
wikis.summary: Seattle Center's project page for the Memorial Stadium redevelopment, covering the construction schedule, partnership and not-for-profit operating model, funding, project timeline and the stadium's history.
wikis.body:
## Status

- Construction is currently under way for the Memorial Stadium redevelopment project, with completion planned for Fall 2027.
- Viewing windows are available on Harrison Street next to Artists at Play and on 3rd Avenue across from the International Fountain.

## Partnership and vision

- The project is "operated under a not-for-profit model managed through a partnership between Seattle Public Schools (SPS), City of Seattle (City), and One Roof Sports & Entertainment."
- It will create a state-of-the-art multi-purpose stadium for student athletics, education, arts, culture, entertainment and community events, integrated with the Seattle Center campus.
- Alongside an improved athletic field, the vision centres on students with performing arts, commencement ceremonies, and social and educational opportunities, and a year-round hub for community events.
- The stadium will be operated as a sustainable not-for-profit venture rather than a commercial enterprise, with collaborations such as the King County Play Equity Coalition. One Roof Sports & Entertainment pledged as part of its RFP response to donate $100,000 annually to support youth access programming at the new stadium for five years, commencing with the first operating year.
- The reimagined stadium will host large civic events including concerts, community festivals and professional sports, featuring new programmable public space and open sightlines linking the stadium with the International Fountain, working toward the goals of Seattle Center's Century 21 Master Plan.
- The project preserves Memorial Wall — honouring local high school students and alumni who lost their lives in World War II — which the Seattle Landmark Preservation Board designated as a landmark.

## Funding

- "An unprecedented $110 million in public funding and a capital campaign generating approximately $30 million in community support."

## Community engagement

- Widespread community outreach led by the Seattle Center Foundation was initiated in 2021 to build support for a new Memorial Stadium and for the SPS BTA levy; outreach expanded to student and cultural groups, Seattle Center staff and resident organizations, tribal representatives, veterans' groups, community-based organizations, and the public via open house events.

## Project timeline

- **2026** — Foundation work and concrete slabs completed; project shifts to vertical construction.
- **2025** — Project reaches $30 million in philanthropic support from Seattle-based businesses, community foundations and local philanthropists; Seattle School Board and Seattle City Council unanimously approve the project's development agreement; "Lights Out... For Now" community open house and preview event held; ceremonial groundbreaking and ground blessing event held; construction begins.
- **2024** — SPS, the City and One Roof Sports & Entertainment align on key project terms to guide formal agreements.
- **2023** — SPS and the City issue an RFP for a private partner; Seattle City Council approves an additional $19 million in project funding in the City capital plan; One Roof Sports & Entertainment announced as potential private partner; Washington state legislature approves $4 million in the capital budget; Seattle Landmarks Preservation Board designates landmark status to Memorial Wall.
- **2022** — Memorandum of Agreement between SPS and the City, with SPS retaining ownership and priority use for student events; Seattle voters approve SPS' Buildings, Technology and Academics/Athletics V Capital Levy (BTA V), which includes $66.5 million for the project; Seattle City Council approves $21 million in project funding.
- **2021** — Letter of Intent signed by SPS and the City outlining the shared goal of replacing Memorial Stadium with a more visionary, multi-use facility.
- **2017** — Partnership agreement between SPS and the City to collaboratively partner on a Memorial Stadium replacement.

## History of the stadium

- SPS' Memorial Stadium is the successor to Civic Field, built in 1927 as part of the City's Civic Complex.
- In 1946 the City deeded the land to SPS to build, operate and maintain a new athletic field. Voters approved a school levy and bonds (issued in 1942 and 1944) to fund school building improvements and construction of today's Memorial Stadium, completed in 1947.
- The stadium was selected as the site for a war memorial by a group of community leaders appointed by Seattle Mayor William Devin after World War II, to the 762 Seattle high-school students and alumni who lost their lives in the war. The Memorial Wall was designed by Garfield High School student Marianne Hanson, with revenues from Thanksgiving Day football games played in the stadium from 1947-49 funding its construction and installation.
- Memorial Stadium hosted the opening and closing ceremonies for the Seattle World's Fair, plus concerts, community events and school events.

Conceptual renderings on the page are provided by One Roof Stadium Partnership.

wikis.title: SEA Airport S Concourse Evolution renovation approved
wikis.summary: Port of Seattle news release on the Commission authorizing initial funding for the $2.5 billion S Concourse Evolution at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, with scope, phasing, sustainability targets and Upgrade SEA programme status.
wikis.body:
## The decision

- The Port of Seattle Commission authorized initial funding "today" for the next significant modernization project at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA) — the S Concourse Evolution (SCE) — with major construction scheduled to start in 2027.
- Part of the $5.5 billion Upgrade SEA capital improvement program, the estimated $2.5 billion S Concourse renovation "will transform a 1973 facility into a world-class concourse that primarily serves international travelers."

## Scope

- The project does not increase gate count on that concourse, as there is no room to expand between the main terminal and the airfield.
- It repurposes, in part, the customs area vacated when the International Arrivals Facility (IAF) opened in 2022.
- The modernization will add 150,000 square feet, including a new Upper Concourse Level, improved dual-level boarding operations for select gates, and expanded dining, retail, lounge and passenger amenities.
- Seismic, structural and building systems upgrades are included.

## Phasing

- The project will be completed in multiple phases over the course of eight years, allowing continuous flight operations at most gates during construction.
- A temporary S Annex east of the facility will be built to support ground boarding operations, to make up for gate closures.
- "The goal is to have only three of the 12 gates impacted by construction at any time."
- All phases are currently estimated to be completed by 2034.

## Sustainability

- Aiming for LEED Silver certification once completed.
- Anticipated 58% reduction of annual operational greenhouse gas emissions and 16% reduction of annual energy use from Port Standard.
- Components: exterior enclosure and high-performance glazing; enhanced lighting and building management systems; electrical equipment in lieu of fossil fuel; low-flow plumbing fixtures; EV charging for aircraft service equipment; reuse of building material.

## Costs and funding

- Total estimated project cost for the SCE is $2.5 billion.
- The Commission authorization is for $1.1 billion to fund the project into 2029; the remaining costs will be presented to the Commissioners for review and consent at a later date.
- Funding comes from a combination of the Airport Development Fund and future revenue bonds. "As with virtually all airport projects, no taxpayer dollars will be used to fund the project."

## Upgrade SEA progress

- N Concourse Modernization — Complete (2021)
- International Arrivals Facility — Complete (2022)
- Restroom Renovation — Complete (2025)
- SEA Gateway Project — Complete (2026)
- C Concourse Expansion — Complete (2026)
- Roadway Improvements — Nearing completion this fall
- Baggage Optimization — In progress (completion by 2029)
- SEA Underground Controls Replacement — In progress (completion by 2027)

## Quotes

- Port of Seattle Commission President Ryan Calkins: "Today's authorization to move forward with the S Concourse Evolution builds on the generational investments we are making at SEA to improve the passenger experience."
- SEA Airport Managing Director Wendy Reiter: "The existing building is over half a century old... we're being innovative by building up and not out. We're mindful of the fact that we have one of the smallest footprints of any major U.S. airport considering our passenger volume."
- Kevin Keady, AECOM West Region Business Leader of Buildings + Places, said the design "is inspired by local, indigenous concepts combined with pragmatic enhancements" and will "benefit the region for the next 50 years."

wikis.title: Metro D Line Subway Extension (Westside Subway)
wikis.summary: LA Metro's project page for the D Line Subway Extension, covering the three construction sections from Koreatown to Westwood, the May 2026 opening of Section 1, current construction status and the project milestone timeline.
wikis.body:
## The project

- The Metro D Line Subway Extension expands the existing subway west from Wilshire/Western in Koreatown nearly nine miles along Wilshire Bl to Westwood.
- Project type: Rail. Current phase: Construction. Estimated project completion: "Section 1: Open".
- Delivered in three sections that "improve access, reduce travel time, and strengthen connections" between Los Angeles job, education, medical and cultural centers along the Wilshire Corridor, "one of the most heavily traveled routes in the region."

## Status update

- Work continues across all three sections.
- Section 1 is open, including new stations at La Brea, Fairfax and La Cienega.
- Section 2 remains active in Beverly Hills and Century City, with station construction progressing underground. In Century City, major street restoration and deck removal along Constellation Bl is planned to begin in spring 2026, which may include temporary lane reductions and weekend work.
- Section 3 continues construction in Westwood, including work at the UCLA and VA Hospital stations, with structural work and preparation for future street restoration; lane reductions and temporary pedestrian detours may occur during off-peak hours.

## Milestone timeline

- **8 May 2026** — Section 1 opens; three new underground stations at Wilshire/La Brea, Wilshire/Fairfax and Wilshire/La Cienega opened.
- **April 2024** — Metro completes five years of tunneling for the D Line Subway Extension Project.
- **October 2023** — Section 3 TBMs break through at Century City Station.
- **April 2023** — Section 3 TBMs arrive at Century City Station "doorsteps".
- **Nov 2022 - Jan 2023** — TBM Harriet and TBM Ruth arrive at the Section 1 interface (Nov 2022 and Jan 2023 respectively), completing tunneling for Section 2.
- **Mar-May 2022** — TBMs Aura (March) and Iris (May) arrive at Westwood/UCLA, completing the first leg of Section 3 tunneling.
- **January 2022** — TBMs Harriet and Ruth arrive at Beverly Dr station, completing the first leg of Section 2 tunneling.
- **May 24, 2021** — Groundbreaking ceremony for Section 3 at the West LA VA Medical Center.
- **July 2020** — TBMs Aura and Iris lowered into the launch box on the VA campus to begin tunneling toward Westwood.
- **Apr 2020 - July 2020** — TBMs Harriet and Ruth begin tunneling from Century City heading east toward Beverly Drive Station (start of Section 2 tunneling).
- **Apr 6, 2020** — Section 1's TBM "Elsie" reaches Wilshire/Fairfax.
- **Jun 2019** — Elsie and Soyeon arrive at Wilshire/Western, completing their first eastbound drive for Section 1.
- **Oct 2018** — TBMs Elsie and Soyeon lowered at Wilshire/La Brea and begin tunneling toward Wilshire/Western.
- **Feb 23, 2018** — Groundbreaking ceremony in Beverly Hills marking the start of Section 2 utility relocation and early works.
- **Nov 7, 2014** — Metro breaks ground on the first segment of the D Line Extension at Wilshire/La Brea.

## Construction mitigation programs

- **Eat Shop Play** — a mitigation program providing marketing and support to local businesses as Metro expands public transportation in Los Angeles.
- **Business Interruption Fund** — grants to local small "mom and pop" businesses directly impacted by Metro's rail construction; businesses must be located along the project rail alignment and may be eligible for up to $60,000 per impact year based on provable revenue loss.
- **Metro Art** — commissioned artists and original public artworks for each new D Line station from Miracle Mile to the West LA VA Medical Center.

## Other items on the page

- A Sep 9, 2026 community meeting presentation is linked, "with station work nearing completion in Section 1 and ongoing work in Sections 2 and 3."
- An online webinar event about the D Line Extension Project is listed for Oct 14th, 12:00 pm - 1:00 pm, free with registration.
- Project team contact: 213.922.6934.

wikis.title: D Line Extension Section 1 (Koreatown to Wilshire/La Cienega)
wikis.summary: The first section of the D Line Subway Extension, from Koreatown to the Wilshire/La Cienega area, which opened on May 8, 2026 with three new stations.
wikis.body:
- Section 1 extends the subway from Koreatown to the Wilshire/La Cienega area, serving the Miracle Mile and surrounding neighborhoods.
- It opened on May 8, 2026.
- Three new underground stations: Wilshire/La Brea, Wilshire/Fairfax and Wilshire/La Cienega.
- Metro describes it as making it "easier to travel between Beverly Hills, Mid-Wilshire, Miracle Mile, Koreatown, Downtown Los Angeles and the wider Metro system with faster, traffic-free trips," giving riders direct access to museums, jobs, healthcare, shopping and neighborhood destinations.
- The stations are fully ADA-accessible and feature modern safety upgrades, intuitive wayfinding and vibrant public art, "supporting everyday travel and the region's major global moments ahead."
- Milestones: groundbreaking at Wilshire/La Brea on Nov 7, 2014; TBMs Elsie and Soyeon lowered Oct 2018; first eastbound drive to Wilshire/Western completed Jun 2019; TBM Elsie reached Wilshire/Fairfax Apr 6, 2020.

wikis.title: D Line Extension Section 2 (Beverly Hills and Century City)
wikis.summary: The second section of the D Line Subway Extension, running west through Beverly Hills and Century City, still under construction.
wikis.body:
- Section 2 continues west through Beverly Hills and Century City, connecting major employment centers and regional destinations.
- It remains active, with station construction progressing underground.
- In Century City, major street restoration and deck removal along Constellation Bl is planned to begin in spring 2026, which may include temporary lane reductions and weekend work; advance notices will be provided to affected businesses and residents.
- Milestones: groundbreaking ceremony in Beverly Hills on Feb 23, 2018 marking the start of utility relocation and early works; TBMs Harriet and Ruth began tunneling from Century City heading east toward Beverly Drive Station between Apr 2020 and July 2020; they arrived at Beverly Dr station in January 2022, completing the first leg of Section 2 tunneling; they arrived at the Section 1 interface in Nov 2022 and Jan 2023, completing tunneling for Section 2.

wikis.title: D Line Extension Section 3 (Westwood and the VA campus)
wikis.summary: The third section of the D Line Subway Extension, extending the line to Westwood and the West LA VA Medical Center, still under construction.
wikis.body:
- Section 3 extends the line to Westwood, improving access to UCLA, major medical facilities and the Westside; it reaches Westwood and the VA campus.
- Construction continues in Westwood, including work at the UCLA and VA Hospital stations, with structural work and preparation for future street restoration; lane reductions and temporary pedestrian detours may occur during off-peak hours.
- Milestones: groundbreaking ceremony at the West LA VA Medical Center on May 24, 2021; TBMs Aura and Iris lowered into the launch box at the end of the line on the VA campus in July 2020 to begin tunneling toward Westwood; Aura arrived March 2022 and Iris May 2022 at Westwood/UCLA, completing the first leg of Section 3 tunneling; Section 3 TBMs arrived at Century City Station in April 2023 and broke through there in October 2023.

wikis.title: SkyLink automated people mover at Los Angeles International Airport
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on SkyLink, LAX's 2.25-mile automated people mover in testing, covering its route and stations, rolling stock, construction history, repeated delays and settlements, and the ongoing litigation between LAWA and LINXS.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- SkyLink is an automated people mover system "currently in testing" to serve Los Angeles International Airport (LAX). Status is given as "In testing, in litigation".
- Owner: Los Angeles World Airports (LAWA). Operator: LAX Integrated Express Solutions (LINXS). Locale: LAX. Stations: 6. Website: lawa.org.
- The 2.25-mile (3.62 km) line will include six stations linking the LAX Rental Car Center, the Metro Rail system, and the LAX West Intermodal Transportation Facility (West ITF) with the airport's central terminal area.
- LINXS — a public-private partnership of ACS, Alstom, Balfour Beatty, Fluor and Hochtief, with assistance from HDR and Flatiron West — was awarded a 25-year contract to design, build, finance, operate and maintain the line.
- Technical: 2 tracks, fully elevated, parallel tracks forming a pinched loop; operating speed 13.5 mph (21.7 km/h) average including stops and 47 mph (75 km/h) top speed.
- Construction was initially scheduled for completion in 2023, but the opening has been repeatedly delayed, and LAWA has not announced a firm opening date. The Los Angeles City Council stepped in on June 26, 2026, referring the issue to the Trade, Travel, and Tourism Committee. The project is the subject of litigation as of July 9, 2026, as testing continues.
- A contract arbitrator previously found LAWA responsible for nearly two years of delay, and a Los Angeles County Civil Grand Jury report concluded the setbacks stemmed from a strained relationship between LAWA and LINXS, political pressure to finish before major regional events, and shortcomings in the contract's dispute-resolution provisions. In total LAWA has agreed to more than US$880 million in dispute-related payments, in addition to the project's US$4.9 billion, 25-year cost.

## Route and stations

- Three stations in the central terminal area (CTA), each with footbridges with moving walkways to nearby terminals: the west station serves terminals 3, 4 and B (Tom Bradley International Terminal); the center station serves terminals 1, 2, 5 and 6; the east station serves terminals 7 and 8 with a future connection to terminal 1.
- Continuing east, the line travels over Sepulveda Boulevard and skirts the airfield where Terminal 9 is planned, then turns north crossing Century Boulevard to the LAX West ITF, a large parking structure with a park-and-ride area and access to nearby hotels.
- The route continues east along 96th Street, passing the maintenance yard, crossing over the Metro Rail tracks to the East ITF station atop the LAX/Metro Transit Center, offering connections to Los Angeles Metro Rail and local buses.
- Trains then enter the LAX Rental Car Center (RCC), "a massive parking structure that will house all major rental car companies operating at LAX."
- Station list, west to east: A West CTA (terminals 3, 4, B; parking garages P3, P4); B Center CTA (terminals 1, 2, 5, 6; parking P2a, P2b, P5, P6); C East CTA (terminals 7, 8; parking P1, P7, Theme Building, Bob Hope USO, future connection to Terminal 1); D Terminal 9 (future infill station); E West ITF (economy parking garage, hotel shuttles, rideshare and taxi pick-up/drop-off, access to Airport Blvd); F East ITF (LAX/Metro Transit Center, private vehicle pick-up/drop-off, LAX FlyAway, charter buses, access to Aviation Blvd, future economy parking garage); G RCC (LAX Rental Car Center). All stations are accessible.

## Service

- SkyLink is expected to operate 24 hours a day. During peak hours (9 a.m. to 11 p.m.), trains will arrive every two minutes. The line will have a 10-minute end-to-end travel time.

## Rolling stock and capacity

- The fleet will consist of 44 Innovia APM 300 vehicles manufactured by Alstom (initially Bombardier Transportation). Each vehicle can accommodate up to 50 passengers and their luggage, with 12 seated and the rest standing.
- During peak periods, nine four-car trains will operate simultaneously; each four-car train can accommodate up to 200 passengers.
- With a two-minute headway, up to 30 trains per hour are expected, carrying up to 6,000 passengers per hour per direction and up to 84,000 daily peak-hour passengers, or up to 30.7 million annual peak-hour passengers; the system could theoretically transport up to 85 million passengers annually in both directions, including up to 23.7 million non-peak passengers.

## Architecture

- The six stations each feature a line of 20-foot diameter circular skylights, with an additional one in the mezzanine of the LAX/Metro Transit Center; the West ITF parking garage features similar circular lighting fixtures.
- New pedestrian walkways employ a Vierendeel truss with rectangular rather than triangular bracing; old-style walkways with triangular bracing still serve parking lots P1, P4, P5 and P7.
- The concrete guideway features "gentle sweeping curves and clean uniform look."
- Each station features a single island platform with level boarding; the proposed Terminal 9 infill station is the exception, with a pair of separate side platforms. The East CTA station features a viewing platform for the Theme Building.

## Background and planning

- LAX "has long struggled with gridlocked traffic on World Way," which can back up onto Century Boulevard or the Airport Tunnel.
- Ahead of the 1984 Summer Olympics, a second level was added to World Way (November 1983 per the photo caption), separating departure drop-offs from arrivals pick-ups; the relief was short-lived and by the 2000s the airport ranked as one of the nation's most congested and hardest to navigate.
- Airport managers went on to spend over US$15 billion to modernize the airport, with an automated people mover as one of the major improvements. Added urgency came in 2017 when Los Angeles was awarded its bid to host the 2028 Summer Olympics, and further urgency from the 2026 FIFA World Cup and the 2027 Super Bowl. In July 2024, Mayor Karen Bass stated that "it absolutely has to be finished by the time of the World Cup."
- After receiving three bids, LAWA chose LINXS. The Los Angeles City Council approved the US$4.9 billion project on April 11, 2018; US$1.9 billion of the total was allocated for initial design and construction.
- Related works: new vertical cores near each terminal plus pedestrian bridges over World Way with moving walkways; cores between terminals 5 and 6, at terminal 7 and at terminal B at a cost of $490 million, with new cores also included in larger renovation projects at terminals 1, 2, 3 and 4.
- SkyLink connects to the West ITF (a US$294.1 million, 4,300-space parking structure), the RCC adjacent to Interstate 405, and the LAX/Metro Transit Center (East ITF) connecting to the Metro Rail C and K Lines.
- Together these projects are called the Landside Access Modernization Program, expected to cost a total of US$5.5 billion. By 2035, SkyLink is projected to reduce vehicle travel in the CTA by about 27% and eliminate more than 3,200 daily car-rental shuttle trips.

## Construction

- In 2018, 2,100 parking spaces in lot C were removed to reconfigure the area for the West ITF. Utility relocation started in the second quarter of 2018.
- Construction on the West ITF officially began in the summer of 2019; ConRAC broke ground in September 2019. The first large concrete pour for SkyLink occurred in September 2020 at the West ITF station.
- Construction on the 2.25 miles of two-track elevated guideway began in spring 2019 with the first underground support columns; the first concrete for the columns was poured in January 2020; guideway concrete pouring began September 2020 and was completed in May 2022. A total of 69,700 cubic yards (53,300 m3) of concrete was poured and one million work hours completed.
- Metro commenced construction on the LAX/Metro Transit Center on June 21, 2021; the station will link SkyLink to the C and K rail lines, Metro Bus and other municipal operators, and will include a customer service center and Metro Bike Hub.
- West ITF's economy parking structure opened on October 19, 2021 after two years of construction; until SkyLink opens, temporary shuttle buses transport passengers between the airport and the facility.
- As of May 2024, overall construction progress was 97.3% complete. On April 29, 2024, the project test drove the one-car Maintenance Service Vehicle on the guideway between the Maintenance and Storage Facility (MSF), West ITF and ConRAC.

## Delays, disputes and settlements

- Construction was originally scheduled for completion in March 2023. In August 2025, Fitch Ratings projected construction would be completed in January 2026, with testing and commissioning continuing through June 2026.
- There are reports of legal disputes between LINXS and some subcontractors potentially causing further delays.
- LAWA underwent several leadership changes during construction: John Ackerman was appointed CEO in February 2024, Chief Development Officer Terri Mestas left the following month, and three additional executives joined in 2024.
- The Los Angeles County Civil Grand Jury report attributed the contract's dispute-resolution shortcomings to the outside law firm Nossaman, retained for its expertise in design-build contracts, and said these factors contributed to hundreds of millions of dollars in additional costs and prolonged dispute resolution.
- On June 7, 2024, a technical expert serving as arbitrator under the contract (the "Project Neutral") ruled that LAWA was responsible for 526 days of delay, "having failed to act in good faith and comply with the contract documents," citing failures to timely integrate the people mover with airport communications systems and issues related to construction of Metro Rail's LAX/Metro Transit Center station, and awarded US$97 million in damages. The Grand Jury said LAWA subsequently lost confidence in the Project Neutral process, believing it biased in favor of the contractor.
- The Project Neutral was the sole dispute-resolution mechanism in the contract, with no panel of arbitrators and no provision to replace the Project Neutral once selected; the Grand Jury characterized these as defects in the contract drafted by Nossaman.
- After the initial ruling LINXS filed an additional 209 claims, which remained unresolved amid a slowdown in construction progress; the report stated LINXS "leveraged the change-order process" and the threat of litigation to obtain settlements.
- LAWA and LINXS reached a "global settlement" covering all outstanding disputes for US$550 million, which formally extended the contractual completion date to December 2025. In total LAWA agreed to more than US$880 million in change orders and dispute-related payments, including approximately US$252 million in design-related changes, the US$97 million from the Project Neutral ruling, and the US$550 million global settlement.
- In 2024 Fitch Ratings cited "extended construction delays, prolonged dispute resolution, and difficulties in the parties' working relationship" when it reevaluated the credit rating of the US$1.2 billion in bonds financing the project; LINXS's private financing is described as "at risk to performance." Fitch's May 30, 2018 presale bond report had described the security package as "benefiting from a joint and several 35% liability cap with creditworthy parent companies." In an August 2025 update Fitch again referred to the ongoing issues in connection with the revised target completion date of June 2026.
- Systems demonstration testing began on April 21, 2026, intending to demonstrate 30 consecutive days of continuous error-free operation without passengers. This testing is ongoing.

## Longstop dates

- There is a contractual project longstop date 12 months after the planned Passenger Service Availability (PSA) date; failure to achieve PSA by the longstop date is considered a developer default under the DBFOM agreement. A similar lenders' longstop date falls 10 months after the planned PSA date.
- On July 21, 2026 Fitch Ratings downgraded approximately $1.2 billion in LINXS APM senior bonds to 'BB' from 'BB+' and placed them on Rating Watch Negative, citing "a precarious position with a limited margin of safety before it could breach the lenders' longstop of Oct. 8, 2026, and the project longstop date of Dec. 8, 2026."

## Litigation

- LINXS sued the city on July 9, 2026 over unresolved contract disputes, following the city's rejection of their claim in January.
- On August 10, 2026 LAWA filed a motion for an automatic 30-day extension, citing "informal efforts to resolve certain disputes," and stating "I intend to file a demurrer, motion to strike, or motion for judgment on the pleadings." A July 24, 2026 filing objects among other things to paragraph 124 of the complaint, involving an overheard discussion of legal strategy.
- The judge ruled in favor of LINXS on a pro hac vice motion, but not with prejudice to LAWA re-raising the same claims in another context. Further explanation may come in a Form CM-110 filing in preparation for an August 31, 2026 case management hearing. The court docket shows the next regularly scheduled hearing set for December 10, 2026.
- A September 3, 2026 filing shows the judge intends to conduct a settlement conference with the parties at their joint request. On September 18, 2026, LINXS requested a hearing, scheduled for September 21, 2026, to extend time for LINXS to respond to LAWA's written discovery.
- Seth Lehman of Fitch Ratings: "When you go into the legal system, it has a timeline of its own."

wikis.title: Los Angeles breaks ground on $2.62 billion LA Convention Center expansion
wikis.summary: ABC7 report on the City of Los Angeles breaking ground on the $2.62 billion Convention Center expansion, with the projected economic figures, the 2028 Olympics deadline and doubts about finishing on time.
wikis.body:
## The groundbreaking

- The city of Los Angeles broke ground Wednesday on a massive expansion of the L.A. Convention Center, "which officials say will support the downtown area's ongoing revitalization."
- Mayor Karen Bass said the $2.62 billion expansion is more than just another project, describing it as an investment for the city and the local economy.
- Bass gave final approval to the Convention Center Expansion Project and announced new efforts she said will support downtown's revitalization.
- The expansion aims to bring more jobs to the downtown area and prepare the facility for the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

## Figures the city gives

- The public infrastructure investment will create more than 15,000 jobs.
- It will add $652 million in general fund tax revenue over 30 years.
- It will draw in over $150 million in additional visitor spending each year.
- Since the expansion was announced, city officials say 100 potential conventions are already interested in using the new convention center.

## Deadline and doubts

- "Some leaders doubt the site will be finished by the city's imposed deadline of March 2028 - just a few months before the Convention Center will be handed over to the International Olympic Committee for its use."
- Bass has acknowledged that it's a risky project, but she expects it will transform the city and attract people to downtown. At a press conference last week, as she gave final approval, Bass said: "This is a very, very serious investment. None of us take this lightly... I think it was a difficult challenge on the City Council for all of us to come to grips with the commitment that we are making but understanding that it is the type of risk that one has to take in order to make a qualitative leap forward."
- City Councilmember Tim McOsker: "The beneficiaries of this project are not here. They are 30 years out, and those beneficiaries will never know that we even existed... That's exactly what business and labor and government are meant to do - come together, build a future for Los Angeles because we believe in the future of Los Angeles."

## Also reported

- At Wednesday's groundbreaking event, City Councilman Curren Price was sent to the hospital after suffering a "health-related incident."

By Tim Pulliam, KABC; City News Service contributed to the report.

wikis.title: Inglewood Council approves Inglewood Transit Connector public-private partnership
wikis.summary: Inglewood Transit Connector press release on the City Council approving a public-private partnership with Elevate Inglewood Development Corporation to build the ITC mobility hubs and rebuild Downtown Inglewood streets, with budget, scope, schedule and workforce commitments.
wikis.body:
## The decision

- The Inglewood City Council voted in favor of a public-private partnership that will build the Inglewood Transit Connector's (ITC) mobility hubs and reenvision the streets of Downtown Inglewood.
- "Construction begins this fall."
- Elevate Inglewood Development Corporation (EIDC) was selected as the Best Value Proposer through a competitive procurement. The consortium is led by Plenary Americas as developer, with Swinerton as design-build contractor and Walter P. Moore as architect of record.
- The project is structured as a Design-Build-Finance-Operate-Maintain (DBFOM) agreement, placing design, construction, financing, operations and maintenance under a single contract with EIDC at a fixed price against a fixed completion date.
- EIDC will operate and maintain the Market & Florence Hub and the pedestrian bridge for 20 years, while the streetscape and the two remaining hubs return to the City upon acceptance. Payments over the operating term are earned against performance standards for availability, cleanliness, safety and security, and state of good repair.

## Why

- More than 60 major annual events at SoFi Stadium, the Intuit Dome, the Kia Forum and other venues in the City's sports and entertainment district bring tens of thousands of visitors into a City of roughly 100,000 residents on a regular basis.
- During the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Metro moved record numbers of fans to and from matches at SoFi Stadium using dedicated bus lanes, signal priority and expanded shuttle service.

## Scope

- Market Street, Manchester Boulevard and Queen Street will be reenvisioned with new hardscape and landscaping, irrigation, traffic controls, wayfinding, street furniture and pedestrian-scale lighting.
- Three mobility hubs will be constructed, collectively delivering more than 1,000 new parking stalls.
- A pedestrian bridge over Florence Avenue will connect the downtown core directly to the Metro K Line's Downtown Inglewood Station.
- The plan preserves all necessary right-of-way for a high-capacity automated people mover system in the future.
- The largest hub, at Market & Florence, brings transit-oriented retail, parking, a bus plaza and a kiss-and-ride lot to downtown. The work is coordinated with the City's Destination Market Street program, which is funding facade and tenant improvements along the same corridor.
- Dedicated event-day shuttle lanes will run from the north and south of the City to the sports and entertainment district, with synchronized signals giving buses priority; improved commuter shuttle service will close the first/last-mile gap between the Metro K and C Lines and key destinations.

## Budget and funding

- The $261 million budget for the design and construction period will be covered entirely by grants from the State of California's Transit and Intercity Rail Capital Program and from Metro.
- No General Fund dollars will go into construction, and no new tax is required to build or operate the system.
- City analysis projects the ITC Program will generate approximately $210 million in tax revenue, $1.5 billion in total economic output, and support hundreds of jobs for Inglewood residents and workers across Los Angeles County over the life of construction and operations.

## Business relocation

- Relocation advisors have been assigned to work one-on-one with tenants being relocated to make way for the Market & Florence Mobility Hub.
- In addition to relocation benefits pursuant to State law, the City is offering incentive grants of up to $250,000 to help those businesses reestablish within the downtown core.

## Jobs and workforce

- The agreement carries a 35% local hiring commitment spanning construction and ongoing operations and maintenance, a goal of 20% local and small business participation, and a Community Workforce Agreement.
- The City is working with the building trades on apprenticeship readiness and with Inglewood Unified School District (IUSD) on a youth engagement and education program.

## What to expect

- Beginning in November, roadway work will occur primarily at night, with mobility hub construction during the day.
- Market Street, Manchester Boulevard and Queen Street will be rebuilt block by block, each block taking roughly two months. Business access will be maintained throughout, with advance notice before activities begin.
- There will be periods of temporary lane closures, sidewalk detours, parking adjustments, construction activity and modified traffic patterns.
- Other Phase 1 elements: Lot T at Prairie and Manchester is complete and served as a flexible event space during the 2026 World Cup. Design of the event-day bus lanes and the Intelligent Transportation Systems program are advancing under separate City contracts, with construction anticipated to begin in 2027.

## About the ITC

- The Inglewood Transit Connector links Downtown Inglewood and the Metro K and C Lines to the City's sports and entertainment district. Phase 1 delivers mobility hubs, dedicated event-day bus lanes, streetscape improvements and intelligent transportation systems, with right-of-way preserved at Market and Manchester for a future automated people mover. All design and construction grant funding for Phase 1 is secured.

## Quotes

- Mayor James T. Butts, Jr.: "This agreement caps our cost, and construction is funded through a partnership with the State and Metro — using grant dollars we competed for and won, and not a dime from the General Fund. When the world arrives in 2028, Inglewood will have the downtown transit capacity to meet the moment, and our residents will have it long after the world goes home."
- Councilmember Eloy Morales, Jr.: "This agreement gives Inglewood one contract, one team, one fixed price and one deadline. The developer carries the cost and schedule risk, which protects Inglewood taxpayers."
- Councilman Alex Padilla: "New sidewalks, lighting and mobility hubs will give our small businesses the foot traffic and the front door they deserve."
- Dale Bonner, Plenary Concessions Executive Chairman, called it "this transformative investment in Downtown Inglewood."
- Councilwoman Dionne Faulk: "The Project Labor Agreement is what makes 35% percent local hire real — it sets the wage floor, the benefit standard and the apprenticeship structure that turn a job into a trade."
- Councilmember Gloria Gray: "A project this size is only as good as the careers it leaves behind... With a 20-year operating term, these jobs do not vanish when the barricades come down."

wikis.title: South Station Tower, Boston
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on South Station Tower, the 51-story skyscraper built over Boston's South Station, covering its design, long planning history, construction from January 2020 to September 2025 and two 2024 site incidents.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- South Station Tower is a skyscraper in Boston, Massachusetts, the high-rise portion of a three-building development built on top of Boston's historic South Station complex.
- Status: Completed. Type: Office, residential. Location: Atlantic Avenue, Boston, Massachusetts, United States. Coordinates 42°21′06″N 71°03′18″W.
- Construction started January 2020; completed September 2025.
- Height: architectural 677 ft (206 m); roof 677 ft (206 m). Floor count: 51.
- Architect: César Pelli. Developer: Hines Interests. Website: southstationtower.com.
- "Construction on Phase 1 of the project, a 51-story, 678-foot tower with offices and condominiums, started in January 2020 and finished in September 2025."
- Upon completion, South Station Tower became the sixth-tallest building in Boston. It is an example of transit-oriented development. The overall project includes condominium units, office space, a parking structure, and possibly hotel space.

## Architecture

- Preliminary design was done by architect Cesar Pelli, "whose designs are reminiscent of his Wells Fargo Center in Minneapolis."
- The structure has been LEED pre-certified "silver" and won the EPA's "Green design" award.
- The tower does not actually touch the South Station building, but occupies the space between the station's tracks and atrium. To provide space for pedestrians, it is built atop an arched base structure anchored by eight columns; loads are transferred via diagonal struts from the tower's exterior to its concrete core, then distributed to the eight columns.
- Part of the tower is cantilevered over the station atrium. The lobby has views of a one-acre sky park on the 11th floor.
- The building has about 680,000 square feet (63,000 m2) of office space and 166 Ritz-Carlton-branded condominium residences on the 36th floor and higher.
- Another part of Phase I, an expanded bus station, uses a foundation put in place when the station was last renovated in the late 1980s.

## Planning history

- Foundation piers for a future high-rise, with posts spaced 35 feet (11 m) apart, were installed between each pair of tracks during the 1980s reconstruction of South Station; these would eventually support the bus station expansion.
- The building was conceived by Tufts University president Jean Mayer, who foresaw an "epicenter of high-profile medical research" in downtown Boston. In 1991 Tufts created a for-profit development subsidiary, TUDC LLC, and acquired the rights to the airspace. Development was complicated by Boston waterfront zoning restrictions requiring pedestrian access to the waterfront.
- In 1997, TUDC brought on Hines Interests LP as a development partner. In 2006, TUDC and Hines filed a Development Plan for the project.
- South Station Tower was originally designed with a height of 759 feet (231 m), including a decorative spire, but the project was downscaled in 2006.
- Approval was obtained by 2008 for a project totaling 2,190,000 square feet (203,000 m2); the tower was planned to break ground in 2008 with completion scheduled for 2010, but the project stalled. Questions were raised in 2007 about the university's role, and Tufts withdrew in 2009.
- As of March 2016 the developer's website said the tower would begin construction early in 2017; the FAA had given approval in February for a tower reaching 677 feet (206 m). The developer's rights to build on the site were scheduled to expire in April 2017 but the state extended them until the end of the year. Construction was halted due to MBTA concerns, but Hines did not stop the project.
- In July 2016 the developer filed a "Notice of Project Change" with the Boston Planning and Development Agency (BPDA), proposing changes including more residential space, with a timeline calling for construction of the high-rise tower to begin in 2017. In December 2016 the BPDA board approved construction.
- It was delayed until December 2017, then delayed again in 2018 due to MBTA concerns on the tower's potential operational and maintenance cost, its capital expenditure and how it was distributed among project stakeholders. In October that year, the MBTA extended the negotiation period with Hines until April 2019.

## Construction

- Construction officially began in January 2020, with a five-year completion timeline. By November 2022, ENR East reported the building's steel frame had reached 109 feet (33 m). Construction was completed in September 2025.
- **March 21, 2024:** a steel beam fell from the top of the tower, damaging several windows before coming to rest on the ninth floor; some equipment from the worksite also fell, landing at street level. The MBTA, which owns South Station and the South Station Bus Terminal, suspended commuter services and ordered work to halt. No injuries were reported, but construction company Suffolk agreed to pause work while investigations proceeded. Work resumed on March 27, 2024 following the conclusion of the stop-work order and OSHA investigations.
- **April 9, 2024:** a fire was started outside the ninth floor by welders. It was quickly put out and the site was again shut down for a safety review; work continued on April 10, 2024.

wikis.title: Opening of the Enterprise Research Campus in Allston
wikis.summary: Press release on Harvard, Tishman Speyer and Breakthrough Properties celebrating completion of the first phase of the nine-acre Enterprise Research Campus in Boston's Allston neighborhood, with each of its buildings and open spaces.
wikis.body:
## The event

- Dateline: BOSTON, June 24, 2026.
- Harvard University, Tishman Speyer and Breakthrough Properties were joined on June 23 by Mayor Michelle Wu "and a host of university, elected, local community and business leaders" to celebrate the completion of the first phase of the Enterprise Research Campus (ERC), "a dynamic, nine-acre mixed-use development in Boston's Allston neighborhood."
- The development is led by Tishman Speyer and Breakthrough in partnership with the Harvard Allston Land Company (HALC).

## What the first phase contains

- Two state-of-the-art laboratory buildings devoted to scientific research and development
- Hundreds of new apartments
- A boutique hotel
- A conference center
- 40,000 square feet of retail and restaurants
- More than two acres of publicly accessible open space anchored by the new Allstonway

## Quotes

- Harvard President Alan Garber: "The Enterprise Research campus is where researchers, entrepreneurs, and creative thinkers will work side by side... Building the companies and the industries of tomorrow. And as new discoveries are made, new challenges are identified. The spaces we have built will evolve."
- Tishman Speyer CEO Rob Speyer: "It's extremely gratifying to see the ERC come to life. From day one, Harvard has been an amazing partner... This is a destination for Harvard, Allston, and visitors from around the world."
- Breakthrough Properties CEO Dan Belldegrun: "With the ERC, we have created a world-leading innovation environment that will complement and accelerate cutting-edge research taking place at Harvard and the surrounding region. With Roche Genetech's innovation center as its anchor, One Milestone will produce dynamic partnerships between academia and industry."

The release also carries an "About Tishman Speyer" section describing the firm as an owner, developer, operator and investment manager in 33 key markets, which since its inception in 1978 has acquired, developed and operated 531 properties totaling 221 million square feet with a combined value of approximately $130 billion (U.S.).

wikis.title: One Milestone life science buildings
wikis.summary: The ERC's premier life science environment, a two-building lab complex anchored by Roche's CVRM Innovation Center.
wikis.body:
- One Milestone is "the ERC's premier life science environment," anchored by Roche's Innovation Center for Cardiovascular, Renal, and Metabolism (CVRM) discovery.
- Developed by Breakthrough Properties, a joint venture of Tishman Speyer and Bellco Capital.
- It "encourages connection and the exchange of ideas through an array of collaboration spaces and amenities, including a Jay Wright-designed fitness center and a double-height conference facility."
- Designed by architectural firms Henning Larsen and Studio Gang.
- The interconnected, two-building complex accommodates companies of all sizes, from large-scale users to emerging start-ups based in StudioLabs, Breakthrough's flexible lab component.

wikis.title: The David Rubenstein Treehouse
wikis.summary: Harvard's first university-wide conference center at the ERC, a mass timber building that opened in October 2025.
wikis.body:
