- The MARTA Rapid A-Line "provides a 5-mile roundtrip that connects Downtown Atlanta to the Capitol Gateway, Summerhill, Peoplestown, and the Atlanta Beltline with fast, frequent premium transit service."
- Connections to MARTA's heavy rail system are provided at Five Points, Georgia State and Garnett Stations.
- Funded through a Federal TIGER Grant and the More MARTA Atlanta Program, in partnership with the City of Atlanta.

## Schedule

- Planning and design work took place between spring 2019 and summer 2022.
- "The first phase of service began April 18, 2026."
- "Construction will be completed and final revenue service will begin in Fall 2026."

## Service features once fully completed

- 14 new stations on the A-Line.
- Level boarding, real-time arrival signage, and off-board fare collection so riders pay before boarding.
- Brand-new 60-foot articulated electric buses.
- Trips every 10 to 12 minutes during peak hours.
- Total travel time from Five Points Station south to Carver Station will be 12–15 minutes.
- 85% dedicated bus lanes with transit signal priority.

## Bus-only lanes (monthly station feature)

- Enforcing the bus-only lanes is "how Rapid A-Line will be able to maintain reliable travel times."
- The lanes have been painted red along the alignment; right turns are allowed from the striped red sections.
- Bus-only lanes will be enforced by the Atlanta Police Department, similar to the streetcar.

## Contact

- MARTA Rapid Response Team: Tameka Barber and Gracie Stuart, rapidaline@itsmarta.com, 404.848.3006.

wikis.title: Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta begins Phase 2 of the Concourse D widening project
wikis.summary: Airport Industry-News reports ATL starting Phase 2 of its Concourse D Widening Project with Module 6, and lists the improvements the rebuilt concourse will bring.
wikis.body:
## The work

- "Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) has commenced Phase 2 of its Concourse D Widening Project with the installation of Module 6."
- "Phase 1 of the project concluded on September 4, 2024, with the attachment of the first five modules to the existing concourse."
- "The second phase will see five additional modules moved and installed by 31 January, with 19 modules planned in total by the project's completion in the summer of 2029."
- The first of the next set of modules was affixed to Concourse D overnight (photo credit: City of Atlanta).

## Improvements listed for the revamped Concourse D

- Larger gate areas: hold rooms will double in size, with seating capacity increasing to 6,400.
- Expanded corridors: walkway width will increase by 29 feet.
- Higher ceilings: ceiling height will rise by 18 feet.
- Increased boarding level space: a 75% boost in square footage.
- Modernised facilities: new restrooms twice their original size and upgraded building systems.
- Optimised aircraft capacity: "Concourse D will accommodate 34 Group III aircraft, eight fewer than before, reflecting the shift to larger-capacity jets."

## Context

- The project is part of ATL's broader effort to enhance passenger experience and adapt to the evolving needs of air travel.
- Article by Tiana May, published 20 Jan 2025. Tagged ATL, United States.

wikis.title: Georgia Tech celebrates completion of George Tower | Scheller Tower
wikis.summary: Georgia Tech's news release on the ribbon-cutting for George Tower | Scheller Tower, a new home for industrial engineering and business education in Tech Square.
wikis.body:
## Event

- ATLANTA (Sept. 18, 2026) — Georgia Tech "today celebrated the completion of George Tower | Scheller Tower, a new home for industrial engineering and business education designed to prepare future leaders and strengthen Georgia's innovation economy."
- The ribbon-cutting ceremony "marks the completion of a project years in the making."
- Pictured at the ribbon cutting (left to right): Matt Dubnik, Georgia State Representative; Pinar Keskinocak, H. Milton Stewart School of Industrial and Systems Engineering Dean; Sonny Perdue, University System of Georgia Chancellor; Penny George; Bill George; Lisa Scheller; Ernie Scheller; Angel Cabrera, Georgia Tech President; Anuj Mehrotra, Ernest Scheller Jr. College of Business Dean; Raheem Beyah, Georgia Tech Provost; Alexandra Akosa-Sissoko; and Buzz.

## The building

- Brings together the H. Milton Stewart School of Industrial and Systems Engineering and the Scheller College of Business in a shared environment for collaboration among students, faculty, researchers, entrepreneurs and industry partners.
- Located in the heart of Tech Square, strengthening connections between Georgia Tech and nearby companies, startups, researchers and entrepreneurs.
- "Designed for the next 50 years," it incorporates advanced systems and sustainable design strategies that significantly reduce energy and water use.
- The project "recently earned LEED Platinum certification, the highest level awarded by the U.S. Green Building Council, and a 4 Peach rating, the highest rating through the Georgia Peach Green Building Rating System administered by the Georgia State Financing and Investment Commission."

## Funding

- Made possible through support from the state of Georgia and donations from Georgia Tech alumni and their families: Bill and Penny George, Ernest "Ernie" Scheller, and H. Milton "Milt" Stewart and Carolyn Stewart, along with many other donors.

## Quote

- Georgia Tech President Ángel Cabrera: "People will notice the striking architecture, the classrooms, and the technology inside the new towers... What matters most is what that design enables — the learning and exchange of ideas between students, the multidisciplinary collaborations between engineering and business faculty, and the support of innovation and entrepreneurship at the heart of Tech Square."

wikis.title: PM Lawrence Wong's speech at the Changi Airport Terminal 5 groundbreaking
wikis.summary: The Prime Minister's Office publishes PM Lawrence Wong's 14 May 2025 speech at the Changi Airport Terminal 5 groundbreaking ceremony, setting out what T5 will be and the wider Changi East development.
wikis.body:
## The occasion

- Speech by Prime Minister and Minister for Finance Lawrence Wong at the Changi Airport Terminal 5 Groundbreaking Ceremony on 14 May 2025.
- "Good afternoon and I am very happy to join all of you today to break ground finally for Changi Terminal 5." He calls it "a very significant milestone in our aviation journey" and notes it falls "in this SG60 year."
- Addressed to Minister Chee Hong Tat, the CAG Chairman and CEO and the Singapore aviation community.

## Background given on Changi

- Singapore used to operate from Paya Lebar Airport; in the 70s consultants recommended expanding Paya Lebar and building a second runway there, saying relocating to Changi would be too expensive and doubting demand, "particularly at a time when the world was still feeling the impact of the 1973 oil crisis."
- Changi has been expanded to its current four terminals, plus Jewel.
- "The aviation ecosystem now contributes 5% of our GDP."
- Changi "has been named the world's best airport by Skytrax again last month – it is the only airport in the world to receive this award 13 times."
- Other countries are investing significantly in modernising airport infrastructure and adjacent infrastructure like airport cities.

## T5

- T5 was announced "way back in 2013," with preparatory works planned soon after; plans were paused because of Covid and the downtime used to refresh and update the plans and do value engineering.
- "In terms of land area, T5 will be as big as all our current terminals combined."
- It "will expand Changi's current capacity by more than 50%" and "allow us to serve about 50 million more passengers annually."
- SIA Group's flights, currently split across three terminals, "can now be consolidated at T5" — "T5 will be the new home for SIA Group" — with space for other carriers to grow.
- Changi has around 170 city links; with T5 Singapore can "reach our target of reaching more than 200 city links by the mid-2030s."
- A smart terminal: state-of-the-art airport systems, automation of passenger-facing and back-end functions such as baggage handling, intelligent systems and data.
- A sustainable terminal: smart building management systems with AI-optimised air-conditioning, intelligent lighting and hybrid cooling; more clean energy. "The team is studying the feasibility of installing a solar system on its roof. And if that happens, it will be the largest rooftop system in Singapore."

## Connections

- An Automated People Mover system will bring passengers from T5's arrival gates to the immigration halls, and will keep T5 connected to the other terminals as Changi Airport "will double in land size."
- A dedicated ground transportation centre will bring together car, taxi, MRT and bus options.
- "The Thomson-East Coast Line will be extended to bring passengers directly from T5 to the city centre, and vice versa."
- Singapore is "working to extend the Cross Island Line to connect T5 to new hubs in Singapore like the Jurong Lake District as well as the Punggol Digital District."
- Through the Thomson-East Coast Line, T5 can connect to "the upcoming JB-Singapore Rapid Transit System or RTS Link terminal at Woodlands North."
- Because T5 will be closer to the Tanah Merah Ferry Terminal, Singapore "can also explore seamless air-sea transfers to destinations in neighbouring countries."

## Changi East development

- Changi East Industrial Zone: "will increase Singapore's air cargo handling capacity significantly" and strengthen Singapore as an integrated logistics hub.
- Changi East Urban District: "a new lifestyle and business hub located right at the doorstep of T5. Concept planning for this is underway."

## Jobs and delivery

- "T5 will be a multi-year project, spanning multiple terms of government."
- Local businesses will have the opportunity to participate in construction; some are already involved in the ongoing works.
- When operational it will create more demand for services and workers, requiring new skillsets in areas like data science, robotics and sustainability.

wikis.title: LTA factsheet: The Next Phase of Rail Development (Singapore)
wikis.summary: Singapore's Land Transport Authority factsheet from the Committee of Supply debate, setting out which rail stages open this year and the status of the JRL, Cross Island Line and new line studies.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- News release dated 04 Mar 2026, issued for the Ministry of Transport's Committee of Supply debate "today."
- LTA "will complete the final stages of works and open the Circle Line Stage 6 (CCL6), Downtown Line 3 extension (DTL3e), and Thomson-East Coast Line Stage 5 (TEL5) this year."
- Construction works for Cross Island Line Phase 3 (CRL3) are "planned to commence next year."
- Engineering studies for the first phases of the Seletar Line, Tengah Line and West Coast Extension of the Jurong Region Line are "planned to commence this year."
- The new stations bring Singapore closer to the Land Transport Master Plan 2040 target of "having 8 in 10 households within a 10-minute walk of a train station by the 2030s."
- Additional engineering hours will be required to integrate the new systems into the existing network.
- Annex A gives the location map of the new JS2A station.

wikis.title: New stations opening this year: CCL6, TEL5 and DTL3e
wikis.summary: The three rail stages LTA says will open in 2026 and their station counts.
wikis.body:
- CCL6 "will close the CCL circle with three new stations between HarbourFront and Marina Bay stations."
- "Steady progress is being made for the ongoing tunnel strengthening works on the CCL, which need to be completed before the remaining testing and preparatory works for CCL6 can resume."
- CCL6 is "on track to open in the middle of this year."
- "Another three new stations under TEL5 and DTL3e are on track to open in the second half of this year."

wikis.title: Jurong Region Line: new JS2A station and Stage 1 delay
wikis.summary: LTA adds a station to the JRL and pushes Stage 1 opening from end-2027 to around mid-2028, with interim bus measures.
wikis.body:
## New station

- "A new station, JS2A, will be added to the JRL," situated between JS2 and JS3 stations, serving future commuter demand in the Tengah area. This brings the total number of JRL stations to 25.
- Civil construction works for the JS2A station structure are underway; JS2A is "targeted to open in the mid-2030s, in tandem with the completion of future developments surrounding the station."

## Stage 1 delay

- "Based on the latest progress for the JRL, an additional six months will be required before the first stage of the JRL can be opened. This means that Stage 1 of the JRL will open around mid-2028, instead of the initial end-2027 timeline."
- LTA has deployed additional manpower and equipment to catch up with earlier delays due to the COVID-19 pandemic, but "could not recover all the earlier delays."
- Examples given: viaduct construction over the Pan-Island Expressway (PIE) could only be carried out during overnight road closures on designated nights; construction of a viaduct over a 25-metre wide canal needed more comprehensive ground reinforcement measures than originally planned.
- Further updates on the opening dates of the second and third stages will come as works progress.

## Interim measures

- Interim shuttle bus services will be introduced in end-2027 to improve transport capacity between areas due to be served by JRL Stage 1.
- Services 97 and 97e will be extended to Tengah on 8 March 2026, giving a direct link to Labrador Park, HarbourFront and the Central Business District.
- Service 181 will be extended from Jurong West to Tengah, and a new City Direct Service 684 will link Brickland and Bukit Batok West with the downtown area.

wikis.title: Cross Island Line phases and Punggol Extension
wikis.summary: Status and target dates for CRL Phases 1, 2 and 3 and the CRL-Punggol Extension.
wikis.body:
- CRL Phase 1, from CR2 Aviation Park station to CR13 Bright Hill station, "has seen significant progress with several stretches of tunnelling work completed, and is targeted to open in 2030."
- CRL Phase 2, extending Phase 1 westwards to the Jurong Lake District, is "advancing steadily with early-stage tunnelling works ongoing."
- The CRL-Punggol Extension (CPE) is "progressing smoothly, with the design and construction of stations underway."
- CRL Phase 2 and CPE are "slated for completion in 2032."
- Engineering studies for CRL Phase 3 "have also been completed"; it will extend Phase 2 further westwards to serve the Jurong Industrial Estate and residential developments in Taman Jurong, and give alternative routes from the North and Northeast to the West.
- LTA plans to commence construction works for CRL Phase 3 next year; it is "slated for completion in the late 2030s."

wikis.title: Seletar Line, Tengah Line and JRL West Coast Extension studies
wikis.summary: Engineering studies planned this year for three future lines and what corridors LTA will explore.
wikis.body:
- LTA plans to commence engineering studies for the Seletar Line and Tengah Line, as well as the West Coast Extension of the JRL, this year.
- "Our initial focus for the Seletar Line will be to provide more travel options for residents in the Northeast." LTA will explore a corridor serving the Sengkang West and Serangoon North areas, with possible connections to the Cross Island Line and Circle Line.
- For the West Coast Extension, the focus is the first phase, which will extend the JRL from JE7 station to CR18 West Coast (working name) station.
- Feasibility studies will continue for the subsequent phases of these lines.

wikis.title: Sungei Bedok MRT station
wikis.summary: Wikipedia's article on Sungei Bedok, a future underground MRT interchange and terminus on Singapore's Downtown and Thomson–East Coast Lines, with its specifications and construction history.
wikis.body:
## The station

- "Sungei Bedok MRT station is a future underground Mass Rapid Transit interchange and terminal station on the Downtown Line and Thomson–East Coast Line in Bedok planning area, Singapore."
- Being built east of where Upper East Coast Road becomes Bedok Road; will serve residents of the Eastwood estate. Nearby facilities include the Bedok Food Centre, Eastwood Centre and the Laguna National Golf & Country Club.
- Location: 3 Bedok Road, Singapore 469731. Coordinates 01°19′13″N 103°57′25″E.
- Station codes DT37 / TE31; station code SBD. Former name: Eastwood.
- Owner: Land Transport Authority. Operators: SBS Transit (Downtown Line) and SMRT Trains (Thomson–East Coast Line).
- Structure: underground, depth 27 metres (89 ft), 2 platform levels, 4 platforms (2 island platforms), 4 tracks. Connections: bus, taxi. Accessible: yes. Electrified.
- Opening: 2H 2026.
- Adjacent stations: Xilin (Downtown Line, towards Bukit Panjang) with Sungei Bedok as terminus; Bedok South (Thomson–East Coast Line, towards Woodlands North); and Changi Terminal 5 (towards Tanah Merah) on the future TEL extension.
- The infobox caption notes a "Construction site of the station in 2026."

## History

- "This station was first announced on 15 August 2014 as part of the Downtown Line stage 3e, consisting of 2 stations between Xilin and Sungei Bedok, and the Thomson–East Coast Line phase 5, also consisting of 2 stations between Bedok South and Sungei Bedok MRT."
- It was expected to be completed in 2024, in tandem with the adjacent East Coast Integrated Depot.
- "However, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, this station was expected to commence passenger service in 2025 instead."
- "Due to challenges of tunnelling near existing critical infrastructure, the station is now expected to commence passenger service in 2026."
- It will serve as the eastern terminus of the Thomson–East Coast Line until 2040, when the line will be extended to Changi Airport Terminal 5 and the existing Changi Airport stations before terminating at Tanah Merah.
- "Contract T312 for the design and construction of Sungei Bedok Station and associated tunnels was awarded to KTC Civil Engineering & Construction Pte Ltd for S$418 million in June 2016. Construction began in 2016."

wikis.title: MOH: Enhancing quality and coordination of care (Committee of Supply 2026)
wikis.summary: Singapore's Ministry of Health press release on expanding healthcare capacity, the NEHR Connect Grant, psychology regulation and new training pathways.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- Press release dated 5 March 2026.
- "To meet the rising demand for healthcare services and manpower, the Ministry of Health (MOH) will continue to expand capacity while enhancing the quality and coordination of care in the healthcare system." Efforts are also underway to transform the workforce.
- The release covers: hospital capacity, the polyclinic network, support for onboarding to the National Electronic Health Record, regulation of psychology practice, an accelerated clinical psychology pathway, and nursing post-diploma work-study programmes.

wikis.title: Expansion of healthcare capacity
wikis.summary: Hospital bed additions and infrastructure projects MOH lists to 2030 and beyond.
wikis.body:
- As announced at the Committee of Supply 2025, MOH is "on track to add about 2,800 new public acute and community hospital beds by 2030."
- The new Singapore General Hospital (SGH) Elective Care Centre "will open by 2027."
- Sengkang General Hospital will add new beds progressively from 2027.
- Woodlands Hospital and Tan Tock Seng Integrated Care Hub "will continue to ramp-up their bed capacity."
- The redeveloped Alexandra Hospital "has commenced construction works and will open progressively from 2028."
- The new Eastern General Hospital Campus at Bedok North, comprising a new integrated general and community hospital, "has commenced construction works and will open progressively from 2029."
- Beyond 2030: design consultancies have commenced for the Tan Tock Seng Hospital Medical Tower, Tengah General and Community Hospital, and the redevelopment of National University Hospital (NUH) Kent Ridge. MOH "will also be calling the design consultancy tender for Phase 2 redevelopment for SGH in the coming weeks."

wikis.title: Growing the polyclinic network
wikis.summary: New and redeveloped polyclinics on MOH's path from 28 to 32 polyclinics by 2030.
wikis.body:
- "There were 28 polyclinics as at end-February 2026. MOH is on track to expand the network of polyclinics to 32 by 2030."
- New polyclinics in Bidadari, Kaki Bukit and Yew Tee are "scheduled to be completed by 2027."
- Taman Jurong Polyclinic is "scheduled to be completed by 2030."
- Beyond 2030, there will be a new polyclinic at Bishan.
- Clementi, Jurong, Queenstown and Toa Payoh polyclinics "will be redeveloped by 2030."
- Beyond 2030, Bukit Merah and Outram polyclinics will be consolidated into one polyclinic at Tiong Bahru.

wikis.title: NEHR Connect Grant and Health Information Act support
wikis.summary: A grant of up to $45 million to help healthcare providers onboard to the National Electronic Health Record, plus related cybersecurity support.
wikis.body:
- MOH will launch the NEHR Connect Grant (NCG), "with up to $45 million set aside over the next four years to support healthcare providers."
- The NCG is one-off funding to defray the costs of adopting a certified health information management system (HIMS) or enhancing an existing HIMS to meet Health Information Act (HIA) requirements.
- "The NCG will be rolled out from July 2026."
- For subscription-based HIMS, the NCG covers approximately two years of subscription costs for HIA-compliant systems; for in-house systems, it covers up to 40% of enhancement costs up to a cap that varies by licensable health sector.
- Providers that have previously received similar MOH funding support for NEHR data contribution are not eligible.
- Providers may also tap Enterprise Singapore's Productivity Solutions Grant for IT/cybersecurity solutions, and support from the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA); SMEs without cybersecurity capabilities can receive up to 70% co-funding to engage CSA-certified consultants (via CSA's CISO as-a-Service for HIA Cybersecurity and Data Security Essentials).
- "Based on the set up of a typical solo practitioner clinic, they may be eligible for approximately $20,000 in grants across the agencies."
- MOH is developing thematic infographics, an implementation guide with templates and a self-assessment tool, and training courses (for example through NTUC LearningHub), and is partnering bodies such as the Singapore Medical Association for webinars and townhalls.
- Information will be available at the Health Information Act website, www.healthinfo.gov.sg.
- HIA will facilitate onboarding of all healthcare providers onto the NEHR; authorised providers may access patient histories during consultations, "thus reducing medical errors and improving clinical decision-making."

wikis.title: Regulatory framework for the practice of psychology
wikis.summary: Five psychology subdisciplines will be registered under the Allied Health Professions Act 2011.
wikis.body:
- An inter-agency Implementation Committee of psychologists, employers, regulators and academics identified five psychological subdisciplines for regulation: "clinical, clinical neuropsychology, forensic, counselling and educational psychology."
- These subdisciplines "provide direct care involving higher-risk assessments and interventions across various sectors that warrant regulatory oversight."
- Psychologists in these subdisciplines will be registered under the Allied Health Professions Act 2011. "Registration will be phased across the five identified subdisciplines, and the detailed requirements and timelines will be announced in due course."
- Requirements are being developed from international standards, local and overseas regulatory frameworks, the current criteria of the Singapore Register of Psychologists and practitioner feedback, with grandfathering provisions for in-service psychologists.
- MOH and partner ministries (MSF, MHA, MINDEF, MOE) will work with the Singapore Psychological Society to raise public awareness of each subdiscipline's scope of practice and protected titles.
- Unregistered psychology subdisciplines "generally operate in lower-risk practice settings"; existing safeguards will continue while MOH monitors the need for further regulation.

wikis.title: Accelerated clinical psychology pathway at NUS
wikis.summary: An accelerated undergraduate-to-master's route into clinical psychology, targeted at the 2026 intake.
wikis.body:
- MOH is working with MOE and the National University of Singapore (NUS) "to offer eligible undergraduates the option of an accelerated pathway to specialise in Clinical Psychology at Master's level."
- "The programme is targeted to roll-out for the undergraduate intake cohort of 2026."
- NUS is curating a curriculum of didactic learning and clinical training during the undergraduate years, with graduates leaving with both a Bachelor's degree with Honours and a Master's degree.
- The pathway complements existing postgraduate pipelines, including NUS's standalone two-year Master of Psychology (Clinical) for those with relevant clinical work experience.

wikis.title: Nursing post-diploma specialty programmes move to work-study format
wikis.summary: MOH will convert nursing post-diploma specialty programmes to a 70:30 work-study model, starting with two advanced diplomas.
wikis.body:
- MOH will work with Nanyang Polytechnic and Ngee Ann Polytechnic "to transit nursing post-diploma specialty programmes to a work-study format with a greater focus on competencies," building on initiatives such as the ITE Work-Study Diploma in Nursing.
- "Nursing work-study programmes have a greater emphasis on work, with a recommended work-study ratio of 70:30," combining academic learning with structured on-the-job training.
- The format lets nurses remain in clinical practice while developing new competencies.
- Existing programmes will be transited in phases; two Advanced Diploma in Nursing programmes — Palliative Care and Community Health — "will be prioritised for initial launch in work-study format. More details will be shared when ready."

wikis.title: Central Kowloon Route Project
wikis.summary: Hong Kong Highways Department project page for the Central Kowloon Route, listing its cost, dates and each construction contract.
wikis.body:
## Project

- Purpose: "To relieve traffic congestion on the existing east-west roads across Central Kowloon."
- "The Central Kowloon Bypass (Yau Ma Tei Section) is a 4.7 km long dual 3-lane trunk road connecting Yau Ma Tei Interchange in West Kowloon to the Kai Tak Development Area and Kowloon Bay in East Kowloon, including a tunnel of about 3.9km long."
- Estimated project cost: HK$42.36 billion.
- Construction commencement date: Dec 2017. Commissioning date: Dec 2025.
- Listed under "Projects Completed in Past 10 Years."
- Consultant (design and construction): Arup – Mott MacDonald Joint Venture, which is also resident engineer on every contract listed.
- Each construction contract's completion is recorded as: "Central Kowloon Bypass (Yau Ma Tei Section) was opened to the public on 21 December 2025."

## Contracts

- **HY/2014/09** — vertical access shaft at Ho Man Tin, ground investigation and horizontal directional coring. Commenced Dec 2017. HK$317 million. Contractor: Nishimatsu Construction Company, Limited.
- **HY/2014/07** — tunnels under the seabed of Kowloon Bay and at Ma Tau Kok, depressed roads and underpass at Kai Tak Development. Commenced Jan 2018. HK$6.24 billion. Contractor: Gammon Construction Limited.
- **HY/2014/08** — tunnel at Yau Ma Tei, reconstruction of a section of the Gascoigne Road Flyover, reprovisioning of affected public facilities at Yau Ma Tei. Commenced Jan 2018. HK$5.02 billion. Contractor: Build King - SK ecoplant Joint Venture.
- **HY/2014/20** — depressed road with western landscaping deck structure at Yau Ma Tei and connection to the existing road network. Commenced Nov 2018. HK$3.46 billion. Contractor: Build King - SK ecoplant Joint Venture.
- **HY/2018/02** — at-grade roads, bridges and Kai Tak Interchange from the Central Kowloon Route to road networks in Kai Tak Development and Kowloon Bay. Commenced Apr 2019. HK$1.97 billion. Contractor: Alchmex – Paul Y Joint Venture.
- **HY/2018/08** — central tunnel, cut-and-cover tunnels at Yau Ma Tei and Ma Tau Kok, piles and diaphragm walls for the Ho Man Tin ventilation building. Commenced Jul 2019. HK$6.23 billion. Contractor: Bouygues Travaux Publics.
- **HY/2019/13** — administration building and ventilation buildings, route-wide electrical and mechanical works. Commenced Jun 2020. HK$5.67 billion. Contractor: Gammon Construction Limited.
- **HY/2023/08** — landscaping works at Yau Ma Tei Landscaped Deck, Yau Ma Tei Gardens, North Tree Park and Kai Tak Phase 2B Landscaped Deck, improvement of a section of Kai Fuk Road, planting of compensatory trees. Commenced Jul 2024, anticipated completion 2028. HK$829 million. Contractor: Build King – Tung Lee Joint Venture.

wikis.title: Trunk Road T2 and infrastructure works at the former South Apron, Hong Kong
wikis.summary: The project website's overview of Trunk Road T2 and the Cha Kwo Ling Tunnel, the middle section of Route 6, with its contracts and project timeline.
wikis.body:
## Project overview

- "The Trunk Road T2 and the Cha Kwo Ling (CKL) Tunnel form the middle section of Route 6." They connect the Central Kowloon Route (CKR) to the west and the main tunnel of the Tseung Kwan O – Lam Tin Tunnel (TKO-LTT) to the east.
- Route 6 forms part of Hong Kong's strategic road network, linking West Kowloon to Tseung Kwan O New Town with intermediate interchanges at Kai Tak and Lam Tin.
- It supports developments including the West Kowloon Cultural District and the West Kowloon Station of the Hong Kong Section of the Guangzhou–Shenzhen–Hong Kong Express Rail Link; the Cruise Terminal, the Kai Tak Development and the Kowloon East Central Business District; and residential/industrial developments in TKO.
- "Upon the completion of T2 Project, the entire Route 6 will be fully commissioned."
- During peak hours, journey time between Tseung Kwan O Town Centre and Yau Ma Tei "will be substantially shortened from about 65 minutes now to 12 minutes" (anticipated).

## Contracts

- **ED/2018/04 — Trunk Road T2 and Infrastructure Works for Developments at the Former South Apron.** Scope: design and construction of a dual two-lane trunk road approximately 3.4 km long, of which about 3.1 km is tunnel; two ventilation buildings at the ends of the trunk road; infrastructure works for developments at the former south apron; and associated electrical and mechanical, civil, structural, building, landscaping, drainage and sewerage works. Commenced 14 November 2019, anticipated completion 2026. Contract sum HK$10.918 billion. Contractor: Bouygues Travaux Publics. Consultant: Hyder-Meinhardt Joint Venture.
- **ED/2020/03 — Trunk Road T2 Traffic Control and Surveillance System and Associated Work.** Scope: design, supply, delivery, installation, testing and commissioning of the traffic control and surveillance system (TCSS) for Trunk Road T2 and its integration with the central system of the TKO-LTT TCSS. Commenced 28 January 2022, anticipated completion 2026. Contract sum HK$203.80 million. Contractor: GTECH Services (Hong Kong) Limited. Consultant: Hyder-Meinhardt Joint Venture.

## Timeline as listed

- Nov 2007 — approval of the draft Kai Tak Outline Zoning Plan, in which the Trunk Road T2 alignment was finalized after a three-stage public consultation process.
- Jan 2013 — consultation with the Sai Kung District Council (SKDC) and Kwun Tong District Council (KTDC) on the TKO-LTT project (including the CKL Tunnel).
- May 2013 — gazette of the proposed road scheme of the TKO-LTT project (G.N. 2569).
- July 2013 — approval of the Environmental Impact Assessment Report for the TKO-LTT project.
- Sep 2013 — approval of the Environmental Impact Assessment Report for Trunk Road T2.
- Oct 2013 — consultation with the Task Force on Kai Tak Harbourfront Development about Trunk Road T2.
- Nov 2013 — consultation with the Housing and Infrastructure Committee of the Kowloon City District Council and the Traffic and Transport Committees of the Wong Tai Sin District Council and KTDC about Trunk Road T2.
- May 2014 — gazette of the authorisation of the TKO-LTT road scheme (G.N. 3063).
- Sep 2014 — gazette of the proposed road scheme of Trunk Road T2 (G.N. 5102).
- Nov 2014 — gazette of the authorisation of the Trunk Road T2 road scheme (G.N. 6608).
- May 2015 — further briefing to SKDC and the KTDC Traffic and Transport Committee on TKO-LTT updates.
- Aug 2015 — consultation with the Task Force about the TKO-LTT project.
- Jun 2018 — consultation with the Legislative Council Panel on Transport on Trunk Road T2 and the CKL Tunnel.
- Apr 2019 — endorsement by the Public Works Subcommittee of the LegCo Finance Committee.
- Oct 2019 — the LegCo Finance Committee approved funding for Trunk Road T2 and the CKL Tunnel.
- Nov 2019 — Contract ED/2018/04 commenced.
- Jan 2022 — Contract ED/2020/03 commenced.

wikis.title: Kwu Tung Station, MTR Northern Link project
wikis.summary: The MTR Northern Link project site's page on the proposed Kwu Tung Station, covering its construction sequence, location, design, sustainability features, construction challenges and the surrounding community.
wikis.body:
## Construction sequence and dates

- "Taking into account the development pace along the Northern Link, we will first commence the construction of Kwu Tung Station on the Lok Ma Chau Spur Line of the East Rail Line and then the construction of the main line, including Kwu Tung Station on the Northern Link, progressively."
- The two stations "will be next to each other and inter-connected."
- "The detailed design of Kwu Tung Station on the East Rail Line has been completed, and the main construction works have already been commenced in 2023, with a target to complete the entire project in 2027."
- Image captions: "Kwu Tung Station on East Rail Line with target construction completion in 2027" and "A full view of Kwu Tung Station with target construction completion in 2034."
- Note repeated on the page: "The station names on the Northern Link are working titles only. All Drawings and visuals are provided for concept illustration only, and the content is subject to change."

## Location

- The proposed station is between Sheung Shui and Lok Ma Chau stations, at the junction of the existing Ma Tso Lung Road and Ho Sheung Heung Road, in the town centre of the future Kwu Tung North New Development Area (NDA).
- It sits at the Town Plaza and will connect residential, retail and commercial developments on both sides of the plaza.
- "The majority of the population of the Kwu Tung North NDA will be distributed within walking distance of the proposed Kwu Tung Station."

## Entrances and interchange

- When Kwu Tung Station on the East Rail Line commences service, the eastern and western sides will each have two entrances/exits connecting to the Kwu Tung North NDA; those on the western side give access to the future public wet market and public transport interchange.
- Further entrances/exits will be added on both sides at a later stage to complement the commissioning of Kwu Tung Station on the Northern Link.
- When the Northern Link station opens, passengers can interchange between the East Rail Line and Northern Link "in the station's paid area," with clear signage.

## Design and sustainability

- An underground station with three levels: platforms in the lower basement, concourse in the upper basement, entrances/exits on the ground floor connecting to the Town Plaza.
- "The overall station design incorporates elements of sustainable development, with a target to attain BEAM Plus Gold Certification for the project."
- Design incorporates Kwu Tung's historical, cultural and natural landscape characteristics; open-design entrances aligning with the proposed natural ventilation and green corridor; skylights and high canopies for air circulation and natural lighting.
- Listed sustainable features: natural lighting, natural ventilation, green roof, neighbourhood integration, inclusive design.
- Inclusive design: passenger lifts, barrier-free accesses, public toilets and a babycare room.
- Building Information Modelling (BIM) has been applied at every stage of the Northern Link project; the team is "actively studying the adoption of the Design for Manufacture and Assembly (DfMA) and Modular Integrated Construction method (MiC)."

## Construction challenges

- Works must be carried out on the operating East Rail Line, including modifying the existing tunnel for station use while maintaining normal train operations, with protection works for existing railway facilities beforehand and close monitoring of excavation "given the high groundwater table in the works area."
- Emergency vehicular access and evacuation routes must be kept clear, so space for works, equipment and staff access is "extremely limited."
- Part of the construction must happen during non-traffic hours at night, "which may be less than several hours per night on several nights per week."
- Part of the station was built earlier: as part of the Lok Ma Chau Spur Line enabling works, tunnel structure works including the tunnel box at underground track level were completed, allowing cut-and-cover construction of the platforms, concourse and entrances above. A photo shows Lok Ma Chau Spur Line construction in Kwu Tung in 2003.

## Theme colour and community

- "The primary theme colour of Kwu Tung Station... echos the long soy sauce manufacturing history of the community," with colours representing the natural beauty of Kwu Tung as highlights.
- Since 1945 Kwu Tung has been a settlement inhabited by the ancient Wai Tau and Hakka communities and a small number of Chiu Chow people; historical documents note that most ethnic minorities used the Chinese character "cave" ("Tung") in place names.
- Local landmarks described: the huge freshwater pipelines of the Dongjiang-Shenzhen Water supply system at the junction of the Ng Tung River (River Indus) and Sheung Yue River (River Beas), a photography and film location ("Zero to Hero," "High Noon"); Long Valley Wetland near Yin Kong, Tsung Pak Long and Ho Sheung Heung, "the largest and most complete freshwater wetland in Hong Kong," attracting migratory birds including Eastern Yellow Wagtail, Common Kestrel and Dusky Thrush; the Lady Ho Tung Welfare Centre, completed in 1933 with donations from Sir Robert Ho Tung and named after his first wife Mak Sau-ying, one of the first rural clinics in the New Territories, revitalised into the Eco-Learn Institute in 2015 and accorded Grade 2 Historical Building status; Kwu Tung Reservoir, the "heart-shaped lake" south of Kwu Tung Village beside Ki Lun Shan; and Kwu Tung Market Shopping Centre, built in the late 1980s.
- Other Northern Link stations listed: Kwu Tung, San Tin, Ngau Tam Mei, Au Tau, Kam Sheung Road.

wikis.title: LCQ6: Hong Kong Park of the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science and Technology Innovation Co-operation Zone
wikis.summary: A Legislative Council question and government reply on tenants, facilities and the Western Cross-River Link Bridge at the Hetao Co-operation Zone's Hong Kong Park.
wikis.body:
## The exchange

- Question by the Hon Chan Yung, reply by the Acting Secretary for Innovation, Technology and Industry, Ms Lillian Cheong, in the Legislative Council on January 28 (2026).
- The question asked about (1) the sectoral and origin mix of enterprises in the Hong Kong Park and investment-attraction plans for the coming six months, (2) progress on supporting infrastructure, and (3) the construction schedule for the Western Cross-River Link Bridge and "contactless clearance."

## Background given

- The Co-operation Zone "is located on both sides of the Shenzhen River and is one of the four major co-operation platforms in the Greater Bay Area under the National 14th Five-Year Plan."
- In November 2024 the HKSAR Government promulgated "The Development Outline for the Hong Kong Park," proposing a two-phase, batch-by-batch development approach.
- "The construction of two wet laboratory buildings and one talent accommodation building under the Batch 1 development of Phase 1 has been completed. The Hong Kong Park of the Co-operation Zone was officially opened in December 2025. The remaining five buildings of the first batch will be completed progressively starting from 2027."
- The Hong Kong-Shenzhen Innovation and Technology Park Limited (HSITPL) has invited private-sector expressions of interest for the remaining Phase 1 land parcels; the Government will consider tendering or public-private partnership models "starting this year."

## Enterprises in the Park

- "As of the end of December 2025, over 60 technology enterprises and institutions have signed leases for spaces in the two wet laboratory buildings and have begun moving in, occupying nearly 80 per cent of the total floor area of these two buildings."
- About 60 per cent of these enterprises are from the Mainland, 15 per cent from overseas and roughly 25 per cent local Hong Kong enterprises.
- By industry: about half in artificial intelligence and data science, close to 40 per cent in life and health sciences, the rest in other frontier fields such as microelectronics, new energy and robotics.
- HSITPL will continue roadshows, exhibitions and major conferences to attract more enterprises.
- Cross-boundary flow of the "four flows" — personnel, materials (e.g. biosamples), capital and data — is being explored with Mainland authorities.

## Facilities

- "The first talent accommodation building welcomed its first batch of residents in December 2025." Food and beverage and living amenities (Chinese, Western and Korean restaurants, fast-food outlets, snack shop, convenience store, ATM, smart parcel lockers) have commenced operation progressively.
- Space will be reserved within the remaining Phase 1 plots for retail, dining and short-term accommodation.
- Transport: the Park Company has arranged shuttle bus services connecting to or passing through Lok Ma Chau Station, Yuen Long Station and Sheung Shui Station; car and bicycle parking are provided; the Transport Department will plan public transport services subject to demand. "In the longer term, the Northern Link Spur Line under planning will pass through the Park with a railway station thereat."

## Western Cross-River Link Bridge

- The project connecting the two parks "has commenced in December 2025."
- Design concept integrates the cross-boundary bridge with the surrounding ecological environment, emphasising low-carbon technology, safety and convenience and scenery, using a "single-span across the river" construction approach.
- "We will strive for the early completion of the relevant construction works, which is targeted to complete by mid-2027."
- On clearance: "The target is to enable pre-verified individuals to enjoy a contactless clearance experience through the use of facial recognition technology."

## Issued

- Ends/Wednesday, January 28, 2026, issued at HKT 14:42.

wikis.title: Dubai Metro Blue Line to start operations on 9 September 2029
wikis.summary: Khaleej Times reports the RTA's announcement of the Dubai Metro Blue Line's opening date, its Dh20.5-billion construction contract and the line's planned specifications.
wikis.body:
## Announcement

- The Dubai Metro Blue Line Project "is expected to start operations on 9-9-2029," the Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) announced on Thursday.
- The RTA has awarded a Dh20.5-billion contract to three Turkish and Chinese companies — Mapa, Limak and CRRC — for the project's construction.
- The article notes the Dubai Metro opened "in the 9th second of the 9th minute at 9pm on 9-9-2009," and the Blue Line's rollout coincides with the metro's 20th anniversary.

## The line

- Spans 30 kilometres with 14 stations and 28 trains in its network.
- Expected to carry 200,000 riders in 2030, rising to 320,000 passengers by 2040.
- Will carry 46,000 passengers per hour in both directions and is expected to reduce traffic congestion on the routes it serves by 20 per cent.
- Provides connectivity between Dubai International Airport and key urban areas, with travel times ranging between 10 and 25 minutes.
- The nine key areas served: Mirdif, Al Warqa, International City 1 and 2, Dubai Silicon Oasis, Academic City, Ras Al Khor Industrial Area, Dubai Creek Harbour and Dubai Festival City.
- Part of the Dubai 2040 Urban Master Plan, which aims to create a '20-minute city' where residents have about 80 per cent of essential services within a 20-minute journey.

## Station design

- New stations will have "a sleek, futuristic design," in contrast to the fully-enclosed stations on the Red and Green Lines.
- The main platform is enclosed by a large, oval-shaped structure arching over the tracks, with symmetrical curved side structures housing the exits.

## Property effects

- A previous Khaleej Times report expects double-digit rises in property prices and rentals in areas such as International City, Silicon Oasis, Ras Al Khor, Mirdif and Al Warqa.
- The RTA said the metro route will appreciate the value of land and properties near stations by up to 25 per cent.

wikis.title: King Salman Stadium unveiled with 92,000 seating capacity
wikis.summary: The Royal Commission for Riyadh City announces the approved designs and plans for King Salman Stadium in northern Riyadh, with its capacity, facilities and completion date.
wikis.body:
## Announcement

- "The Royal Commission for Riyadh City and the Ministry of Sport have announced the designs and plans for the King Salman Stadium and its sporting facilities as one of the world's largest sports arenas." Dated 28 July, 2024.
- The stadium "will serve as the Saudi national team's main headquarters and host major sporting events and activities."
- "The design of King Salman Stadium and its sporting facilities has been approved, with completion scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2029."
- The chosen design came from proposals submitted by six specialized international companies and "draws inspiration from the mountainous landscape, integrating with King Abdulaziz Park through a valley that intersects the surrounding stadium garden and green spaces," meeting FIFA's requirements and sustainability and architectural standards.

## Location

- Situated in northern Riyadh along King Salman Road next to King Abdulaziz Park, near King Khalid International Airport, a Riyadh Metro station and major roadways.

## Size and facilities

- The site covers over 660,000 square meters, with commercial centres and recreational areas.
- Architectural design includes green walls and ceilings "spanning over 96,500 square meters."
- The main stadium will have a seating capacity of 92,000, with a 150-seat royal suite, 120 hospitality suites, 300 VIP seats and 2,200 dignitary seats.
- Sustainable cooling systems for audience seats and the stadium floor, extended indoor screens, indoor gardens, and "a walking track with a scenic view of King Abdulaziz Park atop the stadium."
- Surrounding sports facilities span over 360,000 square meters: two training fields, fan zones, a closed sports hall, an Olympic-sized swimming pool, an athletics track, and outdoor courts for volleyball, basketball and padel tennis, interconnected by a 9-kilometre-long sports track surrounding King Abdulaziz Park.

## Framing given

- The construction "reflects the support of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and HRH Prince Mohammed Bin Salman Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince and Prime Minister."
- The project is tied to Saudi Vision 2030's sports objectives and to boosting investment and the local economy.
- Page footer: "Last Modified: 06/08/2024 - 1:30 pm Saudi Time."

wikis.title: Work suspended on Riyadh's Mukaab megaproject
wikis.summary: Arab News, citing Reuters, reports that Saudi Arabia has suspended planned construction of the Mukaab cube-shaped skyscraper in Riyadh while it reassesses financing and feasibility.
wikis.body:
## Report

- Saudi Arabia "has suspended planned construction of a colossal cube-shaped skyscraper at the center of a downtown development in Riyadh while it reassesses the project's financing and feasibility, four people familiar with the matter said."
- Its future "is now unclear, with work beyond soil excavation and pilings suspended," three of the people said.
- Development of the surrounding real estate is set to continue, five people familiar with the plans said.
- Sources include people familiar with the project's development and people privy to internal deliberations at the PIF.
- Officials from PIF, the Saudi government and the New Murabba project did not respond to Reuters requests for comment.

## The Mukaab as planned

- A 400-meter by 400-meter metal cube containing a dome with an AI-powered display, "the largest on the planet," viewable from a more than 300-meter-tall ziggurat (terraced structure) inside it.

## New Murabba district figures

- Real estate consultancy Knight Frank estimated the district would cost about $50 billion — "roughly equivalent to Jordan's GDP" — with projects commissioned so far valued at around $100 million.
- Initial plans called for completion by 2030; it is now slated to be completed by 2040.
- The development was intended to house 104,000 residential units and add SR180 billion to the Kingdom's GDP, creating 334,000 direct and indirect jobs by 2030, the government had estimated previously.

wikis.title: King Salman Park, Riyadh: construction toward a 2026 first opening
wikis.summary: ArchDaily report on progress at King Salman Park in Riyadh, a 16.9 sq km park on the former airport site, with its design team, cost, transport links and phased opening dates.
wikis.body:
## Project

- King Salman Park is a 16.9-square-kilometre public landscape under construction in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on the grounds of the city's former airport.
- Omrania is lead design consultant, in collaboration with Henning Larsen for master planning and urban design.
- The project "combines ecological restoration, public programming, and mixed-use development" and is conceived as a new civic core for the capital.
- "Initial phases are expected to open in late 2026, with substantial completion targeted for 2027, following a phased construction schedule currently underway."

## Background and cost

- First announced in 2019 by King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud at the initiative of Mohammed bin Salman; overseen by the King Salman Park Foundation.
- Estimated cost: SR 72 billion.
- Part of Riyadh's broader urban transformation agenda.

## Site and transport

- Located near the geographic centre of Riyadh; planned as a transit-oriented destination connected to five metro stations and ten bus rapid transit stops.
- The master plan organises the park around a network of branching valleys inspired by regional wadi systems, converging toward a central open space, structuring circulation and distributing shaded pedestrian corridors, recreational spaces and gathering areas.
- Approximately one million trees are planned across the site, supported by treated wastewater irrigation and soil regeneration layers designed to improve water retention, responding to Riyadh's arid climate.

## Components

- The "Innovation Loop", a circular internal promenade, structures movement within the park; designed for walking, cycling, and electric or autonomous transit, it connects cultural venues, sports facilities and mixed-use zones.
- Planned components include the Royal Arts Complex by Bofill Taller de Arquitectura, with performance and exhibition spaces, a visitors pavilion, and residential and commercial districts framing the landscape.
- The article calls it "one of the largest urban park developments currently underway globally".

## Other Saudi developments mentioned

- The third edition of the Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale opened on January 30, 2026 at JAX District in Riyadh and remains on view through May 2, 2026.
- Riyadh is preparing to host Expo 2030 after its Registration Dossier received formal approval from the Bureau International des Expositions; the event is scheduled from October 1, 2030 to March 31, 2031 on a newly planned site, with a master plan by LAVA - Laboratory for Visionary Architecture.

wikis.title: Diriyah Arena Superblock construction contract awarded to China Harbour Engineering
wikis.summary: Diriyah Company press release announcing a SAR 5.75 billion ($1.53 billion) contract to China Harbour Engineering Company for the Arena Block in Diriyah, including the 20,000-seat Diriyah Arena, three office buildings and parking.
wikis.body:
## The contract

- Diriyah Company has awarded a contract worth SAR 5.75 billion ($1.53 billion) to Branch of China Harbour Engineering Company Ltd (CHEC) for the construction works of the Arena Block.
- The Arena Block is a district comprising the multi-purpose indoor Diriyah Arena, three mixed-use office buildings and a parking facility.
- The contract includes over 4,000 parking spaces supporting both Arena events and office facilities.
- In December 2024, China Harbour Engineering Company was awarded a SAR 758.5 million ($202.2 million) contract by Diriyah Company for bulk excavation works.

## Diriyah Arena

- Gross floor area of approximately 74,000 square metres.
- Seating capacity of 20,000 spectators.
- Designed as a flexible and scalable venue for concerts, sporting events, esports competitions, exhibitions and live shows.
- Designed by HKS Inc.; the design "draws inspiration from the natural geology surrounding Diriyah, while honoring traditional Najdi architectural elements".
- It will join other Diriyah assets including the Royal Diriyah Opera House, nine museums and academies, all featuring Najdi architectural elements inspired by the At-Turaif UNESCO World Heritage Site.

## Office plots

- Three mixed-use office plots designed by John McAslan + Partners, covering approximately 114,000 square metres, "supported by state-of-the-art technology and infrastructure".

## Quotes

- Jerry Inzerillo, Group CEO of Diriyah Company: the arena "will be a landmark entertainment complex in Diriyah that reinforces the City of Earth's growing global role in shaping Saudi Arabia's artistic and cultural future, in alignment with Vision 2030."
- Yang Zhiyuan, CEO of China Harbour Engineering Company Ltd. (Middle East): "This award marks a significant milestone for CHEC in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia."

## Diriyah project figures

- Backed by the Public Investment Fund (PIF), Diriyah spans 14 square kilometres.
- Planned to include homes for approximately 100,000 residents, generate over 178,000 jobs, host approximately 50 million annual visits, and contribute around SAR 70 billion ($18.6 billion) directly to Saudi Arabia's GDP.

wikis.title: Aqua Line (Mumbai Metro)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Mumbai Metro Line 3, the Aqua Line, the city's first fully underground metro, covering its 33.5 km route, phased openings to October 2025, funding, Aarey disputes, construction and operations.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- The Aqua Line (Line 3), also known as the Colaba-Bandra-SEEPZ line, is an operational rapid transit line of the Mumbai Metro running 33.5 km (20.82 mi) from Cuffe Parade in south Mumbai to Aarey JVLR in the north centre.
- It is Mumbai's first fully underground metro line: 27 stations, 26 underground and one at grade, with platform screen doors and CBTC signalling.
- Owned by Mumbai Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. (MMRC) and operated by the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, with Alstom Metropolis driverless rolling stock and a depot at Aarey JVLR.
- Total cost estimated at ₹30,000 crore (US$3.1 billion), with a JICA soft loan of ₹13,235 crore (US$1.4 billion); a funding table in the article totals ₹37,276 crore.
- Daily ridership 150,000 (October 2025), against initial projections of nearly 1.5 million passengers a day.

## Openings

- First phase (BKC to Aarey JVLR, 10 stations, ₹14,120 crore) inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 5 October 2024; the station table gives those stations as opening 7 October 2024.
- Phase 2A (BKC to Acharya Atre Chowk, five stations) inaugurated 9 May 2025 by CM Devendra Fadnavis (station table: 10 May 2025).
- The final 10.99 km stretch from Acharya Atre Chowk to Cuffe Parade was inaugurated by Modi on 8 October 2025 alongside the Navi Mumbai International Airport (station table: 9 October 2025).

## Building it

- Announced as a 20 km Colaba-Bandra line in 2004 and extended to the airport and SEEPZ; Union Cabinet clearance came on 27 June 2013, state cabinet approval on 26 February 2014, and construction began on 21 October 2016 after a foundation stone in August 2014.
- Seven civil packages worth about ₹2,221 crore each were awarded by August 2016 to consortia including L&T-STEC, HCC-Moscow Metrostroy, Doğuş-Soma, CEC-ITD Cementation-Tata Projects and J Kumar-China Railway Tunnel Group.
- Twin 5.85 m tunnels were bored at 20-25 m depth using 17 TBMs with 41 breakthroughs, including a 170 m tunnel under the Mithi River - India's second under-river metro tunnel after Kolkata's.
- Alstom won a EUR 315 million contract in September 2018 for 336 coaches (42 driverless eight-car sets), designed in Bengaluru and built at Sri City.

## Disputes

- The project affects 5,012 trees (1,331 cut, 3,681 replanted) and drew PILs and protests, especially over the Aarey car depot; courts, including the Bombay High Court and the Supreme Court, dismissed or vacated challenges, citing the metro's importance.
- Work at Aarey was stayed by CM Uddhav Thackeray in November 2019 and returned there in July 2022 under the Shinde-Fadnavis government; the delays and COVID-19 caused cost overruns and "delayed the opening of the line by at least 2 years".
- Construction incidents included a fatal tunnel shaft accident in September 2019 and buildings sinking in Mahim in November 2019; the Acharya Atre Chowk platform flooded on 26 May 2025.

## Operations

- No check-in luggage is allowed on board (MMRC: it is "not an 'Airport Express line'"), and bicycles are restricted; fares use an open-loop system accepting RuPay cards.
- Station co-branding rights for five years were licensed at ₹216 crore in September 2022 to Kotak Mahindra Bank, State Bank of India, LIC, ICICI Lombard, Nippon India Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, HDFC Life, Mahindra and AU Bank.

wikis.title: Aqua Line (Mumbai Metro): route, funding, construction and operations
wikis.summary: The main body of the Wikipedia article on Mumbai Metro's Aqua Line (Line 3), covering its specifications, phased openings, funding, planning, legal and environmental disputes, construction, stations, rolling stock and operations.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- The Aqua Line (Line 3), also the Colaba-Bandra-SEEPZ line, is a rapid transit metro line of the Mumbai Metro in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. Status: operational.
- The 33.5 km (20.82 mi) route is Mumbai Metro's first underground line, with 27 stations, 26 underground and one at-grade; it is the first fully underground metro line in Mumbai.
- It runs from Cuffe Parade in the far south to Aarey JVLR in the north centre, with connections to other metro lines, monorail, suburban rail, inter-city rail and Mumbai's international airport, and "is expected to reduce road congestion as well as the load on the Western Line between Bandra and Churchgate".
- Owner Mumbai Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. (MMRC); operator Delhi Metro Rail Corporation; depot Aarey JVLR; rolling stock Alstom Metropolis; track length 67.0 km; two tracks; 1,435 mm standard gauge; 25 kV 50 Hz AC overhead line; operating speed 35 km/h; CBTC signalling.
- Infobox: opened 5 October 2024; last extension 8 October 2025; daily ridership 150,000 (October 2025).
- Total cost estimated at ₹30,000 crore (US$3.1 billion); funded by MMRCL, Padeco, MMRDA and JICA, the last providing a soft loan of ₹13,235 crore (US$1.4 billion).
- The Bandra Kurla Complex-Dharavi section includes a 170-metre (560 ft) twin tunnel under the Mithi River, "the second under-river metro rail tunnel in India after the first tunnel underneath the Hooghly River on Kolkata Metro Green Line".
- Initial projections anticipated daily ridership of nearly 1.5 million passengers; "subsequent estimates indicate that actual usage has reached only about 150,000 passengers per day".

## Openings

- The first phase was inaugurated on 5 October 2024 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi: the ₹14,120 crore BKC to Aarey Jogeshwari-Vikhroli Link Road section with 10 stations (the station table gives these stations' opening as 7 October 2024).
- Phase 2A, BKC to Acharya Atre Chowk, adding five stations, was inaugurated on 9 May 2025 by CM Devendra Fadnavis and others (station table: 10 May 2025).
- The final 10.99 km stretch from Acharya Atre Chowk to Cuffe Parade was inaugurated by Modi, along with the Navi Mumbai International Airport, on 8 October 2025 (station table: 9 October 2025).

## Background and funding

- A 20 km Colaba-Bandra metro line was announced in January 2004 in an MMRDA master plan of 146 km of track, 32 km of it underground; the line was to run underground from Colaba to Mahalaxmi then elevated to Bandra, and MMRDA decided to extend it to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport to increase ridership.
- The 33.5 km Colaba-Bandra-SEEPZ line was estimated to cost ₹21,000 crore, have 27 stations and be the city's first fully underground line; MMRDA said an underground metro minimises land acquisition and traffic disturbance.
- MMRC was constituted as a fully owned company of MMRDA on 30 April 2008; the Central Government gave in-principle approval on 27 February 2012.
- MIAL agreed to bear the cost of three airport-area stations, expected to total ₹777 crore (estimated at ₹518 crore in 2014), raising it through a 'metro component' in the User Development Fee at Mumbai Airport from 2016 to February 2023 (Rs 20 domestic and Rs 120 international per departure).
- In August 2012 the Urban Development Ministry rejected a PPP mode, proposing a 20:80 Centre-State funding pattern with 45% of state equity via a JICA loan. From 2016 JICA provided a soft loan at 1.4% annual interest (elsewhere given as 1.44%), ₹13,235 crore for the ₹23,136 crore project, funding 57.2% of the equity.
- In March 2019 MMRC managing director Ashwini Bhide stated the actual completion cost was ₹30,000 crore.
- Funding table: central government equity ₹3,566 crore (9.57%), state equity ₹3,566 crore (9.57%), central sub-debt ₹1,571.50 crore (4.22%), state sub-debt ₹4,835.55 crore (12.97%), property development + impact fee ₹1,000 crore (2.68%), MIAL stakeholder contribution ₹777 crore (2.08%), ASIDE funding/MMRDA grant ₹679 crore (1.82%), JICA loan ₹21,280.45 crore (57.09%); total ₹37,276 crore (US$3.9 billion).

## Planning

- Union Cabinet clearance on 27 June 2013; MMRC converted into a state-central joint venture with five board members from each. State cabinet approval 26 February 2014. Implemented on an EPC model.
- Foundation stone laid by Chief Minister Prithviraj Chavan at Andheri on 26 August 2014 with Union Urban Development minister Venkaiah Naidu; media called it a cosmetic gesture as developers were not yet decided and construction was expected only by December 2014, days before the 2014 State Assembly election code of conduct. Some citizens protested slow implementation and cost escalation.
- December 2014: a consortium led by AECOM Asia with Padeco (Japan), LBG Inc. (USA) and Egis Rail (France) was appointed general consultant; the agreement was signed 26 May 2015. A new logo by Design Orb was unveiled on 6 July 2015.
- MMRC had to rehabilitate 2,807 families, mostly relocated to Kurla and Chakala, and provided free hotel accommodation to residents of dilapidated buildings along the corridor, mostly in the Girgaum-Kalbadevi belt.
- March 2022: Maharashtra announced a 2.5 km southbound extension from Cuffe Parade adding Navy Nagar station, costing an additional ₹2,301 crore; MMRCL invited DPR bids in August 2022.

## Bidding and contracts

- Pre-qualification bids called in September 2013; turnover requirement reduced on 31 January 2014 to an average annual construction turnover of not less than US$175 million; 14 pre-qualification bids received, nine shortlisted in September 2014.
- The tender was split into seven packages, each a 4-5 km twin tunnel, drawing 31 bids from nine consortiums. Contracts for all seven packages were awarded by August 2016, each about ₹2,221 crore and including around 6.8 km of twin tunnels and 5 stations.
- Package contractors: 1 Cuffe Parade-Hutatma Chowk, ₹2,988.53 crore, Larsen & Toubro and Shanghai Tunnel Engineering Co.; 2 CSMT Metro-Grant Road, ₹2,521.89 crore, Hindustan Construction Co and Moscow Metrostroy; 3 Mumbai Central-Worli, ₹2,557.84 crore, Doğuş and Soma; 4 Siddhivinayak-Sitaladevi, ₹2,830.10 crore, Continental Engineering Corp, ITD Cementation and Tata Projects; 5 Dharavi-Santacruz, ₹2,817.02 crore, J Kumar Infraprojects and China Railway Tunnel Group; 6 CSIA-CSA International, ₹2,118.40 crore; 7 Marol Naka-SEEPZ, ₹2,281.45 crore, Larsen & Toubro and Shanghai Tunnel Engineering Co.; Aarey Depot at grade, ₹328 crore, Sam (India) Builtwell Pvt. Ltd. (contract awarded June 2017, including 2.5 km of storm water drains, rainwater harvesting and diversion of a 1,200 mm MCGM water pipeline).

## Environment, safety and legal issues

- The project affects 5,012 trees, of which 1,331 will be cut and 3,681 re-planted; contracts require consortia to plant three times the trees cut and maintain them at least three years. The Tata Projects/ITD Cementation/CEC Taiwan consortium pledged 2,000 trees instead of the required 450 for package 4's 150 felled trees. MMRC donated 25,000 saplings (announced 28 February 2017) and 16,000 saplings at 25 locations on 11 April 2017, and hired Singapore arborist Simon Leong as tree consultant for six months at $33,000 per month.
- MMRC Director Ashwini Bhide said the 5,000 trees to be cut would reduce carbon dioxide by 6,100 kg while reduced vehicle usage would cut emissions by an estimated 9.9 million kg, and that Kalina and Kanjurmarg depot sites were rejected for lack of land and potential legal disputes.
- A state technical expert committee reported in May 2015 that concretising Aarey would send excess rainwater into the Mithi and flood the airport and Chakala area, as Aarey is a Mithi catchment; the note was by Dr Rakesh Kumar (NEERI) and Dr Shyam Asolekar (IIT-Bombay). On 26 May 2025, days after the line's opening, the Acharya Atre Chowk station platform flooded in heavy rains.
- Safety: September 2019, one man died and one was injured in a tunnel shaft accident between SEEPZ station and the ramp near Aarey Forest. November 2019, the building Laxmi Niwas near Sitladevi station sank at least 6 mm, with 25 families evacuated; within a week Meher Manzil on LJ Road in Mahim also sank. In December 2019 the 120-year-old grade-I heritage Western Railway headquarters was reported under threat from underground blasts at the Oval Maidan site.
- Tree litigation: the Bombay High Court issued an interim order on 9 February 2017 prohibiting tree cutting, hearing PILs by Mina Verma and Pravin Jehangir; on 3 May 2017 it called the metro crucial while reserving its stay, weighing "what is more important - life of a human being or the life of tree"; on 5 May it vacated the stay, saying a balance had to be found and a "harsh stand, which the petitioners want" would make development "impossible". The petitioners' SLP led the Supreme Court to stay tree felling from 15 May 2017 until 18 May.
- Aarey land: the depot was planned on an 81-acre plot in Aarey Colony, requiring felling of more than 2,000 trees; Vanashakti and the Aarey Conservation Group petitioned the NGT in January 2015. The Union Environment Ministry's 5 December 2016 eco-sensitive zone notification excluded 165 hectares in Aarey for the line. The NGT stayed construction in Aarey on 19 December 2016, allowed a casting yard on 5 January 2017, and extended the stay to 17 March 2017. On 29 March 2017 the state forest department said 1,279.74 ha at Aarey had been used for non-forest activities since 1949.
- Larsen & Toubro and Shanghai Tunnel Engineering Co. exited the package 7 MIDC-Aarey Depot contract over the Aarey land issues; MMRC said a new contractor would raise costs by ₹10 crore. A redesigned depot on 25 hectares instead of 33 would cut 1,000 fewer trees. In March 2017 E. Sreedharan wrote to CM Fadnavis supporting the Aarey carshed.
- The Supreme Court rejected the Aarey Conservation Group's plea for an alternative depot site on 16 April 2019; the Bombay High Court dismissed stay petitions on 4 October 2019; the Supreme Court stayed tree cutting on 7 October 2019. On 29 November 2019 CM Uddhav Thackeray stayed carshed work and on 11 December 2019 appointed a committee, which on 29 January 2020 found no viable alternative. In July 2022 the Shinde-Fadnavis government shifted the carshed back to Aarey (25% work done, Kanjurmarg too far and disputed) and retracted the stay on 21 July; the delay and COVID-19 "resulted in high cost overruns in thousands of crores in rupees and also delayed the opening of the line by at least 2 years".

## Construction

- Subcontractors, mostly joint ventures in tunnelling, include L&T-STEC, CEC-ITD CEM-TPL, Dogus-Soma, HCC-MMS and J.Kumar-CRTG; more than 100 subcontractors and third parties were used.
- Two 5.85 m diameter twin tunnels of 33.5 km each were dug at 20-25 metres depth; 17 tunnel boring machines, each about 1,400 tonnes and costing ₹120 crore, recorded 41 breakthroughs. Around 40,000 concrete rings were cast in 65 moulds at six casting yards (four in Wadala, one at Darga, one on the JVLR); the first ring was fabricated on 7 March 2017.
- Hutatma Chowk, Kalbadevi, Girgaum, Grant Road, Shitladevi, Santacruz and Marol Naka stations were built by the New Austrian Tunnelling Method; the other 20 by cut-and-cover.
- The Mithi river crossing tunnel is 170 m long at 15-20 m below the river bed, with a stabling line 12-13 m below the river bed extending to BKC station.
- Construction began 21 October 2016, with full-scale activity from 18 May 2017 after legal delays; officials had warned costs would escalate at ₹4 crore per day.
- At Chira Bazar the alignment runs parallel to a Parsi fire temple whose trust forbids non-Parsi entry, so MMRC agreed to hire a Parsi engineer for the building condition survey, a task made difficult by only about 57,000 Parsis residing in Mumbai.
- An estimated 6 million cubic metres of rubble was to be excavated; plans to use it for the Shiv Smarak monument and the coastal road were made unlikely by monument delays.
- Tunnelling progress: 5,100 m by 10 July 2018; about 10 km by September 2018; 20 km by February 2019; 23.9 km of 52 km (about 45%) by end March 2019; 91% by 17 December 2020. The 27th of 41 breakthroughs came on 19 March 2020 (first underwater tunnel across the Mithi); tunnelling across the Mithi between Dharavi and BKC was completed on 19 August 2020 as the 29th breakthrough.
- On 16 August 2019 CM Fadnavis revealed the rolling stock model and announced the Aqua Line name, for the trains' aqua colour scheme. The first trial run was flagged off by CM Eknath Shinde and Deputy CM Devendra Fadnavis on the 3 km Sariput Nagar-Marol Naka stretch on 30 August 2022.

## Stations

- 27 stations, only the northern terminus Aarey Depot at grade; all stations have platform screen doors. Under the original plan there was no direct airport connectivity; CM Fadnavis directed MMRC to redesign stations for direct access to the airport and Mumbai Central railway station.
- Interchanges with railway lines at Churchgate, Grant Road, Mumbai Central, Mahalaxmi (Western line and Mumbai Monorail), Mumbai CSMT (Central, Harbour and Main line CR), Marol Naka (Metro Line 1), Santacruz (via skywalk) and Bandra Kurla Complex (Metro Line 2 and the upcoming BKC terminal of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor).
- Station list with opening dates: Aarey JVLR (at-grade), SEEPZ, MIDC-Andheri, Marol Naka, CSMIA T2, Sahar Road, CSMIA T1, Santacruz, Bandra Colony, Bandra Kurla Complex - all 7 October 2024; Dharavi, Shitaladevi Mandir, Dadar, Siddhivinayak, Worli, Acharya Atre Chowk - 10 May 2025; Science Centre, Mahalaxmi, Jagannath Shankar Sheth, Grant Road, Girgaon, Kalbadevi, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Hutatma Chowk, Churchgate, Vidhan Bhavan, Cuffe Parade - 9 October 2025.

## Rolling stock, signalling and power

- The car shed is opposite SEEPZ on a 33 hectare (81-acre) plot in Aarey Colony. Tenders for traction, power supply, tunnel ventilation, signalling, train control, platform screen doors and telecommunications were floated in March 2017; ballastless track tenders in May 2017.
- Rolling stock procurement was delayed by a Centre-JICA disagreement over a 75% Make in India requirement; JICA eventually accepted it, so the winner could manufacture at most 25% of cars outside India. Bidding restarted in May 2017 for 31 eight-car train sets, each coach 22.6 m long and 3.2 m wide, with pre-qualification bids from seven firms including Alstom, CAF, CRRC, Hitachi, Kawasaki with BHEL, and Mitsubishi.
- In September 2018 MMRC awarded Alstom and its Indian subsidiary a EUR 315 million contract for 336 coaches: design, manufacture, supply, installation, testing and commissioning of 42 driverless eight-car train sets, carrying capacity 3,000 passengers with around 300 seats per coach in longitudinal arrangement; designed at Alstom's Bengaluru engineering centre and manufactured at Sri City, Andhra Pradesh.
- The line is driverless at automation grade 4, but will employ drivers during its first year; trains use a time-interval system and are connected to the operation control centre. Signalling is Alstom Urbalis 400 CBTC, with no lineside signals.
- MMRDA joint project director Dilip Kawathkar said AC power was chosen after expert study; experts believe the AC decision raised project cost by 15%.

## Operations and revenue

- Passengers may not carry check-in luggage on board - only hand/cabin baggage; MMRC officials said Metro 3 is "not an 'Airport Express line'" and luggage check-in would increase dwell time and headway.
- Bicycles are restricted, mostly for lack of space at peak hours, though MMRCL announced plans to allow them once the whole route is operational.
- Open loop automated fare collection with contactless pre-paid and post-paid smart cards from partnering banks; only RuPay debit and credit cards accepted. In March 2020 MMRC objected to Tata Power's revised electricity tariffs, warning of higher fares.
- On 22 September 2022 MMRCL licensed co-branding/semi-naming rights for stations at ₹216 crore for five years: Kotak Mahindra Bank (BKC and CSMT Metro), State Bank of India (CSMIA Terminal 2, Dadar Metro and Vidhan Bhavan), Life Insurance Corporation (Churchgate Metro and Hutatma Chowk), ICICI Lombard (Siddhivinayak), Nippon India Mutual Fund (Acharya Atre Chowk), ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund (Santacruz Metro), HDFC Life (Mahalaxmi Metro), Mahindra (Worli) and AU Bank (Bandra Colony); rights include in-station branding, train announcements, station maps and a brand prefix to the station name.
- Times Innovative Media OOH Pvt. Ltd secured advertising rights for all 27 stations and 31 trains. On 17 January 2025 MMRCL leased over 1.3 lakh sq ft of commercial space across 27 stations to Tata Trent, Chitale Bandhu, Delicia Foods and others, aiming for ₹20 crore of revenue.

wikis.title: Haneda Airport Access Line
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on JR East's Haneda Airport Access Line, a commuter rail line under construction linking Haneda Airport to central Tokyo, with its three routes, cost and planned fiscal 2031 opening.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- The Haneda Airport Access Line (羽田空港アクセス線) is a commuter rail line under construction by the East Japan Railway Company (JR East) that will link Haneda Airport to central Tokyo.
- Status: under construction; locale Tokyo; heavy rail; two tracks; 1,067 mm (3 ft 6 in) gauge; overhead line, 1,500 V DC.
- Termini: Tokyo Station (tentative) and Haneda Airport New Station.
- Planned opening: JFY 2031 (tentative).
- Construction began on 2 June 2023.
- As of July 2024, JR East plans to open the line in fiscal year 2031 with direct through services to Tokyo Station and Shin-Kiba Station; a third through service to Osaki and Shinjuku is also planned.
- Construction is estimated to cost about ¥280 billion (2022) (equivalent to ¥297.14 billion or US$1.96 billion in 2024).

## History

- 2013: JR East announced in "JR East Group Management Vision V" that it aimed to improve accessibility to Haneda, due to growing demand from air travelers, especially international travelers.
- 2014: JR East released its fundamental construction plan, proposing that a disused freight line southeast of Tamachi Station be connected via a single-track tunnel to the Tokaido Line; the new section would be about 5 km (3.1 mi), running from the existing Tokyo Freight Terminal to a new Haneda Airport New Station (羽田空港新駅) between Terminal 1 and Terminal 2 via a new underwater tunnel.
- JR East initially aimed to open a portion in time for the 2020 Summer Olympics but could not, due to environmental assessment needs.
- 2018: the "Move Up" management vision proposed three conventional lines from the airport: the East Yamanote route, the West Yamanote route and the Coastal Area route.
- 2019: JR East officially launched the environmental assessment.
- 2021: JR East announced Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism approval for construction of the East Yamanote route, intending to start construction in 2022 for completion by 2029.
- 2 June 2023: construction officially began with a groundbreaking ceremony.
- April 2024: plans were altered to preserve a portion of the Meiji-era Takanawa Embankment discovered in 2023; the starting point of the new line would be moved 100 meters to the south (toward Shinagawa).

## Routes

- Three routes from Tokyo Freight Terminal onwards to various points in central Tokyo are under construction. (The article carries a clarification tag from April 2025 asking which routes were selected and are now under construction.)
- East Yamanote route (東山手ルート): from the new airport station between Terminals 1 and 2 to a point near Tamachi Station, using an unused freight line between Tamachi and Tokyo Freight Terminal to connect to the Tokaido Main Line (Ueno-Tokyo Line), giving through service to Tokyo Station, Ueno Station and northbound lines including the Takasaki, Utsunomiya and Joban lines. Tokyo Station to Haneda estimated to fall from 28 minutes to 18 minutes.
- Coastal Area Route (臨海部ルート): connects Tokyo Freight Terminal to the Rinkai Line for Odaiba (Tokyo Teleport Station) and the Tokyo waterfront, allowing future through service to the Keiyo Line for Maihama (Tokyo Disney Resort) and points east in Chiba Prefecture. Haneda to Shin-Kiba would fall from 41 minutes to 20 minutes.
