- During the inauguration of Kartavya Bhavan-3 the government announced a new 7-kilometre extension of the Delhi Metro's Magenta Line from Indraprastha metro station to Ramakrishna Ashram Marg, with nine new stations at Bharat Mandapam, Baroda House, India Gate, Kartavya Bhavan, Central Secretariat, Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum and Shivaji Stadium.

wikis.title: Kartavya Bhavan 1
wikis.summary: The CCS building on the north side of Kartavya Path housing the Ministry of Finance.
wikis.body:
- Located on the north side of Kartavya Path, adjacent to Man Singh Road on its east side and Dr. Rajendra Prasad Road on its north side.
- Inaugurated on 13 February 2026 together with Kartavya Bhavan 2 and Seva Teerth.
- Houses the Ministry of Finance: Department of Expenditure (6th floor), Department of Economic Affairs (5th and 6th floors), Department of Revenue (4th floor).

wikis.title: Kartavya Bhavan 2
wikis.summary: The CCS building between buildings 1 and 3, housing the CBI and several ministries.
wikis.body:
- Located between buildings 1 and 3, connected only by Dr. Rajendra Prasad Road to its north.
- Inaugurated on 13 February 2026.
- Houses: Central Bureau of Investigation (ground-1st floor), Ministry of Education (ground-2nd floor), Chemicals and Fertilizers (2nd floor), Culture (2nd floor), Information and Broadcasting (2nd-3rd floor), Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare (3rd floor), Law and Justice (3rd-4th floor), Defence (5th-6th floor).

wikis.title: Kartavya Bhavan 3
wikis.summary: The first of the ten CCS buildings, inaugurated in August 2025 and housing Home Affairs and other ministries.
wikis.body:
- Located adjacent to Janpath Road on its west side and Dr. Rajendra Prasad Road to the north.
- The first of the ten buildings; the article gives its inauguration as 6 August 2025 in one section and 5 August 2025 in another. Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended the inauguration.
- Houses: Petroleum and Natural Gas (ground-1st floor), Personnel & Training (UG-1st floor), Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (2nd floor), Rural Development (2nd floor), Principal Scientific Adviser (3rd floor), External Affairs (3rd floor), Home Affairs (4th-6th floor).

wikis.title: New Sydney Fish Market grand opening
wikis.summary: Infrastructure NSW announcement that the new Sydney Fish Market at Blackwattle Bay opened on Monday 19 January 2026, with its designers, size, tenants and visitor projections.
wikis.body:
## Opening

- "The highly anticipated new Sydney Fish Market officially opened its doors today, Monday 19 January 2026", marking a major milestone in the NSW Government's urban renewal of Blackwattle Bay.
- Designed by Danish architects 3XN/GXN in collaboration with BVN and Aspect Studios, and built by Multiplex.
- Described as the first significant step in transforming the precinct into a public destination.

## The building

- Standing on the harbour's edge, the market "has already been recognised as Sydney's third major landmark, joining the Sydney Opera House and the Harbour Bridge".
- The redevelopment shifts the area from a working waterfront into a public space with fresh seafood and waterside dining, cafes, bars and specialty stores.

## Size and tenants

- More than 6,000sqm of public open space.
- Double the retail space of the former Pyrmont site, with over 40 food and retail operators, from casual fish and chips to premium dining.

## Precinct effects

- Relocating the market to the head of Blackwattle Bay will allow development of a waterfront promenade connecting the continuous 15km Sydney foreshore walk from Rozelle Bay to Woolloomooloo.
- The new market is expected to attract more than 6 million local and international visitors each year.

wikis.title: Atlassian Central tops out at 39 storeys in Sydney
wikis.summary: ABC News report on the topping-out ceremony for Atlassian Central, the $1.4 billion hybrid timber tower beside Sydney's Central Station, which has reached its full 180-metre height.
wikis.body:
## The milestone

- A "topping out ceremony" was held at the Atlassian Central skyscraper in Sydney's CBD on Wednesday, on the building's 39th storey, marking construction reaching full height.
- The building is described as the world's tallest hybrid timber structure at 180 metres.
- Construction began at the site beside Central Station in 2022 and was estimated to cost $1.4 billion.
- The tower is expected to be completed in 2027.
- The hybrid timber design "also reduced the use of carbon-intensive concrete and steel"; the building has a six-star Green Star target.

## Atlassian on AI and office space

- The ceremony followed the software company cutting nearly 500 jobs from its Australian workforce in March to invest in artificial intelligence and enterprise sales.
- Co-CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes said that move had not reduced the requirement for floor space: "I don't think [AI] stops the need for people coming together to work... We're going to have even more, I suspect, collaboration spaces, meeting spaces."
- Cannon-Brookes said that by the time it opens, "we'll have advanced structural engineering, environmental design, intelligent controls, and a modern data platform, all wired together and working the building with one smart, intelligent system", producing "the most technologically advanced building in Australia".

## Ownership and precinct

- The building is co-owned by Atlassian and commercial real estate firm Dexus, with Atlassian set to occupy about half of the site.
- The lower five floors will house a 500-bed "co-living" hostel operated by YHA Australia.
- It is part of a broader push by the state government and the City of Sydney to set up a "Tech Central" precinct in the Haymarket-Redfern area.
- NSW Treasurer Daniel Mookhey called it an "engineering marvel": "All of Sydney is bearing witness to the rise and rise of an engineering marvel."

wikis.title: Powerhouse Parramatta opening date confirmed
wikis.summary: NSW Government ministerial media release confirming Powerhouse Parramatta will open to the public on Saturday 7 November 2026 and announcing The Mall as its second major opening exhibition.
wikis.body:
## Opening

- Powerhouse Parramatta, described as Western Sydney's first state cultural institution, "will swing open its doors to the public on Saturday 7 November 2026".
- The museum is located on the banks of the Parramatta River. The release calls it "a major new landmark for Australia and a global cultural destination for Western Sydney".
- Its opening "marks the most significant cultural infrastructure project since the Sydney Opera House".

## Cost

- "The Powerhouse Parramatta is $915 million project, including $75 million philanthropic contribution, and the delivery of the new Castle Hill collection storage facility."

## Exhibitions at opening

- Most exhibitions will be free.
- The first five exhibitions "will showcase more than 3000 objects, with more than 1600 from the Powerhouse's own collection, with others sourced from collections around the world".
- The first exhibition, *Task Eternal*, will include the historic Qantas Avro 504k aircraft and explore the intersection of design, innovation and technology.
- *The Mall* "has today been announced as the next opening exhibition", one of five exhibitions premiering at the opening.

## Quotes

- Deputy Premier and Minister for Western Sydney Prue Car: Powerhouse Parramatta "will give our region's young people more and better access to our engineering and innovation history".
- Minister for the Arts John Graham: "When it opens this November, Powerhouse Parramatta will transform Parramatta, linking the centre with the riverfront." Entry to the Museum and most exhibitions will be free.
- Minister for Lands and Property Steve Kamper says the Minns Labor Government "is delivering a world-class cultural institution in the heart of Western Sydney".
- Parliamentary Secretary for the Arts and Member for Granville Julia Finn and Member for Parramatta Donna Davis also comment.
- Powerhouse CEO Lisa Havilah: "We are thrilled to be opening our doors this November with five world-class exhibitions and a program that is as bold and diverse as the communities it serves."

## Related item on the page

- A linked ministerial statement, "Powerhouse Museum leadership update", says Powerhouse Parramatta "is on track for opening on 7 November 2026".

wikis.title: The Mall exhibition
wikis.summary: The second major opening exhibition at Powerhouse Parramatta, examining the history and cultural significance of the shopping mall.
wikis.body:
- *The Mall* "examines the history, evolution and cultural significance of the shopping mall, one of the most influential and ubiquitous forms of architecture in modern life".
- Western Sydney "played a foundational role in the development of global urban shopping centres with Blacktown the location of the very first large-scale, transport-integrated Westfield shopping centre, opened in 1959". From Blacktown and later Parramatta, Westfield exported the urban shopping mall concept to Australia, the United States, United Kingdom, New Zealand and Italy.
- Unfolding across two storeys, it presents "over 560 objects from the Powerhouse Collection, presented alongside more than 280 loans, ephemera and personal stories collected from the local community".

Highlights listed:

- The archive of Austrian-American architect and urban planner Victor Gruen, "presented for the first time".
- Rare archives from Australian brands including Le Specs, Hot Tuna, Mambo, Globe, Crumpler, Above the Clouds and Song for the Mute.
- A reimagining of a 19th-century arcade with window displays developed with Breville, David Jones, Oroton, R.M. Williams and Sportsgirl.
- The signature Levi's 501 jeans worn by Apple co-founder Steve Jobs, and the Predator Boot prototypes conceived by former Liverpool player Craig Johnston and worn by David Beckham.
- An Australian premiere of an animated film by South Korean artist Ayoung Kim, co-commissioned with M+ in Hong Kong.
- The Raindrop Fountain from Roselands in South West Sydney, reimagined and created by industrial design studio Vert.
- Japanese artist yang02's "autonomous ballet of warehouse robots", developed with KNAPP.

wikis.title: São Paulo monorail Line 17 and Guarulhos Aeromovel peoplemover open
wikis.summary: Railway Gazette report on the opening of a limited service on São Paulo's monorail Line 17-Gold to Congonhas Airport and the start of services on the Aeromovel peoplemover at Guarulhos Airport.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- "Monorail Line 17 has opened offering a limited service in São Paulo, providing rail access to Congonhas Airport, and services have also started on Aeromovel peoplemover linking Guarulhos Airport railway station and the terminal buildings."
- Article by Benjámin Zelki, Railway Gazette International, April 24 2026.

## Line 17-Gold

- The initial 6.7 km section was inaugurated on March 31, "no less than 12 years behind its original planned opening date". It links Congonhas Airport with Morumbi on suburban rail Line 9 and serves seven stations.
- Preparatory works began in April 2012; it was initially intended to open in time for the 2014 FIFA World Cup.
- Total cost of the first section: R$5.97bn. Operated by concessionaire ViaMobilidade.

## Guarulhos peoplemover

- Limited revenue services have started on the 2.7 km line linking Guarulhos Airport terminals 1, 2 and 3 with the airport station on suburban rail Line 13.

wikis.title: Monorail Line 17-Gold opening and extensions
wikis.summary: The 6.7 km first section of São Paulo's Line 17-Gold monorail opened on March 31, 12 years late, with limited hours, further stations and planned extensions.
wikis.body:
## Service

- Initial 6.7 km section inaugurated March 31, linking Congonhas Airport with Morumbi on suburban rail Line 9, serving seven stations.
- An eighth station, Washington Luís, is under construction on a branch south of Brooklin Paulista, "expected to open in June".
- Initially operates between 10.00 and 15.00, with headways between 7 and 14 min. "Full service is expected to start in October 2026."
- Operated by concessionaire ViaMobilidade; total cost of the first section R$5.97bn.

## Delays

- Preparatory works began in April 2012, intended to open in time for the 2014 FIFA World Cup, but "the project has faced persistent problems with both procurement and construction".
- São Paulo State Governor Tarcísio de Freitas at the opening ceremony: "Today we are not inaugurating the line, we are ending a cycle of delays... For years, we lived with a structure that consumed resources and remained idle."

## Extensions

- Freitas said extensions would be built at both ends totalling 4.6 km, but did not specify timescales: a one-station southern extension from Washington Luís to Vila Paulista, and three more stations at the northern end from Morumbi to Américo Mourano.
- In the longer term Line 17 is planned to cover a 17.7 km corridor linking Jabaquara on metro Line 1 to São Paulo-Morumbi on metro Line 4.

## Contracts and rolling stock

- The original turnkey contract was awarded in 2011 to the Monotrilho Integração consortium (Andrade Gutierrez, CR Almeida, Montagens e Projetos Especiais, Scomi Engineering). After delays, disputes and contract terminations, parts were re-tendered; in 2020 the remaining civil works went out in several packages, the largest ending with Coesa Engenharia and Constran.
- Initial rolling stock supplier Scomi Engineering had its contract terminated in 2019 after a winding-up order from the Malaysian high court. China's BYD was then selected to deliver 14 five-car trainsets from its SkyRail platform, plus CBTC supporting GoA4 automation, control systems and platform screen doors.
- The vehicles have onboard batteries allowing up to 8 km of independent travel in a power failure.
- Thales Group supplied telecommunications, passenger information systems and CCTV.
- Eight trainsets had been commissioned by late March and a further three delivered to the Água Espraiada depot. Operations are currently supervised by onboard staff, "standard procedure for new automated urban rail lines in São Paulo".

wikis.title: Guarulhos Airport Aeromovel peoplemover
wikis.summary: A 2.7 km automated peoplemover using Aeromovel pressurised air propulsion has begun limited revenue service between Guarulhos Airport terminals and the Line 13 station.
wikis.body:
- The 2.7 km line links São Paulo's Guarulhos Airport terminals 1, 2 and 3 with the airport station on suburban rail Line 13.
- Services started with one vehicle at the end of February; the second vehicle entered service on April 7.
- Uses Aeromovel pressurised air propulsion, "the third commercial use of the technology after Porto Alegre and Jakarta".
- Marcopolo Rail supplied three two-car vehicles.
- Designed, built and operated by the AeroGRU consortium: Aerom, TS Infraestrutura, FBS and Germany's HTB Group.
- The line operates from 16.00 to 00.00; AeroGRU "expects the start of full revenue service with the last vehicle entering service later this year".

wikis.title: First section of São Paulo metro Line 6 opens
wikis.summary: Railway Gazette report on the opening of the first 5.2 km trial section of São Paulo metro Line 6 (Orange) on July 2, with details of the concession, the line's planned full extent and its Alstom trainsets.
wikis.body:
## Opening

- "The first 5·2 km section of São Paulo's metro network's Line 6 (Orange) opened on July 2, with a limited trial service running between João Paulo I and Perdizes."
- Água Branca "is now the deepest metro station in South America at 47·8 m, overtaking Santa Cruz on Line 5 at 41·5 m".
- Services initially operate between 10.00 and 15.00 from Monday to Friday, "with travel being free of charge".
- Francisco Pierrini, CEO of the Concessionária Linha Universidade consortium: "It is with great pride that we celebrate the early delivery of six stations on Line 6... Line 6 will transform people's lives."

## The full line

- Extensions at each end "will eventually take the line to 15.3 km, connecting Brasilândia in the north with São Joaquim in the city centre".
- The 15 stations will serve destinations including schools and seven higher education institutions, "leading to the alternative name 'the University Line'".
- A journey that currently takes up to 90 min by bus will be reduced to 23 min; the line is predicted to carry 633 000 passengers/day when complete.

## Concession history

- A concession to build, operate and maintain Line 6 was originally awarded to the Move São Paulo consortium by the São Paulo state government in mid-2013.
- Construction began in January 2015 but "came to a standstill in 2016 when the concessionaire ran into financial difficulties"; the contract was terminated in December 2018.
- Work was restarted by Linha Universidade. Civil works are by Acciona, the concessionaire's majority shareholder; Alstom supplies the rolling stock.
- Acciona "has supported more than 60 000 people through social programmes focused on education, employability, gender equality and human rights".
- José Manuel Entrecanales, President & CEO of Acciona: "The launch of Line 6 marks the fulfilment of the commitment Acciona made to São Paulo in 2019 and represents a transformative legacy for the city."

## Rolling stock

- Alstom "has so far delivered 12 of the 22 six-car Metropolis trainsets that it is building for Line 6 at its Taubaté plant".
- The 80 km/h stainless steel trainsets are designed to be light, energy-efficient and durable "with a life of more than 40 years", with a capacity of 2 044 passengers. The interior was designed with simulations in Alstom's Lab 4.0 virtual reality laboratory; features include passenger counting systems, dynamic line maps, information screens and CCTV.
- The CBTC "will support GoA4 unattended driverless operation in the future".
- Suely Sola, General Director of Alstom Brazil: Line 6 "also strengthens the national rail industry by boosting local production and a broad supply chain".

wikis.title: Aena's expansion and modernisation of Congonhas Airport, São Paulo
wikis.summary: Aena press release presenting its project to expand and modernise São Paulo's Congonhas Airport, with over BRL 2 billion of investment, a doubled terminal and capacity for 29.5 million passengers a year.
wikis.body:
## The project

- Aena, "which operates 20% of Brazil's air traffic", publicly presented on Monday the project to expand and modernise Congonhas Airport (São Paulo), "the second busiest airport in the country".
- The Spanish airport operator "will invest over BRL 2 billion in this infrastructure over the next few years", including a new passenger terminal that will double the size of the current one.
- The expansion "will increase the airport's capacity to 29.5 million passengers per year".
- Aena's total investment in the Block of Eleven Brazilian Airports (BOAB), which includes Congonhas, "will amount to BRL 4.5 billion".

## Schedule

- "Work on the new São Paulo terminal will begin in 2024 and is scheduled for completion in June 2028."

## What is being built

- The boarding and arrivals area "will double in size to 105,000 square metres".
- The departures terminal will have a new check-in hall and 19 new boarding bridges replacing the current 12, "allowing 70% of boardings to be direct to the aircraft".
- Around 20,000 m² for commercial premises and other services, plus new VIP lounges, offices and business lounges.
- A new 215,000 square metre apron for commercial aviation; aircraft parking areas increase from 30 to 37.
- Existing runways and aprons receive "structural reinforcement"; new aircraft taxiways, a new general aviation service road and a fast runway exit will be built.
- The project "includes the preservation, revitalisation and integration of the areas listed as Historical Heritage".

## Sustainability

- A new electrical substation "which will allow the use of clean energy", a new solid waste collection point and a water treatment station, plus more natural lighting and a more efficient air-conditioning system.

## Quote

- Chairman of Aena, Maurici Lucena, called it "Aena's most important in the international area and whose scope and great technical complexity mean that it is only within the reach of a few airport companies in the world, such as Aena, which has already evidenced in Brazil that it is capable of successfully completing large-scale projects".
- Under the Aena Brazil brand, which manages 17 airports in the country, the operator "successfully completed last year the renovation works in airports of the North-East, with Recife airport at the forefront".

wikis.title: Cora Coralina TBM completes first phase of São Paulo Metro Line 2 tunnelling
wikis.summary: RailwayPro report that Latin America's largest tunnel boring machine finished the first tunnelling phase of the São Paulo Metro Line 2-Green extension on 30 May, with details of the machine, the works completed and the extension's stages.
wikis.body:
## The milestone

- "The largest tunnel boring machine (TBM) in Latin America, known as Cora Coralina, has completed the first phase of tunnelling works on the São Paulo Metro Line 2 Green expansion."
- On Friday, 30 May, the TBM reached the Falchi Gianini ventilation shaft, "its final destination before Vila Prudente station".
- This completes 4.5 km of alignment and 3.7 km of tunnels, connecting five construction shafts and four future stations: Orfanato, Santa Clara, Anália Franco and Vila Formosa, plus the Rapadura Complex.
- From Orfanato station alone the TBM advanced 332 metres, removed 35,000 cubic metres of soil and installed 291 concrete rings.
- Since excavation began at the Rapadura Complex in November 2023, the machine has removed 394,000 cubic metres of soil and placed 2,456 precast rings.

## Next phase

- Cora Coralina "will now be dismantled and transported to the Penha station site, where it will begin tunnelling the second phase in reverse—heading back toward Rapadura".
- Disassembly "will take up to 180 days". Components will be lifted from the Falchi Gianini shaft and moved by truck to the Penha site.

## The machine

- 100 metres long, 2,500 tonnes, with an 11.66-metre-diameter cutterhead, "making it the largest of its kind currently operating in Latin America".
- Can excavate and line up to 15 metres of tunnel per day, supported by conveyor belts, ventilation, a hyperbaric chamber and lining installation equipment.
- Roughly 150 professionals — engineers, technicians, mechanics and electricians — work in three shifts for continuous tunnelling.

## The Line 2-Green extension

- Divided into two stages: the first, Vila Prudente to Vila Formosa, includes four new stations and "is set to open in 2027"; the second, Vila Formosa to Penha, adds four more stations — Santa Isabel, Guilherme Giorgi, Aricanduva and Penha — "with service expected to begin in 2028".
- Funded with BRL 15 billion (USD 2.6 billion) from the Government of São Paulo, the extension "will add 8.3 km of track and eight new stations between Vila Prudente and Penha, interconnecting with Lines 3-Red, 11-Coral, and the future Line 16-Violet".
- Once completed it is expected to benefit an estimated 1.2 million passengers daily in São Paulo's eastern region.

wikis.title: Eglinton Crosstown west extension
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 9.2 km westward extension of Toronto's Line 5 Eglinton from Mount Dennis to Renforth station in Mississauga, covering its planning history, construction contracts, stations and a proposed further extension to Pearson Airport.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- The Eglinton Crosstown west extension "will extend the Toronto subway's Line 5 Eglinton west of Mount Dennis station to Renforth station in the adjacent City of Mississauga in Peel Region".
- 9.2-kilometre (6-mile) extension adding seven new stations – four underground, two elevated and one within an open trench. "The extension is expected to open in 2031."
- Infobox: status "Under construction"; owner Metrolinx; locale Toronto and Mississauga, Ontario; 7 stations; type rapid transit; system Toronto subway; operator Toronto Transit Commission; planned opening 2031; line length 9.2 km (6 mi); standard gauge 1,435 mm.

## Route

- Continues west along Eglinton Avenue from Mount Dennis station at Weston Road. After a short tunnel, a 1.5 km (0.93 mi) elevated structure carries the line over the Humber River, with elevated stations at Jane Street and Scarlett Road.
- The line then enters a 6.3 km (3.9 mi) tunnel with four underground through-stations at Royal York Road, Islington Avenue, Kipling Avenue and Martin Grove Road.
- It terminates at Renforth, a trenched station beside the eastern terminal of the existing Mississauga Transitway BRT facility used by MiWay BRT and GO Transit bus routes.

## Cost and ridership

- Preliminary construction work began in 2020 while the first phase of Line 5 was still under construction; the tunnelling contract was awarded in 2021.
- "Forecast to serve 96,700 daily riders, the project was estimated in 2026 to cost CA$3.97 billion to construct."
- Metrolinx "has proposed extending the line farther to Toronto Pearson International Airport in the future".

## Line 5 background

- Line 5 Eglinton was originally conceived as the Eglinton Crosstown LRT, announced in 2007 by mayor David Miller and TTC chair Adam Giambrone as part of Transit City.
- The first phase "was built between 2011 and 2026 to a truncated route from Mount Dennis station to Kennedy station"; 25 stops and stations along the 19 km (12 mi) route at a cost of CA$12.82 billion.

wikis.title: Surface station plan (2007–2019)
wikis.summary: The extension's earlier planning as a mostly at-grade Eglinton West LRT, including the SmartTrack comparison and 2017 city staff recommendations.
wikis.body:
- Metrolinx had planned to extend the Crosstown west from Mount Dennis along Eglinton Avenue West to Toronto Pearson International Airport. During the 2014 Toronto mayoral election John Tory proposed SmartTrack, which would have put a heavy rail transit line along this section of Eglinton Avenue.
- In 2016 a City of Toronto feasibility report found the SmartTrack proposal would cost from $3.6 billion to $7.7 billion, against $1.3 billion for extending the Eglinton Crosstown as approved, and that light rail "would attract higher ridership than a heavy rail line".
- Chief planner Jennifer Keesmaat recommended extending the Crosstown to Pearson instead. On January 19, 2016, Tory agreed and supported Metrolinx's original plan, including Crosstown West as a light-rail component of SmartTrack.
- In June 2016 the estimated completion date was 2023. The estimated cost to build the Eglinton West LRT was $2.47 billion: City of Toronto $1.18 billion, federal government $822.9 million, and Mississauga plus the Greater Toronto Airports Authority asked for $470 million for the Mississauga portion. Financing approvals were still to be secured as of November 2, 2016.
- Public meetings for the extension, renamed the Eglinton West LRT, began November 13, 2017.
- The 2010 Transit City environmental assessment considered an entirely at-grade line from Weston Road and Mount Dennis; by October 2017 the city was considering grade separation at six intersections (Martin Grove Road, Kipling and Islington Avenues, Royal York and Scarlett Roads, Jane Street) with surface running between stations.
- On November 21, 2017, city staff recommended ten stops between Mount Dennis and Renforth, dropping stops at Rangoon, East Mall and Russell / Eden Valley.
- On November 28, 2017, city staff recommended building the extension without grade separation, concluding a fully at-grade extension would give better access and fewer environmental impacts; Tory recommended more study after public and political feedback. A fully at-grade extension was estimated at $1.5–2.1 billion, with grade separation adding $881.9 million to $1.32 billion.

wikis.title: Grade-separated station plan (2019–present)
wikis.summary: The 2019 Ontario decision to build the extension mostly grade-separated with seven stations, and the cost and ridership comparison with a surface line.
wikis.body:
- In April 2019 Ontario premier Doug Ford announced a GTA transit plan including the extension of Line 5 Eglinton west to Pearson Airport, with a section built underground from Royal York to Martin Grove.
- In February 2020 Metrolinx released an initial business case with four options, three of them below grade. Metrolinx "ultimately decided on a mostly grade-separated line with seven stations (four underground, two elevated, one at ground level)". An updated environmental assessment was finalized in June 2020.
- A mostly grade-separated extension "was expected to cost $4.7 billion" with seven stations and an estimated 37,000 daily boardings; a surface line "would have cost $2.9 billion" with ten ground-level stations and an estimated 42,500 daily boardings.
- Travel time savings underground would have been double those of a surface line, and such a line would be fully weatherproof except at the elevated section, but fewer stations was projected to lower ridership; local bus service would be retained given the wider station spacing.
- During the 2018 Ontario general election, Etobicoke Centre candidates Yvan Baker (Liberal) and Kinga Surma (Progressive Conservative) supported the mostly underground option; only NDP candidate Erica Kelly supported the surface option. Doug Ford preferred mostly underground construction.

wikis.title: Elevated route over the Humber River
wikis.summary: Community and First Nations opposition from 2022 to Metrolinx's decision to cross the Humber River on an elevated guideway, and the failed 2024 injunction.
wikis.body:
- From 2022 a coalition of community groups, including local First Nations groups, objected to Metrolinx's decision to elevate the line to cross the Humber River, raising concerns about mature trees in the Humber River Valley near the proposed Jane and Eglinton station and preferring a fully underground route.
- Metrolinx argued the river valley "had previously experienced extreme flooding issues in 1954 with Hurricane Hazel and again in 2013, and therefore an elevated route was most appropriate", and promised to plant trees to replace all trees cut down.
- In 2023 protests took place, with a tipi and other temporary structures erected by local First Nations groups. The coalition asked Metrolinx to pause development until a resolution was found and requested more "transparency about the project – its costs, its size, and its impact".
- In 2024 an attempt by the coalition to seek an injunction preventing construction "was rejected in the Ontario Superior Court of Justice".

wikis.title: Advance tunnel 1 – Renforth to Scarlett
wikis.summary: The first advance tunnelling contract, awarded to West End Connectors, and the two TBMs Rexy and Renny that bored 6 km of twin tunnels between 2022 and 2024.
wikis.body:
- The Metrolinx and Infrastructure Ontario delivery strategy includes four separate contracts: a first advance tunnel between Renforth Drive and Scarlett Road; a second advance tunnel between Jane Street and Mount Dennis station; an elevated guideway between Scarlett Road and Jane Street; and stations, rail and systems for the entire extension.
- On March 10, 2020, Metrolinx and Infrastructure Ontario issued a request for qualifications for tunnel construction. On May 20, 2021, the design–build–finance contract was awarded to West End Connectors, "a consortium of Dragados, Aecon and Ghella".
- The contract covered 6 km (3.7 mi) of tunnels between Renforth Drive and Scarlett Road, advance civil engineering work including headwalls for future emergency exit buildings and the station, and enabling activities (utility relocations, shaft and headwall supports, temporary power, lighting, ventilation, drainage).
- Tunnelling began on April 11, 2022, from a launch shaft next to Renforth Transitway station. Two TBMs, "dubbed Rexy and Renny", tunnelled 6 km eastwards to west of Scarlett Road where the extraction shaft was located.
- Each TBM weighed about 750 tonnes and measured 6.58 m in diameter and 131 m in length – "longer than those used for the central section" – boring 20 m underground. Renny started in April 2022; Rexy started in early August because the launch area could only launch one TBM at a time.
- Tunnelling was completed two years later: Renny broke through near Scarlett Road in May 2024 and Rexy "three weeks later".
- The underground stations are being built by cut-and-cover, as they are comparatively shallow and Eglinton Avenue's right-of-way is wide there, "as it was originally reserved for the Richview Expressway".

wikis.title: Elevated guideway and advance tunnel 2
wikis.summary: The Aecon contract for the 1.5 km elevated guideway over the Humber River and the Strabag contract for the 500 m tunnels from Jane Street to Mount Dennis.
wikis.body:
## Elevated guideway – Scarlett to Jane

- In December 2021 Metrolinx issued a pre-qualification request for a design–build contract for a 1.5 km (0.93 mi) elevated guideway from the portal west of Scarlett Road to the portal east of Jane Street, connecting both advance tunnel contracts and carrying the line over the Humber River.
- On December 15, 2023, the contract was awarded to Aecon, "with construction of the guideway to begin sometime in 2024".

## Advance tunnel 2 – Jane to Mount Dennis

- On December 2, 2021, Metrolinx and Infrastructure Ontario issued the RFQ for tunnels between Jane Street and Mount Dennis station. On February 16, 2024, the contract was awarded to Strabag.
- It covers the design and construction of 500-metre (1,600 ft) tunnels from east of Jane Street to Mount Dennis station, plus modifications to the station to enable through service.
- In February 2025 construction on this short stretch of twin tunnels began using the sequential excavation method: rather than TBMs, "mining" the tunnels in sections and spraying shotcrete on the exposed walls to reinforce them.

wikis.title: Stations, rail and systems contract
wikis.summary: The design–build contract for the extension's seven stations, track and systems, its bidders, and the stations' temporary working names.
wikis.body:
## The contract

- On March 25, 2024, Metrolinx and Infrastructure Ontario issued an RFQ for the stations, rails and systems contract, covering: construction of seven stations between Mount Dennis and Renforth (four underground, two elevated, one at grade); installation of 9.2 km (5.7 mi) of rail track, signalling and train control, electrification, communications and other equipment; and testing and commissioning of the line.
- On September 27, 2024, an RFP was issued to Integrated Transit Partners (Sacyr, NGE, Siemens, Hatch, Egis, Weston Williamson); Trillium Rail Partners (Amico, Alberici, Acciona, WSP); and WestEx Transit Solutions (Aecon, AtkinsRéalis, Pomerleau, Dragados, Arcadis).
- The successful proponent "was to be invited into a two-year design development phase with Metrolinx, anticipated to have begun in mid-2025" to finalize pricing, scheduling and scoping and reduce project risk before major construction.

## Stations

Seven stations, listed east to west: Jane (elevated), Scarlett (elevated), Royal York (underground), Islington (underground), Kipling (underground), Martin Grove (underground), Renforth (open trench).

- Five stations at cross streets "have temporary working names that conflict with the names of existing stations or stops on Line 2 Bloor–Danforth and Line 6 Finch West", and will ultimately be given alternate names reflecting surrounding neighbourhoods.
- Renforth is on the north side of the existing bus rapid transit station at the eastern terminus of the Mississauga Transitway and is the only station in Mississauga, connecting to MiWay and GO buses.

wikis.title: Further extension to Toronto Pearson International Airport
wikis.summary: A possible further extension north from Renforth station to Pearson Airport, whose route was not finalized as of March 2024.
wikis.body:
- A further extension would take the line north from Renforth station to Toronto Pearson International Airport.
- "As of March 2024, the route for this extension had not been finalized", but a conceptual route curved north, crossed Highway 401, then followed Highway 427 north before turning west toward the airport terminals.
- In March 2024 Metrolinx was working on the project with the Greater Toronto Airports Authority, the airport's operator.
- The initial business case indicated intermediate stations at Convair and Silver Dart, "with the terminus at Pearson Airport's planned Regional Transit Hub east of Airport Road".

wikis.title: Scarborough Subway Extension passes 75 per cent tunnelling
wikis.summary: NOW Toronto report that tunnelling on the 7.8 km Scarborough Subway Extension is more than 75 per cent complete and major construction has started at Lawrence and McCowan Station, with no opening date confirmed.
wikis.body:
## Milestone

- "Tunnelling on the 7.8-kilometre Scarborough Subway Extension is now more than 75 per cent complete."
- Metrolinx and the Ontario government announced "last week" that significant progress had been made on the extension of TTC Line 2.
- Major construction is now underway at the future Lawrence and McCowan Station, near Lawrence Avenue East and McCowan Road, "just steps from Scarborough General Hospital"; crews have begun piling and excavation work. It is the second of the extension's three new stations to enter major construction, after Scarborough Centre Station "last year".

## The extension

- Adds three stations to Line 2: Lawrence and McCowan, Scarborough Centre, and Sheppard and McCowan, "which will serve as the line's new eastern terminus".
- Lawrence and McCowan Station "is expected to serve more than 5,000 riders and accommodate more than 4,000 transfers during rush hour", and will have a bus terminal connecting to express bus routes along Lawrence Avenue.
- Once complete, the province estimates the extension "will support approximately 105,000 daily trips while placing an additional 38,000 residents and 34,000 jobs within a 10-minute walk of rapid transit".

## Opening date

- "Despite the construction progress, there is still no official opening date for the project." Tunnelling began in 2023.
- "In May, the Toronto Star reported that internal TTC emails indicated the project's anticipated opening had slipped from 2030 to 2033", although neither Metrolinx nor the provincial government has officially confirmed that revised timeline.

## Interim service

- Scarborough riders have been waiting for a permanent rapid transit replacement "since the Scarborough RT permanently closed in 2023 following a derailment".
- Riders rely on replacement TTC express buses in dedicated lanes; those buses "are expected to move onto a new dedicated busway along the former RT corridor when it opens in 2027".

wikis.title: New Ontario Science Centre at Ontario Place expected to open in 2029
wikis.summary: Canadian Press report, via Global News, that Infrastructure Ontario told the auditor general the new Ontario Science Centre at Ontario Place is expected to open in 2029 rather than 2028, alongside the audit's cost findings and plans for a temporary centre.
wikis.body:
## The delay

- Infrastructure officials told the auditor general's office "the centre is expected to be up and running in 2029".
- When Premier Doug Ford announced the move last year, from the science centre's east Toronto location to a redeveloped Ontario Place on the waterfront, "the science centre said the new facility would open in 2028".
- In June, when the government announced the abrupt closure of the science centre over structural concerns with the roof, its press release said the Ontario Place facility would open "as early as" 2028.
- A report "earlier this month" from Ontario auditor general Shelley Spence on the Ontario Place redevelopment says "the new building is expected to open in 2029". That information came from Infrastructure Ontario, a spokesperson for the auditor said.

## Reaction

- Jason Ash, co-chair of Save Ontario's Science Centre: "It's really a whole generation of Ontario children who are not going to have access to world-class science education that the Ontario Science Centre has provided for 55 years." He said the majority of its business came from Ontarians, with tourism second.
- Two requests for comment from Infrastructure Minister Kinga Surma went unanswered; a spokesperson said she had been asked not to comment because of a request submitted by the Leader of the Official Opposition to the Integrity Commissioner on October 16th, 2024.
- NDP Leader Marit Stiles' integrity complaint focused largely on the terms and negotiations leading to a 95-year lease for Therme to build and operate a spa and waterpark at Ontario Place, but also alleges "irregularities" with the science centre relocation. Stiles: "Ford and Surma boasted about the new Science Centre opening in 2028, but that sounds like more false promises from a flailing government."

## Costs

- The audit found it will now cost more to build a new science centre at Ontario Place than to maintain the closed site.
- The cost estimate for building and maintaining a new science centre at Ontario Place "has increased by nearly $400 million from the government's spring 2023 business case", to approximately $1.4 billion — "higher than the $1.3-billion estimate for maintaining the attraction at its east Toronto location".
- Spence wrote the increase is due to higher design and construction costs, life cycle and maintenance costs, and ancillary costs from scope changes plus about $61 million in cost escalations.
- Michael Lindsay, at the time president and CEO of Infrastructure Ontario, said he didn't agree the new centre will cost more than rehabilitating the old one, noting that project would also face inflationary increases. On the "as early as" 2028 wording he said it "probably just reflects the realities of procurement and construction".

## Procurement and temporary centre

- An Infrastructure Ontario spokesperson said procurement for the new centre continues, "with the request for proposals stage expected to wrap up next fall". Karen Evans said a firm construction completion date will be posted once a contract is awarded, and the opening date will depend on the centre's move-in timeline: "The overall plan for delivering the vision remains unchanged."
- Ontario plans a temporary science centre in the interim but has given no public updates since issuing an RFP in June. The RFP sought retail or commercial space of about 50,000 to 100,000 square feet — "much smaller than the original building's 568,000 square feet" — with a start date of "no later than" Jan. 1, 2026.
- The RFP sought a lease of up to five years plus three one-year extension options, which Ash said would allow a temporary science centre until 2034.
- The science centre "is currently operating two pop-up exhibits at Harbourfront Centre and the Sherway Gardens mall in Toronto".

wikis.title: Line 6 Finch West begins service in Toronto
wikis.summary: Railway-News report that Toronto's Line 6 Finch West LRT officially began service on 7 December, with 18 stops over almost 11 km and Hitachi Rail's SelTrac CBTC.
wikis.body:
- "Toronto's latest rapid transit line, Line 6 Finch West, has officially begun service", on 7 December.
- Almost 11 kilometres in length, linking Humber College Station in the west to Finch West Station in the east.
- 18 stops; connects with TTC Line 1, GO Transit, MiWay, Zum, York Region Transit and Brampton Transit.
- Day-to-day operation is handled by the Toronto Transit Commission, "which will now be integrated as part Toronto's broader transit system".
- Expected to serve "over 51,000 each weekday across the corridor", with trains every six and a half minutes during rush hours.
- Described as the city's first modern light rail transit line, "expected to carry more than 12 million people per year by 2031".

## Signalling

- Signalling was provided by Hitachi Rail, implementing the latest generation of its Toronto-developed SelTrac Communications-Based Train Control system "for the first time".
- Ziad Rizk, Managing Director, Hitachi Rail: "We have been developing cutting-edge rail technology out of Toronto for 50 years... Our first SelTrac deployment was on Scarborough's Line 3 in 1985, and now 40 years later, Line 6 Finch West is entering service with our made-in-Canada technology."

wikis.title: El Insurgente (Tren Interurbano Mexico City–Toluca)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on El Insurgente, the 57.7 km commuter rail line between Toluca and Mexico City, covering its planning, construction, phased openings and stations.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- El Insurgente (lit. 'The Insurgent') is a 57.7-kilometre (35.9 mi) commuter rail line connecting Mexico City and Toluca in the State of Mexico. As part of the Tren Interurbano system it is formally known as the Tren Interurbano Mexico City–Toluca.
- "The project was announced by President Enrique Peña Nieto on 1 December 2012, and construction began in 2014."
- Infobox: locale Greater Mexico City; termini Zinacantepec and Observatorio; 7 stations; type commuter rail; system Tren Interurbano; rolling stock CAF Civity-based EMUs; opened 15 September 2023; last extension 2 February 2026; line length 57.7 km; two tracks; standard gauge 1,435 mm; overhead line 25 kV 60 Hz AC; operating speed 160 km/h (99 mph).

## Route and design

- The line is electrified and elevated, with a tunnel portion between the State of Mexico and Mexico City.
- Seven stations: four in the State of Mexico and three in Mexico City.
- Designed to complement the Mexico City Metro by terminating at Observatorio station of Line 1 and to provide heavy railway service to the Santa Fe business district.
- A shuttle provides connection to Toluca International Airport at the Metepec station (formerly named Tecnológico).
- The line runs parallel to Avenida Las Torres and Mexican Federal Highway 15 / 15D.
- "The total cost of the project was estimated at $38.6 billion MXN in 2014."

## Openings

- On 1 September 2023 the line was branded El Insurgente, after Miguel Hidalgo.
- 15 September 2023: the first section from Zinacantepec to Lerma opened, with four trains initially running on the section.
- 31 August 2024: the second section from Lerma to Santa Fe was inaugurated.
- 2 February 2026: the third section from Santa Fe to Observatorio was inaugurated, "completing the line".

wikis.title: Route selection and background
wikis.summary: How the Mexico City–Toluca route was chosen from three options in a 2013 cost–benefit analysis, and a later route change at Cuajimalpa.
wikis.body:
- As part of then-President Enrique Peña Nieto's plan to offer public transport from Toluca to Mexico City, a cost–benefit analysis report was drafted and published in November 2013.
- The report proposed several routes, concentrated on the metro terminals of Cuatro Caminos, Tacubaya and Observatorio.
- "Ultimately, the third route along Avenida Las Torres to Observatorio was chosen in order to avert future sprawl, avoid deforestation in the Sierra de las Cruces, and prevent pollution of aquifers that supply water to residents."
- A section of the chosen route "was altered by 4.3 km (2.7 mi) in October 2015 to no longer run above Avenida Vasco de Quiroga in Cuajimalpa".

wikis.title: Construction, contracts and rolling stock
wikis.summary: The three construction sections and their contractors, CAF's EMU order, the depot, construction accidents and cost overruns.
wikis.body:
## Sections

The Secretariat of Communications and Transportation (SCT) divided the project into three sections for contractors to bid on:

- Section 1: the western terminal at Zinacantepec to the eastern tunnel entrance at Sierra de las Cruces, 36.1 km (22.4 mi). Contracts awarded to La Peninsular Compañía Constructora and Constructora de Proyectos Viales de México.
- Section 2: the 4.6 km (2.9 mi) tunnel under Sierra de las Cruces, awarded to Ingenieros Civiles y Asociados.
- Section 3: the 17 km (11 mi) Mexico City portion from the western tunnel entrance to Metro Observatorio station, awarded to a consortium.

## Rolling stock and depot

- CAF was awarded a contract in 2014 to construct 30 EMUs for $11.6 billion MXN (€690 million). "Each EMU will have five cars, have a capacity of 700 passengers, and operate at a maximum speed of 160 km/h (99 mph)." Deliveries began in January 2017.
- The train depot west of Zinacantepec station was built at a cost of MXN942 million; the contract was awarded to a consortium in March 2016.

## Construction and accidents

- In July 2014 a formal ceremony by SCT head Gerardo Ruiz Esparza marked the start of construction.
- 4 May 2016: temporary support structures gave way, causing concrete decking to collapse near Avenida Las Torres and Avenida Colón in Toluca.
- 2 June 2016: bad weather caused concrete-reinforced rebar to fold onto traffic near Avenida Las Torres and Avenida Díaz Mirón in Toluca.
- 7 July 2016: a work site caved in, killing one worker and injuring two.
- 16 July 2016: a construction worker was killed when a truck lost control and struck him at a site in Metepec.

## Delays and cost overruns

- In July 2019 the SCT determined completion would be delayed to the end of 2022. SCT head Javier Jiménez Espriú announced the project was 87% complete; "there have been cost overruns from $42.72 billion MXN in 2015 to $73.72 billion MXN in 2019".
- President Manuel Lopez Obrador inaugurated Section 1 in September 2023, "but since the train runs only through stations in Toluca and does not run through to Mexico City, ridership was exceptionally low as of December 2023".

wikis.title: Stations
wikis.summary: The line's seven stations, their locations and opening dates.
wikis.body:
Stations listed east (Toluca end) to west as numbered in the article, with location and date opened:

1. Zinacantepec – elevated; various intercity routes; Toluca, State of Mexico; opened 15 September 2023.
2. Toluca Centro – various intercity routes.
3. Metepec – shuttle to Toluca International Airport (planned); various intercity routes; Metepec.
4. Lerma – various intercity routes; Lerma.
5. Santa Fe – Cuajimalpa de Morelos, Mexico City; opened 31 August 2024.
6. Vasco de Quiroga – Álvaro Obregón; opened 2 February 2026.
7. Observatorio – connection at Observatorio metro station and the Western Central Bus Terminal.

- A note says the station names are proposed names and "All the stations will be fully accessible to people with disabilities".

wikis.title: Mexico City metro Line 1 fully reopens after CRRC System+ modernisation
wikis.summary: Railway Gazette report that Mexico City's rubber-tyred metro Line 1 has fully reopened following CRRC's System+ modernisation, with details of the concession, contractors and new trainsets.
wikis.body:
## Reopening

- "Mexico City's rubber-tyred metro Line 1 has fully reopened following a comprehensive modernisation project undertaken by China's CRRC."
- The phased upgrade "was completed with a reopening ceremony on November 16".
- Line 1, or the Pink Line, opened in stages in 1969-84 and now runs 19 km from Pantitlán in the east to Observatorio in the west with 20 stations. It carries 243 million passengers/year, "and the modernisation project was launched to address overcrowding, slow operating speeds and uneven headways".

## System+ model

- It was "the first overseas project to use CRRC's System+ model, encompassing financing, new rolling stock and a comprehensive modernisation of the railway and electromechanical systems".
- The 32·2bn pesos PPP concession contract awarded in December 2020 included four years for the refurbishment works, followed by 15 years of operation.
- The first section, Pantitlán – Salto del Agua, was completed in October 2024.

## Contractors

- Main contractor: CRRC's Mexican subsidiary MexiRRC.
- Comsa was awarded a €80m contract for track and electrical system renewals.
- Siemens Mobility equipped the line with CBTC.

## Rolling stock

- CRRC Zhuzhou has supplied 29 tailor-made Type NN-22 trainsets, "27 of which were assembled locally at a plant at Colón near Querétaro with the support of Mexican companies to meet a requirement for 65% local content".
- The nine-car sets are 150 m long with a crush-loaded capacity of 2 200 passengers including 300 seated and 1 900 standing, designed for a maximum speed of 80 km/h.

## What's next

- CRRC "is now targeting more widespread use of the System+ model in the South American market", where since 2022 it has signed contracts including the Medellín 80 Avenue Light Rail project in Colombia, the Rio Metro Line 3 project in Brazil and the Guadalajara Light Rail Line 4 project in Mexico.

wikis.title: New opening date for Estadio Azteca and its 2026 World Cup renovation
wikis.summary: StadiumDB article on Estadio Azteca's reopening date of March 28, 2026 after its most extensive renovation in decades ahead of the FIFA World Cup opening match, listing the works and the disputes around them.
wikis.body:
## Reopening and the World Cup

- "In 2026, Estadio Azteca will host the FIFA World Cup opener for the third time in history — a feat no other stadium in the world has achieved." The article notes Pelé lifted his third World Cup trophy there in 1970 and Diego Maradona played there sixteen years later.
- As part of preparations for the 2026 tournament, co-hosted by Mexico, the USA and Canada, "Azteca closed in May 2024 for a comprehensive overhaul. It is scheduled to reopen on March 28, 2026, just under three months before kickoff."
- During the World Cup the venue will not use its commercial name, Banorte: "FIFA requires neutral naming, so it will appear in official documents as Estadio Ciudad de México."

## The works

- A new hybrid pitch combining natural grass with advanced ventilation, drainage and air-injection systems. "The goal is to prevent issues like the one in 2018, when poor turf conditions led the NFL to cancel a game last minute."
- New locker rooms built directly under the stands, closer to the pitch, requiring reconfiguration of the lower seating.
- All matchday facilities upgraded to modern international standards, including referee rooms, medical areas, media zones and the press conference hall.
- Over 2,200 m² of LED screens inside and on the stadium's façade, supported by 1,200 antennas for Wi-Fi 6. "The entire sales system will operate cash-free."
- Upgraded toilets, sound systems, security with 200 new cameras, elevators and improved circulation paths.
- New hospitality areas covering over 7,000 m², and food services — "previously scarce inside the venue" — fully integrated into the stadium.
- City authorities have announced urban projects around the stadium to improve access, safety and services for the hundreds of thousands of expected visitors.

## Complications

- "Plans for a shopping center and hotel next to the stadium were scrapped after opposition from residents of the Santa Úrsula neighborhood."
- Another dispute involved VIP boxes: "some owners refused to hand them over to FIFA during the tournament, leading to intervention from Mexico's consumer protection agency."
- "Despite the tensions, the works are moving forward."

wikis.title: Cablebús Line 4 Tlalpan–Coyoacán at 20% progress, due December 2027
wikis.summary: Mexican Presidency press release on President Claudia Sheinbaum's site visit to Cablebús Line 4 in Mexico City, reporting 20% progress, completion expected in December 2027, and the line's stations, length and capacity.
wikis.body:
## The visit

- President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo reported that Cablebús Line 4 Tlalpan–Coyoacán "presenta un avance de 20 por ciento y se espera que en diciembre de 2027 esté concluida", during a supervision tour of the Universidad station.
- She called it a project of social justice: "Es un proyecto de justicia social, porque justamente está dedicado para los que menos tienen, el mejor transporte para los que menos tienen... va 20 por ciento de avance, espera terminarse en diciembre de 2027."
- She said Cablebús reduces travel times, is safe, helps make the city visible, and credited Mexico City head of government Clara Brugada Molina with building Line 4 to benefit university students living in Tlalpan, Coyoacán and Cantera reaching Ciudad Universitaria.

## The line

- Line 4 "reducirá a la mitad el tiempo de traslado, con un recorrido de 40 minutos" and will have nine stations: Universidad, Cantera, Perisur, Vasco de Quiroga, Campo Xóchitl, Ceforma, Deportivo Independencia, Cultura Maya and Pedregal de San Nicolás.
- Mexico City mobility secretary Héctor Ulises García Nieto said the line will be 11.4 kilometres long, with more than 70 pylons (postes), nine stations and almost 400 cabins, serving 65 000 passengers, "con potencialidad de atender a más de 155 mil habitantes de 44 colonias".
- Clara Brugada Molina thanked the President for allocating more than 4 700 million pesos (mdp) to the project and for being the first to bring the model to the capital when she was head of government. She reported that 40 million trips are currently made on the three Cablebús lines.

## Studies and design

- Mexico City works and services secretary Raúl Basulto Luviano said most feasibility studies are 100% complete, including hydrological, soil mechanics, geophysical and environmental studies, with urban impact and civil protection studies at 95%.
- Project architect Tatiana Bilbao explained the design sought to form "un eje de confluencia social", generate opportunities through public spaces, and connect the line with urban parks and the Utopías.

wikis.title: Gatwick second runway cleared after court challenge fails
wikis.summary: Construction Enquirer report that the Court of Appeal dismissed the challenge to Gatwick's £2.2bn second runway, clearing the way for construction and full use of the northern runway from 2030.
wikis.body:
## The ruling

- "Gatwick Airport's £2.2bn second runway expansion has cleared its final legal hurdle after the Court of Appeal dismissed a challenge against the project, paving the way for construction to begin."
- Transport secretary Heidi Alexander said the ruling ended years of uncertainty over the project.

## The scheme

- The government said the privately financed scheme "is now on course to bring the airport's standby northern runway into full use from 2030, allowing up to 100,000 additional flights a year and supporting 14,000 jobs across the region".
- The project involves shifting the existing northern runway 12m "to enable simultaneous operations while meeting international safety standards".
- It also includes terminal extensions, new airport buildings and major highway improvements, including a flyover over the South Terminal roundabout and upgrades to the North Terminal roundabout.
- "At peak, around 3,200 construction workers will be on site."
- An image caption describes a "New runway with terminal extensions and new hotels and office buildings", and another a "New South Terminal junction flyover".

## Benefits and conditions

- The Department for Transport said the project "would generate an estimated £1bn a year in economic benefits while increasing airline competition and expanding Gatwick's network of more than 200 destinations".
- The government added that airport expansion projects "remain subject to strict requirements on air quality, carbon emissions and noise, alongside wider investment in sustainable aviation fuels and zero emission aircraft technology".

wikis.title: Olympia London opens as a food, drink and live music destination
wikis.summary: Olympia's press release announcing that the London landmark opened its new rooftop restaurants, public spaces and live music venue on 15 June 2026 as part of its £1.3 billion transformation.
wikis.body:
## The opening

- "Olympia, London's newest destination for food, drink and live music opens today", the 140-year-old landmark "welcomes visitors into its vibrant next chapter".
- The opening marks "the next milestone in Olympia's £1.3 billion transformation", reintroducing the destination "not simply as a venue, but as one of the capital's most exciting new places to eat, meet, discover and stay".
- Michael Volkert, CEO of Olympia: "This summer, Olympia opens its doors to visitors with a full programme of dining, live music, culture and free spaces to explore. Olympia has always brought people together, and we're excited to welcome visitors from near and far to experience everything we have to offer."
- Olympia "has been co-designed by Heatherwick Studio and SPPARC".

## Still to come

- Hyatt Regency London Olympia (6 July) and citizenM London Olympia complete the summer openings. "Further venues and public spaces will be unveiled later in 2026, culminating with the British Airways Theatre opening in 2027."
- One Olympia, a new 550,000 sq ft office building, "will also start welcoming tenants later this year", housing among others Premier League Studios, the Premier League's new international content production arm; an International Convention Centre to complement the existing heritage halls; and The Addison, a premium lounge.

## Heritage halls and events

- The heritage halls, opened 140 years ago, host this summer's programme including the annual London Wine Fair and Hyper Japan, plus events at Olympia for the first time such as London Premier Padel P1 "from 4-9 August".

## Economic projection

- "Once fully operational, Olympia is projected to inject more than £600 million into the UK economy each year, directly generating 7,000 jobs and welcoming a projected 10 million visitors annually."

wikis.title: The British Airways ARC
wikis.summary: Olympia's new 3,800-capacity live music venue operated by AEG Presents, launching with Self Esteem on 16–17 June.
wikis.body:
- "The British Airways ARC a 3,800-capacity venue operated by AEG Presents, which reignites Olympia's rich musical heritage - once graced by legendary acts including Pink Floyd - for a new generation."
- "Launching tomorrow with a stellar programme of live performances, Mercury Prize-nominated artist Self Esteem takes to the stage on 16–17 June, followed by a calendar of acclaimed British and international artists."
- The release describes it as set to make Olympia "one of London's most exciting live entertainment destinations".

wikis.title: The Square summer programme and the Canvas
wikis.summary: Olympia's public spaces open with an immersive art installation, free live music from 15 June and an 83-metre Samsung digital screen.
wikis.body:
## The Square

- The Square "comes alive with an immersive art installation as its centrepiece for the summer programme", designed "to intersect art, play and design".
- Across June there is a programme of free live music and performances for all ages. "From 15 June, a selection of emerging artists, DJs and cultural showcases take place from 12pm onwards, with live music in the first week from Monday until Friday", with highlights including The BRIT School, Essence Martins, Dan Whitlam, Eleni Drake, Alfreda, Ten West and K2K Radio DJs.
- Free events continue "every Wednesday and Sunday until the end of August", including family-friendly activities.

## The Canvas

- The Canvas is "Olympia's 83-metre-long, 8-metre-wide Samsung digital screen", soaring above Emberton Walk, "a showcase of digital art, live content and large-scale activations". Photography credited to Sam Lort.

wikis.title: The new rooftop bars and restaurants
wikis.summary: A collection of bars and restaurants opening on Olympia's rooftop on 15 June, alongside the Pillar Hall restaurant Idalia.
wikis.body:
- Opening 15 June on Olympia's new rooftop is "a collection of 'only-at-Olympia' bars and restaurants", described as West London's go-to alfresco hotspot.
- Venues: Bar Arriba, "a Mexican-inspired bar for cocktails and small plates"; Wolves of Tokyo, "a Japanese restaurant and late-night destination"; Lillie's, "serving seasonal British dishes"; and Arbour, "a multi-concept food hall bringing together a range of independent operators".
- It offers open-air dining, drinks and panoramic views, "designed for every occasion from weekend brunches to late-night cocktails".
- These complement "the grand all-day restaurant, Idalia, which opened in Olympia's historic Pillar Hall back in March".

wikis.title: Hillingdon Hospital redevelopment update (June 2025)
wikis.summary: A report to Hillingdon's Health and Social Care Select Committee summarising progress on the Hillingdon Hospital redevelopment, its wave 1 status, milestone dates and contractor procurement.
wikis.body:
## Status

- Report by Jason Seez, The Hillingdon Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, to the Health and Social Care Select Committee; the committee is asked to note the report. Papers with report: None. Ward: All.
- "Hillingdon will proceed as a wave 1 scheme, with construction expected to start in 2027/28 and a capital envelope of £1-1.5bn" — the redevelopment "will be part of the initial phase of hospital rebuilds and will act as a testbed for future hospital redevelopments in England".
- The redevelopment sits alongside the seven high priority RAAC (reinforced autoclaved aerated concrete) hospitals; "Hillingdon Hospital is one of a small number of schemes that have been selected to proceed in wave 1 and the only one in London".

## Ministerial expectations

Following the Government announcement, the Trust received a letter from the Minister of State for Health confirming wave 1 status and setting out expectations to:

- Develop a Hospital 2.0 compliant design (NHP's standardised approach to design);
- Engage and gain support from Local Authority planners for the H2.0 compliant design;
- Move forward with the Outline Business Case (the second stage of the three stage NHS business case process for major construction schemes) "supported by a programme plan to be agreed by March 2025".

## Site preparation

- An Integrated Site Clearance Programme (ISCP), led by the Redevelopment Estates Lead, comprises the enabling and decant schemes and the BAU site moves, including known gaps.
- The integrated plan informs onward activity through collaborative working between the Redevelopment Estates workstream and Trust BAU teams (clinical, operational and estates / capital planning).
- The enabling and decant programme supports "a cleared site in 2027", including completion of the Furze refurbishment by October 2025; agreement and completion of the next phase of works for the new power supply; and conclusion of the New Hospital Programme (NHP) / NHS England assurance process for the remaining enabling and decant business cases.

## Programme development

- The Trust has received details of budget and the target Gross Internal Floor Area; a schedule of accommodation describing the content and spaces in the hospital is being finalised.
- Work with the New Hospital Programme to align the schedule of accommodation with the budget: "Validation and sign off of this process is expected by mid-July 2025."
- Work has started on enabling strategies including the revised Digital Strategy, Facilities Strategy and Workforce Strategy; work on the Target Operating Model is expected to commence over summer 2025.
- The design refresh "is due to commence in July 2025".

## Draft milestones

| Milestone | Date |
| --- | --- |
| Design refresh begins | July 2025 |
| Contractor selection and onboarding | Early 2026 |
| Outline Business Case submission | October 2026 |
| Full Business Case submission | March 2028 |
| Construction | 2028 - 2032 |
| Hospital available to patients | Early 2033 |

## Contractor selection

- The New Hospital Programme has begun procurement to appoint 10 contractors to the new Hospital 2.0 Alliance (H2A) framework.
- "This £37 billion, multi-supplier framework agreement will be used by Trusts to appoint Alliance Partners who will provide the detailed design, construction and handover of individual New Hospital Programme schemes between 2025 and 2040."
- "NHP is on track to award places on the Hospital 2.0 Alliance framework in Q4 of 2025." The Trust will provide a scheme prospectus to be matched to a contractor through collaborative allocation.

## Engagement

- The Trust will continue to engage staff, patients and the local community, with a broader engagement road map supported by Hillingdon Council, Healthwatch and the wider voluntary charity sector.
- As an anchor institution the Trust has connected with Brunel University "in being a key partner to the hospital rebuild and the opportunities that lie ahead with employment and education pathways", and Hillingdon Chamber of Commerce has invited it to upcoming events and its network with the Heathrow Business Summit and Heathrow's Lift Off Programme.

wikis.title: Earls Court £10bn masterplan backed by both local boroughs
wikis.summary: Earls Court Development Company press release announcing that Kensington & Chelsea and Hammersmith & Fulham planning committees have resolved to grant permission for the £10bn transformation of the 44-acre Earls Court site.
wikis.body:
## The decisions

- "On 16 December, the Planning Committee of the Royal Borough of Kensington & Chelsea passed a resolution to grant planning permission for the transformation of Central London's largest cleared development site. This follows unanimous approval by the London Borough of Hammersmith & Fulham's Planning Committee on 26 November."
- ECDC submitted hybrid planning applications in 2024 to each borough, "with permission sought in outline for the illustrative masterplan, and in detail for six buildings forming the first phase of the development".
- "With detailed permission secured for the first phase, early construction work is expected to begin in 2026." The impetus is now on public–private collaboration "to bring forward the first 1,300 homes within Phase One".

## Who is behind it

- The Earls Court Development Company (ECDC), founded by Delancey and APG, is responsible for the transformation of the 44 acre area on behalf of Earls Court Partnership Limited — a joint venture between Delancey (on behalf of its client funds), Dutch pension fund manager APG, and Places for London, Transport for London's property company.
- "The Earls Court Partnership Limited initially acquired the site in December 2019, and in 2022 subsequently secured control of the adjoining TFL Lillie Bridge Depot and associated land, that forms part of this masterplan."

## What is planned

- c.4,000 homes, including affordable, with the development piloting innovative housing approaches "such as a new tenure aimed at supporting the 'squeezed middle'".
- Leisure and cultural venues within 20 acres of public realm and green space; three new world-class cultural venues plus fixed and pop-up venues, retail, dining and leisure spaces.
- 2.5 million sq ft of workspace focused on the climate innovation sector, "supporting start ups, scale ups, the creative industries and global firms, and delivering around 12,000 on-site jobs"; contributing to the London Growth Plan and Hammersmith & Fulham's Industrial Strategy, Upstream London.
- Overall: "23,500 jobs across the UK and injecting £3bn per annum into the UK economy".
- Transport: three Tube stations on the doorstep, London Overground services and several bus routes, plus new east-west and north-south routes through the site for pedestrians and cyclists.

## Sustainability

- "Climate resilience at its core with over 1,000 trees planted, a zero-carbon energy network and a zero operational carbon target from day one" (elsewhere, "from first occupation").
- Landscape architects SLA and Studio Egret West designed a climate-resilient approach to the 20 acres of public realm and green space, "including planting over 1,000 new trees and an 85% uplift in biodiversity".

## Design team

- Masterplan architects Hawkins\\Brown and Studio Egret West, with SLA working alongside Studio Egret West on landscape architecture, "designed Earls Court as a neighbourhood set for the 22nd Century".
- Sheppard Robson, Serie, Maccreanor Lavington and dRMM worked on the designs submitted in detail; EPR, ACME and Haworth Tompkins designed buildings in outline.
- ZCD Architects helped ECDC set up a Public Realm Inclusivity Panel "involving people across a range of ages and access needs".
- The plans create new residential crescents with taller buildings clustered close to the existing Empress State Building; "the tallest building in the cluster, designed by Sheppard Robson, reaches 42 storeys".
- The masterplan "has been shaped by over four years of extensive engagement and co-design with local residents, business and community groups".

## Quotes

- Rob Heasman, Chief Executive of ECDC: "Our plans will restore Earls Court as a global destination, a place for ingenuity, and for the extraordinary." He said the focus "will now turn firmly to delivery".
- Jamie Ritblat, Founder and Executive Chairman of Delancey: "This is a hugely important milestone. Earls Court will be a beacon for the capital's future as a leading global city."
- Graeme Craig, Director and Chief Executive of Places for London: "This is a unique project and the very definition of connected brownfield land which can deliver on the priorities of London's future", noting training facilities created at Earls Court for the next generation of construction workers.
- Rafael Torres-Villalba, Director European Real Estate for APG, welcomed "the scale of our ambition being backed through the planning process... while providing annually £3billion of GVA to the UK economy".

wikis.title: CDG Express: the journey so far
wikis.summary: The CDG Express operator's page on the project's history, explaining the origins of the Paris–Charles de Gaulle rail link, its 32 km route, stakeholders and 28 March 2027 service start.
wikis.body:
## Service start

- "When it enters service on 28 March 2027, the CDG Express will realise a vision first imagined more than 30 years ago: a direct link between central Paris and its main international airport."
- An FAQ answer says Hello Paris "is hiring in preparation for the service launch, planned for March 2027", with vacancies in driving, maintenance, passenger services and supervision.

## Origins

- "Over 72 million passengers travelled through Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport in 2025, ranking it among the world's leading international hubs." Unlike London, Oslo, Stockholm and Vienna, Paris did not have a direct express link between its main airport and the city centre.
- Feasibility studies began in 1998, "and it soon became clear that Gare de l'Est was the natural choice for the terminal station rather than nearby Gare du Nord, which was already at full capacity".
- Keolis and RATP Dev joined forces in 2018 to create Hello Paris, "pooling their expertise in rail operations, high-density transport network management and service quality". The project "began to take shape in 2019 with the creation of a 32 km rail link between Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport and Gare de l'Est".

## The route

- Several years of studies and planning produced a 32 km route, "including 8 km of new track from Gare de l'Est".
- "Three-quarters of the route is on existing rail lines, which avoided the need to build new tunnels. The route is longer than originally planned, but the dedicated, non-stop service between Charles de Gaulle Airport and Paris will still take only 20 minutes."
- The service makes no stops: it is non-stop between Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport and Gare de l'Est.

## Delivery and financing

- SNCF Réseau and Groupe ADP built the infrastructure and upgraded a substantial portion of the existing rail network north of Paris, "under a public works concession, starting in 2019".
- The CDG Express infrastructure management company oversaw the design, construction and maintenance of the rail facilities in the eight areas crossed by the route. It is owned in equal shares by Groupe ADP, SNCF Réseau and Banque des Territoires, "and financed the entire project without public subsidies".

## Stakeholders listed

- Ministère des Transports (DGITM) – lead coordinating authority for the French State; Gestionnaire d'Infrastructure (GI CDG Express) – infrastructure design and construction; Gares & Connexions – station-space manager; CAF France – trainset manufacturer (Alsace); Groupe ADP – airport interface partner; SNCF Réseau – national rail network manager.

## Quote

- Soledad Valencia-Risseto, Chairwoman of Hello Paris: "Working side by side with our partners in the tourism and airport sectors, we will deliver on our promise to provide an efficient, sustainable and low-carbon transport service that helps enhance Paris's international standing."

wikis.title: Construction starts on the Saint-Ouen Grand Paris-Nord hospital campus
wikis.summary: AP-HP news item reporting that construction of the Saint-Ouen Grand Paris-Nord university hospital campus began on 30 March 2026, for completion by 2032.
wikis.body:
## Start of works

- "À Saint-Ouen, les travaux du campus hospitalo-universitaire Saint-Ouen Grand Paris-Nord ont débuté le 30 mars 2026."
- "À l'horizon 2032", the campus will bring together on one site a new-generation hospital, a university campus for health training and research, and a student residence. The project is "reconnu d'utilité publique".
- The construction phase follows site preparation between 2023 and 2025, "avec notamment la déconstruction de l'usine du groupe Stellantis et la dépollution du terrain".

## Layout

- The future CHU Saint-Ouen Grand Paris-Nord will have two sites, "qui seront à terme reliés par une passerelle enjambant les voies ferrées": to the north, university teaching and research activity plus a student residence; to the south, the new hospital.
- Jean-Baptiste Hagenmüller, directeur délégué à l'AP-HP and project director: "Aujourd'hui, les entreprises en charge de ces deux sites démarrent des opérations de terrassement puis de réalisation des parois moulées - des murs souterrains... Elles vont ensuite ériger la passerelle, puis à partir de 2027, nous commencerons à monter les murs."

## Limiting disruption

- The works follow a "chantier à faibles nuisances" charter: site organisation and methods chosen to limit nuisance as far as possible, with acoustic and vibration probes to monitor vibration and noise, and daily air quality monitoring.
- Continuous dialogue with residents is offered throughout the works, with documents issued regularly on progress, what is coming and possible temporary impacts on daily life in the neighbourhood.

## Related items on the page

- A linked article notes that the prefect of Seine-Saint-Denis granted AP-HP the hospital's building permit on Wednesday 24 September 2025.

wikis.title: RER E: official start date for the extension to Mantes-la-Jolie
wikis.summary: Sortiraparis article reporting that the RER E's EOLE extension to Mantes-la-Jolie will enter commercial service on 28 February 2027, with a gradual increase in frequency.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- "At the Île-de-France Mayors' Fair, held on June 2 in Paris, project managers said the RER E will begin commercial service as far as Mantes-la-Jolie on February 28, 2027."
- The rollout will be gradual: four trains per hour from 28 February 2027, with the ramp-up "expected to continue through the end of 2029, or perhaps into early 2030, with six trains per hour at peak times, according to the Mantes-la-Jolie website".

## The EOLE project
