wikis.summary: ServeTheHome report on NVIDIA's CES 2026 press conference launching the Rubin platform, covering its six new chips, the Vera Rubin NVL72 and HGX Rubin NVL8 systems, DGX SuperPODs and a second-half-2026 availability window.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- By Ryan Smith, ServeTheHome, January 5, 2026.
- At "the first major chipmaker press conference of the day" at CES 2026, NVIDIA announced "the launch of Rubin, the company's next-generation AI platform."
- NVIDIA revealed "that all of the necessary chips are back from the fab and that systems are being brought up in NVIDIA's labs."
- Headline gains: "improving per-GPU AI inference performance by 5x, AI training performance by 3.5x."
- The article calls it "an 'everything remains on schedule' announcement". "To be sure, the hardware is not shipping yet, and the ramp-up for production wo not even start until the second half of the year."
- This was a high-level press conference, not a technical presentation, "though a separate technical blog is being published today."
- Rubin is a platform of six chips: "the significance for NVIDIA on the development and launch of the Rubin platform is not that they developed one high-end chip - it is that they developed six." The article numbers them: Rubin GPU, NVLink Switch (#2), Vera CPU (#3), ConnectX-9 NIC (#4), BlueField 4 DPU (#5), Spectrum-6 (#6).
- NVIDIA describes an updated transformer engine with support for compression as one of their six "technology miracles".

## Availability

- "NVIDIA is expecting to deliver production hardware to partners in time for them to offer products and services in the second half of 2026. NVIDIA also expects to begin offering DGX systems in the same timeframe."
- "According to NVIDIA, AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft, and OCI will all be among the first public clouds to deploy Vera Rubin instances in 2026."

## Headline figures

- Rubin GPU: 50 PFLOPS inference (NVFP4), 35 PFLOPS training (NVFP4), 336 billion transistors, up to 288GB HBM4, 22 TB/second memory bandwidth, dual reticle-sized dies on TSMC 3nm.
- Vera CPU: 88 Olympus cores, 176 threads, up to 1.5TB LPDDR5X, 1.2 TB/second memory bandwidth.
- Vera Rubin NVL72: 72 GPUs (144 dies), 36 Vera CPUs, 220 trillion transistors, 3.6 EFLOPS inference / 2.5 EFLOPS training.
- DGX SuperPOD (Vera Rubin NVL72): 8 racks, 576 GPUs, 288 CPUs, ~600TB memory, 28.8 EFLOPS at NVFP4.
- Power consumption for the Rubin GPU has not been disclosed.

## Naming note

- The Vera Rubin NVL72 rack was "previously known as NVL144".
- In the HBM4 passage the article writes "Vera's HBM4 will afford a total of 22 TB/second of memory bandwidth" while describing the Rubin GPU's memory.

wikis.title: Rubin GPU
wikis.summary: The lead GPU of NVIDIA's Rubin platform, with its compute, memory, transistor and efficiency figures as given at CES 2026.
wikis.body:
- "The star of the show", NVIDIA's next-generation GPU architecture and its lead implementation; part number "to be confirmed". Intended "to leapfrog NVIDIA's Blackwell and Blackwell Ultra (GB200) GPUs."
- "the big driver for the AI market is an updated transformer engine with support for compression - what NVIDIA refers to as one of their six 'technology miracles.'"
- "50 PFLOPS of compute for inference using NVIDIA's NVFP4 format, which is five-times the inference performance of the Blackwell GPU."
- "35 PFLOPS of compute for training using the same NVFP4 format, which would put it three-and-a-half times ahead of Blackwell."
- Dual die chip, two Rubin GPU dies on a single package, fabbed on TSMC's 3nm process, the two dies "reticle sized".
- Paired with "up to 288GB of HBM4 memory, the same capacity available today with Blackwell Ultra." Compared to Blackwell's HBM3e, HBM4 "will afford a total of 22 TB/second of memory bandwidth, a surprising 2.8x more than what Blackwell can offer."
- "the Rubin GPU measures in at 336 billion transistors, 1.6x that of Blackwell."
- "NVIDIA has yet to disclose the power consumption for the GPU. But they are claiming that it will offer eight-times the performance-per-watt of Blackwell when it comes to inference, which can be juxtaposed to the claimed 5x increase in performance."

wikis.title: NVLink 6 and the NVLink Switch chip
wikis.summary: NVLink 6 doubles per-GPU bandwidth and comes with a new liquid-cooled switch chip, chip #2 of the Rubin platform.
wikis.body:
- "NVLink 6 doubles the available bandwidth from NVLink 5, with each GPU now offering 3.6 TB/second of NVLink bandwidth."
- NVIDIA "has developed a new NVLink Switch chip (chip #2)."
- "As you would expect for a doubled transfer rate, NVIDIA has needed to move to 400Gbps SerDes for NVLink 6."
- "with the NVLink 6 Switch chip offering full all-to-all bandwidth to each GPU hooked up to it, that gives the switch chip a total of 28.8 GB/second of bandwidth" (the article's own figure and unit).
- "That much networking traffic in a tight space also generates quite a lot of heat, and as a result the NVLink 6 Switch chip must be liquid cooled."

wikis.title: Vera CPU
wikis.summary: NVIDIA's new 88-core Arm-based Vera CPU, chip #3 of the Rubin platform, with its Olympus cores, SOCAMM memory and confidential-computing role.
wikis.body:
- Vera is "NVIDIA's new high-end ARM-based CPU (chip #3), and the first part of the titular Vera Rubin duo."
- "Each Vera CPU has been confirmed to be comprised of 88 CPU cores, codenamed Olympus, which is an NVIDIA-custom design that implements the Arm v9.2-A architecture."
- "NVIDIA has confirmed that it is an SMT-capable design - allowing for 176 threads - via NVIDIA's spatial multi-threading technology."
- "NVIDIA is touting that Vera will offer twice the data processing performance and twice the compression performance of Grace."
- "Vera will be attached to up to 1.5TB of LPDDR5X memory (3x that of Grace) using SOCAMM modules, which NVIDIA developed in conjunction with Micron." The modular memory "is designed to resolve one of the few drawbacks of Grace-based GB200, namely its use of unchangeable soldered-down memory."
- "a Vera CPU will have access to 1.2 TB/second of memory bandwidth, a bit over 2x the bandwidth of Grace."
- "A typical DGX node will feature one Vera CPU that is paired with two Rubin GPUs, and connected to those GPUs via NVLink-C2C, the latest generation slated to offer 1.8 TB/second of bandwidth."
- Confidential computing: "While Blackwell could already handle encrypted workloads, Grace could not, limiting the size of the confidential domain to just the GPU. But with Vera now fully in sync with NVIDIA's confidential computing technologies on Rubin, it will be possible to have the entire rack encrypted."

wikis.title: ConnectX-9 NIC and BlueField 4 DPU
wikis.summary: Chips #4 and #5 of the Rubin platform: the 1.6 Tb/s ConnectX-9 NIC and the BlueField 4 DPU.
wikis.body:
- "The ConnectX-9 NIC (chip #4) will offer 1.6 Tb/second of networking bandwidth by utilizing 200G PAM4 SerDes. And in larger, multi-rack configurations, it will provide the basis for scale-out networking for larger clusters."
- "the BlueField 4 DPU (chip #5)... combining a 64 core Grace CPU with its own ConnectX-9 NIC."
- "NVIDIA is touting BlueField 4 as offering twice the bandwidth, three-times the memory bandwidth, and six-times the compute performance as BlueField 3."

wikis.title: Spectrum-6 Ethernet switching and co-packaged optics
wikis.summary: Chip #6, the Spectrum-6 switch silicon behind the SN6800 and SN6810 Spectrum-X switches, NVIDIA's first with co-packaged optics.
wikis.body:
- Spectrum-6 (chip #6) "will be the heart of NVIDIA's Spectrum-X switches, which for the first time for the company will implement co-packaged optics to rein in on power consumption."
- Two key switch products: "the SN6800 will offer 512 ports of 800G Ethernet or 2048 ports at 200G, for an aggregate bandwidth of 409.6 Tb/second. Meanwhile the smaller SN6810 will feature 128 ports of 800G or 512 ports of 200G - one quarter that of the SN6800, and at 102.4 Tb/sec aggregate bandwidth, one quarter of the throughput as well."
- "by using a shared laser source and silicon photonics to modulate those lasers, the Spectrum-X switches will be able to provide high-speed optical networking with fewer fragile parts and without the high power cost of traditional optical networking."
- "According to the company, Spectrum-X switches with co-packaged optics will be able to offer 5x the power efficiency and 10x the reliability of an equivalent traditional networking switch."

wikis.title: Vera Rubin NVL72 and HGX Rubin NVL8 systems
wikis.summary: The two Rubin system types: the rack-scale Vera Rubin NVL72 and the x86-oriented 8-way HGX Rubin NVL8 carrier.
wikis.body:
- "NVIDIA is re-affirming that they will be offering two types of Rubin systems": an updated rack-scale NVL72 for the NVIDIA ecosystem, and "a next-generation 8-way HGX carrier design, the HGX Rubin NVL8" for "those who need to keep a toe in the world of x86."
- "a single Vera Rubin NVL72 rack (previously known as NVL144) will be comprised of 72 Vera Rubin GPUs (144 GPU dies) as well as 36 Vera CPUs." All GPUs connected via NVLink switches; "The sum-total of all of this hardware is a whopping 220 trillion transistors."
- Performance: "a Rubin NVL72 rack offers 5x the inference performance, 3.5x the training performance... 3.6 EFLOPS of compute for inference and 2.5 EFLOPS of compute for training."
- Memory: "54TB of LPDDR5X (2.5x that of GB200 NVL72), 20.7TB of HBM4 memory (1.5x that of GB200 NVL72), and a cumulative 1.6PB/second of HBM4 bandwidth (2.8x that of GB200 NVL72)."
- Rack redesign: "NVIDIA has moved to a fully cable free modular tray design... the assembly of a single rack has gone from 100 minutes on Blackwell to just 6 minutes on Rubin", which NVIDIA expects to improve reliability "as the cables themselves were potential failure points."
- "Coupled with some further improvements to NVIDIA's NVLink technology and their second-generation RAS engine, NVIDIA is promising that Vera Rubin NVL72 can achieve zero downtime for health checks and network maintenance."

wikis.title: NVIDIA Inference Context Memory Storage Platform
wikis.summary: A KV caching tier for inference built from partner SSD nodes plus NVIDIA networking hardware, claimed to give 5x inference performance and 5x better power efficiency.
wikis.body:
- "a key value (KV) caching system called the NVIDIA Inference Context Memory Storage Platform", "intended to serve as a KV cache for inferencing."
- Rationale: "the amount of context data generated by modern models is so significant - especially multistep models - there is too much context data to be stored at the node level", leaving operators to "either toss the data and recompute it later, or store it in some fashion."
- "NVIDIA is pitching this as POD-scale optimization technology to work around current bottlenecks in inference performance. At a high level, they are promising as much as a 5x improvement in inference performance and 5x better power efficiency."
- Hardware: "it would not be an NVIDIA box ala the DGX boxes or a Spectrum-X switch. Instead, NVIDIA would provide the parts and let their partners pick up the rest, assembling context memory storage nodes out of SSDs for storage and BlueField/ConnectX hardware to link back to the respective AI nodes."
- Software: "they have added the necessary software functionality to the CUDA stack as well, exposing it in Dynamo, DOCA, and other frameworks."
- The article compares the idea to other KV cache efforts, naming Enfabrica.

wikis.title: DGX SuperPODs for Rubin
wikis.summary: The two Rubin SuperPOD configurations NVIDIA will sell: eight Vera Rubin NVL72 racks, or 64 DGX Rubin NVL8 nodes for x86 users.
wikis.body:
- "the SuperPOD is intended to both serve as a blueprint/proof-of-concept for scale-out GPU systems, but also a commercial product for NVIDIA to sell to customers."
- First configuration: "based around their Vera Rubin NVL72 racks, incorporates 8 of those racks, NVIDIA's Specturm-X Ethernet and Quantum-X800 InfiniBand networking switches, BlueFlield 4 DPUs, and storage nodes for context memory storage."
- "a single DGX SuperPOD with DGX Vera Rubin NVL72 will incorporate 8 NVL72 racks, for a total of 576 GPUs, 288 CPUs, and some 600TB of memory. In terms of total throughput, NVIDIA is touting an enormous 28.8 EFLOPS of compute performance at NVFP4 precision, and with enough NVLInk bandwidth that model partitioning within a rack will no longer be necessary."
- Second configuration: "for x86 users NVIDIA will also be offering SuperPODs built around DGX Rubin NVL8 nodes. This is a less dense option overall, with 64 NVL8 nodes being combined into a single SuperPOD to offer 512 GPUs."

wikis.title: Tesla Q4 and FY 2025 Update (Exhibit 99.1)
wikis.summary: Tesla's quarterly shareholder update filed as SEC Exhibit 99.1, covering Q4 and full-year 2025 financial and operational results, manufacturing and AI infrastructure, Robotaxi and FSD, the xAI investment and the outlook.
wikis.body:
## What this is
- Tesla "Q4 and FY 2025 Update", filed as Exhibit 99.1 (EX-99.1, exhibit991.htm) on SEC EDGAR.
- Sections: Highlights, Financial Summary, Operational Summary, Manufacturing & Hardware, Supporting Infrastructure, AI & Software, Services, Other Updates, Outlook, Photos & Charts, Key Metrics, Financial Statements, Additional Information.

## Headline figures
- Profitability: "$4.4B GAAP operating income in 2025; $1.4B in Q4"; "$3.8B GAAP net income in 2025; $0.8B in Q4"; "$5.9B non-GAAP net income in 2025; $1.8B in Q4" (non-GAAP excludes SBC and digital asset gains/losses, net of tax).
- Cash: operating cash flow $14.7B in 2025, $3.8B in Q4; free cash flow (operating cash flow less capex) $6.2B in 2025, $1.4B in Q4; cash and investments up $7.5B in 2025 to $44.1B.
- Operations highlights: "Began removing safety monitor from our Robotaxis in Austin in January"; record Q4 and FY25 energy storage deployments; record vehicle deliveries in APAC.
- Q4-2025 revenue $24,901M, down 3% YoY; gross profit $5,009M; GAAP gross margin 20.1% (+386 bp YoY); income from operations $1,409M (-11% YoY), operating margin 5.7%; GAAP net income to common stockholders $840M (-61% YoY); diluted GAAP EPS $0.24, non-GAAP $0.50.
- FY2025: total revenues $94,827M (-3%); automotive revenues $69,526M (-10%); energy generation and storage $12,771M (+27%); services and other $12,530M (+19%); income from operations $4,355M (-38%), operating margin 4.6%; GAAP net income $3,794M (-46%); diluted GAAP EPS $1.08; adjusted EBITDA $14,596M.

## Narrative points
- "2025 marked a critical year for Tesla as we further expanded our mission and continued our transition from a hardware-centric business to a physical AI company."
- In 2025 Tesla "completed the refresh of our vehicle lineup with the launch of the new Model Y, including additional variants".
- In 2026 Tesla plans "the ramp of six new production lines across vehicle, robots, energy storage and battery manufacturing".

## Key dates and forward statements stated in the update
- Tesla Semi and Cybercab production ramps in North America "both commencing 1H26"; "Cybercab, Tesla Semi and Megapack 3 are on schedule for volume production starting in 2026."
- Megapack 3 and Megablock production to begin at Megafactory Houston in 2026.
- Optimus Gen 3 to be unveiled "In Q1 of this year"; start of production "planned before the end of 2026"; eventual planned capacity 1 million robots per year.
- AI5 and AI6 inference chips: "production planned for 2027 and 2028, respectively."
- Domestic cathode material in Texas and LFP lines in Nevada "expected to begin production in 2026".
- Robotaxi metro plans: Dallas, Houston, Phoenix, Miami, Orlando, Tampa, Las Vegas all "1H 2026"; Austin "Ramping Unsupervised"; SF Bay Area "Safety Driver".
- xAI investment "expected to close in Q1'2026".
- Webcast of the Q4 2025 results conference call "beginning at 4:30 p.m. CT on January 28, 2026 at ir.tesla.com".
- Risk factors reference the annual report on Form 10-K "filed with the SEC on January 30, 2025".

## Accounting notes the update makes
- 2024 quarterly periods were recast after adoption of the new crypto assets standard.
- From Q1'25, Adjusted EBITDA and non-GAAP net income are presented net of digital assets gains and losses, and capital expenditures include purchases of energy generation and storage systems; all prior periods adjusted.
- From Q4'25, end-of-quarter operating lease count covers new vehicles only (Q3'25 adjusted to exclude used vehicles).

wikis.title: Tesla Q4 and FY 2025 financial summary
wikis.summary: The quarterly and annual financial tables and the year-over-year drivers Tesla gives for revenue, profit and cash.
wikis.body:
- Quarterly (Q4-2024 to Q4-2025): total automotive revenues 19,798 / 13,967 / 16,661 / 21,205 / 17,693 ($M), Q4 YoY -11%; energy generation and storage 3,061 / 2,730 / 2,789 / 3,415 / 3,837 (+25%); services and other 2,848 / 2,638 / 3,046 / 3,475 / 3,371 (+18%); total revenues 25,707 / 19,335 / 22,496 / 28,095 / 24,901 (-3%).
- Q4-2025 gross profit $5,009M, GAAP gross margin 20.1%; operating expenses $3,600M (+39% YoY); income from operations $1,409M; adjusted EBITDA $4,154M (margin 16.7%).
- Q4-2025 cash: operating cash flow $3,813M, capex $2,393M, free cash flow $1,420M; cash, cash equivalents and investments $44,059M (+21% YoY, up $2.4B sequentially "primarily the result of positive free cash flow").
- Annual series 2021-2025: total revenues 53,823 / 81,462 / 96,773 / 97,690 / 94,827 ($M); income from operations 6,523 / 13,656 / 8,891 / 7,076 / 4,355; GAAP net income to common stockholders 5,519 / 12,556 / 14,997 / 7,091 / 3,794; free cash flow 4,983 / 7,561 / 4,357 / 3,581 / 6,220 (2025 +74%).
- Revenue drivers YoY: negatives - decrease in vehicle deliveries, lower regulatory credit revenue; positives - energy generation and storage growth, services and other growth, "positive FX impact of $0.3B", growth in other automotive ancillary sales partly from an increase in FSD subscriptions, higher vehicle ASP.
- Operating income drivers YoY: negatives - increase in SBC and Restructuring and Other charges, higher opex from "AI and other R&D projects and SG&A", higher average cost per vehicle from lower fixed cost absorption and "an increase in tariffs", fewer deliveries, lower regulatory credits.
- Balance sheet at 31-Dec-25: total assets $137,806M, total liabilities $54,941M, total stockholders' equity $82,137M, inventory $12,392M, digital assets $1,008M.
- Q4-2025 automotive gross margin (GAAP) 20.4%; excluding regulatory credit sales (non-GAAP) 17.9%.

wikis.title: Tesla Q4 and FY 2025 operational summary
wikis.summary: Production, delivery, FSD subscription, storage deployment and charging network figures for Q4-2024 through Q4-2025.
wikis.body:
- Q4-2025 production: Model 3/Y 422,652 (-3% YoY); other models 11,706 (-48%); total 434,358 (-5%).
- Q4-2025 deliveries: Model 3/Y 406,585 (-14%); other models 11,642 (-51%); total 418,227 (-16%), of which 10,996 subject to operating lease accounting.
- Cumulative all-time deliveries 8.9 million (+22% YoY); the metric "includes all new Tesla vehicles delivered to customers plus any unsupervised Robotaxis placed into commercial operation" under the 2025 CEO Performance Award.
- Active FSD subscriptions 1.1 million (+38% YoY), including up-front payments and monthly subscriptions, excluding free trials.
- End-of-quarter new-vehicle operating lease count 163,075 (-10%); global vehicle inventory 15 days of supply (+25%).
- Storage deployed 14.2 GWh (+29% YoY).
- Tesla locations 1,553 (+14%); Supercharger stations 8,182 (+17%); Supercharger connectors 77,682 (+19%); "over 3,800 net new Supercharging stalls" added, network up 19% YoY.

wikis.title: Manufacturing and hardware capacity
wikis.summary: Tesla's installed annual manufacturing capacity by site and product, and the automotive, energy and robotics production updates.
wikis.body:
- Automotive capacity: California Model 3/Model Y >550,000 (production), Model S/Model X 100,000 (production); Shanghai Model 3/Model Y >950,000 (production); Berlin Model Y >375,000 (production); Texas Model Y >250,000 and Cybertruck >125,000 (production), Cybercab (tooling); Nevada Tesla Semi (tooling); TBD Roadster (design development).
- Energy: California Megapack 40 GWh and Nevada Powerwall >6 GWh and Shanghai Megapack 40 GWh in production; Texas Megapack under construction. Robotics: California Optimus under construction.
- The update notes "Installed capacity does not equal current production rate".
- Automotive: sales declined sequentially while gross margin improved "even when excluding the impact of regulatory credits"; APAC set a record for deliveries in the quarter; Model Y standard and performance versions rolled out in Q4.
- Energy: highest quarterly energy storage deployments, driven by record Megapack deployments; energy total gross profit rose to a record $1.1 billion, "the fifth consecutive record quarter". In 2025 the global Powerwall network "supported more than 89,000 Virtual Power Plant events across over 1 million installed units, allowing homeowners to save over $1 billion in electricity bills".
- Robotics: Optimus Gen 3 to be unveiled in Q1, "major upgrades from version 2.5, including our latest hand design"; it is "our first design meant for mass production"; first production line being prepared, production planned before the end of 2026, planned capacity 1 million robots per year.

wikis.title: Supporting infrastructure: AI compute and battery
wikis.summary: Cortex AI training compute, battery manufacturing lines and the lithium refinery, plus footprint changes for Robotaxi.
wikis.body:
- AI training compute: Texas Cortex 1 ">100k H100e" in production; Cortex 2 under construction at Gigafactory Texas. "In the first half of 2026, we plan to more than double the size of onsite compute in Texas (in terms of H100 equivalents)."
- Battery manufacturing capacity: Nevada LFP 7 GWh (early ramp); Texas 4680 40 GWh (production), cathode materials 10 GWh (early ramp), lithium refining 30 GWh (early ramp).
- The lithium refinery "commenced pilot production and is the first spodumene to lithium hydroxide refinery in North America".
- Battery packs for certain Model Ys are now produced with 4680 cells; dry-electrode for 4680 cells is made with "both anode and cathode made in Austin".
- Domestic cathode material in Texas and LFP lines in Nevada expected to begin production in 2026.
- Robotaxi support uses the existing charging, service and sales/delivery footprint in the short term, with more capacity needed "as the service expands".

wikis.title: AI and software: FSD v14 and AI5/AI6 chips
wikis.summary: FSD (Supervised) v14, fleet data collection, the in-house AI5 and AI6 inference chips and over-the-air software features.
wikis.body:
- FSD (Supervised) is enhanced "via our end-to-end foundation model trained on both customer and Robotaxi real-world data with our latest version, v14"; v14 "offers unparalleled driver assistance to safely drive to the customer's destination, find a free parking spot and park at that location".
- Footnote throughout: "Active driver supervision required; does not make the vehicle autonomous".
- "Our global fleet can collect the equivalent of over 500 years of continuous driving data per day", calculated at an average of 30 miles per hour.
- In-house AI5 and AI6 inference chips for autonomy progressed during the quarter, "with production planned for 2027 and 2028, respectively". Target for AI5: "a 50x improvement in performance ... relative to AI4 thanks to 10x raw compute, 9x memory capacity and 5x hardened block quantization and softmax function".
- Over-the-air features listed: Grok with navigation commands, Tesla Photobooth, Supercharger Site Maps, Automatic HOV Lane Routing using interior camera occupancy detection, Phone Left Behind Chime and a SpaceX ISS Docking Simulator Game. The Robotaxi iOS app "no longer has a waitlist in the areas we serve".

wikis.title: Robotaxi, FSD rollout and services
wikis.summary: Robotaxi testing and coverage plans, international FSD rollout and the services business.
wikis.body:
- "We began testing driverless Robotaxis in Austin in December and began removing the safety monitor from customer rides in January on a limited basis", which is said to unlock further fleet and coverage expansion in the Austin metro.
- Planned Robotaxi coverage table: California SF Bay Area - Safety Driver; Texas Austin - Ramping Unsupervised; Dallas, Houston, Phoenix, Miami, Orlando, Tampa and Las Vegas - 1H 2026.
- The Bay Area ride-hailing service "began serving the San Jose Airport in October", with plans to expand to other major Bay Area airports "upon receiving required permitting".
- FSD (Supervised) launched in South Korea, "where customers drove over 1 million kilometers using the software in just one month". Regulatory approval still being pursued in China and Europe; ride-along experiences begun in Italy, Germany, France and Switzerland.
- Monthly FSD subscriptions "more than doubled in 2025"; from this quarter access is transitioning "to monthly subscriptions only as we begin to sunset the up-front payment option".
- Services and Other gross profit of approximately $300 million, "partly driven by Part Sales and Supercharging"; Tesla Insurance now offered in Florida, with premium discounts in certain states for driving with FSD (Supervised).

wikis.title: xAI investment and framework agreement
wikis.summary: Tesla's approximately $2 billion investment in xAI Series E Preferred Stock and the accompanying framework agreement.
wikis.body:
- "On January 16, 2026, Tesla entered into an agreement to invest approximately $2 billion to acquire shares of Series E Preferred Stock of xAI as part of their recent publicly-disclosed financing round."
- The investment "was made on market terms consistent with those previously agreed to by other investors in the financing round".
- Framed by Master Plan Part IV: Tesla "is building products and services that bring AI into the physical world" while xAI "is developing leading digital AI products and services, such as its large language model (Grok)".
- Tesla and xAI also entered a framework agreement "providing a framework for evaluating potential AI collaborations between the companies".
- The investment "is subject to customary regulatory conditions with the expectation to close in Q1'2026".

wikis.title: Outlook
wikis.summary: Tesla's stated outlook on volume, cash, profit and product.
wikis.body:
- Volume: focus on "maximum capacity utilization at our factories"; deliveries and deployments will be affected by aggregate demand, supply chain readiness and "allocation decisions between sale to customers or use for our owned and operated fleet".
- Cash: manage for a strong balance sheet and sufficient liquidity to fund the product roadmap, long-term capacity expansion "including further vertical integration" and other expenses.
- Profit: hardware-related profits expected over time "to be accompanied by an acceleration of AI, software and fleet-based profits".
- Product: focus on cost, scale and future monetization via AI software services, "leveraging and optimizing our existing production capacity before building new factories and production lines".
- "Cybercab, Tesla Semi and Megapack 3 are on schedule for volume production starting in 2026. First generation production lines for Optimus are being installed in anticipation of volume production."
- The update flags these as forward-looking statements under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, listing risks including delays in launching or manufacturing products, supplier delivery, factory ramp, tariffs and export controls, and adverse foreign exchange movements.

wikis.title: Optimus (Tesla robot)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Optimus, Tesla's humanoid robot: its announcement and prototype history, planned specifications and production lines, and the mixed press and expert reception.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- "Optimus, also known as Tesla Bot, is a general-purpose robotic humanoid under development by Tesla, Inc. It was announced at the company's Artificial Intelligence (AI) Day event on August 19, 2021, and a prototype was shown in 2022. Musk predicted that it would become the biggest product ever, not just Tesla's biggest product ever. Media and expert opinions based on corporate showcases have been mixed."
- Infobox: Manufacturer Tesla, Inc.; country United States; year of creation 2022; type humanoid; purpose general-purpose. The lead image is "Optimus v.2 in November 2025".

## History

- "On April 7, 2022, a display for the product was featured at the Tesla Giga Texas manufacturing facility during the Cyber Rodeo event. Musk said that he hoped to have the robot production ready by 2023 and claimed Optimus will eventually be able to do \"anything that humans don’t want to do.\""
- June 2022: Musk announced a first prototype to be unveiled later that year at the second AI Day, saying it would not look like the Cyber Rodeo model.
- September 2022: semi-functional prototypes shown at AI Day — "One prototype was able to walk about the stage and another, sleeker version could move its arms."
- September 2023: a video showed Optimus "sorting colored blocks by color, locate its limbs in space, and had increased flexibility as it could maintain a yoga pose."
- Generation 2: "In December 2023, Musk's X page released a video titled \"Optimus\" in which it shows Optimus Generation 2 walking and showing new features, such as dancing and poaching an egg." It "features a slimmer figure with improved hands and movements." A May 2024 update showed tasks at a Tesla factory.
- "Critics pointed out that the robots in the promotional videos required the use of teleoperation in order to perform some of the tasks." Competitors responded with videos of autonomous equivalents.
- "In June 2024, Musk claimed that Optimus would enter limited production in 2025, with plans for over 1,000 to be used in Tesla facilities and the possibility of production for other companies in 2026."
- October 2024 "We, Robot" event: critics again noted teleoperation and a lack of transparency. Musk said Optimus could do a wide range of everyday tasks "and he estimated that the robot would be available for purchase at around US$30,000."
- "In June 2025, Milan Kovac, the head of the Optimus program since 2022, resigned, replaced by Ashok Elluswamy, the head of Tesla autopilot teams."
- "In December 2025, Optimus v2.3 (the black and white version) was shown outside the USA for the first time: on December 13 in London, UK, and December 20 in Berlin, Germany." It greeted attendees with hand gestures, handed out popcorn and posed for photos.

## Generation 3

- "As of April 2026, Tesla has not yet revealed Optimus generation 3. In the Q1 earnings call on April 22, 2026, Elon Musk said that Optimus gen 3 will be unveiled closer to production start."
- Tesla said "First-generation production lines for Optimus are being installed" in Fremont "in anticipation of volume production", designed for 1 million robots a year, with a second-generation line at Gigafactory Texas "designed to deliver a long-term annual production of 10 million robots starting in 2027."
- Musk expects the unreleased Tesla AI5 chip to go into Optimus so it has "enough local intelligence to do useful work even if it loses WiFi or cellular connection", similar to Full Self-Driving; he also said the unreleased AI6 chip would be used. "For a Grok level conversation, Optimus will need a WiFi or cellular connection to Grok level AI."

## Specifications

- "Optimus is planned to measure 5 ft 8 in (173 cm) tall and weigh 125 lb (57 kg)." Per the 2021 AI Day presentation it will be "controlled by the same AI system Tesla is developing for the advanced driver-assistance system used in its cars" and have a carrying capacity of 45 lb (20 kg).
- "the robot's linear actuators utilize planetary roller screw technology rather than traditional ball screws, providing higher shock load resistance during walking motions." Proposed tasks are ones that are "dangerous, repetitive and boring", such as manufacturing assistance.
- "In 2023, the hands of the Generation 2 Optimus had 11 degrees of freedom. In 2024, the Generation 3 hands had 22 degrees of freedom."

## Reception

- After the 2021 AI Day, Bloomberg News called such a product "mission creep" outside "the company’s clean-energy initiatives"; The Washington Post said "Tesla has a history of exaggerating timelines and overpromising"; The Verge wrote that "Tesla’s history is littered with fanciful ideas that never panned out... it’s anyone’s guess as to whether a working Tesla Bot will ever see the light of day" and called the reveal "a bizarre and brilliant bit of tomfoolery".
- The 2022 AI Day prototypes drew praise from some, while others said the demonstrations had already been accomplished elsewhere and doubted Tesla could "outpace other companies working on similar things."
- "In a 2024 essay, Robert Silverberg suggested that Optimus Generation 2 was the realization of the \"humanoids\" in Jack Williamson's classic 1947 science fiction story \"With Folded Hands...\", along with their worst drawbacks."
- Expert views: robotics lecturer Carl Berry called the 2021 presentation "the usual overblown hype"; Gary Marcus said he would "bet that no robot will be able to do all human tasks by the end of 2023"; Deutsche Welle cited Filip Piekniewski, Cynthia Yeung and Tom Ryden calling the project a "complete and utter scam" and criticising the humanoid form.
- "In 2025, Australian roboticist Rodney Brooks, the cofounder of Roomba vacuum creator iRobot, said the idea of humanoid robots as catchall assistants... is \"pure fantasy thinking,\" in part because robots are coordination-challenged."
- Chris Walti, at Tesla for 7 years and first team lead for Optimus until 2022, said humanoid robots were "multiple orders of magnitude" harder than self-driving cars and "kind of a ninth-inning robotics problem, and we're in the third inning."
- "In 2026, Robbie Dickson, founder and CEO of Firgelli Automations and an actuator engineer with over 27 years of experience," said viability depends on "torque density breakthroughs" rather than software alone, requiring "integrated, high-precision linear motion systems, such as inverted planetary roller screws".

## Name

- "Optimus is named after the main character in the Transformers media series, Optimus Prime."
- "Elon Musk declared \"Optimi\" as the official plural of Tesla Optimus."

## External links

- TeslaOptimi.com — Tesla AI & robotics.

wikis.title: The Beekeeper (2024 film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on David Ayer's 2024 action thriller The Beekeeper starring Jason Statham, covering its plot, cast, production, release, box office, reviews and the 2027 sequel.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- "The Beekeeper is a 2024 action thriller film produced and directed by David Ayer and written by Kurt Wimmer."
- "It stars Jason Statham, Emmy Raver-Lampman, Josh Hutcherson, Bobby Naderi, Minnie Driver, Phylicia Rashad, and Jeremy Irons."
- "The film follows a retired government assassin who sets out for revenge after his kind-hearted landlady falls victim to a phishing scam."
- Producers: Bill Block, Jason Statham, David Ayer, Chris Long, Kurt Wimmer. Cinematography: Gabriel Beristain. Editing: Geoffrey O'Brien. Music: David Sardy and Jared Michael Fry.
- Production companies: Miramax, Cedar Park Entertainment, Punch Palace Productions.
- Distributors: Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (through Amazon MGM Studios, United States); Sky Cinema (through StudioCanal, United Kingdom).
- Release date January 12, 2024. Running time 105 minutes. Countries: United States, United Kingdom. Language: English.
- Infobox budget: $40 million. Infobox box office: $162.6 million.
- The infobox starring list does not include Jemma Redgrave, though the cast section lists her as Jessica Danforth, President of the United States.

## Release

- "MGM acquired the film's distribution rights in the United States in August 2022. In February 2023, Sky Cinema acquired the rights in the United Kingdom, with StudioCanal handling the U.K. theatrical release on behalf of Sky Cinema. It was released by Amazon MGM Studios on January 12, 2024."
- "The Beekeeper was released on VOD and digital platforms on January 30, 2024, followed by a release on DVD, Blu-ray and Ultra HD Blu-ray on April 23, 2024."

## Production

- "In August 2021, it was announced that Jason Statham would star in the film for Miramax and would also serve as a producer through his company Punch Palace Productions. David Ayer signed on to direct in May 2022."
- "Principal photography ran in England from September to December 2022. Locations included Tyringham Hall and the Kingsferry Bridge."
- "In preparation for the film's opening scenes, Statham learned several methods of beekeeping and interacted with real bees."

## Box office

- "The Beekeeper grossed $66.2 million in the United States and Canada, and $96.4 million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $162.6 million, against a budget of '$40 million or less'." (The infobox gives the budget flatly as $40 million.)
- "released alongside Mean Girls and The Book of Clarence, and was projected to gross $17-19 million from 3,303 theatres in its opening weekend. It made $6.7 million on its first day, including $2.4 million from Thursday night previews. It went on to debut to $16.6 million, finishing second behind Mean Girls."
- "The film made $8.5 million in its second weekend and $6.7 million in its third weekend, remaining in second at the box office. It spent its first eight weeks in the Top 10 at the domestic box office."

## Critical response

- Rotten Tomatoes: "71% of 182 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 5.9/10." Consensus: "Cheerfully undemanding and enjoyably retrograde, The Beekeeper proves that when it comes to dispensing action-thriller justice, Statham hasn't lost his sting."
- Metacritic: "a score of 53 out of 100, based on 36 critics, indicating 'mixed or average' reviews."
- CinemaScore: average grade "B+" on an A+ to F scale.
- The Guardian "says the non-shooting scenes are rushed and both Rashad and Driver are underused, and describes it as 'a solid, low-stakes, medium-reward new year's effort'."
- Matt Zoller Seitz of RogerEbert praised aspects including its range of villains but wrote: "It's a real shame that The Beekeeper isn't the righteous trash masterpiece that it keeps threatening to turn into."
- John Nugent of Empire said Statham is "as gruffly convincing as he usually is (though it's 20 minutes before he's even allowed to kick any ass)", called the action scenes "horribly inconsistent" and noted "you do have to put up with quite a lot of stuff about bees".

## Cast

- Jason Statham as Adam Clay, "a highly skilled assassin known as a Beekeeper who has retired to live a quiet life"
- Emmy Raver-Lampman as Verona Parker, Eloise's daughter, an FBI agent
- Josh Hutcherson as Derek Danforth, "a tech bro who is the CEO of Danforth Enterprises and the leader of an international scamming ring"
- Bobby Naderi as Matt Wiley, FBI agent and Verona's partner
- Minnie Driver as Janet Harward, the CIA Director
- Jemma Redgrave as Jessica Danforth, President of the United States and Derek's mother
- Phylicia Rashad as Eloise Parker, a retired school teacher and Adam's close friend
- Jeremy Irons as Wallace Westwyld, former CIA director, now head of security for Danforth Enterprises
- David Witts as Mickey Garnett; Michael Epp as Pettis; Taylor James as Lazarus; Enzo Cilenti as Rico Anzalone; Don Gilet as Jackson Prigg; Megan Le as Anisette Landress

## Plot (as summarised on the page)

- In Springfield, Massachusetts, retired teacher Eloise Parker falls for a phishing scam that steals her life savings, "including over $2 million from a charity she runs", and kills herself. Her tenant Adam Clay, a beekeeper, is arrested by FBI agent Verona Parker, then cleared.
- Adam contacts "a mysterious group called the 'Beekeepers'", traces the scammers to a call centre near Springfield run by Mickey Garnett, burns it down and kills Mickey.
- Derek Danforth alerts Wallace Westwyld, "a former CIA director serving as head of security for Danforth Enterprises". The CIA dispatches Anisette, a current Beekeeper, whom Adam kills; "the Beekeepers promptly declare neutrality".
- Adam attacks the Nine Star United Center in Boston, "which oversees Derek's global scam call centers". The Beekeepers are "revealed to be an elite clandestine human intelligence organization tasked with protecting the United States and operating above and beyond governmental jurisdiction, with an organizational culture inspired by worker bees in a beehive".
- Derek is the son of Jessica Danforth, the incumbent President. Adam infiltrates the Danforth coastal mansion, killing the mercenary leader Lazarus. Derek admits "Wallace gave him CIA algorithms, which he used to feed data to his criminal scam empire and to rig Jessica's election"; he shoots Prigg, and Adam shoots Derek before he can kill his mother. Verona lets Adam go, and he "disappears into the sea".

## Sequel: The Beekeeper 2

- "A sequel, The Beekeeper 2, is scheduled for a theatrical release on January 15, 2027."
- "In February 2025, it was announced that a sequel to The Beekeeper was in development, with Timo Tjahjanto directing, and Kurt Wimmer writing the screenplay. Jason Statham would reprise his role as Adam Clay, as well as produce on the film."
- "In May 2025, Kurt Wimmer was replaced by Umair Aleem for the screenplay."
- "In September, Jeremy Irons announced he would reprise his role as Wallace Westwyld. Emmy Raver-Lampman, Bobby Naderi, Jemma Redgrave, Yara Shahidi, Pom Klementieff and Adam Copeland joined the cast later that month."
- "In January 2026, the film was scheduled for a theatrical release in the United States on January 15, 2027."
- A cited Deadline headline adds: "Amazon MGM Lands Worldwide Rights To Jason Statham Sequel 'Beekeeper 2' In $50M+ Deal" (May 6, 2025).

wikis.title: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Voyage of the Dawn Treader (2010 film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 2010 fantasy adventure film directed by Michael Apted - the third Narnia film, the first distributed by 20th Century Fox after Disney's exit - covering plot, cast, production, 3D conversion, release, reviews, box office and the series' later reboot.
wikis.body:
## The film

- A 2010 fantasy adventure film directed by Michael Apted from a screenplay by Christopher Markus, Stephen McFeely and Michael Petroni, based on the 1952 C. S. Lewis novel; sequel to The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian (2008) and the third film in the series.
- The only film in the series not distributed by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures - 20th Century Fox replaced Disney - and the only one released in 3D. Disney came to own the rights to all the films after its 2019 acquisition of 21st Century Fox.
- Production companies Fox 2000 Pictures, Dune Entertainment, Walden Media and Mark Johnson Productions; producers Mark Johnson, Andrew Adamson and Philip Steuer; cinematography Dante Spinotti; editing Rick Shaine; music David Arnold. Running time 113 minutes; UK/US; English.
- Budget "$140–155 million" in the infobox: officially $140 million, with some estimates at $155 million.
- Cast: Georgie Henley, Skandar Keynes, Ben Barnes and Tilda Swinton reprise their roles, with Will Poulter as Eustace Scrubb; Simon Pegg voices Reepicheep (replacing Eddie Izzard) and Liam Neeson voices Aslan.

## Production

- Apted signed on in June 2007 for a planned May 1, 2009 release, with shooting intended for Malta, Prague and Iceland, then Mexico.
- Disney announced on December 24, 2008 that it would no longer co-produce after a budget dispute (Disney wanted a $100 million cap, Walden wanted $140 million); 20th Century Fox was announced as the replacement distributor in January 2009.
- Filming began July 27, 2009 in Queensland, Australia, at Village Roadshow Studios and Cleveland Point, and around White Island off Tauranga, New Zealand; a 145-tonne Dawn Treader was built on a gimbal rather than shooting on water.
- 1,400 visual effects shots. 20th Century Fox announced in February 2010 that the film would be converted to 3D, with Prime Focus Group hired in June 2010.

## Release and reception

- Premiered November 30, 2010 in London as the 64th Royal Film Performance, attended by Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip; released December 9, 2010 in the United Kingdom and December 10, 2010 in the United States (the Release section instead gives December 2, 2010 for Asia and Australia and December 10, 2010 for North America and Europe).
- Mixed reviews: Rotten Tomatoes 49% from 168 reviews (average 5.7/10), Metacritic 53% from 33 reviews, CinemaScore A-.
- The infobox and lead give $415.6 million worldwide; the box office section gives $415.7 million ($104.4 million North America, $311.3 million elsewhere) - the 12th-highest-grossing film worldwide of 2010 and Fox's highest-grossing film of the year. North American opening weekend $24.0 million at #1, far below the first two films.
- Nominated for Best Original Song ("There's a Place for Us" by Carrie Underwood) at the 68th Golden Globe Awards, four Saturn Awards nominations, and won the People's Choice Award for Favorite 3D Live Action Movie and the MovieGuide Most Inspiring Movie award.

## After the film

- A Silver Chair adaptation was announced on March 22, 2011, but in the fall of 2011 Walden Media's contract with the C. S. Lewis estate expired.
- Netflix and the C. S. Lewis Company announced a multi-year Narnia deal on October 3, 2018; Greta Gerwig was hired in July 2023 to write and direct at least two films, and the lead says the series "would instead be rebooted with the Netflix film Narnia: The Magician's Nephew".

wikis.title: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Voyage of the Dawn Treader (2010 film) - plot, cast, production, release and reception
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 2010 fantasy adventure film directed by Michael Apted, covering its plot, cast, troubled development after Disney's exit, 3D conversion, marketing, release, reviews, box office and awards.
wikis.body:
## The film

- "The Chronicles of Narnia: The Voyage of the Dawn Treader is a 2010 fantasy adventure film directed by Michael Apted from a screenplay by Christopher Markus, Stephen McFeely, and Michael Petroni, based on the 1952 novel The Voyage of the Dawn Treader, the third published and fifth chronological novel in the children's book series The Chronicles of Narnia by C. S. Lewis."
- Sequel to The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian (2008) and the third installment in The Chronicles of Narnia film series. It is the only film in the series not distributed by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures, replaced by 20th Century Fox; Disney eventually owned the rights to all the films following the acquisition of 21st Century Fox by Disney in 2019.
- Production companies: Fox 2000 Pictures, Dune Entertainment, Walden Media, Mark Johnson Productions. Distributed by 20th Century Fox.
- Produced by Mark Johnson, Andrew Adamson and Philip Steuer (infobox). Cinematography Dante Spinotti; edited by Rick Shaine; music by David Arnold.
- Running time 113 minutes. Countries: United Kingdom, United States. Language English.
- Budget given in the infobox as "$140–155 million"; the body says the film "was officially budgeted at $140 million, although some estimates put the cost at $155 million".
- Box office given in the infobox as $415.6 million; the box office section says "The film grossed $415.7 million worldwide, including $104.4 million in North America as well as $311.3 million in other territories."
- Release dates in the infobox: November 30, 2010 (Royal Film Performance); December 9, 2010 (United Kingdom); December 10, 2010 (United States).
- It is the only film in the series to be released in 3D.
- Set "three Narnian years after the events of Prince Caspian"; the plot section says "Three Narnian years and one Earth year after the events of Prince Caspian".

## Cast

- Georgie Henley (Lucy Pevensie), Skandar Keynes (Edmund Pevensie), Ben Barnes (King Caspian X) and Tilda Swinton (Jadis, the White Witch) reprise their roles from the second film, with Will Poulter joining as Eustace Scrubb.
- Simon Pegg voices Reepicheep; Pegg replaced Eddie Izzard because director Michael Apted thought his voice "is more mature and serious" than Izzard's. Bill Nighy was originally announced as Izzard's replacement, but the studio thought his voice sounded too old.
- Liam Neeson voices Aslan. Laura Brent plays Lilliandil - the name of Ramandu's Daughter is not given in the novel, so producer Douglas Gresham coined "Lilliandil".
- Others: Gary Sweet (Lord Drinian), Shane Rangi (Tavros the Minotaur), Morgan Evans (Randy the Faun), Steven Rooke (Nausus the Faun), Tony Nixon (1st Mate, Rynelf), Bille Brown (Coriakin), Terry Norris (Lord Bern), Bruce Spence (Lord Rhoop), Arabella Morton (Gael), Arthur Angel (Rhince), Nathaniel Parker (Caspian IX), David Vallon (Governor Gumpas), Michael Foster (Gumpas's money collector), Colin Moody (Pug), Roy Billing (Chief Dufflepud).
- Cameos: William Moseley (Peter Pevensie), Anna Popplewell (Susan Pevensie), and Douglas Gresham as a slave buyer - "Douglas Gresham is the stepson of C. S. Lewis and has made cameo appearances in all three Narnia films, all of which he produced."

## Home media

- 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment released the film on Blu-ray and DVD on April 8, 2011, as a single-disc DVD, a two-disc DVD double pack, a single-disc Blu-ray, and a three-disc Blu-ray with DVD and Digital Copy.
- Extras on the two-disc DVD and three-disc Blu-ray include an animated short "The Untold adventures of the Dawn Treader", a guide to the Dawn Treader, Narnian discovery featurettes, four Fox Movie Channel featurettes, 5 minutes of deleted scenes, eight international music videos, a sword game, five island explorations, the behind-the-scenes featurettes "The Epic Continues", "Portal to Narnia: A Painting Comes to Life" and "Good vs. Evil: Battle on the Sea", and a visual effects progression reel.
- The 3D Blu-ray was released in the U.S. on August 30, 2011. Walden Media President Micheal Flaherty said Fox and Disney home entertainment were developing a collector's-edition box set of the first three films.
- The film became available for streaming on Disney+ on October 9, 2020, following Disney's 2019 acquisition of 20th Century Fox.

## Contradictions inside the page

- Worldwide gross: the infobox says $415.6 million and the lead repeats "$415.6 million worldwide"; the box office section says "$415.7 million worldwide".
- Screenwriting order: the Development section says "Steven Knight wrote the script following a draft by Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely", while the Writing section says "Michael Petroni was hired to rewrite the script with Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely, following a draft written by Richard LaGravenese and Steven Knight."
- Release dates: the infobox and lead give a UK release of December 9, 2010, while the Release section says "It had its major release in Asia and Australia on December 2, 2010, and in North America and Europe on December 10, 2010."
- Producers: the infobox lists Mark Johnson, Andrew Adamson and Philip Steuer, while the Development section says Andrew Adamson "opted to produce, with Mark Johnson, Perry Moore, and Douglas Gresham".

wikis.title: Plot of The Voyage of the Dawn Treader (2010)
wikis.summary: The film's story as the article summarises it, from the painting that pulls the children into Narnia to Aslan's farewell at the world's end.
wikis.body:
- Three Narnian years and one Earth year after Prince Caspian, Edmund and Lucy Pevensie stay with their cousin Eustace Scrubb while Peter and Susan are in America as World War II rages; Edmund is too young to enlist in His Majesty's Armed Forces.
- A painting of a ship transports Edmund, Lucy and Eustace into an ocean in Narnia, where the Dawn Treader rescues them. Caspian invites them on a voyage to rescue the seven Lords of Narnia whom his uncle Miraz exiled.
- In the Lone Islands Caspian and Edmund are imprisoned and Lucy and Eustace sold as slaves; a lost lord reveals that unsold slaves are sacrificed to a green mist. Caspian outlaws the slave trade, appoints the lord governor and receives his sword, one of seven given to the lords by Aslan.
- Lucy is abducted by invisible Dufflepuds and enters the manor of the magician Coriakin, who tells the crew to lay the lords' swords at Aslan's Table on Ramandu's island but warns they will be tested. Lucy recites a beauty incantation and dreams she is Susan, in a world where neither Lucy nor Narnia exists; Aslan chides her for her self-doubt.
- Another sword is recovered from a pool that turns anything it touches into gold. Eustace steals cursed treasure and is transformed into a dragon; Reepicheep befriends him and he becomes useful to the crew.
- At Aslan's Table three lost lords lie in enchanted sleep and one sword is missing. A star descends and becomes Ramandu's daughter Lilliandil, who guides them to the Dark Island, where they find the last lord. The mist uses Edmund's fear to create a sea serpent; the panicked lord wounds Eustace with the last sword and Aslan restores Eustace to a boy for his self-sacrifice, sending him to Ramandu's island with the sword.
- The mist appears to Edmund as Jadis, the White Witch. Eustace places the last sword, the swords unleash their magic, and Edmund, using Peter's sword, slays the sea serpent, waking the three lords. Freeing the sacrificed slaves destroys the Dark Island's mist.
- At a mysterious shore before a massive wave, Aslan says his country lies beyond and those who go can never return. Caspian's duty as king holds him back; Reepicheep goes. Aslan tells Edmund and Lucy they are now too old to return, tells Eustace he may return one day, and encourages them to know him in their world "by another name".
- Back in the bedroom, Eustace hears his mother announce that Jill Pole has come to visit.

wikis.title: Development, writing and filming, including Disney's exit
wikis.summary: How the film changed director, budget, studio and shooting location between 2007 and 2009, and what the script and effects teams changed from the book.
wikis.body:
## Development

- Michael Apted took over as director from Andrew Adamson, who opted to produce. Richard Taylor, Isis Mussenden and Howard Berger continued on production design and practical effects; visual effects supervisor Jim Rygiel, composer David Arnold and cinematographer Dante Spinotti were newcomers to the series.
- When Apted signed on in June 2007, filming was set to begin in January 2008 for a May 1, 2009 release, shooting in Malta then Prague and Iceland.
- Disney then delayed the release to May 7, 2010 "in consideration of the challenging schedules for [its] young actors", moving filming to October 2008. Johnson rescheduled the shoot to Playas de Rosarito, Baja California (Mexico), where two thirds would be shot in the water tank used for Titanic and Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World; filming was also scheduled for Australia. Disney and Walden grew concerned over safety in Mexico, and Australian officials at Warner Roadshow Studios in Queensland offered to base the whole shoot there.
- Disney announced on December 24, 2008 that it would no longer co-produce. Disney and Walden disputed the budget after Prince Caspian grossed far less than The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe: "Disney wanted to limit it to $100 million, whereas Walden wanted a $140 million budget, of which Disney would only need to provide half." Disney also feared the budget would grow during filming and post-production; the Los Angeles Times reported "creative differences".
- Columbia Pictures, Universal, Paramount, Warner Bros. and 20th Century Fox were in negotiations; in January 2009 it was announced 20th Century Fox would replace Walt Disney Pictures as distributor while Disney retained rights to the first two. Producer Mark Johnson said "we made some mistakes with Prince Caspian and I don't want to make them again".

## Writing

- Michael Petroni was hired to rewrite the script with Markus and McFeely, following a draft by Richard LaGravenese and Steven Knight (the Development section instead says Knight wrote the script following a Markus and McFeely draft).
- Apted said the story's episodic and disconnected nature needed revision - the Dark Island, the Sea Serpent and Eustace material. Combining Dawn Treader with The Silver Chair was discussed, as the BBC had combined Dawn Treader and Prince Caspian; some elements were borrowed from The Silver Chair, where Narnians are held hostage and rescued. "The author's estate did not initially receive the change well, but it gained favor after review."
- Eustace has a greater role as a dragon than in the book, towing the ship and attacking the sea serpent. The film omits Aslan peeling Eustace's dragon skin off in layers and the old dragon dying next to its hoard. Walden President Micheal Flaherty said "people don't earn grace; they receive it once they are humbled and aware of their need."

## Filming and effects

- Unit publicist Ernie Malik confirmed filming began on July 27, 2009 on location in Queensland, Australia; at Village Roadshow Studios in August and September 2009, with exterior ship shots at Cleveland Point and the Gold Coast Seaway in September 2009. Additional shots at the Southport School on the Gold Coast, and around White Island off the coast of Tauranga, New Zealand.
- Gore Verbinski and Peter Weir recommended Apted not shoot on water, so a giant Dawn Treader was built on a gimbal at the end of Cleveland Point's peninsula jutting into Moreton Bay; the 145-tonne (160-ton) boat could be rotated through 360 degrees to keep sun angles consistent.
- 1,400 special effects shots were made - more than The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe's 800 and fewer than Prince Caspian's 1,500. Angus Bickerton was lead visual effects supervisor; Jim Rygiel senior visual effects supervisor.
- Moving Picture Company, Framestore CFC, The Senate VFX, Cinesite and The Mill worked on effects. Moving Picture did dragon Eustace (scheduled for around 200 shots) and the Dawn Treader, and revised Reepicheep with saturated colour, bushier eyebrows and ear hair and wirier whiskers. Framestore revised Aslan to a more realistic, darker-maned lion and created 16 different dufflepuds. The Senate did the opening shot of King's College, Cambridge and the star effect on Liliandil. Cinesite did the Dark Island. Fugitive Studios did the end titles using original Pauline Baynes drawings, included partly as an acknowledgment to Baynes, who died in August 2008.

## Music

- David Arnold scored the film with themes composed by Harry Gregson-Williams; it was Arnold's fourth collaboration with Apted after The World Is Not Enough, Enough and Amazing Grace. Scoring sessions took place in September and work was completed on October 8, 2010.
- The original song "There's a Place for Us", written by Carrie Underwood, David Hodges and Hillary Lindsey and recorded by Underwood, was released November 16, 2010 exclusively on iTunes, then on December 7, 2010 by Sony Masterworks.

wikis.title: Conversion to 3D
wikis.summary: The decision to convert the film to 3D in post-production, who did it and why.
wikis.body:
- After the success of the 3D release of Avatar, 20th Century Fox announced in February 2010 that the film would be released in Digital 3D and RealD 3D formats - the first Narnia film with a 3D release.
- Walden had previous 3D experience with James Cameron's documentaries Ghosts of the Abyss and Aliens of the Deep, and Journey to the Center of the Earth with New Line Cinema.
- The filmmakers discussed shooting in 3D during principal photography but decided to shoot with two-dimensional cameras to save costs. Prime Focus Group was hired in June 2010 to convert the film in post-production.
- Joe Dante said Apted was at first skeptical: "If I was gonna do a 3D movie, I would have done it differently"; he later was excited after seeing progress. It was Apted's first 3D film.
- Apted, defending the conversion: "Well, the thing about us is that we have a long time. We decided in February [2010] to make 'The Dawn Treader' a 3D movie, so we had nine months to do it. Some of these other films put 3D in very quickly. I believe something like Clash of the Titans had about eight weeks. So, we have had time to think about it, so it hasn't been a rush. I think we'll get very good value out of it. They won't see anything cheap or nasty. Rest assured of that."
- Johnson later said the 3D release was to help the film at the box office against Tangled, Tron: Legacy and Yogi Bear, which were released in 3D.

wikis.title: Marketing, tie-in books and video games
wikis.summary: The roughly $100 million promotional campaign, the Dawn Treader replica ship, tie-in publishing, the mobile game and the cancelled console game.
wikis.body:
## Promotion

- In addition to its production budget, Fox and Walden spent "around $100 million to promote the film around the world".
- Late November 2009: three stills released on Facebook. February 2010: Narnia.com returned after a nine-month hiatus with set reports; the full site with the first trailer opened June 17, 2010.
- The first promotional banner was presented at the 2010 Cannes Film Festival, followed by a teaser poster in May 2010.
- A Christian Narnia conference was held June 3-6, 2010 at Taylor University in Upland, Indiana, with Apted and producers giving commentary and a 5-minute "super trailer".
- Franklin Graham's Samaritan's Purse ran an international relief campaign, Operation Narnia, donating relief goods to children from July to December 2010.
- The historic caravel ship the Matthew was transformed into a replica of the Dawn Treader and sailed from the Atlantic Ocean to the English Channel in August 2010; the National Maritime Museum in Cornwall made it available to the public from August 28 to August 30, 2010.
- Trailers: first official trailer online June 17, 2010, attached to Toy Story 3 on June 18, 2010 and Alpha and Omega on September 17, 2010, and released on the Diary of a Wimpy Kid DVD; international poster and trailer October 7, 2010; third trailer November 9, 2010.
- To promote the release, ABC and Disney Channel broadcast The Lion, The Witch and the Wardrobe on December 11, 13 and 14, and Syfy screened Prince Caspian on December 12 and 13.
- Apted on the film's heart: "It's a story that has English roots, but it's relatable to every child on the planet because it's about growing up, finding yourself, coming to terms with yourself, and knowing what your values are."

## Books

- HarperCollins published new editions of The Voyage of the Dawn Treader and The Chronicles of Narnia on October 26, 2010 with new film images, plus a Chronicles edition commemorating the 60th anniversary of The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe the same day.
- A movie storybook and other tie-ins came from HarperChildrens, Walden Pond Press and Zondervan. On November 12, 2010 HarperCollins released an enhanced multimedia e-book of The Voyage of the Dawn Treader for platforms including iPad and Android.
- Group Publishing released three previews in its vacation Bible school kit "Fun for the Whole Family Hour" on August 19, 2010; Grace Hill Media released "Narnia Faith" for ministers and pastors on October 12, 2010.

## Games

- A mobile video game, The Chronicles of Narnia: The Voyage of the Dawn Treader, developed by Fox Digital Entertainment, was released in 2010 - a sequel to the Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe and Prince Caspian movie games. The player becomes King Caspian, Lucy or Edmund; gameplay includes sword combat, bosses, simple puzzles and rowboat sections, with health and stamina replenished from bottles, jars and treasure chests.
- Will Wilson of Pocket Gamer gave it 6/10: "The Voyage of the Dawn Treader is a solid movie tie-in that doesn't desecrate the license and will please fans, but it doesn't offer up anything to get pulses racing either".
- In early 2009 Destructoid reported Nihilistic Software was making a console game, assumed for a December 2010 release; less than a year later it was revealed the game was cancelled when Walt Disney Pictures (and Disney Interactive) left the Narnia project in late 2008/early 2009.

wikis.title: Release, critical reception and box office
wikis.summary: The Royal Film Performance premiere, mixed reviews, and the film's takings in North America and overseas.
wikis.body:
## Release

- World premiere November 30, 2010 in London as the 64th Royal Film Performance in Leicester Square - the first time the Royal Film Performance was unveiled in Digital 3D and the second time an opening film bowed at the event, after The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe in 2005. Attendees included Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip.
- Pre-release gala on December 8 in Knoxville, Tennessee, followed by a North American premiere in Louisville, Kentucky on December 9, 2010.
- Originally set for May 2009 under Disney; Fox announced a December 2010 date because it felt Narnia would do better during the holidays. Major release in Asia and Australia December 2, 2010, and in North America and Europe December 10, 2010.

## Critical reception

- Rotten Tomatoes: 49% positive from 168 reviews, average rating 5.7/10. Consensus: "Its leisurely, businesslike pace won't win the franchise many new fans, but Voyage of the Dawn Treader restores some of the Narnia franchise's lost luster with strong performances and impressive special effects."
- Metacritic: score of 53% based on 33 reviews, "mixed to average". CinemaScore opening-weekend polls gave an average grade of A-.
- Roger Ebert (Chicago Sun-Times) gave three stars out of four: "This is a rip-snorting adventure fantasy for families, especially the younger members who are not insistent on continuity."
- Roger Moore (Orlando Sentinel) gave three out of four, calling it "a worthy challenger to the far more popular Harry Potter pictures". The Guardian said it "arrives with confidence and bravado intact. ... and arguably the most Tolkien-esque of the Narnia books". IGN called it "a solid sequel that might even surpass the first entry as the best in the series for some fans".
- The Arizona Republic's Kerry Lengel: "The best thing about the film is neither the top-notch CGI nor the shallow moral lessons but the performance of Georgie Henley as Lucy as well as the performance of her and Edmund's insufferable cousin Eustace Scrubb." Luke Y. Thompson (E! Online) praised Henley, Keynes, Poulter, Pegg and Bille Brown.
- Christian reviewers responded well, keying on the closing scene in which Aslan tells Lucy he is in her world "under another name".

## Commercial analysis and box office

- Brandon Gray of Box Office Mojo: "There certainly will be an audience for this picture, I just don't think it is going to restore the franchise to its former glory."
- Apted on courting Christian audiences: "They got a little careless by taking the faith group for granted—and by neglecting it paid the price. We realized we couldn't make the same mistake. We've got to sell the film to everybody." Fox Filmed Entertainment co-chairman Tom Rothman: "We think this is a tremendously undervalued asset; we believe there is great life in the franchise."
- $415.7 million worldwide: $104.4 million in North America and $311.3 million in other territories; 12th-highest-grossing film worldwide of 2010 and Fox's highest-grossing film of that year.
- Opened in 3,555 North American theaters on December 10, 2010: $8.3 million opening day (against $23 million for The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe and $19.4 million for Prince Caspian) and a #1 opening weekend of $24.0 million (against $65.6 million and $55.0 million).
- Second weekend down 48% to $12.4 million (third behind Tron: Legacy and Yogi Bear); third weekend down 24% to $9.5 million; New Year's weekend up 8% to $10.3 million.
- On January 22, 2011, its 44th day in theaters, it became Fox's first film to gross $100 million in the US and Canada since Alvin and the Chipmunks: The Squeakquel in December 2009, and the slowest Narnia film to reach $100 million there (against nine days and thirteen days).
- Overseas: limited opening weekend December 3-5, 2010 in 9 territories earned $11.9 million (4th). Wide opening December 10-12 in 58 countries topped the box office with $65.8 million, overseas total $79.8 million. Biggest opening market Russia with $10.9 million including previews (best start for the franchise); best Narnia openings in Mexico ($7.1 million) and South Korea ($5.3 million); UK opening only $3.9 million.
- It made GBP 14,317,168 ($23,650,534) at the UK box office, passing Prince Caspian's GBP 11,653,554 on the weekend ending January 9, 2011.
- Second overseas weekend down 53% to $31.2 million ($125.2 million total); Christmas weekend $23.1 million (fifth); New Year's weekend $19.3 million (sixth), $210.2 million overseas total; fifth weekend $18.4 million from 53 markets, including a $6.3 million China opening against Prince Caspian's $3.9 million. On its 12th weekend (February 25-27) it surpassed Prince Caspian's $278 million foreign gross when it opened in Japan with $6.6 million.

wikis.title: The cancelled Silver Chair sequel and the Netflix reboot
wikis.summary: What the article says about the film series after Dawn Treader - the abandoned Silver Chair adaptation and Netflix's Narnia deal.
wikis.body:
- On March 22, 2011 it was announced that an adaptation of The Silver Chair would be the next film in the series; the C. S. Lewis Estate was in final negotiations and had yet to confirm a release date or screenwriter.
- In the fall of 2011, co-producer Douglas Gresham said Walden Media no longer owned the rights to produce another Narnia film, and that if another were made it would not be for another three or four years. The lead states Walden Media's contract with the C. S. Lewis estate expired in the fall of 2011.
- On October 3, 2018 Netflix and the C. S. Lewis Company announced a multi-year agreement to develop a new series of film and TV adaptations of The Chronicles of Narnia; this was interpreted as superseding the Silver Chair plans.
- On June 12, 2019 Matthew Aldrich was announced as creative architect overseeing Narnia development for Netflix. In May 2020 Douglas Gresham said he had not been contacted by Netflix in some time. In July 2023 it was announced Greta Gerwig had been hired to write and direct at least two Narnia films for Netflix.
- The lead says the series "would instead be rebooted with the Netflix film Narnia: The Magician's Nephew".
