wikis.title: Godzilla vs. Kong (2021 film)
wikis.summary: The English Wikipedia article on Godzilla vs. Kong, the 2021 Legendary Monsterverse film directed by Adam Wingard, covering its credits, plot, cast, production, contested budget, HBO Max release and box office.
wikis.body:
## The film

- *Godzilla vs. Kong* is "a 2021 American monster film directed by Adam Wingard", produced by Legendary Pictures and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures; a sequel to *Kong: Skull Island* (2017) and *Godzilla: King of the Monsters* (2019) and the fourth Monsterverse film, the 36th *Godzilla* film and the 12th *King Kong* film.
- Screenplay by Eric Pearson and Max Borenstein, story by Terry Rossio, Michael Dougherty and Zach Shields; music by Tom Holkenborg; running time 113 minutes.
- Starring Alexander Skarsgård, Millie Bobby Brown, Rebecca Hall, Brian Tyree Henry, Shun Oguri, Eiza González, Julian Dennison, Lance Reddick, Kyle Chandler and Demián Bichir, with Kaylee Hottle as Jia.
- Released internationally March 24, 2021 and in the United States March 31, 2021, simultaneously in theatres and on HBO Max, where it streamed exclusively for a month. Japan's release, set for May 14, 2021, was postponed indefinitely on April 30, 2021 and the film opened there July 2, 2021.
- It grossed $470 million worldwide - $101 million in the United States and Canada and $369 million elsewhere - against a break-even point *Variety* put at $330 million, making it "the eighth-highest-grossing film of 2021". It was "the most successful launch title in HBO Max's history until it was overtaken by *Mortal Kombat*."
- Reviews were generally positive: Rotten Tomatoes 76% from 391 reviews (average 6.4/10), Metacritic 59/100 from 57 critics, CinemaScore "A".
- A sequel, *Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire*, also directed by Wingard, was released March 29, 2024 in the United States.

## Production

Announced in October 2015, when the release was "at the time targeted for a May 29, 2020" date. A writers' room led by Terry Rossio was assembled in March 2017; Wingard was announced as director in May 2017. Principal photography began November 12, 2018 in Hawaii and Australia under the working title *Apex*, resumed at Village Roadshow Studios on the Gold Coast in January 2019 for 26 more weeks, and wrapped in April 2019 after shooting in Hong Kong. MPC, Scanline VFX and Weta Digital split the film's "980 complicated effects shots" by location. Wingard said in April 2021 there was enough footage for a five-hour version but that he saw no reason for a director's cut.

## Release conflict

*The Hollywood Reporter* reported in November 2020 that Netflix had offered $200-250 million for the film, but WarnerMedia blocked the deal for its own HBO Max release. Legendary, financiers and backend talent objected and legal action was considered before an agreement was reported in January 2021.

## Contradiction the page records

The article's own footnote sets the reported production budgets against each other: The Numbers reported $155 million; in December 2020 *Variety* reported $160 million and TheWrap $165 million; in January 2021 both *The Hollywood Reporter* and *Deadline Hollywood* stated $200 million, as did Comingsoon.net in February 2021. The infobox gives the range "$155-200 million", while the body says "Legendary financed $120 million while Warner Bros. financed $40 million", with a further $70 million in promotion reported by *Forbes*.

The second part of the capture is the citation list, cited sources (including Wallace 2021, *Godzilla vs. Kong: The Art of the Ultimate Battle Royale*), external links, navigation boxes and categories; it states no publication or last-updated date.

wikis.title: Godzilla vs. Kong (2021 film): plot, cast, production, release and reception
wikis.summary: Part 1 of the English Wikipedia article on Godzilla vs. Kong, covering the 2021 Monsterverse film's credits and infobox figures, plot, cast, production, music, marketing, theatrical and HBO Max release, box office, reviews and awards.
wikis.body:
## The film

- *Godzilla vs. Kong* is "a 2021 American monster film directed by Adam Wingard", produced by Legendary Pictures and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures. It is a sequel to *Kong: Skull Island* (2017) and *Godzilla: King of the Monsters* (2019), the fourth film in Legendary's Monsterverse, the 36th film in the *Godzilla* franchise and the 12th in the *King Kong* franchise.
- Screenplay by Eric Pearson and Max Borenstein; story by Terry Rossio, Michael Dougherty and Zach Shields; based on Godzilla and Mechagodzilla by Toho Co., Ltd. Produced by Thomas Tull, Jon Jashni, Brian Rogers, Mary Parent, Alex Garcia and Eric McLeod.
- Starring Alexander Skarsgård, Millie Bobby Brown, Rebecca Hall, Brian Tyree Henry, Shun Oguri, Eiza González, Julian Dennison, Lance Reddick, Kyle Chandler and Demián Bichir. Brown and Chandler reprise their roles from the previous *Godzilla* film.
- Cinematography Ben Seresin; edited by Josh Schaeffer; music by Tom Holkenborg. Distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures worldwide and Toho-Towa in Japan.
- Release dates: March 24, 2021 (international) and March 31, 2021 (United States). Running time 113 minutes. Country United States; language English.
- Infobox budget "$155-200 million"; box office $470 million.
- Announced in October 2015; writers' room assembled March 2017; Wingard announced as director May 2017; principal photography began November 2018 in Hawaii, Australia and Hong Kong and wrapped in April 2019.
- Delayed from a November 2020 release because of the COVID-19 pandemic. Released in the United States on HBO Max simultaneously with theatres.
- "It broke several pandemic box office records, and grossed $470 million worldwide, against a production budget between $155-200 million and a break-even point of $330 million, making it the eighth-highest-grossing film of 2021."
- "The film was a streaming hit, becoming the most successful launch title in HBO Max's history until it was overtaken by *Mortal Kombat*."
- A sequel, *Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire*, also directed by Wingard, was released on March 29, 2024.

## Plot

Set five years after King Ghidorah was defeated by Godzilla. Kong is monitored by Monarch inside a giant dome on Skull Island, which is struck by a perpetual storm. Jia, the last Iwi native and deaf adopted daughter of Kong expert Ilene Andrews, communicates with Kong using American Sign Language. Apex Cybernetics CEO Walter Simmons recruits Hollow Earth theorist Nathan Lind to lead a search for a power source, using HEAVs (Hollow Earth Anti-gravitational Vehicles). Godzilla attacks the convoy carrying Kong; Kong is airlifted to a Hollow Earth entrance in Antarctica. Bernie Hayes, Madison Russell and Josh Valentine discover Apex's Mechagodzilla, telepathically controlled by Ren Serizawa through neural networks from the severed head of Ghidorah. Godzilla defeats Kong in Hong Kong; Mechagodzilla, possessed by Ghidorah's consciousness, kills Walter and overpowers Godzilla until Kong, revived by Lind detonating the HEAV on his chest, destroys it with an axe charged by Godzilla's atomic breath. Monarch later establishes an observation post in the Hollow Earth, where Kong rules.

## The budget disagreement the page itself records

A footnote lists the reported production budgets side by side:

- The Numbers reported $155 million.
- In December 2020 *Variety* reported $160 million, while TheWrap reported $165 million.
- In January 2021 both *The Hollywood Reporter* and *Deadline Hollywood* stated $200 million; in February 2021 Comingsoon.net also noted $200 million.
- The body separately says "Legendary financed $120 million while Warner Bros. financed $40 million", and *Forbes* reported the film cost $70 million to promote.

## Other figures

- *Variety* reported the film needed to gross at least $330 million to break even; *Deadline Hollywood* estimated a net profit of $96.4 million.
- Worldwide gross $470 million: $101 million in the United States and Canada, $369 million in other territories.
- Home video: $13.2 million on DVD and $22.8 million on Blu-ray, "totaling $36 million in domestic video sales" in the United States and Canada.
- 980 "complicated effects shots".

wikis.title: Godzilla vs. Kong cast and characters
wikis.summary: The principal cast, their characters and what the actors and producers said about them.
wikis.body:
- **Alexander Skarsgård as Dr. Nathan Lind**, a Monarch geologist and chief cartographer who charts the Hollow Earth mission. Skarsgård called him a reluctant hero who is "not an alpha, bad-ass" and "thrown into this very dangerous situation and is definitely not equipped for it", and an homage to 1980s films like *Indiana Jones*, *Romancing the Stone*, *Lethal Weapon* and *Die Hard*. He researched the Hollow Earth and learned American Sign Language to communicate with Kaylee Hottle.
- **Millie Bobby Brown as Madison Russell**, daughter of Mark and the late Emma Russell. Brown described the film as a coming-of-age story in which Madison has "grown-up" and become more "independent". Producer Alex Garcia called Madison the "advocate for Godzilla in this film".
- **Rebecca Hall as Dr. Ilene Andrews**, a Monarch anthropological linguist and Jia's adoptive mother. Hall called her participation "overwhelming" as her first project after her pregnancy but "thrilling", and described Ilene as "the Jane Goodall of Kong".
- **Brian Tyree Henry as Bernie Hayes**, an Apex technician turned conspiracy theorist and whistleblower. Henry called him a "crackpot" with "heart" and "loyalty", said the death of Bernie's wife shaped him, and said "I always refer to Bernie as Anonymous. He can see the injustices, but no one really listens to him."
- **Shun Oguri as Ren Serizawa**, son of the late Ishirō Serizawa and Apex's chief technology officer, the telepathic pilot of Mechagodzilla. Wingard said the character was underwritten for lack of time and that leaving him a mystery was interesting.
- **Eiza González as Maia Simmons**, a top-tier Apex executive and Walter's daughter; she described the film as "slightly comedic".
- **Julian Dennison as Josh Valentine**, Madison's friend and "tech wingman"; he screen-tested with Brown using scenes from *Romeo and Juliet*.
- **Lance Reddick as Guillerman**, the director of Monarch, appearing in only two brief scenes after a boardroom scene was cut.
- **Kyle Chandler as Dr. Mark Russell**, Monarch's deputy director of special projects.
- **Demián Bichir as Walter Simmons**, CEO and founder of Apex Cybernetics, secretly creating Mechagodzilla. Garcia said he is not necessarily a villain but "a very complex character who believes he's doing the right thing".
- **Kaylee Hottle as Jia**, a young deaf orphaned Iwi native bonded with Kong.
- Also Hakeem Kae-Kazim as Admiral Wilcox, Ronny Chieng as Jay Wayne, John Pirruccello as Horace and Chris Chalk as Ben. Allan Henry provided performance capture for Kong; animation supervisor Eric Petey provided Kong's full body and facial capture for the ocean battle. Zhang Ziyi and Jessica Henwick were cast but do not appear in the final cut, with Ziyi intended to reprise her *Godzilla: King of the Monsters* role.

wikis.title: Development and writing of Godzilla vs. Kong
wikis.summary: How the crossover was announced and developed, the 2017 writers' room and the rewrites.
wikis.body:
- September 2015: Legendary moved *Kong: Skull Island* from Universal to Warner Bros., sparking speculation the two monsters would appear together.
- October 2015: Legendary confirmed it would unite Godzilla and King Kong in *Godzilla vs. Kong*, "at the time targeted for a May 29, 2020, release", planning a shared franchise "centered around Monarch" that "brings together Godzilla and Legendary's King Kong in an ecosystem of other giant super-species, both classic and new". Producer Alex Garcia said "the idea is not to remake that movie" (*King Kong vs. Godzilla*).
- May 2017: Adam Wingard announced as director. He had previously been considered by Peter Jackson for an unproduced sequel to Jackson's 2005 *King Kong*. Offered the project by Mary Parent, Wingard said "I jumped at it immediately."
- Wingard watched every *Godzilla* and *King Kong* film, and had pictured the final battle in a "synthwave-style futuristic city backdrop" before receiving a script: "How can we get these two monsters fighting on a synthwave album cover?" He cited the 1976 *King Kong* remake and *Godzilla vs. Destoroyah* as touchstones for empathy, and *Godzilla vs. Mothra*, *Godzilla vs. Destoroyah* and *Shin Godzilla* as inspiration for scale.
- Financing: "Legendary financed $120 million while Warner Bros. financed $40 million."
- March 2017: Legendary assembled a writers room led by Terry Rossio, with J. D. Payne, Patrick McKay, Lindsey Beer, Cat Vasko, T. S. Nowlin, Jack Paglen and J. Michael Straczynski. Rossio wrote a "detailed treatment" green-lit at first-draft stage and said of the monsters, "Kong calls to mind the dangers inherent in unfettered emotion, while Godzilla can be seen to represent the fundamental power of nature. That puts them on pretty equal footing."
- Michael Dougherty and Zach Shields provided rewrites; Eric Pearson and Max Borenstein streamlined the story. Borenstein had originally written Mechagodzilla into *Godzilla: King of the Monsters*, where Dougherty scrapped the character.
- In April 2022, Eiza González revealed much of the original story, including an alternate storyline for her character, was changed during post-production, with Jessica Henwick's character cut entirely.

wikis.title: Casting, filming and post-production
wikis.summary: Casting announcements from 2017 to 2018, the Hawaii, Australia and Hong Kong shoot, and the visual effects work.
wikis.body:
## Casting

- June 2017: Zhang Ziyi joined the Monsterverse with a reportedly "pivotal" role in both films, though she ultimately starred only in *King of the Monsters*.
- June 2018: Julian Dennison cast; Millie Bobby Brown and Kyle Chandler set to reprise their roles. Legendary sent an offer to Frances McDormand. July 2018: Danai Gurira reported in early talks.
- October 2018: Brian Tyree Henry, Demián Bichir, Alexander Skarsgård, Eiza González and Rebecca Hall added. November 2018: Jessica Henwick, Shun Oguri (his Hollywood debut) and Lance Reddick cast. Neither Gurira nor Henwick appeared in the finished film.
- YouTuber and filmmaker James Rolfe was offered a potential cameo by Wingard, but production pressures and the birth of his second daughter meant it could not be arranged.

## Filming

- Principal photography began November 12, 2018 in Hawaii and Australia under the working title *Apex*, expected to end in February 2019; production had initially been slated to begin October 1, 2018.
- Hawaii locations: the USS *Missouri*, Manoa Falls and Downtown Honolulu; a camp on the Kalanianaole Highway closed the Lānaʻi Lookout parking until November 21.
- January 2019: filming resumed at Village Roadshow Studios on the Gold Coast, Queensland for an additional 26 weeks. Australian locations included Miami State High School and parts of Brisbane - the Newstead suburb, the Chinatown Mall in Fortitude Valley and the Wickham Terrace Car Park.
- April 2019: Wingard confirmed via Instagram that Australian filming had wrapped, and revealed Hong Kong as one of the final shooting locations and that principal photography had wrapped.
- Setbacks Wingard described: a viral outbreak (not COVID-19-related) that affected 40 percent of the crew for a week, a camera operator who broke his foot on the third day, and a spider bite that sent Ben Seresin to hospital. Village Roadshow gave them six to seven stages, forcing constant set rotation.

## Post-production

- Co-producer Tamara Kent guided the post-production schedule. Moving Picture Company (MPC), Scanline VFX and Weta Digital created the visual effects; dividing work by monster "didn't make sense" because "they would need to be created by the same team in shots where they fought. So we divided things by location." MPC animated parts of the Hong Kong sequence, Weta all of the Hollow Earth sequences, and Scanline a majority of the Hong Kong sequence and all water environments.
- Effects were originally due December 2019; the delay to a then-November 2020 release gave more time for the film's "980 complicated effects shots".
- In April 2021 Wingard said there was enough footage for a potential five-hour version but that he did not see any reason to do a director's cut: "For better or worse, this is my movie."

wikis.title: Godzilla vs. Kong music
wikis.summary: Tom Holkenborg's score, the soundtrack release and the songs used.
wikis.body:
- June 2020: Tom Holkenborg announced as composer. He had met Wingard in 2018, having recreationally written *Godzilla* music years earlier as a fan; Wingard was "totally in love" with the tweaked material.
- Holkenborg requested a bass drum roughly ten feet in diameter; the builder could only scale it down to eight feet. Lower brass and big tympanis were used to emphasize Godzilla's power, and Holkenborg wanted Godzilla's theme slow and sluggish.
- Wingard felt it was "insincere" to repurpose Akira Ifukube's themes because he associated them with Toho's Godzilla, wanting themes unique to the Monsterverse's Godzilla.
- As with Legendary's previous *Godzilla* trailers, György Ligeti's "Requiem" was used, followed by "Here We Go" by Chris Classic. "The Air That I Breathe" by The Hollies was used in the credits scene.
- The soundtrack was released by WaterTower Music on March 26, 2021.
- For the Japanese release, Man with a Mission contributed the track "Into the Deep"; Wingard said "I'm thrilled that an inspiring song from a groundbreaking band like Man with a Mission will be playing alongside the battle in Godzilla vs. Kong."

wikis.title: Marketing and the HBO Max release dispute
wikis.summary: Promotion from 2019 to 2021, the repeated release-date changes, and the Legendary-WarnerMedia conflict over the simultaneous streaming release.
wikis.body:
## Marketing

- May 2019: first promotional one-sheet poster revealed at the Licensing Expo. June 2019: Warner Bros. screened an early look to European exhibitors at CineEurope. August 2019: Disruptor Beam announced to develop a tie-in mobile game.
- December 2019: a brief clip shown during a Warner Bros. reel at Comic Con Experience, later leaked. January 2020: figure images leaked from the Hong Kong Toys & Games Fair.
- February 2020: Toho and Legendary announced the *Godzilla vs. Kong* Publishing Program - two graphic novels (one following Godzilla, one Kong), an art book, novelizations and a children's book - with licensees including Playmates Toys, Bioworld, Rubies, Funko, 60Out and the Virtual Reality Company.
- April 2020 and July 2020: further toy leaks, revealing Mechagodzilla and a new monster named Nozuki.
- The first full trailer was released January 24, 2021 and "became Warner Bros' biggest trailer debut, earning 25.6 million views in 24 hours on YouTube; 15.8 million from Warner's channel and an additional 9.8 million views from the studio's secondary channels."
- The film had "its first official NFT art release in collaboration with a major studio", and on April 7 *AEW Dynamite* held a special *Godzilla vs. Kong*-themed match. *Forbes* reported the film cost $70 million to promote.

## Release

- Released internationally beginning March 24, 2021, and in the United States on March 31 simultaneously in theatres and on HBO Max, where it streamed exclusively for a month. Regal Cinemas began a limited exhibition on reopening April 2, 2021.
- It had previously been scheduled for March 13, May 22, May 29 and November 20 in 2020, and later May 21, 2021, before the pandemic changes.
- Japan: scheduled for May 14, 2021 by Toho; Toho announced on April 30, 2021 that the Japanese release was postponed indefinitely due to COVID-19. Japanese premiere June 28, 2021; Japanese theatrical release July 2, 2021.
- February 2020: Warner Bros. hosted an unannounced test screening with a "mostly positive" response.
- November 2020: *The Hollywood Reporter* confirmed a streaming release was being considered; Netflix had offered $200-250 million but WarnerMedia blocked the deal in favour of HBO Max. In December 2020 Warner Bros. announced same-day theatrical and HBO Max releases for its 2021 tentpoles with one-month streaming access.
- *Variety* and *Deadline Hollywood* reported Legendary, financiers and talent with backend deals were displeased and that legal action was considered; *Deadline* later reported the film could keep its HBO Max release only if Warner Bros. matched Netflix's $250 million bid. In January 2021 *The Hollywood Reporter* said a legal battle was averted as the parties neared an agreement.
- Home media: digital May 21, 2021; DVD, Blu-ray, 3D Blu-ray and 4K Blu-ray June 15, 2021; re-added to HBO Max August 17, 2021.

wikis.title: Godzilla vs. Kong viewership and box office
wikis.summary: Streaming household figures and the film's opening and total grosses.
wikis.body:
## Viewership

- After the opening weekend Warner Bros. said the film had a "larger viewing audience than any other film or show on HBO Max since launch."
- Samba TV reported 3.6 million US households watched at least the first five minutes between March 31 and April 4, and 225,000 in the UK. It was watched in 5.1 million US households over the first 17 days and over 5.8 million by the end of its first 30 days.
- In January 2022 Akamai reported it was the most pirated film of 2021.

## Box office

- Grossed $101 million in the United States and Canada and $369 million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $470 million. *Variety* put the break-even point at $330 million; *Deadline Hollywood* estimated a net profit of $96.4 million.
- Released a week ahead of the US in 38 overseas countries, projected at around $70 million over five days. In China, projected at around $50 million, it made $21.5 million (RMB 140 million) on its first day.
- It debuted to $123.1 million worldwide, "the biggest worldwide opening of the pandemic for a Hollywood film". Largest markets: China ($69.2 million; RMB 450.5 million), Mexico ($6.5 million), Australia ($6.3 million), Russia ($5.9 million), Taiwan ($5.3 million), India ($4.9 million), Thailand ($3.3 million), South Korea ($2.8 million), Vietnam ($2.5 million), Malaysia ($2.1 million) and Spain ($1.7 million). Indonesia earned $850,000 (Rp. 12.3 billion).
- In the United States and Canada it was initially projected at around $23 million over five days, against around $68 million in a pre-COVID marketplace. It made $9.6 million from 2,409 theatres on its first day, "the best opening-day figure of the pandemic", $6.7 million on its second day, then $31.6 million in three days and $48.1 million over five from 3,064 theatres, "the best opening weekend of the pandemic".
- Second weekend $13.9 million, staying first and becoming the highest-grossing domestic release of the pandemic, passing *Tenet*'s $58.5 million. In the weekend ending June 20, 2021 it became the second film to cross $100 million at the US and Canadian box office during the pandemic, after *A Quiet Place Part II*.

wikis.title: Critical response and accolades
wikis.summary: Aggregate scores, named reviews, and the awards and nominations table.
wikis.body:
## Reviews

- "Generally positive reviews." Rotten Tomatoes: 76% of 391 critics' reviews positive, average rating 6.4/10, consensus "Delivering squarely on its title, Godzilla vs. Kong swats away character development and human drama to deliver all the spectacle you'd expect from giant monsters slugging it out." Metacritic: 59 out of 100 from 57 critics, "mixed or average". CinemaScore: average grade "A" (the highest of the Monsterverse); PostTrak: 86% positive, 74% would definitely recommend.
- Richard Roeper (*Chicago Sun-Times*), 3/4 stars: "Godzilla vs. Kong is the kind of movie you can pretty much forget about almost instantly after you've seen it—but it's also the kind of movie that makes you forget about everything else in your life while you're watching it."
- Jamie Graham (*Total Film*), 3/5: watching the monsters share the screen "for the first time since 1963's King Kong vs. Godzilla, in a series of expertly choreographed battles, packs real wallop".
- Alonso Duralde (TheWrap) said the franchise had "given up on everything but the monster fights". John Nugent (*Empire*), 2/5: "It just depends whether you're willing to sit through the toe-curlingly bad set-up that surrounds it." Jake Wilson (*The Age*), 2.5/5, said "Absolutely no sign of his old personality is evident here" of Wingard.
- The film ranks on Rotten Tomatoes' Best Science Fiction Movies of 2021.

## Accolades

- Honoured with the Seal of Authentic Representation from the Ruderman Family Foundation for Kaylee Hottle's role as Jia.
- Australian Effects & Animation Festival (August 23, 2021): Gold for Weta Digital, Feature Film - VFX; Silver for MPC Film, Feature Film - Sequence ("Hong Kong Battle").
- Saturn Awards (October 25, 2022): won Best Special/Visual Effects (John "D.J." Des Jardin, Bryan Hirota, Kevin Andrew Smith, Pier Lefebvre, Mike Meinardus); nominated Best Science Fiction Film.
- Chinese American Film Festival (November 5, 2021): won Most Popular US Film in China.
- Nominations included Las Vegas Film Critics Society (Best Visual Effects, Best Horror/Sci-Fi Film), Dragon Awards, Denver Film Critics Society, DiscussingFilm Critic Awards, Golden Schmoes (four categories including Best Action Sequence for "Godzilla & Kong vs Mechagodzilla"), Minnesota Film Critics Alliance, North Carolina Film Critics Association (Ken Hanke Memorial Tar Heel Award for Brian Tyree Henry), People's Choice Awards (The Action Movie of 2021), Portland Critics Association, three Visual Effects Society categories, two Hollywood Professional Association Awards and the Satellite Awards.

## Sequel

In March 2022 a sequel was announced to begin filming later that year on the Gold Coast and elsewhere in South East Queensland. In May 2022 Wingard was confirmed to return, with Dan Stevens cast in the lead and Hall, Henry and Hottle reprising their roles. *Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire* was released internationally on March 27, 2024 and in the United States on March 29, 2024.

wikis.title: Godzilla x Kong: Supernova (upcoming film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the upcoming Monsterverse film Godzilla x Kong: Supernova, directed by Grant Sputore and slated for 26 March 2027, covering its cast, development, filming locations and release plans.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- "Godzilla x Kong: Supernova is an upcoming American monster film directed by Grant Sputore. Produced by Legendary Pictures and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures, it is a sequel to Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire, and will serve as the sixth film in Legendary's Monsterverse franchise, as well as the 40th film in the Godzilla franchise and the 14th film in the King Kong franchise."
- Stars Kaitlyn Dever, Dan Stevens, Jack O'Connell, Alycia Debnam-Carey, Matthew Modine, Delroy Lindo and Sam Neill, "with Stevens reprising his role from The New Empire".
- The article carries a maintenance banner: "This article may require copy editing... (July 2026)".

## Infobox

- Directed by Grant Sputore; written by David Callaham; based on Godzilla and SpaceGodzilla by Toho Co. Ltd.
- Produced by Mary Parent, Thomas Tull, Alex Garcia, Jon Jashni. Cinematography Dan Mindel. Edited by Josh Schaeffer. Music by Henry Jackman.
- Production company Legendary Pictures; distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures (worldwide) and Toho (Japan).
- Release date March 26, 2027. Country United States. Language English. (No budget or running time given.)

## Cast

Kaitlyn Dever; Dan Stevens as Trapper; Jack O'Connell; Alycia Debnam-Carey; Delroy Lindo as a Monarch boss; Matthew Modine as a general; Sam Neill; Josh Thomson as Ledon; Bronte Pearce as EDN Tech Gardner; Sami Afuni as Lieutenant Payne.

## Development

- Before the announcement, Adam Wingard (director of Godzilla vs. Kong and The New Empire) said "if you've done two movies, like, maybe you should just go ahead and do a third because, as you said, there's a trilogy in there," adding it "just depends on how [Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire] does and how things kind of shape out." He suggested a next film could follow Godzilla's perspective as The New Empire followed Kong.
- "Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire was released on March 29, 2024, and became the highest-grossing film in the Monsterverse franchise, grossing $571.9 million against a budget of between $135–150 million." Legendary's Mary Parent: "This is certainly an exciting result. We are in a good position to continue the journey, but let's see how Godzilla x Kong unfolds."
- "On May 10, 2024, Legendary announced that David Callaham, who wrote the early drafts for Godzilla (2014), would write a follow-up". The following week Legendary said Wingard would not return "due to scheduling conflicts and commitments with the film Onslaught". "In June 2024, Legendary announced Grant Sputore as the film's new director with the film now scheduled to be released on March 26, 2027."

## Pre-production

- Dan Stevens said of Trapper that "there's many more adventures that you could get out of him" and called Sputore a "great choice".
- "On January 24, 2025, Kaitlyn Dever was the first actress to be cast in the film." A month later O'Connell and Lindo were cast and Stevens confirmed; in March The Hollywood Reporter added Matthew Modine and reported filming expected in April 2025; in April Debnam-Carey and Neill joined.

## Filming and post-production

- Principal photography was expected to begin April 2025 in Australia. "On April 4, Dever told Seven News' Sally Bowrey that filming of the sequel had started, with London-set scenes being filmed in Brisbane, Queensland." On 23 April 2025 Screen Queensland disclosed filming was ongoing at Village Roadshow Studios (Gold Coast).
- Crew: production designer Stefan Dechant, cinematographer Dan Mindel, visual effects supervisor Kelly Port, co-screenwriter Michael Lloyd Green, composer Henry Jackman, editor Josh Schaeffer; Jackman and Schaeffer worked on previous Monsterverse films.
- "On May 9, 2025, a teaser video was released online, revealing the film's title as Godzilla x Kong: Supernova, which sparked speculation among fans that either SpaceGodzilla or Gigan would appear."
- Delroy Lindo said the film will feature a "human element", with characters "as humanly relatable as possible" and that "the human element also has to be compelling for audiences".
- Costume designer Ann Foley said via Instagram that principal photography had concluded in Australia and more filming would take place in Utah. "On August 1, 2025, The Times-Independent reported that filming, which had taken place under the working title Zeus, had just finished in Moab, Utah, its only shooting location in the United States; scenes set in Sedona, Arizona, were filmed in Moab."
- "On August 23, a second unit team led by Darrin Prescott filmed in Mexico City, Mexico, in the areas of Paseo de la Reforma, Santa Fe, and Palacio de Bellas Artes, with the participation of 150 extras." Shooting was then expected in London and Mumbai. "On October 5, 2025, filming started in central London, England, with combat vehicles and extras dressed in British Armed Forces uniforms." On 20 October crew members Dan Mindel and Simon England were seen filming at Chatuchak Weekend Market in Bangkok, Thailand.
- "In November 2025, the Writers Guild of America West initially published the feature credits; Callaham received a \"Story By\" credit and Green received a \"Screenplay By\" credit along with Callaham. The \"Source Material\" credits also revealed that SpaceGodzilla would be featured in the film. However, the Writers Guild later updated the credits in February 2026 by giving Callaham a sole \"Written By\" credit."
- Near the end of April [2026] a synopsis appeared in a China Licensing Expo listing: "As the sixth instalment in the 'MonsterVerse' film series, this movie will delve deeper into the delicate relationship of coexistence and trust between humans and prehistoric behemoths. Meanwhile, the earth-shaking monster storm triggered by the epic clash between Godzilla and Kong, the two guardians of Earth's ecological balance, will once again sweep across the big screen!"

## Release

- "Godzilla x Kong: Supernova is scheduled to be released in the United States by Warner Bros. Pictures on March 26, 2027," in IMAX.

## Note on the Godzilla count

- The article's note explains it will be "the sixth Godzilla film to be completely produced by a Hollywood studio", distinguishing the American releases with added footage (Godzilla, King of the Monsters!, King Kong vs. Godzilla, Godzilla 1985), the Toho–UPA co-production Invasion of Astro-Monster and TriStar's 1998 Godzilla, "the first Godzilla film to be completely produced by an American studio".

wikis.title: The Legend of Zelda (upcoming film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the upcoming live-action The Legend of Zelda film directed by Wes Ball, scheduled for release on 30 April 2027, covering its cast, development, filming and marketing.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- "The Legend of Zelda is an upcoming fantasy adventure film based on the video game series of the same name by Nintendo. It is directed by Wes Ball, written by T. S. Nowlin, and produced by Columbia Pictures, Nintendo, and OddBall Entertainment."
- Stars Benjamin Evan Ainsworth, Bo Bragason, Uli Latukefu, Dichen Lachman, Yvonne Strahovski, Sam Neill and Lydia Peckham.
- Infobox: directed by Wes Ball; screenplay by T. S. Nowlin; based on the series by Nintendo; produced by Shigeru Miyamoto, Avi Arad, Wes Ball, Joe Hartwick Jr.; cinematography Gyula Pados; production companies Columbia Pictures, Nintendo, OddBall Entertainment; distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing; release date April 30, 2027; language English. The logo shown is the one "revealed during The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct".
- "Principal photography began in November 2025, four months after Ainsworth and Bragason's casting was announced, and wrapped in April 2026."

## Cast

Benjamin Evan Ainsworth as Link; Bo Bragason as Princess Zelda; Uli Latukefu as Ganondorf; Dichen Lachman as Impa; Yvonne Strahovski; Sam Neill; Lydia Peckham.

## Development

- "In 2007, Imagi Animation Studios created a pitch reel for a computer-animated The Legend of Zelda film, but Nintendo did not accept the studio's offer, with reluctance in adapting their games following the critical and commercial failure of the 1993 live-action Super Mario Bros. film." The project became public in April 2013 via a proof-of-concept teaser on Vimeo in a former Imagi employee's portfolio.
- "In October 2013, series producer Eiji Aonuma stated that, if development of a film began, the company would want to use the opportunity to embrace audience interaction in some capacity."
- "In June 2023, it was reported that Nintendo was close to closing a deal with Illumination and Universal Pictures"; Illumination CEO Chris Meledandri denied the reports later that month.
- "In November 2023, Nintendo announced that they were developing a live-action The Legend of Zelda film, with Sony Pictures co-financing and handling worldwide theatrical distribution." Wes Ball was hired to direct with Derek Connolly writing; Miyamoto and Arad producing with Ball and Joe Hartwick Jr. through OddBall Entertainment. Miyamoto said he and Arad had worked on a Zelda film for many years.
- Fans found a January 2010 tweet by Ball suggesting a Zelda film as "the next big mo-cap Avatar-like movie", saying he "could never even hope to have the chance to direct it".
- "By June 2025, Connolly had been replaced as screenwriter by T. S. Nowlin, who previously collaborated with Ball on the Maze Runner film series."

## Casting

- "In July 2025, it was announced that Bo Bragason and Benjamin Evan Ainsworth had been cast as Zelda and Link respectively."
- November 2025 leaked filming footage led to speculation about Dichen Lachman as Impa; "Lachman's casting as Impa was confirmed by Deadline Hollywood in August 2026," along with Uli Latukefu as Ganondorf, Yvonne Strahovski, Lydia Peckham, "and Sam Neill in one of his final roles prior to his death in July 2026."

## Filming

- "Principal photography began in November 2025, in Wellington, New Zealand, under the codename Umami, and wrapped in April 2026."
- "Filming also occurred in Otago at Glenorchy, a location prominently used in Peter Jackson's Lord of the Rings trilogy." Gyula Pados served as cinematographer.

## Marketing

- "On November 17, 2025, Nintendo released three photos, showing Ainsworth as Link and Bragason as Zelda in a field."
- "The logo was revealed during a Nintendo Direct presentation centered on the 40th anniversary of the Legend of Zelda franchise, with Miyamoto stating that the lack of a subtitle is intentional and that audiences will understand why upon seeing the film."

## Release

- "The Legend of Zelda is scheduled for release worldwide on April 30, 2027, by Sony Pictures Releasing. It was originally scheduled for March 26 and May 7, 2027."
- "In November 2024, it was revealed in an official financial report from Nintendo that The Legend of Zelda would be released sometime in the latter half of the 2020s, between 2025 and 2029. In March 2025, the film's original release date was announced through the Nintendo Today mobile app, one day after the app's release."

## Note

- The article notes that the original game "was developed by Nintendo R&D4, published by Nintendo, directed by Shigeru Miyamoto and Takashi Tezuka, written by Tezuka and Keiji Terui, produced by Miyamoto, and designed by Miyamoto and Tezuka."
- The capture of the Filming section contains unrendered citation markup, so some sourcing text appears raw in the page.

wikis.title: Star Wars: The Force Awakens
wikis.summary: Wikipedia's article on Star Wars: The Force Awakens, the 2015 J. J. Abrams film that opened the sequel trilogy, covering its script and casting history, filming, music, marketing, release, record-setting box office, reviews, George Lucas's reaction and its awards.
wikis.body:
## The film

- Directed by J. J. Abrams, written by Lawrence Kasdan, Abrams and Michael Arndt, based on characters by George Lucas; produced by Kathleen Kennedy, Abrams and Bryan Burk for Lucasfilm Ltd. and Bad Robot; distributed by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures. Music by John Williams; cinematography by Dan Mindel; edited by Mary Jo Markey and Maryann Brandon. Running time 138 minutes.
- Cast: Harrison Ford, Mark Hamill, Carrie Fisher, Adam Driver, Daisy Ridley, John Boyega, Oscar Isaac, Lupita Nyong'o, Andy Serkis, Domhnall Gleeson, Anthony Daniels, Peter Mayhew and Max von Sydow.
- "The Force Awakens is the first live-action Star Wars film not to be released theatrically by 20th Century Fox", and carries no Fox logo or fanfare.

## Dates and figures

- Premiere December 14, 2015 in Hollywood (TCL Chinese, El Capitan and Dolby Theatres); United States release December 18, 2015, after being moved in November 2013 from an originally planned mid-2015 date. International release began December 16, 2015. Home media April 1 (digital) and April 5, 2016 (disc).
- Budget: the infobox gives "$638.9 million (gross)" and "$535.5 million (net)"; the lead says "On a net budget of $536 million, it is the most expensive film ever made"; the filming section says it was initially estimated at $259-306 million and that 2023 financial accounts showed a gross spend of $533 million and a net cost after tax breaks of $447 million. UK public support totalled £31.6 million ($47.4 million).
- Box office: $936.7 million in the United States and Canada, $1.132 billion elsewhere, $2.07 billion worldwide - the highest-grossing film of 2015 and third highest-grossing of all time; the 24th film to reach $1 billion and, at 12 days, the fastest at the time. Deadline calculated a net profit of $780.1 million.
- Records noted: $57 million in Thursday previews, a $119.1 million opening day (the first film to pass $100 million in a day), a $247.9 million opening weekend, a $149.2 million second weekend, and a $529 million worldwide five-day opening. It was the highest-grossing film ever domestically until Spider-Man: Brand New Day (2026).

## Story

Set thirty years after Return of the Jedi, the film follows Rey, Finn, Poe Dameron and Han Solo searching for Luke Skywalker and fighting in the Resistance, led by General Leia Organa, against Kylo Ren and the First Order. Starkiller Base destroys the New Republic capital Hosnian Prime; Kylo Ren kills his father Han Solo; Rey defeats Ren in a duel and finally finds Luke on Ahch-To.

## Making the film

Abrams was named director in January 2013 after a suggestion by Steven Spielberg; Michael Arndt left the script on October 24, 2013 and Kasdan and Abrams wrote a first draft in six weeks. Filming ran from May 16, 2014 in Abu Dhabi and at Pinewood Studios to November 3, 2014, with locations including Skellig Michael, the Lake District, RAF Greenham Common and Puzzlewood, shot on 35 mm with new Panavision anamorphic lenses plus IMAX 65 mm. Harrison Ford broke his leg on the Millennium Falcon set, halting production for two weeks; Foodles Production (UK) Ltd was fined $1.95 million in October 2016 over the accident. Practical effects were prioritised, with BB-8 built as a working prop. John Williams's score was recorded in 12 sessions between June and November 14, 2015, and Lin-Manuel Miranda co-wrote the cantina music.

## Reception

Rotten Tomatoes 93% of 447 reviews positive (average 8.3/10); Metacritic 80 from 55 critics; CinemaScore "A". Reviews were largely enthusiastic, with dissent over how closely the film echoes A New Hope. George Lucas criticised its "retro feel" in a Charlie Rose interview aired December 24, 2015 and likened the Lucasfilm sale to a "divorce". The film received five Academy Award nominations at the 88th ceremony and four BAFTA nominations, winning one; it was ineligible for the 73rd Golden Globes because nominations closed before release. The first trailer drew a racist backlash against John Boyega's casting, and Rey was attacked as a "Mary Sue" by the group known as the "Fandom Menace". The Last Jedi and The Rise of Skywalker followed.

## Rest of the page

The later parts are the reference list, external links, Star Wars, Lucasfilm and award navigation templates, and the page's portals, authority-control links and categories.

wikis.title: Star Wars: The Force Awakens - plot, cast, production, release and box office
wikis.summary: Part 1 of Wikipedia's article on Star Wars: The Force Awakens, with the infobox, lead, full plot summary, cast list, and the article from development and casting through filming, post-production, music, marketing, release, home media and the opening of the box-office section.
wikis.body:
## Infobox

- Directed by J. J. Abrams; produced by Kathleen Kennedy, J. J. Abrams and Bryan Burk; written by Lawrence Kasdan, J. J. Abrams and Michael Arndt; based on characters by George Lucas.
- Starring Harrison Ford, Mark Hamill, Carrie Fisher, Adam Driver, Daisy Ridley, John Boyega, Oscar Isaac, Lupita Nyong'o, Andy Serkis, Domhnall Gleeson, Anthony Daniels, Peter Mayhew and Max von Sydow.
- Music by John Williams; cinematography Dan Mindel; editing Mary Jo Markey and Maryann Brandon.
- Production companies Lucasfilm Ltd. and Bad Robot; distributed by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures.
- Release dates: December 14, 2015 (Hollywood, Los Angeles) and December 18, 2015 (United States). Runtime 138 minutes. Country United States; language English.
- Budget given in the infobox as "$638.9 million (gross)" and "$535.5 million (net)"; box office $2.071 billion. The lead says "On a net budget of $536 million, it is the most expensive film ever made", while the filming section says the budget "was initially estimated to be between $259 million and $306 million, but in 2023 financial accounts revealed the gross spend was $533 million and the net cost after tax breaks was $447 million".
- The page notes the article is about the film; the soundtrack and Lego Star Wars: The Force Awakens have their own articles.

## Lead

- "Star Wars: The Force Awakens, also known as Star Wars: Episode VII - The Force Awakens, is a 2015 American epic space opera film produced, co-written, and directed by J. J. Abrams." It is the sequel to Return of the Jedi (1983), the first installment of the sequel trilogy and chronologically the seventh film of the "Skywalker Saga", set thirty years after Return of the Jedi.
- Work on it "commenced after the Walt Disney Company's acquisition of Lucasfilm in 2012"; it is the first Star Wars film not to extensively involve George Lucas, who "only served as a creative consultant in the early stages of production".
- "Principal photography began in April 2014 and concluded the following November." Filming took place at Pinewood Studios in England and on location mainly in Abu Dhabi, Iceland and Ireland.
- "On a net budget of $536 million, it is the most expensive film ever made."
- It "premiered in Hollywood, Los Angeles, on December 14, 2015, and was released in the United States on December 18, making it the first live action Star Wars film to be distributed by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures", grossed $2.07 billion worldwide, was the highest-grossing film of 2015 and the third-highest-grossing film at the time of its release, and was nominated for five awards at the 88th Academy Awards. It was followed by The Last Jedi (2017) and The Rise of Skywalker (2019).

## Plot

Thirty years after the Battle of Endor the First Order has risen from the fallen Galactic Empire and seeks to destroy the New Republic, while General Leia Organa leads the Resistance and searches for her lost twin brother Luke Skywalker. On Jakku, Resistance pilot Poe Dameron receives a map to Luke's location before being captured by Kylo Ren; his droid BB-8 escapes with the map and meets the scavenger Rey. The stormtrooper FN-2187, named "Finn" by Poe, helps him escape; after a crash Finn finds Rey and BB-8, and they flee Jakku in the Millennium Falcon, which is then reclaimed by Han Solo and Chewbacca. At Starkiller Base, a planet converted into a superweapon, Supreme Leader Snoke approves General Hux's weapon. On Takodana, Maz Kanata offers help and Rey finds Anakin Skywalker's lightsaber, experiencing visions including being abandoned on Jakku. Starkiller Base destroys the Hosnian system, including the New Republic capital Hosnian Prime. Ren captures Rey, who escapes using a Jedi mind trick; it is revealed that Leia is Ren's mother. Han, Chewbacca and Finn infiltrate the base; Han calls Ren by his birth name, Ben Solo, and is killed by him. Chewbacca wounds Ren and sets off explosives, letting Poe destroy the thermal oscillator. Rey defeats Ren in a lightsaber duel; the base explodes; R2-D2 reveals the rest of the map, pointing to Ahch-To, where Rey finds Luke and presents him with the lightsaber.

## Cast

Harrison Ford as Han Solo; Mark Hamill as Luke Skywalker, "The last Jedi, who has gone into hiding"; Carrie Fisher as General Leia Organa; Adam Driver as Kylo Ren, leader of the Knights of Ren and son of Han and Leia; Daisy Ridley as Rey (Cailey Fleming as young Rey); John Boyega as Finn; Oscar Isaac as Poe Dameron; Lupita Nyong'o as Maz Kanata; Andy Serkis as Supreme Leader Snoke; Domhnall Gleeson as General Hux; Anthony Daniels as C-3PO; Peter Mayhew as Chewbacca (with Joonas Suotamo and Ian Whyte as body doubles because of Mayhew's health problems); Max von Sydow as Lor San Tekka.

Also listed: Tim Rose and Mike Quinn returning as Admiral Ackbar and Nien Nunb with voices by Erik Bauersfeld and Kipsang Rotich; Kenny Baker credited as "consultant" for R2-D2 with Jimmy Vee performing some of the work; Ewan McGregor in an uncredited vocal cameo as Obi-Wan Kenobi in Rey's vision, with archival audio of Frank Oz and Alec Guinness (Oz recorded new dialogue that was replaced with audio from The Empire Strikes Back, and James Arnold Taylor's Kenobi recordings were replaced with McGregor's); Gwendoline Christie as Captain Phasma; Dave Chapman and Brian Herring as BB-8 puppeteers with Bill Hader and Ben Schwartz as "Vocal Consultants"; Ken Leung, Simon Pegg (Unkar Plutt), Greg Grunberg, Kiran Shah, Jessica Henwick, Brian Vernel, Yayan Ruhian and Iko Uwais, Warwick Davis, Anna Brewster, Hannah John-Kamen, Thomas Brodie-Sangster, Kate Fleetwood, Billie Lourd, Emun Elliott, Maisie Richardson-Sellers, Harriet Walter, Mark Stanley, Sebastian Armesto and Pip Torrens; cameos by Daniel Craig, Michael Giacchino and Nigel Godrich as stormtroopers, Morgan Dameron, Gerald W. Abrams and Andrew Jack; and FN-2199 played by Liang Yang and voiced by David Acord.

## Development before Abrams

Lucas discussed sequel-trilogy ideas after the original trilogy but denied any intent to make it; development of a seventh "Skywalker Saga" film began shortly after he sold Lucasfilm to Disney in October 2012, when he said: "I always said I wasn't going to do any more and that's true, because I'm not going to do any more, but that doesn't mean I'm unwilling to turn it over to Kathy to do more." As creative consultant Lucas turned over rough story treatments for Episodes VII-IX, to be read only by Kennedy, Bob Iger, Alan F. Horn and Kevin A. Mayer; he later said Disney had discarded his ideas. Michael Arndt wrote the first screenplay and took part in a writers room with Simon Kinberg, Lawrence Kasdan, Pablo Hidalgo and Kiri Hart; early drafts had Luke appear midway through the film, but Arndt found "every time Luke came in and entered the movie, he just took it over", so Luke became a plot device appearing only in the final scene. Directors considered included David Fincher, Brad Bird (reportedly the "top choice", withdrawn over Tomorrowland), Jon Favreau, Guillermo del Toro, Matthew Vaughn and Colin Trevorrow; Ben Affleck and Neill Blomkamp passed.

## Writing and development

- "After a suggestion by Steven Spielberg to Kennedy, J. J. Abrams was named director in January 2013, with Lawrence Kasdan and Simon Kinberg as project consultants." Kasdan worked to convince Abrams after he initially rejected the offer.
- Michael Arndt worked on the script for eight months but said he needed 18 more; his exit was announced on October 24, 2013, when Kasdan and Abrams took over, planning the story while walking in Santa Monica, New York City, Paris and London. The first draft took six weeks; Abrams confirmed the script was complete in January 2014.
- In April 2014 Lucasfilm clarified that Episodes VII-IX would not feature expanded-universe storylines, though other elements could be included.
- Abrams withheld plot elements such as Rey and Finn's last names; Kennedy said "we haven't mapped out every single detail [of the sequel trilogy] yet". Daisy Ridley later recounted that Abrams had written drafts for episodes 8 and 9.
- A fictional language was developed by YouTube creator Sara Forsberg, who studied languages such as Hindi and Gujarati.
- In November 2015 George Lucas told CBS News' Charlie Rose that Disney had not been "keen" to involve him: "If I get in there, I'm just going to cause trouble because they're not going to do what I want them to do". He also said "They wanted to do a retro movie. I don't like that." In early December 2015 Kennedy told The Hollywood Reporter that Lucas had seen and enjoyed the film, and at the Kennedy Center Honors that month Lucas said, "I think the fans are going to love it, It's very much the kind of movie they've been looking for."

## Pre-production

Confirmed in May 2013 to be filmed in the United Kingdom; Lucasfilm met Chancellor George Osborne, who committed £25 million of public money, and UK production company account filings show the film "ultimately received a total of £31.6 million ($47.4 million) from the government". From September 2013 Bad Robot spaces were converted for a minor portion of US shooting. Crew: costume designer Michael Kaplan, editors Mary Jo Markey and Maryann Brandon, cinematographer Daniel Mindel shooting on 35 mm film (Kodak 5219, announced August 2013), sound designer Ben Burtt, production designers Rick Carter and Darren Gilford, special effects supervisor Chris Corbould, re-recording mixer Gary Rydstrom, supervising sound editor Matthew Wood, visual effects supervisor Roger Guyett and executive producer Jason McGatlin.

## Casting

- Open auditions were held in the UK and US in November 2013 for the roles of "Rachel" and "Thomas"; casting began in earnest in January 2014, with strict nondisclosure agreements.
- Many actors are named as having met or tested: Michael B. Jordan, Saoirse Ronan and David Oyelowo (September 2013); Benedict Cumberbatch, Jack O'Connell, Chiwetel Ejiofor, Alex Pettyfer, Jesse Plemons, Sullivan Stapleton, Tye Sheridan, Hugo Weaving, Michael Fassbender and Adam Driver (January 2014); later Frida Gustavsson, Miles Teller, Maisie Richardson-Sellers, Dev Patel, Courtney Eaton, Eiza Gonzalez, Elizabeth Olsen, Jessica Henwick and Olivia Cooke (callback) for Rey; Joseph David-Jones, Tom Holland and Daryl McCormack for Finn; Eddie Redmayne and Joel Kinnaman for Kylo Ren. A very early report claimed the studio wanted Ryan Gosling, Leonardo DiCaprio and Zac Efron.
- Daisy Ridley was cast by February 2014; a deal with Driver was worked out by the end of that month around his Girls schedule; talks with Andy Serkis and Oscar Isaac began by March. Denis Lawson declined to reprise Wedge Antilles, saying it would have "bored" him.
- In April 2014 Ridley, Boyega, Isaac, Driver, Serkis, Domhnall Gleeson and Max von Sydow were announced, with Ford, Hamill, Fisher, Anthony Daniels, Peter Mayhew and Baker returning; Lupita Nyong'o and Gwendoline Christie were added in June. Boyega got the part after Tom Cruise introduced Abrams to his performance in Attack the Block.
- Hamill was given a personal trainer and nutritionist to resemble an older Luke; Fisher was too but refused to lose weight. A new C-3PO costume was built so Daniels could play the role physically. A flashback in Rey's vision with Robert Boulter standing in for Luke was cut.
- Other casting notes: a UNICEF donation contest in May offered a set visit in Abu Dhabi; Warwick Davis announced in October that he would appear; Debbie Reynolds confirmed in November that Billie Lourd was in the film, having first auditioned for Rey.

## Filming

- Principal photography began in Abu Dhabi on May 16, 2014, based at Pinewood Studios in Buckinghamshire from June. Second-unit secret filming happened around Liwa Oasis; pre-production landscape shots were taken in Iceland. The Rub' al Khali desert in the United Arab Emirates stood in for the planet Jakku.
- Shot on 35 mm with new Panavision anamorphic lenses replicating the original trilogy's look, plus 65 mm IMAX segments using lenses developed for Wally Pfister on The Dark Knight.
- Harrison Ford fractured his leg when a hydraulic door on the Millennium Falcon set fell on him; Abrams said Ford's ankle "went to a 90-degree angle" and production was suspended for two weeks. Abrams fractured a vertebra helping lift the door. In February 2016 the Health and Safety Executive brought four criminal charges against Foodles Production (UK) Ltd, which was fined $1.95 million in October 2016 for two breaches.
- Filming took place over three days from July 28, 2014 at Skellig Michael, County Kerry, Ireland, with Hamill and Ridley; Takodana landscapes were shot in the Lake District in July; the former RAF Greenham Common in Berkshire was used in September; Puzzlewood in the Forest of Dean was also used. Principal photography ended on November 3, 2014.

## Post-production

Real locations and models were favoured over CGI; BB-8 was a physical prop developed by Disney Research, created by Neal Scanlan and operated live on set, and the Holochess sequence used stop-motion supervised by Tippett Studio and Phil Tippett. ILM announced a London facility in February 2014, and its Vancouver branch also worked on the film. In August 2015 Abrams gave an estimated running time of 124 minutes; the final cut runs 138 minutes after edits that removed sequences seen in trailers ("At one point, Maz used to continue along with the characters back to the Resistance base"). The title was announced on November 6, 2014; Pablo Hidalgo revealed in December 2015 that the working title had been Shadow of the Empire.

## Music

John Williams was confirmed in July 2013 to score the sequel trilogy; he began work in December 2014. Recording began June 1, 2015 at Sony Pictures Studios' Barbra Streisand Scoring Stage in Culver City, with William Ross conducting most of the music; 12 sessions over five months to November 14, 2015, with a 90-piece orchestra recording 175 minutes of music, of which nearly an hour was discarded, modified or re-recorded after Abrams re-edited the film. Snoke's theme used a 24-voice men's chorus; Gustavo Dudamel conducted the opening and end titles. The soundtrack was released by Walt Disney Records on December 18, 2015 and runs more than two hours. Lin-Manuel Miranda and Abrams wrote the cantina music together over two months after Williams declined that scene.

## Marketing

Deadline Hollywood estimated the media value at $175 million, a figure The Guardian later put at $423 million including home media revenues. An 88-second teaser released November 28, 2014 drew 58.2 million YouTube views in its first week. Eight mock Topps trading cards followed on December 11, 2014. A second, two-minute teaser premiered at Star Wars Celebration in Anaheim on April 16, 2015 and was viewed over 88 million times in 24 hours. Vanity Fair's exclusive cover issue appeared May 7, 2015 with Annie Leibovitz photos. A behind-the-scenes featurette screened at the 2015 San Diego Comic-Con; Drew Struzan made a commemorative poster for D23 in August 2015; the theatrical poster and third trailer arrived in October 2015, the trailer debuting during Monday Night Football and drawing 128 million views in 24 hours, 16 million from the broadcast. Air France offered a "Flight and Cinema" package; a Google partnership let users pick the Dark or Light Side from November 23; Disney and Verizon made a Google Cardboard VR experience. On December 17, 2015 select US and Canadian theaters showed all six previous films in 2D followed by The Force Awakens in 3D.

## Tie-ins, merchandise and games

"Journey to Star Wars: The Force Awakens" comprised at least 20 canonical books and comics from late 2015. Alan Dean Foster's novelization came out as an e-book on December 18, with the print edition delayed to January 2016; Marvel published a six-issue adaptation between June and November 2016. "Force Friday" on September 4, 2015 launched the merchandise at 12:01 am worldwide, with an 18-hour Disney/Maker Studios YouTube stream from September 3 and a Sphero remote-controlled BB-8; retailers such as Toys "R" Us could not meet demand. Film content was added to Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes, Star Wars Battlefront (Jakku), Star Wars Commander (Takodana) and Disney Infinity 3.0, and Lego Star Wars: The Force Awakens was released by Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment on June 28, 2016.

## Release

- Premiered December 14, 2015 at the TCL Chinese Theatre, El Capitan Theatre and Dolby Theatre in Hollywood, under a white tent along Hollywood Boulevard hosting more than five thousand guests. "The film was originally scheduled for a mid-2015 release, but in November 2013, it was pushed back to December 18, 2015." Released in 3D, RealD 3D, IMAX 3D and 4DX.
- Widest December release in the US and Canada across 4,134 theaters (3,300 3D locations, a record 392 IMAX screens of which 13 were 70 mm, 451 premium large format screens, 146 D-Box locations, plus Dolby Vision in Dolby Cinema); 940 IMAX theaters worldwide, a record. From December 18, 2015 it played every IMAX screen in the US and Canada for four straight weeks to January 14, 2016.
- Advance sales opened October 19, 2015 and crashed ticket sites; Vue Cinemas sold 45,000 tickets in 24 hours; US IMAX pre-sales hit a record $6.5 million in a single day (previous best under $1 million) and total pre-sales passed $50 million, raised to $100 million including $50-60 million in advance sales by December 14.
- It is "the first live-action Star Wars film not to be released theatrically by 20th Century Fox", carrying no Fox logo or fanfare; Bob Iger said omitting Disney branding was "for the fans". A mainland China poster was criticised as racist for shrinking John Boyega's Finn.
- Home media: digital download and Disney Movies Anywhere April 1, 2016; Blu-ray and DVD April 5. First week: 669,318 DVDs and 3.4 million Blu-rays, topping the Nielsen VideoScan First Alert chart with 83% of unit sales on Blu-ray. Overall 2.1 million DVDs and 5.9 million Blu-rays, 8 million copies, and $191 million through home media. A Blu-ray 3D collector's edition followed on November 15 with Abrams commentary; a 2019 DVD "Skywalker Saga" box set; 4K Ultra HD on March 31, 2020 and in the 27-disc Skywalker Saga set on April 20, 2020.
- Broadcast: Starz held US syndication rights from January 2016 and began broadcasting the film across its networks that September.

## Box office (opening of the section)

"Star Wars: The Force Awakens grossed $936.7 million in the United States and Canada and $1.132 billion in other countries for a worldwide total of $2.07 billion, making it the highest-grossing film of 2015 and the third highest-grossing film of all time." Box Office Mojo estimates close to 110 million tickets sold in the US and Canada; the film took 8.6% of all 2015 US and Canadian releases, second only to Titanic's 8.8% in 1997. It was the 24th film to gross $1 billion worldwide and the fastest to that point, in 12 days, and the third to pass $2 billion, on its 53rd day. Deadline Hollywood calculated a net profit of $780.1 million, first on its list of 2015's "Most Valuable Blockbusters". Analysts noted the figures are not adjusted for inflation, under which the first Star Wars film made more.

wikis.title: The Force Awakens: box-office detail, critical response, Lucas's reaction, accolades, fan backlash and sequels
wikis.summary: Part 2 of the Star Wars: The Force Awakens article, with the territory-by-territory box-office records, critics' reviews and aggregate scores, George Lucas's public criticism, awards, the racist fan backlash and the sequels, followed by the start of the reference list.
wikis.body:
## Commercial analysis

The film was "very successful in the United States and Canada" but less so in markets such as India, parts of Asia and Latin America, attributed to its being "a retro film" and weaker nostalgia abroad; marketing focused heavily on China, where the franchise has traditionally lacked resonance. Nancy Tartaglione of Deadline Hollywood argued that on a 40/60 domestic-to-international split it did well overseas. Dergarabedian called it "an absolute, all-out blockbuster without peer in terms of the sheer speed at which it has crossed all of these major box-office milestones." Mike Fleming Jr. of Deadline said "the net profit to Disney was an astounding $780.11M, and the Cash on Cash Return was twice that of any other film [released in 2016], at 2.00".

## United States and Canada

Released December 18, 2015. Record $57 million from Thursday night previews, including a record $5.7 million from 391 IMAX screens. Opening day $119.1 million - "the biggest single- and opening-day record and the first time a film has earned more than $100 million in a single day" - and a record $247.9 million opening weekend, 19% bigger than The Avengers ($207 million) and Jurassic World ($208 million). IMAX opening weekend $30.1 million (12.65%) from 391 theaters; 2D 53% and 3D 47% of the opening gross, with RealD 3D a record $78 million. It set the biggest December opening weekend, a record held for six years until Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021). The second weekend fell only 39.8% to $149.2 million, the biggest second weekend of all time. On January 2, after 16 days, it became the second film after Avatar to gross over $700 million domestically; on January 6 it became the highest-grossing film of all time domestically in 20 days, "and continued to hold this record until it was overtaken by Spider-Man: Brand New Day (2026)". It passed $800 million domestically on January 9 and $900 million on February 5, both unadjusted for inflation. It fell out of the top ten in its eleventh weekend (February 26-28, 2016) and below $1 million in ticket sales in its fourteenth.

## Other territories

Released on over 30,000 screens. It opened December 16, 2015 in 12 markets with $14.1 million on day one, first place in all of them; 42 more countries on December 17 added $58.6 million for $72.7 million in two days and first place in all 44 markets; $129.5 million in three days after $56.8 million on day three, with a UK midnight record of $3.6 million. Opening-day records in the United Kingdom ($14.4 million), Germany ($7.1 million), Australia ($6.8 million), Sweden ($1.7 million), Norway ($1.1 million) and 12 other countries; Spain ($3.5 million) and Japan ($3 million) also strong. Five-day international opening $281 million from 30,000 screens, a December record and third-biggest international opening ever; opening weekends of at least $10 million in the UK ($50.6 million), Germany ($27.5 million), France ($22.5 million), Australia ($19.6 million), Japan ($13.4 million) and Russia ($12.3 million), with all-time biggest openings in 18 countries. Worldwide five-day opening record of $529 million from 74 territories, including a $48 million IMAX record; IMAX passed $70 million in 11 days. The second weekend fell 51% to $136.9 million. India was an exception, opening third with $1.51 million. As of February 2016 the top markets outside the US and Canada were the United Kingdom ($180.7 million), China ($124.5 million), Germany ($109.7 million), Japan ($92.6 million) and France ($88.2 million). It passed $1 billion overseas on January 17, 2016 and topped the international chart for five consecutive weekends before The Revenant; in Japan it led for six straight weekends.

## Critical response

Rotten Tomatoes: "93% of 447 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 8.3/10", consensus quoted on the page. Metacritic 80 out of 100 from 55 critics, "generally favorable". CinemaScore "A" (women and under-25s and under-18s gave "A+"; 98% gave A or B); PostTrak 88% "definite recommend", 96% saying it met or exceeded expectations. Favourable reviews are quoted from Robbie Collin (The Daily Telegraph), Peter Bradshaw (The Guardian), Justin Chang (Variety), Richard Roeper (Chicago Sun-Times), Ann Hornaday (The Washington Post), Lawrence Toppman (The Charlotte Observer), Mick LaSalle (San Francisco Chronicle, highest rating, "the best Star Wars sequel yet"), Frank Pallotta (CNN Business), Tom Long (The Detroit News) and the Tribune-Star. More critical takes came from Stephanie Zacharek (Time), Scott Mendelson (Forbes, "an exercise in fan service"), Brian Merchant (Motherboard) and Gerardo Valero (RogerEbert.com), who said the film "plagiarized" A New Hope.

## George Lucas's reaction

In a Charlie Rose interview aired December 24, 2015, Lucas likened selling Lucasfilm to Disney to a "divorce" and criticised the film's "retro feel": "I worked very hard to make [my films] completely different, with different planets, with different spaceships—you know, to make it new." He likened Disney to "white slavers", drew criticism and apologised. Bob Iger wrote in a 2019 memoir that Lucas "couldn't even hide his disappointment", saying "there's nothing new" and that "there weren't enough visual or technical leaps forward"; Lucas preferred The Last Jedi and Rogue One (2016).

## Accolades

Several awards set their nominations before the December release, making the film ineligible for the 73rd Golden Globe Awards and some other ceremonies; it was added to the 21st Critics' Choice Awards best picture slate by a special board vote, and the 2015 American Film Institute Awards announcement was delayed so it could be named one of the top ten films of 2015. At the 88th Academy Awards it was nominated for Best Film Editing, Best Original Score, Best Sound Editing, Best Sound Mixing and Best Visual Effects. Other nominations include four British Academy Film Awards, winning one, and a Critics' Choice Movie Award.

## Fan backlash

The first trailer in 2015 "spurred a racist backlash against the casting of Boyega, a Black British actor", with boycott calls accusing the film of being "anti-white" and promoting "white genocide", and one account promoting the Cultural Marxism conspiracy theory. Rey was criticised as a "Mary Sue" by fans known as the "Fandom Menace", who blamed Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy for "forced diversity" and pro-feminist politics.

## Sequels

"The Force Awakens was followed by the sequels The Last Jedi and The Rise of Skywalker, which rounded out the sequel trilogy. Both grossed over $1 billion... The Last Jedi garnered positive reviews from critics while The Rise of Skywalker received a mixed response."

## Note

The part ends with a Wikipedia maintenance notice about duplicated citations, tagged August 2026, and the beginning of the numbered reference list.

Mostly the article's numbered reference list - citations to Digital Spy, No Film School, Deadline Hollywood, Fortune, Variety, IGN (a December 18, 2025 piece headlined "Even if You Hate What Followed, The Force Awakens Is Still Great Star Wars") and many other outlets. Media from Commons, quotations from Wikiquote and data from Wikidata; the film at StarWars.com, at Lucasfilm.com, its title listing at the Internet Speculative Fiction Database, and the film at IMDb.

- Star Wars sequel trilogy: The Force Awakens (2015) with its accolades and box office records, The Last Jedi (2017), and the trilogy's other entries.
