wikis.title: How to Train Your Dragon (2025 film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 2025 live-action How to Train Your Dragon remake: cast, production, release, box office, reception, accolades and the 2027 sequel.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- 2025 American fantasy adventure film, a live-action remake of DreamWorks Animation's 2010 animated film, itself "loosely based on the 2003 novel by Cressida Cowell".
- Written and directed by Dean DeBlois, who co-wrote and directed the animated film.
- Production companies: Universal Pictures, DreamWorks Animation, Marc Platt Productions. Distributed by Universal Pictures.
- Produced by Marc Platt and Adam Siegel; cinematography Bill Pope; edited by Wyatt Smith; music by John Powell.
- Running time 125 minutes (BBFC). Country: United States. Language: English.
- Infobox budget: $150 million.
- Described as "DreamWorks Animation's first live-action film since it was spun off from the original live action studio in 2004."

## Cast
- Mason Thames as Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III, "the awkward 16-year-old son of Stoick the Vast".
- Nico Parker as Astrid Hofferson; Gerard Butler as Stoick the Vast, reprising his role from the animated films.
- Nick Frost as Gobber the Belch; Gabriel Howell as Snotlout Jorgenson; Julian Dennison as Fishlegs Ingerman; Bronwyn James as Ruffnut Thorston; Harry Trevaldwyn as Tuffnut Thorston.
- Peter Serafinowicz as Spitelout Jorgenson; Ruth Codd as Phlegma the Fierce; Naomi Wirthner as Gothi; plus villagers played by Murray McArthur, Andrea Ware, Anna Leong Brophy, Marcus Onilude, Peter Selwood, Daniel-John Williams, Kate Kennedy, Selina Jones, Nick Cornwall and Samuel Johnson.

## Production
- February 2023: a live-action adaptation reported in development at Universal with DeBlois directing, writing and producing, Marc Platt and Adam Siegel as co-producers. DeBlois "only accepted to direct the adaptation on the condition that he had full creative control."
- November 2024: Forbes reported Universal had spent "over $50 million on pre-production".
- Casting: Thames and Parker announced May 2023; Butler January 2024, with Frost, Dennison, Howell, James and Trevaldwyn later that month; Ruth Codd in March [2024].
- Principal photography was originally scheduled for July 2023 in Belfast, Northern Ireland, postponed due to the 2023 SAG-AFTRA strike; screen tests were set for December 2023, production planned for mid-to-late January 2024. Filming began January 15, 2024 and wrapped on May 16.
- DeBlois first approached Roger Deakins (visual consultant on the animated films), who declined and recommended Bill Pope. Heavy use of practical sets; filmed with the IMAX format in mind; many scenes re-created shot-for-shot. Butler's Stoick costume "weighed 90 pounds".
- Tindholmur and Drangarnir in the Faroe Islands were used as filming locations for some flight scenes.
- Framestore was the sole visual effects company, splitting work across London, Melbourne, Montreal and Mumbai; Christian Manz was production VFX supervisor. On-set puppets (team led by Tom Wilton) and eight-axis gimbals were used for the dragon performances.
- Music: John Powell revealed in February 2023 he would compose; score released through Back Lot Music day-and-date with the film on June 13, 2025, preceded by the single "Test Driving Toothless".

## Release
- World premiere at CinemaCon, The Colosseum at Caesars Palace, Las Vegas, April 2, 2025.
- First screening outside the United States at the Sydney Film Festival on June 9, 2025; Los Angeles premiere at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures June 7, 2025; New York premiere at the 2025 Tribeca Festival June 11, 2025.
- Theatrical release in the United States June 13, 2025, in RealD 3D, IMAX, Dolby Cinema, 4DX, ScreenX and D-Box. Previously set for March 14, 2025, delayed to June because of the 2023 SAG-AFTRA strike.
- Dedicated to the memory of Gerard Butler's mother, Margaret Coll, who died in February that year aged 81.
- Marketing: first look in Empire's 2025 Preview November 15, 2024; teaser trailer in front of Wicked, online November 19, 2024; Super Bowl LIX spot February 9, 2025; official trailer February 12, 2025 (attached to Captain America: Brave New World); IMAX trailer May 6, 2025. Burger King released four menu items and BMW cars promoted the film.
- Home media: digital download July 15, 2025; 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray, Blu-ray and DVD August 12. First streamed on Peacock October 10, 2025; streamed on Netflix from February 10, 2026 before returning to Peacock for the remaining four months, unlike Universal's other live-action films.

## Box office
- Article text: grossed $263 million in the United States and Canada and $373.4 million in other territories, "for a worldwide total of $636.4 million"; the lead also says $636.4 million and calls it the eighth-highest-grossing film of 2025.
- Infobox gives box office as $636.6 million (Box Office Mojo).
- Projected $65-80 million from 4,000 theaters opening weekend; made $35.6 million on its first day including $11.1 million in previews; debuted to $84.6 million, the best opening of the series and the fourth-highest opening weekend of 2025 at that point. Second weekend $37 million (down 56.8%); third weekend $19.6 million, overtaken by F1.

## Reception
- Rotten Tomatoes: 78% of 259 critics' reviews positive, average rating 6.8/10.
- Metacritic: 61 out of 100 from 43 critics, "generally favorable".
- CinemaScore "A"; PostTrak 94% overall positive, 83% would definitely recommend.
- Mixed critic quotes, e.g. Empire's Helen O'Hara (three of five stars): "It's clearly made with real love and care, but shows far too much deference to its progenitor."; RogerEbert.com's Brian Tallerico (two of four): "the new version of How to Train Your Dragon doesn't do a single thing better than the original."

## Accolades (selected, as tabled)
- Annie Awards, February 21, 2026 - Outstanding Achievement for Character Animation in a Live Action Production - won.
- British Academy Film Awards, February 22, 2026 - Best Special Visual Effects (Christian Manz, Glen McIntosh, Andy Kind, Terry Palmer) - nominated.
- Golden Tomato Awards, January 13, 2026 - Fan Favorite Family Movies - won; Fan Favorite Movies - nominated.
- Also nominated: Astra Creative Arts Awards (December 11, 2025), Astra Film Awards (January 9, 2026), Costume Designers Guild Awards (February 12, 2026), Grammy Awards (February 1, 2026, John Powell), Saturn Awards (March 8, 2026), Visual Effects Society Awards (February 25, 2026).

## Sequel
- On April 2, 2025 at CinemaCon, Universal announced a live-action remake of How to Train Your Dragon 2 (2014) was in development; it was "officially announced and scheduled for release on June 11, 2027".
- Filming began January 26, 2026 in London.

wikis.title: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse (2018 film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia's article on the 2018 animated film Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse - its credits, plot, voice cast, development and animation, release dates, box office, reception and the Spider-Verse films that followed.
wikis.body:
## The film

- "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse is a 2018 American animated superhero film based on the Marvel Comics character Spider-Man", the first animated film in the Spider-Man franchise.
- Directed by Bob Persichetti, Peter Ramsey and Rodney Rothman; screenplay by Phil Lord and Rothman, story by Lord. Produced by Avi Arad, Amy Pascal, Phil Lord, Christopher Miller and Christina Steinberg. Music by Daniel Pemberton; edited by Robert Fisher Jr.
- Produced by Columbia Pictures and Sony Pictures Animation in association with Marvel Entertainment; distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing. Running time 117 minutes.
- Shameik Moore voices Miles Morales, with Jake Johnson, Hailee Steinfeld, Mahershala Ali, Brian Tyree Henry, Lily Tomlin, Luna Lauren Vélez, Zoë Kravitz, John Mulaney, Kimiko Glenn, Nicolas Cage, Kathryn Hahn and Liev Schreiber in supporting roles; Chris Pine voices the Peter Parker of Miles's universe.

## Dates and figures

- Premiered at the Regency Village Theater in Los Angeles on December 1, 2018; released in the United States on December 14, 2018. Earlier announced dates were July 20, 2018 (April 2015) and December 21, 2018 (December 2015), moved up one week in April 2017.
- Budget $90 million; worldwide gross $395 million ($190.2 million United States and Canada, $204.6 million other territories). Opening weekend $35.4 million, "the best ever December opening for an animated film".
- Home media: digital February 26, 2019; Blu-ray, Ultra HD Blu-ray and DVD March 19, 2019, with the short Caught in a Ham and an extended "Alt-Universe Cut".

## Production

- Plans leaked in emails released after the November 2014 Sony hack; Lord and Miller agreed to make it on condition they could adapt Dan Slott's 2014 "Spider-Verse" storyline with Miles Morales as protagonist.
- Animation by Sony Pictures Imageworks in Vancouver, painting 2D comic techniques over CGI frames, without motion blur and switching between 24 and 12 images per second. The crew grew to 142 animators by August 2018 and at one point 177, the largest Imageworks had used on a film; animation finished in October 2018.

## Reception

- Rotten Tomatoes 97% from 399 reviews (average 8.8/10); Metacritic 87 out of 100 from 50 critics; CinemaScore "A+".
- Won Best Animated Feature Film at the 91st Academy Awards, the 76th Golden Globe Awards and the 24th Critics' Choice Awards, the first non-Disney or Pixar winner of the Oscar since Rango (2011).

## Franchise

- Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse was released June 2, 2023; Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse "is scheduled to be released on June 18, 2027". Spider-Punk and Spider-Gwen spin-offs were confirmed in active development in February 2026.

## About the capture

- Parts 2 and 3 of the capture hold the article's raw citation wikitext, rendered reference list, navigation boxes and categories; the article text itself is in part 1. The page states no last-edited date.

wikis.title: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse (2018 film): plot, cast, production, release and reception
wikis.summary: Wikipedia's article body on the 2018 animated film Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse, covering its credits and infobox figures, plot, voice cast, development and animation, release, box office, critical response, accolades and franchise plans.
wikis.body:
## Film and credits

- "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse is a 2018 American animated superhero film based on the Marvel Comics character Spider-Man"; the first animated film in the Spider-Man franchise.
- Directed by Bob Persichetti, Peter Ramsey and Rodney Rothman; screenplay by Phil Lord and Rothman, story by Phil Lord; based on Marvel Comics.
- Produced by Avi Arad, Amy Pascal, Phil Lord, Christopher Miller and Christina Steinberg. Edited by Robert Fisher Jr. Music by Daniel Pemberton.
- Production companies: Columbia Pictures, Marvel Entertainment, Sony Pictures Animation, Pascal Pictures, Arad Productions, Lord Miller Productions. Distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing.
- Release dates: December 1, 2018 (Regency Village Theater) and December 14, 2018 (United States). Running time 117 minutes. Country United States, language English.
- Budget $90 million; box office $395 million (infobox). Body text: $190.2 million in the United States and Canada, $204.6 million in other territories, "for a total worldwide gross of $395 million, against a production budget of $90 million".
- Dedicated to the memories of Spider-Man creators Stan Lee and Steve Ditko, "who both died in 2018".

## Plot

- New York City teenager Miles Morales, son of police officer Jefferson Davis, is bitten by a radioactive spider in an abandoned metro station and gains spider-like abilities; there he finds a collider built by Kingpin, who wants to abduct alternate versions of his late wife Vanessa and son Richard.
- Peter Parker is wounded by the Green Goblin and murdered by Kingpin after giving Miles a USB flash drive designed to sabotage the collider. Miles meets an alternate Peter B. Parker at Peter's grave.
- At Alchemax they meet its proprietor Olivia Octavius (this universe's Doctor Octopus), who finds Peter will die of cellular decay if he stays; Gwen Stacy, a Spider-Woman from another dimension, saves them. Aunt May shelters Spider-Man Noir, Peni Parker and Spider-Ham, who are also deteriorating.
- Miles discovers his uncle Aaron is the Prowler; Aaron spares him and is fatally shot by Kingpin. Peter B. Parker restrains Miles and plans to sacrifice himself, but Miles frees himself, makes his own suit with Aunt May's help, sends the other Spider-People home and throws Kingpin at the collider's kill switch.
- Post-credits: Gwen contacts Miles from her home dimension; Miguel O'Hara travels to Earth-67 and argues with its Spider-Man. A note says that in Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse (2023) the Gwen scene "is established to take place sixteen months later".

## Voice cast

- Shameik Moore as Miles Morales / Spider-Man; Jake Johnson as Peter B. Parker ("a disheveled, jaded and brown-haired 38-year-old counterpart"); Hailee Steinfeld as Gwen Stacy / Spider-Gwen; Mahershala Ali as Aaron Davis / The Prowler; Brian Tyree Henry as Jefferson Davis; Lily Tomlin as May Parker; Luna Lauren Vélez as Rio Morales; Zoë Kravitz as Mary Jane Parker; John Mulaney as Peter Porker / Spider-Ham; Kimiko Glenn as Peni Parker / SP//dr; Nicolas Cage as Spider-Man Noir; Kathryn Hahn as Olivia Octavius / Doctor Octopus; Liev Schreiber as Wilson Fisk / Kingpin.
- Chris Pine voices the Peter Parker native to Miles's dimension. Additional voices: Lake Bell (Vanessa Fisk), Jorma Taccone (Norman Osborn / Green Goblin, and the 1967-series Spider-Man credited as "Last Dude"), Marvin "Krondon" Jones III (Tombstone), Joaquín Cosío (Scorpion), Post Malone (a bystander).
- Post-credits cameos: Oscar Isaac as Miguel O'Hara and Greta Lee as Lyla (credited "Interesting Person #1" and "#2").
- Stan Lee appears in a posthumous cameo as a character named Stan who sells Morales a Spider-Man costume; an archival Cliff Robertson recording from Spider-Man 2 (2004) is used for Ben Parker. Brian Tyree Henry, aged thirty-five, said he was too young to play a teenager's father but took the role after learning Miles was the only black and Latino Spider-Man.
- Ganke Lee's role was cut down because Spider-Man: Homecoming had the similar character Ned Leeds; Peter Sohn was cast before the dialogue was cut and later voiced him in the sequel.

## Development and writing

- Plans surfaced in emails released after "the November 2014 hacking of Sony's computers", between Amy Pascal and Doug Belgrad, about an animated comedy film with Phil Lord and Christopher Miller.
- Lord and Miller agreed on condition they could adapt Dan Slott's 2014 "Spider-Verse" storyline with Miles Morales as protagonist.
- "At the 2015 CinemaCon in April", Tom Rothman announced a July 20, 2018 release date, producers Lord, Miller, Avi Arad, Matt Tolmach and Pascal.
- December 2015: release moved to December 21, 2018; Bob Persichetti chosen to direct that month. By June 2016 Lord had written a full script. Peter Ramsey joined as co-director at the end of 2016. February 2017: Alex Hirsch named a story contributor, Christina Steinberg replaced Tolmach as producer. In April [2017] the date was pushed up one week to December 14, 2018. Rodney Rothman added as co-director by December 2017, when the full title was announced.
- The first full cut of animatics and storyboards ran over two hours; the directors said the final runtime would be between 90 and 120 minutes. One year before release Lord and Rothman rewrote the story and "substantially rewritten the third act".
- A Miles/Gwen romance was scrapped. A cancelled post-credits scene would have had cameos by Tobey Maguire, Andrew Garfield and Tom Holland.

## Casting dates

- April 2017: Shameik Moore cast, with Liev Schreiber as the then-unspecified main villain. A month later Mahershala Ali and Brian Tyree Henry joined. April 2018: Jake Johnson cast as Peter B. Parker. June 2018: Sony confirmed Schreiber as Kingpin, Steinfeld, Vélez and Tomlin. A month later Cage, Mulaney and Glenn were announced. November 2018: Chris Pine and Oscar Isaac announced.

## Animation and design

- Animation handled by Sony Pictures Imageworks in Vancouver. Two animators took around a year to create 10 seconds of footage matching the producers' vision.
- Crew grew from a single animator (Alberto Mielgo, later let go over artistic differences) to 60, reaching 142 animators by August 2018 and at one point 177, "the largest animation crew that Sony Pictures Imageworks had ever used for a film". Animation work was completed in October 2018.
- CGI frames were painted over in 2D so every frame would "look like a comic panel"; no motion blur, using motion smearing as in the 1942 Looney Tunes short The Dover Boys; frame rate varied between 24 images (ones) and 12 images (twos) per second, Miles animated at 12 and Peter at 24 in the forest swing.
- Other techniques: deliberately misaligned colors for depth of field, halftones and Ben-Day dots, Kirby Krackle, motion lines, onomatopoeia. Character designer Shiyoon Kim; Craig Kellman designed Spider-Ham; Justin K. Thompson production designer; Danny Dimian visual effects supervisor.

## Music

- Daniel Pemberton announced as composer in July 2018. Soundtrack album released by Republic Records on December 14, score album by Sony Classical Records on December 17, and the EP A Very Spidey Christmas announced December 20 and released the next day (five songs by Moore, Johnson and Pine).
- Elliphant's "To the End" was released as a single in January 2019.

## Release and marketing

- Released by Sony Pictures Releasing under its Columbia Pictures label on December 14, 2018; premiered at the Regency Village Theater in Los Angeles on December 1, 2018 with tributes to Stan Lee and Steve Ditko.
- A teaser trailer debuted at the 2017 Comic Con Experience; the official trailer was released at the start of June 2018 and "generated 164 thousand conversations across social media platforms within a day" and 44 million views in three days. A second trailer came in October 2018 ahead of a New York Comic Con panel that showed the first 35 minutes.
- November 2018: Sony launched the Spider-Verse Web AR Experience by 8th Wall and Trigger on Amazon Web Services. The film received "a $115 million promotional 'boost'" from partners including the Ad Council, McDonald's, Synchrony Bank, Nike, General Mills, Hasbro, Genting Cruise Lines, Tencent QQ, eBay, Vodafone, Garmin, Adobe and Wacom.
- December 21, 2018: an unlockable costume added to Marvel's Spider-Man on PlayStation 4; December 29: Sony published the screenplay online.

## Home media

- Digital download February 26, 2019; Blu-ray, Ultra HD Blu-ray and DVD on March 19, all with the Spider-Ham short Caught in a Ham and an extended "Alt-Universe Cut" with 30 minutes of unreleased footage. Blu-ray 3D in several regions outside the US and UK on April 10, 2019.
- Aired on Sky Cinema Premiere in the UK in 2019, drawing 1.1 million viewers, the year's eighth most-watched film on pay TV channels.
- April 2021: Sony's deal with Disney covering Disney+ and Hulu; on Disney+ in the UK, Australia and Japan from June 17, 2022 and in Latin America and Europe from September 9, 2022.

## Box office

- Projected $30–35 million from 3,813 theaters; made $12.6 million on its first day including $3.5 million from Thursday night previews, and debuted to $35.4 million, first place and "the best ever December opening for an animated film".
- Second weekend $16.7 million (fourth), third weekend $18.3 million (fourth), fifth weekend $13 million (fourth).
- On March 1–3 [2019], after the Academy Award win, it added 1,661 theaters (total 2,104) and made $2.1 million, a 138% increase.
- On January 31, 2019 it passed Hotel Transylvania 2 as Sony Pictures Animation's highest-grossing film domestically, unadjusted for inflation.

## Critical response and accolades

- Rotten Tomatoes: 97% approval based on 399 reviews, average 8.8/10, described as the best-reviewed superhero film on the site. Metacritic: 87 out of 100 from 50 critics ("universal acclaim"). CinemaScore "A+"; PostTrak 90% overall positive, 80% "definite recommend", 5 stars.
- Reviews quoted include David Ehrlich (IndieWire, "B+"), Oliver Jones (New York Observer, 3.5/4), Johnny Oleksinski (New York Post, 3.5/4), Christy Lemire, Todd McCarthy, William Bibbiani, Justin Chang, David Sims and Katie Walsh.
- Won Best Animated Feature Film at the 76th Golden Globe Awards, the 24th Critics' Choice Awards and the 91st Academy Awards; "the first non-Disney or Pixar film to win Best Animated Feature since Rango (2011), becoming the 6th non-Disney/Pixar film to win". Also successful at the 72nd British Academy Film Awards and 46th Annie Awards.
- Appeared first on 5 critics' top ten lists according to Metacritic; number 9 on New York Magazine's best films of the decade; the screenplay ranked seventy-one on the Writers Guild of America's "101 Greatest Screenplays of the 21st Century (So Far)" in December 2021.
- Praise from Tom Holland, Chris Pratt, Patton Oswalt, Kevin Smith, Barry Jenkins, Rian Johnson ("the Velvet Underground of superhero movies"), James Gunn and Kevin Feige. Yoshiyuki Tomino, in a lecture at Takarazuka University, said: "At first glance, it looks like a live-action film, and it's very experimental in various places."
- Cited as an influence on The Mitchells vs. the Machines (2021), The Bad Guys (2022–present), Puss in Boots: The Last Wish (2022), Ms. Marvel (2022), Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant Mayhem (2023), Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur and Entergalactic (2022).

## Franchise

- Sequel Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse released June 2, 2023, surpassing Into the Spider-Verse's box office; the third film, Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse, "is scheduled to be released on June 18, 2027".
- A Spider-Women spin-off announced in 2018 with Bek Smith attached as screenwriter and Lauren Montgomery in talks to direct; Lord and Miller confirmed as producers in April 2021; Pascal and Arad reaffirmed development in May 2023. "In February 2026, it was confirmed that both a Spider-Punk and a Spider-Gwen spin-off were in active development."
- Possible TV series: Lord and Miller signed a five-year deal with Sony Pictures Television by April 2019.

wikis.title: Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia's article on the 2023 animated film Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse - its plot and voice cast, six-universe animation, reported production strain, $690.8 million box office and awards, and the sequel and spin-offs to come.
wikis.body:
## The film

- *Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse* is a 2023 American animated superhero film directed by Joaquim Dos Santos, Kemp Powers and Justin K. Thompson, written by Phil Lord, Christopher Miller and Dave Callaham, and the sequel to *Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse* (2018). Produced by Columbia Pictures and Sony Pictures Animation in association with Marvel Entertainment; distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing.
- Shameik Moore voices Miles Morales, with Hailee Steinfeld, Brian Tyree Henry, Luna Lauren Velez, Jake Johnson, Jason Schwartzman, Issa Rae, Karan Soni, Shea Whigham, Greta Lee, Daniel Kaluuya, Mahershala Ali and Oscar Isaac. Miles and Gwen Stacy travel the multiverse and meet the Spider-Society, whose leader Miguel O'Hara insists on unbreakable "canon events".
- Premiered May 30, 2023 (Grand Rex, Paris, and the Regency Village Theater, Los Angeles) and released in the United States on June 2, 2023, in premium large formats and IMAX, not in 3D. Running time 140 minutes - the longest American animated film by runtime at the time of release.

## Figures, including where the page disagrees with itself

- Budget: the infobox gives $125 million; the lead says "$100-150 million"; the Vulture source quoted in the reference list calls it "the $150 million Sony project".
- Box office $690.8 million: $381.6 million in the United States and Canada and $309.2 million elsewhere, passing *Into the Spider-Verse*'s $384.5 million after 12 days and making it Sony Pictures Animation's highest-grossing film. Deadline Hollywood calculated a $328 million net profit. Opening weekend $120.7 million domestic from 4,313 theaters and $88.1 million from 59 international markets.
- Scale: around 1,000 crew - the largest of any animated film; 240 characters across six universes per Lord and Miller in April 2022, while Thompson said in May 2023 the film has 280 (later around 630) Spider-Man variations, 95 (later 150) of them unique named characters.
- Reviews: Rotten Tomatoes 95% of 386 critics (8.6/10); Metacritic 86/100 from 60 critics; CinemaScore "A"; PostTrak 93% positive.

## How it was made

- Sony began developing the sequel by the end of November 2018; it was announced in November 2019 for April 8, 2022, moved to October 7, 2022 during the COVID-19 pandemic, split into two films in December 2021, renamed *Across the Spider-Verse* and *Beyond the Spider-Verse* in April 2022 and released June 2, 2023. Animation began June 9, 2020 at Sony Pictures Imageworks in Vancouver and finished May 20, 2023, 13 days before release.
- Six animation styles were built so each universe looks drawn by a different artist: watercolour Earth-65 reacting to Gwen's emotions, "Mumbattan" Earth-50101, Syd Mead-influenced Nueva York, Spider-Punk's Xerox-and-zine New London, and Earth-42. A Lego sequence was animated by 14-year-old Preston Mutanga after the filmmakers saw his fan-made Lego teaser.
- On June 23, 2023 Vulture reported four workers alleging that repeated changes requested by Lord to finished animation caused long overtime and drove over 100 artists off the project before completion; Sony denied the allegations and Amy Pascal called heavy revision normal.

## Release and after

- Withdrawn from cinemas across the MENA region over brief transgender iconography, including a "Protect Trans Kids" flag in Gwen's bedroom, which fuelled readings of her arc as a transgender allegory - though she is not identified as transgender in the film.
- At least two theatrical versions circulated, differing in small dialogue and animation details, and Sony re-sent prints with a new audio mix on June 9, 2023 after sound complaints; the digital release is an "international version" with lines removed. Digital August 8, 2023; disc September 5, 2023; Netflix October 31, 2023; Disney+ May 1, 2025.
- Awards: Academy Award nomination for Best Animated Feature; a clean sweep of seven Annie Awards; wins at the Critics' Choice Movie Awards and Producers Guild of America Awards; BAFTA and Golden Globe nominations; an American Film Institute top-ten film of 2023 and the National Board of Review's Best Animated Film.
- *Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse* is scheduled for June 18, 2027. Spin-offs *Spider-Women* and *Spider-Punk* are in development, and the manga *Spider-Man: Octopus Girl* / *Octo-Girl* began serialization on June 20, 2023.

## Rest of the page

- Roughly three-quarters of the captured source is citation apparatus: about 170 raw `<ref name="...">{{Cite ...}}</ref>` templates and a rendered reference list of about 167 numbered entries, followed by award navigation boxes and the article's category list. The article also carries a duplicated-citations cleanup notice tagged August 2026.

wikis.title: Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse: plot, cast, production and reception
wikis.summary: The body of Wikipedia's article on the 2023 animated film Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse, covering its plot, voice cast, development and animation, the Vulture working-conditions report, its $690.8 million box office, reviews and the planned sequel and spin-offs.
wikis.body:
## The film

- *Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse* is a 2023 American animated superhero film directed by Joaquim Dos Santos, Kemp Powers and Justin K. Thompson, from a screenplay by the writing team of Phil Lord and Christopher Miller and Dave Callaham. It is the sequel to *Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse* (2018), based on the Marvel Comics character Spider-Man, produced by Columbia Pictures and Sony Pictures Animation in association with Marvel Entertainment.
- Shameik Moore stars as Miles Morales, with Hailee Steinfeld, Brian Tyree Henry, Luna Lauren Velez, Jake Johnson, Jason Schwartzman, Issa Rae, Karan Soni, Shea Whigham, Greta Lee, Daniel Kaluuya, Mahershala Ali and Oscar Isaac.
- Infobox credits: producers Phil Lord, Christopher Miller, Amy Pascal, Avi Arad and Christina Steinberg; edited by Michael Andrews; music by Daniel Pemberton; production companies Columbia Pictures, Marvel Entertainment, Sony Pictures Animation, Pascal Pictures, Lord Miller Productions and Arad Productions; distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing; country United States; language English.
- Release dates: May 30, 2023 (Regency Village Theater) and June 2, 2023 (United States). Running time 140 minutes. Budget $125 million. Box office $690.8 million.

## Figures the page gives more than once

- Budget: the infobox says $125 million; the lead says the film "had a budget of $100-150 million"; the article's Vulture citation describes it as "the $150 million Sony project".
- Scale: the lead and production sections say the film had the largest crew of any animated film ever, with around 1,000 people; Lord and Miller said in April 2022 it had 240 characters across six universes, while co-director Justin K. Thompson said in May 2023 the film includes 280 (later expanded to around 630) variations of Spider-Man, 95 (later 150) of which are unique named characters.
- Runtime: at 140 minutes it was the longest American animated film by runtime at the time of its release, surpassing *Consuming Spirits* (2012).

## Dates

- Sony began developing a sequel by the end of November 2018; it was officially announced in November 2019 with a release date of April 8, 2022, shifted to October 7, 2022 (COVID-19 pandemic), then to June 2, 2023.
- Animation production started June 9, 2020; production on the film was completed May 20, 2023, 13 days before the US release.
- Premiered May 30, 2023 at the Grand Rex in Paris and the Regency Village Theater in Los Angeles; released in the United States on June 2 in premium large formats and IMAX, not in 3D; premiered in Beijing May 31 and released in China June 2; re-released in IMAX in limited theaters on January 19, 2024, marking the debut of a new Columbia Pictures logo for the studio's 100th anniversary.
- Digital download August 8, 2023; Ultra HD Blu-ray, Blu-ray and DVD September 5, 2023; Netflix in the United States October 31, 2023; Disney+ May 1, 2025.

## Future projects

- *Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse*, the third and final film of the trilogy, is scheduled for release on June 18, 2027, with Bob Persichetti and Justin K. Thompson directing and Lord, Miller and Callaham writing; Moore, Steinfeld, Schwartzman, Soni, Kaluuya and Jerome reprise their roles. It had earlier been delayed to June 25, 2027 after the 2023 Writers Guild of America strike before moving up.
- *Spider-Women*, in development since November 2018 (Bek Smith writing, Lauren Montgomery in talks to direct), would focus on Gwen Stacy, Cindy Moon / Silk and Jess Drew; Pascal called *Across the Spider-Verse* a "launching pad" for it.
- A *Spider-Punk* spin-off was revealed in early development in August 2025 with Kaluuya co-writing with Ajon Singh and expected to reprise his role; in December 2025 Kaluuya said it was in its final stages of writing. In February 2026 Sony Pictures Animation presidents Kristine Belson and Damien de Froberville reconfirmed both spin-offs were in development, projecting release after *Beyond the Spider-Verse*.
- A manga spin-off, *Spider-Man: Octopus Girl* by Hideyuki Furuhashi and Betten Court, began serialization on Shueisha's Shonen Jump+ on June 20, 2023, about Doctor Octopus reawakening in the body of a Japanese middle schooler named Otoha Okutamiya. Viz Media licensed it in February 2024 for English publication in the fourth quarter of 2024 as *Spider-Man: Octo-Girl*. Serialization ended January 7, 2025 and returned December 4, 2025.

## Maintenance notice

- The article carries a duplicated-citations cleanup notice generated by the DuplicateReferences script, naming a GamesRadar "ending explained" URL used at refs 125 and 132.

wikis.title: Plot
wikis.summary: The article's plot summary: Gwen Stacy's exposure on Earth-65, Miles Morales versus the Spot, and the Spider-Society's doctrine of canon events.
wikis.body:
- On Earth-65, Spider-Woman Gwen Stacy is estranged from her father George Stacy, who is hunting her for killing Peter Parker - an accident after Peter turned into the Lizard. She fights an alternate Vulture, is helped by Miguel O'Hara and Jess Drew, reveals her identity to George and leaves with Miguel and Jess.
- On Earth-1610, 16 months after the destruction of the Alchemax collider, Miles Morales struggles to balance being Spider-Man with his family, and is grounded after being late to a party for his father Jeff's promotion to police captain. He meets the Spot, an Alchemax scientist whose body was infused with portals in the collider's destruction, who reveals the radioactive spider that gave Miles his powers came from Earth-42. The Spot learns to traverse universes and empower himself with other dimensions' colliders.
- Gwen and Miles reconnect; Gwen fears that "a Gwen Stacy falling for Spider-Man never ends well". Following her to Earth-50101, Miles teams with Pavitr Prabhakar and Hobie Brown against the Spot, shares a vision of the Spot's future attacks - including the deaths of Jeff and Inspector Singh - and saves Singh, which begins the collapse of that world.
- In Nueva York on Earth-928, Miguel, leader of the Spider-Society, explains that each Spider-Person's story contains "canon events", such as the death of a police captain close to Spider-Man, which cannot be disrupted without risking that universe and the multiverse. Miles realizes the Spot killing Jeff is a canon event, refuses to accept it, and is imprisoned; he escapes with Hobie's help. Miguel reveals Miles was never supposed to be Spider-Man - the Earth-42 spider was not meant to bite him, which left Earth-42 without a Spider-Man and led to the Spot's creation and the death of Earth-1610's Peter Parker. Miles escapes with Margo Kess's help; Gwen defends him and is exiled home.
- George reconciles with Gwen by resigning from the force instead of arresting her, preventing his canon event, and gives her a portal device left by Hobie. Miles arrives on Earth-42, where his uncle Aaron Davis is alive, Jeff is dead and New York is crime-ridden; Aaron and that world's Miles, the Prowler, restrain him. Gwen promises Earth-1610's Rio and Jeff she will bring Miles back and teams with Peter B., Mayday, Pavitr, Hobie, Margo, Spider-Man Noir, Peni Parker and Spider-Ham.

wikis.title: Voice cast and character appearances
wikis.summary: The film's voice cast, the dozens of Spider-People who appear, and the archival and live-action cameos.
wikis.body:
- Shameik Moore as Miles Morales / Spider-Man of Earth-1610; Hailee Steinfeld as Gwen Stacy / Spider-Woman of Earth-65; Brian Tyree Henry as Jefferson Morales (ne Davis), newly promoted police captain (this credit is tagged "[failed verification]"); Lauren Velez as Rio Morales and her Earth-42 counterpart; Jake Johnson as Peter B. Parker of Earth-616B, now married to Mary Jane with daughter Mayday.
- Jason Schwartzman as Johnathon Ohnn / the Spot, a former Alchemax scientist; the Spot was not originally the main antagonist and was at first dismissed by Lord and Miller when Avi Arad suggested him, until his powers' potential was discussed. Issa Rae as the pregnant Jess Drew of Earth-332, Miguel's right hand, who keeps no secret identity. Karan Soni as Pavitr Prabhakar / Spider-Man India of Earth-50101, living in Mumbattan. Shea Whigham as George Stacy; Greta Lee as the AI Lyla; Daniel Kaluuya as Hobie Brown / Spider-Punk of Earth-138; Mahershala Ali as Earth-42's Aaron Davis; Oscar Isaac as Miguel O'Hara / Spider-Man 2099 of Earth-928, a "ninja-vampire" Spider-Man Isaac called "the one Spider-Man that doesn't have a sense of humor".
- Also: Jorma Taccone as Adriano Tumino / Vulture from an Italian Renaissance-inspired universe and as the 1967 series Spider-Man; Jharrel Jerome as Miles G. Morales / Prowler of Earth-42; Andy Samberg (Ben Reilly / Scarlet Spider), Amandla Stenberg (Margo Kess / Spider-Byte), Kimiko Glenn (Peni Parker), Taran Killam (Web-Slinger), Mike Rianda (Spider-Therapist), Sofia Barclay (Malala Windsor / Spider-UK, an original incarnation who wears a hijab), Danielle Perez (Charlotte Webber / Sun-Spider, a fan-created character who uses a wheelchair) and Metro Boomin as Metro Spider-Man.
- Spider-Men from other media: the *Spider-Man Unlimited* (1999-2001) Peter Parker; Nic Novicki as Lego Spider-Man; Josh Keaton from *The Spectacular Spider-Man* (2008-2009); Yuri Lowenthal from Insomniac's *Marvel's Spider-Man* games.
- Smaller roles: Melissa Sturm (MJ Parker), Rachel Dratch (counselor C. Weber), Ziggy Marley (Lenny), Peter Sohn (Ganke Lee, after his dialogue was cut from the first film), Elizabeth Perkins (Earth-65's Aunt May), Atsuko Okatsuka (Yuri Watanabe), Ayo Edebiri, Antonia Lentini and Nicole Delaney (Gwen's bandmates Glory, Betty and MJ), Jack Quaid (Earth-65's Peter Parker) and J. K. Simmons as versions of J. Jonah Jameson.
- Live-action and archival: Donald Glover as an alternate Aaron Davis / Prowler from *Spider-Man: Homecoming* (2017); Peggy Lu as Mrs. Chen from Sony's Spider-Man Universe (Earth-688); archival footage of Tobey Maguire, Andrew Garfield, Kirsten Dunst, Bryce Dallas Howard, Cliff Robertson and Denis Leary; archival audio of Alfred Molina's Doctor Octopus from *No Way Home* (2021) for a comics-accurate hologram; archival audio of John Mulaney's Spider-Ham; archival stills of Chloe Bennet's Quake on a noticeboard in Miles's bedroom.

wikis.title: Development and casting
wikis.summary: How Sony developed the sequel from 2018, split it into two films, and assembled its voice cast between 2019 and 2023.
wikis.body:
- By the end of November 2018, ahead of *Into the Spider-Verse*'s release, Sony Pictures Animation had begun developing a sequel because of the "incredible buzz", working from "seeds [that were] planted" in the first film. Joaquim Dos Santos and David Callaham were set to direct and write, with Amy Pascal producing and Lord, Miller, Arad and Steinberg expected to return. In December 2018 Pascal said it would focus on Miles and Gwen, exploring a romance cut from the first film, and serve as a "launching pad" for a female-focused spin-off.
- Officially confirmed in November 2019 with an April 8, 2022 release date, shifted to October 7, 2022 in April 2020.
- February 2021: Miller said he and Lord were writing with Callaham and that Peter Ramsey would executive produce. Before finalizing a script, villain or universes, the team decided the film had to be about family and the struggle of being "a son and a Spider-Man". In April 2021 Kemp Powers and Justin K. Thompson were announced as co-directors (all three had worked on it from the start; Thompson was production designer on the first film), with Alonzo Ruvalcaba co-producing and Aditya Sood, Bob Persichetti, Rodney Rothman, Rebecca Karch and Brian Michael Bendis joining Ramsey as executive producers.
- December 2021: Lord and Miller revealed the film was split into *Across the Spider-Verse (Part One)* and *(Part Two)* because the story was too much for one film, with both worked on simultaneously. In April 2022 they were renamed *Across the Spider-Verse* and *Beyond the Spider-Verse*, and *Across* moved to June 2, 2023. Lord and Miller said they had told Sony it would be the same size as the first film but it ended up with the largest crew of any animated film, around 1,000 people, 240 characters and six universes. Rejected characters included versions of Green Goblin, Doctor Octopus, Kraven the Hunter, Mysterio, Electro, Shocker, Rhino, Hobgoblin, Chameleon, Puma, Leap-Frog, Alistair Smythe, Grizzly, Boomerang, Screwball, Big Wheel, Beetle and Diamondhead.
- Casting: Issa Rae (June 2021), Jake Johnson confirmed a month later, Oscar Isaac in December 2021. Tom Holland revealed Pascal had approached him during *No Way Home* filming; Jeff Sneider of The Ankler reported in February 2023 that Holland was set to appear in a live-action sequence and that this caused the delay from 2022 to 2023 - Holland ultimately did not appear. April 2022: Henry, Velez and Dratch. June 2022: Schwartzman as the Spot (added after Arad's suggestion; a second antagonist was later written out), plus Whigham and Taccone. November 2022: Kaluuya. December 2022: the *Spectacular Spider-Man* Peter Parker, whose showrunner Greg Weisman said he was not informed. January 2023: Nicolas Cage confirmed he would not return as Spider-Man Noir. February 2023: Soni. April-May 2023: Samberg and Stenberg.
- Delilah, an assassin and bartender at the Bar with No Name, was meant to appear but her scene was cut; she was later included in Insomniac's *Spider-Man 2* (2023).

wikis.title: Animation and design
wikis.summary: Six distinct animation styles by Sony Pictures Imageworks, the look of each universe, and how individual characters were designed.
wikis.body:
- Animated by Sony Pictures Imageworks in Vancouver with visual effects supervisor Michael Lasker. Design work on new characters had begun by November 2019 (comic artist Kris Anka was a character designer); lead animator Nick Kondo announced production had started on June 9, 2020.
- Each universe was designed to look as though drawn by a different artist. Having learned new tools on *The Mitchells vs. the Machines* (2021), Lord and Miller used them for six animation styles so the visuals would shift with each new environment.
- Earth-65 (Gwen's) looks like "impressionistic" watercolor paintings; the team built a simulator for it and used a palette reflecting Gwen's emotions like a "three dimensional mood ring". Thompson said the colour-emotion idea came from the torn-dress scene in *Cinderella* (1950); Miller intended it to recall the *Spider-Gwen* comic covers.
- Earth-50101 was nicknamed "Mumbattan" after Mumbai and Manhattan, based on Gotham Entertainment Group's *Spider-Man: India*. Nueva York, the Marvel 2099 New York, was heavily influenced by Syd Mead's neo-futurist illustrations and by Ron Cobb, John Bell, John Berkey, John Harris, Ralph McQuarrie and Oscar Niemeyer's architecture - an authoritarian, brutalist, minimalist environment reflecting Miguel O'Hara's "clean, strong, unified, front-facing ideology", undercut underground.
- Spider-Punk's "punky New London" style took two to three years to develop, inspired by 1970s punk album covers, posters and zines, emulating Xerox prints with a grayed-out, low-toner quality; his body is animated on 3s or 2s, his guitar on 4s and his outline on 2s or 1s, against the film's predominant 2s. The final universe kept "tightly under wraps" was Earth-42.
- The Lego sequence was made by 14-year-old Canadian animator Preston Mutanga, added late after the filmmakers were impressed by his fan-made Lego recreation of the first teaser and tracked him down.
- Character design: Miles was updated for a growth spurt; Gwen got a new haircut and costume. Rick Leonardi, co-creator of Spider-Man 2099, adapted his own designs; Brian Stelfreeze shaped Jess Drew. The Spot's design, influenced by Egon Schiele, evolves from an "unfinished sketch [with] blue construction lines" as he gains control, with portals meant to look like "living ink that had spilled or splattered". The Vulture got a Renaissance design from Leonardo da Vinci's workbooks; the "Go Home Machine" spider was influenced by, and named "Ynyr" after, *Krull* (1983). Gwen's pink hair highlights came from a reference mix-up with Gwen Poole - production designer Patrick O'Keefe credited artist Peter Chan in January 2024, based on Gurihiru's *The Unbelievable Gwenpool*, with her bedroom palette also drawn from Gwenpool's hospital gown. Margo Kess / Spider-Byte took the longest to design and animate, with 1980s-90s hologram technology as reference. Miguel's suit resembles video screening, with a "laser cape" that fluctuates in visibility.

wikis.title: Post-production and the allegations of poor working conditions
wikis.summary: The film's cliffhanger ending, its completion 13 days before release, and Vulture's June 2023 report that constant revisions drove over 100 artists off the project.
wikis.body:
- In May 2023 Powers said the film ends on a cliffhanger and Dos Santos compared it to *The Empire Strikes Back* (1980). Powers: "*Across the Spider-Verse* is a movie on its own, but it definitely ends on a bit of a cliffhanger... it helps that we knew going in that this was part two of a three-part story."
- Powers also said the film is not "tied" to the Marvel Cinematic Universe, despite Miguel's line telling Gwen not to "get [him] started on Doctor Strange and that little nerd back on Earth-199999", which attributes *No Way Home*'s events to the collider explosion - a throwaway line Lord and Miller came up with. Donald Glover's live-action Prowler cameo depicts him as a prisoner of the Spider-Society displaced from his home reality.
- Production was completed on May 20, 2023, 13 days before the US release date.
- On June 23, 2023 Vulture reported that four people who worked on the film alleged production difficulties from numerous requests by Lord for changes to already finished animation and his need to approve layouts early. His directions were said to take precedence over the directing team's and to have caused weeks of long overtime as animators drastically revised portions of the film several times; over 100 artists were said to have left before completion, with *Into the Spider-Verse* and *The Mitchells vs. the Machines* said to have suffered similar issues. One artist said *Beyond the Spider-Verse* had not progressed and there was "no way that" it would meet its scheduled March 2024 release window.
- Sony denied the allegations about *Across the Spider-Verse*'s production while declining to comment on a possible sequel delay; producer Amy Pascal called heavy revision normal. After the 2023 Writers Guild of America strike, *Beyond the Spider-Verse* was delayed to June 25, 2027 and then moved up to June 18, 2027.

wikis.title: Music and marketing
wikis.summary: Daniel Pemberton's score, Metro Boomin's soundtrack, and the film's promotional campaign and tie-ins.
wikis.body:
- Daniel Pemberton confirmed in December 2020 that he would return to score the sequel. In December 2022 Lord and Miller confirmed Metro Boomin would create music for the soundtrack, featuring 21 Savage, Swae Lee, Lil Wayne, Future, Nas, ASAP Rocky, Lil Uzi Vert, Wizkid, Coi Leray, Offset, Becky G, Shenseea, A Boogie wit da Hoodie, JID, Don Toliver, James Blake and 2 Chainz. The Japanese release featured an original song, "Realize" by Lisa. The single "Mona Lisa" by Dominic Fike was released on June 2, 2023, originally for the soundtrack's deluxe edition, then removed days later and added to some versions of Fike's album *Sunburn* (July 7, 2023) - a passage the article tags "[better source needed]".
- Daniel Kaluuya searched Spotify for "Spider-Punk" fan playlists to gauge the character's energy, wanted the voice "to feel like a song", and the take used in the film had him "rapping, but in a punk style".
- Marketing: a May 2020 promotional partnership with Hyundai Motor Company; a prologue at Comic Con Experience in December 2021 revealing the title and two-part structure; 15 minutes of unfinished animation at CinemaCon in April 2022 and the same footage with updated animation at Annecy in June; Funko Pops in February 2023; another 14 minutes at CinemaCon in April 2023. The second trailer, released April 4, 2023, gained 148.6 million views in 24 hours - the most-viewed second trailer for a Marvel film in that span and the most-viewed superhero trailer of the summer - and was discussed by Rolling Stone's Larisha Paul, Entertainment Weekly's Christian Holub and The Hollywood Reporter's Abid Rahman.
- Tie-ins: a Burger King collaboration from May 15, 2023 (Spider-Verse Whopper with a red bun, Spider-Verse Sundae); a Nike Air Jordan 1 High OG on May 20; Fortnite skins of Miles Morales and Spider-Man 2099 added by Epic Games on May 23; limited-edition ZOTAC RTX 4070 graphics cards.

wikis.title: Themes
wikis.summary: What the article says the film is about: canon events and determinism, Miles's individuality, and community and support.
wikis.body:
- The film tackles trauma and the necessity for heroes to suffer for the greater good, represented through Miguel's enforced theory of the canon: the Spider-Society holds that certain "canon events" keep the Spider-Verse stable and that interfering - saving someone "destined" to die - can destroy a dimension. Miles opposes this, and the two clash over ideals. Shameik Moore said Miguel is not a villain but "just not on the same side of the fence as Miles", following a different "moral compass", and that the film shows "power lies in unity".
- Individuality and choice are challenged by determinism: the Spider-Society calls Miles an "anomaly" and interdimensional error because the spider that bit him came from another dimension, and he chooses his individuality against a corrupted system to save his father. Gwen is torn between the Society and her bond with Miles, forced to follow a doctrine she does not agree with under threat of banishment; exiled for defending Miles, she is spared arrest when George chooses love for his daughter over pursuit, saving himself from his canon event, which spurs her to reform the Spider Gang.
- Support and connection run through the film. Lord said Miles is trying to be his own person without losing where he came from. Thompson described Miles and Gwen as seeing each other as "the only one person in any dimension that can understand them". Jess takes Gwen in as a pupil and becomes a mother figure, though that relationship fades, while Hobie stays loyal to both.
- Kaluuya said Hobie stands for resistance against a corrupt system, observing that "even though there is community that is seemingly heroes empowering people, they can still form an establishment that eradicates the individual".
- The creators wanted to reinforce the first film's message that "anyone can wear the mask", developing "canon events" as meta-commentary on "canon, and rules and who gets to be [Spider-Man]"; Miles's isolation and conflict with the Society was based on the negative fan response to the character in his early Marvel Comics appearances, with Thompson saying "the entire world should be represented in that character".

wikis.title: Release, box office, reviews and accolades
wikis.summary: The film's release and versions, the MENA withdrawal over transgender iconography, its $690.8 million gross, critical acclaim and awards.
wikis.body:
- Release: premiered May 30, 2023 at the Grand Rex in Paris and the Regency Village Theater in Los Angeles; US release June 2 in premium large formats and IMAX, not in 3D; Beijing premiere May 31 and China release June 2; IMAX re-release January 19, 2024 with a new 100th-anniversary Columbia Pictures logo.
- Versions: on June 9, 2023 Sony sent theaters an updated version with new audio mixing after sound-mixing complaints; an official source told Variety the issues were at only a "handful of theaters" but all prints were updated. At least two versions with slight differences in dialogue and animation were reported - in one, a Miguel-Lyla scene ends with a fist bump, in another with a selfie - confirmed by associate editor Andy Leviton. The digital release removed several lines; Miller described it as "an international version" made for translation and French censorship approval, with shots "cleaned up and tweaked" - "it's like there's a multiverse of the movie" - while Lord thought some changes improved the film; some alterations were controversial with fans.
- MENA: release was delayed in the region to June 22, 2023 and then withdrawn because the film briefly features transgender iconography, including a "Protect Trans Kids" transgender flag in Gwen's bedroom. This prompted readings of Gwen's arc as a transgender allegory, supported by the flag's colours recurring in her scenes; others noted those colours were already used by the comics' Spider-Woman Gwen Stacy, so they are not proof the character is trans. She is not identified as transgender in the film.
- Streaming rights: Sony's April 2021 deals gave Netflix exclusive "pay 1 window" rights (typically 18 months, building on a 2014 output deal with Sony Pictures Animation) and Disney "pay 2 window" rights for Disney+, Hulu and linear networks. Netflix US October 31, 2023; Disney+ May 1, 2025.
- Box office: $381.6 million in the United States and Canada and $309.2 million elsewhere for $690.8 million worldwide; it passed *Into the Spider-Verse*'s $384.5 million total after 12 days and overtook *The Smurfs* as Sony Pictures Animation's highest-grossing film. Deadline Hollywood calculated a net profit of $328 million, third on its 2023 "Most Valuable Blockbusters" list. It made $17.35 million in Thursday previews (third-best for an animated film after *The Lion King* and *Incredibles 2*), $51.7 million on Friday and $120.7 million in its opening weekend from 4,313 theaters - second-highest of 2023 behind *The Super Mario Bros. Movie* ($146.4 million) and eighth-best ever for an animated film - then $55.5 million, $27.8 million and $19.3 million in weekends two to four. Internationally it took $88.1 million from 59 markets in its opening weekend, $47 million in weekend two (a 44% drop) and $27.6 million from 60 markets in weekend three; top territories as of July 9, 2023 were China ($49.6 million), the UK ($35 million), Mexico ($27.8 million), Australia ($20.6 million) and France ($13.4 million).
- Reviews: Rotten Tomatoes 95% of 386 critics, average 8.6/10, consensus "Just as visually dazzling and action-packed as its predecessor, *Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse* thrills from start to cliffhanger conclusion." Metacritic 86/100 from 60 critics ("universal acclaim"); CinemaScore "A"; PostTrak 93% positive with 82% definite recommendation. Brian Tallerico (RogerEbert.com) gave 4/4; Ann Hornaday (The Washington Post) 3/4; Richard Roeper (Chicago Sun-Times) 3/4; Kevin Maher (The Times) 4/5; praise also from Rolling Stone, Vulture and The Atlantic. Kyle Smith (The Wall Street Journal) called it "visually hypercaffeinated" with a slow first half and "too many long monologues"; Jake Wilson (The Age) gave 3/5.
- Accolades: nominated for Best Animated Feature at the 96th Academy Awards; seven Annie Awards, winning all; two BAFTA nominations; three Critics' Choice Movie Awards, winning one; three Golden Globe nominations; named one of the ten best films of 2023 by the American Film Institute; won the National Board of Review Award for Best Animated Film; IndieWire listed it as the second greatest animated film of the 21st century.
- Other responses: Guillermo del Toro said "Spider-Verse will fulfill and heal"; Andrew Garfield called it "a masterpiece of pure cinema"; Bryce Dallas Howard called it "an astonishing film on every level"; the *Kung Fu Panda 4* filmmakers cited the films as inspiration for their "inkbrush" fight scenes. A "canon events" meme spread on TikTok after release, and Collins Dictionary selected "canon event" as one of ten contenders for its 2023 Word of the Year, defining it as "an event that is essential to the formation of an individual's character or identity".

wikis.title: Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse (upcoming film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia's article on Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse, the third Spider-Verse film - its credits, premise, returning voice cast, long production delays and its scheduled June 18, 2027 release.
wikis.body:
## The film

- An upcoming American animated superhero film based on the Marvel Comics character Miles Morales / Spider-Man, "the direct sequel to Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse (2023) and the final installment in the Spider-Verse trilogy".
- Directed by Bob Persichetti and Justin K. Thompson, written by Phil Lord, Christopher Miller and David Callaham; produced by Lord, Miller, Amy Pascal, Avi Arad and Jinko Gotoh. Cinematography Alice Brooks, editing Mike Andrews, music Daniel Pemberton.
- Produced by Columbia Pictures and Sony Pictures Animation with Arad Productions, Lord Miller Productions and Pascal Pictures; distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing. No runtime, budget or gross is given.
- Shameik Moore returns as Miles Morales, with Hailee Steinfeld, Brian Tyree Henry, Lauren Vélez, Jake Johnson, Jason Schwartzman (the Spot), Karan Soni, John Mulaney, Kimiko Glenn, Daniel Kaluuya, Mahershala Ali, Nicolas Cage and Oscar Isaac, plus Marvin Jones III, Greta Lee and Jharrel Jerome.

## Story

- Begins immediately after the Across the Spider-Verse cliffhanger, with Miles trapped on Earth-42, on the run from the Spider-People across the multiverse and trying to save his family. Lord and Miller call it the most emotional film of the trilogy and a "massive finale" with a "satisfying conclusion".

## Release date history

- Scheduled for release in the United States on June 18, 2027, in IMAX and premium large formats - "the first Sony animated film to do so" - presented in IMAX's 1.43:1 aspect ratio.
- Earlier dates: March 29, 2024 (set April 2022), removed from the schedule in July 2023 during the SAG-AFTRA strike; June 4, 2027 announced at CinemaCon in March 2025; pushed to June 25, 2027 in July 2025; moved up to June 18, 2027 in September 2025.

## Production

- Development began by November 2018; the sequel was split into two films by February 2021, revealed in December 2021. Work on the third film was shelved to finish Across the Spider-Verse, and production resumed by December 2023 after the strike.
- Persichetti and Thompson were confirmed as directors in December 2024. The film uses a wider variation of animation styles than the first two, with Sony Pictures Imageworks providing art and designs and Unreal Engine previsualization; Miller said generative AI would not be used.
- First footage shown at CinemaCon in March 2025 and again in April 2026; a four-and-a-half-minute rough cut leaked online in August, which Miller condemned as not fully rendered.

## About the capture

- Part 2 of the capture is the article's reference list, navigation boxes and categories; the article text is in part 1. The page states no last-edited date.

wikis.title: Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse: premise, cast, production and release date
wikis.summary: Wikipedia's article body on the upcoming animated film Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse, covering its credits, premise, voice cast, development and delays, writing, animation, marketing and its June 18, 2027 release date.
wikis.body:
## Film and credits

- "Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse is an upcoming American animated superhero film based on the Marvel Comics character Miles Morales / Spider-Man", the direct sequel to Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse (2023) and "the final installment in the Spider-Verse trilogy".
- Directed by Bob Persichetti and Justin K. Thompson; written by Phil Lord, Christopher Miller and David Callaham. Produced by Phil Lord, Christopher Miller, Amy Pascal, Avi Arad and Jinko Gotoh.
- Cinematography Alice Brooks; edited by Mike Andrews; music by Daniel Pemberton.
- Production companies: Columbia Pictures, Sony Pictures Animation, Arad Productions, Lord Miller Productions, Pascal Pictures. Distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing.
- Release date June 18, 2027. Country United States, language English. The infobox gives no runtime, budget or gross.

## Premise

- Begins immediately after the events of Across the Spider-Verse (2023), "following Miles Morales trapped and on the run in an alternate universe while trying to save his family".

## Voice cast

- Shameik Moore as Miles Morales / Spider-Man, the Spider-Man of Earth-1610 trapped on Earth-42; Hailee Steinfeld as Gwen Stacy / Spider-Gwen of Earth-65, "Miles's love interest"; Brian Tyree Henry as Jefferson Morales (nee Davis), a police officer "recently promoted to captain"; Lauren Vélez as Rio Morales; Jake Johnson as Peter B. Parker of Earth-616B, now married to Mary Jane Watson with a daughter named Mayday.
- Jason Schwartzman as Dr. Johnathon Ohnn / The Spot, "Miles's nemesis, he sets out to destroy their home universe and murder Miles's father"; Karan Soni as Pavitr Prabhakar / Spider-Man India of Mumbattan; John Mulaney as Peter Porker / Spider-Ham; Daniel Kaluuya as Hobie Brown / Spider-Punk of Earth-138; Mahershala Ali as the Earth-42 Aaron Davis; Nicolas Cage as Spider-Man Noir; Kimiko Glenn as Peni Parker / SP//dr; Oscar Isaac as Miguel O'Hara / Spider-Man 2099 of Earth-928, leader of the Spider-Society.
- Also reprising roles: Marvin Jones III as Lonnie Lincoln / Tombstone, Greta Lee as the AI assistant Lyla, and Jharrel Jerome as the Earth-42 Miles G. Morales / The Prowler.

## Development timeline

- By November 2018, ahead of Into the Spider-Verse's release the next month, Sony Pictures Animation had begun developing a sequel. Lord and Miller decided by February 2021 to split the second film into two parts; this was revealed in December 2021 as Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse (Part One) and (Part Two), worked on simultaneously with directors Joaquim Dos Santos, Kemp Powers and Justin K. Thompson.
- In April 2022 the second part was dated March 29, 2024, when Sony pushed the first part from October 2022 to June 2023, and the films were renamed Across the Spider-Verse and Beyond the Spider-Verse. Script, storyboards and visual development work for the third film were reportedly shelved so the second could be finished; Beyond was internally not expected to meet the March 2024 date and "was not expected to be released until 2026 or 2027".
- At Annecy in June 2022 Sony announced the Spot would be the antagonist of both films.
- May 2023: Miller said the beginning and ending were relatively figured out but the middle was "still a little squishy". July 2023: Sony removed the film from its release schedule because the SAG-AFTRA strike prevented voice recording, and gave the March 2024 date to Ghostbusters: Frozen Empire. The strike ended in November; production had resumed by December 2023.
- June 2024: Pemberton said the team was "beavering away" and wanted to avoid the "mistakes" of third installments such as The Godfather Part III (1990). August 2024: Karan Soni said voice recording was slated to begin in "a few months" and the film was "deep in production".
- September 2024: journalist Jeff Sneider reported the film was "unlikely to be released until 2027 at the earliest", partly because Sony was not expected to release it in the same calendar year as Spider-Man: Brand New Day, "scheduled for release in July 2026"; Pemberton and Miller denied that a majority of the film had been "scrapped".
- December 2024: Persichetti and Thompson confirmed as directors, Jinko Gotoh joined as producer, and Lord, Miller and David Callaham confirmed as writers. January 2025: Jharrel Jerome said voice recording had yet to begin.
- March 2025 (CinemaCon): new release date announced as June 4, 2027. July 2025: delayed three weeks to June 25, 2027. September 2025: moved up to June 18, 2027.
- February 2026: Sony Pictures Animation co-presidents Damien de Froberville and Kristine Belson described Lord and Miller frequently iterating on the story, helped by their editing Project Hail Mary (2026) on the Sony lot. Lord and Miller cited the delays as the crew "[h]aving to take it apart to put it back together again". The following month they reaffirmed the June 2027 date, and in early July said the crew was well into editing, "coming together really well".

## Writing

- Lord and Miller call it the most emotional film of the trilogy, a "massive finale" giving a "satisfying conclusion".
- The story starts immediately after the Across the Spider-Verse cliffhanger with Miles trapped on Earth-42 and dealing with a "sense of betrayal"; Miles is on the run as a fugitive from the Spider-People and may not be able to rely on friends such as Gwen.
- The writers only found a complete three-act structure once they devised a middle theme: "when your family is broken apart by your calling, your talents, how do you put them back together? How do you have it all?"

## Voice recording

- Delayed by the SAG-AFTRA strike by July 2023, set to resume that November. Steinfeld had started recording by April [2025] and said they were "well into" the process; Moore and Jerome were recording by August; Johnson had been recording for several months by March 2026; Lee recorded alongside Across the Spider-Verse.

## Animation, design and music

- The film "features a wider variation of animation styles than the first two films". Sony Pictures Imageworks is providing art and designs; Mike Andrews returns as lead editor; Miller said they used the Unreal Engine and a virtual camera for previsualization after doing so with cinematographer Greig Fraser on Project Hail Mary.
- Designed to fit IMAX's 1.43:1 expanded aspect ratio, with artistically abstract portal scenes for the Spot.
- Miller said generative AI would not be used in the film; Sony Pictures Imageworks used some machine learning technology, distinct from generative AI, on the preceding films. This followed Sony Pictures CEO Tony Vinciquerra saying in May 2024 that the studio was exploring AI to make films less expensive.
- Daniel Pemberton confirmed his return in June 2024, working to connect the score with those of the prior films.

## Marketing

- First footage debuted at Sony's CinemaCon panel in March 2025, with a monologue of Miles declaring he would do things "his way"; Sony released five promotional stills. New footage was presented at CinemaCon in April 2026 with four additional stills.
- "The four-and-a-half-minute-long rough cut footage leaked online in August" [2025 or 2026 not stated in that sentence]; Miller condemned the leak and said the footage was not yet complete or fully rendered. Coverage quoted from The Hollywood Reporter, Kotaku and Gizmodo.

## Release

- Scheduled for theatrical release by Sony Pictures Releasing in the United States on June 18, 2027, in IMAX and premium large formats, "the first Sony animated film to do so", presented in 1.43:1 for IMAX.
- Originally scheduled for March 29, 2024; removed from the calendar in July 2023; given June 4, 2027 in March 2025; pushed three weeks to June 25 "to accommodate the film's K–12 target audience and international markets"; then moved forward a week for the Father's Day weekend.
- Home media: April 2021 Sony deals with Netflix ("pay 1 window", typically 18 months, covering the Into the Spider-Verse sequels) and Disney ("pay 2 window" for Disney+, Hulu and Disney's linear networks). In January 2026 Sony and Netflix announced a new agreement giving Netflix pay 1 rights globally, beginning later in 2026 as territory rights became available and fully taking effect in early 2029.
