wikis.title: Shrek (2001 film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia's article on Shrek - its credits, plot, the recasting from Chris Farley to Mike Myers, PDI's animation, its May 2001 release, box office, acclaim, first Academy Award for Best Animated Feature and the sequels that followed.
wikis.body:
## The film

- A 2001 American animated fantasy comedy film directed by Andrew Adamson and Vicky Jenson, written by Ted Elliott, Terry Rossio, Joe Stillman and Roger S. H. Schulman, "loosely based on the 1990 children's picture book Shrek! by William Steig", and the first installment in the Shrek film series.
- Stars Mike Myers as Shrek, Eddie Murphy as Donkey, Cameron Diaz as Princess Fiona and John Lithgow as Lord Farquaad. Produced by Aron Warner, John H. Williams and Jeffrey Katzenberg for DreamWorks Animation and PDI/DreamWorks; music by Harry Gregson-Williams and John Powell. Running time 90 minutes; budget $60 million.

## Dates and figures

- Premiered at the Mann Village Theatre in Westwood on April 22, 2001 and released in the United States on May 18, 2001; competed for the Palme d'Or at the 2001 Cannes Film Festival. Re-released theatrically in the United States on May 15, 2026 for its 25th anniversary.
- Worldwide gross is given as $494.3 million in the infobox and lead, while the box office section says it closed on December 6, 2001 with $267.7 million domestic and $216.7 million overseas "for a worldwide total of $484.4 million". Either way it is called the fourth highest-grossing film of 2001.
- Opening weekend $42.3 million from 3,587 theaters. Home video: released on VHS and DVD November 2, 2001, selling 2.5 million DVDs in three days and generating more than $420 million in DVD and VHS revenue.

## Production

- Steven Spielberg bought the book's rights in 1991; Katzenberg put the film into active development in November 1995 at DreamWorks.
- Chris Farley recorded nearly all of Shrek's dialogue before dying in 1997; Mike Myers replaced him, insisted on a script rewrite and later re-recorded his lines with a Scottish accent after seeing a rough cut in February 2000.
- The film was first planned as a motion-capture hybrid; after the May 1997 test failed, Pacific Data Images took over from 1998 and produced the final computer animation, finished in 2000. The film has 31 sequences, 1,288 shots and 36 in-film locations.

## Reception and legacy

- Rotten Tomatoes 89% from 214 reviews (average 7.8/10); Metacritic 84 out of 100 from 34 critics; CinemaScore "A".
- Won the first Academy Award for Best Animated Feature and was nominated for Best Adapted Screenplay; won the BAFTA for Best Adapted Screenplay and several Annie Awards; named one of the AFI's top ten films of 2001.
- Selected for the National Film Registry in 2020, "the first animated film of the 21st century to be preserved".
- Followed by Shrek 2 (2004), Shrek the Third (2007) and Shrek Forever After (2010); Shrek 5 is scheduled for 2027 and the spin-off Donkey for June 30, 2028.

## About the capture

- Part 2 of the capture is the reference list, navigation boxes and categories; the article text is in part 1. The page states no last-edited date.

wikis.title: Shrek (2001 film): plot, voice cast, production, release, reception, accolades and legacy
wikis.summary: Wikipedia's article body on the 2001 DreamWorks film Shrek, covering its credits and figures, plot, voice cast, development from William Steig's book, the recasting after Chris Farley's death, animation, music, home media, box office, reviews, its awards table and the later Shrek films.
wikis.body:
## Film and credits

- "Shrek is a 2001 American animated fantasy comedy film directed by Andrew Adamson and Vicky Jenson, and written by Ted Elliott, Terry Rossio, Joe Stillman, and Roger S. H. Schulman, loosely based on the 1990 children's picture book Shrek! by William Steig." First installment in the Shrek film series.
- Produced by Aron Warner, John H. Williams and Jeffrey Katzenberg; edited by Sim Evan-Jones; music by Harry Gregson-Williams and John Powell.
- Production companies DreamWorks Animation and PDI/DreamWorks; distributed by DreamWorks Pictures (through DreamWorks Distribution). A note says that in July 2014 the distribution rights were bought by DreamWorks Animation from Paramount Pictures and transferred to 20th Century Fox before reverting to Universal Pictures in 2018.
- Release dates: April 22, 2001 (Mann Village Theatre) and May 18, 2001 (United States). Running time 90 minutes. Country United States, language English.
- Budget $60 million. Box office given in the infobox and lead as $494.3 million (sourced to The Numbers).
- Shown at the 2001 Cannes Film Festival competing for the Palme d'Or. The lead calls it "the first animated film since The Missing Link (1980) to be chosen as main competition at the festival"; a footnote instead says Shrek "is the first animated film to have entered in competition from the festival for five decades, since Disney's Peter Pan (1953)".
- In 2020 the Library of Congress selected Shrek for the National Film Registry, "becoming the first animated film of the 21st century to be preserved".

## Plot

- Shrek is an ogre whose swamp is overrun by fairy tale creatures exiled by Lord Farquaad of Duloc. Shrek and Donkey confront Farquaad, who agrees to relocate the creatures if Shrek rescues Princess Fiona from a dragon-guarded castle so Farquaad can marry her and become king.
- Fiona transforms into an ogress at night; only "true love's first kiss" will break the spell and let her "take love's true form". Shrek mishears her and brings Farquaad to marry her.
- Shrek interrupts the wedding; Dragon, ridden by Donkey, devours Farquaad; Shrek and Fiona kiss, the curse breaks and she remains an ogress. They marry in the swamp and leave for their honeymoon (the honeymoon is noted "As depicted in Shrek 2 (2004)").

## Voice cast

- Mike Myers as Shrek and one of the Three Blind Mice; Eddie Murphy as Donkey; Cameron Diaz as Princess Fiona; John Lithgow as Lord Farquaad; Vincent Cassel as "Monsieur" Robin Hood; Conrad Vernon as Gingerbread Man; Chris Miller as Magic Mirror and Geppetto; Cody Cameron as Pinocchio and the Three Little Pigs; Simon J. Smith as Blind Mouse; Christopher Knights as Thelonius and a Blind Mouse; Aron Warner as Big Bad Wolf; Jim Cummings as Captain of the Guards; Kathleen Freeman as the Old Woman (her last film role before her death); Andrew Adamson as Duloc Mascot; Bobby Block as Baby Bear; Michael Galasso as Peter Pan.

## Development

- Steven Spielberg bought the rights to Steig's book in 1991, before DreamWorks was founded, planning a traditionally animated film with Bill Murray as Shrek and Steve Martin as Donkey. Producer John H. Williams brought the book to DreamWorks, and after buying the rights Katzenberg put it in active development in November 1995.
- Adamson and Kelly Asbury joined in 1997 to co-direct; Asbury left a year later for Spirit: Stallion of the Cimarron and was replaced by story artist Vicky Jenson.
- Early development 1996–1997 used Photoshop concept art placing Shrek's home in a garbage dump near a settlement "referenced as Wart Creek". Donkey was modeled on Pericles (born 1994; died 2025), a miniature donkey from Barron Park in Palo Alto, California. Supervising animator Raman Hui did over 100 sculptures of Fiona. Art directors visited Hearst Castle, Stratford upon Avon and Dordogne; art director Douglas Rogers visited a magnolia plantation in Charleston, South Carolina for the swamp. Goldilocks and Sleeping Beauty were planned but unused.
- Elliott and Rossio began writing in 1997 and worked on the project for two years, and were also credited as co-producers.

## Casting

- Nicolas Cage was offered the role of Shrek and turned it down; Ian Bagg auditioned and was rejected.
- "Chris Farley was initially hired to voice Shrek, and he had recorded nearly all of the dialogue for the character, but died before completing the project." David Spade said Farley had 5 days of voice work left; a story reel with Farley's dialogue leaked in August 2015.
- Katzenberg pitched the film to Mike Myers at the premiere of Saving Private Ryan (1998); Myers insisted on a complete script rewrite. Myers recorded through 1999 and, after seeing a rough cut in February 2000, asked to re-record all his lines with a Scottish accent. Katzenberg said: "It was so good we took $4M worth of animation out and did it again." Myers disputed the cost, saying "it didn't cost the studio 'millions of dollars'" and that he went in for twenty sessions instead of ten for the same pay.
- Janeane Garofalo was set to play Princess Fiona alongside Farley but was fired for unexplained reasons. Chris Rock says DreamWorks twice asked him to replace Murphy as Donkey and he regrets turning it down.

## Animation

- Shrek was originally to be a live-action/animation hybrid with motion-captured computer graphics using an ExpertVision Hires Falcon 10 camera system, with Softimage and Mental Ray. After a year and a half of R&D the test screened in May 1997; Katzenberg said "It looked terrible, it didn't work, it wasn't funny, and we didn't like it." The test, Shrek – I Feel Good Animation Test, was not released publicly until 2023, posted by production designer Barry E. Jackson on YouTube (elsewhere the article calls it "The film's 1996 animation test").
- Pacific Data Images began production with the studio in 1998, using its proprietary Fluid Animation System plus Maya for cloth and for Fiona's and Farquaad's hair. Ken Bielenberg led the visual effects group.
- "Shrek has 31 sequences, with 1,288 total shots" and 36 separate in-film locations, which DreamWorks claimed was more than any previous computer-animated feature. The animation was completed in 2000.

## Music

- Third DreamWorks animated film with Harry Gregson-Williams and John Powell after Antz (1998) and Chicken Run (2000). Score recorded at Abbey Road Studios by Nick Wollage and Slamm Andrews.
- Smash Mouth's "All Star" was used in the opening credits after being a placeholder; Self's "Stay Home" moved to the credits. Katzenberg suggested redoing the ending "to go out with a big laugh", adding Smash Mouth's cover of The Monkees' "I'm a Believer".
- Rufus Wainwright's "Hallelujah" is on the soundtrack album but John Cale's version is in the film.

## Release and marketing

- Premiered at the Mann Village Theatre in Westwood on April 22, 2001; released in the United States on May 18, 2001. "In celebration of its 25th anniversary, Shrek was theatrically re-released in the United States on May 15, 2026."
- A planned IMAX 3D re-release for the Christmas season of 2001 or the following summer, with new sequences and an alternate ending, was dropped over "creative changes", resulting in a loss of $1.18 million, down from IMAX's profit of $3.24 million. A THX trailer with Shrek and Donkey planned for November 2001 was cut.
- Radio Disney was told not to allow ads for the film, later relaxed to allow soundtrack ads. Burger King began promotions on May 7, 2001 with nine Candy Caddies; Baskin-Robbins ran an 8-week promotion.

## Home media

- Released on VHS and DVD on November 2, 2001, selling 2.5 million DVDs in the first three days - passing The Phantom Menace's record - plus 4.5 million VHS copies in the same span. Both included the 3-minute short Shrek in the Swamp Karaoke Dance Party.
- Its video release made more than $100 million in the weekend Monsters, Inc. opened to more than $62 million. It became the biggest selling DVD at the time with over 5.5 million sales, generated more than $420 million in DVD and VHS revenue and had sold more than 21 million of the 23 million copies shipped by January 2002, with more than 10 million DVDs sold worldwide by then.
- Blu-ray 3D released December 1, 2010 with its sequels; 2D Blu-ray boxset six days later; Ultra HD Blu-ray on May 11, 2021 for the 20th anniversary. DreamWorks Animation was purchased by NBCUniversal for $3.8 billion on April 28, 2016.

## Box office

- Opened on around 6,000 screens across 3,587 theaters, then the second highest number of locations in history behind Mission: Impossible 2; eleven locations screened it digitally.
- First day $11.6 million; opening weekend $42.3 million (average $11,805), first place. Second weekend $42.5 million, $55.2 million over the four-day Memorial Day weekend, second behind Pearl Harbor. Third weekend $28.2 million.
- By mid-June 2001 it was the top-grossing movie of the year domestically until Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone in December. It closed on December 6, 2001 with "$267.7 million domestically, along with $216.7 million overseas, for a worldwide total of $484.4 million" - against the $494.3 million worldwide figure in the infobox and lead. Fourth highest-grossing film of 2001.
- Became the highest-grossing animated film released in Australia, passing The Lion King (1994); in the United Kingdom it earned $20.3 million since opening.

## Critical response

- Rotten Tomatoes: 89% of 214 reviews positive, average 7.8/10. Metacritic: 84 out of 100 from 34 critics ("universal acclaim"). CinemaScore grade "A".
- Roger Ebert gave four stars out of four, "jolly and wicked, filled with sly in-jokes and yet somehow possessing a heart". Other praise quoted from Susan Wloszczyna, Richard Schickel, Peter Rainer, Peter Travers, James Berardinelli (3.5/4), Kenneth Turan, Lisa Schwarzbaum (A−), Elvis Mitchell (4/5), Stephen Hunter (5/5) and others. William Steig and his wife Jeanne "loved it".
- Mixed and negative: Mark Caro (2.5/4), Michael Atkinson, Christy Lemire ("90-minute onslaught of in-jokes") and Anthony Lane.

## Accolades (table)

- 74th Academy Awards: won Best Animated Feature (Aron Warner) - the first-ever award in that category, beating Monsters, Inc. and Jimmy Neutron: Boy Genius - and was nominated for Best Adapted Screenplay, the first animated film nominated in that category.
- 55th BAFTA Awards: won Best Adapted Screenplay; nominated for Best Film, Best Actor in a Supporting Role (Eddie Murphy, noted as the first and so far only actor to receive a BAFTA nomination for a voice-over performance), Best Film Music, Best Sound and Best Visual Effects.
- 29th Annie Awards: wins including Animated Theatrical Feature, Directing (Adamson and Jenson), Music Score, Production Design, Storyboarding, Writing, Effects Animation and Voice Acting (Eddie Murphy).
- American Film Institute Awards: AFI Movie of the Year, won. 2001 Cannes Film Festival: Palme d'Or, nominated. 7th Critics' Choice Awards: won Best Animated Feature, nominated Best Picture. 59th Golden Globe Awards: nominated Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy. 28th People's Choice Awards: won Favorite Motion Picture and Favorite Actor in a Comedy (Murphy). Also nominations at the Grammys, MTV Movie Awards, Kids' Choice Awards (two wins listed for Murphy), Saturn Awards, PGA (the first animated film to earn a PGA nomination), BET and Black Reel Awards.

## Legacy and other media

- AFI's 10 Top 10 (June 2008): eighth best animated film and "the only non-Disney·Pixar film in the Top 10". Second in Channel 4's "100 Greatest Family Films" behind E.T.; sixth in Channel 4's 100 Greatest Cartoons (2005); third on Bravo's 100 funniest films (2006). Shrek received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in May 2010.
- Video games include Shrek (2001), Shrek: Hassle at the Castle (2002), Shrek: Extra Large (2002), Shrek: Super Party (2002) and Shrek SuperSlam (2005), plus appearances in Tony Hawk's Underground 2 (2004) and the 2026 mobile game FIFA Heroes. Dark Horse Comics released a three-issue adaptation in 2003.
- Shrek The Musical (music by Jeanine Tesori, book and lyrics by David Lindsay-Abaire) opened on Broadway December 14, 2008 and closed January 3, 2010 after 441 performances; a North American tour opened July 25, 2010 in Chicago and a West End production on June 7, 2011. It won the 2009 Tony Award for Best Costume Design.
- The fan remake Shrek Retold was released through 3GI Industries on November 29, 2018, made by 200 filmmakers.

## Sequels

- Shrek 2 (2004), Shrek the Third (2007) and Shrek Forever After (2010), plus the shorts Shrek the Halls (2007) and Scared Shrekless (2010) and the spin-offs Puss in Boots (2011) and Puss in Boots: The Last Wish (2022).
- Murphy said in June 2024 that he had begun voice recording for Shrek 5 months earlier. "Shrek 5 is scheduled to be released in 2027." A spin-off film, Donkey, is in development, "set for June 30, 2028".

wikis.title: Shrek the Third
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 2007 DreamWorks Animation film Shrek the Third: plot, voice cast, production, box office, reviews, awards, home media, marketing and the sequels.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- 2007 American animated fantasy comedy film, "loosely based on the 1990 children's picture book Shrek! by William Steig", produced by DreamWorks Animation with PDI/DreamWorks and distributed by Paramount Pictures.
- Directed by Chris Miller; screenplay by Jeffrey Price, Peter S. Seaman, Miller and producer Aron Warner; story by Andrew Adamson; edited by Michael Andrews; music by Harry Gregson-Williams.
- Sequel to Shrek 2 (2004) and the third installment in the Shrek film series.
- Running time 93 minutes; country United States; language English. Budget $160 million; box office $808.3 million.
- Release dates: May 6, 2007 (Mann Village Theatre premiere, Westwood, Los Angeles) and May 18, 2007 (United States).
- Plot premise: Prince Charming plots to overthrow Shrek and Fiona, who inherit the throne after King Harold's death; Shrek tries to install Fiona's "underachieving 16-year-old cousin Artie" instead.

## Voice cast
- Mike Myers (Shrek), Eddie Murphy (Donkey), Cameron Diaz (Princess Fiona), Antonio Banderas (Puss in Boots), Julie Andrews (Queen Lillian), John Cleese (King Harold), Rupert Everett (Prince Charming), Eric Idle (Merlin), Justin Timberlake (Arthur "Artie" Pendragon).
- Also Susanne Blakeslee, Cody Cameron, Larry King, Christopher Knights, John Krasinski (Lancelot), Ian McShane (Captain Hook), Cheri Oteri, Regis Philbin, Amy Poehler, Seth Rogen, Maya Rudolph (Rapunzel), Amy Sedaris, Conrad Vernon, Aron Warner, Tom Kane, Chris Miller, Mark Valley and Kari Wahlgren.

## Production
- After Shrek 2's success in May 2004, DreamWorks Animation CEO Jeffrey Katzenberg planned a five-film arc beginning with Shrek (2001) and concluding with a fifth installment.
- Screenwriters Jeffrey Price and Peter S. Seaman were hired, with Jon Zack as a consultant.
- Andrew Adamson did not direct, being occupied with The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, but stayed on as executive producer advising "approximately every four months". Chris Miller directed with Raman Hui co-directing.
- Working title Shrek 3; by March 2006 the title had changed to Shrek the Third. Miller said they "didn't want to just sort of title it like it was just a sequel", wanting "something to make it stand on its own"; Hui said "It's about Shrek becoming the new king of Far Far Away; the title sounds kind of royal as well."
- Originally set for November 2006; in December 2004 moved to May 2007. Katzenberg: "The sheer magnitude of the Shrek franchise has led us to conclude that a May release date, with a DVD release around the holiday season, will enable us to best maximize performance and increase profitability..." Flushed Away took the November 2006 slot. The change came the day after Disney/Pixar moved Cars from November 4, 2005 to June 9, 2006.

## Box office
- Opened in 4,122 North American cinemas on May 18, 2007, grossing $38 million on its first day - then the biggest opening day for an animated film, a record held until Toy Story 3 in 2010.
- First weekend $121.6 million, then the best opening weekend ever for an animated film and the second-highest US opening of 2007 behind Spider-Man 3; the animated record stood nine years until Finding Dory's $135.1 million in 2016. At the time it was the third-highest opening weekend of all time domestically.
- Grossed $322.7 million in the United States and $485.6 million overseas for a cumulative $808.3 million; fourth-highest-grossing film worldwide of 2007, second-highest in the US that year, highest-grossing animated film of 2007 and third-highest-grossing animated film ever at the time, behind Finding Nemo and Shrek 2. Estimated 46,907,000 tickets sold in North America.
- Released in the United Kingdom on June 29, 2007, topping the box office for two weekends before Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix.

## Critical response
- Rotten Tomatoes: 41% approval from 210 reviews, average 5.5/10, "the lowest-rated film in the Shrek franchise by the website to date"; consensus: "Shrek the Third has pop culture potshots galore, but at the expense of the heart, charm, and wit that made the first two Shreks classics."
- Metacritic: 58 out of 100 from 35 critics, "mixed or average reviews". CinemaScore "B+", the lowest grade in the franchise.
- Carina Chocano (Los Angeles Times) questioned the target demographic: "Does a kids' movie really need, among other similar touches, a Hooters joke?" David Ansen (Newsweek): "It's a movie at war with itself: a kiddie movie that doesn't really want to be one."
- Peter Bradshaw (The Guardian) gave 2 of 5, calling Merlin a "frankly unfunny new character" and a "rip-off of Albus Dumbledore"; The Times of London also 2 of 5; Roger Ebert gave two and a half of four, "a damped-down return"; Richard Roeper and Michael Phillips both gave "Two Thumbs Down"; Stephen Hunter (The Washington Post) called it a "paradox" both "quite funny and quite bad". A. O. Scott (The New York Times) was more positive: "at once more energetic and more relaxed [than its predecessors]".

## Awards and nominations
- Nominated: Annie Awards - Directing in an Animated Feature Production (Chris Miller, Raman Hui); BAFTA Awards - Best Animated Film (Chris Miller); Golden Reel Award - Best Sound Editing in Feature Film: Animated; VES Awards - Outstanding Effects in an Animated Motion Picture and Outstanding Performance by an Animated Character; Kids Choice Awards - Favorite Animated Movie and Favorite Voice (Cameron Diaz, Mike Myers nominated).
- Won: Kids Choice Awards Favorite Voice From an Animated Movie (Eddie Murphy); People's Choice Awards Favorite Family Movie.

## Home media and marketing
- Released on DVD and HD DVD November 13, 2007 (DVD in pan and scan and widescreen); the HD DVD used 1.78:1 1080p with Dolby Digital Plus 5.1 and HDi interactive extras.
- After Paramount discontinued HD DVD - making this "the only DreamWorks Animation film to be released on that format" - it came to Blu-ray on September 16, 2008, in the Shrek: The Whole Story boxset on December 7, 2010, separately again on August 30, 2011, on Blu-ray 3D on November 1, 2011 as a Best Buy exclusive, and on Ultra HD Blu-ray on September 12, 2023 from Universal Pictures Home Entertainment.
- DVD and Blu-ray sales revenue: $179.1 million.
- Large marketing campaign with toys, books, games and clothes through 2007; a tie-in video game for Wii, PlayStation 2, Xbox 360, Game Boy Advance, PSP, PC and Nintendo DS; a Gameloft mobile game in May 2007; Shrek n' Roll on Xbox Live Arcade November 14, 2007; a Stern Pinball machine.
- Adult Swim comedy team Tim and Eric, annoyed by the volume of advertising, independently "promoted" the film in internet videos and on television and radio.

## Controversy
- The coconut horse-hoof sound gag in Prince Charming's dinner theater repeats a joke from Monty Python and the Holy Grail, which also starred John Cleese and Eric Idle. Idle walked out of the premiere (later reentering) and said he was considering suing the producers over the unauthorized use of the gag; the producers said they were honoring Idle and Cleese.

## Sequels
- Followed by Shrek Forever After, released in theaters May 21, 2010, "and will be followed by Shrek 5, which is in development and set for release on June 30, 2027".

wikis.title: Shrek 5
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the upcoming DreamWorks Animation film Shrek 5: premise, voice cast, its long development history, music, marketing, its June 30, 2027 release date and the Donkey spin-off.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- "Shrek 5 is an upcoming American animated fantasy comedy film loosely based on the 1990 children's picture book Shrek! by William Steig and produced by DreamWorks Animation."
- Sequel to Shrek Forever After (2010); the fifth main installment in the Shrek film series and the seventh overall.
- Directed by Walt Dohrn and Conrad Vernon; written by Michael McCullers; produced by Chris Meledandri and Gina Shay; music by John Powell; distributed by Universal Pictures.
- Infobox release date: June 30, 2027. Country United States, language English.
- Premise: the film "follows Shrek, Donkey, and Princess Fiona on an adventure in a city called 'Further Further Away', alongside Shrek and Fiona's three children."
- The teaser poster shown in the article carries a "former release date".

## Voice cast
- Mike Myers as Shrek, Eddie Murphy as Donkey, Cameron Diaz as Princess Fiona (all reprising their roles).
- Zendaya as Felicia; Skyler Gisondo as Farkle; Marcello Hernandez as Fergus; Conrad Vernon as The Gingerbread Man.

## Background
- After Shrek 2's success in May 2004, DreamWorks Animation co-founder and then-CEO Jeffrey Katzenberg planned a five-film story arc; after Shrek the Third (2007) he announced the fifth film would be released in 2013.
- In May 2009 DreamWorks announced the fourth film's title as Shrek Forever After (originally Shrek Goes Fourth), indicating it would be the last; Bill Damaschke said "All that was loved about Shrek in the first film is brought to the final film".
- Writer Josh Klausner explained in 2010 that "there were originally going to be five Shrek movies" before Katzenberg decided the story they had was "the right way for Shrek's journey to end".
- In February 2014 Katzenberg hinted a fifth film might still be made: "We're not finished, and more importantly, neither is he".

## Development
- June 2016: two months before Comcast-owned NBCUniversal completed its $3.8 billion purchase of DreamWorks Animation - and the same month the US Department of Justice approved the acquisition - NBCUniversal chief Steve Burke discussed plans to revive the Shrek franchise.
- September 2016: Eddie Murphy announced the script for the fifth film had been completed. The original story was written by Michael McCullers based on his own idea; in March 2017 McCullers said it featured "a pretty big reinvention" for the series.
- November 2018: Variety reported Illumination CEO Chris Meledandri had been tasked as an executive producer of both the untitled Shrek film and Puss in Boots: The Last Wish (2022).
- December 2022: Antonio Banderas reiterated a new Shrek film was in development; the film was teased in The Last Wish's mid-credits scene.
- April 2023: Meledandri confirmed a fifth film in development, with Murphy, Myers and Diaz in negotiations; he said the filmmakers would "look at what the core elements are that audiences have loved" and "honor those elements", comparing the approach to The Super Mario Bros. Movie.
- June 2024: Murphy revealed he had started recording his lines as Donkey "a couple of months earlier". The following month DreamWorks confirmed Myers, Murphy and Diaz would reprise their roles in a film tentatively titled Shrek 5, with Walt Dohrn directing, Brad Ableson co-directing and Gina Shay co-producing with Meledandri.
- January 2025: Conrad Vernon returned to direct alongside Dohrn. Late February 2025: Zendaya joined as Shrek and Fiona's daughter Felicia. By July 2025 voice recording was still underway according to Murphy. November 2025: during the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, Skyler Gisondo and Marcello Hernandez were announced as sons Farkle and Fergus. August 2026: voice acting was announced as completed, with the film mixing "edgy humor mixed with the heart" like the previous films.

## Music
- June 2026: John Powell, who co-scored the first Shrek film with Harry Gregson-Williams, was announced as composer.
- Gregson-Williams said it was "absolutely right and proper that he would be doing it" and "I had my amazing decade with Shrek, and I'll be first in line to see what John does with it." Powell said he wanted the score to sound "new and interesting, but warm and familiar as well."

## Marketing
- The first-look cast announcement trailer was released February 27, 2025, introducing a new visual style and updated character appearances that sparked debate, with parallels drawn to the backlash over Sonic the Hedgehog's 2019 redesign; others were more positive "partially due to the technological advancements since the last main installment".
- The first official teaser trailer was released on June 16, 2026.

## Release
- Scheduled for release in the United States on June 30, 2027. Originally set for July 1, 2026, then pushed to December 23, 2026 (with Illumination's Minions & Monsters taking the original date) before the current date. It "will be released 17 years after the release of Shrek Forever After".
- Under Universal's long-term deal with Netflix for its animated films, the film is contracted to stream in the US on Peacock for the first four months of its pay-TV window, then Netflix for ten months, then back to Peacock for four months.

## Future
- A spin-off prequel titled Donkey is set for June 30, 2028, with Charlie Bean directing and Eddie Murphy reprising the title role.
- In May 2026 Dana Carvey stated that Mike Myers directly told him "We're doing two more [Shrek films]."

wikis.title: Superman (2025 film) (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia's article on James Gunn's Superman (2025), the first DC Universe film - its plot and cast, the long road from the abandoned Man of Steel sequel, filming in 2024, its $618.7 million box office and reception, and the announced follow-up Man of Tomorrow.
wikis.body:
## The film

- *Superman* is a 2025 American superhero film written and directed by James Gunn, the first film in the DC Universe (DCU), part of "Chapter One: Gods and Monsters", and a reboot of the *Superman* film series. Produced by Gunn and Peter Safran of DC Studios; distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures; 129 minutes.
- David Corenswet stars as Kal-El / Clark Kent / Superman with Rachel Brosnahan (Lois Lane), Nicholas Hoult (Lex Luthor), Edi Gathegi (Mister Terrific), Anthony Carrigan (Metamorpho), Nathan Fillion (Guy Gardner / Green Lantern) and Isabela Merced (Hawkgirl). Superman faces the consequences of intervening in a conflict between Boravia and Jarhanpur, orchestrated by Luthor.
- Premiered at the TCL Chinese Theater on July 7, 2025; released internationally July 9 and in the United States and China July 11, in IMAX, RealD 3D, Dolby Cinema, ScreenX and 4DX. Digital August 15, HBO Max September 19, disc September 23.

## Money

- Infobox budget $225 million, described as the net production budget with incentives and tax breaks factored in. A reported gross production budget of $363.8 million (tied to Ohio's over-$11-million tax credit on a $37 million state spend) was disputed by Gunn.
- Marketing: approximately $200 million per The Hollywood Reporter, for about $400 million total with production; Variety reported $125 million.
- Box office: $354.2 million in the United States and Canada and $264.5 million elsewhere, $618.7 million worldwide - tenth highest-grossing film of 2025 and the highest-grossing superhero film of the year. Opening weekend $125 million domestic, about $95 million international. Variety expected approximately $125 million theatrical profit; Bloomberg Businessweek and TheWrap reported over $100 million in profit.
- Salaries: Corenswet and Brosnahan $750,000 each; Hoult $2 million as highest-paid actor; Gunn $15 million for the film plus his DC Studios salary.

## How it was made

- Development on a *Man of Steel* sequel with Henry Cavill began by October 2014 and was dead by May 2020; Gunn began work on a new, standalone Superman film around late August 2022 and became DC Studios co-CEO with Safran that October. Announced as *Superman: Legacy* in January 2023 for July 11, 2025; Gunn confirmed as director in March 2023; title shortened to *Superman* in February 2024.
- Principal photography ran February 29 to July 30, 2024, under the working title *Genesis*: one week in Adventdalen, Svalbard, for the Fortress of Solitude, then Trilith Studios in Atlanta and location work in Cleveland and Cincinnati. Shot entirely on IMAX-certified Red cameras by Henry Braham. Picture lock June 5, 2025.
- 1,766 visual effects shots from Framestore, Industrial Light & Magic and Weta FX. Score by John Murphy with David Fleming, using a new version of John Williams's "Superman March".
- Chief comic influences: *All-Star Superman* (2005-2008) by Grant Morrison and Frank Quitely and *Superman: Birthright* (2003-2004) by Mark Waid, Leinil Francis Yu and Gerry Alanguilan.

## Reception and what follows

- Rotten Tomatoes 83% of 505 critics (7.2/10); Metacritic 68/100 from 58 critics; CinemaScore "A-". Critics called it fun, colorful and earnest, with some finding it overstuffed; Corenswet, Brosnahan and Hoult were praised. Some critics read the Boravia-Jarhanpur war as mirroring the Gaza war; Gunn says the script predated it.
- Awards: wins at the Astra Film Awards, Capri Hollywood and the Critics' Choice Super Awards (Best Superhero Movie, Best Actor for Corenswet), with many visual effects nominations; shortlisted for Best Sound and Best Visual Effects at the 98th Academy Awards.
- Follow-up film *Man of Tomorrow*, written and directed by Gunn, is scheduled for July 9, 2027, co-headlined by Corenswet and Hoult with Lars Eidinger as Brainiac. Two spin-off series are in the works: *The People v. Gorilla Grodd* with Skyler Gisondo as Jimmy Olsen, ordered for HBO Max in August 2026, and a Mister Terrific series with Allan Heinberg writing the pilot.
- The Joe Shuster estate's January 2025 suit against Warner Bros. Discovery over international distribution rights was dismissed in April for lack of jurisdiction, refiled in the New York Supreme Court, and its injunction request denied in early June.

## Rest of the page

- Roughly two-thirds of the captured source is the article's raw citation wikitext: several hundred `<ref name="...">{{Cite ...}}</ref>` templates dated from 2012-era DCEU coverage to September 2025, almost all with web.archive.org archive links.

wikis.title: Superman (2025 film): plot, cast and production
wikis.summary: The main body of Wikipedia's article on James Gunn's Superman (2025), covering its plot, cast, development at DC Studios, casting, filming in Svalbard, Georgia and Ohio, post-production, music, marketing and theatrical release.
wikis.body:
## The film

- *Superman* is a 2025 American superhero film written and directed by James Gunn, based on the DC Comics character. It is the first film in the DC Universe (DCU) and a reboot of the *Superman* film series, and the first film of the DCU's "Chapter One: Gods and Monsters".
- David Corenswet stars as Kal-El / Clark Kent / Superman, with Rachel Brosnahan, Nicholas Hoult, Edi Gathegi, Anthony Carrigan, Nathan Fillion and Isabela Merced. Produced by Gunn and Peter Safran of DC Studios.
- Infobox credits: cinematography Henry Braham; edited by William Hoy and Craig Alpert; music by John Murphy and David Fleming; production companies DC Studios, Troll Court Entertainment and The Safran Company; distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures; country United States; language English.
- Running time 129 minutes. Release dates: July 7, 2025 (TCL Chinese Theater premiere) and July 11, 2025 (United States). Budget listed as $225 million; box office $618.7 million.
- Released internationally on July 9 and in the United States and China on July 11, in IMAX, RealD 3D, Dolby Cinema, ScreenX and 4DX.

## Budget figures the article gives

- Infobox budget: $225 million, described later as a net production budget "with incentives and tax breaks factored in".
- A reported total gross production budget of $363.8 million appears in connection with Ohio's tax credit (over $11 million awarded, based on a $37 million spend in the state); Gunn disputed the accuracy of that figure, which would have made it one of the most expensive superhero films ever made. An HTML comment in the infobox notes the $363.8 million figure "has been disputed".
- Marketing: The Hollywood Reporter reported DC Studios and Warner Bros. spent approximately $200 million on marketing, for a total around $400 million with production; Variety reported marketing cost $125 million.
- Salaries: Corenswet and Brosnahan each earned $750,000; Hoult was the highest-paid actor at $2 million; all were eligible for box office bonuses. Gunn was paid $15 million for the film, plus his seven-figure DC Studios salary.

## Timeline of the production

- Development on a *Man of Steel* (2013) sequel began by October 2014 with Henry Cavill set to return; by May 2020 Warner Bros. was no longer developing it.
- Gunn began work on a new Superman film around late August 2022; he and Safran were announced as co-chairs and co-CEOs of DC Studios at the end of October 2022; Gunn was publicly revealed to be writing the film in December 2022.
- January 2023: the film announced as *Superman: Legacy*, first film of Chapter One: Gods and Monsters, with a July 11, 2025 release date - which coincides with the birthday of Gunn's late father.
- March 2023: Gunn confirmed as director. June 27, 2023: Corenswet and Brosnahan cast. July 11-12, 2023: Merced, Gathegi, Fillion and Carrigan cast, just before the SAG-AFTRA strike began on July 14.
- End of February 2024: title shortened to *Superman*. Principal photography began February 29, 2024 - Superman's birthday in the comic books - under the working title *Genesis*, starting in the Adventdalen valley in Svalbard, Norway. Filming wrapped July 30, 2024.
- Picture lock on June 5, 2025, after test screenings from early December 2024 and pick-up shoots in Los Angeles and Atlanta.

## Notes and disputes recorded in the article

- Bassem Youssef said he had been cast (reportedly as Rumaan Harjadi) and that his character was removed, possibly because of his October 2023 comments criticizing the Israeli government during the Gaza war; Gunn disputed this, saying the role was never formally offered and the character was cut after the strike ended and before those comments.
- The Hollywood Reporter reported Pom Klementieff and Miriam Shor were in the cast; Gunn said Klementieff was not involved and Shor had not been cast (Klementieff was later confirmed as a Superman robot voice).
- Gunn said "Superman is the story of America" and "an immigrant that came from other places"; this drew backlash from some Trump supporters and MAGA members, with some Fox News pundits calling the film "Superwoke". Gunn responded that the film is "about kindness and I think that's something everyone can relate to".

wikis.title: Plot
wikis.summary: The article's plot summary of Superman (2025), from the Boravia-Jarhanpur conflict to Lex Luthor's exposure.
wikis.body:
- Clark Kent / Superman stops Boravia from invading neighboring Jarhanpur and warns Boravian president Vasil Ghurkos to leave Jarhanpur alone. In Metropolis he is defeated for the first time by a metahuman called the "Hammer of Boravia" and flees to his Fortress of Solitude in Antarctica with the superpowered dog Krypto, followed by Angela Spica / The Engineer, an ally of tech billionaire Lex Luthor.
- Superman's robots heal him with concentrated solar radiation and play a message from his birth parents Jor-El and Lara Lor-Van, who sent him from the destroyed planet Krypton; the message was damaged so only the first half plays.
- Lois Lane, his girlfriend and Daily Planet colleague, interviews him, pressing him on the legal and ethical implications of his actions in Boravia. Luthor unleashes a kaiju on Metropolis as a distraction, infiltrates the Fortress with Ultraman and the Engineer, captures Krypto and restores the damaged message. Superman fights the kaiju alongside the "Justice Gang" - Green Lantern, Mister Terrific and Hawkgirl - and Mister Terrific kills the creature despite Superman wanting it taken alive. Luthor broadcasts the full message, whose second half urges Superman to conquer Earth and take many wives to restore the Kryptonian race.
- Public opinion turns against Superman; he surrenders to the U.S. government, which hands him to Luthor, who detains him in an artificial pocket universe holding his enemies. Metamorpho is forced to transmute a hand into Kryptonite; Luthor murders Superman supporter Malik Ali during questioning. Metamorpho helps Superman escape with Joey and Krypto; Lois convinces Mister Terrific to help, and they rescue the others. Jonathan Kent tells the demoralized Superman that his choices and actions determine who he is.
- Eve Teschmacher gives Jimmy Olsen evidence that Luthor is aiding Boravia in return for half of Jarhanpur's territory. Luthor opens an unstable portal that splits Metropolis in half; Hawkgirl kills Ghurkos; Superman learns Ultraman is a clone of himself and knocks him into a black hole; Mister Terrific closes the rift. Luthor says he orchestrated the Jarhanpur conflict to implicate Superman, driven by envy.
- Lois and Jimmy expose Luthor, who is arrested. Lois says she loves Clark. Superman's cousin Kara Zor-El drunkenly arrives to collect Krypto.

wikis.title: Cast and characters
wikis.summary: Who plays whom in Superman (2025) and what the actors and Gunn say about the characters, including cameos and cross-DCU roles.
wikis.body:
- **David Corenswet** as Kal-El / Clark Kent / Superman, and also as Ultraman, an armored clone created by Luthor who masquerades as the "Hammer of Boravia" and is controlled by drones and voice prompts. Gunn said this Superman is around 25, more established than Tom Welling's *Smallville* version but younger than Henry Cavill's. Safran described him as "the embodiment of truth, justice and the American way" and "kindness in a world that thinks of kindness as old-fashioned". Corenswet drew on *All-Star Superman* and Christopher Reeve's posture, and on his 6 ft 8 in (2.03 m), 270-pound brother-in-law. Gunn consulted Tom King on the hypnotic glasses that distort Clark's appearance. Oliver Diego Silva plays Clark at age two.
- **Rachel Brosnahan** as Lois Lane, who "isn't so sure about him"; Brosnahan called her "fiercely intelligent" and consulted journalists.
- **Nicholas Hoult** as Lex Luthor, CEO of LuthorCorp, inspired by Michael Rosenbaum's *Smallville* Luthor and by Steve Jobs for the uniform; Gunn drew on Brian Azzarello's *Lex Luthor: Man of Steel* (2005) and Jerry Siegel's 1950s-60s "reckless scientific genius".
- **Edi Gathegi** as Michael Holt / Mister Terrific, an "atheist who believes in justice"; **Anthony Carrigan** as Rex Mason / Metamorpho; **Nathan Fillion** as Guy Gardner / Green Lantern, keeping the comics bowl cut; **Isabela Merced** as Kendra Saunders / Hawkgirl - all members of the Justice Gang sponsored by Maxwell Lord.
- Daily Planet: Skyler Gisondo (Jimmy Olsen), Wendell Pierce (Perry White, whose grudge is that Luthor had an affair with his wife), Beck Bennett (Steve Lombard), Mikaela Hoover (Cat Grant), Christopher McDonald (Ron Troupe).
- Pruitt Taylor Vince and Neva Howell as Jonathan and Martha Kent; Bradley Cooper and Angela Sarafyan as Jor-El and Lara Lor-Van; robot voices by Alan Tudyk ("Four", later named Gary), Michael Rooker ("One"), Pom Klementieff ("Five") and Grace Chan ("Twelve"), with Jennifer Holland uncredited; Dinesh Thyagarajan as Malik "Mali" Ali; dog actor Jolene standing in for the mostly-VFX Krypto, modeled on Gunn's dog Ozu.
- Luthor's circle: Sara Sampaio (Eve Teschmacher), Maria Gabriela de Faria (Angela Spica / The Engineer, of the Authority), Zlatko Buric (Vasil Ghurkos), Terence Rosemore (Otis Berg), Stephen Blackehart (Sydney Happersen), Trevor Newlin (Mister Handsome), Michael Ian Black (Cleavis Thornwaite of *The Sphere*), James Hiroyuki Liao (General Mori).
- Cross-DCU and cameos: Frank Grillo (Rick Flag Sr., from *Creature Commandos*), Tinashe Kajese-Bolden (Flo Crawley), Milly Alcock (uncredited as Kara Zor-El / Supergirl), John Cena (uncredited as Peacemaker), Sean Gunn (Maxwell Lord), Will Reeve as a GBS News reporter, Michael Rosenbaum voicing a Raptor guard, Louisa Krause as Sapphire Stagg.

wikis.title: Background: the abandoned Man of Steel sequel
wikis.summary: Warner Bros.' repeated attempts at a Superman film with Henry Cavill between 2014 and 2022, before Gunn's version.
wikis.body:
- In 2012 Warner Bros. planned for *Man of Steel* (2013) to start a shared universe, which became the DC Extended Universe (DCEU). A full DC slate was announced in October 2014, prioritizing *Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice* (2016) after *Man of Steel* failed to meet financial expectations; an undated *Man of Steel* sequel with Cavill was said to be in development. Zack Snyder said the imprisoned Kryptonians and Brainiac had been considered as antagonists.
- The sequel was a top priority in August 2016 (confirmed by Cavill's manager Dany Garcia); Amy Adams said in November that a screenplay was being written. Matthew Vaughn was the studio's top choice to direct by March 2017; he and Mark Millar had earlier pitched a trilogy in which Krypton's destruction happens after Superman has grown up there.
- After the troubled production of *Justice League* (2017) the studio reevaluated its DC approach; by the end of 2017 a sequel was not coming "anytime soon, if at all", with producer Charles Roven saying there were story ideas but no script.
- July 2018: Christopher McQuarrie and Cavill pitched a Superman film partly inspired by *Up* (2009); Warner Bros. did not pursue it. Later in 2018 the studio asked Gunn to write and direct a Superman film; uncertain and without a clear vision, he made *The Suicide Squad* (2021) instead, "the easier path".
- September 2018: Cavill's cameo in *Shazam!* fell through over contract issues and *Mission: Impossible* scheduling; he was reported to be parting ways with the studio, but said in November 2019 he had not given up. Warner Bros. was talking to J. J. Abrams and Michael B. Jordan, who pitched himself as a Black Superman. In February 2021 Ta-Nehisi Coates was revealed to be writing a Superman film produced by Abrams.
- October 2022: Cavill's cameo in *Black Adam*, approved by Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy after Dwayne Johnson approached them, led to renewed pursuit of a Cavill-led sequel; Steven Knight wrote a treatment reportedly featuring Brainiac that executives were not thrilled with, and Michael Bay was eyed to direct. Cavill had signed a one-off deal for *Black Adam* with only a verbal agreement about continuing.

wikis.title: Development at DC Studios and the film's influences
wikis.summary: How Gunn and Safran's DC Studios took over, announced Superman: Legacy for July 11, 2025, and what comics and films inspired it.
wikis.body:
- April 2022: Discovery, Inc. and WarnerMedia merged into Warner Bros. Discovery under David Zaslav, who searched for a Kevin Feige equivalent, feeling DC lacked a "coherent creative and brand strategy" and was underusing Superman.
- Around late August 2022 Gunn was hired to work on a Superman film that was not a *Man of Steel* sequel and would be standalone from the DCEU. Gunn and Safran were announced as co-chairs and co-CEOs of DC Studios at the end of October 2022 and, a week into the job, began an eight-to-ten-year plan for a DCU that would be a "soft reboot" of the DCEU.
- November 2022: work on the *Man of Steel* sequel stalled; Gunn was revealed to be writing a new DC film. In December he announced it was a Superman film focused on a younger version of the character, therefore not starring Cavill; it would not retell the origin and would focus on him as a young reporter. Gunn and Safran met Cavill to explain the decision.
- January 2023: the DCU slate was unveiled, beginning with Chapter One: Gods and Monsters; the film was titled *Superman: Legacy* with a July 11, 2025 release date, the birthday of Gunn's late father.
- Influences Gunn cited: *All-Star Superman* (2005-2008) by Grant Morrison and Frank Quitely; the Superman animated shorts (1941-1943) and *Superman: The Animated Series* (1996-2000); *Superman: Birthright* (2003-04); the "Brainiac" arc (2008); *Superman: Ending Battle* (2002); *Superman for All Seasons* (1998); *Kingdom Come* (1996); Morrison's *Action Comics* run; "Whatever Happened to the Man of Tomorrow?" (1986); and the kaiju film *Godzilla Minus One* (2023). He considered using Brainiac as antagonist, and sought to "balance what was classic and what was completely new" with Silver Age imagery.
- March 2023: Tom King said Gunn was directing, which Gunn confirmed; Safran was confirmed as producer, through The Safran Company and Troll Court Entertainment. Gunn was hesitant to direct until he saw how Superman's Kryptonian and Smallville parentage would inform the characterization, an aspect he connected to his late father.
- Gunn in April 2025 on the approach: "I knew what I wanted to do in creating a story that was both utterly human and utterly fantastic... the flying dog, the giant Kaiju, pocket universes, science and sorcery, and all these things that were in the old Max Fleischer cartoons."

wikis.title: Casting and pre-production around the 2023 strikes
wikis.summary: Auditions, screen tests and casting announcements for Superman between April 2023 and February 2024, shaped by the WGA and SAG-AFTRA strikes.
wikis.body:
- Production design, costume design and casting began in April 2023, with production designer Beth Mickle and costume designer Judianna Makovsky returning from *The Suicide Squad* and *Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3*. Filming was then set for January 2024. Gunn completed the first draft at the end of April 2023.
- Gunn wanted a Superman with humanity, kindness and compassion, "somebody who you want to give a hug". Audition tapes arrived by early May 2023; Corenswet, whose performance in *Pearl* (2022) stood out to Gunn, became a top contender. Also considered: Jacob Elordi (who declined to read), Tom Brittney, Andrew Richardson; self-tapes came from Patrick Schwarzenegger, Pierson Fode and Jack Quaid. For Lois: Emma Mackey, Brosnahan, Samara Weaving and Phoebe Dynevor, with Dynevor a final contender; Brosnahan taped with her husband Jason Ralph reading Superman.
- Hoult, runner-up for Batman in *The Batman* (2022), was eyed for Luthor but chose to audition for Superman. Mister Terrific testing used the label "Apex".
- Mid-June 2023: in-person screen tests at the Warner Bros. lot in Burbank paired Hoult/Brosnahan, Brittney/Dynevor and Corenswet/Mackey; the Superman contenders tested in one of Cavill's old DCEU suits, in poor condition - Gunn said Brittney "messed it up" and it was then "torn to shreds" by the too-tall Corenswet. Gunn edited the tests for a committee including Zaslav.
- June 27, 2023: Corenswet and Brosnahan announced. Gunn offered Corenswet the role while he was filming *Twisters* (2024) on condition he treat everyone with kindness and respect.
- July 11, 2023: Merced, Gathegi and Fillion announced; Carrigan the next day. Gathegi was cast over 200 other actors. Deals were rushed before the SAG-AFTRA strike began July 14.
- After the strikes: the WGA strike ended in September 2023 and the SAG-AFTRA strike on November 9, moving filming to March 2024 while keeping the July 2025 date. De Faria was revealed as The Engineer in mid-November; Gisondo and Sampaio were announced in November (all three cast before the strike). Hoult finalized his deal for Luthor in December 2023, after Gunn contacted him about the role. Sean Gunn was cast as Maxwell Lord for future DCU projects. Milly Alcock was cast as Supergirl at the end of January 2024, having tested in costume on the Atlanta set.
- February 2024: pre-production in Ohio began; the state announced Cleveland and Cincinnati filming with over $11 million in tax credits. A table read was held February 22; the title was shortened to *Superman* the following week, Gunn saying the film was about looking forward while *Legacy* looked backward.

wikis.title: Filming
wikis.summary: Principal photography from February 29 to July 30, 2024, in Svalbard, at Trilith Studios in Atlanta and on location in Cleveland and Cincinnati.
wikis.body:
- Principal photography began February 29, 2024, Superman's birthday in the comics, under the working title *Genesis*. One week was shot in the Adventdalen valley in Svalbard, Norway, for the Fortress of Solitude, chosen for its natural beauty and similarity to Antarctica.
- Henry Braham returned as cinematographer from the later *Guardians of the Galaxy* films, *The Suicide Squad* and *The Flash*. The entire film was shot on IMAX-certified Red Digital Cinema cameras. Legacy Effects provided practical effects: character designs, prosthetic makeup, specialty suits and animatronics. Filming had been delayed from January 2024 by the SAG-AFTRA strike and was expected to last around four months.
- Filming at Trilith Studios in Atlanta, Georgia, had begun by March 8; Cleveland and Cincinnati filming was set for 37 days between April 1 and August 23; Macon, Georgia was also expected.
- Corenswet and Brosnahan shot a 12-minute interview scene, which Gunn described as ten percent of the film shot in two days, calling their chemistry "palpable"; *His Girl Friday* (1940) was a major reference, with witty comedy inspired by Preston Sturges.
- Ohio: production moved to Northeast Ohio on June 14 at Headlands Beach State Park in Mentor; six weeks in Cleveland began downtown on June 24. Locations included Ontario Street, the Cleveland Greyhound Station, Public Square, the Detroit-Superior Bridge, PNC Plaza, Progressive Field and Cleveland Arcade, with exteriors of the Huntington Bank Building, Key Tower and the Soldiers' and Sailors' Monument. The Leader Building stood in for the Daily Planet and Key Tower for Stagg Enterprises. Cleveland filming finished July 16; the production moved to Cincinnati by July 18, shooting at the Cincinnati Museum Center in Union Terminal and in the Lytle Tunnel. Filming wrapped July 30.

wikis.title: Post-production, visual effects and music
wikis.summary: Editing, pick-ups and picture lock, the 1,766 visual effects shots split between Framestore, ILM and Weta FX, and John Murphy and David Fleming's score.
wikis.body:
- Test screenings began by the start of December 2024, followed by a day-and-a-half of individual pick-up shots in Los Angeles, which Gunn said were to "enhance the film" rather than reshoot scenes; three days of pick-ups took place in Atlanta by the end of May 2025. Gunn said the film was completed and received a picture lock on June 5, 2025.
- William Hoy and Craig Alpert co-edited, after *The Batman* and *Blue Beetle* (2023) respectively.
- Visual effects: much of the *Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3* team returned, including supervisor Stephane Ceretti; work was provided by Framestore, Industrial Light & Magic and Weta FX. The film has 1,766 visual effects shots. Framestore created Krypto (shared as an asset with ILM and Weta) and worked on the Fortress of Solitude; ILM scanned Legacy's practical Hammer of Boravia build for the full CG version and created Metropolis using New York City as a scale reference and Cleveland plates; Weta created the kaiju, using ILM's Metropolis asset, and a digital Cleveland Public Square was built for shots drones could not achieve.
- Music: Gunn said in December 2023 that most of the score and major themes were written before the composer deal closed; John Murphy was announced in February 2024, having scored *The Suicide Squad*, *The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special* and *Vol. 3*. In December 2024 Gunn confirmed Murphy was using a new version of John Williams's "Superman March" from the 1978 film. The film has only two licensed songs, "Punkrocker" by Teddybears & Iggy Pop and "5 Years Time" by Noah and the Whale. David Fleming was revealed in April 2025 to be sharing score credit. The end credits feature an original song, "The Mighty Crabjoys Theme", written by Gunn with Foxy Shazam members Eric Nally and Devin Williams.

wikis.title: Marketing and promotion
wikis.summary: The campaign from the January 2023 All-Star Superman announcement image through trailers, the world tour, the Shard statue and tie-ins.
wikis.body:
- Gunn used the cover art of *All-Star Superman* #1 for the January 2023 announcement and again in March when confirming he would direct. He marked the February 2024 start of filming with a picture of Superman's logo, noted for its similarity to the *Kingdom Come* costume but in classic yellow and red.
- CinemaCon April 2024: Safran on stage, with Gunn, Corenswet and Brosnahan on video; a full look at the emblem was unveiled and Gunn promised an in-person "Summer of Superman" the following year. A first-look image of Corenswet in costume was released in early May 2024, drawing comment on the return of the red briefs and comparisons to Jim Lee's New 52 design. A Fortress of Solitude display appeared at Warner Bros.'s Licensing Expo booth in Las Vegas.
- The first image of Krypto was released in October 2024 for "Adopt a Shelter Dog" month. A motion poster on December 16 used a slowed-down "Superman March" with an electric guitar opening; a teaser trailer was screened for press that day and released publicly on December 19, drawing over 250 million global views in 24 hours - the most-viewed and discussed trailer for a DC Comics or Warner Bros. film in that period. WaterTower Music released "Theme from Superman (Trailer Version)" as a single.
- February 2025: the film co-sponsored Animal Planet's *Puppy Bowl XXI*, with Gunn and Ozu introducing new footage and a "Krypto Super Play" award. DC Studios hired former Apple TV+ and Disney marketing executive Ricky Strauss to consult, after Warner Bros. global marketing chief Josh Goldstine's exit. Safran said Zaslav had "rallied the entire company" behind the film as with *Barbie* (2023).
- CinemaCon April 2025: Gunn, Corenswet, Brosnahan and Hoult showed an extended sequence and behind-the-scenes footage; the extended footage screened before IMAX showings of *A Minecraft Movie*, and the behind-the-scenes footage was released April 18, the anniversary of *Action Comics* #1 (1938).
- Tie-ins: DC Comics and Milk-Bone's *Superman: A Friendship Unleashed* (May 2025, also at San Diego Comic-Con in July); the children's book *Superman: Friends and Foes!* and prequel junior novel *Superman: Welcome to Metropolis* in early June; Funko and McFarlane Toys figures; a Lola Cars Formula E livery at the 2025 Berlin ePrix.
- Trailers: an official trailer on May 14 (praised by Bleeding Cool's Ray Flook; IGN's Wesley Yin-Poole and Polygon's Michael McWhertor noted the interview scene's questioning of Superman's intervention in a foreign war) and a final trailer on June 11, one month before release, called the "most revealing trailer to date" by Gizmodo's Germain Lussier.
- Events: the first 30 minutes screened at CineEurope in Barcelona on June 17 and at the SM Mall of Asia in Manila on June 19, starting a seven-city "Superman World Tour". An 11 ft (3.4 m) Superman statue modeled on Corenswet was suspended from the Shard in London on July 1 - the largest public sculpture displayed in the United Kingdom, four months in the making - with 25 pop-up Daily Planet newsstand kiosks around London and a fan event at Cineworld Leicester Square on July 2. Fandango and Amazon Prime early access screenings on July 8 became Fandango's best-selling first-day presales of the year, surpassing *The Fantastic Four: First Steps*.

wikis.title: Superman (2025): lawsuit, home media, box office, reception and follow-ups
wikis.summary: The later sections of Wikipedia's Superman (2025) article - the Shuster estate lawsuit, home media, box office totals, reviews, awards and the Man of Tomorrow and spin-off series - followed by the start of the reference list.
wikis.body:
## Key figures

- Box office: $354.2 million in the United States and Canada and $264.5 million elsewhere, for $618.7 million worldwide - the tenth highest-grossing film of 2025 and the highest-grossing superhero film of that year, and the first DC film to surpass all Marvel films released in a single year since *The Dark Knight* in 2008.
- Profit: Variety expected a theatrical profit of approximately $125 million; Bloomberg Businessweek and TheWrap both reported over $100 million in profit from ticket sales, online home media rentals and merchandise partnerships.
- Opening: $56.5 million on day one, $125 million opening weekend, first place; $57 million in weekend two (a 54% drop); $24.9 million in weekend three (a 57% drop), second behind *The Fantastic Four: First Steps*.
- Reviews: Rotten Tomatoes 83% of 505 critics, average 7.2/10; Metacritic 68/100 from 58 critics ("generally favorable"); CinemaScore "A-" (the same as *Man of Steel*); PostTrak 86% positive, 74% definite recommend.
- Release windows: digital download August 15, 2025; HBO Max September 19 (35-day and 70-day windows are both cited); Ultra HD Blu-ray, Blu-ray and DVD September 23.

## Sections in this part

- The Joe Shuster estate lawsuit over international distribution rights.
- Home media and streaming performance.
- Box office projections and results, domestic and international.
- Critical response, positive and negative, and the Boravia-Jarhanpur political reading.
- An accolades table and awards submissions.
- The follow-up film *Man of Tomorrow* and two spin-off television series.

wikis.title: Joe Shuster estate lawsuit
wikis.summary: The 2025 suit by Superman co-creator Joe Shuster's estate against Warner Bros. Discovery over international distribution rights, and its dismissal.
wikis.body:
- January 2025: the estate of Superman co-creator Joe Shuster filed a lawsuit against WBD, asserting that rights to distribute the film in some international territories had reverted to them under different copyright laws - the United Kingdom, Ireland and Australia in 2017, and Canada in 2021.
- Two months later WBD filed a motion to dismiss, citing prior rejected copyright lawsuits.
- The suit was dismissed in April for lack of jurisdiction, refiled with the New York Supreme Court a month later with an injunction requested, and that motion was denied in early June.

wikis.title: Home media and streaming
wikis.summary: Digital, HBO Max and disc releases of Superman in August and September 2025 and its streaming viewership.
wikis.body:
- Digital download on August 15, 2025; HBO Max on September 19, after a respective 35-day and 70-day theatrical window; Ultra HD Blu-ray, Blu-ray and DVD on September 23.
- Extras include deleted scenes, a making-of documentary, a Gunn commentary, the first short of the animated series *Krypto Saves the Day!* and various featurettes.
- Gunn said the early digital release let audiences watch it before the second season of *Peacemaker* (2025), which connects to the film.
- The film drew 13 million global viewers in its first ten days on HBO Max, the highest for that period for a "pay-one" film on the service since *Barbie* in December 2023, and lifted viewership of other Superman titles including *Super/Man: The Christopher Reeve Story* (2024), the 1978 *Superman*, *Superman Returns* (2006) and *Man of Steel*.

wikis.title: Box office performance
wikis.summary: Projections before release and the film's domestic, international and worldwide grosses.
wikis.body:
- Projections: TheWrap estimated in early June 2025 that the film needed more than $500 million worldwide to be profitable and about $700 million to be a success - a notion Gunn disputed. The Hollywood Reporter estimated a domestic opening around $175 million and a potential global total over $1 billion, noting production and marketing costs around $400 million. Three weeks out, projections were $125-145 million (approximately $135 million) domestically, above *Man of Steel*'s $116 million debut, while DC Studios and Warner Bros. estimated a more conservative $90-125 million; a $175 million debut would have beaten *Batman v Superman*'s $166 million. Deadline projected $115-130 million in release week.
- Previews: $2.8 million from Tuesday Amazon Prime screenings, with final Thursday previews of $22.5 million including those - then the best preview gross of 2025 until *The Fantastic Four: First Steps* two weeks later, a record for any Gunn film, and above Warner Bros.'s previous record with *Barbie*.
- Results: $56.5 million opening day (second-highest of 2025 behind *A Minecraft Movie*); $125 million opening weekend, the biggest opening for a standalone Superman film and second-biggest for a film featuring Superman behind *Batman v Superman*, and third-highest of 2025 behind *A Minecraft Movie* and *Lilo & Stitch*. Second weekend $57 million (54% drop, better than *Captain America: Brave New World* at 68% and *Thunderbolts\** at 56%; Comscore's Paul Dergarabedian called it "indicative of a marketplace that's embracing the film"). Third weekend $24.9 million (57% drop).
- Milestones: first DC film since *The Batman* (2022) to pass $300 million domestically (end of July) and $600 million globally (late August). It still earned over $1 million domestically in week nine across 1,187 theatres, was cut to 390 theatres in week 10 and pulled from domestic theatres after week 12.
- International: an estimated $95 million in its opening weekend for a $220 million global total. Top territories: United Kingdom ($9.8 million), Mexico ($8.8 million), China ($6.6 million), Brazil ($5.9 million), Australia ($5.3 million), France ($4.2 million), Korea ($4.2 million), India ($3.8 million), Spain ($2.9 million), Japan ($2.5 million). Its perceived underperformance abroad - it debuted fourth in China - was partly attributed to the character's American roots, with David A. Gross of FranchiseRe saying "Superman has always been identified as a quintessentially American character and story, and in some parts of the world, America is currently not enjoying its greatest popularity".

wikis.title: Critical response
wikis.summary: Aggregate scores and a range of positive and negative reviews, plus the debate over the film's Boravia-Jarhanpur war.
wikis.body:
- Critics found the film fun, colorful and earnest, though some felt it was overstuffed with characters and ideas; the performances of Corenswet, Brosnahan and Hoult were praised. Rotten Tomatoes: 83% of 505 critics, 7.2/10 average, with the consensus "Pulling off the heroic feat of fleshing out a dynamic new world while putting its champion's big, beating heart front and center, this Superman flies high as a Man of Tomorrow grounded in the here and now." Metacritic: 68/100 from 58 critics. CinemaScore "A-"; PostTrak 86% positive and 74% definite recommendation.
- Positive: IGN 8/10, "wonderfully entertaining and heartfelt"; Scott Phillips (Forbes) on the visuals, humor and tone; Trace Sauveur (AwardsWatch) on the no-origin-story approach; Jake Cole (Slant); Cody Dericks (Next Best Picture) on the casting; Glen Weldon (NPR): it "delivers a Superman deeply in touch with his humanity, and perfectly representative of the essence of the character"; Liz Shannon Miller (Consequence); William Bibbiani (TheWrap): "James Gunn tried to make a great Superman movie... He succeeded"; Nicholas Barber (BBC Culture) three stars out of five; Alissa Wilkinson (The New York Times), comparing it to *Iron Man* (2008); Owen Gleiberman (Variety); David Crow (Den of Geek).
- Negative: Peter Bradshaw (The Guardian) two out of five, criticizing the "pointless, cluttered backstory" and "yet another CGI city-leveling finale"; Sophie Butcher (Empire) two out of five, "the final act sinks into CGI chaos"; Erik Kain (Forbes) two out of five on the "overstuffed, badly-paced plot"; Mark Kermode called it "tonally all over the place" and "messy" but "unexpectedly good fun".
- Some critics argued the war between Boravia - an aggressor backed by Luthor and the United States - and Jarhanpur mirrors the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, particularly the Gaza war that began in 2023; Gunn has maintained that the script predated the war and was not intended as an allegory.

wikis.title: Accolades
wikis.summary: The article's awards table for Superman, dominated by visual effects nominations, plus Academy Award shortlists and Golden Globe submissions.
wikis.body:
- Wins: Astra Film Awards (January 9, 2026) Best Action or Science Fiction Feature; Capri Hollywood International Film Festival (January 5, 2026) Best Visual Effects for Stephane Ceretti, Enrico Damm, Stephane Naze and Guy Williams; Critics' Choice Super Awards (August 6, 2026) Best Superhero Movie and Best Actor in a Superhero Movie for David Corenswet.
- Nominations include: Annie Awards (February 21, 2026) character animation; Astra Creative Arts Awards (December 11, 2025) visual effects, stunts and marketing campaign; Astra Midseason Movie Awards (July 3, 2025) Most Anticipated Film; Critics' Choice Movie Awards (January 4, 2026) visual effects; Critics' Choice Super Awards for Edi Gathegi, Nicholas Hoult, Rachel Brosnahan and Hoult as Best Villain; Golden Trailer Awards (May 29, 2025) for the "Fight" trailer; Hugo Awards (August 30, 2026) Best Dramatic Presentation, Long Form; Latino Entertainment Journalists Association; Movieguide Awards; National Film Awards UK (July 1, 2026) Best International Film; North Carolina Film Critics Association; Online Film Critics Society; Satellite Awards; Saturn Awards (March 8, 2026) in seven categories including Best Film Direction for James Gunn, Best Actor for Corenswet, Best Actress for Brosnahan, production design for Beth Mickle and costume design for Judianna Makovsky; and four Visual Effects Society Awards (February 25, 2026) for Krypto, the Metropolis city destruction, compositing and lighting, and the Fortress of Solitude.
- *Superman* was shortlisted for Best Sound and Best Visual Effects at the 98th Academy Awards. For the 83rd Golden Globes it was submitted for Best Motion Picture - Drama and Cinematic and Box Office Achievement, with Corenswet, Brosnahan, Hoult, Gunn (director and screenplay) and "The Mighty Crabjoys Theme" by Gunn, Eric Nally and Devin Williams also submitted.

wikis.title: Man of Tomorrow and the spin-off series
wikis.summary: The follow-up film scheduled for July 9, 2027 and the two announced DCU television series drawn from Superman's supporting cast.
wikis.body:
- June 2025: Gunn said he had begun writing a follow-up that would not be a direct sequel but would feature Superman in a major role. Corenswet and Brosnahan had sequel options, but no direct sequel was expected to be announced imminently after the July release.
- The follow-up, *Man of Tomorrow*, was announced in September 2025 with Gunn directing, scheduled for release on July 9, 2027. Gunn described it as the next story in the "Superman Saga", "as much a Lex movie as it is a Superman movie", with the pair working together against a bigger threat.
- Returning: Corenswet and Hoult co-headlining, with Brosnahan, Gisondo, Sampaio, De Faria, Merced, Gathegi, Fillion, Grillo and Alcock. Joining: Lars Eidinger as antagonist Brainiac; Aaron Pierre as Green Lantern John Stewart from the DCU series *Lanterns* (2026); Xolo Mariduena reprising Jaime Reyes / Blue Beetle from *Blue Beetle* (2023); Adria Arjona, reportedly as Maxima; and Andre Royo, Matthew Lillard and Sinqua Walls in undisclosed roles.
- July 2025: Gunn was reported to be considering spin-off series for Mister Terrific and Jimmy Olsen. The Olsen series was announced that November with Dan Perrault and Tony Yacenda as writers, executive producers and showrunners and Gisondo reprising his role; it was ordered for HBO Max in August 2026 as an eight-episode half-hour mockumentary comedy titled *The People v. Gorilla Grodd*, presented as a true crime docuseries in which Olsen and other Daily Planet reporters investigate whether Gorilla Grodd was wrongfully convicted of murdering his father, the king of Gorilla City. Jimmy Tatro stars as Grodd with Mary Holland as female lead Sandra; Wendell Pierce, Beck Bennett and Mikaela Hoover reprise their roles, with Eduardo Franco, Arian Moayed, Perrault, Andrew Leeds and Tim Baltz in undisclosed roles. Filming is scheduled to start in late 2026.
- The Mister Terrific series was revealed to be in active development in July 2026, with Allan Heinberg writing the pilot.
