**Final citations.** The part opens with the last numbered references, among them Richard Brody's and Anthony Lane's New Yorker reviews (both April 26, 2019), The Hollywood Reporter's Oscars, Annie Awards, BAFTA and Critics' Choice winners lists, NBC News on Avengers being among the top Wikipedia articles of 2019, Empire's "The 100 Greatest Movies of the 21st Century" (March 18, 2020) and ComicBook.com on the Oscars Cheer Moment contest (February 27, 2022).

Sequel-related citations follow: Bob Iger not ruling out more Avengers films (THR, May 8, 2018); the Russos saying they were done with the MCU "for the foreseeable future" (GamesRadar+, April 25, 2019); Feige saying more Avengers movies would come "at some point" (IGN, January 11, 2021); Comic-Con 2022 coverage (Variety, July 23, 2022) and the Russos not directing The Kang Dynasty or Secret Wars (IGN, July 24, 2022); Cretton's hiring (THR, July 26, 2022) and departure (Deadline, November 15, 2023); Loveness and Waldron writing assignments (Deadline, September 14 and October 3, 2022; November 27, 2023); "Marvel Drops Jonathan Majors After Assault, Harassment Verdict" (THR, December 18, 2023); the Doomsday/Secret Wars announcement (Variety, July 28, 2024); the Doomsday cast unveiling (THR, March 26, 2025); Disney pushing the two Avengers dates (Deadline, May 22, 2025); the first Doomsday trailer with the Russos on bringing Cap back (Total Film, December 23, 2025); Marvel on the X-Men return as an "opportunity to pit multiple universes against each other" (Entertainment Weekly, April 17, 2026); and "'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Writers Are Working on Marvel's 'Avengers' Movies" (TheWrap, August 7, 2026).

**External links.** Official website; Avengers: Endgame at IMDb; at Disney A to Z; and the script (archived December 7, 2019 at the Wayback Machine).

**Navigation boxes.** An Avengers box (members, enemies, titles, creators Stan Lee and Jack Kirby, affiliated teams) and a Marvel Cinematic Universe film list by phase - Phase Three ending with Avengers: Endgame and Spider-Man: Far From Home; Phase Four (Black Widow, Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, Eternals, Spider-Man: No Way Home, Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, Thor: Love and Thunder, Werewolf by Night, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever, The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special); Phase Five (Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania, Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3, The Marvels, Deadpool & Wolverine, Captain America: Brave New World, Thunderbolts*); and Phase Six beginning with The Fantastic Four.

wikis.title: Production of Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia's production article on Marvel Studios' Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars, covering development from the 2022 Kang Dynasty announcement through the Russo brothers' return, casting, filming at Pinewood and 2026 post-production, followed by its reference list.
wikis.body:
## The films

- *Avengers: Doomsday* and *Avengers: Secret Wars* are American superhero films from Marvel Studios, distributed by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures; the fifth and sixth *Avengers* films after *Avengers: Endgame* (2019) and the 39th and 40th MCU films, both in Phase Six.
- Directed by Anthony and Joe Russo; screenplays by Michael Waldron, Stephen McFeely, Chris McKenna and Erik Sommers; produced by Kevin Feige, Louis D'Esposito and Jonathan Schwartz; music by Alan Silvestri; cinematography by Newton Thomas Sigel; edited by Jeffrey Ford and Matthew Schmidt.
- Release dates: December 18, 2026 (*Doomsday*) and December 17, 2027 (*Secret Wars*).
- Cast headlined by Robert Downey Jr. (as Victor von Doom / Doctor Doom), Chris Evans, Pedro Pascal, Anthony Mackie, Vanessa Kirby, Ebon Moss-Bachrach, Simu Liu, Joseph Quinn and Letitia Wright.

## How the project changed

- Announced at SDCC in July 2022 as *Avengers: The Kang Dynasty* (May 2, 2025) and *Avengers: Secret Wars* (November 7, 2025), with Destin Daniel Cretton directing and Jonathan Majors as Kang.
- After Majors's March 2023 arrest, Jeff Loveness's exit, Cretton's November 2023 departure and Majors's firing in December 2023 (found guilty of harassment and reckless assault in the third degree), Marvel rewrote both films to minimize or remove Kang and pivoted to Doctor Doom.
- At SDCC in July 2024 the Russo brothers were confirmed as directors, the first film was retitled *Avengers: Doomsday*, and Downey was cast as Doctor Doom. Reported pay: $40 million for the Russos and $50 million for Downey per film, with box office bonuses.
- Release dates moved from May 2025/November 2025 to May 2026/May 2027 (June 2023) and then, in May 2025, to December 18, 2026 and December 17, 2027.

## Making the films

- Production is based at Pinewood Studios in Buckinghamshire, England. *Doomsday* principal photography ran from April 28, 2025 (working title *Apple Pie 1*) to September 19, 2025, with location work in Bahrain, at Windsor Great Park and at Shinfield Studios; filming began without a finished script. *Secret Wars* photography is scheduled to begin in late 2026 for approximately six months.
- 26 *Doomsday* cast members were announced at the end of March 2025, including Fox X-Men actors Kelsey Grammer, Patrick Stewart, Ian McKellen, Alan Cumming, Rebecca Romijn and James Marsden. Deadline reported potential for more than 60 returning actors.
- Runtime: estimated at about two-and-a-half hours (*Doomsday*) and three hours (*Secret Wars*) in March 2025; a 165-minute *Doomsday* runtime was set for ticketing in July 2026, which The Hollywood Reporter said was "unlikely to be locked this far in advance".
- Feige says *Secret Wars* will "reset" the MCU into a "streamlined, simplified, single universe" with a recast X-Men team, while avoiding the word "reboot" - "a scary word".
- Reports the article leaves unresolved include whether Ryan Reynolds appears as Deadpool in *Doomsday* (The Hollywood Reporter and TheWrap say yes, Deadline says he is not set to appear) and Famke Janssen's denial that she returns as Jean Grey.

## Rest of the page

- Most of the source is its citation apparatus: several hundred raw `<ref>` citation templates, a rendered numbered reference list of roughly 170 entries dated from December 2017 to August 2026, and Wikipedia navigation boxes for the Avengers, the MCU and other Marvel films.

wikis.title: Production of Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars
wikis.summary: The article body on how Marvel Studios' Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars were developed, written, cast, designed, filmed and edited, from the 2022 Kang Dynasty announcement to post-production in 2026.
wikis.body:
## What the films are

- *Avengers: Doomsday* and *Avengers: Secret Wars* are American superhero films based on the Marvel Comics team the Avengers, produced by Marvel Studios and distributed by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures. They are the fifth and sixth installments of the *Avengers* film series after *Avengers: Endgame* (2019), and the 39th and 40th films of the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU).
- Directed by Anthony and Joe Russo, from screenplays by Michael Waldron, Stephen McFeely, and the writing team of Chris McKenna and Erik Sommers.
- Ensemble cast headlined by Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Pedro Pascal, Anthony Mackie, Vanessa Kirby, Ebon Moss-Bachrach, Simu Liu, Joseph Quinn and Letitia Wright. In *Doomsday*, the Avengers, Wakandans, Fantastic Four, New Avengers and the X-Men team up against Doctor Doom (Downey).
- Infobox credits: produced by Kevin Feige, Louis D'Esposito and Jonathan Schwartz; music by Alan Silvestri; cinematography by Newton Thomas Sigel; edited by Jeffrey Ford and Matthew Schmidt; production company Marvel Studios; based on *The Avengers* by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby; country United States; language English. The infobox budget field is empty.
- Release dates given in the infobox and lead: December 18, 2026 (*Doomsday*) and December 17, 2027 (*Secret Wars*), both part of Phase Six of the MCU.
- Both films are being produced at Pinewood Studios in England. Filming for *Doomsday* took place from April to September 2025; filming for *Secret Wars* is scheduled to begin in mid-2026 (the lead's wording; the Filming section says principal photography is "scheduled to begin in late 2026").

## Sequence of events

- **July 2022 (SDCC):** Feige announces *Avengers: The Kang Dynasty* (May 2, 2025) and *Avengers: Secret Wars* (November 7, 2025) to close Phase Six and "The Multiverse Saga".
- **September/October 2022:** Jeff Loveness hired to write *The Kang Dynasty*; Waldron hired for *Secret Wars*, whose date moves to May 1, 2026.
- **June 2023:** dates pushed to May 1, 2026 and May 7, 2027, in part because scripts were not ready before the 2023 Writers Guild of America strike.
- **November 2023:** Destin Daniel Cretton steps down as director; Waldron hired to rewrite *The Kang Dynasty*. **December 2023:** Jonathan Majors fired by Disney and Marvel Studios after being found guilty of harassment and reckless assault in the third degree.
- **February 2024:** *Avengers 5* confirmed to be retitled to no longer reference Kang.
- **July 2024 (SDCC):** the Russo brothers confirmed as directors of both films; *Avengers 5* revealed as *Avengers: Doomsday*; Downey cast as Victor von Doom / Doctor Doom; McFeely writing both films; filming set to begin in early 2025 in London.
- **April 28, 2025:** principal photography on *Doomsday* begins at Pinewood under the working title *Apple Pie 1*; it wraps on September 19 (2025).
- **May 2025:** Disney delays *Doomsday* to December 18, 2026, and *Secret Wars* to December 17, 2027, "to allow more time for production to be completed".
- **2026:** additional photography for *Doomsday*; pre-production on *Secret Wars* underway by April 2026, simultaneous with *Doomsday* post-production; *Secret Wars* principal photography scheduled to begin in late 2026 and last approximately six months.

## Figures the article gives

- The Walt Disney Company's acquisition of 21st Century Fox returned the film rights of Deadpool, the X-Men and the Fantastic Four to Marvel Studios.
- Majors was set to receive $20 million with back-end compensation for *The Kang Dynasty*.
- The Russos and Downey were reported to be earning $40 million and $50 million respectively for each film, with bonuses based on box office performance and potential for Downey's salary to double. Downey had earned $500-600 million total for his previous MCU appearances.
- In June 2024 Deadline Hollywood reported potential for more than 60 actors to reprise MCU roles in the first film; 26 cast members were officially announced at the start of production at the end of March 2025.
- Runtime: in March 2025 the Russos estimated *Doomsday* at approximately two-and-a-half hours and *Secret Wars* at approximately three hours; a 165-minute runtime was set when *Doomsday*'s premium large format tickets went on sale in July 2026.

## Hedged or disputed points the article flags

- Whether Ryan Reynolds appears as Deadpool in *Doomsday*: The Hollywood Reporter's Heat Vision reported he would; Anthony D'Alessandro of Deadline Hollywood reported Reynolds "was not set to appear" and had not been seen on set; Umberto Gonzalez of TheWrap reported he would appear but said sources "were not yet ready to go on the record". His SDCC July 2026 appearance in a Deadpool suit was a joke and "whether he actually has a role in Doomsday was not explicitly confirmed".
- Benedict Cumberbatch first said he would no longer appear in *Doomsday*, then said he had been mistaken and would appear in both films.
- Chris Evans denied he would be in the film, saying he was "happily retired" from Marvel, before his return as Steve Rogers was confirmed with the December 2025 teasers.
- Famke Janssen: Chris Claremont stated in January 2026 that she would return as Jean Grey; Janssen denied it and in June 2026 said Marvel "made a mistake" by not asking her to return.
- The editing credits for Ford and Schmidt carry "[independent source needed]" tags.

wikis.title: Background and announcement as The Kang Dynasty and Secret Wars
wikis.summary: How the two films were first conceived and announced in July 2022 as Avengers: The Kang Dynasty and Avengers: Secret Wars, with Destin Daniel Cretton directing and Kang the Conqueror as the villain.
wikis.body:
- April 2018: discussing Disney's acquisition of 21st Century Fox, which returned the rights of Deadpool, the X-Men and the Fantastic Four to Marvel Studios, Joe Russo said it would be interesting to introduce those characters using a *Secret Wars* film. *Secret Wars* is the name of a 1984-85 comic crossover by Jim Shooter and a 2015-16 storyline by Jonathan Hickman, both following Marvel characters converging on the planet Battleworld.
- May 2018: Disney CEO Bob Iger said Marvel was focusing on new characters after *Endgame*, but another *Avengers* film could happen eventually.
- April 2019: *Infinity War* and *Endgame* writers Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely said they would return to write a *Secret Wars* film if the Russos directed.
- July 2020: Joe Russo said "to execute something on the scale of *Infinity War* was directly related to the dream of *Secret Wars*, which is even larger in scale".
- January 2021: Feige said another *Avengers* film would happen eventually. August 2021: Shooter said Marvel executives had attempted to secure the rights to his *Secret Wars* storyline; Marvel would not confirm a film.
- Jonathan Majors had been cast as Kang in September 2020 for *Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania* (2023) and was introduced as the variant He Who Remains in season one of *Loki* (2021). Waldron called Kang a "time-traveling, multiversal adversary" and the MCU's "next big cross-movie villain"; Loveness called him a "top-tier, A-list Avengers villain". *Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness* (2022) introduced "incursions", a key idea of the 2015 *Secret Wars* comic.
- July 2022, SDCC: Feige announced *Avengers: The Kang Dynasty* (May 2, 2025) and *Avengers: Secret Wars* (November 7, 2025), concluding Phase Six and "The Multiverse Saga" (Phases Four, Five and Six). The first film was inspired by the 2001-02 "Kang Dynasty" storyline by Kurt Busiek. Feige said there was "nobody's shoulders I'd rather be putting the Multiverse Saga on" than Majors's, and confirmed the Russos were not returning.
- Cretton, director of *Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings* (2021), was revealed as director of *The Kang Dynasty* shortly after SDCC, hired for that film only. Loveness was hired to write it in September 2022. Waldron, considered the frontrunner, was hired for *Secret Wars* in October 2022, when its release moved to May 1, 2026.
- January 2023: Majors confirmed to appear in *Secret Wars* as well. Loveness said in March 2023 that the Fantastic Four and X-Men would not appear because their MCU introductions were "pretty far away".

wikis.title: Firing of Jonathan Majors and creative shifts
wikis.summary: Majors's 2023 arrest and firing, Loveness's and Cretton's exits, and Marvel's pivot away from the Kang storyline toward Doctor Doom.
wikis.body:
- Following Majors's arrest in March 2023 and subsequent assault allegations, Marvel Studios had not yet discussed removing him from the MCU by the following month; he was still attached to both films and was set to receive $20 million with back-end compensation for *The Kang Dynasty*, with Disney reportedly monitoring the situation.
- Joanna Robinson of The Ringer called the allegations a "huge problem", saying it was unprecedented for the studio to plan so much of the franchise on one character and actor, and that there were conflicting reports on how Marvel would proceed.
- *The Kang Dynasty* was then scheduled to begin filming in early 2024. In May 2023 Jeff Sneider reported Loveness had exited before the start of the 2023 Writers Guild of America strike. In June the release dates moved to May 1, 2026, and May 7, 2027, in part because the scripts were not ready before the strike.
- November 2023: Tatiana Siegel at Variety reported executives had discussed bringing back the original Avengers cast, including Downey and Scarlett Johansson (Feige later denied this), and had started discussing alternatives to the Kang storyline, including pivoting to Doctor Doom - already expected to be a major antagonist of *Secret Wars*. Changes were reportedly considered after *Quantumania*'s disappointing box office.
- Robinson reported Loveness departed because he was closely associated with Kang and Marvel was "moving away" from that; Aaron Couch and Borys Kit of The Hollywood Reporter said he completed a draft first.
- Mid-November 2023: Cretton stepped down to focus on other MCU projects, an exit described as amicable and partially attributed to schedule delays. He later said he did not feel like the right fit and went on to direct *Spider-Man: Brand New Day* (2026). Waldron was hired to rewrite *The Kang Dynasty* at the end of the month.
- December 2023: Majors was fired by Disney and Marvel Studios after being found guilty of harassment and reckless assault in the third degree; the studio began referring to the film internally as *Avengers 5*. Sneider reported Marvel was developing *Secret Wars* as a "giant five-hour movie" split into two parts a year apart, and was searching for a director who had not previously directed a Marvel film. Filming was delayed to late 2024.
- February 2024: Couch and Kit said Marvel was "cleaning up the creative mess", with both films rewritten to minimize or remove Kang, and confirmed *Avengers 5* was being retitled.

wikis.title: New work as Doomsday and Secret Wars
wikis.summary: The 2024 relaunch of the project: Downey cast as Doctor Doom, the Russo brothers returning to direct, the Doomsday title, salaries and the May 2025 date delay.
wikis.body:
- Commentators noted issue #5 of the 2015 *Secret Wars* comic appears in a February 2024 trailer for *Deadpool & Wolverine* (2024).
- Mid-March 2024: Shawn Levy was quietly asked to direct *Avengers 5* and turned it down over scheduling with *Stranger Things* season five (2025). In April, filming was reported to be beginning in early 2025 after a delay of several months. In May, Waldron turned in a new draft given to Levy, who was still the studio's top choice; other directors were considered and Levy had not committed, also citing *Star Wars: Starfighter* (2027).
- Marvel approached Downey about playing Victor von Doom / Doctor Doom; he had auditioned for that role in Fox's *Fantastic Four* (2005). Feige said the studio felt, even before Majors's legal issues, that Kang "wasn't big enough, wasn't Thanos", and that casting Downey was a long-term plan to "take one of our greatest characters and utilize one of our greatest actors": "He played the most iconic hero. Let's have him play the most iconic villain."
- Downey said he would only return if the Russo brothers returned as directors. The Russos were reluctant, feeling "creatively spent"; after McFeely approached them with an idea, they entered early talks by mid-July 2024. Matthew Belloni of Puck reported CAA suggested Greg Berlanti and Noah Hawley, who were turned down by Feige. Downey signed to star by late July; Sneider reported he would be introduced in *The Fantastic Four: First Steps* (2025).
- SDCC, end of July 2024: the Russos confirmed as directors of both films; *Avengers 5* retitled *Avengers: Doomsday*; McFeely taking over as writer of both; filming set for early 2025 in London. Markus did not return, focusing on AGBO. Majors said he was "heartbroken" and remained open to returning as Kang.
- Pay: the Russos and Downey reported at $40 million and $50 million respectively per film, plus box office bonuses with potential for Downey's salary to double; Downey also negotiated private jet travel, dedicated personal security and multiple trailers with personal chefs. Chris Hemsworth was reported by Belloni to have a major role and be the "second lead".
- May 2025: Disney delayed *Doomsday* to December 18, 2026, and *Secret Wars* to December 17, 2027.
- July 2025: Feige revealed Waldron was helping McFeely with the scripts; Chris McKenna and Erik Sommers left *Brand New Day* to work on them. In September (2026) Waldron explained all four writers were working together at that point, around his commitments to *Chad Powers* (2025-present).
- January 2026: Justin Kroll of Deadline Hollywood reported Feige had been solely focused on the two films for the last year. Louis D'Esposito and Jonathan Schwartz also produce *Doomsday* alongside Feige. Pre-production on *Secret Wars* was underway by April 2026, simultaneous with *Doomsday* post-production.

wikis.title: Writing and story
wikis.summary: The comic inspirations, how the films connect to Endgame and the Multiverse Saga, and what Feige and the Russos say Secret Wars will do to the MCU.
wikis.body:
- March 2025: the Russos confirmed the 1984-85 *Secret Wars* event and the 2015-16 storyline both serve as "loose inspiration". Feige said "Time Runs Out", the prelude to the 2015-16 story, was also an inspiration. Speculation followed about elements of the 2012 "Avengers vs. X-Men" crossover and Jonathan Maberry's 2010 *Doomwar*. *Once Upon a Time in the West* (1968) was an additional inspiration for *Doomsday*.
- The Russos said they wanted to restore the franchise's focus on a central narrative. Joe Russo called the September 2026 re-release of *Endgame* under the name *Avengers Endgame: Encore* "required viewing" for the new film.
- *Doomsday* features heroes from three universes converging: the Avengers, Wakandans and New Avengers from Earth-616; the Fantastic Four from Earth-828; and the "original" X-Men from a separate universe.
- *Doomsday* is set fourteen months after *Thunderbolts\** and four years after the main events of *First Steps*, at the same time as that film's mid-credits scene introducing Doom.
- April 2025: Anthony Mackie said *Doomsday* would have a cliffhanger ending and "everyone is expendable". Feige said the relationship between the two films would differ from that between *Infinity War* and *Endgame*; the Russos saw them as a new beginning. Feige: "*Endgame*, literally, was about endings. *Secret Wars* is about beginnings."
- Ebon Moss-Bachrach said he was given a full *Doomsday* script but it did not have a completed third act or ending, and much of it changed during filming. Lewis Pullman said each character gets their own moment rather than cameos. Tenoch Huerta said the film is about characters colliding and then dealing with specific tasks to survive.
- Siegel clarified that Reed Richards would have an integral role but not as the "centerpiece", after comments by *First Steps* director Matt Shakman caused misconceptions.
- On Steve Rogers's return, the Russos called him "the character that changed our lives... it was always going to come back"; Evans had received pitches (including taking the Nomad mantle) that "never quite felt right" until the *Doomsday* pitch, and described the arc as "brutal".
- November 2024: Feige said Fox X-Men characters would keep appearing up to *Secret Wars*, which would introduce a "new age of mutants and of the X-Men"; The Wall Street Journal reported a ten-year plan for those characters. July 2025: Feige confirmed *Secret Wars* would "reset" the MCU with a new "singular timeline" and a recast X-Men team, avoiding the term "reboot", "a scary word". A year later: it would "establish a streamlined, simplified, single universe that audiences can keep up with. Some things will be familiar, but many, many things will be entirely new." He called it "as ambitious a project as we've ever embarked on".
- The book *MCU: The Reign of Marvel Studios* (2023) by Robinson, Dave Gonzales and Gavin Edwards includes a Feige quote that Robinson felt implied *Secret Wars* would be a soft reboot.

wikis.title: Casting
wikis.summary: The ensemble assembled for Doomsday and Secret Wars, including the 26 cast members announced in March 2025, the returning Fox X-Men actors and the unresolved reports about Deadpool and Wolverine.
wikis.body:
- June 2024: Deadline Hollywood described the first film as more of an ensemble than prior *Avengers* films, with potential for more than 60 actors to reprise MCU roles; Feige cautioned not all new Multiverse Saga characters would fit. Magnetic baseball cards were used to track available characters and actors, as on *Infinity War* and *Endgame*.
- Early reports: Benedict Cumberbatch (Doctor Strange, June 2024); Jeremy Renner as Hawkeye (Sneider, July 2024); Downey's Doctor Doom casting announced at SDCC ("new mask, same task"); Thunderbolts\* and *First Steps* cast reprising, including Pedro Pascal, Vanessa Kirby, Joseph Quinn and Ebon Moss-Bachrach; Tom Holland expected as Spider-Man.
- December 2024: Chris Evans, Anthony Mackie and Hayley Atwell reported for *Doomsday*; Evans's role unclear (Rogers or the Human Torch variant), with Sneider suggesting Nomad. Evans denied involvement, saying he was "happily retired" from Marvel.
- January 2025: Sneider reported Marvel was casting an alternate T'Challa / Black Panther starting with *Doomsday*, later saying it was for T'Challa II / Toussaint, introduced as a child in *Black Panther: Wakanda Forever* (2022); the original T'Challa actor Chadwick Boseman died in August 2020.
- End of March 2025: Marvel officially announced 26 cast members for *Doomsday* - Chris Hemsworth, Kirby, Mackie, Sebastian Stan, Letitia Wright, Paul Rudd, Wyatt Russell, Tenoch Huerta Mejia, Moss-Bachrach, Simu Liu, Florence Pugh, Lewis Pullman, Danny Ramirez, Quinn, David Harbour, Winston Duke, Hannah John-Kamen, Tom Hiddleston, Channing Tatum and Pascal, plus Fox X-Men returnees Kelsey Grammer, Patrick Stewart, Ian McKellen, Alan Cumming, Rebecca Romijn and James Marsden. Couch and Kit reported only about half the cast had been revealed, noting the absence of Holland and Evans; Atwell was reported to have signed for both films.
- May 2025: photos in Bahrain revealed Mabel Cadena (Namora) and Alex Livinalli (Attuma) returning.
- August 2025: Reynolds posted a graffiti-vandalized Avengers logo, prompting conflicting reports over whether Deadpool appears (see the disagreement noted on the main page). Reynolds said it was simply his favorite design of the flag from *Deadpool & Wolverine*.
- December 2025 teasers confirmed Evans as Rogers and revealed India Rose Hemsworth returning as Love from *Thor: Love and Thunder* (2022).
- April 2026: a CinemaCon trailer revealed Kathryn Newton reprising Cassie Lang; Wesley Holloway also announced. July 2026 SDCC: Atwell officially confirmed as Carter; Reynolds appeared in a Deadpool suit to jokingly ask for a role. August 2026 D23: Reynolds and Jackman appeared by video message, Jackman jokingly offering to join.
- *Secret Wars* casting: Sadie Sink (November 2025), cast as Jean Grey for *Brand New Day*; Wright and Liu returning as Shuri and Shang-Chi; Paul Bettany as Vision; Evans confirmed in June (2026); Sneider reported Ryan Gosling as Johnny Blaze / Ghost Rider ahead of a solo *Ghost Rider* (2028); Noah Jupe cast in an undisclosed "key" role at the start of September.

wikis.title: Design
wikis.summary: Production and costume design for the two films, including reused Baxter Building sets and comics-accurate X-Men and Namor costumes.
wikis.body:
- Gavin Bocquet was set as production designer for *Doomsday*, reteaming with the Russos after season two of their series *Citadel* (2023-present).
- The Baxter Building sets designed by Kasra Farahani for *First Steps* were reused, with some updates, for *Doomsday*, which also features sets similar to those in the Fox X-Men films.
- Costume designers Judianna Makovsky and Graham Churchyard returned from previous MCU films for *Doomsday* and *Secret Wars* respectively.
- The X-Men wear comics-based costumes: Cyclops in a yellow and blue suit based on Jim Lee's "classic" design, without the yellow trunks; Xavier in a grey jacket with a black-and-red X symbol based on Grant Morrison and Frank Quitely's *New X-Men* (2001-2004).
- Namor wears a comics-accurate black suit with shimmering blue scales and a high collar, reminiscent of the moisture suit first seen in *Sub-Mariner* vol. 1 #67 (November 1973), and no longer has the facial piercings from *Wakanda Forever*.
- The Russos said Doom's costume was their favorite to date, feeling the character and the costume "really, really fit" each other.

wikis.title: Filming
wikis.summary: The filming plan and principal photography of Doomsday at Pinewood and on location from April to September 2025, and the schedule for Secret Wars.
wikis.body:
- October 2024: the Russos said the two films were being produced together like *Infinity War* and *Endgame* but would not be filmed back-to-back (there were four weeks between those two shoots); Anthony said around a year would separate the shoots. Joe later said they were being made "fairly back-to-back".
- Early 2025: *Doomsday* filming reported for March to August. Mackie said he was splitting time between London and filming *12 12 12* in Budapest. The Russos said filming would occur primarily on soundstages and chosen locations to avoid leaked set photos.
- Production for both films is based at Pinewood Studios in Buckinghamshire, England. Some "pre-photography" for *Doomsday* occurred in April 2025, including the *Thunderbolts\** post-credits scene shot with the New Avengers cast, filmed by the Russos accompanied by *Thunderbolts\** director Jake Schreier. The Russos also directed the *First Steps* mid-credits scene during *Doomsday* production.
- Principal photography began on April 28 under the working title *Apple Pie 1*, having originally been expected in early 2024 before Majors's firing and the creative shifts. Cinematographer Newton Thomas Sigel reteamed with the Russos after *Citadel* and *Cherry* (2021). Filming began without a finished script; the Russos said they usually change scripts during rehearsals.
- Locations: Bahrain by the end of May 2025; four days at Windsor Great Park in mid-to-late June with sets for a spaceship and a 1960s-style bungalow called the "Luke Cage house" ("Luke Cage" was the codename for Evans, used to keep his return secret); an additional Windsor Great Park day in August with a set called "Annie Reynolds's house"; Shinfield Studios in Berkshire.
- By late July the *First Steps* cast had finished half their scenes; Romijn had filmed some scenes and was unsure if more were needed because the script was still being written. Pascal and Cumming finished by early August - Cumming's *The Traitors* schedule meant his scenes were shot together using green screens and other techniques. Wright wrapped in late August. Tatum relied on his stunt double after an on-set injury. Filming wrapped on September 19.
- *Secret Wars*: principal photography scheduled to begin in late 2026, around a year after *Doomsday* finished, lasting approximately six months. At the end of July 2026 Anthony Russo said filming would begin "soon". Moss-Bachrach was expected to start in August 2026, after his Broadway run in *Dog Day Afternoon* (2026).

wikis.title: Post-production, additional photography and music
wikis.summary: Editing and runtime reports for Doomsday, the 2026 reshoots, and Alan Silvestri scoring both films.
wikis.body:
- Jeffrey Ford and Matthew Schmidt are editing both films after working on previous MCU media (both credits carry an "[independent source needed]" tag in the article).
- March 2025: the Russos estimated *Doomsday* at approximately two-and-a-half hours and *Secret Wars* at approximately three hours.
- July 2026: with *Doomsday*'s premium large format tickets going on sale, a 165-minute runtime was set so theaters could schedule showtimes; The Hollywood Reporter noted the final cut was "unlikely to be locked this far in advance" and could only change within a small margin. Shortly after, the Russos said they were "deep" in editing but had not finished the film, were still shaping it and finding new moments, and that the runtime would be "substantial".
- Additional photography: The Hollywood Reporter reported a "healthy" amount for *Doomsday*, expected in early 2026. Harbour said he was returning to London soon after February 2026 for the reshoots; Duke confirmed in May that additional photography had been taking place; the next month Harbour said reshoots with himself and other Avengers actors had been taking place at Pinewood in London.
- Music: in April 2024 Alan Silvestri indicated he could be composing for an upcoming MCU project after *Infinity War*, *Endgame* and other MCU films; that July he was confirmed to be returning for both *Doomsday* and *Secret Wars*.
- The article's "See also" points to *Production of Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame*.

wikis.title: Citation source code for the Doomsday and Secret Wars production article (references 1-100)
wikis.summary: Raw Wikipedia reference wikitext for the production article, holding roughly 100 named citations from a December 2017 Disney press release through mid-2025 trade reporting.
wikis.body:
- This part is not article prose: it is the page's raw citation markup, a run of about 100 `<ref name="...">{{Cite ...}}</ref>` templates with titles, authors, dates, URLs, archive URLs and access dates.
- It opens with the reference named `FoxDisneyPressRelease`: a Walt Disney Company press release dated December 14, 2017, titled "The Walt Disney Company To Acquire Twenty-First Century Fox, Inc., After Spinoff of Certain Businesses, For $52.4 Billion in Stock".
- It ends mid-run with `WSJMay2025` - Ben Fritz, "Disney Wanted More From Marvel. Now It Wants Less.", The Wall Street Journal, May 2, 2025, marked `url-access=limited` - and the start of `FeigeConferenceJul2025Variety2` by Adam B. Vary.
- Reference names track the article's narrative, e.g. `IgerAvengersFuture`, `FeigeFuture`, `JoeRussoSWApr2018`, `BothSWsInspirations`, `ThunderboltsNewAvengers`.
- Most-cited domains in this run: deadline.com, hollywoodreporter.com, variety.com, comicbook.com, screenrant.com, gamesradar.com, collider.com, ign.com and cbr.com; almost every citation carries a web.archive.org archive URL.

- Reference names in this run include `FeigeConferenceJul2025THR`, `ShakmanBaton`, `FeigeFFDoomsday`, `PascalNotAvengersLeader`, `FSMidCredits`, `RomijnFilmingJul2025` and `PascalWrap`.

wikis.title: End of the citation markup and the rendered reference list (notes 1-162)

wikis.body:
- The first part of this section is the tail of the raw citation markup (about 19 more `<ref name="...">` templates), including `CummingWrap` (Brenton Blanchet and Scott Huver, August 17, 2025, on Alan Cumming playing Nightcrawler), `TatumSep2025`, `WrightWrap`, `AvengersDoomsdayFilmingWrap`, `HarbourJun2026`, `DukeMay2026`, `SilvestriApr2024` (Emily Murray, Total Film / GamesRadar+, April 30, 2024) and `SilvestriJul2024` (Film Music Reporter, July 29, 2024, "Alan Silvestri to Score Marvel Studios' 'Avengers: Doomsday' & 'Secret Wars'").
- The rest is the rendered reference list: about 162 numbered entries in citation style with author, date, title, publication, archive date and retrieval date.
- The list begins with the December 14, 2017 Disney press release on the 21st Century Fox acquisition, then Thomas Bacon (Screen Rant, April 10, 2018), Aaron Couch (The Hollywood Reporter, May 8, 2018) and Christopher Fiduccia (Screen Rant, April 9, 2019).
- It ends with a PDF listing for "Matthew Schmidt" from Independent Artist Group (archived August 16, 2026) and James Hibberd, "'Avengers: Doomsday' Tickets to Go On Sale Next Week, Runtime Revealed (Exclusive)", The Hollywood Reporter, July 13, 2026.
- Cited outlets in this run include Collider, The Hollywood Reporter, GamesRadar+, People, Variety, 9meters.com and the Reading Chronicle.

Team for Action-Thriller 'Ordained' (Exclusive)", The Hollywood Reporter, November 12, 2025; George Lewis, David Harbour saying *Avengers: Doomsday* is the "biggest thing I've ever done", Digital Spy, February 28, 2026; Hazeeq Sukri, Winston Duke on "crazy surprises" in *Avengers: Doomsday*, CNA Lifestyle, August 28, 2026; Perri Nemiroff and Chris McPherson, "David Harbour Gives Honest 'Avengers: Doomsday' Reaction After Test Screening Rumors [Exclusive]", Collider, June 2, 2026; Emily Murray, "The composer behind Marvel's Avengers: Endgame teases a return to the MCU", Total Film / GamesRadar+, April 30, 2024; and "Alan Silvestri to Score Marvel Studios' 'Avengers: Doomsday' & 'Secret Wars'", Film Music Reporter, July 29, 2024.

- Further list links cover Fox's X-Men films (through *Dark Phoenix* (2019) and *The New Mutants* (2020)) and other Marvel-derived films such as *Howard the Duck* (1986), *Daredevil* (2003), *Elektra* (2005), *Man-Thing* (2005), *Black Widow* (2021), *Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings* (2021), *Eternals* (2021), *Morbius* (2022), *Madame Web* (2024), *Kraven the Hunter* (2024) and *Thunderbolts\** (2025), plus the Kick-Ass imprint.

wikis.title: Damn You Hollywood: A Quiet Place - Day One (2024) (podcast episode)
wikis.summary: A 2h 9m Radulich in Broadcasting episode published 2 July 2024 in which Robert Winfree and Mark Radulich review A Quiet Place: Day One, run through its box office, read the critics and close with MMA and wrestling plugs.
wikis.body:
## The episode

- "Damn You Hollywood: A Quiet Place - Day One (2024)", from the show Radulich in Broadcasting, published "July 2, 2024 at 3:36 AM UTC", length 2h 9m, rated Explicit.
- "Robert Winfree and Mark Radulich present their A Quiet Place Day One 2024 Movie Review!"

## The film, per the episode description

- A Quiet Place: Day One is a 2024 American apocalyptic horror film written and directed by Michael Sarnoski from a story with John Krasinski, the third installment in the series and a spin-off prequel, starring Lupita Nyong'o with Joseph Quinn, Alex Wolff and Djimon Hounsou.
- Jeff Nichols was set to write and direct from November 2020 and finished a script by May 2021 before dropping out in October 2021; Sarnoski was announced in January 2022. Principal photography ran February 2023 to April 2023 in London, England.
- It premiered at the Tribeca Festival on June 26, 2024, was released in the United States by Paramount Pictures on June 28, 2024, "received generally positive reviews from critics and has grossed $98 million worldwide".

## The review

- The hosts recap the earlier films, praising the first for being optimistic and about a family rather than the creatures, and calling Part II the weakest of the three.
- Day One's story is walked through: a hospice patient with an unspecified terminal illness heads for a Harlem pizzeria as the creatures arrive, joined by a young Englishman and a cat named Frodo, and ends by drawing the creatures away so he can reach a boat.
- Both find the two leads thinly written but the tension and the theme of finding a reason to live effective. Radulich argues the film should have had no musical score and that its sound design is only adequate; both say Djimon Hounsou was advertised far beyond his screen time.

## Box office and critics

- "On a budget of sixty seven million dollars, this thing has made ninety eight point five million dollars as of this recording on Monday, July first"; as of June 30, 2024, $53 million in the US and Canada and $45.5 million elsewhere. Opening day $22.5 million including $6.8 million in previews, "the best of the series"; opening weekend $53 million, second behind Inside Out 2, which had just crossed $1 billion worldwide.
- Rotten Tomatoes: 83% top critics, 85% all critics, 74 verified audience, 70 all audiences. Quotes are read from Grace Randolph, James Berardinelli, Amy Nicholson, Kurt Loder and others.

## Plugs

- Closing segments cover UFC 303 (McGregor's withdrawal, Pereira's second-round head kick, Dan Ige on four hours' notice) and WWE (Paul Heyman, Solo Sikoa, Jacob Fatu, Roman Reigns off TV), plus the show's upcoming schedule.

## About the capture

- The page carries Apple Podcasts chrome (country picker, sign-in prompts) and a machine-generated transcript that garbles several names; the transcript is split across the two parts. The page states no last-modified date beyond its publication date.

wikis.title: Damn You Hollywood: A Quiet Place - Day One (2024) - episode details and the first half of the review
wikis.summary: The Apple Podcasts page for the Radulich in Broadcasting episode reviewing A Quiet Place: Day One, with the episode's publication details and description and the first half of the transcript, in which Robert Winfree and Mark Radulich discuss the earlier films, recap Day One's plot and argue about its characters, score and sound design.
wikis.body:
## Episode details

- Title: "Damn You Hollywood: A Quiet Place - Day One (2024)"; show: Radulich in Broadcasting; frequency "Updated Daily".
- Published "July 2, 2024 at 3:36 AM UTC"; the page also shows the date "July 2, 2024". Length 2h 9m. Rating: Explicit.
- "Robert Winfree and Mark Radulich present their A Quiet Place Day One 2024 Movie Review!"
- The episode description states: A Quiet Place: Day One is a 2024 American apocalyptic horror film written and directed by Michael Sarnoski from a story he conceived with John Krasinski; the third installment in the series, a spin-off and prequel; starring Lupita Nyong'o as a terminally ill woman during the beginning of an invasion of New York City by extraterrestrial creatures with an acute sense of hearing, with Joseph Quinn, Alex Wolff and Djimon Hounsou, who reprises his role from the second film.
- Development began in November 2020 with Jeff Nichols set to write and direct; his script was complete by May 2021, but in October 2021 he dropped out over creative differences; in January 2022 Sarnoski was announced as replacement, approached by Krasinski because of Pig (2021). "Principal photography took place from February 2023 to April 2023 in London, England."
- The film "premiered at the Tribeca Festival on June 26, 2024, and was released in the United States by Paramount Pictures on June 28, 2024", received generally positive reviews "and has grossed $98 million worldwide".
- The page carries a disclaimer about offensive language and adult humour, links to Mark Radulich's social accounts, and then the episode transcript (which is machine-generated and garbles several names).

## Talking about the earlier films

- Winfree says the review was going to be called "in the ring"; the hosts open with a Hulk Hogan story about Andre the Giant and Randy Savage.
- Radulich says he had never seen A Quiet Place until "this past Sunday", and that his son had watched a Pitch Meeting video about it first, which spoiled the experience.
- Both praise the first film for being optimistic rather than bleak, and for being about a family rather than the creatures; Radulich says the final third, when it "descends into ... killing the aliens", lost him.
- On A Quiet Place Part II, Winfree calls it "the weakest of the three": the family leaves the farm, meets Cillian Murphy's character, and the plan is to broadcast the daughter's cochlear implant feedback over a radio station; the opening sequence showing that family's day one "is actually a really good sequence".
- Radulich objects that Day One does not make clear that the creatures landed everywhere and not only on Manhattan; Winfree answers that Part II shows them hitting a smaller town too, and that "they landed everywhere".

## Plot recap of Day One

- An opening title card says New York City gives off the sound of a constant scream because of its noise.
- Lupita Nyong'o plays a woman with a terminal illness, "presumably cancer but never specified", living in a hospice centre; the group takes an excursion into the city to see a marionette puppet show. She wants pizza from a particular place in Harlem that was meaningful to her and her father.
- The creatures arrive, she survives and wakes in the theatre with other survivors; helicopters with loudspeakers give instructions, the bridges are blown up, and it is quickly realised the creatures cannot swim. Survivors are directed to a ferry at South Street Seaport, but she walks the other way towards Harlem.
- She is joined by a young Englishman (Joseph Quinn), who came to New York for law school, and by her cat, named Frodo. They reach the pizzeria to find it burned out; he later finds pizza elsewhere and brings it back, they share it and swap jackets, and she gives him the cat.
- She distracts the creatures so he can reach a boat, then sits in Harlem playing music aloud, ending the film on her own terms.

## The hosts' criticisms

- Radulich's son Jonas rated it "like a five out of ten" and asked why it was made; the hosts agree the film is about tension rather than jump scares, and about hope and human connection rather than the monsters.
- Both find Nyong'o's character thin - "she's just dying cancer lady through this whole movie" - and say Quinn's character is never developed because the film cannot slow down; Winfree argues the emotional journey still works and that "watching interesting characters do nothing is maybe more frustrating than watching flat characters do things that are interesting".
- Radulich argues at length that neither this film nor the first should have used a musical score, saying ambient sound alone would have added to the tension, and that the sound design here is "just sort of adequate" compared with Evil Dead Rise; Winfree is "torn", noting how critical scores are to films.
- Radulich discloses that he has "almost died twice from cancer" and describes chemotherapy, mouth infections and a broken jaw, saying this is why the character's arc lands for him.

wikis.title: Segment: the earlier A Quiet Place films
wikis.summary: The hosts compare A Quiet Place (2018) and A Quiet Place Part II before reviewing the prequel.
wikis.body:
- Radulich had never seen the first film until the Sunday before recording; Winfree reviewed Part II "back in our Audio only Days" with Alexis and Jason.
- Both praise the first film's opening, where a child's noisy toy gets him killed, and the deaf girl's point of view when "that first sound cuts in and we see everyone else react to it first and then we hear it".
- The first film is called optimistic and tragic rather than bleak, and not "a meat factory"; its finale is "largely saved by the emotional moment when Krasinski sacrifices himself".
- Part II is called the weakest of the three: the family leaves the farm, meets Cillian Murphy's character, and plans to broadcast the daughter's cochlear-implant feedback from an island radio station; its day-one opening sequence is praised.

wikis.title: Segment: plot synopsis of A Quiet Place: Day One
wikis.summary: Winfree's walkthrough of the film's story, from the hospice excursion into Manhattan to the ending in Harlem.
wikis.body:
- Opening title card on New York's constant noise; Nyong'o's character is in a hospice with a terminal illness, "presumably cancer but never specified", and joins an excursion to a marionette puppet show.
- She wants a particular pizza from a Harlem pizzeria tied to her father, a jazz pianist. The creatures arrive during the trip; the bridges and tunnels are destroyed and helicopters direct survivors to a ferry at South Street Seaport.
- She walks north against the flow towards Harlem with her cat, Frodo, joined by a young Englishman in New York for law school; the hosts note the walk takes a couple of days.
- The pizzeria is burned out; he finds pizza elsewhere, they share it and a drink at the bar where her father played, trade jackets, and she gives him the cat.
- She draws the creatures away so he can swim to a boat, then plays music aloud in Harlem as the film ends.

wikis.title: Segment: score, sound design and characters
wikis.summary: The hosts' craft criticism of Day One - the musical score, the sound design and the thinness of the two leads.
wikis.body:
- Radulich argues neither A Quiet Place nor Day One should have had a score: "If you eliminate the score and the movie is just the noise of the scene ... I think would have added to the tension". He says his daughter Lily made the same criticism.
- Winfree is unsure, noting a score's importance (Halloween, a Mission: Impossible sequence rescued by changing its music) and suspecting producers insisted on one.
- Radulich compares the sound design unfavourably with Evil Dead Rise and says the film never conveys how loud a small sound is in a silent night; Winfree calls the sound "slightly better than competent".
- Both find the leads underwritten - the woman is "just dying cancer lady", and the Englishman is never developed because the film cannot slow down - while arguing the film's strength is tension and its theme of finding a reason to live.

wikis.title: Damn You Hollywood on A Quiet Place: Day One - box office, critics and the hosts' plugs
wikis.summary: The second half of the episode transcript: the argument over Djimon Hounsou's small role, the box office segment with Day One's gross and the weekend chart, industry talk about Pixar and the summer slate, the critical-review segment and the hosts' MMA and wrestling plugs.
wikis.body:
## Djimon Hounsou's role

- Radulich complains that Djimon Hounsou was "advertised disproportionate to his appearance in the film" and that the part could have gone to an unknown actor; Winfree agrees about the marketing but defends hiring "a guy who you knew could do the job".
- Both praise Hounsou's one big scene, in which he silences and kills a panicking man in a stairwell while his son watches.
- Winfree's closing argument: like the first film, this one is strong "because it's not about the monsters" - it is "about finding reasons to live ... about reconnecting and finding the value in what it means to be human".

## Box office segment

- "On a budget of sixty seven million dollars, this thing has made ninety eight point five million dollars as of this recording on Monday, July first ... twenty twenty four." (The episode description separately says the film "has grossed $98 million worldwide".)
- "As of June thirty[th], twenty twenty four", Day One had grossed "fifty three million in the US and Canada and forty five point five million in other territories".
- Released alongside Horizon: An American Saga – Chapter 1 and projected to gross "forty to fifty million from almost four thousand theaters"; it made "twenty two point five million on its first day, including six[point] eight million from Thursday night previews, the best of the series", and debuted to $53 million, second behind holdover Inside Out 2.
- Winfree says the film "needs to make ... between one twenty and one thirty in order for Paramount to break out the Champagne", and that "it's gonna be fine".
- Radulich says he read that a two-pronged franchise is being considered: a prequel series alongside films following the Emily Blunt family.

## Weekend and worldwide charts

- Domestic weekend: Inside Out 2 number one for a third week; A Quiet Place: Day One number two; Horizon: An American Saga – Chapter 1 number three with $11 million; Bad Boys fell from two to four; Kalki 2898 AD number five; The Bikeriders three to six; Garfield five to seven; Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes number eight; Kinds of Kindness thirteen to nine on its wide release; further titles listed down to number forty.
- Worldwide: Inside Out 2 crossed the billion-dollar mark; Dune: Part Two second at over $700 million; Godzilla x Kong about $200 million behind it, with a third film greenlit; Kung Fu Panda 4 at $543 million; Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes almost $400 million; Bad Boys: Ride or Die $331 million; The Garfield Movie $239 million; Despicable Me 4 already $25 million from limited overseas release.
- Industry talk: the hosts trace Pixar from Luca and Turning Red going to Disney+, Lightyear bombing and Elemental slowly earning back audience trust, to Inside Out 2's billion.
- Upcoming: Despicable Me 4 on July 3; Twisters on July 19, which Winfree expects to be number one of its week and Radulich predicts will make "North [of] the five hundred million"; Deadpool & Wolverine at the end of July; Borderlands, Alien: Romulus and The Crow in August; Longlegs as Winfree's underdog pick.

## Critical review segment

- Rotten Tomatoes figures read out: "tough critics is eighty three percent ... all critics, it's eighty five"; "verified audience is seventy four, All audiences is seventy".
- The AI-written summary is read: "grounded in raw humanity by Lupita Nyong'o's and Joseph Quinn's [performances]. The sideways entry into A Quiet Place finds fresh notes of fright to play amongst the silence."
- Quotes are read from Mark Jackson (Epoch Times), James Berardinelli (ReelViews - "although some scenes are suffused with suffocating tension ... Day One at times feels more like an art house movie than something made for mainstream audiences"), Sarah Michelle Fetters (moviefreak.com), Sarah G. Vincent, Sarah Gopaul, Kevin Carr, Nick Johnson, Grace Randolph (Beyond the Trailer - "a very well made film, with excellent performances from Nyong'o and Quinn ... also a surprisingly sad film"), Joseph Robinson (Fish Jelly Films), Amy Nicholson (Washington Post), Kurt Loder, Eric Martin and Jeffrey Harris (411mania).

## Plugs and schedule

- No other podcast that week because of the July 4th holiday; next up is Despicable Me 4, and on July 11 the second half of a "High School in Trouble" series with Pat Mullen and Ronnie Adams covering The Substitute, The Principal and 187, after an earlier run of Stand and Deliver, Lean On Me and Dangerous Minds.
- Radulich describes retooling the schedule to add more guests and to give the year-in-review segment its own show.
- Winfree recaps UFC 303 on International Fight Week: Conor McGregor broke a toe two weeks out and pulled out of the planned main event with Michael Chandler; Alex Pereira vs Jiri Prochazka became the main event and Diego Lopes vs Brian Ortega the co-main; Ortega missed featherweight, the bout moved to 155 pounds, and he then withdrew with "a fever of one hundred and three degrees"; Dan Ige took the fight on four hours' notice. Pereira won with "a beautiful headkick thirteen seconds into the second round".
- WWE: Winfree describes Paul Heyman refusing to acknowledge Solo Sikoa at Madison Square Garden, Jacob Fatu's debut taking out Kevin Owens, Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes, and Roman Reigns being off television since losing the belt at WrestleMania while shooting a heist comedy.

wikis.title: Segment: the money
wikis.summary: The episode's box office segment on Day One's budget, gross and opening weekend, plus the domestic and worldwide charts.
wikis.body:
- Budget "sixty seven million dollars"; gross "ninety eight point five million dollars as of this recording on Monday, July first ... twenty twenty four".
- As of June 30, 2024: $53 million in the US and Canada and $45.5 million in other territories. Projected $40–50 million from almost 4,000 theatres; first day $22.5 million including $6.8 million in Thursday previews, "the best of the series"; debut $53 million, second behind Inside Out 2.
- Winfree says it needs "between one twenty and one thirty" for Paramount to celebrate.
- Domestic chart: Inside Out 2 first for a third week, Day One second, Horizon: An American Saga – Chapter 1 third with $11 million, then Bad Boys, Kalki 2898 AD, The Bikeriders, Garfield, Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes, Kinds of Kindness.
- Worldwide: Inside Out 2 past $1 billion; Dune: Part Two over $700 million; Kung Fu Panda 4 $543 million; Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes almost $400 million; Bad Boys: Ride or Die $331 million; The Garfield Movie $239 million; Despicable Me 4 $25 million from early overseas release.

wikis.title: Segment: the critical review
wikis.summary: The hosts read Rotten Tomatoes scores and critic quotes for A Quiet Place: Day One and react to each.
wikis.body:
- Rotten Tomatoes: top critics 83%, all critics 85%; verified audience 74, all audiences 70.
- The site's AI-written summary praises the film as "grounded in raw humanity by Lupita Nyong'o's and Joseph Quinn's" performances.
- Critics quoted include Mark Jackson (Epoch Times), James Berardinelli (ReelViews), Sarah Michelle Fetters (moviefreak.com), Sarah G. Vincent, Sarah Gopaul, Kevin Carr, Nick Johnson, Grace Randolph (Beyond the Trailer), Joseph Robinson (Fish Jelly Films), Amy Nicholson (Washington Post), Kurt Loder, Eric Martin and Jeffrey Harris (411mania).
- Winfree objects to Randolph calling the film sad - "It's poignant, but it's not sad" - and to Eric Martin calling it the best-directed film in the franchise.

wikis.title: Segment: plugs - UFC 303 and WWE
wikis.summary: Winfree's closing plugs recapping UFC 303 and recent WWE SmackDown angles.
wikis.body:
- UFC 303 during International Fight Week: Conor McGregor broke a toe two weeks out, cancelling his return against Michael Chandler; Alex Pereira vs Jiri Prochazka replaced it as the main event, with Diego Lopes vs Brian Ortega as co-main.
- The original co-main, Jamahal Hill vs Khalil Rountree, fell apart through a drug-test issue and a knee injury, with replacements Carlos Ulberg, Anthony Smith and Roman Dolidze.
- Ortega could not make 145 pounds, so the bout moved to 155; he then withdrew with a fever of 103 degrees and Dan Ige took the fight on four hours' notice.
- Pereira won by head kick "thirteen seconds into the second round"; Winfree calls him probably the biggest star in the sport and notes he wants a third weight class.
- WWE: Paul Heyman refused to acknowledge Solo Sikoa at Madison Square Garden and was put through the announce table by Jacob Fatu, whose debut took out Kevin Owens, Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes; Roman Reigns has been off TV since WrestleMania, shooting a heist comedy.

wikis.title: Falcon 9 Block 5 | Crew-13 (Launch Library 2 API record)
wikis.summary: The Space Devs' Launch Library 2 API record for SpaceX Crew-13, giving its to-be-confirmed 1 October 2026 launch time, crew, Falcon 9 booster and Crew Dragon, launch pad and the dated schedule updates behind the delay.
wikis.body:
## The launch

- "Falcon 9 Block 5 | Crew-13", id 18441371-8b2e-457c-afb5-1ec1b11ab630, served by ll.thespacedevs.com/2.3.0 in detailed mode.
- Status "To Be Confirmed" (TBC) - "Awaiting official confirmation - current date is known with some certainty."
- `net` 2026-10-01T15:10:06Z, with the launch window start and end at the same instant and T-0 accurate to the second. Record last updated 2026-09-18T15:35:11Z.
- Launch service provider SpaceX; `webcast_live` false; no info or video URLs, timeline or mission patches.

## Mission and crew

- Mission "Crew-13", type Human Exploration, to Low Earth Orbit: "SpaceX Crew-13 is the thirteenth crewed operational flight of a Crew Dragon spacecraft to the International Space Station as part of NASA's Commercial Crew Program."
- Crew, listed for both launch and landing: Jessica Watkins (Spacecraft Commander, NASA), Joshua Kutryk (Flight Engineer, Canadian Space Agency), Luke Delaney (Pilot, NASA) and Sergey Teteryatnikov (Flight Engineer, ROSCOSMOS).
- Programs: Commercial Crew Program (from 2011-04-18; Boeing, NASA, SpaceX) and International Space Station (from 1998-11-20).

## Hardware

- Falcon 9 Block 5: maiden flight 2018-05-11, 633 launches with 632 successful and 1 failed, 111 pending; 70.0 m long, 3.65 m diameter, launch mass 549.0, LEO capacity 22800, listed launch cost $52,000,000.
- First stage B1101 flying its 3rd flight, reused, previously flown on Crew-12 on 2026-02-13; it will land at Landing Zone 40 (LZ-40) in a Return to Launch Site landing, 0.3 downrange.
- Spacecraft Crew Dragon Grace (C213), "first used for Axiom-4", of the four-seat Crew Dragon 2 configuration; it is bound for the International Space Station and "will splash down in the Pacific Ocean" under parachutes.

## Pad

- Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral SFS, FL, USA, operated by SpaceX, at 28.56194122, -80.57735736; 401 launches from the pad and 1129 from the location. Pad turnaround P17DT20H21M6S.
- Launch attempt counters: orbital 7410, location 1131, pad 402, agency 734 (for the year: 237, 55, 48 and 115).

## Schedule history

- Updates by Cosmic_Penguin run from "NET mid-September" (2026-04-23) through "NET September 12" and an updated launch time (2026-08-03), "Launch delayed due to Dragon propulsion system leak" (2026-08-30, citing a NASA blog post of 2026-08-29), "NET early October" (2026-09-16) and finally "NET October 1, TBC." (2026-09-18).

wikis.body:
## The endpoint

- `GET /2.3.0/launches/18441371-8b2e-457c-afb5-1ec1b11ab630/` on ll.thespacedevs.com, returning `HTTP 200 OK`, `Content-Type: application/json`, in `"response_mode": "detailed"`.
- The page's browsable-API header documents the Launch Instance endpoint: modes (`list`, `normal`, `detailed`), a long list of filter parameters, searchable fields, ordering by `id`, `last_updated`, `name` or `net`, a `limit` capped at 100, and `?format=json`.

## The launch

- `"name": "Falcon 9 Block 5 | Crew-13"`, slug `falcon-9-block-5-crew-13`, id `18441371-8b2e-457c-afb5-1ec1b11ab630`; `launch_designator` null.
- Status id 8, `"To Be Confirmed"` (TBC): "Awaiting official confirmation - current date is known with some certainty."
- `"last_updated": "2026-09-18T15:35:11Z"`. `"net": "2026-10-01T15:10:06Z"`, with `window_start` and `window_end` both the same instant and `net_precision` "Second" - "The T-0 is accurate to the second."
- `probability` and `weather_concerns` null; `failreason` empty; `hashtag` null. Image: "Crew Dragon at sunset", credit SpaceX, licence CC BY-NC 2.0.

## Launch service provider

- SpaceX (abbrev SpX), id 121, Commercial, United States of America; founded 2002; administrator "CEO: Elon Musk"; launchers "Falcon | Starship"; spacecraft "Dragon".
- Totals given for the agency: 730 launches, 715 successful, 15 failed, 215 consecutive successful, 128 pending; 702 attempted landings with 674 successful and 29 failed.

## Rocket

- Configuration "Falcon 9 Block 5" (name Falcon 9, variant Block 5), family Falcon, manufacturer SpaceX.
- Maiden flight 2018-05-11; 633 total launches, 632 successful, 1 failed, 111 pending, 335 consecutive successful.
- Length 70.0 m, diameter 3.65 m, launch mass 549.0, thrust to orbit 7607, LEO capacity 22800, GTO capacity 8300, 2 stages, reusable, `"launch_cost": 52000000`.
- The Falcon family record: maiden flight 2010-06-04, 689 launches, 685 successful, 4 failed, 112 pending, 653 attempted landings with 639 successful.

## First stage and landing

- Core serial `B1101`, status active, first launch date 2026-01-04T06:48:10Z, 2 flights so far; this is `launcher_flight_number` 3 and `reused` true.
- Previous flight "Falcon 9 Block 5 | Crew-12" on 2026-02-13T10:15:56Z.
- Landing attempt true, success null: "The Falcon 9 first stage B1101 will land back at the launch site after its 3rd flight." Landing location "Landing Zone 40" (LZ-40), described as a "Landing Pad at SLC-40 for Falcon 9 boosters. Built as an replacement for LZ-1 & LZ-2", at 28.5634384, -80.5752619, with 6 attempted and 6 successful landings. Landing type "Return to Launch Site" (RTLS); downrange distance 0.3.

## Spacecraft stage

- Destination "International Space Station"; `mission_end` null; turn-around time P443DT5H40M6S.
- Spacecraft "Crew Dragon Grace", serial `C213`, status Active, "Crew Dragon spacecraft first used for Axiom-4"; 1 flight so far, time in space P20DT2H58M8S, time docked P18DT44M.
- Configuration "Crew Dragon 2": human-rated, crew capacity 4, height 7.2, diameter 3.7, payload capacity 6000, maiden flight 2019-03-02, 22 launches all successful, 21 attempted landings with 20 successful and 1 failed; "Able to fly for up to one week of free flight or two years docked."
- Landing attempt true: "The Crew Dragon Grace capsule will splash down in the Pacific Ocean", type "Parachute Landing".
- The crew list begins here with Jessica Watkins (Spacecraft Commander, NASA, born 1988-05-14, United States of America), Joshua Kutryk (Flight Engineer, Canadian Space Agency, born 1982-03-21, Canada) and Luke Delaney (Pilot, NASA, born 1979-01-01, United States of America); the part ends inside Delaney's record.
- The rocket configuration also lists the programs it flies for, including Commercial Resupply Services and the Commercial Crew Program.
