wikis.title: TELT press dossier on the Lyon-Turin cross-border section (Mont-Cenis base tunnel)
wikis.summary: TELT's 20-page French-language press dossier describing the company, the Lyon-Turin railway line, its binational 'single worksite' rules, the local territories, R&D, and the state of each underground and surface worksite as of July 2026.
wikis.body:
## What this is
- A 20-page PDF press dossier ("Dossier de presse") from TELT, with press contacts in France (Herve de Lacotte, Sara Settembrino) and Italy (Davide Fuschi, Sara Settembrino), web telt.eu and infopress@telt-sas.com.
- Sections: company presentation, TELT and the Lyon-Turin line, focus on the "chantier unique", TELT and the territories, research and development, underground worksites (as of July 2026), open-air worksites (as of July 2026) and completed works.

## The company and the project
- TELT (Tunnel Euralpin Lyon-Turin) is the Franco-Italian public promoter responsible for building and then operating the cross-border section of the future freight and passenger line between Lyon and Turin.
- The main infrastructure under construction is the Mont-Cenis base tunnel, "avec ses 57,5 km, sera le plus long tunnel ferroviaire du monde". "La date d'achevement est prevue en 2033."
- TELT was created on 23 February 2015 under an international France-Italy agreement signed in January 2012; it is a French simplified joint-stock company owned 50% by the French State and 50% by the Italian State through the Ferrovie dello Stato Italiane group.
- Four international agreements underpin the works: the 1996 creation of the Lyon-Turin CIG, the 2001 launch of preparatory activities, the 2012 setting of construction/operating conditions and TELT's remit, and the 2015 launch of definitive works following a 2016 additional protocol.
- TELT succeeded Lyon Turin Ferroviaire (LTF), which coordinated studies and preliminary works from 2001 to 2012; LTF succeeded Alpetunnel, created in 1994.

## Key figures (stated "en date de jullet 2026")
- More than 49.2 km excavated in total, of which almost 21.6 km of the base tunnel itself, out of the 164 km of tunnel planned for the whole project (about 30.1% of the total already done): two parallel rail tunnels, 4 access adits (descenderies) and 204 safety cross-passages.
- 113 km of geological soundings and core drilling carried out in Italy and France.
- 11 worksites opened for surface and underground works, of which 4 are for excavating the base tunnel - 3 in France and 1 in Italy.
- More than 3,000 people employed on the worksites, rising to 4,000 at peak (plus 4,000 indirect jobs).
- 7 tunnel boring machines in total will dig 75% of the two tubes of the base tunnel, each 57.5 km long.
- 100% of the tunnel's civil engineering works awarded, worth more than 4 billion euros.
- Both excavated-material recovery lots have been awarded, on the French and Italian sides (CO11 and CO10).

## Financing and governance
- The studies and reconnaissance phase was co-financed 50% by France and 50% by Italy, after a European contribution of 50% of eligible costs.
- The first works phase was co-financed 42.1% by France and 57.9% by Italy, after a European contribution of 40% of eligible costs.
- European funds flow through the grant agreement between the EU, France and Italy under the Connecting Europe Facility (MIE); French funds through annual agreements between AFITF and TELT; Italian funds by "lots de construction", of which CIPES has financed four of five. Co-financing arrangements for later phases are still being defined.
- The board has ten voting members appointed by the two States plus one representative each of the European Commission, the Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes region and the Piedmont region; France designates the chairman, Italy the director general.
- Current chairman Daniel Bursaux (term April 2022 - February 2027) and director general Maurizio Bufalini (term July 2023 - February 2027).
- Two binational bodies oversee performance: the Contracts Commission (12 independent experts, renewable 5-year terms) and the Permanent Control Service (12 members, renewable 5-year terms).
- TELT joined the United Nations Global Compact in 2015.

## The line
- The future Lyon-Turin line is 270 km long, 70% in France and 30% in Italy, at the heart of the Mediterranean Corridor, one of the 9 axes of the European TEN-T network linking Spain to Eastern Europe.
- Three sections: the 65 km cross-border section under TELT (base tunnel, connections to national lines and the two international stations of Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne in Savoie and Susa in Piedmont); the French part Lyon to Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne, about 160 km, under SNCF Reseau; the Italian part from the Turin junction to Bussoleno, about 50 km, under Rete Ferroviaria Italiana (RFI).
- The historic line and the Frejus tunnel, "en service depuis plus de 150 ans", can no longer carry the required traffic.
- Six other European base tunnels are cited: Gotthard (57 km), Brenner (56 km), Koralm (32 km), Semmering (27 km), Ceneri (15.4), Loetschberg (34.6 km).
- Freight benefits: new European standards will allow trains of up to 2,000 tonnes against 600-700 tonnes today; one train can carry the equivalent of 50 lorries, so the line will remove "environ un million de poids lourds par an" from Alpine roads, cutting greenhouse gas emissions by up to 1 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent a year.
- Passenger benefits: 22 long-distance trains a day against 6 today on the historic Lyon-Turin line, shorter journey times and more connections.

wikis.title: The binational 'chantier unique' rules
wikis.summary: TELT's single set of rules across French and Italian sites: workplace safety, transnational anti-mafia controls, excavated-material reuse and environmental monitoring.
wikis.body:
- TELT treats all its French and Italian sites as a single binational worksite, with one set of rules for itself and its suppliers combining the best of Italian and French regulation on safety, transparency and integrity, circular economy of excavated materials and the environment.
- Safety: since 2015 the "Mission S" strategy commits contractors and workers at every stage, on the principle that safety is a shared responsibility, investing in knowledge, continuous training and innovative technologies.
- Anti-mafia: "pour la premiere fois en Europe, une reglementation anti-mafia transnationale est en application", with the same procedures whichever country a site is in. The French and Italian regional prefectures share information with police support and can run joint inspections; checks cover contractors and the whole subcontracting chain for any contract value, and third-country firms too, carried out by the Italian or French prefecture depending on where works start or where the firm does most of its business. Firms passing all checks join a binational "liste blanche".
- Excavated materials: under a 2023 agreement drawn up by the intergovernmental commission and ratified by France and Italy, TELT may reuse excavated materials across national borders - the first application in Europe of the circular economy principle on a single binational worksite. Spoil is sorted by environmental and geomechanical classification: the best is turned into aggregates for tunnel lining concrete segments or road and rail embankments; the rest is used for filling and reshaping in renaturation and ecological restoration. With CERN, the Polytechnic University of Turin and CETU, TELT aims to reuse up to 60% of the material extracted, "soit environ 37 millions de tonnes".
- Environmental monitoring: a common French-Italian environmental policy imposes the same standards on all firms; monitoring units measure parameters inside and outside the sites under national control bodies. Water is the central point - protecting water sources through route choices and innovative sealing methods, quality checks at many capture points, and reuse of water for industrial purposes such as cement production or damping stockpiles and access tracks against dust.

wikis.title: TELT and the territories: Maurienne and the Susa Valley
wikis.summary: The local programmes accompanying the works in the Maurienne valley in France and the Susa Valley in Italy.
wikis.body:
- The Maurienne is a 120 km Alpine valley in Savoie crossed by the Arc, with about 43,000 inhabitants at an average density of 22 per km2; its traditional farming economy is now complemented by electrochemical industry, aluminium refining, hydroelectric plants and summer and winter tourism.
- The "Demarche Grand Chantier", led by the French State through the Savoie prefecture with the Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes region and the Savoie department, covers recruitment, training, worker accommodation and mobilisation of local and regional firms, treating the project as a lever for local development.
  - MELT - Mon Emploi Lyon Turin connects recruiters and future employees through a free programme run by France Travail and the Mission Locale Jeunes du Pays de Maurienne, open to all profiles interested in underground work, with social clauses imposed on firms and training offered before arrival on site.
  - "Mon logement Lyon Turin" renovates vacant or run-down housing in the Maurienne to house workers while improving the building stock, mobilising exceptional funding for energy-efficiency upgrades of private and public housing.
- The Susa Valley is 80 km long with more than 90,000 inhabitants, a long-standing route between France and Italy, with international ski resorts and Roman and medieval heritage promoted since the 2021 "Destination touristique Vallee de Suse" agreement.
- Piedmont's regional law 4/2011 promotes actions for the municipalities affected by the base tunnel. Under it, the "Pacte pour le territoire" was signed in November 2018 for vocational training, local employment, heritage and property recovery and worker housing.
- Two further measures became operational in 2024: the "Reseau pour la Vallee de Suse" (Rete per la Valsusa), from an agreement between the Piedmont Region, Agenzia Piemonte Lavoro and TELT, for training young people and placing job-seekers, with work-study apprenticeships, supply-chain academies and advanced IT training; and "Valsusa Maison de l'Habitat", modelled on the French experience, a desk matching public and private property owners with firms working under Lyon-Turin subcontracts to house workers employed between Salbertrand and Susa.

wikis.title: Research, development and artificial intelligence
wikis.summary: TELT's research partnerships, benchmarking of comparable projects and its AI work towards a 'connected tunnel'.
wikis.body:
- Since 2015 TELT has signed numerous agreements with major European research institutes, building two kinds of partnership: commissioned studies on specific technical problems, and research projects in which TELT's own operation and organisation are the object of study.
- 16 research projects are active, representing an investment of about one million euros co-financing grants and doctorates, plus 15 partnerships with research institutes.
- Main research fields: large infrastructure, rail mobility, environment, workplace safety, new technologies, control and certification processes, and legal and economic matters.
- Partners are both French and Italian, among them the University and Polytechnic of Turin, Grenoble Ecole de Management and the University of Milan Bicocca.
- Benchmarking: TELT systematically analysed 72 rail, road and metro tunnel infrastructure projects on 5 continents and 11 international projects on the reuse of excavated soils in rail and road tunnels and hydroelectric pipelines on 3 continents, then formed partnerships with Rail Baltica, CERN, ITER, Links Foundation and the Societe des Grands Projets (formerly Societe du Grand Paris).
- AI: TELT has taken part since 2022 in Claire, a pan-European network of AI research laboratories, and works with Adra, the EU agency drafting the European AI Act policy, pursuing the objective of the "Tunnel connecte".

wikis.title: Excavation techniques
wikis.summary: The geology of the Mont-Cenis crossing and the mix of TBM and traditional excavation used.
wikis.body:
- The Mont-Cenis base tunnel crosses the French and Italian Alps in "l'un des systemes geologiques les plus complexes d'Europe", with granular soils (alluvial deposits) and rock formations (schists) requiring different works by geological domain.
- About 65 km of drill cores have been extracted and analysed, identifying 7 geological domains.
- Of the 164 km of galleries planned for the whole work (base tunnel, access adits and safety cross-passages), 60% will be dug by tunnel boring machine and 40% by traditional methods using explosives and rock breakers.
- Mechanised excavation uses custom-built TBMs that automate excavation, mucking and material transport.
- Traditional blasting is used in the most complex mountain stretches: holes are drilled, filled with explosives and fired, then the wall is consolidated with ribs and sprayed concrete, sometimes reinforced with steel bars.
- Where rock is weaker and explosives cannot be used, a rock breaker is used, with consolidation by ribs and concrete.

wikis.title: Underground worksites in progress (July 2026)
wikis.summary: The state of the five underground operational worksites - CO8, CO6/7, CO5a, CO5 and CO3/4 - and their contractor groupings.
wikis.body:
- Saint-Julien-Montdenis, base tunnel excavation towards Saint-Martin-la-Porte (CO8): excavation of the tunnel entrance began in December 2022 and continues over the 2.8 km stretch from the French portal, working from the Villard-Clement platform that previously hosted the cut-and-cover works. Excavation is traditional (rock breaker or explosives), with final lining of the already-dug segment under way; the site will finish with a cut-and-cover section joining the existing one and restoration of the area. Grouping: IMPLENIA Suisse (lead) / IMPLENIA France / NGE / ITINERA / RIZZANI de ECCHER.
- Saint-Martin-la-Porte and La Praz, base tunnel to Modane (CO6/7): excavation of 23.1 km of base tunnel from two working platforms, sections of both tubes under way by traditional method with final lining in parallel, plus logistics galleries linking the existing adit's cross-passages to the outside platform and to the technical caverns for TBM assembly. "Depuis la mi-septembre, le tunnelier Viviana a commence le creusement des 9 km de tunnel de base entre Saint-Martin-la-Porte et Modane"; progress is currently slower because the TBM faces "une configuration geologique particulierement complexe", and firms are working to cross this critical zone safely using the experience gained with the TBM Federica. The sector also includes the La Praz safety site, cross-passages every 333 metres, technical rooms, niches and operating and safety galleries. Total galleries to dig: 43.5 km, from the 17.5 km network already built between 2003 and 2022. Communes concerned: Saint-Martin-la-Porte, Saint-Michel-de-Maurienne, Orelle, Saint Andre, Villargondran, Saint-Julien-Montdenis. Grouping: VINCI Construction Grands Projets (lead) / Dodin Campenon Bernard / VINCI Construction France TP Lyon / WeBuild.
- Avrieux and Villarodin/Bourget, underground works and ventilation shafts (CO5a): four vertical parallel shafts 500 m long at 1,300 m altitude, 5.2 m in diameter, bored with Raise Boring Machines - pilot holes first, then a reamer raised to cut the shaft, with spoil falling to the shaft foot chamber and removed through the existing adit. Construction of the safety site tunnels and technical caverns, up to 22 m high and 23 m wide, is now finished; they will host assembly of the two TBMs that will then dig towards Italy. Grouping: VINCI Construction Grands Projets (lead) / DODIN CAMPENON BERNARD / CAMPENON BERNARD Centre Est / WeBuild / MASTER DRILLING Europe.
- Villarodin-Bourget/Modane, base tunnel Modane-Italy (CO5): since January 2025 the firms building the 22 km stretch between the existing Villarodin-Bourget/Modane adit and the Clarea site in Italy have been setting up. Digging will be by two TBMs towards Turin and traditional method (hydraulic rock breaker and/or explosives) towards Lyon; also the Modane safety site, cross-passages every 333 metres and the niches and transverse galleries needed for operation and safety. Communes: Villarodin-Bourget, Modane, Avrieux, Aussois. Grouping: EIFFAGE Genie Civil (lead) / SPIE BATIGNOLLES / GHELLA / COGEIS.
- Chiomonte, base tunnel worksite (CO3/4): the main Italian site of the cross-border section and, since 2012, a site of national strategic interest; it is the access point to the Italian base tunnel works. Firms must build both tubes up to the Susa entrance using two dual-mode TBMs able to change excavation mode with the ground. Preparations are under way to start traditional excavation of the Maddalena 2 tunnel and to receive the TBM that will dig the base tunnel. At peak "environ 700 personnes devraient etre employees sur ce chantier". Grouping: Itinera (lead), Ghella, Spie Batignolles.

wikis.title: Open-air worksites (July 2026)
wikis.summary: Surface works at Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne, San Didero, Salbertrand and the Susa plain.
wikis.body:
- Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne, rail interconnection (CO9): after the transitional multimodal hub entered service in June 2022 - replacing the old station during the works and itself later replaced by the definitive international station - interconnection works with the historic line are under way. Under an agreement with SNCF Reseau.
- San Didero, relocation of the Susa autoport: the new autoport between San Didero and Bruzolo is part of the definitive Lyon-Turin project and replaces the one at Susa, where the new international station is planned. It is being built by motorway concessionaire Sitaf under delegated project management through an agreement with TELT, on about 68,000 m2 between the A32 motorway and the "Mont-Cenis" national road 25. The project was approved by all competent bodies and minimises woodland use: interference concerns 0.5% of the woods of San Didero and Bruzolo and 0.08% of all woods on the valley floor around the Dora Riparia; areas not used will be restored. "Sa construction est quasiment terminee et des activites administratives sont en cours pour son ouverture."
- Salbertrand, materials recovery site (CO10): TELT has finished clearing materials abandoned over the years to free the area for sorting and recovering excavated material from the Italian side of the base tunnel, for reuse in structural concrete for tunnel linings and in road and rail embankments. A first removal phase ran between 2021 and 2022 and the last part of the site was cleaned in summer 2024, under prescription no. 9 of CIPE resolution no. 39 of 26 April 2018, updated by CIPESS resolution no. 3/2022. An environmental impact monitoring plan is active, with results shared with Arpa Piemonte and local stakeholders. Preparatory works are under way and in January 2026 the metal deck of the new bridge over the Dora Riparia linking the site to the A32 was put in place.
- Susa plain, preliminary activities for surface works: preliminary activities and land acquisition are under way for the progressive setting up of the planned worksite, covering both CO3/4 (base tunnel excavation emerging at Susa) and CO10 (excavated material management, using the former autoport area as temporary storage). Tenders are under way for the interconnection gallery with the historic Susa/Bussoleno line and for the open-air stretch leading to the base tunnel entrance at Susa.
- Two further worksites are dedicated to excavated-material recovery: CO10 in Italy and CO11 in France.

wikis.title: Completed works
wikis.summary: The list of structures the dossier records as finished, with their dates.
wikis.body:
- The Chiomonte geological gallery (Susa Valley, 7,020 m) was completed in 2017.
- The exchange niches inside the Maddalena 1 tunnel at Chiomonte were completed in November 2023.
- At Saint-Julien-Montdenis, the "tranchee couverte" - the artificial tunnel forming the base tunnel entrance - was completed in autumn 2021.
- Since mid-June 2022 the new PEM (Pole d'Echange Multimodal) has been in service at Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne; work had begun in 2019 and was carried out by SNCF Reseau with TELT. It will later be replaced by the definitive international station.
- At Saint-Martin-la-Porte, 9 km of base tunnel were dug with the TBM Federica, completed in 2019; a further 1.5 km was finished there in 2021 by traditional method.
- At Villargondran, bank reinforcement works along the Arc were finished in autumn 2021, protecting the Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne basin from flooding and preparing the platform for further infrastructure; work also adapted the Resses d'en Bas logistics site for part of the excavated-material management works.
- The Modane/Fournaux bypass, letting lorries and site vehicles avoid the town centre, was completed between 2024 and 2025.
- In January 2026 construction of the new interchange on the A32 motorway at Chiomonte was completed, allowing site machinery to move without affecting local traffic.
- Access galleries needed to start works inside the mountain were completed in 2007 at Villarodin-Bourget/Modane (4,000 m), 2009 at La Praz (2,480 m), 2010 at Saint-Martin-la-Porte (2,400 m) and 2016 at Saint-Martin-la-Porte (1,800 m).

wikis.title: As a Reincarnated Aristocrat, I'll Use My Appraisal Skill to Rise in the World
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Miraijin A's isekai light novel series, its Natsumi Inoue manga and its anime television adaptation, including the third season scheduled for September 2026.
wikis.body:
## The series

- A Japanese light novel series written by Miraijin A (転生貴族、鑑定スキルで成り上がる ...), listed under the genre isekai.
- Began on the Shōsetsuka ni Narō website on October 31, 2019; published in print by Kodansha with illustrations by Jimmy under Kodansha Ranobe Books from July 2, 2020. Nine volumes as of June 2026. Kodansha USA announced an English licence in March 2022.
- A manga adaptation illustrated by Natsumi Inoue began in Magazine Pocket on June 26, 2020; twenty-one tankōbon volumes as of June 2026. Kodansha USA licensed it in November 2021, first English volume September 2022.

## Plot

A Japanese salaryman dies and reincarnates as Ars Louvent, heir of a noble family, with the skill to appraise other people's talents and aptitudes. He recruits gifted retainers ahead of a war of succession, is promoted to Lord of Canarre, and goes to war with the neighbouring Duchy of Seitz. Main characters include Ritsu Muses, Charlotte Wraith, Rosell Kischa and Ars' fiancée Lysia Plaid (voiced by Kana Hanazawa).

## Anime

- Announced May 9, 2023. Directed by Takao Kato, music by Kujira Yumemi; broadcast on JNN (CBC, TBS), BS Nittere and AT-X on the Agaru Anime block. 24 episodes listed.
- Season 1: produced by Studio Mother, scripts by Yasuhiro Nakanishi, character designs by Yūko Yahiro; aired April 7 to June 23, 2024. Opening "Blue Days" by True, ending "Finally" by Kana Hanazawa. Streamed by Crunchyroll worldwide outside East Asia; Medialink for East and Southeast Asia on Ani-One Asia.
- Season 2: aired September 29 to December 22, 2024. Opening "SKILLAWAKE" by PassCode, ending "Familiar" by Yuki Tanaka.
- Season 3: produced by GeyeG Pictures, scheduled to premiere September 27, 2026 (the lead says "September 2026"); opening "Still Water" by Rico Sasaki, ending "Hibi o Koete" by Akuruyo no Hitsuji. The infobox credits Daisuke Ōhigashi with season 3 scripts.

## Reception

- The manga won the U-Next Prize at the 2021 Next Manga Award and ranked 18th in the web manga category.
- By November 2021 the web novel had been viewed more than 30 million times; by September 2024 the series had five million copies in circulation.
- Richard Eisenbeis (Anime News Network) called the anime's first episodes a "simple and predictable pattern" that improves once Lysia is introduced.

wikis.title: As a Reincarnated Aristocrat, I'll Use My Appraisal Skill to Rise in the World - series, characters and media
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Miraijin A's isekai light novel series and its manga and anime adaptations, with plot, characters, volume lists and the anime's three seasons.
wikis.body:
## The series

- "As a Reincarnated Aristocrat, I'll Use My Appraisal Skill to Rise in the World" (転生貴族、鑑定スキルで成り上がる ～弱小領地を受け継いだので、優秀な人材を増やしていたら、最強領地になってた～, Tensei Kizoku Kantei Sukiru de Nariagaru: Jakushō Ryōchi o Uketsuidanode, Yūshūna Jinzai o Fuyashite Itara, Saikyō Ryōchi ni Natteta) is a Japanese light novel series written by Miraijin A. Genre listed as isekai.
- It originated on the Shōsetsuka ni Narō website (original run October 31, 2019 – present) before being published in print with illustrations by Jimmy by Kodansha under the Kodansha Ranobe Books imprint from July 2, 2020. English publisher: Kodansha USA (NA). "As of June 2026, nine volumes have been released."
- Manga adaptation illustrated by Natsumi Inoue, serialized on Magazine Pocket from June 26, 2020; "As of June 2026, the manga's individual chapters have been collected into twenty-one tankōbon volumes."
- Anime television series directed by Takao Kato, written by Yasuhiro Nakanishi (S1-S2) and Daisuke Ōhigashi (S3), music by Kujira Yumemi; studios Studio Mother (S1-S2) and GeyeG Pictures (S3); licensed by Crunchyroll (streaming) and Medialink (East/Southeast Asia); networks JNN (CBC, TBS), BS Nittere, AT-X. Original run April 7, 2024 – present, 24 episodes.

## Plot

"A Japanese salaryman dies and reincarnates in another world as Ars Louvent, heir of a noble family and discovers that he also possesses the skill to appraise the talents and aptitudes of other people." He recruits people who excel in magic, swordsmanship, strategy and diplomacy as servants and allies before an imminent war for the throne's succession; he is promoted to Lord of Canarre and goes to war with the neighboring Duchy of Seitz against a wicked lord.

## Reception

- In the 2021 Next Manga Award, the manga won the U-Next Prize and ranked 18th in the web manga category.
- "By November 2021, the web novel had been viewed more than 30 million times."
- "By September 2024, the series had five million copies in circulation."
- Richard Eisenbeis wrote in Anime News Network that the anime's first episodes are "simple and predictable pattern", that the introduction of Lysia "breaks the pattern things get more interesting", and that Ars' reaction to Lysia's ability adds stakes and drama; he concluded the anime blends comedy and heartwarming moments, "highlighting the hope that one good leader can bring peace and prosperity to a failing empire".

## See also

- Sentenced to Be a Hero, a light novel series whose manga adaptation is also illustrated by Natsumi Inoue.

## Inconsistencies inside the page

- The lead image caption names the character "Ritsu Mouses", while the character section spells the name "Ritsu Muses" (リーツ・ミューセス, Rītsu Myūsesu).
- Mireille Grangeon's entry calls her "the older sister of Thomas Grunzeon, adviser of Valmarque", while the character named elsewhere is "Thomas Grangeon", "Vasmarque's right hand man and Mireille's brother".
- The manga volume table gives the same original ISBN 978-4-06-528664-7 for both volume 8 (August 9, 2022) and volume 10 (February 9, 2023).
- The infobox credits Daisuke Ōhigashi with season 3 scripts, while the Anime section names only Yasuhiro Nakanishi as scriptwriter.

wikis.title: Characters of As a Reincarnated Aristocrat
wikis.summary: The main and secondary characters listed in the article with their Japanese voice actors and roles.
wikis.body:
## Main

- Ars Louvent (アルス・ローベント) - voiced by Natsumi Fujiwara. Heir to House Louvent, which rules the town of Lamberk; the reincarnation of a Japanese salaryman, able to appraise others and measure their talents, and recruits notable individuals as retainers to bolster Lamberk's fighting force.
- Ritsu Muses (リーツ・ミューセス) - voiced by Taito Ban. An orphan from the Marca race who suffers discrimination; Ars' first retainer, and becomes commander of the Louvent army.
- Charlotte Wraith (シャーロット・レイス) - voiced by Narumi Kaho. An orphan Ars bought from slave traders; excels in magic and leads the Louvent magician platoon; sees Ars like a little brother.
- Rosell Kischa (ロセル・キーシャ) - voiced by Miho Okasaki. A child of the Louvent territory with a natural gift as a tactician; becomes the army's strategist.
- Lysia Plaid (リシア・プレイド) - voiced by Kana Hanazawa. Ars' fiancée, excelling in politics and diplomacy; Ars is wary of her high ambition stat but she falls in love with him and becomes his wife and closest confidant.
- Raven Louvent (レイヴン・ローベント) - voiced by Hiroki Tōchi. Head of House Louvent and Ars' father; dies of illness while Ars is a child.
- Mireille Grangeon (ミレーユ・グランジオン) - voiced by Hitomi Nabatame. A former noble who travelled the world drinking; discovered by the Shadows and recruited by Ars as strategist and tactician.
- Fahm (ファム) - voiced by Haruka Tomatsu. Leader of the mercenary band Shadow; looks and sounds like a girl but is a guy, usually posing as a waitress, and uses shadow magic to conceal himself. Later becomes Ars' retainer.

## Secondary

- Sofia Louvent (Ayako Kawasumi) - Ars' mother.
- Hammond Plaid (Kōzō Shioya) - Lysia's father and Ars' father-in-law.
- Kreiz Louvent (Chiharu Hokaze) - Ars' younger brother; Wren Louvent (Kanon Takao) - Ars' younger sister.
- Couran Saremakia (Kazuhiko Inoue) - oldest son of the late Duke of Missian, wins a war of succession with his brother with Ars' help; Lenge's father and Vasmarque's brother.
- Vasmarque Saremakia (Kenyu Horiuchi) - Couran's brother, challenges him for Missian and is executed after losing.
- Thomas Grangeon (Yasuhiro Mamiya) - Vasmarque's right-hand man and Mireille's brother; joins Ars' faction after the war.
- Lenge Saremakia (Sho Nogami) - son of Couran.
- Chacma Drees (Kōji Yusa).
- Selena Bandol (Yuki Tanaka) - daughter of Fraedor Bandol, a mage rivalling Charlotte; she and her father defect from Vasmarque to Ars.
- Ruper Louston (Tomoaki Maeno) - a lord forced to work for Vasmarque for the safety of his kidnapped pregnant wife; allies with Ars after the rescue.
- Clamant Maitrow III (Yuichi Nakamura) - leader of a mercenary company, on neither side, who helps Ars defeat Jean and Dan.
- Braham Joe (Shūichi Uchida) - an axe-wielding warrior who defects to Ars after losing to Ritsu and becomes his apprentice.
- Jean Tendry (Yūichirō Umehara) - lord of Castle Rolto and a Vasmarque ally who murdered his father; defeated by Clamant and surrenders.
- Dan Allest (Masashi Yamane) - Jean's right-hand man, evenly matched with Ritsu; defeated by Ritsu and surrenders.

wikis.title: Grand Theft Auto VI
wikis.summary: Wikipedia's article on Grand Theft Auto VI, Rockstar's upcoming game set in Leonida and scheduled for 19 November 2026, with its development, delays, marketing and the 2022 and 2026 leaks.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- The source is the English Wikipedia article on *Grand Theft Auto VI*, the upcoming Rockstar Games action-adventure game, covering gameplay, setting, development, release history, promotion, the 2022 and 2026 leaks, and awards. Part 1 is the article; parts 2 and 3 are its reference list, external links, navigation boxes and categories.

## Key facts
- Developed and published by Rockstar Games, the eighth main *Grand Theft Auto* game (sixteenth overall) after *Grand Theft Auto V* (2013); producer Rob Nelson, writers Rupert Humphries and Michael Wiafe, RAGE engine, single-player action-adventure.
- Release given as 19 November 2026 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, with "no Windows release scheduled as of September 2026" and 30 fps on both consoles at launch (confirmed August 2026). Physical copies, containing download codes rather than discs, are set for stores on 12 November.
- Release history: a 2025 window from the first trailer (December 2023), delayed in May 2025 to 26 May 2026, then in November 2025 to 19 November 2026 for additional polishing.
- Set in the fictional state of Leonida (based on Florida) with Vice City, Grassrivers and the Leonida Keys; the map is "reported to be three times larger than the playable area of *Red Dead Redemption 2*". Protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, "a Bonnie and Clyde-type narrative".
- Development: preliminary work from 2014, early development from late 2018, principal production from 2020 as *Project Americas*; teams more than doubled since *Red Dead Redemption 2*. Budget rumoured at US$1-2 billion, "though the figure remains unverified". Rockstar fired 34 employees in October 2025 over confidential information; the IWGB alleged union busting.
- Commerce: priced at $79.99; preorders opened 25 June 2026 with Take-Two calling sales "unprecedented and astonishing"; Newzoo estimated US$260 million in seven days and 37-51 million copies in the first week; DFC Intelligence projected $3.2 billion in first-year earnings. Rockstar says there will be no microtransactions at launch and no generative AI.
- Promotion: first trailer 5 December 2023 (leaked a day early), second trailer 6 May 2025 with "a record 475 million views across all platforms within 24 hours"; a Netflix "extended look" premiered 27 August 2026; *Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album*, 34 original songs, announced 17 September 2026.
- Leaks: the September 2022 "teapotuberhacker" breach (90 videos, 50 minutes of footage; a $5 million cost per Rockstar's court statement; a 17-year-old Lapsus$ member placed under an indefinite hospital order, moved to prison in July 2026 for a new trial in November) and the August 2026 "CyberLeek" leak of the map and footage, met with Take-Two subpoena requests to Discord, Microsoft and X Corp.
- Awards: Most Wanted / Most Anticipated Game at the Golden Joystick Awards and The Game Awards in 2024 and 2025, plus Best Game Trailer in 2025.

## Date wording
- The parts give no publication or last-updated date for the page; its footer carries only an oldid, and its dated items are maintenance tags and a September 2026 merge proposal.

wikis.title: Grand Theft Auto VI
wikis.summary: The Wikipedia article on Rockstar Games' upcoming Grand Theft Auto VI, covering its gameplay, Leonida setting, development, 19 November 2026 release, promotion, leaks and awards.
wikis.body:
## Game
- *Grand Theft Auto VI* is "an upcoming action-adventure game developed and published by Rockstar Games", due to be the eighth main *Grand Theft Auto* game after *Grand Theft Auto V* (2013) and the sixteenth entry overall.
- Infobox: developer and publisher Rockstar Games; producer Rob Nelson; artist Aaron Garbut; writers Rupert Humphries and Michael Wiafe; engine RAGE; platforms PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S; release 19 November 2026; genre action-adventure; mode single-player. A banner at the top labels it an "Upcoming video game" and dates it "2026 video game"; a merge proposal for *Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album* is marked "Proposed since September 2026".
- Set in the fictional US state of Leonida, based on Florida, following the criminal duo Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos in an open world that includes the Miami-inspired Vice City.

## Gameplay
- Single-player, third-person, playable as Jason or Lucia; fighting NPCs, stealing vehicles, robbing establishments, police chases; free-roam activities include skydiving, wrestling, basketball, exercising and scuba diving.
- Characters gain or lose weight, and staying awake for days shows on their faces. A "Criminal Profile" rating tracks each character's reputation, similar to *Red Dead Redemption 2*'s honour system; Rockstar says it tracks whether a character "keeps their crimes professional or commits unnecessary violence".
- Players can split the two characters up or play together; their relationship depends on the player's actions and, per Rockstar, "will be optional". A social media app, Snapmatic, returns from *Grand Theft Auto V* and parodies 2020s apps such as TikTok and Instagram. Appearance (hair, clothes, accessories) can be changed.

## Setting and characters
- The map "is reported to be three times larger than the playable area of *Red Dead Redemption 2*" and includes Vice City, Grassrivers and the Leonida Keys (inspired by Miami, the Everglades and the Florida Keys), plus Ambrosia, Mount Kalaga National Park and Port Gellhorn.
- The world parodies 2020s American culture: social media and influencer culture, law enforcement tactics and technology such as police body cameras, and memes such as Florida Man.
- Jason Duval worked for local drug runners in the Leonida Keys after serving in the Army; Lucia Caminos is called the series' first non-optional female protagonist, imprisoned at Leonida Penitentiary. A note records that several sources described Lucia as the series' first female protagonist, while *Grand Theft Auto* (1997), the Game Boy Color *Grand Theft Auto 2* (2000) and *Grand Theft Auto Online* (2013) had optional female playable characters (avatars without unique dialogue, and a mute protagonist).
- After a failed bank heist the duo encounter a state-wide conspiracy. Other characters: Cal Hampton, Boobie Ike, Dre'Quan Priest (Only Raw Records), Bae-Luxe and Roxy (Real Dimez), Raul Bautista and Brian Heder (Stephen Root).

## Development
- Preliminary work began in 2014 after *Grand Theft Auto V*; early development started in late 2018 after *Red Dead Redemption 2*; principal production began in 2020, code-named *Project Americas*.
- Worldwide development teams "more than doubled" since *Red Dead Redemption 2*; the studio avoided its standard crunch practices and jokes about marginalised groups. First main entry since the 1997 original not written by Dan Houser, who left Rockstar in 2020.
- Resources were reallocated from *Red Dead Online* and planned remasters in 2022; a note says remasters of *Grand Theft Auto IV* and *Red Dead Redemption* were paused after backlash to *The Trilogy - The Definitive Edition* (2021).
- "Rumours and analysts suggested the budget surpassed US$1-2 billion, which would make it the most expensive game ever developed, though the figure remains unverified."
- Rockstar required a return to offices from April 2024 "for productivity and security"; the IWGB criticised the change. In October 2025 Rockstar fired 34 employees (a note: 31 from Rockstar North, 3 from Rockstar Toronto) over "public discussion and distribution of confidential information"; the IWGB accused Rockstar of union busting.

## Research and design
- Rob Nelson, Rockstar North's head of development and co-studio head, said internal pressure exceeded external. Rupert Humphries, senior VP of narrative, described "a Bonnie and Clyde-type narrative".
- A dedicated research team was based in Miami; Nelson said "Florida and Miami have perhaps one of the most diverse and interesting populations in the world". Field trips met law enforcement, club promoters, former criminals and gun dealers.
- Senior art director for characters Jamie-Lee Lloyd on cross-referencing journalism and books; writer Michael Wiafe on "a sense of discovery"; the team liked Miami bass, Kodak Black and Sexyy Red.
- A Los Angeles team works mostly on NPCs; the vehicle handling team includes race-car drivers. More than 50 street artists were engaged for in-game murals, including Stockyard (based on Wynwood). Stu Petri, VP of 2D/UI design, wanted in-game brands to "reflect the aspirations, aesthetics, and lifestyles". Miami stylist Jillian Carr worked from 2023 on a "fashion ecosystem"; "Vice City is built around vanity".

## Release
- Planned for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and Series S, "with no Windows release scheduled as of September 2026". In August 2026 Rockstar confirmed 30 frames per second on both consoles at launch.
- The first trailer in December 2023 gave a 2025 release window; after March 2024 delay reports Take-Two said it remained on schedule for late 2025; in May 2025 it was delayed to 26 May 2026; in November 2025, the week after the 34 firings, Rockstar delayed it to 19 November 2026 for "additional polishing". Journalists noted the firings did not cause the delay; a Rockstar North employee said morale was "at rock bottom".
- Rockstar confirmed development was "well underway" on 4 February 2022.
- Price: "it was ultimately priced at $79.99" (some industry figures hoped for more than the standard US$70). Analyst projections in notes: Niko Partners estimated first-day sell-through over US$1.2 billion; DFC Intelligence projected first-year earnings of $3.2 billion (40 million copies) including $1 billion in preorders; Circana predicted a record-spending market "rebound".
- Awards for anticipation: Golden Joystick Awards and The Game Awards in both 2024 and 2025.

## Promotion
- The first trailer was announced for December 2023, Rockstar's 25th anniversary; a low-quality version leaked a day early on 4 December and Rockstar published the official version, revealing title, protagonists, setting, release window and consoles.
- Trailer records as the page states them: broke the record for most first-day views on a non-music YouTube video within 12 hours with 46 million; third-most first-day views overall with 93 million; most-liked game trailer with 8.9 million likes in 24 hours; second-most-viewed game trailer by January 2024 with 168 million views; second-most-viewed trailer ever by November 2025 with 268 million; surpassed the lifetime views of *Grand Theft Auto V*'s 2011 reveal trailer within two days with 101 million.
- Tom Petty's "Love Is a Long Road" (near-37,000% increase in Spotify streams, almost 250,000 Shazam searches, second on the worldwide iTunes chart) featured in the first trailer.
- Second trailer released 6 May 2025 with a website update of 70 screenshots; recorded on PlayStation 5; songs include the Pointer Sisters' "Hot Together" (182,000% Spotify increase), Wang Chung's "Everybody Have Fun Tonight", "Child Support" by Zenglen and Tammy Wynette's "Talkin' to Myself Again". It took "a record 475 million views across all platforms within 24 hours", surpassing *Deadpool & Wolverine*'s 365 million, and was itself surpassed in March 2026 by *Spider-Man: Brand New Day* (over 500 million in 12 hours, 718.6 million in 24). It won Best Game Trailer at the 2025 Golden Joystick Awards.
- Cover art and special editions unveiled 18 June 2026: an Ultimate Edition with extra clothing, hairstyles, locations, missions, tattoos, vehicles and weapons, and a preorder Vintage Vice City Pack. Rockstar confirmed to Kinda Funny there would be no microtransactions at launch and no generative AI in the game.
- Physical versions contain download codes instead of discs "to prevent leaks and reselling", in stores on 12 November, allowing pre-loading a week before the game unlocks; players and journalists criticised edition-locked content and the lack of discs, and some retailers refused to stock the game.
- Preorders opened 25 June; Take-Two called sales "unprecedented and astonishing" without sharing figures; Newzoo estimated a record US$260 million in seven days and 37-51 million copies ($3.3-4.5 billion) in the first week; Sensor Tower estimated 89% of preorders were for the Ultimate Edition.
- Marketing partners included Netflix, Inc. and PlayStation; *Dazed* ran a cover story published online 26 August; an "extended look" premiered on Netflix on 27 August ahead of YouTube, with Netflix and Twitch hitting technical issues from demand; Miami-Dade County pitched extending the campaign across Miami.
- On 17 September 2026 Rockstar announced *Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album*, a soundtrack of 34 original songs.

## Leaks
- **2022 "teapotuberhacker"**: 90 videos with 50 minutes of work-in-progress footage were posted to GTAForums on 18 September 2022, downloaded from Rockstar's internal Slack; the hacker threatened to publish source code, assets and internal builds. Rockstar said in court the incident cost $5 million and thousands of staff hours. A 17-year-old from Oxfordshire, a key member of Lapsus$, was arrested by City of London Police on 22 September; he had breached Rockstar while on bail using a phone, television and Fire TV Stick. He was tried at Southwark Crown Court in mid-2023 for twelve offences, deemed unfit to stand trial due to his autism, found by a jury to have committed the acts, and placed under an indefinite hospital order in December; he was moved to a prison in July 2026 to await a new trial in November.
- **2026 "CyberLeek"**: leaked the in-game map and several minutes of footage in August 2026, demanding changes to edition-only content and the lack of discs; a "$CYBERLEEK" meme coin watermark raised scam concerns, and CyberLeek burned coins valued at more than US$1 million. At least sixteen videos leaked over nine days by 26 August, with paid-token voting on what leaked next; some footage raised concerns about a graphical downgrade. Take-Two filed subpoena requests with Discord, Microsoft and X Corp. in the US District Court for the Southern District of New York. Rockstar acknowledged the leaks on 26 August, calling them "heartbreaking for our team". On 27 August media reported CyberLeek had withdrawn roughly $268,000 in transaction fees to four crypto wallets hours before the Netflix reveal, collapsing the coin's value.
- **Other**: in January 2025 a Reddit user posted a photo and two videos of a PS5 dev kit running the game, filmed at Rockstar San Diego in mid-2021; Polygon's Ian Walker called it the "worst leak of all time". The leaks were referenced in the second trailer ("just fixing some leaks"). In November development footage appeared in a former Rockstar animator's showreel.

## Accolades
- 2024: Golden Joystick Awards Most Wanted Game (won); The Game Awards 2024 Most Anticipated Game (won).
- 2025: Golden Joystick Awards Best Game Trailer (won) and Most Wanted Game (won); The Game Awards 2025 Most Anticipated Game (won).

wikis.title: Dominion: Prequel to the Exorcist (2005 film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Paul Schrader's shelved-then-released Exorcist prequel Dominion, covering its plot, cast, the production history it shares with Exorcist: The Beginning, its improvised post-production, limited release and mixed reviews.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- "Dominion: Prequel to the Exorcist is a 2005 American supernatural horror film directed by Paul Schrader and written by William Wisher Jr. and Caleb Carr. The film serves as an alternative prequel to The Exorcist (1973) and is the fifth installment in The Exorcist series. It was intended to be the official prequel to The Exorcist before it was retooled into Exorcist: The Beginning (2004), as Morgan Creek Productions executives feared the already completed film would be unsuccessful."
- Stars Stellan Skarsgård, Clara Bellar, Gabriel Mann and Billy Crawford.
- "Dominion: Prequel to the Exorcist received a limited release in the United States on May 20, 2005, by Warner Bros. Pictures, after Exorcist: The Beginning became a financial and critical failure. The film received highly mixed reviews from critics, but was generally deemed an improvement over its earlier version."
- Infobox: based on characters by William Peter Blatty; produced by James G. Robinson; cinematography Vittorio Storaro; edited by Tim Silano; music by Trevor Rabin, Angelo Badalamenti and Dog Fashion Disco; production company Morgan Creek Productions; distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures; release dates March 18, 2005 (BIFFF) and May 20, 2005 (United States); running time 116 minutes; budget $30 million; box office $251,495.

## Plot (as summarised by the article)

In 1944 an SS lieutenant, Kessel, forces Father Lankester Merrin, parish priest of a village in occupied Holland, to take part in arbitrary executions in exchange for sparing the village. In 1947 Merrin, his faith shattered, is an archaeologist at Derati in the Turkana region of British Kenya, excavating "a Byzantine church built around the 5th century—long before Christianity had reached that region of Africa". With Father Francis, Major Granville, the guide Chuma, the doctor Rachel Lesno and the convert Emekwi, he finds the church pristine, "as though it had been deliberately buried immediately after its construction was completed", and beneath it a crypt with a demonic idol where human sacrifice was performed. Merrin takes the disabled outcast Cheche to Rachel for treatment. Two British soldiers looting the church are found dead, one beheaded, one crucified head downward; Granville blames the Turkana and shoots a young woman. The warrior Jomo slaughters the mission school students before being shot. Francis realises Cheche's recovery is not a miracle and plans a baptism at the church; Granville shoots himself. The demon in Cheche attacks the baptism; an earthquake seals the church. Francis is found tied to a tree, shot with arrows, and begs Merrin to perform an exorcism. Merrin finds the possessed Cheche below; the demon offers to rewrite his past, and in the hallucination his refusal gets him and all the villagers killed. As an aurora appears the demon's influence drives Rachel to attempt suicide, Emekwi to beat his wife and the Turkana to charge the British. "The exorcism eventually succeeds and the demon leaves Cheche's body, causing him to regress to his former condition." An elder warns the demon will pursue Merrin, who leaves for Rome with his faith regained.

## Cast

Stellan Skarsgård as Father Lankester Merrin; Gabriel Mann as Father Francis; Clara Bellar as Rachel Lesno; Billy Crawford as Cheche; Ralph Brown as Sergeant Major; Israel Aduramo as Jomo; Andrew French as Chuma; Antonie Kamerling as Kessel; Julian Wadham as Major Granville; Eddie Osei as Emekwi; Rick Warden as Corporal Williams; Mary Beth Hurt as Pazuzu (uncredited).

## Production

- "Producer James G. Robinson first began development on an untitled prequel to The Exorcist (1973) in 1997, with the first draft of the screenplay penned by William Wisher Jr." Tom McLoughlin was hired in October 1999 and departed over script issues; in October 2001 John Frankenheimer was reported aboard with a Caleb Carr revision and Liam Neeson attached as Merrin; Frankenheimer stepped down over declining health and was replaced by Schrader.
- Gabriel Mann joined in April 2002; the film was titled Exorcist: The Beginning the next month, with Skarsgård replacing Neeson and Billy Crawford cast.
- "Principal photography on Schrader's film began on November 11, 2002 in Morocco with Vittorio Storaro handling cinematography duties." Six weeks in Morocco, two months in Rome; "By the time filming had wrapped in February 2003, six writers had contributed to the screenplay and the budget had nearly doubled."
- "An early cut of Schrader's film that ran at 130 minutes was shown to the studio in early 2003. The cut was widely derided due to a lack of scares and gore." Schrader opposed re-editing, said he faithfully adapted Carr's screenplay and that the studio had "buyer's remorse". Sheldon Kahn re-cut the film without him; Schrader was "livid". "Carr was expected for rewrites, but instead the studio opted to fire Schrader and scrap the film entirely in August 2003."
- Renny Harlin was hired after proposing a rewrite, new cast and more action; revisions were by Carr, Skip Woods, Alexi Hawley and Harlin. Skarsgård and Julian Wadham were the only cast retained. Harlin's shoot began in winter 2003 in Rome and ran twelve weeks.
- "In April 2004, Warner Home Video began to consider releasing Schrader's film direct to video. With a budget upward of $90 million, Exorcist: The Beginning opened on August 20, 2004 and underperformed at the box office and was critically panned." Schrader saw it on opening weekend with Blatty and told The Independent: "This is really bad. If it stays this bad, I bet there's a chance I can get mine resurrected".
- "In September 2004, Morgan Creek began discussions with Schrader on possibly giving his version a limited theatrical release in 2005." Editor Tim Silano insisted Schrader be brought back to oversee his own material. "Morgan Creek allocated $35,000 and a very short amount of time for Schrader to finish his version."
- The small budget forced compromises: no money for ADR, no return of Storaro for colour timing (Schrader and Silano approximated it), and no full original score. "the score was developed piecemeal, with fourteen minutes (including a central theme) being composed without payment by Angelo Badalamenti. The final twenty minutes of the film were scored by the American metal band Dog Fashion Disco (the unusual choice stemming from Schrader's son Sam's affection for the group), while the balance of the score - about an hour's worth - was recycled from Trevor Rabin's work for the Harlin version." Dog Fashion Disco also "finessed" the whole score for unity.
- "In March 2005, after a private screening in New York, the film was titled Paul Schrader's Exorcist: The Original Prequel. Other working titles at that time included Exorcist IV, and Dark Angel. By April, the film was officially titled Dominion."

## Release and box office

- Limited theatrical release on May 20, 2005 in the United States by Warner Bros. Pictures. "In the United States, the film grossed $251,495."

## Reception

- Blatty called Dominion "a handsome, classy, elegant piece of work"; "critical reaction to the film was mixed."
- Rotten Tomatoes: 29% from 45 reviews, average 4.7/10; consensus: "While director Schrader's attempt at a literate, internal exposition on evil temptations and human sin is admirable, this prequel suffers from hit-and-miss psychological tension, poor visual effects, and weak writing -- an overambitious failure of a horror movie." Metacritic: 55 of 100 from 16 reviews, "mixed or average". By comparison Exorcist: The Beginning holds 11% on Rotten Tomatoes and 30 on Metacritic.
- Roger Ebert gave three of four stars, writing that it "does something risky and daring in this time of jaded horror movies: it takes evil seriously". Leslie Felperin (Variety) called it "intelligent, quietly subversive" and said "Schrader has delivered a 100% Paul Schrader film, drenched in the spiritual and moral angst that's watermarked his career from Taxi Driver (as a writer) to Auto Focus (as a director)".
- Owen Gleiberman (Entertainment Weekly): "Schrader's film is a notch better than Harlin's, but when you boil out the demon feathers, it's the same damn movie". Scott Tobias (The A.V. Club) praised "a quietly mesmerizing performance" from Skarsgård and said it "takes demon possession out of head-spinning literalism".
- David Edelstein (Slate): "a good, thoughtful horror picture—and thiiis close to being a very good one." Brent Simon (IGN) scored it 4 out of 10: "The overall feeling Dominion gives off is one of rootless languor... It's not blood or gore that's missing, its context; Dominion is too polite and urbane to frighten".
- Director Erik Kristopher Myers, "the first to ever review the film in 2005", wrote that Schrader's film "is the first to synthesize the elements of each one... and presents us with an Exorcist that owes as much to Friedkin as it does to Boorman and Blatty."

## Home media

- "The film was released on DVD and VHS October 25, 2005 by Warner Home Video and included deleted scenes, photo gallery, and an audio commentary by Schrader."
- "On October 10, 2006, the film was released with The Exorcist (and its extended cut, The Exorcist: The Version You've Never Seen), Exorcist II: The Heretic, The Exorcist III and Exorcist: The Beginning in a box set titled The Exorcist: The Complete Anthology, with a Blu-ray version releasing on September 23, 2014. It was also released in a standalone Blu-ray by Sony Pictures Home Entertainment on October 13, 2020."

wikis.title: 2026-27 NBA season
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the upcoming 81st NBA season: schedule, retirements and draft, coaching changes, preseason and international games, the NBA Cup, uniform changes, national and local media deals and the Clippers salary cap punishments.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- "The 2026-27 NBA season is the upcoming 81st season of the National Basketball Association (NBA)." 30 teams, 82 games.
- Regular season scheduled from October 20, 2026 to April 11, 2027; the fourth edition of the in-season NBA Cup from October 30 to December 11, 2026; play-in tournament April 13-16, 2027; playoffs April-May 2027; Finals June 2027.
- The 2027 NBA All-Star Game is scheduled for February 21, 2027 at the Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, Arizona.
- Infobox TV partners: ESPN/ABC, NBC/NBCSN, NBA TV; streaming partners ESPN app/Disney+, Peacock, Amazon Prime Video.
- Top draft pick: AJ Dybantsa, picked by the Washington Wizards.
- The NBA released the regular-season schedule on August 13, "with select games announced in advance of the full schedule release."

## International media and radio (not in the topic pages above)
- Prime Video will stream 20 additional regular-season games in Mexico, Brazil, France, Italy, Spain, Germany, the United Kingdom and Ireland and, beginning this season, Canada, plus a conference final and the NBA Finals in six of the 11 years of the deal.
- ESPN airs its slate in Latin America, sub-Saharan Africa, Oceania and the Netherlands, and via Disney+ in select Asian and European markets. NBC airs its slate on Sky Sports in the UK and Italy and distributes games in the Caribbean and sub-Saharan Africa. TNT Sports airs games in Poland, Denmark, Finland, Norway, Sweden and Latin America (excluding Brazil and Mexico). NBA TV international airs games in select countries.
- Radio: ESPN Radio has select regular-season games, all playoff games and the NBA Finals; this is the seventh season of the league's multi-year deal with SiriusXM and SiriusXM Canada simulcasting all 30 teams' local broadcasts.

## Notable occurrences
- "On September 2, the NBA announced punishments related to the Los Angeles Clippers salary cap scandal. The Clippers were stripped of five first-round picks, one each from 2029 to 2033, given a $30 million fine, and owner Steve Ballmer was suspended from league and team activities for one year. Kawhi Leonard was required to pay the league $700,000, and two executives were also suspended without pay."

wikis.title: Retirements, draft and free agency
wikis.summary: The off-season retirements noted by the article, the 2026 draft and the free agency calendar.
wikis.body:
- July 4, 2026: Garrett Temple was hired as an assistant coach for the Dallas Mavericks; "He played for 12 teams over a 17-year career."
- July 7, 2026: Kyle Lowry announced his retirement after 20 NBA seasons, an NBA champion with the Toronto Raptors in 2019 and "the last active player from the 2006 NBA draft".
- August 12, 2026: Russell Westbrook announced his retirement after 18 seasons, having reached the NBA Finals with the Oklahoma City Thunder in 2012 and won the NBA Most Valuable Player award in 2017.
- The 2026 NBA draft took place on June 23-24 at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York.
- Free agency negotiations began June 30 at 6 p.m. ET; players may be signed after the July moratorium on July 6 at 12:00 p.m. ET.

wikis.title: Coaching changes
wikis.summary: The six head-coaching changes and the dates of each departure and hire.
wikis.body:
- Chicago Bulls: Billy Donovan to Tiago Splitter. Dallas Mavericks: Jason Kidd to Dusty May. Milwaukee Bucks: Doc Rivers to Taylor Jenkins. New Orleans Pelicans: James Borrego (interim) to Jamahl Mosley. Orlando Magic: Jamahl Mosley to Sean Sweeney. Portland Trail Blazers: Tiago Splitter (interim) to Micah Nori.
- April 13, 2026: Doc Rivers resigned as head coach of the Milwaukee Bucks.
- April 21, 2026: Billy Donovan stepped down as the Chicago Bulls' head coach.
- April 30, 2026: the Bucks hired Taylor Jenkins.
- May 4, 2026: the Orlando Magic fired Jamahl Mosley after five seasons.
- May 18, 2026: the New Orleans Pelicans hired Jamahl Mosley.
- May 19, 2026: the Dallas Mavericks and Jason Kidd "mutually agreed to part ways".
- June 1, 2026: the Magic hired Sean Sweeney. June 16, 2026: the Bulls hired Tiago Splitter. June 23, 2026: the Trail Blazers hired Micah Nori and the Mavericks hired Dusty May.

- Listed Global Games: NBA Mexico City Game 2026 on November 7, Denver Nuggets vs Indiana Pacers at Mexico City Arena; NBA Paris Game 2027 on January 14, New Orleans Pelicans vs San Antonio Spurs at Accor Arena; NBA Manchester Game 2027 on January 17, San Antonio Spurs vs New Orleans Pelicans at Co-op Live. Winners listed as TBD.

wikis.title: 2026 NBA Cup format
wikis.summary: The in-season tournament's structure and the move of the championship game to Hinkle Fieldhouse.
wikis.body:
- The NBA Cup "is expected to have the same basic structure as previous seasons": all games except the championship final count toward the regular-season standings; six intraconference pools of five (three per conference); group games against each other pool team (two home, two away) on Fridays and other select days in November; pool winners plus two wild cards (one per conference) advance to a single-elimination tournament in early December.
- Only 80 regular-season games per team are initially announced in the offseason; the first two tournament rounds count as games 81 and 82, and the championship game is "an extra 83rd game that does not count toward the regular season". Teams eliminated earlier are scheduled additional games against other eliminated teams in the same conference to reach 82.
- The semifinals move to the home arenas of the higher-seeded teams in each conference.
- "The championship game for this edition will be held at Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, Indiana as part of a new vision to host the game at more distinct and iconic basketball arenas", replacing T-Mobile Arena in Paradise, Nevada, which hosted the first three editions.

wikis.title: Uniform and logo changes
wikis.summary: New looks unveiled by the Houston Rockets and Minnesota Timberwolves.
wikis.body:
- The Houston Rockets unveiled new uniforms "resembling the 'ketchup and mustard' look that was used during their back-to-back championships in 1994 and 1995". The "R" logo remains the primary mark, "but with an added yellow accent to reflect its reintroduction into the Rockets' color scheme".
- The Minnesota Timberwolves unveiled a new logo and uniforms: the logo resembles their 2017 mark but in a colour scheme similar to the one used from the franchise's inception in 1989 until 1996; the Icon and Association uniforms resemble the original look and the Statement uniform resembles their black uniforms from the Kevin Garnett era.

wikis.title: National television, streaming and postseason coverage
wikis.summary: The second season of the 11-year ESPN, NBC, Amazon and NBA TV deals and how the schedule and playoffs are split.
wikis.body:
- "This will be the second season of 11-year deals with the ESPN family of networks, NBC Sports, Amazon Prime Video and NBA TV."
- ESPN primarily carries Wednesday night games and the NBA All-Star Celebrity Game, and produces NBA Saturday Primetime and NBA Sunday Showcase on ABC, five ESPN/ABC simulcasts on Christmas Day and the primetime doubleheader on the final night of the regular season; ESPN-only games remain non-exclusive alongside regional broadcasts. Its schedule adds a Thursday doubleheader in opening week, an NBA Cup group stage tripleheader on November 25, select Friday games January-March, a Saturday west coast game on March 13 and an Easter Sunday doubleheader on March 28. On April 11 two games with playoff implications will be flexed into an ESPN primetime doubleheader.
- NBA Saturday Primetime on ABC runs seven select weeks between December and March including a quadruple header on January 30; NBA Sunday Showcase is doubleheaders on three consecutive weekends in late February and March, "partly due to ABC carrying Super Bowl LXI in mid-February, airing the NFL's championship game for the first time since 2006". ABC will also air a Sunday doubleheader on the day of the Academy Awards for the first time since 2007, at 12 and 2:30 p.m. ET leading into the 99th Academy Awards.
- NBC keeps opening night games, Coast 2 Coast Tuesday doubleheaders, late-season Sunday Night Basketball, Martin Luther King Jr. Day games and the All-Star Game; "11 more games will air on broadcast television" than the prior season. Opening night NBA Tip-Off expands to a tripleheader for the first time. NBC formalised its late-December doubleheaders as Holiday Hoops on December 22, 28 and 29. Sunday Night Basketball expands to 16 games, adding two weeks of standalone January games airing against the NFL playoffs. Daytime tripleheaders are scheduled on MLK Day and Presidents' Day. NBCSN is the overflow channel and simulcasts Peacock telecasts; Telemundo has Spanish-language broadcasts of 10 Sunday Night Basketball games and the All-Star Game.
- NBA TV televises select games when other broadcasters are not airing, including the Mexico City Global Game.
- Streaming: Amazon Prime Video keeps Friday night doubleheaders (including most NBA Cup group stage nights, one leading out its Black Friday Football game on November 27), late-season Thursday and Saturday afternoon games, "the entire knockout round of the NBA Cup and both European Global games"; with Christmas Day on a Friday in 2026 its doubleheader that week moves to Wednesday, December 23, and its Thursday schedule starts with a New Year's Eve afternoon game before the Thursday Night Football finale. The ESPN app's Unlimited plan streams all ESPN-produced games, with select games on the Select plan or Disney+. Peacock simulcasts all NBC network games plus Monday night games most weeks. NBA League Pass continues to offer out-of-market games and live NBA TV.
- Postseason: Amazon streams all play-in games; the first two playoff rounds are split between Amazon (9-17 first-round and 5-9 second-round games), ESPN/ABC (about 18 games across the two rounds) and NBC/Peacock (15-23 first-round and 7-11 second-round games, at least half on NBC). By rotation ESPN/ABC airs the Western Conference Finals and Amazon exclusively streams the Eastern Conference Finals; "ABC will exclusively air the NBA Finals for its 25th consecutive season."

wikis.title: Local rights after FanDuel Sports Network
wikis.summary: How the 13 affected teams replaced FanDuel Sports Network, and the league's proposed streaming hub.
wikis.body:
- "FanDuel Sports Network wound down operations after the 2025-26 season, impacting 13 teams." DAZN and FuboTV both expressed interest in acquiring rights, though Fubo pulled its offers as not "fiscally prudent".
- Detroit Pistons: multi-year agreement with Scripps Sports for broadcast television and a DTC service, flagship WMYD.
- Miami Heat: signed with BH Media's WPLG, streaming on the Local 10+ Platinum app.
- Milwaukee Bucks: signed with Good Karma Sports (owner of radio partner WTMJ), flagship Rincon's WVTV-DT2, which "had last carried Bucks games in 1993-94".
- Atlanta Hawks: multi-year agreement with Gray Media for WANF in Atlanta and Peachtree Sports Network statewide.
- Minnesota Timberwolves, Indiana Pacers, Cleveland Cavaliers and San Antonio Spurs: exclusive regional deals with DAZN, streaming on branded subscription services; Cavaliers broadcasts produced by Rock Entertainment Sports Network. Free packages: 15 games each for the Timberwolves and Cavaliers, 22 for the Pacers; 15 Pacers games, the 15 Cavaliers games and 22 Spurs games also simulcast on broadcast TV. The Spurs' subscription includes Austin Spurs and San Antonio FC content.
- Charlotte Hornets and Orlando Magic: signed with Cox Media Group, flagships WAXN-TV and WRDQ with selected games on WSOC-TV and WFTV; the Magic will host a DTC service on DAZN.
- Oklahoma City Thunder: agreement with Griffin Media for the "Thunder Gameday Network", mostly on cable-exclusive feeds of KSBI and KQCW with ten free-to-air games (six on KSBI/KQCW, four on KWTV and KOTV), plus a "Thunder+" DTC service housed within the NBA app.
- The NBA "has reportedly explored the possibility of building a 'streaming hub' to centralize in-market digital rights", with discussions reported with Amazon, DAZN, ESPN and YouTube TV; some teams signed short-term deals or included exit clauses to join it.
- May 2026: Gray Media renewed with the Phoenix Suns through 2030, taking over digital rights and launching an Arizona's Family Sports app. July 2026: DAZN became the DTC platform for MSG Network and YES Network (Knicks and Nets), replacing the Gotham Sports App, and will offer Monumental+ as an add-on after acquiring ViewLift Media from Ted Leonsis.

wikis.title: Nike unveils the Caitlin 1, Caitlin Clark's first signature shoe, with six 2026 colourways
wikis.summary: Sneaker Freaker article on Nike's reveal of the Caitlin 1 signature basketball shoe, its technology and design details, Clark's quotes and the six colourways' release dates and style codes.
wikis.body:
## The reveal

- Nike revealed the full set of **Caitlin 1** sneakers "to land across the next few months" — the "inaugural six-stack of Caitlin 1s".
- Caitlin Clark signed "the richest deal ever negotiated for a women's hooper" shortly after becoming **2024's number one draft pick**. Her contract with Nike included a signature shoe.
- Clark "spent at least two years rocking Kobe Protro models on the hardwood before finally announcing the Caitlin 1 in **July of this year**", and has been teasing colourways since.
- She plays for the **Indiana Fever**.

## Clark's quotes

- "We're trying to make the best shoe there's ever been. It checks every box."
- "I hope every boy and girl put this shoe on and hope that they can have a signature one day, or that they can go on the court and make 35-foot threes. I hope this gives them that sense of belief and that sense of confidence to achieve whatever they want to."
- "A lot of thought and time has gone into this shoe. I never thought I would have my own signature shoe, and now that I do, it's pretty special. I can't wait to share this moment with so many people."

## Technology

- A brand-new upper called **Nike Opticast**, "which brings lightness and locked support".
- An "inventive cast polyurethane node system" spread across various heights of the build, designed to diminish drag and boost energy efficiency.
- An **Air Zoom Turbo** unit in the forefoot with a **Cushlon** midsole.
- A full range of youth sizing, "not just shrunken versions of the adult pairs" but redesigned for kids' play to enhance range of motion and flexibility.

## Design details

- Nike Opticast nodes assemble a series of Cs on the lateral panel; the medial features a pattern tessellating the number **2**, Clark's jersey number.
- The tongue carries Clark's signature logo.
- The sockliner has a cement-inspired look, "a nod to the court in the driveway of Clark's childhood home".
- The outsole carries the lines "Shoot More Threes", "From Anywhere" and "It Was Never a Long Shot."

## Release calendar (six colourways for the rest of 2026)

| Colourway | Release date | Style code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Caitlin Blue | 01 Oct 26 | IH7423-400 |
| Warning Code | 01 Oct 26 | IH7423-700 |
| Midnight Fever | 14 Oct 26 | IH7423-600 |
| Cave Stone | 03 Nov 26 | IH7423-101 |
| Ice Cold | 24 Nov 26 | IH7423-100 |
| Purple Venom | 12 Dec 26 | IH7423-500 |

- "Where to buy" links: Nike and Dick's Sporting Goods for Caitlin Blue; Nike for the rest.
- Article by Zoë Radas, dated 15 Sep 26, filed under Releases / Basketball.
