wikis.title: NVIDIA Rubin platform launch (six new chips)
wikis.summary: NVIDIA newsroom press release from CES announcing the Rubin AI platform — six new chips, the Vera Rubin NVL72 and HGX Rubin NVL8 systems, new storage and Ethernet products, partner quotes and availability.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- Headline: "NVIDIA Kicks Off the Next Generation of AI With Rubin — Six New Chips, One Incredible AI Supercomputer", subtitled "Extreme Codesign Across NVIDIA Vera CPU, Rubin GPU, NVLink 6 Switch, ConnectX-9 SuperNIC, BlueField-4 DPU and Spectrum-6 Ethernet Switch Slashes Training Time and Inference Token Generation Cost". Dated January 5, 2026, datelined "CES".
- News summary bullets: up to "10x reduction in inference token cost and 4x reduction in number of GPUs to train MoE models, compared with the NVIDIA Blackwell platform"; Spectrum-X Ethernet Photonics switch systems deliver "5x improved power efficiency and uptime"; a new NVIDIA Inference Context Memory Storage Platform with BlueField-4 "to accelerate agentic AI reasoning"; "Microsoft’s next-generation Fairwater AI superfactories — featuring NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale systems — will scale to hundreds of thousands of NVIDIA Vera Rubin Superchips"; "CoreWeave among first to offer NVIDIA Rubin"; an expanded Red Hat collaboration.
- Jensen Huang, founder and CEO: "Rubin arrives at exactly the right moment, as AI computing demand for both training and inference is going through the roof... With our annual cadence of delivering a new generation of AI supercomputers — and extreme codesign across six new chips — Rubin takes a giant leap toward the next frontier of AI."
- "Named for Vera Florence Cooper Rubin — the trailblazing American astronomer... — the Rubin platform features the NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale solution and the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 system."
- The six chips: NVIDIA Vera CPU, Rubin GPU, NVLink 6 Switch, ConnectX-9 SuperNIC, BlueField-4 DPU and Spectrum-6 Ethernet Switch. The five innovations are "the latest generations of NVIDIA NVLink interconnect technology, Transformer Engine, Confidential Computing and RAS Engine, as well as the NVIDIA Vera CPU."

## Ecosystem

- Expected adopters: "Amazon Web Services (AWS), Anthropic, Black Forest Labs, Cisco, Cohere, CoreWeave, Cursor, Dell Technologies, Google, Harvey, HPE, Lambda, Lenovo, Meta, Microsoft, Mistral AI, Nebius, Nscale, OpenAI, OpenEvidence, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), Perplexity, Runway, Supermicro, Thinking Machines Lab and xAI."
- Quotes from Sam Altman ("Intelligence scales with compute..."), Dario Amodei ("The efficiency gains in the NVIDIA Rubin platform represent the kind of infrastructure progress that enables longer memory, better reasoning and more reliable outputs."), Mark Zuckerberg, Elon Musk ("NVIDIA Rubin will be a rocket engine for AI..."), Satya Nadella, Mike Intrator (CoreWeave), Matt Garman (AWS: "AWS and NVIDIA have been driving cloud AI innovation together for more than 15 years."), Sundar Pichai, Clay Magouyrk (Oracle), Michael Dell, Antonio Neri (HPE) and Yuanqing Yang (Lenovo).
- "The Rubin platform marks NVIDIA’s third-generation rack-scale architecture, with more than 80 NVIDIA MGX ecosystem partners."
- Infrastructure software and storage partners: "AIC, Canonical, Cloudian, DDN, Dell, HPE, Hitachi Vantara, IBM, NetApp, Nutanix, Pure Storage, Supermicro, SUSE, VAST Data and WEKA".
- "Red Hat today announced an expanded collaboration with NVIDIA to deliver a complete AI stack optimized for the NVIDIA Rubin platform with Red Hat’s hybrid cloud portfolio, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Red Hat OpenShift and Red Hat AI."

## Availability

- "NVIDIA Rubin is in full production, and Rubin-based products will be available from partners the second half of 2026."
- First cloud providers deploying Vera Rubin instances in 2026: AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft and OCI, plus NVIDIA Cloud Partners CoreWeave, Lambda, Nebius and Nscale. Cisco, Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro are expected to deliver servers.

## Disclaimers

- The release carries a forward-looking-statements notice under Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933 and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, and states that "Many of the products and features described herein remain in various stages and will be offered on a when-and-if-available basis."
- Media contact: Kristin Uchiyama, Corporate Communications, NVIDIA Corporation, press@nvidia.com. Footer: "Copyright © 2026 NVIDIA Corporation". Readers are pointed to "NVIDIA Live at CES" and the "Inside Vera Rubin" technical blog.

## Other newsroom items listed

"NVIDIA Expands Open Source CUDA-Q Platform for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing" (September 14, 2026); "NVIDIA and Palantir Bring Sovereign Intelligence to Critical Supply Chains" (September 10, 2026); "NVIDIA Expands AI Infrastructure Capacity in Partnership With Australia’s Data Center Ecosystem" (September 9, 2026); "NVIDIA and MediaTek Deepen Long-Standing Partnership..." (August 31, 2026); "NVIDIA Announces Upcoming Event for Financial Community" (August 27, 2026).

wikis.title: Sixth-Generation NVIDIA NVLink
wikis.summary: The NVLink 6 switch and its bandwidth figures for the Rubin platform.
wikis.body:
- "Delivers the fast, seamless GPU-to-GPU communication required for today’s massive MoE models."
- "Each GPU offers 3.6TB/s of bandwidth, while the Vera Rubin NVL72 rack provides 260TB/s — more bandwidth than the entire internet."
- Built-in in-network compute speeds collective operations, with new features "for enhanced serviceability and resiliency".

wikis.title: NVIDIA Vera CPU
wikis.summary: Rubin's CPU, built for agentic reasoning with 88 custom Olympus cores.
wikis.body:
- "Designed for agentic reasoning, NVIDIA Vera is the most power‑efficient CPU for large-scale AI factories."
- "built with 88 NVIDIA custom Olympus cores, full Armv9.2 compatibility and ultrafast NVLink-C2C connectivity."
- "Vera delivers exceptional performance, bandwidth and industry‑leading efficiency to support a full range of modern data center workloads."

wikis.title: NVIDIA Rubin GPU
wikis.summary: The Rubin GPU and its third-generation Transformer Engine.
wikis.body: - "Featuring a third-generation Transformer Engine with hardware-accelerated adaptive compression, Rubin GPU delivers 50 petaflops of NVFP4 compute for AI inference."

wikis.title: Confidential Computing and the RAS Engine
wikis.summary: Third-generation Confidential Computing and the second-generation RAS Engine on Rubin.
wikis.body:
- "Vera Rubin NVL72 is the first rack-scale platform to deliver NVIDIA Confidential Computing — which maintains data security across CPU, GPU and NVLink domains — protecting the world’s largest proprietary models, training and inference workloads."
- Second-Generation RAS Engine: "real-time health checks, fault tolerance and proactive maintenance to maximize system productivity. The rack’s modular, cable-free tray design enables up to 18x faster assembly and servicing than Blackwell."

wikis.title: Inference Context Memory Storage Platform and BlueField-4
wikis.summary: Rubin's AI-native storage platform for inference context, and the ASTRA trust architecture.
wikis.body:
- "NVIDIA Rubin introduces NVIDIA Inference Context Memory Storage Platform, a new class of AI-native storage infrastructure designed to scale inference context at gigascale."
- "Powered by NVIDIA BlueField-4, the platform enables efficient sharing and reuse of key-value cache data across AI infrastructure, improving responsiveness and throughput while enabling predictable, power-efficient scaling of agentic AI."
- "BlueField-4 also introduces Advanced Secure Trusted Resource Architecture, or ASTRA, a system-level trust architecture that gives AI infrastructure builders a single, trusted control point to securely provision, isolate and operate large-scale AI environments without compromising performance."

wikis.title: Spectrum-6 and Spectrum-X Ethernet
wikis.summary: Rubin's Ethernet networking generation, including photonics switches and cross-site Spectrum-XGS.
wikis.body:
- "NVIDIA Spectrum-6 Ethernet is the next generation of Ethernet for AI networking... enabled by 200G SerDes communication circuitry, co-packaged optics and AI-optimized fabrics."
- "Spectrum-X Ethernet Photonics co-packaged optical switch systems deliver 10x greater reliability and 5x longer uptime for AI applications while achieving 5x better power efficiency".
- "Spectrum-XGS Ethernet technology... enables facilities separated by hundreds of kilometers and more to function as a single AI environment."
- These are said to "pave the way for future million-GPU environments".

wikis.title: Vera Rubin NVL72, HGX Rubin NVL8 and DGX SuperPOD
wikis.summary: The system form factors Rubin ships in.
wikis.body:
- "NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 offers a unified, secure system that combines 72 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs, 36 NVIDIA Vera CPUs, NVIDIA NVLink 6, NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs and NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs."
- "NVIDIA will also offer the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, a server board that links eight Rubin GPUs through NVLink to support x86-based generative AI platforms."
- "NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD serves as a reference for deploying Rubin-based systems at scale, integrating either NVIDIA DGX Vera Rubin NVL72 or DGX Rubin NVL8 systems with NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs, NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, NVIDIA InfiniBand networking and NVIDIA Mission Control software."

wikis.title: Microsoft and CoreWeave deployments
wikis.summary: The two named deployment commitments in the release.
wikis.body:
- "Microsoft will deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale systems as part of next-generation AI data centers, including future Fairwater AI superfactory sites," which "will scale to hundreds of thousands of NVIDIA Vera Rubin Superchips". Microsoft Azure "will offer a tightly optimized platform".
- "CoreWeave will integrate NVIDIA Rubin-based systems into its AI cloud platform beginning in the second half of 2026," operated through CoreWeave Mission Control; "CoreWeave is built to operate multiple architectures side by side".

wikis.title: Google and Samsung's Android XR glasses previewed at I/O 2026 with multiple styles
wikis.summary: 9to5Google report from Google I/O 2026 on the first Google-Samsung Android XR smart glasses, their Gentle Monster and Warby Parker styles, Gemini features and 'Fall' 2026 timeline.
wikis.body:
## What was announced

- On-stage at **Google I/O 2026**, Google and Samsung previewed the first Android XR glasses built as a collaboration between the two companies, and confirmed "multiple style offerings".
- "With a name and other key details forthcoming" — the products are previews from their joint smart-glasses effort on the Android XR platform.
- Design partners: **Gentle Monster** for "disruptive yet refined aesthetics" and **Warby Parker** for "refined and timeless designs".

## Features (from Samsung's press release)

- The glasses are designed as "a companion to your smartphone" and a means to "access help through voice interaction".
- Samsung quoted: "Built to understand the world alongside users in real time, the new intelligent eyewear provides everyday support while keeping users hands-free and heads-up. Users can access navigation assistance by simply asking Gemini with their voices, receive personalized suggestions such as a nearby coffee shop on their walking route, or even place an order for pickup. Users can also receive summarized notifications for important texts and add events to their calendars. Additional features include real-time translations with audio that matches to the speaker's voice, as well as the ability to translate text on menus or signs in the user's line of sight. Working seamlessly within the Galaxy ecosystem, the device helps users easily manage everyday tasks or effortlessly capture photos, all without taking their phone out."
- All powered by Gemini. Listed uses include navigation assistance, placing orders at restaurants, summarized notifications for "important texts", calendar additions and real-time translation.

## Styles and timing

- No pricing details in this first preview; multiple styles confirmed.
- **Two styles were shown**, with the "first collections" coming later this year. "A previous leak had shown an additional style not seen in today's teaser."
- **Display versions are coming sometime in 2027**, Google said during I/O.
- Samsung teases a **"Fall" 2026** timeline for the release of its first Android XR glasses, with "additional details" in the "coming months".
- 9to5Google's expectation: "we'll probably hear more about these during the Fold 8 launch in July, as expected, but without a release alongside the new foldables."

## Byline

- Ben Schoon, 9to5Google, May 19 2026 - 12:30 pm PT. Tags on the page: Google I/O 2026, Samsung, Android XR, Galaxy Glasses.

wikis.title: Diablo 4 Season 15 & Diablo 5: BlizzCon 2026 announcements
wikis.summary: An MMOExp article summarising BlizzCon 2026 Day 1's Diablo announcements: the September 15, 2026 Season 15 nostalgia update, the Mufisto the Cow God event, the 2027 Amazon class pack and Diablo 5's spring 2029 target.
wikis.body:
## The article
- "Diablo 4 Season 15 & Diablo 5: BlizzCon 2026 Release Dates, Amazon Class & Major Updates" on mmoexp.com, by Chloe Moreau, "Created: September 14, 2026", filed under Diablo 4, 815 views.
- Author note: she "helped organize gaming meetups and small LAN events in Brussels for years" and writes French-language content.

## Summary as given
- "BlizzCon 2026 Day 1 delivered the most extensive Diablo franchise updates in series history, confirming the highly anticipated Diablo 5 launch window, a massive nostalgia-focused Diablo 4 Season 15, and brand-new playable content for Diablo 4."
- The breakdown covers "official release dates, core gameplay overhauls, limited-time boss events, upcoming class packs, and long-term franchise roadmap changes", and highlights "the 2029 Diablo 5 launch target and September 15, 2026 Season 15 go-live plans".
- Final verdict: the announcements are "the franchise's most ambitious content roadmap to date", with "three years of ongoing Diablo 4 support and a groundbreaking sequel on the horizon".
- The page carries item- and gold-selling promotions for Diablo 4, which are not part of the announcements.

wikis.title: Diablo 4 Season 15: nostalgia update
wikis.summary: The 30th-anniversary season reviving Diablo 1 and 2 content, launching September 15, 2026.
wikis.body:
- "Diablo 4 Season 15 stands out as the franchise's biggest nostalgia-driven update, celebrating 30 years of Diablo history by reviving classic dungeons, bosses, and audio from Diablo 1 and Diablo 2."
- "The season officially launches on September 15, 2026, aligning with the Nintendo Switch 2 port release of the original Diablo 1."
- Unlike limited seasonal events, it "fully reintroduces iconic legacy content": remastered classic dungeons "including the Tristram Cathedral and World Stone Chamber", and returning bosses with "authentic voice lines, original soundtracks, and reimagined combat mechanics".
- "A standout feature is the return of Deckard Cain, with original voice actor Michael Goff recording new narrative poems to guide players through nostalgic gameplay sequences."

wikis.title: Mufisto the Cow God event
wikis.summary: The limited-time community boss event replacing Diablo 4's world bosses.
wikis.body:
- "Running until September 14, 2026, right before Season 14 concludes, the Mufisto the Cow God event replaces all Diablo 4 world bosses with this unique seasonal enemy."
- Mufisto's core ability "spawns roaming spirit cows that steal player skills on contact"; stacked skill theft restricts combat, "forcing players to trigger a unique moo mechanic three times to reclaim lost abilities".
- Community goal: "If players collectively secure 300,000 Mufisto kills across all platforms, the entire community unlocks exclusive cosmetic mount trophies."
- The boss "features layered terrain manipulation and crowd-control attacks".

wikis.title: 2027 Amazon class pack
wikis.summary: Diablo 4's first standalone paid character pack, confirmed for the first half of 2027.
wikis.body:
- "Blizzard confirmed the Amazon class will arrive in Diablo 4 during the first half of 2027, marking the franchise's first standalone character pack."
- "Unlike previous expansions that include multiple zones and story acts, this is a dedicated paid class-focused DLC, signaling a new post-launch content strategy for Diablo 4."
- The model "shifts away from full expansion cycles, offering frequent, targeted content updates to keep the game fresh until Diablo 5 launches"; Blizzard "teases additional character packs may follow, creating a steady pipeline of new playable classes for Diablo 4 players through 2029".

wikis.title: Diablo 5: spring 2029 target and core overhauls
wikis.summary: The sequel's confirmed development, launch window, procedural maps and setting.
wikis.body:
- "BlizzCon 2026 officially confirmed Diablo 5 is in active development, with a targeted spring 2029 launch window."
- "The sequel is not replacing Diablo 4, which will continue receiving seasonal updates and class packs for the next three years."
- "The biggest Diablo 5 gameplay shift is the return of fully procedural overworld and dungeon maps, reviving the classic Diablo 1 and Diablo 2 roguelike core loop", reversing Diablo 4's shared open-world design for "a lonelier, more atmospheric dark fantasy experience".
- Setting: "a post-apocalyptic Sanctuary setting where Diablo achieves victory over humanity"; players take the role of "the West March heir, with direct bloodline ties to Diablo 1's Prince Aiden".

wikis.title: Diablo 5 systems and class lineup
wikis.summary: The caravan hub, launch classes including the Plague Knight, and Diablo 2-inspired itemization.
wikis.body:
- "A brand-new caravan hub system replaces static towns in Diablo 5", a mobile player base travelling with the character through the campaign, with recruitable NPC companions including blacksmiths and quest givers. "All side quests tie exclusively to companion storylines, eliminating generic open-world fetch tasks."
- "Blizzard plans a record launch class roster for Diablo 5, including fan-favorite returning classes Demon Hunter and Monk, plus an all-new Plague Knight class" - "a heavy armored combatant that spreads battlefield diseases and consumes them to amplify offensive power".
- Itemization "returns to classic Diablo 2-inspired mechanics": multi-socket gear, functional set items, variable inventory item sizing and reintroduced rune systems. "Stat-based equipment requirements are in testing, with flexible equip bonuses planned to avoid rigid build restrictions."

wikis.title: Player recommendations
wikis.summary: The article's advice for preparing for Season 15, the Amazon pack and Diablo 5.
wikis.body:
- "Players should prioritize completing Mufisto event kills before September 14, 2026, to secure the community cosmetic reward ahead of Season 15's launch."
- "Leveling alternate characters to level 40 is ideal for early Season 15 nostalgic dungeon runs, matching BlizzCon demo build power levels for balanced gameplay."
- For 2027's Amazon class pack: "saving in-game currency and testing ranged build archetypes".
- For Diablo 5: "following quarterly developer updates starting in 2027 will provide early access to community feedback-driven development changes".

wikis.title: Children of Blood and Bone (film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the upcoming Paramount film Children of Blood and Bone, directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood - its cast and credits, the long development from Fox 2000 to Lucasfilm to Paramount, filming in Lagos, the colorism and author-fallout controversy, and the January 15, 2027 release.
wikis.body:
## What the film is

- "Children of Blood and Bone is an upcoming American fantasy film directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood, who co-wrote the screenplay with Tomi Adeyemi, based on the 2018 novel by Adeyemi." The short description calls it an "Upcoming film directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood".
- "Children of Blood and Bone is scheduled to be released by Paramount Pictures in the United States on January 15, 2027." The Release section adds that this includes "engagements in IMAX".

## Infobox credits

- Directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood. Screenplay by Gina Prince-Bythewood and Tomi Adeyemi. Based on Children of Blood and Bone by Tomi Adeyemi.
- Produced by Wyck Godfrey, Marty Bowen, Karen Rosenfelt, Matt Jackson.
- Starring (infobox order): Thuso Mbedu, Damson Idris, Amandla Stenberg, Tosin Cole, Cynthia Erivo, Lashana Lynch, Zackary Momoh, Richard Mofe-Damijo, Chiwetel Ejiofor, Regina King, Idris Elba, Viola Davis.
- Cinematography Polly Morgan. Edited by Terilyn A. Shropshire. Music by Terence Blanchard.
- Production companies: Temple Hill Entertainment, Sunswept Entertainment, Jackson Pictures. Distributed by Paramount Pictures.
- Release date January 15, 2027. Running time 146 minutes, cited to the Irish Film Classification Office listing "Children of Blood and Bone (12A)" dated September 2, 2026. Country United States; language English. The infobox budget and gross fields are empty.
- The infobox image is captioned "Zelie's character poster".

## Cast

- Thuso Mbedu as Zelie; Damson Idris as Prince Inan; Amandla Stenberg as Princess Amari; Tosin Cole as Tzain; Cynthia Erivo as Admiral Kaea; Lashana Lynch as Jumoke; Zackary Momoh as Adetayo; Richard Mofe-Damijo (no role given); Chiwetel Ejiofor as King Saran; Regina King as Queen Nehanda; Idris Elba as Lekan; Viola Davis as Mama Agba; Saniyya Sidney (no role given); Diaana Babnicova as Folake; Bukky Bakray as Binta; Ayra Starr, Shamz Garuba, Kola Bodunde, Pamilerin Ayodeji and Temi Fagbenle (no roles given).
- The section's opening sentence lists a shorter ensemble: "The ensemble cast of Children Of Blood and Bones includes Thuso Mbedu, Damson Idris, Amandla Stenberg, Tosin Cole, Cynthia Erivo, Lashana Lynch, Regina King, Chiwetel Ejiofor and Ayra Starr" - it names Ayra Starr but not Idris Elba, Viola Davis, Zackary Momoh or Richard Mofe-Damijo, who are in the infobox list.

## Development

- "Prior to publication", Adeyemi's novel was optioned for a film adaptation produced by Fox 2000 Pictures and Temple Hill Entertainment in March 2017.
- February 2019: Rick Famuyiwa announced as director.
- After Disney completed its acquisition of 21st Century Fox in March 2019, which shuttered Fox 2000, the project was transferred to Lucasfilm, "marking the studio's first original live-action project since its acquisition by Disney in 2012". Kay Oyegun was announced to write the script in August 2019.
- September 2019: Walt Disney Studios president Alan Horn told The Hollywood Reporter that Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy was working with 20th Century Fox chairwoman Emma Watts on developing the film.
- Fourth quarter of 2021: Lucasfilm put the project in turnaround. Per The Hollywood Reporter, Adeyemi had become dissatisfied with the pace of Lucasfilm's adaptation efforts and asked to serve as scriptwriter, which Lucasfilm declined; wanting to focus on Star Wars, Indiana Jones and Willow, Lucasfilm let the rights lapse.
- By January 2022 Paramount Pictures had acquired the rights "for a guaranteed exclusive theatrical release", with Temple Hill Entertainment producing alongside Sunswept Entertainment; Adeyemi would write the script and serve as executive producer.
- December 2023: Gina Prince-Bythewood hired to direct and further develop the script.

## Casting, filming and music

- September 2024: Thuso Mbedu cast in the lead role.
- January 2025: Amandla Stenberg, Damson Idris, Tosin Cole, Viola Davis, Cynthia Erivo, Idris Elba, Lashana Lynch and Chiwetel Ejiofor added, with Regina King, Diaana Babnicova and Bukky Bakray in negotiations.
- March [2025]: Saniyya Sidney, Zackary Momoh, Richard Mofe-Damijo, Ayra Starr, Pamilerin Ayodeji, Shamz Garuba, Kola Bodunde and Temi Fagbenle "rounded out the cast".
- "Principal photography began in Lagos in February 2025 and concluded on June 2, 2025."
- Terence Blanchard composed the score.

## Controversy

- The casting of Stenberg and Mbedu "sparked online backlash over colorism, as they are lighter-skinned than the characters from the novel". Stenberg posted an eight-minute TikTok video in February 2025 saying Adeyemi wanted her in the role and that she "would never go after a role that [she] didn't feel like was right for [her] to chase."
- July 2026: Adeyemi revealed she had distanced herself from the adaptation "for unspecified reasons" and had blocked Stenberg on social media; she said she would not watch the film, though she did not mind others seeing it, and could not continue "being hurt and attacked behind the scenes". In a later video the same month she said she left the film's set "hyperventilating and sobbing", with many witnesses present, calling it "the worst thing I have ever had to live through".
- August 2026: Vanity Fair reported the distancing was due to Adeyemi's strained relationship with Stenberg, stemming from her not approving of Stenberg's TikTok response and "culminating into tensions on the set when Adeyemi arrived to film her cameo appearance". The report noted her recent statements contrasted sharply with earlier positive statements about the film.

## Related works the page lists

- Legacy of Orisha novels by Tomi Adeyemi: Children of Blood and Bone (2018), Children of Virtue and Vengeance (2019), Children of Anguish and Anarchy (2024); film: Children of Blood and Bone (2027).
- Films directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood: Love & Basketball (2000), Disappearing Acts (2000), The Secret Life of Bees (2008), Beyond the Lights (2014), The Old Guard (2020), The Woman King (2022), Children of Blood and Bone (2027).
- Categories include "Upcoming films", "2027 films", "2027 fantasy films", "Films shot in Lagos", "Upcoming IMAX films", "Casting controversies in film", "Paramount Pictures films" and "Temple Hill Entertainment films".
- External links: Children of Blood and Bone at IMDb. The article is available in 9 languages.

## Sources cited for the key claims

- Release date and cast: Angelique Jackson, Variety, January 22, 2025. CinemaCon tease: Matt Grobar, Deadline, April 16, 2026.
- Runtime: Irish Film Classification Office, September 2, 2026.
- Wrap of shooting: Dennis Ade Peter, OkayAfrica, June 2, 2025. Lagos start: Harsh Vardhan, Moviedelic, January 15, 2025.
- Adeyemi fallout: Ryan Gajewski, The Hollywood Reporter, July 5, 2026; Benjamin Lindsay, TheWrap, July 29, 2026; Rebecca Ford, Vanity Fair, August 13, 2026.

wikis.title: The 20 Most Anticipated Movies of 2027
wikis.summary: Geek Vibes Nation's countdown of the 20 films it most anticipates in 2027, with release dates, casts and directors, plus notes on date clashes and The Batman: Part II moving to 2028.
wikis.body:
## The article

- "The 20 Most Anticipated Movies Of 2027", by Cainan, filed under Movie News, September 9, 2026, on geekvibesnation.com. No comments at the time of capture.
- Framing: "2027 is going to be crowded. Marvel is preparing to close the Multiverse Saga. DC is bringing Superman back. Middle-earth is returning to theaters. Nintendo is finally taking The Legend of Zelda into live action. Miles Morales has unfinished business across the Spider-Verse, and Ryan Gosling is heading into a completely new corner of the Star Wars galaxy."
- Caveat: "Some of these dates will almost certainly shift before opening night," and projects "without firm enough release plans" were left off.

## The countdown, 20 to 1 (dates as the article gives them)

Entries 20 to 13 have their own topic pages below. The remainder:

- **12. Star Wars: Starfighter** — May 28, 2027. "Shawn Levy directs Star Wars: Starfighter, a standalone adventure starring Ryan Gosling and set approximately five years after The Rise of Skywalker," the furthest forward point in the theatrical timeline. Ensemble: Flynn Gray, Matt Smith, Mia Goth, Aaron Pierre and Amy Adams. "Very little about the actual story has been revealed."
- **11. How to Train Your Dragon 2** — June 11, 2027. Mason Thames and Nico Parker return as Hiccup and Astrid, Gerard Butler as Stoick; it adapts the second animated film, introducing Valka and "the dragon-controlling warlord Drago Bludvist". "Cate Blanchett returns to play Valka after voicing the character in the animated movies"; Dean DeBlois directs again.
- **10. Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse** — June 18, 2027. Shameik Moore returns as Miles alongside Hailee Steinfeld's Gwen Stacy, "with Bob Persichetti and Justin K. Thompson directing", finishing the cliffhanger left by Across the Spider-Verse.
- **9. Shrek 5** — June 30, 2027. "Mike Myers, Eddie Murphy and Cameron Diaz return as Shrek, Donkey and Fiona more than 15 years after the last mainline installment. Zendaya joins the next generation of the family," with an updated animation style.
- **8. Man of Tomorrow** — July 9, 2027. James Gunn writes and directs; David Corenswet's Superman and Nicholas Hoult's Lex Luthor "forced into an uneasy alliance when an even larger threat arrives". "Lars Eidinger has joined the cast as Brainiac"; Rachel Brosnahan returns as Lois Lane. Gunn has stressed it is not "a traditional numbered Superman 2".
- **7. A Quiet Place Part III** — July 30, 2027. "John Krasinski returns to write and direct," with Emily Blunt, Millicent Simmonds, Noah Jupe and Cillian Murphy. "The second film left Regan discovering that high-frequency sound could be broadcast as a weapon against the creatures."
- **6. The Bluey Movie** — August 6, 2027. "creator Joe Brumm writing and directing. Melanie Zanetti and David McCormack return as Chilli and Bandit, with Bluey and Bingo naturally at the center of the adventure."
- **5. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant Mayhem 2** — August 13, 2027. The sequel is expected to deliver on the first film's Shredder tease.
- **4. The Simpsons Movie sequel** — September 3, 2027. "Two decades after Springfield was trapped underneath a giant dome"; a sequel to 2007's The Simpsons Movie. "Plot details are still being kept under wraps."
- **3. Frozen III** — November 24, 2027. "eight years after Frozen II, bringing Kristen Bell, Idina Menzel and Josh Gad back to Arendelle." Disney "has already revealed that the third movie is part of a larger story substantial enough to continue into Frozen IV". The article notes Frozen II "made more than $1.4 billion worldwide."
- **2. The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum** — December 17, 2027. "Andy Serkis directs and stars"; Peter Jackson, Fran Walsh and Philippa Boyens are "once again creatively involved". The story "draws from material surrounding the search for Gollum during the years leading toward The Fellowship of the Ring."
- **1. Avengers: Secret Wars** — no date in its entry; the article later says it opens December 17. It "arrives one year after Avengers: Doomsday and serves as the culmination of Marvel Studios' Multiverse Saga. Anthony and Joe Russo return to direct, with Stephen McFeely writing and Robert Downey Jr.'s Victor von Doom positioned at the center". It notes "Jonathan Hickman's 2015 Secret Wars famously destroyed Marvel's multiverse and rebuilt reality around Battleworld under the rule of Doctor Doom."

## Box office clashes the article flags

- "January 15 currently puts Children of Blood and Bone directly against The Beekeeper 2."
- June: How to Train Your Dragon 2 (June 11), Beyond the Spider-Verse (June 18), Shrek 5 (June 30).
- "As currently scheduled, Avengers: Secret Wars and The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum both open December 17."

## Other observations

- Video game movies: "Now Sonic the Hedgehog 4 is part of a billion-dollar franchise, while Nintendo and Sony are treating The Legend of Zelda as one of their biggest theatrical releases," following Mario, Sonic and Minecraft.
- Horror: Flanagan's Exorcist is called "probably the most creatively interesting", with "Universal and Blumhouse effectively handed one of horror's most famous properties to a filmmaker with a completely different vision." Also dated in 2027 are "another Paranormal Activity and Universal's next Mummy film."
- "If you remember seeing The Batman: Part II on older 2027 movie lists... Warner Bros. has since moved the movie to February 18, 2028." (The introduction says the move was to "February 2028".)
- The author bio reads: "DC Fanboy! Superman is the greatest comic book character of all time. Favorite movies are Man of Steel, Goonies, Back To the Future".

wikis.title: Children of Blood and Bone (No. 20)
wikis.summary: Paramount's fantasy adaptation opening 2027 on 15 January.
wikis.body:
- Release date: January 15, 2027.
- "Gina Prince-Bythewood directs the adaptation of Tomi Adeyemi's bestselling novel, which takes audiences into the fantasy kingdom of Orïsha, where magic has been violently stripped away from its people."
- "The story follows Zélie as she embarks on a dangerous mission to restore what was lost and challenge the king responsible for suppressing magic."
- "The project has assembled a large cast and is being positioned as a genuine theatrical fantasy event rather than a streaming-first YA adaptation."
- The article notes it is scheduled against The Beekeeper 2 on the same weekend.

wikis.title: The Beekeeper 2 (No. 19)
wikis.summary: Jason Statham returns as Adam Clay under a new director.
wikis.body:
- No release date is given in the entry; the article's box office section says January 15 puts it against Children of Blood and Bone.
- "The sequel brings Statham back while Nobody 2 filmmaker Timo Tjahjanto steps behind the camera."
- "Jeremy Irons, Emmy Raver-Lampman and Bobby Naderi are among the returning cast, while Pom Klementieff joins the sequel."

wikis.title: Narnia: The Magician's Nephew (No. 18)
wikis.summary: Greta Gerwig's Narnia for Netflix, with a theatrical window before streaming.
wikis.body:
- Release date: February 12, 2027. Netflix premiere: April 2, 2027.
- "Rather than beginning with another adaptation of The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, Gerwig is starting chronologically with The Magician's Nephew," a story set "long before Peter, Susan, Edmund and Lucy discover the wardrobe" that "explores the creation of Narnia itself."
- "The cast includes Emma Mackey, Carey Mulligan, Daniel Craig and Meryl Streep."
- "Netflix is giving Narnia a full theatrical window beginning February 12 before bringing it to the streaming service in April."

wikis.title: The Thomas Crown Affair (No. 17)
wikis.summary: Michael B. Jordan directs and stars in the new Thomas Crown Affair.
wikis.body:
- Release date: March 5, 2027.
- "Michael B. Jordan is taking on another movie previously led by Steve McQueen and Pierce Brosnan. But he's not simply starring. Jordan also directs... his second feature behind the camera following Creed III."
- "Adria Arjona joins Jordan alongside an impressive ensemble including Kenneth Branagh, Aubrey Plaza, Lily Gladstone, Danai Gurira and Ruth Negga."
- "Jordan has described the movie as a reimagining rather than an attempt to simply recreate the earlier versions."

wikis.title: Mike Flanagan's new Exorcist movie (No. 16)
wikis.summary: A new story in The Exorcist world written and directed by Mike Flanagan.
wikis.body:
- Release date: March 12, 2027.
- Flanagan "is writing and directing a completely new story set within the world of The Exorcist. It isn't a sequel to The Exorcist: Believer and isn't being positioned as another remake of William Friedkin's original."
- "Scarlett Johansson leads an enormous cast that also includes Chiwetel Ejiofor, Laurence Fishburne, Diane Lane, Carla Gugino and several familiar members of Flanagan's acting ensemble."
- Elsewhere the article says Universal and Blumhouse handed the property to Flanagan.

wikis.title: Sonic the Hedgehog 4 (No. 15)
wikis.summary: Paramount's fourth Sonic film, expected to draw on Sonic CD.
wikis.body:
- Release date: March 19, 2027.
- "Jeff Fowler returning to direct and Ben Schwartz once again voicing Sonic."
- "The next installment is expected to draw heavily from Sonic CD, which makes Amy Rose and Metal Sonic particularly important additions. Kristen Bell joins the franchise as Amy, while familiar characters including Tails, Knuckles and Shadow keep expanding a universe..."

wikis.title: Godzilla x Kong: Supernova (No. 14)
wikis.summary: Legendary's next Monsterverse entry.
wikis.body:
- Release date: March 26, 2027.
- It "continues Legendary's Monsterverse after Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire demonstrated that audiences were still very interested in watching gigantic creatures solve disagreements with their fists."
- "Legendary has described the film as another chapter in the shared universe, with Godzilla and Kong facing a catastrophic new threat."

wikis.title: The Legend of Zelda (No. 13)
wikis.summary: Nintendo and Sony's live-action Zelda film directed by Wes Ball.
wikis.body:
- Release date: April 30, 2027.
- "Nintendo is producing alongside Sony Pictures, with Wes Ball directing."
- The article calls it "the video game adaptation with the highest degree of difficulty", saying Hyrule "needs to feel like a world rather than a collection of references. Link needs to work as an actual protagonist. Zelda needs meaningful agency. And whatever version of Ganondorf eventually emerges needs to feel appropriately mythic."

wikis.title: The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian (2008 film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Andrew Adamson's 2008 Narnia sequel for Disney and Walden Media - its story, cast, European production, visual effects, May 2008 release, mixed-to-positive reviews and $419.6 million gross.
wikis.body:
## The film

- A 2008 high fantasy film directed by Andrew Adamson and written by Adamson, Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely, based on C. S. Lewis's 1951 novel and the second installment in The Chronicles of Narnia film series. Produced by Walt Disney Pictures and Walden Media; distributed by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures. 150 minutes. Budget $225 million; box office $419.6 million.
- Georgie Henley, Skandar Keynes, William Moseley and Anna Popplewell reprise their roles, with Ben Barnes as Caspian, Sergio Castellitto as King Miraz, Peter Dinklage as Trumpkin, Warwick Davis as Nikabrik, Liam Neeson voicing Aslan and Eddie Izzard voicing Reepicheep.
- The four Pevensies return to Narnia almost 1,300 years later to help Prince Caspian against his uncle Miraz; Miraz is killed by Lord Sopespian, Aslan's river god destroys the Telmarine army, and Caspian becomes king.

## Production

- The script was written before the first film was released so that filming could start before the actors grew too old; the writers restructured the novel to bring the Pevensies back into Narnia earlier and added a Peter-Caspian rivalry and a Susan-Caspian romance.
- The Telmarines were designed as stereotypically Spanish, with conquistador- and samurai-based masked helmets and El Greco-inspired costumes; the Narnians were made wilder. 4,600 make-up jobs were performed.
- Filming began February 12, 2007 in Auckland, with most of the shoot in Europe: Barrandov Studios in Prague (including a 200-foot castle built in the open air), the Soča Valley in Slovenia (a bridge modelled on Caesar's Rhine bridge), Ústí nad Labem in the Czech Republic and Poland. Filming finished by September 8, 2007.
- Over 1,500 visual effects shots, against 800 on the first film; post-production was based in the UK for tax credits, so the film legally qualifies as a British film.
- Harry Gregson-Williams scored the film at Abbey Road Studios between January and April 2008, with songs by Regina Spektor, Oren Lavie and Switchfoot.

## Release and reception

- Premiered at the Ziegfeld Theatre in New York City on May 7, 2008; released May 16 in the United States and June 26 in the United Kingdom, with a British premiere at the O2 Arena on June 19. Disney spent $175 million on promotion.
- Rotten Tomatoes 66% from 188 reviews (average 6.4/10); Metacritic 62 from 34 critics; CinemaScore "A−". Critics praised the effects and production design; some objected to the violence and to the Telmarines' Mediterranean coding.
- US and Canada opening weekend $55 million at number one, short of an expected $80 million and below the first film's $65.6 million. Final US and Canada gross $141.6 million; worldwide total given as $419.6 million in the infobox and $419.7 million in the box office section - the tenth-highest-grossing film of 2008 and Disney's second-highest of the year after WALL-E.
- Producer Mark Johnson said in 2010 that "We made some mistakes with Prince Caspian", calling it "a little bit too rough" for families and too much of a "boys' action movie".
- It won Choice Movie: Action at the 2008 Teen Choice Awards and a BMI Film Music Award, with nominations including four Saturn Awards, two Visual Effects Society Awards and three Young Artist Awards.
- It was the last Narnia film co-produced by Walt Disney Pictures; 20th Century Fox distributed The Voyage of the Dawn Treader (2010) after budget disputes with Walden Media.

wikis.title: The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian (2008 film) - plot, cast, production, release and reception
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Andrew Adamson's 2008 Narnia sequel, covering its story, cast, writing and design choices, European filming, visual effects, release, reviews, $419.6 million gross and awards.
wikis.body:
## The film

- "The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian is a 2008 high fantasy film, directed by Andrew Adamson, and written by Adamson, Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely." Based on the 1951 novel Prince Caspian, the second in C. S. Lewis's children's book series, and the second installment in The Chronicles of Narnia film series.
- Produced by Mark Johnson, Andrew Adamson and Philip Steuer; cinematography Karl Walter Lindenlaub; edited by Sim Evan-Jones; music by Harry Gregson-Williams. Production companies Walt Disney Pictures and Walden Media; distributed by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures.
- Release dates: May 7, 2008 (New York City); May 16, 2008 (United States); June 26, 2008 (United Kingdom). Running time 150 minutes. Countries United Kingdom and United States; language English.
- Budget $225 million; box office $419.6 million in the infobox. "It grossed $419.6 million on a budget of $225 million, becoming the tenth-highest-grossing film of 2008."
- Georgie Henley, Skandar Keynes, William Moseley and Anna Popplewell reprise their roles from the previous film. The plot has the four Pevensie siblings return to Narnia to aid Prince Caspian against his corrupt uncle, King Miraz.
- "Work on the script began before the first film, The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, was released, so that filming could begin before the actors grew too old for their parts."
- Filming began in February 2007 in New Zealand, but most shooting took place in Central Europe for the larger sets available; Adamson based post-production in the United Kingdom because of recent tax credits.
- It was the last Narnia film co-produced by Walt Disney Pictures - 20th Century Fox distributed The Voyage of the Dawn Treader (2010) after budgetary disputes between Disney and Walden Media - but Disney's 2019 purchase of 21st Century Fox means Disney now owns the rights to all the films.

## Music

- Harry Gregson-Williams, composer of The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, began composing in December 2007; recording began at Abbey Road Studios the following month and finished by April 2008, with the Crouch End Festival Chorus.
- The soundtrack features Regina Spektor's "The Call", Oren Lavie's "Dance 'Round The Memory Tree" and Switchfoot's "This Is Home". Imogen Heap, who sang "Can't Take It In" for the first film, wrote a new song Gregson-Williams considered too dark.
- The score is darker to match the film. Caspian's theme was meant to convey vulnerability and grow more vibrant as he became heroic; it originally used a 3/4 time signature but the opening scene required 4/4. The heroic theme from the first film was inverted to represent Miraz's cunning. A muted trumpet presented Reepicheep's militaristic, organised character; a small pennywhistle arrangement was rejected as too cute for the night raid's tension.

## Contradictions inside the page

- Worldwide gross: the infobox and lead give $419.6 million, while the Box office section says "the worldwide total stands at $419.7 million".
- Saturn Awards: the Critical response section says it was nominated for "Best Fantasy Film, Best Costumes, Best Make-up, and Best Special Effects at the Saturn Awards", while the accolades table lists the fourth nomination as "Best Visual Effects".
- UK release: the infobox gives June 26, 2008 for the United Kingdom, while the Release section describes the British premiere at the O2 Arena on June 19.

wikis.title: Plot of Prince Caspian (2008)
wikis.summary: The film's story as the article summarises it, from Caspian's flight to Miraz's death and the Pevensies' departure.
wikis.body:
- In Narnia, almost 1,300 years after the Pevensies left, the Telmarine prince Caspian is awakened by his mentor Doctor Cornelius, who tells him his aunt has just given birth to a son and his life is in grave danger. Cornelius gives him Queen Susan's ancient magical horn. Fleeing, Caspian falls from his horse and meets the dwarfs Trumpkin and Nikabrik and the badger Trufflehunter; Trumpkin sacrifices himself and is captured. Caspian blows the horn to summon help.
- In England, one year after they left Narnia, the four Pevensie children wait at the Strand tube station for the train to boarding school; the station tears apart and they are transported back to Narnia, where they find Cair Paravel attacked and ruined. They save Trumpkin from drowning. Lucy sees Aslan showing a safe path but her siblings cannot see him; she later contacts Aslan in a dream, and only Edmund believes her.
- Nikabrik and Trufflehunter lead Caspian to the Dancing Lawn, where the old Narnians assemble and Caspian convinces them to help him win his throne. Caspian's troops and the Pevensies journey to Aslan's How, a huge underground hall built over the Stone Table. Peter decides to attack Miraz's castle rather than wait for Aslan; Caspian, learning Miraz killed his father, confronts his uncle and compromises the attack, which fails with many Narnians killed.
- Nikabrik, a werewolf and a hag use black sorcery to summon the White Witch, who from inside a wall of ice tries to get a drop of Caspian's and then Peter's blood; Edmund, Trumpkin and Lucy kill the rogues and Edmund shatters the ice.
- Peter challenges Miraz to a duel to buy Lucy time to find Aslan, wounds him and gives his sword to Caspian, who spares Miraz. Lord Sopespian kills Miraz with an arrow and blames the Narnians, igniting a battle. Lucy finds Aslan, who awakens the trees; the forest attacks the Telmarines and Aslan summons a river god who wipes out most of the Telmarine army including Sopespian. The survivors surrender.
- Caspian becomes King of Narnia and brings peace between Narnians and Telmarines. Peter and Susan reveal Aslan has told them they will never re-enter Narnia, though Edmund and Lucy might still come back.

wikis.title: Cast of Prince Caspian
wikis.summary: The Pevensies, Telmarines, Narnians and cameo roles listed in the article, with the casting and performance notes attached to each.
wikis.body:
## Pevensies

- Georgie Henley as Lucy Pevensie. Henley said Lucy represents faith, being the youngest and most open-minded. During filming her baby teeth were falling out, so she wore fake teeth.
- Skandar Keynes as Edmund Pevensie. The writers saw him "as our Han Solo", "[doing] the right thing" and "probably going to be a little low-key about it". Keynes bruised his heel jumping onto a horse during a stunt.
- William Moseley as Peter Pevensie. In a departure from the novel, Peter has a rivalry with Caspian; Moseley: "Peter came back to Narnia expecting to be king again and that everyone would do as he said, and Caspian is unwilling to let him take over ... it's a lot about humility ... they start off as these sort of angry teenagers, and become kings at the end." He trained for three months in New York City.
- Anna Popplewell as Susan Pevensie. Adamson convinced Douglas Gresham to have her present during battles, suggesting her passive role in the novel reflected Lewis's view of women before he met Joy Gresham: "I think [Lewis] cast women down in the earlier books, but when you look at The Horse and His Boy, it has a strong female character. Doug's mother was a strong woman." Adamson also had her fall for Caspian: "The kids are growing up. If you look at Ben and you look at Anna, it seems really implausible that they wouldn't have some feelings for each other."

## Telmarines

- Ben Barnes as Prince Caspian X. Adamson: "Caspian is a coming-of-age and, to some degree, a loss of innocence story." Andrew Garfield auditioned but was passed over for not being "handsome enough" according to his agent; Nicholas Hoult also auditioned. "While in the novel Caspian is a 13-year-old child, in the film he is a 15-year-old adult young man." Barnes was cast two and a half weeks after meeting the filmmakers and spent two months in New Zealand horse riding and stunt training. He modelled his Spanish accent on Mandy Patinkin's Inigo Montoya in The Princess Bride. He left England without telling the Royal National Theatre, which he was set to tour with in The History Boys; they considered suing for breach of contract but decided against it.
- Sergio Castellitto as King Miraz - his first villain role; he compared the character to King Claudius in Hamlet.
- Pierfrancesco Favino as General Glozelle, who plots with Sopespian but repents and volunteers to go to the Pevensies' world - Favino's idea, as Glozelle originally died in battle. Adamson called him "a real Benedict Arnold"; Favino often acted as translator on set.
- Damián Alcázar as Lord Sopespian. Adamson: "In some ways Sopespian turns out to be the real bad guy of the film ... Sopespian, like Shakespeare's Iago, is trying to manipulate the situation". Alcázar was first offered Miraz but was recast when his height was judged unable to intimidate the taller Barnes.
- Vincent Grass as Dr. Cornelius, Caspian's half-dwarf mentor; Adamson compared their relationship to Aristotle and Alexander the Great. His role is much smaller than in the novel and he is referred to only as "Professor".
- Alicia Borrachero as Queen Prunaprismia, Miraz's wife, the second volunteer to go back to our world with her child.
- Simón Andreu as Lord Scythley; Predrag Bjelac as Lord Donnon; David Bowles as Lord Gregoire; Juan Diego Montoya Garcia as Lord Montoya.

## Narnians

- Liam Neeson as the voice of Aslan, who is "more parental here, [he] lets the kids, well, make their own mistakes". Aslan's entrance was filmed as a dream sequence. Neeson: "[I] see him more as the spirit of the planet—this living, breathing planet." Aslan's size was increased by fifteen percent and his eyes changed to look less "Egyptian".
- Peter Dinklage as Trumpkin, the first choice after Adamson and Johnson saw him in The Station Agent. Dinklage: "often, you get the hero and the villain and not much in between. Trumpkin is in between." His prosthetics took three hours to apply and restricted his performance to his eyes.
- Warwick Davis as Nikabrik, a descendant of Ginarrbrik who bears one of his rings; casting him was against type, and Berger covered all his face bar his eyelids in prosthetics. Nikabrik's nose was based on Berger. Davis played Reepicheep in the 1989 BBC production of Prince Caspian.
- Ken Stott as the voice of Trufflehunter, "a walking and talking Narnian library [who is] totally old-school"; the animators visited a badger sanctuary.
- Eddie Izzard as the voice of Reepicheep, chosen from over 100 auditions. Izzard played him as "a cross between Mad Max and a Stormtrooper from Star Wars", interpreting him as someone whose family was killed by the Telmarines. Adamson told the animators to rent as many Errol Flynn films as possible.
- Cornell John as Glenstorm the centaur, imagined as 170 years old, conveying "honour, pride and tradition"; Lejla Abbasová as Windmane; Yemi Akinyemi as Ironhoof; Carlos Da Silva as Suncloud; Ephraim Goldin as Rainstone.
- David Walliams as the voice of the Bulgy Bear; Klara Issova as the Narnian Hag, using some Arabic words in her incantation; Gomez Mussenden as the child centaur Lightning Bolt; Jan Pavel Filipensky as the giant Wimbleweather.
- Shane Rangi as Asterius, an elderly Minotaur (voiced by Josh Campbell), killed holding the gate open; Rangi also played the werewolf and stood in for Aslan, the Bulgy Bear and the wild bear. He lost four kilograms wearing his costumes and knocked himself against the castle's rising gate.

## Cameos

- Tilda Swinton reprises Jadis, the White Witch, whose ghost appears; she and her two children also cameoed as centaurs.
- Composer Harry Gregson-Williams as the voice of Pattertwig, a squirrel - Adamson felt he had "squirrel-like energy".
- Douglas Gresham as a Telmarine crier.

wikis.title: Writing and design
wikis.summary: Why the sequel was written early, how the script restructured the novel, and how the Narnians and Spanish-styled Telmarines were designed.
wikis.body:
## Writing

- The screenplay for Prince Caspian was already written before The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe was released. Adamson said the decision was made to follow the publication order "because 'if we don't make it now we'll never be able to, because the [actors will] be too old'". Prince Caspian, the second published novel, is the fourth chronologically. The writers briefly considered combining Caspian with The Voyage of the Dawn Treader, as the BBC did.
- Douglas Gresham: "We had some difficulty figuring out how to make Caspian work as a film. In the book, the children arrive in Narnia, and they all sit down around the campfire and Trumpkin tells them the story of Prince Caspian – which means that the four Pevensie children vanish for half of the book."
- Markus and McFeely wanted to explore how the Pevensies felt returning from Narnia: "[C. S. Lewis] doesn't much consider what it would be like for a King of Narnia to return to being a 1940s schoolchild." They brought the Pevensies back into Narnia nearer the start to weave the two stories together, added a sense of guilt at Narnia's destruction, and gave Peter hubris so his arrogance means he cannot see Aslan.
- Adamson wanted a larger scale: "I've gained confidence having gone through the first. This time, I was able to go larger [in] scale, with more extras and bigger battle scenes." A new raid on Miraz's castle was created, inspired by a passage where Reepicheep says he would like to attack the castle; Adamson felt mythological Greek creatures storming a castle was highly original. He copied Alfred Hitchcock by "tell[ing] people at the end of the scene, 'Now just give me something where you're not thinking about anything.'"

## Design

- Adamson described the film as darker: it takes place "another 1300 years later, [and] Narnia has been oppressed by Telmarines for a large period of that time, so it's a dirtier, grittier, darker place than the last world was" and "This one is more of a boy's movie. It's a harsher world. The villains are human, and that lends a more realistic attitude."
- Creatures were designed by Jordu Schell and supervised by Howard Berger, who said Prince Caspian would be more medieval than the first film. Berger's children critiqued his designs - his son thought the werewolf's ears were silly, so they were made smaller.
- The Narnians were made wilder in appearance, having been forced into the forests, with more variety of ages, sizes and races. Black dwarfs were distinguished from red dwarfs by more leather and jewellery and a darker colour scheme. Fighting styles were made distinguishable - Minotaurs have maces, centaurs use swords. The satyrs were redesigned. "Four thousand and six hundred make-up jobs were performed, which Berger believes is a record."
- The Telmarines, including Caspian, were interpreted as Spanish because of their pirate origins, which Mark Johnson said made Caspian "a contrast to the lily-white [Pevensies]". Production designer Roger Ford originally wanted them French, but the crew could not shoot at Pierrefonds Castle for Miraz's lair.
- Weta Workshop made masked helmets and horse faceplates. The stunt soldiers wield 200 polearms in two styles, 200 rapiers, over a hundred falchions, 250 shields and 55 crossbows; Caspian's sword is a variation of the Royal Guard's weapons.
- Costume designer Isis Mussenden looked to El Greco's paintings, wanting colours that looked "acidic and hot and cool at the same time". The masked helmets are based on conquistadors and samurai. An eagle emblem was incorporated into the characters' lairs "to make them feel fascist".

wikis.title: Filming and visual effects
wikis.summary: The New Zealand, Czech, Slovenian and Polish shoot, the sets built and restored, and the 1,500-plus visual effects shots done in the UK.
wikis.body:
## Filming

- Eight months were spent scouting locations, including Ireland, China and Argentina, before New Zealand, Prague, Slovenia and Poland were chosen. Adamson decided New Zealand lacked enough sound stages for the larger scale; filming mostly in Europe also allowed shooting during summer on both continents, "although the weather turned out to be so erratic during filming that Adamson joked he had been lied to".
- Filming began on February 12, 2007 in Auckland. The Pevensies' return to the ruined Cair Paravel was shot at Cathedral Cove, chosen for a tunnel-like arch echoing the train tunnel. Henderson Valley Studios was used for the ancient treasure room and the Underground station.
- On April 1, 2007 the crew began filming at Barrandov Studios in Prague, building Miraz's castle, Aslan's How and the Narnians' underground hiding places. The 200-foot-tall (61 m) castle was built to scale because Adamson felt he had overused digital sets on the last film; it was built in the open air during winter, with temperatures dropping to −4 °F (−20 °C). Miraz's courtyard was the largest set of production designer Roger Ford's career. Ford's crew put a camera inside a badger's den to study Trufflehunter's den, whose roof had to be raised three inches because Ben Barnes was too tall.
- In June 2007 the bridge battle was shot near Bovec in the Soča Valley, Slovenia, chosen for its resemblance to New Zealand. A large bridge modelled on the one Julius Caesar built to cross the Rhine was built in around forty days (Caesar supposedly took ten); authorities allowed only that build time so as not to disrupt summer activities. The crew dug a trench to change the river's course and deepen the riverbed, and cut down 100 trees for shots of the Telmarines building the bridge. The bridge stood for two months before being dismantled and partly recycled.
- Part of the battle was shot at Ústí nad Labem in the Czech Republic; only the entrance to Aslan's How was built on location. Moseley and Castellitto began training for the duel in November 2006; stunt coordinator Allan Poppleton doubled for Castellitto in some shots, and cameras were built into their shields for claustrophobic shots, with the main camera on a 360-degree track.
- A large hole was dug for the pillar-collapse scene and the earth restored afterwards; grass was restored after cavalry charges; 18,000 fern plants were imported to the Czech Republic to create a forest; a Poland scene involving building a cliff face also had to leave no trace. Filming finished by September 8, 2007.

## Visual effects

- "Prince Caspian has over 1,500 visual effects shots, more than The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe's 800 visual effects shots, yet the film had less time to complete them." The scale led Adamson to base production in the UK for new tax credits, so the film legally qualifies as a British film; the director only had to walk five minutes from the editing room.
- Moving Picture Company and Framestore CFC worked alongside Weta Digital: Framestore did Aslan, Trufflehunter and the door in the air; Scanline did the River-god; Weta the werewolf, wild bear and Miraz's castle; MPC and Escape Studios the main battle, tunnel scene, castle assault, council scenes and other creatures.
- Alex Funke directed the miniatures unit, including 1/24- and 1/100-scale miniatures of Miraz's castle and a scale model of the Narnians' cave hideouts. Cornell John wore Power Risers (mechanical stilts with springs) so centaurs could walk during dialogue. The animatronic Minotaur heads were improved to lip sync but had to be revamped digitally.
- In the climactic battle 150 extras stood in for the Narnians and 300 for the Telmarines, digitally duplicated to 1,000 Narnians and 5,000 Telmarines. Centaurs and fauns were made entirely digital; the dryads were fully computer-generated. Framestore replaced Georgie Henley's arm with a digital version so Lucy could hug Aslan. A motion control rig was built for the gryphons.
- Adamson was proudest of the river-god: "It was a really masterful effect: to control water like that is incredibly difficult ... The [visual effects company] told us they'd been waiting to do a shot like that for ten years."
- The film features windmill-like catapults that fire rapidly and a ballista firing three projectiles at a time; practical versions were metal with painted fibreglass on top, the catapult's upper half painted blue for digital replacement.

wikis.title: Release, marketing and home media
wikis.summary: The release-date shift, the New York and O2 premieres, the PG rating, the $175 million marketing campaign and the DVD and Blu-ray editions.
wikis.body:
## Release

- Disney announced a December 14, 2007 release date during pre-production but pushed it to May 16, 2008 to avoid competing with The Water Horse, another Walden Media production; Disney also noted the Harry Potter films had moved from winter to summer, and Narnia could too because the film was darker and more like an action film.
- World premiere at the Ziegfeld Theatre in New York City on May 7, 2008. The British premiere was at the O2 Arena on June 19 - "the first time the dome has hosted a film screening" - with around 10,000 attending and proceeds going to Great Ormond Street Hospital.
- It opened in 3,929 theaters in the United States and Canada on May 16, 2008. The MPAA gave it a PG; to earn the rating, which the filmmakers were contractually bound by Disney to achieve, Adamson altered a shot of a fallen helmet to make clear it did not contain a severed head. Adamson made numerous edits after showing the film to a young audience.

## Marketing

- On top of the $225 million budget (almost $100 million of it on effects), Disney spent $175 million promoting the film.
- Play Along Toys made a Miraz's castle playset, 3 3/4-inch and 7-inch action figures and roleplaying costumes; Weta Workshop's Collectibles unit made statues, busts and helmets; there was also a Monopoly edition. In the UK, Damaris Trust produced church and school resources for the official UK Narnia website.
- In June 2008 the "Journey into Narnia: Prince Caspian" attraction opened at Disney's Hollywood Studios with a recreation of the Stone Table, behind-the-scenes footage, concept art, storyboards, props and costumes.
- Marketing focused on action; unlike for The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, Disney and Walden did not screen the film for pastors or give Bible-based study guides in North America.

## Home media

- Released on DVD and Blu-ray in the UK on November 17, 2008, in North America on December 2, 2008 and in Australia on November 27, 2008. It was the top-selling DVD of its release week in the U.S., taking in $54.7 million.
- One-disc and three-disc DVD editions (two-disc only in the UK) and two-disc and three-disc Blu-ray editions (two-disc only in the UK); extras include an Adamson commentary, blooper reel, deleted scenes and documentaries, with a digital copy on the third disc. The Blu-ray used Circle-Vision 360° to let viewers watch the night raid from different angles.
- An additional disc of special features was only available in Japan and Zavvi stores in the UK; a version with electronic press kit material was exclusive to Sanity stores in Australia. By the end of 2008 the film earned almost $71 million in DVD sales.

wikis.title: Critical response, box office and accolades
wikis.summary: The film's reviews and criticisms, its opening and worldwide takings, and the awards it was nominated for or won.
wikis.body:
## Critical response

- Rotten Tomatoes: 66% positive from 188 reviews, average 6.4/10. Consensus: "The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian is an entertaining family adventure worthy of the standard set by its predecessor." Metacritic: 62 out of 100 from 34 critics, "generally favorable". CinemaScore: "A−".
- Leonard Maltin gave three of four stars, calling the performances "strong", the storytelling "solid" and the scenery "breathtaking", though "it's a dark tale, and the climactic battle scenes go on at length."
- Todd McCarthy (Variety) felt Adamson's direction had a "surer sense of cinematic values" and that "the four kids overall have more character and are therefore more interesting to watch than they were before, and Italian actor Castellitto registers strongly with evil that's implacable but not overplayed."
- Michael Rechtshaffen (The Hollywood Reporter) noted "the loss of innocence theme ... significantly deepened" and highlighted Peter Dinklage, who "outmaneuver[ed] the title character as Narnia's most colorful new inhabitant".
- Criticisms of the film's messages: Mick Lasalle (San Francisco Chronicle) wrote that "basically, this is a movie about kids who go into another world and dimension and spend the whole time killing people"; Alonso Duralde (MSNBC) noted "all the heroes have British accents while the Telmarines are all decidedly Mediterranean in appearance and inflection"; an Anglican Journal review found it much lighter on religious faith and deficient on character and emotion.
- In 2010 producer Mark Johnson admitted "We made some mistakes with Prince Caspian and I don't want to make them again", saying it lacked some of the "wonder and magic of Narnia", was "a little bit too rough" for families and was too much of a "boys' action movie".

## Box office

- Opened on May 16 in the United States and Canada with $55 million from 8,400 screens at 3,929 theaters, ranking #1 and taking the spot from Iron Man. Disney said it was happy, "although the opening fell short of industry expectations of $80 million and was also behind The Lion, The Witch and the Wardrobe's opening gross of $65.6 million." By June 1 it had grossed $115 million, against $153 million for the first film in the same time. Disney CEO Robert Iger attributed the underperformance to release between Iron Man and Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull.
- It also opened at number one in twelve other countries on May 16, grossing $22.1 million for a worldwide opening of about $77 million. Russia opened with $6.7 million, the biggest opening of the year; Mexico $6.3 million (15% more than the first film); South Korea $4 million; India $2 million (triple the first film); Malaysia $1.1 million; Argentina $1 million on June 13.
- "Prince Caspian made $141.6 million in the United States and Canada while the worldwide total stands at $419.7 million" - the tenth-highest-grossing film of 2008 worldwide and Disney's second-highest-grossing film of 2008 after WALL-E.

## Accolades

| Year | Award | Category/Recipient | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2008 | MTV Movie Awards | Best Summer Movie So Far | Nominated |
| 2008 | Teen Choice Awards | Choice Movie: Action | Won |
| 2008 | Teen Choice Awards | Choice Movie: Male Breakout Star (Ben Barnes) | Nominated |
| 2008 | National Movie Awards | Best Family Film | Nominated |
