wikis.title: FOMC Summary of Economic Projections, March 22, 2023
wikis.summary: The Federal Reserve's Summary of Economic Projections released with the March 21-22, 2023 FOMC meeting: participants' medians, central tendencies and ranges for GDP growth, unemployment, PCE inflation and the federal funds rate through 2025 and the longer run, plus the uncertainty and risk material.
wikis.body:
## What this is
- PDF, 17 pages, headed "For release at 2:00 p.m., EDT, March 22, 2023": the Summary of Economic Projections (SEP) issued "In conjunction with the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting held on March 21-22, 2023".
- Participants submitted projections "of the most likely outcomes for real gross domestic product (GDP) growth, the unemployment rate, and inflation for each year from 2023 to 2025 and over the longer run", each based on information available at the meeting and on "her or his assessment of appropriate monetary policy - including a path for the federal funds rate and its longer-run value".
- "Appropriate monetary policy" is defined as the future path of policy each participant deems most likely to foster outcomes "that best satisfy his or her individual interpretation of the statutory mandate to promote maximum employment and price stability."
- Table 1 shows median, central tendency and range, with each variable's March 2023 projection followed by the "December projection" made at the December 13-14, 2022 FOMC meeting. "One participant did not submit longer-run projections for the change in real GDP, the unemployment rate, or the federal funds rate" at each of those two meetings.
- Definitions: the median is the middle projection; the central tendency "excludes the three highest and three lowest projections"; the range "includes all participants' projections". GDP and inflation projections are Q4-over-Q4 percent changes; unemployment projections are the Q4 average civilian unemployment rate; federal funds rate projections are the midpoint of the appropriate target range (or target level) at year-end or in the longer run. "Longer-run projections for core PCE inflation are not collected."

## Medians (March 2023, with the December 2022 projection in brackets)
- Change in real GDP: 2023 0.4 [0.5]; 2024 1.2 [1.6]; 2025 1.9 [1.8]; longer run 1.8 [1.8].
- Unemployment rate: 2023 4.5 [4.6]; 2024 4.6 [4.6]; 2025 4.6 [4.5]; longer run 4.0 [4.0].
- PCE inflation: 2023 3.3 [3.1]; 2024 2.5 [2.5]; 2025 2.1 [2.1]; longer run 2.0 [2.0].
- Core PCE inflation: 2023 3.6 [3.5]; 2024 2.6 [2.5]; 2025 2.1 [2.1].
- Federal funds rate: 2023 5.1 [5.1]; 2024 4.3 [4.1]; 2025 3.1 [3.1]; longer run 2.5 [2.5].

## Central tendencies and ranges as tabled (March 2023, December in brackets)
- Change in real GDP - central tendency: 2023 0.0-0.8 [0.4-1.0]; 2024 1.0-1.5 [1.3-2.0]; 2025 1.7-2.1 [1.6-2.0]; longer run 1.7-2.0 [1.7-2.0]. Range: 2023 -0.2-1.3 [-0.5-1.0]; 2024 0.3-2.0 [0.5-2.4]; 2025 1.5-2.2 [1.4-2.3]; longer run 1.6-2.5 [1.6-2.5].
- Unemployment rate - central tendency: 2023 4.0-4.7 [4.4-4.7]; 2024 4.3-4.9 [4.3-4.8]; 2025 4.3-4.8 [4.0-4.7]; longer run 3.8-4.3 [3.8-4.3]. Range: 2023 3.9-4.8 [4.0-5.3]; 2024 4.0-5.2 [4.0-5.0]; 2025 3.8-4.9 [3.8-4.8]; longer run 3.5-4.7 [3.5-4.8].
- PCE inflation - central tendency: 2023 3.0-3.8 [2.9-3.5]; 2024 2.2-2.8 [2.3-2.7]; 2025 2.0-2.2 [2.0-2.2]; longer run 2.0 [2.0]. Range: 2023 2.8-4.1 [2.6-4.1]; 2024 2.0-3.5 [2.2-3.5]; 2025 2.0-3.0 [2.0-3.0]; longer run 2.0 [2.0].
- Core PCE inflation - central tendency: 2023 3.5-3.9 [3.2-3.7]; 2024 2.3-2.8 [2.3-2.7]; 2025 2.0-2.2 [2.0-2.2]. Range: 2023 3.5-4.1 [3.0-3.8]; 2024 2.1-3.1 [2.2-3.0]; 2025 2.0-3.0 [2.0-3.0].
- Federal funds rate - central tendency: 2023 5.1-5.6 [5.1-5.4]; 2024 3.9-5.1 [3.9-4.9]; 2025 2.9-3.9 [2.6-3.9]; longer run 2.4-2.6 [2.3-2.5]. Range: 2023 4.9-5.9 [4.9-5.6]; 2024 3.4-5.6 [3.1-5.6]; 2025 2.4-5.6 [2.4-5.6]; longer run 2.3-3.6 [2.3-3.3].
- (The PDF text interleaves each variable's March row with its "December projection" row; the pairings above follow that order.)

## Figures
- Figure 1: medians, central tendencies and ranges of economic projections, 2023-25 and over the longer run, against actual values.
- Figure 2: "FOMC participants' assessments of appropriate monetary policy: Midpoint of target range" - the dot plot, where "Each shaded circle indicates the value (rounded to the nearest 1/8 percentage point) of an individual participant's judgment" for year-end or the longer run; one participant did not submit a longer-run federal funds rate projection.
- Figures 3.A-3.E: distributions of participants' projections for real GDP growth, the unemployment rate, PCE inflation, core PCE inflation (2023-25 only) and the federal funds rate.
- Figures 4.A-4.C: uncertainty and risks for GDP growth, unemployment and PCE inflation - median projection with a confidence interval "based on root mean squared errors of various private and government forecasts made over the previous 20 years", plus participants' own uncertainty and risk assessments.
- Figure 4.D and 4.E: diffusion indexes of participants' uncertainty assessments and risk weightings - "the number of participants who responded 'Higher' minus the number who responded 'Lower', divided by the total", and the equivalent for "Weighted to the Upside" minus "Weighted to the Downside". Both figures exclude March 2020, "when no projections were submitted".
- Figure 5: uncertainty and risks in projections of the federal funds rate; its confidence interval "is not strictly consistent with the projections for the federal funds rate, primarily because these projections are not forecasts of the likeliest outcomes", and is "assumed to be symmetric except when it is truncated at zero", a truncation that "would not be intended to indicate the likelihood of the use of negative interest rates".

## Table 2 - average historical projection error ranges (percentage points)
- Change in real GDP: 2023 +/- 1.5; 2024 +/- 2.0; 2025 +/- 2.3.
- Unemployment rate: +/- 0.8; +/- 1.4; +/- 1.9.
- Total consumer prices (the overall consumer price index): +/- 1.4; +/- 1.8; +/- 1.7.
- Short-term interest rates (the federal funds rate for Federal Reserve staff forecasts, the 3-month Treasury bill rate for others): +/- 1.0; +/- 2.0; +/- 2.5.
- "Error ranges shown are measured as plus or minus the root mean squared error of projections for 2003 through 2022 that were released in the spring by various private and government forecasters", implying "about a 70 percent probability" that outcomes fall in the implied ranges. Reference: David Reifschneider and Peter Tulip (2017), "Gauging the Uncertainty of the Economic Outlook Using Historical Forecasting Errors: The Federal Reserve's Approach", FEDS 2017-020.

## Forecast Uncertainty box
- Worked example: if projections were for GDP and total consumer prices rising steadily at 3 percent and 2 percent respectively, and uncertainty were similar to the past with balanced risks, table 2 would imply "a probability of about 70 percent that actual GDP would expand within a range of 1.5 to 4.5 percent in the current year, 1.0 to 5.0 percent in the second year, and 0.7 to 5.3 percent in the third year", with corresponding 70 percent intervals for overall inflation of "0.6 to 3.4 percent in the current year, 0.2 to 3.8 percent in the second year, and 0.3 to 3.7 percent in the third year".
- The box notes that projection distributions may not be symmetric - "the unemployment rate cannot be negative" - and that participants separately judge whether uncertainty is greater than, smaller than or broadly similar to typical levels of the past 20 years, and whether risks are weighted to the upside or downside.

wikis.title: AMD launches Helios rack system and MI450 GPUs to rival Nvidia
wikis.summary: Yahoo Finance article (from Quartz) on AMD's launch of its Helios rack-scale AI system and next-generation data centre GPUs, and the Anthropic and Microsoft deals behind it.
wikis.body:
## Article

- Headline: "AMD launches Helios rack system and MI450 GPUs to rival Nvidia".
- By Cris Tolomia, Quartz, carried on Yahoo Finance. "July 23, 2026", "2 min read". Image credit: Ying Tang/NurPhoto via Getty Images.
- Footer: "Copyright © 2026 Yahoo."

## The launch

- "AMD is launching its next generation of AI data center hardware Thursday at an event in San Francisco, seeking to capture market share from Nvidia in the data center chip sector, according to Reuters."
- Helios is described as a "rack-scale system, which combines Instinct MI455X GPUs, EPYC 'Venice' CPUs, Pensando networking chips, and ROCm software in an integrated platform for AI training and inference, AMD said." (The headline instead names "MI450 GPUs".)
- "The company is also expected to formally launch its Venice CPU for data centers, according to Reuters."
- On the Microsoft deal, "AMD positions Helios as its first rival to Nvidia's rack-scale AI systems."

## Anthropic partnership

- Announced "Wednesday": a partnership "to deploy up to 2 gigawatts of Instinct MI450 Series GPUs in Helios rack-scale systems, with the first gigawatt of deployment beginning in the first half of 2027."
- "AMD also committed to make a strategic equity investment of up to $5 billion in Anthropic, the company said."
- "AMD and Anthropic are launching a multi-year engineering collaboration to use Anthropic's Claude AI to optimize workloads for AMD Instinct GPUs and accelerate AMD's ROCm software development. AMD will also adopt Claude across its engineering and product development teams."
- Tom Brown, co-founder and chief compute officer at Anthropic: "Access to compute is central to keeping Claude at the frontier and meeting demand from our customers... By partnering with AMD across the stack, we are securing the capacity we need and optimizing it for training and serving Claude."
- AMD CEO Lisa Su said the Anthropic deal "brings together Anthropic's leadership in frontier AI with the full strength of AMD high-performance computing."

## Microsoft partnership

- "Earlier this week, AMD also announced an expanded partnership with Microsoft, under which Microsoft will deploy Helios on Azure to power frontier model inference."
- "AMD said it expects to begin shipping Helios to customers, including Microsoft, in the second half of 2026."

## Market figures

- "Nvidia commands upward of 95% of the data center GPU market, with AMD holding around 4.5%, according to Futurum Group estimates cited by CNBC."
- "AMD's data center segment posted $5.78 billion in revenue in the first quarter of 2026, a 57% increase from the prior year, driven by demand for EPYC server processors and Instinct GPU shipments."

## Market data shown on the page

- Tickers beside the article: AMD +2.70%, NVDA +1.34%.
- Market strip: S&P 500 7,650.50 (+12.74, +0.17%); Dow 30 51,682.64 (-95.40, -0.18%); Nasdaq 26,522.55 (+104.24, +0.39%); Russell 2000 2,860.40 (-14.23, -0.50%); VIX 14.81 (-0.63, -4.08%); Gold 4,424.90 (+25.20, +0.57%); Bitcoin USD 80,402.39 (-702.65, -0.87%); Crude Oil Oct 26 96.08 (-1.15, -1.18%).

## Naming discrepancy within the page

- The headline says "MI450 GPUs"; the body says Helios combines "Instinct MI455X GPUs" and that the Anthropic deployment uses "Instinct MI450 Series GPUs".

wikis.title: Eli Lilly wins FDA approval for weight loss pill, tees up Novo rivalry
wikis.summary: Yahoo Finance article of 2 April 2026 reporting FDA approval of Eli Lilly's oral GLP-1 orforglipron, branded Foundayo, and how it lines up against Novo Nordisk's Wegovy pill.
wikis.body:
## Approval

- "The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Eli Lilly's orforglipron pill for weight loss, ending Novo Nordisk's first mover advantage in the US after just three months."
- The oral glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) "will be branded under the name Foundayo".
- "Lilly expects to launch the drug on its direct-to-consumer channel by 6 April, with retail pharmacy and telehealth provider availability following soon after."
- The decision was based on the ATTAIN clinical programme, "which demonstrated that patients taking the highest dose of Foundayo who remained on treatment lost an average of 12.4% of their body weight."
- "The approval marks the first new molecular entity (NME) approved under the FDA's national priority voucher (CNPV) programme", a pathway launched by Commissioner Marty Makary "to streamline approvals for drugs that showcased a US-centric potential."
- GlobalData senior analyst Shehroz Mahmood: "The FDA's approval of Foundayo (orforglipron) marks a pivotal moment in the oral GLP-1RA obesity space and validates the CNPV programme, which has led to the fastest new molecular entity approval since 2002."

## Rivalry with Novo Nordisk

- Foundayo competes with Novo's Wegovy pill (semaglutide), "which launched in the US in January 2026".
- Foundayo has no meal restrictions; oral Wegovy "must be taken on an empty stomach each morning".
- As a small molecule, Foundayo has "more straightforward manufacturing and scalability processes" than the peptide-based Wegovy.
- "While no direct head-to-head trials have been conducted, the Wegovy pill on average leads to 2.2% better weight loss."
- Mahmood: "Overall, Lilly faces a fundamentally different competitive challenge than the injectable era, where efficacy superiority enabled Zepbound to overcome Wegovy's first-mover advantage – the oral battleground instead hinges on manufacturing scalability, direct-to-patient marketing reach, and cash-pay pricing strategies, amongst others, each carrying strategic weight."
- "Buoyed by obesity drug sales, Lilly's growth soared by 45% in 2025, contrasting with less lucrative financial results for Novo." Citi analysts forecast that Foundayo's lack of fasting requirements "will place it in pole position to continue Lilly's cardiometabolic dominance".

## Byline

- Robert Barrie, April 2, 2026, 3 min read. Tickers shown alongside: LLY, NOVO-B.CO.

wikis.title: FDA approval letter: Foundayo (orforglipron) tablets, NDA 220934
wikis.summary: The FDA's NDA approval letter to Eli Lilly for Foundayo (orforglipron) tablets for weight reduction, setting out the approved indication, labeling and dating requirements, waived and deferred pediatric studies, and the required postmarketing studies and trials with their timetables.
wikis.body:
## The document

- 12-page PDF headed "NDA 220934 / NDA APPROVAL", addressed to Eli Lilly and Company, "Attention: Ingrid Hensley, PhD, Executive Director, Global Regulatory Affairs – Americas Region, Lilly Corporate Center, Drop Code 2543, Indianapolis, IN 46285".
- "Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) received January 20, 2026, and your amendments, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Foundayo (orforglipron) tablets."
- Indication: "This NDA provides for the use of Foundayo (orforglipron) tablets in combination with a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long term in adults with obesity or adults with overweight in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbid condition."
- "We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling."
- Signed "Lisa B. Yanoff, MD, Deputy Director, Office of Cardiology, Hematology, Endocrinology, and Nephrology, Office of New Drugs, Center for Drug Evaluation and Research"; the appended electronic signature page records "LISA B YANOFF 04/01/2026 09:10:30 AM". Reference ID: 5773652. Regulatory Project Manager: "Arati B. Kamath, PhD... at (301) 796-3159 or Arati.Kamath@fda.hhs.gov". Enclosures: content of labeling (Prescribing Information, Medication Guide) and carton and container labeling.

## Labeling, carton and dating requirements

- Content of labeling must be submitted in structured product labeling (SPL) format via eLIST "no later than 14 days from the date of this letter" and "must be identical to the enclosed labeling".
- Final printed carton and container labeling must be submitted "as soon as they are available, but no more than 30 days after they are printed", designated "Final Printed Carton and Container Labeling for approved NDA 220934"; FDA approval of that submission "is not required before the labeling is used."
- Dating period: "Based on the stability data submitted to date, the expiry dating period for Foundayo (orforglipron) tablets shall be 24 months from the date of manufacture when stored at 20°C to 25°C." Ongoing stability results, including from the first three production lots, go in the annual report.
- "Your application for Foundayo was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion".

## Pediatric assessments (PREA)

- "We are waiving the pediatric study requirement for ages birth to less than 6 years for orforglipron because the product does not represent a meaningful therapeutic benefit over existing therapies for pediatric patients in this age group and is not likely to be used in a substantial number of pediatric patients in this group." Weight loss is not recommended for ages 0–2; for ages 2–6 drug treatment offers no meaningful benefit over diet and lifestyle. This follows draft guidance "Obesity and Overweight: Developing Drugs and Biological Products for Weight Reduction, which recommends that pediatric trials should include subjects aged 6 years and older."
- "We are deferring submission of your pediatric studies for ages 6 to 11 years inclusive and 12 to 17 years inclusive because this product is ready for approval for use in adults and the pediatric studies have not been completed."
- **4977-1**: complete the ongoing 72-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, parallel-arm study J4M-MC-PW01 (ADVANCE-ATTAIN-ADOLESCENTS) in patients aged 12 to less than 18 with obesity. Study completion March 2028; final report submission December 2028.
- **4977-2**: conduct an 84-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study J4M-MC-PW03 in patients aged 6 to less than 12 with obesity. Draft protocol October 2027; final protocol January 2028; March 2031; final report February 2032.
- Protocols go to IND 156143 with a cross-reference letter; reports must be marked "SUBMISSION OF REQUIRED PEDIATRIC ASSESSMENTS".

## Postmarketing requirements under 505(o)

- FDA determined that spontaneous adverse event analysis and the active postmarket risk identification system "will not be sufficient to assess the signal of the serious risk of medullary thyroid cancer, and to identify unexpected serious risks of long-term use in pediatric patients with obesity, and exposure to orforglipron in pregnancy."
- **4977-3**: establish a disease-based pediatric obesity registry and conduct "a registry-based cohort study of at least 10 years duration to describe growth and development (height, weight, and pubertal development by Tanner staging), adverse events (including fractures and malnutrition), and development of obesity-related comorbid conditions." Timetable (per a submission the letter dates once as "March 2025, 2026" and elsewhere as "March 25, 2026"): draft protocol April 2027; final protocol April 2028; interim reports April 2029 through April 2038; final report April 2039.
- **4977-4**: a global prospective pregnancy exposure registry, "preferably a disease-based multi-product pregnancy registry", comparing maternal, fetal and infant outcomes against unexposed comparators, recording "pregnancy complications, major and minor congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, elective terminations, preterm births, small-for-gestational-age births" with infant outcomes "through at least the first year of life." Draft protocol October 2026; final protocol October 2027; interim reports June 2028, 2030, 2032, 2034, 2036, 2037; final report June 2038.
- **4977-5**: an additional pregnancy study of a different design (for example a claims or electronic medical record cohort). Draft protocol February 2027; final protocol February 2028; interim reports September 2030, 2032, 2034; final report September 2035.
- **4977-6**: "a medullary thyroid carcinoma registry-based case series of at least 15 years duration to systematically monitor the annual incidence of medullary thyroid carcinoma in the United States and to identify any increase related to the introduction of orforglipron". Final protocol April 2027; interim reports May 2028 through May 2042 plus August 2042; final report August 2043.
- FDA further determined "that only a clinical trial (rather than a nonclinical or observational study) will be sufficient to assess a signal of a serious risk of retained gastric contents and to identify an unexpected serious risk for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), drug-induced liver injury (DILI), and exposure to orforglipron during lactation."
- **4977-7**: complete the ongoing randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial J2A-MC-GZGS (ACHIEVE-4) with adjudicated MACE ("cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, hospitalization for unstable angina, and nonfatal stroke") and a DILI assessment "including Hy's Law plots, shift tables for liver enzymes and bilirubin, and case reports in FDA-preferred DILI format". Trial completion April 2026; final report July 2026.
- **4977-8**: a clinical pharmacology trial using ultrasound "to measure the effect of both temporary withholding of orforglipron and fasting duration on retained gastric contents to evaluate delayed gastric emptying associated with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) use". Draft protocol March 2027; final protocol September 2027; December 2028; final report March 2029.
- **4977-9**: "Conduct a milk-only lactation study in lactating women who have received a dose of orforglipron to assess concentrations of orforglipron in breast milk using a validated assay." Draft protocol December 2026; final protocol June 2027; June 2028; final report June 2029.
- Clinical protocols go to IND 156143; submissions must be headed "REQUIRED POSTMARKETING PROTOCOL UNDER 505(o)", "REQUIRED POSTMARKETING FINAL REPORT UNDER 505(o)" or "REQUIRED POSTMARKETING CORRESPONDENCE UNDER 505(o)". Status must be reported annually; "Failure to submit an annual report for studies or clinical trials required under 505(o) on the date required will be considered a violation of FDCA section 505(o)(3)(E)(ii) and could result in enforcement action."

## Requested enhanced pharmacovigilance

- "We request that for Foundayo, for a period of 5 years following initial U.S. approval date," Lilly submit "all serious unexpected domestic and foreign postmarketing cases of DILI attributable to orforglipron, resulting in jaundice, liver failure, liver transplant, or death as 15-day “Alert reports”", and provide detailed analyses of potential DILI events, "defined as all cases meeting potential Hy's Law (alanine aminotransferase (ALT) or aspartate aminotransferase (AST) ≥3x ULN with total bilirubin (TB) ≥2x ULN) or having transaminase elevations >10x ULN", in the PADER or PBRER periodic safety report.
- The analyses should assess causality with indication, temporal association, duration of therapy, signs and symptoms, baseline and peak ALT/AST/TB, concomitant therapies, confounders, dechallenge/rechallenge and outcome, plus "a graph displaying sequential ALT, AST, and TB on the y-axis and time (in days) on the x-axis" for cases suggesting causality, and medical literature reviews of DILI case reports.

## Other sections

- Promotional materials: advisory comments may be requested; final promotional materials and the Prescribing Information must be submitted at initial dissemination with Form FDA 2253 under 21 CFR 314.81(b)(3)(i).
- Reporting requirements under 21 CFR 314.80 and 314.81 are restated.
- "New molecular entities qualify for a post approval feedback meeting."
- Compendial standards: a drug with a USP-NF recognised name "generally must comply with the compendial standards for strength, quality, and purity, unless the difference... is plainly stated on its label (see FD&C Act § 501(b), 21 USC 351(b))."

The only date the document states for itself is the electronic signature date, 04/01/2026.

wikis.title: Lilly's weight loss pill wins FDA approval
wikis.summary: EMJ GOLD news item of 2 April 2026 on the FDA approval of Eli Lilly's oral GLP-1 orforglipron, with dosing, launch timing and ATTAIN trial results.
wikis.body:
## Approval

- "Eli Lilly's weight loss pill won FDA approval on Wednesday 1 April." The article itself is dated 2 Apr 2026.
- The glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, orforglipron, "was approved for use in combination with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity, facilitating long-term weight loss in adults with obesity or those with overweight and at least one weight-related comorbid condition."
- "Lilly has reportedly submitted orforglipron for approval for weight management, Type 2 diabetes or a combination of the two in more than 40 countries and has plans to launch shortly."
- "Prescriptions will be accepted immediately and shipping will begin on 6 April, the company said."
- The page does not give the drug a brand name.

## Dosing

- "Orforglipron is a once-daily oral medication with a starting dosage of 0.8 mg that should not be used in combination with another GLP-1."

## The ATTAIN trials

- "Two randomised, double-blind trials saw adults with obesity or overweight with one or more weight-related medical conditions take orforglipron for 72 weeks, in combination with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity."
- ATTAIN-1: "people who continually took the highest dose of orforglipron lost an average of more than 12% of their body weight, compared with around 1% in the placebo cohort."
- "Participants taking the drug, regardless of trial completion, lost an average of more than 10% of their body weight, compared to approximately 2% with placebo."
- "Orforglipron also led to reductions in cardiovascular risk, including waist circumference, non-HDL cholesterol, triglycerides and systolic blood pressure across all doses."
- Dr Deborah Horn (Director of the Center for Obesity Medicine, McGovern Medical School, UTHealth Houston) is quoted saying the drug "delivered an average of 12.4% weight loss at the highest dose in clinical trials", alongside the body text's "more than 12%" figure for ATTAIN-1 completers.

## Quotes

- David A. Ricks, Chair and CEO, Eli Lilly and Company: "Today, fewer than 1 in 10 people who could benefit from a GLP-1 are taking one, held back by access, stigma, perceived complexity or the belief that their condition isn't serious enough for treatment." He adds the drug "can help level the playing field for those living with obesity or who are overweight and living with weight-related complications" and calls it "obesity care designed for the real world."
- Dr Horn: "People living with obesity need treatment options that meet them where they are – and for many, a once-daily pill that can be taken with no food or water restrictions can offer them greater flexibility in how they approach their treatment."

## Byline

- Author: Anna Caldwell, EMJ GOLD. The page states the site "is intended for healthcare professionals" and carries a Creative Commons Attribution-Non Commercial 4.0 licence note.

wikis.title: 'Children Of Blood And Bone' News & Updates: Everything We Know (podcast episode)
wikis.summary: A 29-minute Bookshelf Chronicles episode on Paramount's Children of Blood and Bone film: its January 15, 2027 release, the A-list cast, author Tomi Adeyemi's refusal to watch it, and the absence of sequel plans.
wikis.body:
## The episode
- Podcast: The Bookshelf Chronicles, updated weekly; length 29 minutes, rating Clean. Published "August 30, 2026 at 2:52 PM UTC". The page notes "This episode includes AI-generated content."
- Episode description: "The film adaptation of Tomi Adeyemi's popular fantasy novel, Children of Blood and Bone, is scheduled for a theatrical release on January 15, 2027. Directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood, the movie features a prominent cast including Thuso Mbedu, Amandla Stenberg, and Viola Davis. The story follows a young woman's quest to restore magic to the land of Orisha after it was suppressed by a tyrannical king. While the author co-wrote the screenplay, she has publicly stated that she does not intend to watch the final production due to a difficult experience during the process. Although the original book is part of a trilogy, there are currently no official plans to produce sequels for the big screen."
- The hosts say they are "looking at a really fascinating deadline report from July 29, 2026" about the state of the production.
- Budget figures given in the episode differ: the film is described early on as "a massive $100 million blockbuster adaptation", and later as a "$150 million movie" that Paramount felt the IP could not open on its own.
- Names in the transcript are as transcribed and some spellings vary (for example "Adaimeza"/"Ada Yemi" for Adeyemi, "Prince Bythewood", "King Serena"/"King Saren" for King Saran).

wikis.title: Adapting Orisha's magic system
wikis.summary: Why the book's ancestral, elemental magic is described as a problem for a blockbuster VFX pipeline.
wikis.body:
- In the book the Magi are "deeply tethered to elemental and spiritual forces" - water workers controlling tides, soul summoners like Zelie's mother Jumoke - "not a wand waving incantation based system like you'd see in Harry Potter", but "an intrinsic biological and spiritual connection to the environment".
- King Saran's purge is "framed explicitly as a strike against something he deems unnatural", which the hosts read as an allegory "for cultural erasure ... the suppression of indigenous practices": "The magic in Orisha isn't just a weapon, it's an identity."
- The VFX argument: blockbuster magic "is almost always kinetic ... energy blasts, shields, glowing geometric shapes" and easily programmable, but rendering soul summoning so it conveys "historical trauma and cultural lineage" without looking like "a glowing blue ghost from Ghostbusters" is the trap.
- One host counters that water and fire are solved problems; the reply is that "the contextual application is where the friction happens": if a water worker's magic is rendered like Avatar: The Last Airbender's martial-arts elemental combat, "it strips the narrative of its weight", while studios want "clarity and spectacle" for a global audience and trailers.
- The claim: focus-group pressure would push toward reshoots or "a massive VFX overhaul to make it punchier", and "the moment you optimize cultural trauma for a four quadrant of popcorn demographic, you break the core truth of the source material."

wikis.title: The casting strategy and its budget logic
wikis.summary: An unusually A-list roster for a YA adaptation, and why the hosts read it as studio anxiety.
wikis.body:
- The standard YA economic model (The Hunger Games, The Maze Runner, Twilight) is "relatively unknown, inexpensive young actors in the leads", one or two veteran character actors "like Donald Sutherland in Hunger Games", and the rest of the budget on VFX and marketing, keeping above-the-line costs low.
- "Paramount did the exact opposite here", reuniting the core team from The Woman King (2022): director Gina Prince-Bythewood, Thuso Mbedu starring as Zelie and Viola Davis as Mama Agba.
- Supporting cast named in the episode: Cynthia Erivo "coming off Wicked" as Admiral Kea, Idris Elba as Lekhan, Lashana Lynch as Jamoke, Chiwetel Ejiofor as King Saran, Regina King as Queen Nahanda, plus Amandla Stenberg and Damson Idris. The hosts call it "a staggering concentration of A-list, Oscar-winning, and global franchise talent ... essentially unprecedented for this genre".
- Two performers (transcribed as "Pimler Naideji and Shams Garuba") were brought in "via an open casting call in Nigeria, which is amazing for grounding the cultural roots".
- The reading: hiring Elba, Davis and King buys "global marketing reach", because "Paramount clearly felt that the IP of Children of Blood and Bone, despite being a massive bestseller, wasn't strong enough on its own to open a $150 million movie globally."
- The cost to the script: "script economy is a zero-sum game" in a roughly 120-page film, so ten pages of King Saran backstory for Chiwetel Ejiofor means ten pages cut from Zelie's journey or Zane's development, and a too-charismatic king risks the audience "empathizing with the oppressor over the oppressed teenagers".

wikis.title: Prince Inan and the problem of ambiguity
wikis.summary: How the story's morally torn prince is said to sit badly with a four-quadrant blockbuster.
wikis.body:
- The report is said to note that Zelie and her brother Zain must team up with "the literal children of King Saran" - Amari and Prince Inan.
- "Prince Inan, played by Damson Idris, harbors doubts about taking his father's crown and following his ruthless example" - the "sins of the father" trope, compared to "a corporate whistleblower scenario" where "the heir of a corrupt dynasty realis[es] the family business is totally toxic".
- The adaptation problem: a novel can give 20 pages of internal monologue about guilt and indoctrination, but film has "only action and dialogue" short of "a really clunky voiceover", so screenwriters "have to invent external conflicts that just don't exist in the book".
- The hosts argue studio pressure would flatten him: "The studio apparatus hates ambiguity. Ambiguity doesn't sell toys, and it doesn't play well in test screenings", pushing Inan into "a definitive box" - brainwashed villain or instantly reformed hero - which "completely destroys the thematic weight of his character arc" and "lets the audience off the hook".

wikis.title: Tomi Adeyemi's co-writing credit and her public boycott
wikis.summary: The centrepiece: the author shares the screenplay credit yet says she will not watch the film.
wikis.body:
- "Tomi Adeyemi, the author of the book, is officially credited as the co-writer of the screenplay alongside director Gina Prince-Bythewood."
- "She took to Instagram, posted a video describing her time on set, called the experience explicitly painful, and stated unequivocally that she will not be watching the film."
- On what a writing credit is worth: in publishing "the author has the final say on the manuscript", but in film "the writer is essentially a below-the-line employee" and "once the script is locked and production begins, the director is the absolute authority on set". The WGA arbitrates credits, "but a credit does not equal on-set power" - if the director or studio wants an explosion where the script had a quiet ancestral ritual, the author has "no legal mechanism to stop them".
- Scripts are also rewritten during production by improvisation, blocking changes and studio notes, so for an author used to complete control, "painful is probably an understatement".
- On the PR mechanics: such statements are "almost unheard of" because creatives are usually bound by non-disclosure and non-disparagement clauses; saying "my experience was painful and I won't watch it" is treated as "a legally gray area ... expression of personal boundaries rather than a direct libel". The hosts read it as "a firewall" signalling to her fan base that the film "is not my final product".

wikis.title: The January 15, 2027 release date
wikis.summary: Whether a mid-January slot with a six-month trailer lead is a burial or counter-programming.
wikis.body:
- "Paramount slated the film for January 15th, 2027. The trailer was released way back in late July 2026" - "almost a six-month marketing window".
- The traditional reading is that "January is the graveyard", the "dump month" where studios "quietly bury movies that tested poorly".
- The counter-argument: "the economics have shifted slightly in the last decade" because a spectacle film in "a barren January landscape faces literally zero competition" and can have the IMAX screens to itself; "Movies like American Sniper or Black Panther, which released in February, proved that early-year windows can be incredibly lucrative if the movie is an event."
- Conclusion given: "We can't say it definitively based only on the date", but combined with the sequel news "the picture becomes incredibly bleak for the future of the IP."

wikis.title: No plans for the sequels
wikis.summary: Why capping a completed trilogy at one film is read as the studio cutting its losses.
wikis.body:
- The trilogy is complete: "Children Virtue and Vengeance was published in 2019, and Children of Anguish and Anarchy wrapped up the saga in 2024. The IP is proven, the fan base is completely established, and the narrative roadmap is fully written."
- "Yet, the report explicitly states there are currently no plans to adapt the next two books."
- Normally a studio "options a trilogy and greenlights the sequels concurrently" for economies of scale - it is "exponentially cheaper to leave [a set] standing and shoot the sequel six months later" - and to lock in actors before their quotes "skyrocket".
- The hosts' conclusion: the studio "decided that moving forward was actually a higher financial risk than just walking away", comparing it to "a venture capital firm pulling their funding right before a Series B round because the founding CEO went rogue".
- Marketing logic: every sequel press junket would face "the author hates this, why are you still making it?", and "A YA franchise lives and dies by its core fandom" - without Adeyemi's endorsement "the franchise has a built-in ceiling".

wikis.title: Adeyemi's pivot to The Siren and future deals
wikis.summary: The author's new novel and how the hosts expect her to negotiate the next adaptation.
wikis.body:
- "The report notes she is releasing a new novel, The Siren, at the end of September."
- The hosts frame publishing as "an autocracy" where "A blank page doesn't have a visual effects budget, it doesn't require notes from a marketing executive in Burbank, and it doesn't have to accommodate the schedule of an A-list actor."
- They judge it "highly unlikely a commercial author intentionally writes an unadaptable book because the financial incentives of a film option are simply too large to ignore"; what changes is "the legal architecture of the deal".
- Expected demands next time: "an executive producer credit with contractual veto power over the director" or "final cut approval on the script before cameras roll", "something almost exclusively reserved for legacy writers like J.K. Rowling or Stephen King".
- Closing framing: the on-screen fight against a system erasing intrinsic magic mirrors "an author fighting a massive monolithic studio system", and the finished film "is the surviving wreckage of a collision between art and commerce".

wikis.title: Exorcist II: The Heretic
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 1977 film Exorcist II: The Heretic - its plot and cast, John Boorman's troubled production, box office, its famously hostile reception, home media releases and legacy.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- 1977 American supernatural science fiction horror film directed by John Boorman, written by William Goodhart, based on characters by William Peter Blatty. Produced by Boorman and Richard Lederer; distributed by Warner Bros.
- Stars Linda Blair, Richard Burton, Louise Fletcher, Max von Sydow, Kitty Winn, Paul Henreid and James Earl Jones. Cinematography William A. Fraker; edited by Tom Priestley; music by Ennio Morricone.
- Released in the United States on June 17, 1977. Running time 102 minutes. Budget $14 million; box office $30.7 million.
- "It is the second installment in The Exorcist film series and the sequel to The Exorcist (1973)" and "was the last film to feature veteran actor Paul Henreid before his death on March 29, 1992."
- Set four years after the first film, it centres on "the now 16-year-old Regan MacNeil, who is still recovering from her previous demonic possession".
- "The film received generally negative reviews from critics and is often considered to be one of the worst films ever made. Despite earning over $30 million domestically against a $14 million production budget, the negative reception meant that the next film in The Exorcist series would not come until The Exorcist III on August 17, 1990."

## Plot
- Father Philip Lamont, a priest struggling with his faith, botches an exorcism in Latin America in which the possessed woman dies in a fire. He is assigned to investigate the death of Father Lankester Merrin, who is facing posthumous heresy charges over his writings "as Church authorities are trying to modernise and do not want to acknowledge that Satan exists".
- Regan, living in New York with guardian Sharon Spencer, is monitored by Dr. Gene Tuskin, who hypnotises her using a "synchronizer", "a revolutionary biofeedback device used by two people to synchronize their brainwaves".
- Linked to Regan, Lamont is taken by Pazuzu to witness Merrin exorcising a boy, Kokumo, in Africa; he travels to Africa to find the adult Kokumo, now a scientist studying how to prevent locust swarms, and learns Pazuzu attacks people with psychic healing abilities. Regan telepathically helps an autistic girl to speak.
- Merrin belonged to "a group of theologians that believed psychic powers were a spiritual gift that would one day be shared by all people" and saw Kokumo and Regan as forerunners of a new humanity.
- At the Georgetown house, Pazuzu tempts Lamont as a succubus doppelganger of Regan; a taxi crashes into the house, Sharon sets herself on fire, Lamont kills the doppelganger, and Regan banishes the locusts with the bullroarer ritual Kokumo had attempted. Sharon dies and Tuskin tells Lamont to watch over Regan.

## Cast
- Linda Blair (Regan MacNeil), Kitty Winn (Sharon Spencer), Richard Burton (Father Philip Lamont), Louise Fletcher (Dr. Gene Tuskin), Max von Sydow (Father Lankester Merrin), Paul Henreid (Cardinal Jaros), James Earl Jones (Kokumo), Joey Green (Young Kokumo), Ned Beatty (Edwards), Dana Plato (uncredited), Karen Knapp (uncredited voice of Pazuzu).

## Development
- Neither Blatty nor Friedkin wanted to be involved, having filed lawsuits against the studio and each other "over profits, credits, and Blatty being barred from post-production during the first film".
- Co-producer Richard Lederer described the original plan: "What we essentially wanted to do with the sequel was to redo the first movie... Have the central figure, an investigative priest, interview everyone involved with the exorcism, then fade out to unused footage, unused angles from the first film. A low-budget rehash - about $3 million - of The Exorcist, a rather cynical approach to movie-making, I'll admit."
- Playwright William Goodhart wrote the screenplay, titled The Heretic, based around the theories of Pierre Teilhard de Chardin, the Jesuit who inspired Father Merrin; it took "a more metaphysical and intellectual approach", centring good and evil on human consciousness.
- Sam O'Steen initially agreed to direct but never attached; John Boorman signed on, saying "the idea of making a metaphysical thriller greatly appealed to my psyche". He had earlier turned down the original film, finding the story "rather repulsive", but saw in the sequel "the chance to make an extremely ambitious film without having to spend the time developing this connection".

## Casting
- Linda Blair returned but "refused to wear demon make-up" (a double was used for flashbacks). Max von Sydow was persuaded back despite concerns about the first film's impact. Kitty Winn returned as Sharon after "Ellen Burstyn flatly refused to return as Chris MacNeil".
- William O'Malley could not return as Father Dyer, so the character became Father Philip Lamont. Jon Voight, David Carradine, Jack Nicholson and Christopher Walken were considered or offered the part; Voight signed but left in April 1976 when "differences about the role could not be resolved", and was replaced by Richard Burton.
- Dr. Gene Tuskin was originally written for a man (Chris Sarandon and George Segal considered); after the change, Ann-Margret and Jane Fonda were considered, and Louise Fletcher - fresh from her Best Actress Oscar for One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest - took the role.

## Filming and production problems
- Principal photography began at Burbank Studios on May 24, 1976 with a budget of $11 million; "the film ultimately cost $14 million to make".
- Location plans (including Ethiopia and the Vatican) proved impossible, so key exteriors were shot on the Warner Bros. backlot; the MacNeil house and the "Hitchcock Steps" had to be replicated because permission was refused. Two weeks were filmed in the New York area, including a rooftop scene atop 666 Fifth Avenue with "no stunt person and no special effects", and scenes at Pennsylvania Station in Newark, New Jersey.
- Boorman was unhappy with Goodhart's script; Goodhart refused a rewrite incorporating Rospo Pallenberg's ideas, so Pallenberg and Boorman rewrote it, with constant rewriting during shooting and no settled ending. Linda Blair: "It was a really good script at first. Then after everybody signed on they rewrote it five times and it ended up nothing like the same movie."
- Problems included Boorman contracting San Joaquin Valley fever, cancelling production for over a month; oversaturated footage requiring reshoots; imported locusts dying (2,500 shipped in, dying at 100 a day); editor John Merritt quitting, replaced by Tom Priestley; and gallbladder infections for Kitty Winn and Louise Fletcher.
- Blair said Pallenberg "directed a lot of the film as well as did rewrites"; he was credited as second unit director and "creative associate".

## Box office
- "The Heretic was Warner Bros.'s largest day and date launch, opening in 725 theatres in the United States and Canada" and setting an opening weekend record for the studio with $6.7 million, "but poor word of mouth dramatically hampered its performance". It grossed $30,749,142 in the United States, "turning a profit but still disappointing in comparison to the original film's gross".

## Critical reception
- The premiere in New York reportedly drew derisive laughter; Blatty claimed to have been the first to laugh ("You'd think we were watching The Producers"). Friedkin recalled a story of angry audience members chasing Warner Bros. executives down the street within ten minutes, and called the film "a stupid mess made by a dumb guy - John Boorman by name", "the worst piece of crap I've ever seen" and "a freaking disgrace", adding "That film was made by a demented mind."
- Variety: "Exorcist II is not as good as The Exorcist. It isn't even close." Mark Kermode: "Exorcist II is demonstrably the worst film ever made." Gene Siskel gave zero stars out of four, calling it "the worst major motion picture I've seen in almost eight years on the job". John Simon, Vincent Canby, Time's Christopher Porterfield, Alexander Walker, Fernando Trueba in El Pais and many others were similarly dismissive; Leonard Maltin called it a "preposterous sequel" whose "Special effects are the only virtue in this turkey".
- Dissenting views: Pauline Kael preferred it to the original, writing that it "had more visual magic than a dozen movies"; Kim Newman found it "very interesting"; Martin Scorsese said "The Heretic surpasses it. Maybe Boorman failed to execute the material, but the movie still deserved better than it got."
- Bob McCabe's The Exorcist: Out of the Shadows (2000) quotes Blair calling it "one of the big disappointments of my career" and Boorman: "The sin I committed was not giving the audience what it wanted in terms of horror... There's this wild beast out there which is the audience. I created this arena and I just didn't throw enough Christians into it." McCabe notes that in a list of The 50 Worst Movies Ever Made it "came in at number two", beaten only by Plan 9 from Outer Space.
- Boorman in 2005: "I saw [it] as a kind of riposte to the ugliness and darkness of The Exorcist... I denied them what they wanted and they were pissed off about it - quite rightly... But it had one of the most disastrous openings ever - there were riots! And we recut the actual prints in the theatres, about six a day, but it didn't help."
- "As of January 2025", Rotten Tomatoes gives 10% from 69 reviews, average 3.6/10, with the consensus "Hokey mystical effects, lousy plotting, and worse acting directly tarnishes the first's chilling legacy." Metacritic: 39 out of 100 from 11 critics, "generally unfavorable".

## Home media and legacy
- Originally on VHS in the United States, with a LaserDisc released only in Japan; VHS reissue December 4, 1992 from Warner Home Video; first DVD August 6, 2002 in Snapcase packaging, a second DVD November 3, 2009, and inclusion in "The Complete Anthology" DVD set of all five franchise films on October 10, 2006.
- Blu-ray debut September 23, 2014, individually and in the Complete Anthology. On September 25, 2018 Scream Factory released a two-disc "Collector's Edition" with the theatrical cut, "a shorter alternative version of the film", new interviews with Linda Blair and editor Tom Priestly and commentaries from Boorman and consultant Scott Bosco; Arrow Video gave it a Region B release on October 7, 2024 with five commentary tracks in total.
- "Boorman and the Devil (2025), a documentary film about Exorcist II: The Heretic's troubled production, was released."
- Bibliography listed includes Barbara Pallenberg's The Making of Exorcist II: The Heretic (1977) and Declan Neil Fernandez's Horrible and Fascinating - John Boorman's Exorcist II: The Heretic (2022).

wikis.title: Sonic the Hedgehog 2 (2022 film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Paramount's 2022 Sonic sequel directed by Jeff Fowler - its Master Emerald story, cast including Idris Elba's Knuckles, Vancouver and Hawaii shoot, record video-game-film opening and $405.4 million gross.
wikis.body:
## The film

- A 2022 action-adventure comedy film based on the Sonic video game series, the second in the Sonic film series, directed by Jeff Fowler from a screenplay by Pat Casey, Josh Miller and John Whittington. Production companies Original Film, Marza Animation Planet and Blur Studio; distributed by Paramount Pictures. 122 minutes; United States and Japan; English. Budget $90–110 million; box office $405.4 million.
- Ben Schwartz, Jim Carrey, James Marsden, Tika Sumpter, Natasha Rothwell, Colleen O'Shaughnessey and Adam Pally reprise their roles, with Shemar Moore and Idris Elba joining. Sonic and Tails race Dr. Robotnik and Knuckles to the Master Emerald; the emerald shatters into the seven Chaos Emeralds and Sonic becomes Super Sonic. A tag has Agent Stone overhear Commander Walters learning of the facility housing Project Shadow.
- Tom Holkenborg scored the film; Kid Cudi's "Stars in the Sky" was the only original song.

## Production

- Paramount confirmed the sequel in May 2020, with Fowler, Casey, Miller and the cast returning. It is inspired by Sonic the Hedgehog 2 (1992), Sonic the Hedgehog 3 and Sonic & Knuckles (both 1994) without adapting any of them - Fowler called it "a melting pot".
- Idris Elba was announced as Knuckles on August 10, 2021, after Jason Momoa had been reported as a candidate in February 2021.
- Principal photography began in Vancouver on March 15, 2021 under the working title "Emerald Hill"; Vancouver filming concluded on May 12 and filming wrapped in Hawaii on June 25. Visual effects came from Marza Animation Planet and MPC, with 185 shots from DNEG.

## Release and reception

- Released internationally on March 30, 2022 (UK April 1), premiered in Los Angeles on April 5, released in the United States on April 8 and in Japan on August 19. The Russian release, set for March 31, was postponed in response to the Russian invasion of Ukraine.
- Rotten Tomatoes 69% from 182 reviews (average 6/10); Metacritic 47 from 33 critics; CinemaScore "A"; PostTrak 87% positive.
- $190.9 million in the United States and Canada and $214.5 million elsewhere for $405.4 million worldwide. Its $72.1 million three-day opening beat the original's $58 million and Bruce Almighty's $68 million to become Jim Carrey's highest three-day domestic opening and Paramount's biggest since 2014, and broke the video-game-adaptation opening record until The Super Mario Bros. Movie ($146.4 million) a year later.
- Won Favorite Movie at the Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards and Best Movies for Families at the Movieguide Awards; nominated for Best Adaptation at The Game Awards and Outstanding Voice Performance (Idris Elba) at the Black Reel Awards.

## Follow-ups

- Sonic the Hedgehog 3 was released theatrically on December 20, 2024 and the Knuckles spin-off series on Paramount+ on April 26, 2024; Sonic the Hedgehog 4 "will be released in 2027".

wikis.title: Sonic the Hedgehog 2 (2022 film) - plot, cast, production, release, box office and reception
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Paramount's 2022 Sonic sequel directed by Jeff Fowler, covering its story, cast, Vancouver and Hawaii shoot, marketing, $405.4 million box office, mixed reviews and awards.
wikis.body:
## The film

- "Sonic the Hedgehog 2 is a 2022 action-adventure comedy film based on the Sonic video game series." The second film in the Sonic film series, directed by Jeff Fowler from a screenplay by Pat Casey, Josh Miller and John Whittington, with story by Casey and Miller. Based on Sonic the Hedgehog by Sega.
- Produced by Neal H. Moritz, Toby Ascher, Toru Nakahara and Hitoshi Okuno; cinematography Brandon Trost; edited by Jim May; music by Tom Holkenborg. Production companies Original Film, Marza Animation Planet and Blur Studio; distributed by Paramount Pictures.
- Release dates: March 30, 2022 (International); April 8, 2022 (United States); August 19, 2022 (Japan). Running time 122 minutes. Countries United States and Japan; language English.
- Budget $90–110 million; box office $405.4 million.
- "In the film, Sonic and his friend Tails (O'Shaughnessey) embark on a journey to find the Master Emerald before their nemesis, Dr. Robotnik, and his accomplice, Knuckles the Echidna (Elba)."
- "Like its predecessor, it set several box office records for a video game film and received mixed reviews from critics."
- Sonic the Hedgehog 3 and the television spin-off Knuckles were released in 2024, "while Sonic the Hedgehog 4 will be released in 2027".

## Music

- Tom Holkenborg, composer of the first film, was announced on December 8, 2021 as returning to score the film.
- The film was supported by the single "Stars in the Sky" by Kid Cudi, "the only original song recorded for the film". The soundtrack album was released by Paramount Music on April 8, 2022.

## Home media

- Released for download and streaming on Paramount+ on May 24, 2022; EPIX added it the same day under Paramount's pay-one-window deal. DVD, Blu-ray and Ultra HD Blu-ray followed on August 9, 2022.
- The digital and Blu-ray releases come with an exclusive short film, Sonic Drone Home, animated by Marza Animation Planet, written by Pat Casey and Josh Miller, directed by David Nelson and produced by Moritz, Ascher, Nakahara and Okuno. Sonic, Tails and Knuckles face one of Robotnik's drones in Green Hills' scrapyard; Schwartz reprises Sonic, while Tails, Knuckles and the drone Unit are voiced by Alicyn Packard (replacing O'Shaughnessey), Fred Tatasciore (replacing Elba) and Aaron Landon.

## Sequel film and television series

- In February 2022, Sega of America and Paramount Pictures confirmed Sonic the Hedgehog 3 and a Knuckles spin-off miniseries were in development. Elba reprises Knuckles for the series, released on Paramount+ on April 26, 2024 after being delayed from 2023 by the 2023 Actors and Writers Strike.
- Sonic the Hedgehog 3 was released theatrically on December 20, 2024, with Schwartz returning and Casey, Miller and Whittington writing. Filming began in July 2023 in Farnham, Surrey, England, "albeit with no actors due to the 2023 SAG-AFTRA strike".
- In April 2022, after Carrey said he was considering retirement, producers Moritz and Ascher confirmed his Robotnik role would not be recast if he retired, though they hoped for scripts good enough to keep him; in February 2024 it was confirmed Carrey would reprise the role.

## Inconsistencies inside the page

- Opening-weekend projection: the Box office section says the film "was projected to gross at least $55 million from 4,232 theatres in its opening weekend", while the cited Deadline Hollywood headline reads "Sonic The Hedgehog 2 To Keep Spring Thing Going With $50M+ Start".
- Filming dates: the lead says "Filming took place from March to June 2021 in Vancouver and Hawaii", while the Filming section says the BC Film Commission listed production as running March 15 to May 10, 2021, that Vancouver filming concluded on May 12 and that filming wrapped in Hawaii on June 25.

wikis.title: Plot of Sonic the Hedgehog 2
wikis.summary: The film's story as the article summarises it, from Robotnik's return to the Master Emerald's shattering and the Project Shadow tease.
wikis.body:
- Sonic lives with the Wachowskis and acts as a vigilante hero with little success. Tom advises patience and leaves with Maddie for her sister Rachel's wedding in Hawaii, leaving Sonic in charge of the house.
- Sonic is ambushed by Dr. Robotnik, who has escaped the mushroom planet he was banished to, and Knuckles, an echidna warrior who is his newest henchman. Knuckles demands the location of the Master Emerald - "an ancient relic that grants its user ultimate power and the ability to change reality to their will" - to bring honor to his ancestors. Miles "Tails" Prower rescues Sonic and warns him about Knuckles.
- Following clues on a map from Sonic's late guardian Longclaw, Sonic and Tails find a compass in a temple in Siberia. Knuckles reveals he lost his whole tribe the same day Sonic lost Longclaw, but he and Robotnik steal the compass. Knuckles grows suspicious of Robotnik when he mocks Sonic for saving an injured Tails instead of the compass before an avalanche.
- Tom uses a ring to teleport Sonic and Tails to the wedding, where Rachel's fiancé Randall and the guests reveal themselves as undercover G.U.N. agents who set up the wedding to capture Sonic and Tails, and arrest Tom. Maddie and a vengeful Rachel save them; Rachel reconciles with Randall after he confirms his feelings are real. Meanwhile Knuckles and Robotnik find an underwater temple containing the Master Emerald.
- Sonic faces Knuckles alone at the temple; Robotnik seizes the emerald, collapsing and sinking the temple, then betrays Knuckles. Sonic and Knuckles rescue one another and escape as a recovered Tails arrives in a biplane.
- In Green Hills, Robotnik uses the emerald to build a giant robot resembling himself. Sonic, Tails and Knuckles fight it; the emerald shatters in Sonic's hands into the seven Chaos Emeralds, and Sonic inadvertently transforms into Super Sonic, destroying the robot and letting Robotnik collapse with it. Knuckles repairs the Master Emerald and makes a pact with Sonic and Tails to protect it.
- While G.U.N. searches for Robotnik, Agent Stone poses as a soldier and overhears Commander Walters receiving information about a secret research facility - the one housing Project Shadow.

wikis.title: Cast of Sonic the Hedgehog 2
wikis.summary: The voice and live-action cast listed in the article, with the notes on Elba's Knuckles and O'Shaughnessey's Tails.
wikis.body:
## Voice

- Ben Schwartz as Sonic the Hedgehog, "an anthropomorphic blue hedgehog with superhuman speed"; archival recordings of Benjamin L. Valic as young Sonic are used in flashbacks.
- Colleen O'Shaughnessey as Miles "Tails" Prower - "the only voice cast member from the Sonic the Hedgehog video games to reprise her role for the film", after voicing him in the first film's post-credits scene.
- Idris Elba as Knuckles the Echidna, newly cast. Elba prepared by exploring the character's backstory and identity; Fowler wanted a portrayal reminiscent of Knuckles's early appearances, saying "his entire existence is about honor and about being a warrior" and describing him as "a force of nature".
- Donna J. Fulks as Longclaw, an anthropomorphic owl, Sonic's late caregiver and the former guardian of the Master Emerald.

## Live-action

- Jim Carrey as Doctor Robotnik; James Marsden as Tom Wachowski, sheriff of Green Hills, Montana; Tika Sumpter as Maddie Wachowski; Natasha Rothwell as Rachel, Maddie's older sister; Adam Pally as deputy Wade Whipple; Lee Majdoub as Agent Stone; Tom Butler as Commander Walters, Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and now leader of G.U.N.; Shemar Moore as Randall Handel, Rachel's fiancé and a G.U.N. agent; Melody Nosipho Niemann as Jojo, Rachel's daughter.

wikis.title: Development, casting, filming and visual effects
wikis.summary: How the sequel was greenlit after the first film, the casting of Knuckles, the Vancouver and Hawaii shoot under the working title Emerald Hill, and the effects vendors.
wikis.body:
## Development

- In April 2020 James Marsden expressed interest in a sequel featuring game characters including Tails, who appeared in the first film's mid-credits scene. Jeff Fowler wanted a sequel focused on Sonic and Tails' friendship and developing Dr. Robotnik. Ben Schwartz said it made sense Paramount had not announced a sequel because of the COVID-19 pandemic.
- In May 2020 Paramount confirmed a sequel was in development with Fowler returning to direct and Casey and Miller writing; Moritz, Ascher and Nakahara producing (having co-produced the first film alongside Takeshi Ito), and Tim Miller, Hajime Satomi and Haruki Satomi returning as executive producers.
- In December 2020 storyboard artist Fill Marc confirmed Tyson Hesse, who redesigned Sonic for the first film, would return. The title was announced in February 2021; in May a synopsis was released via a Paramount copyright registration.
- "The film is inspired by the video games Sonic the Hedgehog 2 (1992), Sonic the Hedgehog 3, and Sonic & Knuckles (both 1994), but is not a direct adaptation of either." Fowler described it as "a melting pot" of ideas from several Sonic games.

## Casting

- On January 27, 2020 Jim Carrey said Robotnik could be expanded: "I wouldn't mind going to do another one because it was so much fun, first of all, and a real challenge to convince people that I have a triple-digit IQ... There is so much room, you know, Robotnik has not reached his apotheosis."
- On March 6 Marsden confirmed he had signed for multiple sequels; the rest of the returning cast, including Carrey, was confirmed through 2021. In February 2021 Jason Momoa was reported as being considered for Knuckles. Shemar Moore joined on June 16, later confirmed as Randall; Idris Elba was announced as Knuckles on August 10.
- For the Japanese dub, the Hololive Production-affiliated VTuber Inugami Korone, the Japanese brand ambassador of the Sonic series, voiced a character.
- Shadow the Hedgehog made his live-action debut in a non-speaking cameo in the mid-credits scene, meant to tease a larger role in future films.

## Filming

- In December 2020 the BC Film Commission listed production as occurring from March 15 to May 10, 2021, under the working title "Emerald Hill", a reference to the opening zone of the Sonic the Hedgehog 2 video game. In January 2021 Tika Sumpter revealed the film would shoot in Vancouver and Hawaii.
- Principal photography began in Vancouver on March 15, 2021 with Brandon Trost as cinematographer. Carrey held a raffle on May 7 to give away a Chevrolet Blazer as thanks to the crew; the car went to a grip. Vancouver filming concluded on May 12 and filming wrapped in Hawaii on June 25.

## Visual effects and animation

- Visual effects and animation were provided by Sega's Marza Animation Planet and Moving Picture Company (MPC), both of which worked on the first film. John Whittington was announced as co-screenwriter on August 10, 2021.
- DNEG provided the visual effects for the mushroom planet and the robot's cockpit, "giving it a total of 185 shots used in the film from the studio". Additional services came from Animism Studios, Fish Flight Entertainment, Fatbelly VFX, Unit Motion Design and Track VFX; Unlisted Studio produced the animation for the Master Emerald backstory.

wikis.title: Release and marketing
wikis.summary: The staggered international and US release, the postponed Russian release, and the trailer, poster and tie-in campaign.
wikis.body:
## Theatrical release

- On March 1, 2022 Paramount announced it would postpone the film's Russian release, originally scheduled for March 31, until further notice in response to the Russian invasion of Ukraine. On March 14, when US tickets went on sale, an early access "Fan Event" screening was announced for April 6.
- It was first released in several international markets including France, the Philippines and the Netherlands on March 30, 2022, and the United Kingdom on April 1, 2022.
- The world premiere was at the Regency Village Theatre in Los Angeles on April 5, 2022; it was theatrically released in the United States on April 8, 2022.

## Marketing

- The teaser poster was revealed on December 8, 2021 and the first trailer released at The Game Awards 2021 the next day, including a reworked version of Masato Nakamura's "Emerald Hill Zone" music from the original game. "Fans reacted very positively, with Elba as Knuckles attracting particular praise", in contrast to the first film's initial trailer of April 30, 2019.
- Paramount released four TV spots in the week before Super Bowl LVI, revealing the Giant Eggman Robot, plus a special spot during the Super Bowl on February 13, 2022.
- "The theatrical release poster excluded O'Shaughnessey's name, leading to fan outcry." Updated posters shortly after added her name and Sumpter's to the upper billing block.
- The second and final trailer was released on March 14, 2022, alongside a poster resembling the North American box art of the original Sonic the Hedgehog 2 game.
- Paramount spent less than $18 million on US television spots, generating 717 million impressions. On March 29, 2022 King partnered with Sega and Paramount on a special edition of Candy Crush Saga; The Mill did the visuals for the Happy Meal advertisements.

wikis.title: Box office performance
wikis.summary: The film's record-setting opening, its North American and international takings and the records it set and lost.
wikis.body:
- Grossed $190.9 million in the United States and Canada and $214.5 million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $405.4 million.
- In the US and Canada it opened alongside Ambulance and the wide expansion of Everything Everywhere All at Once, projected to gross at least $55 million from 4,232 theatres. With a target audience aged 16 to 25, its release coincided with the start of spring break in 15% of K-12 schools.
- It made $26.8 million on its first day including $6.25 million from Thursday night previews, doubling the original's figure, and $72.1 million over the three-day opening weekend - surpassing the original's $58 million and Bruce Almighty's $68 million to become Jim Carrey's highest three-day domestic opening and Paramount's biggest three-day opening since 2014. Six million tickets were sold in the US and Canada that weekend.
- "It broke the opening record for a video game movie adaptation, which was previously held by the original Sonic the Hedgehog and was surpassed a year later by The Super Mario Bros. Movie ($146.4 million)."
- Opening audiences: 61% male; 46% aged 18-34 and 32% below 17; ethnic breakdown 38% Hispanic/Latin American, 29% Caucasian, 20% African American, 13% Asian or other.
- It had the best pandemic-era opening for a children's film, the all-time seventh best April opening, the second best opening of early 2022 and the fifth best opening since 2020.
- Second weekend $29.3 million, second behind Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore; it returned to the top on Easter Monday with $4.5 million. By its third weekend it surpassed the original to become the highest-grossing video game film in North America, and it stayed in the top ten until dropping out in its twelfth weekend. It was the ninth-highest-grossing film of 2022 in the US and Canada.
- Internationally it opened in 31 markets with $26.1 million in its first weekend, outpacing the original. France took $1.2 million on its first day, topping the charts and beating the first film's opening day by 30%. In the United Kingdom it debuted at number one and retook the top spot from Fantastic Beasts in its fourth weekend with GBP 20.2 million in four weeks.
- It crossed $300 million worldwide by its fifth weekend and $400 million by its thirteenth.

wikis.title: Critical response and accolades
wikis.summary: The film's aggregate scores, a range of published reviews, the Stobotnik fan response, and the awards it won and was nominated for.
wikis.body:
## Critical response

- Rotten Tomatoes: 69% approval from 182 reviews, average 6/10. Consensus: "It isn't as much fun as the little blue guy's greatest games, but if you enjoyed the first film, Sonic the Hedgehog 2 serves as a generally acceptable sequel."
- Metacritic: 47 out of 100 from 33 critics, "mixed or average reviews". CinemaScore "A" (the same as the first film); PostTrak 87% positive, with 74% saying they would definitely recommend it.
- Amy Nicholson (The New York Times), positive: "Jim Carrey's reprised role as a villainous weirdo helps this fast-paced, family-friendly video-game-movie sequel maintain a refreshing silliness."
- Nell Minow (Rogerebert.com), two of four: "Yes, we know we're appropriating details from better movies. It is over-plotted, with three different storylines mixing comedy and adventure."
- Alex Stednan (IGN), seven of ten: it "brings all the humor and charm of its predecessor, while also being delightfully more loyal to its source material."
- Carlos Aguilar (The Wrap), positive; Leslie Felperin (The Guardian), three of four: "there's not very much to say about it, other than it's mildly amusing and reasonably competently assembled."
- Brian Shea (Game Informer), 8.5 of 10: the film "clears the higher bar, delivering a better movie in nearly every way." Ross Bonamie (Collider), "C+".
- John Nugent (Empire), two of five: "Sonic's second outing is little more than a half-baked half-term distraction tool — though Jim Carrey's outrageously committed performance nearly saves the day." Brian Lloyd (Entertainment.ie), three of five: "Idris Elba as Knuckles is the most galaxy-brain casting idea ever conceived of."
- Bob Hoose (Plugged In), positive. Thomas Floyd (The Washington Post), two of four: "it's especially perplexing that this video game-inspired sequel should be, of all things, a bit sluggish." Siddhant Adlakha (IndieWire), "C−": "It's visual soup where nothing pops or stands out."
- "Fan reactions to the evolving relationship between Agent Stone and Doctor Robotnik in the film were favorable, prompting the creation of shipping and fan fiction, sometimes under the name Stobotnik, that was acknowledged by Majdoub and Carrey."

## Accolades

| Award | Date | Category | Recipient(s) | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The Game Awards | December 8, 2022 | Best Adaptation | Sonic the Hedgehog 2 | Nominated |
| Golden Trailer Awards | October 6, 2022 | Best Animation/Family Poster | Sonic the Hedgehog 2 (WORKS ADV) | Nominated |
| Black Reel Awards | February 6, 2023 | Outstanding Voice Performance | Idris Elba | Nominated |
| Movieguide Awards | February 26, 2023 | Best Movies for Families | Sonic the Hedgehog 2 | Won |
| Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards | March 4, 2023 | Favorite Movie | Sonic the Hedgehog 2 | Won |
| Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards | March 4, 2023 | Favorite Movie Actor | Jim Carrey | Nominated |
