wikis.title: Why the Unemployment Rate Fell While Hiring Slowed in 2026 (Fexingo podcast, 11 August 2026)
wikis.summary: Podcast episode explaining how the July 2026 US jobs report showed a 23,000 payroll loss alongside unemployment falling from 4.2 to 4.1 percent, attributing it to a shrinking labor force.
wikis.body:
## The episode

- "The Labor Market Podcast with Fexingo: Jobs Reports, Unemployment, and Wage Growth", episode "Why the Unemployment Rate Fell While Hiring Slowed in 2026". Season 4, Episode 156. Length 8 min. Rating Clean. Show frequency "Updated Daily".
- Published August 11, 2026 at 6:42 PM UTC (page label "August 11"). Hosts named as Lucas and Luna.

## The puzzle in the July 2026 jobs report

- "the July jobs report landed last Friday, and the headline was brutal: the U.S. economy lost 23,000 jobs. That's the first negative print in years."
- "the unemployment rate actually fell, from 4.2 percent down to 4.1 percent."
- The description frames it as: "the unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1 percent even as nonfarm payrolls shrank by 23,000 jobs".

## The explanation given

- Two surveys: the 23,000 job loss "comes from the establishment survey - it asks businesses how many people they have on the payroll", while the unemployment rate "comes from the household survey - it asks individuals whether they're working or looking for work".
- "In July, they diverged in a big way. The establishment survey showed payrolls shrinking, but the household survey showed the number of unemployed people actually dropping."
- "the unemployment rate only falls if people either find jobs or leave the labor force entirely. And in this case, it's the latter." "The labor force participation rate has been drifting down, and in June we saw 111,000 workers just leave the labor force."
- "When the unemployment rate falls because people are dropping out, it's a very different signal than when it falls because hiring is robust. The Fed looks at this and sees a labor market that's cooling, not one that's tight."

## Other figures quoted

- Job openings "down to 7.36 million in June from 7.54 million in May".
- Average hourly earnings "still up around 3.5 percent year-over-year", cooled "from the 4 percent plus peaks we saw a couple years ago" but "still above the pre-pandemic trend of around 3 percent".
- Weekly earnings "are actually doing better" than hourly, "because hours worked have been creeping up".
- Initial jobless claims "hovering around 199,000, which is historically very low"; "layoffs remain at record lows".

## Interpretation offered

- "Labor hoarding": "After the pain of trying to hire during the post-pandemic recovery, companies are reluctant to let people go." So "the low unemployment rate is almost masking the underlying weakness".
- If participation recovered, "the unemployment rate could actually tick up, even if the economy is adding jobs".
- The Fed "have already cut rates a couple of times this year, and the market is pricing in more cuts. But if the unemployment rate stays low and wages keep growing, they might be less inclined to move aggressively." The Fed is described as "in a wait and see mode".
- For workers: "layoffs are still rare, so job security is relatively high", but "the pace of hiring is slowing, which means it might take longer to find a new job if you do lose yours".
- By sector: "Some sectors, like health care and government, are still adding jobs consistently. But others, like manufacturing and retail, are flat or even shrinking."
- Stated takeaway: "the unemployment rate falling to 4.1 percent isn't the good news it might seem. It's really a story about people leaving the labor force, not about a booming job market."

## What the hosts say comes next

- "We'll be keeping an eye on the August report, which comes out in early September. If the participation rate starts to recover, we could see the unemployment rate jump, even if hiring improves."

wikis.title: How the Russell 2000 Is Pricing In a 2027 Recession (Fexingo podcast, 4 July 2026)
wikis.summary: Podcast episode arguing that the Russell 2000's weakness against a record S&P 500 may be pricing in a 2027 recession, with the index levels, P/E spread and volatility readings quoted.
wikis.body:
## The episode

- "The Stock Market Podcast with Fexingo: Daily Equities, Earnings, and Wall Street Conversations", episode "How the Russell 2000 Is Pricing In a 2027 Recession". Season 2, Episode 91. Length 8 min. Rating Clean. Show frequency "Updated Daily".
- Published July 4, 2026 at 8:45 PM UTC (the page also shows a "July 4" label).
- Hosts named in the description as Lucas and Luna.

## Market levels quoted

- S&P 500 at 7,483. The description says "up 1.8% on the week"; the transcript says "up nearly 2% on the week".
- Russell 2000 at 2,996, "down 0.5%" on the week.
- Dow "hit 52,900"; the NASDAQ "added 2.1%".
- VIX at 15.81, "down 8.5% on the week". VVIX at 88.80, "basically unchanged on the week".
- Fed funds rate "still at 3.63%, flat since June".

## The divergence argument

- "Small caps have been underperforming large caps for most of 2026." "The Russell is still roughly 15% below its all-time high from late 2021, while the S&P 500 is up about 20% from that same peak" - described as "a four-and-a-half-year period of basically flat to negative returns" for an index "that historically compounds at about 10% a year".
- Valuation: "the Russell 2000's forward price to earnings ratio is currently around 14.5. The S&P 500's forward P/E is about 22. That's a spread of roughly 7.5 multiple points". The transcript calls that "the widest it's been since the early 2000s, outside of the 2020 pandemic dip"; Apple's episode description instead calls it "the Russell's 35-year-low relative valuation versus the S&P 500".
- Why small caps sell off first: the Russell is "dominated by domestic, cyclical companies - regional banks, industrials, consumer discretionary names", while mega caps ("Apple, Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet") "have global revenue streams, huge cash piles, and products people buy regardless of the cycle".
- Rate sensitivity: "Small companies are much more sensitive to interest rates because they carry more floating-rate debt. And they can't issue bonds at 4% like Apple can." Referred to as "a long lag effect from the rate hikes that started in 2022".
- Index composition: about 2,000 companies, "many of them are unprofitable", median market cap "around $1.5 billion", and "a lot of companies that went public during the 2020-2021 SPAC boom. Many of those have been terrible investments."

## Volatility read

- The VIX at 15.81 says "large-cap options traders are complacent", while "the Russell's behavior says the real economy is not complacent at all".
- On the VVIX ("essentially the volatility of the VIX"): at 88.80 and flat, "the fear of fear isn't really spiking, but it's not collapsing either. That's a kind of uneasy calm," suggesting "there's a tail risk that people are hedging against, even if the headline VIX is low".

## Positioning discussion (hedged, both sides given)

- The bull case: selective quality small caps "with positive free cash flow, low debt, and revenue growth that's not dependent on a booming economy" are at "a discount relative to both history and large-cap peers"; and "some analysts arguing that the small-cap discount is a buying opportunity precisely because the market is pricing in a recession that might not happen".
- Timing: "If a recession hits in 2027, that's a year and a half away. The market usually starts to recover about six months before the recession ends."
- The bear case: "The Russell could get cheaper before it gets better. The spread could widen to 10 multiple points." If the recession happens, "the Russell goes lower, and the mega caps hold up better".
- Counter-point on mega caps: "If the economy slows enough, even Apple's services revenue will dip. And the valuations on mega caps are higher, so there's more room for multiple compression."
- Conclusion offered: "the risk-reward for selective small caps - quality ones - looks more attractive than it has in years. But I wouldn't buy the index blindly."
- Takeaways to watch: the Russell 2000 versus S&P 500 gap narrowing, and "if the VIX stays low but the VVIX starts spiking, that's a warning sign".

## Note

- The 2027 recession is discussed throughout as something the market may be pricing in, not as a forecast the hosts assert: "whether small-cap weakness is pricing in a 2027 recession or just a rotation that hasn't run its course yet".

- The host describes it as an episode of "The Terminal List: After Action", going "through the new Season 2 trailer shot by shot, looking at the story, characters, military details, weapons, gear and the connections to both The Terminal List: Dark Wolf and Jack Carr's True Believer."
- Spoiler warning: "This breakdown contains spoilers for Jack Carr's True Believer novel as we compare the source material with what Prime Video appears to be setting up for Season 2."

## What the trailer is said to show

- "James Reece's exile in Africa and the London terrorist attack", plus Raife Hastings, Freddy Strain, Jules Landry, Mo Farooq "and some major True Believer clues".
- Covered: "James Reece's life in exile, Rich Hastings in Mozambique, Katie Buranek following the #WhereIsJamesReece trail, Raife Hastings working the intelligence picture, the London attack that kills 113 people, Freddy Strain bringing Reece back into the fight, Jules Landry's potentially much darker role, and the possibility that we're already seeing pieces of the Odessa storyline."
- Weapons and gear: "the suppressed H&K MP7, M4-pattern rifles, Reece's SIG P226/MK25, what appears to be a SIG Spear, CQB sequences, sniper/observer positions and rotary-wing operations — including some personal thoughts from my own experience with the MP7, M4-family rifles and P226."
- "Mo Farooq appears to be wearing an Eastern Arabic-dial Seiko 5 on a NATO strap — so naturally I wore mine for the episode."
- "With Chris Pratt returning as James Reece, and characters from Dark Wolf carrying directly into Season 2, this is looking much bigger, more international and far more espionage-driven than Season 1."
- Questions put to listeners: what they spotted in the trailer, whether Jules Landry will follow his True Believer storyline, whether Freddy Strain makes it out of Season 2, and how closely the series will follow the Odessa storyline.
- "The Terminal List Season 2 premieres October 21 on Prime Video."

- "The Irish government is expected to spend €58 million on the event, with €22.5 million of that cost going to an event licence fee from the European Tour."

"The Western Rail Corridor, Limerick to Foynes and Clonmel to Thurles railway lines must reopen on time for the event to reduce road traffic."

wikis.title: Super Bowl LXII
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Super Bowl LXII, the NFL championship game for the 2027 season, scheduled for 13 February 2028 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, with host selection and broadcast arrangements.
wikis.body:
## The game

- "Super Bowl LXII is the planned American football championship game of the National Football League (NFL) for the 2027 season. The game is scheduled to be played on February 13, 2028, at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia."
- Short description: "2028 National Football League championship game". A hatnote records that "2028 Super Bowl" redirects here, and points to Super Bowl LXIII for "the Super Bowl at the completion of the 2028 season".
- "This game will be the fourth Super Bowl hosted by the city of Atlanta. It will also be the second at this venue, the first being Super Bowl LIII in 2019."
- Infobox: Date February 13, 2028; Stadium Mercedes-Benz Stadium, Atlanta, Georgia; previous LXI, next LXIII. Image caption: "Mercedes-Benz Stadium decorated for Super Bowl LIII in 2019".
- No teams, coaches, referee, record, ratings or commercial figures are filled in.

## Host selection

- "The league has made all decisions regarding hosting sites from Super Bowl LVII onward. There is no bidding process per site. The league selects a potential venue unilaterally, the chosen team puts together a hosting proposal, and then the league votes to determine whether it is acceptable."
- "On October 15, 2024, the NFL announced that Mercedes-Benz Stadium, home of the Atlanta Falcons, was selected as the Super Bowl site."

## Broadcasting

- United States television: "Super Bowl LXII is scheduled to be televised by CBS. It will be the fifth Super Bowl to be broadcast as part of the 11-year NFL television contract, which allows a four-year rotation between CBS, Fox, NBC, and ABC/ESPN." The infobox adds Univision (Spanish) as a broadcast network, with SAP on CBS.
- Streaming: "planned to be streamed live on Paramount+, as well as NFL+ via mobile devices". The infobox also lists Vix (Spanish).
- Radio: "Westwood One holds the national radio rights to the game."
- International: in the United Kingdom and Ireland "the game will be televised on the free-to-air Channel 5, which is partially league-owned and part of the CBS Sports family"; in Latin America by ESPN and Disney+; in Germany and Austria "by TBC".

## Cited sources (titles and dates as given)

- Myles Simmons, "Super Bowl LXII will be played on February 13, 2028", Pro Football Talk, July 24, 2026.
- Herbie Teopie, "Arizona, New Orleans chosen as Super Bowl hosts", NFL.com, May 23, 2018.
- "Atlanta to Host Super Bowl LXII in 2028", atlantafalcons.com, October 15, 2024.
- Jonathan Jones, "NFL announces Atlanta will host Super Bowl LXII in 2028, marking fourth time city landed big event", CBS Sports, October 15, 2024.
- Joe Lucia, "Westwood One has a new deal with the NFL, with all primetime games available for free in the NFL app", Awful Announcing, March 28, 2022.

## Page metadata

- Categories include "2027 NFL season", "2028 in American football", "2028 in Atlanta", "Scheduled sports events".
- A navbox on the page lists this game as "LXII (2027)" in the AFC package carrier sequence, i.e. by season rather than by the February 2028 playing date.

wikis.title: Path of the Total Solar Eclipse of 2033 Mar 30
wikis.summary: NASA/GSFC eclipse page by Fred Espenak tabulating the umbral path of the 30 March 2033 total solar eclipse at 120-second intervals, with greatest eclipse and duration.
wikis.body:
## What the page is

- "Path of the Total Solar Eclipse of 2033 Mar 30" by Fred Espenak.
- The table "delineates the path of the Moon's umbral shadow", giving WGS 84 geographic coordinates of the northern and southern limits and the central line "at 120-second intervals".
- Central-line local circumstances listed: ratio of the apparent diameters of the Moon to the Sun, the Sun's altitude and azimuth (degrees), path width (kilometers) and duration (minutes and seconds).
- Links offered to an Orthographic Map, Google Map, Animated Map, Path Table, Besselian Elements Table and Saros 120 Table.

## Path figures

- Tabulated Universal Times run from 17:42 to 18:20, with "Limits" rows at each end.
- Opening limits row: 64°51.8'N 175°18.1'E (north) / 58°04.0'N 179°28.4'W (south) / 60°56.7'N 178°26.4'E central line; diameter ratio 1.043; path width 744 km; duration 02m13.6s.
- Closing limits row: 78°56.8'N 156°01.1'E / 84°39.7'N 124°22.7'E / 82°28.4'N 142°55.2'E central line; ratio 1.043; width 758 km; duration 02m13.4s.
- Maximum tabulated central duration is 02m37.0s at 18:00–18:02 UT; the widest tabulated path is 834 km at 17:48.
- ΔT = 78.9 seconds.

## Greatest eclipse and greatest duration

- Greatest Eclipse (GE): Time = 18:01:16.4 UT, Lat = 71°18.9'N, Long = 155°48.5'W; Sun altitude 11.2°, Sun azimuth 111.1°; path width 781.0 km; central duration 02m37.0s.
- Greatest Duration (GD): Time = 18:01:00 UT, Lat = 71°10'N, Long = 155°54'W; Sun altitude 11.2°, Sun azimuth 110.9°; path width 782.3 km; central duration 02m37.0s.

## Method and caveats

- "Predictions for the Total Solar Eclipse of 2033 Mar 30 were generated using the VSOP87/ELP2000-85 solar and lunar ephemerides and a value of ΔT = 78.9 seconds."
- "The eclipse predictions presented here DO NOT include the effects of mountains and valleys along the edge of the Moon. Such corrections for the lunar limb profile may shift the limits of the eclipse path north or south by ~1-3 kilometers, and change the eclipse duration by ~1-3 seconds. More detailed predictions including the effects of the lunar limb profile are normally posted 12-18 months before each eclipse".
- Acknowledgment requested: "Eclipse Predictions by Fred Espenak, NASA's GSFC".

## Date on the page

- The page ends with the bare date "2014 Feb 26", with no label saying whether it is a publication or revision date; the page states no published or last-updated date in words.

wikis.title: Path of the Total Solar Eclipse of 2043 Apr 09 (NASA/GSFC)
wikis.summary: Fred Espenak's NASA eclipse-path page for the total solar eclipse of 2043 April 09, giving the umbral path table, its limits, ΔT and the method behind the predictions.
wikis.body:
## What the page gives

"The following table delineates the path of the Moon's umbral shadow during the Total Solar Eclipse of 2043 Apr 09." Geographic coordinates (WGS 84) of the northern and southern limits and the central line are listed "at 120-second intervals", which the page says "provides adequate detail for making plots of the path on larger scale maps". Local circumstances on the central line are said to include the ratio of the apparent diameters of the Moon to the Sun, the Sun's altitude and azimuth (degrees), the path width (kilometers) and the duration on the central line (minutes and seconds). Author credit: Fred Espenak.

## The table in this capture

Headed "Total Solar Eclipse of 2043 Apr 09" and then marked **"Non-Central Eclipse"**. The rows present are:

- Limits — 62 16.0N 166 38.9E (northern limit) / 62 16.0N 166 38.9E (southern limit); no central-line, ratio, altitude, azimuth, width or duration values
- 18:56 (Universal Time) — 61 15.8N 152 00.8E (northern limit); the remaining columns are blank
- Limits — 63 54.9N 165 55.0E / 63 54.9N 165 55.0E; remaining columns blank

So although the page's title calls it a total solar eclipse, the table is labelled a non-central eclipse and the central-line columns carry no values.

- ΔT = 86.4 seconds.

## Method and caveats

- "Predictions for the Total Solar Eclipse of 2043 Apr 09 were generated using the VSOP87/ELP2000-85 solar and lunar ephemerides and a value of ΔT = 86.4 seconds."
- "The eclipse predictions presented here DO NOT include the effects of mountains and valleys along the edge of the Moon. Such corrections for the lunar limb profile may shift the limits of the eclipse path north or south by ~1-3 kilometers, and change the eclipse duration by ~1-3 seconds."
- "More detailed predictions including the effects of the lunar limb profile are normally posted 12-18 months before each eclipse".
- Acknowledgments: "All eclipse calculations are by Fred Espenak, and he assumes full responsibility for their accuracy." Reuse is permitted with the credit "Eclipse Predictions by Fred Espenak, NASA's GSFC".

## Related links the page offers

Orthographic Map, Google Map, Animated Map, Besselian Elements Table, **Saros 149 Table**, Eclipse Predictions, plus decade tables of solar eclipses (1901–2100), the World Atlas of Solar Eclipse Maps, the Javascript Solar Eclipse Explorer, the Solar Eclipse Search Engine (-1999 to +3000) and the Five Millennium Canon of Solar Eclipses.

The page ends with an unlabelled date line, "2014 Feb 26".

wikis.title: MetroLink given green light by An Coimisiún Pleanála
wikis.summary: RTÉ News report that An Coimisiún Pleanála granted the Railway Order for Dublin's MetroLink, with the route, the conditions attached and the remaining Cabinet approval step.
wikis.body:
## The decision

- "Permission has been granted for Dublin's long-awaited MetroLink project linking the city centre to the airport."
- "An Coimisiún Pleanála published the Railway order this morning which gives construction for the MetroLink Project the green light."
- "It is almost three years since An Comisiún Pleanála began considering whether to give the green light to the plans, after Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII) applied for the Railway Order in **November 2022**."

## The project

- "The MetroLink plan consists of a new **18.8km** railway line, most of which will be underground, from **Charlemont** near Dublin city centre to **Swords Estuary** in the north of the county."
- "The project was first mooted in the year **2000**, but it was shelved during the financial crisis." Later in the piece: "A metro for Dublin was first proposed **over 25 years ago** with repeated attempts made across decades."
- An artist's impression on the page shows the Ballymun entrance to MetroLink.

## Conditions attached

- Conditions include "complying with certain requirements to ensure protection of amenities and the preservation of features of heritage importance".
- An expert panel "will have to review and sign off on 'assessments' of certain locations including the area around Charlemont Station", largely focused on "sensitive buildings" and "protected structures", "to ensure both protection of architectural heritage and to mitigate the risk of building damage during construction".
- Proposals must also be submitted where construction will disrupt residential services and activities. Examples given: before development commences the developer "shall make an alternative training facility for Fingallians GAA"; in Glasnevin, removal of car parking spaces at one apartment complex, **The Court**, "will require the developer making an alternative number of spaces available for affected residents until the completion of Glasnevin Station".

## Reaction and next steps

- Minister for Transport **Darragh O'Brien** called it a "critical nation-building project for Ireland's future": "MetroLink will be transformative for the people of North Dublin and - by linking directly with Dublin airport, DART, heavy rail, Luas and bus services - the entire country." He added it "will provide a fast, high capacity, high frequency public transport route, and it will enable the construction of tens of thousands of new homes."
- "While it has now been given the green light by An Comisiún Pleanala, it must get **final Cabinet approval** before construction can begin."
- "Construction is expected to take several years with the **final costs not yet known**."
- "The plans for MetroLink have raised concerns by many regarding cost overruns and delays."

## Byline

- By Karen Creed and Samantha Libreri, RTÉ News. "Updated / Thursday, 2 Oct 2025 23:25".

wikis.body:
## What the page is

The English-language home page of the "Senate Department for Economic Affairs, Energy and Public Enterprises" on Berlin.de. It is mostly a set of teasers linking on to sections, each with a line of text and a "More information" link.

## Sections and their teaser text

- **Berlin - The Right Location** — "Berlin offers excellent conditions for every type of company. Find out why."
- **Business Support** — "We support business through various activities and partners. Find out why Berlin is the right place to start a business and about the kind of support we offer using the links below."
- **Economics and Technology** — "Berlin - the Citiy of Technology, Zukunftsorte and Smart City." (the page's own spelling)
- **Startups** — "The Berlin startup ecosystem has developed into an indispensable and stable pillar of the Berlin economy."
- **Tourism** — "A key sector in Berlin."
- **Funding Partners** — "In Berlin, a broad spectrum of funding is not just designed to promote innovative business ideas and investment, but also to support current businesses."
- **Zukunftsorte** — "Zukunftsorte are sites with potential space for development and a strong link to science and research."
- **Brexit** — "If you consider relocating your business, Berlin is the place to be. The capital of the EU's strongest economy offers ideal conditions for any kind of business."
- **Point of Single Contact** — "Entrepreneurs in Berlin (as well as aspiring entrepreneurs) can take care of their official business tasks conveniently and securely online on this website and thus save any unnecessary time to visit local authorities."

## People and contact

- **Franziska Giffey** — "Mayor of Berlin and Senator for Economic Affairs, Energy and Public Enterprises."
- Senate Department for Economic Affairs, Energy and Public Enterprises, Martin-Luther-Straße 105, 10825 Berlin.
- Telephone: +49 (0) 30 9013-0. E-Mail: post@senweb.berlin.de.

## DIWI chatbot

The page carries a chatbot notice, given in German: "Hallo, ich bin der DIWI-Chatbot – Ihr digitaler Lotse für wirtschaftsbezogene Fragen an die Berliner Verwaltung. Ich befinde mich aktuell in einer Pilotphase und verbessere mich stetig." It says the bot uses AI ("Dabei setze ich KI ein") and may consult several sources, so answers can take longer; feedback goes to ea@senweb.berlin.de. Users are told: "Bitte geben Sie keine persönlichen, sensiblen oder betrieblichen Daten ein (z. B. Namen, Adressen, Telefonnummern, Geburtsdaten, interne Firmendaten)." The chat can be used in English or another language.

The page also links an accessibility statement and the State Commissioner for Digital Accessibility. It states no publication or last-updated date.

## Market

- Question: "Fed decision in October?", under the FED category; page title adds "Odds & Predictions 2026".
- Page shows "Begins in 38 days · Oct 28, 1:00pm EDT".
- Series KXFEDDECISION; event KXFEDDECISION-26OCT; highlighted market KXFEDDECISION-26OCT-H25. Volume shown: $1,947,655 vol. Noted as mutually exclusive.

## Odds shown on the page

| Outcome | Chance | Yes | No |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hike 25bps | 55% | 55¢ | 46¢ |
| Fed maintains rate | 44% | 45¢ | 56¢ |
| Hike >25bps | 2% | 2¢ | 99¢ |

"Fed Rate After Meeting" strikes: Above 3.75% 98% (No 2¢); Above 4.00% 58% (up 1, Yes 58¢ / No 43¢); Above 4.25% 2% (Yes 2¢ / No 99¢); "8 more".

The order ticket shows Hike 25bps at YES 55¢ / NO 46¢ and "Odds 57% chance", against the 55% in the list. Max payout date Oct 28, 2026.

## Rules

- "Hike 25bps" resolves Yes if the Federal Reserve does a hike of 25bps on October 28, 2026. Outcome verified from the Federal Reserve.
- Mutually exclusive: "if the Federal Reserve hikes by 50bps, the 50bps market will resolve to Yes and the 25bps market will resolve to No. Only one bucket, at maximum, can resolve to Yes."
- "Note 4/28/25: For the markets beginning after the May meeting, if a scheduled FOMC meeting is canceled and does not occur on its scheduled date, then the strike for 'Fed maintains rate' will resolve to Yes and all others will resolve to No."

## Timeline and payout

- Market open: Sep 29, 2025 · 10:00am EDT. Market closes: Oct 28, 2026 · 1:59pm EDT. Projected payout: Oct 28, 2026 · 2:09pm EDT.

## About text on the page

"The FOMC meeting determines interest rate policy. Hiking rates cools down the economy and combats inflation, cutting rates stimulates growth, and keeping rates stable reflects confidence in current conditions. Fun fact: The Federal Reserve's first interest rate cut was in response to the 1929 stock market crash!" Sourced from the St. Louis Fed.

wikis.title: Frank R. Bowerman Landfill Fact Sheet
wikis.summary: Two-page OC Waste & Recycling fact sheet on the Frank R. Bowerman Landfill in Irvine, California, covering its history, capacity, hours, environmental systems and landfill-gas power plant.
wikis.body:
## The site

- Frank R. Bowerman Landfill, Central Region, Irvine, California — "Commercial Disposal Only".
- Location: 11002 Bee Canyon Access Rd., Irvine, California 92602. Phone 949-551-7100; OCLandfills.com; social handle @ocwaste.
- Opened in 1990; owned and operated by the County of Orange.
- "One of the largest landfills in the United States" and "one of the first lined landfills in California".
- Accepts non-hazardous, municipal solid waste from commercial haulers only.
- "Maximum permitted daily refuse is 11,500 tons".
- "Approximately 725 acres with about 534 acres to be used for waste disposal".
- "Converts landfill gas to energy, which powers more than 25,000 average Orange County homes".
- "Open space is the planned end-use of the site".
- Bee Canyon Greenery Composting Facility opened in 2020.

## History

- The landfill opened in 1990 and "was originally called the Bee Canyon Landfill because it is located in Bee Canyon. The area was once used for beekeeping."
- "The name was changed to honor Frank R. Bowerman after his retirement from the County of Orange. Mr. Bowerman was the first director and chief engineer of the department, and was he was responsible for the Bee Canyon Landfill's planning and development." (wording as printed)

## Operating hours and access

- Monday–Saturday; 7 a.m. - 4 p.m. for all commercial customers; 4 p.m. - 5 p.m. for transfer trucks only; closed on major holidays.
- "No public disposal allowed"; commercial self-haul "must have valid business licenses or contractors cards".
- Public services: landfill tours — free tours are offered and scheduled via http://www.oclandfills.com/landfill/landfill_tours.

## Environmental protection

- "Composite liner system to protect groundwater."
- "Landfill gas monitoring, recovery, and control systems with more than 120 wells."
- Groundwater monitoring wells; groundwater collection system; leachate collection and recovery system.
- Load check inspectors "to collect and dispose of any hazardous waste"; radioactive waste observation program.
- "Erosion, fire, dust, insect, rodent, bird, noise, and litter control systems."
- "Approximately 45 acres have been restored and include wetland, riparian and coastal sage scrub habitats."
- Mattress recycling and metals salvaging operation.

## Renewable energy

- "In April 2016 Bowerman Power began operation of a renewable energy power plant that utilizes landfill gas to produce up to 22 megawatts of electricity."

## Regulation

- "OC Waste & Recycling works cooperatively with regulators to ensure that the landfill operates in full compliance with all Federal, State, and Local codes, ordinances, and regulations."
- Subject to regular inspections from CalRecycle and its local enforcement agency, the California Regional Water Quality Control Board, and the South Coast Air Quality Management District.

## Awards listed

- American Society of Civil Engineers — Outstanding Energy Project
- Energy Association of Engineers — Innovative Energy of the Year Project
- Orange County Business Council — Sustainable and Green Development
- SWANA — Gold Excellence

## Document

- PDF, 2 pages, marked "Revised Dec. 2020" — a month only, with no day given.

wikis.title: Intel launches the Movidius Neural Compute Stick
wikis.summary: Intel Newsroom news byte of 20 July 2017 announcing the Movidius Neural Compute Stick, a USB-based deep learning inference kit, with its price, specs and availability.
wikis.body:
## Announcement

- Intel Newsroom "News Byte", dated July 20, 2017 (PDF, 3 pages).
- "Today, Intel launched the Movidius Neural Compute Stick, the world's first USB-based deep learning inference kit and self-contained artificial intelligence (AI) accelerator that delivers dedicated deep neural network processing capabilities to a wide range of host devices at the edge."
- Aimed at product developers, researchers and makers; meant to reduce barriers to developing, tuning and deploying AI applications in a small form factor.

## Hardware and performance

- Quote from Remi El-Ouazzane, vice president and general manager of Movidius, an Intel company: "The Myriad 2 VPU housed inside the Movidius Neural Compute Stick provides powerful, yet efficient performance – more than 100 gigaflops of performance within a 1W power envelope – to run real-time deep neural networks directly from the device. This enables a wide range of AI applications to be deployed offline."

## Capabilities listed

- **Compile**: automatically convert a trained Caffe-based convolutional neural network (CNN) into an embedded neural network optimized for the onboard Movidius Myriad 2 VPU.
- **Tune**: layer-by-layer performance metrics for industry-standard and custom neural networks; validation scripts compare the accuracy of the optimized on-device model against the original PC-based model.
- **Accelerate**: the device can act as a discrete neural network accelerator, adding dedicated deep learning inference to existing computing platforms.

## Availability and price

- "Movidius Neural Compute Stick is now available for purchase through select distributors for MSRP $79 and at the conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) in Honolulu, Hawaii, from July 22-25."

## Context given

- The release frames Intel's AI portfolio: training on the Intel Nervana cloud, Intel Xeon Scalable processors for emerging workloads (AI, VR/AR, automated driving), and Movidius vision processing unit (VPU) technology at the edge.
- It describes machine intelligence development in two stages: training an algorithm on large sets of sample data, and running it in an end-application ("inference"), with edge inference benefiting latency, power consumption and privacy.
- The archived page carries later Intel Newsroom items dated April 2021 in its sidebars (for example "SD Supercomputer Center Selects Habana, Intel for Efficient AI", April 8, 2021).

wikis.title: Sonic the Hedgehog (2020 film)
wikis.summary: The English Wikipedia article on the 2020 Sonic the Hedgehog film, covering its credits, plot, cast, the decades of abandoned adaptations, the trailer backlash that forced a redesign and three-month delay, and its record video-game-film opening.
wikis.body:
## The film

- "*Sonic the Hedgehog* is a 2020 action-adventure comedy film based on the *Sonic* video game series", the first in the *Sonic the Hedgehog* film series, directed by Jeff Fowler in his feature debut and written by Pat Casey and Josh Miller.
- Produced by Neal H. Moritz, Toby Ascher, Toru Nakahara and Takeshi Ito for Original Film, Marza Animation Planet and Blur Studio; distributed by Paramount Pictures. Score by Tom Holkenborg.
- Premiered at the Paramount Pictures lot on January 25, 2020; released in the United States on February 14, 2020 and in Japan on June 26, 2020 after a pandemic delay from March 27. Running time 99 minutes; budget $85-90 million; box office $320 million.
- Ben Schwartz voices Sonic, with James Marsden as Sheriff Tom Wachowski, Jim Carrey as Dr. Robotnik, Tika Sumpter as Maddie, Natasha Rothwell, Adam Pally and Neal McDonough. Colleen O'Shaughnessey reprises Tails uncredited in the mid-credits scene.

## A long road to the screen

Development began in 1993; a 1994 MGM and Trilogy Entertainment deal produced Richard Jefferies's 1995 treatment *Sonic: Wonders of the World* before MGM cancelled it, and later attempts by Ben Hurst and by Ken Penders (*Sonic Armageddon*, pitched 2003, dropped 2007) also failed. Sony acquired the rights in 2013 and announced a Columbia Pictures / Marza Animation Planet co-production in June 2014; Jeff Fowler was hired to direct in 2016; Paramount acquired the project in October 2017 after Sony put it in turnaround. The working title during production was "Casino Night".

## The redesign

The December 2018 teaser poster and the April 2019 trailer drew heavy criticism of Sonic's humanoid design - Gita Jackson of Kotaku called the trailer "horrific" and "a blight upon this weary earth", and co-creator Yuji Naka was "shocked". Fowler announced the redesign on May 2, 2019 and the film moved from November 8, 2019 to February 14, 2020. Tyson Hesse was brought on to lead the redesign (the article also says "Sonic was redesigned by Marza Animation Planet"), which "added an estimated $5 million to the production budget, took around five months, and was achieved without overtime." The second trailer, released November 12, 2019, "received thousands of likes and the highest like-to-dislike ratio of any trailer on Google in the last three years", and the trailers together drew more than 500 million views.

## Reception

- Opened to $58 million over three days and $70 million over the four-day President's Day weekend, "breaking *Detective Pikachu*'s record for the biggest opening weekend by a video game-based film", and on March 14, 2020 became the highest-grossing video game film in US box office history.
- Worldwide $320 million - $149 million in the United States and Canada, $170.7 million elsewhere - the sixth-highest-grossing film of 2020 and "the highest-grossing superhero film of the year, ending Marvel Studios' decade-long run".
- Mixed reviews: Rotten Tomatoes 64% from 252 reviews (average 5.9/10), Metacritic 47/100 from 42 critics, CinemaScore "A".
- Jim Carrey won Best Villain in a Movie and Ben Schwartz Best Animated or VFX Performance at the 2021 Critics' Choice Super Awards and Hollywood Critics Association Awards respectively; other nominations included the Saturn Awards and Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards.

## Sequels

*Sonic the Hedgehog 2* (2022), *Sonic the Hedgehog 3* (2024), the Paramount+ miniseries *Knuckles* (April 2024) with Idris Elba, and a fourth film announced in December 2024 "set to release in theatres on March 19, 2027."

The second part of the capture is external links, the Sonic media navigation boxes and the category list; no published or last-updated date is stated.

wikis.title: Sonic the Hedgehog (2020 film): plot, cast, production, redesign, release and reception
wikis.summary: Part 1 of the English Wikipedia article on the 2020 Sonic the Hedgehog film, covering its credits and infobox figures, plot, cast, the decades of abandoned adaptations, the 2013-2018 development and casting, the post-trailer redesign and delay, box office, reviews, awards and the franchise that followed.
wikis.body:
## The film

- "*Sonic the Hedgehog* is a 2020 action-adventure comedy film based on the *Sonic* video game series. It is the first installment in the *Sonic the Hedgehog* film series", directed by Jeff Fowler in his feature directorial debut and written by Pat Casey and Josh Miller.
- Based on *Sonic the Hedgehog* by Sega. Produced by Neal H. Moritz, Toby Ascher, Toru Nakahara and Takeshi Ito. Cinematography Stephen F. Windon; edited by Stacey Schroeder and Debra Neil-Fisher; music by Tom Holkenborg.
- Production companies Original Film, Marza Animation Planet and Blur Studio; distributed by Paramount Pictures.
- Release dates: January 25, 2020 (Paramount Pictures lot), February 14, 2020 (United States), June 26, 2020 (Japan). Running time 99 minutes. Countries United States and Japan; language English. Budget $85-90 million; box office $320 million.
- Starring James Marsden, Ben Schwartz, Tika Sumpter, Natasha Rothwell, Adam Pally, Neal McDonough and Jim Carrey.
- "Development for a *Sonic* film began in the 1990s but did not leave the planning stage until Sony Pictures acquired the film rights in 2013. Fowler was hired in 2016. After Sony put the project in turnaround, Paramount Pictures acquired it in 2017."
- "Following negative reaction to the film's first trailer, wherein Sonic appeared to look like a real hedgehog, Paramount delayed the film by three months to redesign Sonic to more resemble his look in the video games."
- "It set the record for the biggest opening weekend for a video game film in the United States and Canada and grossed $320 million worldwide, becoming the sixth highest-grossing film of 2020 and the highest-grossing video game film adaptation in North America."
- Followed by *Sonic the Hedgehog 2* (2022), *Sonic the Hedgehog 3* (2024) and the miniseries *Knuckles* (2024); a fourth film announced in December 2024 "is set to release in theatres on March 19, 2027."

## Plot

Sonic, raised by the owl Longclaw, is sent to Earth with a bag of golden rings that open portals. Ten years later he lives hidden near Green Hills, Montana, and accidentally triggers an electromagnetic pulse causing a power outage across the Pacific Northwest. The Department of Defense enlists Doctor Robotnik to find the cause. Sheriff Tom Wachowski tranquilises Sonic, who drops his rings through a portal onto the roof of the Transamerica Pyramid; the two travel to San Francisco to recover them. Robotnik, having found a quill that can power his machines, pursues Sonic worldwide until the Green Hills townsfolk intervene and Sonic destroys his hovercraft and sends him through a ring portal to the mushroom planet. In the closing scenes Robotnik plots his return, and "a two-tailed Fox emerges from a ring portal in search of Sonic."

## Figures

- Budget "estimated at being between $85 million and $90 million"; the redesign "added an estimated $5 million to the production budget, took around five months, and was achieved without overtime."
- Worldwide gross $320 million: $149 million in the United States and Canada and $170.7 million in other territories.
- Home video: the DVD and Blu-ray releases "crossed 2 million units sold in the United States by January 2021 and earned about $50 million in US sales revenue as of 16 April 2022".
- Admissions: "15,876,790 tickets in the United States and Canada (annual rank #3), 6,811,679 tickets in Mexico (annual #1), 893,634 in Peru (annual #2), 468,697 in Ecuador (annual #1), 67,230 in the Dominican Republic (annual #2), 12,454,206 in Europe (annual #3), 3,001,403 in Brazil (annual #3), 698,500 in China, 687,740 in Argentina (annual #3), and 118,725 in South Korea, for a combined 41,078,604 tickets sold in these territories."

## Attributions the page gives differently in two places

The visual effects section says "Artist Tyson Hesse, who worked on previous *Sonic the Hedgehog* media and ultimately served as co-producer on the film, was brought on to lead the redesign", and in the next sentence says "Sonic was redesigned by Marza Animation Planet."

wikis.title: Cast of Sonic the Hedgehog
wikis.summary: The voice and live-action cast and their characters, including the uncredited Tails cameo.
wikis.body:
## Voice

- Ben Schwartz as Sonic the Hedgehog, "an anthropomorphic blue hedgehog with superhuman speed"; Schwartz also provided the facial motion-capture. Benjamin L. Valic voices Young Sonic.
- Donna J. Fulks as Longclaw, "an anthropomorphic brown owl who was Sonic's caregiver as a child".
- "Colleen O'Shaughnessey reprises her role from the games in an uncredited role as Miles 'Tails' Prower ... in the mid-credits scene."

## Live-action

- Jim Carrey as Dr. Robotnik. Carrey compared the character to his Riddler in *Batman Forever* (1995): "I wouldn't put one against the other. I think they'd be a great team. But you know, it's like Robotnik and every supervillain basically comes from a place of neglect with a feeling of absolute worthlessness that manifests itself in magnificent creations that are designed to control the world".
- James Marsden as Tom Wachowski, sheriff of Green Hills; Tika Sumpter as Maddie Wachowski, a veterinarian and Tom's wife.
- Lee Majdoub as Agent Stone, Robotnik's assistant; Adam Pally as Wade Whipple, a deputy sheriff; Natasha Rothwell as Rachel, Maddie's older sister; Melody Nosipho Niemann as Jojo.
- Tom Butler as Commander Walters, Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff; Neal McDonough as Major Bennington.
- Frank C. Turner as Crazy Carl, a conspiracy theorist - "Turner previously portrayed the character in *Kickin' It Old Skool*." Garry Chalk as the U.S. Navy Chief of Staff - "Chalk previously voiced Grounder and Robotnik in *Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog* and *Sonic Underground* respectively."
- Michael Hogan as the Air Force Chief of Staff; Peter James Bryant as Army Chief of Staff; Shannon Chan-Kent as a roadhouse waitress.

wikis.title: The abandoned Sonic films of the 1990s and 2000s
wikis.summary: The MGM, Ben Hurst and Ken Penders attempts to get a Sonic film made before 2013.
wikis.body:
- "Development for a film adaptation of the *Sonic the Hedgehog* video game franchise began in 1993 during production of DIC Entertainment's television show *Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog*." Michealene Risley negotiated with Hollywood producers; Sega of America CEO Tom Kalinske "was wary of damaging the brand, citing the commercial and critical failures of the *Super Mario Bros.* (1993) and *Street Fighter* (1994) films."
- "In August 1994, Sega struck a development deal with Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer and Trilogy Entertainment Group, with Pen Densham as executive producer." Richard Jefferies was hired to write a treatment and asked to feature the forthcoming Sega Saturn; his *Sonic: Wonders of the World* was submitted in May 1995. Sega COO Shinobu Toyoda suggested replacing Robotnik with a meaner villain. "MGM canceled the project after a failed attempt to revive it at DreamWorks. Jefferies suggested that the film was scrapped as both Sega and MGM wanted a higher share of the profits, while Densham said it followed creative differences between Sega and Trilogy."
- In the late 1990s Ben Hurst tried to conclude the animated *Sonic the Hedgehog* series as a feature. Ken Penders "allegedly told Sega that Hurst was trying to co-opt the franchise, leading Sega to dismiss Hurst and his proposal." Hurst tried again from 2005 to 2006 without success.
- "In September 2003, Penders pitched his own concept for a *Sonic* film, *Sonic Armageddon*", an origin story and series reset. "The project was dropped in 2007 due to a corporate upheaval and the death of Sega licensing manager Robert Leffler, who had supported Penders."

wikis.title: Development and casting
wikis.summary: Sony's 2013 acquisition, Paramount taking over in 2017, and how the cast was assembled in 2018.
wikis.body:
## Development

- "In 2013, Sony Pictures Entertainment acquired the rights to produce and distribute a *Sonic* film. On June 10, 2014, a live-action animated film was announced as a joint venture between Sony Pictures's Columbia Pictures and Marza Animation Planet, a Japan-based subsidiary of Sega Sammy Holdings which had produced CGI cutscenes for several *Sonic* games." It would be produced by Neal H. Moritz under his Original Film banner with Takeshi Ito, Mie Onishi and Toru Nakahara, and written by Evan Susser and Van Robichaux.
- "In February 2016, Sega CEO said the film was scheduled for 2018. Hajime Satomi, Blur Studio's Tim Miller, and Jeff Fowler were hired in 2016 to develop the film", with Fowler directing and Miller as executive producer. Blur had produced cutscenes for *Shadow the Hedgehog* (2005) - for which Fowler did animation and directed cutscenes - and *Sonic the Hedgehog* (2006).
- "Patrick Casey, Josh Miller, and Oren Uziel were writing the screenplay, while Casey and Miller wrote the story, however, the former two received sole writing credit while Uziel went uncredited."
- "On October 2, 2017, Paramount Pictures announced that they had acquired the rights after Sony put the film in turnaround. Almost all of the production team remained unchanged. Coincidentally, Paramount and Sega had once been sister companies under Gulf and Western Industries; Gulf and Western sold Sega's assets in 1984."
- The working title during production was "Casino Night", named after a stage in the games. Early drafts featured Super Sonic; Fowler felt "it didn't make sense to obviously bring in the Super Sonic thing just yet". "Casey and Miller reportedly described the film as not faithful to the game, while producer Toby Ascher favored their buddy comedy approach."

## Casting

- May 2018: Paul Rudd was reported in talks for Tom, "which was later denied by Paramount"; a day later James Marsden was cast in an undisclosed role later revealed as Tom Wachowski.
- June 2018: Tika Sumpter cast as Maddie and Jim Carrey as Dr. Robotnik.
- August 2018: Ben Schwartz joined to voice Sonic, "a rare occasion in which the character would not be voiced by Roger Craig Smith, who voices Sonic in most incarnations since 2010." Schwartz, a fan of the original games, had done a test reading while Fowler and Miller pitched the project to studios. Adam Pally and Neal McDonough were added later that month; Debs Howard and Elfina Luk joined that November. "Riff Raff was cast in an undisclosed role but was cut from the film."

wikis.title: Filming, visual effects and the Sonic redesign
wikis.summary: The 2018 shoot, the CGI design of Sonic and the redesign forced by the first trailer's reception.
wikis.body:
## Filming

- "Principal photography began in mid-September 2018 and ended in Vancouver, Ladysmith, and Vancouver Island on October 16, 2018. Key production scenes were also filmed in Liwa Oasis, United Arab Emirates. During filming, Schwartz was unavailable, so a stand-in performed alongside Marsden."

## Visual effects and design

- Visual effects by Moving Picture Company (MPC), Marza Animation Planet, Blur Studio, Trixter and Digital Domain.
- "The production team created a live-action version of Sonic using CGI, adding fur, new running sneakers, two separate eyes, and a more human like physique. They used Ted, the living teddy bear from the *Ted* films, as a reference to insert a CGI character into a real-world setting."
- Tim Miller: "It would be weird, and it would feel like he was running around nude if he was some sort of otter-like thing. It was always, for us, fur, and we never considered anything different." According to Miller, Sega was "not entirely happy" with the design of Sonic's eyes.
- "On May 2, 2019, in response to the criticism, Fowler announced on Twitter that Sonic would be redesigned. The film was delayed from its original release date of November 8, 2019, to February 14, 2020, as a result."
- "Artist Tyson Hesse, who worked on previous *Sonic the Hedgehog* media and ultimately served as co-producer on the film, was brought on to lead the redesign. Sonic was given larger and differently colored eyes, new sneakers, white gloves, and a less humanlike body". The article then adds "Sonic was redesigned by Marza Animation Planet."
- "The redesign added an estimated $5 million to the production budget, took around five months, and was achieved without overtime."

wikis.title: Music and soundtrack
wikis.summary: Tom Holkenborg's score and the songs on the soundtrack album.
wikis.body:
- "In February 2019, Tom Holkenborg, who previously collaborated with executive producer Miller on *Deadpool* (2016), was hired to compose the score. The soundtrack was released alongside the film on February 14, 2020, in both digital and physical formats."
- "Riff Raff, who had a role in the film but was cut due to controversy against him, appears on the soundtrack."
- An original song, "Boom" by X Ambassadors, appears on the soundtrack; the single was released January 24, 2020 by Atlantic Records.
- "'Speed Me Up' by American musicians Wiz Khalifa, Lil Yachty, Ty Dolla Sign, and Sueco the Child received 15 million streams, along with 1.8 billion views for the 'Speed Me Up' TikTok challenge."
- "Friends" by Hyper Potions, previously the opening theme of *Sonic Mania* (2017), also appears, "along with arrangements of tracks from Masato Nakamura's score for the original *Sonic the Hedgehog* (1991)."
- "Holkenborg attempted to capture the feel of Nakamura's soundtracks for the *Sonic* and *Sonic the Hedgehog 2* (1992) games, using Yamaha digital FM synthesizers (such as the DX7) similar to the Sega Genesis/Mega Drive console's Yamaha YM2612 sound chip."

wikis.title: Release, the trailer backlash and home media
wikis.summary: The shifting release dates, the reception of the first and second trailers, and the pandemic-shortened home video window.
wikis.body:
## Theatrical

- Scheduled for 2018 by Sony Pictures Releasing; in February 2018 Paramount rescheduled to November 15, 2019, "later moved up to a week earlier on November 8". After the redesign announcement it was "delayed for the final time by three months, to February 14, 2020"; *Playing with Fire* took the original date.
- "The world premiere took place at the Paramount Pictures studio lot in Los Angeles on January 25, 2020." Released theatrically in the United States in 4DX and Dolby Cinema formats. The Japanese release moved from March 27, 2020 to June 26 "due to the COVID-19 pandemic."

## Marketing and the backlash

- "Test footage was screened at the Comic Con Experience in Brazil on December 9, 2018", followed by a teaser poster the same day showing Sonic's silhouette with the tagline "A Whole New Speed of Hero". It was compared unfavourably to *Detective Pikachu*, and "Sonic's humanoid appearance was described as evoking an uncanny valley response." Former Sonic Team members "expressed surprise"; a leaked second poster drew complaints about the positioning of Sonic's legs, "spawning an Internet meme in which users recreated the position". The official Twitter account posted an image of Sonic behind a sign reading "Can't a guy work out?". Sonic co-creator Yuji Naka was "shocked" by the design "and felt the ratio of Sonic's head and abdomen was imbalanced".
- "The first trailer premiered on April 4, 2019, at CinemaCon in Las Vegas, and was released online on April 30. It received near-unanimous criticism, with Gita Jackson of Kotaku calling it 'horrific' and 'a blight upon this weary earth'." Some found the use of Coolio's "Gangsta's Paradise" jarring; CNET's Sean Keane praised the humour and game references. "Within two days, the trailer was viewed more than 20 million times on YouTube, and had received hundreds of thousands of dislikes, drastically outnumbering its likes."
- "A second trailer revealing the redesigned Sonic was released on November 12, 2019" to far more positive responses, praising the design, tone, humour and the use of J. J. Fad's "Supersonic" and the Ramones' "Blitzkrieg Bop". Naka said the new design was "much more Sonic-like". The second trailer "received thousands of likes and the highest like-to-dislike ratio of any trailer on Google in the last three years", and "[t]he trailers garnered a total of more than 500 million views worldwide."
- The film's Sonic was added as a playable character to the mobile games *Sonic Dash* (2013) and *Sonic Forces: Speed Battle* (2017). A modified version of the original design, "Ugly Sonic", appeared in *Chip 'n Dale: Rescue Rangers* (2022), voiced by Tim Robinson; director Akiva Schaffer said MPC "was able to provide the original Sonic model for the film."

## Home media

- "On March 20, 2020, Paramount announced that *Sonic the Hedgehog* would be released to home media in the United States and Canada before the end of the usual 90-day theatrical run", because of theatre closures during the pandemic. Digital release March 31, 2020; DVD, Blu-ray and Ultra HD Blu-ray on May 19, 2020, all including an original short film, *Around the World in 80 Seconds*.
- "The film topped the American Blu-ray and DVD charts for several weeks upon release" and was "the sixth top-selling home video film of 2020 in the United States". It moved to Hulu on February 18, 2021 and Amazon Prime Video the next day.

wikis.title: Box office
wikis.summary: The record-setting opening weekend and the domestic and international grosses.
wikis.body:
- Grossed $149 million in the United States and Canada and $170.7 million elsewhere, "for a worldwide total of $320 million. It was the sixth-highest-grossing film of 2020, and the highest-grossing superhero film of the year, ending Marvel Studios' decade-long run of having the highest-grossing film of the genre (from 2010 to 2019)."
- Released alongside *Fantasy Island*, *The Photograph* and *Downhill*, "initially projected to gross $40-50 million from 4,130 theaters in its four-day President's Day opening weekend". After $21 million on the first day, including $3 million from Thursday previews, estimates rose to $64 million.
- "It went on to top the box office with a $58 million debut over the three-day weekend, and $70 million over the four, breaking *Detective Pikachu*'s record for the biggest opening weekend by a video game-based film. It was also the fourth-best President's Day holiday weekend and Jim Carrey's second biggest opening weekend, behind *Bruce Almighty* (2003)."
- The success was attributed partly to the redesign and its publicity and partly to the later date meaning less family-film competition. "Opening day audiences was 56% male, with 70% under 25 years."
- Second weekend $26.2 million, staying first, for a ten-day domestic total of $106.6 million; third weekend $16.3 million, "dethroned by newcomer *The Invisible Man*". "On March 14, 2020, it became the highest-grossing film based on a video game in US box office history, surpassing *Detective Pikachu*."
- Internationally it opened in 40 countries for $43 million, with the largest openings $6.7 million in Mexico, $6.2 million in the United Kingdom, $4.3 million in France, $3.3 million in Germany and $3 million in Brazil; $101 million worldwide over three days and $113 million over four.
- Second weekend: $38.3 million from 56 countries for a ten-day overseas gross of $96.5 million, and $64.6 million globally for a ten-day worldwide gross of $203.1 million, with the largest markets the United Kingdom ($19.1 million), Mexico ($12.3 million) and France ($9.1 million), plus a number-one debut in Russia ($6.3 million).
- It opened in Japan on June 26, 2020, debuting at No. 6. In China the release was postponed by the pandemic, "eventually receiving a July 31 date and underperforming at the Chinese box office due to new pandemic-related theatre policies there."

wikis.title: Critical response, accolades and the franchise
wikis.summary: Aggregate scores and named reviews, the awards table, the novelization and the sequels.
wikis.body:
## Reviews

- "*Sonic the Hedgehog* received mixed reviews, with critics praising Sonic's redesign, humor and cast performances, but criticizing its product placements and unoriginal story." Rotten Tomatoes: 64% of 252 reviews positive, average 5.9/10, consensus "Fittingly fleet and frequently fun, Sonic the Hedgehog is a video game-inspired adventure the whole family can enjoy -- and a fine excuse for Jim Carrey to tap into the manic energy that launched his career." Metacritic: 47 out of 100 from 42 critics, "mixed or average". CinemaScore "A"; PostTrak 4 out of 5 stars, "with 66% of viewers they surveyed saying they would definitely recommend it."
- Akeem Lawanson (IGN), 7/10: "this family-friendly action-comedy suffers from a simplistic story and leans too heavily on tired visual clichés" but is "boosted by solid performances from Ben Schwartz as Sonic and Jim Carrey as Dr. Robotnik."
- Dami Lee (*The Verge*) praised the nostalgic elements; Corey Plante (*Inverse*) called it "a road trip superhero movie" and "the best superhero movie of 2020" so far; John DeFore (*The Hollywood Reporter*): "Flesh-and-blood actors help keep this game derived kids' flick afloat."
- Gene Park (*The Washington Post*): "the furthest thing from *Cats*, despite the early comparisons."
- Amon Warrman (*Empire*), two of five: "An on-form Jim Carrey can't stop Sonic's live-action debut from feeling like a missed opportunity."
- Ben Kenigsberg (*The New York Times*), negative: "Sonic now resembles a cartoon hedgehog instead of a spray-painted marmot. But if anything was done to de-genericize the script, it hasn't helped."
- Owen Gleiberman (*Variety*): "I would also call the overly kiddified tone of the movie a mistake." Steve Rose (*The Guardian*), two of five, found the friendship message "trite and familiar". Simon Abrams (RogerEbert.com), one of four. Tim Grierson (*Screen Daily*): "Sadly, Sonic isn't swift enough to deliver."

## Accolades

- 2020: SXSW Film Festival, Excellence in Title Design - nominated. People's Choice Awards, The Family Movie of 2020 - nominated.
- 2021: Critics' Choice Super Awards - Best Villain in a Movie won by Jim Carrey; Best Superhero Movie and Best Actor in a Superhero Movie (Ben Schwartz and Jim Carrey) nominated. Hollywood Critics Association Awards - Best Animated or VFX Performance won by Ben Schwartz; Best Blockbuster and Best Visual Effects (Ged Wright) nominated. Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards - Favorite Movie and Favorite Movie Actor (Jim Carrey) nominated. Ursa Major Awards, Best Motion Picture - nominated. Saturn Awards, Best Fantasy Film Release - nominated.

## Franchise

- "A novel based on the film, *Sonic the Hedgehog: The Official Movie Novelization*, written by Kiel Phegley and published by Penguin Books, was released alongside the film on February 14, 2020."
- "*Sonic the Hedgehog 2* was released in 2022, followed by *Sonic the Hedgehog 3* in 2024. In December 2024, a fourth film was announced and is set to release in theatres on March 19, 2027."
- "In April 2024, a spin-off miniseries, *Knuckles*, starring Idris Elba as Knuckles the Echidna, was released on Paramount+."
- The article carries a maintenance notice that it "contains one or more duplicated citations", dated August 2026.

## Market

- Question: "When will the Knesset approve a new government?", under the INTERNATIONAL category. Subtitle on the page: "Resolves on the Knesset floor vote".
- Series KXISRAELCONF; event KXISRAELCONF-27FEB03; highlighted market KXISRAELCONF-27FEB03-26DEC23.

## Odds shown on the page

| Strike | Chance | Yes | No |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before Dec 23, 2026 | 35% | 33¢ | 77¢ |
| Before Jan 20, 2027 | 77% | 82¢ | 28¢ |
| Before Feb 3, 2027 | 89% | 95¢ | 12¢ |

The order ticket shows "Before Dec 23, 2026" at YES 33¢ / NO 77¢ and "Odds 35% chance". Max payout date Dec 22, 2026.

## Rules

- "Before Dec 23, 2026" resolves Yes if the Knesset approves a new government in a vote of confidence before Dec 23, 2026. Outcome verified from The Knesset.
- Explicitly not qualifying: "The President tasking a candidate with forming a government, any extension of that mandate, a signed coalition agreement, an announced agreement in principle between parties, and the continued operation of the outgoing caretaker government", nor "the swearing-in of individual ministers before the Knesset has voted."
- Qualifying events include parliamentary approval with binding effect; a formal commitment by the head of state or government with constitutional authority; an official statement by an authorized minister; an official government press release; a formal declaration during official government proceedings. Announcements with a specified future implementation date, phased implementation announcements and coalition or multi-party agreements also qualify where they constitute an agreement or announcement of the specified action.
- Not qualifying: preliminary discussions or negotiations without commitment; conditional agreements; statements by opposition parties or unauthorized representatives; leaked documents or unofficial reports; proposals or draft legislation without formal approval; retraction of a previously announced commitment.
- "Where the statutory mandate periods expire without a qualifying agreement or announcement having occurred, every market resolves to NO, including where that triggers a fresh election."

## Timeline and payout

- Market open: Aug 21, 2026 · 3:00pm EDT. Closes after the outcome occurs; projected payout 30 minutes after closing.
- "This market will close and expire early if the event described in the Payout Criterion occurs. Otherwise, it closes by Dec 22, 2026 at 11:59pm EST."

## Breaking-news headlines carried on the page

- The Jerusalem Post, Sep 19: "Netanyahu's pardon may shape coalition talks, election deadlock, Isaac Herzog hints" — the president says his considerations on Netanyahu's pardon request are "solely substantive".
- The Jerusalem Post, Sep 15: "Knesset list deadline yields no clarity as both Israeli blocs fall short of 61".
- Anadolu Ajansi, Sep 10: "46 days before Israel election, neither bloc assured of forming government" — "Polls show opposition Yashar party ahead of Netanyahu's Likud, but neither side has the 61 seats needed to form a government".

The order ticket shows "Above $99,999.99" at YES 28¢ / NO 73¢ and "Odds 29% chance", against the 28% in the list. Max payout date Dec 31, 2026.

## Rules

- "Above $99,999.99" resolves Yes if the Bitcoin spot price according to the CF Bitcoin Real-Time Index is above $99,999.99 "starting 01/02/2026 06:00 PM and before Dec 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET". Outcome verified from CF Benchmarks.
- "The market resolves based on the CF Bitcoin Real-Time Index (BRTI) using a trimmed mean calculation. The resolution value is calculated by taking all BRTI values for each minute from market issuance until the specified time on the target date, removing the top 20% and bottom 20% of values, then averaging the remaining 60% of values."
- "If the BRTI crosses the threshold at any point during the measurement period (triggering early expiration), the market immediately resolves. If no data is available at the expiration time, the market resolves to No."

## Timeline and payout

- Market open: Jan 2, 2026 · 6:00pm EST. Closes after the outcome occurs; projected payout 1 hour after closing.

wikis.title: The Debate: German far right's breakout moment? AfD party eyes outright win in regional election
wikis.summary: Apple Podcasts episode page for a 4 September 2026 France 24 debate on the AfD's push for an outright majority in Saxony-Anhalt and the wider European far right.
wikis.body:
## Episode

- Show: "The Debate" (channel: FRANCE 24 English); length 43 min; published September 4, 2026 at 9:29 AM UTC. The page also heads it "September 4".
- Produced by François Picard, Rebecca Gnignati, Juliette Laffont, Juliette Brown, Charles Wente.

## What the description says

- "Could Europeans awaken next Monday to another shock bellwether moment? German voters could for the first time since World War II give an outright majority to a far-right party in regional elections."
- The episode asks about "the AfD's push in Saxony-Anhalt and a charismatic lead candidate whose campaign strives to put charm above the vitriol usually associated with a party with pro-Nazi roots."
- On the state: "Saxony-Anhalt has a familiar tale: that of a former East German state rattled by globalisation with declining industry and an ageing population", contrasted with "the dynamism of not-so-far-off cities like Berlin and Leipzig."
- "Speaking of Leipzig, the German government this week directly accused Russia over last month's drone attack on a Ukrainian cargo plane at Leipzig airport."
- It asks whether German voters care "that we're talking about the same Russia that's actively aligned with Moscow and a Trump administration that claims immigrants are a bigger threat to Europe than Russian hostility?"
- Looking ahead: "These questions may be the warmup for next spring's French presidential poll, where Marine Le Pen's party this week floated the idea of banning the Muslim headscarf in public."
- "Both the far-right National Rally and Germany's AfD oppose a more federal Europe. What happens if they win?"

wikis.title: Annular Solar Eclipse of 2028 Jan 26
wikis.summary: NASA/GSFC interactive Google-map page for the Annular Solar Eclipse of 2028 Jan 26, giving its greatest duration, Saros number and prediction parameters.
wikis.body:
## The eclipse

- Page covers the **Annular Solar Eclipse of 2028 Jan 26** and shows its path on an interactive Google map.
- Greatest Duration on this page: "In this case, the Greatest Duration is 10m30.6s." That is the point along the path where the annular eclipse lasts longest.
- The map marks the northern and southern path limits in blue and the central line in red; the yellow lines crossing the path give "the time and position of maximum eclipse at 10-minute intervals."
- The green marker labeled GE is the point of Greatest Eclipse; the magenta marker labeled GD is the point of Greatest Duration.
- The page states you "MUST be somewhere within the central path (between the blue lines) to see the annular phase of the eclipse", and that the eclipse is longest on the central line.

## Predictions and accuracy

- Predictions "were generated using the VSOP87/ELP2000-85 solar and lunar ephemerides and a value of ΔT = 71.9 seconds."
- The predictions "DO NOT include the effects of mountains and valleys along the edge of the Moon." Such lunar limb corrections "may shift the limits of the eclipse path north or south by ~1-3 kilometers, and change the eclipse duration by ~1-3 seconds"; in the map's popup predictions they "may change the contact times and eclipse durations by ~1-3 seconds", and "The exact location of Greatest Duration may also change by ~10-20 kilometers."
- "More detailed predictions including the effects of the lunar limb profile are normally posted 12-18 months before each eclipse".
- Clicking the map adds a marker whose popup gives Eclipse Type (total, annular or partial), Duration of Annularity, Eclipse Magnitude ("the fraction of the Sun's diameter eclipsed"), Eclipse Obscuration ("the fraction of the Sun's area eclipsed"), and a table of event times in Universal Time with the Sun's altitude and azimuth.
- Viewing advice given: "better to see a shorter eclipse from clear sky that a longer eclipse under clouds."

## Other pages offered for this eclipse

Orthographic Map, Google Map, Animated Map, Path Table, Besselian Elements Table, Saros 141 Table.

## Credit and page date

- "All eclipse calculations are by Fred Espenak, and he assumes full responsibility for their accuracy." Reuse is permitted with the acknowledgment "Eclipse Predictions by Fred Espenak, NASA's GSFC".
- Footnote 1 notes other interactive Google eclipse maps "include those by Xavier Jubier".
- The page ends with the bare date "2014 Mar 14", carrying no label of its own.

wikis.title: Path of the Annular Solar Eclipse of 2044 Feb 28
wikis.summary: NASA/GSFC eclipse page by Fred Espenak tabulating the antumbral path of the 28 February 2044 annular solar eclipse at 120-second intervals, with greatest eclipse and duration.
wikis.body:
## What the page is

- "Path of the Annular Solar Eclipse of 2044 Feb 28" by Fred Espenak.
- The table "delineates the path of the Moon's antumbral shadow", giving WGS 84 coordinates of the northern and southern limits and the central line "at 120-second intervals".
- Central-line local circumstances listed: Moon/Sun apparent diameter ratio, Sun altitude and azimuth (degrees), path width (kilometers) and duration (minutes and seconds).
- Links offered to an Orthographic Map, Google Map, Animated Map, Path Table, Besselian Elements Table and Saros 121 Table.

## Path figures

- Tabulated Universal Times run from 20:06 to 20:40, with "Limits" rows at each end; the path lies in southern-hemisphere latitudes (roughly 52°S to 70°S).
- Opening limits row: 70°08.0'S 005°39.1'W (north and south limits identical) with central line 64°40.6'S 014°00.5'W; ratio 0.000; width 0 km; duration 00m00.0s.
- Closing limits row: 52°00.2'S 027°12.8'W with central line 57°39.9'S 021°57.5'W; ratio 0.000; width 0 km; duration 00m00.0s.
- Central-line rows appear only between 20:18 and 20:30; the diameter ratio there is 0.959–0.960 and the tabulated central duration stays at about 02m27s. Path width in those rows ranges from 2172 km to 2559 km.
- ΔT = 87.1 seconds.

## Greatest eclipse and greatest duration

- Greatest Eclipse (GE): Time = 20:23:11.9 UT, Lat = 62°10.7'S, Long = 025°34.4'W; Sun altitude 3.7°, Sun azimuth 260.1°; path width 2250.6 km; central duration 02m27.2s.
- Greatest Duration (GD): Time = 20:16:21 UT, Lat = 64°41'S, Long = 014°00'W; Sun altitude 0.0°, Sun azimuth 251.4°; path width 2594.5 km; central duration 02m27.4s.

## Method and caveats

- "Predictions for the Annular Solar Eclipse of 2044 Feb 28 were generated using the VSOP87/ELP2000-85 solar and lunar ephemerides and a value of ΔT = 87.1 seconds."
- The predictions "DO NOT include the effects of mountains and valleys along the edge of the Moon"; lunar limb corrections "may shift the limits of the eclipse path north or south by ~1-3 kilometers, and change the eclipse duration by ~1-3 seconds", with more detailed predictions "normally posted 12-18 months before each eclipse".
- Acknowledgment requested: "Eclipse Predictions by Fred Espenak, NASA's GSFC".

- The page ends with the bare date "2014 Feb 26", with no label saying whether it is a publication or revision date; the page states no published or last-updated date in words.

wikis.summary: NASA/GSFC interactive Google-map page for the Total Solar Eclipse of 2046 Aug 02, giving its greatest duration, Saros number and prediction parameters.
wikis.body:
## The eclipse

- Page covers the **Total Solar Eclipse of 2046 Aug 02** and shows its path on an interactive Google map.
- Greatest Duration on this page: "In this case, the Greatest Duration is 04m51.6s." That is the point along the path where the total eclipse lasts longest.
- The map marks the northern and southern path limits in blue and the central line in red; the yellow lines crossing the path give "the time and position of maximum eclipse at 10-minute intervals."
- The green marker labeled GE is the point of Greatest Eclipse; the magenta marker labeled GD is the point of Greatest Duration.
- The page states you "MUST be somewhere within the central path (between the blue lines) to see the total phase of the eclipse", and that the eclipse is longest on the central line.

## Predictions and accuracy

- Predictions "were generated using the VSOP87/ELP2000-85 solar and lunar ephemerides and a value of ΔT = 89.1 seconds."
- The predictions "DO NOT include the effects of mountains and valleys along the edge of the Moon." Such lunar limb corrections "may shift the limits of the eclipse path north or south by ~1-3 kilometers, and change the eclipse duration by ~1-3 seconds"; in the map's popup predictions they "may change the contact times and eclipse durations by ~1-3 seconds", and "The exact location of Greatest Duration may also change by ~10-20 kilometers."

wikis.title: Shanghai East Railway Station to offer integrated travel experience
wikis.summary: Shanghai government English-site republication of a China Daily report on the start of main construction at Shanghai East Railway Station, with the hub's size, schedule and builders.
wikis.body:
## Construction start

- "The Shanghai East Railway Station officially began its main construction on March 18 with the installation of the first steel column, marking a significant milestone in the development of the one-stop integrated transportation hub, according to official sources."
- "Known as the eastern hub, the project is scheduled to be operational in July 2027, offering seamless connections to high-speed rail, urban railway, metro lines, buses and the airport, according to Chen Weige, Party chief of the Shanghai East Railway Station's project management department under China Railway Shanghai Group Co."

## Site and size

- "Located about 5 kilometers from Terminal 1 of Shanghai Pudong International Airport in the city's Pudong New Area, the station will span a construction area of more than 1.3 million square meters."
- "Its high-speed railway station building will cover 160,000 square meters and feature 15 platforms and 30 tracks."
- Chen, at the March 18 groundbreaking ceremony: "Once completed, the eastern hub will be an upgraded version of the existing Hongqiao transportation hub."

## Progress

- "So far, 85 percent of its underground engineering floor has been completed, while 55 percent of the ground-level structural plate has been built, meeting conditions to begin construction of the station building."
- Chen: "We will strive for excellence in project quality, integrating digitalization and intelligent technologies into the design to create a high-quality landmark offering a premium travel experience." And: "We will adhere to the highest standards and best practices from previous projects to create a new benchmark for the modern era."

## Builders

- "The project is being built by a consortium led by Shanghai Construction Group and China Railway 24th Bureau Group Corp."
- Zhang Chuan, vice-president of Eastern Hub Group: "The construction will emphasize efficiency, safety and quality."

## Hongqiao comparison and policy context

- "Hongqiao hub, currently Shanghai's largest integrated transportation hub, handled 406.6 million passenger trips last year, with an average daily volume of 1.1 million trips, according to the Shanghai Municipal Transportation Commission."
- "Together, the two hubs will reinforce Shanghai's position as a world-class transportation center connecting the Yangtze River Delta region with global networks".
- "The State Council, China's Cabinet, approved the general plan for constructing the eastern hub international business cooperation zone in February last year." The city plans to leverage institutional innovations from the China (Shanghai) Pilot Free Trade Zone, improve international business connectivity and better integrate domestic and international markets.

## Credit

- Credited to chinadaily.com.cn, dated March 19, 2025. Images credited to the WeChat account shanghaifabu.
