wikis.title: Parker Solar Probe Ready for Launch on Mission to the Sun
wikis.summary: NASA image feature showing Parker Solar Probe packed inside its Delta IV Heavy fairing ahead of its August 11, 2018 launch to the Sun.
wikis.body:
## What the page shows

- An image article (marked "1 min read", credited to NASA) of NASA's Parker Solar Probe "Packed safely inside the United Launch Alliance Delta IV Heavy rocket payload fairing".
- Image caption: "Inside the United Launch Alliance Delta IV Heavy rocket payload fairing on Wednesday, August 8, 2018, the Parker Solar is slated to launch at 3:33 a.m. EDT, Saturday, August 11."

## Launch details stated

- Launch vehicle: United Launch Alliance Delta IV Heavy.
- "slated to launch on Saturday, August 11, 2018, at 3:33 a.m. EDT from Launch Complex 37, Cape Canaveral Air Force Station, Florida."
- The page keeps the hedge "is slated to launch" - it describes a launch still to come.

## Mission

- "The Parker Solar Probe will travel through the Sun's atmosphere, closer to the surface than any spacecraft before it."
- "The mission will revolutionize our understanding of the Sun, where changing conditions can propagate out into the solar system, affecting Earth and other worlds."

## Credit

- Image Credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls.
- Page dated "Aug 10, 2018"; the caption dates the photograph to Wednesday, August 8, 2018.

wikis.title: Nike Caitlin 1 "Caitlin Blue" release details
wikis.summary: Sole Retriever release page for Caitlin Clark's first signature sneaker, the Nike Caitlin 1 in Caitlin Blue, with its 1 October 2026 date, prices, SKU and technology.
wikis.body:
## Release details

- Product: Nike Caitlin 1 Caitlin Blue. Release date: October 1, 2026. SKU: IH7423-400. Colorway: Racer Blue/Multi-Color.
- Retail price: $140. The page also shows a "Live Price" of $498.
- "The Nike Caitlin 1 Caitlin Blue will be released October 1, 2026 through Nike and select retailers online and in-store. Available in unisex, GS, and PS sizing, the retail price is set at $140, $115, and $105, respectively."
- Where to buy panel: Raffles 0/0, Releases 2/2, In stock 3.

## Quick facts as listed

- "Caitlin Clark's first sneaker, the Caitlin 1, debuts in the Caitlin Blue colorway"
- "The pair will be released October 1, 2026 for $140 in unisex sizing"
- "Nike uses Opticast technology on the upper to create the mini 'C' and '2' nodes"
- "Inside, the shoe uses Cushlon foam and Air Zoom Turbo"

## Lead-up

- "Clark has been teasing the Caitlin 1 throughout this week, first by changing her Instagram handle to 'caitlin1,' then swapping her profile picture on the platform to upclose shots of the shoe's upper."
- "She even slyly revealed the global launch date of the first colorway via a fit check before the Fever game on June 16, with her friendship bracelet displaying the October 1, 2026 date."
- An IG dump followed, "including a picture of Travis Scott wearing the sneaker", before "Nike has officially unveiled the Nike Caitlin 1."

## Design and technology

- Clark told Travis and Jason Kelce on their New Heights podcast: "The technology that we're gonna put into it isn't anything that they've ever put into a basketball shoe before" — the article says she meant Opticast.
- "The tech is used across the upper to create the polyurethane nodes that create a 'C' shape on the lateral side and the number '2' on the medial side."
- The look is compared to what Eric Avar designed for Kobe Bryant on the Nike Kobe 6, "a shoe that Caitlin has loved throughout her playing career"; the nodes "serve a purpose by reducing drag on the shoe since they form a wave-like pattern."
- Cushioning: "Cushlon foam in the midsole for a soft, plush underfoot experience, and an Air Zoom Turbo unit in the forefoot for a snappy, responsive boost."
- "For the debut Caitlin Blue colorway, Nike and Clark take inspiration from the depth of the sky, the infinite possibilities it represents, and Caitlin Clark's unlimited range on the court."

## Quote

- Clark: "Having my own shoe has been a dream for as long as I can remember, and seeing it come to life is pretty incredible. I wanted it to reflect how I play—fast, confident, and ready to let it fly. Nike and I really crushed it. It was a true partnership. They listened to every detail, and the innovation is designed for my game. Seeing the finished product for the first time will forever be a core memory."

## Byline

- Nicholas Vlahos, Sole Retriever. Published June 17, 2026 at 11:30 AM. Article tags shown: Caitlin 1, Caitlin Clark, Nike, WNBA, Basketball.

wikis.title: Tesla Optimus production at Fremont and the delayed V3 reveal
wikis.summary: Electrek report on Tesla's Q1 2026 earnings call, where Elon Musk set Optimus production at Fremont for late July or August and pushed the Gen 3 reveal again.
wikis.body:
## What was said on the call

- "During Tesla's Q1 2026 earnings call today, CEO Elon Musk confirmed that Optimus robot production will begin at Fremont in late July or August - just four months after the last Model S and X roll off the line in early May."
- Musk warned initial output will be "quite slow", calling it "literally impossible to predict" the production rate this year, given Optimus has 10,000 unique parts across an entirely new production line.
- He declined to give any production target for 2026, saying only that initial skills for the robots will be "simple skills in the factory".

## Converting the Model S/X line

- "The last Model S and X vehicles will be produced in early May, ending a 14-year production run for the Model S and 11 years for the Model X."
- "Combined, Tesla produced over 610,000 of these vehicles - but sales had dwindled to roughly 30,000 annually, a fraction of the line's 100,000-unit capacity."
- Tesla will dismantle the entire line from the ground up, starting with smaller parts production equipment and working forward to final assembly, "which Musk said will be torn down next month", then install entirely new equipment for Optimus including wiring, communications and testing infrastructure.
- Musk: "If we were able to go from stopping production on one line, dismantling that entire line, reinstalling a whole new line, and turning that on in a matter of four months, that is an insanely fast speed. I don't think any other company on Earth has ever done that before."

## The 10,000-part problem

- Optimus is described as a brand-new product on a brand-new line with over 10,000 unique components, none of which have been through mass production.
- Musk: "It will move as fast as the least lucky, slowest, dumbest part in the entire 10,000. It is impossible to predict these things."
- The article calls this a walk-back from Musk's January 2025 prediction of "roughly 10,000 Optimus robots" being built that year, a target it says Tesla missed entirely, with Musk admitting in January 2026 that zero Optimus robots were doing "useful work" in Tesla's factories.

## Second factory and Gen 3 reveal

- Musk confirmed a second Optimus factory under construction at Giga Texas, "with production expected to begin around summer 2027", on the north campus expansion, "expected to eventually produce the higher-volume Gen 4 variant".
- The Gen 3 reveal was "originally expected in Q1 2026"; Musk pushed it to "probably middle of this year". The stated reason: competitors "do a frame-by-frame analysis whenever we release something and copy everything they possibly can."
- The headline calls this reveal "Optimus V3" while the body calls it "Gen 3".

## Competitors named

- Boston Dynamics is shipping its electric Atlas humanoid to Hyundai factories this year, "with plans for a production facility capable of 30,000 units annually".
- Figure AI, "valued at $39 billion", has an active pilot deployment at BMW.
- Agility Robotics' Digit is "already commercially deployed in customer warehouses, including at a Toyota plant in Ontario".

## Byline

- Fred Lambert, "Apr 22 2026 - 5:15 pm PT". The piece ends with an opinion section ("Electrek's Take") not summarized here.

wikis.title: Ford Universal EV Platform and the $30,000 midsize electric pickup
wikis.summary: EVwire report on Ford's unveiling of its Universal EV Platform and the roughly $30,000 midsize electric pickup to be built at Louisville Assembly Plant in 2027.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- "Ford unveiled the Ford Universal EV Platform, a new fundamental approach to how Ford makes its electric vehicles, starting with a four-door midsize $30,000 electric pickup truck built in the Louisville Assembly Plant in 2027."
- Ford called it a "Model T moment" for its EVs; a Ford Model T was placed next to the stage.
- Result of a "skunkworks" EV design center in Long Beach, California.
- No vehicle specifications were released; the writer notes "there seems to be at least one prototype out there that they showed selected employees."

## The truck

- Midsize four-door electric pickup, "targeted starting price of about $30,000", assembled at Louisville Assembly Plant, "reaching customers in 2027".
- "targeted 0-60 time as fast as a Mustang EcoBoost, with more downforce."
- Forecast to have more passenger room than the latest Toyota RAV4, before the frunk and truck bed; gear can be locked in the bed without a roof rack or hitch rack.
- Ford says the truck has a lower five-year cost of ownership than a three-year-old used Tesla Model Y.
- Additional specifications - "reveal date, starting price, EPA-estimated battery range, battery sizes, and charge times" - "will be communicated later."

## Platform and battery

- Parts reduced by 20% versus a typical vehicle, 25% fewer fasteners, 40% fewer workstations dock-to-dock, 15% faster assembly time.
- Wiring harness ">4,000 feet (1.3 kilometers) shorter and 10 kilograms lighter (22 pounds)" than the one in Ford's first-gen electric SUV.
- New zonal electric architecture; "no mention of 48V, and the platform will reportedly stay at 400V."
- Prismatic LFP batteries used as a structural sub-assembly that also serves as the vehicle's floor, made in the US; "there will reportedly be NMC longer range versions, too."
- The article attributes to InsideEVs, from a media briefing, that Ford aims to make the battery 15% smaller than the BYD Atto 3's, which by EVwire's own calculation "would put it at ~51kWh usable energy" and "might mean it falls into a 150-200 mile usable range". These are the writer's calculations, not Ford figures.

## Assembly "tree"

- Ford transformed the traditional assembly line into an "assembly tree": three sub-assemblies run down their own lines simultaneously and then join.
- Large single-piece aluminum unicastings replace dozens of smaller parts, letting front and rear be assembled separately; they are then combined with the third sub-assembly, the structural battery, which is independently assembled with seats, consoles and carpeting.
- Parts travel to operators in a kit containing all fasteners, scanners and power tools needed, in the correct orientation.
- Ford says the system "dramatically improves ergonomics for employees by reducing twisting, reaching and bending"; the livestream cited 63% less sitting inside the vehicle to install parts and 60%+ improvement in overhead reaching.

## Louisville Assembly Plant

- Plant expands by 52,000 square feet to move material more efficiently.
- Digital upgrades to give it "the fastest network with the most access points out of any Ford plant globally"; Ford said it will have the highest level of automation of all Ford plants.
- Assembly of the midsize electric truck "could be up to 40% faster than the Louisville Assembly Plant's current vehicles."
- Ford "plans to invest nearly $2 billion in the Louisville Assembly Plant", "securing 2,200 hourly jobs", supported by an incentive offer from the Kentucky Economic Development Finance Authority.

## Quotes

- Jim Farley, Ford President and CEO: "We took a radical approach to a very hard challenge: Create affordable vehicles that delight customers in every way that matters - design, innovation, flexibility, space, driving pleasure, and cost of ownership - and do it with American workers."
- Doug Field, Ford chief EV, digital and design officer: "We took inspiration from the Model T - the universal car that changed the world... Our new zonal electric architecture unlocks capabilities the industry has never seen. This isn't a stripped-down, old-school vehicle." Elsewhere quoted as "This is not going to be a stripped-down, old-school vehicle as a path to low cost."

## Byline and sources

- Jaan Juurikas, "Aug 11, 2025". Source given as "Ford press release, and the livestream of the event."
- The page's headline dates the launch to 2027 while the byline is 2025; the article covers the unveiling, not the launch.

wikis.title: The Hobbit: The Desolation of Smaug (2013 film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia's article on Peter Jackson's 2013 film The Hobbit: The Desolation of Smaug - credits, plot, the full cast list, production and score, marketing and release dates, home media, $959 million box office and critical reception.
wikis.body:
## Infobox

- **The Hobbit: The Desolation of Smaug**, "2013 fantasy film directed by Peter Jackson". Screenplay by **Fran Walsh, Philippa Boyens, Peter Jackson and Guillermo del Toro**; based on *The Hobbit* by J. R. R. Tolkien.
- Produced by Carolynne Cunningham, Zane Weiner, Fran Walsh and Peter Jackson. Cinematography **Andrew Lesnie**; edited by **Jabez Olssen**; music by **Howard Shore**.
- Production companies **New Line Cinema**, **Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Pictures**, **WingNut Films**; distributed by **Warner Bros. Pictures**.
- Release dates **2 December 2013** (Los Angeles premiere), **12 December 2013** (New Zealand), **13 December 2013** (United States). Running time **161 minutes**; countries New Zealand and United States; language English.
- Budget **$217-250 million**; box office **$959 million**.
- Billed cast: Ian McKellen, Martin Freeman, Richard Armitage, Benedict Cumberbatch, Evangeline Lilly, Lee Pace, Luke Evans, Ken Stott, James Nesbitt, Orlando Bloom.

## Lead

- Sequel to 2012's *The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey*, the second instalment in *The Hobbit* trilogy and a prequel to Jackson's *The Lord of the Rings* trilogy.
- Bilbo Baggins continues with Thorin Oakenshield and the dwarves toward the Lonely Mountain and the dragon Smaug, pursued by the orcs Azog the Defiler and his son Bolg, while Gandalf investigates "the return of a long-forgotten evil force in the ruins of Dol Guldur".
- "The films were shot simultaneously in 3D at a projection rate of 48 frames per second, with principal photography taking place around New Zealand and at Pinewood Studios. Additional filming took place throughout May 2013."
- Premiered in Los Angeles 2 December 2013, released 12 December in New Zealand and 13 December in the United States. "Produced by Warner Bros Pictures through its subsidiary New Line Cinema, the film received mostly positive reviews and grossed $959 million at the worldwide box office, making it the fourth highest-grossing film of 2013."
- Nominated at the 86th Academy Awards for **Best Sound Editing, Best Sound Mixing and Best Visual Effects**. The final instalment, *The Hobbit: The Battle of the Five Armies*, was released in 2014.

## Where the article disagrees with itself

- **Release dates**: the infobox and lead give New Zealand 12 December and the US 13 December 2013; the Theatrical release section says the film "was released internationally on 11 December 2013 and in the United Kingdom and United States on 13 December 2013", without the New Zealand date.
- **Critical reaction**: the lead says the film "received mostly positive reviews", while the Critical response section records that before release E! reported reviews had been "mixed", though "much better" than the previous film.

## Plot (as summarised in the article)

- After the battle with Azog, Gandalf takes Thorin's company to Beorn, a skin-changer who becomes a bear. The Necromancer summons Azog to Dol Guldur to marshal his forces, and Azog gives the hunt for Thorin to Bolg.
- Beorn escorts them to Mirkwood; Gandalf finds Black Speech on an old ruin and, following a request from Galadriel, leaves to investigate the tombs of the Nazgûl. The company strays from the path and is caught by giant spiders; Bilbo frees them with the ring and glimpses its dark influence when he "brutally kills a giant centipede" to retrieve it.
- Wood-elves led by Tauriel and Legolas capture the dwarves and bring Thorin to Thranduil, who imprisons them after Thorin confronts him over abandoning Erebor 60 years earlier. Bilbo frees them in empty wine barrels; a three-way river battle with elves and Bolg's orcs leaves Kíli wounded by a Morgul shaft.
- Thranduil seals his kingdom after an orc captive reveals an army massing in the south; Tauriel leaves to help the dwarves and Legolas follows. Gandalf and Radagast find the Nazgûl tombs empty and deduce Sauron has returned.
- Bard the bargeman smuggles the company into Esgaroth; Thorin promises the Master a share of the treasure. Kíli stays behind with Fíli, Óin and Bofur. Bilbo finds the hidden entrance, is sent for the Arkenstone and wakes Smaug.
- Bard, descendant of Dale's last ruler, prepares the last black arrow but is arrested; Bolg's orcs attack the four dwarves in Laketown until Tauriel and Legolas intervene, Bolg escaping.
- Gandalf enters Dol Guldur alone, is overpowered by the Necromancer - revealed as Sauron - and watches Azog's army march on the Lonely Mountain. Inside, Bilbo and the dwarves relight the forge with Smaug's flames and bury him in molten gold, but he emerges and flies off to destroy Laketown.

## Cast

- **Martin Freeman** (Bilbo Baggins), **Ian McKellen** (Gandalf the Grey), **Richard Armitage** (Thorin Oakenshield II), **Benedict Cumberbatch** (Smaug, vocal performance and motion capture, and The Necromancer / Sauron), **Evangeline Lilly** (Tauriel, "the elven chief of the Mirkwood Guards"), **Luke Evans** (Bard the Bowman, and his ancestor Girion in a flashback), **Lee Pace** (Thranduil), **Stephen Fry** (Master of Lake-town), **Orlando Bloom** (Legolas Greenleaf).
- Dwarves: Graham McTavish (Dwalin), Ken Stott (Balin), Aidan Turner (Kíli), Dean O'Gorman (Fíli), Mark Hadlow (Dori), Jed Brophy (Nori), Adam Brown (Ori), John Callen (Óin), Peter Hambleton (Glóin, father of Gimli), William Kircher (Bifur), James Nesbitt (Bofur), Stephen Hunter (Bombur).
- Also Cate Blanchett (Galadriel), Mikael Persbrandt (Beorn), Sylvester McCoy (Radagast the Brown), Manu Bennett (Azog the Defiler), Lawrence Makoare (Bolg), Craig Hall (Galion), Ryan Gage (Alfrid), John Bell (Bain), Mark Mitchinson (Braga), Ben Mitchell (Narzug), Stephen Ure (Fimbul), Robin Kerr (Elros), Simon London (Feren), Dallas Barnett (Bill Ferny Snr).
- Extended Edition only: **Antony Sher as Thráin**, Thorin's father held captive at Dol Guldur.
- Cameos: Peter Jackson reprises the man eating a carrot in Bree; his daughter Katie plays Barliman Butterbur's wife Betsy; Philippa Boyens's daughter Phoebe and scale double Kiran Shah appear in the Prancing Pony; James Nesbitt's daughters Peggy and Mary play Bard's daughters Sigrid and Tilda; Stephen Colbert and his family, WingNut Films assistant Norman Kali and producer Zane Weiner appear as Lake-town spies; editor Jabez Olssen appears as a fishmonger. Brian Sergent and Peter Vere-Jones voice the Mirkwood spiders - "This was the final performance of Vere-Jones before his death in January 2021."

## Production

- Most filming finished during 2012, ending in **July 2012**. Additional shooting for this film and *The Battle of the Five Armies* began in New Zealand in **May 2013** and lasted **10 weeks**. Unmanned aerial vehicles (drones) were used for some shots.

## Score

- Composed and conducted by **Howard Shore** "in association with local New Zealand writing teams" and performed by the **New Zealand Symphony Orchestra**. The soundtrack album was released **10 December 2013** and "received positive reviews, especially for its new themes".
- **Ed Sheeran** wrote and recorded "**I See Fire**" for the end credits; it was released on iTunes on **5 November 2013**.

## Marketing

- Peter Jackson gave the first details at a live event on **24 March 2013**, accessible with a code included with DVD editions of *An Unexpected Journey*. He described Tauriel as part of the elven guard and a bodyguard of Thranduil, and showed a scene of Gandalf and Radagast discovering the Ringwraiths released from their graves.
- First trailer **11 June 2013**; an extra-long three-minute trailer/sneak peek on **4 November 2013**, which "revealed new footage and major plot points". The same day a live online fan event hosted by Anderson Cooper in New York ran across eleven cities with Jackson, Jed Brophy, Evangeline Lilly, Lee Pace, Orlando Bloom, Luke Evans, Andy Serkis and Richard Armitage.
- Freeman, Armitage, Cumberbatch, Evans, Lilly, Jackson and, "to a lesser extent", Bloom and McKellen did the press tour.

## Release and home media

- Premiere at the Dolby Theatre, Los Angeles, **2 December 2013**; international release **11 December 2013**; UK and US **13 December 2013**. An extended edition had a limited re-release on **7 October 2015** with a special greeting from Peter Jackson.
- DVD, Blu-ray and Blu-ray 3D: **7 April 2014** in the UK, **8 April 2014** in the US, in a Limited Collector's Edition combo pack, a Blu-ray 3D combo, a Blu-ray combo and a two-disc DVD special edition, with three making-of featurettes, four production web videos and the "I See Fire" music video. Home video earned **$95.1 million** on **4.7 million copies**, the fifth best-selling title of 2014.
- Extended edition: digital **21 October 2014**; DVD, Blu-ray and 3D Blu-ray **3 November 2014** (UK) and **4 November 2014** (US), with **25 minutes** of new material and original music.
- Ultra HD Blu-ray **30 November 2020** (UK) and **1 December 2020** (US) with the rest of the trilogy in both cuts.

## Box office

- **$258.4 million** in North America and **$700.6 million** elsewhere for **$959 million** worldwide; Deadline Hollywood estimated profit of **$134.1 million**. Fourth highest-grossing film of 2013, with **$209 million** worldwide on its opening weekend.
- North America: **$8.8 million** at midnight openings, the second-highest December showing ever behind the first instalment; **$31.2 million** opening day, topping the box office; **$73.6 million** opening weekend, a 13% drop from its predecessor; number one for three consecutive weekends.
- International: released on **16,405 screens**, earning **$135.4 million** in its opening weekend, with the largest openings in China ($33.0 million), Germany ($19.0 million) and the United Kingdom, Ireland and Malta ($15.2 million). Number one outside North America for four consecutive weekends and five in total. The highest-grossing film of 2013 in many European countries and in New Zealand and Fiji.

## Critical response

- Rotten Tomatoes **74%**, average 6.80/10 from 251 reviews; consensus: "While still slightly hamstrung by 'middle chapter' narrative problems and its formidable length, The Desolation of Smaug represents a more confident, exciting second chapter for the Hobbit series." Metacritic **66 out of 100** from 44 reviews, "generally favorable". CinemaScore **A−**, down from the first film's A.
- Early reaction: Metro called it "glowing" and a "spectacle"; The Guardian reported "much stronger early reviews"; E! reported reviews had been "mixed" but "much better" than the previous film; after international release MTV called the reaction "positive" and the Los Angeles Times said the consensus was that the film "reinvigorates" the series, putting it "back on course".
- Favourable: Nick de Semlyen (Empire) 5/5 - "Middle-earth's got its mojo back. A huge improvement on the previous instalment". Richard Corliss (TIME) named it one of the top ten films of 2013 - "close to the grandeur of Jackson's Lord of the Rings films". Justin Chang (Variety): the trilogy "finds its footing in this much more exciting and purposeful second chapter". Todd McCarthy (The Hollywood Reporter) found "nearly everything" an improvement and praised the High Frame Rate over *An Unexpected Journey*'s. Mark Hughes (Forbes): "another grand entry in the Tolkien saga". Peter Bradshaw (The Guardian) 4/5. Total Film 4/5, with Matt Maytum noting "middle-act wobbles" but praising "rousing action... incredible visuals... and one stupendous dragon". Jim Vejvoda (IGN) 8.5/10.
- Unfavourable: Peter Travers (Rolling Stone) 2.5/4 called it "a little less long and a little less boring" than the first, praised Smaug as "a bloody wonder of slithering fright" but criticised the padding of "a slender novel". Robbie Collin (The Daily Telegraph) 2/5 said Jackson "is mostly stalling for time: two or three truly great sequences tangled up in long beards and longer pit-stops", and disapproved of the added love triangle: "let's at least accept that Tolkien would probably not have been among them".

wikis.title: Cast and cameos
wikis.summary: Who plays whom, including Cumberbatch's double role, the Extended Edition addition and the family cameos.
wikis.body:
- **Benedict Cumberbatch** performs Smaug through voice and motion capture, and also plays The Necromancer, "later revealed to be the Dark Lord Sauron".
- **Luke Evans** plays Bard the Bowman and also his ancestor Girion, the last king of old Dale, in a flashback.
- **Evangeline Lilly** plays Tauriel, chief of the Mirkwood Guards, who falls in love with Kíli (Aidan Turner); **Lee Pace** is Thranduil, **Orlando Bloom** Legolas, **Stephen Fry** the Master of Lake-town.
- The thirteen dwarves are played by Richard Armitage, Graham McTavish, Ken Stott, Aidan Turner, Dean O'Gorman, Mark Hadlow, Jed Brophy, Adam Brown, John Callen, Peter Hambleton (Glóin, "father of Gimli"), William Kircher, James Nesbitt and Stephen Hunter.
- **Antony Sher appears as Thráin, Thorin's father held captive at Dol Guldur, only in the Extended Edition.**
- Cameos: Peter Jackson reprises the man eating a carrot in Bree; his daughter Katie plays Betsy Butterbur; Philippa Boyens's daughter Phoebe and scale double Kiran Shah appear in the Prancing Pony; James Nesbitt's daughters Peggy and Mary play Sigrid and Tilda; Stephen Colbert and family, Norman Kali and Zane Weiner are Lake-town spies; editor Jabez Olssen is a fishmonger.
- Brian Sergent and Peter Vere-Jones voice the Mirkwood spiders; it was Vere-Jones's final performance before his death in January 2021.

wikis.summary: When the film was shot and who made its score and end-credits song.
wikis.body:
- The trilogy was shot simultaneously in 3D at **48 frames per second**, with principal photography around New Zealand and at Pinewood Studios.
- Most filming finished during 2012, ending in **July 2012**; additional shooting for this film and *The Battle of the Five Armies* began in New Zealand in **May 2013** and lasted **10 weeks**.
- Drones were used for some shots in the film.
- The score was composed and conducted by **Howard Shore** "in association with local New Zealand writing teams" and performed by the **New Zealand Symphony Orchestra**; the soundtrack album came out **10 December 2013** and was praised especially for its new themes.
- **Ed Sheeran** wrote and recorded "**I See Fire**" for the end credits, released on iTunes **5 November 2013**, with a music video included in the home release extras.

wikis.title: Dates announced for next 2 Oscar ceremonies
wikis.summary: NBC Los Angeles news item reporting the Academy's announcement of the dates of the 99th and 100th Academy Awards ceremonies, the last two to be held at the Dolby Theatre.
wikis.body:
## What the Academy announced
- "The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences Tuesday announced the dates of the next two Academy Awards ceremonies -- the last Oscar ceremonies that will be held at the Dolby Theatre in Hollywood."
- The 99th Oscars will be held March 14, 2027.
- The 100th ceremony will take place March 5, 2028.
- "Both ceremonies will begin at 4 p.m. Pacific Time."
- Nominations for the 99th Oscars will be announced Jan. 21, 2027.
- The Academy's annual Governors Awards event will be held "this year on Nov. 15".

## Venue and broadcaster changes
- "Beginning with the 101st Oscars in 2029, the ceremony will move to the Peacock Theater at L.A. Live in downtown Los Angeles."
- The Academy "last month" announced an agreement with theater owner AEG to hold the ceremony at the downtown venue "through at least 2039".
- "Also in 2029, the Oscar telecast will move from ABC to YouTube."

## Publication
- NBC Los Angeles, by City News Service. Published April 7, 2026; updated April 7, 2026 at 2:31 pm. Tagged under "Academy Awards".

wikis.title: 2027 UEFA Champions League final: Estadio Metropolitano, Madrid
wikis.summary: UEFA.com article confirming Madrid's Estadio Metropolitano as host of the 2026/27 Champions League final on Saturday 5 June 2027, with the venue's history and the winners' rewards.
wikis.body:
## The decision

- "Madrid's **Estadio Metropolitano** has been selected as the host for the **2026/27 UEFA Champions League final**, which is scheduled for **Saturday 5 June 2027**."
- Article summary: "The 2026/27 UEFA Champions League final will take place at Atlético de Madrid's Estadio Metropolitano."
- Article dated **Wednesday, September 9, 2026**.
- Photo caption: "The Estadio Metropolitano will mark its tenth anniversary in 2027".

## Where and when

- "This will be the Estadio Metropolitano's **second** Champions League final, having staged the **2019** decider when Liverpool defeated Tottenham 2-0."
- "Home of Atlético de Madrid since **2017**, the venue is in the **Rosas** neighbourhood of the Spanish capital."
- "It will be Madrid's **sixth final** in all (only London has hosted more). The Estadio Santiago Bernabéu staged the European Cup finals of **1957, 1969, 1980 and 2010**."
- The 5 June 2027 final marks "the conclusion of the **72nd season** of Europe's elite club competition and the **35th** since it was renamed the UEFA Champions League".
- "Details of where to watch the Champions League final will be available here in due course."

## Extra time and penalties

- "If scores are level at the end of normal time, two 15-minute periods of extra time are played. If one of the teams scores more goals than the other during extra time, that team are declared the winners. If scores remain level after extra time, the winners are determined by a penalty shoot-out."

## History of the Estadio Metropolitano

- "The reconstructed stadium replaced the Vicente Calderón as home of three-time UEFA Europa League winners Atlético de Madrid." It "is named in honour of the original Estadio Metropolitano – Atleti's home until **1966**."
- "Estadio Metropolitano opened to the public on **16 September 2017** when Atleti faced Málaga in La Liga; **Antoine Griezmann** scored the stadium's first goal in a **1-0** home win."
- "Located on the Avenida Luis Aragonés (named in honour of Spain's UEFA EURO 2008-winning coach), it has a capacity of around **70,000**."
- "Built with environmental concerns in mind, the stadium's LED lighting and solar panels reduce energy consumption, while recycled rainwater irrigates the pitch. The stadium was the **first 100% LED stadium in the world**."
- "Located in the north east of Madrid, it is easily reached on subway line seven (station: Estadio Metropolitano)." (The article separately places the venue "in the Rosas neighbourhood of the Spanish capital".)
- "The stadium has also been shortlisted to hold matches at the **2030 FIFA World Cup** finals", and has hosted rugby union matches, the World Rugby Sevens Series Grand Final, boxing events and music concerts.

## What the winners get

- "The UEFA Champions League trophy stands **73.5cm** tall and weighs **7.5kg**. 'Everybody in football is keen to get their hands on it,' said creator **Jürg Stadelmann**."
- The winners "will also earn the right to play against the winners of the 2026/27 UEFA Europa League in the **2027 UEFA Super Cup**", and "gain an automatic place in the league phase of the 2027/28 Champions League, if they have not qualified via their domestic competition."

## Future finals

- **2028**: Munich Football Arena, Munich.
- **2029**: Camp Nou, Barcelona.

wikis.title: Where is the Ballon d'Or 2026 ceremony? Why the gala has moved from Paris
wikis.summary: Yahoo Sports republication of a Sporting News article of 8 September 2026 explaining that the 2026 Ballon d'Or gala moves to London on 26 October and why.
wikis.body:
## Venue and date

- "The 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony is being held in London, UK. Organisers have not yet announced the venue, but it will reportedly be the London Palladium, a world-famous theatre that opened in 1910."
- "It is the first time the gala will take place in England's capital city."
- "The ceremony is on Monday, October 26, 2026. It is due to begin at 8 p.m. local time (3 p.m. ET), with the red-carpet event beginning around 90 minutes earlier."
- "The Ballon d'Or awards ceremony is now less than two months away", with "the nominees due to be announced on September 8".

## Why London

- "The ceremony is in London in 2026 to mark the 70th anniversary of the awarding of the very first Ballon d'Or."
- "In 1956, Sir Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize at a smaller and far less glamorous event in Blackpool on England's northwest coast."
- Organisers, confirming the venue change: "The legendary Blackpool and Stoke winger was a true ambassador of football, dedicating a lifelong devotion to his craft, a commitment to enthral, and to fair play", and "as the Ballon d'Or becomes of septuagenarian age, it is fitting in such a landmark year to celebrate the finest present-day exponents of the beautiful game in the beating heart of the country that first conceived of it."

## Stanley Matthews

- Nicknamed "The Wizard of Dribble"; "considered one of England's finest ever soccer players".
- He "spent most of his long playing career at Stoke City and Blackpool, although he played briefly for Toronto City in Canada", and "played until he was 50 years old".
- "He remains both the oldest man to appear in England's highest league and to represent the national team, with his final cap coming at the age of 42."
- "Matthews was already 41 when he won the very first Ballon d'Or." Pele "reportedly said Matthews was 'the man who taught us the way football should be played.'"

## Previous venues

- "Since 2019, the Ballon d'Or ceremony has been held at the Theatre du Chatelet in Paris, France"; earlier Paris venues included the Eiffel Tower.
- "Between 2010 and 2015, when the award was called the FIFA Ballon d'Or due to a partnership with the game's governing body, the ceremony was typically held in Zurich, Switzerland."
- The prize was "created by French publication France Football".

## Byline

- Joe Wright, Tue, Sep 8, 2026, 3 min read. The page notes the story "originally appeared on The Sporting News".

wikis.title: 2027 Grammy Awards: nominations and telecast dates set for move to ABC and Hulu
wikis.summary: Variety report that the 69th Grammy Awards will air Feb. 7, 2027 on ABC, Hulu and Disney+, with nominations on Nov. 16.
wikis.body:
## Dates

- "The Grammy Awards will be held on Feb. 7, 2027, as the ceremony moves to ABC, Hulu and Disney+ in the U.S. after more than 50 years on CBS."
- "Nominations for the 69th annual Grammy kudos will be revealed on Nov. 16."
- Eligibility period "runs Aug. 31, 2025 through Aug. 31, 2026."
- First-round nominations voting: Oct. 12-22. Final round voting: Dec. 10, 2026-Jan. 7, 2027.

## Venue and production

- "The ceremony will originate live from Crypto.com Arena in downtown Los Angeles."
- "There's no official word on a producer yet but it is expected that Ben Winston will continue at the helm of the event that he has steered since 2021" - the article's own hedge.

## Quotes

- Harvey Mason jr., CEO of the Grammys: "The Grammys are all about celebrating the music that moves the world, and this moment is built on exactly that... This is an exciting time for us as an organization - a new home and a bold new chapter for the Grammy Awards. We're just getting started and the best is yet to come."
- Rita Ferro, Disney's president of global advertising, on Monday's "Daily Variety" podcast: "Come January, we have four of the biggest live events across entertainment and sports. We have the college football championship. Then we go to the first time ever the Grammys will be on ABC and across our our portfolio of streaming platforms. A week later, we'll have the Super Bowl for the first time in over 20 years on ESPN and ABC. And a couple weeks later, we're going to have the Oscars. Four events that would normally sit across four different companies are all sitting here."

## Byline and photo

- By William Earl, "May 12, 2026 2:29pm PT".
- Photo caption: "Bad Bunny collects a trophy at the 2026 Grammy Awards in February". Image credit Billboard via Getty Images.

wikis.title: John Deere Manufacturing: A Giant Emerges
wikis.summary: Free Documentary - Engineering video page about the John Deere combine harvester factory in Zweibruecken and the T670 machine built there.
wikis.body:
## The video
- Title: "John Deere Manufacturing: A Giant Emerges | FD Engineering". Channel: Free Documentary - Engineering. Published 2024-12-27.

## The factory
- "Zweibruecken in Rheinland-Pfalz is home to one of Europe's largest combine harvester factories." (written "Zweibrucken"/"Zweibrücken" in the description.)
- The harvesters made there "are not only delivered across Europe but are also exported and used worldwide".

## The T670 combine harvester
- Described as "a veritable harvesting factory on wheels".
- "In one hour, this XXL combine can harvest up to 50 tons of grain."
- "Standing at 4 meters high and weighing an impressive 21 tons, the T670 is one of the largest and most formidable agricultural vehicles globally."

## What the documentary covers
- The manufacturing process from design and engineering through the assembly line, the T670 working in the field, and interviews with engineers.
- The description also links a related film, "Caterpillar Manufacturing - Inside the Factories Building Behemoths".

wikis.title: Giant Autoclave: World's Largest Gold Extractor
wikis.summary: Free Documentary - Engineering video page about moving the world's largest gold-extraction autoclave from Belgium to a gold plant in Russia.
wikis.body:
## The video
- Title: "Giant Autoclave: World's Largest Gold Extractor | Mega Transports | FD Engineering". Channel: Free Documentary - Engineering. Published 2024-12-01.

## The machine
- "A unique mega transport made of steel and titanium with a special purpose: to extract tons of gold. This so-called autoclave is the biggest of its kind."
- "Its weight: over one thousand tons."
- "At seven and a half metres in diameter, it is as high as a house."
- "And at fifty-one metres in length, it is as long as four trucks lined up one behind the other."

## The route
- "The starting point: Geel in Belgium. From the departure point, the journey follows roads and rivers to Antwerp."
- "From there, a heavy-lift cargo ship will take the autoclave to the easternmost seaport in Russia. The route then follows the river Armur to the gold plant." (the description spells the river "Armur".)
- "A total of twenty-five thousand kilometres."

## The obstacles
- Motorways and bridges "some of them so low that the clearance will be just a few centimeters"; getting stuck underneath is called "an absolute No-Go" for "a multi-million dollar machine filled with sensitive technology".
- "Weather conditions in Russia means transport is possible only during a few weeks each year. The river level is otherwise too high." Missing the window means waiting "a whole year".
- "And this year of all years, the water level is higher than ever. Will the team successfully battle against this once-in-a-century flood?"
- The description also links a related film, "Titans of Transport - Moving the World's Heaviest Objects".

wikis.title: Rare Earth Mining: The Key to our Technological Future
wikis.summary: Free Documentary - Engineering video page on rare earth mining, China's share of production, the environmental cost and the search for alternatives.
wikis.body:
## The video
- Title: "Rare Earth Mining: The Key to our Technological Future | FD Engineering". Channel: Free Documentary - Engineering. Published 2023-08-11.

## What the description states
- "Smart phones, laptops, touch screens, wind turbines, hybrid vehicles: they all need rare earth materials."
- "Today China mines an incredible 97% of all rare earth minerals extracted worldwide."
- "The Chinese government makes good use of this monopoly: recently, it cut production by about two-thirds. Within days the prices of some rare earth metals shot up by 1000%."
- Downsides given: "Environmental pollution, destroyed landscapes and radioactive residues, as rare earth metal deposits are usually laced with radioactive minerals and are extremely difficult to refine."

## The research the film follows
- Researchers drilling for new deposits "in Europe and Australia".
- Attempts at "new, more environmentally friendly ways of processing the materials".
- Recycling rare earths "out of old mobile phones and computers".
- Physicists and chemists "working on ground-breaking new materials that could soon replace rare earths completely".
- The description also links a related film, "Mega Machines: Taming Mechanical Giants".

wikis.title: Microsoft Windows 8.1 Gets October Release Date
wikis.summary: eWeek report that Microsoft set October 17 as the release date for the free Windows 8.1 update, with a summary of the update's features.
wikis.body:
## Release date

- "The first major update to Microsoft's flagship Windows 8 operating system will be officially released Oct. 17, the company announced."
- Microsoft spokesman Brandon LeBlanc said in an Aug 14 blog post that the free update will arrive "just before Windows 8 celebrates its 1-year anniversary".
- LeBlanc, quoted: "starting at 12 a.m. on Oct. 18 in New Zealand (that's 4 a.m., Oct. 17 in Redmond), Windows 8.1 will begin rolling out worldwide as a free update for consumers on Windows 8 through the Windows Store."
- "Windows 8.1 will also be available at retail and on new devices starting on Oct. 18 by market," he wrote.
- The page gives two dates for the same rollout: Oct. 17 as the official release date, a first availability at 12 a.m. Oct. 18 New Zealand time (4 a.m. Oct. 17 in Redmond), and retail and new devices from Oct. 18 by market.

## Hardware expectations

- "Microsoft and several of its OEM partners are widely expected to debut new Windows 8 systems, including small tablets" - the article's own hedge.
- Existing devices named as benefiting from the upgrade: Microsoft's Surface and Lenovo's Yoga 11S. LeBlanc: "If you buy a Windows 8 device today, you can look forward to the new features and improvements from Windows 8.1 in October."

## Features

- Available at the time as a public preview for enterprise users and consumers.
- Option to boot directly to the desktop view instead of the Live Tile interface; the Start button reappears after being dropped in favour of the search charm and hot corners.
- Tighter integration with "Microsoft's soon-to-be-renamed cloud storage service, SkyDrive"; Internet Explorer 11; expanded personalization; streamlined Windows Store.
- 3D printing: Microsoft announced "in late June" that Windows 8.1 would include 3D printer and file format support. Shanen Boettcher, general manager of Microsoft's Startup Business Group, in a June 26 blog post: "Making a 3D object on your PC will be as easy as writing a document in Word and sending it to print. Just as desktop publishing transformed how we write, we think desktop manufacturing will transform how we create."
- Windows 8.1 Enterprise adds virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) support and DirectAccess; conforms to Open Mobile Alliance Device Management (OMA-DM) standards and offers device lockdown, encryption and selective wipe of corporate data without affecting personal data.

## Byline and dates

- Written by Pedro Hernandez. "PUBLISHED: AUG 15, 2013". "UPDATED: FEB 2, 2021". Marked a 2 minute read.

wikis.title: SimCity Cities of Tomorrow expansion pack available now
wikis.summary: Electronic Arts press release of 12 November 2013 announcing that the SimCity Cities of Tomorrow expansion pack is on sale for PC and Mac, with its new content and specializations.
wikis.body:
## Announcement

- Press release dated November 12, 2013, datelined REDWOOD CITY, Calif. (BUSINESS WIRE), issued by Electronic Arts Inc. (NASDAQ: EA). PDF, 2 pages.
- "Electronic Arts Inc. (NASDAQ: EA) today announced that the SimCity Cities of Tomorrow expansion pack is now available for PC and Mac at retail stores across North America and for digital download on Origin."
- The expansion "offers the more than two million players worldwide the opportunity to futurize every aspect of their cities with the help of plausible future technologies".
- "New MegaTowers, new city specializations, new future technology and new transportation methods will transform the way that cities take shape and evolve."

## Content

- Players choose "to create a utopian society underpinned by clean technology under the auspices of The Academy, or encourage giant corporation OmegaCo to strip-mine natural resources and pollute in the name of making massive profits."
- MegaTowers are "massive structures that players build high into the sky and dwarf the rest of the city"; with the right balance they "become self-sustaining monoliths that cater to all of the needs of the Sims under one roof."
- Players can also "rain chaos upon them by unleashing an all-new disaster exclusive to this expansion pack."
- Quote from Patrick Buechner, General Manager, Maxis Emeryville: "MegaTowers, futurization, and the battle between Green and Greed, these are the main foundations that drive an all-new experience in SimCity Cities of Tomorrow." He adds that The Academy's "clean utopian world" "requires a wealthy workforce that demands a higher style of living", while OmegaCo, "while extremely profitable, will take its toll on your Sims as the factories devour your natural resources and spit them back out in the form of harmful pollution."

## Compatibility and availability

- "The SimCity base game is available on PC and Mac and was developed by Maxis. The base game and expansion pack are cross-platform compatible, so all players play together across the same servers."
- Owners of the expansion "can play alongside those who do not own the expansion pack and provide them with futurization benefits when they play together in the same region."
- "Launched last March, SimCity has had eight major game updates that have made upgrades to the core simulation and provided game content at no additional cost."
- "SimCity Cities of Tomorrow is now available in North America for PC and Mac and is rated E10+ by the ESRB." A footnote adds: "Requires SimCity base game to play."

## About the companies (as stated)

- Maxis, "originally founded in 1987, and now an Electronic Arts label with studios in Emeryville, Redwood Shores, and Salt Lake City", created SimCity, Spore and The Sims.
- EA "has more than 300 million registered players in over 200 countries" and "In fiscal year 2013, EA posted GAAP net revenue of $3.8 billion"; headquartered in Redwood City, California.
- Media contacts: Charlie Sinhaseni (Manager) and Rachel Steinberg (Sr. Publicist), Maxis/EA.

wikis.title: Amazon Leo targets mid-2026 commercial launch as enterprise beta goes live
wikis.summary: Report on Amazon's satellite internet service Leo (formerly Project Kuiper) entering enterprise beta on April 8, 2026 with commercial availability targeted for mid-2026, its three terminal tiers, its FCC deadline shortfall and its competition with Starlink.
wikis.body:
## The rebrand and the beta

- Amazon's satellite internet service was rebranded from Project Kuiper to Amazon Leo in November 2025.
- It "entered enterprise beta on April 8, 2026, with commercial availability targeted for mid-2026 per Andy Jassy's annual shareholder letter". Jassy's letter came the day after the beta launched.
- Amazon received FCC approval for a 3,236-satellite low-earth-orbit constellation in 2020; first production satellites launched in April 2025 on an Atlas V operated by United Launch Alliance.
- A business preview programme opened to select enterprise partners shortly after the rebrand.
- The page places Leo "alongside Amazon's $50 billion Trainium chip investment as one of the defining bets in the company's current capital allocation cycle".
- Beta customers: Verizon and AT&T (North America), Vodafone and Vodacom (Europe and Africa), JetBlue (in-flight connectivity), NBN Co (Australia), Vrio (Latin America), NASA, plus Hunt Energy and Crane Worldwide Logistics.

## Three terminals

- **Leo Nano** - consumer and light-enterprise; seven inches square, 2.2 pounds, rated to 100 Mbps download.
- **Leo Pro** - small business, rural operators, mobile backhaul; eleven inches square, 5.3 pounds, priced at under $400, rated to 400 Mbps.
- **Leo Ultra** - enterprise flagship; 20-by-30-inch installation, 43 pounds, 1 Gbps download and 400 Mbps upload, for maritime vessels, commercial aircraft and large-campus deployments.
- Jassy claimed in the shareholder letter that Leo terminals deliver "six to eight times better uplink performance and twice the downlink performance" versus satellite alternatives available to enterprise customers; the page says the claim "will be scrutinised closely once commercial service begins".
- The article's summary says the tiers deliver "up to 1 Gbps for enterprise users".

## FCC deadline and launch shortfall

- The Generation 1 licence requires half the planned 3,236 satellites - 1,618 - in orbit and operational by July 30, 2026.
- As of early April 2026 Amazon has "between 210 and 241 satellites in orbit" (the summary says "approximately 210 to 241"), which the page calls a figure making the original deadline "effectively unreachable".
- Amazon filed a formal request with the FCC in January 2026 for a two-year extension, citing a shortage of available launch vehicles.
- Alongside the filing Amazon disclosed 10 additional Falcon 9 launch contracts with SpaceX and 12 additional New Glenn contracts with Blue Origin (the summary describes this as "22 additional launches").
- Blue Origin separately filed with the FCC for a 51,600-satellite Project Sunrise constellation and a 5,408-satellite TeraWave optical backhaul network.
- The FCC approved Amazon's Generation 2 constellation in February 2026, clearing the path to a potential 7,727-satellite network.
- Contracted vehicles: Atlas V and Vulcan Centaur (ULA), Falcon 9 (SpaceX), Ariane 6 (Arianespace), New Glenn (Blue Origin).

## Starlink and Globalstar

- Starlink generated $10.6 billion in revenue in 2025 at a 54 per cent EBITDA margin, with more than 10 million paying subscribers in more than 100 countries and a constellation of "7,600 to 8,000-plus satellites".
- SpaceX "has filed for the largest IPO in history, seeking to raise $75 billion at a valuation of up to $1.75 trillion, potentially as early as June 2026".
- Leo is being sold primarily through carrier partners and enterprise integrators at launch, using Verizon's, AT&T's and Delta's existing customer relationships.
- Delta has contracted Leo for in-flight Wi-Fi across 500 aircraft starting in 2028, free to SkyMiles members.
- Amazon is "reportedly in talks to acquire Globalstar for approximately $9 billion", which would give access to L-band spectrum; Apple holds a 20 per cent stake in Globalstar through a $1.5 billion investment.

## Byline

- Story by Alina Maria Stan; published April 10, 2026 at 12:54 pm. The page also states "This article was published on April 10, 2026".

wikis.title: Project Helix: building the next generation of Xbox (GDC 2026)
wikis.summary: Xbox Wire post summarising Jason Ronald's Xbox Developer Summit keynote at GDC on March 11, 2026, announcing the next-generation console Project Helix, Xbox mode for Windows 11 and Xbox Play Anywhere milestones.
wikis.body:
## Source

- Xbox Wire post by Jason Ronald, VP, Next Generation, XBOX, dated March 11, 2026, marked "4 min read".
- "This is a summary of my Xbox Developer Summit keynote address, delivered March 11 at the 2026 Game Developer Conference."

## Project Helix (next-generation console)

- The team is "deep in development on our next generation Xbox console, Project Helix", described as the "next-generation first-party console", "designed to play your Xbox console and PC games".
- Powered by a custom AMD SoC, part of a "multi-year partnership with AMD", and "co-designed for the next generation of DirectX and FSR"; the summary says the team is "using FSR Next to power what comes next".
- Claims: "an order of magnitude leap in ray tracing performance and capability", intelligence integrated "directly into the graphics and compute pipeline", and gains in efficiency, scale and visual ambition.
- "I'm excited to share we plan to ship alpha versions of the hardware to developers beginning in 2027."

## Xbox mode on Windows

- "Starting in April, Xbox mode will begin rolling out to Windows in select markets."
- Brought to Windows 11 after debuting "an early version with the ROG Xbox Ally handhelds"; it gives a "full screen and controller optimized Xbox experience" and lets players switch between productivity and play.

## Xbox Play Anywhere and back compatibility

- The Xbox Play Anywhere catalog "now spans more than 1,500 games" / "has grown to over 1,500 games", and "500 development teams have already shipped games with Xbox Play Anywhere".
- Games bought once carry progress across screens.
- Commitment to "keeping games from four generations of Xbox playable for years to come", with "new ways to play some of the most iconic games from our past" rolling out as part of the 25th anniversary later this year.

## Anniversary and developers

- "As we celebrate 25 years of Xbox this year", with thanks to "more than 5,000 developers around the world currently building for Xbox".
- Named upcoming releases: the return of Halo and Gears of War, plus Beethoven & Dinosaur's *Mixtape* and *Crimson Desert* from Pearl Abyss.
- The post says more will be shared "later this year".

## Tags on the post

- Filed under: Future of Play, AMD, Console, GDC, hardware, Microsoft, pc gaming, Project Helix, Xbox, Xbox Mode, Xbox Play Anywhere.

wikis.title: The Thomas Crown Affair (2027 film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the upcoming American action romantic heist film directed by Michael B. Jordan, a second remake of the 1968 film, scheduled for release in the United States on March 5, 2027.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- "The Thomas Crown Affair is an upcoming American action romantic heist film directed by Michael B. Jordan and written by Drew Pearce and Jason Hall." It is described as a second remake of the 1968 film; the first remake was released in 1999.
- Based on *The Thomas Crown Affair* by Alan R. Trustman; story by Alan R. Trustman and Drew Pearce.
- Producers: Michael B. Jordan, Patrick McCormick, Marc Toberoff, Charles Roven.
- Cinematography: Bradford Young. Music by Jon Batiste.
- Production companies: Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, Outlier Society, Atlas Entertainment, Toberoff Productions.
- Distributed by Amazon MGM Studios (United States) and Sony Pictures Releasing International (International).
- Country: United States. Language: English.

## Premise

- "Thomas Crown is a billionaire who cleverly steals a painting while another heist fails. Followed by an insurance investigator, the two fall in love during the cat and mouse game."

## Cast

- Michael B. Jordan as Thomas Crown; Adria Arjona; Kenneth Branagh; Lily Gladstone; Danai Gurira; Pilou Asbæk; Aiysha Hart.
- The infobox starring list gives Jordan, Branagh, Arjona, Gladstone, Gurira and Asbæk (it does not list Aiysha Hart).

## Production

- February 2016: Jordan approached Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer to pitch a new adaptation of the 1968 film, hoping to star.
- April 2019: reported that Anthony Russo and Joe Russo would produce an adaptation with their company AGBO.
- April 2023: after acquiring MGM, Amazon announced plans to reboot the franchise through Amazon Studios, later rebranded Amazon MGM Studios.
- September 2024: announced Jordan would direct and produce, with Drew Pearce writing, based on a previous draft by Wes Tooke and Justin Britt-Gibson.
- March 2025: Taylor Russell cast as co-lead. July 2025: Branagh, Gladstone, Gurira, Asbæk and Hart added, with Charles Roven and Atlas Entertainment joining.
- Russell left during filming due to creative differences and was replaced by Adria Arjona.
- Principal photography began July 7, 2025 at Elstree Studios in England; filming wrapped in November 2025.
- April 2026: announced that Jon Batiste would compose the score.

## Release

- "The Thomas Crown Affair is scheduled to be released in the United States on March 5, 2027, in IMAX." The infobox gives the same release date.

## Contradiction within the page

- The body says that in November 2025 "Aubrey Plaza, Paapa Essiedu, and Ruth Negga were confirmed for the cast, but it was later stated that it was incorrectly reported", and the cited Variety note says "An earlier version of the transcript incorrectly named Ruth Negga, Paapa Essiedu and Audrey Plaza as part of 'The Thomas Crown Affair' cast." A later cited source (The Hollywood Reporter, January 6, 2026) nonetheless states the cast "also includes Kenneth Branagh, Aubrey Plaza, Pilou Asbaek, Paapa Essiedu, Lily Gladstone, Danai Gurira, Ruth Negga and more." Neither the cast section nor the infobox lists Plaza, Essiedu or Negga.

## Screenplay credit note

- The article text credits the screenplay to "Drew Pearce and Jason Hall" and the infobox lists both, while the production section mentions only Pearce as writer when the job was announced in September 2024.

## Categories

- Listed categories include Upcoming films, 2027 films, 2027 American films, 2020s heist films, 2020s romantic thriller films, Amazon MGM Studios films, Films shot at Elstree Studios, Upcoming IMAX films and Sony Pictures films.

wikis.title: How to Train Your Dragon: The Hidden World (2019 film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia's article on the 2019 DreamWorks Animation film How to Train Your Dragon: The Hidden World - credits, plot, voice cast, its long development and repeatedly moved release date, $540 million box office, reviews, awards and spin-offs.
wikis.body:
## Infobox

- **How to Train Your Dragon: The Hidden World**, "2019 DreamWorks Animation film". Written and directed by **Dean DeBlois**; based on the *How to Train Your Dragon* books by **Cressida Cowell**.
- Produced by **Brad Lewis** and **Bonnie Arnold**. Edited by John K. Carr; music by **John Powell**. Production company **DreamWorks Animation**; distributed by **Universal Pictures**.
- Release dates **January 3, 2019** (Australia) and **February 22, 2019** (United States). Running time **104 minutes**; country United States; language English.
- Budget **$129 million**; box office **$540 million**.
- Billed cast: Jay Baruchel, America Ferrera, F. Murray Abraham, Cate Blanchett, Gerard Butler, Craig Ferguson, Jonah Hill, Christopher Mintz-Plasse, Kristen Wiig, Kit Harington.

## Lead

- Sequel to *How to Train Your Dragon 2* (2014) and "the final installment of the How to Train Your Dragon trilogy".
- "The film follows 21-year-old Hiccup seeking a dragon utopia known as the 'Hidden World' while coming to terms with Toothless's new bond with a female Fury, as they deal with the threat of Grimmel the Grisly, a ruthless dragon hunter."
- Discussions about a third film began in **December 2010**; DeBlois later said the second film was intentionally designed as the second act of a trilogy. "The animation challenges of the production required DreamWorks Animation to update and invent new software to handle complex tasks, such as lighting the Light Fury dragon."
- Released in Australia **January 3, 2019** and the US **February 22, 2019** by Universal Pictures. It "received positive reviews, with critics considering it a satisfying conclusion to the trilogy, with praise for its animation, voice acting, score, and emotional weight."
- Grossed **$540 million** and received "five Annie Awards nominations, a Golden Globe nomination, and a nomination for Best Animated Feature at the 92nd Academy Awards".

## Plot (as summarised in the article)

- A year after becoming chieftain, Hiccup and the dragon riders keep rescuing captured dragons, leaving Berk overpopulated and under attack from hunters. Hiccup decides to find the "Hidden World" his late father Stoick spoke of. Warlords give a captive white Light Fury to the hunter Grimmel the Grisly as bait to capture Toothless for use as an alpha.
- Toothless and the Light Fury meet in the woods. Grimmel visits Hiccup demanding Toothless, boasting of driving the Night Furies to near-extinction; his Deathgrippers destroy Hiccup's house and Berk, and the Berkians leave, settling an island they call "New Berk".
- Hiccup rebuilds an automatic tailfin so Toothless can fly solo; Toothless flies off with the Light Fury. The riders try to capture Grimmel, fall into his trap and escape, except Ruffnut, whom he releases out of irritation.
- Hiccup and Astrid find the Hidden World, where Toothless is now alpha with the Light Fury as his mate. Ruffnut unknowingly leads Grimmel to New Berk; he captures Toothless and the Light Fury and uses Toothless's alpha status to seize Berk's dragons.
- The riders attack in wingsuits; Hiccup frees Toothless, chases Grimmel, and when Toothless is tranquilised mid-air frees the Light Fury to save him. Hiccup removes his prosthetic leg, which Grimmel is holding, leaving him to fall to his death.
- Hiccup and Toothless accept that dragons are not safe among humans, and the Berkians release their dragons to the Hidden World. Months later Hiccup and Astrid marry and become chieftains.
- A decade later Toothless and the Light Fury have three hybrid fledglings called Night Lights; Hiccup, Astrid and their two children sail to visit them at the edge of the Hidden World. Hiccup vows the dragons will stay hidden until humans and dragons can co-exist.
- Notes: the previous events are from *How to Train Your Dragon 2* (2014); the earlier automatic tailfin appeared in the short *Gift of the Night Fury* (2011); the children are named Zephyr and Nuffink in the short *How to Train Your Dragon: Homecoming* (2019).

## Voice cast

- **Jay Baruchel** (Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III), with A.J. Kane as younger Hiccup; **America Ferrera** (Astrid Hofferson, "Hiccup's fiancee"); **F. Murray Abraham** (Grimmel the Grisly, "responsible for the near-extinction of the Night Furies"); **Cate Blanchett** (Valka); **Gerard Butler** (Stoick the Vast, in flashbacks); **Craig Ferguson** (Gobber the Belch); **Jonah Hill** (Snotlout); **Christopher Mintz-Plasse** (Fishlegs); **Kristen Wiig** (Ruffnut); **Kit Harington** (Eret).
- **Justin Rupple** as Tuffnut: T.J. Miller voiced the role in the first two films and the series and was set to return, but "DreamWorks chose to recast Miller after the actor was accused of sexual assault and arrested for calling in a fake bomb threat"; Rupple dubbed over Miller's lines.
- Also Julia Emelin (Griselda the Grievous), Ólafur Darri Ólafsson (Ragnar the Rock), James Sie (Chaghatai Khan), David Tennant (Ivar the Witless and Spitelout Jorgenson), Robin Atkin Downes (Ack), Kieron Elliot (Hoark), Ashley Jensen (Phlegma the Fierce), Gideon Emery (a trapper), and **Randy Thom** providing vocal effects for Toothless, Stormfly and the Light Fury.

## Production

- **December 2010**: DreamWorks Animation CEO Jeffrey Katzenberg announced a third film - "How To Train Your Dragon is at least three: maybe more, but we know there are at least three chapters to that story."
- DeBlois said *How to Train Your Dragon 2* was deliberately the second act: "There are certain characters and situations that come into play in the second film that will become much more crucial to the story by the third." He said in an interview the third part would be released in 2016.
- Cressida Cowell said the trilogy and the book series would have similar endings, with "an explanation as to why dragons are no more".
- Producers Bonnie Arnold and Brad Lewis; executive producers DeBlois and Chris Sanders (executive producer of the second film and co-director of the first).
- **November 14, 2017**: Kit Harington confirmed to reprise Eret and F. Murray Abraham announced as joining.
- Djimon Hounsou was to return as Drago Bludvist, originally to be redeemed by the end, but halfway through development DreamWorks co-founder **Steven Spielberg** convinced DeBlois that Drago's redemption "required more screen time that they could not provide", so the character was cut.
- **April 17, 2018**: DreamWorks Animation announced the title *How to Train Your Dragon: The Hidden World*.
- The production required DreamWorks Animation "to update and invent new software to handle complex tasks, such as lighting the Light Fury dragon".

## Music

- Score by **John Powell**, as on the previous two films, with Batu Sener, Anthony Willis and Paul Mounsey credited as additional composers.
- **Jónsi**, returning from the previous films, wrote "**Together from Afar**", released as a single on **January 31, 2019**, and provided vocals for a track titled "The Hidden World".

## Release

- Date history: announced by 20th Century Fox (then DreamWorks Animation's distributor) in September 2012 for **June 17, 2016**; pushed in September 2014 to **June 9, 2017**; in January 2015 to **June 29, 2018** after DreamWorks Animation's restructuring and lay-offs; moved up on June 18, 2016 to **May 18, 2018**, taking *The Lego Movie 2: The Second Part*'s slot; pushed on December 5, 2016 to **March 1, 2019**; finally moved up to **February 22, 2019**, taking the slot of the live-action DreamWorks film *The Turning*, which went to January 24, 2020.
- DeBlois on the delays: "these movies take three years. I think it was a little ambitious to say 2016... they kind of throw darts out into the future and wherever they land they call that a release date until we start talking about it in practical terms."
- It "was the first DreamWorks Animation film to be distributed by Universal Pictures, following Comcast and NBCUniversal's acquisition of DreamWorks Animation in 2016".
- Home media: digital in the US **May 7, 2019**; 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray, Blu-ray and DVD from Universal Pictures Home Entertainment **May 21, 2019**. Both include the 2018 short films *Bilby* and *Bird Karma*.
- Games: unlike the first two films there is no tie-in game of the plot; instead two games are set before it - *DreamWorks Dragons: Dawn of New Riders* (Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Windows) and the match-3 mobile game *Dragons: Titan Uprising* (iOS, Android).

## Box office

- **$160.9 million** in the United States and Canada, **$379 million** in other territories, **$540 million** worldwide against a **$129 million** budget. Deadline Hollywood calculated net profit of **$130 million**, placing it 12th on its list of 2019's "Most Valuable Blockbusters".
- US and Canada: early screenings at 1,000 theaters on **February 2, 2019** grossed **$2.5 million**, "one of the highest advance showing totals ever". Released alongside the wide expansion of *Fighting with My Family*, projected at $40-45 million from **4,259** theaters; after **$17.5 million** on day one (including $3 million in Thursday previews), projections rose to $60 million and it opened to **$55 million**, first at the box office. Second weekend **$30 million**, still first, before *Captain Marvel* took over in its third.
- Australia: **$1.5 million** opening day, a record for a DreamWorks Animation film there, surpassing *Shrek 2*. New Zealand: **$173,000** opening day, the studio's second biggest there behind *Shrek 2*. By its third weekend of international release it had grossed $41 million. As of March 24, 2019 its largest other markets were China ($53.7 million), Russia ($26.8 million), France ($25.0 million), the United Kingdom ($24.8 million) and Mexico ($21.0 million).

## Critical response

- Rotten Tomatoes **90%** from 271 reviews, average 7.3/10; consensus: "The rare trilogy capper that really works, How to Train Your Dragon: The Hidden World brings its saga to a visually dazzling and emotionally affecting conclusion." Metacritic **71 out of 100** from 42 critics, "generally favorable". CinemaScore **A**, the same as the first two films; PostTrak 90% positive and 77% "definite recommend".
- Jennifer Bisset (CNET) praised the voice performances, visuals and action, and the Hiccup-Toothless relationship: "with heavy, satisfied hearts, we let him, and Hiccup, go."
- Michael Nordine (IndieWire) gave it a B: "The Hidden World strikes a bittersweet chord in reminding its young audience that all good things - including the age of dragons - must come to an end", calling the animation "striking" and the film's highlight.
- Ben Kenigsberg (The New York Times) wrote it was "More bittersweet and less triumphal than its predecessors... If you truly love that dragon you trained, its message says, let him go."
- Criticism: Movie Crypt found too many juggled sub-plots and an obligatory ending - "the final resolution rings hollow... the dragons and their champions certainly earned a better conclusion than that." Kerry Lengel (The Arizona Republic) called it "a lazy effort" with a plot that is "thin and holey".

## Accolades

- **Academy Awards** (February 9, 2020): nominated Best Animated Feature - Dean DeBlois, Bonnie Arnold and Brad Lewis.
- **Annie Awards** (January 25, 2020): five nominations - Best Animated Feature; Character Animation (Dane Stogner, Rani Naamani); Production Design (Pierre-Olivier Vincent, Kirsten Kawamura, Woonyoung Jung, Iuri Lioi); Writing (DeBlois); Editorial (John K. Carr, Mark Hester, Mary Blee).
- **Wins**: National Board of Review Best Animated Film (December 3, 2019); Hollywood Music in Media Award for Original Score - Animated Film (**John Powell**, November 20, 2019); World Soundtrack Awards Public Choice Award (John Powell, October 18, 2019).
- Nominations also from the Golden Globe Awards (Best Animated Feature Film, January 5, 2020), Critics' Choice, the Producers Guild, the Art Directors Guild, the Artios Awards, the Cinema Audio Society, the Golden Reel Awards, three Golden Trailer categories, the Visual Effects Society (two), the Satellite Awards, the Saturn Awards, the Movieguide Awards, the People's Choice Awards (Favorite Family Movie; Animated Movie Star - America Ferrera), the Society of Composers & Lyricists, the International Film Music Critics Association, and many regional critics' groups (Chicago, Detroit, Florida, Georgia, Houston, Hollywood, Online, San Diego, San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle, St. Louis, Toronto, Washington D.C.).

## Spin-offs

- The short film *How to Train Your Dragon: Homecoming* was released **December 3, 2019**, set before the epilogue, with Hiccup and Astrid teaching their children about the friendship between humans and dragons.
- The animated series *DreamWorks Dragons: The Nine Realms* premiered in **October 2021** and ran for eight seasons, concluding in **December 2023**; set 1,300 years after *The Hidden World*, it follows Tom Kullerson, a descendant of Hiccup and Astrid, and his dragon Thunder, a descendant of Toothless and the Light Fury.
