wikis.title: Pierce Manufacturing: Building the Most Advanced Fire Trucks
wikis.summary: YouTube page for a Free Documentary - Engineering film following a Pierce Enforcer fire truck through the company's Wisconsin factory.
wikis.body:
## The company as described

- Pierce Manufacturing, located in Wisconsin, USA, "the world's largest producer of fire trucks, building an impressive 1,400 vehicles annually".
- "Each truck is unique, customized to the precise specifications of its buyer", from the initial 3D model design to final assembly, "ensuring no two trucks are alike".
- "With over 13,000 individual components - many painstakingly crafted by hand".
- Decorative touches such as lettering and "North America's iconic coats of arms" are hand-painted using genuine gold leaf.
- "Pierce's team of 3,000 skilled employees, each with an average of 12 years of professional experience."

## The Enforcer build followed in the film

- The Enforcer is described as "one of Pierce's most popular models".
- The process starts with the construction of a robust chassis and includes installation of the TAK-4 independent suspension system, "originally developed for the military", which "ensures stability during high-speed turns, preventing rollovers".
- "After three months of meticulous assembly, the final challenge is the installation of a massive 33-meter turntable ladder on the Enforcer's roof."
- Using dual crane winches, workers position and secure "this multi-ton component with millimeter precision - one misstep could damage critical cables".
- Once mounted, "the truck undergoes a rigorous final inspection".

## Page details

- Channel: Free Documentary - Engineering. Published 2025-04-04. Hashtag #manufacturing.

wikis.title: Making the Pirelli P Zero tyre
wikis.summary: Free Documentary - Engineering episode on Pirelli's tyre manufacturing at Settimo Torinese and the development of the P Zero, with the company's production and staffing figures.
wikis.body:
## Pirelli by the numbers (as the page gives them)

- "Capacity: 75 million car tyres a year."
- "32,000 employees worldwide, including 1,400 engineers."
- Manufacturing at Settimo Torinese, Italy, "on 200,000 square meters of floor space".
- Headquarters and the development and testing department are in Milan.

## The P Zero

- Described as "Pirelli's flagship product".
- "It takes: 100 constituent materials, fifteen manufacturing steps, and over 50 performance tests undertaken in high-tech laboratories."
- The aim is "the best possible compromise between three irreconcilable and contradictory properties: low rolling resistance, strong grip and low wear".
- "A new tyre is specially developed for each car brand. The P-Zeros development is based on the experience gathered in the Formula One World Championship, for which Pirelli is the sole supplier."

## What a tyre is made of

- "Natural rubber is the basic raw material for around 130 years."
- Also "a precisely measured blend of fillers, antioxidants, plasticizers, and curing agents".
- "Up to ten different rubber compounds are required for different zones of the tire. Together with textile fibers and steel wires."

Channel: Free Documentary - Engineering. Published 2025-04-25.

wikis.title: Inside Sany's excavator mega factory at Lingang
wikis.summary: Free Documentary - Engineering episode inside Sany's excavator plant in Lingang, China, with its investment, staffing, robot use and the SY215 excavator's figures.
wikis.body:
## The factory

- Lingang, China. "Home to one of the largest and most modern excavator factory in the world!"
- "1000 square meters of production area, equipped with high-tech machines of the latest generation" (the page's own wording).
- "For half a billion euros, the construction machinery giant has built the mega factory."
- "Now 1,600 specialists ensure a breathtaking output: theoretically every ten minutes a new excavator can roll off the production line!"
- Sany is described as "China's market leader" aiming "to become the number one in the world".

## Robots

- Production halls are equipped with the latest generation of robots, which "process up to 250 tons of steel every day".
- In the welding plant "twenty-four workers were replaced by thirty-two robots. They do the work in half the time." Also described as more precise, safer and more cost-effective in the long run.

## The SY215 excavator

- Sany's top-seller in the mid-range class.
- Price: "one hundred and ten thousand euros" - "cheaper than any competitor model from Europe or United States".
- "Its most spectacular feature: a blackbox that sends all of the recorded vehicle-data to the control centre in China. In real-time."
- "The Chinese produce the twenty-three ton monster in just twenty-four working hours."
- At the "marriage section" the "heavily swaying, twelve-tonne upper part has to be moved with millimetre precision onto the narrow slewing ring"; the specialists have ten minutes at that station.

Channel: Free Documentary - Engineering. Published 2025-04-13.

wikis.title: World's Largest Aircraft Graveyard: How to Store and Revive Planes (FD Engineering)
wikis.summary: A Free Documentary - Engineering video page about the Tarmac Aerosave aircraft storage site at Teruel, Spain, and a Lufthansa mission to return a stored A340-600 to service.
wikis.body:
## The video
- YouTube video "World's Largest Aircraft Graveyard: How to Store and Revive Planes | FD Engineering" on the channel **Free Documentary - Engineering**, published **2025-01-03T14:00:53Z**.

## What the description says
- "In the Spanish semi-desert near Teruel lies one of the world's largest aircraft parking lots."
- "Entire fleets were flown to Teruel during the pandemic, including jumbo jets and even the Airbus A380. Now, they sit idle in Teruel's sand."
- Cost claim: "Ten years ago, each A380 cost 400 million euros. Now, they suddenly have no value and are considered unsellable."
- Operator: "Tarmac Aerosave is the world leader for a sustainable business model helping aviation into a new era of circular economy."
- "How to mothball airplanes and still keep them airworthy is a well-guarded secret." Technicians are described as "packaging artists" because the aircraft "must be protected from the weather and animals".
- Two Lufthansa pilots set out "to retrieve a decommissioned A340-600", "one of the oldest in the Lufthansa fleet", which "due to high demand on the lucrative route from Munich to North America… is set to fly again"; the description says "It turn out to become an adventurous project."
- A new hangar is being built at Teruel: "From 2024, it will be able to accommodate the maintenance or scrapping of two A380s simultaneously."
- The page calls it "the first documentary produced for a TV network revealing the secrets of Teruel as Europe's most important airfield for airplanes while waiting on their verdict".

## Other
- Links a related video, "World's Strongest Planes - Steel Beasts of the Sky".
- Hashtags: #FreeDocumentary #Documentary #aircraftgraveyard. The page also carries the channel's blurb defining engineering ("the branch of science and technology concerned with the design, building and use of engines, machines and structures", attributed to "the Webster definition").

## Video

- Title: "Logistical Masterpieces: Revolutionary Ports Compared | Legends vs Modern Icons | FD Engineering"
- Channel: Free Documentary - Engineering
- Published: 2023-06-02 (13:00:54Z)
- Billed as "Legends vs Modern Icons: Ports | Alexandria vs Port of Rotterdam".

## The contest

"A contest of superlatives – The ancient port of Alexandria versus the port of Rotterdam! Two opponents. Three categories. And lots of surprises. Which port revolutionises maritime trade? Which of the contenders enables the most handling of cargo? And which port features the most state-of-the-art technology?"

## The series

"In LEGENDS VS MODERN ICONS, the world's latest engineering achievements, high-tech vehicles and superlative constructions compete against their legendary equivalents that are world famous and milestones in their own field. Can a modern luxury cruise ship outperform the famous Titanic? Is Wembley Stadium superior to the Colosseum? Each episode showcases one battle between a legend and its iconic modern equivalent." Other episodes linked: Towers, Stadiums, Planes, Skyscrapers, Bridges.

## Note on the figures

The description gives the Port of Rotterdam's area as "one hundred and twenty-seven thousand square kilometres" while in the same sentence calling it "twice the size of Manhattan"; both wordings are recorded as given, in the Rotterdam topic page.

Only the video's title, channel, publication date and description were captured; there is no transcript, so nothing is recorded here about what is said in the video itself.

wikis.title: The ancient port of Alexandria
wikis.summary: The description's account of Alexandria as the biggest port of its time, with its dimensions, ship capacity and the lighthouse of Pharos.
wikis.body:
- "The ancient port of Alexandria - the biggest port of its time and the most important trading hub of the ancient world. And a destination for hundreds of thousands of seafarers, traders and travellers from all over the world."
- "The huge seaport was almost four kilometres long and covered an area totalling eleven square kilometres."
- "Experts believe up to five hundred ships could anchor here at the same time – an absolute record."
- "The port's landmark and one of the seven ancient wonders of the world is the lighthouse of Pharos. State-of-the-art technology enabled its light to be seen from a distance of fifty kilometres."
- "Thanks to its gigantic harbour, Egypt became the leading trading power of the ancient world."

wikis.title: The Port of Rotterdam
wikis.summary: The description's account of Rotterdam as Europe's largest port, with its stated area, annual ship and cargo throughput and automation.
wikis.body:
- "The ancient port of Alexandria faces the Port of Rotterdam – the largest port in Europe."
- Area as stated: "Covering an area totalling one hundred and twenty-seven thousand square kilometres – the Port of Rotterdam is twice the size of Manhattan." The two halves of that sentence do not agree in scale; both are recorded as the description gives them.
- "One hundred and fifty thousand ships and four hundred and seventy million tons of cargo handled per year."
- "A logistical masterpiece – possible only by using state-of-the-art technology and fully automated systems."

wikis.title: Zeekr-built Waymo Ojai robotaxis enter US service as Waymo reaches 14 cities
wikis.summary: CarNewsChina report on Waymo launching driverless ride-hailing in Denver, San Diego and Tampa on September 1, 2026 with the Zeekr-built Ojai, covering the vehicle's specs, import volumes, tariff costs and how it fits Waymo's fleet.
wikis.body:
## Launch and footprint

- "Waymo began public driverless ride-hailing services in Denver, San Diego, and Tampa on September 1, expanding its U.S. operating footprint to 14 cities."
- Denver and San Diego launched with the Zeekr-built Ojai as the exclusive vehicle platform, as Waymo transitions away from its Jaguar I-Pace fleet.
- The page's headline reads "Zeekr robotaxis hit American streets as Waymo footprint reaches 14 cities"; the in-page headline reads "Zeekr robotaxis expand to 14 American cities as a part of Waymo fleet".
- Published Sep 4, 2026 1:36 PM CEST by Adrian Leung; marked "5 min to read".

## The vehicle

- The Waymo Ojai is "internally identified as the Zeekr CM1e and previously associated with the Zeekr RT designation"; Waymo adopted the Ojai name in January 2026.
- Manufactured in Ningbo, China, then shipped to the US for autonomous-system integration in Mesa, Arizona. Zeekr supplies the vehicle platform; Waymo supplies the autonomous driving system, computing hardware and sensors; Magna is involved in downstream integration.
- Uses Geely's SEA-M architecture with redundant steer-by-wire and brake-by-wire.
- Single rear permanent-magnet synchronous motor: 200 kW (268 hp), 342 N·m (252 lb-ft), with a 93 kWh gross-capacity battery, actively liquid cooled.
- 4,640 mm long, 3,000 mm wheelbase, opposing sliding doors around a B-pillarless opening; 2+3 cabin leaving four usable passenger positions because the driver's seat is unavailable to riders.
- Waymo's sixth-generation system: four LiDAR units, six radar sensors, 13 external cameras with 17-megapixel imagers, versus 29 cameras and five LiDARs on the fifth-generation Jaguar I-Pace. Heated sensor housings and 10 miniature wipers, each less than 3 inches (76 mm) long, clear snow, slush and ice.
- Denver adds "a cold-weather, high-altitude environment to the Ojai's commercial deployment".

## Import volumes and fleet

- "More than 3,200 CM1e chassis had landed through the Port of Los Angeles by the end of August, with more than 2,600 arriving during the first eight months of 2026, according to customs and logistics records."
- About 300 Ojai vehicles currently carry commercial public riders nationwide; roughly 2,900 additional units remain in integration, calibration, storage or reserve around Mesa.
- Denver and San Diego opened with limited initial availability; Waymo says it will steadily expand access.
- Waymo "has surpassed 500,000 fully autonomous EV trips per week and targets 1 million weekly trips by the end of 2026"; its total US commercial fleet across I-Pace and Ojai "has surpassed 4,000 vehicles".

## Import treatment and costs

- The CM1e ships without autonomous computing, external sensing hardware, telematics and other connected-vehicle systems; customs treats it as "an incomplete mechanical rolling glider". Waymo and Magna install that hardware in Mesa.
- Engineering lineage extends to Zeekr Technology Europe's development operations in Gothenburg, Sweden.
- Declared base value approximately 38,000-39,000 USD per chassis; a customs analysis estimates an overall import-related cost burden of roughly 102.5% to 127.5% (standard passenger-vehicle tariff, the Section 301 duty on Chinese BEVs, and other customs and port charges).
- Estimated landed cost of the glider approximately 78,000-86,500 USD; completed vehicle after Waymo's hardware roughly 103,000-110,000 USD; a Waymo Jaguar I-Pace with autonomous hardware historically approximately 200,000 USD. "These are industry estimates, not Waymo-disclosed acquisition costs." A linked related article is headlined with "102.5% tariffs".
- "Waymo's actual supplier pricing and vehicle-level economics remain undisclosed."

## Regulatory and platform context

- The Bureau of Industry and Security has proposed restrictions covering certain Chinese-origin connected-vehicle software and hardware; NHTSA records show a federal certification and remediation history for the CM1e, with pre-production vehicles remediated for the front passenger seat rail, C-pillar trim and restraint-system software before passenger fleet deployment.
- Jaguar I-Pace production at Magna Steyr ended in late 2024 and GM cancelled the Cruise Origin program in 2024, leaving fewer production-ready platforms.
- Waymo is also developing a platform with Hyundai Motor Group, integrating its sixth-generation Driver into the Hyundai IONIQ 5, with assembly planned at Hyundai's Georgia operation; public-road validation began in 2026, but "there is no evidence that the Hyundai platform is entering commercial driverless service at a volume equivalent to the current Zeekr program".
- The Ojai is separate from Zeekr's consumer-market Mix, though both are associated with Geely's SEA-M architecture.

wikis.title: The Beekeeper 2
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the upcoming action thriller sequel directed by Timo Tjahjanto and starring Jason Statham, scheduled for release in Germany on January 14, 2027 and in the US and UK on January 15, 2027.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- "The Beekeeper 2 is an upcoming action thriller film directed by Timo Tjahjanto and written by Umair Aleem." Sequel to *The Beekeeper* (2024).
- Produced by Jason Statham, Chris Long and Kurt Wimmer.
- Cinematography by Callan Green. Production companies: Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, Miramax, Punch Palace Productions, Long Shot Productions. Distributed by Amazon MGM Studios.
- Countries: United States, United Kingdom. Language: English. The article is short-described as a "2027 American film" while the infobox lists both countries.

## Premise

- "Adam Clay becomes a wanted man when he has to save the President of the United States from his own organization, the Beekeepers, who have gone rogue."

## Cast

- Jason Statham as Adam Clay, "a highly skilled assassin known as The Beekeeper".
- Emmy Raver-Lampman as Verona Parker, an FBI agent; Bobby Naderi as Matt Wiley, an FBI agent and Verona's partner; Jemma Redgrave as Jessica Danforth, President of the United States; Jeremy Irons as Wallace Westwyld, former CIA Director now head of security for Danforth Enterprises.
- Joining: Yara Shahidi, Pom Klementieff, Adam Copeland.

## Production

- February 2025: sequel announced in development, Timo Tjahjanto directing and Kurt Wimmer writing; Statham to reprise Adam Clay and produce.
- May 2025: Wimmer replaced by Umair Aleem as screenwriter.
- September 2025: Jeremy Irons announced as returning; Raver-Lampman, Naderi, Redgrave, Shahidi, Klementieff and Copeland joined later that month.
- Principal photography began September 26, 2025, at Shepperton Studios. Callan Green is cinematographer, his second collaboration with Tjahjanto after *Nobody 2*.
- "On November 29, Tjahjanto announced via Instagram that filming for the movie had wrapped."

## Release

- Infobox release dates: January 14, 2027 (Germany); January 15, 2027 (United States and United Kingdom).
- Body: "The Beekeeper 2 is scheduled to be released theatrically in Germany on January 14, 2027, by Leonine Studios, followed by the United States and United Kingdom the following day, by Amazon MGM Studios."
- The Release section also states it "is scheduled to be released worldwide on January 15, 2027, by Amazon MGM Studios" - which sits against the same section's statement that Germany opens on January 14, 2027.
- May 2025: Amazon MGM Studios confirmed as distributor, acquiring worldwide rights "for over $50 million" (a cited Deadline headline calls it a "$50M+ Deal").
- November 2025: Black Bear Pictures to handle sales at the American Film Market for the Middle East, North Africa and Asia, Amazon MGM retaining all other rights.
- March 2026: Leonine Studios, which distributed the first film in Germany, acquired rights for German-speaking Europe excluding the pay-one window (retained by Amazon Prime Video), scheduling the German theatrical release for January 14, 2027.
- The infobox budget and gross fields are empty.

## Categories

- Includes Upcoming films, 2027 films, 2027 American films, 2020s crime thriller films, Amazon MGM Studios films, Miramax films, Films shot at Shepperton Studios.

wikis.title: Path of the Hybrid Solar Eclipse of 2050 May 20
wikis.summary: NASA eclipse-site path table by Fred Espenak for the Hybrid Solar Eclipse of 2050 May 20, listing the umbral shadow's northern and southern limits and central line at 120-second intervals plus the instants of Greatest Eclipse and Greatest Duration.
wikis.body:
## What the page is

- "Path of the Hybrid Solar Eclipse of 2050 May 20" by Fred Espenak, on NASA's eclipse site (GSFC).
- "The following table delineates the path of the Moon's umbral shadow during the Hybrid Solar Eclipse of 2050 May 20. The geographic coordinates (WGS 84) of the northern and southern limits and the central line are listed at 120-second intervals." This is said to provide "adequate detail for making plots of the path on larger scale maps".
- Local circumstances on the central line in the table: "the ratio of the apparent diameters of the Moon to the Sun, the Sun's altitude and azimuth (degrees), the path width (kilometers) and the duration on the central line (minutes and seconds)".
- Global visibility is shown on an Orthographic Map; the path is shown in greater detail on a Google Map; table features are described in the "Key to Solar Eclipse Path Tables".

## The path table

- Times run in Universal Time from the opening "Limits" row through 19:48 to 21:34, then a closing "Limits" row.
- Opening limits: northern limit 59°53.4'S 168°25.2'W, southern limit 60°04.7'S 168°09.9'W, central line 59°59.0'S 168°17.6'W; diameter ratio 0.996, Sun altitude 0°, path width 25 km, central duration 00m17.0s.
- Closing limits: northern limit 49°22.6'S 080°02.7'W, southern limit 49°38.4'S 080°10.5'W, central line 49°30.5'S 080°06.6'W; ratio 0.995, Sun altitude 0°, width 29 km, duration 00m20.2s.
- The Moon/Sun diameter ratio in the table runs from 0.996 at the start up through 1.000 and to a maximum 1.004 in mid-path, then back down to 0.995 at the end - the hybrid character. At 19:54 UT the central line is at 51°08.7'S 150°49.3'W with ratio 1.000, path width 1 km and central duration 00m00.8s; the same near-zero width recurs at 21:26 UT (42°26.9'S 099°18.8'W, width 1 km, 00m00.8s).
- Maximum tabulated central duration is 00m21.4s at 20:40 UT (central line 40°11.0'S 124°14.3'W, Sun altitude 29°, azimuth 353°, width 27 km).
- ΔT = 94.5 seconds.

## Greatest Eclipse and Greatest Duration

- Greatest Eclipse (GE): Time = 20:41:15.0 UT, Lat = 40°05.3'S, Long = 123°42.4'W, Sun Altitude = 29.4°, Sun Azimuth = 352.0°, Path Width = 26.7 km, Central Duration = 00m21.3s.
- Greatest Duration (GD): Time = 20:39:15 UT, Lat = 40°15'S, Long = 124°33'W, Sun Altitude = 29.3°, Sun Azimuth = 353.4°, Path Width = 26.6 km, Central Duration = 00m21.4s.

## Prediction basis and caveats

- "Predictions for the Hybrid Solar Eclipse of 2050 May 20 were generated using the VSOP87/ELP2000-85 solar and lunar ephemerides and a value of ΔT = 94.5 seconds."
- "The eclipse predictions presented here DO NOT include the effects of mountains and valleys along the edge of the Moon. Such corrections for the lunar limb profile may shift the limits of the eclipse path north or south by ~1-3 kilometers, and change the eclipse duration by ~1-3 seconds." More detailed predictions including the lunar limb profile "are normally posted 12-18 months before each eclipse".

## Related pages and credit

- Links for this eclipse: Orthographic Map, Google Map, Animated Map, Path Table, Besselian Elements Table, Saros 148 Table.
- "All eclipse calculations are by Fred Espenak, and he assumes full responsibility for their accuracy." Reproduction is permitted with the acknowledgment "Eclipse Predictions by Fred Espenak, NASA's GSFC".
- The page ends with the unlabelled date "2014 Feb 26".

wikis.title: Nike Caitlin 1 colorways and release dates
wikis.summary: SneakerFiles guide to Caitlin Clark's first Nike signature shoe, listing its technology, pricing and every announced colorway with release dates and style codes.
wikis.body:
## The shoe

- "Caitlin Clark's first signature shoe with Nike Basketball, the Nike Caitlin 1, will debut on October 1, 2026."
- "The model will be released in multiple colorways in 2026 and 2027 in women's sizes."
- Sizing and pricing: "adult sizes ($140), Grade School ($115), and Preschool sizes ($105)." The release section repeats: "the retail price for women's is $140, Grade School is $115, and Preschool sizes are $105."
- Launching at Nike Basketball retailers, including Nike.com. Where to buy: Nike, Foot Locker, DSG, Hibbett.
- Designers, per the FAQ: "Ben Nethongkome and Alex Zerzan."
- The page says the release section "will be updated with the latest colorways and release dates" and that it will "continue to update as new colorways leak."

## Technology

- Clark on New Heights Podcast with the Kelce Brothers: "The technology we're putting into my shoe isn't anything Nike has ever put into a basketball shoe before."
- Introduces "a new innovation known as Nike Opticast": an upper "constructed with cast polyurethane nodes that create a unique textured appearance while helping reduce drag during movement", designed around Clark's speed, quick changes of direction and creating space.
- Cushioning: "a full-length Cushlon foam midsole paired with a forefoot Air Zoom Turbo unit."
- Branding: Clark's interlocking "CC" logo, "an interlocking design that represents her precision and confidence", across shoe and apparel; "The logo has already debuted on apparel."

## Colorways

Fourteen colorways are listed; the first eight have their own topic pages here, in the page's order. The remaining six as the page lists them:

- "Laser Orange" - Laser Orange/Racer Blue, Holiday 2026, IH7423-800, $140.
- "Purple Venom" - Purple Venom/Laser Crimson, Holiday 2026, IH7423-500, $140.
- "Cavestone" - Light Orewood Brown/Cavestone, Holiday 2026, IH7423-101, $140.
- "Multi-Color" - Racer Blue/Multi-Color, Holiday 2026, IH7423-400, $140.
- "Halloween" - Black/Black-Ghost Green-Mint Foam-Racer Blue, October 2026, JA4290-001, $140.
- "Christmas" - Metallic Silver/Racer Blue-Metallic Cool Grey-Black, December 2026, JA4289-001, $140.
- The page says that alongside "the traditional inline pairs, special iterations for Halloween and Christmas will also be released."
- Note: the page gives the same color description (White/Racer Blue) and the same style code (IH7423-100) for both "Racer Blue" (October 1, 2026) and "Snow White" (Holiday 2026).

## FAQ

- Full family sizing: "Yes, the shoes will be available in adult and kids' sizes."
- Matching apparel: "Nike is expected to release apparel alongside the sneaker" - the page's own hedge.
- Limited release: "The first drop could be more limited due to high demand, but wider releases may follow depending on how the launch performs."

## Byline

- By Brian Betschart, Sep 19, 2026.

wikis.title: Boeing confirms 777-9 first delivery in 2027 after a 7-year, $15 billion delay
wikis.summary: Simple Flying report on Boeing's first-quarter 2026 results confirming it anticipates first 777-9 delivery in 2027, with the programme's charges, certification phases, customer expectations and stored early-build aircraft.
wikis.body:
## The confirmation

- In its first quarter 2026 results Boeing said the programme "continued to make progress" on 777-9 certification and that it "anticipates first delivery in 2027", which the article reads as confirming that launch customer Lufthansa "should finally receive the long-delayed jet next year".
- Quoted: "The 777X program has continued to make steady progress on 777-9 certification… The company anticipates first delivery in 2027."
- Milestones cited in the release include "FAA approval to begin the Type Inspection Authorization 4A phase of certification flight testing"; Boeing is "sticking to the timeline that it had pushed out as recently as last October".
- Published Apr 23, 2026, 5:43 PM EDT, by Paul Hartley.

## The delay and the bill

- "The aircraft was originally due to enter service in 2020, meaning it is now running 7 years late."
- "Boeing has also taken roughly $15 billion in charges on the program"; "Reuters reported in February that Boeing had already taken $15 billion in charges on the development program".
- Cost recovery math given: "using the widely cited 777-9 list price of about $440 million with $50 million in profit, Boeing will need to sell roughly 300 aircraft to match those overruns".

## Top 5 customers for the 777X (firm orders)

- Emirates 270; Qatar Airways 124; Cathay Pacific 35; Lufthansa 27; British Airways 24.

## Airline expectations

- Lufthansa is "set to be the launch customer for the 777-9"; Boeing has been preparing a production-standard Lufthansa 777-9 for flight testing, "while Lufthansa Aviation Training says delivery is currently scheduled for mid-2027".
- "Cathay Pacific also said in March that it expects its first 777-9 in 2027, and Emirates has signaled it is planning for late 2027 as well."
- "The 777-8F freighter is expected to follow in 2028, although Boeing has given no assurance around that timeline."

## Certification status

- "In March, the FAA cleared the 777-9 to move into Type Inspection Authorization Phase 4A"; Boeing reiterated in its Q1 results that Phase 4A had begun.
- Test-fleet activity on FlightRadar24: "three of the five aircraft have amassed over 40 flights so far this month, with two airborne at the time of writing".
- "There were still two more approval gates to get through once 4A is completed — Phase 4B and Phase 5 — before moving into broader functionality and reliability work and the operational proving needed for airline service, including ETOPS-related work on production-standard aircraft."
- The article's reading: "much of 2026 will be spent finishing formal flight-test phases and validating production-standard aircraft".

## Stored early-build aircraft

- Boeing "already has a sizable inventory of 777Xs built, assembled between 2018 and 2022".
- "According to The Seattle Times, Boeing has already assembled as many as 26 777X aircraft, five of which are being used for test flights", leaving 21 stored at Paine Field (PAE), "parked nose-to-tail on a runway with large blocks hanging from their wings in place of engines".
- Compared with the 787 "terrible teens" built before the programme stabilised, which "later required expensive rework"; one example, "the 17th Dreamliner to roll off the production line in Everett, which has just 13 flight hours, was recently scrapped for parts".
- Early-build 777Xs "can require configuration changes, engineering updates, inspection work, or cabin and systems modifications before they are genuinely delivery-ready".

## Other notes

- The article says Lufthansa will be relieved to retire older quad-jets such as the Airbus A340-600 and 747-400.

wikis.title: Waymo opens the Zeekr-built Ojai robotaxi to all riders
wikis.summary: Electrek report that Waymo has opened its next-generation, Zeekr-built Ojai robotaxi to all riders in San Francisco, Los Angeles and Phoenix, with detail on the vehicle, its import under tariffs, its sensor suite and Waymo's scaling plans.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- "Waymo is now letting all riders in San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Phoenix hail its next-generation Ojai robotaxi — a vehicle built in China by Zeekr."
- Waymo announced "today" that the Ojai, "which had been limited to free early-access rides since it started offering trips in the new robotaxi on May 28", is open to the general public across all three markets "as the Alphabet unit begins commercial operations with the platform".
- Riders "may be matched with an Ojai when one is available nearby"; Waymo says it will eventually let passengers choose between the Ojai and its existing Jaguar I-PACE fleet.
- Alongside the opening, Waymo rolled out "Gemini in Waymo" and a redesigned rider app. "Ojai rides are coming next to select riders in Denver, San Diego, and Las Vegas, with more cities later this year."
- By Fred Lambert, Aug 20 2026 - 7:46 am PT.

## A Chinese EV you can't buy

- The Ojai's base vehicle is manufactured by Zeekr, "the premium EV brand owned by China's Geely Holding Group", on Zeekr's SEA-M architecture, "with the body designed in Sweden".
- US tariffs and "an incoming federal rule" have effectively locked Chinese passenger EVs out of the US market.
- "According to Forbes, Waymo has brought more than 3,200 Zeekr vehicles into the US through the Port of Los Angeles since 2024, with more than 2,600 of those arriving in 2026 alone — all while paying a tariff of roughly 127.5% on Chinese EVs."
- "The base price is believed to be quite affordable"; the completed vehicle's total is "expected to be less than half the reported cost of the Jaguar I-PACE robotaxis it is replacing".
- The vehicles must clear the US Commerce Department's connected-vehicle rule, "which takes effect for 2027 and bans vehicle-connectivity and driver-assist hardware or software sourced from China or Russia". The Zeekrs "arrive stripped of Chinese connectivity hardware and sensors", and Waymo installs its own US-designed compute and sensor suite; final assembly is at Waymo's Mesa, Arizona facility with supplier Magna.

## Inside the Ojai

- Designed "as a purpose-built robotaxi rather than a retrofit"; van-style EV with a flat floor, low step-in height and wide "elevator-like" gondola doors on both sides.
- Cabin: extra legroom and headroom, three adaptive screens for route, music and climate, charging ports, cup holders, grab bars and braille labeling for accessibility.
- Waymo's sixth-generation Driver uses "13 cameras, four lidars, and six radar units" - "a 42% cut in sensor count from the fifth-generation system" - and "Waymo has said the hardware now runs under $20,000 per vehicle".

## Scaling

- "As of last week, Waymo had nearly 1,000 Ojai robotaxis staged at its Arizona factory, with hundreds already converted and ready to deploy alongside its roughly 3,700 Jaguar I-PACE vehicles."
- Waymo is "currently running about 500,000 paid rides per week across roughly a dozen cities and is targeting 1 million weekly rides as it scales".
- Waymo is "also bringing the Hyundai Ioniq 5 online as a second robotaxi".

## Electrek's Take

- Argues the story is about the economics of autonomy: Waymo "is willing to eat a 127.5% tariff and still come out ahead because the Zeekr Ojai is dramatically cheaper than the Jaguar I-PACEs it's phasing out", having driven the sensor stack "under $20,000".

wikis.title: Intelligent eyewear with Gemini coming this fall (Google I/O 2026)
wikis.summary: Google blog post from I/O 2026 announcing Android XR intelligent eyewear - audio glasses launching first later this fall with frames from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker - and the Gemini features they will carry.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- Posted May 19, 2026 by Shahram Izadi, VP & GM, XR, on the Google blog (Android/Platforms). Headline on the page: "Intelligent eyewear is coming this fall"; the page's own title tag reads "Intelligent eyewear with Gemini is coming this fall".
- Standfirst: "We're revealing new frames from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, plus features that let you get directions, send texts, snap photos and more — all without taking out your phone."
- "Today at Google I/O 2026, we shared more about intelligent eyewear: glasses that deliver help in the moment without taking you out of it."
- Android XR is described as "the platform we've built with Samsung and Qualcomm".
- "There will be two types of intelligent eyewear: audio glasses that offer spoken help in your ear, and display glasses that show you the information you need, right when you need it."
- "Audio glasses are launching first, coming later this fall."
- The post is filed in the collection "I/O 2026".

## Frames

- Google "partnered with Samsung and eyewear brands Gentle Monster and Warby Parker".
- "Today, we gave a sneak peek at two of the first designs that will launch as part of Gentle Monster and Warby Parker's full collections later this year."

## Features coming to audio glasses

- Access Gemini by saying "Hey Google" or tapping the side of the frame.
- **Ask about what you see** - ask Gemini about anything in view, e.g. reviews for a restaurant you are walking past, the name of a cloud formation, decoding a confusing parking sign.
- **Navigate with ease** - "Glasses know where you're standing and which direction you're facing", giving natural turn-by-turn directions; Gemini can add stops or find nearby restaurants based on preferences.
- **Stay connected, hands-free** - manage calls, send texts, have Gemini summarize missed messages, or ask to listen to music "that complements your environment — all on crisp, clear and private over-ear speakers".
- **Capture and edit** - snap photos and videos; "With a single command you can take a picture and use Nano Banana to remove background distractions or playfully transform your images. Try, 'Hey Google, take a picture and put everyone in funny hats.'"
- **Translate speech and writing** - real-time translations "with audio that matches the tone and pitch of the speaker's voice", or look at text on menus and signs to hear a translation.
- **Get help with tasks** - "Gemini Intelligence handles multi-step tasks in the background. Gemini can prepare your coffee order on Doordash while your phone stays in your pocket. All that's left for you is the final order confirmation."
- **Tap into your apps** - order a ride with Uber, learn a language with Mondly and more by voice using the phone's apps. "Glasses pair with both Android and iOS phones."

## Closing

- "Stay tuned for more in the coming months."

wikis.title: AMD CEO says next-gen Xbox semi-custom SoC supports a 2027 launch
wikis.summary: TweakTown news item quoting AMD CEO Lisa Su's Q4 2025 earnings-call remark that the semi-custom SoC for Microsoft's next-gen Xbox is progressing well for a 2027 launch, alongside leaked "Magnus" APU specifications.
wikis.body:
## The AMD statement

- "AMD CEO Dr. Lisa Su recently said that the semi-custom SoC in development for Microsoft's next-generation Xbox console is 'progressing well to support a launch in 2027'."
- Quoted from AMD's Q4 2025 earnings call: "For 2026, we expect semi-custom SoC annual revenue to decline by a significant double-digit percentage as we enter the seventh year of what has been a very strong console cycle. From a product standpoint, Valve is on track to begin shipping its AMD-powered Steam Machine early this year. And development of Microsoft's next-gen Xbox featuring an AMD semi-custom SoC is progressing well to support a launch in 2027".
- Published Feb 5, 2026 8:35 PM CST by Anthony Garreffa; marked "45-second read time". News source given at the foot: wccftech.com.

## Leaked "Magnus" APU details (attributed to leaker Moore's Law is Dead)

- "68 CUs of RDNA 5 GPU power", which the article says is more than the PlayStation 6, "which reportedly has 52-54 CUs of RDNA 5".
- "At least 24MB of L2 cache for the GPU, up to 3 x Zen 6 CPU cores joined by 8 x Zen 6c cores with 12MB of L3 cache".
- "192-bit memory bus with up to a whopping 48GB of GDDR7 memory", versus leaks putting the PS6 at a 160-bit bus and up to 40GB of RAM.

## The full leaked spec list as printed

1. 144mm² SoC (N3P) + 264mm² GPU (N3C/P) = 408mm²
2. "Likely 250-350W TDP (estimation, not 100%)"
3. 68 x RDNA 5 CUs (disabled from up to 70 CU) - 4 Shader Engines total = 3 x 9 WGP + 1 x 8 WGP; each Shader Engine has 2 x Shader Arrays
4. At least 24MB L2 cache for the GPU
5. Up to 3 x Zen 6 + 8 x Zen 6c with 12MB L3 cache
6. 192-bit memory bus with up to 48GB of GDDR7
7. NPU with up to 110 TOPS @ 6W or 46 TOPS @ 1.2W (two power consumption modes)
8. Targeting 2027 for launch

## Note on the summary line

- The article's TL;DR describes the CPU side as "3 Zen 6 plus 8 Zen 6c CPU cores" and says the chip is "surpassing PlayStation 6 specs"; the body gives the same figures as "up to 3 x Zen 6" cores. The chip is called both "Magnus" APU and a semi-custom SoC.

wikis.title: 2027 Men's Rugby World Cup in Australia
wikis.summary: Wikipedia's article on the 2027 Men's Rugby World Cup - the 11th edition, in Australia from 1 October to 13 November 2027, covering the bidding, the expansion to 24 teams, venues, qualified teams, the December 2025 draw, the fixture list and the tournament's broadcasters and sponsors.
wikis.body:
## Tournament details (infobox)

- **2027 Rugby World Cup**, slogan "**Go All Out!**". Host nation **Australia**. Venues **8 (in 7 host cities)**. Dates **1 October - 13 November 2027**. Number of nations **24 (77 qualifying)**. Previous: 2023. Next: 2031.

## Lead

- "The 2027 Men's Rugby World Cup is scheduled to be the 11th edition of the Rugby World Cup, the quadrennial world championship for men's rugby union teams", in Australia from 1 October to 13 November 2027.
- "It will be the first tournament to be branded as the Men's Rugby World Cup, a change that was announced in October 2023 to promote gender parity. It will also be the first to host 24 teams."
- South Africa are the two-time defending champions after beating New Zealand in the 2023 final. **Hong Kong will make their Rugby World Cup debut.**

## An inconsistency in the fixture tables

- The Pool C table says "First match(es) will be played: 4 October 2027", but the fixture list beneath it opens with **Argentina v Canada on 3 October 2027** at Brisbane Stadium.
- The venue story also reverses within the same month: in early January 2025 it was reported that no matches would be played in Victoria after the state government pulled its bid, and later that month the host-city list confirmed that Victoria would host games in Melbourne after all.

## Host selection and bidding

- World Rugby hoped to award the 2027 and 2031 men's World Cups, and the 2025 and 2029 Women's World Cups, by **May 2022**. Talks with prospective nations began February 2021, the formal candidate process three months later, and finalists were evaluated in February 2022.
- By June 2019 **Argentina, Australia and Russia** had declared interest; Argentina withdrew in April 2020. The United States and South Africa were speculated about, but the South African Rugby Union said it would not bid.
- Chairman **Bill Beaumont** suggested in late 2018 that the post-2023 host could be an emerging nation; CEO **Brett Gosper** suggested in 2019 that 2027 and 2031 might be awarded together, as England 2015 and Japan 2019 were, to allow "a bolder decision and a traditional decision".
- Three consecutive Northern Hemisphere World Cups (England 2015, Japan 2019, France 2023) made Southern Hemisphere countries the favourites.
- **On 12 May 2022 it was announced that Australia would host the 2027 Rugby World Cup.**
- **Australia's bid**: announced by Rugby Australia on **13 December 2017**. Australia co-hosted the inaugural 1987 World Cup with New Zealand and hosted the 2003 tournament alone.
- **Argentina** announced a bid on 5 October 2016 and withdrew in April 2020 "to strengthen the Australian bid". It "is the only country to reach the World Cup semi-finals that has not hosted any World Cup matches".
- **Russia**: Stanislav Druzhinin of the Russian Rugby Union said on 31 May 2019 that Russia would apply, using 2018 FIFA World Cup stadiums; President Vladimir Putin backed the bid. The union could not proceed after the Court of Arbitration for Sport imposed a two-year ban on 17 December 2020 on Russia hosting major sports tournaments.

## Expansion to 24 teams

- Talk of expansion intensified after the performances of Chile and Portugal at the 2023 Rugby World Cup; on **4 October 2023** it was reported that World Rugby had decided to expand to 24 teams "in order to help grow the sport". A "Swiss model" pool stage or six pools of four plus a round of 16 were considered.
- The expansion was confirmed on **24 October 2023**, with the format confirmed in **October 2025**.
- Format change from the structure used since 2003: instead of four pools of five, there are **six pools of four**. The top two from each pool plus the **four best third-placed teams** go to a knockout stage beginning with a new **Round of 16**. The tournament will have **52 matches**, up from 48 since 2003.

## Venues

- Eight venues in seven cities. The **opening match and opening ceremony** will be at **Perth Stadium**; the **final, both semi-finals and the bronze final** at **Stadium Australia**, Sydney.
- Capacities listed: Stadium Australia, Sydney **82,000**; Perth Stadium **65,000**; Adelaide Oval **53,500**; Docklands Stadium, Melbourne **53,000**; Brisbane Stadium **52,500**; Sydney Football Stadium **42,500** (rectangular mode); Newcastle Stadium **33,000**; North Queensland Stadium, Townsville **25,455**.
- **Melbourne**: in early January 2025 it was reported that no matches would be in Victoria after the state government pulled its bid "in protest of Rugby Australia's (RA) revocation of Melbourne Rebels' participation in Super Rugby Pacific"; later that month Melbourne was confirmed as a host city, with the venue undecided. In **January 2026** Docklands Stadium was confirmed, World Rugby "reportedly struck a deal" to use it instead of the Melbourne Cricket Ground after the MCG's availability in October 2027 could not be guaranteed "due to an exclusive clause in a deal between the Victorian government and the National Football League (NFL)".
- Match allocation: Adelaide six pool matches; Brisbane six pool, two round-of-16 and two quarter-finals; Melbourne six pool and two round-of-16; Newcastle four pool; Perth the opening ceremony, five pool and two round-of-16; Stadium Australia two pool, two quarter-finals, two semi-finals, the bronze final and the final; Sydney Football Stadium three pool and two round-of-16; Townsville four pool matches.
- Notes say Stadium Australia, Adelaide Oval, Docklands Stadium and Brisbane Stadium were used in the 2003 Rugby World Cup, and that the new Sydney Football Stadium stands on the site of the old one, also used in 2003.

## Qualification

- **12 teams qualified automatically** as hosts and by finishing in the top three of their 2023 pools. The process for the rest was confirmed by World Rugby on **13 August 2024**: four from Europe, three from the Pacific, one each from Africa, Asia and South America, one from a South America/Pacific play-off, and one from a **four-team repechage** of Belgium, Namibia, Samoa and Brazil - Brazil replacing Paraguay "after the latter had fielded an ineligible player in their third-place playoff in the South American qualifier".
- Qualified teams, with qualification route and world ranking as of 1 December 2025:
  - **Africa**: South Africa (2023 pool stage; rank 1; champions 1995, 2007, 2019, 2023), Zimbabwe (2025 Rugby Africa Cup winners; rank 24; 2 previous appearances).
  - **Asia**: Hong Kong (2025 Asia Rugby Championship winners; rank 23; **debut**).
  - **Europe**: England (rank 3; champions 2003), France (5; runners-up 1987, 1999, 2011), Ireland (4; eight quarter-finals), Italy (10), Scotland (9; fourth place 1991), Wales (11; third place 1987), Georgia (2025 Rugby Europe Championship winners; 13), Spain (Europe 2; 15; one previous appearance, 1999), Romania (Europe 3; 22; nine appearances), Portugal (Europe 4; 20; 2007 and 2023).
  - **Pacific**: Australia (hosts; 7; champions 1991, 1999), Fiji (8; quarter-finals 1987, 2007, 2023), Japan (12; quarter-finals 2019), New Zealand (2; champions 1987, 2011, 2015), Tonga (2025 Pacific Nations Cup third place; 18), Samoa (final qualifier; 19; quarter-finals 1991, 1995), Canada (Pacific Nations Cup fourth; 25; quarter-finals 1991), United States (Pacific Nations Cup fifth; 16).
  - **South America**: Argentina (6; third place 2007), Uruguay (2025 Sudamérica Rugby Championship winners; 14), Chile (Pacific/Sudamérica play-off winner; 17; one appearance, 2023).
- A note explains that Fiji and Japan, the top two of the 2025 Pacific Nations Cup, had already qualified from 2023, so the next placed teams took the Pacific berths.

## Draw

- Confirmed in May 2025 for **3 December 2025**, with the format confirmed in September 2025. "For the first time, the draw took place after all teams had qualified."
- All 24 qualified teams were ranked in the world top 25; the only top-25 team to miss out was **21st-ranked Belgium**, who drew with Samoa on the final matchday of the Final Qualification Tournament and finished one point behind them.
- Teams were split into four bands of six using the World Rugby Rankings at the end of the 2025 November international window - Band 1 seeds 1-6, Band 2 seeds 7-12, Band 3 seeds 13-18, Band 4 seeds 19-24 - with one team from each band drawn into each pool. As hosts, **Australia was automatically allocated to Pool A**.
- Bands as listed: Band 1 - South Africa (1), New Zealand (2), England (3), Ireland (4), France (5), Argentina (6). Band 2 - Australia (7), Fiji (8), Scotland (9), Italy (10), Wales (11), Japan (12). Band 3 - Georgia (13), Uruguay (14), Spain (15), United States (16), Chile (17), Tonga (18). Band 4 - Samoa (19), Portugal (20), Romania (22), Hong Kong (23), Zimbabwe (24), Canada (25).

## Pools

- **Pool A**: New Zealand, Australia (hosts), Chile, Hong Kong. **Pool B**: South Africa, Italy, Georgia, Romania. **Pool C**: Argentina, Fiji, Spain, Canada. **Pool D**: Ireland, Scotland, Uruguay, Portugal. **Pool E**: France, Japan, United States, Samoa. **Pool F**: England, Wales, Tonga, Zimbabwe.
- Points: four for a win, two for a draw, a try bonus point for four or more tries, a losing bonus point for losing by fewer than eight points.
- Tie-breakers in order: head-to-head result; points difference; try difference; points scored; tries scored; then the **World Rugby Rankings as of 18 October 2027**. With three or more teams tied, the process repeats from the first criterion once the highest-ranked team is settled.
- Pool fixtures (dates and venues as listed):
  - **A**: 1 Oct Australia v Hong Kong, Perth; 2 Oct New Zealand v Chile, Perth; 9 Oct New Zealand v Australia, Stadium Australia; 9 Oct Chile v Hong Kong, Townsville; 15 Oct New Zealand v Hong Kong, Melbourne; 16 Oct Australia v Chile, Brisbane.
  - **B**: 3 Oct South Africa v Italy, Adelaide; 3 Oct Georgia v Romania, Townsville; 10 Oct South Africa v Georgia, Brisbane; 11 Oct Italy v Romania, Sydney Football Stadium; 17 Oct Italy v Georgia, Newcastle; 17 Oct South Africa v Romania, Perth.
  - **C**: 3 Oct Argentina v Canada, Brisbane; 4 Oct Fiji v Spain, Newcastle; 10 Oct Fiji v Canada, Adelaide; 10 Oct Argentina v Spain, Melbourne; 16 Oct Argentina v Fiji, Adelaide; 17 Oct Spain v Canada, Townsville.
  - **D**: 3 Oct Scotland v Uruguay, Melbourne; 4 Oct Ireland v Portugal, Sydney Football Stadium; 10 Oct Ireland v Scotland, Perth; 11 Oct Uruguay v Portugal, Newcastle; 17 Oct Ireland v Uruguay, Melbourne; 17 Oct Scotland v Portugal, Brisbane.
  - **E**: 2 Oct France v United States, Melbourne; 3 Oct Japan v Samoa, Newcastle; 9 Oct United States v Samoa, Perth; 9 Oct France v Japan, Brisbane; 15 Oct Japan v United States, Adelaide; 17 Oct France v Samoa, Sydney Football Stadium.
  - **F**: 2 Oct Wales v Zimbabwe, Adelaide; 2 Oct England v Tonga, Brisbane; 8 Oct Wales v Tonga, Melbourne; 8 Oct England v Zimbabwe, Adelaide; 15 Oct Tonga v Zimbabwe, Townsville; 16 Oct England v Wales, Stadium Australia.

## Knockout stage

- Four single-elimination rounds plus a third-place playoff. A tie in regulation is settled by two 10-minute periods of extra time, then a 10-minute sudden-death period, then a kicking competition.
- Pool winners and runners-up have fixed bracket positions; the four best third-placed teams can take several positions. "if the 3rd place team comes from any of pools A, B, C, or D they can only appear in one Round of 16 knockout match; meanwhile if the 3rd place team is from Pools E and/or F they can potentially appear in any of the slots, to ensure that only novel games take place during the first two knockout rounds." Fifteen combinations of third-placed pools are listed, each accommodated in only one way.
- Third-place ties are broken by points difference, points scored, tries scored, then the World Rugby Men's Ranking as of **18 October 2027**.
- **Round of 16, 23 October 2027**: 2nd Pool C v 2nd Pool F, Sydney Football Stadium, 14:15 AEDT; 1st Pool A v 3rd Pool C/E/F, Brisbane, 15:45 AEST; 1st Pool E v 2nd Pool D, Melbourne, 19:15 AEDT; 1st Pool B v 3rd Pool D/E/F, Perth, 18:45 AWST.
- **Round of 16, 24 October 2027**: 1st Pool C v 3rd Pool A/E/F, Sydney Football Stadium, 14:15; 1st Pool D v 3rd Pool B/E/F, Melbourne, 16:45; 2nd Pool A v 2nd Pool E, Brisbane, 18:15 AEST; 1st Pool F v 2nd Pool B, Perth, 18:45 AWST.
- **Quarter-finals**: 30 October, Stadium Australia 16:45 and Brisbane 18:45; 31 October, Brisbane 16:00 and Stadium Australia 20:00.
- **Semi-finals**: 5 November and 6 November, both 20:00 AEDT at Stadium Australia.
- **Bronze final**: 12 November 2027, 19:45 AEDT, Stadium Australia. **Final**: 13 November 2027, 20:00 AEDT, Stadium Australia.

## Broadcasting rights

- Australia: **Stan Sport** and **Nine Network**. France: **TF1**. New Zealand: **Sky Sport** and **Sky Open**. Sub-Saharan Africa: **SuperSport** (a note says the Canal+ Group agreed with World Rugby for rights on SuperSport, on DStv). United Kingdom: **ITV**. United States: **Paramount+**.

## Marketing and sponsorship

- The first tournament branded the **Men's Rugby World Cup**, announced October 2023; all previous editions were simply the Rugby World Cup, with the women's tournament branded Women's Rugby World Cup from 1991 to 2017 and without a gender designation in 2021.
- **Principal partners**: Asahi Breweries (Asahi Super Dry extended its principal partnership to 2029 in October 2024), Emirates (a "record-breaking partnership extension" announced 26 November 2025), Visa (joined 14 September 2026 for Australia 2027 and 2029).
- **Official partners**: Coca-Cola (announced 23 June 2026), Liqui Moly (28 January 2025, for 2027 and 2029).
- **Official suppliers and supporters**: ChildFund Rugby, Dove Men+Care (Unilever, April 2025), Fanatics, Gilbert (match ball unveiled 1 December 2025 with its partnership extended to 2033), Lipovitan D (22 October 2025), Macron (apparel to 2029), Meiji (27 March 2026), Mitsubishi Estate (29 January 2025), Ticketmaster (official ticketing provider for 2027 and 2029, 4 March 2025).

- **12 teams qualified automatically** as hosts or by finishing in the top three of their 2023 Rugby World Cup pools.
- The rest of the process was confirmed by World Rugby on **13 August 2024**: four teams from Europe, three from the Pacific, one each from Africa, Asia and South America, one from a South America/Pacific play-off, and the last from a four-team repechage.
- The **Final Qualification Tournament** comprised Belgium (winners of their continental ranking finals), Namibia (continental runners-up), Samoa (loser of the South America/Pacific play-off) and Brazil, who replaced Paraguay "after the latter had fielded an ineligible player in their third-place playoff in the South American qualifier". Samoa took the place; Belgium, ranked 21st, drew with Samoa on the final matchday and finished a point behind.
- New or rare qualifiers: **Hong Kong** (2025 Asia Rugby Championship winners) make their debut; Zimbabwe return via the 2025 Rugby Africa Cup after appearances in 1987 and 1991; Spain qualify for a second tournament after 1999; Chile for a second after 2023.
- Europe's qualifiers beyond the automatic places came through the 2025 Rugby Europe Championship: Georgia (winners), Spain (runners-up), Romania (third), Portugal (fourth).
- Pacific places went to Tonga, Canada and the United States via the 2025 World Rugby Pacific Nations Cup, since Fiji and Japan, its top two, had already qualified from 2023.
- Uruguay qualified as 2025 Sudamérica Rugby Championship winners, Chile through the Pacific/Sudamérica play-off.

wikis.title: The 3 December 2025 draw and the six pools
wikis.summary: How the bands were set, what each pool contains, and the pool-stage scoring and tie-breakers.
wikis.body:
- The draw was confirmed in May 2025 for **3 December 2025**, with its format confirmed in September 2025. "For the first time, the draw took place after all teams had qualified."
- Teams were split into four bands of six by the World Rugby Rankings at the end of the 2025 November international window (Band 1 seeds 1-6 through Band 4 seeds 19-24), one from each band per pool, with hosts **Australia placed in Pool A**.
- Bands: 1 - South Africa, New Zealand, England, Ireland, France, Argentina. 2 - Australia, Fiji, Scotland, Italy, Wales, Japan. 3 - Georgia, Uruguay, Spain, United States, Chile, Tonga. 4 - Samoa, Portugal, Romania, Hong Kong, Zimbabwe, Canada.
- Pools drawn: **A** New Zealand, Australia, Chile, Hong Kong. **B** South Africa, Italy, Georgia, Romania. **C** Argentina, Fiji, Spain, Canada. **D** Ireland, Scotland, Uruguay, Portugal. **E** France, Japan, United States, Samoa. **F** England, Wales, Tonga, Zimbabwe.
- Scoring: four points for a win, two for a draw, a bonus point for four or more tries, a bonus point for losing by fewer than eight points.
- Tie-breakers: head-to-head, points difference, try difference, points scored, tries scored, then the World Rugby Rankings of **18 October 2027**.

wikis.title: Fixtures and the knockout bracket
wikis.summary: The pool schedule from 1 October and the round of 16 through to the 13 November final.
wikis.body:
- The pool stage runs **1-17 October 2027**, opening with Australia v Hong Kong at Perth Stadium on 1 October. Marquee pool matches include New Zealand v Australia at Stadium Australia on 9 October and England v Wales at Stadium Australia on 16 October.
- The Pool C table says its first match is 4 October, while its own fixture list begins with Argentina v Canada on 3 October.
- **Round of 16**: 23 October at Sydney Football Stadium, Brisbane, Melbourne and Perth; 24 October at the same four venues.
- **Quarter-finals**: 30 October at Stadium Australia (16:45 AEDT) and Brisbane (18:45 AEST); 31 October at Brisbane (16:00) and Stadium Australia (20:00).
- **Semi-finals**: 5 and 6 November, both 20:00 AEDT at Stadium Australia. **Bronze final**: 12 November, 19:45. **Final**: 13 November 2027, 20:00 AEDT, Stadium Australia.
- Knockout ties level after regulation go to two 10-minute periods of extra time, then a 10-minute sudden-death period, then a kicking competition.
- Third-placed qualifiers are slotted so that "only novel games take place during the first two knockout rounds": third-placed teams from pools A-D can only appear in one specific round-of-16 match, while those from pools E and F can fill any slot. Fifteen combinations are tabulated, each with a single arrangement.

wikis.title: Diablo 4 BlizzCon 2026 roadmap: Amazon class, Netflix adaptation and Switch 2 port
wikis.summary: Windows Central news report on the Diablo 4 announcements at BlizzCon 2026 - the Amazon class in the first half of 2027, Season 15, a Nintendo Switch 2 release and a confirmed Netflix collaboration.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- Report by Jennifer Young, published 12 September 2026, "2 min read", on the Diablo 4 announcements at "today's BlizzCon" opening ceremony, where "Blizzard laid out their roadmap for keeping the game fresh well into 2027".
- The article notes the separate "Diablo 5 reveal" as "a bombshell" at the same show.
- Other BlizzCon 2026 items listed in a sidebar: "Warcraft 3's first DLC in 23 years", "Xal'atath joins Heroes of the Storm", "Diablo 5 surprise announcement", "A new hero joins Overwatch", "WoW Forever is Classic+", "Starcraft's new squad shooter". A video is embedded: "Diablo | BlizzCon 2026 | 30 Years of Hell - YouTube".

## The announcements

- **Amazon class** - "the Amazon class is finally heading to Diablo 4 in the first half of 2027", set in "her proper homeland of Skovos", following the Nahantu and Scosglen regions explored in Lord of Hatred. It "promises to inject a whole new combat style and tactical depth into the current roster".
- **Season 15 (Season of Hell's Legacy)** - a "massive franchise 30th-anniversary celebration" featuring past enemies, legacy items "like In Geom, Stone of Jordan, etc." and "encounters involving the Prime Evils themselves".
- **Nintendo Switch 2** - "Blizzard officially confirmed that Diablo 4: The Age of Hatred collection is heading to the Nintendo Switch 2".
- **Netflix** - "There's also confirmation that the long-rumored Netflix collaboration is actually happening"; "We don't know anything else at this stage".

## Class-rollout context given

- Lord of Hatred "launched earlier this year with Paladin", and many fans expected the Amazon as the expansion's second class, "but we got the Warlock at the time".
- The article reads the rollout as a balance between new archetypes (Spiritborn, Warlock) and returning classics (Paladin, now the Amazon "from Diablo 2").
