wikis.title: The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey (2012 film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Peter Jackson's 2012 first Hobbit film - its story, cast, the production Jackson took over from Guillermo del Toro, its first-ever wide 48 fps release, $1.017 billion gross and mixed reviews.
wikis.body:
## The film

- A 2012 epic fantasy film directed by Peter Jackson from a screenplay by Fran Walsh, Philippa Boyens, Jackson and Guillermo del Toro, based on Tolkien's 1937 novel and the first of The Hobbit trilogy, a prequel to The Lord of the Rings trilogy set sixty years earlier, with parts adapted from the appendices to The Return of the King.
- Production companies New Line Cinema, Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Pictures and WingNut Films; distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures. 169 minutes; New Zealand and United States; English. Budget $200–315 million; box office $1.017 billion.
- Martin Freeman plays Bilbo Baggins, Ian McKellen Gandalf and Richard Armitage Thorin Oakenshield, with Ken Stott, Cate Blanchett, Ian Holm, Christopher Lee, Hugo Weaving, James Nesbitt, Elijah Wood, Andy Serkis, Sylvester McCoy, Barry Humphries, Manu Bennett and Benedict Cumberbatch (voice of Smaug and the Necromancer).
- Howard Shore composed the score, performed by the London Philharmonic Orchestra, London Voices and Tiffin' Boys Choir.

## Production

- Del Toro was to direct a two-film adaptation but left in May 2010 after about two years, "due to delays caused in part by financial problems at Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer"; Jackson was announced as director that October.
- Principal photography on the Hobbit films ran from 21 March 2011 to 6 July 2012 in New Zealand, 266 days of filming, with An Unexpected Journey pick-ups in July 2012.
- Jackson said he started shooting "with most of it not prepped at all", without storyboards and with unfinished scripts: "I spent most of The Hobbit feeling like I was not on top of it."
- It was the first feature film with a wide release shot and projected at 48 frames per second, advertised as "High Frame Rate", though most cinemas projected a converted 24 fps version.
- Up to 27 of about 150 animals housed for the production died - horses, goats, chickens and one sheep.

## Release and reception

- World premiere at the Embassy Theatre in Wellington on 28 November 2012, with around 100,000 people on the red carpet; New Zealand release 12 December, Europe 13 December, United States, Canada and India 14 December, Australia 26 December. Wellington was renamed the "Middle of Middle-earth" for the premiere week.
- $303 million in the United States and Canada and $718.1 million elsewhere for a worldwide $1.017 billion (the components sum to about $1.021 billion) - the 15th film to reach $1 billion and the fourth highest-grossing film of 2012. It set December records for midnight ($13.0 million), opening day ($37.1 million) and opening weekend ($84.62 million).
- Rotten Tomatoes 64% from 303 reviews (average 6.60/10); Metacritic 58 from 40 critics; CinemaScore "A". Debate centred on length, the high frame rate and comparison with The Lord of the Rings.
- Three Academy Award nominations (Visual Effects, Production Design, Makeup and Hairstyling), nine Saturn Award nominations (winning Best Production Design), and Empire Awards for Best Actor (Martin Freeman) and Best Science Fiction/Fantasy Film.
- The Desolation of Smaug and The Battle of the Five Armies followed in 2013 and 2014.

wikis.title: The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey (2012 film) - plot, cast, production, release and reception
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Peter Jackson's 2012 first Hobbit film, covering its story, large cast, troubled development after Guillermo del Toro's exit, 48 fps release, $1.017 billion box office, mixed reviews and awards.
wikis.body:
## The film

- "The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey is a 2012 epic fantasy film directed by Peter Jackson from a screenplay by Fran Walsh, Philippa Boyens, Jackson, and Guillermo del Toro." Based on the 1937 novel The Hobbit by J. R. R. Tolkien.
- "The film is the first installment in The Hobbit trilogy, acting as a prequel to Jackson's The Lord of the Rings trilogy (2001–2003). The story is set in Middle-earth sixty years before the main events of The Lord of the Rings and portions of the film are adapted from the appendices to Tolkien's The Return of the King."
- Produced by Carolynne Cunningham, Zane Weiner, Fran Walsh and Peter Jackson; cinematography Andrew Lesnie; edited by Jabez Olssen; music by Howard Shore. Production companies New Line Cinema, Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Pictures and WingNut Films; distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures.
- Release dates: 28 November 2012 (Wellington premiere); 12 December 2012 (New Zealand); 14 December 2012 (United States). Running time 169 minutes. Countries New Zealand and United States; language English.
- Budget $200–315 million; box office $1.017 billion.
- It was released "almost nine years after the release of The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King". It "received mixed reviews from critics and grossed $1.017 billion at the box office, making it the fourth highest-grossing film of 2012", and at the 85th Academy Awards was nominated for Best Production Design, Best Makeup and Hairstyling and Best Visual Effects.
- "Two sequels, The Desolation of Smaug and The Battle of the Five Armies followed in 2013 and 2014, respectively."
- A page banner reads: "This is an accepted version of this page. This is the latest accepted revision, reviewed on 14 September 2026."

## Score

- "The musical score for An Unexpected Journey was composed, orchestrated, and conducted by Howard Shore. It was performed by the London Philharmonic Orchestra, London Voices and Tiffin' Boys Choir and featured several vocal soloists. The score reprised many themes from the Lord of the Rings trilogy but also introduced numerous new themes, including Shore's orchestral setting of the diegetic 'Misty Mountains' song."

## Animal deaths

- "At the facility where about 150 animals were housed for the production of The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey, up to 27 animals died. The animals in question were horses, goats, chickens and one sheep."

## Video games

- Guardians of Middle-earth, "released with the special disclaimer on the front art, marking the connection to the feature film", containing models and characters from the film including Nori, Gollum and Dwalin.
- Lego The Lord of the Rings, released around the same time, containing a Lego model of Radagast based on his portrayal in the film.
- The Hobbit: Kingdoms of Middle-earth, featuring characters, locations and elements of the official soundtrack.

## Inconsistencies inside the page

- Worldwide gross: the infobox and lead give $1.017 billion, while the Box office section's components - "$303 million in the United States and Canada and $718.1 million elsewhere" - sum to about $1.021 billion.
- Runtime: the infobox gives 169 minutes and Peter Travers cites "The 169 minutes of screen time", while Peter Bradshaw writes "After 170 minutes, I felt that I had had enough of a pretty good thing."
- Release dates: the infobox lists 12 December 2012 for New Zealand and 14 December 2012 for the United States, while the Theatrical release section adds 13 December 2012 for Europe, 14 December 2012 for India, Canada and the United States, and 26 December 2012 for Australia - and notes a 65th Royal Film Performance screening in London on 12 December 2012.

wikis.title: Plot of The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey
wikis.summary: The film's story as the article summarises it, from Smaug's sacking of Erebor to the company's escape to Carrock.
wikis.body:
- Before his 111th birthday, the Hobbit Bilbo Baggins writes a story of his adventure for his nephew Frodo.
- Many years earlier the Dwarf king Thrór led his kin to prosperity under the Lonely Mountain until the dragon Smaug arrived, destroyed Dale, drove out the Dwarves and took their gold. Thrór's grandson Thorin Oakenshield appealed to Elf king Thranduil for help and was denied, "causing him to hate Elves".
- In the Shire, 51-year-old Bilbo is tricked by Gandalf the Grey into hosting a dinner for Thorin and his company: Balin, Dwalin, Fíli, Kíli, Dori, Nori, Ori, Óin, Glóin, Bifur, Bofur and Bombur. Gandalf wants Bilbo as the company's "burglar". Bilbo changes his mind after they leave without him and races to join them.
- They are captured by three Trolls; Bilbo delays them until dawn and Gandalf exposes them to sunlight, turning them to stone. In the Trolls' cave they find treasure and Elven blades - Thorin takes Orcrist, Gandalf takes Glamdring, and Gandalf gives an Elven dagger to Bilbo.
- Radagast the Brown tells Gandalf of his encounter with the Necromancer at Dol Guldur, a sorcerer corrupting Greenwood with dark magic. Chased by Orcs, Gandalf leads them through a hidden passage to Rivendell, where Lord Elrond finds the hidden indication of a secret door on the map of the Lonely Mountain, visible only on Durin's Day. Gandalf presents the White Council - Elrond, Galadriel and Saruman the White - with a Morgul blade, the Witch-king of Angmar's weapon, which Radagast obtained from Dol Guldur, as a sign the Necromancer is linked to an eventual return of Sauron. Saruman asks Gandalf to end the quest; Gandalf secretly tells Galadriel he anticipated this and had the Dwarves move on without him.
- In the Misty Mountains the company evades Stone Giants, shelters in a cave and is captured by Goblins and taken to the Great Goblin. Bilbo falls into a crevice and meets Gollum, who accidentally drops a golden ring. Bilbo pockets it, wins a riddle game, discovers the ring grants invisibility, and spares Gollum out of pity.
- The Great Goblin reveals that Azog, an Orc war-chief who killed Thrór and lost a hand to Thorin outside Moria, has placed a bounty on Thorin. Gandalf arrives, kills the Great Goblin and helps the Dwarves escape. Azog ambushes them; Thorin charges him and is injured by his Warg; Bilbo saves Thorin as eagles summoned by Gandalf arrive.
- At Carrock, Gandalf heals Thorin, who renounces his disdain for Bilbo. They see the Lonely Mountain, "where the sleeping Smaug is awoken by a thrush knocking a snail against a stone".

wikis.title: Cast and cameos
wikis.summary: The film's principal cast, the dwarves and orcs, and the family and crew cameos, plus how the cast overlaps with The Lord of the Rings.
wikis.body:
- The article notes Galadriel, Saruman and Frodo Baggins appear in The Lord of the Rings novel but not The Hobbit, that Radagast was dropped from the Lord of the Rings films, and that "Only Bilbo is portrayed by a different actor in the two sets of films, as the age difference affects his character more."
- Martin Freeman as Young Bilbo Baggins; Ian Holm, who played Old Bilbo in The Lord of the Rings, appears in scenes set directly before The Fellowship of the Ring.
- Ian McKellen as Gandalf the Grey; Richard Armitage as Thorin Oakenshield II.
- The dwarves: Ken Stott as Balin ("always their look-out man"); Graham McTavish as Dwalin; Aidan Turner as Kíli; Dean O'Gorman as Fíli; Mark Hadlow as Dori (also Bert the Stone-troll); Jed Brophy as Nori; Adam Brown as Ori; John Callen as Óin; Peter Hambleton as Glóin (also William the Stone-troll); William Kircher as Bifur (also Tom the Stone-troll); James Nesbitt as Bofur, "a disarmingly forthright, funny and occasionally brave Dwarf"; Stephen Hunter as Bombur.
- Cate Blanchett as Galadriel; Hugo Weaving as Elrond; Christopher Lee as Saruman the White; Elijah Wood as Frodo Baggins; Sylvester McCoy as Radagast the Brown; Andy Serkis as Gollum through motion-capture, who "also acted as second unit director of the trilogy".
- Manu Bennett as Azog the Defiler, "the Orc chieftain of Moria who beheaded King Thrór in the battle of Azanulbizar"; Barry Humphries as the Great Goblin; Conan Stevens as Bolg, son of Azog; John Rawls as Yazneg, with movement choreographer Terry Notary playing Yazneg during pick-up shots; Bret McKenzie as Lindir; Kiran Shah as the Goblin scribe; Jeffrey Thomas as Thrór; Stephen Ure as Fimbul and as the goblin Grinnah; Michael Mizrahi as Thráin II.
- Benedict Cumberbatch voices Smaug and the Necromancer, providing performance capture for the character's brief appearance.
- Cameos: Peter Jackson and Jabez Olssen as Erebor Dwarf refugees in the prologue; picture double Hayden J. Weal as a dwarf carrying gems; James Nesbitt's then-wife Sonia Forbes-Adam as Belladonna Took, Bilbo's mother; Nesbitt's daughters Peggy and Mary as children of Dale; Luke Evans as Girion; production designer Dan Hennah as the Old Took. Jackson's daughter, Philippa Boyens's second son and Andy Serkis's children appear in the Old Took's party; Olssen's wife and children, Richard Taylor's children and Ra Vincent's children appear in the market scene, where Ain'tItCoolNews.com writer Eric Vespe plays Fredegar Chubb, the fish seller. The appearances in the Old Took's party and the market scene are shown only in the extended edition.

wikis.title: Development, filming and the 48 fps high frame rate
wikis.summary: Del Toro's departure, Jackson taking over without preparation, the back-to-back shoot, and the film's record-first 48 frames per second release.
wikis.body:
## Development

- A film adaptation was in development for several years after the success of The Lord of the Rings trilogy. "Jackson was initially going to produce and write a two-film adaptation of The Hobbit, which was to be directed by Guillermo del Toro. Del Toro left the project in May 2010, after about two years of working with Jackson and his production team, due to delays caused in part by financial problems at Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer. Jackson was announced as director that October."
- The Hobbit films were produced back to back. "Principal photography for The Hobbit films began on 21 March 2011 in New Zealand and ended on 6 July 2012, after 266 days of filming. Pick-ups for An Unexpected Journey were filmed in July 2012 as well. Work on the film was expected to be completed on 26 November, just two days prior to the film's Wellington premiere."
- Jackson on taking over: "Because Guillermo del Toro had to leave and I jumped in and took over, we didn't wind the clock back a year and a half and give me a year and a half prep to design the movie, which was different to what he was doing. It was impossible, and as a result of it being impossible I just started shooting the movie with most of it not prepped at all. You're going on to a set and you're winging it, you've got these massively complicated scenes, no storyboards and you're making it up there and then on the spot."
- He also said: "I spent most of The Hobbit feeling like I was not on top of it. Even from a script point of view, Fran [Walsh], Philippa [Boyens] and I hadn't got the entire scripts written to our satisfaction, so that was a very high pressure situation". The article notes he explains in the DVD/Blu-ray featurettes how the crew overcame the obstacles, "especially the shooting of the Battle of the Five Armies which was shifted from 2012 to 2013 to be properly planned and shot".

## High frame rate

- "The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey used a shooting and projection frame rate of 48 frames per second, becoming the first feature film with a wide release to do so. The new projection rate was advertised as 'High Frame Rate' to the general public. However, the majority of cinemas projected the film at the industry standard 24 fps after the film was converted."

wikis.title: Marketing, theatrical release and home media
wikis.summary: The trailer and Comic-Con push, Wellington's 'Middle of Middle-earth' week and the world premiere, and the DVD, Blu-ray and 4K releases.
wikis.body:
## Marketing

- The first trailer screened before the Jackson-produced The Adventures of Tintin in the US on 21 December 2011 and was released online the same day. Geoff Boucher of the Los Angeles Times: "While it was all too fleeting there was enough in it to stir the heart of fans." Jen Chaney of The Washington Post: "Visually and tonally, this preview ... looks like a perfect match for the Frodo Baggins tales that released in 2001, 2002 and 2003. […] This clip is all about reacquainting us with Middle-earth."
- Jackson, Freeman, McKellen, Armitage, Serkis, Wood and Philippa Boyens appeared at the 2012 San Diego Comic-Con, screening 12 minutes of footage.
- On 8 October 2012 Wellington Mayor Celia Wade-Brown announced that for the week of the premiere the capital of New Zealand would be renamed the "Middle of Middle-earth".
- An Air New Zealand Boeing 777-300 carried "The Airline of Middle-earth" livery to promote the film.

## Theatrical release

- World premiere on 28 November 2012 at the Embassy Theatre in Wellington, with full theatrical release in New Zealand on 12 December; 13 December 2012 in Europe; 14 December 2012 in India, Canada and the United States; and 26 December 2012 (Boxing Day) in Australia.
- It was screened at the 65th Royal Film Performance in London on 12 December 2012 in aid of the Film & TV Charity, with Prince William attending and speaking with Martin Freeman about his enthusiasm for Tolkien's works. Prince Charles had visited Peter Jackson, the Wētā Workshop and cast members a week before the New Zealand premiere.
- "Around 100,000 people lined the red carpet on Courtenay Place for the film's premiere, and the entire event was broadcast live on TV in New Zealand, as well as streaming over the internet."
- An extended edition had a limited re-release on 5 October 2015 with a special greeting from Peter Jackson.

## Home media

- Released on DVD, Blu-ray and Blu-ray 3D on 19 March 2013, with an extended edition adding 13 minutes of footage and three bonus discs of roughly nine hours of special features on 5 November 2013. UK release 8 April 2013.
- "An Unexpected Journey's home video sales made a revenue of $99 million with 6.2 million copies sold, making it the third best-selling title of 2013 behind Despicable Me 2 and The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 2."
- Released on Ultra HD Blu-ray on 30 November 2020 in the United Kingdom and 1 December 2020 in the United States, with the rest of the trilogy in theatrical and extended editions.

wikis.title: Box office performance
wikis.summary: The film's billion-dollar worldwide gross and the December records it set in North America and abroad.
wikis.body:
- "The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey grossed $303 million in the United States and Canada and $718.1 million elsewhere for a worldwide total of $1.017 billion, becoming the 15th film in history to reach $1 billion. It is the fourth highest-grossing film of 2012."
- Worldwide opening weekend of $222.6 million, including $15.1 million from 452 IMAX theatres - "an IMAX opening-weekend record for December".
- It earned $13.0 million during its midnight run, a December midnight record previously held by Avatar, then topped the box office on its opening day (Friday, 14 December 2012) with $37.1 million from 4,045 theatres, a December opening-day record previously held by The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King.
- First weekend $84.62 million, first place and a then-December opening-weekend record previously held by I Am Legend. 3D showings were 49% of weekend ticket sales; IMAX generated $10.1 million (12% of the weekend gross).
- Second weekend: down 57% to $36.7 million but still first. Third weekend: down only 11% to $32.9 million, still first.
- Internationally it earned $11.2 million on its opening day (Wednesday, 12 December 2012) from 16 markets and "a five-day opening-weekend gross of just under $138 million" through its first Sunday, topping the box office outside North America on two consecutive weekends.
- In Sweden it had the second-largest five-day opening with $6.2 million, behind Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2. Its three largest openings were the UK, Ireland and Malta ($18.8 million); Russia and the CIS ($17.8 million); and Germany ($17.1 million).

wikis.title: Critical response
wikis.summary: The film's aggregate scores and the range of published reviews, with the recurring arguments about length and the 48 fps look.
wikis.body:
- After the New Zealand premiere, Television New Zealand noted responses were "largely positive" but with "mixed responses to the film's technological advances". After the international release, Forbes called reviews "unenthusiastic" and the Los Angeles Times said the consensus is that the film "stumbles".
- Rotten Tomatoes: 64% from 303 reviews, average 6.60/10. Consensus: "Peter Jackson's return to Middle-earth is an earnest, visually resplendent trip, but the film's deliberate pace robs the material of some of its majesty." Metacritic: 58 out of 100 from 40 critics, "mixed or average reviews". CinemaScore opening-weekend grade "A".
- "The main contention of debate was regarding the film's length, its high frame rate, and whether or not the film matched the level of expectation built from The Lord of the Rings film trilogy, while the film's visual style, special effects, music score, and cast were praised, especially the performances of Martin Freeman, Ian McKellen, Richard Armitage, and Andy Serkis."
- Peter Travers (Rolling Stone) criticised "48 frames per second… Couple that with 3D and the movie looks so hyper-real that you see everything that's fake about it… The 169 minutes of screen time hurts, since the first 45 minutes of the film traps us in the hobbit home of the young Bilbo Baggins," but added that once the journey starts "things perk up considerably".
- Robbie Collin (The Daily Telegraph), two of five: "Thank heavens for Andy Serkis, whose riddling return as Gollum steals the entire film… As a lover of cinema, Jackson's film bored me rigid; as a lover of Tolkien, it broke my heart." He called it "so stuffed with extraneous faff and flummery that it often barely feels like Tolkien at all – more a dire, fan-written internet tribute."
- Keith Uhlich (Time Out): "a mesmerizing study in excess … bursting with surplus characters, wall-to-wall special effects, unapologetically drawn-out story tangents and double the frame rate (48 over 24) of the average movie."
- Peter Bradshaw (The Guardian): "After 170 minutes, I felt that I had had enough of a pretty good thing. The trilogy will test the stamina of the non-believers, and many might feel ... that the traditional filmic look of Lord of the Rings was better."
- Richard Lawson (The Atlantic Wire): "this is a dismally unattractive movie, featuring too many shots that I'm sure were lovely at some point but are now ruined and chintzified by the terrible technology monster."
- Positive notices: Matthew Leyland (Total Film), five stars - "Charming, spectacular, technically audacious… in short, everything you expect from a Peter Jackson movie"; Ed Gonzalez (Slant), three of four; Todd McCarthy (The Hollywood Reporter) - "a purist's delight… [And leads to] an undeniably exciting, action-packed climax", though "there is much that is flat-footed and tedious as well, especially in the early going"; Kate Muir (The Times), four of five, saying the 48 fps 3D gives "lurid clarity"; Dan Jolin (Empire), four of five - "There is treasure here".

wikis.title: Accolades
wikis.summary: The film's Oscar nominations, its Saturn and Empire Awards and the other critics' honours listed.
wikis.body:
- Three Academy Award nominations: Best Visual Effects, Best Production Design and Best Makeup and Hairstyling, at the 85th Academy Awards.
- Praise from the Broadcast Film Critics Association and from the Houston Film Critics Society, Phoenix Film Critics Society and Washington D.C. Area Film Critics Association.
- "The film's team won an Academy Scientific and Technical Award—the Scientific and Engineering Award for inventing a technique which has made huge advances in bringing to life computer-generated characters such as Gollum in the film to the screen."
- In January 2013 it was nominated in the Best Live Action Motion Picture category at the Cinema Audio Society Awards, awarded on 16 February.
- It led the nominations at the 39th Saturn Awards with nine, "more than The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring which earned eight nominations at the time of its release", including Best Director (Jackson's eleventh Saturn nomination), Best Actor for Martin Freeman, Best Supporting Actor for Ian McKellen (his third nomination for playing Gandalf) and Best Music for Howard Shore. It won Best Production Design for Dan Hennah, Ra Vincent and Simon Bright.
- Five nominations at the 18th Empire Awards, winning Best Actor for Martin Freeman and Best Science Fiction/Fantasy Film.
- Two nominations at the 2013 MTV Movie Awards - Best Scared-as-S**t Performance and Best Hero for Martin Freeman, who won the latter.
- Six nominations at the 2013 SFX Awards, including Best Film, Best Director for Peter Jackson and four acting nominations.

The level and change are also published at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

wikis.title: Catalog of Solar Eclipses of Saros 127
wikis.summary: NASA/GSFC eclipse catalogue page giving the statistics and full eclipse-by-eclipse table for solar Saros series 127, from 0991 Oct 10 to 2452 Mar 21.
wikis.body:
## What the page is

A Saros series catalogue page from NASA's eclipse site listing "concise details and local circumstances at greatest eclipse for every solar eclipse in Saros 127".

## The Saros cycle (as the page explains it)

- The Saros cycle is "a period of approximately 6,585.3 days (18 years 11 days 8 hours)".
- Eclipses one Saros apart "share a very similar geometry", occurring at the same node with the Moon at nearly the same distance from Earth and at the same time of year.
- "Each series typically lasts 12 to 13 centuries and contains 70 or more eclipses." A series begins with partial eclipses near one pole, produces several dozen central eclipses, then ends with partials near the opposite pole.

## Statistics for Saros 127

- All eclipses of Saros 127 "occur at the Moons ascending node and the Moon moves southward with each eclipse".
- First Eclipse = 0991 Oct 10 14:31:21 TD (partial, northern hemisphere).
- Last Eclipse = 2452 Mar 21 17:01:31 TD (partial, southern hemisphere).
- Duration of Saros 127 = 1460.44 years.
- Composed of 82 solar eclipses: 40 partial (48.8%), 0 annular (0.0%), 42 total (51.2%), 0 hybrid (0.0%).
- All 42 umbral eclipses are Central (two limits) - 100%; none central (one limit) or non-central.
- Sequence string for the 82 eclipses: `20P 42T 20P`.

## Extremes

- Longest total solar eclipse: 1532 Aug 30, 05m40s.
- Shortest total solar eclipse: 2091 Aug 15, 01m38s.
- Largest partial solar eclipse: 1334 May 04, magnitude 0.98297.
- Smallest partial solar eclipse: 2452 Mar 21, magnitude 0.02617.

## Catalog columns

Each row carries: sequence number, relative number, calendar date, TD of greatest eclipse, delta-T (s), lunation number, eclipse type, gamma, eclipse magnitude, latitude and longitude of greatest eclipse, Sun altitude, path width (km) and central duration.

## Sample rows from the catalog (21st century onward)

- 2001 Jun 21 12:04:46 TD - T, gamma -0.5701, mag 1.0495, 11.3S 2.7E, Sun alt 55 deg, path 200 km, 04m57s.
- 2019 Jul 02 19:24:07 TD - T, gamma -0.6466, mag 1.0459, 17.4S 109.0W, alt 50 deg, path 201 km, 04m33s.
- 2037 Jul 13 02:40:36 TD - T, gamma -0.7246, mag 1.0413, 24.8S 139.1E, alt 43 deg, path 201 km, 03m58s.
- 2055 Jul 24 09:57:50 TD - T, gamma -0.8012, mag 1.0359, 33.3S 25.8E, alt 37 deg, path 202 km, 03m17s.
- 2073 Aug 03 17:15:23 TD - T, gamma -0.8763, mag 1.0294, 43.2S 89.4W, alt 28 deg, path 206 km, 02m29s.
- 2091 Aug 15 00:34:43 TD - T, gamma -0.9490, mag 1.0216, 55.6S 150.5E, alt 18 deg, path 236 km, 01m38s.
- 2109 Aug 26 07:57:26 TD - P (first of the closing partial group), gamma -1.0178, mag 0.9670, 71.4S 5.1E.

## Calendar and predictions

- Gregorian calendar for all dates from 1582 Oct 15 onwards; Julian before that. Years are numbered astronomically and include year 0.
- Sun coordinates from VSOP87 (Bretagnon and Francou, 1988); Moon from ELP-2000/82 (Chapront-Touze and Chapront, 1983); lunar secular acceleration n-dot = -25.858 arc-sec/cy*cy (Chapront, Chapront-Touze and Francou, 2002).
- delta-T: pre-1950s from empirical fits by Morrison and Stephenson (2004); 1955-present from published observations; future extrapolated from current values weighted by the long-term tidal trend.

## Credits

Based on *Five Millennium Canon of Solar Eclipses: -1999 to +3000* and *Five Millennium Catalog of Solar Eclipses: -1999 to +3000*. wikis.title: Catalog of Solar Eclipses of Saros 129
wikis.summary: NASA/GSFC eclipse catalogue page giving the statistics and full eclipse-by-eclipse table for solar Saros series 129, from 1103 Oct 03 to 2528 Feb 21.
wikis.body:
## What the page is

A Saros series catalogue page from NASA's eclipse site listing "concise details and local circumstances at greatest eclipse for every solar eclipse in Saros 129".

## The Saros cycle (as the page explains it)

- The Saros cycle is "a period of approximately 6,585.3 days (18 years 11 days 8 hours)"; eclipses one Saros apart "share a very similar geometry".
- "Each series typically lasts 12 to 13 centuries and contains 70 or more eclipses", beginning with partials near one pole and ending with partials near the opposite pole.

## Statistics for Saros 129

- All eclipses of Saros 129 "occur at the Moons ascending node and the Moon moves southward with each eclipse".
- First Eclipse = 1103 Oct 03 03:17:50 TD (partial, northern hemisphere).
- Last Eclipse = 2528 Feb 21 12:36:45 TD (partial, southern hemisphere).
- Duration of Saros 129 = 1424.38 years.
- Composed of 80 solar eclipses: 39 partial (48.8%), 29 annular (36.2%), 9 total (11.2%), 3 hybrid (3.8%).
- Of 41 umbral eclipses: 40 Central (two limits) (97.6%), 1 Central (one limit) (2.4%), 0 non-central.
- Sequence string for the 80 eclipses: `20P 29A 3H 9T 19P`.

## Extremes

- Longest annular: 1698 Oct 04, 05m10s. Shortest annular: 1969 Mar 18, 00m26s.
- Longest total: 2131 Jun 25, 03m43s. Shortest total: 2041 Apr 30, 01m51s.
- Longest hybrid: 2023 Apr 20, 01m16s. Shortest hybrid: 1987 Mar 29, 00m08s.
- Largest partial: 1446 Apr 26, magnitude 0.91473. Smallest partial: 2528 Feb 21, magnitude 0.02182.

## Catalog columns

Sequence number, relative number, calendar date, TD of greatest eclipse, delta-T (s), lunation number, eclipse type, gamma, eclipse magnitude, latitude and longitude of greatest eclipse, Sun altitude, path width (km) and central duration.

## Sample rows from the catalog (modern members)

- 1969 Mar 18 04:54:57 TD - A, gamma -0.2704, mag 0.9954, 14.8S 116.3E, alt 74 deg, path 16 km, 00m26s.
- 1987 Mar 29 12:49:47 TD - H, gamma -0.3053, mag 1.0013, 12.3S 2.3W, alt 72 deg, path 5 km, 00m08s.
- 2005 Apr 08 20:36:51 TD - H, gamma -0.3473, mag 1.0074, 10.6S 119.0W, alt 70 deg, path 27 km, 00m42s.
- 2023 Apr 20 04:17:56 TD - H, gamma -0.3952, mag 1.0132, 9.6S 125.8E, alt 67 deg, path 49 km, 01m16s.
- 2041 Apr 30 11:52:21 TD - T, gamma -0.4492, mag 1.0189, 9.6S 12.2E, alt 63 deg, path 72 km, 01m51s.
- 2059 May 11 19:22:16 TD - T, gamma -0.5080, mag 1.0242, 10.7S 100.4W, alt 59 deg, path 95 km, 02m23s.
- 2077 May 22 02:46:05 TD - T, gamma -0.5725, mag 1.0290, 13.1S 148.3E, alt 55 deg, path 119 km, 02m54s.
- 2095 Jun 02 10:07:40 TD - T, gamma -0.6396, mag 1.0332, 16.7S 37.2E, alt 50 deg, path 145 km, 03m18s.
- 2131 Jun 25 00:43:16 TD - T, gamma -0.7813, mag 1.0393, 28.1S 174.7E, alt 38 deg, path 211 km, 03m43s.
- 2185 Jul 26 22:38:16 TD - Ts (the one central, one-limit member), gamma -0.9967, mag 1.0370, 67.9S 178.5W, alt 1 deg, 02m27s.

## Calendar and predictions

- Gregorian calendar from 1582 Oct 15 onwards, Julian before; years numbered astronomically, including year 0.
- Sun from VSOP87 (Bretagnon and Francou, 1988); Moon from ELP-2000/82 (Chapront-Touze and Chapront, 1983); n-dot = -25.858 arc-sec/cy*cy (Chapront, Chapront-Touze and Francou, 2002).
- delta-T: pre-1950s from Morrison and Stephenson (2004); 1955-present from published observations; future extrapolated with the long-term tidal trend.

## Credits

Based on the *Five Millennium Canon* and *Five Millennium Catalog of Solar Eclipses: -1999 to +3000*; maps by Dan McGlaun, Besselian elements by Jean Meeus. "Fred Espenak assumes full responsibility for the accuracy of all eclipse calculations." Reuse permitted with the acknowledgment "Eclipse Predictions by Fred Espenak (NASA's GSFC)".

The page ends with the bare date stamp "2009 Sep 26".

wikis.title: 2032 Summer Paralympics (Brisbane)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 2032 Summer Paralympics in Brisbane, Australia - scheduled 24 August to 5 September 2032 - covering the host arrangement, accessibility concerns and the sports federations campaigning for inclusion.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- "The 2032 Summer Paralympics, also known as the Brisbane 2032 Summer Paralympic Games, and branded as Brisbane 2032, will be the 19th edition of the Summer Paralympic Games, an international multi-sport parasports event governed by the International Paralympic Committee."
- Scheduled to be held in Brisbane, Queensland, Australia, from 24 August to 5 September 2032. The infobox gives Opening 24 August 2032, Closing 5 September 2032, Stadium: Brisbane Olympic Stadium, and titles the Games "XIX Paralympic Games" (logo shown is "Provisional logo").
- "It will be the second Summer Paralympics held in Australia, following the 2000 Summer Paralympics in Sydney, New South Wales."
- Preceded by Los Angeles 2028; succeeded by "TBD 2036".

## Bids and organisation

- "As per the agreement between the International Olympic Committee and the International Paralympic Committee in 2001, a city which wins the Olympic Games host bid will also stage the Paralympic Games."
- "Brisbane Organising Committee for the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games was established by the Queensland Government to plan, organise and deliver the Olympic and Paralympic Games in accordance with the host contract" (cited to the Brisbane Olympic and Paralympic Games Arrangements Act 2021).
- The Venues section carries only a link to the main article "Venues of the 2032 Summer Olympics and Paralympics".

## Transportation and accessibility concerns

- In November 2022 advocates including Paralympian Karni Liddell "raised concerns about Brisbane's preparedness to host the Paralympics in 2032, citing many instances where there was a lack of appropriate accessibility for people with disabilities throughout the city", and implored organisers to consult the disability sector.
- Youngcare Connect manager Shane Jamieson "accused the city of being 'completely ill-prepared' to host the Paralympics", saying future development before 2032 would rely on consultation with people with disabilities.
- Queensland Human Rights Commissioner Scott McDougall said Queensland "was still lagging behind in relation to making public transport fully accessible to those with a disability, with 40% of railway stations in South East Queensland still only accessible by stairs".
- The cited article is headlined "Paralympian Karni Liddell says Brisbane's lack of accessibility hasn't changed in 30 years" (The Courier-Mail, 16 November 2022).

## Sports programme

- "The initial sports programme is yet to be determined." Federations announcing campaigns for inclusion:
- **Rugby league** - July 2021: International Rugby League declared an intent to campaign for inclusion in the 2032 Olympics and Paralympics, "focusing on wheelchair rugby league for the Paralympics and league nines for the Olympics".
- **Blind cricket** - in 2024 cricketer Nathan Lyon said he wanted blind cricket included, after standard cricket was selected for the 2028 Summer Olympics; Cricket Australia and Paralympics Australia "have also indicated support". In June 2025 IPC president Andrew Parsons "confirmed that a gold medal match held at The Gabba is a possibility should the sport be included". (The cited article is dated 4 June 2025.)
- **Lawn bowls** - July 2025: World Bowls and Bowls Australia jointly launched a campaign for inclusion in both the 2032 Olympics and Paralympics; if included it "would be featured alongside related sport boccia". (The cited Bowls Australia item is dated 28 July 2025.)
- **Para sailing** - December 2025: World Sailing submitted a proposal to reinstate para sailing, "arguing that the sport has grown in participation since it was last featured". Sailing "was a demonstration sport in 1996, before becoming an official sport from 2000 to 2016". (Cited World Sailing item dated 16 December 2025.)
- **Women's blind football** - August 2026: International Blind Sports Federation president Ilgar Rahimov said the organisation "was to work towards the inclusion of women's blind football through increasing the participation of women by supporting national teams and organising international competitions". "Blind football has only had a men's competition since its inclusion in 2004." (Cited IBSA item dated 14 August 2026, headlined "Two Years to LA28: The Games Begin Long Before the Opening Ceremony".)

## Categories

- Includes 2032 Summer Paralympics, Scheduled multi-sport events, International sports competitions hosted by Australia, Sports competitions in Brisbane, 2032 in disability sport.

wikis.summary: A Free Documentary - Engineering video page on Taycan production at Porsche's Zuffenhausen plant, with the Taycan Turbo S performance and battery figures its description gives.
wikis.body:
## What the page is
YouTube page for "Porsche Factory: Inside the Ultra-Modern Taycan Assembly Line | FD Engineering" on **Free Documentary - Engineering**, published 2026-08-21. Metadata and description only.

## The car
- The **Taycan Turbo S** is called "one of its most ambitious cars ever built".
- "Producing up to **761 horsepower** and accelerating from **0 to 100 km/h in just 2.8 seconds**".
- It "combines Porsche performance with an entirely new generation of technology".

## The factory
- "At Porsche's headquarters in **Zuffenhausen**, a new high-tech factory was built specifically for the Taycan."
- "Across three floors, autonomous transport systems, industrial robots and hundreds of skilled workers transform the body shell into a finished electric sports car."

## Production steps followed
Body construction; the **800-volt** electric motors; installation of the "massive **650 kg** battery"; the automated "marriage" of powertrain and body; "rigorous final quality tests every vehicle must pass before leaving the factory".

## Related link in the description
"Spider Excavator Manufacturing - Inside the Menzi Muck Factory" (youtu.be/CN1xviB0R7k).

wikis.title: BettingPros: 2026 Heisman Trophy betting preview
wikis.summary: A 44-minute BettingPros Podcast episode from 19 August 2026 in which Seth Woolcock and Scott Bogman work through the 2026 Heisman Trophy futures market - voting trends, the November games that could decide it, and their picks from CJ Carr at +750 down to a 225-to-1 flyer.
wikis.body:
## The episode

- "**2026 Heisman Trophy Betting Preview: Best Bets, Favorites, Longshots & Value Picks (Ep. 1040)**", **BettingPros Podcast**, channel **The Volume**, frequency "Updated Weekly".
- Published "**August 19, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC**"; length **44 min**; episode **1040**; rating Clean.
- The page's "Hosts & Guests" block lists only **Joe Pisapia** as host, but the episode itself is hosted by **Seth Woolcock** with **Scott Bogman**.
- Description: "Who will win the 2026 Heisman Trophy? Seth Woolcock and Scott Bogman break down the 2026 Heisman Trophy betting market, including the historical trends, voter blueprint, key showcase games, favorites, mid-tier values and long-shot futures you need to know before Week 0."
- Timestamps given (noted as "may be off due to ads"): Intro 0:00:00; Futures Factory: Heisman Voter Blueprint 0:02:57; Past Trends 0:05:59; Key November Showcase Games 0:08:32; CJ Carr +750 0:11:16; Arch Manning +809 0:14:59; Premium giveaway 0:18:08; Darian Mensah +1200 0:18:53; Trinidad Chambliss +1329 0:22:17; Julian Sayin +1329 0:24:50; Dante Moore +1567 0:26:52; Jeremiah Smith +1329 0:29:17; Malachi Toney +4000 0:32:00; app promo 0:33:59; Bogman's long shots 0:34:37; Seth's long shots 0:38:15; Outro 0:43:15.
- The show is recorded "roughly a week out" from live college football action, before Week 0.

## The Heisman voter blueprint

- The award was first given in **1935**, originally as the **Downtown Athletic Club Trophy**, later renamed for coach and athletic director **John Heisman**.
- It is voted on by **870 sports media members** spread evenly across the six US regions, plus all living former Heisman winners, and "brand new this season, the single collective fan vote compiled via the Heisman Hopefuls Platform". Woolcock says fan voting appears to open around week two and to run weekly, calls it "wonky", and says he is not factoring it into the betting markets.
- Trends cited: a quarterback has won "in eight of the last ten years and sixteen of the last twenty years"; only eight winners in the 20-year span have been underclassmen; the last freshman to win was **Jameis Winston in 2013**.
- "in twenty twenty five, Travis Hunter actually became just the fourth Heisman winner from a team with four or more losses, the first since nineteen sixty nine" - so they favour players on elite teams.
- The last Group of Six player to win was **BYU quarterback Ty Detmer in 1990**, so the show sticks to Power Four players.
- Schools with the most winners: **USC with eight**, then Ohio State, Oklahoma and Notre Dame with seven each, and **Alabama with four**. Programs with no winner include **Tennessee, Clemson and Ole Miss**.
- Bogman also says of recent years, "Fernando Mendoza was clearly the winner to me. Travis Hunter was clearly the winner to me as well", and opens the show arguing Vince Young was snubbed in 2005.

## Key November showcase games

- **Week 10, November 7**: No. 13 Alabama at No. 11 LSU; No. 3 Georgia at No. 9 Ole Miss; No. 7 Miami at No. 4 Notre Dame; No. 2 Oregon at No. 1 Ohio State. Rankings are said to come from a poll released the previous day.
- **Week 11**: No. 9 Ole Miss at No. 10 Oklahoma; No. 5 Texas at No. 11 LSU; No. 14 USC at No. 6 Indiana.
- **Week 12**: "Not a whole lot happening there."
- **Week 13 (rivalry week)**: No. 16 Michigan at No. 1 Ohio State.
- Woolcock: "these Heisman cases might be built and lost surrounding those games in week ten, eleven, and thirteen."

## Top-tier favourites

- **CJ Carr (QB, Notre Dame), +750** - the betting favourite, best price found across prediction markets and retail sportsbooks. A four-star recruit who started in 2025, throwing for "about twenty seven hundred plus yards" with a **66% completion rate and 24 touchdowns**, ranking **fifth in passing efficiency rating and third in yards per attempt**. Notre Dame lose Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price from the backfield; Carr gets receiver Jaden Greathouse back from injury plus Ohio State transfers Quincy Porter Jr. and Mylan Graham, freshman Elijah Burris (son of Plaxico Burress) and Larry Fitzgerald's son. His season hinges on games at BYU and against Miami. Bogman: "This schedule is a cake walk... you're probably just walking to New York." Woolcock says he is otherwise fading Notre Dame - he has a parlay on Notre Dame missing the playoff and BYU making it at **12-to-1** - but sees +750 as the way to back a favourite.
- **Arch Manning (QB, Texas), +809** on a prediction market. A rocky start to 2025 but **19 total touchdowns in his final six games**. Texas added the portal's No. 1 receiver **Cam Coleman** from Auburn, running back **Hollywood Smothers** from NC State and **Raleek Brown** from ASU, behind what the hosts call one of the best offensive lines in the country - though left tackle **Trevor Goosby**, a projected top-15 to 20 pick, has just been reported with a bone bruise. Texas face Ohio State in week two, the Red River rivalry on October 10, then Missouri, at LSU, at Texas A&M, Ole Miss and Florida - "the third hardest schedule in the country this season". Bogman already has a ticket and would double down if Manning has a merely pedestrian game against Ohio State, warning that a big game would cut the price to about **+350**.

## Mid-tier values

- **Darian Mensah (QB, Miami), 12-to-1** - a former two-star recruit who took Tulane to an AAC title game as a sophomore, leading the conference in completion percentage and yards per attempt, then led Duke to an ACC championship game win with a conference-leading **3,900 passing yards and 34 touchdowns**. He joins Mario Cristobal's line with former Duke receiver **Cooper Barkate** and ACC Rookie of the Year **Malachi Toney**, plus Mark Fletcher in the backfield and freshman lineman Jackson Cantwell. Miami lost a lot on defence and has the **fourth easiest Power Four schedule** by the gap between FPI and strength of schedule (behind Texas Tech, Notre Dame and Penn State). Bogman on the transfer-portal controversy: "I'm not going to kill a young man for making a young man decision."
- **Trinidad Chambliss (QB, Ole Miss), +1329** - "the latest D two transfer to breakout in twenty twenty five" after Austin Simmons was injured in week three, leading the conference with nearly **4,000 passing yards, 24 touchdowns and three interceptions**, plus **500-plus rushing yards and eight scores**, taking Ole Miss to the CFP semi-finals without Lane Kiffin. Now facing the **fifth hardest schedule** with an underwhelming new receiving corps - at Vandy, Missouri, at Texas, Auburn, Georgia, at Oklahoma after the bye. Woolcock: "I love the player, I don't like the price", and holds a ticket on Ole Miss missing the playoff.
- **Julian Sayin (QB, Ohio State), +1329** - finished **fourth in the 2025 Heisman voting** in his first season starting. Not the athlete Chambliss or Manning is, but with "poise in the pocket" and "precision accuracy". He lost Carnell Tate and his top three tight ends to the NFL but keeps **Jeremiah Smith**, slot receiver Brandon Inniss and the No. 1 receiver recruit **Chris Henry Jr.**, with **Bo Jackson** in the backfield. Both hosts think the crowded offence will split his case; Bogman says Sayin must look good at Indiana, at USC, against Oregon and against Michigan - "there's more outs on saying than there are reasons to be in".
- **Dante Moore (QB, Oregon), +1567** - the shortest price Woolcock has bet, on a quarterback who "was probably gonna be the second overall pick in the draft if he declared last year". In 2025 he was **sixth in the country in passing touchdowns** and **fourth in completion percentage**, leading Oregon to a CFP semi-final. Loaded backfield (though Davidson is banged up), Corey Moore leading the receivers, "maybe the best tight end in the country", veteran line. Both call him **the best value on the board under 20-to-1**; Bogman says it comes down to the game at Ohio State, with USC, Michigan and Washington all winnable.

## Skill players

- **Jeremiah Smith (WR, Ohio State), +1329** - the highest-priced position player, with back-to-back seasons of **1,200-plus yards and 12-plus touchdowns**, All-American honours and "the six most Heisman Trophy votes" last year (87 catches, 1,243 yards, 12 receiving touchdowns plus a rushing one). Bogman compares the benchmark to **DeVonta Smith's 98 catches, 1,511 yards and 17 touchdowns**, and suggests Smith may now need "over one hundred catches, maybe sixteen hundred yards and closer to twenty touchdowns". Woolcock had him at **16-to-1** the previous year and calls +1329 too short, especially if Chris Henry Jr. breaks out. He notes his own past position-player tickets: 65-to-1 on Travis Hunter two years ago, 60-to-1 on Jeremiah Love last year.
- **Malachi Toney (WR, Miami), 40-to-1** - 5-foot-11 with "elite acceleration", he had a nation-high **109 receptions for 1,200-plus yards and 13 total touchdowns** (10 receiving, one rushing, two passing) as a true freshman, winning **ACC Rookie of the Year and First Team All-ACC**. Bogman compares him to Tyreek Hill, notes that the 2025 regular-season line of "eighty four nine to seventy and seven" would not win the award, and says he is worth "a quarter unit something bet - it's a long shot, but it's not a crazy, crazy long shot".

## Bogman's long shots

- **Jean Mateer, +3000 (30-to-1)** - slowed by a thumb injury last year; "a much better runner than Mendoza, not nearly the passer", with "Riley Leonard kind of craziness... no risk and no biscuit". Bogman is less excited about his team.
- **Byron Brown (Auburn), 50-to-1** - "this is just for stats"; if he posts big passing and 1,000 rushing yards he will be in the conversation late, but Auburn has an FPI of 22 and the **13th hardest schedule** and Bogman doubts the team is good enough.
- **Bear Bachmeier (BYU), +6000 (60-to-1)** - ran for 11 touchdowns last season alongside LJ Martin and threw for 3,000 yards and 15 touchdowns after Jake Retzlaff was booted late in the season. "Just a little sprinkle."

## Seth's long shots

- **Sam Leavitt (LSU), 25-to-1** - also backed at 45-to-1 to be the first overall pick if Manning does not come out. A former four-star and the **2024 Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year** who took Arizona State with Cam Skattebo to a Big 12 title and a CFP run; now with Lane Kiffin, left tackle Jordan Seaton, tight end Trey'Dez Green and a deep receiver group. "if he can win in Week one and then he goes into Oxford and comes out with a win... twenty five to one will not be around".
- **Keelan Russell (Alabama), 30-to-1** - a five-star dual-threat quarterback nobody has seen play, with a good receiving corps and "a soft first five games", making a cash-out live heading into week six against Georgia; if Ryan Grubb cannot fix the running game it will be all on Russell.
- **Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele (Cal), 65-to-1** - a true freshman last year who helped Cal win seven games, finishing **fourth in the conference in passing yards and fifth in touchdown passes**, with **four ACC Rookie of the Week** and **two ACC Quarterback of the Week** awards, now with an elite defensive coach and a strong portal class. Woolcock likens the possible path to "a Haynes King type of situation".
- **Jared Curtis (Vanderbilt), +22500 (225-to-1)** - "your DJEN bet of the season", the top-ranked pocket-passing quarterback in the 2026 class, expected to win the job; Woolcock thinks the price would fall to 200 or 150-to-1 if he does. Vanderbilt open with Austin Peay, Delaware, NC State and then at Auburn in week four.
- Bogman's view: "this is probably one of the worst years to throw a sprinkle on a long shot because there's so much at the top" - he most likes the Keelan Russell call, because Alabama is on television every week, and Sam Leavitt for the same visibility at LSU, while calling Sagapolutele and Curtis "probably flushing money".

wikis.title: Who votes for the Heisman, and what the trends say
wikis.summary: The award's history, the 2026 voting body including a new fan vote, and the historical patterns the hosts bet on.
wikis.body:
- First awarded in **1935** as the **Downtown Athletic Club Trophy**, later renamed for coach and athletic director **John Heisman**.
- Voted on by **870 sports media members** spread evenly across six US regions, plus all living former winners, and new for this season "the single collective fan vote compiled via the Heisman Hopefuls Platform". Fan voting appears to open around week two and run weekly; Woolcock calls it "wonky" and excludes it from his betting analysis.
- A quarterback has won "in eight of the last ten years and sixteen of the last twenty years"; only eight winners in that 20-year span were underclassmen; the last freshman winner was **Jameis Winston in 2013**.
- "in twenty twenty five, Travis Hunter actually became just the fourth Heisman winner from a team with four or more losses, the first since nineteen sixty nine" - so the hosts want players on elite teams.
- The last Group of Six winner was **BYU's Ty Detmer in 1990**, so the show sticks to Power Four players.
- Most winners: USC 8; Ohio State, Oklahoma and Notre Dame 7 each; Alabama 4. Programs with none: **Tennessee, Clemson, Ole Miss**.
- Bogman calls it "my favorite individual award in sports", says recent winners Fernando Mendoza and Travis Hunter were clear choices, and opens by arguing Vince Young was snubbed in 2005.

wikis.title: The November games that could decide the race
wikis.summary: The showcase weekends the hosts say will make or break Heisman cases.
wikis.body:
- **Week 10, November 7** - "don't make any plans": No. 13 Alabama at No. 11 LSU; No. 3 Georgia at No. 9 Ole Miss; No. 7 Miami at No. 4 Notre Dame; No. 2 Oregon at No. 1 Ohio State. The rankings are from a poll released the day before recording.
- **Week 11**: No. 9 Ole Miss at No. 10 Oklahoma; No. 5 Texas at No. 11 LSU; No. 14 USC at No. 6 Indiana.
- **Week 12**: quiet - "if you have to schedule something with the family... make it week eleven or week twelve".
- **Week 13, rivalry week**: No. 16 Michigan at No. 1 Ohio State.
- Bogman notes the Ohio State-Oregon game could feature two Ohio State candidates, Sayin and Smith, plus Notre Dame-Miami pairing "CJ Carr and Darian Mensah, two of your favorites"; Arch Manning at LSU is expected to be a night game though no start time is set.
- Woolcock: "these Heisman cases might be built and lost surrounding those games in week ten, eleven, and thirteen."

wikis.title: CJ Carr and Arch Manning at the top of the board
wikis.summary: The two shortest prices, their supporting casts and the hosts' timing advice.
wikis.body:
- **CJ Carr (QB, Notre Dame), +750** - the best price across prediction markets and retail books. A four-star recruit who started in 2025 for "about twenty seven hundred plus yards", a **66% completion rate and 24 touchdowns**, ranking fifth in passing efficiency and third in yards per attempt.
- Notre Dame lose Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price from the backfield; Carr regains receiver Jaden Greathouse from injury and adds Ohio State transfers Quincy Porter Jr. and Mylan Graham, freshman Elijah Burris (son of Plaxico Burress) and Larry Fitzgerald's son.
- His case rests on at BYU and versus Miami. Bogman: "This schedule is a cake walk... if you play well in those games and you don't drop a weird Northern Illinois esque type game... you're probably just walking to New York."
- Woolcock is fading Notre Dame elsewhere - a 12-to-1 parlay on Notre Dame missing the playoff and BYU making it - but says +750 is unlikely to get better.
- **Arch Manning (QB, Texas), +809** on a prediction market. After a rocky start he threw **19 total touchdowns in his last six games of 2025**. Texas added Cam Coleman (Auburn, the portal's No. 1 receiver), Hollywood Smothers (NC State) and Raleek Brown (ASU); left tackle Trevor Goosby, a projected top-15 to 20 pick, has just been reported with a bone bruise.
- Texas face Ohio State in week two, Red River on October 10, then Missouri, at LSU, at Texas A&M, Ole Miss and Florida - "the third hardest schedule in the country".
- Bogman already holds a ticket, would double down if Manning is merely pedestrian against Ohio State, and warns that a big game would cut him to about **+350**.

wikis.title: The mid-tier quarterbacks
wikis.summary: Mensah, Chambliss, Sayin and Moore - and why Dante Moore is called the best value under 20-to-1.
wikis.body:
- **Darian Mensah (QB, Miami), 12-to-1** - a former two-star who took Tulane to an AAC title game, leading the conference in completion percentage and yards per attempt, then led Duke to an ACC title game win with a conference-leading **3,900 yards and 34 touchdowns**. Now with Cooper Barkate, Malachi Toney, Mark Fletcher and a strong Mario Cristobal offensive line, on the **fourth easiest Power Four schedule** by FPI-minus-strength-of-schedule (behind Texas Tech, Notre Dame and Penn State). Miami lost heavily on defence, so they may have to outscore opponents.
- **Trinidad Chambliss (QB, Ole Miss), +1329** - a D-II transfer who took over in week three of 2025, led the conference with nearly **4,000 passing yards, 24 touchdowns and three interceptions**, added **500-plus rushing yards and eight scores**, and reached the CFP semi-finals without Lane Kiffin. Now the **fifth hardest schedule** and a new, underwhelming receiving corps. Woolcock: "I love the player, I don't like the price", expecting a possible four-loss season.
- **Julian Sayin (QB, Ohio State), +1329** - fourth in 2025 Heisman voting as a first-year starter, praised for poise and accuracy rather than athleticism. He keeps Jeremiah Smith, Brandon Inniss and top recruit Chris Henry Jr., plus Bo Jackson at running back, but both hosts think the crowded offence dilutes his case. Bogman: he must look good at Indiana, at USC, versus Oregon and versus Michigan - "there's more outs on saying than there are reasons to be in".
- **Dante Moore (QB, Oregon), +1567** - the shortest price Woolcock has bet. "probably gonna be the second overall pick in the draft if he declared last year"; in 2025 he was sixth nationally in passing touchdowns and fourth in completion percentage, reaching a CFP semi-final. Loaded backfield, Corey Moore at receiver, "maybe the best tight end in the country", veteran line. Both call him **the best value on the board under 20-to-1**, with the Ohio State game the swing factor.

wikis.title: The two wide receivers on the board
wikis.summary: Jeremiah Smith at +1329 and Malachi Toney at 40-to-1.
wikis.body:

Back-to-back seasons over **1,200 yards and 12 touchdowns**, All-American honours, and "the six most Heisman Trophy votes" last year, on 87 catches for 1,243 yards, 12 receiving touchdowns and a rushing score.

He expects Smith to be the first non-quarterback drafted in 2027.
- Woolcock is out at this price - he had a 16-to-1 ticket the year before and would want 16 to 18-to-1 - and worries Chris Henry Jr.'s buzz could take shine away. His past position-player tickets: 65-to-1 Travis Hunter two years ago, 60-to-1 Jeremiah Love last year.
- **Malachi Toney (WR, Miami), 40-to-1** - 5-foot-11 with "elite acceleration" and "that twitch", he posted a nation-high **109 receptions, 1,200-plus yards and 13 total touchdowns** (10 receiving, one rushing, two passing) as a true freshman, winning **ACC Rookie of the Year and First Team All-ACC**.

wikis.body:
## The market

- Category: Geopolitics - Ukraine. Title: "Ukraine signs peace deal with Russia before 2027?"
- Price shown: "11% chance".
- Volume: $2,772,623 (a second volume figure further down the page reads $2,773,205). End Date: Jan 1, 2027; the chart label and the FAQ give Dec 31, 2026. Market Opened: Nov 5, 2025, 12:56 PM ET. Resolver: 0x65070BE91...
- Chart strip markers: "Past", Nov 1, Jan 1, 2027. An "Order Book" tab is shown.

## Rules

- Resolves "Yes" if Ukraine signs any written instrument "(e.g., treaty, ceasefire/armistice, framework/'roadmap,' exchange of letters, or mediated agreement text)" that "(i) includes both Ukraine and the Russian Federation as parties, and (ii) either ends hostilities/establishes a ceasefire or commits both sides to a defined process toward ending the war (i.e., stated objective of peace/normalization plus principles, steps, and/or a timetable) by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to 'No'."
- "Only Ukraine's signature is required; Russia's signature or ratification is not."
- Excluded: "Localized, temporary, or issue-specific arrangements - such as airstrike-limitation or deconfliction protocols, humanitarian pauses, evacuation corridors, prisoner-exchange or trade/export arrangements, border/DMZ adjustments, or ceasefires limited to a particular sector/front/municipality."
- "The document must bear a wet-ink or officially issued electronic signature of an authorized Ukrainian representative. Unsigned agreements (e.g., the 2023 Ohrid arrangement) will not qualify regardless of if they are otherwise officially enacted."
- "The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting."

## Market Context (page's own AI-generated note)

Labelled "Experimental AI-generated summary referencing Polymarket data. This is not trading advice and plays no role in how this market resolves. - Updated Sep 20, 2026, 3:15 PM UTC".

- "US-mediated diplomatic efforts resumed in early September 2026 with envoys visiting Moscow and Kyiv, leading both sides to signal openness to trilateral talks potentially in October."
- "Core obstacles persist, particularly Russia's demands for additional Ukrainian territory in Donbas and Ukraine's refusal to concede land without durable security guarantees."
- "Ongoing airstrikes, Russia's rejection of interim ceasefires, and stalled prior rounds in Abu Dhabi and Geneva underscore the entrenched positions."
- Winter military pressure and the need for multiple negotiation phases "align with trader consensus that a comprehensive peace agreement remains improbable before 2027."

## Related markets listed

- "Ukraine signs peace deal with Russia by October 31?" 2%
- "Russia x Ukraine ceasefire agreement by December 31, 2027?" 71%
- "Russia x Ukraine Peace Combo" 6%

Comments: 223. FAQ boilerplate: "$2.8 million in total trading volume since the market launched on Nov 5, 2025".
