wikis.title: Star Wars: Starfighter (upcoming film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia's article on Star Wars: Starfighter, Shawn Levy's Lucasfilm film starring Ryan Gosling - its development from 2022, the cast, the 2025 shoot in the UK and Sardinia, Thomas Newman's score and the 28 May 2027 release date.
wikis.body:
## Infobox

- **Star Wars: Starfighter**, "Upcoming film directed by Shawn Levy". Directed by **Shawn Levy**; written by **Jonathan Tropper**; based on characters by **George Lucas**.
- Produced by Shawn Levy and **Kathleen Kennedy**. Cinematography **Claudio Miranda**; edited by **Adam Gerstel**; music by **Thomas Newman**.
- Production companies **Lucasfilm** and **21 Laps Entertainment**; distributed by **Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures**.
- Release date **May 28, 2027**. Country United States; language English. Runtime, budget and gross are blank.
- Starring **Ryan Gosling, Flynn Gray, Matt Smith, Mia Goth, Aaron Pierre, Simon Bird, Jamael Westman, Daniel Ings and Amy Adams**.
- A hatnote distinguishes it from the unrelated 2001 video game of the same title.

## Lead

- "an upcoming American space opera film... intended to be an installment in the Star Wars franchise and set five years after the events of the film Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker (2019)".
- Levy entered talks to direct in **November 2022**; development was delayed by the **2023 Writers Guild of America strike** and was in early stages in October 2023. Tropper was hired in **July 2024**. The title and Gosling's casting were announced in **April 2025**, the full cast in **August** when filming began in the United Kingdom; filming also took place in **Sardinia**, Italy, and concluded in **December**.
- Scheduled for release in the United States on **May 28, 2027**.

## One point stated two ways

- The lead says the film is "set five years after the events of... The Rise of Skywalker (2019)", while the Development section reports Kathleen Kennedy saying "it would be set around five or six years after Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker (2019)".

## Cast

- **Ryan Gosling as Kade Auberon**; **Flynn Gray**, cast as the nephew of Gosling's character; **Matt Smith**; **Mia Goth**; **Aaron Pierre**; **Simon Bird**; **Jamael Westman**; **Daniel Ings**; **Amy Adams**, cast as the mother of Gray's character.

## Development

- Shawn Levy flew to London in the mid-2010s specifically to meet Lucasfilm president **Kathleen Kennedy** and express his love for *Star Wars* and his wish to make a film; discussions were put on hold while he worked on *Stranger Things* (2016-2025).
- Kennedy contacted him again in 2022; he entered talks that **November** and confirmed the deal a month later, acknowledging that many announced *Star Wars* films had not come to fruition but saying he was confident and eager to start writing after finishing *Deadpool & Wolverine* (2024).
- Development had only just begun when the **2023 Writers Guild of America strike** started in May 2023 and halted it. That **October**, after the strike, Levy said development had resumed; Kennedy's mandate was for him "to bring a similar story and tone from his other films to Star Wars".
- In November 2023 **Dave Filoni** was revealed as Lucasfilm's chief creative officer, to be directly involved in planning future films and series.
- **July 2024**: Jonathan Tropper, a previous Levy collaborator, hired to write.
- **December 2024**: journalist Jeff Sneider reported that Levy was "holding a window" for production to begin in September 2025, and that **Daisy Ridley** would reprise Rey in a mentorship role to a teenage boy or young man protagonist - a role she was also reported to have in separate *Star Wars* films in development from Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy and Simon Kinberg.
- **January 2025**: Ryan Gosling entered talks to star. Levy had planned another film next, but Gosling's interest moved this one forward, potentially filming in late 2025. Levy and 21 Laps would produce with Kennedy and Lucasfilm. Levy was considered a "must-have, must-keep director" for Disney after *Deadpool & Wolverine*.
- Kennedy said this would be the next *Star Wars* film after **The Mandalorian and Grogu (2026)**, set around five or six years after *The Rise of Skywalker*, separate from the Skywalker Saga, with mostly new characters though some sequel-trilogy characters could return. It was intended to be standalone and not launch sequels.

## Pre-production

- At **Star Wars Celebration Japan in April 2025** the film was titled *Star Wars: Starfighter*, given the **May 28, 2027** release date, Gosling confirmed, and filming confirmed for later that year.
- Casting was underway for a teenage actor to play the nephew of Gosling's character and for male and female antagonists pursuing them. **Mikey Madison** was in brief negotiations for the female antagonist but declined by mid-April over a salary dispute; **Mia Goth** took the role in June.
- **Matt Smith**, who had been cast in an undisclosed role for *The Rise of Skywalker* but did not appear, joined as another antagonist in August; Levy said it "feels like it's destiny fulfilled".
- At the start of filming at the end of August, Lucasfilm confirmed Smith and Goth and announced newcomer **Flynn Gray** with Aaron Pierre, Simon Bird, Jamael Westman, Daniel Ings and Amy Adams.
- Levy on the pressure: "nothing is as religious an allegiance as Star Wars"; the film is "not a sequel, it's not a prequel, it's not legacy characters. And it's not in a period of time in the galaxy that's ever been explored... we are inventing everything in the movie... design choices, character choices, planet choices, costume choices, droid choices, alien choices, all of it needs to feel Star Wars-y."
- Tropper called it "a simpler movie" than the Skywalker Saga films, free of the mythology, with "as few barriers of entry as possible for new fans and viewers".
- Levy named *Return of the Jedi* (1983) as the biggest influence - "the combination of theme, levity, adventure, heart, spectacle. Somehow that movie just got it right for me."
- Costume designer **Suttirat Anne Larlarb** returned from *Obi-Wan Kenobi* (2022).

## Filming

- Principal photography began **August 28, 2025** in the United Kingdom with **Claudio Miranda** as cinematographer.
- By mid-September filming was in **Sardinia**, Italy, with Levy releasing an image of shooting in the Mediterranean Sea.
- In early November Levy took a short break to promote the fifth season of *Stranger Things* (2025); filming was more than halfway complete.
- At the end of November Levy said part of the third act was reworked because "things didn't align", and that he was glad the original idea did not work out, feeling the new one was much better.
- Matt Smith filmed his scenes in December; Levy announced the wrap on **December 18**.
- Kennedy said relying on an inexperienced child actor was risky and "they got lucky with Gray", adding that the structure put him "one-on-one" with a different major actor every few weeks - "the best university" for a young actor.
- **Steven Spielberg and Tom Cruise both visited the set**, with Cruise "serving as a camera operator for a lightsaber duel set in a boggy marsh".

## Post-production and music

- **Adam Gerstel** edited, after the second season of *The Mandalorian* (2020); the article flags this line as needing an independent source.
- In **November 2025** Levy revealed **Thomas Newman** was composing. Levy wanted music that was "big-hearted", "classically inspired" and built on multiple themes like John Williams's *Star Wars* scores, but not a "remix" of Williams's music. Newman, composer of some of Levy's favourite scores, joined after reading the script and hearing Levy's vision.

## Marketing and release

- Footage was shown at **CineEurope in June 2026**; Levy and Gosling promoted the film at Disney's **D23** convention in August, where more footage was shown.
- Scheduled for release in the United States on **May 28, 2027**; the film "is expected to be released in IMAX", a line tagged as needing an update.

wikis.title: A Quiet Place Part III
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the upcoming John Krasinski horror film A Quiet Place Part III, covering its cast, production timeline and July 30, 2027 US release date.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- "**A Quiet Place Part III** is an upcoming American post-apocalyptic horror film written and directed by **John Krasinski**."
- "The **fourth installment** in the A Quiet Place film series, the film is the sequel to *A Quiet Place Part II* (2020), serving as the **third and final film in a trilogy** that began with *A Quiet Place* (2018)."
- Emily Blunt, Cillian Murphy, Millicent Simmonds and Noah Jupe reprise their roles from *Part II*; Jack O'Connell, Katy O'Brian and Jason Clarke join the cast.
- Infobox: based on characters by **Bryan Woods and Scott Beck**; produced by John Krasinski, **Michael Bay**, **Andrew Form**, **Brad Fuller**; cinematography **Arnau Valls Colomer**; production companies **Platinum Dunes** and **Sunday Night Productions**; distributed by **Paramount Pictures**; country United States; language English. No runtime, budget or gross given.

## Cast

- **Emily Blunt** as Evelyn Abbott, "a recently widowed mother who leads her family to search for other people".
- **Cillian Murphy** as Emmett, "a close family friend of the Abbotts who is a hardened, reclusive survivor".
- **Millicent Simmonds** as Regan Abbott, Evelyn's deaf daughter.
- **Noah Jupe** as Marcus Abbott, Evelyn's son.
- **Jack O'Connell** as a National Guardsman.
- **Katy O'Brian**; **Jason Clarke** (roles not given).
- **Alex Wolff** as Reuben, "a hospice nurse who died in New York City when the Death Angels invaded".

## Production

- May 2021: Emily Blunt revealed Krasinski had plans for a third film, saying the Quiet Place films are intended to be a trilogy; he had wanted to see how *Part II* was received first.
- July 2021: Blunt confirmed Krasinski was working on a third installment, separate from the spin-off *A Quiet Place: Day One* (2024), intending to direct again.
- August 2025: Krasinski confirmed to be directing, writing and co-producing.
- March 2026: the cast was revealed.
- May 2026: revealed that Alex Wolff would reprise his role from *A Quiet Place: Day One*.
- "Principal photography began on **May 10, 2026**", with Arnau Valls Colomer as cinematographer.
- "By **June 9**, Murphy, Simmonds, O'Connell, and Clarke were filming their scenes but Blunt had yet to start due to back-to-back press tours for *The Devil Wears Prada 2* and *Disclosure Day*."

## Release

- "A Quiet Place Part III is scheduled to be released in the United States by Paramount Pictures on **July 30, 2027**."
- "It was previously scheduled to release on **July 9, 2027**." A cited Deadline piece of October 2, 2025 is titled "'A Quiet Place Part III' Moves To Later In July 2027 - Update"; an earlier Deadline piece of August 1, 2025 announced a "Summer 2027 Release".
- The film-series navbox lists the film as "Part III (2027)".

wikis.title: The Bluey Movie
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on The Bluey Movie, the upcoming Joe Brumm animated feature based on the series Bluey, covering its premise, cast, production, 3D animation switch and 6 August 2027 release.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- "The Bluey Movie is an upcoming animated comedy film based on the Australian children's television series Bluey. It is written and directed by series creator Joe Brumm, and is produced by Ludo Studio and BBC Studios."
- "In the film, a busy day for the Heeler family is upended by a big surprise."
- Scheduled "to be released in theaters by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures on 6 August 2027" - the Release section says "theatrically worldwide on 6 August 2027".
- Countries: Australia, United Kingdom. Language: English. Runtime, budget and gross are not stated (the infobox carries "MUST HAVE RELIABLE SOURCE" placeholders).

## Credits from the infobox

- Directed by and written by Joe Brumm; based on *Bluey* by Joe Brumm.
- Produced by Amber Naismith. Music by Joff Bush.
- Starring Melanie Zanetti and David McCormack.
- Production companies: Ludo Studio (a note says it is "Credited as 'Judo Studio'"; the BBC Studios site's footer and the teaser trailer carry copyright information for "Judo Pty Ltd") and BBC Studios.
- Distributed by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures, "under the Walt Disney Pictures banner".

## Premise (as quoted from The Walt Disney Company)

"The CG-animated film based on the beloved series about Bluey, a lovable, inexhaustible, blue heeler dog who lives with her Mum, Dad, and little sister, Bingo, takes place on an action-packed day when a big surprise changes everything for Bluey and her family."

## Voice cast

- Melanie Zanetti as Chilli Heeler; David McCormack as Bandit Heeler.
- "As with the television series, the child actors are kept anonymous to protect their privacy."

## Production

- Brumm "enjoyed the experience of working on the long-form series 3 episode 'The Sign' and told the press he thought that making a feature film would be the natural next step". Ahead of that episode's release in April 2024, executive producer Daley Pearson expressed interest in a film adaptation.
- "In December 2024, BBC Studios and The Walt Disney Company announced that a Bluey film, provisionally titled Bluey: The Movie, was in development." Brumm was set to write and direct; "Richard Jeffery will serve as co-director after directing the television episodes 'Sleepytime' and 'The Sign'" (the infobox lists Brumm alone as director).
- The regular series voice cast and crew, including the anonymous child actors, will return; Joff Bush returns as composer; Amber Naismith produces; Cosmic Dino Studio provides the animation.
- "In March 2026, the film had been given the title The Bluey Movie, which was confirmed with the reveal of the teaser trailer at the D23 Expo in August 2026."
- Australian studio Cosmic Dino Studio provides the 3D computer animation, "in contrast to the television series' 2D animation". Brumm at the D23 Expo panel: "We're always striving to get a beauty of nature in the show, and I wanted to have every tool available to capture a beautiful blade of grass and light rays and all that, and I wanted kids to be able to feel like they could reach in and give these little dogs a scratch on their furry heads."
- "The Bluey Movie is a joint collaboration between Disney, BBC Studios and Ludo Studio. Disney will handle global theatrical and streaming rights, the latter outside of Australia. BBC Studios will be responsible for financing and licensing rights, and Ludo Studio will produce the film."
- "Financial support for the film is provided by the federal government of Australia and the state government of Queensland by tax incentives."

## Marketing

"A teaser trailer debuted at the D23 Expo on 14 August 2026. Fans shared mixed opinions on social media regarding the designs of the traditionally 2D characters that were converted to 3D."

## Home media

"After its theatrical release, the film will stream on ABC iView and ABC Kids in Australia, and Disney+ in United States."

## Sources cited (selection)

Deadline, 17 December 2024, "'Bluey' To Bark On Big Screen: 2027 Movie In Works At Disney & BBC Studios"; Deadline, 4 September 2025, "'Bluey' Movie Gets August 2027 Release Date"; Deadline, 14 August 2026, "'The Bluey Movie' Trailer: Beloved Kids Show Character Dogpaddles To Big Screen For First Time - D23"; Variety, 15 August 2026, "The Bluey Movie First Look: Bluey and Her Family Hit the Big Screen With New 3D Animation Style".

wikis.title: 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, giving the announcement and ceremony dates, the prize amount, who may nominate, and the publicly reported nominees and their nominators.
wikis.body:
## The award

- "The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize is an international peace prize established according to Alfred Nobel's will that will be announced on 9 October 2026 by the Norwegian Nobel Committee in Oslo, Norway, and awarded on 10 December 2026."
- Infobox: Date - 9 October 2026 (announcement), 10 December 2026 (ceremony). Location - Oslo, Norway. Presented by the Norwegian Nobel Committee. Reward - 9.0 million SEK. First award - 1901. Previous: 2025; next: 2027.
- Criterion quoted: "to the person (or group) who shall have done the most or the best work for fraternity between nations, for the abolition or reduction of standing armies and for the holding and promotion of peace congresses."

## Candidates

- "Though nominations are strictly kept a secret, several Norwegian parliamentarians and other academics are privileged to publicly announce their preferred candidates simply to raise publicity both for the nominee and the nominator."
- "208 candidates and 79 organisations have been nominated." (A cited Reuters item is headed "Some 287 nominated for 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, Trump likely among them".)

## Qualified nominators

Per the statutes of the Nobel Foundation, a nomination is valid from: members of national assemblies and national governments and current heads of state; members of the International Court of Justice and Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague; members of the Institut de Droit International; members of the international board of the Women's International League for Peace and Freedom; university professors, professors emeriti and associate professors of history, social sciences, law, philosophy, theology and religion, plus university rectors and directors; directors of peace research institutes and foreign policy institutes; past Nobel Peace Prize laureates; members of the main board of laureate organizations; current and former members of the Norwegian Nobel Committee (current members' proposals due "no later than at the first meeting of the Committee after 1 February"); and former advisers to the Committee.

## Nominations confirmed by news agencies - individuals

- **Mykola Kuleba** (1972-), Ukraine - "for rescuing Ukrainian children"; nominated by the Peace Research Institute Oslo (jointly with Save the Children).
- **Hussam Abu Safiya** (1973-), Palestine and **Sara Al-Saqqa** (1992-), Palestine - with Albanese, "as an expression of respect for the courage, efforts, and perseverance of individuals who defend fundamental human values in the most difficult circumstances, representing a contribution to peace that transcends political divisions"; nominated by Matjaz Nemec et al.
- **Francesca Albanese** (1977-), Italy - "for through her work, she has upheld the principles of international law and nonviolent accountability while amplifying the rights and voices of those most impacted by war, genocide, and injustice" (International Civil Society Action Network, founded 2006, and Women's Alliance for Security Leadership, founded 2015); and "for her work for peace by reporting on the atrocities in Gaza, promoting concrete measures to end the war and pointing out the duty of Western leaders to stop their complicity in Israel's violations of international law" (Marie Sneve Martinussen, 1985-); also in the joint Nemec nomination.
- **John Coale** (1946-), United States - with Trump, "for the successful mediation resulting in the release of over 300 political prisoners in Belarus and the restoration of diplomatic dialogue to stabilize security on the European Union's eastern borders"; nominators listed as Ignas Vegele (1975-), Rimas Jonas Jankunas (1967-) and Petras Grazulis (1958-).
- **Alokiir Malual**, South Sudan - "who has worked for many years to advance peace, dialogue and women's participation in the peace process in South Sudan"; nominated by Wolfgang Wagner (1989-), John Hogan (1986-), Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam.
- **Maia Sandu** (1972-), Moldova - "for her nonviolent struggle for democracy, the rule of law and peace"; nominated by Arild Hermstad (1966-).
- **Greta Thunberg** (2003-), Sweden - "for her principled and non-violent efforts for peace, justice and international solidarity, especially in her efforts for Gaza, climate, and indigenous peoples"; nominated by Froya Sjursaether (2006-).
- **Donald Trump** (1946-), United States - "for his role in brokering a historic ceasefire between Israel and Hamas, a diplomatic breakthrough achieved through direct engagement with Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey" (Anna Paulina Luna, 1989-); "in recognition of his historic Abraham Accords and his record of advancing decisive diplomacy and delivering peace through strength" (Claudia Tenney, 1961-); and the Belarus mediation nomination with Coale.
- **Volodymyr Zelenskyy** (1978-), Ukraine - "[with the people of Ukraine] for their efforts to preserve the peace of European democracies against Russian aggression"; nominated by Dag Oistein Endsjo (1968-).
- **Yulia Navalnaya** (1977-), Russia - "for her work as a Russian opposition leader following the death of her husband, Alexei Navalny"; nominator listed as TBD.
- **Pope Leo XIV** (1955-), Vatican City / Peru / United States - "for his focus on humility, service, and climate action"; nominated by Christopher Hale (1989-).
- **Dr. Hak Ja Han**, South Korea - "her lifelong dedication to international peacebuilding, interfaith dialogue, humanitarian cooperation, and reconciliation on the Korean Peninsula"; nominated by Dr. Jan Figel (1960-).
- **Nikolai Kurbatov** (1990-), Russia - nominated by Konstantin Klimenko-Bogdanov (1962-).
- **Arthur Denouveaux** (1986-), France - nominated by Eric Bothorel (1966-).

## Nominations - organizations

- **Save the Children** (founded 1919, London) - "with Mykola Kuleba for rescuing Ukrainian children"; Peace Research Institute Oslo.
- **International Association of Judges** (founded 1953, Salzburg) and **International Criminal Court & International Court of Justice** (founded 1945, The Hague) - "for their important function in defending democratic principles and controlling the exercise of authority"; Even Eriksen (1995-).
- **Sudan's Emergency Response Rooms** - "creating a, volunteer-led, grassroots network that provides lifesaving aid - food, medical care, and evacuation - amidst the 2023-2026 Sudanese civil war"; Peace Research Institute Oslo.
- **Minneapolis** (founded 1856), United States - "for the moral leadership of the people and city of Minneapolis [setting] an example for those struggling against fascism everywhere on the face of a troubled planet" (The Nation, founded 1865); and "as tribute to the Minneapolis residents' fight against the immigration police ICE, responding with non-violence and solidarity" (Julie Estdahl Stuestol, 1983-).
- **People of Ukraine** - with Zelenskyy; Dag Oistein Endsjo.
- **The Citizen Collective of the 'Light Revolution'**, South Korea - "through disciplined, large-scale, and nonviolent civic resistance, the movement played a decisive role in defending constitutional democracy against martial law, protecting fundamental human rights, and preventing the escalation of political crisis into widespread violence"; nominated by Euiyoung Kim, Anselmo Lee, Pablo Onate, David Farrell and Azul Aguiar.
- **Concordis International**, Central African Republic - "of peacebuilding work in fragile conflict zones"; Quakers Britain and USA.
- **UNRWA** (founded 1949, Amman) - "for through its continuous and life-sustaining work, UNRWA has made a significant and lasting contribution to peace, human security and stability"; Une Bastholm (1989-).
- **World Trade Organisation** (founded 1995, Geneva) - "its role as a cornerstone of the rules-based multilateral trading system, which aids in preventing trade wars and economic coercion, thereby fostering international stability"; Peace Research Institute Oslo.
- **Yad Vashem** (founded 1953, Jerusalem) - "one of the worlds most significant institutions in the fight against antisemitism, hate ideologies, and historical distortion"; Joel Ystebo (2001-).

## Note

On the Nemec nomination: "Led by Nemec, the nomination was signed by nearly 300 eligible proposers from 33 countries, including Brazil, South Africa, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom."

The article also carries the standard list of past laureates, ending with 2025: Maria Corina Machado.

wikis.title: Path of the Total Solar Eclipse of 2037 Jul 13
wikis.summary: NASA/GSFC path table by Fred Espenak giving the coordinates, width and duration of the umbral shadow track of the total solar eclipse of 2037 July 13.
wikis.body:
## What the page is

- Tabulates the path of the Moon's **umbral** shadow during the **Total Solar Eclipse of 2037 Jul 13**, credited to **Fred Espenak** (NASA's GSFC).
- Coordinates (WGS 84) of the northern limit, southern limit and central line at **120-second intervals**; central-line circumstances give the Moon/Sun diameter ratio, Sun altitude and azimuth (degrees), path width (km) and duration (minutes and seconds).

## Path

- **Limits at path start**: central line 39 42.5S 089 17.6E, diameter ratio 1.029, Sun altitude 0, path width 124 km, central duration 01m49.6s.
- **Limits at path end**: central line 45 17.9S 170 24.3W, ratio 1.030, Sun altitude 0, width 128 km, duration 01m53.2s.

## Greatest eclipse and greatest duration

- **Greatest Eclipse (GE)**: Time = 02:39:13.3 UT, Lat = 24°46.1'S, Long = 139°04.5'E; Sun altitude 43.4°, Sun azimuth 3.3°, path width 200.7 km, central duration 03m58.4s.
- **Greatest Duration (GD)**: Time = 02:39:41 UT, Lat = 24°47'S, Long = 139°14'E; Sun altitude 43.4°, Sun azimuth 2.9°, path width 200.6 km, central duration 03m58.4s.

## Predictions

- Generated using the **VSOP87/ELP2000-85** solar and lunar ephemerides and **ΔT = 81.9 seconds**.
- Predictions "DO NOT include the effects of mountains and valleys along the edge of the Moon"; lunar limb profile corrections "may shift the limits of the eclipse path north or south by ~1-3 kilometers, and change the eclipse duration by ~1-3 seconds".
- Linked resources: orthographic map, Google map, animated map, path table, Besselian elements table and a Saros table.
- Acknowledgment requested: "Eclipse Predictions by Fred Espenak, NASA's GSFC".

wikis.title: Rasuwa flood, Nepal: a glacier collapse that became a debris flow
wikis.summary: YouTube page for an Overengineered documentary arguing the Rasuwa flood in Nepal was a debris flow that grew as it travelled down-valley from a small glacier collapse.
wikis.body:
## The video

- Title: "Nepal Flood Explained: How a Glacier Became a Wall of Water"
- Channel: Overengineered
- Published: 2026-09-02T16:56:12Z

## What the description says

- "The Rasuwa flood was described by survivors as a wall of water. It was not water."
- "What reached those villages in the Rasuwa district of Nepal was more than half solid material by volume, closer to wet concrete than to a river, carrying boulders large enough to destroy buildings on impact."
- "That is why the Nepal flood left total destruction where an ordinary flood would have left standing walls."
- "And the Nepal glacier collapse that caused it did not happen anywhere near those villages. It happened thousands of metres above them, kilometres up the valley."
- "The mass that came off that mountain was not large enough to do this. On satellite imagery the source zone is a small scar high on a rock face in terrain where nobody lives. Follow the valley down and you reach devastation tens of kilometres away."
- "Those two things do not connect until you understand what happened in between. The flow grew the entire way down."
- Closing line: "Our thoughts are with everyone still searching for family in Rasuwa and downstream."
- Hashtags: #RasuwaFlood #NepalFlood #GlacierCollapse #Nepal #Himalaya #DebrisFlow #Geology #Documentary. No date for the flood itself is given.

wikis.title: The 400 km Wall Japan Built to Stop the Sea
wikis.summary: Overengineered video page on the chain of concrete seawalls built along Japan's northeastern coast after the 2011 tsunami, and the argument over them.
wikis.body:
## What the source says
- "After the 2011 tsunami, Japan made a decision that split the country in half."
- "Along roughly 400 kilometres of its northeastern coastline, it began building a chain of concrete seawalls. Some stand over twelve metres tall."
- "In parts of Iwate and Miyagi, entire fishing towns now sit behind a barrier so high that residents can no longer see the ocean their families have lived beside for generations."
- "It cost billions. It took more than a decade to build." No specific cost figure is given.
- "And nobody actually knows if it will work."
- The video "breaks down what Japan built, why the engineering had to be completely rethought after 2011, and why the people it was built to protect are still arguing about whether it should exist at all."

## The argument as the page frames it
- "The argument is not really about concrete. It is about what a country owes people living on a dangerous coast, and whether the right answer is a wall, a relocation, or an evacuation plan. Japan chose all three in different places, and the outcome looks very different town to town."
- "Some residents say the walls kept their communities alive. Others say they were handed a structure they never asked for that destroyed the reason they lived there in the first place. Both are describing the same coastline."

## Chapters listed
- 00:00 The Wall that Hides the Ocean
- 05:25 Anatomy of a Magnitude 9.0 Earthquake

- Channel: Free Documentary - Engineering

## What the description says
- The largest nuclear fusion reactor in the world is being built in the south of France: **Iter**. "The objective: being able to supply unlimited, clean energy to mankind."
- "Perhaps the most important component is a gigantic magnet, strong enough to lift an entire container ship."
- The part magnet is **nine metres wide and three hundred tons**, and reaches France by cargo ship "from all corners of the world".
- The final and trickiest stage runs from the seaport of "Sur les Fos" near Marseille to the Iter construction site in Provence.
- That stage is **130 kilometres**: the team has to cross a lake, pass through **sixteen villages** and "blast their way through a mass of rock", with a constant police convoy securing the passage.
- On arrival, scientists test all parts: "Even the smallest scratch can make the highly sensitive custom-made product unusable and thus set the entire project back by years."

wikis.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin chips begin shipping to cloud providers
wikis.summary: GCN report that NVIDIA's Vera Rubin AI platform has reached full production and is shipping to cloud and system partners, with the platform's chip line-up, NVL72 rack specifications and market context.
wikis.body:
## The news

- By Hugo Rojas, "August 4, 2026 - 8:00 AM", filed under Technology, "4 min read".
- "NVIDIA's next-generation Vera Rubin AI chip platform has moved from production lines into active shipments."
- "On July 21, NVIDIA confirmed the platform had reached full production, with Ian Buck, the company's vice president of accelerated computing, telling reporters at NVIDIA headquarters that systems are now shipping to customers including OpenAI, CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Meta, and Dell."
- "NVIDIA had announced at GTC Taipei on May 31 that the Vera Rubin platform was ramping into full production, with Taiwan's top server makers and global supply chain leaders manufacturing Vera Rubin-based systems at scale."

## What the platform is

- "The Rubin platform comprises six chips in total, the NVLink 6 Switch, ConnectX-9 SuperNIC, BlueField-4 DPU, and Spectrum-6 Ethernet Switch, in addition to the Vera CPU and Rubin GPU."
- "On March 16, 2026, at GTC in San Jose, NVIDIA announced the platform had expanded to seven chips in full production, with the newly integrated NVIDIA Groq 3 LPU joining the existing six to scale the world's largest AI factories."
- "With extreme co-design, NVIDIA takes rack-scale integration to the next level, making the rack system a unit of compute, a single distributed accelerator."
- "Vera is the successor to NVIDIA's Grace CPU, while Rubin succeeds Blackwell, with NVIDIA claiming Rubin will be capable of achieving 5x and 3.5x of inference and training performance, respectively, compared to Blackwell."
- "The Rubin platform harnesses extreme co-design across hardware and software to deliver up to a 10x reduction in inference token cost compared with the NVIDIA Blackwell platform."

## Partners and deployment

- "NVIDIA Rubin is in full production, with Rubin-based products available from partners in the second half of 2026."
- "Among the first cloud providers to deploy Vera Rubin-based instances will be AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft and OCI, as well as NVIDIA Cloud Partners CoreWeave, Lambda, Nebius and Nscale."
- "Microsoft will deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale systems as part of next-generation AI data centers, including future Fairwater AI superfactory sites."
- "Dell Technologies, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro, together with ASUS, Foxconn, GIGABYTE, Pegatron, Quanta Cloud Technology, Wistron and Wiwynn, are adopting NVIDIA DSX to accelerate AI factory ramp with Vera Rubin."
- "According to the official NVIDIA newsroom announcement from May 31, production shipments of Vera Rubin are set to begin starting this fall."
- "CoreWeave, one of the first cloud providers to receive the hardware, told Bloomberg that its NVL72 racks are delivering ten times the token output of the previous generation."

## Rack-scale specifications

- "Vera Rubin is NVIDIA's most extensive POD-scale platform, five purpose-built racks operating as one massive AI supercomputer for agentic workloads."
- "The flagship NVL72 rack integrates 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs connected by NVLink 6, along with ConnectX-9 SuperNICs and BlueField-4 DPUs, delivering up to 10x higher inference throughput per watt at one-tenth the cost per token versus Blackwell."
- "Each Rubin GPU carries 288 GB of HBM4 memory with up to 22 TB/s of bandwidth, compared with the Blackwell Ultra B300's 8 TB/s memory bandwidth."
- "The Vera Rubin NVL72 rack will also be 100 percent liquid cooled and feature cable-free modular tray designs, which NVIDIA claims will allow installation times to be reduced from two hours to five minutes, in comparison to its Blackwell equivalent."

## Market context

- "NVIDIA executed an aggressive 18-month development cycle from Blackwell's launch to Rubin production, compressing what typically spans 24 to 30 months in semiconductor development."
- "The Semiconductor Industry Association reported global semiconductor sales of $120.6 billion during the month of May 2026, an increase of 9.2% compared to the April 2026 total of $110.5 billion and 104.1% more than the May 2025 total of $59.1 billion."
- "The same wave of AI inference demand that is filling Rubin-equipped racks has pushed enterprise AI inference providers, such as Fireworks AI, to raise $1.505 billion at a $17.5 billion valuation".

## Internal inconsistencies to note

- Chip count: the article says the platform "comprises six chips in total" and also that on March 16, 2026 NVIDIA "announced the platform had expanded to seven chips in full production" with the Groq 3 LPU, then describes "extreme co-design across six types of chips".
- Shipping timing: it states shipments were confirmed on July 21 and that "systems are now shipping", while also citing the May 31 NVIDIA newsroom announcement that "production shipments of Vera Rubin are set to begin starting this fall".

wikis.title: Meta Connect 2026 set for September 23-24 with a smart glasses tease
wikis.summary: Road to VR report that Meta's annual Connect event returns on September 23-24 at Menlo Park, alongside Mark Zuckerberg's teaser photo of what looks like new smart glasses.
wikis.body:
## The news

- By Ben Lang, May 12, 2026 (25 comments).
- "Meta's annual Connect event is set to return on September 23-24."
- "The company teased what appears to be a new pair of smart glasses, and said its event will focus on 'the latest in VR, wearables, metaverse, and AI.'"
- "As with previous years, the event will be held at the Menlo Park campus, with significant keynotes and announcements being streamed online."
- "Alongside the Connect date announcement, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg shared a photo on social media teasing what's likely to be a new pair of the company's smart glasses which now span audio-only and a pair with a monocular display. In the photo the glasses were scratched out with blue markings to hide any identifying features." Images are credited "Image courtesy Mark Zuckerberg".

## The author's commentary ("My Take")

- "The last 12 months have been anything but smooth sailing for those who are part of the XR industry. Canceled projects, layoffs, and closures at many of Meta's internal XR studios have shown the company's shifting of priorities away from XR and more toward its smart glasses business."
- "Meta insists it's still committed to building and investing in XR, positioning its moves as necessary steps to course-correct on initiatives that didn't pan out as expected."
- "One major thing driving uncertainty in XR right now is that Meta has announced several new pairs of smart glasses, but has not been clear about plans for upcoming Quest devices (the last of which, Quest 3S, was launched more than a year-and-a-half ago)."
- "Reporting suggests Meta's headset plans have been shifting internally; rumors have been swirling about a high-end puck-focused headset that would be a Vision Pro competitor, or a more affordable next-gen Quest."
- "Meta announcing a new headset at Connect is probably the strongest signal the company could send to show both confidence and direction in its ecosystem. If a new headset isn't announced, it will surely have the opposite effect."

## Related headlines on the page

- "Meta Reportedly Unveiling Next-gen MR Headset at Connect, Hologram-like Call Experience" - Scott Hayden, September 16, 2026.
- Also listed: "Steam Frame Review - Power-user's Playground" (Sept 16, 2026); "Unseen Reality XR Glasses Secures $1.2M in Successful Kickstarter" (Sept 18, 2026); "Valve Announces Steam Frame Price, Release Date, and Accessories" (Sept 14, 2026).

wikis.title: Amazon says it has enough satellites to start Leo service later this year
wikis.summary: CNBC report that Amazon's Leo satellite internet constellation passed 390 satellites after an Atlas V launch, enough to begin initial commercial service later in 2026.
wikis.body:
## The news

- By Annie Palmer, "Published Thu, Jul 2 2026 2:28 PM EDT".
- "Amazon said it now has enough satellites in orbit to begin 'initial service' of its Leo internet-from-space network later this year."
- "The company shipped 29 satellites into orbit around 12:30 a.m. ET on Thursday atop a United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket."
- "The mission brings Amazon's total constellation to more than 390 satellites, which is 'enough to support continuous service across initial latitudes,'" wrote Chris Weber, vice president of business and product for Amazon Leo, on X.
- "In November, Amazon began offering an 'enterprise preview' of Leo for select businesses, but it has yet to launch its service for consumers and government customers."
- "Amazon's initial commercial service will likely be limited to users in certain geographies. Future missions will 'add coverage and capacity,' Weber said."

## Competition with Starlink

- Key points: Leo "will compete with SpaceX's Starlink, which was created four years before Amazon's announced its entry into the market, and has more than 10,000 satellites in its constellation."
- Body: "SpaceX had a four-year head start on Amazon, launching Starlink in 2015. It has since amassed a constellation of around 10,000 satellites and more than 10 million subscribers."
- "Amazon announced the creation of Kuiper in 2019, and later changed the name to Leo."

## Constellation plans and delays

- "Amazon aims to build a constellation of roughly 7,700 satellites, but the effort has been slowed by a shortage of rocket capacity."
- "In its January request for an extension on regulatory deployment deadlines, the company cited delays beyond its control, including a 'shortage in the near-term availability' of rockets."
- "Amazon in 2022 signed a historic deal to reserve rocket launches with ULA, Arianespace and Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin, before purchasing rides with SpaceX. Many of those providers have experienced delays with their launch vehicles."
- "Another setback came in May, when one of Blue Origin's New Glenn rockets exploded on the launchpad during a hot-fire test, just days before it was slated to carry a batch of Amazon satellites. The company is currently rebuilding the pad, and working to determine what caused the anomaly."
- "Bezos and Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp have said the company is determined to return New Glenn to flight later this year. New Glenn is a giant, partially reusable rocket that seeks to compete with SpaceX's Starship rocket and can carry heavier payloads of up to 45 metric tons to low Earth orbit." A video is captioned "Jeff Bezos on Blue Origin: We will be flying again before the end of this year".

## Next launches

- "Amazon said Thursday its next Leo mission will use ULA's Vulcan heavy-lift rocket, 'which will carry even larger Leo payloads and help increase our deployment rate.'"
- Melissa Wuerl, Leo's director of launch systems: "With hundreds of flight-ready satellites standing by at the Cape and a new, dedicated vertical integration facility ready to support Leo Vulcan 1 and subsequent missions, we have a clear path to increase launch and deployment cadence, helping us quickly expand network coverage following an initial service rollout later this year."

## Notes

- A photo caption refers to an "Atlas V rocket... carrying Amazon's Project Kuiper internet network satellites... at the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Cape Canaveral, Florida, U.S., April 28, 2025."
- Starlink's constellation size is "more than 10,000 satellites" in the key points and "around 10,000 satellites" in the body.

wikis.title: Ford Fathom electric pickup, production in Q1 2027
wikis.summary: Electrek report that Ford's midsize electric pickup, the Fathom, goes on sale in early 2027 from $28,350, built on the Universal EV platform at the Louisville Assembly Plant.
wikis.body:
## The vehicle and dates

- By Peter Johnson, "Aug 13 2026 - 6:00 am PT".
- "The Ford Fathom will go on sale in early 2027, starting at $28,350."
- "Ford said the electric pickup is on track to go into production at its Louisville Assembly plant in Q1 2027."
- "Ford revealed the name and starting price of the upcoming midsize electric pickup last week, the first vehicle based on its Universal EV (UEV) platform."
- "The first prototypes will roll off the assembly lines at Ford's 3-million-square-foot Louisville Assembly Plant (LAP) in the first quarter of 2027."
- "The new UEV Production System and assembly tree will go online in the first quarter of 2027, starting with the Ford Fathom."

## The plant and the investment

- "Ford announced plans a year ago to transform it from a gas-powered vehicle plant into a facility for building fully electric vehicles, starting with the Fathom."
- "The $5 billion investment will create 4,000 new jobs at both the Louisville Assembly Plant and BlueOval Battery Park Michigan, and it will help fund the new equipment needed for the UEV platform."

## The UEV Production System

- "Instead of a fully assembled vehicle rolling down the line, the UEV Production System breaks the vehicle into three sections: the front clip, rear clip, and battery deck."
- "Ford will use large unicastings to build the front and rear body sections. The single large aluminum casting piece replaces dozens of stamped and other welded components it currently uses."
- "The method cuts the number of parts from 146 to build the current Maverick to just two for the Fathom."
- "In the third line, the interior components (seats, consoles, and carpeting) are installed on top of the battery housing, which serves as the vehicle's floor. The battery itself is then attached from the bottom."
- "Ford said the UEV Production System will enable it to assemble the Fathom 40% faster than current vehicles at the plant."
- Bryce Currie, Ford's chief manufacturing officer, said it is more ergonomic and will "require less twisting, turning, and bending": "We've engineered an 84% reduction in reaching over the fender... The wiring harness is also more than 4,000 feet shorter and 22 pounds lighter than in our first-gen electric SUV, making it much easier to install."
- "LAP will have the highest level of automation in final assembly across all Ford plants globally."
- "Ford installed a software module flash station, a first at one of its assembly plants... Before, if an issue were detected, updates would take about 10 minutes per vehicle. Now, it can be done as the vehicle rolls down the assembly line. With 5G in the facility, operators can diagnose and perform quality checks instantly."

## Features

- "Ford said the Fathom will have more interior passenger space than a Toyota RAV4."
- "It will also be equipped with a large, high-resolution touchscreen, bidirectional charging enabling vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities, a digital key, and Apple CarPlay and Android Auto as standard."
- "The Ford Fathom will also be the first vehicle to have Apple Maps integrated directly into the navigation system, with turn-by-turn directions, EV routing, and more."

## Images

- Photos are captioned "Covered Ford Fathom vehicle (Source: Ford)" and "Covered Ford Fathom UEV Production System at the Louisville Assembly Plant (Source: Ford)"; the truck itself is shown covered.

wikis.title: Waymo's Ojai robotaxi, a Zeekr-built minivan, opens to select riders
wikis.summary: TechCrunch report that Waymo has begun giving select riders in Los Angeles, Phoenix and San Francisco access to the Ojai, a Zeekr-made electric minivan carrying Waymo's sixth-generation driving system.
wikis.body:
## The launch

- By Kirsten Korosec, 9:52 AM PDT, May 28, 2026.
- "Waymo has started giving select riders in Los Angeles, Phoenix, and San Francisco access to its newest robotaxi: an all-electric, minivan-like vehicle that is designed to lower costs and handle the use and abuse of hundreds of thousands of riders."
- "Waymo said Thursday it will eventually expand access to the vehicle, a modified Zeekr-made minivan called the Ojai (pronounced oh-hi), to more riders and cities."
- "For now, the Alphabet-owned company is offering a limited number of customers free rides in the Ojai to gather feedback and further refine the robotaxi experience."
- The vehicle is described as blue-hued.

## Context given

- The launch "comes after years of development and testing - all in the pursuit of creating a vehicle that is accessible, comfortable, easy-to-maintain, and that importantly costs less to build and operate."
- It "comes amid a challenging time for Waymo, which recently suspended robotaxi service on freeways in Los Angeles, Miami, Phoenix, and San Francisco to improve how its vehicles behave in construction zones."
- "Waymo also paused services in Atlanta, Georgia and San Antonio, Texas to address problems with flooding in those cities."

## The vehicle

- "While the vehicle is loaded with Waymo's hardware and software, its foundation comes from Zeekr, the brand owned by China's Geely Holding Group."
- "The companies partnered in 2021 and showed off a concept of the purpose-built robotaxi in late 2022. Waymo has spent nearly two years testing the prototype, and later a production-intent version of the vehicle on public roads."
- "The minivan, which was designed in Sweden and manufactured in China, is based on the SEA-M architecture, a refined version of Zeekr's original Sustainable Experience Architecture (SEA) meant for 'future mobility products' like robotaxis and logistics vehicles."
- Sixth-generation system: "13 cameras, four lidar sensors, six radar units, and an array of external audio receivers."
- That system "is the keystone to Waymo's commercial strategy because it's designed to be modular", applicable to multiple vehicles, "including two that have already been announced, the Zeekr minivan and the Hyundai Ioniq 5."
- Rider features: flat floor, low step-in height, gondola-like doors on both sides, charging ports, cup holders, increased leg and head room, grab bars, braille above various buttons, and "three large adaptive screens, where customers can access the route, change music, control climate, and provide rider tips."
- Also an easier-to-clean interior, faster charging, a modular design and increased battery capacity, "all details that can help reduce costs and make maintenance and repairs more efficient."

## Scale figures

- "More than 500,000 paid robotaxi rides every week."
- Waymo's fleet "today is about 3,700 Jaguar I-Pace vehicles."
- "The stripped-down Zeekr vehicles - which don't contain any Chinese connected car tech - are sent to Waymo's Arizona factory, where they are outfitted with all of its robotaxi bells and whistles."
- "The company said it is now scaling toward a capacity of tens of thousands of units annually starting with the Ojai, and followed by the Hyundai Ioniq 5."

## Page tags

- autonomous vehicles, robotaxi, Transportation, Waymo, zeekr.

wikis.title: Samsung and Google show intelligent eyewear with Gentle Monster and Warby Parker
wikis.summary: Samsung newsroom release from Google I/O 2026 unveiling two premium styles of AI intelligent eyewear made with Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, due to launch in the fall in select markets.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- Dated 5/19/2026, filed under Wearables. Subhead: "Created in partnership with Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, the new intelligent eyewear combines AI into everyday wearability".
- "Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. and Google today unveiled new intelligent eyewear at Google I/O 2026 by giving a first look at two premium styles created with eyewear partners Gentle Monster and Warby Parker."
- "Designed to work as a companion device to a mobile phone, the new eyewear enables users to access help through voice interaction and connect seamlessly to their phones, all through a familiar form factor."
- "Gentle Monster presents styles with disruptive yet refined aesthetics, while Warby Parker showcases refined and timeless designs."

## What it does

- "Built to understand the world alongside users in real time, the new intelligent eyewear provides everyday support while keeping users hands-free and heads-up."
- "Users can access navigation assistance by simply asking Gemini with their voices, receive personalized suggestions such as a nearby coffee shop on their walking route, or even place an order for pickup."
- "Users can also receive summarized notifications for important texts and add events to their calendars."
- "Additional features include real-time translations with audio that matches the speaker's voice, as well as the ability to translate text on menus or signs in the user's line of sight."
- "Working seamlessly within the Galaxy ecosystem, the device helps users easily manage everyday tasks or effortlessly capture photos, all without taking their phone out."

## Availability

- "The first collections of intelligent eyewear are scheduled to launch this fall in select markets, with additional details to be announced in the coming months."
- Footnote: "Availability may vary depending on market. All functionalities, features, specifications and other product information provided in this document ... are subject to change without notice."

## Quotes

- Jay Kim, Executive Vice President and Head of Customer Experience Office, Mobile eXperience (MX) Business at Samsung Electronics: "This intelligent eyewear marks an important step in Samsung's vision for AI... With this new AI form factor, we are further expanding the Galaxy device ecosystem, where each device is optimized to deliver unique AI experiences that best fit each form."
- Shahram Izadi, Vice President and GM of Android XR at Google: "Intelligent eyewear represents a powerful step forward in our shared vision with Samsung to make AI more helpful and accessible in everyday life. Combining the best of Google's AI and the Android ecosystem together with Samsung's leadership in mobile hardware and Gentle Monster and Warby Parker's premium design, we are helping users stay connected and fashionable in a more natural, hands-free way."
- Hankook Kim, Founder and CEO of Gentle Monster: "Intelligent eyewear should feel as emotionally expressive as it is technologically advanced. Our vision was to merge fashion and technology in a way that feels bold, beautiful and human, bringing Gentle Monster's disruptive design identity into a new era of intelligent eyewear with Samsung and Google."
- Dave Gilboa, Co-Founder and Co-CEO of Warby Parker: "Eyewear is deeply personal, which is why every detail matters when integrating advanced technology into frames people wear every day. Our Intelligent Eyewear is designed to feel intuitive, combining Warby Parker's signature design with precision optics and exceptional comfort to help people stay focused on the moments in front of them."

## Page furniture

- Tags: Artificial Intelligence (AI), Google, Wearable. A press kit of 5 items (6.49 MB) with Gentle Monster and Warby Parker lifestyle and product images. Media contact: Mobile Experience (MX), SamsungMobilePR@edelman.com.

wikis.title: Diablo announcements at the BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony
wikis.summary: Blizzard news recap of the Diablo reveals at the BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony: Diablo V for Spring 2029, a Netflix animated series, the Amazon class, Season of Hell's Legacy and Diablo IV on Nintendo Switch 2.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- Posted on Blizzard News under Diablo IV, by Blizzard Entertainment. "Thirty years in, Diablo has never had more content ahead of it than now."
- "During the BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony, we offered the first glimpse of Diablo V (coming Spring 2029), announced a new animated series set in the world of Diablo in development with Netflix, revealed the Amazon class pack coming to Diablo IV in 2027, unveiled Season of Hell's Legacy, and confirmed that Diablo IV is coming to Nintendo Switch 2."
- "The celebration continues throughout BlizzCon with developer panels, live gameplay, and more from across the franchise, including Diablo Immortal x Spawn."
- "More than 130 million players worldwide have entered Sanctuary across the Diablo franchise."

## Dates stated

- Diablo V: "coming Spring 2029".
- Amazon class: "coming to Diablo IV in the first half of 2027" (the opening summary says "in 2027").
- Season of Hell's Legacy: "begins rolling out on September 15, 9:30 a.m. PT".
- Diablo IV: Age of Hatred Collection on Nintendo Switch 2: "September 15".
- Panels: Saturday, September 12, 2026 and Sunday, September 13, 2026.

## A naming inconsistency on the page

- The Diablo V section says "Join us for Diablo V: Forging the Next Era panel on September 12, 1:45 p.m. PT"; the schedule lower down lists the same slot as "Diablo V: Forging the Future - Main Stage, 1:45 p.m. PT".

## Where to watch

- Anaheim Convention Center, or YouTube.com/Diablo and Twitch.tv/Diablo; the Voice Actors' Panel is simulcast on YouTube.com/Blizzard or Twitch.tv/Blizzard.

wikis.title: Diablo V: Coming Spring 2029
wikis.summary: Diablo V is officially in development for Spring 2029, set in a Sanctuary where Diablo has won.
wikis.body:
- "Sanctuary has fallen. Diablo won."
- "Diablo V is officially in development and coming Spring 2029."

wikis.body:

wikis.title: The Amazon class pack for Diablo IV
wikis.summary: The Amazon returns to Sanctuary as a Diablo IV class in the first half of 2027, with bow and javelin.
wikis.body:
- "The Amazon is coming to Diablo IV in the first half of 2027."
- "She hails from the island of Skovos, revealed for the first time in Diablo IV in Lord of Hatred."

wikis.title: Season of Hell's Legacy

wikis.body:

wikis.title: Shrek Forever After (2010 film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia's article on Shrek Forever After, DreamWorks Animation's fourth Shrek film - its credits and plot, the development from Shrek Goes Fourth to the final chapter, the Tribeca premiere, $752.6 million box office, mixed reviews, awards and the Shrek 5 and Donkey follow-ups.
wikis.body:
## Infobox

- **Shrek Forever After**, "2010 DreamWorks Animation film". Directed by **Mike Mitchell**; written by **Josh Klausner and Darren Lemke**; based on *Shrek!* by **William Steig**.
- Produced by Gina Shay and Teresa Cheng. Cinematography **Yong Duk Jhun**; edited by **Nick Fletcher**; music by **Harry Gregson-Williams**.
- Production company **DreamWorks Animation**; distributed by **Paramount Pictures**.
- Release dates **April 21, 2010** (Tribeca Film Festival) and **May 21, 2010** (United States). Running time **93 minutes**; country United States; language English.
- Budget **$135-165 million**; box office **$756.2 million**.
- Voice cast billed: Mike Myers, Eddie Murphy, Cameron Diaz, Antonio Banderas, Julie Andrews, John Cleese, Walt Dohrn.
- Notes: the film is "Also known as *Shrek 4*, previously promoted as *Shrek Goes Fourth* and *Shrek: The Final Chapter*, and released on home media as *Shrek Forever After: The Final Chapter*". Distribution rights were bought back by DreamWorks Animation from Paramount in July 2014, moved to 20th Century Fox, and reverted to Universal Pictures in 2018 after NBCUniversal's 2016 acquisition.

## Figures the article gives two ways

- **Worldwide gross**: the infobox says **$756.2 million** and the lead "grossed $756 million", while the box office section gives **$238.7 million** in North America plus **$513.9 million** elsewhere for **$752.6 million**.
- **Budget**: the cited sources behind the $135-165 million range say the film "cost about $135 million to make" and that "Worldwide marketing costs will be about $165 million".
- **Ranking for 2010**: the lead and box office section call it the **fifth highest-grossing film of 2010** worldwide, while the same section says it "ended its box office run ranked domestically as the eighth highest-grossing film of 2010".

## Lead

- A 2010 American animated fantasy comedy, sequel to *Shrek the Third* (2007) and the fourth instalment in the franchise, with Myers, Murphy, Diaz, Banderas, Andrews and Cleese reprising and **Walt Dohrn** joining.
- "The story follows Shrek, now a domesticated family man and local celebrity, longing for his days of solitude and being feared, leading him to make a magic deal with the deceitful imp Rumpelstiltskin, which creates grave consequences."
- Premiered at the **Tribeca Film Festival on April 21, 2010**, released by Paramount in the US on **May 21**. "The film received mixed reviews from critics and grossed $756 million, becoming the fifth-highest-grossing film of 2010."
- Though intended as the final film, **Shrek 5** was announced in 2024 for **June 30, 2027**; the spin-offs *Puss in Boots* (2011) and *Puss in Boots: The Last Wish* (2022) have been released, and a Donkey spin-off is in development.

## Plot (as summarised in the article)

- Years earlier, King Harold and Queen Lillian, despairing of freeing Fiona from her curse, go to **Rumpelstiltskin**, whose magical contract would lift it in exchange for the Kingdom of Far Far Away - until a messenger reports that Shrek has rescued her. Rumpel has held a grudge since.
- In the present, Shrek, tired of family life and celebrity, storms out of his children's first birthday party and lashes out at Fiona. Rumpel fakes distress to draw him in and offers "a day as a 'real ogre' in exchange for a day from his childhood being erased". Shrek signs and is sent into an alternate reality.
- There, Fiona is a fugitive, his swamp is deserted, and Rumpel rules a dystopian Far Far Away where ogres are enslaved: the erased day was the day Shrek was born, so Harold and Lillian signed the contract and disappeared. When the day ends Shrek will cease to exist.
- Shrek escapes with **Donkey**, who befriends him after seeing him cry, and they find the exit clause - "**true love's kiss**". They meet a still-cursed Fiona leading an ogre resistance and a lazy, overweight **Puss in Boots** kept as her pet. Fiona, who lost hope of true love after never being rescued, rebuffs Shrek.
- Rumpel's hired **Pied Piper** captures most of the ogres during an ambush. Fiona's reluctant kiss fails. Rumpel offers a wish to whoever brings him Shrek, so Shrek turns himself in and uses the granted wish to free the other ogres.
- Rumpel tries to execute Shrek and Fiona with the enslaved Dragon, but Donkey, Puss and the freed ogres storm the castle. As Shrek fades, Fiona - now in love - kisses him; she remains an ogre in daylight, her curse broken into "love's true form". The alternate reality collapses and Shrek returns to the party, embracing his family; later he hosts a party in his swamp with an imprisoned Rumpel in attendance.

## Voice cast

- Mike Myers (Shrek), Eddie Murphy (Donkey), Cameron Diaz (Princess Fiona), Antonio Banderas (Puss in Boots), Julie Andrews (Queen Lillian), John Cleese (King Harold), **Walt Dohrn (Rumpelstiltskin)**.
- Ogres: **Jon Hamm** (Brogan), **Jane Lynch** (Gretched), **Craig Robinson** (Cookie).
- Witches: Lake Bell (Patrol Witch and Wagon Witch No. 2), **Kathy Griffin** (Dancing Witch and Wagon Witch No. 1), Mary Kay Place (Witch Guard No. 1), **Kristen Schaal** (Pumpkin Witch and Palace Witch), **Meredith Vieira** (Broomsy Witch), Billie Hayes (Cackling Witch).
- Also **Ryan Seacrest** (Father of Butter Pants), Cody Cameron (Pinocchio and Three Pigs), **Larry King** (Doris the Ugly Stepsister), **Regis Philbin** (Mabel the Ugly Stepsister), Christopher Knights (Blind Mice), Conrad Vernon (Gingerbread Man and Muffin Man), Aron Warner (Wolf), Dante James Hauser (Fergus), Chris Miller (Magic Mirror and Geppetto), **Jeremy Steig** (Pied Piper), and director **Mike Mitchell** (Witch Guard No. 2 and Butter Pants).

## Production

- After *Shrek 2*'s success in May 2004, DreamWorks Animation CEO **Jeffrey Katzenberg** planned a five-film arc beginning with *Shrek* (2001).
- In **May 2007** Katzenberg was reported to announce *Shrek 4* as a prequel about Shrek's origin, promising to explain how he ended up in the swamp; *National Geographic Kids* suggested a deleted *Shrek the Third* scene with a talking tree could be reused, and one early draft included a flashback to Shrek's adolescence.
- **October 2007**: Katzenberg announced the title ***Shrek Goes Fourth*** - "Shrek goes out into the world, forth!". **May 2009**: retitled ***Shrek Forever After***.
- November 2009: Bill Damaschke, head of creative production, said "All that was loved about Shrek in the first film is brought to the final film". The film pays tribute to the original - Shrek asking villagers to run away, Fiona blowing up a bird with her singing - and to the second, with Puss facing Shrek for the first time, the crew intending to sum up the series.
- **Tim Sullivan** was hired to write in March 2005 but was replaced by **Darren Lemke and Josh Klausner**. Klausner: "When I first came onto the project, it wasn't supposed to be the final chapter - there were originally going to be 5 Shrek movies. Then, about a year into the development, Jeffrey Katzenberg decided that the story that we'd come up with was the right way for Shrek's journey to end, which was incredibly flattering."
- **Mike Mitchell** was announced as director in May 2007, shortly before the third film's release. He felt the influence of *It's a Wonderful Life* and chose to homage rather than parody it, embracing that "Shrek isn't the same ogre he was at the start of the original film".
- "Much of the film was written and recorded in New York City." The score was again by **Harry Gregson-Williams**.

## Release, merchandise and home media

- Premiered at the **Tribeca Film Festival, April 21, 2010**; released **May 20, 2010 in Russia** and **May 21 in the United States**.
- **McDonald's** released drinking glasses with painted characters from the film in 2010; the paint contained **cadmium**, and McDonald's recalled **12 million** glasses and paid customers to return them.
- Home media: DVD, Blu-ray 3D and Blu-ray on **December 7, 2010**, marketed as *Shrek Forever After: The Final Chapter*, making **$76.5 million** in disc sales, and included in the *Shrek: The Whole Story* box set released the same day. A 4K release and a 4-Movie Collection followed on **June 11, 2024** from Universal Pictures Home Entertainment.
- A tie-in action-adventure video game was released by **Activision on May 18, 2010**.

## Box office

- **$238.7 million** in North America, **$513.9 million** elsewhere, **$752.6 million** worldwide - the fifth highest-grossing film of 2010.
- It "had the widest release for an animated film (4,359 theaters, later expanded to 4,386) in North America". Opening day, May 21, 2010: number one with **$20.8 million**, below the previous two *Shrek* films' opening days. Three-day opening **$70.8 million**, "lower than box office analysts' predictions of an opening of $105 million" and lower than the previous films. DreamWorks Animation's head of worldwide marketing Anne Globe said they were "happy with the film's opening" as it debuted at No. 1 with the fourth-best animated opening at the time in the US and Canada.
- It was the number one film for three consecutive weekends and finished eighth among 2010 domestic releases; executives were impressed by the $238.7 million domestic total for a fourth instalment "seemingly being outgrown by its fans".
- Outside North America it topped the weekend box office once, on **July 16-18, 2010**, with $46.3 million. **Russia and the CIS** were its second-biggest market, with a record animated opening of **$19.7 million** and a **$51.4 million** total; the **United Kingdom, Ireland and Malta** came third, opening with £8.96 million ($13.6 million) and finishing on £31.1 million ($51.1 million).
- "At the end of its box office run, Shrek Forever After became DreamWorks Animation's highest grossing animated film at the international box office."

## Critical response

- Rotten Tomatoes **58%** from 195 reviews, average 5.9/10; consensus: "While not without its moments, Shrek Forever After too often feels like a rote rehashing of the franchise's earlier entries." Metacritic **58 out of 100** from 35 critics, "mixed or average". CinemaScore **A**, matching *Shrek* and *Shrek 2* and above *Shrek the Third*'s B+.
- Stephen Holden (The New York Times): the film is fortified by "its brilliantly realized principal characters, who nearly a decade after the first 'Shrek' film remain as vital and engaging fusions of image, personality and voice as any characters in the history of animation."
- Pete Hammond (BoxOffice) 4.5/5: "Hilarious and heartfelt from start to finish, this is the best Shrek of them all, and that's no fairy tale", noting it borrows liberally from Frank Capra's *It's a Wonderful Life*.
- James Berardinelli (Reelviews) 3/4: "Even though Shrek Forever After is obligatory and unnecessary, it's better than Shrek the Third". James White (Empire) 4/5: "With How to Train Your Dragon and a balanced, darker-hued and very funny Shrek finale, they've found the magic again."
- Lisa Schwarzbaum (Entertainment Weekly) B−: "the magic is gone and Shrek Forever After is no longer an ogre phenomenon to reckon with." Peter Travers (Rolling Stone): "It's a fun ride. What's missing is the excitement of a new interpretation." Mary Pols (Time): "Can an ogre jump a shark? I think so."

## Accolades

- **Wins**: Golden Trailer Awards, Best Animation/Family for "Best Ever" (Aspect Ratio), June 10, 2010; Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards (US), Favorite Voice From An Animated Movie - **Eddie Murphy**, April 2, 2011.
- **Nominations**: five Annie Awards (animated effects - Andrew Young Kim; music - Harry Gregson-Williams; production design - Peter Zaslav; storyboarding - Paul Fisher; voice acting - Cameron Diaz), February 5, 2011; British Academy Children's Awards Kid's Vote - Film; The Comedy Awards Best Animated Comedy Movie; Movieguide Best Movies for Families; National Movie Awards Most Anticipated Movie Of The Summer; Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards Australia Fave Movie; Nickelodeon US Favorite Animated Movie and Favorite Voice (Cameron Diaz); People's Choice Awards Favorite Family Movie; **Saturn Awards Best Animated Film** (June 23, 2011); Teen Choice Awards Choice Movie: Animated Film; and two Visual Effects Society categories.

## Future

- In 2014 Katzenberg told Fox Business Network, "But I think you can be confident that we'll have another chapter in the Shrek series. We're not finished and, more importantly, neither is he." After Comcast and NBCUniversal acquired DreamWorks Animation in 2016, NBCUniversal President and CEO Steve Burke discussed reviving the franchise; The Hollywood Reporter cited sources in July 2016 saying a fifth film was planned for 2019, and by late 2016 reports said the script was complete.
- **April 2023**: four months after *Puss in Boots: The Last Wish*, executive producer **Chris Meledandri** confirmed a fifth film with the original cast in talks. **June 2024**: Eddie Murphy said he had begun recording *Shrek 5*, due **June 30, 2027**.
- **Donkey spin-off**: in early talks from April 2023; Murphy said in June 2024 it was greenlit and would begin production after *Shrek 5*. In May 2025 Chris Meledandri was revealed as producer and **Christopher Knights** as editor. In July 2025 Murphy confirmed voice recording would begin in September, that the story centres on his character, his dragon wife and their hybrid children, and that it was expected in **2028**.
