wikis.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the upcoming Middle-earth film directed by and starring Andy Serkis, following Strider's hunt for Gollum, shot in Wellington from July 2026 and scheduled for release on 17 December 2027.
wikis.body:
## The film

- An upcoming fantasy film directed by Andy Serkis, written by Fran Walsh, Philippa Boyens, Phoebe Gittins and Arty Papageorgiou, based on characters created by J. R. R. Tolkien and expanding on Peter Jackson's Lord of the Rings (2001-2003) and Hobbit (2012-2014) trilogies.
- It follows Strider's hunt for Gollum between the two trilogies and during The Fellowship of the Ring (2001), up to the Company of the Ring entering the Mines of Moria, and "is told from Gollum's perspective".
- Produced by Peter Jackson, Fran Walsh, Philippa Boyens and Zane Weiner; cinematography James Friend. New Line Cinema, WingNut Films and The Imaginarium Studios; distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures. New Zealand and United States; English.
- Cast: Andy Serkis (Gollum / Sméagol, via motion capture), Ian McKellen (Gandalf the Grey), Kate Winslet (Marigol), Jamie Dornan (Strider / Aragorn), Leo Woodall (Halvard), Lee Pace (Thranduil), Elijah Wood (Frodo Baggins) and Anya Taylor-Joy (Seren).

## Development

- In February 2023 Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav announced a new agreement with Embracer Group's Middle-earth Enterprises to develop multiple new live-action Lord of the Rings films; insiders said Warner Bros. wanted to stay in Tolkien's Third Age and away from Amazon's Second Age series The Rings of Power.
- Around October 2023 Jackson, Walsh and Boyens approached Serkis about directing a Gollum-focused film; he called it "a dream come true". The project and title were announced in May 2024, then intended for release in 2026.
- Serkis described it as "a deep dive where we investigate Gollum's character"; Boyens called it "a bridging film" and an origin story for Gollum. He and the producers drew inspiration from how Joker (2019) explores its title character's psychology.
- Pre-production began when Serkis travelled to New Zealand in September 2025. Returning crew include production designer Dan Hennah, illustrator John Howe and prosthetics supervisor Gino Acevedo; the film is made with Wētā Workshop and Wētā FX in Wellington.
- Kate Winslet's casting as "female lead" was confirmed in March 2026 after Serkis and Jackson spent much of 2025 persuading her to move her family to New Zealand. Aragorn was recast, confirmed by Serkis in early April 2026, and the full cast was announced at CinemaCon that month, with Anya Taylor-Joy added in June.

## Filming and release

- Principal photography began in July 2026 in Wellington and is expected to continue until October.
- It uses motion capture improvements Wētā FX made on the Planet of the Apes and Avatar franchises and digital de-aging for returning actors, which Boyens called "digital make-up", combined with miniatures and prosthetics.
- Scheduled for theatrical release by Warner Bros. Pictures in the United States on 17 December 2027.

wikis.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum - upcoming film directed by Andy Serkis
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the upcoming Middle-earth film directed by and starring Andy Serkis, covering its premise, cast, development from the 2023 Warner Bros.-Embracer deal, Wellington shoot and 17 December 2027 release date.
wikis.body:
## The film

- "The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum is an upcoming fantasy film directed by Andy Serkis, written by Fran Walsh, Philippa Boyens, Phoebe Gittins, and Arty Papageorgiou, and based on characters created by J. R. R. Tolkien."
- "Expanding on producer Peter Jackson's The Lord of the Rings (2001–2003) and The Hobbit (2012–2014) film trilogies, it follows Strider's hunt for Gollum between the events of the two trilogies and during the film The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring (2001)."
- Produced by Peter Jackson, Fran Walsh, Philippa Boyens and Zane Weiner; cinematography James Friend. Production companies New Line Cinema, WingNut Films and The Imaginarium Studios; distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures.
- Release date 17 December 2027. Countries New Zealand and United States; language English. The infobox lists no runtime, budget or box office.
- Starring Andy Serkis, Ian McKellen, Kate Winslet, Jamie Dornan (Strider), Leo Woodall, Lee Pace, Elijah Wood and Anya Taylor-Joy.
- "Development of new films based on the appendices of Tolkien's novel The Lord of the Rings (1954–1955) was announced in February 2023, with Jackson, Walsh, and Boyens returning from the previous films as producers. That October, they approached Serkis—who portrayed Gollum in the trilogies and directed second unit for the Hobbit films—about directing and starring in a new film. His involvement was announced alongside the title in May 2024, when writing was underway."
- "Pre-production started in September 2025 in Wellington, New Zealand, where the previous films were made, with several cast and crew members returning from the trilogies. Additional casting took place through early 2026, and filming is taking place from July to October."
- A hatnote says the film is "Not to be confused with the 2009 fan film The Hunt for Gollum".

## External links and navboxes in this part

- The film at IMDb.
- "Middle-earth film franchise" navbox: The Lord of the Rings film trilogy (2001-2003) and The Hobbit film trilogy (2012-2014) with their soundtracks and songs; other films The War of the Rohirrim (2024) and The Hunt for Gollum (2027); and a video game list.
- "Middle-earth in motion pictures" navbox, which lists The Hunt for Gollum (2027) under "Other" in the Peter Jackson live-action series, alongside television entries including The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power (2022-present) and fan films The Hunt for Gollum (2009) and Born of Hope (2009).
- "The Lord of the Rings" navbox covering Tolkien's volumes, elements, analysis, peoples, world and related works.

## Shifting dates inside the page

- Release: the May 2024 announcement said the film "was intended to be released in 2026"; in February 2025 Serkis expected release around December 2027, and a week later it was scheduled for 17 December 2027.
- Filming start: by the end of 2024 filming "was set to begin in early 2026"; McKellen said it would begin in May 2026; principal photography actually "began in July 2026".
- Casting rumours versus the announcement: Leo Woodall was rumoured to have been cast as Aragorn but was announced as Halvard, with Jamie Dornan as Strider / Aragorn; Anya Taylor-Joy was rumoured as Arwen but was confirmed as Seren.

wikis.title: Premise and cast of The Hunt for Gollum
wikis.summary: Where the film sits in the Middle-earth timeline and who plays whom, with the article's notes on each role.
wikis.body:
## Premise

- "The Hunt for Gollum is set between the events of Peter Jackson's The Hobbit (2012–2014) and The Lord of the Rings (2001–2003) film trilogies, and during the events of the film The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring (2001) leading up to the Company of the Ring entering the Mines of Moria. It features the Wizard Gandalf sending the ranger Strider to hunt for the creature Gollum. The film is told from Gollum's perspective."

## Cast

- Andy Serkis as Gollum and Sméagol - "a Hobbit of the Stoor branch whose mind is poisoned by the One Ring". As in the two trilogies, Serkis portrays the character via motion capture. He did not need to practice the voice because it "never left me... [the character is] indelibly part of my personality now". He and the producers "took inspiration from how the film Joker (2019) explores the psychology of its title character while telling a larger story".
- Ian McKellen as Gandalf the Grey, "a wandering Wizard who sends Strider to hunt for Gollum".
- Kate Winslet as Marigol.
- Jamie Dornan as Strider, "Chief of the Dúnedain rangers who hunts for Gollum. He is later revealed to be Aragorn, heir to the throne of Gondor", but Serkis said the film shows him where he "wouldn't think of himself as Aragorn... He's living in the wilderness. He's a doomed lone ranger."
- Leo Woodall as Halvard, a Dúnedain ranger who travels with Strider.
- Lee Pace as Thranduil, the Elven king of the Woodland Realm.
- Elijah Wood as Frodo Baggins, "a young Hobbit who inherits the One Ring from his uncle Bilbo Baggins".
- Anya Taylor-Joy as Seren, "a Sindar Elf of the Woodland Realm who is trusted by Thranduil".

wikis.title: Development of the new Lord of the Rings films
wikis.summary: The February 2023 Warner Bros. and Embracer agreement, how Jackson, Walsh and Boyens brought in Andy Serkis, and how the project was announced and dated.
wikis.body:
- "Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav announced in February 2023 that the company had signed a new agreement with Embracer Group's Middle-earth Enterprises—holder of the right to adapt J. R. R. Tolkien's novels The Hobbit (1937) and The Lord of the Rings (1954–1955)—to develop multiple new The Lord of the Rings live-action films", while the franchise was also being expanded with the animated The Lord of the Rings: The War of the Rohirrim (2024).
- Jackson, Walsh and Boyens said Warner Bros. and Embracer were keeping them "in the loop". Boyens said working on The War of the Rohirrim "reignited the trio's passion for the world of Middle-earth and showed the potential for more stories to be told based on the appendices".
- Warner Bros. Pictures CEOs Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy brokered the agreement and visited Jackson in New Zealand. "Industry insiders said Warner Bros. wanted to distance future films from the Amazon series The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power (2022–present) and would continue to tell stories set in Tolkien's Third Age, avoiding the series' Second Age setting."
- Serkis was asked in March 2023 whether he would return and said he would if Jackson, Walsh and Boyens did. "Around October of that year, the trio approached Serkis about him directing a new film focused on Gollum." Serkis, a second unit director on the Hobbit films, called the chance to direct "a dream come true".
- In May 2024 Zaslav announced Jackson, Walsh and Boyens were producing two new films for Warner Bros. and New Line, "the first of which had the working title The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum and was intended to be released in 2026". Serkis was set to direct and star. Walsh and Boyens were in the early stages of writing with The War of the Rohirrim writers Phoebe Gittins, who is Boyens's daughter, and Arty Papageorgiou. Ken Kamins was executive producing with Serkis and Jonathan Cavendish of the Imaginarium Studios.
- Serkis said the film was being made with Wētā Workshop, Wētā FX and others from the trilogies, based again in Wellington - "a relief for local filmmakers after production on The Rings of Power had been moved away from New Zealand". He described the film as "a deep dive where we investigate Gollum's character".
- Commentators expected an adaptation of the appendices material in which Gandalf and Aragorn hunt Gollum during The Fellowship of the Ring; Jackson had discussed adapting it in the 1990s and it was later made as a fan film, The Hunt for Gollum (2009).
- Actors who expressed interest in returning included Viggo Mortensen (Aragorn), Ian McKellen (Gandalf), Cate Blanchett (Galadriel), Orlando Bloom (Legolas), John Rhys-Davies (Gimli) and Liv Tyler (Arwen); "Hugo Weaving (Elrond) said he was not interested in returning."
- Boyens described the film as "a bridging film" and an origin story for Gollum, covering "a specific chunk of incredible untold story, told through the perspective of this incredible creature", noting that during the Hobbit films the producers had initially planned a "bridge" film that changed during production.
- In February 2025 Serkis said writing was still early, pre-production would begin later that year and take six or seven months, filming would be in 2026 and release around December 2027; a week later it was scheduled for 17 December 2027. In August, Zaslav praised the script. McKellen said filming would begin in May 2026 and revealed Frodo Baggins would appear; Wood said he had read the script and it had many cameo opportunities.

wikis.title: Pre-production and casting in 2025-2026
wikis.summary: Serkis's arrival in New Zealand, the returning cast and crew, the rumours about recasting Aragorn, and the CinemaCon cast announcement.
wikis.body:
- "Serkis travelled to New Zealand in September 2025 to begin pre-production."
- In early 2026 McKellen and Wood were reported to be reprising their roles, although Wood said they were not yet allowed to say so officially. McKellen confirmed his return: "I cannot have anybody else play Gandalf". Wood felt the same about Frodo and said the film was "getting the band back together", with many of the same department heads as the trilogies.
- Rumours at the time included that Aragorn would be recast with a younger actor and that Kate Winslet - who starred in Jackson's Heavenly Creatures (1994) - would join. Winslet's casting as the film's "female lead" was confirmed in March. "Serkis and Jackson spent much of 2025 convincing Winslet to move her family from the United Kingdom to New Zealand for the duration of filming so she could join the cast."
- Zane Weiner had been added to the producing team by then, returning from the trilogies.
- Also in March 2026, returning crew were confirmed: production designer Dan Hennah, illustrator John Howe and prosthetics supervisor Gino Acevedo (the article flags this with "better source needed"). Leo Woodall was rumoured as Aragorn and Anya Taylor-Joy as Arwen, the role Liv Tyler played previously.
- In early April Serkis confirmed they were recasting Aragorn. Later that month at CinemaCon, Warner Bros. announced the cast: Serkis as Gollum / Sméagol; McKellen as Gandalf; Winslet as Marigol; Jamie Dornan as Strider / Aragorn; Woodall as Halvard; Lee Pace as Thranduil, reprising his Hobbit role; and Wood as Frodo. In June, Taylor-Joy was confirmed as Seren.

wikis.title: Filming and release plans
wikis.summary: The Wellington shoot from July 2026, the motion capture and de-aging technology used, and the scheduled release date.
wikis.body:
- "Principal photography began in July 2026 in Wellington, New Zealand, with James Friend as the cinematographer" (the article flags the cinematographer claim with "independent source needed").
- "The film is taking advantage of improvements in motion capture technology that Wētā FX made with the Planet of the Apes and Avatar franchises, and is also using digital de-aging technology for returning actors, which Boyens called 'digital make-up'."
- Serkis wanted to combine new technology with traditional filmmaking techniques including miniatures and prosthetics, and said the film would "technically, visually, and stylistically" merge Jackson's approaches to the two trilogies.
- "Filming is expected to continue until October."
- "The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum is scheduled to be released theatrically by Warner Bros. Pictures in the United States on 17 December 2027."

wikis.title: 99th Academy Awards
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 99th Academy Awards, scheduled for March 14, 2027 at the Dolby Theatre, covering its key voting dates, Governors Awards honorees and the rule changes taking effect for the ceremony.
wikis.body:
## The ceremony

- "The 99th Academy Awards ceremony, presented by the **Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (AMPAS)**, are scheduled to take place **March 14, 2027**, at the **Dolby Theatre** in Hollywood, Los Angeles."
- "During the gala, the AMPAS will present Academy Awards (commonly referred to as the Oscars) in **24 categories**, honoring films released in **2026**."
- "**Conan O'Brien** will host for the third straight year."
- Infobox: produced by **Raj Kapoor** and **Katy Mullan**; network - Broadcast: **ABC**, Streaming: **Hulu**; previous 98th, next 100th.
- "On **April 7, 2026**, AMPAS announced the date of the ceremony and key dates pertaining to the 99th edition."
- "On **May 12, 2026**, it was announced that Raj Kapoor and Katy Mullan would return as executive producers for the **fourth year in a row**, and that Conan O'Brien would return as host for the third year in a row." The same paragraph quotes AMPAS CEO **Bill Kramer** and president **Lynette Howell Taylor** saying the pair "have produced such captivating, entertaining and heartfelt shows over the **last two years**".

## Key dates

| Date | Event |
| --- | --- |
| December 7, 2026 | Preliminary voting begins |
| December 11, 2026 | Preliminary voting ends |
| January 11, 2027 | Nominations voting begins |
| January 15, 2027 | Nominations voting ends |
| January 21, 2027 | Nominations announced |
| February 25, 2027 | Final voting begins |
| March 4, 2027 | Final voting ends |
| March 14, 2027 | Ceremony |

## Governors Awards

- The Academy "is set to hold its **17th Governors Awards** ceremony at the **Ray Dolby Ballroom** of the Ovation Hollywood complex in Hollywood on **November 15, 2026**".
- "On **June 10, 2026**, The Academy announced recipients on the Governors Awards."
- **Academy Honorary Awards**: **Glenn Close** - "throughout her extraordinary body of work, Glenn Close's unparalleled emotional range has brought to life some of the most complex characters in cinema"; **Floyd Norman** - "the legendary animator who has broken barriers and inspired generations of artists over his remarkable career"; **Ridley Scott** - "a true visionary whose decades-long legacy has left an immeasurable impact on global cinema and culture".
- **Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award**: **Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler**, who "play a central role in American independent cinema, championing bold, ambitious and distinctive storytelling".

## Rule and eligibility changes (announced May 1, 2026)

- **Best International Feature Film** eligibility expands to include non-English-language films that win top jury awards at **Berlin (Golden Bear)**, **Busan (Best Film Award)**, **Cannes (Palme d'Or)**, **Sundance (World Cinema Grand Jury Prize)**, **Toronto (Platform Prize)** and **Venice (Golden Lion)**, in addition to country submissions. The page attributes the change to "high-profile and politically motivated snubs (such as *Anatomy of a Fall* and *It Was Just an Accident*)". Films themselves "will be formally credited as recipients, rather than the submitting country"; the director continues to accept on behalf of the film's creative team, and a submitting country of a national submission still receives a statuette and inscription.
- An individual actor "may now hold **multiple nominations in a single acting category**" for performances in different films, "rather than only receiving a nomination for the performance that received the most votes", in alignment with categories such as Best Director.
- Eligibility rules for the acting and writing categories "now explicitly prohibit the use of **generative artificial intelligence**", with writing categories restricted to "works of human authorship" and acting categories requiring roles to be held by a billed cast member and "demonstrably performed by humans with their consent".

wikis.title: NHL releases its 2026-27 regular-season schedule
wikis.summary: NHL.com announcement of the 1,344-game 2026-27 regular-season schedule, with 84 games per team, opening night on Sept. 29 and the season's outdoor, international and All-Star dates.
wikis.body:
## The release

- By NHL.com, July 16, 2026. Subhead: "1,344-game slate, with 84 games per team, begins Sept. 29".
- "The NHL released its 1,344-game, 2026-27 regular-season schedule on Thursday."
- "Each team will play 84 games this season, up from 82, with the home openers having been announced Wednesday."
- A downloadable "Official 2026-27 Regular Season Schedule (7.16)", dated Jul 16, 2026, 15.92 MB, is linked.

## Opening night, Sept. 29

- "The seasons starts on Sept. 29 with a nationally televised tripleheader on ESPN in the United States and a doubleheader on Sportsnet in Canada."
- "The Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes will raise their banner in the season opener against the Florida Panthers at Lenovo Center (5 p.m. ET; ESPN)."
- Rest of the ESPN tripleheader: "the New York Rangers visiting the Boston Bruins (8 p.m.) followed by the Chicago Blackhawks at the Western Conference champion Vegas Golden Knights (10:30 p.m. ET)."
- Sportsnet: "No. 1 pick Gavin McKenna likely making his NHL debut for the Toronto Maple Leafs against the Montreal Canadiens (7 p.m. ET). Then the Vancouver Canucks visit the Edmonton Oilers (10 p.m. ET)."
- "The next night, Sept. 30, TNT will have a doubleheader with two rivalry games; the Pittsburgh Penguins visiting the Philadelphia Flyers (7:30 p.m. ET) and the Los Angeles Kings visiting the Colorado Avalanche (10 p.m. ET)."

## Key dates

- "The season will conclude with all 32 teams in action on Saturday, April 10." Two days have all 32 teams in action: "Oct. 13 and April 10."
- International: "two games in Finland in November (12, 14), two games in Germany in December (18, 20)". "The Hurricanes and Seattle Kraken will play in Helsinki in the Global Series Finland, while the Chicago Blackhawks and Ottawa Senators will meet in Dusseldorf in the Global Series Germany."
- Outdoor games (three in all): the 2026 Tim Hortons NHL Heritage Classic in Winnipeg, the Jets hosting the Canadiens, Oct. 25; "The Utah Mammoth will host their first outdoor game against the Avalanche at Rice-Eccles Stadium, home of the University of Utah, on Dec. 31 in the Discover NHL Winter Classic"; and "The Dallas Stars will host the Vegas Golden Knights in the 2027 Navy Federal Credit Union NHL Stadium Series at AT&T Stadium, home of the NFL's Dallas Cowboys, on Feb. 20."
- All-Star: "After the All-Star Game wasn't held the past two seasons due to the 4 Nations Face-Off in 2025 and 2026 Winter Olympics, it returns this season to UBS Arena, home of the New York Islanders. The Skills competition will be Feb. 5, and the new-look All-Star Game will be Feb. 6."
- Other: "the Thanksgiving Showdown between the Rangers and Boston Bruins on Nov. 28, and a Stanley Cup rematch on Dec. 21 in Vegas and Jan. 17 in Carolina."
- New this season: "numerous Monday weekday matinee/European primetime games, allowing fans in Europe to watch their favorite teams and the NHL's biggest stars in prime time during the week."

## Broadcast

- "The Stanley Cup Final will be broadcast exclusively on TNT in the United States and Sportsnet in Canada."
- "The Walt Disney Company (ESPN/ABC), TNT Sports (TNT/HBO Max) and Sportsnet are the NHL's national broadcast partners for the 2026-27 season... Complete broadcast details will be announced when available."

## Related items listed

- "2026-27 NHL season to start on Sept. 29 with Carolina-Florida, Toronto-Montreal" (Jul 15, 2026); "2026-27 NHL schedule has plenty of must-see games" (Jul 16, 2026).

wikis.title: 69th Annual Grammy Awards
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the upcoming 69th Annual Grammy Awards of February 7, 2027, covering the date and venue, the move to ABC/Disney+/Hulu, and the category, criteria and voting changes announced for the 2027 ceremony.
wikis.body:
## The ceremony

- "The 69th Annual Grammy Awards are an upcoming music awards ceremony which will honor the best recordings, compositions, and artists from **August 31, 2025, to August 28, 2026**, as chosen by the members of the **Recording Academy**, on **February 7, 2027**."
- "It is the **24th ceremony** to be held at the **Crypto.com Arena** in Los Angeles, California, and **a host has yet to be announced**."
- "It is the first Grammy ceremony to be broadcast on **ABC** since the 14th Annual Grammy Awards in **1972**, and the first to be broadcast on **Disney+ and Hulu** following a new **ten-year deal** between the Recording Academy and the Walt Disney Company, which was announced on **October 30, 2024**."
- "The ceremony follows on from the 68th Annual Grammy Awards, which were the last to air on **CBS**."
- "The nominations for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards will be announced on **November 16, 2026**."
- Infobox: website grammy.com; network ABC / Disney+ / Hulu; previous 68th, next 70th. Most awards, most nominations, host and ratings fields are empty.

## Background: changes announced June 16, 2026

"On June 16, 2026, the Recording Academy announced several changes for different categories and updates on eligibility rules for the 2027 ceremony."

### Category changes

- "**Four new categories** - Best Asian Pop Music Performance, Best R&B Collaboration or Duo/Group Performance, Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance, and Best Latin Song."
- Best Folk Album renamed **Best Contemporary Folk Album**; **Best Traditional Folk Album** "is making a comeback for the first time since 2011".
- Best R&B Performance renamed **Best R&B Solo Performance**.

### Criteria amendments

- Artists may now submit themselves **four times** for Best New Artist consideration, "an increase from the previous limit of three". Once an artist achieves a nomination, receives a nomination in any other Grammy category, or submits four times without a Best New Artist nomination, they are ineligible.
- The threshold of new recordings required for an album to be eligible "is reduced from **75% to 66%**".
- Internet-only releases are now eligible in Best Album Notes and Best Historical Album.
- Songwriters and composers of new material on winning albums in the genre categories "will now receive an award in parity with the recognition currently awarded to producers and engineers".
- Minor description updates to Best Contemporary Classical Composition, Best Musical Theater Album, Best Country Song, Best Country Solo Performance, Best Country Duo/Group Performance, Best Bluegrass Album, Best Children's Music Album, Best Alternative Music Performance, Best Alternative Music Album and Best Regional Roots Music Album.

### Voting amendments

- Previously all Academy members voted in the six general field categories plus ten more across no more than three genre fields.
- "As of the 2027 ceremony, some members have the option to vote in **fifteen categories across all genre fields** instead based on their own professional credits and contributions to the music industry." Members requesting that ballot "will need to meet certain criteria".

## Contradiction within the page

- The body says "**Four new categories**" and names four. Three cited reference titles on the same page say **five**: NARAS, June 16, 2026, "Five New Categories And Rule Updates Take Effect For 2027 Grammys"; Rolling Stone, "Grammys Announce Five New Categories, Including Best R&B Collaboration and Best Latin Song"; Billboard, "2027 Grammy Changes: 5 New Categories...". A Gold Derby citation says "Asian Pop Music one of 5 categories added".

## Categories listed

- The page lists the full slate by field: General Field (Record, Album, Song of the Year, Best New Artist, Producer of the Year Non-Classical, Songwriter of the Year Non-Classical); Pop & Dance/Electronic; Rock, Metal & Alternative; R&B, Rap & Spoken Word Poetry; Jazz, Traditional Pop, Contemporary Instrumental & Musical Theater; Country & American Roots; Gospel & Contemporary Christian; Latin, Global, African, Reggae & New Age, Ambient or Chant; Children's, Comedy, Audio Book Narration & Storytelling, Visual Media & Music Video/Film; Package, Notes & Historical; Production, Engineering, Composition & Arrangement; and Classical.

wikis.body:
## The market

- Question: "Recession next year?" Listed under GROWTH; the page title reads "Recession next year? Odds & Predictions 2027".
- Series: KXRECSSNBER. Event: KXRECSSNBER-27. Market: KXRECSSNBER-27.
- Volume shown: "$448,819 vol". The chart runs Apr, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep on a 20%-60% scale.

## Prices as shown

- Trade panel: "YES 24c, NO 78c", "25% chance", "3.25% Interest", "Max payout Jan 31, 2028".

## Rules

- "Resolves Yes if there are two consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth in Q4 2026 through Q4 2027, according to the Bureau of Economic Analysis. Outcome verified from Bureau of Economic Analysis."
- "For the avoidance of doubt, qualifying consecutive quarters may include Q4 2026 and Q1 2027."
- "GDP growth refers to the quarter-over-quarter annualized percent change in real GDP as reported in the Advance Estimate for each quarter."
- "The market will close at the sooner of the occurrence of the event or 8:25 AM ET on the morning of the expected release of the Advance Estimate of 2027 Q4 GDP. The market will expire at the sooner of the occurrence of the event or the first 10:00 AM ET after the release of the Advance Estimate of 2027 Q4 GDP."
- Insider trading prohibited for persons employed by any of the Source Agencies and persons holding material non-public information on the underlying.

## Timeline

- Market open: "Apr 24, 2026 - 3:15pm EDT". Market closes: "After the outcome occurs". Projected payout: "1 hour after closing".
- "If this event occurs, the market will close the following 10am ET. Otherwise, it closes by Jan 31, 2028 at 8:25am EST."

## The page's "About" note

- "A recession is an economic downturn characterized by two consecutive quarters of negative economic growth, or negative GDP. Recessions can lead to job losses, reduced consumer confidence, and financial challenges for businesses. Fun fact: The word 'recession' has been used to describe economic setbacks since the 19th century, but the modern concept of recessions as we understand them today emerged during the Great Depression of the 1930s." Source credited: EveryCRSReport.com.

## Breaking-news items listed on the page

- Business Insider, Sep 12: "A veteran economist tells us why he sees a recession and a stock crash by the end of 2027" - "Henrik Zeberg, an economist who studies business cycles, laid out his timeline for how and when a downturn could hit markets and the economy."
- Bloomberg, 7h: "Australia's Treasurer Warns of Economic Risks as Population Ages" - Jim Chalmers warned the economy faces "serious risks" as the population ages and grows more slowly.
- Morningstar, Sep 18: "What's Ahead in 2027 and Beyond for Inflation, Fed Rate Cuts, and More" - "Rate hikes this year will give way to large rate cuts in 2027 and 2028."

Note: the trade panel shows "25% chance" alongside a YES price of 24c; the user comments on the page are traders' opinions, not site statements.

wikis.title: 2027 Cricket World Cup
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 2027 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, covering its dates, the new Super Series/Super 7 format, qualification, venues and knockout schedule.
wikis.body:
## Tournament

- "The 2027 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup will be the 14th edition of the Cricket World Cup ... It is scheduled to be played in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia from 4 October to 21 November 2027."
- "This will be the second time that South Africa and Zimbabwe will have co-hosted the tournament, having co-hosted the 2003 edition, while Namibia will host it for the first time."
- Infobox: Dates 4 October - 21 November 2027; Administrator International Cricket Council; format One Day International; tournament formats Preliminary stage, Group stage, Super 7 and Knockout stage; Participants 14; Matches 57. Previous edition 2023, next 2031.
- "The last tournament, held in 2023 in India was contested by 10 teams. Australia are the defending champions, having defeated India in the final of the previous edition."
- "In November 2021, the ICC announced that the 2027 Cricket World Cup will be played in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia."

## Format (announced 15 July 2026)

"On 15 July 2026, the ICC announced a new format for the tournament, which is intended to increase the competitiveness of matches and reduce the overall duration of the tournament, while maintaining a 14-team field."

- **Round 1 - Super Series (3 matches):** "The three lowest-seeded teams in the field will compete in a three-match play-in round, played in round-robin format. The winner of this stage will advance to the 12-team main pool for the second round."
- **Round 2 (30 matches):** "The 12 teams will then be split into two groups of six; the top three teams from each group, along with the best fourth-placed team across both groups, will advance to the Super 7 stage."
- **Round 3 - Super 7 (21 matches):** "The seven qualified teams will compete in a single round-robin pool, with the top four teams qualifying for the semi-finals."
- **Knockout stage (3 matches):** first plays fourth, second plays third; the two winners meet in the final.

## Preparations

"In preparation for the 2027 Cricket World Cup, a 15-member organising committee of the tournament was finalised in August 2025. Trevor Manuel was named chair." Former Deputy President of South Africa Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka "was also named as one of the seven independent directors of the tournament."

## Qualification

- "Hosts South Africa and Zimbabwe will qualify automatically for the tournament, along with the top eight teams in the ICC ODI rankings as of 30 September 2026. The remaining four places will be decided through qualifying tournaments."
- "Although Namibia will co-host the competition for the first time, they will not be guaranteed a spot because they are not a full ICC member and, as a result, will have to go through the standard qualification pathway."
- Qualification table: Hosts - 16 November 2021 - 2 teams (South Africa listed); ICC Men's ODI Team Rankings (top 8 excluding hosts) - 30 September 2026 - 8 teams TBD; 2027 Cricket World Cup Qualifier - 22 February - 23 March 2027, in Namibia/South Africa - 4 teams TBD. Total 14.
- "The winner of the Qualifier will advance directly to the Second round whilst the teams that finished second, third and fourth will contest in the Super Series."

## Venues

- "Cricket South Africa confirmed eight shortlisted venues in April 2024. In August 2025, it was announced that 44 matches would be hosted by South Africa across the eight venues, while Zimbabwe and Namibia would host the remaining 10 matches." (That 44 + 10 = 54 predates the July 2026 format change; the infobox gives 57 matches, matching the new 3 + 30 + 21 + 3 structure.)

wikis.title: 2027 Africa Cup of Nations
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, co-hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from 19 June to 17 July 2027, covering host selection, qualification, the co-hosts' records and the candidate venues.
wikis.body:
## Tournament

- "The 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, also referred to as AFCON 2027 or CAN 2027, and for sponsorship purposes as the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations PAMOJA 2027 ... will be the 36th edition of the African football tournament organised by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) as a biennial tournament. It will be hosted by Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania from 19 June to 17 July 2027."
- Swahili title given: "Kombe la Mataifa ya Afrika 2027". A note explains: "Pamoja means together in Swahili, which is one of the official languages of the three host countries."
- Infobox: Host countries Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda; Dates 19 June - 17 July; Teams 24; Venues 10 (in 7 host cities). Previous edition 2025, next 2028.
- "This edition of the tournament will be the first to be hosted by three countries, and the first in five decades to be organised in the CECAFA region, since it was hosted by Ethiopia in 1976."
- "This event is part of the Africa Cup of Nations' 70th anniversary. It will also be the last one to be held in odd-numbered years, as CAF announced in December 2025 that AFCON would become a Quadrennial tournament from 2028 onwards."
- "Morocco are the defending champions after being controversially awarded the 2025 title after an appeal and despite Senegal originally winning 1-0 in the final."

## Host selection

- "On 7 April 2023, CAF decided to choose the host nations for the 2025 and 2027 editions of the tournament on the same day. On 27 September the same year, CAF announced that the 2027 edition will be hosted by Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda."
- Bids: Botswana and Zambia; Nigeria and Benin (which also bid for the 2025 edition); Senegal; Kenya / Tanzania / Uganda (selected).

## Qualification

- "Qualifying matches will be played during FIFA international windows in March 2026 (preliminary round), September/October 2026 (matchdays 1-4), and November 2026 (matchdays 5-6). The draw was broadcast live on CAF's official digital platforms and through its broadcast partners."
- Qualified so far - the three co-hosts, all qualified 27 September 2023:
  - **Kenya** - 7th appearance; first 1972, last 2019; streak 1; previous best Group stage (1972, 1988, 1990, 1992, 2004, 2019).
  - **Tanzania** - 5th appearance; first 1980, last 2025; streak 3; previous best Round of 16 (2025).
  - **Uganda** - 9th appearance; first 1962; streak 2; previous best Runners-up (1978). Its previous appearances are listed as 1962, 1968, 1974, 1976, 1978, 2017, 2019 and 2025.
- FIFA world rankings at the start of the tournament are listed as TBD.

## Venues

- "Since the competition will be jointly hosted by three countries, it was initially reported that each host nation would provide three stadiums, bringing the total number of venues to nine. Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda each proposed two host cities during the early planning stages of the tournament."
- "Subsequent planning discussions indicated that the tournament could be staged across a broader geographic footprint, with up to ten host cities in total. However, in Kenya, Nairobi now remains the only proposed host city after the exclusion of Eldoret and Kakamega. Tanzania is expected to host matches in the cities of Dar es Salaam, Arusha and Zanzibar while Uganda has put forward Kampala, Hoima and Lira as potential venues."

List of candidate host cities:

| Hoima | Hoima City Stadium | 20,000 (new) |

| Lira | Akii Bua Stadium | 20,000 |

The page's stadium navbox gives a different set of grounds for the tournament: Moi International Sports Centre (Nairobi), Talanta Sports Stadium (Nairobi), Kipchoge Keino Stadium (Eldoret), Benjamin Mkapa Stadium and Chamazi Stadium (Dar es Salaam), CCM Kirumba Stadium (Mwanza), Samia Suluhu Hassan Stadium (Arusha), Mandela National Stadium and Nakivubo Stadium (Kampala), and Hoima Sports Stadium (Hoima) - including Eldoret, which the body says has been excluded.

The article's location map marks Eldoret (Kipchoge Keino Stadium), Nairobi (Moi International Stadium, Nyayo National Stadium, Talanta Sports Stadium), Arusha (Samia Suluhu Hassan Stadium), Dar es Salaam (Benjamin Mkapa Stadium, Chamazi Stadium), Zanzibar (Zanzibar Fumba Stadium), Hoima (Hoima City Stadium) and Kampala (Mandela National Stadium, Nakivubo Stadium).

wikis.title: Path of the Annular Solar Eclipse of 2032 May 09
wikis.summary: NASA GSFC eclipse page by Fred Espenak giving the path table, greatest eclipse and greatest duration circumstances for the annular solar eclipse of 9 May 2032.
wikis.body:
## What the page is

- A path table for the "Annular Solar Eclipse of 2032 May 09", by Fred Espenak, on NASA's GSFC eclipse site.
- "The following table delineates the path of the Moon's antumbral shadow"; geographic coordinates (WGS 84) of the northern and southern limits and the central line are listed at 120-second intervals.
- Central-line local circumstances include the Moon/Sun apparent-diameter ratio, the Sun's altitude and azimuth (degrees), the path width (kilometers) and the duration on the central line.
- Global visibility is on an Orthographic Map, the path in detail on a Google Map. Other links: Animated Map, Path Table, Besselian Elements Table, Saros 148 Table.

## Key circumstances

- Instant of Greatest Eclipse: "Time = 13:25:23.8 UT, Lat = 51 deg 15.5' S, Long = 007 deg 03.5' W", Sun Altitude 19.9 deg, Sun Azimuth 344.6 deg, Path Width 43.7 km, Central Duration 00m21.9s.
- Instant of Greatest Duration: "Time = 14:03:01 UT, Lat = 55 deg 41' S, Long = 030 deg 39' E", Sun Altitude 0.0 deg, Sun Azimuth 302.4 deg, Path Width 91.0 km, Central Duration 00m43.1s.
- Delta T = 78.2 seconds.

## Path extent

- Limits at the start: central line 69 deg 57.6' S, 042 deg 31.2' W, path width 87 km, duration 00m40.8s.
- Limits at the end: central line 55 deg 41.0' S, 030 deg 39.2' E, path width 91 km, duration 00m43.1s.
- Tabulated times run 12:48 to 14:02 UT; the whole tabulated path lies in southern latitudes (about 69 deg S to 49 deg S), crossing from about 042 deg W to about 030 deg E.
- Moon/Sun diameter ratio runs 0.990 at the limits to 0.996 near mid-eclipse.

## Prediction basis and caveats

- "Predictions ... were generated using the VSOP87/ELP2000-85 solar and lunar ephemerides and a value of Delta T = 78.2 seconds."
- "The eclipse predictions presented here DO NOT include the effects of mountains and valleys along the edge of the Moon. Such corrections for the lunar limb profile may shift the limits of the eclipse path north or south by ~1-3 kilometers, and change the eclipse duration by ~1-3 seconds."
- "More detailed predictions including the effects of the lunar limb profile are normally posted 12-18 months before each eclipse".
- "All eclipse calculations are by Fred Espenak, and he assumes full responsibility for their accuracy." Reproduction permitted with the acknowledgment "Eclipse Predictions by Fred Espenak, NASA's GSFC".
- The page carries the date "2014 Feb 26" at its foot.

wikis.title: Berlin signs an exclusivity agreement with Projektpartnerschaft Quartier ICC for the ICC Berlin
wikis.summary: Berlin Senate press release of 2 September 2026 announcing that the State of Berlin and the best bidder, Projektpartnerschaft Quartier ICC, signed an exclusivity agreement for the International Congress Centrum through 30 June 2027.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- Press release ("Pressemitteilung vom 02.09.2026") from the Senatsverwaltung für Wirtschaft, Energie und Betriebe.
- In the ongoing award procedure for the Internationale Congress Centrum (ICC), the State of Berlin and the best bidder ("Bestbieterin") Projektpartnerschaft Quartier ICC signed an exclusivity agreement "heute, am 2. September 2026".
- The partnership thereby gains exclusivity "bis zum 30. Juni 2027" for the ICC and its associated car park, and for the plot at Messedamm 9.

## What the exclusivity phase is for

- The phase serves to conduct negotiations between the State of Berlin and the partnership on the planned award of a heritable building right (Erbbaurechtsvergabe).
- "Ziel ist eine Beurkundung des Erbbaurechtsvertrages nach Befassung des Berliner Abgeordnetenhauses im nächsten Jahr."
- The finalised contract will, after notarisation, be submitted to the Abgeordnetenhaus von Berlin for approval; the heritable building right is envisaged "mit einer Laufzeit von 99 Jahren". The parliamentary process follows the Landeshaushaltsordnung.
- The basis for further talks is the concept the partnership submitted in the competitive dialogue after several months of work and discussions with a jury, presented to the public on 26 June 2026.

## Quotes

- Senator Franziska Giffey: "Mit der Exklusivitätsvereinbarung gehen wir nun den nächsten wichtigen Schritt auf dem Weg zur Wiederbelebung des ICC. In den kommenden Monaten wollen wir gemeinsam mit der Projektpartnerschaft Quartier ICC zu einem tragfähigen Ergebnis kommen. Damit sind wir im Zeitplan und arbeiten weiter daran, dass die zukunftsweisenden Pläne der Projektpartnerschaft Wirklichkeit werden können. Denn weiter gilt unser Leitspruch: 'ICC dauert noch ein bisschen, aber wird mega'."
- Tatjana Adams, member of the management of BIM Berliner Immobilienmanagement GmbH: "In den kommenden Monaten wollen wir den Erbbaurechtsvertrag zur Beurkundungsreife bringen. Damit legen wir die Grundlage für den Abschluss des Vergabeverfahrens und die anschließende Zuschlagserteilung für die Projektpartnerschaft Quartier ICC, vorbehaltlich der Zustimmung der zuständigen Gremien. So schaffen wir die vertraglichen Voraussetzungen dafür, dass das Konzept für das ICC umgesetzt werden kann."
- Projektpartnerschaft Quartier ICC: "Die Exklusivitätsvereinbarung ist für uns als Projektpartnerschaft Quartier ICC ein weiterer Meilenstein, das ikonische Gebäude ICC wie auch das darum liegende Quartier wieder zu einem belebten Ort in der Stadt zu entwickeln. Vor allem mit Kunst- und Kultur, aber auch vielen anderen wichtigen und interessanten Inhalten, soll dies langfristig und nachhaltig gelingen; damit das ICC wieder ein lebendiger Ort für alle Berliner und Berlinerinnen sowie für die Gäste der Stadt sein wird. Es bleibt eine große und spannende Herausforderung, heute sind wir wieder einen Schritt weitergekommen."

## The procedure and the consortium

- The award procedure started in November 2024 with a participation competition (Teilnahmewettbewerb); Projektpartnerschaft Quartier ICC emerged as the successful applicant and best bidder.
- It unites several companies and experts from project development, urban planning, architecture, heritage conservation, art and culture management, engineering, construction and project management.
- Members: Arup Deutschland GmbH, Coloured Fields GmbH, GRAFT Gesellschaft von Architekten mbH, HOCHTIEF Infrastructure GmbH, ICCA Projektgruppe / Stiftung Kunstforum Berliner Volksbank, KVL Projektmanagement Berlin GmbH, Max Dudler GmbH, MIB AG Immobilien und Beteiligungen, and schneider+schumacher Planungsgesellschaft mbH.

## Contact

- Senatsverwaltung für Wirtschaft, Energie und Betriebe, Pressestelle, Martin-Luther-Straße 105, 10825 Berlin, Tel. (030) 9013-8451; press spokeswoman Lisa Frerichs, (030) 9013-8112.
- Also offered as a PDF, "20260902 PM Weiterer Meilenstein für das ICC Berlin..." (130.3 kB).

wikis.title: Six Flags Qiddiya City
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Six Flags Qiddiya City, the Saudi amusement park that opened on 31 December 2025, covering its development, opening, six themed areas and its world-record attractions.
wikis.body:
## The park

- "Six Flags Qiddiya City is an amusement park located in Qiddiya City, Riyadh Province, Saudi Arabia. Owned by the Qiddiya Investment Company, it is operated and managed by Six Flags Entertainment Corporation. It is the first Six Flags theme park in Asia and features Falcons Flight, the world's tallest, fastest, and longest roller coaster."
- Arabic name: ستة أعلام مدينة القدية (romanized Sittat A'lam Madinat al-Qiddiya).
- Infobox: Status Operating; Opened December 31, 2025; Area 320,000 m2 (79 acres); Attractions total 28, roller coasters 8, water rides 5; website sixflagsqiddiyacity.com. Coordinates 24 deg 35' 19.6" N, 46 deg 19' 57.6" E.

## History

- "On April 4, 2018, Six Flags Entertainment Corporation announced the development of a new park in Riyadh backed by the Public Investment Fund, Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, under Saudi Vision 2030, a government initiative to diversify the country's economy. The park was initially slated for a 2022 opening."
- "On August 26, 2019, the Qiddiya Investment Company unveiled plans for the 79-acre park's design. These included 28 attractions over six themed park areas with a mix of both thrill rides and family-friendly rides. They announced Falcons Flight, which would be the world's longest, tallest, and fastest roller coaster upon completion. The park's opening date was then moved to 2023."
- "On December 12, 2021, Qiddiya Investment Company awarded a $1 billion contract to Almabani General Contractors based in Saudi Arabia and Bouygues Batiment International based in France to begin construction on the park." (A cited Qiddiya release is headed "Qiddiya Awards SAR 3.75B to Build Six Flags Qiddiya City".)
- "In 2024, UK Export Finance designated the Six Flags Qiddiya project as 'Category A' under its social and environmental risk framework, identifying a potential for significant adverse impact during construction and operation, requiring ongoing monitoring of labour conditions during construction."

## Opening

- "On November 16, 2025, it was announced that Six Flags Qiddiya City would officially open on December 31, 2025. Ticket prices were confirmed to start at US$87 (SAR 325) for adults and US$74 (SAR 275) for children, with free admission for infants under four years old. Tickets grant unlimited access to all rides and attractions in the park for a full day."
- A soft opening was held for employees' families and selected media influencers. "Around two weeks prior to the official opening ceremony, WWE stars including Randy Orton, Liv Morgan, Omos, Tiffany Stratton, and Grayson Waller visited Six Flags Qiddiya City while on tour in Saudi Arabia to promote the Riyadh Season and the 2026 Royal Rumble."
- "On December 29, 2025, the park was officially inaugurated in a ceremony under the patronage of the Governor of Riyadh Province, Faisal bin Bandar, who formally announced the opening before guests and officials in attendance. The event also featured a live performance by Alicia Keys."
- "Six Flags Qiddiya City officially opened to the public on New Year's Eve 2025, becoming the first Six Flags park in Asia and the first located outside North America since 2004 following the sale and spin-off of the former Six Flags European Division theme parks (Six Flags Holland and Six Flags Belgium) to Palamon Capital Partners (StarParks)."

## Areas

Six themed areas: Steam Town, City of Thrills, Twilight Gardens, Discovery Springs, Grand Exposition and Valley of Fortune. All rides listed are given the year 2025. (The article's ride tables list 26 attractions, while the infobox and the 2019 design announcement both give a total of 28.)

## World records claimed

| Attraction | Record | Specifications |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Falcons Flight | Tallest, fastest and longest roller coaster | Height 195 m (640 ft); top speed 250 km/h (155 mph); track length 4,250 m (2.6 mi); classified as an Exa Coaster |
| Sirocco Tower | Tallest free-standing shot tower | Height 145 m (475 ft) |
| Gyrospin | Tallest pendulum ride | Maximum swing height 53 m (173 ft) |
| Iron Rattler | Tallest tilt coaster | Height 63.4 m (208 ft); top speed 118 km/h (73 mph) |
| Spitfire | Tallest inverted triple-launch roller coaster | Height 73 m (240 ft) |

## Sources cited (selection)

Attractions Magazine, Blake Taylor, "Six Flags Qiddiya City opening planned for late 2025 with world's tallest & fastest roller coaster" (10 October 2025); Al Arabiya English, "Six Flags Qiddiya City opening date announced" (16 November 2025); Arab News, "Saudi Arabia's Qiddiya City opens Six Flags theme park" (30 December 2025); TradeArabia, "Six Flags Qiddiya City opens" (30 December 2025).

wikis.title: Steam Town
wikis.summary: The Steam Town area of Six Flags Qiddiya City and its four rides.
wikis.body:
Steam Town "is themed around 'mechanical marvels' and 'dynamic contraptions.'" All rides opened 2025.

- **Iron Rattler** (Vekoma) - "A steel tilt coaster which is the world's tallest of its kind." Records table: height 63.4 m (208 ft), top speed 118 km/h (73 mph).
- **Saw Mill Falls** (Mack Rides) - a water coaster ride.
- **Sprockenator** (Zamperla) - "A dynamic ride with rotating arms carrying gondolas."
- **Steel Stampede** (manufacturer unknown) - a spinning platform ride.

wikis.title: City of Thrills
wikis.summary: The City of Thrills area of Six Flags Qiddiya City, home of Falcons Flight and Sirocco Tower.
wikis.body:
City of Thrills "is described as a 'future city' with Arabic design motifs." All rides opened 2025.

- **Adrena-Line** (Vekoma) - a high-speed suspended coaster.
- **Falcons Flight** (Intamin) - "A steel exa coaster. It is the world's tallest, longest, and fastest roller coaster. It is the signature attraction of Six Flags Qiddiya City." Height 195 m (640 ft), top speed 250 km/h (155 mph), track length 4,250 m (2.6 mi).
- **Sirocco Tower** (S&S - Sansei Technologies) - "A drop tower ride. It is the world's tallest drop tower." Listed in the records table as the tallest free-standing shot tower at 145 m (475 ft).
- **Wind Rider** (Zamperla) - a kite flyer ride.

wikis.title: Twilight Gardens
wikis.summary: The family-oriented Twilight Gardens area of Six Flags Qiddiya City and its four rides.
wikis.body:
Twilight Gardens is "an 'oversized landscape' geared towards children and families." All rides opened 2025.

- **Amirat Al-Buhayra (Princess of the Lake)** (manufacturer unknown) - an interactive water ride.
- **Kaleidoscope Balloons** (manufacturer unknown) - a balloon race ride.
- **The Enchanted Greenhouse** (ETF Ride Systems) - a family dark ride.
- **Twilight Express** (Vekoma) - a steel family coaster.

wikis.title: Discovery Springs
wikis.summary: Discovery Springs, the aquatic desert-oasis area of Six Flags Qiddiya City, and its five rides.
wikis.body:
Discovery Springs "is the aquatic section of the park, meant to represent a desert oasis." All rides opened 2025.

- **Big Splash** (Zamperla) - a water plunge ride.
- **Into the Deep** (Triotech) - a dark ride.
- **Sea Stallion** (Maurer Rides) - a steel "rider-controlled" coaster.
- **Water Wheel** (manufacturer unknown) - a spinning family water ride.
- **Zoomaflooma** (WhiteWater West) - a log flume ride.

wikis.title: Grand Exposition
wikis.summary: The Grand Exposition area of Six Flags Qiddiya City, inspired by international exhibitions, and its five rides.
wikis.body:
Grand Exposition "is inspired by the 'innovation' and 'nostalgia' of international exhibitions." All rides opened 2025.

- **Arabian Carousel** (manufacturer unknown) - "A carousel with horses and camels which features Arabian melodies."
- **Colossus** (Great Coasters International) - a wooden hybrid coaster.
- **Expo Flyer** (manufacturer unknown) - a swing ride.
- **Gyrospin** (Zamperla) - "A 173-foot tall pendulum ride"; the records table calls it the tallest pendulum ride, maximum swing height 53 m (173 ft).
- **Roundabout** (manufacturer unknown) - a bumper car ride.

wikis.title: Valley of Fortune
wikis.summary: The Valley of Fortune adventure area of Six Flags Qiddiya City, home of the Spitfire launch coaster.
wikis.body:
Valley of Fortune is "a 'land of adventure' with a backdrop of 'time-worn architectural ruins.'" All rides opened 2025. The article's area photo is captioned "The entrance to Spitfire in the Valley of Fortune area of the park."

- **Canyon Charters** (manufacturer unknown) - an elevated swing ride.
- **Skywatch** (Intamin) - a flying tent flat ride.
- **Spitfire** (Intamin) - "A steel launch coaster. It features the tallest inversion on a roller coaster." The records table calls it the tallest inverted triple-launch roller coaster, height 73 m (240 ft).
- **Treasure Trail** (Zamperla) - a family dark ride.

wikis.title: SEA Gateway Project completion at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport
wikis.summary: Port of Seattle news release marking the completion of major construction on the $546 million SEA Gateway Project with Alaska Airlines, and listing other Upgrade SEA projects still to come.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- Dated January 28, 2026. The Port of Seattle joined Alaska Airlines "to celebrate the completion of major construction for the SEA Gateway Project today".
- The project reworked the north end of the main terminal at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA), "transforming the airport's front door and the customer experience from curb to gate", after "two years of construction walls and scaffolding".
- Subhead: "New technology, a redesigned checkpoint, bag claim upgrades, and public art improve customer experience".

## Cost and scope

- The project is described as "$546 million".
- It adds "Alaska Airlines innovation technology with the first at-scale automated bag drops", efficiency upgrades, light-filled open spaces, Bridge Level check-in, upgraded baggage claim devices, digital monitors, new art displays, a redesigned security checkpoint, upgraded restrooms, and new entry/exit doorways with safety bollards and accessibility ramps.

### Detail listed

- Redesigned Checkpoint 6: "doubled the space in front, tripled the recompose area in the back, and reconfigured the six lanes for higher efficiency."
- New Bridge Level check-in/bag drop "between Skybridges 5 and 6".
- Baggage Claim Level: "new claim devices at 15 and 16, lighting, ceiling fixtures, digital monitors, widened seating areas, and multiple art display cases."
- Drives: refreshed door portals, new access ramps at all entrances/exits "updated to meet ADA standards", longevity modifications for two glass elevators.
- Restrooms: "six more women's stalls, 4 more men's fixtures, Companion Care adult changing tables, Nursing Room, and water fountain and refill station."
- Public art: "eight major public art installations in the project: 2 on Bag Claim level, 2 on Skybridge level, and 4 on Ticketing and Esplanade level."
- Sustainability: "On track to achieve LEED Silver for Commercial Interiors certification".
- Infrastructure: "HVA, electrical, plumbing, plus fire and life safety systems."

## Quotes

- Port of Seattle Commission President Ryan Calkins: "Everyone has worked tirelessly to bring this multi-level project to life as a portal to the Pacific Northwest. This level of customer service and ease is what people have come to expect of a top-tier international airport, and together, we've delivered."
- Shane Jones, Senior Vice President of Fleet, Revenue Products and Real Estate at Alaska Airlines: "From initial planning to final construction, this project has been years in the making in partnership with the Port of Seattle - achieving the goal of reducing the time our guests spend in line at the airport. We now have an amazing space with innovative technology in our lobby that provides for a more seamless travel experience."

## Still to come and recently opened

- The completion "kicks off a year of Upgrade SEA projects finishing ahead of this summer's international soccer tournament", placed "in June".
- Coming: the C Concourse Expansion ("four new floors of amenities and services") and Roadway Improvements ("two more lanes and efficiencies into the airport garage and drives").
- Opened in the last year: redesigned Checkpoint 6 (used "prior to the winter holidays"), new Checkpoint 1 at the south end of Baggage Claim (opened in June), "$62 million went into completing Restroom Renovations on B, C, and D Concourses", and the A Concourse Expansion for Lounges.
- "93% of all passengers made it through security checkpoints in less than 20 minutes in 2024".

## Alaska Air Group boilerplate

- Alaska Airlines, Hawaiian Airlines and Horizon Air are subsidiaries of Alaska Air Group; McGee Air Services is a subsidiary of Alaska Airlines. Hubs: Seattle, Honolulu, Portland, Anchorage, Los Angeles, San Diego, San Francisco; "more than 140 destinations". "We'll serve Europe beginning in spring 2026." Hawaiian is "scheduled to join oneworld in spring 2026". NYSE ticker "ALK".

## Related item on the page

- "Updated September 11, 2026: SEA Spot Saver will no longer be available starting on November 30, 2026. All reservations booked from now until November 29 will be honored at TSA Checkpoint 4."

## Contacts

- Perry Cooper, SEA Airport, (206) 787-4923; Ray Lane, Alaska Airlines, (206) 304-0008.

- "The information that the contractor was bankrupted by the Taipei Performing Arts Centre (TPAC) was sourced from the South China Morning Post. According to other sources, the contractor was bankrupted for multiple reasons."

wikis.title: 'Marriagetoxin' gets a second season in Winter 2027
wikis.summary: MyAnimeList news item reporting that a second season of the anime Marriagetoxin is in production and is scheduled to premiere in January 2027, with details of the first season and the manga's volume releases.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- "The **13th and final episode** of *Marriagetoxin* ended with an announcement **on Tuesday** that a **second season is in production**. The official website also revealed an announcement promo."
- "The second season is scheduled to premiere on **Kansai TV and Fuji TV's new Karnival!! programming slot at 11:00 p.m. in January 2027**."
- Headline and tags call it **Winter 2027**; tags on the item: "Adapts Manga", "New Anime", "Winter 2027".

## First season

- "Produced by **Bones Film**, the first season adapting **Joumyaku** and **Mizuki Yoda**'s action manga debuted on **April 7**."
- "**Crunchyroll** streamed the series with multiple subtitles and dubs."

## Manga

- "Joumyaku and Yoda began serializing the manga on the **Shounen Jump+** web magazine in **April 2022**."
- The publisher (spelled "Shuesiha" on the page) "published the **17th volume on April 3**, with the **18th volume** planned for a **July 3** release."
- "**VIZ Media** licensed the manga for English release in **June 2023** and published the **13th volume on June 9**, with the **14th volume** scheduled for an **August 11** release."

## Synopsis (from the official site, as quoted on the page)

- The Poison Masters have perfected the art of assassination for centuries; the **Gero family** is one of the five most powerful families of Masters. **Hikaru Gero**, heir to the bloodline, has lived in the underworld far from love or marriage.
- To keep the bloodline alive the head of the Gero family declares that Hikaru's sister will be forced to bear an heir. Hikaru then crosses paths with **Mei Kinosaki**, "a brilliant marriage swindler who also happens to be his current assassination target", and asks her to help him get married. Quoted line: "...That's the first time anyone's ever proposed like that."

## Links and sourcing

- Official site: https://www.marriagetoxin-anime.com/ ; official X: @marritoxi_PR.
- "Source: animate Times". Byline "by Syureria", timestamped "Jun 30, 8:07 AM" - the page gives **no year** for that timestamp.

wikis.title: Official site of the Tougen Anki anime
wikis.summary: The Japanese official website for the Tougen Anki TV anime, covering the series' background, the second season's 2 October 2026 broadcast and streaming plan, staff, cast, music, Blu-rays and events.
wikis.body:
## Introduction

- Tougen Anki (桃源暗鬼) is a manga by Yura Urushibara (漆原侑来) serialised in Weekly Shounen Champion (週刊少年チャンピオン), Akita Shoten. It takes the folk tale Momotarou as its subject and depicts a conflict between those carrying the blood of oni and those carrying the blood of Momotarou.
- "コミックス累計部数は650万部突破" - cumulative comics circulation has passed 6.5 million copies.
- The "『桃源暗鬼』プロジェクト" started in June 2023 (2023年6月): first a stage play, second the TV anime, third a game adaptation.
- Broadcast history as stated: "2025年7月〜TVアニメ『桃源暗鬼』第一クール・京都編、10月〜TVアニメ『桃源暗鬼』第二クール・練馬編が放送。2026年10月2日より第二期 ～日光・華厳の滝編～の放送が決定。" - first cour (Kyoto arc) from July 2025, second cour (Nerima arc) from October, second season (Nikko/Kegon Falls arc) confirmed from 2 October 2026.
- Story premise: Shiki Ichinose (一ノ瀬四季), living as an ordinary human, is suddenly attacked by a mysterious man belonging to the "桃太郎機関" (Momotarou Kikan); fleeing with his foster father he learns his pursuers carry the blood of Momotarou and that he carries the blood of an oni.

## On air

- Second season "～日光・華厳の滝編～": from 2 October 2026, every Friday at 11:30 p.m. (毎週金曜よる11時30分), on the Nippon TV network's "FRIDAY ANIME NIGHT（フラアニ）" block, "全国30局ネットで放送開始" (30 stations nationwide).
- BS Nittele (ＢＳ日テレ): from 5 October, every Monday at 11:30 p.m.
- The station list runs from Sapporo Television Broadcasting and Aomori Broadcasting through Nippon Television itself to Kagoshima Yomiuri TV (30 stations listed).

## Streaming

- Early distribution (先行配信): after broadcast, fastest domestic streaming on ABEMA, d Anime Store, U-NEXT and Anime Houdai, "10月2日より毎週金曜よる24:30～".
- Subscription streaming (見放題配信): rolling out on AnimeFesta, Disney+, DMM TV, FOD, Hulu, J:COM STREAM, Lemino, milplus, Netflix, Prime Video, TELASA, WOWOW On Demand, Bandai Channel, Furatto Douga, "10月5日より毎週月曜よる24:30～".
- Rental streaming (レンタル配信): Google TV/YouTube, HAPPY!Douga, J:COM STREAM, milplus, Prime Video, TELASA, Video Market, Niconico Channel, Bandai Channel, Videx, Movie Full plus, from 5 October, Mondays 24:30.
- Latest episode free (最新話無料配信): ABEMA from 2 October, Fridays 24:30; TVer catch-up from 8 October, Thursdays 24:30.
- "※配信時間は変更の可能性があります。" - streaming times may change.

## Staff

- Original work: Yura Urushibara. Director: Ato Nonaka (野中阿斗). Composition coach: Hiroyuki Hashimoto (橋本裕之). Assistant director: Yoshitsugu Kimura (木村佳嗣). Series composition and script: Yukie Sugawara (菅原雪絵). Character design: Ryouko Amisaki (網サキ涼子). Art setting: Toshiko Kaizu (海津利子). Art director: Scott MacDonald. Colour design: Saki Tada and Maya Ooba. Director of photography: Naoki Serizawa (芹澤直樹). CG director: Ryouta Fukushima, assistant Toshiki Mako. Editing: Yumika Okazaki. Sound director: Satoki Iida (飯田里樹). Music: KOHTA YAMAMOTO. Music production: Pony Canyon (ポニーキャニオン). Animation production: Studio Hibari (スタジオ雲雀).

## Music

- Nikko/Kegon Falls arc opening: "BACKLASH" by Hiromitsu Kitayama; ending: "手と手" by TRACK15.
- Nerima arc opening: "阿弥陀籤" by 超学生; ending: "ACTION" by eill.
- First opening: "OVERNIGHT" by THE ORAL CIGARETTES; first ending: "What is justice?" by BAND-MAID. An original soundtrack is listed.

## Cast (as listed)

- 一ノ瀬四季 - 浦 和希; 無陀野無人 - 神谷浩史; 皇后崎 迅 - 西山宏太朗; 屏風ヶ浦帆稀 - 石見舞菜香; 矢颪 碇 - 坂田将吾; 遊摺部従児 - 花江夏樹; 手術岾ロクロ - 三浦 魁; 漣 水鶏 - 愛美; 花魁坂京夜 - 木村良平; 猫咲波久礼 - 岡本信彦; 印南 幽 - 伊東健人; 等々力 颯 - 梶原岳人; 鳥飼羽李 - 熊谷健太郎; 不破真一 - 長岡龍歩; 囲 岬 - 大野智敬; 百目鬼 剛 - 大畑伸太郎; 乙原響太郎 - 榊原優希; 蛭沼 灯 - 羽多野 渉; 海月巳代 - 上田 瞳; 桃裏 楔 - 鈴村健一; 桃次 歪 - 梶 裕貴; 桃尾旋律 - 谷山紀章.

## Blu-ray and events

- Blu-ray volumes 1-6 for the Kyoto and Nerima arcs (京都編&練馬編), and volumes 1-6 for the Nikko/Kegon Falls arc.
- Events announced: an original-work x anime special event (原作×アニメ スペシャルイベント); an advance screening of the Nikko/Kegon Falls arc (先行上映会); "桃源暗鬼スペシャルイベント ONI×MOMO CLASH!"; a "Nerima Premiere"; and a "ジャパンプレミア" (Japan Premiere).
- The site links an English site. It states no publication or update date.

wikis.title: Mega Machines: Taming Mechanical Giants (FD Engineering)
wikis.summary: A Free Documentary - Engineering compilation on Germany's largest machines, in two timestamped segments: tunnel boring at the Albvorlandtunnel and Liebherr mobile cranes.
wikis.body:
## What the page is
YouTube page for "Mega Machines: Taming Mechanical Giants | FD Engineering" on **Free Documentary - Engineering**, published 2023-08-06. Metadata and description only; the description sets out two timestamped segments.

## Framing
- "Huge tools make possible in a few days or hours what used to take hundreds of workers weeks or months."
- "They operate **Germany's largest and strongest machines**. With courage and sure instinct, they control machines weighing tons with millimetre precision."
- Questions posed: "What do the men have to bring along if they want to operate Germany's largest machines safely and how are such mega-aggregates manufactured?"
- "The German mechanical engineering industry is world-famous. **Men & Machines** shows why."

## Segments
- **00:00 Mole of Steel** - the Albvorlandtunnel construction site between Stuttgart and Ulm, with two huge tunnel drilling machines.
- **00:46:08 Mobile Monster Cranes** - mobile cranes, centred on the nine-axle **LTM 11200-9.1**.

## Related links in the description
"Mega Factories: Manpower Meets High-Tech" (youtu.be/DVpfAN6l5Nk); "Extreme Constructions - Complete Series" (youtu.be/XKndrP5zT-c).

- "Over the centuries, Venice has had to invent and innovate, finding new technical solutions to keep the city vital, vibrant, and dry without sacrificing its soul."

wikis.summary: A Free Documentary - Engineering video page on Rheinmetall's HX81 heavy military transporter, with its engine, weight, payload and production figures.
wikis.body:
## What the page is
YouTube page for "Rheinmetall Manufacturing: Massive Machines for Extreme Conditions | FD Engineering" on **Free Documentary - Engineering**, published 2025-02-28. Metadata and description only.

## The vehicle
- "The **HX81**, developed by **Rheinmetall**, is the German **Bundeswehr's** most powerful transport vehicle."
- "Powered by a **680 hp V8 diesel engine** and equipped with all-wheel drive across its **eight wheels**."
- "**Manufactured in Vienna**", it "measures **over ten meters** in length, weighs **23 tons when empty**, and can transport loads of **up to 130 tons** when paired with a semi-trailer."
- "Its two **25-ton winches** enable the efficient recovery and loading of disabled battle tanks."

## Service and production
- "**Since 2021**, the HX81 has been deployed by the **Austrian 14th Armored Battalion** as a heavy-duty transport solution, capable of carrying payloads of **up to 70 tons**." (Note the page gives two payload figures - up to 130 tons with a semi-trailer, up to 70 tons in Austrian service.)
- "Rheinmetall produces **up to 50 units annually**, featuring a modular design that allows for rapid adaptation to varying threat scenarios, including an **armored cab option**."

wikis.title: Inside Liebherr: Creating the Largest Mobile Cranes in the World (FD Engineering)
wikis.summary: A Free Documentary - Engineering video page on Liebherr and its LTM 1750 mobile crane, with capacity, height, price and parts-count figures.
wikis.body:
## What the page is
YouTube page for "Inside Liebherr: Creating the Largest Mobile Cranes in the World | FD Engineering" on **Free Documentary - Engineering**, published 2024-12-22. Metadata and description only.

## The company
- "The **Liebherr** family company, based in **Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany**, is the global market leader in the mobile and crawler cranes sector, with around **30,000** of the company's mobile cranes currently in service worldwide."

## The LTM 1750
- "the largest mobile crane in the world that can drive on the road with its enormous telescopic boom mounted."
- "maximum load capacity of **800 tons** with a **52-meter** telescopic boom and a maximum lift height of **152 meters**."
- "The crane consists of four elements: the carrier, the superstructure, the engine, and the telescopic boom."
- Frame sections consist of "**over 1000 individual parts** that all have to be joined together exactly according to the fabrication plan."
- "The LTM 1750 costs approximately **€4 million** and is equipped with hydraulic axle suspension."
- "The crane can maneuver on site with a load on the hook and can lift up to **1.8 tonnes** at the maximum operating radius of **160 meters**."

## Related link in the description
"Caterpillar Manufacturing - Inside the Factories Building Behemoths" (youtu.be/6I6D3TT5Vmk).
