wikis.title: 2013 L.A. Auto Show preview: what to expect
wikis.summary: Cars.com preview of the 2013 Los Angeles Auto Show, with dates, ticket prices and the world and North American debuts expected.
wikis.body:
## Dates, place and prices

- "The 2013 L.A. Auto Show is open to the public Nov. 22-Dec. 1 - with press-only events Nov. 19-21 - at the Los Angeles Convention Center, 1201 S. Figueroa St. in downtown Los Angeles."
- Hours: Nov. 22, 11 a.m.-10 p.m.; Nov. 23, 9 a.m.-10 p.m.; Nov. 24, 9 a.m.-8 p.m.; Nov. 25-27, 11 a.m.-10 p.m.; Nov. 28 (Thanksgiving), 9 a.m.-8 p.m.; Nov. 29, 9 a.m.-10 p.m.; Nov. 30, 9 a.m.-10 p.m.; Dec. 1, 9 a.m.-8 p.m.
- "Admission is $10 for visitors age 13 or older Monday through Thursday and $12 Friday and Saturday; children age 6 to 12 are $6, and 5 or younger are free with an adult; senior citizens age 65 or older are $8 (weekdays only)." Tickets online or at the door; "the show entrance closes one hour before the end of each day."

## Scale of the show

- "With an anticipated 56 world and North American debuts, visitors will get their first glimpse of some exciting models we'll all be hearing a lot about for the next five months."
- The L.A. show "is the last big show of the calendar year - but the first of the new auto-show season"; New York's hook is "most attended", Chicago's "most square footage", Detroit's "most important".
- "Also among nearly two-dozen world debuts slated for the event are the Nissan NISMO Juke RS and NISMO concept." Further world debuts expected from "four Mercedes-Benz models and two Porsche offerings, as well as others from BMW, Chevrolet, Ford, Honda, Hyundai, Jaguar, Land Rover, Mini, Subaru and Toyota."
- North American debuts: "the Mercedes-Benz GLA250 and S63; BMW 4 Series coupe, i8, i3, 5 Series sedan and 5 Series Grand Turismo; Jaguar C-X17; Cadillac Escalade; a high-performance model from Nissan; three Volkswagen offerings, including the e-Golf; and five Audi models."
- "Organizers said the 2013 lineup underscores rising trends in green technology, luxury vehicles and innovative concepts. The roster reportedly includes: more than two-dozen green vehicles from Acura, BMW, Honda, Hyundai, Mercedes-Benz, Porsche and Volkswagen; nearly 20 luxury debuts from BMW, Maserati, Mercedes-Benz and others; and in addition to the already-announced Cadillac Elmiraj concept, an anticipated dozen concept cars from Jaguar, Mercedes-Benz, Subaru, Volkswagen and Volvo."
- The range runs "from luxury vehicles such as the 2014 Porsche Macan compact crossover, a smaller cousin to the Cayenne, to less sexy but perhaps more important new models like the 2014 Honda Civic."

## The cars Cars.com says it will look for

Acura RLX Sport Hybrid SH-AWD; BMW 4 Series convertible; BMW i8; 2014 BMW 5 Series Gran Turismo; BMW Concept X4; Cadillac Elmiraj concept; 2015 Cadillac Escalade; 2014 Honda Civic; Jaguar C-X17; Kia K900; Land Rover Range Rover Long-Wheelbase; Land Rover Range Rover Autobiography Black; 2015 Mercedes-Benz GLA250; 2014 Mercedes-Benz S63; 2014 Mini Cooper Hardtop; Nissan NISMO Juke RS; Nissan NISMO concept; 2014 Porsche Macan; Volkswagen e-Golf.

## Editor's note and page dating

- "Editor's note: This post was updated to include the 2014 Mini Cooper Hardtop and the correct show dates."
- The dateline reads "By Matt Schmitz, March 5, 2015", although the article previews a show held Nov. 22-Dec. 1 (the URL path is /articles/2013/11/). The page is tagged "automatic-content-migration".
- The debut list names the "Mercedes-Benz GLA250" and "Cadillac Escalade" where the look-for list says "2015 Mercedes-Benz GLA250" and "2015 Cadillac Escalade".

wikis.title: NVIDIA SHIELD tablet and SHIELD wireless controller
wikis.summary: VideoCardz post ahead of NVIDIA's July 22nd announcement of the SHIELD Tablet and a SHIELD wireless controller, with specifications and prices.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- "On July 22nd NVIDIA will announce its own device, called SHIELD Tablet. It will be accompanied by wireless controller designed specifically for NVIDIA SHIELD family, meaning you will be able to control either SHIELD tablet or SHIELD console."
- Published Jul 18, 2014, 15:26 GMT, by WhyCry, in the Graphics news section.

## SHIELD tablet specifications as given

- "SHIELD tablet is 8 inch device with 1920x1200 resolution."
- "It has 2GB RAM, Tegra K1 SoC with 192 CUDA cores, QuadCore 2.2 GHz A15 CPU."
- "Tablet has dual speakers and 5 MPIX 'selfie' camera."

## Prices

- "The SHIELD tablet will be available in two versions, the cheaper 16GB model costs $299 and it only has WIFI connection. NVIDIA will ask you for $100 more if you decide to get a 32GB model with LTE modem on board."
- "The SHIELD controller costs $59, however I cannot confirm yet if it works with other devices".

## Tegra K1 background

- "In January NVIDIA announced its new mobile processor called Tegra K1. It is the first SoC to include a full cluster of 192 CUDA cores bringing incredible graphics performance to mobile market."
- "We had to wait 5 months to see first tablets to use this processor", with the Xiaomi MiPad named as the earlier option; "DigitalStorm recently posted a review of this particular tablet".

## Hedges and tone

- Written in the first person; the author notes SHIELD console availability in Europe is hard to come by, and the controller's compatibility with other devices is explicitly unconfirmed.

wikis.title: Apple's October 2014 event: iPad Air 2, iPad Mini 3, new Macs and an Apple Pay launch date
wikis.summary: CBS News report on Apple's 16 October 2014 Cupertino event, covering the iPad Air 2 and iPad Mini 3, updated Macs, iOS 8 and Yosemite, and the Monday launch of Apple Pay.
wikis.body:
## The event

- Apple held an event in Cupertino, California on Thursday; a photo caption shows Phil Schiller speaking "at Apple headquarters in Cupertino, Calif., Oct. 16, 2014."
- Apple unveiled the iPad Mini 3 and iPad Air 2, "touting the latter as the 'world's thinnest tablet' as the company tries to reverse lackluster demand for tablet computers."
- It also introduced updated operating software and announced Apple Pay "will launch on Monday."
- Comedian Stephen Colbert made a speaker-phone cameo "touting Apple's security features."

## Prices and availability

- iPad Air 2 "$499 and up"; iPad Mini 3 "will start at $399". Pre-orders "begin on Friday."

## Context the page gives

- Apple Pay was first announced at the iPhone 6 launch event Sept. 9; the iPhone 6 and 6 Plus "hit the market Sept. 19" and were, per Tim Cook, the fastest-selling in Apple's history, "more than 10 million units snapped up over the first weekend."
- Cook: "It's been an incredible year and tremendously busy already... This is the strongest lineup of products Apple has ever had."
- The Apple Watch "won't be available till early next year."
- Apple "sold 13.3 million iPads last quarter, down from the previous year and below Wall Street estimates"; first-half sales were "a 13 percent drop from the same period last year."
- "Since the iPad's release in 2010, more than 225 million have been sold."
- Per IDC, the iPad's share slipped "from 68 percent of the tablet market at beginning of 2012, to about 27 percent last quarter", with competition from the Samsung Galaxy Tab, Microsoft Surface and Google Nexus.
- Gartner analyst Van Baker told CNET: "The industry kind of set its expectations wrong about iPads... Everyone assumed the tablet was kind of like the phone, so the upgrade cycle would be like the phone. That's not true."
- Cook said in July he remains "bullish": "We still feel the category as a whole is in its early days, and there's still significant innovation that can be brought to the iPad, and we can do that."
- Apple is "normally intensely secretive... even imposing a $50 million penalty on vendors who leak information", but iPad details "had been widely reported"; on Wednesday Apple "prematurely posted photos of the iPad Air 2 and iPad Mini 3 on the iTunes website, then quickly took them down."

## Note on an internal inconsistency

- The article attributes to CNET that "the new Mini features a fourth-generation Intel Core processor as well as upgraded Wi-Fi and graphic abilities" in the paragraph about the iPad Mini 3; the CNET quote immediately following in the same passage is about the Mac Mini.

wikis.title: iPad Air 2
wikis.summary: Apple's new full-size tablet, pitched as the world's thinnest, at $499 and up.
wikis.body:
- Phil Schiller, Apple's senior VP of worldwide marketing, said the iPad Air 2 is 6.1 millimetres thick with a new anti-reflective coating, "a first for a tablet".
- Better camera and faster processor, with a "new-generation A8X chip".
- "For the first time on an iPad, you can take time lapse and slo-motion video."
- Includes a Touch ID fingerprint sensor.
- "$499 and up"; pre-orders begin Friday.
- Called the "world's thinnest tablet".

wikis.title: iPad Mini 3
wikis.summary: A slightly updated small iPad starting at $399, in silver, space gray and gold.
wikis.body:
- "A slightly updated iPad Mini 3", in silver, space gray and gold.
- Citing CNET, the article says "the new Mini features a fourth-generation Intel Core processor as well as upgraded Wi-Fi and graphic abilities" (stated in the iPad Mini 3 paragraph, alongside a CNET quote about the Mac Mini).
- Has a Touch ID fingerprint sensor, "a feature that's been available on iPhones since last year."
- Starts at $399; pre-orders begin Friday.

wikis.title: Apple Pay launch
wikis.summary: Apple's mobile payments system was given a Monday launch date, with 500 banks signed up.
wikis.body:
- Apple Pay "will launch on Monday".
- Tim Cook said 500 banks and many of the largest retailers in the world have agreed to support it.
- It is also available on the iPhone 6 and 6 Plus, and was first announced at the iPhone 6 launch event Sept. 9.
- On iPhones it uses NFC (near-field communication) to transmit secure payments to participating retailers.
- Partners named: American Express (AXP), Mastercard (MA), Visa (V); Apple says it "will work at more than 220,000 retailers nationwide, including Walgreens, McDonald's, Disney, Target, Subway, Whole Foods and other major chains."
- Apple "may be seeking to broaden the iPad's functionality by incorporating Apple Pay technology" for in-app shopping.

wikis.title: Mac updates
wikis.summary: Apple updated its Mac line, including an iMac with a Retina 5K display and a refreshed Mac Mini.
wikis.body:
- Schiller announced the high-resolution Retina 5K display is coming to the iMac: an "iMac with the most incredible display we've ever made."
- A photo caption says Apple unveiled "a Mac with 5K retina display".
- CNET senior writer Shara Tibken on the Mac Mini: "The Mac Mini hadn't been refreshed for two years... The device is Apple's most affordable computer, and it has a cult following."

wikis.title: iOS 8 and OS X Yosemite
wikis.summary: Craig Federighi showed off iOS 8, the updated Mac operating system Yosemite, and Continuity.
wikis.body:
- Craig Federighi, senior VP of Mac Software Engineering, showed the new features of iOS 8 and Yosemite, calling them the "most advanced operating system on the planet."
- "What really sets iOS apart is the incredible technologies it puts in the hands of our developers."
- He touted "Continuity" features, which allow users to "start on one device and pick up on another", showing photos favorited on his iPhone appearing on his iPad.

wikis.title: The Exorcist: Martyrs
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on The Exorcist: Martyrs, Mike Flanagan's upcoming seventh Exorcist film, covering its premise, cast, the abandoned Deceiver sequels, filming and its 12 March 2027 release.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- "The Exorcist: Martyrs is an upcoming American supernatural horror film written and directed by Mike Flanagan. It is the seventh film in The Exorcist franchise."
- "Jason Blum serves as a producer through his Blumhouse - Atomic Monster banner, David Robinson through his Morgan Creek Entertainment studio, and Flanagan through Red Room Pictures."
- "The film is scheduled to be released by Universal Pictures on March 12, 2027." Country: United States. Language: English.
- Infobox credits: directed and written by Mike Flanagan; based on characters by William Peter Blatty; produced by Jason Blum, David Robinson and Mike Flanagan; cinematography by Michael Fimognari; edited by Mike Flanagan. Production companies: Blumhouse Productions, Atomic Monster, Morgan Creek Entertainment, Red Room Pictures. Distributed by Universal Pictures.
- Summary of the path to production: "Prior to the project's announcement, a sequel was planned for The Exorcist: Believer (2023) entitled The Exorcist: Deceiver, with David Gordon Green originally set to return as director, but he left the project following the critical and commercial failure of Believer. In May 2024, Deceiver and its sequel were officially canceled when the new film was announced ... After two release delays, casting took place throughout November 2025 to March 2026, when principal photography began in New York City, and wrapped in June."

## Premise (quoted from Comic Book Movie)

"A single-mother cop who, 13 years after taking down a notorious satanic serial killer, investigates a new series of murders connected to her past while her 12-year-old son becomes the target of a terrifying demonic force."

## Cast

Infobox starring list: Scarlett Johansson, Chiwetel Ejiofor, Jacobi Jupe, Sasha Calle, Hamish Linklater, Carl Lumbly, John Gallagher Jr., Benjamin Pajak, Carla Gugino, John Leguizamo, Diane Lane, Laurence Fishburne.

The cast section gives only one role: "John Leguizamo as Father Sunday, an infamous satanic serial killer", then lists Rahul Kohli, Gil Bellows, Robert Longstreet, Matt Biedel, Samantha Sloyan and Kate Siegel without roles. Elsewhere the article reports that "Ejiofor would play an 'ex-con turned priest' whereas Johansson would play the mother of Jupe's character."

## Development as Deceiver

- "In July 2021, two sequels to The Exorcist: Believer (2023) were confirmed to be in development with the same creative team of David Gordon Green, Danny McBride, Peter Sattler, and Scott Teems on board. Two years later, Universal Pictures announced that the first sequel would be titled The Exorcist: Deceiver."
- "After the poor reception of Believer, sources from The Hollywood Reporter claimed there would almost certainly be some degree of creative re-think for the next two films and that Green recently expressed some doubt about his participation. In January 2024, Green stepped down from Deceiver and the film was removed from the release schedule shortly after."

## Development as Martyrs

- "In May 2024, it was announced that Mike Flanagan was in talks to write, produce and direct the next The Exorcist film. Later that month, Flanagan was confirmed to be doing so for a new Exorcist film to be made as a 'new radical take' with plans for Deceiver and its sequel being scrapped."
- Flanagan said he had been "very aggressively" chasing the job, "seeing an opportunity to do something that had never been done within the series, honoring what had come before but without building it on nostalgia", and saw "a chance to make the scariest film he had ever made".
- Because of the commitment, Flanagan "was unavailable to direct the Clayface (2026) film he had written set in the DC Universe (DCU) for James Gunn and Peter Safran, leading them to hire James Watkins".
- "In June 2025, Flanagan revealed in a Tumblr post that the film was not going to begin production until after he finished work on the 2026 miniseries adaptation of Stephen King's novel Carrie (1974) for Amazon Prime Video and that there was 'no way it's coming out next March'."
- Casting: Scarlett Johansson in the lead role in November 2025, when Atomic Monster also joined the production team; Jacobi Jupe in December 2025; Diane Lane in January 2026; Chiwetel Ejiofor and Laurence Fishburne in February 2026; Sasha Calle and John Leguizamo in March 2026 "alongside Rahul Kohli, Hamish Linklater, Gil Bellows, Carl Lumbly, John Gallagher Jr., Benjamin Pajak, Carla Gugino, Robert Longstreet, Matt Biedel, Samantha Sloyan and Kate Siegel, all eleven frequent collaborators of Flanagan."
- "In December 2025, Jeff Sneider reported that Johansson's commitments to the film had been adjusted to accommodate the schedule of The Batman: Part II (2028), for which she had entered negotiations to discuss an undisclosed role she was 'aggressively' pursuing."
- "In June 2026, the official Red Room Pictures website revealed the film's title as The Exorcist: Martyrs."

## Filming

"Principal photography began in New York City on March 13, 2026, with Michael Fimognari serving as the cinematographer. Filming wrapped on June 9, 2026."

## Release

"The film is scheduled to be released in the United States on March 12, 2027, by Universal Pictures. It was previously scheduled to be released on April 18, 2025, and March 13, 2026, before being removed from Universal's release schedule in June 2025."

## Sources cited (selection)

Comic Book Movie, Mark Cassidy, "The Exorcist: Martyrs - First Synopsis And Character Details For Mike Flanagan's Horror Reboot Revealed" (September 12, 2026); Deadline, "Mike Flanagan In Talks To Direct Next 'Exorcist' Movie For Blumhouse, Universal" (May 2, 2024); The Hollywood Reporter, "Next 'Exorcist' Movie Shifts Gears With Mike Flanagan Set to Direct a New Take" (May 29, 2024).

wikis.title: Four new accessible CTA Red Line stations to open July 20, 2025
wikis.summary: CTA press release announcing that the rebuilt Lawrence, Argyle, Berwyn and Bryn Mawr Red Line stations will open on July 20, 2025 as part of the $2.1 billion Red and Purple Modernization Phase One project.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- "Mayor **Brandon Johnson** today announced that four fully reconstructed Red Line stations in **Edgewater and Uptown** will open on **Sunday, July 20, 2025**, as part of the CTA's historic **$2.1 billion** Red and Purple Modernization (RPM) Phase One Project."
- Subhead: "CTA to open Red Line stations at Lawrence, Argyle, Berwyn and Bryn Mawr with elevators and escalators as the agency nears completion of the Red and Purple Modernization (RPM) Phase One Project".
- "Major project construction will be completed this year."
- "The opening of four new contiguous stations marks the first time that this many stations have opened simultaneously since the **Orange Line in 1993**."

## Quotes

- Mayor Johnson: "With the RPM improvements, the Red Line on the North Side is more accessible to all Chicagoans... The Red Line is the backbone of our City and is critical to our economic vibrancy, which is why I am proud to support investments like RPM and the future Red Line Extension Project on the Far South Side."
- CTA Acting President **Nora Leerhsen**: "We are proud to bring new, accessible Red Line stations to our customers... By opening these four stations that will be accessible to customers with disabilities, we move closer to our goal of having all of our CTA stations fully accessible." She thanks "Senators Durbin and Duckworth and the rest of the Illinois Congressional delegation".

## The stations

- **Lawrence**: 1120 W. Lawrence Ave., Chicago, IL 60640
- **Argyle**: 1118 W. Argyle St., Chicago, IL 60640
- **Berwyn**: 1119 W. Berwyn St., Chicago, IL 60640
- **Bryn Mawr**: 1116 W. Bryn Mawr Ave., Chicago, IL 60640
- **Bryn Mawr - Hollywood entrance**: 1119 W. Hollywood Ave., Chicago, IL 60640
- Amenities: "elevators and escalators at main stationhouse entrances; wider platforms; large translucent overhead canopies for increased protection from inclement weather; platform benches; and turnstiles and Ventra fare machines."
- "Temporary CTA Argyle and Bryn Mawr stations currently serving customers during construction will close when the new stations open."

## Track and signals

- New track, support structures, bridges and viaducts along the **1.3-mile Lawrence to Bryn Mawr corridor**, replacing century-old deteriorated structures.
- The new track bridge design improves sightlines at cross streets "with the elimination of columns in the middle of the street"; the new elevated structure is built higher to meet modern clearance standards.
- The new signal system "replaces a more than **60-year-old** system".

## RPM Phase One overview

- "RPM Phase One Project construction began in **2019**" and has three major components:
  1. Reconstruction of the Lawrence, Argyle, Berwyn and Bryn Mawr stations into larger, fully accessible stations, and replacement of track structure "totaling **six track-miles**".
  2. New **Red-Purple Bypass** construction (completed in **2021**) and reconstruction of Red and Purple Line track structure between **Belmont and Newport/Cornelia**.
  3. Installation of a new signal system on **23 track miles** between **Howard and Belmont**.

## Public space under the 'L' tracks

- Follows the demolition of 1.3 miles of century-old concrete embankment wall.
- "CTA plans to develop **10 blocks** of open space located under the new Red and Purple Line tracks between **Lawrence and Ardmore** avenues based on input from the community."
- Design plans include "a pedestrian trail, dog parks, playground, fitness area, benches, and flexible-use plaza space for community events."
- "Construction is expected to begin in **2026** and be completed in **2027**."

## The Red Line and RPM

- "The CTA's Red Line is CTA's busiest rail line, providing nearly **40 million rides in 2024**."
- RPM is a multi-phase programme that "will rebuild the **9.6-mile** stretch of Red and Purple Line track structure and stations on the North Side that are a century old."
- More at transitchicago.com/RPM.

## The retailer

- "Moon Audio is an authorized Astell&Kern dealer." CEO **Drew Baird, P.E.** "carefully selects and curates each product in this collection".
- Promises listed: engineer-vetted products; "A broad lineup of portable hi-fi equipment, including A&ultima flagship DAPs, PD Series players, IEMs, amplifiers, DACs, and accessories"; genuine equipment with full manufacturer warranty; white-glove concierge guidance; educational guides and comparisons.
- Site banner: "FREE SHIPPING on US orders over $99"; "International Orders $399 & Up: Use 'World20' To Save $20".

## About Astell&Kern

- "Astell&Kern's story began in **South Korea in 2013**, when **iRiver** debuted the **AK100** digital audio player. They later released the **AKR01** in-ear monitors (IEMs) to use with the DAP."
- "iRiver specifically coined the name Astell&Kern in **October of 2013** to develop their in-house products."
- "Today, the brand is best known for their high-end music players and hi-res portable audio devices." Products are described as having "a futuristic feel and look ... modern metal aesthetics, sharp edges, and sleek designs".

## Product lineup as described

- **Flagship reference players**: "Models such as the **A&ultima SP4000 and SP4000T**, and the **A&ultima SP3000M** represent the flagship end of the lineup".
- **Tube and solid-state**: "The **SP4000T** ... offering a tube-driven signal path for those seeking a different listening presentation."
- **Portable players**: "Portable models such as the **PD10 and PD20**".
- **In-ear monitors**: "including the **NOVUS**, **XIO**, and **Luna**".
- **Amps, DACs and accessories**: "the **HC5 Portable USB DAC Headphone Amp** and **AK PA10 Amplifier**", plus a **DAP Docking Cradle**.
- Pairing recommendation throughout: Moon Audio's own **Dragon Audio Cables**.

## Contradiction within the page

- The body names the flagship A&ultima players as "SP4000 and **SP4000T**" plus the SP3000M. The linked buying-guide blurb at the foot of the page instead describes "flagship A&ultima players (**SP4000, SP3000T**) down to entry-level A&norma DAPs (**SR35**)". The body never mentions the A&norma SR35 or an SP3000T.

## Shipping, warranty and support

- "All eligible products include full manufacturer warranty coverage and support."
- "In-stock products typically ship within **1 business day**. Special orders require an additional **5 days** to process and fulfill."

## FAQ

- **What is a DAP**: "a dedicated device designed to store and play digital music files, particularly high-resolution and lossless formats", with hardware optimized for high-fidelity listening rather than a smartphone's general purpose.
- **High-resolution audio**: "CD audio uses a **44.1 kHz** sample rate and **16-bit** depth, while hi-res audio typically uses a higher sample rate, bit depth, or both."
- **Memory cards**: "According to the supplied collection information, current-generation **Octa-Core and Quad-Core** Astell & Kern players officially support microSD cards **up to 1TB**. Previous-generation models officially support cards **up to 512GB**."
- **Streaming**: Wi-Fi-enabled players can support streaming, "with available services depending on the player and its software support"; models with Astell&Kern's **OpenApp** service can support compatible streaming applications, and compatibility "can vary by model and region".
- **AK Connect**: "allows compatible Astell&Kern players to stream music stored elsewhere on your network, such as on a computer, music server, or network-attached storage (NAS) device. It uses the **DLNA** networking protocol".

## Linked guide

- "Astell&Kern DAP, IEM & Gear Buying Guide" at https://www.moon-audio.com/blogs/expert-advice/astell-kern-guide-page - said to cover the brand's history, "proprietary **TERATON ALPHA** sound tech, streaming/Roon support, and Dragon cable pairing recommendations for each device".

wikis.title: Sydney Metro Southwest project update, October 2024
wikis.summary: Four-page Sydney Metro community newsletter on the final conversion shutdown of the T3 Bankstown Line, the opening of Sydney Metro City, replacement Southwest Link buses and the testing programme ahead of Sydenham-Bankstown metro services.
wikis.body:
## Document

- "Sydney Metro City & Southwest", sydneymetro.info - "Southwest Metro project update, **October 2024**" (PDF, 4 pages). Footer: "© Sydney Metro 2024. 24130-CSW 09.24".
- Banner line: "Sydney Metro City is now open."

## Final conversion shutdown

- "The **T3 Bankstown Line** between **Sydenham and Bankstown** was closed on **Monday 30 September** to enable the final conversion of the **130-year-old** line to modern metro standards."
- "Travel on replacement bus services, known as **Southwest Link**, is free for all passengers for the entire conversion period, **until the estimated completion date of late 2025**."
- The shutdown is needed for works that can only be done once Sydney Trains services stop - installing platform screen doors, upgrading tracks and corridor, and train testing and commissioning.
- When complete, passengers get "a 21st century high-tech metro line with a **train every four minutes during the peak**", fully accessible stations and services.

## Sydney Metro City

- "Sydney Metro City officially opened on **Monday 19 August 2024**."
- "Within the first four weeks of the city section opening between **Chatswood and Sydenham**, more than **five million metro trips** were taken on the new **M1 Northwest and City Line**, averaging **200,000 trips per weekday** and **99.36 per cent** of services ran on time."
- City services run "every four minutes in the peak, five minutes during the interpeak ... and every 10 minutes during off peak and on the weekend."

## Southwest Link buses

- Stations between Sydenham and Bankstown "have closed for **around 12 months**"; key features: three dedicated bus routes (SW1, SW2, SW3); "a bus every **two to four minutes** in peak periods across some routes"; a mix of all-stops and limited-stops services. Frequencies given as "Every 2 to 4 minutes during peak periods / At least every 10 minutes across most of the day / At least every 15 minutes late at night".
- All routes use low-floor accessible buses. Travel is free for the duration of the final conversion; fares still apply on regular train, bus, ferry and light rail, and Opal benefits still apply.
- Parking arrangements near impacted stations change "across the **12 month** final conversion period".

## Project timeline (as printed)

- Southwest EIS exhibition - 2017; Southwest SPIR exhibition - July 2018; Southwest Metro project approved - December 2018; Early works - 2019-2020; Construction - Late 2020 onwards.
- "Sydney Metro services begin between Chatswood and Sydenham - **August 2024**"; "Closure of T3 Bankstown Line for **up to 12 months** for final metro works - **30 September 2024**" ("We are here"); "Sydney Metro services begin between Sydenham and Bankstown - **2025**"; "Final precinct and cycling upgrade works completed - **2025-2026**".

## Construction lookahead

- First two months focus on: installing platform screen doors at all stations between **Marrickville and Bankstown**; installing "the remaining **81 (of 170)** mechanical gap fillers across **eight stations**"; new vertical screen barriers, low traffic barriers on kerb edges or adjacent security fencing "at **eight station bridges, seven corridor bridges and 66 non bridges**"; removing and replacing station fencing; final adjustments to overhead wiring and tracks.
- Then, during testing and commissioning: refurbishing station buildings and platform surfaces, tactiles and wayfinding signage, public domain finishes (landscaping, footpath rectification, bike parking, lighting), bollards and barriers at entrances, painting and repairs, and commissioning and testing of equipment.

## Completed work

- Sydenham Station upgrade - new pedestrian concourse and Burrows Avenue entrance now open.
- New lifts open at **Wiley Park, Dulwich Hill, Hurlstone Park, Punchbowl and Canterbury**.
- New pedestrian footbridge at Dulwich Hill connecting to the light rail station.
- Public art and glazing complete at Sydenham, Marrickville, Dulwich Hill, Hurlstone Park, Canterbury, Campsie, Belmore, Wiley Park and Punchbowl.
- Renewed pedestrian concourse and shopfronts at Campsie; new public plaza next to Belmore Station now open.
- New Kiss and Ride zones at Sydenham, Dulwich Hill, Hurlstone Park, Canterbury, Campsie, Belmore, Lakemba, Wiley Park and Punchbowl.
- "**89 of 170** mechanical gap fillers are now installed across Marrickville, Dulwich Hill, Canterbury and Campsie stations."

## Active transport

- "A permanent active transport link running between Sydenham and Bankstown will be ready for cyclists and pedestrians **a year after Southwest Metro services opening**."
- The new **Southwest Active Transport Link** will feature extra footpaths, new separated cycleways, shared zones and designated crossings.
- "An interim cycleway and pedestrian path between **Sydenham and Marrickville** stations has opened".
- Also: designated bike parking, additional share bikes, directional signage and reduced speed zones.

## Security

- A "high-tech new intrusion detection security system will be installed between Sydenham and Bankstown": fibre optic cables on the rail corridor security fence trigger an alert to the **Sydney Metro Operational Control Centre (OCC)** on contact, and CCTV cameras inside the corridor automatically point at the impacted fence section.

## Testing and commissioning

1. **Low speed manual testing** - trains manually driven at a maximum of **25km/h**, testing acceleration, braking, functionality and reliability.
2. **Loaded testing** - trains "filled with over one hundred 1000-litre water containers to simulate the weight of a fully loaded train".
3. **High speed automated testing** - automated trains reaching a maximum of **110km/h**.
4. **Trial running** - the line is handed to the operator to run trains to a full working timetable with operational and customer checks.
5. **Passenger services begin** - Southwest Metro opens to passengers.

- The programme precedes a safety assessment and approval by "the independent national rail safety regulator", following a similar process to the Chatswood-Sydenham testing.
- "A series of weekend and overnight possessions are expected to take place on the City metro line to integrate the network with the metro extension to Bankstown. Specific dates will be provided closer to the time."
- Some works not required for operations - precinct works, upgrades outside the rail corridor, fencing and access improvements - "may continue being delivered after the metro becomes operational".

## Contact

- Community infoline 1800 171 386 (open 24 hours); sydneymetro@transport.nsw.gov.au; PO Box K659, Haymarket NSW 1240. Translating and Interpreting Service on 131 450.

wikis.title: How to Train Your Dragon 2 (2027 film)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the live-action How to Train Your Dragon 2, the 2027 DreamWorks/Universal sequel directed by Dean DeBlois, covering its cast, production, filming and release date.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- "How to Train Your Dragon 2 is an upcoming American fantasy adventure film and a live-action remake of the 2014 animated film by DreamWorks Animation, itself loosely based on Cressida Cowell's book series. It will be the second installment of the live-action How to Train Your Dragon film series following How to Train Your Dragon (2025), and the fifth film overall in the franchise."
- "Written and directed by Dean DeBlois, the film stars Mason Thames, Nico Parker, Gabriel Howell, Julian Dennison, Bronwyn James, Harry Trevaldwyn, Nick Frost, and Gerard Butler, all reprising their roles from the first film, with Cate Blanchett reprising her role as Valka from the animated films and Olafur Darri Olafsson joining the cast alongside Phil Dunster."
- "How to Train Your Dragon 2 is scheduled to be theatrically released in the United States by Universal Pictures on June 11, 2027."
- Infobox credits: directed by and screenplay by Dean DeBlois; based on *How to Train Your Dragon* by Cressida Cowell; produced by Marc Platt and Adam Siegel; cinematography Bill Pope; edited by Paul Machliss; music by John Powell. Production companies DreamWorks Animation and Marc Platt Productions; distributed by Universal Pictures. Country United States, language English. Runtime, budget and gross are not stated (placeholder comments requiring a reliable source).
- The infobox starring list is shorter than the lead's: Mason Thames, Nico Parker, Nick Frost, Olafur Darri Olafsson, Phil Dunster, Cate Blanchett, Gerard Butler.

## Cast

- **Mason Thames** as Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III, "the son of Valka and Stoick the Vast, and Astrid's boyfriend-turned-husband".
- **Nico Parker** as Astrid Hofferson, "Hiccup's girlfriend-turned-wife".
- **Cate Blanchett** as Valka, "Hiccup's long-lost mother and Stoick's wife, who lives as a hermit protecting dragons"; reprising her role from the animated films.
- **Gerard Butler** as Stoick the Vast, "Berk's chieftain, Hiccup's father and Valka's husband"; also reprising his animated role.
- **Nick Frost** as Gobber the Belch, "Berk's blacksmith and Stoick's best friend and advisor with customizable prosthetics that go over where his right hand used to be".
- **Olafur Darri Olafsson** as Drago Bludvist, "a ruthless warlord and dragon hunter who seeks to take over the world with a dragon army". He "previously voiced Ragnar the Rock in How to Train Your Dragon: The Hidden World (2019), the third animated film."
- **Phil Dunster** as Eret, son of Eret, "a dragon trapper who sells captured dragons to Drago".
- **Gabriel Howell** as Snotlout Jorgenson, Hiccup's rival.
- **Julian Dennison** as Fishlegs Ingerman, "Hiccup's best friend who is obsessed with memorizing dragon statistics".
- **Bronwyn James** as Ruffnut Thorston and **Harry Trevaldwyn** as Tuffnut Thorston, twin siblings.

## Development

- "On April 2, 2025, during CinemaCon, it was announced that a sequel to How to Train Your Dragon (2025) was in development, with Dean DeBlois returning to write and direct."
- "In January 2026, it was revealed that most of the cast would return from the first film, with Cate Blanchett reprising her role as Valka from the animated films and Olafur Darri Olafsson joining the cast as Drago Bludvist."
- "Phil Dunster joined the cast as Eret, son of Eret later that same month."

## Filming

- "Principal photography began on January 26, 2026, at Sky Studios Elstree in London, as announced by DeBlois on Instagram, and it was expected to wrap in April. DeBlois revealed that filming had wrapped on May 15." (A cited April 2025 CinemaHolic article is headed "How to Train Your Dragon 2 Starts Filming in Belfast in January 2026", naming a different location.)
- "In April 2026, while the film was in production, a special effects technician severed multiple fingers in an incident involving a saw in a workshop at Sky Studios Elstree."

## Sources cited (selection)

Deadline, "'How To Train Your Dragon 2' Live-Action Sequel Happening, Set For 2027 - CinemaCon" (April 2, 2025); The Hollywood Reporter, Borys Kit, "Cate Blanchett Returning as Valka for Universal's Live-Action Remake" (January 15, 2026); Deadline, Justin Kroll, "Olafur Darri Olafsson Joins Universal's Live-Action 'How To Train Your Dragon 2' As Drago" (January 16, 2026); KATV, "'How to Train Your Dragon 2' crew member severed multiple fingers during production" (April 22, 2026).

wikis.title: AMD says Helios racks and MI400 series GPUs on track for 2H 2026
wikis.summary: The Next Platform report on AMD executives rejecting a SemiAnalysis claim of Helios rack delays, with detail on the MI400 series lineup and how ZT Systems' engineering model de-risks the rack.
wikis.body:
## The dispute over timing

- SemiAnalysis, in a report accompanying an update to its **InferenceX** AI inference benchmark (formerly **InferenceMax**), wrote: "Engineering samples and low volume production of AMD's first rack scale **MI455X UALoE72** system will be in **H2 2026**, while due to manufacturing delays, the mass production ramp and first production tokens will only be generated on an MI455X UALoE72 by **Q2 2027**."
- The article says this "was a bit perplexing", since AMD "did not mention any delays in its most recent quarterly results from a few weeks ago", results posted on **February 3**, and such a material delay "would run the company afoul of the US Securities and Exchange Commission should it have been true at the time". "The further rumors on the street were that the Helios rack system delays were due to some **thermal issue** in the design."
- On a **New Street Research** conference call "last week", **Forrest Norrod**, general manager of the Data Center Solutions business group, rejected this: "I have no idea where this purported issue around thermals is coming from... We have no significant thermal issue. The risk around the thermal design at the component level all the way through the rack level was retired quite some time ago... Lisa showed the first silicon, we are right on track with where we thought we would be, both in terms of the readiness of the overall solution as well as the readiness of the silicon. And we are **highly confident of ramping Helios in high volume in the second half of the year**."
- SemiAnalysis "declared correctly that thus far only **Nvidia, AWS, and Google** have created rackscale systems that are deployed today, and that AMD was working on it." Named platforms: Nvidia's "Oberon" NVL72 with "Blackwell" B200 and B300; AWS Trainium2 and Trainium3; Google's seven generations of TPU systems (with a caveat that TPU v1-v3 used hard-wired torus interconnects and only TPU v4 introduced the "Palomar" optical circuit switch).

## Helios and the MI400 series

- AMD has been working with **Meta Platforms** on the **Open Rack Wide v3** specification, "a double-wide rack that AMD calls **Helios**".
- Helios is "the platform for delivering rackscale compute based on the '**Altair**' **MI400 series** GPU accelerators. This series includes the **MI450**, the **MI430X**, and the **MI455X** for the Helios rackscale systems, which will have **64, 72, or 128 GPUs per system**, and possibly the **MI440X** for eight-way system nodes."

## ZT Systems and the manufacturing model

- **Doug Huang**, a co-founder of **ZT Systems** - "acquired by AMD last year to underpin its rackscale system engineering efforts" - is now senior vice president in charge of the Data Center Platform Engineering group.
- AMD "spent **$4.9 billion** to acquire ZT Systems back in **August 2024**", and "sold the manufacturing arm of ZT Systems to **Sanmina** for **$3 billion** last fall". ZT Systems was "a $10 billion system manufacturer with rackscale system cred when AMD bought it".
- The article is "reasonably certain" the initial Helios New Product Introduction (NPI) partner "is none other than Sanmina".
- Huang explained they "use what amounts to dummy hot plates to simulate the CPUs and GPUs long before they come back from the fabs" so the thermals and physical specs are known in advance - what he called "early risk retirement".
- Every component is tested, then tested when assembled into racks, then the racks are tested before shipping, and the shipping process itself is tested.
- Huang: "The factories nowadays are really extensions to the labs, because we go so fast that we don't have the time that we have had before to do everything in series... it is super-important to have an environment and a partner understands that, and that the supply chain has so many components in this complex solution."

## Context given

- Helios "may be AMD's first rackscale design, just like the NVL36 and NVL72 rackscale machines that were supposed to be based on Hopper were - and never came to market except for one machine sold to AWS. But this is not the first rackscale machine that ZT Systems has developed, and it is not the first one for Meta Platforms, either, which started the **Open Compute Project** back in **2011**."
- Article tags: amd, zt systems, rackscale, open rack wide v3, mi455x, mi400, meta platforms, helios, gpu, compute.

wikis.title: AMD takes the AI fight to Nvidia with the Helios rack-scale system
wikis.summary: The Register's report on AMD's Q3 2025 earnings call, where CEO Lisa Su said the Helios rack-scale architecture and MI400 series GPUs launch in 2026 and detailed the quarter's segment results.
wikis.body:
## Helios and MI400

- "AMD plans to launch its **Helios** rack-scale architecture in **2026** as a direct challenge to Nvidia in the AI infrastructure market, pending successful integration of its next-gen GPUs and processors."
- President & CEO **Dr Lisa Su** said the datacenter AI business is to enter "its next phase of growth", with customer interest building ahead of the launch of the **MI400 series** GPU accelerators and Helios "next year".
- AMD showed off Helios "in June, at an event in **San Jose, California**". It "is designed to operate a rack full of accelerators as if they were one single large GPU, like Nvidia's **DGX GB200 NVL72** system."
- Su: "Helios integrates our **Instinct MI400 Series GPUs**, **Epyc Venice CPUs** and **Pensando NICs** in a double-wide rack solution optimized for the performance, power, cooling and serviceability required for the next generation of AI infrastructure and supports **Meta's new open rack wide standard**."
- "**Venice** is the codename for AMD's 6th-gen Epyc CPUs, set to be produced using **TSMC's 2nm** manufacturing process, also due next year."
- Su: "Development of both our MI400 Series GPUs and Helios rack is progressing rapidly, supported by deep technical engagements across a growing set of hyperscalers, AI companies and OEM and ODM partners to enable large-scale deployments next year."
- The **ZT Systems** team, "a maker of high-performance servers for cloud operators that AMD acquired last year", is "playing a critical role in Helios development".
- On the **MI450**: customers "will buy them as part of the rack-scale solutions. 'We will have other form factors as well for the MI450 Series, but there's a lot of interest in the full rack-scale solution.'"

## CPU demand and the OpenAI deal

- Su: "A number of our large hyperscale clients are now forecasting significant CPU build into 2026... it is a positive demand environment, and it is because AI is requiring quite a bit of general-purpose compute."
- **Timothy Arcuri** of UBS Investment Bank asked about AMD's **OpenAI** agreement "announced last month": "It looks like they could be something like **half of your datacenter GPU revenue in the 2027, 2028 time frame**. So how much risk... is there around that single customer for you?"
- Su said the deal "had been in the works for quite some time" and AMD is happy with the planned scale: "I think we're dimensioning the supply chain in such a way that we would have ample supply to have multiple customers at similar scale as we go into the '27, '28 time frame, and that's certainly the goal."
- CFO **Jean Hu**: "We're not guiding 2026, but our priority in datacenter GPU business is to really expand the top line revenue growth and the gross margin dollars."

## Q3 2025 results (quarter ended September 27)

- Overall revenue grew **36 percent to $9.2 billion** year on year.
- **Datacenter**: revenue up **22 percent to $4.3 billion**, attributed to sales of **Instinct MI350 series** GPUs and server share gains.
- Server CPU revenue "reached an all-time high, driven by rapid adoption of AMD's **5th Gen Epyc Turin** processors, which accounted for **nearly half** of overall Epyc revenue during the quarter."
- **Client and gaming**: revenue up **73 percent to $4 billion**; Su: "Our PC processor business is performing exceptionally well with record quarterly sales as breadth of our leadership Ryzen portfolio accelerates growth."
- **Embedded**: revenue declined **8 percent year-on-year to $857 million**, though AMD says it is on track for "a second straight year of record design wins".
- **Q4 2025 outlook**: revenue of **$9.6 billion, plus or minus $300 million**, "which would represent year-on-year growth of roughly **25 percent**". "The firm said that its current outlook does not include any revenue from AMD Instinct **MI308** shipments to China."

## Related links on the page

- "Stargate is nowhere near big enough to make OpenAI's tie-ups with AMD and Nvidia work"; "Microsoft CTO says he wants to swap most AMD and Nvidia GPUs for homemade chips"; "AMD tries to catch CUDA with performance-boosting ROCm 7 software".

wikis.title: FDA approves Lilly's Foundayo (orforglipron) for weight loss
wikis.summary: Eli Lilly news release of 1 April 2026 announcing FDA approval of Foundayo (orforglipron), an oral GLP-1 pill for obesity, with its trial results, pricing, availability and safety information.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- "INDIANAPOLIS, April 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY) today announced the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Foundayo (orforglipron) for adults with obesity, or overweight with weight-related medical problems."
- Headline: "the only GLP-1 pill for weight loss that can be taken any time of day without food or water restrictions".
- "When used alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity, Foundayo helps individuals lose excess body weight and keep the weight off."
- "Foundayo will be available via LillyDirect, with prescriptions accepted immediately and shipping beginning April 6, followed shortly after by broad availability through U.S. retail pharmacies and telehealth providers."
- It is "Lilly's second FDA-approved obesity medicine".

## Trial results cited

- Headline bullet: "Adults taking Foundayo lost an average of 27 pounds on the highest dose in the ATTAIN-1 clinical trial".
- "In the ATTAIN-1 trial, individuals taking the highest dose of Foundayo and who stayed on treatment lost an average of 27.3 pounds (12.4%) compared to 2.2 pounds (0.9%) with placebo." This is the efficacy estimand, which "represents efficacy had all randomized participants remained on study intervention (with possible dose interruptions and modifications) for 72 weeks without initiating prohibited weight management treatments."
- "Participants taking Foundayo, regardless of trial completion, lost an average of 25 pounds (11.1%), compared to 5.3 pounds (2.1%) with placebo." This is the treatment-regimen estimand.
- "In the ATTAIN program, Foundayo also led to reductions in many markers of cardiovascular risk, including waist circumference, non-HDL cholesterol, triglycerides and systolic blood pressure across all doses."

## Quotes

- Deborah Horn, DO, director of the Center for Obesity Medicine at McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston: "People living with obesity need treatment options that meet them where they are - and for many, a once-daily pill that can be taken with no food or water restrictions can offer them greater flexibility ... With Foundayo, we now have an oral option that delivered an average of 12.4% weight loss at the highest dose in clinical trials."
- David A. Ricks, chair and CEO of Eli Lilly: "Today, fewer than 1 in 10 people who could benefit from a GLP-1 are taking one, held back by access, stigma, perceived complexity or the belief that their condition isn't serious enough for treatment ... As a convenient, once-daily oral pill that delivers meaningful weight loss, this is obesity care designed for the real world."
- Joe Nadglowski, president and CEO of the Obesity Action Coalition: "There is no single path that works for everyone living with overweight or obesity. New treatment options expand choice and help more people find care that fits their lives."

## Pricing and access

- "Eligible people with commercial insurance may pay as little as $25 per month with the Foundayo savings card."
- "Individuals opting for self-pay can access Foundayo starting at $149 per month for the lowest dose."
- "Eligible Medicare Part D individuals may be able to get Foundayo for $50 per month, beginning as soon as July 1, 2026."
- "Lilly has submitted orforglipron for weight management and/or type 2 diabetes in more than 40 countries and plans to launch in each country shortly after approval."

## About the medicine

- "Foundayo is a once-daily small molecule (non-peptide) oral glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist that can be taken any time of the day without restrictions on food and water intake."
- "Orforglipron was discovered by Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and licensed by Lilly in 2018."
- "In addition to chronic weight management, orforglipron is being studied as a potential treatment for type 2 diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea, osteoarthritis knee pain, hypertension, peripheral artery disease and stress urinary incontinence."
- Available as 0.8 mg, 2.5 mg, 5.5 mg, 9 mg, 14.5 mg or 17.2 mg oral tablets. Taken by mouth once each day, with or without food; tablets swallowed whole.

## ATTAIN clinical trial program

- "The ATTAIN Phase 3 global clinical development program for orforglipron has enrolled more than 4,500 people with obesity or overweight across two global registration trials."
- **ATTAIN-1 (NCT05869903)**: "a Phase 3, 72-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial" in adults with obesity, or overweight with at least one of hypertension, dyslipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea or cardiovascular disease, without diabetes. "The trial randomized 3,127 participants across the U.S., Brazil, China, India, Japan, South Korea, Puerto Rico, Slovakia, Spain and Taiwan." Primary objective: superiority to placebo in body weight reduction from baseline after 72 weeks.
- **ATTAIN-2 (NCT05872620)**: same design in adults with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes; "randomized over 1,600 participants across the U.S., Argentina, Australia, Brazil, China, Czechia, Germany, Greece, India, South Korea and Puerto Rico". Primary objective: superiority to placebo in mean body weight change from baseline at 72 weeks.

## Safety information

- "Use of Foundayo with other GLP-1 receptor agonist medicines is not recommended. It is not known whether Foundayo is safe and effective for use in children."
- Warning: "Foundayo may cause tumors in the thyroid, including thyroid cancer. Watch for possible symptoms, such as a lump or swelling in the neck, hoarseness, trouble swallowing or shortness of breath."
- Do not use with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2), or after a serious allergic reaction to orforglipron or its ingredients.
- Serious side effects listed: pancreatitis; severe stomach problems; dehydration leading to kidney problems; low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), with higher risk alongside insulin or a sulfonylurea; serious allergic reactions; changes in vision in patients with type 2 diabetes; gallbladder problems; and food or liquid getting into the lungs during anesthesia or deep sedation.
- "The most common side effects of Foundayo include nausea, constipation, diarrhea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach (abdominal) pain, headache, swollen belly, feeling tired, belching, heartburn, gas, and hair loss."
- "Birth control pills may not work as well while taking Foundayo. Your healthcare provider may recommend another type of birth control for 30 days after starting Foundayo and for 30 days after each dose increase."
- A pregnancy exposure registry will be set up; breastfeeding "is not recommended during treatment".
- Material code on the release: "OG CON BS APR2026". "Foundayo is a trademark of Eli Lilly and Company."

## Reference cited for the food-intake claim

Ma X, Liu R, Pratt EJ, Benson CT, Bhattachar SN, Sloop KW. "Effect of Food Consumption on the Pharmacokinetics, Safety, and Tolerability of Once-Daily Orally Administered Orforglipron (LY3502970), a Non-peptide GLP-1 Receptor Agonist." Diabetes Ther. 2024 Apr;15(4):819-832.

wikis.title: Intel Nova Lake leak: Core Ultra Series 400 branding and staggered 2027 launch
wikis.summary: Tom's Hardware news report on a leaked Intel Nova Lake roadmap, covering the rumoured Core Ultra Series 400 branding, the staggered 2027 launch windows and the flagship 52-core chip's specifications.
wikis.body:
## The report

- Headline: "Intel Nova Lake leak points to Core Ultra Series 400 branding, staggered release next year - hotly anticipated flagship 52-core desktop CPU might not arrive until late 2027". By Kunal Khullar, news contributor; published 17 July 2026. Standfirst: "A huge leap for desktop processors incoming?"
- "Intel was expected to unveil its next-generation desktop processors later this year. The upcoming Nova Lake lineup has been making the rounds online, and a new report from VideoCardz suggests that Intel could introduce it under the Core Ultra Series 400 branding."
- "For context, the current Arrow Lake and Arrow Lake Refresh desktop CPUs follow the Core Ultra Series 200 naming scheme, while Intel's latest Panther Lake mobile processors carry the Core Ultra Series 300 branding."

## Rumoured launch timeline

- "Intel will initially introduce a 28-core DS package, which is expected to launch between January and March 2027. The new DS suffix is said to be an internal package designation for processors featuring dual-compute tiles."
- "This will reportedly be followed by 28-core K-series (unlocked) models between March and April 2027, while 16-core and 8-core variants are expected to arrive between late March and May 2027."
- "The flagship 52-core DS model is reportedly scheduled for a much later launch, potentially between late May and September 2027."
- The article's table ("Rumored Nova Lake launch timeline", columns P-cores / E-cores / LPE-cores / expected launch) is only partly filled in the captured page: 52-core DS - 16 / 32 / 4 - "Late May to September 2027"; 28-core DS - 8 - "January to March 2027"; 28-core K-series - "March to April 2027"; 16-core - "Late March to May 2027"; 8-core - 0.
- "The report also claims to reveal the review embargo windows and launch timeline for several Nova Lake models."

## Flagship specifications (as rumoured)

- "The flagship desktop SKU, featuring a 52-core configuration, is expected to combine 16 Coyote Cove Performance (P) cores, 32 Arctic Wolf Efficiency (E) cores, and four Low Power Efficiency (LPE) cores."
- "This would be a notable jump over the current Core Ultra 9 285K, which features a total of 24-cores."
- "The introduction of Coyote Cove and Arctic Wolf also points to an entirely new CPU architecture, replacing the Lion Cove and Skymont cores found in Arrow Lake."

## Platform

- "Nova Lake is also rumored to bring new platform upgrades including support for DDR5-8000 memory, up to 24 PCIe 5.0 lanes for expansion, Thunderbolt 5, and Intel's next-generation Xe3 Celestial integrated graphics."
- "The processors are also expected to feature an upgraded NPU5 for AI workloads along with a 150W Processor Base Power (PBP) and 253W Maximum Turbo Power (MTP) on the flagship model, despite the substantial increase in core count."
- "Earlier reports have also indicated that Nova Lake will transition to a new LGA1954 socket, meaning users will likely need a new motherboard to upgrade from the existing Arrow Lake platform."
- "While Intel is yet to officially confirm a launch date for Nova Lake, various leaks have suggested that the lineup could be one of the company's biggest generational leaps in recent years."

## Related headlines listed on the page

"Intel's Core Ultra 400 'Nova Lake' launch schedule leaks out"; "Intel's next-gen 52-core Nova Lake CPU could pull up to 474W" (a different power figure from the 253W MTP given in this article); "Intel reportedly adding two new 22-core SKUs with game-boosting cache to Nova Lake-S lineup"; "Intel reportedly cans 12Xe option for Nova Lake-S desktop".

The article carries 17 comments.

wikis.title: Windows Central: Microsoft's 2027 next-gen Xbox strategy
wikis.summary: Windows Central report by Jez Corden on Microsoft's 'Gen-10' Xbox, its Windows-based design, AMD's 2027 launch comment, pricing uncertainty and the planned OEM hardware ecosystem.
wikis.body:
## The report

- Headline on the page: "The next Xbox is coming in 2027, and the strategy behind it is a bigger deal than people realize" (browser title: "Exclusive: Microsoft's 2027 Xbox could be a huge shift for the platform"). By Jez Corden, Executive Editor; published 8 February 2026.
- Standfirst: "From AMD's claims of a 2027 Xbox, to the idea of a plurality of Xbox Gen-10 consoles - lets sift through some fresh details."

## The core claim

- "The next-gen Xbox is starting to take shape, and new signals from ASUS suggest Microsoft is targeting 2027 for its next major hardware push. That lines up with what I reported last year: Microsoft's future console is shaping up to be far closer to a streamlined Windows 11 gaming PC than a traditional Xbox box."
- "The next Xbox would run a TV-first console interface by default, but underneath, it's essentially a full Windows machine capable of running Xbox titles, legacy games, and a wide range of PC software."
- "For an idea of how the Gen 10 Xbox will function, you can look to the current Xbox Ally ... The Xbox interface will sit on top of Windows, disabling unnecessary processes to create a gaming-first environment. You will be able to exit out to full Windows, much like you can exit out to Linux on the Steam Deck."
- "The Gen-10 Xbox 'PC' will also run all of your current Xbox games, in addition to games from Windows 11 PC stores like Steam."

## Launch window

- "Last summer, Xbox President Sarah Bond reiterated commitment to first-party Xbox hardware ... Bond noted that it had entered a multi-year partnership with long-time collaborator AMD for the next-gen Xbox, and that it would retain backward compatibility with all current Xbox console games."
- AMD CEO Lisa Su, on an earnings call with investors (via Tom's Hardware): "Development of Microsoft's next-gen Xbox featuring an AMD semi-custom SoC is progressing well to support a launch in 2027."
- "I'm told Microsoft insiders were a little taken off-guard by Lisa Su's comments on Xbox's Gen-10 timeline."
- "AMD's internal codename for the Xbox SoC is 'Magnus,' our sources confirm, although that is not Microsoft's codename for the actual device itself."
- "Microsoft hasn't fully internally committed to a hard 2027 launch window for the next-gen Xbox platform, since so much of it hinges on improvements to Windows 11 and other factors ... You can think of 2027 as the 'best case scenario,' but having a polished experience is the north star for Xbox."
- One line later in the piece says instead that new accessories could appear "even before the next Xbox launches later this year", which does not match the 2027 window given elsewhere in the same article.

## Price

- "There are a ton of rumors flying around about potential price points for the next-gen Xbox, but the truth is, Microsoft itself doesn't know how much the next-gen Xbox will be just yet."
- Reasons given: "Global tariffs, component costs, geopolitics, and supply issues have prices heavily in flux right now", with RAM costs spiralling and U.S. tariff taxes pushing up consumer prices; TV manufacturers are dropping 8K on price grounds and "Nintendo recently warned investors that it may be considering a price increase for its Switch 2 platform."
- "It does sound as though the next-gen Xbox is pushing for a more premium experience from its first-party offering."
- "Even if the next-gen Xbox comes in at around $1,000 dollars as some expect, Xbox Series S players shouldn't expect to be suddenly cut off and priced out."
- "I'm told Microsoft expects the Gen-9 Xbox Series X|S and PS5 to have a longer tail than usual as a result of this 'broadening' hardware endpoint ecosystem."

## Hardware ecosystem

- "I'm told Microsoft is also working with OEMs such as ASUS and the like to build a variety of options for next-gen Xbox gamers across a range of price points, like the two Xbox Ally models."
- "Despite rumors to the contrary, I'm told Microsoft also still wants to make a first-party Xbox handheld eventually, too, even if the traditional next-gen Xbox console is the focus for now."
- "Xbox's first-party console will be the baseline, quintessential 'Xbox' experience, but we could see more expensive, even more super-premium Xbox 'consoles' from Microsoft's Windows partners, as well as slimmed-down, more affordable options on top."
- "Microsoft is currently testing a new NPU-powered highlights reel feature for the Xbox Ally X, which will take your gameplay clips and automatically generate a shareable video of your best gameplay moments. This feature is slated to drop in March, 2026, all being well."
- "Epic recently told us it's ready to bring its own Epic Games Store to the next Xbox, and Steam is a clear shoo-in."
- "We should hear more updates on this front at GDC 2026" regarding opening the Xbox platform for developers.
- "Xbox likely won't expect the kinds of volumes seen by previous generations with its first-party offering ... You can think of the next-gen Xbox similarly to how Microsoft handles Surface - a curated boutique experience in a wider Xbox hardware ecosystem."
- Closing assessment: "It's Microsoft's most ambitious hardware plan since the inception of Windows itself, but also, for Xbox, probably its most risky."

## Price listings on the page

The article's deals module lists the ROG Xbox Ally at $599.99 (ASUS) and an ASUS ROG Xbox Ally bundle at $899 (Walmart).

wikis.title: F1 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix 2026: date, schedule and history
wikis.summary: RacingNews365 race hub for the 2026 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, giving the 4-6 December session schedule and start times, Yas Marina Circuit facts and a history of past editions.
wikis.body:
## 2026 race

- "The F1 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix is scheduled to take place on the weekend of **4 - 6 December**, and will be the **24th and final race** of the Formula 1 season."
- Circuit: **Yas Marina Circuit**, Edition 2026.

### Session schedule as tabulated

| Session | Date | Time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free practice 1 | Friday 4 December | 10:30 - 11:30 |
| Free practice 2 | Friday 4 December | 14:00 - 15:00 |
| Free practice 3 | Saturday 5 December | 11:30 - 12:30 |
| Qualifying | Saturday 5 December | 15:00 - 16:00 |
| Race | Sunday 6 December | 14:00 - 16:00 |

### Contradictions within the page on the 2026 times

- **Qualifying**: the prose says "qualifying on Saturday 5 December at **14:00 GMT**"; the schedule table lists qualifying at **15:00 - 16:00**.
- **Race start**: the prose says "The Formula One Abu Dhabi Grand Prix starts on Sunday 6 December at **13:00 GMT**"; the schedule table lists the race at **14:00 - 16:00**.

## Circuit and event profile

- First GP **2009**; last GP **2025**; number of races **17**; first held 2009.
- **Laps 58**; **circuit length 5.281 kilometres**; lap record **1:26.103 (2021)**.
- 2025 result: winner **Max Verstappen**, second **Oscar Piastri**, third **Lando Norris**.

### Contradiction on circuit length

- The profile box gives **5.281 kilometres**; the description says "the track stretches over **four and a half kilometers**"; the history section calls it "the **5.5km** ultramodern Yas Marina Circuit".

## Circuit background

- Built after Abu Dhabi sought its own Grand Prix circuit at the end of the 2000s, with Qatar hosting MotoGP and Bahrain already on the F1 calendar; "no expense was spared".
- Features: "the pit lane exit runs underneath the first corner, and at one point, the drivers even race under a hotel"; a Monaco-style final section with walls close to the asphalt; located on **Yas Island**, "specially developed for the occasion".
- "In the lead-up to the **2021** race, the circuit underwent modifications in several areas to improve overtaking opportunities", in response to criticism that the race sometimes lacked excitement.
- Plans to develop Yas Island were announced in **2006**; work began in **2007**; the circuit debuted in **2009**.

## History of past editions

- **2009**: initially planned as the 19th and final race of the season, moved up by two weeks after the Canadian and French Grands Prix were cancelled. Jenson Button had already clinched the title in Brazil, where Brawn GP took the Constructors' Championship. Lewis Hamilton took pole but retired with brake failure; **Sebastian Vettel** led a Red Bull 1-2 ahead of Mark Webber, with Button third. Final F1 appearances for Kazuki Nakajima, Giancarlo Fisichella and the Brawn GP, BMW Sauber and Toyota teams.
- **2010**: title decided at Yas Marina for the first time. Fernando Alonso led Webber by eight points and Vettel by 15, with Hamilton 24 points behind. Vettel took pole and the win to become "the youngest F1 World Champion at **23 years and 134 days**"; Hamilton and Button completed the podium. The race was the last with **Bridgestone** as sole tyre supplier, **Pirelli** taking over for 2011 "having last competed in the sport back in 1991".
- **2012**: Kimi Raikkonen won, his first victory since returning from a two-year hiatus. **2013**: Vettel led every lap for his third Abu Dhabi win.
- **2014**: final round with the championship on the line; "For the first time ever, **double points** were awarded for the event" - a system that "turned out to be a one-off". Nico Rosberg took third practice and qualifying, but Hamilton won the race ahead of Felipe Massa and Valtteri Bottas to take his second title.
- **2016**: Rosberg entered with a **12-point** lead; Mercedes had already clinched the Constructors' title with a **226 points** lead over Red Bull. Hamilton took pole and won, but Rosberg's second place clinched his maiden Drivers' Championship; he announced his retirement one week later.
- **2021**: Hamilton and **Max Verstappen** arrived level on points. Verstappen took pole, Hamilton led, then Nicholas Latifi crashed with a few laps remaining, bringing out the Safety Car. Verstappen pitted for Soft tyres while Hamilton stayed out on Hards; lapped cars were initially told they could not unlap themselves, then the five cars between the pair were allowed to. With one lap remaining Verstappen overtook Hamilton for the win and his first World Championship. "The manner in which the final laps of the race unfolded proved controversial", the FIA said it would investigate, and "In the months that followed, Race Director **Michael Masi** departed his role."

## Records

- Drivers: **Lewis Hamilton** five wins at Yas Marina; **Sebastian Vettel** and **Max Verstappen** three each; **Kimi Raikkonen**, **Nico Rosberg** and **Valtteri Bottas** one each.
- Constructors: **Mercedes** seven wins, **Red Bull** six, **Lotus** and **McLaren** one each.

## Also on the page

- A 2026 calendar box listing Azerbaijan GP 26 Sep 2026, Bahrain GP 04 Oct 2026, Singapore GP 11 Oct 2026, United States GP 25 Oct 2026, Mexico City GP 01 Nov 2026, Brazilian GP 08 Nov 2026.
