wikis.title: 2028 Summer Paralympics
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the LA28 Summer Paralympic Games of 15-27 August 2028 in Los Angeles, covering the bid, venues, the 23-sport programme with paraclimbing's debut, the schedule and the emblem.
wikis.body:
## The Games

- "The 2028 Summer Paralympics, also known as the Los Angeles 2028 Summer Paralympic Games, and branded as LA28, will be the 18th edition of the Summer Paralympic Games, an international multi-sport parasports event governed by the International Paralympic Committee. The Games are scheduled to take place from August 15 to August 27, 2028, in Los Angeles, California, United States."
- "Marking Los Angeles' first time as the host of the Paralympics, the Games will be the first Summer Paralympics in the United States since the 1996 edition in Atlanta, Georgia, and the third overall. The Games will include the debut of paraclimbing as an event."
- Infobox: XVIII Paralympic Games; Athletes 4,400 (expected); Events 560 in 23 sports; Opening August 15, 2028; Closing August 27, 2028. Opening ceremony at SoFi Stadium (named "2028 Stadium" during the Games), closing ceremony at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Previous summer edition Paris 2024, next Brisbane 2032.

## Bids

- "As part of a formal agreement between the International Paralympic Committee and the International Olympic Committee first established in 2001, the winner of the bid for the Summer Olympics also holds the Summer Paralympics."
- A process to award the 2024 and 2028 Games simultaneously to Los Angeles and Paris "was approved at an Extraordinary IOC Session on July 11, 2017, in Lausanne. Paris was understood to be the preferred host for the 2024 Games. On July 31, 2017, the IOC announced Los Angeles as the sole candidate for the 2028 Games ... Both decisions were ratified at the 131st IOC Session on September 13, 2017."

## Venues

- "The Paralympic venue plan was announced on June 3, 2025, using most of the same venues as the Olympics."
- "Unlike the Olympics, SoFi Stadium will not be used for swimming, as it will be needed by the Los Angeles Chargers and Rams for their NFL preseason games; swimming will take place at a temporary stadium on the grounds of the Long Beach Convention and Entertainment Center (which will host artistic swimming and water polo during the Olympics) instead. Some Paralympic athletes expressed disappointment at the decision, believing that it created an inequity between the Olympics and Paralympics."

## Sports programme

- "The program for the 2028 Summer Paralympics will feature a record 560 events in 23 sports - an increase of 11 events and one sport over 2024. It will feature the 22 sports contested in 2024, as well as the Paralympic debut of sport climbing (paraclimbing)."
- "IPC president Andrew Parsons stated that LA28 would be the most gender-balanced Paralympics in its history; there will be an increase of 12 women's events (a record 247) and three mixed/open events over 2024, and a decrease of four men's events. With these changes, a record 17 sports will have full gender parity, an increase of six over 2024."
- "A record 33 sports applied for consideration by the IPC, including bids to reinstate CP football (formerly football 7-a-side) and sailing, and bids for arm wrestling, beach paravolley, paraclimbing, para dance sport, golf, karate, powerchair football, para surfing, and wheelchair handball as new sports. The IPC shortlisted paraclimbing and para surfing for consideration by the LA28 organizing committee, with paraclimbing being selected as the 23rd sport in June 2024."

Event counts by sport: Archery (9), Athletics (164), Badminton (16), Blind football (1), Boccia (11), Canoe (10), Climbing (8), Cycling (51), Equestrian (11), Fencing (16), Goalball (2), Judo (16), Powerlifting (20), Rowing (5), Shooting (13), Sitting volleyball (2), Swimming (142), Table tennis (32), Taekwondo (10), Triathlon (12), Wheelchair basketball (2), Wheelchair rugby (1), Wheelchair tennis (6).

## Calendar

- "On November 19, 2025, the organizing committee published the first version of the competition schedule. The International Paralympic Committee approved the final schedule, and dates for the Summer Paralympic Games were released on May 27, 2026."
- The calendar runs 13-27 August 2028, with the opening ceremony on the 15th and the closing ceremony on the 27th.
- Daily medal events listed: 0, 0, 0, 25, 48, 48, 66, 40, 38, 51, 43, 59, 65, 55, 20 - the row's own total reads 565, while the cumulative row ends at 560, the figure the article and infobox give.

## Marketing

"The emblems for the 2028 Summer Olympics and Paralympics were unveiled on September 1, 2020, featuring the characters 'LA' and '28' in a stacked layout. The 'A' in 'LA' is designed to be interchangeable, with variations created in collaboration with local athletes, artists, and celebrities. Among the larger suite of logo variants are versions designed in collaboration with Paralympic athletes, including Scout Bassett (which is inspired by the infinity symbol), Ezra Frech, Lex Gillette, Jamal Hill, and Oz Sanchez."

## Sources cited (selection)

International Paralympic Committee, "LA28 Paralympic Games medal event programme and athlete quotas confirmed" (June 3, 2025); LA28.org, "LA28 Unveils 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Opening and Closing Ceremony Locations" (May 8, 2025); ABC News, "Paralympians express upset and disappointment over swimming venues for LA28" (July 10, 2025); IPC, "LA28 reveals comprehensive Paralympic competition schedule" (May 27, 2026).

wikis.title: Miami-Dade launches Metro Express BRT to South Dade on October 27
wikis.summary: Miami-Dade County press release announcing Metro Express, the county's first bus rapid transit line, opening 27 October 2025 between Florida City and Dadeland South, with its stations, funding and ribbon cutting.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- Press release from Miami-Dade County, dated 2025-10-04, 8:00 am. Media contact: Stephany Heilbron Monsalve, 305-310-8349. Issued by the Department of Transportation and Public Works.
- "Miami-Dade County will make history soon by launching Metro Express - the County's first-ever Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system and the longest all-electric BRT service in the nation, designed to transform how thousands of Miami-Dade residents move along the busy US-1 corridor."
- "Starting on October 27, 2025, the Miami-Dade Department of Transportation and Public Works (DTPW) will offer South Dade commuters access to a brand-new, comfortable and reliable transit connection from Florida City to Dadeland South."

## Ribbon cutting

"To commemorate the occasion, Miami-Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava and DTPW leadership, along with the Board of County Commissioners, state and federal officials, partners, and stakeholders, will celebrate with a ribbon cutting ceremony on Wednesday, October 22nd at one of the 14 new signature BRT stations."

## The service

- "Stretching 20 miles along US-1 down to Florida City, Metro Express will run on a dedicated lane protected by gate arms, and prioritized during rush hour, to ensure an efficient and safe ride from beginning to end."
- "At the heart of the new Metro Express service are 14 new signature BRT stations, which offer amenities such as air-conditioned waiting areas to provide comfort and protection from the elements, a modern design with ample shade, bike friendly boarding and storage, water fountains, free Wi-Fi, and charging stations for mobile devices. All amenities combined, plus the ability to pay before you board, deliver a new enhanced experience for Metro Express passengers."

## Quotes

- Mayor Daniella Levine Cava: "Metro Express will transform the way South Dade moves by connecting residents with an easier, greener and smarter service to key destinations including job centers, schools, parks, shopping areas and other transit services ... I am proud to welcome a new era of public transportation, where sustainability meets efficiency and technology powers every ride. The South Dade TransitWay brings smarter infrastructure to make the daily commute more convenient, meeting today's needs and tomorrow's growth."
- DTPW Director and CEO Stacy L. Miller, P.E.: "The Metro Express BRT service was designed for safety and efficiency at every touchpoint. Level boarding, clear wayfinding, well-lit platforms, and traffic signal priority make trips safer and simpler. This is a modern transit experience built to transform the way we move."

## Funding

"The project was funded with a $100 million investment by each of the partnering agencies: Miami-Dade County through the People's Transportation half penny surtax, the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT), and the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) through its capital investment grant."

"Developed as part of the SMART Program, Metro Express reflects Miami-Dade County's long-term commitment to modern, sustainable infrastructure."

## Department information on the page

DTPW is based at Overtown Transit Village North, 701 NW 1st Court, Miami 33136. Its mass transit system is listed as Metrobus, BRT Metro Express, Metrorail, Metromover, MetroConnect microtransit service and Special Transportation Service. The department also manages countywide traffic signals, signage, pavement markings and street lighting, movable and fixed bridges, roadway repairs, the Rickenbacker and Venetian causeways, the County Stormwater Utility, and permitting for work within County rights-of-way.

wikis.title: Beijing Tongzhou railway station
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Beijing Tongzhou railway station (Beijing Sub-Center station), the underground hub in Tongzhou District that opened on 30 December 2025, with its lines, size, cost and designers.
wikis.body:
## The station

- "Beijing Tongzhou railway station (Chinese: 北京通州站; pinyin: Beijing tongzhou zhan), also known as Beijing Municipal Administrative Center railway station and Beijing Sub-Center railway station, is a railway station in Tongyun Subdistrict, Tongzhou District, Beijing."
- "Construction of the Integrated Transportation Hub (ITH) started construction on 30 November 2019. It opened on 30 December 2025. It will be the largest underground railway station in Asia."
- Coordinates 39 deg 54' 08" N, 116 deg 42' 08" E.
- Owner: Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei Intercity Railway Investment Co., Ltd. Operator: China Railway Beijing Group.
- Structure: underground; depth 32 metres (105 ft). Platforms: 6 island, 2 side. Connections: Beiyunhedong station.

## Lines served

- China Railway: Beijing-Tangshan intercity railway; Beijing-Binhai intercity railway.
- Beijing Suburban Railway: Sub-Central line (extension under planning).
- Beijing Subway: Line 6 (via Beiyunhedong); Line 22 (under construction); Line M101 (under planning).
- Adjacent stations on Line 6 (transfer at Beiyunhedong): Beiyunhexi (towards Jin'anqiao) and Haojiafu (towards Luyang). Future Line 22 service, "Opening 2026": Yunhe Shangwuqu (towards Dongdaqiao) and Zhengwuzhongxin (towards Pinggu).

## Size and cost

"The total site area of the Integrated Transport Hub is 70 hectares (170 acres), with a floorage of 2,230,000 square metres (24,000,000 sq ft) overground. The total investment of the Integrated Transport Hub is approximately 42.1 billion Renminbi."

## Design

"This station and the ITH are designed by AREP, Beijing General Municipal Engineering Design & Research Institute, China Railway Design Corporation, and China Architecture Design Group."

## Future development

- "The Pinggu line of the Beijing Subway is currently under construction and is expected to open in late 2026."
- An image caption notes: "When Beijing Tongzhou railway station was opened, the sign for the Pinggu Line (Line 22) was already hung."
- A cited 2021 Chinese source quotes an earlier plan for the Line 22 Chaoyang section - "计划2025年建成通车" (planned to be completed and opened in 2025).
- A 2019 Xinhua source cited for the hub is headed "北京：副中心枢纽站开工 2024年底通车" (construction started; through traffic by the end of 2024), an earlier date than the actual 30 December 2025 opening.

## Sources cited (selection)

The Beijing News, 2025-12-26, "北京通州站12月30日开通，接入地铁6号线"; China Daily, Cheng Yang, 2025-12-31, "New Beijing rail station to be a major transport hub"; China Railway, 2022-11-16, "Asia's Largest Underground Transportation Complex Hub Enters New Construction Phase"; english.news.cn, "Main structure of Asia's largest underground transportation hub completed"; AREP, "AREP wins the bid for overall design project for integrated transportation hub of Beijing sub-center station".

wikis.title: Mexico-Pachuca "Felipe Ángeles" train, AIFA-Pachuca section
wikis.summary: Proyectos México project page for the AIFA-Pachuca section of the Mexico-Pachuca "Felipe Ángeles" passenger train, with its characteristics, investment, timetable and the project's press-release and progress history.
wikis.body:
## The project

- "The Mexico-Pachuca '**Felipe Ángeles**' Passenger Train project is part of the Government of Mexico's priority national strategy to reactivate and modernize the public passenger rail transport service. The project is integrated into the '**Plan México**'", in three stages:
  1. The Government of Mexico acquired the **Suburbano Train** - Buenavista terminal in Mexico City to Cuautitlán, State of Mexico - "as part of the recovery of passenger trains to operate the network publicly through the National Infrastructure Fund (**Fonadin**)."
  2. "The connection of the Suburbano Train via the **Lechería** station, featuring a **23-km branch line and seven stations** leading to the **Felipe Ángeles International Airport (AIFA)**."
  3. "The connection of the train running from AIFA to the city of **Pachuca** in the state of **Hidalgo**, spanning **65 km of electrified double-track**, which will feature **four stations and four train stops**."
- "Jul. 16, 2026. Modification to Fonadin's Assignment Title for the construction, operation, and provision of suburban and interurban passenger services on the **Buenavista-Pachuca** rail route."
- Page disclaimer: "This information is preliminary and subject to review and continuous updates as the project progresses."
- The page states "**Last revision: September 2026**" (month only, no day).

## AIFA - Pachuca section: key characteristics

- States covered: **State of Mexico (35 km)** and **Hidalgo (30 km)**.
- Service type: passenger. Route length: "**65 km** of electrified double track on existing right of way (DEFENSA)".
- Fleet: electric trains. Design speed: **maximum 120 km/h**. Passenger capacity: **718 passengers per train**.
- **Estimated investment: 44 billion MXN.**
- Required infrastructure: "**2 viaducts (5.89 km), 4 electrical substations, 51.67 km of cut-and-fill works**".
- "Start of works: Preliminary works and studies began in **October 2024**; construction officially commenced in **March 2025**."
- Connection: "The project will link with the Buenavista-Lecheria-AIFA branch, connecting Mexico City with the AIFA and Pachuca."
- "Execution period and start of operations: **2 years (2025-2027)**."
- "Project lead: Construction is led by the **Secretaría de la Defensa Nacional (DEFENSA)** through the **Felipe Ángeles Engineers Corps**."

## Buenavista - Cuautitlán section (Suburban Rail)

- "The Suburban Train on its Buenavista-Cuautitlán stretch, began operations in **2008**, spanning a length of **27 km** across **seven stations**. In **2025**, it recorded **45.1 million users**."
- "In **April 2026**, the Government of Mexico announced an agreement to acquire **100% of the equity stake** and publicly operate the system through Fonadin, via the creation of a State-Owned Majority-Interest Company."
- Characteristics as listed: "**25.5 km** of electrified double-track on the Buenavista-Cuautitlán route, featuring **five stations** (Fortuna, Tlalnepantla, San Rafael, Lechería, and Tultitlán) and **two terminals** (Buenavista and Cuautitlán)."
- Trains: "**20 four-car electric trains** (capacity: **1,130 passengers**) with a maximum speed of **120 km/h** and an average speed of **65 km/h**." Capacity: "Approximately **350,000 passengers**."

## Buenavista - AIFA section (Lechería-AIFA branch)

- "The Felipe Ángeles Train, on its Buenavista-AIFA section, began operations on **April 26, 2026**, covering a **41-km** route between the Buenavista terminal and AIFA in **less than 60 minutes** (19.5 km between Buenavista and Lechería, and 22.94 km between Lechería and AIFA)."
- "It consists of **six stations and one terminal** (Cueyamil, La Loma, Teyahualco, Prados Sur, Cajiga, Xaltocan, and the **AIFA-Clara Krause** terminal), all located within the State of Mexico."
- "The system operates with **10-car coupled trains measuring 100 meters** in length. Each single train has a capacity of **719 passengers**, which can be coupled to accommodate **over 1,400 passengers**. It features a maximum speed of **120 km/h**, an average operating speed of **65 km/h**, and a frequency of **15 minutes**."
- Transfers: to the Suburban Rail toward Cuautitlán; in Mexico City to Metro Line 3, Metrobús Lines 1, 3 and 4 and Ecobici; in the State of Mexico to Mexibús and local transit.
- Connected municipalities and areas: Lechería, Tultepec, Jaltenco and Zumpango.
- "From April 26, its commercial launch date, through **June 30, 2026**, the train recorded **over two million passengers** carried".

## Contradictions within the page

- **Number of AIFA-Pachuca stations and length**: the project description says the AIFA-Pachuca stage spans "65 km of electrified double-track, which will feature **four stations and four train stops**", and the key characteristics repeat "65 km". A video note from the 24 April 2026 construction supervision instead says "There will be **six stations** from AIFA to Pachuca, covering a **5 km** stretch."
- **Suburbano route length**: the narrative says the Buenavista-Cuautitlán stretch spans "**27 km** across seven stations"; the characteristics list "**25.5 km** ... five stations ... and two terminals".
- **Lechería-AIFA daily ridership**: a video caption says the Lechería-AIFA train "transports **30,000 passengers** daily", while the 26 April 2026 press release is headed "'Felipe Ángeles' Buenavista-AIFA Train to Transport **57,000** Daily Passengers".
- **Journey time**: the text says Buenavista to AIFA takes "less than 60 minutes"; a video caption says "30,000 passengers travel from Mexico City to AIFA in **50 minutes**".
- **Fleet size for AIFA-Pachuca**: the 24 April 2026 supervision note says "It will feature **15 electric trains**; the first one will arrive in September"; a separate video caption describes the Lechería-AIFA train as having "**10** state-of-the-art trains".

## Reported construction progress over time

- "Mañanera del Pueblo", Oct. 22, 2025: "Right-of-way acquisition for passenger trains shows **66% progress**."
- Dec. 4, 2025: "The Mexico City-Pachuca Train has **five heavy-construction fronts** and is generating more than **9,000 jobs**."
- Feb. 19, 2026: "The construction of the Mexico City-Pachuca railway is **21.15% complete**."
- Apr. 24, 2026: "Mexico City-Pachuca Train Reaches **30% Progress** and Generates **10,000 Jobs**, President Claudia Sheinbaum Reports During Inspection Tour."
- Jun. 25, 2026: "The construction of the Mexico City - Pachuca railway shows a **37.06% progress**."

## Selected press releases listed (2026)

- Aug. 17: "Social justice for families living near the AIFA-Pachuca Train project: Sedatu, SICT, and Conavi deliver **28 homes** due to relocation."
- Jul. 05: "ATTRAPI evaluates the interior and exterior of the Buenavista-Pachuca Train."
- Jun. 25: "We are well ahead of schedule; the goal is to inaugurate the **Mexico City-Pachuca and Mexico City-Querétaro routes in 2027**: President **Claudia Sheinbaum**." Also: "Sedatu and SICT have cleared more than **28 million square meters** for railway right-of-way."
- Jun. 15: "Lecheria-AIFA Train solidifies its position as a modern mobility alternative with **over one million passengers**."
- Jun. 04: "SICT grants Lechería-AIFA train allocation title to **Banobras**."
- May. 20: "'Honesty Delivers Results': President Claudia Sheinbaum Highlights That Her Administration Will Build at Least **2,377 KM** of Public Railways." A video note of the same date: "The first train for the AIFA-Pachuca route will arrive in **September of this year**, while the one for the CDMX-Querétaro route is expected in the **first half of 2027**."
- May. 05: "CFE, Key to Guaranteeing Reliable Power Supply along the Felipe Ángeles Train's Buenavista-AIFA Route."
- May. 04: "'Felipe Ángeles' Train Transports **Over 206,000 Passengers** During Its First Week of Operation."
- Apr. 26: inauguration of the Felipe Ángeles Buenavista-AIFA Train by President Sheinbaum.
- Apr. 24: "'Felipe Ángeles' Train, on its AIFA-Pachuca Stretch, to Transport **107,000 Daily Passengers**."
- Apr. 23: "Suburban Train Transitions from Private Hands to the People of Mexico: President Announces Acquisition and Name Change to 'Felipe Ángeles' Train."
- Feb. 19: "President Highlights Public Collaboration in Clearing Over **24 Million Square Meters** of Right-of-Way."

## Site

- Published by Mexico Projects Hub / Proyectos México; footer "D.R. © Banco Nacional de Obras y Servicios Públicos, S.N.C., Ciudad de México, 2026."
- Linked related projects: Public Passenger Railway Service; Felipe Ángeles International Airport; 0280 Cuautitlán-Buenavista Suburban Train Route; Expansion of Line 1 of the Lechería-Jaltocan Suburban Train - AIFA.

wikis.body:
## What the page is
YouTube page for "Construction of the World's Largest Clock | Mega Projects | FD Engineering" on **Free Documentary - Engineering**, published 2025-03-02. Metadata and description only.

## The clock
- "the world's largest tower clock in **Mecca**, the Holy City of Islam."
- "The minute hand measures **23 meters** in length and its giant clock face is **43 meters** in diameter - therefore this gigantic clock tower is **35 times larger than Big Ben**."
- "At the end of construction it is clear that the building at the center of the sacred site breaks **over 30 world records**."

- The architecture firm **SL Rasch** in Germany worked with partners.
- "The team enters the project with a high-rise building already under construction, a tower not designed to support a **150-meter-high clock tower** and a strict weight limit of **82,000 tons**."
- The team "battle to construct the world's largest clock at dizzying heights and in racing winds."
- Questions posed: "How do you keep the structure as light as possible? And how do you deal with the toughest logistical challenge of all: a construction site out of bounds to everyone but Muslims."
- "Time is short and the schedule is fixed." No dates are given.

wikis.title: Mega Ship Surgery: Stretching the ferry Peter Pan by 30 Meters (FD Engineering)
wikis.summary: A Free Documentary - Engineering video page on lengthening the car ferry Peter Pan at German Dry Docks in Bremerhaven, with its lengths, schedule and the problems met.
wikis.body:
## What the page is
YouTube page for "Mega Ship Surgery | How Engineers Stretched a Ferry by 30 Meters | FD Engineering" on **Free Documentary - Engineering**, published 2025-08-29. Metadata and description only.

## The job
- "The **Peter Pan**, a large car ferry, is about to undergo a remarkable transformation: it will be lengthened **from 190 to 220 meters**."
- "engineers cut the ship in two and insert a **30-meter prefabricated section** built at another shipyard, **200 kilometers away**."
- "The entire project must be completed in just **58 days**."
- The yard is **German Dry Docks in Bremerhaven**; **sixty workers** begin preparations even during the ferry's final voyage there.
- "to meet the specifications of the shipping company **TT-Line**, they use a cutting method that has never been applied in this way before."

## Problems the film follows
- "the two massive halves of the ship - each weighing **several thousand tons** - do not separate as planned because some steel beams are still connected."
- "The ship can only be moved when the dock is flooded, meaning areas like the engine room must be carefully sealed to protect sensitive systems."
- "the new mid-section has to arrive in Bremerhaven on time and fit precisely between the two halves."
- "With the first passengers already booked on the renewed Peter Pan, everything must come together smoothly and on schedule."

## Related link in the description
"Inside Airbus - World's Most Complex Supply Chain" (youtu.be/XQWD-PTFdew).

- "The most modern warship in the Danish Navy - the **HDMS Absalon** needs a major overhaul. **Every 5 years**, the warship is docked, and checked to the bones."
- "This happens in **Orskov Yard in Frederikshavn, North Denmark**."
- "The flexible support ship is **137 meters long** and equipped with high-precision weapon systems: From torpedoes to machine guns to anti-missile weapons."
- "Thanks to its smooth and angled outer skin, the Absalon reflects only a fraction of radar radiation, making her extremely difficult to detect. The tracking systems of the warship itself, on the other hand, are highly sensitive."
- "Space for **two helicopters**, two separate engines, bulletproof steel and the most sophisticated technology - all of this is due to be inspected."
- "The most complex of all the processes: Checking the marine shaft device. Which, in effect, means cutting a hole in the ship to remove the rudder and propellers."
- "The bow thruster is removed and maintained, as well as the sonar - a top secret mission."
- Upgrades: "The technicians install a brand new **UV filter system for cleaning the ballast water**; painters give the entire ship a new look."
- "All of this happens under extreme time pressure: the team has only **5 weeks**."

## Related link
- "Creating the Perfect Tire - Manufacturing at Pirelli".

The capture is the video page's metadata and description only; no transcript.

wikis.title: The World's First Renewable Island: Samso (FD Engineering)
wikis.summary: An Islands of the Future episode page on the Danish island of Samso and how its 4,000 inhabitants took over their own energy supply from the late 1990s.
wikis.body:
## What the page is
YouTube page for "The World's First Renewable Island | Islands of the Future: Samso | FD Engineering" on **Free Documentary - Engineering**, published 2025-05-30. Metadata and description only.

## Samso
- "**Samso** in the Baltic is the energy paragon among Europe's islands."
- "At the end of the **1990s** the **4,000 inhabitants** had already decided to take the matter of energy supplies into their own hands."
- "Using **wind turbines**, **straw-fuelled thermal power stations** and what are called **'cows' milk heat exchangers'**, they have progressively tapped all the clean energy sources the island has to offer."

## Series framing
"The world is in an energy crisis that's getting worse all the time. Oil and gas cost more and more. Coal is fuelling global climate change." Answers "are being found... on the islands of Europe", where islanders "have always had to cope with restricted space and limited resources."

## Related link in the description
"Islands of the Future - El Hierro" (youtu.be/A9h2pCsevZY).

wikis.title: The Gigantic Self-Sufficient Icebreaker: Le Commandant Charcot (FD Engineering)
wikis.summary: A Free Documentary - Engineering video page on the polar cruise ship Commandant Charcot, its six-year build and its self-sufficiency, filmed on a Svalbard cruise.
wikis.body:
## What the page is
YouTube page for "Ingenious Construction: The Gigantic Self-Sufficient Icebreaker | FD Engineering" on **Free Documentary - Engineering**, published 2024-10-27. The description's own heading reads "Genius Construction". Metadata and description only.

## The ship
- **"The Commandant Charcot"** is "the only cruise ship that can navigate through the thickest ice of the **Arctic Ocean** and the most hostile seas of the **Antarctic**."
- "Incorporating technology never before seen on a cruise ship", it "took **six years** to build and involved **hundreds of engineers and workers** all over Europe."
- It can "withstand the extreme pressure of the ice, and navigate **in reverse** to carve its way through it."
- "in the most remote areas of the planet, the ship can also produce its **own electricity and drinking water** for total autonomy."

## The film
"a **ten-day cruise** around the **Svalbard Archipelago** in the Far North", with "unprecedented access to the ship's most intricate facilities, stunning computer-generated images, and first-hand accounts from its designers."

## Related link in the description
"World's Strongest Ships - Titanic Forces of the Sea" (youtu.be/PiVsNiymsNg).

wikis.title: Geothermal Power: Untapped Energy Beneath Our Feet - Iceland (FD Engineering)
wikis.summary: An Islands of the Future episode page on Iceland's geothermal power, stating the island has five large-scale geothermal stations.
wikis.body:
## What the page is
YouTube page for "Geothermal Power: Untapped Energy Beneath Our Feet | Islands of the Future: Iceland | FD Engineering" on **Free Documentary - Engineering**, published 2025-02-16. Metadata and description only.

## Iceland
- "It's not only small islands, though, that have the chance of solving the crucial issue of energy for the future, as is shown by the example of **Iceland**."
- "With its wealth of **volcanoes and glaciers**, the island has all the favourable preconditions you could ask for."
- "There are now **five large-scale geothermal power stations** on the island, which convert volcanically heated water into electricity."
- No station names, capacities or dates are given.

## Series framing
"The world is in an energy crisis that's getting worse all the time. Oil and gas cost more and more. Coal is fuelling global climate change." Answers "are being found in the sea, off the coast of the continent - on the islands of Europe."

## Related link in the description
"Mechanical Batteries - The Future of Energy Storage" (youtu.be/trA5s2iGj2A).

wikis.title: Marine Energy: Harnessing the Ocean's Power - Orkney (FD Engineering)
wikis.summary: An Islands of the Future episode page on the Orkney Islands and the European Marine Energy Centre at Stromness.
wikis.body:
## What the page is
YouTube page for "Marine Energy: Harnessing the Ocean's Power | Islands of the Future: Orkney | FD Engineering" on **Free Documentary - Engineering**, published 2025-02-09. Metadata and description only.

## Orkney
- "The **Orkney Islands** north of **Scotland** have taken a different route. The archipelago is a rugged place. The winds roar here incessantly and the Atlantic breakers have created a craggy cliff coastline."

wikis.title: Fire Truck Manufacturing: Inside the Pierce Factory (FD Engineering)

wikis.body:

YouTube page for "Fire Truck Manufacturing: Inside the Largest Factory | FD Engineering" on **Free Documentary - Engineering**, published 2024-09-06. Metadata and description only.

- The subject is the **Pierce Manufacturing** factory, producing "custom-built fire trucks that meet the exacting standards of fire departments around the world."

wikis.title: Sewers of Paris: The Revolutionary Construction of a City Beneath (FD Engineering)
wikis.summary: A Free Documentary - Engineering video page on the Paris sewer network, its Haussmann-era origins and its 2,600 kilometres of galleries.
wikis.body:
## What the page is
YouTube page for "Sewers of Paris: The Revolutionary Construction of a City Beneath | FD Engineering" on **Free Documentary - Engineering**, published 2023-10-13. The description's own heading calls it "An Underground City: Inside the Enormous Sewers of Paris". Metadata and description only.

## The network
- "Paris' history can also be told by its sewers. A **Haussmann** legacy that remains in use nearly **150 years** after its creation."
- "This gigantic, complex network is a maze of tunnels: **2,600 kilometers of galleries**, same as the distance between Paris and Moscow, allowing Parisians to carry away their wastewater while also providing them with clean drinking water."
- Built in the **19th century**; the film asks how it "continue[s] to display unrivaled modernity even in this day and age", "What ingenious systems were set up to move millions of cubic meters of water without using any energy?", "What are the roles of the **gate boats, tanks, and spillways**?" and "How do these sewers improve the health of the environment?"
- The workers manage the network "in a dark, confined setting fraught with **lethal gas** on a daily basis".
- The film uses "highly eloquent computer-generated imagery".

## Related link in the description
"Transforming a City - Mega Construction in the Center of Paris" (youtu.be/w4ujyEkYAf8).

wikis.title: Vital Precision: Building Alton Towers' Wicker Man Roller Coaster (FD Engineering)
wikis.summary: A Free Documentary - Engineering video page on Alton Towers building a wooden roller coaster after the 2015 Smiler crash, with the injury figures the description gives.
wikis.body:
## What the page is
YouTube page for "Vital Precision: Building a Wooden Roller Coaster | FD Engineering" on **Free Documentary - Engineering**, published 2023-09-29. Metadata and description only.

## The park and the accident
- "**Alton Towers** is the UK's most popular theme park, attracting millions of visitors each year."
- "on **June 2nd 2015**, something went very wrong. Two carriages collided on one of the park's most popular rides, **the Smiler**. **16 people were injured, five of them seriously**."
- "The ride was closed for the rest of the season and visitor numbers dropped."

## The new ride
- "For the past **three years** the park has been working on how to attract the public back."
- "As well as installing new safety features throughout the park they began developing a new, and even scarier, ride."
- "For inspiration they turned to the themes that also inspired a **70s cult horror movie. The Wickerman**."
- The film follows the ride being "built, tested and launched", with "Alton Towers staff and rollercoaster enthusiasts from all over the UK", asking "will a ride based on **wood, fire and ancient rituals** be enough to bring the thrill seekers back?"

## Related link in the description
"Extreme Constructions - Complete Series" (youtu.be/XKndrP5zT-c).

- "Marble is the most luxurious stone in the world. But it has to be extracted from the mountain through a tough, dangerous process. Only the 'Stone Men' can master this."

wikis.title: Qualcomm's mobile and home connectivity demonstrations at MWC 2015
wikis.summary: Qualcomm press release of March 2, 2015 listing the LTE-Advanced, LTE-Broadcast, LTE/Wi-Fi convergence and smart-lighting demonstrations Qualcomm Technologies and Qualcomm Atheros showed at Mobile World Congress in Barcelona.
wikis.body:
## The release

- "BARCELONA, Spain, March 2, 2015 /PRNewswire/ -- **Qualcomm Incorporated** (NASDAQ: QCOM) announced today that its subsidiaries, **Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. (QTI)** and **Qualcomm Atheros, Inc.**, will showcase an array of connected mobile and home experiences at **Mobile World Congress (MWC)**".
- The demonstrations are "Powered by the latest Qualcomm® Snapdragon™ technologies, and leading-edge LTE-Advanced and Wi-Fi connectivity solutions".
- "Attendees of Mobile World Congress can experience live demonstrations of next-generation mobile connectivity at the Qualcomm booth in **Hall 3, Stand #3E10**."

## Quote

- **Cristiano Amon**, executive vice president, Qualcomm Technologies, Inc., and co-president, QCT: "Mobile connectivity is the integral part of every aspect of the mobile experience and the advances we are showcasing at MWC 2015 will take the industry to new heights. With LTE-Advanced multiplying connectivity speeds, LTE-Broadcast redefining the way we experience premium content delivery, and LTE and Wi-Fi convergence designed to empower operators to provide truly seamless communications for consumers, Qualcomm Technologies' inventions continue to define what is possible through wireless technology."

## What was announced (details in the topic pages)

- **Category 11 LTE-Advanced carrier aggregation** - first public demonstration, up to 600 Mbps.
- **Category 9 LTE-A carrier aggregation** demonstrations at up to 450 Mbps, with LG, Telstra, NETGEAR, Ericsson, CMCC and ZTE, plus LTE TDD-FDD 2x CA at the Ericsson and Nokia booths.
- **Category 6 Dual SIM** connectivity at up to 300 Mbps.
- **LTE-Broadcast** app-update delivery with Facebook and Ericsson.
- **LTE/Wi-Fi Call Continuity** using QTI's IMS client, with Ericsson.
- **LTE/Wi-Fi Link Aggregation**, first public demonstration, with Samsung Electronics' Networks Business, Alcatel-Lucent and KT.
- **LTE-U** (LTE in unlicensed spectrum) live demonstrations in multiple 5GHz channels.
- **LIFX White 800** Wi-Fi smart light using Qualcomm Atheros' QCA4002.

## About Qualcomm (as stated)

- "Qualcomm Incorporated (NASDAQ: QCOM) is a world leader in 3G, 4G and next-generation wireless technologies", including the licensing business **QTL** and "the vast majority of its patent portfolio".
- "Qualcomm Technologies, Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary... operates, along with its subsidiaries, substantially all of Qualcomm's engineering, research and development functions, and substantially all of its products and services businesses, including its semiconductor business, **QCT**."
- "For more than 25 years, Qualcomm ideas and inventions have driven the evolution of digital communications".

## Contacts

- Jon Carvill, Corporate Communications, 1-858-845-5959, corpcomm@qualcomm.com; Warren Kneeshaw, Investor Relations, 1-858-658-4813, ir@qualcomm.com. Source: Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.

wikis.title: Category 11 LTE-Advanced carrier aggregation demonstration
wikis.summary: Qualcomm Technologies' first public demonstration of Category 11 LTE-Advanced carrier aggregation, reaching download speeds of up to 600 Mbps.
wikis.body:
- "QTI will feature the **first public demonstration** of Category 11 LTE-Advanced (LTE-A) Carrier Aggregation (CA) connectivity."
- "Utilizing LTE **Category 11 three-channel 60MHz CA** and **256 Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM)**, and infrastructure provided by **Ericsson**, QTI will showcase download speeds of **up to 600 Mbps**."
- "Such technology is designed to offer OEMs with the latest connectivity options where the 256QAM addition provides enhanced network efficiency, especially in **small cell deployments** for mobile operators."

wikis.title: Category 9 LTE-A carrier aggregation demonstrations
wikis.summary: A set of Category 9 LTE-A carrier aggregation demonstrations at up to 450 Mbps with LG, Telstra, NETGEAR, Ericsson, China Mobile and ZTE, plus LTE TDD-FDD aggregation at partner booths.

wikis.title: Category 6 Dual SIM LTE-A connectivity
wikis.summary: A demonstration of Category 6 LTE-A carrier aggregation in a dual-SIM dual-standby configuration at speeds up to 300 Mbps.
wikis.body:
- "Combining next-generation LTE-A technology with its multimode capabilities, a demonstration for **Category 6 Dual SIM** connectivity will also be featured, showcasing how mobile users can take advantage of speeds **up to 300Mbps** in mobile devices without compromising the benefits of Dual SIM use in many countries around the world."
- "QTI's solution includes LTE-A CA in a **dual standby configuration with dual receive**, which is designed to result in fewer missed calls and lower strain on data throughput."

wikis.title: LTE-Broadcast app updates with Facebook and Ericsson
wikis.summary: A demonstration with Facebook and Ericsson of pushing application updates simultaneously to many devices over LTE-Broadcast.
wikis.body:
- "QTI is teaming up with **Facebook** and **Ericsson** to demonstrate the ability to efficiently push application updates simultaneously to many mobile devices via **LTE-Broadcast**."
- The technology "is designed to utilize the scale of operator LTE networks, relieve network congestion, and deliver high-quality video and large files, all with minimal impact on network capacity".
- "application vendors and app store owners can successfully push application updates to user devices, which offers background file delivery of services and significantly reduces download time and improves network efficiency."
- "With more than a **billion users worldwide**, Facebook's interest in LTE-Broadcast further validates QTI's LTE technology leadership and the value of the business case for evolved Multimedia Broadcast Multicast Service (**eMBMS**)."

wikis.title: LTE/Wi-Fi Call Continuity
wikis.summary: A demonstration with Ericsson of seamless transfer of voice and video calls between LTE and Wi-Fi using QTI's IMS client.
wikis.body:
- "Using QTI's **IP Multimedia Services (IMS)** client, QTI is teaming with **Ericsson** to demonstrate **LTE/Wi-Fi Call Continuity**, which is designed to support seamless transfers of voice and video calls between LTE and Wi-Fi without the hassle of dropping the call."
- "The IMS client gives mobile operators the ability to offload voice and/or video calls to Wi-Fi as a way to optimize network usage and extend LTE calling coverage."
- "With Call Continuity, operators can now offer new bandwidth-intensive video calling services, while offloading some of the added traffic to Wi-Fi networks at the same time."

wikis.title: LTE/Wi-Fi Link Aggregation
wikis.summary: The first public demonstration of aggregating LTE and Wi-Fi radio links in the device, with Samsung's Networks Business, Alcatel-Lucent and KT.
wikis.body:
- "Through efforts made by QTI, **Networks Business of Samsung Electronics**, **Alcatel-Lucent** and **KT**, LTE/Wi-Fi Link Aggregation will be demonstrated publicly **for the first time**."
- "Until now, operator Wi-Fi has existed independently of the operator's LTE network. This technology will bring operator Wi-Fi access points under the direct real-time control of the LTE radio network **without the need for modifications**."
- It lets operators "tap into the capacity of the Wi-Fi access points they own or control, by aggregating LTE and Wi-Fi radio links together in the mobile device", giving users faster throughput and direct access to operator services in more places, and operators "unprecedented levels of control, mobility and offload".

wikis.title: LTE in unlicensed spectrum (LTE-U)
wikis.summary: Live demonstrations of LTE-U coexisting with Wi-Fi in multiple 5GHz channels, plus LTE-U integration into Qualcomm's small cell and RF transceiver products.
wikis.body:
- "To showcase the co-existence of LTE-A and Wi-Fi, QTI will conduct live demonstrations of **LTE in an unlicensed spectrum (LTE-U)**."
- "Extending LTE-A to unlicensed spectrum in a way that coexists with Wi-Fi allows operators to utilize available unlicensed spectrum effectively."
- "The demonstration will show LTE-U in **multiple 5GHz channels**."
- "QTI recently announced the integration of LTE-U into its **FSM99xx** small cells product portfolio, along with the **WTR3950**, the first commercial RF transceiver to support LTE-U in mobile devices."

wikis.title: LIFX White 800 Wi-Fi smart light
wikis.summary: LIFX's announcement, with Qualcomm Atheros, of the LIFX White 800 tunable-white smart bulb built on the QCA4002 Wi-Fi solution.
wikis.body:
- "In conjunction with **Qualcomm Atheros**, **LIFX** announces it will expand its family of smart lights to include the **LIFX White 800**, a new smart light with tunable whites utilizing the **QCA4002**, a feature-rich, low-power Wi-Fi solution by Qualcomm Atheros."
- "The LIFX White 800 allows for ranges of warm white shades to bluish-white variations on daylight adjustable from any smart device."
- "Thanks to built-in Wi-Fi, it connects directly to a home's Wi-Fi network **without the need for a hub or bridge**."
- "The lights are fully compatible with the **Allseen Alliance's** open-source **Lighting Service Framework (LSF)**, which is designed to provide interoperability with **AllJoyn**® enabled smart devices in the home, and are certified 'Designed for AllSeen.'"
- "The LIFX White 800 is powered by the **Lighting Connectivity Module (LCM)**, a turnkey Wi-Fi based smart lighting platform."

wikis.title: Heisman Trophy balloting history and information
wikis.summary: The Heisman Trophy Trust's page explaining who votes for the Heisman, how the ballot and point system work, the key 2026 voting dates and an FAQ on how finalists are chosen.
wikis.body:
## Who votes

- "It was decided that **sports journalists** were the most logical group for this task. As informed, competent and impartial observers, they comprise the vast majority of the electors."
- **Sectional Representatives** "oversaw ballot distribution across broad geographic regions, helped establish fair representation across the country, and laid the foundation for the award's status". "Today, the role of Sectional Representative is largely honorary."
- Recognised Sectional Representatives listed: Chuck Benedict (Glendale News Press, Far West)*, Dave Campbell (Waco-Tribune Herald, Southwest)*, Beano Cook (ESPN, Mid Atlantic)*, Lee Corso (ESPN, South), Don Criqui (CBS Sports, Northeast), Pat Haden (NBC Sports, Far West), Bob Hammel (The Herald Times, Mid West)*, Bob Hammond (Laramie Boomerang, Far West), Tom Harmon (Football Today, Far West)*, Pat Livingston (Pittsburgh Press, Mid Atlantic)*, Jimmie McDowell (Mississippi Sports, South)*, Fred Russell (Nashville Banner, South)*, Dick Weiss (New York Daily News, Mid Atlantic), Maury White (Des Moines Register and Tribune, Mid West)*. ("* indicates deceased".)
- **State Representatives** "are responsible for selecting the voters in each state". "The number of votes allotted to each state reflects both its size and the number of media outlets covering college football, so larger states like California and Texas naturally receive more votes than smaller states such as Vermont and Delaware."

## The six sections

- **Far West**: AZ, CA, HI, ID, MT, ND, NV, OR, SD, UT, WA, WY
- **Mid Atlantic**: DC, DE, MD, NC, NJ, PA, SC, VA, WV
- **Mid West**: IA, IL, IN, MI, MN, OH, WI
- **North East**: CT, MA, ME, NH, NYC, NY, RI, VT
- **South**: AL, FL, GA, KY, LA, MS, TN
- **Southwest**: AR, CO, KS, MO, NE, NM, OK, TX

## The electorate and the ballot

- "Each Section within the United States has **145 media votes**, totaling **870 media votes** across the country. Additionally every living Heisman winner, **60 presently**, has a vote as well."
- "In **1999**, The Heisman Trophy agreed to develop a special program to allow the public at large to become part of the balloting process by permitting **one (1) fan vote** eligible in the overall tabulation, bringing the total number of voters for the **2026 Heisman race to 931**."
- "The actual ballots include a space for electors to designate **three individuals**... The first choice on an elector's ballot receives **three points**..., the second choice receives **two points** and the third choice receives **one point**. A first, second and third choice must be indicated on each ballot." The point system was created "in an effort to eliminate any sectional favoritism". "Ballots are void unless confirmed electronically by the elector."
- Eligibility, quoted from the ballots: "In order that there will be no misunderstanding regarding the eligibility of a candidate, the recipient of the award MUST be a bona fide student of an accredited college or university including the United States Academies. The recipients must be in compliance with the bylaws defining an NCAA student athlete."

## Key Heisman dates for 2026

- **Thursday, December 3**: Ballots distributed to electors, including online login credentials.
- **Saturday, December 5**: Online voting website opens at 5 p.m. EST.
- **Monday, December 7**: Ballots due by 5 p.m. EST.
- **Monday, December 7**: The 2026 Heisman Finalists are announced in the evening.
- **Saturday, December 12**: "The announcement of the 2026 Heisman Trophy Winner via the televised Heisman Ceremony on **ABC**. (Private Event)"

## Heisman Fan Vote

- Cast at heismanfanvote.com, or on social media by posting "@HeismanTrophy I want to vote for #PlayerName".
- "Fans may cast vote **once per day** on the Heisman website and **one vote per day per social media platform**. The Heisman Fan Vote leaderboard is updated every **Friday at 12:00 p.m. ET**."

## FAQ on finalists

- **What is a finalist**: "an active college football player who receives an invitation to attend the annual Heisman ceremony held in New York City each December. Whether that player shows up or not, he is considered a finalist."
- **History**: "Prior to **1982**, only the winner of the Heisman was invited to New York, so there was no such thing as a 'Heisman finalist'." **Herschel Walker, John Elway and Eric Dickerson** were the first finalists, "though Elway did not attend that year's event". "There have been **184 finalists** since that 1982 ceremony."
- **How many**: "Starting in **2021**, the Heisman Trophy Trust has officially invited **four finalists** annually". Before that the number varied, with always at least three; "the total did rise to as high as **eight invitees in 1989** (though only four actually attended)". Since 1982 the most common total invited was **five (11 times)**, then **four (10 times)** and **three (nine times)**; **six** were invited in **1994 and 2013**. "To date, there have never been more than six finalists to actually attend a ceremony."
- **How determined**: "As of 2021, the four invited Heisman finalists are determined by the **top four individuals that receive the most votes**." Before 2021 the number depended on how close successive point totals were. Examples given: in **2008**, Florida's **Tim Tebow** finished third with **1,575 points** while fourth-place **Graham Harrell** of Texas Tech had **213 points**, so Harrell was not invited and the ceremony had three finalists; in **2010**, **Kellen Moore**'s fourth place of **635 points** was close to **LaMichael James**' third place of **916**, so Moore was included, while fifth-placed **Justin Blackmon** of Oklahoma State "had just **105 points**", capping the finalists at four.
- **When**: "The finalists are announced on the **Monday prior** to the televised Heisman Trophy Ceremony."

## Also on the page

- Recent posts listed: "Heisman Hopefuls Entering Week 3"; "Heisman Seasons That Opened With Uphill Battles"; "Thirteen Heisman Winners Kick Off Their 2026 NFL Seasons This Week"; "Impressive performances abounded during the first full weekend of college football". A "2025 Heisman Almanac" link appears in the footer.

- Market open: **Feb 26, 2025 · 10:00am EST**. Market closes: "After the outcome occurs". Projected payout: "30 minutes after closing".
- "This market will close and expire early if the event occurs. Otherwise, it closes by **Jan 1, 2031 at 10:00am EST**."
- The page title says "2030" while the rules and close date both say before Jan 1, 2031.

## Insider trading prohibitions (summary of the listed categories)

- Candidates listed in the event and their immediate family (spouses and dependents); paid campaign staffers; third-party vendors, contractors, consultants and outside counsel engaged by a campaign.
- Paid employees of national, state or congressional party organizations (DNC, RNC, DCCC, NRCC, DSCC, NRSC), of PACs and Super PACs active in a listed race, and registered federal lobbyists retained by them.
- Holders of federal and statewide public office; state legislators on committees with jurisdiction over election administration in a state with a listed race.
- All staff of the U.S. House, the U.S. Senate, the Executive Office of the President, the U.S. Supreme Court; FEC commissioners and staff; senior (Schedule C) staff of federal agencies with election jurisdiction, "including without limitation the Department of Justice (Public Integrity Section, Election Crimes Branch, and Civil Rights Division Voting Section) and the Department of Homeland Security (CISA)".
- Federal and state judges presiding over related litigation; all Electors; Secretaries of State and election administration officials and senior staff; "Any person working in a vote-tallying capacity, or who has the potential ability to observe official vote counts before they are public".
- Paid employees of major polling organizations (with the Exchange maintaining and publishing the list of "major" ones, noting the ban "does not apply to all employees of Quinnipiac University despite the presence of Quinnipiac University's polling division").
- Decision Desk employees at major media organizations "including but not limited to Fox News, ABC News, the Associated Press, CNN, CBS News, Decision Desk HQ, NBC News, The New York Times, and Reuters", and exit-polling/election-night survey operations "including but not limited to Edison Research and the National Election Pool".

That's the promise House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries has made, previewing an ambitious agenda if Democrats seize majority control from Republicans in the midterm elections."

wikis.title: Bosch press kit: chip factory of the future in Dresden
wikis.summary: Bosch Media Service press-kit page for the opening of the company's 300-millimetre wafer fab in Dresden, indexing the releases, factsheets, images and videos and carrying Bosch's corporate boilerplate.
wikis.body:
## The press kit

- Bosch Media Service presskit, headed "**Bosch opens chip factory of the future in Dresden**", dated at the top **25.05.2021**, tagged "#Connected mobility".
- Media contact: **Athanassios Kaliudis**, "Spokesperson mobility, software, semiconductor", +49 711 811-7497, athanassios.kaliudis@de.bosch.com.
- Contents listed: press releases, fact sheets, photos, videos and links, plus a "Video recording press conference" and a "Video recording opening ceremony". Media counts: **Images (63)**, **Videos (06)**.

## Items in the kit, with their dates

- **Lead release, 07.06.2021**: press release "Bosch opens wafer fab of the future in Dresden".
- **07.06.2021**, presentations: "Bosch opens new wafer fab in Dresden: fully connected, full of artificial intelligence"; "Come and see the future in Dresden: the new wafer fab is giving birth to technology for tomorrow's world".
- **25.05.2021**, press release: "Six reasons why Bosch's new 300-millimeter wafer fab is one of the world's most modern chip factories".
- **08.03.2021**, press release: "Bosch reaches milestone on the way to opening new wafer fab in Dresden".
- Factsheets: **21.08.2023** "300 milimeters wafer fab in Dresden"; **28.05.2021** "Semiconductor production at Bosch"; **28.10.2021** "Reutlingen wafer fab"; **25.05.2021** "Semiconductor terminology"; **25.05.2021** "Facts, figures, and amazing truths about semiconductors".
- The page's own date stamp is 25.05.2021, although it indexes material dated up to 2023 and an "Explore more" list of Bosch press releases dated **17.09.2026**, **15.09.2026** and **14.09.2026**, and its boilerplate carries 2025 figures.

## What the image and video captions name

- "Official opening of the **300-millimeter wafer fab** in Dresden"; "**Michael Kretschmer**, Minister-President of **Saxony**".
- "Plant with '**digital twin**'"; "**MEMS sensors** from Bosch"; "Bosch semiconductor portfolio"; "First wafers pass through **fully automated** fabrication process at Bosch's new wafer fab in Dresden".
- TV footage includes drone recordings and footage of the construction work.

## Bosch boilerplate (as printed on the page)

- "Mobility is the largest Bosch Group business sector. It generated sales of **55,8 billion euros in 2025**, and thus contributed around **61 percent** of total sales." Main areas: "electrification, software and services, semiconductors and sensors, vehicle computers, advanced driver assistance systems, systems for vehicle dynamics control, repair-shop concepts, as well as technology and services for the automotive aftermarket and fleets."
- "Bosch is synonymous with important automotive innovations, such as electronic engine management, the **ESP** anti-skid system, and **common-rail diesel** technology."
- "The Bosch Group ... employs roughly **413,000 associates** worldwide (as of **December 31, 2025**). The company generated sales of **91 billion euros in 2025**." Four business sectors: Mobility, Industrial Technology, Consumer Goods, and Energy and Building Technology.
- "The Bosch Group comprises **Robert Bosch GmbH** and its roughly **500** subsidiary and regional companies in over **60 countries**." "Bosch employs some **82,000 associates** in research and development."
- Motto quoted: technology "Invented for life". Further information at www.bosch.com and www.bosch-press.com.

## Note on the capture

- The captured page is the press-kit index rather than the press release itself: apart from the boilerplate and the dated list above, it is largely asset titles and share/download controls. It gives no figures for the fab's investment, capacity or headcount.

wikis.title: Ford's 2027 midsize electric pickup with a $30K start price
wikis.summary: Equipment World report on Ford's announcement of a US-built 2027 midsize electric pickup starting around $30,000, its $5 billion plant investment and the new Universal EV Platform and "assembly tree" production system.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- "Following news Ford was **delaying updates to its electric Ford F-150 Lightning until 2028**, the company revealed it will produce a new, smaller electric pickup for **2027** - a midsize model with a starting price of about **$30,000**."
- The photo caption dates the announcement: "Ford President and CEO announces on **August 11** a 2027 midsize electric truck to be assembled in **Louisville, Kentucky**, and its battery package in **Marshall, Michigan**."
- Ford "will spend **$5 billion combined** to expand its **Louisville Assembly Plant** in Kentucky and on its **BlueOval Battery Park Michigan** complex. The company says the investments will require **4,000 employees**, a mix of new and current."
- President and CEO **Jim Farley** "likened it to a modern-day version of Ford's historic assembly line invention for the Model T developed **120 years ago**". "The company notes that the $30,000 price tag is equivalent to the price of a newly produced Model T in the early 1900s, when adjusted for inflation."
- Farley: "We tore up the moving assembly line concept and designed a better one. And we found a path to be the first automaker to make prismatic LFP batteries in the U.S."

## The truck

- Four-door midsize pickup, "powered by lighter, lower-cost **lithium iron phosphate prismatic batteries**", assembled in Louisville, "with a targeted customer delivery of **2027** and a starting price of around **$30,000**".
- For comparison, the article notes "The starting MSRP for a **2025 Ford Lightning Pro is $54,780**", and that Ford "has delayed updates to the best-selling electric pickup in the U.S. and its **E-Transit** commercial van until **2028**."
- The LFP battery packs are "**cobalt- and nickel-free**" and "will serve as the vehicle floor's substructure. 'This low center of gravity improves handling, creates a quiet cabin and provides a surprising amount of interior space,' the company says."
- "The result will be a truck with more passenger room than **Toyota's RAV4**, with a bed and front trunk, or 'frunk,' according to Ford."
- "Ford says it is shooting for the same **0-60 mph** speed as its **Mustang EcoBoost**, which is about **4.5 seconds**."
- "Ford claims the truck will have a lower cost of ownership over five years than a three-year-old used **Tesla Model Y**."
- "Further details, including battery range and charge time, will be revealed later, according to Ford."

## Universal EV Platform

- The platform "reduces parts by **20%**", "requires **25% fewer fasteners** and a **40% reduction in workstations**", and "should speed up assembly by **15%**".
- The midsize pickup "will be the first vehicle produced under the new platform, with Ford saying more vehicles will follow." The platform "enables a family of affordable vehicles to be produced at scale for customers - electric, fun to drive and digitally advanced with over-the-air updates that will keep improving the vehicle."

## The "assembly tree"

- "Instead of one long conveyor, three sub-assemblies run down their own lines simultaneously and then join together. Large single-piece aluminum unicastings replace dozens of smaller parts, enabling the front and rear of the vehicle to be assembled separately."
- The battery system, seats, consoles and carpeting are assembled separately in parallel; components then arrive at Louisville "as a kit that includes the fasteners, scanners and power tools laid out in order of assembly".
- "Ford says this Universal EV Production System will increase assembly speed by **40%** at the Louisville plant. 'Some of that time will be reinvested into insourcing and automation to improve quality and cost, ultimately netting a **15% speed improvement**,' according to Ford."

## Plant investment and jobs

- Of the $5 billion, "**$2 billion** will go to the Louisville plant where **2,200 hourly employees** will work, the company says. However, that's a drop from the current **2,800** employed at the plant, according to courier-journal.com."
- "The company told the newspaper there will be **no layoffs**, that employees will be offered buyouts or allowed to transfer to other plants."
- "The **Kentucky Economic Development Finance Authority** provided **$120 million in tax incentives** for the plant's **52,000-square-foot** expansion, according to courier-journal.com."
- "For battery production, the remaining **$3 billion** will go to the BlueOval Battery Park Michigan. The plant will start building the prismatic LFP batteries **next year**, according to Ford."

## Note

- The plant headcount figures sit awkwardly together on the page: the investment "will require 4,000 employees, a mix of new and current", while Louisville is said to employ 2,200 hourly workers, down from 2,800 today.

wikis.title: Spotify Wrapped 2025: the top artists, songs, albums, podcasts and audiobooks
wikis.summary: Spotify Newsroom's 2025 Wrapped announcement, giving the global and U.S. top-ten lists for artists, songs, albums, podcasts and audiobooks along with the trends Spotify draws from them.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- Published on the Spotify Newsroom, dated **December 3, 2025**, tagged "2025 WRAPPED".
- "With more than **700 million listeners** around the world turning to Spotify to soundtrack their lives, it's time to look back at the audio that defined the year."
- "The year in music was marked by the return of a global superstar to the top spot, powerful collaborations that became instant classics, and a film soundtrack that took the world by storm. Meanwhile, in the world of podcasts and audiobooks, long-running fan favorites continued their dominance while the fantasy genre proved its undeniable power."

## Headline result

- "For the **fourth time**, after claiming the title in **2020, 2021, and 2022**, our users have crowned **Bad Bunny** Spotify's top artist globally, with **19.8 billion streams** this year."
- "He also clinched the global top album of 2025 with **DeBÍ TiRAR MáS FOToS**."
- Spotify is "launching a global campaign honoring the superstar and his fans, including a short film, **Leap Year**, unique fan activations around the globe, and on-platform surprises."
- "Rounding out the top five artists are **Taylor Swift** in second place (but **first in the U.S.**), followed by **The Weeknd** (third), **Drake** (fourth), and **Billie Eilish** (fifth)."

## Sections

The article breaks its results into music, podcasts and audiobooks, then repeats the lists for the U.S. - see the topic pages.

wikis.title: Wrapped 2025: global music lists
wikis.summary: Spotify's global top-ten artists, songs and albums of 2025, with the collaboration and soundtrack trends Spotify highlights.
wikis.body:
**Trend**: "This year's most-streamed music tells a story of both superstar collaborations and enduring fan favorites." **Lady Gaga and Bruno Mars**' "Die With A Smile" took top song globally "with over **1.7 billion streams**", while **ROSÉ and Bruno Mars** took number three with "APT.". "Billie Eilish's 'BIRDS OF A FEATHER' climbed from number three in 2024 to the number-two spot this year." On albums, "the influence of the screen was also undeniable, as **KPop Demon Hunters (Soundtrack from the Netflix Film)** captured the number-two spot", and Billie Eilish's *HIT ME HARD AND SOFT* and Sabrina Carpenter's *Short n' Sweet* "both returned to the top five for the second year in a row".

**Top artists globally**: 1 Bad Bunny, 2 Taylor Swift, 3 The Weeknd, 4 Drake, 5 Billie Eilish, 6 Kendrick Lamar, 7 Bruno Mars, 8 Ariana Grande, 9 Arijit Singh, 10 Fuerza Regida.

**Top songs globally**: 1 "Die With A Smile" - Lady Gaga and Bruno Mars; 2 "BIRDS OF A FEATHER" - Billie Eilish; 3 "APT." - ROSÉ and Bruno Mars; 4 "Ordinary" - Alex Warren; 5 "DtMF" - Bad Bunny; 6 "back to friends" - sombr; 7 "Golden" - HUNTR/X, EJAE, AUDREY NUNA, REI AMI, KPop Demon Hunters Cast; 8 "luther (with sza)" - Kendrick Lamar and SZA; 9 "That's So True" - Gracie Abrams; 10 "Wildflower" - Billie Eilish.

**Top albums globally**: 1 *DeBÍ TiRAR MáS FOToS* - Bad Bunny; 2 *KPop Demon Hunters (Soundtrack from the Netflix Film)* - KPop Demon Hunters Cast, HUNTR/X, Saja Boys; 3 *HIT ME HARD AND SOFT* - Billie Eilish; 4 *SOS Deluxe: LANA* - SZA; 5 *Short n' Sweet* - Sabrina Carpenter; 6 *MAYHEM* - Lady Gaga; 7 *You'll Be Alright, Kid* - Alex Warren; 8 *I'm The Problem* - Morgan Wallen; 9 *GNX* - Kendrick Lamar; 10 *Un Verano Sin Ti* - Bad Bunny.

wikis.title: Wrapped 2025: global podcasts
wikis.summary: Spotify's global top-ten podcasts of 2025, led by The Joe Rogan Experience for a sixth consecutive year.
wikis.body:
- "For the **sixth consecutive year**, **The Joe Rogan Experience** was Spotify's top podcast globally, followed by **The Diary Of A CEO with Steven Bartlett** and **The Mel Robbins Podcast** in second and third place, respectively."
- "podcasts also became the go-to space for making sense of 2025's biggest cultural moments in real time. From decoding the **TikTok blackout** to reacting to unscripted awards show drama and celebrity engagements, listeners turned to a wide range of shows for instant analysis and community."

## Video
- Title: "Europe's Mega Port: The Giant Logistics Hub of Rotterdam | FD Engineering"
- Channel: Free Documentary - Engineering
- Published: 2026-04-02

## Figures the description gives
- "The Port of Rotterdam is among the largest logistics centers in the world. With a handling capacity of about **one million three hundred thousand tons - per day**!"
- "More than **180,000 people** work in the port area" - "From maritime pilots and terminal operators to coast guards."
- "Every year, more than **130,000 ships** call at Europe's largest seaport. Container ships, inland ships and cruise ships. A total of **350 a day**."
- "With **140 million tons of container goods** entering the port each year, 'unwanted' cargo also gets through."
- "**Europol estimates that half of all cocaine circulating in Europe is smuggled through Rotterdam.** Suspicious containers are a case for customs. **650 officers** are on duty in the Port of Rotterdam every day."
- "The operator **ECT** opened the **world's first automated terminal** here all the way back in **1993**. The **100 automated vehicles** are the secret of this terminal's success. They were invented in Rotterdam, and are now gaining ground at more and more ports around the world. They save on personnel costs - and time."
- "The Universe of the port of Rotterdam: A giant hub, **bigger than the island of Manhattan**."
- "Punctuality is the definitive factor for success at Europe's largest port."

## Video
- Title: "Reviving a War Machine: Saab JAS 39 Gripen Maintenance | FD Engineering"
- Channel: Free Documentary - Engineering
- Published: 2025-05-11

## What the description says
- "It is one of the most popular and best fighter jets in the world: **JAS 39**. The so called 'Gripen' is a light single-engine multirole fighter aircraft manufactured by the Swedish aerospace company **Saab**."
- "At the **Czech Air Force Base in Caslav**, the jet gets the biggest overhaul of its lifetime!"
- "In only **40 days**, the Gripen is stripped down to its bone, everything from the ejection seat to the engine is removed and checked."
- "The **14 Gripen** of the airbase are part of the '**Quick Reaction Alert**' Force of **NATO**. If they are not in the air, the airspace is not protected. That puts a lot of time pressure and liability to the **11 mechanics**, who are responsible for the aircraft."
- Checks listed: the hydraulic system, all moving parts and the oil ("the aircraft's blood ... without it, the pilot is not able to control the jet"); the ejection seat ("the pilot's life insurance"); the access panel ("the skin"); "the biggest part is the engine check: the turbine is the heart of the Gripen"; and finally the weapon system ("the fist") is disassembled "so the gun is working when it is needed in action".
- "Every fault they will find means a delay to the schedule."
