wikis.title: Boston Dynamics to Begin Production on Redesigned Atlas Humanoid in 2026
wikis.summary: A3's trade report from CES 2026 on Boston Dynamics unveiling the production Atlas, giving the robot's specifications, its safety design, the Google DeepMind partnership and Hyundai's deployment plans.
wikis.body:
## The event

- By Brian Heater, Managing Editor, A3; dated 01/05/2026.
- "Boston Dynamics tagged along with parent company Hyundai to Las Vegas for this year's CES... 2026 is seeing it take centerstage, as robotics takes an increased focus at the one-time consumer electronics show."
- "The event saw a handful of big announcements, including an embodied AI partnership with Google's DeepMind division, as well as the debut of the production version of the company's electric humanoid, Atlas."
- "Up to now, Boston Dynamics videos have featured a technically impressive - but considerably less scalable - version of the bipedal robot, owing in part to expensive production costs."

## Production and customers

- "This version, while not cheap, is going going into production this year, with the first models landing roles in Hyundai's own Robotics Metaplant Application Center (RMAC), as well as Google's DeepMind offices."
- "Additional customers beyond Hyundai and Google will begin receiving the robot at some point in early 2027, per the company."
- "Hyundai had previously stated its intent to deploy '10,000s of thousands' of Boston Dynamics robotics in its facilities in coming years - a list that also includes the company's Stretch and Spot systems."
- "Hyundai has also claimed that a recent $26 billion investment in U.S. manufacturing put its high-profile robotics division on track to produce around 30,000 systems per year from a single factory."

## Specifications as this page gives them

- "The new robot is 6.2 feet tall and sports a 7.5-foot reach. It's able to lift payloads of up to 66 pounds and operate in temperatures ranging from -4 to 104F." The temperature range matters "for warehouses that rely on truck deliveries, which can get extremely hot and cold when exposed to the elements".
- "an IP67 - meaning the humanoid sports strong water- and dust-proofing, so you can actually hose it off, as needed."
- "The new Atlas operates with a stated battery life of four hours, prolonged indefinitely by the robot's ability to hot swap its own on-board batteries in around three minutes."

## Safety design

- The system is pitched to operate "outside a controlled, cage environment, alongside human coworkers, making safety paramount". Boston Dynamics has been among a handful of humanoid firms, including Agility, working to write standards for these systems.
- Quoting the company: "Leveraging best practices from the autonomous vehicle industry, Atlas has an onboard safety system to help it detect people and vehicles in busy workplaces. This allows for operation with fenceless guarding; if a person walks by within a certain radius, the robot pauses and waits for them to pass. The robot is also designed with padding and minimal pinch points as added safety precautions around people."

## Google DeepMind partnership

- "CES also sees the announcements of a new partnership between Boston Dynamics and Google DeepMind - though the deal isn't exactly an exclusive for either side. Google's operations have enlisted Apptronik Apollo humanoid robots in public-facing tests, while Boston Dynamics has previously teamed with TRI (Toyota Research Institute) on AI learning research."
- Carolina Parada, Google DeepMind senior director: "We developed our Gemini Robotics models to bring AI into the physical world. We are excited to begin working with the Boston Dynamics team to explore what's possible with their new Atlas robot as we develop new models to expand the impact of robotics, and to scale robots safely and efficiently."
- The research, deploying Gemini Robotics foundational models on the new humanoid, is set to begin in "the coming months".

## Context and caveats the writer adds

- Robert Playter, CEO: "This is the best robot we have ever built. Atlas is going to revolutionize the way industry works..."
- On the company's claim that "Atlas will add value from day one, and much like Spot and Stretch, most customers will see ROI within the first two years of adoption", the writer notes: "we'll obviously have to just wait and see on that one. Return on investment remains a massive question mark as far as deploying these systems in the field, and use cases are likely to be fairly limited in the earliest stages."
- Boston Dynamics is "a bit less clear on what the initial tasks will be", saying it is "starting to work with select customers to evaluate, train, and perfect feature-rich, autonomous material handling solutions". Material handling has been the key focus for Agility, "whose Digit robot has made the most real-world progress among U.S.-based humanoids".
- "Boston Dynamics only announced its intention to build a commercial humanoid in 2024, after it became clear that recent AI advances had accelerated the pace of how robots could be trained and deployed into real-world applications."
- "Atlas will be its third commercially available robot, following the Spot quadruped and Stretch, a truck unloading robot... Atlas will join Stretch in focusing on factory and warehouse floors."

wikis.title: NEO Home Robot launch and ordering page
wikis.summary: 1X's own page announcing NEO, its consumer home humanoid - the chores and assistant features, the tendon-drive hardware platform, and pre-order pricing and delivery plans.
wikis.body:
## The launch

- Dated OCT 28 '25, bylined Eric Jang, Dar Sleeper and Bernt Bornich.
- "Palo Alto, CA, October 28, 2025 - 1X is proud to announce the launch of NEO, the world's first consumer-ready humanoid robot designed to transform life at home. NEO automates everyday chores and offers personalized assistance so people can spend more time on the things that matter."
- "With intuitive, user-friendly features and a revolutionary hardware platform, NEO is the safest, most affordable, and most capable humanoid on earth."
- Bernt Bornich, CEO and Founder: "Humanoids were long a thing of sci-fi... then they were a thing of research, but today - with the launch of NEO - humanoid robots become a product. Something that you and me can reach out and touch."

## What NEO does

- **Chores:** owners give NEO a list of tasks, schedule when they should be done, "and come back to a cleaner space every day". It can also handle chores in real time nearby. Tasks named: folding laundry, organizing shelves, tidying spaces. "For any chore that NEO doesn't yet know, owners can schedule a 1X Expert to guide it through unknown tasks - helping NEO learn while getting the job done."
- **Personalized intelligence:** a built-in large language model for natural conversation; it can recognize ingredients on a kitchen counter and suggest dishes. "Memory enables continuity across conversations, allowing NEO to recall past context and adapt its responses over time" - scheduling appointments, birthday reminders, grocery lists, tracking progress in language lessons.
- **Autonomy and learning:** "NEO will arrive to early owners with the ability to handle basic tasks, and with continued use, learn and develop new skills. From the first day, NEO performs functions like opening doors for guests, fetching items, and turning off the lights at night - and grows in abilities with every software update." It uses 1X's AI model trained on real-world data.

## Hardware

- A platform that "succeeds 1X's prior models (NEO Gamma and NEO Beta)".
- "NEO is built with 1X's patented Tendon Drive that uses the highest-torque density motors on earth to drive its tendon-based transmissions. This one-of-a-kind actuation system creates gentle movements that make NEO uniquely safe and compliant around people."
- "Human Level Dexterity (22 DoF Hands) and a head-to-toe soft body made of custom 3D lattice polymer structures."
- "At just 66 pounds (29.94 kg), NEO is capable of lifting over 150 pounds (68 kg) and carrying 55 pounds (24.95kg), and has a noise level of 22dB - making it more silent than a modern day refrigerator."
- Built-in WiFi, Bluetooth and 5G, plus "a three-stage speaker in the pelvis and chest area, giving owners a built-in mobile home entertainment system".
- Design: "organic neutral tones, and a soft knit suit and shoes", meant to complement living spaces rather than disrupt them.

## Pricing and availability

- "NEO is now available for pre-order, with first orders shipping to consumer homes in 2026."
- Available via 1X's online store (1x.tech/order) in three colors: Tan, Gray, Dark Brown.
- "Early Access for $20,000, which includes priority delivery in 2026. There is also a subscription model offering of $499/month which will be shipped at a later date."
- "1X will start delivering NEOs primarily in the U.S in 2026 and expand to other markets starting in 2027."

## Later items listed on the page

- "NEO's Hands | An API to the Physical World" (JUL 09 '26): "our breakthrough 25 Degree of Freedom (DOF), tendon-driven hands for the NEO humanoid platform - achieving near human-level dexterity, strength, safety, and reliability."
- Bill Nash announced as CFO (JUL 02 '26) and Tom Sanocki as VP of Engineering (JUN 25 '26).
- Credit given: "Eli Russell Linnetz for capturing NEO for this campaign."

wikis.title: Boston Dynamics Unveils New Atlas Robot to Revolutionize Industry
wikis.summary: Boston Dynamics' announcement of the product version of its electric Atlas humanoid at CES 2026, with production plans, committed deployments, the robot's specifications and the Google DeepMind and Hyundai Mobis partnerships.
wikis.body:
## The unveiling

- "LAS VEGAS (Jan. 5, 2026) - Boston Dynamics, the global leader in mobile robotics, unveiled the product version of its new Atlas robot at the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas today."
- "The fully electric humanoid was revealed during Hyundai's global CES media day presentation, which also featured a live stage demonstration of the prototype version of Atlas, in addition to a rousing dance performance by a troupe of its famous Spot robots."

## Production and deployments

- "The company will begin production of the new Atlas robots at its Boston headquarters immediately."
- "All Atlas deployments are already fully committed for 2026, with fleets scheduled to ship to Hyundai's Robotics Metaplant Application Center (RMAC) and Google DeepMind in the coming months."
- "The company plans to add additional customers in early 2027."

## Quotes

- Robert Playter, CEO of Boston Dynamics: "For more than 30 years, Boston Dynamics has been building some of the world's most advanced robots. This is the best robot we have ever built. Atlas is going to revolutionize the way industry works, and it marks the first step toward a long-term goal we have dreamed about since we were children - useful robots that can walk into our homes and help make our lives safer, more productive, and more fulfilling."
- Zack Jackowski, GM of Atlas: "Our new Atlas is the most production friendly robot we've ever designed. This generation of Atlas significantly reduces the amount of unique parts in the robot, and every component has been designed for compatibility with automotive supply chains. With Hyundai Motor Group's backing, we will achieve the best reliability and economies of scale in the industry."

## What Atlas is

- "an enterprise grade humanoid robot that can perform a wide array of industrial tasks, from material handling to order fulfilment. The robot learns new tasks quickly, adapts to dynamic environments, lifts heavy loads, and works autonomously with minimal supervision."
- It "does not need to stop even when its battery power runs low - it will autonomously navigate to a charging station, swap out its own batteries, and get right back to work."
- It connects to MES, WMS and other industrial systems via Boston Dynamics' Orbit software, and "once a single Atlas robot learns a new task, that task can immediately be replicated across the entire fleet of robots".
- Control: three modes - autonomous, teleoperated, or a tablet steering interface.
- Specifications: "56 degrees of freedom, fully rotational joints, a reach extending to 2.3M (7.5 ft), and the strength to lift up to 50 kg (110 lbs)".
- "extremely water-resistant and can operate at diverse temperature ranges from -20 to 40 C (-4 to 104 F)". Safety features include human detection and fenceless guarding; it can be integrated into workflows using barcode scanners or RFID.

## Partnerships announced alongside

- A new partnership with Google DeepMind "that aims to integrate cutting edge Google DeepMind foundation models into Atlas to give the robot greater cognitive capabilities".
- "Hyundai Mobis will supply the actuators for Atlas, and the two organizations will work together to build a highly reliable component supply chain and accelerate the pace of actuator development and production."

## Hyundai's plans

- "Hyundai Motor Group, Boston Dynamics' majority shareholder, is preparing to deploy tens of thousands of Boston Dynamics' robots into its own manufacturing facilities."
- "The company also recently announced a $26 billion investment in its U.S. operations, including plans to build a new robotics factory capable of producing 30,000 robots per year."

## Portfolio (as stated in the boilerplate)

- Spot, a quadruped for industrial inspections and public safety; Stretch, a box-moving robot deployed with logistics and retail customers; and Atlas, "our electric humanoid platform currently in development".

wikis.title: Boston Dynamics Atlas Named 'Best Robot' in Best of CES 2026 Awards by CNET Group
wikis.summary: Hyundai's newsroom release on Atlas winning CNET Group's 'Best Robot' at CES 2026, with the judges' reasoning and the deployment timeline for Atlas at Metaplant America.
wikis.body:
## The award

- "SEOUL/LAS VEGAS, January 9, 2026 - Hyundai Motor Group (the Group) affiliate Boston Dynamics' Atlas has won CNET Group's 'Best Robot' award as part of the Best of CES 2026 awards." (The newsroom page itself is dated January 12, 2026.)
- "CNET Group is comprised of the leading technology brands CNET, PCMag, Mashable, ZDNET, and Lifehacker."
- The awards "are voted on by leading tech journalists from CNET, PCMag, Mashable, ZDNET and Lifehacker", with a voting panel of more than 40 experts.
- Atlas won "thanks to several key factors, including its natural, human-like walk and sleek design".

## What the judges said

- CNET Group: "The Atlas was hands-down the best of the humanoid bunch we saw at CES 2026. The prototype version demoed at the show impressed us with its naturalistic walking gait. Meanwhile, the sleek product version is ready to be deployed into Hyundai manufacturing facilities from this year, where it might just be working on your next car."
- "According to CNET Group, Best of CES award winners are '...the most inspiring, boundary-pushing tech products that will define the technology landscape this year.'"

## Robert Playter, Boston Dynamics CEO

- "We were honored and excited to accept the 'Best of CES' award in the robotics category last night. Atlas is the best robot we have ever built, and this kind of recognition is a testament to all the hard work our teams have put into bringing the world's most capable humanoid to market. We would like to thank the CNET Group, all our colleagues back in Boston, and the entire Hyundai Motor Group family for providing such an amazing showcase for our new robot at CES 2026."

## Deployment timeline

- "Atlas will be deployed at Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America in Savannah, Georgia by 2028, initially focusing on processes with proven safety and quality benefits, such as parts sequencing."
- "By 2030, applications will extend to component assembly, and over time, Atlas will also take on tasks involving repetitive motions, heavy loads, and other complex operations - ensuring safer working environments for factory employees to advance smart factory innovation."
- "As Atlas's performance is validated, the Group aims to progressively scale adoption across entire production sites."
- A headline bullet also gives "Atlas to be deployed at Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America in the U.S. by 2028, with the aim of further global expansion by 2030".

## Context

- "Unveiled as part of Hyundai Motor Group's AI Robotics Strategy in Las Vegas, Atlas made its debut at CES, the world's most powerful tech event, showcasing how humans will partner with co-working robots in the future."
- "Atlas made its debut at Hyundai Motor Group's CES 2026 media conference, which outlined the Group's AI robotics strategy to lead the physical AI era."
- Atlas is described as "a general-purpose humanoid... built to integrate with existing facilities, ensuring the flexibility to adapt as business needs evolve".
- Page tags: #Boston Dynamics #Atlas #CES #CNET #Best Robot

wikis.title: Hyundai Motor Group Announces AI Robotics Strategy to Lead Human-Centered Robotics Era at CES 2026
wikis.summary: Hyundai Motor Group's CES 2026 press release setting out its AI Robotics Strategy - three foundational partnerships, the Atlas product model and its specifications, and the RMAC-to-Metaplant deployment timeline.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- "SEOUL/LAS VEGAS, January 5, 2026 - Hyundai Motor Group (the Group) today unveiled its transformative AI Robotics Strategy at the Consumer Electronics Show 2026 (CES 2026), presenting a bold roadmap for advancing human-robot collaboration under the theme 'Partnering Human Progress'."
- The theme builds on CES 2022's 'Expanding Human Reach', "evolving hardware-driven robotics into adaptive, artificial intelligence-driven robots designed to amplify human potential".
- The Group showcased Atlas, Spot and MobED with AI Robotics integration at its CES 2026 booth, "featuring interactive experiences and live demonstrations".

## The three foundational partnerships

1. **Partnering humans with co-working robots:** "Robots designed to assist and collaborate with people starting from manufacturing environments, performing hazardous and dangerous, as well as repetitive tasks."
2. **Partnering the Group Value Network with Boston Dynamics:** "Combining Boston Dynamics' expertise in AI Robotics with Hyundai Motor Group's global scale and manufacturing capabilities to create safe training grounds and an End-to-End (E2E) AI Robotics value chain."
3. **Partnering with AI leaders:** "Collaborating with global AI pioneers to open new chapters in AI Robotics innovation and drive the vision of 'Progress for Humanity'."

## Physical AI

- "Physical AI refers to the tangible realization of technologies that collect data using hardware in real-world environments to make autonomous decisions - spanning areas such as robotics, smart factories, and autonomous driving."
- The Group will "establish a cycle of continuous improvement by digitizing real-world data for AI learning", and "promote the establishment of the Hyundai Motor Group Physical AI Application Center". It also "plans to build a robot manufacturing and foundry plant based on customized robotics technologies developed through Physical AI".

## Existing deployments

- "Spot, the agile quadruped, is now operational in more than 40 countries, performing critical tasks such as data collection and safety monitoring in industrial sites."
- "Stretch, the warehouse robot, has unloaded more than 20 million boxes globally since its launch in 2023."
- Boston Dynamics "has been a pioneer in pushing the boundaries of robotics for more than 30 years".

## Atlas

- "Unveiled at CES 2026, the Atlas humanoid robot presents a groundbreaking leap in robotics innovation designed for industrial applications."
- "The Atlas prototype serves as a research model, testing core capabilities essential for future products."
- The Atlas product has "56 degrees of freedom (DoF), most with fully rotational joints, and human-scale hands with tactile sensing", supporting "material sequencing, assembly, and machine tending".
- Capabilities listed:
  - **Ease of task training:** "Most tasks can be taught in under a day."
  - **Autonomy and self-sufficiency:** "Atlas operates independently from day one, with capabilities such as automatic battery replacement and continuous operation."
  - **Strength and precision:** "Able to lift up to 110 lbs (50 kg) and perform precision tasks."
  - **Durable and weatherproof:** "water resistant, designed for washdowns, and operates at its full capabilities - including strength capacity - between -4 and 104 degrees Fahrenheit (20C to 40 Celsius)".
- "Hyundai Motor Group expects humanoids to become the largest segment of the Physical AI market in the future and has set a goal to mass-produce the Atlas product model."

## Deployment timeline

- Headline bullet: "Atlas to be deployed at HMGMA by 2028 for sequencing tasks, advancing human-centric smart factory innovation."
- "the Group plans to integrate Atlas across its global network, including Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America (HMGMA) in Savannah, Georgia."
- "Beginning in 2028, Atlas will be introduced on processes with proven safety and quality benefits, such as parts sequencing. By 2030, applications will extend to component assembly, and over time, Atlas will also take on tasks involving repetitive motions, heavy loads, and other complex operations."
- "RMAC anchors the Group's AI Robotics roadmap, with the facility set to open in 2026, in the U.S. By 2028, RMAC-trained Atlas robots will be deployed for highly repetitive sequencing tasks, progressing to complex assembly work by 2030."

## The Group Value Network

- At its core is "an End-to-End (E2E) AI Robotics Value Chain, leveraging the Group's world-class automotive production infrastructure, know-how for safety and reliability, and the diverse technological capabilities of its affiliates".
- **Software-Defined Factory (SDF):** "an advanced smart factory powered by data and software", first introduced at Hyundai Motor Group Innovation Center Singapore (HMGICS) and evolving into the latest SDF platform at HMGMA.
- **Robot Metaplant Application Center (RMAC):** "the 'engine' of the Group's AI Robotics business, where robots learn human collaboration by mapping movements such as lifts, turns, and recoveries into precision training for repetitive and complex tasks." Training data from RMAC plus real operational data from SDF "create a cyclical synergy that enables continuous retraining".
- **Affiliate roles:** Hyundai Motor Company and Kia provide manufacturing infrastructure, process control and large-scale production data; Hyundai Mobis works with Boston Dynamics on high-performance actuators, marking "its official entry into the global robotics components market"; Hyundai Glovis optimizes logistics and supply chain management.
- **NVIDIA:** "Since last January, the Group has continued to strengthen its strategic partnership with NVIDIA", planning to use NVIDIA's AI infrastructure, simulation libraries and frameworks. "the Ministry of Science and ICT of the Republic of Korea, Hyundai Motor Group, and NVIDIA signed an MoU to enhance national Physical AI capabilities."
- Boston Dynamics and Google DeepMind's collaboration on next-generation humanoids is listed among the AI partnerships.

wikis.title: Introducing Blue Jay and Project Eluna, Amazon's latest robotics and AI technology for its operations
wikis.summary: Amazon's announcement of two operations systems - the Blue Jay multi-arm robotic workstation and the Project Eluna agentic AI assistant - carrying a later update saying Blue Jay is no longer in use.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- Published October 22, 2025, written by Tyler Greenawalt, under Amazon Robotics / Artificial Intelligence / Operations.
- Standfirst: "Designed with Amazon's front-line employees in mind, these innovations reduce repetitive tasks, improve safety, and boost productivity - while speeding up delivery."
- Two new systems: "Blue Jay, a system coordinating multiple robotic arms, and Project Eluna, an agentic AI model helping operators make more informed decisions."
- They "build on recent advances like Vulcan and DeepFleet, extending Amazon's approach to physical AI - technology that learns from contact, coordinates at scale, and supports people in the real world."

## The update on the page

- "Update February 25, 2026: Amazon is no longer utilizing Blue Jay in operations. However, the underlying technology used to develop the program will continue to support employees across our network."

## Quotes

- Tye Brady, chief technologist for Amazon Robotics: "Our latest innovations are great examples of how we're using AI and robotics to create an even better experience for our employees and customers."
- Brady again: "The real headline isn't about robots. It's about people - and the future of work we're building together."

## Employees and training

- The stated goal across the innovations: "reduce highly repetitive tasks, improve ergonomics, and expand career pathways."
- Amazon is investing in training through Career Choice, apprenticeships in mechatronics and robotics, and new AI education offerings.
- The page notes Amazon is "actively hiring at operations facilities across the country, with recent announcements to fill 250,000 positions for the holiday season".

## Related systems named

- **Vulcan:** "Amazon's first robot with a sense of touch designed to assist with ergonomically challenging tasks".
- **DeepFleet:** "an AI foundation model that coordinates large fleets of mobile robots across facilities".

wikis.title: Blue Jay
wikis.summary: A next-generation robotics system coordinating multiple robotic arms in one workspace to pick, stow and consolidate, tested in South Carolina and withdrawn in February 2026.
wikis.body:
- "Blue Jay is an extra set of hands that helps employees with tasks that involve reaching and lifting. It's a next-generation robotics system that coordinates multiple robotic arms to perform many tasks at once, collapsing what used to be three separate robotic stations into one streamlined workspace that can pick, stow, and consolidate in a single place."
- "Visually, Blue Jay operates like a juggler who never drops a ball - only here, the 'balls' are tens of thousands of items moving at high speed."
- Development "moved from concept to production in just over a year - a process that formerly took three or more years for earlier Amazon systems like Robin, Cardinal, or Sparrow", using digital twins to iterate on dozens of prototypes.
- "Blue Jay is already being tested in production at one of our facilities in South Carolina, where it's already able to pick, stow, and consolidate approximately 75% of all the various types of items we store at our sites. Over time, it will serve as a core technology helping power Amazon's Same-Day sites."
- It "helps keep employees working in their ergonomic 'power zone,' reducing repetitive reaching and lifting".
- The page's own update of February 25, 2026 states Amazon is no longer utilizing Blue Jay in operations, and that the underlying technology will continue to support employees across the network.

wikis.title: Project Eluna
wikis.summary: An agentic AI system that reasons over a building's historical and real-time data to anticipate bottlenecks and recommend actions to operators, piloted in Tennessee.
wikis.body:
- "Operations managers constantly monitor dozens of dashboards while responding to technology breakdowns, reallocating resources, and making rapid-fire decisions. Project Eluna acts like an extra teammate, helping reduce that cognitive load."
- "Project Eluna is an agentic AI system - designed to act with a degree of autonomy, reasoning through complex operational situations and recommending actions to operators. It pulls in historical and real-time data across a building to anticipate bottlenecks and keep operations running smoothly."
- "Project Eluna will be piloted at a fulfillment center in Tennessee to assist operators this holiday season, working initially on sortation optimization."
- Operators can ask questions like "Where should we shift people to avoid a bottleneck?" and receive data-backed recommendations. "The goal: less putting out fires, more foresight."
- The page's February 2026 update concerns Blue Jay only; it says nothing about Project Eluna being withdrawn.

wikis.title: Seven Japanese firms show general-purpose robot prototypes; ugo unveils the Nova semi-humanoid
wikis.summary: Robostart's report from the Physical AI Summit in Tokyo on 16 September 2026, where AIRoA first showed the prototypes from its NEDO-commissioned domestic general-purpose robot competition, led by ugo's new Nova.
wikis.body:
## The event

- "2026年9月16日、東京で開催された「フィジカルAI Summit」において" - on 16 September 2026, at the Physical AI Summit held in Tokyo, the AI Robot Association (AIRoA) showed for the first time the results of its domestic general-purpose robot development competition.
- Prototypes of dual-arm mobile manipulators from seven companies were lined up: ugo, THK, Nachi (不二越), Keigan, HatsuMuv, Enactic and EmplifAI.
- Article published 2026.9.17 Thu 12:01.

## The competition

- The "domestic general-purpose robot development competition" is run by AIRoA as part of a project commissioned by NEDO.
- Its aim is to accelerate domestic development of practical general-purpose robots - specifically "dual-arm mobile manipulators" with two arms that move themselves and perform varied work - to strengthen Japan's robot industry. Selected companies built their prototypes in about six months.
- Eight companies were originally selected: Enactic, EmplifAI, Keigan, THK, Telexistence, HatsuMuv, Nachi and ugo. All but Telexistence exhibited at this summit.
- It is not a contest that picks a single best machine. AIRoA takes delivery at prototype, improved-machine and mass-production stages from robots meeting its specifications and criteria; companies clearing each stage move to the next, and several may proceed.
- Mass-produced robots are planned to be used as machines that collect real-world data for the robot foundation model being developed under the NEDO project.

## Why every exhibit was teleoperated

- All seven assume teleoperation, a human driving the robot with controllers.
- This is deliberate: AIRoA's implementation guidelines state explicitly that "自律動作は評価対象外" - autonomous operation is outside the scope of evaluation.
- What is evaluated is how far teleoperation can carry out pick-and-place, cleaning, opening and closing doors, shelf stocking, manipulation of flexible objects such as cables, tool use and sorting - scored on success rate, speed and quality of the result.
- The reasoning: autonomous work needs real-world data on how humans grasp, lift, carry and use tools. A human first teaches the robot by teleoperation, the motions accumulate as training data, the AI learns from it, and the range of autonomous tasks grows. The seven prototypes are the stage of building the domestic hardware base for that.

wikis.title: ugo Nova
wikis.summary: ugo's new domestically built semi-humanoid, redesigned from scratch for physical AI, with 22 degrees of freedom and mass production planned for 2027.
wikis.body:
- The highest-profile exhibit was ugo's new domestic semi-humanoid "ugo Nova".
- A wheeled semi-humanoid meant to enter existing workplaces and "see", "grasp", "carry" and "operate". Designed and manufactured in Japan, with mass production planned to start in 2027.
- ugo says Nova is not an improvement on an existing machine: hardware and software were redesigned from zero on the premise of physical AI, with attention to safety and to a design that fits its surroundings as well as to whole-body work performance.
- Specifications: 22 degrees of freedom in total, 7 per arm; payload of up to 4 kg per arm and 10 kg with both; a waist lift mechanism for work at different heights; Mecanum wheels for omnidirectional movement; NVIDIA Jetson Thor as the main processor; 6 hours of battery life.
- A defining feature is that teleoperation feeds straight into AI training-data collection: an operator drives Nova with bilateral or VR controllers and the robot's motions are recorded as data. The bilateral control uses Asratec technology, and Asratec also developed the bilateral controller used for physical AI data collection.
- The same day, ugo announced "ugo Physical AI Fabric", a product and service group combining Nova with a data collection kit, "ugo Data Factory" and "ugo Model Lab", connecting real-world data collection, AI model development and evaluation, on-site operation and continuous learning.

wikis.title: Keigan - KeiganGPR
wikis.summary: A 24-axis general-purpose robot designed from its actuators up, with its design published so owners can repair it themselves; release planned within 2027.
wikis.body:
- KeiganGPR was designed from scratch on the company's actuator and AMR (autonomous mobile robot) technology.
- Configuration: an AMR base, waist, two 7-axis arms and a head - 24 axes in total. Intended to work not only in factories and logistics but in shops and living spaces.
- Its distinguishing idea is "publish the design so you can fix it yourself". From its AMR experience Keigan says repair and maintenance on site are a major problem, so for KeiganGPR it will publish mechanism CAD, mechanical interface specifications, CAN communication specifications, ROS 2 drivers, URDF and repair and maintenance information.
- It uses the company's leader-follower control scheme to transfer a human's hand movements to the robot, accumulating operation data for future learning.
- Release is planned within 2027.

wikis.title: THK - what building the real machine revealed
wikis.summary: THK's dual-arm manipulator, and the fingertip precision and grip-feel problems that only appeared on the real hardware, with measured success rates before and after the fix.
wikis.body:
- THK built a dual-arm mobile manipulator using its own machine element parts, designed for reduced wiring and low power consumption, using a leader-follower scheme where the robot reproduces the movement of a leader device the human operates.
- Evaluating the real machine surfaced unanticipated problems. The main ones were fingertip precision and a lack of "grasping feel". The team had assumed widening the robot's range of motion would be enough, but in practice fingertip wobble, rigidity and the shape of the gripper fingers largely determined the success rate.
- After revising the control, wrist rigidity and finger shape, and using bilateral control to return the sensation of gripping to the operator, the "tool use (nail hammering)" evaluation task went from a 0% success rate before the fix to 80%, and "flexible object manipulation (cable connection)" from 0% to 40%.
- THK says the exercise showed the importance of finding, early and through real-machine testing, problems that cannot be anticipated at the design stage.

wikis.title: HatsuMuv - giving the robot human sight and hearing
wikis.summary: A prototype built around the operator's abilities and research flexibility, with fisheye cameras, independent microphones and a swappable compute module.
wikis.body:
- HatsuMuv has worked on character robots combining anime character modelling, motion, staging, AI and real-machine control; Asratec also assisted with this prototype.
- The prototype prioritises the operator's "human control ability" and "flexibility of the research environment" for researchers experimenting with robots.
- A lift mechanism changes its height from about 100 cm to 160 cm, and four independently driven and steered wheels give omnidirectional movement.
- Two wide-view fisheye cameras in the head help the operator judge distance and depth, and independent left and right microphones make hearing as well as sight available for teleoperation and data collection.
- A modular structure lets a configuration with NVIDIA Jetson Thor be swapped for one with a laptop PC, so the research environment can be changed easily.

wikis.title: Nachi - industrial robot technology for the next generation
wikis.summary: Nachi built its prototype on its industrial robot heritage, adding flexibility, affinity with people and autonomy.
wikis.body:
- Nachi (不二越) approached general-purpose robot development for the physical AI era on the base of its long-standing industrial robot technology.
- Industrial robots have prioritised productivity, reliability and maintainability; meanwhile manufacturing sites increasingly need automation for work that conventional automation equipment handles poorly - high-mix low-volume production, inspection and improvement work.
- The prototype therefore keeps the productivity and reliability of conventional industrial robots while raising "flexibility", "affinity with people" and "autonomy".
- Combined with AI models developed by AIRoA, the company aims at a robot that works near people like a "colleague".

wikis.title: EmplifAI - a five-company consortium
wikis.summary: EmplifAI developed its entry as a consortium including Mazda, Airia, TASKO and Asratec.
wikis.body: - EmplifAI formed a consortium with Mazda, Airia (アイリア), TASKO and Asratec for this development, pooling the knowledge of five companies.

wikis.title: Amazon winds down the Blue Jay warehouse robot
wikis.summary: BGR reports that Amazon has stopped using Blue Jay, the multi-limbed warehouse robot it launched in October 2025, and sets out the cost, integration and strategy reasons given for it.
wikis.body:
## What happened

- "After less than six months on the job, Amazon has fired its latest warehouse robot." Blue Jay launched in October 2025 as a multi-limbed robot intended to be "an extra set of hands" in Amazon's warehouses.
- The wind down was "First reported by Business Insider".
- Amazon states that Blue Jay's "underlying technology" will "continue to support employees across our network".

## Why it was sidelined

- "cost considerations and implementation issues, alongside shifting priorities in Amazon's warehouse systems, has led to the innovative robot being sidelined."
- Blue Jay "proved exceptionally expensive and difficult to manufacture", and "its incorporation into warehouse workflows proved less than ideal".
- The page frames these as common problems in AI-forward warehouses: "high upfront costs, complex systems integration, technical issues, and a shortage of trained personnel often doom projects like Blue Jay before they begin."

## What Blue Jay was

- Launched alongside Amazon's agentic AI system Project Eluna in October 2025, and described by Amazon as functioning like "a juggler who never drops a ball" - an extra set of hands consolidating several robotic systems into a single station.
- At release it was touted as "already able to pick, stow, and consolidate approximately 75% of all the various types of items we store at our sites", in the company's South Carolina facility.
- An Amazon spokesperson told TechCrunch that Blue Jay was launched as a prototype rather than a fully-fledged, mass-deployed program; the page notes Amazon's press release at the time declined to mention this.
- Development took only a year, against over three years each for previous projects Robin and Sparrow, using digital twins to "build systems like Blue Jay smarter and more quickly".

## Amazon's wider warehouse plans

- Blue Jay was envisioned as a cog in Amazon's "Local Vending Machine" system of large, highly automated warehouses. Sources interviewed by Business Insider say the company is moving to a system called "Orbital": a more malleable, reconfigurable structure with smaller warehouses, meant to help Whole Foods handle perishable and frozen goods and support grocery delivery. Business Insider reports that transition "won't take place until 2027".
- A New York Times report citing internal documents, published a day before Blue Jay's announcement, says Amazon plans to automate roughly 75 percent of its operations and estimated it could reduce US hiring needs by upwards of 160,000 people by 2027, worth roughly 30 cents saved per item.
- Amazon founded its robotics program in 2012 and has deployed over 1 million robots across its warehouses. Its Vulcan program, also debuting in 2025, was its first robot with a "sense of touch" - a two-armed robot with cameras and suction cups that rearranges and moves packing compartments.
- Amazon "kicks off its plan to up AI spending by $200 billion in 2026".

## Context the page adds

- The page cites Tesla's Optimus as another humanoid programme whose "public snafus" have been contentious, noting Elon Musk has touted the technology as delivering $10 trillion in future revenue.

wikis.title: AGIBOT rolls out its 10,000th humanoid robot
wikis.summary: The Robot Report covers AGIBOT's claim to be one of the first companies to have rolled out 10,000 humanoid robots, with its production curve, deployment sectors and international partnerships.
wikis.body:
## The claim

- AGIBOT Innovation Technology Co. "today claimed that it is one of the first companies to have rolled out 10,000 humanoid robots" (article dated March 31, 2026).
- The Shanghai-based company said this marks a transition from early-stage validation to scalable, real-world robot deployments.
- Peng Zhihui, chief technology officer: "Reaching 10,000 units is not simply about producing more robots; it reflects a fundamental shift in our ability to scale... we are seeing a pivot from small-scale, niche applications to robust, large-scale commercial demand. The widespread deployment of AGIBOT's robots is no longer about seeking technical viability, but about delivering scalable value and driving the adoption of embodied AI."

## Production curve

- "it took nearly two years to reach its first 1,000 units, followed by about a year to scale from 1,000 to 5,000 robots. The next jump took another year."
- The page also states: "In just three months, AGIBOT said it went from 5,000 to 10,000 units shipped" - credited to a maturing supply chain, continuous improvement in manufacturing efficiency, and accelerating production of its complex hardware. (The article gives both "another year" and "three months" for that last step.)
- In January, AGIBOT debuted in the U.S. at CES and said it had released more than 5,100 robots.

## Rankings and company

- According to Omdia, the startup was the No. 1 shipper of humanoids in 2025; IDC ranked AGIBOT first in total shipment volume and leading in entertainment, research and education, exhibition and reception, and manufacturing.
- Founded in 2023, also known as Zhiyuan Robotics Co. It describes its approach as "1 Robotic Body + 3 Intelligence" - a robotic body combined with interaction, manipulation and locomotion intelligence.

## Deployments and partnerships

- A "significant portion" of its humanoids operate in real-world environments in logistics, retail, hospitality and education, and its robots "have begun entering industrial workflows".
- Deployments are growing beyond the Chinese market - Europe, North America, Japan, South Korea, Southeast Asia and the Middle East.
- Last month it launched its full robot portfolio with Minth Group in Germany, and it recently signed its first operator agreement with Singtel Enterprise in Singapore.

## Regulatory note

- U.S. lawmakers have proposed prohibiting federal purchase or use of certain Chinese-made robots with the American Security Robotics Act; the sponsors expressed concern about cybersecurity vulnerabilities.

## Other 2026 activity

- In January 2026 AGIBOT launched the Genie Sim 3.0 robot simulation platform and was recognized with "Best of CES" awards.
- It is conducting the AGIBOT World Challenge at ICRA 2026 in Vienna in June.
- Pictured: AGIBOT co-founder and CTO Zhuhui Peng, the A3 humanoid, and Senior Vice President Chuang Wang.

wikis.title: 1X's $20K Robot Targets US Homes in 2026, Aims to Reduce the 'Creepy' Factor
wikis.summary: eWeek's piece on 1X's NEO home humanoid - its price and 2026 US shipping plan, the design choices meant to avoid the uncanny valley, and the human-in-the-loop training behind the first wave.
wikis.body:
## The plan

- "Silicon Valley startup 1X Technologies is taking the giant leap from factory floors to family living rooms."
- "Their flagship humanoid, Neo, is slated to begin shipping to US households throughout 2026. Priced at $20,000, the 5-foot-6 robot is designed to be a helpful, albeit robotic, member of the household."
- "Unlike its industrial predecessor, Eve, which rolled on wheels, Neo walks on two legs."
- Dar Sleeper, 1X's VP of product and design, on the unboxing, speaking to Dezeen: "Then it'll walk off and introduce itself, and then get a bunch of information and ask you your name and all that."

## Designed to be 'cool', not creepy

- "One of the biggest hurdles for home robotics isn't just the mechanics; it's the uncanny valley factor." The 1X team, "which includes veterans from Nike, Tesla, and Yeezy, focused heavily on aesthetics and tactile comfort."
- Designer Danny Chambers, formerly of Nike, told Dezeen's Ellen Eberhardt: "There's this really interesting dialogue around whether this is skin or clothing."
- "The robot is encased in a soft, 3D-knit bodysuit rather than cold metal or hard plastic." Chambers: "We're really trying to make it feel safe in your house... More like a couch than a refrigerator, for example."
- When founder Bernt Bornich hired Sleeper, "His prompt was: Can you make this cool?"
- On proportions, the team "intentionally steered away from making Neo look too masculine or feminine, opting for a genderless, almost 'cartoonish' appearance". Sleeper: "A body envelope really quickly either gets sexualized or scary. If the shoulders are too broad, you feel threatened. If the abdominals are too tapered, it gets a little too sexy."

## Human-in-the-loop training

- "While Neo is designed to be fully autonomous eventually, it isn't quite there yet. The first wave of robots will be partly controlled via teleoperation."
- "This human-in-the-loop system allows the AI, a mix of OpenAI models and 1X's own tech, to learn from a diverse range of real-world home environments."
- "The goal is to eventually assist people with genuine needs, such as elderly parents or people with disabilities. However, the company admits these complex use cases are still being refined."
- "Early adopters won't just be customers; they'll effectively help train the next generation of AI-powered assistants."

## Note

- Written by Aminu Abdullahi, Apr 27, 2026, a "2 minute read". Much of the quoted material is attributed to an exclusive Dezeen interview rather than to eWeek's own reporting. The page carries no mention of the Hayward factory.

wikis.title: Figure scales BotQ to one humanoid robot per hour
wikis.summary: Interesting Engineering reports Figure's 24x manufacturing scale-up at its BotQ facility in California, with the yields, testing regime and the Helix perception upgrade the larger fleet enabled.
wikis.body:
## The ramp

- "In the last 120 days, Figure scaled manufacturing 24x - from 1 robot/day to 1 robot/hour."
- At its manufacturing facility, BotQ, in California, output went from one robot per day to one per hour, "a 24-fold increase achieved in under four months".
- The ramp-up, "supported by custom software and over 150 networked workstations, has enabled the delivery of more than 350 units".
- Figure has "transitioned its BotQ facility from prototype development to full-scale production, establishing dedicated lines for all critical modules of the Figure 03 humanoid robot".
- "Last year, Figure revealed its plans for the BotQ facility, an in-house factory dedicated to humanoid robots, targeting 12,000 units annually with plans to scale production further."

## Yields and testing

- Supplier quality was strengthened through strict qualification processes, with over 50 in-process inspection points.
- End-of-line first-pass yield has exceeded 80 percent; battery production has reached a 99.3 percent yield, with over 500 units shipped and more than 9,000 actuators produced.
- "Each robot undergoes over 80 functional tests, including stress and burn-in exercises such as squats and jogging, to eliminate early failures."

## Fleet operations

- The growing fleet generates large-scale data for Helix, the company's humanoid AI model, and enables real-world deployment across research, commercial and domestic use cases.
- Operational scale has improved diagnostics and rapid failure analysis; software fallback systems let robots keep working through minor faults. With high-frequency issues resolved, focus has shifted to edge-case failures.
- Figure has built internal service, fleet management and over-the-air update systems for continuous monitoring, upgrades and feedback across deployed robots.

## Perception-conditioned whole-body control

- Figure introduced an upgrade to its AI model Helix System 0 (S0) enabling perception-conditioned whole-body control.
- Previously the model relied solely on proprioception - joint states and body motion - limiting navigation of stairs or uneven terrain. S0 now integrates visual input from onboard stereo cameras, converting RGB images into a 3D spatial representation, so the robot can both "feel" and "see" the terrain.
- The system is trained end-to-end with reinforcement learning in simulation across diverse, randomized terrains, and "the learned behaviors transfer directly to real-world environments without additional calibration or fine-tuning", addressing the sim-to-real challenge.
- Robots can traverse stairs and varied surfaces with human-like stability, even under changing lighting.

wikis.title: NVIDIA Isaac GR00T Reference Humanoid Robot for academic research
wikis.summary: Pulse 2.0 covers NVIDIA's announcement of the Isaac GR00T Reference Humanoid Robot, its hardware and software stack, launch research partners, availability and the quotes given with it.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- NVIDIA announced the NVIDIA Isaac GR00T Reference Humanoid Robot, "describing it as the first open humanoid robot reference design built on NVIDIA Jetson Thor and the NVIDIA Isaac GR00T development platform".
- NVIDIA said it is designed to help democratize humanoid robotics research by combining advanced hardware, onboard AI computing and an open software stack "without requiring researchers to rely on proprietary systems".

## What is in it

- The reference design integrates a Unitree H2 Plus humanoid robot, Sharpa Wave five-finger tactile hands, NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor onboard computing and the Isaac GR00T software platform into a single development system.
- It is intended to streamline workflows spanning hardware integration, data collection, simulation, training, evaluation and deployment.
- The robot "stands nearly six feet tall, weighs approximately 150 pounds, and offers 75 total degrees of freedom across its body and hands".
- It includes stereo vision cameras, wrist-mounted cameras, an inertial measurement unit, voice interaction, and "a battery capable of delivering roughly three hours of operation".
- The onboard Jetson AGX Thor T5000 compute module is powered by NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture and "delivers up to 2,070 FP4 teraflops of AI performance".
- The Isaac GR00T platform includes tools for robot teleoperation, foundation models for humanoid reasoning and learning, simulation and training software through Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab, ROS middleware, and deployment on Jetson Thor. Researchers can use the complete stack or individual components.

## Adopters and availability

- Research institutions "expected to adopt the platform" include Ai2, ETH Zurich, Stanford Robotics Center and UC San Diego Advanced Robotics and Controls Laboratory. NVIDIA Research will also use the design to advance future Isaac GR00T models, frameworks and hardware.
- The Isaac GR00T developer platform will support the Unitree G1 humanoid robot.
- "NVIDIA said the Isaac GR00T Reference Humanoid Robot will be available from Unitree Robotics in late 2026." NVIDIA also plans to release the Isaac GR00T reference workflow for the Unitree G1 on GitHub and Hugging Face.

## Quotes

- Jensen Huang, Founder and CEO, NVIDIA: "Humanoid robots will bring physical AI to the world's largest industries, opening a multitrillion-dollar economic opportunity. The NVIDIA Isaac GR00T Reference Humanoid Robot gives researchers a single, open platform to make breakthrough discoveries toward general-purpose physical intelligence."
- Steve Cousins, Executive Director, Stanford Robotics Center: "Robotics moves fastest when researchers can build on open platforms, share code and test ideas on real machines."
- Marco Hutter, Professor, ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab, on having "a state-of-the-art humanoid platform for collecting data, testing algorithms and validating robot behaviors".
- Deepak Pathak, Cofounder and CEO, Skild AI: "A reference design lets more researchers participate in frontier humanoid research and move from ideas to experiments faster."
- Dieter Fox, Senior Research Director, Ai2 and Professor, University of Washington, on Ai2's mission "to accelerate robotics through open science".
- Michael Yip, Professor, UC San Diego and Director, Advanced Robotics and Controls Laboratory, on accelerating loco-manipulation research.

wikis.title: Unitree Robotics stock soars 460% in Shanghai IPO debut
wikis.summary: Quartz, on Yahoo Finance, reports Unitree Robotics' first session on Shanghai's STAR Market - the closing price, valuation, IPO proceeds and backers - with the company's financials and the trade pressure around the listing.
wikis.body:
## The debut

- "Unitree Robotics stock closed 460% above its IPO price on Wednesday, finishing at 845 yuan after the humanoid robot maker's first session on Shanghai's STAR Market, having briefly surged nearly 630% before pulling back."
- "The closing price values Unitree at roughly $50 billion, according to Reuters."
- The first-day gain exceeded the average opening-day pop of 279% for new listings in China so far this year, and came even as China's benchmark index fell 3% on the day.

## The offering

- The Hangzhou-based company priced shares at 150.8 yuan each, "bringing in approximately 6.1 billion yuan ($905 million) in total proceeds".
- Among the backers was Chinese AI company DeepSeek, which put in about 140.8 million yuan according to a company filing; Tencent holds a stake as a prior investor.
- The listing follows that of memory chipmaker CXMT on the same exchange last month, when that company's stock rose 466% on its first trading day.

## The company

- Unitree competes with Tesla and Hyundai Motor Group-owned Boston Dynamics, according to Reuters. It makes bipedal humanoid robots designed to walk and handle objects, alongside quadruped models deployed for applications such as identifying hazards.
- "Also on Monday, Unitree introduced a humanoid robot dubbed 'Superman,' which it says can jump two meters from a standing position and run at speeds of up to 12.66 meters per second."
- Revenue rose to 1.70 billion yuan in 2025 from 392.77 million yuan in 2024, with a net profit of 278.21 million yuan in 2025, according to its prospectus. It shipped more than 5,000 humanoid units in 2025.

## Context and risk

- The listing arrived as the World Robot Conference opened in Beijing, drawing hundreds of companies - predominantly Chinese - to show off new products.
- William Xin, chairman of Spring Mountain Pu Jiang Investment Management: "At this early stage of competition, whoever gets listed and has visibility can grab the resources and have staying power" - noting that the vast majority of rivals in the sector have yet to turn a profit.
- Unitree's prospectus identified the U.S. among its key markets and flagged potential American trade restrictions as a geopolitical risk. "The FCC added foreign-made humanoid and quadruped robots to its Covered List in late July, citing national security concerns, prompting China's commerce ministry to threaten countermeasures." Overseas sales accounted for about 44% of Unitree's main-business revenue in 2025.

wikis.title: World Humanoid Robot Games (RoboCup event listing)

wikis.title: ugo announces the ugo Nova semi-humanoid robot
wikis.summary: A trade write-up of ugo Inc.'s announcement of ugo Nova, a Japanese-built wheeled dual-arm semi-humanoid, covering its role in the NEDO/AIRoA project, its specifications and its data-collection workflow.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- "ugo Inc. has announced the domestically produced semi-humanoid robot 'ugo Nova' on September 16, 2026."
- "ugo Nova is a domestically produced robot, with design and manufacturing carried out entirely in Japan, and mass production is scheduled to begin in 2027."
- "This robot will be proposed by the AI Robot Association (AIRoA) as part of a project commissioned by NEDO (New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization) to develop a domestically produced general-purpose robot."
- It "can convert human work directly into high-quality learning data, which can then be used in the development of robot base models for physical AI".

## What it is

- A wheeled, dual-arm semi-humanoid robot "developed to handle diverse tasks in human work environments", combining a flexible dual-arm and upper-body mechanism giving access to the same workspace as humans with the autonomous movement technology of the ugo series.
- Intended both as a platform for physical AI research, data collection and model verification, and for "actual business implementation and operation" - "a robot that connects research and development to social implementation in a single unit".

## Specifications

- Cameras are standardly mounted on the head and hands to acquire visual data for learning physical AI, "allowing for immediate data collection after setup".
- Arm control supports a high control cycle of 100Hz, "enabling high-speed and smooth motion recording with high precision".
- Teleoperation is supported using bilateral controllers and VR controllers, reflecting the operator's movements while recording the operations as training data.
- Dual arms with a degree of freedom similar to human arms, plus a multi-joint waist mechanism allowing rotation and flexion of the upper body, for work "from handling items near the floor to accessing overhead shelves".
- Payload: "a maximum of 4kg per arm, and a maximum of 10kg with both arms" - for transport, picking and handling in manufacturing sites and warehouses.
- Movement uses a Mecanum system for on-the-spot direction changes and lateral movement without rotation, working in narrow passages and keeping a stable posture when applying force with both arms.
- "it supports continuous operation for up to 6 hours".
- Equipped with "NVIDIA Jetson Thor", so AI models can be inferred and trained in real time on the robot itself without relying on the cloud, giving low-latency recognition, decision-making and action.

## The workflow

1. **Demonstration of work and data collection:** operators use bilateral controllers or VR devices to operate ugo Nova and demonstrate the movements they want to train. "Multimodal data such as video during operation, joint information, torque, end effector position, and operation commands are collected in time synchronization."
2. **AI model training:** the collected data is quality-controlled and compiled into a dataset used for additional training of the robot base model.
3. **Application to actual machine and verification:** the trained model is applied to ugo Nova and evaluated by inference and operation in a real environment.

- "A key feature of ugo Nova is that it can handle not only 'collecting data' but also 'running the model' with a single device."

## Future outlook

- ugo will accumulate and use data collected in the field and, "through imitation learning and the development of robot base models, will expand the range of tasks that robots can handle and promote gradual autonomy".
- Beyond hardware, it plans integrated services spanning data collection, start-up and utilisation consulting, and AI model development, evaluation and implementation support.

*Source given by the page: ugo Inc.*

wikis.title: Japan's new robots push physical AI forward at a Tokyo summit
wikis.summary: A Euronews video report from a one-day physical AI summit in Tokyo on 16 September 2026, showing prototype robots from THK, Nachi, HatsuMuv and ugo and noting how far they still depend on human operators.
wikis.body:
## The event

- "Technology companies gathered in Tokyo on 16 September 2026 for a one-day summit focused on physical AI, showcasing robots designed to perform tasks in the real world."
- Page updated: 16/09/2026 - 10:19 GMT+2.
- "Robots are getting to grips with the physical world in Tokyo, where technology companies are showcasing machines designed to handle objects, perform industrial tasks and work alongside humans."
- "The demonstrations offer a glimpse of how AI could move beyond screens and software, giving machines the ability to interact with their surroundings and carry out physical tasks."

## Robots shown

- **THK:** a machine that "picks up bottles, bags and boxes under the remote control of a single operator". "Its articulated arms and grippers also allow it to hammer a nail into a piece of wood, demonstrating the precision and dexterity needed for more complex tasks."
- **Nachi, HatsuMuv and ugo** are also presenting their latest robotic systems.
- **ugo Nova:** "Ugo is showcasing its semi-humanoid ugo Nova, which performs a drilling task under remote control." Designed to work in environments built for humans, "the robot has two seven-axis arms as well as additional joints in its head and waist. It is also designed to collect real-world data that can be used to train physical AI models."

## The limits

- "But the demonstrations also reveal the technology's current limits. Many of the robots still depend on human operators, with developers now working to give them greater autonomy as investment in AI-powered machines grows in Japan."

*Format: a No Comment video report. Tags carried by the page: Japan, Robotic, AI, Humanoid robot, Tokyo, Technology.*

wikis.title: Age of Empires: Definitive Edition release date set for October 19, 2017
wikis.summary: GameSpot news report that Microsoft dated the Age of Empires: Definitive Edition remaster for October 19, 2017, announced at an Age of Empires event alongside a beta and further series announcements.
wikis.body:
## Release date

- "To coincide with the exact 20-year anniversary of the original game, the remastered version launches on October 19, 2017."
- Announced at a Microsoft event dedicated to Age of Empires, held the day after "Sunday's Xbox-centric Gamescom livestream"; the series "celebrates its 20-year anniversary this year".
- Age of Empires: Definitive Edition "will be a Windows 10 exclusive when it releases in October".
- A beta "is set to begin tomorrow, August 22".

## The remaster

- First announced at E3 in June.
- "The remaster provides updated visuals and a variety of other modern improvements, like a new UI, the ability to attack-move, control groups, an idle villagers button, and better online multiplayer."
- A new trailer debuted alongside the date, highlighting "new zoom levels, improved destruction, and an enhanced soundtrack".

## Other announcements at the event

- Microsoft "also revealed Definitive Editions of Age of Empires II and III are also on the way".
- "Even more significantly, a full-on sequel, Age of Empires IV, was confirmed."

## Article details

- By Chris Pereira on August 21, 2017 at 2:51PM PDT.
- Game hub data: Age of Empires, first released Sep 30, 1997; platforms DC, GIZ, MAC, MOBI, PC, PS.

wikis.title: Tesla's $5 billion Gigafactory and its battery-material demand
wikis.summary: Visual Capitalist infographic post on Tesla's planned $5 billion Gigafactory, its battery output and cost goals, and the effect it would have on graphite, cobalt and lithium supply.
wikis.body:
## The Gigafactory

- "With $5 billion in capital expenditures and 6,500 high tech jobs, several states continue to court Tesla Motors to build their next megaproject within their borders."
- The Tesla Gigafactory is "slated to open doors in 2017" and "will set a new precedent for economies of scale in battery production."
- "Tesla's new factory will produce more lithium-ion batteries under one roof than all of 2013's global production combined."
- The electric car company estimates this will cut costs per kWh by 30%.
- Tesla's product strategy relies on it: "The Gen III is supposed to retail for only $35,000, which is only half the cost of the more upscale Model S."
- UBS notes that raw materials make up 70% of the cost of each lithium-ion battery.
- Published July 22, 2014 4:10 pm, by Jeff Desjardins. The post credits Lomiko Metals (TSX-V: LMR) and Global Cobalt (TSX-V: GCO) for helping put the infographic together, and thanks Simon Moores and The Gold Report.

## Graphite

- In 2013, flake graphite production was 375,000 tonnes.
- "The Gigafactory alone would add another 126,000 tonnes (34% increase) over 2013 production."
- The increase on battery-grade graphite demand would be 154%.

## Cobalt

- 55% of cobalt comes from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
- "Tesla says they do not source from the Congo, so this makes getting cobalt a little more difficult."
- 42% of cobalt demand is from batteries, making it the metal's #1 use.
- Current Tesla batteries use about 9% cobalt by weight (NCA formulation).

## Lithium

- "There has been a steady supply of lithium in Chile since 1996, so this will likely be the easiest commodity to source."

wikis.title: SolPad announces specs, pricing and pre-order date for SolPad Mobile
wikis.summary: AltEnergyMag's excerpt of a CleanTechnica story reporting that Silicon Valley startup SolPad has released specs, pricing and a pre-order date for its all-in-one mobile solar-plus-storage product.
wikis.body:
## What is reported

- "The Silicon Valley startup SolPad has just announced the specs, pricing, and pre-order date for its all-in-one solar plus storage mobile solution, which could help usher in a new era of entry-level solar."
- The product is referred to as the SolPad Mobile; the company "has released additional details about how much it will cost and when it will be available".
- "It looks like the SolPad Mobile is getting ready to enter the market."

## Earlier coverage and reaction

- CleanTechnica "first covered the SolPad product back in October of last year, with writer Matthew Klippenstein calling it 'a glimpse of the future.'"
- That article "raised a lot of questions in the comments section about the details and reliability of such a device": some comments "called it vaporware", others questioned "the wisdom of integrating batteries into the body of a solar panel and the legality of simply plugging such a system into the grid without an adequate grid-tie arrangement", and others asked why it was needed "with the current state of solar technology".

## Page data

- Source credited: CleanTechnica, by Derek Markham. Posted 01/18/17, 05:55 AM. Categories: Solar & Wind, Energy Storage & Distribution; tagged "portable solar".
- The page carries only an excerpt, ending "Cont'd..." - the actual specs, prices and pre-order date are not given in this text.

wikis.title: Intel Core i3-8121U "Cannon Lake" debuts in the Lenovo Ideapad 330
wikis.summary: Report that a JD.com listing shows Lenovo's Ideapad 330 shipping with Intel's 10 nm Core i3-8121U, detailing the laptop's specs and Chinese prices.
wikis.body:
## The listing
- "Online Chinese retailer JD.com has listed Lenovo's latest Cannon Lake-based Ideapad 330 laptop on its website."

## Processor
- "The Ideapad 330 incorporates an Intel Core i3-8121U dual-core processor fabricated on Intel's 10 nm process."
- "The processor comes with a base frequency of 2.2 GHz and lacks integrated graphics as it's been disabled."
- "Therefore, Lenovo pairs the Intel Core i3-8121U processor with an AMD Radeon RX 540 2GB graphics card in this particular laptop."

## Configurations
- "The base model is equipped with 4 GB of DDR4-2400 memory and a 500 GB 5400RPM hard drive."
- "JD.com also offers numerous configurations including one with 8 GB of memory, 256 GB SSD and 1 TB hard drive."

## Chassis and display
- "The 15.6-inch Ideapad 330 uses a TN panel with a resolution of 1366 x 768 pixels."
- "The laptop measures 378 x 260 x 22.7 mm and weights approximately 2.1 kg."
- "According to JD.com, the battery life is estimated to around five hours."
- Connectivity: "a Gigabit Ethernet port, two USB 3.0 Type-A ports, a single USB Type-C port, a 3.5mm jack, a HDMI port, and a CD/DVD drive."

## Price
- "The base model costs 3299 CNY (~$445) while the highest-end model will set you back 4299 CNY (~$580)."

- by Chino, May 14th 2018 12:19 (page dated Monday, May 14th 2018). Source: JD.
