wikis.title: Second launch attempt for NASA's Parker Solar Probe
wikis.summary: New York Times piece on the scrubbed first Parker Solar Probe launch and the second attempt set for Sunday 3:31 a.m. Eastern, with the launch-window and mission constraints.
wikis.body:
## The scrub and the next attempt

- "NASA's Parker Solar Probe did not get off the ground early Saturday morning as a few glitches halted the countdown, and then time ran out in the 65-minute launch window."
- "A second attempt will occur Sunday morning at 3:31 a.m. Eastern time."
- The attempt "will be streamed online on NASA TV starting at 3 a.m."
- Weather is "not ideal, with only a 60 percent chance of favorable conditions"; on Monday "odds improve to an 80 percent likelihood of good weather, according to Air Force forecasts."
- Launch deadline: "The deadline is Aug. 23, when Venus moves too far out of position." A photo caption says the launch "must happen by Aug. 23."

## Vehicle and spacecraft

- The spacecraft is on top of a Delta IV Heavy rocket "built and operated by United Launch Alliance, a joint venture between Boeing and Lockheed Martin."
- The rocket was photographed at Cape Canaveral, Fla.
- "The spacecraft is small, about the size of a car and weighing 1,400 pounds, but there is a third stage to give an additional velocity boost."
- NASA "touts" that it will one day "touch the sun."

## Why the early hour

- "The main constraint on the launch time is to get the spacecraft to its first rendezvous with Venus in November. At this hour, the launchpad is pointed in the right direction to get to Venus."
- Reaching the sun takes "more than 50 times as much" energy as reaching Mars, because Earth moves at 67,000 miles per hour in its orbit; to spiral inward the spacecraft "has to shed some of that energy, and that means launching at high speed in the direction opposite to Earth's motion."
- Another constraint is "making sure that the spacecraft passes as quickly as possible through the Van Allen belt, a region around Earth of intense radiation" that "can scramble the spacecraft's electronics."

## Mission and name

- The probe "will study the sun's outer atmosphere and the particles it produces known as solar wind."
- Named after Eugene N. Parker, who "predicted the existence of solar wind in 1958"; the article notes it is "the first named for a living person."

## Byline and dates

- By Kenneth Chang, Aug. 11, 2018. An accompanying video was "Published On Aug. 10, 2018".

wikis.title: Ming-Chi Kuo's Apple Watch Series 4 predictions: bigger display, new design, more sensors
wikis.summary: Forbes article running through analyst Ming-Chi Kuo's predictions for the next Apple Watch - a new design, a 15% bigger display, better battery life, more sensors and a second-half-of-2018 release - with the writer's own guesses marked as such.
wikis.body:
## The source of the predictions
- Ming-Chi Kuo left KGI Securities to join TF International Securities.
- "Today, in a note reported by 9to5Mac, he has detailed the what and when of all Apple's products for the rest of 2018, including new iPhones (three of them), new iPads with Face ID and a new Apple Watch."

## New design
- "Back in March, the analyst predicted that the next Apple Watch, presumably to be called Series 4, will be the first Watch to have a design strikingly different from all the Watches that have preceded it."
- "There are no explicit details of what the new design will look like"; the writer's expectation of a rounded rectangle is his own guess.

## Bigger display
- "Kuo is sticking to his expectation, expressed back in March, that the display on Apple Watch Series 4 will be 15% bigger than on current models."
- The writer expects narrower bezels to keep the Watch about the same size and current Watch Bands still working, marked as his own view.

## Battery life
- The writer says battery life "is going to get better", and speculates a slightly thicker Watch could hold a battery modification; no Kuo figure is given.

## Sensors
- "Kuo said that there would be more sensors built in, to add extra functionality, especially in terms for health monitoring."
- The writer notes other rumors "such as the idea that the Digital Crown will have a heart rate monitor in it".

## Price and release date
- "There's no exact price suggested"; the writer guesses prices roughly the same as then, perhaps a lower-price entry-level model or a Series 3 at a lower price.
- "Kuo has previously said he expects the Watch to go on sale in the second half of 2018."
- The writer's own guess: "like last year and year before, the next Apple Watch will be announced in early to mid-September, going on sale a week or two later."

## Byline
- David Phelan, Contributor, Jun 26, 2018, 06:00pm.

wikis.title: Volkswagen names its first ID. model the ID.3
wikis.summary: Volkswagen's Wolfsburg press release announcing that the first model of its all-electric ID. family will be called ID.3, ahead of its world premiere at the IAA.
wikis.body:
## Announcement

- Dateline: **Wolfsburg 2019-05-08**.
- Volkswagen officially announced the name of the first model of the new ID. family: **ID.3** (footnoted on the page as "Study").
- The announcement comes "months before its official world premiere at the IAA international motor show".
- "With immediate effect, potential customers can register for an exclusive special edition of the ID.3", shown on the page in camouflage.

## Why the number 3

- It indicates the ID. belongs to the **compact segment**, the class distinction in internal and industry-wide classification systems.
- The ID.3 "follows the Beetle and the Golf to introduce the third major chapter of strategic importance for the history of the brand".

## What ID. stands for

- "intelligent design, identity and visionary technologies".
- Every member of the family will bear the name ID., "a new, independent series of products in the brand portfolio".

## Quotes and targets

- Jürgen Stackmann, Member of the Board of Management Volkswagen Brand for Sales, Marketing & After Sales: "With the ID.3, we are starting from the centre, the Volkswagen brand's core, in which the majority of the models and sales volume can be found. The number 3 also signals expandability into the segments above and below it. We have a lot in the pipeline."
- With its e-mobility campaign the brand "is willing to become the number one brand globally by 2025, with more than 20 purely electrically driven models and more than a million vehicles sold annually, all of which being both networked and emission-free".

## Models to follow

- Additional models previewed by the concept cars **ID. CROZZ**, **ID. VIZZION** and **ID. ROOMZZ**, which will in future also be named with model numbers.

wikis.title: Amazon's solar energy initiative on fulfillment center rooftops
wikis.summary: Amazon press release announcing rooftop solar systems on more than 15 U.S. fulfillment and sortation centers in 2017 and 50 globally by 2020, plus solar-installer training for associates.
wikis.body:
## The announcement
- Dateline: "SEATTLE --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Mar. 2, 2017--(NASDAQ: AMZN)".
- "Amazon today announced a new initiative to generate clean energy by installing solar panels on its fulfillment facilities around the world."
- "The company plans to deploy large-scale solar systems on rooftops of more than 15 fulfillment and sortation centers in the U.S. this year and is planning to deploy solar systems on 50 fulfillment and sortation centers globally by 2020."
- Release subheads: "Amazon to install solar systems on 50 fulfillment facility rooftops worldwide by 2020" and "Initial 15 solar installations planned for completion by the end of 2017 will generate up to 41 MW".

## Capacity and sites
- "The initial solar projects planned for completion by the end of 2017 will generate up to 41 megawatts (MW) of power at Amazon facilities in California, New Jersey, Maryland, Nevada and Delaware."
- "Depending on the specific project, time of year and other factors, a solar installation could generate as much as 80 percent of a single fulfillment facility's annual energy needs."
- At the Patterson, California fulfillment center, "solar panels installed on the rooftop... cover more than three-quarters of the 1.1 million square foot building's rooftop."

## Quotes
- Dave Clark, Senior Vice President of Worldwide Operations: "As our fulfillment network continues to expand, we want to help generate more renewable energy at both existing and new facilities around the world in partnership with community and business leaders... By diversifying our energy portfolio, we can keep business costs low and pass along further savings to customers. It's a win-win."
- Kara Hurst, Director of Amazon's Worldwide Sustainability: "The NABCEP professional accreditation is a spring board for fulfillment center associates to enter a rapidly growing and in-demand workforce outside of Amazon as PV installers."

## Other renewable energy projects cited
- "the company's largest wind farm to date, located in Texas."
- "a network of wind and solar farms in Indiana, North Carolina, Ohio and Virginia are delivering energy onto the electric grid that powers AWS data centers."
- "To date, Amazon has announced or commenced construction on projects which will generate a total of 3.6 million MW of renewable energy."
- "Amazon was the leading corporate purchaser of renewable energy in the US in 2016, according to the 2017 State of Green Business report."
- Also green corporate rooftops and the District Energy Project, "which uses recycled energy for heating the company's corporate headquarters in Seattle."

## Career Choice and solar training
- Amazon "has expanded its innovative Career Choice program to include funding for associates to earn North American Board of Certified Energy Practitioners (NABCEP) certification."
- To qualify, "associates in this program will participate in 40 to 80 hours of PV design principles and practices learning, OSHA training, and hands-on installations," provided by local community colleges and other participating accredited educational organizations.
- "According to the annual National Solar Jobs Census, one in 50 new jobs created in 2016 was in the solar industry across the country, which is a 25 percent increase from the previous year."

wikis.title: Amazon reaches solar panels on over 50 fulfillment centers, ahead of its 2020 target
wikis.summary: Neowin report that Amazon has met, ahead of its 2020 target, its 2017 goal of putting solar panels on 50 fulfillment centers worldwide, now totalling 51 rooftop installations and 98 MW.
wikis.body:
## The milestone
- "In March of 2017, it announced the intention to install solar panels on 50 of its fulfillment centers worldwide by the year 2020, a goal which it has now achieved."
- "Amazon now has 51 rooftop installations - 32 in the U.S., 12 in Europe, and seven in India - totaling 98 MW of capacity."

## Wider renewables figures
- In solar and wind power installations regardless of placement, "the company now operates 61 such solutions with a capacity of 1,04 GW and an annual energy output of 3.1 million MWh".
- "A big part of that total value is no doubt the Texas-based wind farm which has a one million MWh annual output, and was built about two years ago."

## Shipment Zero
- The milestone "is part of its Shipment Zero vision, which seeks to make shipments net zero carbon, with 50% of the aforementioned shipments being net zero by the year 2030".
- "The eventual goal is, of course, the transition of all operations to 100% reliance on renewables rather than fossil fuels."

## Byline
- By Florin Bodnarescu, Neowin, Jul 25, 2019 13:50 EDT.

wikis.title: Lithium-ion battery megafactories and 2020 capacity
wikis.summary: Visual Capitalist Chart of the Week on the lithium-ion megafactories being built by Tesla, LG Chem, Foxconn, BYD and Boston Power, and what they would do to world battery capacity by 2020.
wikis.body:
## The chart's claim

- "Everyone has heard about Tesla's $5 Billion Gigafactory and its potential to double lithium-ion battery production capacity. However, it turns out that this merely a cog in the wheel of a bigger trend."
- "Data from Simon Moores of Benchmark Mineral Intelligence shows that there are several other large-scale facilities coming online in the next five years that will potentially bring that number substantially higher."

## Capacity figures

- "Today's production capacity is approximately 35 GWh worldwide."
- "once Tesla's Gigafactory and the other facilities being built by LG Chem, Foxconn, BYD, and Boston Power are complete, we will have a total capacity in 2020 of around 122 GWh."
- "This exponential ramping up of production capabilities proves that companies are serious about scale and reducing costs."

## Raw materials

- "For investors and speculators in the lithium, graphite, and cobalt sectors, there is no doubt that this could be a big boon. While these megafactories will have more negotiating power in their contracts for industrial metal sourcing, they will not be able to create this supply out of thin air."
- "These companies will need a diverse array of sources for industrial metals to reduce any supply risks. The sources also need to be socially responsible, ethical, and professionally managed."
- "Tesla has already stated that they are unwilling to source from places like the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where over half of cobalt supply originates."

## Publication

- Filed under ENERGY; "The Chart of the Week is a weekly Visual Capitalist feature on Fridays."
- Published May 8, 2015 4:56 pm, by Jeff Desjardins.
- Related topics listed: Battery, Graphite, Tesla, Gigafactory, Cobalt, Lithium-Ion, Lithium, Li-Ion, Megafactory, Production.

## Note

- The captured page continues into unrelated later Visual Capitalist articles (on U.S. crude oil supply and on how Europe generates its electricity); they are not part of this article.

wikis.title: TSMC delivers complete 5nm design infrastructure through its Open Innovation Platform
wikis.summary: TSMC press release announcing the full release of its 5nm design infrastructure within the Open Innovation Platform, covering PDKs, EDA tool and flow certification, IP, the 5nm process's density and speed gains, and availability.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- "Hsinchu, Taiwan, R.O.C., April 3, 2019—TSMC today announced delivery of the complete version of its 5 nanometer (nm) design infrastructure within the Open Innovation Platform® (OIP)."
- Issued by TSMC; "Issued on: 2019/04/03".
- Subtitle: "Enabling next-generation silicon designs targeting advanced mobile and high-performance computing applications".
- The full release "enables 5nm systems-on-chip (SoC) designs in next-generation advanced mobile and high-performance computing (HPC) applications, targeting high-growth 5G and artificial intelligence markets".
- Leading EDA and IP vendors collaborated with TSMC to develop and validate the infrastructure - technology files, PDKs, tools, flows and IP - "through multiple silicon test vehicles".

## The 5nm process

- "TSMC's 5nm process is already in risk production".
- Compared with TSMC's 7nm process, "its innovative scaling features deliver 1.8X logic density and 15% speed gain on an ARM® Cortex®-A72 core, along with superior SRAM and analog area reduction enabled by the process architecture".
- It "enjoys the benefits of process simplification provided by EUV lithography, and is making excellent progress in yield learning, achieving the best technology maturity at the same corresponding stage as compared to TSMC's previous nodes".

## What the infrastructure includes

- Full versions of the 5nm Design Rule Manual (DRM), SPICE model, process design kits (PDKs) and silicon-validated foundation and interface IP; support for "a full range of certified EDA tools and design flows".
- Customers "have already started intensive design engagements, paving the way for product tape-outs, pilot activities and early sampling".

## PDKs and EDA tool certification

- "The latest 5nm PDKs are now available for production design", including device symbols, Pcells, netlisting and techfiles, enabling custom design, simulation, implementation, dummy fill, extraction, physical verification and signoff.
- TSMC collaborated with Cadence, Synopsys, Mentor Graphics and ANSYS to certify full-line EDA tools through the TSMC OIP EDA Tool Certification Program.
- Categories covered: simulation, physical implementation (Custom Design, APR), timing signoff (STA, Transistor-level STA), Electromigration and IR drop (Gate-level and Transistor-level), physical verifications (DRC, LVS) and RC extractions (RCX).

## Design flows

- TSMC "added another layer of design flow certification with EDA partners using real designs to validate integrated tool flow for both custom and digital designs".
- Certification criteria: "tools' feature readiness, robustness, performance, correlation between implementation and sign-off tools, and design constraints compliance with real designs".
- Reference flows provided for both mobile and HPC applications.

## IP

- Foundation IP includes high-density and high-performance standard cell libraries and memory compilers, available from TSMC and its IP ecosystem partners.
- Partner interface IP cores: LPDDR or MIPI PHYs optimized for mobile; enterprise-dedicated DDR PHYs for HPC; USB and PCIe PHYs for both. "These 5nm IP cores are ready for design starts, and IP Silicon reports are available from TSMC and its partners."

## Availability

- "The entire TSMC 5nm design infrastructure is available now from TSMC Online for customer downloads."

## Quotes

- Cliff Hou, Vice President of Research & Development/Technology Development, TSMC: "TSMC's 5-nanometer technology offers our customers the industry's most advanced logic process to address the exponentially growing demand for computing power driven by AI and 5G... 5-nanometer technology requires deeper design-technology co-optimization."
- Dr. Aniruth Devgan, President, Cadence: Cadence "has undergone TSMC's latest 5nm v1.0 certification process" and "several mutual customers have successfully done 5nm production tapeouts using Cadence's tools, flows and IP for full production development".
- Joe Sawicki, Executive Vice President, Mentor IC EDA: "Our Analog FastSPICE and Calibre physical verification platforms have been in use at the 5nm node with TSMC's early customers."
- Sassine Ghazi, co-General Manager, Design Group, Synopsys: using "Synopsys' Fusion Design Platform and DesignWare IP, designers can achieve compressed schedules on their competitive high-performance computing designs targeting the 5G mobile and artificial intelligence markets".

## About TSMC (as stated in the release)

- "TSMC pioneered the pure-play foundry business model when it was founded in 1987 and has been the world's largest dedicated semiconductor foundry ever since."
- "TSMC serves its customers with annual capacity of 12 million 12-inch equivalent wafers in 2019 from fabs in Taiwan, the United States, and China", with technologies "from 0.5 micron plus all the way to foundry's most advanced processes, which is 7-nanometer today".
- Headquartered in Hsinchu, Taiwan.

wikis.title: 5G expected to roll out widely in 2020
wikis.summary: Axios piece arguing that in 2020 5G support will be built into a wide range of devices and that carrier networks will expand to cover more of the country.
wikis.body:
## Main point

- "While 5G started to arrive this year, you really had to seek out the next-generation experience": buyers had to find a carrier that covered part of their city, then buy one of the handful of phones supporting the new network technology.
- Why it matters: "Next year, the script will flip, as 5G support will be baked into a wide range of devices and networks expand to cover more of the country."
- "Every new generation of cellular technology has an awkward initial phase, but 5G is actually poised to arrive more smoothly than its predecessors."

## Details

- By Ina Fried.
- Dated Dec 5, 2019.
- The page text carries only the introduction; no further body sections were present.

wikis.title: Jeddah Tower construction update, April 2017
wikis.summary: Progress report on the Jeddah Tower in Saudi Arabia as of April 2017, with its height reached, cost, schedule and place in the Kingdom City project.
wikis.body:
## Project

- Jeddah Tower, "previously known as Kingdom Tower", is "currently under construction with a planned completion date of 2020", in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
- "It will be about 1,000 meters, or one kilometer (3,280 feet) tall".
- "when complete in 2020 will be second tallest building in the world after 'The tower at dubai creek harbor' in dubai, UAE".
- Cost: "jeddah tower will cost US$1.23 billion".

## Construction timeline

- "Construction started on April 1, 2013."
- "Piling work was completed in December 2013."
- "Above-ground construction commenced in September 2014."
- "As of April 2017, jeddah tower stand 220m tall and 50 floor high." The central core containing elevator shafts and stairwells has reached Level 50.
- Construction "was momentarily halted during summer last year due to unknown reason, but restarted in September again".
- "the official construction estimate is five years and three months (63 months)", while "others calculate that it will take significantly longer Time to complete, over seven years, based on the duration of Burj Khalifa's construction".

## Technology

- Construction "will rely on cutting-edge technology, including the high-strength reinforced concrete and the pumps used to elevate it to record heights, similar to what was used during Burj Khalifa's construction".
- Bob Sinn, principal of Thornton Tomasetti: "Concrete quality is getting better and better, as is pumping technology. There have been very strong advances in reinforced concrete over the last 20 years." He continued: "'Jeddah Tower construction' is certainly feasible. It's not a structural challenge."

## Kingdom City project

- The Jeddah Tower is "the first phase of the whole kingdom city project".
- Phase 2 "will consist of building all other infrastructure such as several other skyscrapers, apartment buildings and other social centers".
- Phase 3 "will be to promote jeddah city by encouraging tourism".
- "The total cost of the project will be $20 billion. The whole Kingdom city project will be completed by 2025."

wikis.title: Suzhou Zhongnan Tower structural design (Thornton Tomasetti project page)
wikis.summary: Thornton Tomasetti's project page for the 103-story Suzhou Zhongnan Tower in Suzhou, China, covering its dimensions, revised height, structural system and damping solution.
wikis.body:
## Project details

- Project: Suzhou Zhongnan Tower (also called Suzhou Zhongnan Center in the image captions).
- Project Partners: Gensler. Owner: Zhongnan Group.
- Location: Suzhou, China. Completion Date: Ongoing.
- Area: 3.9 million ft². Height: 1,637 ft. Number of Stories: 103.
- Lead contact: Yi Zhu, Managing Principal.
- "This 103-story mixed-use tower utilizes innovative structural systems and analysis techniques to create an efficient and economical design."

## Overview

- Suzhou is described as "the second largest city in the Jiangsu province" and "an important economic hub in East China".
- The tower holds office, residences and a hotel, with five stories below grade and an eight-story, long-span podium with ballroom and conference facilities; the top features a two-story observation deck.
- "Our team completed the structural design of the original 729-meter-tall Zhongnan Tower in 2014, and the construction stopped after the concrete piles were finished. The tower design was revised in 2019 with the height reduced to 499 meters."
- Thornton Tomasetti is providing structural design services to Gensler for the new tower and previously did so for the original one.

## Highlights

- The pile foundation built for the original tower is fully utilized by the new one.
- Structural system: a concrete core, a mega frame of SRC mega columns and belt trusses, and outrigger trusses linking the core and mega columns.
- A hollow core with the cross-web walls removed realizes the architect's vision of seven large atriums; thickened solid slabs act as rigid diaphragms at refuge levels for core stability.
- Foundation uses concrete bored piles with post grouting; the core-outrigger-mega frame system meets the strict story drift ratio against wind and seismic loads.
- The tower features "a unique crystal crown that resembles a four-petal yellow Osmanthus flower", its structure being eight perimeter mega columns and central flange walls supporting a helipad and a hanging structure for the tuned mass damper (TMD).
- The top is designed to meet the H10 requirements of Japanese standards - "only 10% of people can feel building motion during a 10-year wind event".
- The damping solution combines a 300-ton TMD and a tuned sloshing damper (TSD) based on a 1000-ton water tank: "This marks the first time this approach has been adopted for a supertall building."
- The TMD is suspended by a structural device with multiple hanging masses that can swing in opposite directions, "making it more efficient than a traditional single mass damper".

## Capabilities listed

- Expertise: Structural Analysis & Design. Technology: Tuned Mass Dampers.

wikis.title: Phil Spencer on why Microsoft announced a new Xbox at E3 2018
wikis.summary: GameSpot report on Xbox boss Phil Spencer explaining his E3 2018 next-console announcement and the features he wants from it.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- Xbox boss Phil Spencer "announced plans for a new Xbox console on the Xbox E3 2018 stage" without sharing specifics.
- Speaking to GameSpot sister site Giant Bomb, Spencer said he made the announcement to assure people that consoles remain important to Microsoft.
- Spencer: "Anybody who might worry about our console future, I just wanted to put that at ease. I wanted people to know that I love the track record of our hardware team ... we have some ideas in the future [about streaming] but it's not tomorrow. I didn't want people to think we were going to walk away from that part of the brand in the business because it's really important to us."

## Wanted features for the next Xbox

- Higher frame rates.
- A box that launches games faster.
- Addressing the balance between CPU and GPU on console, which Spencer said is currently "out of whack" compared to PC.

## Xbox inside Microsoft

- A few years earlier there were "rumours and reports about Microsoft apparently wanting to sell off the Xbox brand."
- When CEO Satya Nadella arrived, Spencer said there were questions along the lines of "Why is Microsoft in the video game space?" - framed as an "honest" discussion about Microsoft's direction rather than condemnation.

## Unconfirmed reports

- "There are rumours circulating online at E3 this week that Microsoft's new console is codenamed Scarlet and may launch in 2020, though Microsoft has not commented."
- By Eddie Makuch.

wikis.title: Renderings of Related Companies and Wynn Resorts' master plan for Hudson Yards phase two
wikis.summary: New York YIMBY article presenting new renderings of the $12 billion mixed-use gaming complex proposed by Related Companies and Wynn Resorts for the Western Rail Yards, with the program, tower heights and casino licensing timeline.
wikis.body:
## The proposal

- "New renderings have been revealed for Related Companies and Wynn Resorts' $12 billion mixed-use gaming complex proposal for the second phase of Hudson Yards."
- Designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill.
- Program: multiple skyscrapers housing 1,500 apartments, 2 million square feet of office space, a public grade school, a 5.6-acre park called Hudson Green designed by Hollander Design and Sasaki, and a daycare center.
- Site: directly west of the first phase of Hudson Yards over the 13-acre Western Rail Yards, bound by West 33rd Street to the north, West 30th Street to the south, Eleventh Avenue to the east and West Street to the west.

## The towers

- "Each of the three proposed supertall skyscrapers features a distinct design with a different massing, facade, and crown."
- Wynn Resorts tower: 80 stories, 1,189 feet, at the northern end of the rail yards by the corner of Eleventh Avenue and West 33rd Street, near the Jacob K. Javits Center and the northernmost terminus of the High Line's third phase. "The symmetrically tapering structure, vaguely reminiscent of Kohn Pedersen Fox's Lotte World Tower in Seoul, is planned to yield 2.7 million square feet with 1,750 guest rooms along with a conference center, retail, and restaurant space. The Wynn hotel signature is displayed on the southern face of the sloping crown."
- Office tower: "To the south across the central public park is a 1,366-foot supertall office skyscraper clad in a glass curtain wall with tubular pleating on its northern and southern elevations."
- Residential tower: "The third supertall, an 1,172-foot-tall residential skyscraper, would sit directly to the west of the tallest component and features the most distinctive design, beginning with a base of massive cylindrical columns straddling the High Line that fan out into a multifaceted rectangular massing culminating in three stepped volumes."

## What the renderings show

- The main aerial rendering shows the entire scope of the second phase from over the Hudson River; areas between the towers are "populated with lush greenery and public walkways facing the High Line".
- Renderings of the low-rise Wynn Resorts casino and adjacent lawn emphasise "the building's flowing design, curved metallic surfaces, and landscaped terraces and roof deck"; views look east toward Thomas Heatherwick's Vessel sculpture, west toward the Hudson River, and from the intersection of Eleventh Avenue and West 33rd Street.
- "A dog run and a rock-climbing wall are among the outdoor facilities shown flanking the High Line at the base of one of the supertall skyscrapers."
- Renderings along West 30th Street show new ground-floor retail space beneath the High Line and garden beds along the sidewalks between Eleventh Avenue and West Street.
- Some renderings "were among the first batch released from our last update in March".

## Quote

- Bruce Beal Jr., president of Related Companies: "Finishing the undeveloped yards will not only create 35,000 unionized construction jobs during development, but 5,000 permanent union careers in the resort, which is the economic engine that supports all of these wonderful community benefits, including the affordable housing, public park, and transportation improvements."

## Licensing and transit

- "It remains to be seen which of the various proposed New York City casino sites will end up securing the three gaming licenses up for bidding by the state."
- "The winning developers are expected to pay at least $500 million in upfront license fees to operate the casino. The state Gaming Commission is expected to award licenses by December 31, 2025."
- "The closest subway from phase two of Hudson Yards is the local 7 train with the southernmost entry found between 50 and 55 Hudson Yards."

## Byline

- By Michael Young and Matt Pruznick, 8:00 AM on August 29, 2024; renderings courtesy of Related Companies and Wynn Resorts.

wikis.title: University of Manchester ceramic coating for hypersonic flight
wikis.summary: The Engineer reports a carbide coating developed at the University of Manchester with Central South University and the Royce Institute that performs 12 times better than zirconium carbide for hypersonic applications.
wikis.body:
## The coating

- "A new type of ceramic coating developed at the University of Manchester has the potential to 'revolutionise' hypersonic flight, according to its creators."
- Developed in collaboration with Central South University (CSU), China, and the Royce Institute.
- It is a carbide coating that "performs 12 times better than Zirconium carbide (ZrC), a widely used UHTC often found in tool bits".
- Performance is attributed to "its unique structural make-up, which provides excellent heat resistance and improved oxidation resistance".
- Manufactured using reactive melt infiltration (RMI), "which reduces the time needed to make such materials", and reinforced with carbon-carbon composite (C/C composite), "making it extremely resistant to typical surface degradation".

## The problem

- Hypersonic flight is "defined as Mach five or above" and "would see aircraft subjected to external temperatures between 2,000 and 3,000°C, leading to structural challenges caused by oxidation and ablation".
- Current spacecraft and missiles rely on ultra-high temperature ceramics (UHTCs), but according to Manchester University "conventional UHTCs can't currently satisfy the associated ablation requirements of hypersonic flight".

## Quotes

- Philip Withers, Regius Professor at Manchester University: "At present one of the biggest challenges is how to protect critical components such as leading edges, combustors and nose tips so that they survive the severe oxidation and extreme scouring of heat fluxes such temperatures cause to excess during flight."
- Ping Xiao, Professor of Materials Science, who led the study at the University of Manchester: "Current candidate UHTCs for use in extreme environments are limited and it is worthwhile exploring the potential of new single-phase ceramics in terms of reduced evaporation and better oxidation resistance." He added: "it has been shown that introducing such ceramics into carbon fibre-reinforced carbon matrix composites may be an effective way of improving thermal-shock resistance."

## Publication

- The Engineer, News, filed under Aerospace and Materials, 10 Jul 2017.

wikis.title: World population projected to reach 9.7 billion by 2050 (World Population Prospects: The 2015 Revision)
wikis.summary: UN DESA news release on the launch of "World Population Prospects: The 2015 Revision", giving its projections for world population, country rankings, Africa's growth, ageing and life expectancy.
wikis.body:
## The launch
- "29 July 2015, New York".
- "The current world population of 7.3 billion is expected to reach 8.5 billion by 2030, 9.7 billion in 2050 and 11.2 billion in 2100, according to a new UN DESA report, 'World Population Prospects: The 2015 Revision', launched today."
- "The 2015 Revision of World Population Prospects is the 24th round of official UN population estimates and projections that have been prepared by UN DESA's Population Division."
- Wu Hongbo, UN Under-Secretary-General for Economic and Social Affairs: "Understanding the demographic changes that are likely to unfold over the coming years, as well as the challenges and opportunities that they present for achieving sustainable development, is key to the design and implementation of the new development agenda."

## Where growth is concentrated
- "During 2015-2050, half of the world's population growth is expected to be concentrated in nine countries: India, Nigeria, Pakistan, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, United Republic of Tanzania, United States of America (USA), Indonesia and Uganda, listed according to the size of their contribution to the total growth."

## Shifts in country rankings
- China and India each have more than 1 billion people, "representing 19 and 18 % of the world's population, respectively. But by 2022, the population of India is expected to surpass that of China."
- Among the ten largest countries, one is in Africa (Nigeria), five in Asia (Bangladesh, China, India, Indonesia, Pakistan), two in Latin America (Brazil, Mexico), one in Northern America (USA) and one in Europe (Russian Federation).
- "The population of Nigeria is projected to surpass that of the United States by about 2050, at which point it would become the third largest country in the world."
- "By 2050, six countries are expected to exceed 300 million: China, India, Indonesia, Nigeria, Pakistan, and the USA."

## Africa
- Africa "is expected to account for more than half of the world's population growth between 2015 and 2050".
- "The populations of 28 African countries are projected to more than double, and by 2100, ten African countries are projected to have increased by at least a factor of five: Angola, Burundi, Democratic Republic of Congo, Malawi, Mali, Niger, Somalia, Uganda, United Republic of Tanzania and Zambia."
- John Wilmoth, Director of the Population Division: "The concentration of population growth in the poorest countries presents its own set of challenges, making it more difficult to eradicate poverty and inequality, to combat hunger and malnutrition, and to expand educational enrolment and health systems, all of which are crucial to the success of the new sustainable development agenda."

## Fertility and ageing
- "In recent years, fertility has declined in virtually all areas of the world, even in Africa where fertility levels remain the highest of any major area."
- "Globally the number of persons aged 60 or above is expected to more than double by 2050 and more than triple by 2100."
- Europe: 34 % of the population projected to be over 60 years old by 2050. Latin America and the Caribbean and Asia: from 11%-12% today to more than 25% by 2050. Africa: from 5% today to 9% by 2050.

## Life expectancy and child mortality
- "The six-year average gain in life expectancy among the poorest countries, from 56 years in 2000-2005 to 62 years in 2010-2015, is roughly double the increase recorded for the rest of the world."
- Differences across major areas and income groups "are expected to diminish significantly by 2045-2050".
- "Between 2000-2005 and 2010-2015, under-five mortality fell by more than 30% in 86 countries, of which 13 countries saw a decline of more than 50%. In the same time period, the rate decreased by more than 20% in 156 countries."

## Young populations
- "In Africa, children under age 15 account for 41% of the population in 2015 and young persons aged 15 to 24 account for a further 19%."
- Latin America and the Caribbean and Asia have smaller shares of children (26 and 24 % respectively) and similar shares of youth (17 and 16%).
- "In total, these three regions are home to 1.7 billion children and 1.1 billion young persons in 2015."

## Hedge the report keeps
- "While there is always some degree of uncertainty surrounding any projection, the large number of young people in Africa... ensures that the region will play a central role in shaping the size and distribution of the world's population over the coming decades."

wikis.title: Will humans reach a Type 1 civilization by 2100? Kardashev scale speculations
wikis.summary: h+ Magazine article by Len Rosen setting out the Kardashev scale of civilizations and Michio Kaku's speculation on when humanity might reach each type.
wikis.body:
## The Kardashev scale

- "Nikolai Kardashev, a Soviet astrophysicist born in 1932, devised a method of rating advanced civilizations."
- The stages, by how much energy a society maximizes: (1) the energy striking a planet from its local star; (2) all the energy emitted by a local star; (3) the energy from all the stars in its galaxy; (4) the energy from all galaxies and the intergalactic medium in the Universe. "He categorized each of these stages as Type 1 through Type 4."

## Where humanity sits

- "We are Type 0, somewhere between 0.7 and 0.72 producing 15 Terawatts of energy, a mere fraction of the energy a Type 1 would harvest from the physical world."
- "The renowned theoretical physicist, Michio Kaku, has speculated on Kardashev's scale and believes humanity will attain Type 1 status within a century or two" - through harnessing fusion and antimatter.

## Speculative timeline (the article's, based on Kaku)

- "By 2100 A.D. as Kaku predicts we will approach a Type 1." Capturing all solar energy reaching Earth, "increasing our energy supply by a factor of 100-billion"; nanotechnology and warp drive propulsion harnessed.
- "By 2200 A.D., a mere century later we will approach Type 2, harnessing all the energy of our Sun, another 100-billion-fold increase." Extra-solar, inhabiting planets on many nearby stars.
- "By 3000 A.D. we will have harnessed the energy of every star in the Milky Way, another 100-billion-fold energy increase" - Type 3, traversing the galaxy.
- Type 4 "we will reach much further into the future, to 12000 A.D.", having "transcended the physical reality of our Universe" and possibly reached parallel universes in the multiverse.

## Means described for each step

- Type 2: maximize antimatter as an energy source, harvest star matter, possibly build Dyson spheres to encase stars.
- Type 3: tap the energy of black holes "and even find the other side, the white holes, that propel matter outwards".
- Type 4: harness dark and extra-galactic energy; "such a civilization would be unrecognizable to us as such because it would be indistinguishable from the Universe itself".

## Closing argument

- "Technological breakthroughs that at one time took a century to achieve, now can happen in a year"; fusion is named as one of the harder technologies, but "today we are much closer to achieving that fusion breakthrough".

## Byline

- Author: Len Rosen, of Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Published July 29, 2014 under Dyson Spheres, Energy, Futurism, images, Kardashev Scale, Predictions.
- "This article originally appeared on his blog here: http://www.21stcentech.com/humans-achieve-type-1-civilization-2100/".

wikis.title: GameSpot review of the Dead Space remake
wikis.summary: GameSpot's review of EA Motive's 2023 Dead Space remake, covering its story and gameplay changes from the 2008 original and the 9/10 "Superb" verdict.
wikis.body:
## The review

- "Dead Space Remake Review - Hits The Marker", by Richard Wakeling on January 25, 2023 at 2:38PM PST.
- Review Verdict: 9, "SUPERB".
- Richard "finished Dead Space in around nine hours"; review code was provided by the publisher.
- Related tags: PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X.
- Dead Space: First Released Jan 27, 2023. Platforms: PC, PS5, XBSX.
- The remake is by EA Motive; the original 2008 game is by EA. "14 years is a long time in the video games industry".

## Story changes

- The basic beats of the original narrative remain, starting with arrival on the USG Ishimura, a "planet cracker-class ship" floating above the planet of Aegis VII after a distress signal.
- Once-silent protagonist Isaac Clarke has been given a voice; actor Gunner Wright reprises the role after voicing Isaac in Dead Space's sequels.
- Much of the script has been rewritten to accommodate Isaac's speech.
- The church of Unitology is much more prominent, especially early on.
- Kendra Daniels has been rewritten from prickly and antagonistic into "an empathetic character".

## Structure and level changes

- The vast majority of the remake is structurally identical to the original, from the dash to the elevator after the Necromorph reveal to disabling the Wheezers poisoning the air on the Hydroponics Deck.
- Zero-gravity sequences now let you leap from the ground and use suit thrusters to move freely, instead of rigidly hopping surface to surface; this will feel familiar to players of Dead Space 2.
- Sections such as the Ishimura's hanger have expanded in scope; the ADS cannon repair has been redesigned from "a stale turret shooting gallery" into "a treacherous spacewalk", carrying over into fights against The Leviathan.
- A new security clearance system initially locks certain rooms and lockers, with higher clearance unlocked through the story.
- New bespoke side quests require backtracking; travel between parts of the ship is now seamless. The review says the side quests "essentially boil down to picking up an item or activating a previously recorded message".

## Weapons and combat

- Special weapon upgrades carried over from the 2011 sequel: a Plasma Cutter mod that sets targets alight for burn damage over time; a Disc Ripper mod that ricochets sawblades through multiple enemies. Mods are scattered throughout the Ishimura.
- Primary fire modes largely unchanged; several weapons have new secondary functions.
- The Pulse Rifle now has a dual-purpose proximity mine that works as a trap or makeshift grenade launcher.
- The Flamethrower's new secondary fire shoots a wall of flame to cordon enemies off from one another.
- The Force Gun, previously "little more than a tool for pushing enemies away", now unleashes a blast that rips skin and muscle off the bone; its secondary fire shoots a gravity well that pulls enemies toward it.
- Necromorphs can only be killed by slicing off their limbs.

## Visuals

- The overhauled visuals are described as "phenomenal across the board".
- The new "peeling system" strips skin, fat and muscle layers from enemies with each successive wound, leaving exposed bones that can be snapped.
- The green light running up the spine of Isaac's suit is a visual indicator of his health.

## The Good / The Bad (as listed)

- The Good: combat remains uniquely gratifying and reworked weapons improve the limb-dismembering action; secondary fire modes give extra strategic options; zero-G sections are much more interesting and not as rigid; Isaac's newfound voice gives him agency and the story is expanded engagingly.
- The Bad: side quests aren't particularly interesting and revolve around stale backtracking.

## Retail note

- Listed at $18.99 at GameStop for XBSX and PS5.

wikis.title: Final Fantasy XVI: release date, story and everything we know
wikis.summary: GameSpot feature gathering what is known about Final Fantasy XVI before launch: its June 22, 2023 PS5 release, exclusivity window, story and characters, Eikon battles, combat, length and preorder editions.
wikis.body:
## Release date and platforms

- "Final Fantasy XVI is scheduled to release exclusively for PlayStation 5 on June 22, 2023."
- The game will not be cross-generation; "PS4 owners will have to make the move to PS5 in order to play it." Square Enix's reveal trailer noted the game will "not [be] available on other platforms for a limited time after release on PS5", and that "The following content is captured on PC emulating the PS5 experience".
- "Final Fantasy XVI has officially gone gold, which means that the game is ready to be pressed onto discs–though development will still continue."
- Square Enix confirmed in recent trailers that the game is coming to PC; "PlayStation 5 exclusivity will end December 31, 2023, or roughly six months after the game's initial release."
- No confirmation from Square Enix about an Xbox version. Game hub lists platforms PC, PS5, XBSX; "First Released Jun 22, 2023".
- "The latest game arrives six years after the last numbered entry in the mainline series."

## Story and characters

- Set in the world of Valisthea, with conflict between realms and political drama, and a focus on Dominants — "the few special people who can wield the power of Eikons, which are what summons are called in FFXVI's world".
- Yoshida told GameSpot the story will span three different eras: Clive in his teens, 20s, and 30s.
- Clive Rosfield is the son of his realm's archduke and wields Eikon-related powers but "isn't necessarily a Dominant himself"; he is sworn to protect his brother Joshua, who was fated as a Dominant and summons Phoenix. The trailer ends in a battle between Phoenix and Ifrit.
- Jill Warrick comes from another realm, "was essentially adopted by the Rosfields, and acts as a mediary between warring nations"; a trusted confidant to Clive and Joshua.
- Other Eikons seen include Shiva and Titan; there is a fight against an armour-clad lance-wielding Dragoon, "said to be an Imperial Viper".
- The world revolves around Mothercrystals, "which are said to bless the land with aether (basically magic)", while a destructive force called The Blight washes over the world. Tagline: "The legacy of the crystals has shaped our history for long enough."
- Yoshida on themes: "You're going to focus on those motivations and those struggles, and then, you're going to delve even deeper and into darker themes when it comes to how people should live; should people live the life that was chosen for them or fight to break free from that kind of destiny?"

## Trailers and rating

- The first trailer was titled "Awakening", offering four minutes of story, cutscenes and gameplay, with an orchestrated theme including the Crystal Prelude.
- A new trailer revealed at The Game Awards 2022 is titled "Revenge", showing Espers including Odin and Ifrit.
- "This will also be the first Final Fantasy game to receive an M-rating". The rating covers sex scenes that are "not fully shown" and violence including "blood, intentional deaths, torture...victims suffering" and "hate crimes".
- Producer Naoki Yoshida: "To make sure that we could tell the story that we wanted in the way that we wanted to, we decided to pursue a mature rating in most of the regions that will be releasing the game... this is because we felt it was necessary to allow us to explore those more mature themes that the game tackles."

## Eikon battles

- The second trailer, shown at Sony's June State of Play, showcased Eikon vs Eikon battles as major setpieces.
- Yoshida said these battles will all be unique — "one might emulate a wrestling match while another might look like a 3D shooter" — and estimated there are roughly 20 of them in all, alongside smaller-scale battles against standard enemies, mini-bosses and human-sized Eikons.
- The battles take place in wide-open spaces, but Square Enix has clarified FFXVI isn't an open-world game.

## Logo

- Artist Yoshitaka Amano's logo features Ifrit and Phoenix face-to-face in a fight, the battle that concludes the trailer.

## Gameplay

- Action-RPG combat with similarities to FFXV and FF7 Remake; Clive casts fireballs, fights at melee range with his sword and warp-like abilities, and uses Eikon-tied powers.
- Clive is accompanied by AI-controlled party members plus a "faithful buddy" character who can be given direct commands.
- Ryota Suzuki, a combat designer on Devil May Cry 5 and Dragon's Dogma, is battle director.
- April's State of Play showed 20 minutes of gameplay. Clive can be customised through a "massive skill tree" whose abilities can be reset at any time.
- Players travel between locations via a world map that is updated as the game progresses; there are several levels rather than an open world. Cid's Hideaway, unlocked later, is where Clive upgrades gear, buys weapons and armour, trains and picks up side quests.
- Takai has acknowledged God of War influences; the mission structure follows recent God of War games closely, with other influences from movies, games and anime.

## Difficulty rings

- Challenge is tuned with five special rings rather than menu options: one simplifies combat so "one button automatically controls your combos", another extends the dodge window.
- Rings are equipped in the three accessory slots, so each assist ring means one fewer customisation accessory.

## Length

- Game director Hiroshi Takai and producer Naoki Yoshida "estimate that the base game can be completed in around 35 hours, but for completionists looking to finish 100% of the game, expect around 70 to 80 hours".

## Development

- Developed by Creative Business Unit III, the division behind Final Fantasy XIV. Naoki Yoshida leads production; Hiroshi Takai directs.
- Square Enix launched an official website with looks at the world and characters.

## Editions and preorder bonuses

- Standard edition: $70; preordering from Best Buy adds a free steelbook case.
- Deluxe edition: $100, with a cloth world map of Valisthea and the Special Clive Rosfield steelbook case.
- Collector's edition: $350, including the base game, Premium Statue – Phoenix vs Ifrit, metal Eikon pin collection, Special Clive Rosfield steelbook case, cloth world map of Valisthea, bonus in-game weapon Blood Sword, digital mini artbook, digital mini soundtrack, The Realms of Valisthea wall banners (6-inch printed cloth banners) and the FFXVI preorder steelbook.
- Preorder items: the Cat Sith Charm (boosts Gil gain) and Braveheart weapon at just about every retailer; the Scholar's Spectacles (boosts XP gain) only with the Collector's Edition, Deluxe Edition (Digital) and Standard Edition (Digital).

## Article details

- By Michael Higham, Steve Watts, Darryn Bonthuys and Jessica Cogswell on June 6, 2023 at 11:38AM PDT.

wikis.title: GameSpot review of Elden Ring - "Death Of The Wild"
wikis.summary: GameSpot's review-in-progress of Elden Ring by Tamoor Hussain, scoring it 10 / Essential and describing its open world, new mechanics, difficulty and multiplayer.
wikis.body:
## The review

- Headline: "Elden Ring Review - Death Of The Wild".
- By Tamoor Hussain, "on March 15, 2022 at 5:17PM PDT".
- "First Released Feb 25, 2022"; platform listed as PC, status "released".
- Score: 10, "Essential".
- Deck: "From Software's latest is a masterpiece of open-world design that places exploration and player agency at the heart of the experience."

## Premise as described

- The setting is the Lands Between. "The world is ruled by five Elden Lords, each in possession of a shard of the titular Elden Ring. As a lowly Tarnished, you aim to defeat these corrupt lords, take their shards, stand before the Erdtree, and become an Elden Lord in your own right."
- The reviewer defeated Godrick The Golden, "the first of five Elden Lords", fifteen hours in, and had defeated only two of the five by the 35-hour mark.

## Design points noted

- "There's no map until you find an item that reveals the topography of a region", and points of interest are not marked until visited. "There is no minimap, just a compass to show the cardinal directions and any waypoints you've placed."
- Quests "aren't noted down or tracked in any kind of log"; areas are not gated by level.
- Sites of Grace function as rest points "in the same way Bonfires, Lanterns, or Idols did in other titles", each showing "a dim trail of golden light pointing in the general direction of… something".

## New mechanics

- A jump, "pulled from the more dynamic movement style of Sekiro", usable for traversal and for a leaping strike that can break an enemy's defense.
- A heavy counter after blocking, dealing "a good amount of damage" and potentially opening a critical strike.
- Spirit Ashes: summonable, upgradable AI-controlled fighters (a pack of wolves, a mage, a poison-spewing jellyfish). "Spirit Ashes can only be used in specific locations and only once per life" and are "better equipped for pulling aggro than securing victories".
- Stakes of Marika: small statues scattered in the open world that act as respawn points near challenging areas instead of returning the player to a Site of Grace.

## Locations named

- Limgrave, Liurnia of the Lakes, Caelid, Caria Manor, Stormvale Castle, Redmane Castle, Raya Lucaria.
- The player's spectral steed is named Torrent.

## Story and credits

- On George R.R. Martin: "there's little in Elden Ring that stands out as having his fingerprints on it"; the delivery is "unmistakably Hidetaka Miyazaki and the From Software team". Martin "helped lay the foundation for" the expansive world.

## Multiplayer

- Co-op requires "jumping through hoops such as being positioned in specific ways, using specific items to establish connections, and sticking to certain areas"; "difficulty scales to account for multiple combatants".
- Players can invade other players' worlds "and attempt to assassinate them".

## Verdict boxes

- The Good: exploration and discovery driven entirely by the player; stunning world design blending a new open world with classic enclosed Soulsborne-style locations; challenging combat; a visually stunning, diverse world; "a compelling, layered, and multi-faceted story".
- The Bad: "Still, at its core, a difficult game designed for a specific kind of person with little in the way of approachability options"; "Online multiplayer still requires jumping through hoops".

## Editor's note

- "I have played over 50 hours of the game"; because of remaining content and untested online multiplayer, "this article will remain as a review-in-progress. In the coming weeks, it will be finalized and, depending on the overall experience, the score may be subject to change."
- "Tamoor played Elden Ring on PC and PS5"; "Review code was provided by the publisher."

## Retail line on the page

- "$59.99 on Bestbuy".

wikis.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 campaign review (GameSpot)
wikis.summary: GameSpot's review of the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II campaign, giving its verdict of 8, the game's story, missions and mechanics, and the release details listed with it.
wikis.body:
## The review
- "Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 Campaign Review - Just Like Old Times", by S.E. Doster, October 21, 2022 at 7:55PM PDT.
- Review Verdict: 8, "GREAT".
- The Good: "A perfect dose of nostalgia while still telling a fresh story"; "More player choice and open-world-style moments"; "A great looking blockbuster". The Bad: "Weird save point locations make for difficult respawning".
- Editor's note: "Given the staggered release of Call of Duty Modern Warfare 2's campaign and multiplayer, as well as Warzone 2.0, GameSpot will be publishing three separate reviews."
- The reviewer "completed Modern Warfare 2's campaign in just over six hours on Regular"; PS5 review code was provided by the publisher.

## Story
- "Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2's story picks up three years after the events of 2019's rebooted Modern Warfare."
- Task Force 141 comprises Captain Price, Simon "Ghost" Riley, Kyle "Gaz" Garrick and John "Soap" MacTavish; a new ally is Colonel Alejandro Vargas of the Mexican Special Forces. General Shepherd is reintroduced from the original campaign; Kate Laswell and Shadow Company return.
- "A United States airstrike kills Al-Qatala leader General Ghorbrani, whose successor, Hassan Zyani, vows revenge and teams up with an international drug cartel to transport stolen U.S. ballistic missiles."
- Locations include Amsterdam, Mexico, Chicago and parts of Al Mazrah, "the fictional setting of Warzone 2.0's map".

## Missions and mechanics
- "Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 features 17 campaign missions."
- Named missions discussed: Recon By Fire, Close Air (an AC-130 gunship sequence), Violence and Timing.
- New maneuvering mechanics let players swap seats in a vehicle and stand on car roofs to hijack another vehicle.
- A new crafting layer requires scavenging to craft mines, smoke bombs, shivs and a pry tool; new equipment includes "the new snake cam device to slide under a door jam".
- Optional dialogue options let the player talk to fellow soldiers.
- The reviewer played on Regular difficulty and found enemy AI spots the player more easily than in past games; checkpoints "were spread out pretty far in some missions".
- On PlayStation 5 "the graphics were sharp and everything ran smoothly", with no crashes, major bugs or performance issues.

## Game details listed
- Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II - First Released Oct 28, 2022. Platforms: PC, PS4, PS5, XONE, XBSX.

wikis.title: GameSpot review of The Quarry
wikis.summary: GameSpot's review of Supermassive Games' horror game The Quarry, covering its setup, cast, mechanics and the 9/10 "Superb" verdict.
wikis.body:
## The review

- "The Quarry Review - Summer Scare Fest", by Richard Wakeling on June 8, 2022 at 5:59AM PDT.
- Review Verdict: 9, "SUPERB".
- Richard "finished The Quarry in just under 10 hours"; review code was provided by the publisher.
- Related tags: PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X.
- The Quarry: First Released Jun 10, 2022. Platforms: PC, PS4, PS5, XONE, XBSX.

## The game

- The Quarry is Supermassive Games' "spiritual successor to Until Dawn", a "new 10-hour horror game" that follows the formula of Until Dawn, after the studio's shorter stories in The Dark Pictures Anthology series.
- After a prologue, the first act begins on the last day of summer camp; the kids have been sent home and only the counselors and the camp's owner remain. When their minivan fails to start, the counselors spend another night together and throw a party.
- The player switches between control of all nine counselors as they attempt to survive the night.
- Named counselors include Jacob "the boisterous jock", Dylan "the wisecracking oddball" and Abigail "the socially awkward artist".

## Influences and cast

- The summer camp setting is described as inspired by Friday the 13th and Sleepaway Camp; its self-awareness is likened to the Scream franchise, with allusions to The Texas Chainsaw Massacre and The Hills Have Eyes.
- Supporting roles feature horror mainstays David Arquette, Lin Shaye, Lance Henriksen and Ted Raimi.

## Mechanics

- Built on choice and consequence: decisions include picking between dialogue options, choosing which path to take, or pulling a shotgun's trigger. "Play your cards right and you could see everyone survive the night, or fail so catastrophically that no one is left alive come sunrise."
- Quick-time events require flicking the left analog stick in the right direction, with face buttons for occasional button mashing and holding your breath.
- Death is not final: if a character dies, the player can spend one of three lives to rewind time. The review notes a fatal choice may have occurred 20 minutes earlier, meaning replaying a lengthy chunk.
- Exploration uncovers collectibles and tarot cards that "offer a brief glimpse into the future"; the game uses fixed camera angles at times but mostly over-the-shoulder control, with cinematic letterboxing and a slow walking speed.
- Movie Mode lets players watch events unfold, choosing a playthrough where everyone lives or dies, or using director mode to predetermine the behavior of all nine counselors.
- "The mechanics haven't evolved since Until Dawn was released seven years ago".

## The Good / The Bad (as listed)

- The Good: its love for horror movies is infectious; the ensemble cast is wonderful; dialogue is snappy and genuinely funny; palpable sense of weight behind many choices and consequences.
- The Bad: suffers from some pacing issues; exploration drags due to a glacial walking speed.

## Retail note

- Listed at $18.93 at Amazon for PS4, XONE, PS5, XBSX.

wikis.title: A Plague Tale: Requiem review (GameSpot)
wikis.summary: GameSpot's review of A Plague Tale: Requiem, scoring it 7/10 and describing its stealth-action systems, companions, setting and story.
wikis.body:
## Verdict

- Review Verdict: 7, "GOOD".
- Standfirst: "A Plague Tale: Requiem eventually expands in scope and improves upon its predecessor's stealth action, but the heartrending story of two siblings battling against the odds is where it truly excels."
- The Good, as listed: tells a harrowing, heartrending tale of two siblings fighting against the odds; the rats are still horrifying, "especially now there are significantly more of them"; its picturesque setting offers a powerful contrast to the game's terrors; some environments are larger, giving more options.
- The Bad, as listed: "Takes a long time to increase its scope, so the early hours aren't particularly interesting"; "Confined combat sequences are a frustrating case of trial and error"; "The story runs into some pacing issues once it delves into heavy exposition".

## The game

- Developer: Asobo Studio. Platforms tagged: PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X; game hub lists NS, PC, PS5, XBSX. "First Released Oct 17, 2022".
- Rat technology: "Whereas the first game could handle 5,000 rats at any one time, its sequel can populate the screen with a staggering 300,000." A Plague Tale: Innocence was released in 2019.
- Story setup: Amicia de Rune, a teenage girl, protects her younger brother Hugo across a plague-stricken 14th-century France in search of a cure for his illness. "The narrative picks up six months after the first game ended, with Amicia and Hugo traveling to the region of Provence in southern France, bordering the Mediterranean Sea."

## Systems described

- Amicia's sling kills helmet-less enemies and can strike crates of armor as a distraction; alchemical ammo lights or snuffs out fires to control light-averse rats.
- Amicia can counter armored enemies after being spotted, stunning them; single-use knives finish them off and also open padlocked workbenches holding crafting materials. The sling can strangle unarmored enemies from behind.
- Stealth options include tall grass, crawling under carts and throwing pots. Unlike the first game, the player can re-enter stealth after being caught by breaking line-of-sight and hiding.
- "The game starts to stretch its legs around five hours in", introducing a crossbow that can kill most armored enemies with a single bolt (ammunition scarce) and Hugo's ability to control the rats directly, limited by a gauge that fills with use.
- Companions: Arnaud, "a gruff soldier who can be directed to fight enemies with the press of a button" — if he dies it triggers a game over; Sophia, "a pirate you meet in the latter half of the game", with a shard of glass to deflect sunlight and set dry grass alight.
- Skill system: pacifist play unlocks stealth skills (faster crouched movement, quieter movement); aggressive play unlocks a push that shoves enemies into fire or rats and faster sling chokes.
- Light puzzle-solving involves light sources in rat-infested areas; forced confined combat scenarios require killing everyone in the player's path.

## Review details

- By Richard Wakeling on October 17, 2022 at 11:04AM PDT.
- "Richard completed A Plague Tale: Requiem in 14 hours, picking up most of the collectibles along the way. Review code was provided by the publisher."

wikis.title: Yellen says US will run out of cash by June 5 (X-date)
wikis.summary: New York Times report on Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen's letter moving the projected US X-date to June 5, 2023, amid debt-limit talks between the White House and House Republicans.
wikis.body:
## Yellen's new estimate

- Treasury Secretary Janet L. Yellen said on Friday that the United States "will run out of money to pay its bills on time by June 5", moving the goal post back slightly.
- The letter provided "the most precise date yet"; Yellen had previously said the nation could hit the X-date "as soon as June 1".
- By Alan Rappeport, reporting from Washington, May 26, 2023. Print version: Section A, Page 16, New York edition, headline "Yellen Expects U.S. Will Run Out of Cash by June 5".

## The fiscal position

- The White House and House Republicans have been racing to reach a deal to lift the nation's $31.4 trillion borrowing cap.
- The Treasury Department hit its statutory debt limit on Jan. 19 and has been employing "extraordinary measures".
- The federal government is required to make more than $130 billion in scheduled payments during the first two days of June, including money to veterans and Social Security and Medicare recipients; those payments will leave Treasury with "an extremely low level of resources".
- Yellen wrote: "Our projected resources would be inadequate to satisfy all of these obligations."
- The Treasury Department's cash balance fell to $38.8 billion on Thursday.
- New extraordinary measures in the letter involved moving $2 billion of Treasury securities between the Civil Service Retirement and Disability Fund and the Federal Financing Bank.
- Yellen wrote: "The extremely low level of remaining resources demands that I exhaust all available extraordinary measures to avoid being unable to meet all of the government's commitments."

## Reaction

- President Biden, departing the White House for Camp David on Friday evening: "Things are looking good. I'm very optimistic," adding, "I'm hopeful we'll know by tonight whether we are going to be able to have a deal."
- Representative Patrick T. McHenry (Republican, North Carolina) said the more precise date "puts additional pressure on us", and: "We've got to be in the closing hours because of the timeline. I don't know if it's in the next day or two or three, but it's got to come together."
- Members of the House Freedom Caucus wrote to Speaker Kevin McCarthy urging party leaders to demand that Yellen "furnish a complete justification" of her June 1 projection, accusing her of "manipulative timing".
- Wally Adeyemo, deputy Treasury secretary, told CNN on Friday: "Congress has the ability to do that, and the president is calling on them to act on that as quickly as possible."
- Lael Brainard, director of the White House's National Economic Council: "Negotiators have made progress toward a reasonable, bipartisan budget agreement in recent days, and the Secretary's letter underscores the urgent need for Congress to act swiftly to prevent default."

## Outside estimates and markets

- The Bipartisan Policy Center said earlier that week that the U.S. faced an "elevated risk" of running out of cash to pay its bills between June 2 and 13 if Congress does not raise or suspend the debt limit.
- Fitch Ratings placed the nation's top AAA credit rating on review for a possible downgrade that week; DBRS Morningstar did the same on Thursday.
- Yellen wrote: "We have learned from past debt limit impasses that waiting until the last minute to suspend or increase the debt limit can cause serious harm to business and consumer confidence, raise short-term borrowing costs for taxpayers, and negatively impact the credit rating of the United States."

## Shape of a possible deal

- No deal had been announced, but the contours of an agreement would raise the debt limit for two years while imposing strict caps on discretionary spending not related to the military or veterans for the same period.
- Biden administration officials downplayed avoiding default by prioritizing payments to bondholders, and dismissed invoking the 14th Amendment.

Luke Broadwater contributed reporting.

wikis.title: Frito-Lay and Quaker open the Greenhouse Learning Center for compostable packaging
wikis.summary: Packaging World report on the Greenhouse Learning Center that Frito-Lay North America and Quaker Oats opened at PepsiCo's R&D headquarters in Plano, Texas, to field test compostable packaging materials.
wikis.body:
## The facility

- "Frito-Lay North America and The Quaker Oats Company recently unveiled its Greenhouse Learning Center at its R&D headquarters in Plano, Tex., during a ribbon-cutting ceremony."
- "Just a week after an official ribbon-cutting ceremony, Frito-Lay North America invited a select group of media to tour what it says is a first-of-its kind facility globally for PepsiCo that will enable on-site testing and analysis of compostable packaging materials."
- It is "a custom-designed R&D facility in Plano, Texas, that tests compostable packaging in different environments including hot composting, cold composting, and home composting".
- Technical Director, PepsiCo R&D Senior Fellow Sridevi Narayan-Sarathy led the media tour.

## Testing speed

- "It can take up to six months to get results from outside testing facilities on the composability of a new material or package."
- At the center the R&D team can evaluate "in as little as three months or less" whether a material has potential for industrial or home compostability.
- "It will enable products to move from testing to certification-ready at least two to three times faster to fast-track new packaging."

## Composting processes tested

- Hot composting, which simulates industrial composting: "microbial activity within the compost pile is optimized with regular turning of the pile to create heat, resulting in finished compost in a much shorter period of time".
- Cold composting, "where material is continually added to a compost pile without turning the material".
- Home composting, examined through the use of a composting bin.
- The team is also examining how compostable materials impact soil and plants such as dill, basil and cilantro - "which are then being used by the site's cafeteria chefs" - as well as canola and corn, "which can be used as feedstock for the production of biopolymers".

## PepsiCo Positive (pep+) goal

- The center "represents a key milestone in achieving PepsiCo's PepsiCo Positive (pep+) packaging goal to design 100% of its packaging to be recyclable, compostable, biodegradable, or reusable by 2025".
- David Allen, vice president, chief sustainability officer for PepsiCo Foods North America, said the program, "launched just over a year ago", is "a fundamental transformation in PepsiCo's business": "It's about putting sustainability at the center of how we create growth and value for the organization and do that in a way that makes sure we're operating within planetary boundaries, and we're making a positive impact on the planet and the people."
- One of pep+'s three pillars is creating a positive value chain, where circularity and the sustainable packaging vision sit; guided by Science Based Targets initiatives (SBTi), PepsiCo is working across all divisions and formats "to build better packaging for a better world".

## Frito-Lay's compostable packaging journey

- Frito-Lay North America is described as "the $23 billion convenient foods division of PepsiCo., Inc.", relying heavily on flexible film packaging for brands including Lay's and Ruffles, Doritos and Tostitos, Fritos and SunChips.
- Yolanda Malone, vice president Global Foods Packaging, PepsiCo, on current snack packaging: "there are nine layers in all, providing print, lamination, and barrier functionality". "We have a really well-honed, functioning package today. But in order for us to achieve our aspirations to make our packaging 100% recyclable, compostable, biodegradable, or reusable, we have to make some changes."
- "In 2010, ahead of its time, Frito-Lay launched a 100% industrially compostable bag for its SunChips snack brand, but consumer pushback on the noise the bag created sent the company back to the drawing board."
- Malone: "There was a lot of feedback, but we continued our journey. And so from 2017 through today, we've launched our Off The Eaten Path, second-generation compostable bag" (without the loud crinkling sound).
- Frito-Lay "has introduced other options made from 85% renewable plant materials that produce approximately 60% lower greenhouse gas emissions than traditional snack bags".
- The company is now "focusing its efforts on engineering home-compostable and biodegradable packaging".

## Industry aims

- Denise Lefebvre, senior vice president of R&D for PepsiCo: "Our sustainable packaging vision is to build a world where packaging need never become waste... We're actively changing our own compostable snack packaging technologies. By sharing these technologies, we're inviting the industry to make these changes as well. We are prioritizing, investing in, and expediting projects to build a more circular, inclusive economy."
- The center also aims to change industry standards by educating partners and stakeholders, demonstrating circularity with biodegradable materials, and providing training to co-ops and visitors.
- Allen: "We look forward to leveraging key findings from the Greenhouse Learning Center, alongside our scale, reach, and expertise across North America and globally, to drive progress across our organization and the entire industry."

## Byline

- Anne Marie Mohan, Packaging World, Apr 6, 2023.

wikis.title: Hivemapper reaches 1 million unique kilometers mapped
wikis.summary: Hivemapper blog post announcing 1,000,000 km of unique street-level imagery, plus Hivemapper Fleets, a HONEY airdrop under MIP-2, and the arithmetic behind its "5x faster than Google Street View" claim.
wikis.body:
## Milestone

- "Today, thanks to the work of map contributors all over the world, Hivemapper eclipsed 1,000,000 KM of unique street-level imagery!"
- "Over only the last 3 months, the Hivemapper community has done what took Google Street View 5x longer to do."
- Contributors "have also mapped unique places where Google Street View does not have any coverage."
- "As of March 8th, all pre-orders have been fulfilled (ahead of schedule!)", and the core team "shipped significant updates to both the Hivmeapper Dashcam firmware and the Hivemapper App".
- Next milestone named: "10M unique road km mapped"; "We believe the next 10M km will be unlocked with fleets."

## What the post covers

- The 1M km milestone and exponential contributor growth
- Hivemapper Fleets ("We will soon launch")
- MIP-2 and a 1000 HONEY token airdrop

- Maps are used "by companies across industries like logistics, insurance, real estate, utilities, and government."
- GIFs in the post illustrate scaling coverage "in the United States, Europe, and South Korea."
- "Hivemapper's mission is to build a continuously updating global map of our world."
