- Posted March 23, 2023.

wikis.title: 1 million unique road km mapped in three months
wikis.summary: The milestone itself: 1,000,000 km of unique street-level imagery, reached 5x faster than Google Street View, alongside fulfilled pre-orders and firmware updates.
wikis.body:
- "Hivemapper eclipsed 1,000,000 KM of unique street-level imagery" thanks to map contributors worldwide.
- "Individual contributors helped grow the map to 1M unique road km in just 3 months."
- Contributors have grown the map "exponentially, faster than we expected", including "unique places where Google Street View does not have any coverage."
- The post frames this as a property of "an open, permissionless map": "underserved areas will be seen, and neglected regions can bring their roads online permissionslessly."
- "As of March 8th, all pre-orders have been fulfilled (ahead of schedule!)", plus updates to the Hivemapper Dashcam firmware and the Hivemapper App.
- Next target: "10M unique road km mapped".

wikis.title: Hivemapper Fleets
wikis.summary: A coming feature for creating and managing driver fleets, with HONEY splits, pitched on quality, coverage and freshness.
wikis.body:
- "We will soon launch Hivemapper Fleets, a way to create and manage fleets."
- "After you create a fleet on Hivemapper, you can add fleet managers and drivers and set how you'd like to split HONEY tokens between yourself and members."
- "We released and announced Hivemapper Fleets Beta at the end of September and have been iterating on it since then."
- Quality: "Fleet drivers are more likely to collect better quality imagery because they are often professional drivers and will mount the Hivemapper Dashcam following best practices."
- Coverage: "50 Uber drivers in London, UK, can generate 10,000 to 15,000 unique road miles per week".
- Freshness: "Mail delivery vehicles see most parts of a given city on a weekly basis ensuring that the map is refreshed."
- "Maps with the highest refresh rate are the most valuable."

wikis.title: MIP-2 and the 1000 HONEY dashcam airdrop
wikis.summary: A Hivemapper Foundation proposal reshaping HONEY rewards plus a token airdrop for dashcams bought before June 17, 2023 in MIP-2 regions.
wikis.body:
- "the Hivemapper Foundation introduced Map Improvement Proposal 2 (MIP-2), which improves aspects of the HONEY reward program to incentivize better coverage and freshness in high-demand regions and countries."
- "the Hivemapper Foundation is offering a 1000 HONEY token airdrop to all Hivemapper Dashcams activated and purchased on our store or an authorized reseller before June 17, 2023, where the shipping address is in a MIP-2 region and country."
- "Our goal is to incentivize more drivers to join the Hivemapper Network in high-demand regions to provide coverage and freshness."

wikis.title: How the 5x factor was calculated
wikis.summary: The post's arithmetic comparing Hivemapper's monthly coverage rate with Google Street View's five-year average.
wikis.body:
- "Over the past month, Hivemapper contributors added 660,000 km of unique coverage. That statistic is published daily in real time on our Explorer page."
- "Google launched Street View in May 2007 and by June 2012, they had mapped 8 million kilometers of roads."
- "Averaged over 60 months, that is 133k kilometers per month, or 5x slower."
- "This comparison is very conservative because it compares Google's average over five years with Hivemapper's current monthly run rate" - Google was "most likely adding coverage more slowly than this 5-year average at the beginning", and "Hivemapper's growth rate is currently accelerating as more of the dashcams we've already sold come online."
- "However, this is probably the safest number to use, based only on Google's public statements."

wikis.title: China adds 1 trillion yuan of stimulus as recovery slows
wikis.summary: Bloomberg report on China's State Council outlining a 19-point policy package with a further 1 trillion yuan ($146 billion) of funding, largely for infrastructure.
wikis.body:
## What happened

- China "stepped up its economic stimulus with a further 1 trillion yuan ($146 billion) of funding largely focused on infrastructure spending".
- The support "likely won't go far enough to counter the damage from repeated Covid lockdowns and a property market slump".

## The package

- The State Council, China's Cabinet, outlined a 19-point policy package on Wednesday.
- Includes another 300 billion yuan that state policy banks can invest in infrastructure projects, on top of 300 billion yuan already announced at the end of June.
- Local governments will be allocated 500 billion yuan of special bonds from previously unused quotas.

## Headline points

- "State Council outlines 19 policies including policy bank funds".
- "Growth likely to be sluggish barring major stimulus: Goldman".

wikis.title: Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index falls to lowest level since March 2021 (April 2024)
wikis.summary: Report that Cox Automotive's Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index fell 14.0% year-over-year in April 2024 to 198.4, its lowest reading in more than three years, with the declines by market class.
wikis.body:
## Headline figures

- "Wholesale vehicle prices continued their downward slope in April, falling double-digit percentages from a year ago."
- Cox Automotive's Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index "for the month fell below 200 for the first time in more than three years".
- Adjusting for mix, mileage and seasonality, wholesale vehicle prices were down 14.0% year-over-year and 2.3% month-over-month.
- Unadjusted, prices fell 11.9% year-over-year and 0.6% from March.
- The index reading was 198.4, "the lowest it has been since March 2021, when it came in at 195.4".
- The figures come from a Data Point report accompanying the index.

## Year-over-year declines by market class

- Compact cars: down 17.6% (heftiest decline).
- Midsize cars: down 16.8%.
- Pickups: down 15.2%.
- SUV/CUV: down 14.6%.
- Luxury: down 12.9%.
- Non-electric vehicles: down 13.1%.
- EVs: down 17.5% from April 2023.

## Byline

- Auto Remarketing Staff, Tuesday, May 7, 2024, 03:49 PM.

wikis.title: Telegraph Defence in Depth: China's 48-hour window to attack Taiwan
wikis.summary: Telegraph video analysis arguing a Chinese move on Taiwan is a question of when not if, built around a reported 48-hour attack window, Xi's 2027 readiness date and the military balance across the strait.
wikis.body:
## The 48-hour window

- "According to diplomatic sources in the UK, Beijing believes there is a 48-hour window in which it can attack Taiwan before any international consensus forms."
- "In that time Chinese forces would need to get across the Taiwan Strait, onto the land and cut off the political and military leadership in Taiwan." The piece calls this "a tall order."

## Timing

- "President Xi has made no bones about saying that 2027 is the date that he wants the Chinese army to be 'ready' to take back Taiwan. Now, that doesn't mean that they will invade in 2027, but certainly implies a significant milestone."
- "Ely Ratner, the senior Pentagon official in charge of the Indo-Pacific region, has said he doesn't expect anything to happen before the end of the decade."
- "with China yet to see the full results of the war in Ukraine, their confidence in being able to act in the next few years remains unclear."
- Framing: "it's just a question of when, not if, Beijing moves on Taipei."

## Chinese military build-up

- "The Chief of Britain's Defence Staff says that their navy is increasing by the size of the entire Royal Navy every four years. The same thing is happening in areas of space, cyber, air and land."
- "the Chinese military is untested. It hasn't fought a war since 1979 when it invaded Vietnam."
- "we don't know if the organisation is very top-down or if the lower level commanders are able to make decisions for themselves".

## How an attack might go

- "the island of Formosa, where the capital Taipei stands, lies 70 miles across the Taiwan Strait."
- "The most likely scenario for an attack would start with a massive cyber attack to paralyse Taiwan's decision-making bodies - both military and political - and then a lightning strike to get across the strait and onto the island."
- An amphibious assault is called "a very tricky operation": Chinese forces would face "US-supplied cruise missiles and anti-ship missiles", would "have to sink the Taiwanese navy and submarines", and would land where "there will be thousands of people waiting for you - both in the military, and mobilised personnel."
- "Taiwan will make itself a porcupine. A small, really sharp, nasty little thing that is just indigestible to China."
- "China will have seen how Russia, which has a land border with Ukraine, got into all sorts of trouble on launching their invasion."

## Political framing

- "China wants Taiwan to be reunified with the mainland, and it is said that no Chinese premier would be able to stay in position if they renounced their claim to Taiwan."
- "Xi Jinping is on a one-way journey - there's no status quo here."
- On the international response: "With the West focused on Ukraine, is there enough capacity in the system to handle another crisis in southeast Asia? If you were Xi Jinping, would you gamble that there is not?"

## Credits

- Dominic Nicholls (Associate Editor), Elliott Daly (Video Producer), Josh Bourne (Senior Video Editor), Telegraph Video.
- Published 07 April 2023 8:00am BST.
- Related topics listed: Xi Jinping, South China Sea, China, Taiwan, Russia-Ukraine war, Cyber attacks.

wikis.title: China's $23 trillion local government debt and the restructuring of Hegang
wikis.summary: Bloomberg feature (opening section only, rest behind a subscription wall) on China's local government debt and what the coal town of Hegang's financial restructuring signals for other indebted municipalities.
wikis.body:
## Headline claim

- Headline: "China's $23 Trillion Local Debt Mess Is About to Get Worse".
- Standfirst: "What happened in cash-strapped Hegang points to a long economic slog for the rest of the country."
- Filed under Politics / The Big Take, by Bloomberg News.

## Hegang

- "In 2021, a remote coal town in northeastern China was forced to undergo an unprecedented financial restructuring."
- Hegang is "a city with nearly a million people near the Russian border".
- It "had debt of more than double its fiscal income when it hit the headlines almost 18 months ago".
- "It was the first time a city administration had taken official emergency steps since the State Council unveiled rules in 2016 on how local governments, from counties to provinces, should deal with debt risks."
- The piece says its struggles since are "an ominous sign for President Xi Jinping as other heavily indebted municipalities look set to follow suit".

## Note

- Only the opening paragraphs were accessible; the remainder of the feature is behind Bloomberg's subscriber wall.

wikis.title: Brenner Base Tunnel delayed again, opening now 2032
wikis.summary: International Railway Journal report that BBT SE has pushed Brenner Base Tunnel completion to no earlier than 2031 and opening to 2032, and that the Tyrol and South Tyrol governors have publicly protested.
wikis.body:
## The delay

- "On May 21, Austro-Italian tunnel construction company Brenner Basis Tunnel (BBT SE), which is jointly owned by Austrian and Italian national rail infrastructure managers OeBB and RFI, revealed that completion of the tunnel is now unlikely before 2031 with opening no earlier than 2032, four years later than planned, and two years later than the previous forecast completion date of 2030."
- The tunnel links Innsbruck, Austria with Fortezza, Italy; original planned completion was 2028.
- Project figures: EUR 8.7bn, 55km Brenner Base Tunnel (BBT).

## Construction progress

- "Currently 140km of the 230km of tunnels required for the project have been built, 48km of which are main running tunnels, 52km comprise exploratory tunnels and 40km are other tunnel structures for access or logistics."
- "Several contracts for tunnelling works have yet to be awarded although progress is expected later this year."
- "BBT SE cancelled a key contract on October 27 2020 to construct the 18km section known as Lot H51 between Pfons and the border at Brenner. The contract also included around 9km of exploratory tunnelling, an emergency access adit and an underground emergency evacuation halt at St Jodok."
- That cancellation and the re-tendering "now underway" made completion in 2028 unlikely, "and this has now been confirmed."
- "Work on other sections continues and contracts for the southernmost section of upgraded line in Italy were awarded in March."

## Governors' protest

- "THE governor of Italy's South Tyrol region and his colleague in the Austrian province of Tyrol have publicly criticised the latest delay."
- The governors "have called for solutions to construction problems in order to be able to put the Brenner Base Tunnel into operation as quickly as possible" and "say they believe technical difficulties are being exacerbated by national interests in both Italy and Austria."
- Both called for "political and technical coordination between the European Union, Italy and Austria to be intensified to resolve outstanding railway engineering and procurement law issues."
- Tyrol governor Guenther Platter: "The population along the Brenner Corridor is placing great hopes in the Brenner Base Tunnel so that the quality of life can be improved... At the same time, the Brenner Corridor needs a competitive railway in order to be able to transport goods in an environmentally friendly and efficient way"
- Joint statement: "Since some of the delays, according to BBT SE, are due to the revision and harmonisation of railway equipment, we expect no more technical or national hurdles will arise in the future... The top priority (for the regions) is to use the full potential of the BBT for shifting freight and passenger traffic to rail. National thinking is absolutely out of place in this context."

## Byline

- Written by Keith Fender, May 27, 2021.

wikis.title: AMD confirms an early-2026 Steam Machine and an RDNA 5 Xbox SoC for 2027
wikis.summary: Report on AMD's Q4 earnings call guidance confirming Valve's Steam Machine ships early in 2026 and Microsoft's next-gen Xbox SoC launches in 2027, with rumoured Xbox "Magnus" specifications.
wikis.body:
## What AMD said
- "AMD posted its record fourth quarter revenue of $10.3 billion in 2025, and during the earnings call, the company issued some guidance on the upcoming product portfolio."
- Dr. Lisa Su: "For 2026, we expect semi-custom SoC annual revenue to decline by a significant double-digit percentage as we enter the seventh year of what has been a very strong console cycle. From a product standpoint, Valve is on track to begin shipping its AMD-powered Steam Machine early this year, and development of Microsoft's next-gen Xbox featuring an AMD semi-custom SoC is progressing well to support a launch in 2027."
- "While the Steam Machine specifications are confirmed, Xbox 'Magnus' SoC is still largely a collection of rumored specifications."

## The two products
- Valve's Steam Machine, AMD-powered, shipping early in 2026.
- Microsoft's next-generation Xbox, with an RDNA 5-based AMD semi-custom SoC codenamed "Magnus," for a 2027 launch.
- "Both platforms are anticipated to launch in 2027" — the next Xbox and Sony's PlayStation 6.

## Source
- AMD Earnings Call Transcript. By AleksandarK, Feb 4th 2026 05:36 (page dated Wednesday, February 4th 2026).

wikis.summary: AMD confirms Valve's AMD-powered Steam Machine is on track to begin shipping early in 2026.

wikis.title: Xbox "Magnus" SoC and the 2027 console generation
wikis.summary: Rumoured specifications for the RDNA 5-based AMD semi-custom SoC in Microsoft's next-generation Xbox, due in 2027.
wikis.body:
- AMD's custom SoC division "will deliver an RDNA 5-based SoC for the next-generation Xbox console"; Lisa Su said development "is progressing well to support a launch in 2027."
- Rumoured to be "the largest APU ever designed for a consumer console, with a 408 mm² chiplet design. Of this, 144 mm² is dedicated to the SoC built on TSMC's N3P node, while the GPU occupies 264 mm²."
- "expected to include up to 11 CPU cores—three Zen 6 and eight Zen 6c—alongside a substantial GPU setup with 68 RDNA 5 compute units, four shader engines, and at least 24 MB of L2 cache."
- "Memory might expand to 48 GB of GDDR7 on a 192-bit bus. A dedicated NPU is rumored to offer significant on-device AI performance, with reports suggesting up to 110 TOPS."
- "Microsoft aiming for top-tier performance and versatility, creating a system that blurs the line between console and gaming PC. This system will reportedly be an all-in-one console and a PC, or there will be two separate systems that Microsoft is preparing for consumers next year."
- "This is a complete opposite to Sony, who seems to be refining the PlayStation 6 with a focus on a more traditional console design. Both platforms are anticipated to launch in 2027."

wikis.title: Diablo 4 Season of Hell's Legacy adds Diablo himself; Amazon class coming in 2027

wikis.body:
## Season of Hell's Legacy

- "After more than three years, Diablo 4 is finally getting its big, bad, final boss: Diablo himself is coming to the game next week in season 15."
- The season is called Season of Hell's Legacy and "launches on September 15".
- It brings "everything full circle for the series' 30th anniversary" with Diablo plus "the other two Prime Evils, Mephisto and Baal", the "iconic friendly character, Deckard Cain, and new Legendary items inspired by the series' past".
- The season adds "familiar characters, locations, and items inspired by all eras of the APRG's history".

## Amazon class

- Blizzard announced Diablo 4's next new class, the Amazon, "a fan-favorite from Diablo 2".
- It arrives in "the first half of 2027".
- "The Amazon class wields a bow, naturally, but will also bring an entirely new weapon, the Javelin", shown in gameplay footage.

## BlizzCon context

- "Diablo was a huge focus of this year's BlizzCon 2026, mostly headlined by the announcement of Diablo 5."
- "Blizzard managed to keep the lid on Diablo 5 ahead of the event, so its reveal was quite the surprise indeed, but the studio made it very clear that it's not ready to abandon Diablo 4."
- Video referenced: "Diablo | BlizzCon 2026 | 30 Years of Hell" on YouTube.

## Page data

- News by Jordan Gerblick, published 12 September 2026. Image credit: Blizzard.

wikis.title: PlayStation 6 reportedly planned for late 2027 alongside the new Xbox
wikis.summary: GameGPU report that, on the basis of insider Kepler L2's data about AMD and NVIDIA production plans, the PlayStation 6 is being prepared for the holiday season in late 2027, in parallel with Microsoft's Xbox Helix.
wikis.body:
## The claim
- "New evidence has emerged in the tech community indicating that the next-generation PlayStation 6 home gaming console is being prepared for the holiday season in late 2027."
- "The current discussions stem from data from insider Kepler L2 regarding the production plans of chipmakers AMD and NVIDIA for the period 2027-2028."

## The chip evidence
- "The specialized AT2 graphics chip based on the microarchitecture RDNA 5 is the only major gaming-class silicon solution scheduled for mass production in 2027, while other consumer discrete graphics card lines from both developers have been postponed to 2028."
- "The AT2 GPU is directly linked to the hardware platform of Microsoft's upcoming Xbox Helix game console, the first devkits of which are expected to be available to partner studios in early 2027."
- "This cycle closely mirrors the preparations for the launch of the Xbox Series X consoles in 2020, when proprietary hardware samples began arriving to developers well in advance."

## Why both at once
- "Microsoft's desire to secure a leading position in the pre-holiday period in late 2027 is forcing Sony to adhere to a mirrored production schedule and release the PlayStation 6 in parallel, preventing the user base from shifting to a competing ecosystem."

## Prices and dates
- "Semiconductor industry analysts emphasize that the absence of official statements regarding exact retail prices or specific launch dates is the accepted standard at this stage of system design."
- "Platform holders traditionally set final price lists in dollars ($) and euros (EUR) only a few months before the devices hit store shelves, depending on contract wafer manufacturing costs and exchange rate fluctuations."
- "The simultaneous debut of ninth-generation consoles based on AMD's custom architectures will allow both corporations to offer comparable levels of base hardware performance in modern video games."

## Byline
- By Evgen Kovalov, HARDWARE section, 18 September 2026.

wikis.title: DOE splits the $3 billion LBNF/DUNE neutrino experiment into two phases
wikis.summary: Science news article on the Department of Energy's decision to build the LBNF/DUNE neutrino megaproject in two phases, the scaled-back first phase, its costs and dates, and the race with Japan's Hyper-Kamiokande.
wikis.body:
## The decision

- "Struggling with cost overruns, the Department of Energy (DOE) has decided to build the United States's next great particle physics experiment in two phases, officials told physicists this month."
- The megaproject is two intertwined efforts: the Long-Baseline Neutrino Facility (LBNF) and the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE).
- It "won't be completed to its original specs until the mid-2030s instead of late this decade", and its already ballooning cost will increase even further.
- "the adjusted plan should get a slimmed version of LBNF/DUNE running as early as 2029", researchers say.
- Jim Siegrist, DOE's associate director for high energy physics, laid the plan out by video on 16 March during the Snowmass community planning exercise. "DOE believes there is still a chance for LBNF/DUNE to come first," Siegrist wrote in an email.
- The revised plan makes clear that "the current $3 billion cost estimate - nearly twice the original - now applies to the first phase alone."
- By Adrian Cho, 29 Mar 2022, 3:30 PM ET. A version appeared in Science, Vol 376, Issue 6588. doi: 10.1126/science.abq2832.

## Scaled-back phase one

- The project will start smaller, with a detector in South Dakota containing just two of four planned argon modules, with a combined target mass of no more than 24,000 tons.
- The power of the proton beam at Fermilab will be limited to 1.2 megawatts, and the detector at the lab will be simpler.
- After completing the first phase, DOE could pursue the bigger detector and better beam in an upgrade "likely costing hundreds of millions of dollars".
- With just that first phase, LBNF/DUNE should still be capable of measuring CP violation.

## The original plan

- U.S. physicists rallied around the experiment in 2013 in the previous Snowmass; a year later DOE's Particle Physics Project Prioritization Panel (P5) named it the new flagship domestic effort.
- In 2015 DOE embraced the P5 vision: an internationally funded experiment with a liquid argon detector of target mass at least 40,000 tons, a neutrino beam powered by a multimegawatt proton beam, and a smaller detector at Fermilab to monitor the outgoing beam.
- "It would cost less than $1.9 billion and be completed by 2028, DOE estimated."
- Refurbishment and excavation at the mine have helped drive up the cost and delay progress.

## What the experiment does

- LBNF/DUNE would shoot an intense beam of muon neutrinos from Fermilab to a detector 1300 kilometers away in the abandoned Homestake gold mine in Lead, South Dakota.
- Filled with frigid liquid argon, the DUNE detector would capture collisions of neutrinos and atomic nuclei in unprecedented detail.
- It would test the theory of neutrino oscillations and search for charge-parity (CP) violation, an asymmetry between the oscillations of neutrinos and antineutrinos.

## The rival: Hyper-Kamiokande

- Physicists with Japan's Hyper-K say they'll start to take data in 2028, a year before LBNF/DUNE.
- Hyper-K will consist of a subterranean cylindrical tank 70 meters tall filled with 260,000 tons of ultrapure water, with some 40,000 phototubes; neutrinos are fired from the Japan Proton Accelerator Research Complex in Tokai, 295 kilometers to the east.
- Matthew Malek, a Hyper-K physicist at the University of Sheffield, says workers in Japan have already begun excavation and, given Japan's relatively conservative scheduling, the date is likely to hold: "At this stage, there's really no chance that DUNE will turn on before Hyper-K."
- Marvin Marshak, a DUNE physicist at the University of Minnesota, Twin Cities: "One thing I learned over the last 50-some years that I've been doing this is not to over-estimate your competition."
- Both will also search for neutrinos from supernova explosions and signs that protons can decay.

## Voices from the collaboration

- Regina Rameika, a neutrino physicist at Fermilab and co-spokesperson for the 1400-member DUNE collaboration, says physicists involved suggested the change in tack: "We are all on the same page about what comes first and what comes second."
- Ines Gil-Botella, a DUNE physicist at Spain's Center for Energy, Environmental, and Technological Research: "We need to work harder to reduce as much as possible any delays between phase one and phase two." She says DUNE's ultimate goal is to probe the three-neutrino model precisely enough to see whether it breaks down, and that Hyper-K will struggle to do so for technical reasons.
- Tao Han, a theorist at the University of Pittsburgh involved in Snowmass organizing: "We will have the community support to reach our final goal."
- Malek wonders whether the new plan is DOE's way of saying the first stage is all it will build: "When you build something in multiple stages, the odds of getting beyond the first stage are more unlikely than likely."
- Mary Bishai, a DUNE physicist at Brookhaven National Laboratory: "Jim Siegrist said 'Go to Snowmass and come back with a plan for the third and fourth detector modules.' He didn't say, 'We're done.'"

## US program in flux

- DOE has asked physicists to weigh the scientific case for the second phase in the new Snowmass process and subsequent P5 prioritization.
- Fermilab is searching for a new director after Nigel Lockyer announced in September 2021 he would step down - 3 months before DOE failed the lab in its annual performance review, citing in part the troubles with LBNF/DUNE.
- On 31 March, Siegrist, 69, will retire after 10 years leading DOE's high energy physics program.

wikis.title: Further delays to Grand Paris Express lines 15 South, 16 and 17
wikis.summary: International Railway Journal analysis of the delays Societe des Grands Projets announced on February 18 to the Grand Paris Express metro, with the revised opening schedule and Valerie Pecresse's call for a joint supervision team.
wikis.body:
## What happened

- "SOCIETE des Grands Projets (SGP), the state-owned project delivery company responsible for the late-running Grand Paris Express automated metro project, announced further delays on February 18."
- Line 15 South "will now open during the fourth quarter of 2026", with lines 16 and 17 delayed by a further six months because their automatic train operation (ATO) system is shared with Line 15 South.
- "Delivery of the first sections of lines 16 and 17 is pushed back to the second quarter of 2027."
- Valerie Pecresse, president of Ile-de-France Mobility (IdFM), described herself as "shocked" by the scale of the new delays and called for a joint technical supervision and coordination team, bringing together the French government and IdFM, to monitor SGP's work.

## Revised opening schedule by section

- Line 15 South: Noisy-Champs - Pont de Sevres, Q4 2026
- Line 15 West: Pont de Sevres - Saint-Denis-Pleyel, 2031
- Line 15 East: Saint-Denis-Pleyel - Champigny Centre, 2031
- Line 16: Saint-Denis-Pleyel - Clichy-Montfermeil, Q2 2027
- Line 16: Clichy-Montfermeil - Noisy-Champs, end 2028
- Line 17: Saint-Denis-Pleyel - Le Bourget Airport, Q2 2027
- Line 17: Le Bourget Airport - Parc des Expositions, end 2028
- Line 17: Parc des Expositions - Le Mesnil Amelot, end 2030
- Line 18: Massy Palaiseau - Christ de Saclay, Q4 2026
- Line 18: Massy Palaiseau - Orly Airport, Q4 2027
- Line 18: Christ de Saclay - Versailles Chantiers, end 2030

## IdFM's response

- IdFM points out that "despite these delays, Line 15 South was still being announced last autumn as opening at the end of 2025".
- It says "there remains a risk that it will not open before 2027", which it calls "very bad news" for the hundreds of thousands of people living or working in the inner suburbs of Paris "who have been awaiting its completion for over 15 years".
- Pecresse "has been raising the alarm over the delays... over the last few last months without being heard", IdFM says.
- Pecresse says the new supervisory team must ensure the additional delays do not push completion of Line 15 South beyond the end of 2026, and must provide "precise and transparent" information in real time to the SGP supervisory board.
- She wants future infrastructure manager RATP GI and operators ORA (Line 15 South) and Keolis (lines 16 and 17) closely involved with work underway so handover is not further delayed.
- IdFM says it would be "unacceptable" if training staff on the new line and its equipment delayed the opening schedule "as was the case with the last three stations on Line 14 to Orly Airport"; the rolling stock it financed is already being delivered by Alstom and it selected the future operators in mid-2023.
- Pecresse also wants the Ramette/Bense team to examine Line 18, where she says no project review has yet been undertaken and different technologies and suppliers are being used.

## The independent report

- The scale of the delays "was revealed in an independent report commissioned last November at the request of the IdFM president".
- Produced by Yves Ramette, a former CEO of Paris metro operator RATP, and Didier Bense, former director general of the Ile-de-France region at French National Railways (SNCF).
- It attributed the larger than expected Line 15 delays to civil engineering work behind schedule and "errors in the coordination of and integration of the different project stages and contracts".
- It highlighted the risk to lines 16 and 17 from the Line 15 delays, "as all three share a common test section".

## Operators and suppliers

- ORA is a consortium led by majority shareholder RATP Dev, partnered with Alstom and ComfortDelGro of Singapore.

## SGP's comment

- SGP board president Jean-Francois Monteils: "SGP's teams and its partners are fully mobilised to deliver this exceptional transport project in the best possible conditions."
- "These efforts enabled us to reach the essential stage of conducting the first ATO trials last year. The latter revealed new problems, which have led us to incur this additional delay, in order to guarantee an optimum level of performance."

## Byline

- Analysis, February 25, 2025, written by Robert Preston.

wikis.title: North East Link Program, Melbourne
wikis.summary: Victoria's Big Build overview of the North East Link Program, which bundles the North East Link tunnels, the M80 Ring Road completion and the Eastern Freeway Upgrades.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- "North East Link is more than just the state's longest road tunnels - we're bringing 3 big road projects together."
- Connects the Eastern Freeway to "the new 6.5km North East Link tunnels from Bulleen to Watsonia", linking Melbourne's east up to the M80 Ring Road in Greensborough, "cutting travel times by 35 minutes and taking 15,000 trucks off local roads a day".
- Community investment: "millions of dollars in upgrades to sports grounds at local schools, clubs and playing fields"; "$10 million worth of community grants" over the life of the project; "50 MCGs of new community parklands and open space across the north east".

## Builders and staging

- "In late 2021, we appointed Spark to build the North East Link tunnels from Watsonia to Bulleen", including interchanges at Lower Plenty Road and Manningham Road, new parklands, wetlands, bike and walking paths and local road improvements. "Works are in full swing with tunnelling underway."
- "In late 2023, 2 delivery teams were appointed for the overhaul of the first part of the Eastern Freeway and the completion of the M80 Ring Road."
- The Eastern Freeway Upgrades "will be delivered in 3 stages. Major works from Burke Road to Tram Road are underway."
- Designs for the remaining stages, Hoddle Street to Burke Road and Tram Road to Springvale Road, "will be on exhibition for community feedback as we bring builders on board from 2025".
- The M80 Ring Road completion "is planned to open at the same time as the North East Link tunnels from Watsonia to Bulleen and the Eastern Freeway Upgrades from Hoddle Street to Springvale Road".

The page is marked "Last updated 6 May 2026" and carries "Copyright (c) 2026, State Government of Victoria, Australia".

wikis.title: North East Link tunnels (Watsonia to Bulleen)
wikis.summary: Victoria's longest twin road tunnels, 6.5km from Watsonia to Bulleen, with new parklands and a tree-lined boulevard.
wikis.body:
- "Victoria's longest twin road tunnels will stretch 6.5km from Watsonia to Bulleen, taking cars and trucks under instead of through suburbs."
- Also creates "5 MCGs of parklands along Banyule Creek at Borlase Reserve and a new 2km tree-lined boulevard on Greensborough Road".
- Spark was appointed in late 2021 to build the tunnels, including interchanges at Lower Plenty Road and Manningham Road, new parklands, wetlands, bike and walking paths and local road improvements; "tunnelling underway".

wikis.title: M80 Ring Road Completion
wikis.summary: Completion of the M80 Ring Road at Greensborough with two new interchanges and grade-separated through traffic.
wikis.body:
- "The completed M80 Ring Road will take 19,000 cars and trucks a day off Greensborough Road with through traffic passing under Grimshaw Street, Elder Street and Watsonia Road."
- "Two new interchanges at the M80 Ring Road and Grimshaw Street will ease congestion and slash travel times, with dedicated lanes for local trips and express lanes to the North East Link tunnels."
- "More than 10km of new and upgraded walking and cycling paths and better connections to Watsonia Station and shops."
- Planned to open at the same time as the North East Link tunnels and the Eastern Freeway Upgrades from Hoddle Street to Springvale Road.

wikis.title: Eastern Freeway Upgrades
wikis.summary: Upgrade of the Eastern Freeway with express lanes, new traffic technology and Melbourne's first dedicated busway, connecting to the North East Link tunnels at Bulleen.
wikis.body:
- "We're upgrading the Eastern Freeway with new express lanes, new traffic management technology and Melbourne's first dedicated busway."
- Connects the Eastern Freeway to the new North East Link tunnels in Bulleen, "cutting travel times by 35 minutes and taking 15,000 trucks a day off local roads".
- Also builds "new and upgraded walking and cycling paths, bridges and underpasses", upgrades Koonung Creek Reserve, revitalises wetlands and waterways and plants new trees and plants.
- "A tougher noise standard and new and upgraded noise walls will also deliver better noise protection for residents."
- Delivered in 3 stages; major works from Burke Road to Tram Road are underway.

wikis.title: OpenAI API deprecations and model retirement schedule
wikis.summary: OpenAI's platform documentation page listing every API deprecation, its notice-period policy, and the shutdown dates and recommended replacements for retired models and endpoints.
wikis.body:
## What the page is

- "This page lists all API deprecations, along with recommended replacements."
- "As we launch safer and more capable models, we regularly retire older models... Impacted customers will always be notified by email and in our documentation along with blog posts for larger changes."

## Notice-period policy

- **Generally available models: at least 6 months.**
- **Specialized variants of generally available models: at least 3 months** - examples given: chat variants such as `gpt-5.1-chat-latest`, Codex variants such as `gpt-5.3-codex`, deep research variants such as `o3-deep-research`.
- **Preview models** (identified by `preview` in the name) "may be retired with much shorter notice, such as **2 weeks**" - examples `computer-use-preview`, `gpt-4o-audio-preview`. "We don't recommend using preview models for business-critical production workloads unless you can migrate on short notice."
- "If safety or compliance concerns require us to retire a model sooner, we will provide as much notice as reasonably possible."
- "In some cases, developers may be able to provision dedicated capacity for continued access after a model's shutdown date."

## Deprecation vs. legacy

- "When we announce that a model or endpoint is being deprecated, it immediately becomes deprecated. All deprecated models and endpoints will also have a shut down date."
- "We use the terms 'sunset' and 'shut down' interchangeably."
- "'Legacy' refer[s] to models and endpoints that no longer receive updates... You can expect that a legacy model or endpoint will be deprecated at some point in the future."

## Upcoming deprecations (most recent first)

- **2026-09-11: GPT-5.4-Cyber** - `gpt-5.4-cyber` removed **Oct 1, 2026**, replace with `gpt-5.6-cyber`.
- **2026-08-26: Transcription models** - `whisper-1`, `gpt-4o-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize` removed **Feb 26, 2027**, replace with `gpt-live-transcribe` or `gpt-transcribe`.
- **2026-07-20: Legacy audio, realtime and transcription models** - removal **Jan 20, 2027**.
- **2026-06-11: GPT-5 and o3 snapshots** - removal **Dec 11, 2026**.
- **2026-06-03: Reusable prompts** - `v1/prompts` API and reusable prompt objects shut down **Nov 30, 2026**.
- **2026-06-03: Evals platform** - read-only **Oct 31, 2026**, dashboard and API shut down **Nov 30, 2026**.
- **2026-06-03: Agent Builder** - shut down **Nov 30, 2026**; "ChatKit remains available."
- **2026-06-02: GPT Image models** - `gpt-image-1-mini`, `gpt-image-1.5`, `chatgpt-image-latest` removed **Dec 1, 2026**, replace with `gpt-image-2`.
- **Self-serve fine-tuning update (announced May 7, 2026)** - from **May 7, 2026** creating fine-tuning jobs or training is not available to organizations that have not previously run fine-tuning; from **July 2, 2026** not available to organizations that have not run inference on a fine-tuned model in the past 60 days; on **Jan 6, 2027** active existing customers can no longer create new fine-tuning jobs. "Inference on fine-tuned models will continue to be available until the base models are deprecated."
- **2026-04-22: Legacy GPT model snapshots** - shutdown **October 23, 2026** for `gpt-3.5-turbo-0125`, `gpt-4-0613`, `gpt-4-1106-preview`, `gpt-4-turbo`, `gpt-4.1-nano`, `gpt-4o-2024-05-13`, `gpt-image-1`, `o1`, `o1-pro`, `o3-mini`, `o4-mini`, `ft-o4-mini-2025-04-16`, plus fine-tuned versions `ft-gpt-3.5-turbo`, `ft-gpt-4`, `ft-gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14`, `ft-babbage-002`, `ft-davinci-002`. Substitutes are `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, `gpt-5.6-luna` and `gpt-image-2`.
- **2026-03-24: Sora 2 video generation models and Videos API** - removal **2026-09-24**, no replacement listed.
- **2025-09-26: Legacy GPT model snapshots** - `gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct`, `babbage-002`, `davinci-002`, `gpt-3.5-turbo-1106` shut down **2026-09-28**, replace with `gpt-5.6-terra`.

## Past deprecations listed

- **2026-05-08**: `gpt-5.2-chat-latest` and `gpt-5.3-chat-latest` - shut down **Aug 10, 2026**, replace with `gpt-5.6-sol`.
- **2026-04-22** (July 2026 shutdown): access shut down **July 23, 2026** for `computer-use-preview`, `gpt-4o-search-preview-2025-03-11`, `gpt-4o-mini-search-preview-2025-03-11`, `gpt-5-chat-latest`, `gpt-5-codex`, `gpt-5.1-chat-latest`, `gpt-5.1-codex`, `gpt-5.1-codex-max`, `gpt-5.1-codex-mini`, `gpt-5.2-codex`, `gpt-audio-mini-2025-10-06`, `gpt-realtime-mini-2025-10-06`, `o3-deep-research`, `o4-mini-deep-research`.
- **2025-11-18**: `chatgpt-4o-latest` removed **2026-02-17**, replace with `gpt-5.1-chat-latest`.
- **2025-11-17**: `codex-mini-latest` removed **2026-02-12**, replace with `gpt-5-codex-mini`; the legacy local shell tool is no longer supported.
- **2025-11-14**: `dall-e-2` and `dall-e-3` removed **2026-05-12**.
- **2025-09-26** (March 2026 shutdown): `gpt-4-0314`, `gpt-4-1106-preview`, `gpt-4-0125-preview` shut down **2026-03-26**.
- **2025-09-15**: Realtime API Beta (`OpenAI-Beta: realtime=v1`) removed **2026-05-12**; `gpt-4o-realtime-preview` and `gpt-4o-audio-preview` families removed **2026-05-07**.
- **2025-08-20**: **Assistants API** shut down **2026-08-26**, "one year later" than the August 26th, 2025 notice; replace with the **Responses API and Conversations API**.
- **2025-06-10**: `gpt-4o-realtime-preview-2024-10-01` and `gpt-4o-audio-preview-2024-10-01` removed **2025-10-10**.
- **2025-04-28**: `text-moderation-007/stable/latest` removed **2025-10-27** (replace with `omni-moderation`); `o1-preview` removed **2025-07-28** (replace with `o3`), `o1-mini` removed **2025-10-27** (replace with `o4-mini`).
- **2025-04-14**: `gpt-4.5-preview` removed **2025-07-14**, replace with `gpt-4.1`.
- **2024-10-02**: Assistants API beta v1 (`OpenAI-Beta: assistants=v1`) discontinued **December 18, 2024**.
- **2024-08-29**: new fine-tuning training on `babbage-002` and `davinci-002` ended **October 28, 2024**.
- **2024-06-06**: `gpt-4-32k` family (**$60.00 / 1M input tokens + $120 / 1M output tokens**) shut down **2025-06-06**; `gpt-4-vision-preview` and `gpt-4-1106-vision-preview` (**$10.00 / 1M input + $30 / 1M output**) shut down **2024-12-06**; replacement `gpt-4o`.
- **2023-11-06**: `gpt-3.5-turbo-0613` (**$1.50 / 1M input + $2.00 / 1M output**) and `gpt-3.5-turbo-16k-0613` (**$3.00 / 1M input + $4.00 / 1M output**) shut down **2024-09-13**.
- **2023-08-22**: the `/v1/fine-tunes` API shut down **January 04, 2024**, replaced by `/v1/fine_tuning/jobs`.
- **2023-07-06**: InstructGPT models, base GPT models, edit models and first-generation text embedding models shut down **January 04, 2024**.
- **2023-06-13**: `gpt-4-0314` (**$30.00 / 1M input + $60.00 / 1M output**) legacy "at earliest 2024-06-13"; `gpt-3.5-turbo-0301` shut down **2024-09-13**; `gpt-4-32k-0314` shut down **2025-06-06**.
- **2023-03-20**: Codex models `code-davinci-002/001`, `code-cushman-002/001` shut down **2023-03-23**.
- **2022-06-03**: legacy endpoints `/v1/engines`, `/v1/search`, `/v1/classifications`, `/v1/answers` shut down **2022-12-03**.

wikis.title: First section of Lima metro Line 2 opens
wikis.summary: International Railway Journal report on the opening of Stage 1A of Lima metro Line 2, its first-week ridership, the wider project's cost and concession, and tunnelling progress on later stages.
wikis.body:
## Opening and first week

- The Lima and Callao Urban Transport Authority (ATU) reports that the first week of operations saw over 93,000 passengers travel on the first section of Lima metro Line 2, running underground for 5km from Mercado Santa Anita to Evitamiento.
- Trial operations began after the official opening of Stage 1A on December 21 by the president of Peru, Ms Dina Boluarte, with minister for transport and communications Mr Raúl Pérez Reyes.
- Travel is free during the 90-day period of trial operations; passengers must pay Soles 7.50 ($US 2) for a rechargeable card, usable also on Line 1 and other public transport in the capital, to be loaded with tickets when revenue services commence.
- Stage 1A has three intermediate stations: Óvalo Santa Anita, Colectora Industrial and Hermilio Valdizán. End-to-end journey time is 7 minutes, compared with 30 minutes by bus.

## The full line

- When completed, Line 2 will run 27km from the district of Ate Vitarte east of the city centre to the port of Callao in the west.
- It is expected to carry 644,000 passengers per day, with an end-to-end journey time of 45 minutes.
- "The first section of Line 2 was originally expected to open in 2017 with the remaining three sections completed by 2021."

## Concession and equipment

- The Consorzio Metro Linea 2 consortium — ACS Dragados and FCC (Spain), Salini Impreglio (Italy), Hitachi Rail Italy, Ansaldo STS and Cosapi (Peru) — was awarded a 35-year PPP concession to finance, build, operate and maintain Line 2 in 2014.
- The consortium has provided $US 1.2bn in financing for the $US 5.8bn project.
- Hitachi has supplied 42 six-car articulated trains, each accommodating up to 1168 passengers including 168 seated.
- Line 2 is electrified at 1.5kV dc overhead; Siemens was awarded the electrification contract in 2016.

## Tunnelling progress

- The Ministry of Transport and Communications announced on January 8 that 4km of tunnel has been completed on Stage 1B from San Juan de Dios station, west of Evitamiento, as far as Cangallo.
- The latest TBM drive, at 16m per day, was the 902m section from 28 de Julio to Cangallo, built of 531 rings formed of 3717 tunnel lining segments.
- The TBM will proceed to Manco Cápac and conclude Stage 1B tunnelling at Parque Murillo, followed by a drive on Stage 2 to Insurgentes, where the second TBM has so far completed 4km of tunnel towards Puerto del Callao.

## Quotes

- Boluarte: "This project has been stuck for 11 years, but when there is a political decision, it can be unblocked and move forward."
- Boluarte: "Four months ago we announced the start of trial operations and we are fulfilling that promise. This government is one of deeds and not words."

## Article details

- Written by Robert Preston; dated January 22, 2024.

wikis.title: Brisbane Stadium, the planned Victoria Park main stadium for the 2032 Olympics
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the planned 63,000-seat Brisbane Stadium at Victoria Park: its cost and timeline, the scrapped Gabba options, the proposals reviewed, pre-construction steps, opposition and legal challenges, and post-Olympic tenants.
wikis.body:
## Key facts

- "Brisbane Stadium is a planned multi-purpose stadium to be built in Victoria Park, in the Brisbane suburb of Herston." Described as a "Proposed stadium in Brisbane, Australia".
- Location: Victoria Park, Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. Coordinates 27 deg 27'1"S 153 deg 1'12"E.
- Capacity: 63,000 (seated).
- Groundbreaking: "June 2026 (expected)". Opened: "2031/2032 (expected)".
- Cost: "A$3.785 billion (estimated)".
- Architects: Cox Architecture, Hassell, Azusa Sekkei. Structural engineers: Arup, Schlaich Bergermann Partner.
- Tenants listed: AFL - Brisbane Lions (2033); Cricket - Queensland Bulls (2033), Brisbane Heat (2033).

## Role at the Games

- "It will serve as the main stadium for the 2032 Summer Olympic and Paralympic Games."
- "The 63,000-seat stadium is expected to host the opening and closing ceremonies, as well as the athletics events during the games."
- Afterwards "it will replace the Gabba as Brisbane's main Australian rules football and cricket stadium".
- "The stadium development is part of the 2032 Delivery Plan, announced to the public on 25 March 2025 by the Crisafulli government. It falls within the A$7.1 billion funding envelope set aside for 2032 Games infrastructure."
- "The planned location of the stadium has drawn opposition groups and has ongoing legal challenges."

## Location and site history

- Victoria Park is "a heritage listed park located in Herston and Spring Hill, north of the Brisbane central business district". "Multiple locations within the park were looked at and a site near to Gilchrist Avenue was identified."
- "Victoria Park was traditionally a meeting and gathering place for Indigenous groups travelling through the area." It has hosted a migrant workers' camp, a shanty town and a medical precinct; "The park was named Victoria Park in 1875."
- During World War II the site was partially occupied by United States forces, with many military buildings; "After the war and until the late 70s the buildings were used as temporary accommodation."
- The site "had been long neglected for future development, as factors such as swampy grounds, unexploded ammunition from World War II, and previously used rubbish dumping grounds have posed safety risks and budget blow outs".
- "Part of the park was converted into a golf course in 1931, but Brisbane City Council developed plans in 2020 to convert the 64 hectare site back into a park."

wikis.title: Cancelled Gabba reconstruction
wikis.summary: How the A$1 billion Gabba rebuild grew to A$2.7 billion and was scrapped in March 2024 in favour of Lang Park and QSAC, and the political fallout.
wikis.body:
- "On 24 February 2021, the Future Host Commission of the International Olympic Committee selected Brisbane as its preferred candidate to host the 2032 Summer Olympics and Paralympics; Brisbane were officially awarded the Games on 21 July."
- "In April 2021... the state of Queensland announced plans for a A$1 billion reconstruction of the Gabba to serve as the main stadium. The reconstruction would expand its seating capacity to 50,000, and feature a new pedestrian plaza."
- Scrutiny grew after Victoria withdrew from hosting the 2026 Commonwealth Games over cost concerns; "by February 2023, the projected cost had grown to A$2.7 billion", with Brisbane City Council, the Brisbane Lions and Cricket Australia expected to cover two thirds of the cost - the "final straw".
- "In March 2024, following an independent review launched by Queensland Premier Steven Miles and led by former Lord Mayor Graham Quirk, the Gabba project was scrapped in favour of refurbishing Lang Park and Queensland Sport and Athletics Centre (QSAC) to host the ceremonies and athletics respectively."
- "A new stadium at Victoria Park was recommended by Quirk before being dismissed by the government due to its A$3.4 billion cost"; Miles wanted a "low-cost" games and could not justify a high-cost stadium "when Queenslanders are struggling with housing and other costs".
- In August 2024 the Brisbane Design Alliance proposed "Northshore Vision 2050" at Hamilton, whose first stage was a sports and entertainment district anchored by a new 60,000-seat stadium, budgeted at A$6 billion and claimed to be privately funded; Miles said there was "no chance" a stadium could be built solely through private funding.
- In September 2024 former Premier of Western Australia Colin Barnett suggested on 4BC that Queensland build a copy of Perth Stadium.
- Many Queenslanders criticised "embarrassing" and "cheapskate" approaches. During the 2024 Queensland state election campaign, Liberal National leader David Crisafulli promised another independent review, said Queenslanders felt "embarrassed" by the QSAC decision (which "would have been the smallest Olympic athletics venue since 1928"), and said the government had "locked themselves into a facility that does neither a long-term legacy nor create a world-class buzz."
- "Crisafulli promised to not build a new stadium (and especially to not build one in Victoria Park)". "In October 2024, the Liberal National Party was elected as the state government, and Crisafulli launched a 100-day independent review."

wikis.title: Stadium proposals submitted to the second review
wikis.summary: The four proposals put to the 100-day review: Arcadis at Victoria Park, IHAL's Gabba rebuild, Richard Kirk's 'Gabba West', and WilkinsonEyre's Mayne Yard stadium.
wikis.body:
- **Arcadis**: a new stadium and indoor arena at Victoria Park plus an aquatic centre on the site of the Centenary Pool Complex, budgeted at A$5.4 billion, "which the firm argued was A$200 million cheaper than the combined costs of building the Brisbane Live arena in its current state, and renovating the Gabba, Lang Park, and QSAC". Their proposal emphasised that discussions had centred on the "cost" of the games rather than long-term "value". "The idea of a stadium at Victoria Park was backed by organising committee president Andrew Liveris."
- **IHAL Architects**: a reconstruction of the Gabba with 55,000-seat capacity, a new pedestrian plaza bordering the Riverside Expressway and linking a footpath to the Goodwill Bridge, and Brisbane Live built opposite. The firm called it the most "logical" and "cheapest" option, and one that would not "[take] over a park that's so incredible and pristine."
- **Richard Kirk Architect**: a new 60,000-seat stadium dubbed "Gabba West" above Woolloongabba railway station, across the street from the existing Gabba ("Gabba East"), which would be a practice and support facility during the Games then demolished and redeveloped. Kirk argued for minimal disruption and no relocation of tenants or nearby buildings such as East Brisbane State School; he proposed "40% of the stadium's structure be constructed using renewable materials, and that it be the largest timber-braced stadium in the world", and said it could achieve a six-star Green Star rating unlike the Victoria Park proposals.
- **WilkinsonEyre**: a new 60,000-seat stadium on the Mayne Yard, a rail yard operated by Queensland Rail, requiring relocation of the yard. Modelled after Perth Stadium, with a warm-up track under the spaghetti junction, a temporary indoor arena similar to the Basketball Arena used at the 2012 Summer Olympics in London, and a residential area. "This project was considered to be more costly (expected to be A$6 billion) and logistically challenging". Former Premier Campbell Newman supported it, arguing the Victoria Park plan "would lead to a major loss of green space in the city centre".

wikis.title: The Victoria Park stadium decision, 25 March 2025
wikis.summary: Crisafulli's announcement of a 63,000-seat stadium at Victoria Park, its estimated A$3.785 billion cost, the green-space figures and his apology for breaking a campaign promise.
wikis.body:
- "On 25 March 2025, Premier Crisafulli announced that as a result of the review, a new 63,000-seat stadium would be constructed at Victoria Park to host the ceremonies and athletics."
- "After the conclusion of the Games, the Gabba will be demolished and its site will be redeveloped as a residential neighbourhood; the Olympic stadium will succeed it as Brisbane's main football and cricket stadium."
- "According to the review, the stadium will cost an estimated $3.785 billion, although this figure is yet to be publicly confirmed."
- Designer Michael Rayner said the outcome was similar to a proposal he mentioned in a 2019 lecture, a cluster of major venues that would be "as great a hallmark of Brisbane as Melbourne Park is to Melbourne". He had thought the stadium, Brisbane Live and the pool would take less than a third of Victoria Park, leaving "some 30 hectares or so for the public, about twice the area of Sydney's Hyde Park"; with Brisbane Live to be built elsewhere he thought the stadium and pool would take "only... around 20% of the 64-hectare park".
- "The 100-day review noted that 68% (47.02 hectares) of the total area of the park would be retained as green space, with the stadium itself taking up less than 10% of the area."
- Crisafulli apologised for breaking his campaign promise not to build a new stadium, saying the Gabba was poorly maintained and approaching the end of its useful life, that the new stadium would provide a stronger legacy, and that "any other choice would have meant placing the government's interests ahead of the interests of Queensland".

wikis.title: Pre-construction steps
wikis.summary: Arup's masterplan appointment, geotechnical work, the architect shortlist and selection, the site confirmation and land transfer, contractor finalists and the rejected trademark.
wikis.body:
- September 2025: "the Queensland Government appointed Arup Group to be the contractor for the masterplan, including the stadium, National Aquatic Centre, Olympic Village, and surrounding public and green spaces after previously opening an expression of interest earlier in the month".
- "On 15 October 2025, geotechnical investigation began on Victoria Park. The GIICA also affirmed that it was working closely with Brisbane City Council to plan appropriate drilling locations, and consulted local aboriginal parties on undertaking duty of care obligations during the process."
- December 2025: The Courier-Mail reported four architects shortlisted - Populous, Herzog & de Meuron / Architectus, Gerkan, Marg and Partners / Blight Rayner Architecture, and Warren and Mahoney.
- "On 5 January 2026, it was announced that the Japanese-Australian design consortium involving Cox Architecture, Hassell and Azusa Sekkei had been selected to be the architects for the stadium." Cox and Hassell were previously architects for Perth Stadium and involved in redevelopments of the Adelaide Oval and the Melbourne Cricket Ground; Azusa Sekkei previously constructed the Japan National Stadium, built for the 2020 Summer Olympics and Paralympics.
- "On 24 March 2026, it was announced that early works was to occur once the land the stadium will be built on is transferred to the Games Independent Infrastructure and Coordination Authority (GIICA) on 1 June. The Queensland Government also confirmed the stadium will be located in a 'central position' near Gilchrist Avenue, within proximity to existing transport infrastructure."
- "On 9 April 2026, the GIICA announced that two joint ventures had been selected as finalists to be contractors for the construction of the stadium, those being BESIX Watpac-John Holland Group and Built Australia-Sacyr."
- "In September 2026, an attempt to trademark the name 'Brisbane Stadium' was rejected by IP Australia for being too descriptive and not distinctive."

wikis.title: Opposition and legal challenges
wikis.summary: Save Victoria Park's campaign, the heritage listing overridden by state legislation, Turrbal cultural significance and two federal heritage challenges.
wikis.body:
- "The construction of a stadium in Victoria Park is opposed by community group Save Victoria Park." They argue it "would remove one Brisbane's few inner-city green areas and that the park has the potential to become as valuable a public space as Federation Square, Melbourne and Sydney Park".
- "The group successfully supported the expansion of heritage protection over the entire park in 2025; however this listing was ineffective at protecting the park following the passage of state legislation exempting the stadium from existing state planning, heritage and environmental laws."
- Queensland Deputy Premier Jarrod Bleijie: "Save Victoria Park are just a bunch of NIMBYs who don't want anything to happen. This park ... was a golf course. Before it was a golf course, it was a dump for goodness sake."
- "The site of the stadium holds cultural significance to the Turrbal people. The park was a native camping ground and food-gathering place and hosted the corroboree, which is the traditional dance for First Nations people."
- Historian Ray Kerkhove, who conducted multiple heritage assessments for different levels of government, "stated that the site is probably the most significant site of Indigenous heritage in central Brisbane and that it would be destroyed by the stadium".
- Yagarabul Elder Gaja Kerry Charlton said "there are ancient trees, artefacts and very important eco-systems existing there... [and that] there may be ancestral remains".
- "These concerns have formed the basis of two legal challenges to the stadium's construction under section 10 of the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Heritage Protection Act (Cth)." The legislation lets the federal environment minister declare protection where satisfied "the area is a significant Aboriginal area".
- "Minister Murray Watt stated that he had received 5 applications, one of which was withdrawn and another in relation to drilling in the proposed site, which he rejected. Watt appointed an independent facilitator to mediate in the matter to allow cultural sites to be respected and construction to incorporate heritage and assist him in making a decision on the other three applications."

wikis.title: Post-Olympic use
wikis.summary: The tenants inheriting the stadium and Cricket Australia's allocation of the first 2033-34 Ashes test.
wikis.body:
- "Following the Olympics, the new stadium will inherit the Gabba's current tenants, including the Brisbane Lions of the Australian Football League, the Queensland Bulls in domestic cricket, and the Brisbane Heat of the Big Bash League and Women's Big Bash League."
- "On 26 March 2025, Cricket Australia announced that the first test of the 2033-34 Ashes series would be held at the new stadium, as one of its first major sporting events following the Olympics and Paralympics. As part of this agreement, the Gabba will host Australia test matches annually from 2027-28 to 2031-32 as part of the lead-up to the Olympics."

wikis.title: Transport to the site
wikis.summary: Busway, rail, a planned new station and motorway access around the proposed stadium.
wikis.body:
- "Transport around the proposed area of the stadium includes the nearby QUT Kelvin Grove busway station, situated on the Northern Busway, connecting the site directly to CBD, as well as access to the newly opened Brisbane Metro."
- Nearby railway stations: Exhibition (adjacent to Brisbane Showgrounds), Fortitude Valley, Roma Street and Bowen Hills. "These stations provide access to all six of Queensland Rail's railway lines."
- "There are also plans for a new railway station closer to the stadium, which would be built on the Exhibition Loop and on Cross River Rail, immediately north of the tunnel portal."
- "The Inner City Bypass, completed in 2002, allows easy access to South East Queensland's motorway network, connecting drivers beyond the Sunshine Coast on the Bruce Highway and south towards the Gold Coast on the Pacific Motorway."

wikis.title: Grand Egyptian Museum opening date set for 1 November
wikis.summary: Ahram Online report that President El-Sisi directed the Grand Egyptian Museum's opening be set for 1 November after the 3 July opening was postponed.
wikis.body:
## The decision

- "President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi has directed setting of the opening date of the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM) for 1 November."
- In a cabinet meeting on Wednesday, Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly "directed all ministries and relevant bodies to complete all arrangements to ensure the full readiness of the GEM for its grand opening on the set date".

## Earlier postponement

- "The GEM's grand opening was slated for 3 July, but the government postponed the event on 21 June after the outbreak of war between Israel and Iran."

## What officials said

- Madbouly "emphasized that the GEM's opening would be an exceptional international event to be added to a rich series of distinguished national events linked to modern Egyptian history".
- The museum "represents a global cultural, civilizational, and touristic landmark that highlights the greatness of Egyptian heritage across its various eras".

## The museum

- Built on 500,000 square metres.
- Trapezoidal architectural design with "distinguished external walls"; offers "an enormous panoramic view of the Giza Plateau".
- Houses objects from ancient Egypt "spanning from prehistory to the early Roman period".
- Displays will include "the unique treasures of the boy king Tutankhamun, some of which will see the light of day for the first time".

## Byline

- Ahram Online, Wednesday 6 Aug 2025. Headline marked UPDATED.

wikis.title: CDG Express departures and timetables
wikis.summary: Operator page giving the CDG Express train timetable, frequency, platforms and ticket validity rules between Paris Gare de l'Est and Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport.
wikis.body:
## Service at a glance

- "one train every 15 minutes, from 5 am to midnight, 7 days a week, both ways".
- "Trains leave every 15 minutes, every day, from 5 am to midnight."
- A train is ready at the platform 15 minutes before departure.
- Tickets can be used at the traveller's convenience; no booking required - "buy your ticket and take any CDG Express train".

## From Gare de l'Est to Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport

- When: 5.08 am - 12.08 am.
- How often: Every 15 minutes, 365 days a year.
- Where: Gare de l'Est - Platforms 2, 3 and 4.
- Listed departures/arrivals: 05:08/05:28, 05:23/05:43, 05:38/05:58, 05:53/06:13, 06:08/06:28, 06:23/06:43, 06:38/06:58, 06:53/07:13, 07:08/07:28.
- Timetable PDF: 185.2 Ko.

## From Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport to Gare de l'Est

- When: 5.01 am - 12.01 am.
- How often: Every 15 minutes, 365 days a year.
- Where: CDG2 TGV station - Platforms 1X and 2X.
- Listed departures/arrivals: 05:01/05:21, 05:16/05:46, 05:31/05:51, 05:56/06:16, 06:01/06:21, 06:26/06:46, 06:31/06:51, 06:56/07:16, 07:01/07:21.

## Good to know

- Trains run on a dedicated track and leave at fixed times, every 15 minutes, every day of the year, in both directions.
- Trains run at regular intervals from early morning to midnight, including off-peak times, public holidays, weekends and school holidays.
- Screens in the stations display the next departures and arrivals.

## Journey times quoted from Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport

- Eiffel Tower: 40 minutes.
- La Defense: 35 minutes.
- Montmartre - Sacre Coeur: 30 minutes.
- The Louvre: 45 minutes.

## Tickets (FAQ)

- Number of stops: "None." The CDG Express provides a non-stop service between Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport and Gare de l'Est.
- A return ticket can be bought without a fixed return date, as long as the inbound ticket is used within 90 days of using the outbound ticket.
- One-way tickets are valid for 24 months after purchase; on a return ticket the outbound ticket is also valid for 24 months.
