wikis.title: Apple Watch Ultra 4 expectations ahead of Apple's 9 September 2026 event
wikis.summary: the5krunner's pre-event predictions for the Apple Watch Ultra 4 - design, chip, sensors, GNSS, battery and price - plus an added update scoring those predictions against Apple's confirmed Ultra 4.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- Post by the5krunner, 7 September 2026, "Last Updated on 9 September 2026".
- The author's headline prediction: "I expect three things from Wednesday: a new AI Siri co-processor, a meaninglessly brighter AMOLED, and one solitary hour of extra battery life."
- "Apple has confirmed the September 9 event."

## Update added 9 September 2026 - how the predictions scored

- "Apple has now confirmed the Ultra 4."
- Design: correct. "Same 49mm case, same display, no redesign."
- S11 chip: correct, new chip confirmed.
- Battery: "better than predicted. I called 15 to 17 hours of GPS recording; Apple confirmed 18 hours, which is the first time the Ultra clears a full Ironman without Low Power Mode."
- No new GNSS chip: correct, "and Apple actually removed GLONASS from the constellation list, which on testing improves accuracy rather than reducing it. GLONASS is the least accurate of the major constellations."
- Touch ID: correct, not this year.
- Optical HR sensor: "the new Health Sensing System on Series 12 is a significant hardware change"; "Ultra 4's sensor position relative to Ultra 3 has not yet been tested."
- Price: correct, $799 unchanged.

## What's overdue but not broken (per the post)

- Optical HR sensor: 5 years old, no accuracy complaints.
- Accelerometer and gyroscope: 5 years at current tier, since Series 7, no accuracy complaints.
- Chip architecture: 3 years on the same Sawtooth cores, "longer than any prior generation", no performance complaints.
- GNSS chip: 2021 Broadcom part, no successor, "still competitive with Garmin's best dual-frequency watches on accuracy testing".
- Ultra case: same dimensions for 3 straight generations, no durability complaints.
- "The chip refresh happens because Apple always ships a new chip. The rest stays because it works."

wikis.title: Ultra 4 design: no overhaul expected
wikis.summary: Why the post expects the Ultra 4 case and display to carry over from the Ultra 3, with only a brightness bump.
wikis.body:
- "Ultra 3 already got its refresh last year: thinner bezels, a larger display area, and the move to LTPO3. Don't expect the exterior to change."
- Gurman/Bloomberg: "no major overhaul this cycle, bigger redesign pushed to 2027 or later."
- "Ultra's footprint has held at 49mm by 44mm across three straight generations."
- "Apple's current spec page lists the depth as 12mm, down from the 14.4mm figure quoted at launch and still shown on most spec trackers, suggesting a remeasurement rather than an actual hardware change."
- Expect the same titanium case, flat display, Digital Crown and Action Button.
- Display: LTPO3 arrived with Ultra 3 last year and "every current report has Ultra 4 keeping the same panel generation". "MicroLED remains cancelled or delayed well past 2026."
- "The one plausible display change is a brightness bump, with current reporting pointing to somewhere around 3,200 to 3,500 nits, up from 3,000."

wikis.title: Chip: an S11 expected, gains in on-device AI
wikis.summary: The post's case that Ultra 4 gets a new chip number after the longest unchanged run of any Apple Watch chip generation.
wikis.body:
- "This year's chip should be an S11, Apple's next number after skipping a refresh on Series 11 and Ultra 3."
- "Series 9 and Series 10 both used Sawtooth cores derived from the A16 Bionic, the same core generation rather than literally the same chip."
- "Ultra 3 and Series 11 repeated the S10 chip in 2025, the second straight year on that chip after Series 10 introduced it in 2024, and the third straight year on the underlying Sawtooth core architecture counting S9 in 2023."
- "That's the longest unchanged run of any Apple Watch chip generation."
- "A new chip name for Ultra 4 is close to certain."
- "Expect the real gain in on-device AI processing for Siri and health-data analysis, not raw speed."

wikis.title: Optical HR sensor: accuracy, not new metrics
wikis.summary: Why a refreshed optical heart-rate sensor would improve accuracy rather than add measurements.
wikis.body:
- "A new Apple OHR sensor is unlikely to sense any new metric (other than EDA/stress)."
- "Rumours of live blood pressure readings or non-invasive blood glucose rank as highly as the discovery that fairies are real."
- Better HR/HRV precision "could lead to more acute BP trend info and proper overnight HRV averages for 'recovery'".
- "Unchanged since Series 6 in 2020, five years and six chip generations" - "the longest-standing unrefreshed component on the watch".
- "Reviews across that period rate Apple's HR accuracy as competitive during sustained effort."
- "Expect better accuracy and lower power draw if it's refreshed."
- "Apple has used most optical HR refreshes to improve accuracy rather than add a new measurement type, though the Series 6 refresh was the exception, adding blood oxygen monitoring."

wikis.title: Touch ID: not this year
wikis.summary: The post treats a Touch ID sensor on the Ultra 4 as close to settled against.
wikis.body:
- "Gurman's reporting has been consistent enough here to treat it as close to settled."
- "Gurman has downplayed this repeatedly."
- "A side-button or Digital Crown biometric sensor is a bigger mechanical change than a design-stable year supports."
- "Expect it to be held back again."

wikis.title: GNSS chipset: no new chip, and no tri-band
wikis.summary: The supplier evidence behind the prediction that Ultra 4 keeps Broadcom's 2021 dual-frequency GNSS part, and what an in-house chip would save.
wikis.body:
- "Apple's GNSS silicon comes from Broadcom, not an in-house design."
- "Broadcom's last publicly announced dual-frequency wearable chip is the BCM4778, launched in September 2021." "Nothing in Broadcom's current wearable lineup matches tri-band."
- If Apple ever moves to tri-band "it would mean switching away from Broadcom to an already-released chipset from a generic GNSS supplier such as Airoha".
- "Huawei's Watch GT Runner 2 already ships tri-frequency GNSS on an in-house chip."
- "New firmware-level GNSS behaviour, the kind Garmin's Fenix 9 investigation uncovered, wouldn't prove new silicon on its own."
- On an in-house GNSS chip: Apple has insourced the W-series wireless chip, the U-series UWB chip and the C1 modem replacing Qualcomm in the iPhone; "No leak or filing currently claims this for Ultra 4."
- Power maths: "Broadcom's BCM4778 draws 4mW on L1 alone, 6mW with L1 and L5 both active." Against Ultra 3's 2.313 Wh battery and its 14-hour full-precision workout rating, "that's roughly 3.6% of total system power"; halving it "saves under 2% of total draw, worth adding roughly 15 minutes of per-second GNSS recording".
- "Display, optical HR and the processor account for the overwhelming majority of the draw, which is why Low Power Mode trades those down rather than touching GNSS."

wikis.title: Battery: a modest gain predicted
wikis.summary: The post's battery prediction of 15 to 17 hours of GNSS recording and its warning about circulating standby-time figures.
wikis.body:
- "I'd hope for 15 hours of proper GNSS recording."
- "Watch Ultra 3: Existing 14 hours of continuous GNSS-and-HR workout recording at full precision. At best, expect Ultra 4 to hit 15 to 17 hours, thanks to chip efficiency, display gains, and a refreshed optical HR sensor."
- "Ignore the 48 to 72-hour figures circulating in unnamed-source leaks. Those describe smartwatch standby time, not workout recording."
- "Even at 17 hours, a watch branded Ultra falls short of what some ultra-distance races demand, often past 24 hours of continuous GPS tracking. Battery dgradation is also a factor to consider."
- "Any real battery gain has to come from S11-generation efficiency across the whole chip package, not the GPS chip specifically."
- (The later update records that "Apple confirmed 18 hours".)

wikis.title: Price and release
wikis.summary: The predicted $799 price and a late-September shipping window.
wikis.body:
- "Shipping is likely towards the latter half of September."
- "No credible source has the Ultra rising above $799 for a fourth generation."
- "Apple has confirmed the September 9 event."
- (The later update records the price prediction as "correct, $799 unchanged".)

wikis.title: watchOS 27 sport and health features
wikis.summary: The software features the post says watchOS 27 already delivered, plus rumoured additions.
wikis.body:
- "Beyond carrying that software forward, expect little new for sport from the Ultra 4 hardware itself."
- On-watch Workout Buddy, no iPhone required nearby.
- More accurate treadmill distance tracking through improved motion algorithms.
- Expanded coaching insights tied to pace, distance and duration.
- "Also rumoured are a RECOVERY app and improved strength training features."

wikis.title: Mac mini announcement as Tim Cook's last Apple product
wikis.summary: MacRumors article reporting that the new Mac mini, unveiled alongside a new Mac Studio, is likely the final product announced under Tim Cook before John Ternus becomes Apple CEO on September 1.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- "Apple's latest Mac mini was just unveiled alongside a new Mac Studio, and outgoing CEO Tim Cook announced it on social media the way he has announced probably hundreds of other Apple products before it."
- Cook posted on X (Twitter): "The new Mac mini is here. Small in size. Big on performance. From everyday productivity to all things AI, it can help you do it all." - @tim_cook, August 25, 2026.
- The Mac mini refresh was "officially announced in a press release, and without a keynote or a stage", and "asks customers to bring their own display and peripherals."

## The CEO handover

- "Cook hands the reins to incoming CEO John Ternus on September 1, and Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports that the Mac mini will probably be the final new product to debut under Cook's watch."
- "Everything rumored to be in the pipeline behind it - from new iPhone 18 Pro models to the company's first foldable (aka 'iPhone Ultra') - will become Ternus's to unveil."
- "Apple's fall iPhone event this year is expected to take place on September 9."
- "15 years ago this week, Cook took over from Steve Jobs and inherited a company defined by the iPhone and iPad."
- Cook "will remain at Apple as executive chairman, where he will engage with policymakers and help Apple navigate mounting regulatory pressure."

## Product calendar entries on the page

- Mac mini - "Pre-Order Now, Launches Sep 22" - "M6 and M5 Pro chip options, N1 networking chip, and more."
- Mac Studio - "Pre-Order Now, Launches Sep 22" - "M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips with up to 512GB of memory".

## Byline

- Tuesday August 25, 2026 8:39 am PDT by Tim Hardwick.

wikis.title: Samsung begins official rollout of One UI 9
wikis.summary: Samsung press release announcing that the One UI 9 rollout begins September 16, 2026 with the Galaxy S26, S26+ and S26 Ultra, and setting out its new capture, AI, support, security and privacy features.
wikis.body:
## Rollout

- "Samsung Electronics today announced the expansion of One UI 9 to more Galaxy devices, with the rollout beginning today starting with the Galaxy S26, S26+, and S26 Ultra."
- Subheadline: "Rollout starts today, Sept. 16, starting with the Galaxy S26, S26+, and S26 Ultra".
- "Following its debut on Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Fold8, and Flip8, One UI 9 brings an easier, more seamless mobile experience across form factors, as well as enhanced Galaxy AI that is richer, more personal, and more helpful."
- Footnote: "As of the publication of this press release, the official One UI 9 has been rolled out to Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Galaxy Z Fold8, and Galaxy Z Flip8. The update is expected to gradually roll out to other Galaxy devices."
- Dateline: Korea on September 16, 2026.

## What is new

- Capture, personalize and manage: My FanCam; Generative and Editable Cards on Now Brief; Warranty and Care.
- Do more with less effort: Now Nudge; Creative Studio; Interpreter; Document Scan; Voice Recorder.
- Security and privacy: Security Brief; Privacy Alerts; Scam Detection.

## Related press releases listed

- "Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Fold8 and Flip8: Foldables, Perfected for Every Way of Living" — July 22, 2026.
- "Samsung Launches One UI 9 Beta for Galaxy S26 Series Users" — May 12, 2026.
- "Samsung's One UI 8.5 Official Rollout Starts May 6" — May 6, 2026.
- "Samsung Galaxy S26 FE: Delivering the Latest Flagship Experience, Focused on What Matters Most" — August 27, 2026.

wikis.title: My FanCam
wikis.summary: One UI 9 video feature that tracks and keeps a selected person centred in recorded video.
wikis.body:
- "My FanCam automatically tracks a selected person in a recorded video and keeps them centered, intelligently reframing the footage as the scene moves."
- "This allows users to turn dynamic moments into social-ready content with less manual editing." Examples given: "a child's performance, a friend on the dance floor, or an exciting moment during a sporting event".
- Footnote: "My FanCam feature requires a Samsung Account login. Availability may vary by video. Not supported if there is no subject to track. Accuracy of results is not guaranteed."

wikis.title: Generative and Editable Cards on Now Brief
wikis.summary: New One UI 9 cards that let users choose what appears in their daily Now Brief summaries.
wikis.body:
- "The new Generative and Editable Cards on Now Brief help users choose what appears in their daily summaries."
- "Users can create cards across health, weather, and video so their daily brief reflects the information most relevant to them."
- Footnote: "Now Brief feature requires Samsung Account login. Available functions and features may vary by country, region, language, device model, and app. Some features may require a network connection. Customized briefing content provided is based only on the personal information to which the user has consented. Accuracy of generated results is not guaranteed."

wikis.title: Warranty and Care
wikis.summary: One UI 9 Settings menu section bringing warranty checks, self-diagnostics, repair estimates and Samsung Care+ management into the device.
wikis.body:
- "Warranty and Care brings device support and protection directly into the Settings menu."
- "Users can now check warranty coverage across connected mobile devices, run self-diagnostics, view repair estimates, and manage Samsung Care+ or book a service appointment with just a few taps."
- Footnote: "Available features in Warranty and care menu may differ by country/region. Warranty information is available for devices linked to the user's Samsung Account. Ask Bixby features and supported content may vary by country or language. Estimated repair cost availability may vary by device model/region. Samsung Care+ availability, coverage, pricing, and eligibility requirements may vary by country/region and a deductible (service fee) may apply."

wikis.title: Now Nudge
wikis.summary: Context-aware suggestions that One UI 9 surfaces across more moments in the Galaxy experience.
wikis.body:
- "Now Nudge can surface timely, context-aware suggestions across more moments in the Galaxy experience, helping users take the next step without breaking their flow."
- Example: "when making plans over text, users can pull up reservation details or save a shared location without leaving the conversation."
- Footnote: "Now Nudge feature requires a Samsung Account login. Available functions and features may vary by country, region, and language. Text message prompts are available with certain third-party messaging apps, including Samsung Messages, Google Messages, and Google Chat. Split view supported apps may vary. Photo sharing in Now Nudge works by analyzing available image content. Accuracy of results is not guaranteed."

wikis.title: Creative Studio event-based prompts
wikis.summary: Creative Studio in One UI 9 suggests image-generation ideas tied to upcoming events.
wikis.body:
- "Creative Studio now suggests image-generation ideas based on relevant upcoming events."
- Example: "when a friend's birthday is approaching, users may see a prompt to create a themed image or greeting, allowing them to quickly create something meaningful for the occasion."

wikis.title: Interpreter Thread View and faster translation
wikis.summary: One UI 9's Interpreter adds a Thread View and speeds up Conversation Mode translation and Galaxy Buds playback.
wikis.body:
- "Interpreter introduces a new Thread View that enables users to better follow translated conversations by quickly referencing earlier exchanges."
- "In addition, faster translation in Conversation Mode and quicker playback with compatible Galaxy Buds help reduce delays, making conversations feel more natural and continuous."
- Footnote: "Interpreter requires Samsung Account login. Certain languages may require language pack download. Service availability may vary by language. Accuracy of results is not guaranteed. Availability and supported features may vary by country, region, or carrier. Availability of supported languages may vary."

wikis.title: Document Scan and Voice Recorder improvements
wikis.summary: One UI 9 improves scanning of curved or folded pages and restructures Voice Recorder summaries.
wikis.body:
- "Document Scan now allows users to digitize challenging materials such as curved book pages and corner-folded papers with less manual adjustment."
- "The large-screen-optimized views on compatible Galaxy devices, along with an improved Finger Eraser, help create cleaner and more usable scans."
- "Voice Recorder presents summaries in a clearer, more structured format, using elements such as headings and tables to make key information easier to scan at a glance."

wikis.title: Security Brief, Privacy Alerts and Scam Detection
wikis.summary: One UI 9's security and privacy additions: security updates in Now Brief, on-device privacy risk alerts, and Scam Detection in more countries.
wikis.body:
- "Security Brief brings key security and privacy updates like alerts for malware, apps from unknown sources, and unnecessary permissions to Now Brief, helping users identify potential issues earlier and determine when action is necessary."
- "Privacy Alerts use on-device AI to identify potential privacy risks, including unnecessary attempts to access permissions in the background, giving users greater awareness of how their information is being accessed."
- "Scam Detection expands to additional countries and languages, bringing protection against potential scam calls to more Galaxy users across supported markets." Footnote: "Scam Detection will be available in Japan, Canada, and India."
- Privacy Alerts supported devices listed: Galaxy S26, S26 Ultra, S25, S25 FE, S24, S24 FE, S23, S23 FE, Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Fold8, Flip8, Fold7, Flip7, Fol6 (as printed), Flip6, Fold5, Flip5, Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra, Tab S11, Tab S10 Ultra, Tab S10 Plus, Tab S9 Ultra, Tab S9 Plus, and Tab S9. "Privacy alerts, may not account for all relevant factors".

wikis.title: Calvin Harris announces first ever Australian headline tour for February 2027
wikis.summary: Ticketmaster AU guide announcing Calvin Harris - Australia Tour 2027, with its four dates, presale and onsale times, VIP packages and ticketing rules.
wikis.body:
## The tour

- "Global electronic powerhouse, GRAMMY Award winner, and multi-platinum record-breaking DJ and producer, Calvin Harris, announces his first ever Australian headline tour."
- "Calvin Harris - Australia Tour 2027 will light up major venues across the country next February!"

## Dates

- February 18, 2027 - Langley Park, Perth WA
- February 19, 2027 - RNA Showgrounds, Brisbane QLD
- February 20, 2027 - The Domain, Sydney NSW
- February 26, 2027 - Flemington Racecourse, Melbourne VIC

## On sale

- Telstra Plus Presale: 11am on Monday, 21 September (local time).
- Artist Presale: 12pm on Wednesday, 23 September (local time).
- General Onsale: 1pm on Thursday, 24 September (local time).
- Telstra Plus Presale is only for active Telstra customers.
- Artist Presale is open to "All fans who sign up for first access tickets via Untitled Group Co:Brand before Thursday 24 September, 11:00am*" (local time for the venue).

## Ticket rules

- Maximum 4 tickets per transaction during the Telstra Plus Presale; 6 tickets per transaction during the Artist Presale and General Onsale.
- Tickets are mobile-only and digital, accessed via the Ticketmaster App; "there will be no printed tickets".
- A My Ticketmaster account is needed to access tickets.
- The tour "will be 18+. Valid I.D will be required for entry."
- Accessible tickets via the Ticketmaster website, a Help Centre request (topic: Accessible Bookings, event: Calvin Harris), or the Accessible Booking Line on 1300 446 925, Monday to Sunday, 9:00 am - 5:00 pm AEDT.

## VIP experiences

- VIP LOUNGE + GA - "a premium hospitality experience for guests looking to relax, recharge and enjoy the event in comfort", with "No direct stage viewing - a hospitality first lounge experience". Includes 1 x General Admission Ticket, dedicated VIP entry lane, exclusive access to the VIP Lounge, private VIP bar, VIP amenities (cloakroom, phone charging station), photobooth, commemorative laminate and lanyard, exclusive VIP merch item.
- VIP + STAGE FRONT GA - "combines the premium viewing experience of Front GA with full access to the VIP Lounge". Includes 1 x Stage Front GA Ticket, dedicated Stage Front GA viewing area and VIP entry lane, access to the VIP Lounge, private VIP bar, VIP amenities (cloakroom, phone charging station), photobooth, commemorative laminate and lanyard, exclusive VIP merch item.

## Videos embedded

- Calvin Harris, Jazzy - Satisfy (Official Visualiser).
- Calvin Harris, Kasabian - Release The Pressure (Official Visualiser).
- Calvin Harris, Jessie Reyez - Ocean (Official Visualiser).
- Calvin Harris, Clementine Douglas - Blessings (Official Video).

## Byline

- Rebecca Keith / September 16, 2026.

wikis.title: One UI 9 global release dates revealed by Samsung Thailand
wikis.summary: SamMobile report that a Samsung Thailand newsroom post suggests One UI 9 global release dates: the Galaxy S26 series on September 21, the Galaxy S25 series and Z Flip 7/Fold 7 on September 28, and the Galaxy S23 FE by October.
wikis.body:
## TL;DR as the article gives it
- "Samsung Thailand's newsroom post suggests One UI 9 could reach the Galaxy S26 series globally on September 21, after debuting in Korea on September 16."
- "The Galaxy Z Flip 7, Fold 7, and S25 series are listed for a September 28 One UI 9 update."
- "The Galaxy S23 FE is also mentioned, with One UI 9 expected to arrive by October."

## Galaxy S26 series
- Samsung "finally started rolling out the One UI 9.0 update for the Galaxy S26 series a few days ago, following months of beta testing". The update "debuted in Korea on September 16".
- "September 21 is the day when the Galaxy S26 series will receive One UI 9.0 in Thailand, and possibly other regions beyond South Korea."
- "One UI 8 also arrived a few days later elsewhere than it did in Korea, and now we're seeing a similar pattern."

## Galaxy S25, Z Flip 7 and Fold 7
- "Samsung Thailand also says that the Galaxy S25 series, the Galaxy Z Flip 7, and the Galaxy Z Fold 7 will receive One UI 9.0 on September 28."

## Galaxy S23 FE
- "According to the newsroom post from Thailand, One UI 9.0 will reach the Galaxy S23 FE by October."

## Hedges the article keeps
- Samsung Thailand's announcement "may have revealed the official One UI 9.0 release dates for the global market, not just Korea".
- "Either that, or the dates correspond strictly to Thailand. It's equally likely, considering that no other Samsung portal besides Thailand went into this much detail about the dates."
- "Given the unusual way this information reached us through a single newsroom portal, it could be a tentative plan that's still subject to change."

## Byline
- By Mihai Matei, Senior Editor. Tagged Android 17, One UI 9.0 and the Galaxy S23 FE, S25/S25 Plus/S25 Ultra, S26/S26 Plus/S26 Ultra, Z Flip 7 and Z Fold 7.

wikis.title: When the Galaxy S25 and Galaxy Z7 series get One UI 9
wikis.summary: GSMArena news item reporting, via Samsung Thailand, that the Galaxy S25 series and Galaxy Z7 foldables will receive One UI 9 on September 28, with the Galaxy S23 FE to follow by October.
wikis.body:
## The update timeline
- "Samsung started rolling out the One UI 9 update for the Galaxy S26, S26+ and S26 Ultra yesterday (the S26 FE came with One UI 9 out of the box)."
- The global press release "doesn't really mention older devices - there is a note about which models will get the Privacy Alerts feature, but nothing on when the actual update might arrive."
- "Samsung Thailand was more forthcoming with details on the timeline - the Galaxy S25 series and the Galaxy Z7 foldables will get One UI 9 on September 28."
- Press release quoted: "The update will continue to reach the Galaxy S23 FE by October of this year."

## Devices named
- Samsung Galaxy S25, S25+, S25 Ultra, S25 Edge, S25 FE
- Samsung Galaxy Z Fold7, Galaxy Z Flip7
- Samsung Galaxy S26, S26+, S26 Ultra, S26 FE

## Support notes
- "The Galaxy S23 FE was only promised 4 major OS updates when it launched with Android 13, so this should be its last one. The same applies to the other Galaxy S23 models, though they weren't mentioned by name in the press release."
- "The Galaxy S22 series already got its last major update (Android 16/One UI 8), but it is still receiving quarterly security patches."

- Galaxy S26+ 256GB/12GB RAM: $739.99 / GBP 749.89; 512GB/12GB: $970.99 / GBP 755.00

wikis.title: The Best New Gadgets and Hi-Fi Releases of 2026 (Gear Patrol rolling round-up)
wikis.summary: Gear Patrol's continuously updated 2026 list of new tech and hi-fi releases, spanning Apple's foldable iPhone, Bose's Lifestyle Ultra range, new cameras, televisions, turntables and loudspeakers with their prices.
wikis.body:
## What the source is

A rolling round-up on Gear Patrol of the year's new tech, gadget and hi-fi releases, described by the page as "a rolling list" that "is routinely updated throughout the year". Its framing at the time of capture: "We're already more than halfway through September and, naturally, a lot of new tech and gadgets have been announced since the start of the year." The capture's standfirst mentions "Bose's newest workout headphones, Ikea's affordable desktop speakers and new planar magnetic headphones".

## Phones and personal tech

- **Apple iPhone Duo** — Apple's first foldable iPhone, a 7.6-inch Super Retina XDR inner display and 5.4-inch outer display, A20 Pro chip, 48-megapixel Dual Fusion camera, under-display FaceTime camera. From $2,000, Apple's most expensive iPhone.
- **Apple AirPods 5** — successors to AirPods 4, both models now with active noise cancellation, promising up to 50 percent better ANC. From $129 without the wireless charging case.
- **Light Flip** — Light Phone's first flip phone, a minimalist handset in a Motorola Razr-esque design.
- Also listed: Google Pixel 11 Series, Google Pixel Tag, Microsoft Surface Pro (2026), Nothing Ear (3a), Meta Glasses.

## Headphones and earbuds

- **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (2nd Gen)** — same cuff-shaped design, louder audio, better call quality and battery, upgraded case with wireless charging. $299, the same price as the 2023 originals.
- **Sony WH-1000XM4C** — midrange ANC headphones sharing the WH-1000XM4's 40mm drivers and QN1 processor, with a 10-band equalizer and a new lavender finish. $300, $50 less than the original XM4 at launch.
- **Skullcandy Crusher 1080 ANC** — built with Bose, the first non-Bose headphones with Bose's QuietControl adaptive ANC, plus TrueSpatial and the WaveForm Audio Engine.
- Also listed: Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen), Meze Audio Alba S, Noble Audio FoKus Apollo Pro, Marshall Milton A.N.C, Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2, Grado Classic Series.

## Home cinema and television

- **Sonos Beam Ultra** — nine drivers including two up-firing, true 7.1.2 Dolby Atmos, in much the same body as the Beam (Gen 2). $699, a $200 increase.
- **Bose Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar** — new flagship Dolby Atmos soundbar, 5.2 channels and nine drivers, $1,099, a direct rival to the $1,099 Sonos Arc Ultra.
- **Bose Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer** — flagship wireless subwoofer for 2026 at $899, matching the Sonos Sub 4.
- **Bose Lifestyle Ultra Speaker** — entry-level smart speaker, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth plus an auxiliary jack, two front-firing and one up-firing driver.
- **Roku Pro Series OLED TVs** — Roku's first OLED TVs in two models, 55- and 65-inch, with Automatic Game Mode and AMD FreeSync Premium. Pro Series OLED from $999 available now; Pro Series LX OLED from $1,299 available this October, with 144Hz refresh and a brighter picture.
- Also listed: Sony Bravia 6, Sony Bravia 9 II True RGB TV, LG Micro RGB evo TV, Samsung Q-Series Soundbars (2026).

## Hi-fi components, turntables and loudspeakers

- **Schiit Bifrost 3** — third-generation DAC with new Mesh conversion architecture and a built-in Forkbeard module for app control, making it a digital pre-amplifier. $699 black, $729 silver, a $100 price cut.
- **Clearaudio Compact Phono** — the brand's most compact phono amplifier, 3.15 x 4.53 x 1.02 inches, MM and MC support, $639.
- **Monitor Audio Hyphn (Custom Editions)** — the $99,000 flagship floorstander, released 2023, now customisable in more than 200 colours in gloss, matte or metallic.
- **Audiovector R5 Arreté** — 3.5-way floorstanders, the first R Series models with technology from the $165,000 R10 Arreté.
- **Sony PS-LX5BT** — fully automatic Bluetooth turntable above the PS-LX3BT, with a higher-end cartridge and gold-plated jacks, $100 more.
- Also listed: Dali Basik Sub, Esoteric T-01, Kanto Audio Obi3 (Gen 2), Fiio CP11, Fiio EH13, Fiio Snowsky Nature, Q Acoustics 3040c, Focal Scala Utopia Evo M, Focal Diva Alta Utopia, Sonus Faber Olympica G3, Fluance RT87, Clearaudio N2, Audio-Technica AT-MCD1, Ortofon MC Vertex, Astell&Kern SP4000T, Luxman D-100 Centennial, Bang & Olufsen Beosystem 9000c (Fragment Edition), Wrensilva Studio, Revel Performa4 Series, Victrola, Ikea Kallsup.

## Cameras and other gadgets

- **Canon EOS R6 V** — Canon's first full-frame camera aimed at vloggers, the 32.5-megapixel sensor of the EOS R6 III ($2,799) and 7K/60p RAW video, without an electronic viewfinder.
- **Sony RX10 V** — successor to the 2017 RX10 IV, 20.1MP 1-inch stacked sensor, 24-600mm optical zoom, new processor and AI tracking.
- **Kodak EC35** — the most affordable Kodak-branded 35mm film camera, below the $99 Snapic A1 of late 2025; 25mm lens, fixed f/10 aperture and 1/100 second shutter, built-in flash.
- **Satechi MacBook Neo Collection** — two USB-C hubs at $45 each and the Slim EX wireless mouse at $30, matched to the MacBook Neo.
- Also listed: Analogue Pocket (Supreme Edition), Insta360 X6, Soundpeats UU2, Audio-Technica ATH-M20xSTS StreamSet, Dyson HushJet Mini Cool, Polaroid Hi-Print 3×3, Kerr Acoustic K400.

wikis.title: Gear Patrol 2026 releases, part 1: Apple phones and earbuds, Bose, Sony and hi-fi components
wikis.summary: The first stretch of Gear Patrol's rolling 2026 gadget and hi-fi round-up, covering Apple's foldable iPhone and AirPods 5, Bose and Sony headphones, and desktop hi-fi components.
wikis.body:
## What this part covers

A rolling list, "routinely updated throughout the year", of new tech and hi-fi releases of 2026. The page's own framing: "We're already more than halfway through September and, naturally, a lot of new tech and gadgets have been announced since the start of the year."

## Products in this part

Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (2nd Gen), Clearaudio Compact Phono, Schiit Bifrost 3, Apple iPhone Duo, Apple AirPods 5, Sony WH-1000XM4C, Dali Basik Sub, Sonos Beam Ultra, Roku Pro Series OLED TVs, Sony Bravia 6, Meze Audio Alba S, Audio-Technica ATH-M20xSTS StreamSet, Fiio CP11, Esoteric T-01, Analogue Pocket (Supreme Edition), Kanto Audio Obi3 (Gen 2), Google Pixel 11 Series, Google Pixel Tag, Insta360 X6, Fiio Snowsky Nature, Soundpeats UU2, Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen) and Q Acoustics 3040c.

wikis.title: Apple iPhone Duo
wikis.summary: Apple's first foldable iPhone, starting at $2,000 and its most expensive iPhone.
wikis.body: The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable iPhone. It features a 7.6-inch Super Retina XDR inner display and a 5.4-inch outer display, "making it work like an iPhone and iPad mini all rolled into one". Its specialized software lets it work in various orientations and keeps the hinge crease barely visible. It runs on the same A20 Pro chip as the iPhone 18 Pro and uses a 48-megapixel Dual Fusion camera system. An under-display FaceTime camera keeps the inner screen fully uninterrupted. Starting at $2,000, it is also Apple's most expensive iPhone.

wikis.title: Apple AirPods 5
wikis.summary: Successors to the AirPods 4, adding active noise cancellation across both models, from $129.
wikis.body: The AirPods 5 are the successors to the AirPods 4. They keep the same open-ear design — no silicone earbud tip, so outside noise is more audible — and come in two models, one with a wireless charging case and one without. Unlike the AirPods 4, both AirPods 5 models support active noise cancellation. Thanks to a new multiport acoustic architecture and software tweaks, they promise up to 50 percent better active noise cancellation, and a more natural-sounding transparency mode, compared with AirPods 4. Starting at $129 without the wireless charging case, they are the most affordable AirPods Apple sells.

wikis.title: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (2nd Gen)
wikis.summary: Second-generation cuff-shaped open earbuds at $299, the same price as the 2023 originals.
wikis.body: Bose's second-generation Ultra Open Earbuds keep the cuff-shaped design of the originals but promise improved audio that gets considerably louder, described as "a common problem with these types of open earbuds". They also have better call quality and longer battery life. The charging case was upgraded considerably, with a new metallic cap with a beveled finish and support for wireless charging. They cost $299, the same price as the 2023-released originals.

wikis.title: Sony WH-1000XM4C
wikis.summary: Sony's new midrange noise-cancelling headphones at $300, sharing hardware with the WH-1000XM4.
wikis.body: The Sony WH-1000XM4C is the brand's new midrange option for noise-canceling headphones. They are essentially the same as the 2024-released WH-1000XM4, with identical hardware, the same 40mm drivers, and the same QN1 processor for active noise cancellation. Sony gave them a 10-band equalizer instead of the XM4's 5-band equalizer and added more custom options when creating a sound profile. They come in a new lavender finish alongside standard silver and black. The WH-1000XM4C costs $300, $50 less than the original XM4 when it launched six years ago.

wikis.title: Sonos Beam Ultra
wikis.summary: The next evolution of the Beam soundbar, with nine drivers and 7.1.2 Dolby Atmos, at $699.
wikis.body: The Sonos Beam Ultra is the next evolution of the Beam (Gen 2) soundbar. Where the Beam (Gen 2) packs five drivers, the Beam Ultra adds four more, including two dedicated up-firing drivers. According to the brand it can deliver true 7.1.2 Dolby Atmos and warmer bass, in a body more or less the same size as the previous Beam. The Beam Ultra costs $699, a $200 increase over the Beam (Gen 2), "so it can't really be considered 'affordable' in the same way".

wikis.title: Roku Pro Series OLED TVs
wikis.summary: Roku's first OLED TVs, in two models from $999 and $1,299.
wikis.body: Roku has introduced its first OLED TVs, "designed for those who want OLED-level picture quality without paying OLED-level prices". There are two models, the Pro Series OLED and the Pro Series LX OLED. Each is a 4K TV with gaming-specific features including an Automatic Game Mode and AMD FreeSync Premium, and each is available in 55- and 65-inch sizes. The LX OLED models are higher-end, with faster refresh rates (144Hz vs 120Hz) and a brighter picture. Each runs Roku's latest smart operating system. The Pro Series OLED TVs start at $999 and are available now; the Pro Series LX OLED TVs start at $1,299 and will be available this October.

wikis.title: Schiit Bifrost 3
wikis.summary: Schiit's third-generation DAC, $699 in black and $729 in silver, $100 cheaper than its predecessor.
wikis.body: The Bifrost 3 is Schiit's third-generation digital-to-analog converter (DAC), designed to elevate a desktop or home stereo system. Compared with the previous Bifrost it has three upgrades: a new Mesh conversion architecture promising improved sound; a built-in Forkbeard module adding app support to adjust EQ, balance, loudness and volume and monitor advanced system settings, effectively turning the Bifrost into a digital pre-amplifier; and a $100 price cut. It costs $699 in black and $729 in silver.

wikis.title: Clearaudio Compact Phono
wikis.summary: Clearaudio's most compact phono amplifier to date, at $639.
wikis.body: Clearaudio's Compact Phono is its most compact phono amplifier to date. Measuring 3.15 x 4.53 x 1.02 inches, the company claims it is small enough to fit discreetly into virtually any setup. It supports MM and MC cartridges, with a button on the rear panel to switch between operations, making it compatible with a wide range of turntables. At $639 it is also one of the brand's most affordable phono preamps.

wikis.title: Gear Patrol 2026 releases, part 2: cameras, minimalist phones and high-end loudspeakers
wikis.summary: The middle stretch of the round-up, covering Kodak and Sony cameras, the Light Flip phone, a Skullcandy–Bose collaboration and flagship loudspeakers.
wikis.body:
## What this part covers

A continuation of the same rolling 2026 list.

## Products in this part

Kodak EC35, Light Flip, Monitor Audio Hyphn (Custom Editions), Skullcandy Crusher 1080 ANC, Satechi MacBook Neo Collection, Sony RX10 V, Nothing Ear (3a), Focal Scala Utopia Evo M, Sonus Faber Olympica G3, Fiio EH13, Meta Glasses, Focal Diva Alta Utopia, Microsoft Surface Pro (2026), Fluance RT87, Clearaudio N2, Audio-Technica AT-MCD1, Ortofon MC Vertex, Astell&Kern SP4000T, Sony Bravia 9 II True RGB TV, Luxman D-100 Centennial, Bang & Olufsen Beosystem 9000c (Fragment Edition), Noble Audio FoKus Apollo Pro, Marshall Milton A.N.C and Wrensilva Studio.

wikis.title: Kodak EC35
wikis.summary: The most affordable Kodak-branded 35mm film camera, positioned below the $99 Snapic A1.
wikis.body: The Kodak EC35 is the most affordable Kodak-branded 35mm film camera. It is positioned as an even more affordable option than the brand's $99 Snapic A1, released in late 2025. The EC35 packs a 25mm lens with a fixed f/10 aperture and a fixed 1/100 second shutter speed. It features a slide cover for protecting the lens and a built-in flash, which requires AA batteries. It takes Kodak Ultramax 400 film.

wikis.title: Light Flip
wikis.summary: Light Phone's first flip phone, a minimalist "dumb" phone in a Motorola Razr-esque design.
wikis.body: Light Phone has been making "dumb" phones for years, designed to fight the addictive nature of today's social media apps and doomscrolling. These minimalist phones carry just the bare necessities: phone, text, navigation, alarm and music. The Flip stays true to that ethos but packages it in a nostalgic Motorola Razr-esque design — the company's first-ever flip phone.

wikis.title: Skullcandy Crusher 1080 ANC
wikis.summary: Skullcandy's noise-cancelling headphones built with Bose technology, the first non-Bose headphones with QuietControl adaptive ANC.
wikis.body: Skullcandy teamed up with Bose to create its newest noise-canceling wireless headphones. The Crusher 1080 ANC packs a lot of Bose's technologies: most notably they are the first non-Bose headphones to feature Bose's QuietControl adaptive ANC technology. They also feature Bose's TrueSpatial spatial audio technology and run on Bose's WaveForm Audio Engine.

wikis.title: Sony RX10 V
wikis.summary: The long-awaited successor to the 2017 RX10 IV, a compact with a 24-600mm zoom.
wikis.body: The Sony RX10 V is the long-awaited successor to the company's 2017-released RX10 IV. Like its predecessor it is a compact camera with a 20.1MP 1-inch stacked sensor and zoom capabilities from a 24-600mm optical zoom lens. Sony updated the RX10 V with a brand new processor and advanced AI-tracking capabilities; the source notes "nine years is a long time in the camera world".

wikis.title: Monitor Audio Hyphn (Custom Editions)
wikis.summary: A customisation programme for Monitor Audio's $99,000 flagship floorstanding loudspeaker.
wikis.body: The Hyphn is Monitor Audio's flagship floorstanding loudspeaker. Released in 2023, the British hi-fi maker has called it its "most creatively ambitious, technically advanced" loudspeaker ever. It costs $99,000. Since its release it has been offered in three finishes. Monitor Audio has now launched a program allowing the Hyphn to be customized in more than 200 colours, available in gloss, matte or metallic finishes.

wikis.title: Satechi MacBook Neo Collection
wikis.summary: Three accessories matched to Apple's entry-level MacBook Neo, from $30 to $45.
wikis.body: Satechi's MacBook Neo Collection is a series of accessories designed to work with and match Apple's most entry-level laptop, the MacBook Neo. There are three accessories: two USB-C hubs, the OntheGo 5-in-1 Multiport Adapter ($45) and the USB-C Snap Hub ($45), and the Slim EX wireless mouse ($30). All three come in the same four colourful finishes.

wikis.title: Gear Patrol 2026 releases, part 3: Bose Lifestyle Ultra, home cinema and turntables
wikis.summary: The last stretch of the round-up, covering Canon's vlogging camera, Bose's Lifestyle Ultra range, high-end loudspeakers and new turntables.
wikis.body:
## What this part covers

The closing stretch of the same rolling 2026 list.

## Products in this part

Canon EOS R6 V, Bose Lifestyle Ultra Speaker, Bose Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar, Bose Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer, Audiovector R5 Arreté, Sony PS-LX5BT, Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2 (Midnight Blue and Pearl Blue), Kerr Acoustic K400, Victrola, LG Micro RGB evo TV, Dyson HushJet Mini Cool, Polaroid Hi-Print 3×3, Samsung Q-Series Soundbars (2026), Revel Performa4 Series, Ikea Kallsup and Grado Classic Series.

wikis.title: Bose Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar
wikis.summary: Bose's new flagship Dolby Atmos soundbar at $1,099, positioned against the Sonos Arc Ultra.
wikis.body: The Bose Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar is the company's new flagship Dolby Atmos soundbar, taking that title from Bose's Smart Ultra Soundbar, which was released in late 2023 and priced at $999. At $1,099 it is priced and positioned as a direct rival to Sonos's current flagship soundbar, the $1,099 Arc Ultra. It is a 5.2-channel soundbar with nine drivers: four front-facing full-range drivers, two up-firing full-range drivers and others.

wikis.title: Bose Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer
wikis.summary: Bose's flagship wireless subwoofer for 2026 at $899, matching the price of the Sonos Sub 4.
wikis.body: The Bose Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer is the company's flagship wireless subwoofer for 2026. Priced at $899, it is a direct rival to the Sonos Sub 4, which costs exactly the same. According to the brand it "delivers deep, controlled bass that remains clear at any volume, adding weight and authority for the ultimate home theater experience".

wikis.title: Bose Lifestyle Ultra Speaker
wikis.summary: Bose's new entry-level smart speaker with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and an auxiliary jack.
wikis.body: The Bose Lifestyle Ultra Speaker is the company's new entry-level smart speaker with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth streaming capabilities. It also has an auxiliary jack, so it can be used as a wired speaker with a computer or turntable. As a standalone mono speaker it features two front-firing and one up-firing driver, and two can be configured as a stereo pair.

wikis.title: Canon EOS R6 V
wikis.summary: Canon's first full-frame camera aimed squarely at vloggers, dropping the electronic viewfinder.
wikis.body: The Canon EOS R6 V is the company's first full-frame camera squarely aimed at vloggers. It inherits the same 32.5-megapixel sensor used in the EOS R6 III ($2,799), as well as the same 7K/60p RAW video shooting capabilities. It lacks an electronic viewfinder in favour of a lighter design. According to the brand, the R6 V is "designed for creatives who capture video on a daily basis who want control, operability" and related qualities.

wikis.title: Audiovector R5 Arreté
wikis.summary: High-end floorstanding loudspeakers inheriting technology from the $165,000 R10 Arreté.
wikis.body: Audiovector's R5 Arreté is a pair of high-end floorstanding loudspeakers that, according to the brand, are the first models in the R Series to carry technologies inherited directly from its flagship $165,000 R10 Arreté loudspeakers. Each loudspeaker has a 3.5-way design and packs the same tweeter and midrange drivers as the R10 Arreté, but not as many of them, and no long-throw bass drivers.

wikis.title: Sony PS-LX5BT
wikis.summary: Sony's higher-end 2026 automatic turntable with Bluetooth, $100 above the PS-LX3BT.
wikis.body: The Sony PS-LX5BT is the brand's other new turntable for 2026, positioned as a slightly higher-end version of the company's PS-LX3BT. Both are fully automatic turntables with a nearly identical design and built-in Bluetooth. The PS-LX5BT comes with more premium components, including a higher-end cartridge and gold-plated audio jacks, and is $100 more expensive.

wikis.title: Meze Audio Alba S: the Alba earbuds without the USB-C adapter, for $129
wikis.summary: Gear Patrol report that Meze Audio now sells its entry-level Alba in-ear monitors without the bundled USB-C DAC adapter, as the Alba S, at $129 instead of $159.
wikis.body:
## The new product

- Meze Audio has started selling the Alba without its custom USB-C adapter; "Meze is calling these adaptor-less models the Alba S."
- Price drops "from $159 to $129".
- "They are available on the company's website now."
- The Alba S has a gold-plated 3.5mm jack and ships with "the same detachable, braided SPC cables as the standard Alba models".
- Spotted by eCoustics.

## The standard Alba

- Meze Audio is "a Romanian hi-fi company best known for its high-end and beautifully designed headphones, many of which cost several thousand bucks".
- The Alba was introduced in 2024 as the brand's most affordable set of in-ear monitors at $159, "designed for new hi-fi fans who wanted to take a first step into high-end wired audio".
- "The Alba still costs $159 and remains the most affordable in-ear monitor the company makes."
- Each Alba earbud has a 10.8mm dynamic driver with a frequency range of 15-25kHz; according to the company it delivers a neutral sound profile "with an added touch of warmth".
- The Alba ships with a custom 3.5mm-to-USB-C adapter with its own built-in DAC, to plug into an iPhone, Android or desktop.

## Meze's other IEMs

- "The only other IEMs Meze makes are the Astru, which it just introduced this spring and cost $899."

## Page data

- By Tucker Bowe. Published August 25, 2026.

wikis.title: Fosi Audio Disc Nano portable CD player
wikis.summary: Gear Patrol's write-up of Fosi Audio's Disc Nano, a $99 half-exposed portable CD player with Bluetooth and a MagSafe ring, due later in September 2026.
wikis.body:
## The product

- The **Disc Nano** is "Fosi Audio's first portable CD player" and is described as "very much a modern-day Walkman".
- It has a built-in battery and supports **Bluetooth streaming**, so it can play CDs and stream their audio to wireless headphones, earbuds or speakers.
- Outputs: **3.5mm** and **4.4mm**, for a wide range of wired headphones.
- DAC: **Cirrus Logic CS43198**, "allowing to play up to **32-bit** audio".

## Design

- A "distinctive half-exposed design" - "the full CD isn't protected while it's playing".
- That design choice "lets Fosi Audio market the Disc Nano as the **'world's smallest portable CD player'**".
- It integrates a standard **MagSafe ring mount**: "This doesn't let it charge wirelessly, but it does let it stick to any MagSafe-compatible device, including most smartphones."
- Fosi Audio claims the Disc Nano combines "the timeless appeal of physical media with modern portability and design".

## Price and availability

- "Fosi Audio's Disc Nano CD player will be available **later this month**. It'll cost **$99**."
- Available in two finishes, black and white.

## Background: the Merak

- Fosi Audio introduced the **Merak**, "its first-ever venture into CD players, earlier this year".
- The Merak is meant for desktop use, **lacks a built-in battery** and must stay connected to power.
- It costs **$140** and can function as an all-in-one digital transport, DAC and headphone amplifier.

wikis.title: Fiio Snowsky Echo Nano, a $50 portable hi-fi player
wikis.summary: Gear Patrol report on the Fiio Snowsky Echo Nano, a $50 microSD-based portable hi-fi player that the brand says "reimagines the iconic 2000s era MP3 player".
wikis.body:
## The product

- The Snowsky Echo Nano is a portable hi-fi player that, according to the brand, "reimagines the iconic 2000s era MP3 player".
- It accesses a digital library via a microSD card and "doesn't run any apps, so you won't find Spotify or Apple Music on it"; designed as "a distraction-free way of listening to your digital music library".
- Supports microSD cards up to 256GB, "which should store around 500 albums".

## Specifications given

- DAC: Cirrus Logic CS43131, enabling high-resolution audio with native DSD decoding.
- Formats supported: WAV, FLAC, APE, MP3, M4A and OGG.
- 3.5mm single-ended headphone jack.
- Build: CNC-machined 6-series aluminum.
- 0.91-inch OLED display and a tactile metal scroll wheel; "Navigating your music promises to be a one-handed operation."
- Battery life "up to seven-hour"; charges via USB-C.
- Weight: 33.5 grams - "about as much as an AA battery".
- 5-band dynamic equalizer with six built-in presets, plus custom EQ.
- Can function as a USB DAC for a smartphone or laptop; USB-C jack on its side next to the microSD slot.

## Price and availability

- Costs "just $50".
- Seven colour options: black, white, pink, sky blue, green, purple and titanium.
- "It's available now." Listed at $50 at Amazon.

## Snowsky sub-brand context

- "In the last year, Fiio has released several audio products under its budget-friendly Snowsky sub-brand."
- Examples given: the Snowsky Tiny, a $20 portable DAC and headphone amplifier, and the Snowsky Disc, "a tiny portable hi-fi player that works kind of like an old iPod and costs just $80".

## Page data

- By Tucker Bowe. Published August 7, 2026; Updated August 7, 2026.

wikis.title: Astell&Kern PD5 digital audio player announcement
wikis.summary: Forbes article on Astell&Kern's announcement of the PD5 digital audio player, covering its switchable Quad/Octa-DAC design, battery life, EnviroTune feature and show appearances.
wikis.body:
## Announcement

- "Korean audio specialist Astell&Kern has announced the launch of a new digital audio player."
- The PD5 is the successor to the brand's multi-award-winning A&norma SR35.
- It "will be on show at this weekend's Hong Kong AV show".
- By Mark Sparrow, Forbes senior contributor; Aug 03, 2026, 10:00pm EDT.

## Design and DACs

- Encased in an elegant aluminum body, designed to fit comfortably in one hand.
- At its heart are "no fewer than eight Cirrus Logic CS43198 DACs", with a switchable Quad/Octa-DAC architecture.
- Listeners can choose between Quad-DAC and Octa-DAC operation: Quad-DAC mode prioritizes battery life for extended listening, while Octa-DAC mode "unlocks the player's full sonic potential", which A&K says can deliver class-defining performance for a DAP of this size.

## Battery and charging

- In Quad-DAC mode the PD5 can play for up to 28 hours on a single charge.
- Supports PD 3.0 charging, cutting charge time to around 2.5 hours.

## EnviroTune

- EnviroTune analyses ambient noise and then automatically optimizes playback to suit the current environment, whether commuting, working somewhere noisy or listening in a quieter space.

## Playback and connectivity

- Bit-perfect playback up to 32-bit/384kHz PCM and native DSD256.
- Octa-core processor and full Android OS platform optimized for music streaming services.
- Dual-band Wi-Fi, Bluetooth 5.3 and broad codec support including Qualcomm aptX HD, LDAC and LHDC.

## Show appearances

- Hong Kong AV Show (debut).
- Shenzhen International Audio Show, "from the August 14 to 16, 2026".
- CanJam SoCal 2026, which runs from August 29 to 30, in the United States.

## Pricing

- "Further details, pricing and availability will be announced soon."

wikis.title: Wazamonogatari: Karen Ogre episode set for winter 2026 broadcast
wikis.summary: Anime News Network report that Aniplex revealed a new visual and a winter 2026 broadcast for the "Wazamonogatari: Karen Ogre" episode of the MONOGATARI Series: OFF & MONSTER Season anime.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- "Aniplex revealed a new visual and the winter 2026 broadcast for the upcoming 'Wazamonogatari: Karen Ogre' episode of the MONOGATARI Series: OFF & MONSTER Season anime on Thursday."
- Subhead: "New episode is titled 'Wazamonogatari: Karen Ogre'".
- Source: Press release.

## Staff

- "Franchise veteran Akiyuki Simbo is again serving as chief director and Midori Yoshizawa is directing the new episode at SHAFT."
- "Fuyashi Tou returns to oversee the series scripts with Simbo, and Akio Watanabe is also back as character designer and chief animation director."
- Copyright line: (c) Nisio Isin / Kodansha, Aniplex, SHAFT.

## Anime so far

- "The anime began streaming exclusively on the ABEMA service in Japan in July 2024. The anime's 14th episode streamed in October 2024. Crunchyroll streamed the anime as it was released in Japan."

## Novel background as given

- "NisiOisin's novel series began with the two-volume Bakemonogatari story in 2006, and it served as the basis for the first anime adaptation of the novels in 2009."
- "The novel series' 'final season' ended with Zoku Owarimonogatari in September 2014, but it featured a teaser for 'Monogatari Series, Next Season Tsugimonogatari.' Tsugimonogatari is the latest novel in the series, and it shipped in October 2025."
- "Four 'Off Season' volumes - Orokamonogatari, Wazamonogatari, Nademonogatari, and Musubimonogatari - shipped in October 2015, January 2016, July 2016, and January 2017, respectively. The volumes tell a series of short stories set at different points throughout the series."
- "The novel series' 'Monster Season' launched with the Shinobumonogatari novel in July 2017. Other novels in the season include Yoimonogatari, Amarimonogatari, Ogimonogatari, and the two-volume Shinomonogatari novel, which shipped in August 2021. The novels tell a continuation of the franchise, taking place in college."

## Byline

- Posted on 2026-07-02 05:00 EDT by Rafael Antonio Pineda.

wikis.title: Rotel adds Michi Prestige P430 preamplifier and S430 power amplifier
wikis.summary: Gear Patrol report on two new components in Rotel's flagship Michi range - the Michi Prestige P430 stereo preamplifier and Michi Prestige S430 stereo power amplifier, $4,000 each and available this month.
wikis.body:
## What was announced

- Rotel, described by the article as a "Japanese hi-fi brand," has made "two additions to its flagship Michi range of hi-fi components": the Michi Prestige P430 stereo preamplifier and the Michi Prestige S430 stereo power amplifier.
- "They're designed to work together as the backbone of a pretty elite hi-fi system."

## Price and availability

- Both "will be available this month."
- "Both cost $4,000 each, so the stack will set you back $8,000."

## Context given by the article

- "Just last month, Rotel introduced the Amora 5 bookshelf speakers," its first pair of loudspeakers "in roughly 35 years"; a pair costs $1,000.
- By Tucker Bowe; published and updated September 7, 2026.

wikis.title: Rotel Michi Prestige S430 stereo power amplifier
wikis.summary: Class AB power amplifier rated 230 watts per channel into 8 ohms, $4,000.
wikis.body:
- Uses a Class AB design.
- Delivers 230 watts per channel into 8 ohms or 390 watts per channel into 4 ohms.
- Rotel says it "provides the dynamic headroom needed to reveal greater scale and impact from high-performance loudspeakers."
- Aluminum chassis; large front-panel display that "you can choose to show UV meters while the music is playing." The company calls it a "refined visual presence."
- Price: $4,000. Available this month.

wikis.title: Rotel Michi Prestige P430 stereo preamplifier
wikis.summary: Preamplifier with a 32-bit DAC, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi streaming, HDMI ARC and a moving-magnet phono stage, $4,000.
wikis.body:
- "The P430 stereo preamplifier adds controls, a 32-bit DAC, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi streaming, and physical connections for both analog and digital sources; it supports HDMI ARC input for TV integration, plus a built-in moving-magnet phono stage for TV connectivity."
- Described elsewhere on the page as housing "a high-resolution DAC, an ultra-low-noise power supply and inputs for connecting to a wide variety of sources."
- Rotel says the P430's "ultra-low-noise architecture, isolated power regulation, and balanced signal path preserve resolution, dynamics, and soundstage precision."
- Price: $4,000. Available this month.
- A photo caption on the page states "The P430 is a stereo preamplifier capable of delivering 390 watts (into 4 ohms)."

wikis.title: Yamaha WXA-70A streaming amplifier and WXC-70A network streamer
wikis.summary: Gear Patrol report on Yamaha's first compact streaming components in over a decade - the WXA-70A streaming amplifier and WXC-70A network streamer - with prices and a November 2026 release.
wikis.body:
## What was announced

- Yamaha has released "two compact streaming components: a streaming amp and a network streamer" - the WXA-70A and WXC-70A.
- "They're the first compact streamers that Yamaha has released in over a decade."
- The article attributes the move to "the rise of multi-room audio and hi-fi streaming."

## Shared features

- Both use the same audiophile-grade DAC (ESS Sabre).
- Both support AirPlay 2, Google Cast, Spotify Connect, Tidal Connect, Qobuz Connect and Roon Ready, plus Bluetooth.
- Both support Yamaha's MusicCast, so they can be grouped in a larger multi-room audio system.
- Both have various digital and analog inputs, support connection to a CD player or turntable (with a built-in phono preamp), and each has an HDMI eARC input to connect to a TV.
- Both come in silver or black finishes.

## Yamaha's statement

- "The WXA-70A and WXC-70A were created for music lovers who want to enjoy exceptional sound combined with simple operation and ease of use. These models bring together Yamaha Hi-Fi heritage with the most popular streaming platforms and intuitive operation, making it easier to build a system that fits the way people listen today."

## Price and availability

- WXA-70A: $1,300. WXC-70A: $1,000.
- "They will be available in November 2026."
- By Tucker Bowe; published and updated August 27, 2026.

wikis.title: Yamaha WXA-70A compact streaming amplifier
wikis.summary: Streaming amplifier rated 70 watts per channel into 8 ohms, $1,300, available November 2026.
wikis.body:
- A streaming amplifier "designed to breathe new life into an old pair of passive speakers."
- Delivers 70 watts (at 8 ohms) or 105 watts (at 4 ohms) per channel, "making it a good fit for a wide range of bookshelf and floorstanding speakers."
- Has an HDMI eARC input to connect a TV to the hi-fi system; built-in phono preamp for a turntable.
- ESS Sabre DAC; AirPlay 2, Google Cast, Spotify Connect, Tidal Connect, Qobuz Connect, Roon Ready, Bluetooth, MusicCast.
- Price $1,300; silver or black; available November 2026.

wikis.title: Yamaha WXC-70A compact network streamer
wikis.summary: Network streamer / streaming preamplifier without an amplifier section, $1,000, available November 2026.
wikis.body:
- "The Yamaha WXC-70A is a network streamer or streaming preamplifier. It lacks an amplifier section, so it's designed to pair with an existing amplifier and deliver high-resolution streaming and modern connectivity."
- Yamaha says it pairs well with its A-S Series integrated amplifiers.
- Same ESS Sabre DAC and streaming support as the WXA-70A, including Bluetooth; HDMI eARC input; built-in phono preamp.
- Price $1,000; silver or black; available November 2026.

wikis.title: Yamaha WXA-70A and WXC-70A compact streaming components
wikis.summary: Forbes article on Yamaha's announcement of two compact streaming components - the WXA-70A streaming amplifier and WXC-70A streaming preamplifier - with their shared features, prices and November 2026 availability.
wikis.body:
## Announcement

- "Yamaha has announced two sleek streaming components designed for the digital age: the WXA-70A streaming amplifier and the WXC-70A streaming preamplifier."
- By Mark Sparrow, Forbes senior contributor; Aug 27, 2026, 09:00am EDT.
- Alex Sadeghian, Director of Consumer Audio Marketing at Yamaha: "The WXA-70A and WXC-70A were created for music lovers who demand exceptional sound without operational complexity... These models bridge Yamaha's Hi-Fi heritage with today's most popular streaming platforms. Whether you are building a new music system from scratch or upgrading an existing setup, they deliver remarkable sound quality, flexibility, and long-term value."

## Shared features

- Audiophile-grade ESS SABRE DAC "tuned for clean and detailed sound".
- Out of the box both support AirPlay 2, Google Cast, Spotify Connect, TIDAL Connect, Qobuz Connect and Roon Ready.
- Built-in MusicCast for multi-room control through a single app; different tracks to separate rooms or grouped for synchronized, house-wide audio.
- HDMI eARC port for single-cable setup with compatible televisions, allowing power and volume control via the TV remote.
- A full suite of analog and digital inputs for sources such as CD players or turntables (requiring a phono preamp).
- YPAO calibration microphone; the automated system analyzes room acoustics and speaker placement, while YPAO R.S.C. (Reflected Sound Control) tames early acoustic reflections.
- Control4 compatibility, web-based setup, IR inputs and 12V trigger support for smart home integration.

## Pricing and availability

- Both "will be available in November 2026" and can be ordered in Black or Silver finishes.
- WXA-70A Compact Streaming Amplifier: $1,299.95 / GBP 1,199 / EUR 1,399.
- WXC-70A Compact Streaming Preamplifier: $999.95 / GBP 859 / EUR 999.

- "The WXA-70A is designed to transform passive speakers into a standalone, modern Hi-Fi system or it can act as a multi-room extension for Yamaha's AVENTAGE home theater lineup."
- ESS SABRE DAC; AirPlay 2, Google Cast, Spotify Connect, TIDAL Connect, Qobuz Connect, Roon Ready.
- MusicCast multi-room; HDMI eARC; YPAO calibration with YPAO R.S.C.
- Control4 compatibility, web-based setup, IR inputs, 12V trigger.
- Available in November 2026 in Black or Silver.
- Price: $1,299.95 / GBP 1,199 / EUR 1,399.

- MusicCast multi-room; HDMI eARC; YPAO calibration with YPAO R.S.C.
- Control4 compatibility, web-based setup, IR inputs, 12V trigger.
- Available in November 2026 in Black or Silver.
- Price: $999.95 / GBP 859 / EUR 999.

wikis.title: MONOGATARI Series: OFF & MONSTER Season anime gets a new episode
wikis.summary: Anime News Network report that the MONOGATARI Series: OFF & MONSTER Season anime will get a new episode, with a teaser visual, special video and returning staff.
wikis.body:
## Announcement

- "The official website for the MONOGATARI Series: OFF & MONSTER Season anime announced on Thursday that it will get a new episode, and revealed a special video and the teaser visual."
- "The anime's staff also started streaming a 'next episode preview' video, featuring 'DJ Nadeko x Bro. Yotsugi'."

## Staff

- Franchise veteran Akiyuki Simbo is "again serving as chief director".
- Midori Yoshizawa is directing the new episode at SHAFT.
- Fuyashi Tou returns to oversee the series scripts with Simbo.
- Akio Watanabe is back as character designer and chief animation director.

## Broadcast history given

- The anime "began streaming exclusively on the ABEMA service in Japan in July 2024."
- "The anime's 14th episode streamed on October 19."
- Crunchyroll streamed the anime as it was released in Japan.

## Novel background given

- NisiOisin's novel series began with the two-volume Bakemonogatari story in 2006, the basis for the first anime adaptation in 2009.
- The novel series' "final season" ended with Zoku Owarimonogatari in September 2014, but featured a teaser for "Monogatari Series, Next Season Tsugimonogatari."
- Four "Off Season" volumes - Orokamonogatari, Wazamonogatari, Nademonogatari and Musubimonogatari - shipped in October 2015, January 2016, July 2016 and January 2017 respectively; they "tell a series of short stories set at different points throughout the series."
- The "Monster Season" launched with the Shinobumonogatari novel in July 2017; other novels include Yoimonogatari, Amarimonogatari, Ogimonogatari and the two-volume Shinomonogatari, which shipped in August 2021. "The novels tell a continuation of the franchise, taking place in college."
- "The latest novel in the franchise is Ikusamonogatari, which shipped in May 2023."

## Credits

- Posted 2025-07-03 06:30 EDT by Joanna Cayanan.
- Sources: MONOGATARI Series: OFF & MONSTER Season anime's website, Mainichi Shimbun's Mantan Web.

wikis.title: Sonos Ace Ultra headphones announced at $449
wikis.summary: Gear Patrol's report on Sonos officially announcing the Ace Ultra noise-canceling headphones - their hardware upgrades, Wi-Fi Headphone Linking feature, $449 price and September 29th shipping.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- "Sonos has officially announced the Ace Ultra, the next generation of the Ace, the brand's original wireless noise-canceling headphones, which were released in May 2024."
- On the surface they are "practically identical to the Ace": same soft edges, lightweight, with metal and vegan leather accents.
- Launching in four finishes instead of two: standard white and black, plus sand (beige) and agave (blue).

## Hardware

- New custom 40mm drivers.
- "Twice-as-powerful active noise cancellation, thanks to a new processor and two extra mics (now 10 instead of 8)".
- Battery life "up to 35 hours with ANC turned on (up from the Ace's 30 hours)".
- Supports wired audio via USB-C or 3.5mm connection.
- Sonos claims the Ace Ultra is "the first headphone to be built on its Headphone Engine 2".

## Wi-Fi and Headphone Linking

- Sonos says the new headphones have "redesigned Wi-Fi hardware and secure credential storage" for better integration with an existing home Sonos system.
- This enables "Headphone linking" and support for Wi-Fi streaming.
- Headphone Linking connects the Ace Ultra directly to the home's Sonos speaker system over Wi-Fi; a button press switches audio from the speakers to the headphones and another press switches back. Sonos says it gives listeners "the ability to push and pull sound between nearby speakers and their ears."
- Caveat: "it won't be available on all Ace Ultra headphones at launch" - Headphone Linking is technically an "Early Access" feature users must opt in to try, "so it may take some time for the feature to roll out to the masses".
- Wi-Fi streaming "(potentially) gives listeners access to higher-resolution audio than Bluetooth"; "At the time of writing, Sonos hasn't specified exactly how high-res that is."
- Like their predecessors, the Ace Ultra also supports TV Audio Swap for owners of a Sonos soundbar.

## Background on the original Ace

- The original Sonos Ace "didn't sell very well" because they were expensive and lacked exclusive features; they "only supported Bluetooth streaming. No Wi-Fi", with TV Audio Swap as the one standout feature, which required a Sonos soundbar.

## Price and availability

- "The Sonos Ace Ultra is available for preorder now and will start shipping September 29th."
- $449 - "the exact same as the Ace at launch" - in four colors: black, white, sand and agave.
- "At the time of writing, it's unclear if Sonos will phase out the original Ace or just permanently drop the price."

## Byline

- Gear Patrol, by Tucker Bowe, Published September 1, 2026.

wikis.title: Sonos Play portable speaker in a new sand finish
wikis.summary: Gear Patrol report that Sonos quietly added a "sand" finish to its Play portable speaker alongside its larger announcement day, with price and shipping details.
wikis.body:
## The news

- Sonos introduced a new version of its newest portable speaker, the Play, in a new "sand" finish, announced "yesterday" alongside the company's larger event.
- Since its release "this past spring", the Play had only been available in black or white finishes; sand is a third finish.
- The sand finish is the same "sand" finish Sonos offers its Ace Ultra headphones in.
- By Tucker Bowe, published September 2, 2026.

## The rest of the announcement day

- "Yesterday, Sonos had arguably its biggest day of announcements in years." It introduced two new products, the Ace Ultra headphones and the Beam Ultra soundbar, as well as a rebranded app, Sonos 27, and opened its audio platform to numerous third-party AI assistants (including OpenAI's ChatGPT).

## About the Play

- "Introduced in March 2026, the Play is Sonos's Goldilocks portable speaker that's positioned between the Move 2 and Roam 2."
- It is essentially a smaller, more affordable version of the Move 2, with all the same abilities but roughly half the size.

## New rear-channel feature

- Thanks to the announcements, both the Move 2 and Play have gained a new ability: with a pair of each plus a Sonos soundbar, they can be designated as rear-channel speakers.
- "It's the first time Sonos has enabled such a feature in its portable speakers."

## Price and availability

- The Sonos Play in the new sand finish is available for preorder now and starts shipping at the end of the month.
- It costs $299, the same as the black or white models.

wikis.title: KEF Outdoor Collection backyard speakers
wikis.summary: Gear Patrol report on KEF's new Outdoor Collection of weather-sealed outdoor speakers with Uni-Q drivers, giving the range's models, prices and April 2027 availability.
wikis.body:
## The launch

- "KEF is bringing its famed sound and Uni-Q drivers outdoors with its all-new collection of backyard speakers, aptly named the KEF Outdoor Collection."
- From KEF's press release: "The Outdoor Collection brings KEF's signature high-fidelity sound where it's never been before... From intimate garden retreats to expansive terraces and commercial hospitality settings."
- The brand says the collection "seamlessly extends KEF's legendary sound beyond the home and into the natural world."

## The range

- Includes two satellite speakers, four bollard (vertical, post-shaped) speakers and two bollard subwoofers, each with different sizes and prices. The system is powered by one of KEF's Kasa amplifiers.
- Each speaker comes with KEF's signature Uni-Q driver array, which places the tweeter at the centre of the midrange and bass drivers. "It's the first time KEF has ever integrated its Uni-Q driver in an outdoor speaker, let alone a collection."
- Per the brand, the Uni-Q driver "creates a single point source of sound, delivering a seamless, expansive soundstage that envelops every listener equally."
- Two larger bollard speakers have a three-way design and an integrated subwoofer. The landscape satellite speakers "are designed for flexible placement", with various accessories sold for them.
- "Each speaker in the Outdoor Collection has a UV-resistant, weather-sealed design that's rated between IP66 and IPX5."
- The SR6Q are the larger of the two landscape satellite speakers.

## Price and availability

- Four packs of landscape satellite speakers: $2,000 (SR4Q) and $3,000 (SR6Q).
- The four bollard speakers range from $1,500/ea to $4,000.
- The two subwoofers cost $2,000 (BL8b) and $2,500 (BL12b).
- KEF makes four different Kasa amplifiers, ranging from $1,600 to $4,000, "designed to power immersive outdoor systems or even an outdoor home theater system".
- Two speaker system packages, each including a Kasa network DSP amplifier, range from $5,000 to $8,000.
- "The KEF Outdoor Collection will be available starting April 2027." Listed as "STARTS AT $2,000".

## Article details

- By Tucker Bowe; published September 2, 2026.

wikis.title: KEF LS LUXE wireless speakers
wikis.summary: Forbes report on KEF's launch of the LS LUXE wireless speakers designed with Ross Lovegrove, covering their drivers, Velocity Control Technology, wireless and wired connections, accessories and pricing.
wikis.body:
## The launch

- British audio brand KEF, "in business for 65 years", announced "one of its most ambitious creations to date: the LS LUXE".
- Developed in partnership with designer Ross Lovegrove, continuing KEF collaborations that include Muon, Mu headphones and the Muo portable speaker.
- Grace Lo, KEF's president and head of global marketing: "At KEF, we have always aimed to redefine the listening experience and make it truly inspiring. LS LUXE is that vision realized. True luxury doesn't announce itself - it transforms the atmosphere of a space, blending design excellence and acoustic mastery in a way that feels both immersive and effortless."
- The company claims the breakthroughs together will "set a new definition for wireless hi-fi and elevated living".

## Drivers and cabinet

- KEF's 12th-generation, 6.5-inch Uni-Q driver with Metamaterial Absorption Technology (MAT).
- Metamaterial Absorption Technology "acts as an acoustic black hole by absorbing 99% of unwanted rear sound from the tweeter to virtually eliminate distortion".
- The tweeter is positioned at the acoustic center of the woofer.
- Rounded, low-diffraction design; "flexible decoupling chassis and advanced bulk molding compound", said to set "a benchmark beyond KEF's gold-standard LS50 Wireless II".

## Velocity Control Technology

- The LS LUXE is "the first speaker to feature KEF's Velocity Control Technology", building on the debut of the KEF XIO soundbar.
- "The closed-loop system uses a velocity sensor to monitor the Uni-Q driver in real time, feeding data instantly to a custom amplifier that corrects any movement inconsistencies."

## Amplification and DSP

- "Combining a 100W Class AB and 280W Class D current-drive amplifier per speaker".
- KEF's proprietary Music Integrity Engine uses DSP algorithms "to maintain definition and performance as the amplifiers work harder".

## Connectivity

- Built on KEF's W2 wireless platform; handles "high-fidelity, lossless audio formats up to 24-bit/384kHz" and multi-room audio.
- Streaming: Tidal, Amazon Music, Qobuz, Deezer "and more", via Spotify Connect, Tidal Connect, QPlay, AirPlay or Google Cast; Roon-ready "(available in 2027)".
- Wired: HDMI eARC, analogue, optical and coaxial; each speaker has a dedicated subwoofer output; streams from local NAS drives or music servers, "supporting lossless formats up to 24-bit/384kHz PCM and DSD".

## Setup and control

- Setup via the KEF Connect app, with Normal or Expert modes for granular EQ control in dBs.
- "An Advanced Room EQ DSP automatically adapts the speaker to suit the space it's used in, while dedicated subwoofer presets guarantee integration with KEF's subwoofer range."
- Control via the app or the C3 remote, which has an aluminum top plate, backlit buttons and a customizable favorite button; each speaker includes the C3 remote.

## Finishes and accessories

- Three colorways: Dusk Titanium, Eclipse Black and Mineral White.
- Optional S-LUXE floor stands with integrated cable management.
- K-Stream interspeaker cable "enables high-resolution audio transfer with up to 8 meters of placement flexibility".
- KW1 wireless subwoofer adapter kit for a cable-free connection to KEF subwoofers. Accessories sold separately.

## Pricing and availability

- "The KEF LS LUXE speakers are available now and are priced at $4,000 / £3,500 / €4,000 per pair."
- "The S-LUXE floor stands are available now and priced at $800 / £800 / €900."

## Byline

- By Mark Sparrow, Forbes Senior Contributor. "Jul 30, 2026, 04:00am EDT".

wikis.title: JBL Pulse 6 portable speaker
wikis.summary: JBL product page for the Pulse 6 portable Bluetooth speaker, covering its 360-degree lightshow, sound features, battery life, waterproofing and price.
wikis.body:
