wikis.title: Buchardt Audio E50-S bookshelf speakers
wikis.summary: Gear Patrol's report on Buchardt Audio's E50-S passive bookshelf speakers - how they differ from the E-50, their sensitivity, price of €4,100 and October shipping.
wikis.body:
## The speakers

- Buchardt Audio, a Danish loudspeaker specialist, is introducing the E50-S, "new and improved versions of its E-50, its most high-end and expensive passive bookshelf speaker".
- "The 'S' in the E50-S stands for 'Sensitivity.' Thus, they promise to be easier to drive than the E50."
- Compared with the E-50, the E-50S have a larger cabinet, a larger woofer, and a refined tweeter and crossover design.
- Buchardt describes the E-50S not as an upgrade over the E-50 but as a different approach, "retaining the core DNA while making the E Series suitable for a wider range of customers".
- Sound: Buchardt claims "you get less overall bass, but more focus on the midrange, which enhances vocals, provides a very textured sound, and generally allows the midrange to take a more prominent position in the mix."
- 2-way design with two passive radiators located on the back, "which allows such a compact speaker to deliver more bass and be situated closer to walls".
- Sensitivity of 88dB vs 85dB for the E-50, so they don't need as powerful an amplifier; per the brand the E50-S can be used "with anything from small 15-watt tube amplifiers and up, while still providing respectable output levels".
- Black grilles come with each pair.
- Buchardt says they cater to audiophiles who "simply prefer a sound with less focus on the bass and more emphasis on midrange detail and clarity".

## Price and availability

- A pair of E-50S costs €4,100 (roughly $4,750); the higher price than the E-50 "primarily comes down to its more advanced and costly crossover design".
- Three finishes: natural oak, smoked oak or charcoal.
- "They are available now from the company's website. Shipping is expected to start in October."

## Related products mentioned

- The original E-50, introduced in late 2024, was called by Buchardt its "masterpiece" and "the peak of [its] capabilities in terms of sound, craftsmanship, and design"; passive 2-way bookshelf speakers handcrafted out of solid oak, a pair costing €3,950 (roughly $4,600).
- Earlier in the year Buchardt introduced the S400 MK3, "a complete redesign from the original S400" with a larger cabinet, new drivers and a new bass-reflex design with a rear-mounted port; a pair starts at $2,400.

## Byline

- Gear Patrol, by Tucker Bowe, Published August 25, 2026, Updated August 25, 2026.

wikis.title: Monitor Audio Silver Series 8G loudspeaker range
wikis.summary: Announcement of Monitor Audio's new Silver Series 8G loudspeakers, listing the models, the driver and crossover changes over the 7G range, and US prices.
wikis.body:
## The range
- "the British hi-fi manufacturer is introducing the next generation of its Silver Series range of loudspeakers, which sits just above the Bronze Series."
- "the all-new Silver Series 8G was created with 'one clear objective: to set a new benchmark for high-fidelity performance at its price point.'"
- "Monitor Audio's all-new Silver Series 8G consists of seven different loudspeaker models: two bookshelf, two floorstanding, one center channel and one on-wall."
- The company claims "the range is as potent as it is flexible, engineered to perform beautifully in any system configuration, and any space."

## Changes over the Silver Series 7G (released in 2021)
- "every Silver Series 8G loudspeaker features a new-and-improved proprietary C-CAM (Ceramic-Coated Aluminium/Magnesium) driver, which now has the latest generation of RST III (Rigid Surface Technology)." The brand says the increased structural rigidity enables "greater accuracy, control and transparency across the entire frequency range."
- "each Silver Series 8G loudspeaker packs an updated C-CAM Gold Dome tweeter, which features an optimized vented rear chamber, a newly engineered shorting ring, and the latest UD Waveguide II technology," claimed to give "smoother, more natural treble reproduction with improved clarity, consistency and dispersion."
- "a new crossover design promising a cleaner, more transparent signal path."
- "a new port technology (inspired by 'the interlocking wing feathers of an owl') to help extend bass."
- "unlike the previous Silver Series 7G, the Silver Series 8G range has an on-wall speaker, which gives home theater enthusiasts more flexibility to create high-performance 5.1-channel systems up through full 7.1.4 Dolby Atmos installations."

## Price and availability
- "As of August 2026, Monitor Audio's Silver Series 8G is now available."
- Finishes: High Gloss Black, Satin White and European Walnut.
- Silver 300 8G floorstanding: $2,600/pair. Silver 500 8G floorstanding: $3,300/pair.
- Silver 50 8G bookshelf: $1,050/pair. Silver 100 8G standmount: $2,000/pair.
- Silver Centre 8G center channel: $1,050. Silver AMS 8G Dolby Atmos modules: $1,200/pair. Silver On-Wall 8G: $575/each.
- Range listed as "STARTS AT $575".

## Other Monitor Audio ranges mentioned
- "Just last month, Monitor Audio introduced a new option for its flagship Hyphn floorstanding loudspeakers, which sell for $99,000/pair. Since their release in 2023, they have come in three standard finishes. But now, customers can customize them in more than 200 colors... These Hyphn (Custom Editions) cost $109,000/pair."
- "Its most entry-level loudspeaker range is the Bronze Series... The 2025-released Bronze Series 7G consists of five loudspeaker models... The range starts at $700."

## Byline
- By Tucker Bowe. Published August 17, 2026; Updated August 17, 2026.

wikis.title: Q Acoustics 3040c floorstanding loudspeakers
wikis.summary: Launch report on Q Acoustics' 3040c compact floorstanding speakers, covering their drivers, cabinet design, finishes, price and full tech specs.
wikis.body:
## Launch

- British audio brand Q Acoustics has launched the 3040c floorstanding loudspeakers, "the final piece to slot into the Q Acoustic 3000c series of loudspeakers", aimed at listeners upgrading from bookshelf speakers without sacrificing living space.
- Price per pair: "$1,099 / GBP 599 / EUR 899". "available now".
- Finishes: Satin Black, Satin White, Pink Oak and Claro Walnut (the pricing section spells the third "Pin Oak").

## Design and technology

- Driver platform: the C3 (pronounced 'C-cubed') Continuous Curved Cone with a mid/bass profile, "touted as a rare breakthrough in loudspeaker driver design because it combines the powerful bass response of a traditional straight conic cone with the midrange clarity and high-frequency control of a flared design". The 3040c uses twin 4.75-inch C3 mid/bass drivers.
- Tweeter inspired by the flagship Concept series: "a floating design that's hermetically sealed and mechanically isolated from the cabinet's baffle"; with a vented inner chamber Q Acoustics claims "ultra-low distortion" and a lower crossover point.
- Point-to-Point bracing fitted to internal cabinet areas prone to low-end vibrations, "designed to deliver a more focused stereo image for a wider and better-controlled soundstage".
- Helmholtz Pressure Equalizer tubes inside the cabinet "so that internal pressures are nullified and frequency response is improved".
- "With no visible joints or bolts, the 3040c has a minimalist aesthetic, fronted by a one-piece satin nickel and satin chrome driver trim."
- Like the larger 3050c, it has "a solid aluminum stabilizer design, with top-adjustable spikes for easy levelling"; the range inherits the 5000 series' low-profile terminal panel with recessed binding posts for placement closer to the wall.

## Tech specs

- Woofer: 2 x 120mm (4.75in). Tweeter: 1 x 22mm (0.9in).
- Frequency response (-6 dB): 43Hz - 30kHz.
- Nominal impedance 6 ohms; minimum impedance 4 ohms.
- Sensitivity (1 m, 2.83 Vrms @ 1kHz): 88dB.
- Recommended amplifier power: 25 - 120W. Crossover frequency: 2.4kHz.
- Effective volume: 26.8 Litres.
- Dimensions (HxWxD): 942 x 285 x 281mm (37.1 x 11.2 x 11.1 inches), including spikes and stabilizer.
- Weight per loudspeaker: 14.6 Kg (32.1 lbs).

wikis.title: Triangle AIO Twin speakers in a new Macassar finish
wikis.summary: Gear Patrol report that French loudspeaker maker Triangle has released its AIO Twin active wireless speaker system in a Macassar finish, available now at $899.
wikis.body:
## The news

- "As of today, Triangle has announced that it's releasing its AIO Twin speaker system in a new finish: Macassar."
- The AIO Twin was "Introduced in 2021" and brings "the company's signature sound to a sub-$1,000 price point."
- Triangle is described as a French loudspeaker specialist.

## The finish

- "The new Macassar finish is inspired by Macassar ebony, an Indonesian hardwood known for its dark brown color and striking golden-yellow stripes."
- "the finish is unique because its appearance changes with the room's lighting or your viewing angle."
- Triangle claims "its interpretation on the AIO Twin reveals a vertical grain in which fine lines with golden highlights run through a rich, dark brown base, creating a natural contrast of great elegance."
- Ships with matching oblong grilles made by Gabriel, "an iconic Scandinavian fabric company" (Danish fabric specialists); Triangle claims the brown grilles complement "the warm tones of the wood veneer, while adding a contemporary touch to the overall design." The magnetic grilles are optional and "can easily be popped off."

## Specifications

- Two bookshelf-sized speakers: one active (housing all the amplification and connections) and one passive.
- Each speaker: two-way design pairing a 1-inch silk dome tweeter and a 5-inch mid-woofer.
- System output: 100 watts of power.
- Wireless: high-resolution streaming over Wi-Fi (up to 24-bit/192kHz), plus Bluetooth.
- Wired: digital and analog inputs; a switchable MM phono preamplifier for connecting a turntable directly; an AUX jack for computer-speaker use; an optical connection for TV use.

## Price and availability

- "Triangle's AIO Twin speaker system in the new Macassar finish is available now from the company's website. It costs $899, the same as other models in traditional finishes."

## Context given

- "In January of this year, Triangle introduced the Capella 2, a second-generation version of its 2024-released wireless speaker system. It features a pair of active bookshelf speakers and a separate streaming hub (which houses all its wireless and wired connections). The system costs $3,500."

## Byline

- By Tucker Bowe. Published August 5, 2026; Updated August 5, 2026.

wikis.title: Pro-Ject Harley-Davidson special-edition turntable
wikis.summary: Report on Pro-Ject's new Harley-Davidson special-edition turntable, its Bar & Shield-shaped chassis, materials and price.
wikis.body:
## Launch

- Austrian hi-fi manufacturer Pro-Ject has added a Harley-Davidson turntable to its Artist Collection, which it has run "Since 2015" and which has included turntables for Elvis, AC/DC, Metallica and The Beatles.
- Pro-Ject claims the turntable "brings the 'mechanical soul' of the open road to your living space" and calls the collaboration a "tribute to iconic motorcycle craftsmanship".

## Design

- The chassis is "shaped like Harley-Davidson's Bar & Shield logo".
- Pro-Ject says it captures "the industrial elegance of a Harley-Davidson cruiser", combining "rugged materials like polished aluminum and stainless steel with a genuine leather mat, reminiscent of a classic bike saddle".
- "The glass platter is a heavy, zero-resonance design."
- It "doesn't have a built-in phono stage, but comes with Pro-Ject's Connect it Phono E 5P/RCA phono cable".

## Price and availability

- "It costs $3,299" - listed as "$3,299 AT PRO-JECT AUDIO SYSTEMS".
- "Pro-Ject hasn't specified how many of these special edition turntables it will produce. But judging by its previous releases, don't expect many."

wikis.title: Pro-Ject E1.2 BT Bluetooth turntable and E1.2 Phono launch
wikis.summary: Forbes report on Pro-Ject Audio Systems adding the Bluetooth E1.2 BT turntable, its hand-painted Colour finishes and a UK-only E1.2 Phono to its E-Line, with prices and specifications.
wikis.body:
## What was launched

- Austria's Pro-Ject Audio Systems "has expanded its E-Line of vinyl turntables with the launch of the E1.2 BT," a Bluetooth turntable bringing "plug-and-play simplicity to playing classic vinyl recordings."
- At the same time Pro-Ject added the E1.2 Phono to the E1.2 range for U.K. buyers.
- Both are based on the E1.2 turntable, "which was introduced in the summer of 2025."

## Pricing and availability

- E1.2 BT: available now, $549 / GBP399 / EUR399 in the three standard finishes.
- The five new Color finishes: $649 / GBP449 / EUR449.
- E1.2 Phono: available now in High Gloss Black, Satin White and Walnut, $449 / GBP319 / EUR359.

## Shared design points

- Handmade in Europe, "made with engineered components and designed for long-term serviceability, including a 25-year spare-parts availability guarantee."
- Tracking force and anti-skating are set at the factory.
- 730g die-cast aluminum platter; pre-adjusted Pro-Ject Pick it MM E cartridge on a precision tonearm; engineered sub-platter and bearing.

## Tech specs (E1.2 BT)

- Speed: 33, 45 (electronic speed change).
- Wow & flutter: 33: +/-0,23%; 45: +/-0,21%. Speed drift: 33: +/-0,7%; 45: +/-0,6%.
- Signal-to-noise: 65dB.
- Effective tonearm length/mass: 218.5mm / 7g; overhang 22mm.
- Platter bearing: stainless steel axle in bronze bushing.
- Bluetooth 5.4; codecs SBC, aptX HD, aptX adaptive; protocol A2DP Source.
- Included: 15V DC / 0,8A power supply, dust cover, 7-inch single adapter.
- Power consumption 4.5W; dimensions (WxHxD) 420 x 112 x 330mm; weight 3.6kg.
- By Mark Sparrow, Senior Contributor.

wikis.title: Pro-Ject E1.2 BT
wikis.summary: Bluetooth 5.4 turntable in the E-Line that transmits vinyl playback wirelessly, priced from $549 / GBP399 / EUR399.
wikis.body:
- "At the heart of the E1.2 BT is a new-generation Qualcomm Bluetooth transmitter module that runs on Bluetooth 5.4 and supports the apt-X HD and apt-X Adaptive audio codecs."
- Can wirelessly transmit vinyl playback to compatible Bluetooth speakers, headphones and amplifiers, including Pro-Ject's own wireless speakers such as the Uni Box S3 or Wireless Box E.
- Has a dedicated pairing button that initiates direct pairing "instead of having to power-cycle the turntable and its Bluetooth module to reconnect."
- Has all the key design and performance features of the Award-winning E1.2: factory-set tracking force and anti-skating, 730g die-cast aluminum platter, pre-adjusted Pro-Ject Pick it MM E cartridge.
- Standard finishes: High Gloss Black, Satin White and Walnut vinyl wraps. Price $549 / GBP399 / EUR399.
- A special E1.2 Colour version comes in hand-painted Satin Black, Satin White, Satin Fir Green, Satin Golden Yellow and Satin Steel Blue, mounted on a CNC-machined MDF chassis "for extra rigidity and resistance to resonances" and designed to complement Pro-Ject's Speaker Box range. Price $649 / GBP449 / EUR449.

wikis.title: Pro-Ject E1.2 Phono
wikis.summary: UK-market E1.2 variant adding a switchable phono preamplifier, priced $449 / GBP319 / EUR359.
wikis.body:
- Added to the E1.2 range for U.K. buyers at the same time as the E1.2 BT launch.
- "Based on the original E1.2 and available in the standard finishes, it adds a switchable high-quality phono preamplifier so the turntable can be connected directly to any line or CD input."
- Available now in High Gloss Black, Satin White and Walnut.
- Price: $449 / GBP319 / EUR359.
- Like the E1.2 and E1.2 BT, handmade in Europe with a 25-year spare-parts availability guarantee.

wikis.title: Kanto Audio Obi3 (Gen 2) turntable
wikis.summary: Gear Patrol article on Kanto Audio's second-generation Obi3 turntable, covering what changed from the original, its specs, accessories and $250 price.
wikis.body:
## The product

- Kanto Audio, "a Canadian hi-fi brand that's best known for its popular powered speaker systems", is introducing the Obi3 (Gen 2), the successor to its first-ever turntable.
- "Last year, in October 2025, the company made waves by introducing its first-ever turntable: the Obi3." It is an entry-level belt-drive turntable with a switchable phono stage and built-in Bluetooth, and "costs just $200".
- The Gen 2 arrives "less than a year later"; the original Obi3 is one "which the company seems to be phasing out".

## Carried over from the original

- Manual belt-drive turntable with a switchable phono stage and built-in Bluetooth, usable with wired and wireless systems, including streaming vinyl to wireless speakers or headphones.
- Same preinstalled moving-magnet cartridge: Audio-Technica AT3600L.
- Same aluminum J-shaped tonearm.
- Finishes: black, white, green, ice blue and walnut.
- Onboard phono preamp gives a direct RCA connection without an external amplifier; adjustable counterweight and dedicated anti-skate control.

## The "Gen 2" upgrades (three notable things)

- Heavier build: still a weighted aluminum platter and engineered wood plinth, but "significantly heavier... to better eliminate unwanted vibrations". The Obi3 weighs 8.6 pounds; the Obi3 (Gen 2) weighs 12.1 pounds.
- Built-in speed sensor on the platter, "designed to measure actual rotation and correct the speed continuously as the record plays".
- Auto-stop feature that "halts the platter at the end of the record to help protect the stylus (and the vinyl)".

## Quote

- Brett Smalley, Director of Marketing, Kanto Audio: "We wanted the 2nd gen of Obi3 to feel like a high-end turntable at an entry-level price. One you can set up, adjust and grow into."

## Accessories

- Kanto Audio is launching a suite of accessories sold separately: various platter mats and cover sleeves, plus cartridge alignment and clean kits.

## Price and availability

- $250, "a $50 price hike compared to the original model".
- "The Kanto Audio Obi3 (Gen 2) is available now. The full range of Kanto's turntable accessories is available now, too."

## Other Kanto context in the article

- "Just this spring, the company rolled out second-generation versions of its Yu4, Yu6 and Tuk ranges, as well as introduced a new flagship powered speaker system named the Tuk Grand. The powered speakers range from $450 to $1,000."

## Byline

- By Tucker Bowe. Published August 13, 2026; updated August 13, 2026.

wikis.title: Marantz CINEMA Series 2 AV receivers announced
wikis.summary: Audioholics preview of Marantz's CINEMA Series 2 AV receiver refresh - the CINEMA 50, 60, 60 DAB and 70s Series 2 - with their new 32-bit DAC, expanded Dirac Live, prices and shipping dates.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- Marantz is "refreshing the heart of its home theater lineup with the new CINEMA Series 2 family."
- Updated lineup: CINEMA 50 Series 2, CINEMA 60 Series 2, CINEMA 60 DAB Series 2 for Europe, and CINEMA 70s Series 2.
- The CINEMA 30 and CINEMA 40 stay "firmly positioned as Marantz's flagship integrated AV receivers" and are not replaced.

## Pricing and availability

- "The Marantz CINEMA Series 2 receivers are scheduled to begin shipping through authorized Marantz dealers on August 12, 2026, with the exception of the slimline CINEMA 70s Series 2, which is expected to arrive on September 15, 2026."
- CINEMA 50 Series 2: $3,000 USD. CINEMA 60 Series 2: $2,000 USD. CINEMA 70s Series 2: $1,500 USD.
- "European customers will also have access to the CINEMA 60 DAB Series 2, which adds integrated DAB radio functionality and is not planned for North America."

## Platform changes across the family

- New 32-bit, eight-channel DAC architecture giving "dedicated simultaneous high-resolution conversion across every audio channel." Marantz says the result is "greater precision, improved imaging, enhanced dynamic expression and more coherent surround performance throughout the listening environment."
- HDMI platform updated to add 1440p video pass-through and AMD FreeSync support.
- Upgraded HEOS streaming platform; enhanced Web Control 2.0 interface.
- Installer tools: HDMI Diagnostics 2.0 and Channel Level Monitoring.
- Full channel preamp outputs continue across the family.
- Every Series 2 receiver "continues to be meticulously tuned by the company's Sound Master," preserving what Marantz calls the Signature Marantz Sound.

## Dirac Live

- Optional Dirac Live Room Correction, "previously reserved for higher tier models," is now available on the CINEMA 60 Series 2, CINEMA 60 DAB Series 2 and CINEMA 70s Series 2.
- The CINEMA 50 Series 2 "continues to offer the full Dirac ecosystem, including Dirac Live Room Correction, Dirac Live Bass Control, and Dirac Live Active Room Treatment (ART)."

## Lineup table as published

| Model | Amplifier Channels | Processing | Dirac Live | MSRP |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CINEMA 50 Series 2 | 9 | 11.4 | Yes, including Bass Control & ART | $3,000 |
| CINEMA 60 Series 2 | 7 | 7.2 | Optional | $2,000 |
| CINEMA 70s Series 2 | 7 (Slimline) | 7.2 | Optional | $1,500 |

## Source note

- By Tony Leotta, August 03, 2026 12:25. The page states: "Unless otherwise indicated, this is a preview article for the featured product. A formal review may or may not follow in the future."
- The article also notes Marantz "recently expanded its two channel lineup with the new MODEL 70 integrated amplifier and CD 70 CD player."

wikis.title: Marantz CINEMA 50 Series 2
wikis.summary: Top model of the Series 2 refresh at $3,000, with nine amplifier channels, 11.4 processing, the full Dirac ecosystem and two exclusive features.
wikis.body:
- MSRP $3,000 USD; shipping from August 12, 2026.
- Nine channels of onboard amplification with support for up to 11.4 channels of processing, for Dolby Atmos, DTS:X and Auro 3D speaker layouts.
- Full Dirac ecosystem: Dirac Live Room Correction, Dirac Live Bass Control and Dirac Live Active Room Treatment (ART).
- New 32-bit, eight-channel DAC architecture; updated power supply capacitors, "while its amplifier topology and power transformers remain largely unchanged."
- Exclusive: Dolby Atmos Channel Expander, which "intelligently utilizes all available speakers when playing compatible channel based Dolby Atmos content."
- Also new: Center Bi Amp Mode, "allowing compatible speakers to dedicate separate amplifier channels to the high and low frequency sections of the center speaker."
- Gains all platform enhancements: upgraded HEOS streaming, 1440p pass-through and AMD FreeSync, Web Control 2.0, HDMI Diagnostics 2.0 and Channel Level Monitoring; full channel preamp outputs.

wikis.title: Marantz CINEMA 60 Series 2
wikis.summary: $2,000 seven-channel receiver that gains optional Dirac Live Ready support for the first time at this tier.
wikis.body:
- MSRP $2,000 USD; shipping from August 12, 2026.
- 7 amplifier channels, 7.2 processing; optional Dirac Live.
- "Perhaps the biggest news is the addition of Dirac Live Ready support" - previous generations required moving higher up the product range.
- Benefits from the new DAC architecture, upgraded HEOS platform, "future Bluetooth LE Audio support," and enhanced gaming compatibility including 1440p video passthrough and AMD FreeSync support.
- A CINEMA 60 DAB Series 2 variant with integrated DAB radio is for Europe only.

wikis.title: Marantz CINEMA 70s Series 2
wikis.summary: Slimline $1,500 receiver arriving September 15, 2026, with the Series 2 platform and optional Dirac Live Room Correction.
wikis.body:
- MSRP $1,500 USD; "expected to arrive on September 15, 2026."
- 7 amplifier channels (slimline), 7.2 processing; optional Dirac Live.
- Carries the new 32-bit, eight-channel DAC architecture, upgraded HEOS platform, enhanced gaming capabilities and expanded connectivity "despite the receiver's smaller footprint."
- "One of the biggest upgrades is the addition of optional Dirac Live Room Correction."
- Has full channel preamp outputs.

wikis.title: Marantz CINEMA 60 DAB Series 2 (Europe)
wikis.summary: European-only variant of the CINEMA 60 Series 2 adding integrated DAB radio.
wikis.body:
- Part of the updated lineup, listed as "CINEMA 60 DAB Series 2 for Europe."
- "European customers will also have access to the CINEMA 60 DAB Series 2, which adds integrated DAB radio functionality and is not planned for North America."
- Included among the models gaining optional Dirac Live Room Correction.
- No separate price is given in the article.

wikis.title: Orange Amps Baby Terror micro amplifier
wikis.summary: Press release announcing Orange Amps' 20-Watt solid-state Baby Terror lunchbox guitar head, its features, launch date and prices.
wikis.body:
## Announcement

- "29th July 2026 - London, UK - Orange Amps announce the release of the 'Baby Terror', an analogue micro-lunchbox addition amplifier to its Baby series."
- Described as "A new 20 Watt-solid-state, analogue, micro-amp with tone shaping, footswitchable volume boost and studio-ready connectivity in an Orange lunchbox format".
- "Delivering 20 Watts of quality Orange sound, in a head built for backpacks, desktops, rehearsal rooms and small stages."

## Controls and features

- Retains Orange's lunchbox footprint, with Gain and Volume alongside "a full three-band EQ and Presence control".
- "Tubby" switch "lets more low end through early in the signal path, adding fullness and body to clean and 'dirty-clean' sounds"; switching Tubby off gives "a leaner, more focused response".
- A second, footswitchable volume for solos or louder passages "without changing their gain or EQ".
- Rear panel: effects loop; balanced line out with ground lift for recording interfaces and live rigs, allowing the preamp signal to be taken into a DAW with impulse responses and plug-ins; 8- and 16-ohm speaker outputs.
- "single ended, class A, JFET front end"; comes with "a quality padded custom-designed protective bag".

## Quote

- Sarah Yule, Managing Director of Orange Amps: "The Baby Terror is proof that small does not have to mean less features. It is small enough to carry with one hand, but serious enough to become your main amp - however big your rig is."

## Launch and pricing

- "The Orange Baby Terror launches globally on Wednesday 29th July 2026."
- Pricing: "UK RRP- GBP 199 / EU SSP - EUR 229 / USA - $249".

wikis.title: Insta360 Luna Pro 8K gimbal camera
wikis.summary: Insta360's product page for the Luna Pro, an 8K gimbal camera with a 1-inch sensor and Leica Summicron lens, listing its imaging features, shooting modes, hardware specs and accessories.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- "Insta360 Luna Pro - 8K Gimbal Camera"; marketing line "Drawn to brilliance."
- Headline features: "8K Gimbal Camera with 1\" Sensor", Leica Summicron Lens with 1" 8K Sensor, 4K60fps Portrait Videos & Live Frame, 4x HighRes Zoom, Detachable 2" OLED Touchscreen, Dual AI Chip, AI-Powered Deep Track & Rapid Focus, 10-bit I-Log.

## Lens and imaging

- Leica Summicron lens: F1.8 aperture, "14 Stops Max. Dynamic Range", 20mm equivalent focal length, minimum focus distance 9cm, 1" sensor.
- 8K Dolby Vision; 4K120fps Slow-Mo.
- "Capture 4K video with up to 4x HighRes Zoom and 2x lossless zoom."
- 4K30fps Vertical Video "with 6K oversampling".
- 37MP UltraPhoto stills, "with the exclusive Leica watermark".
- Built-in Leica color profiles and cinematic filters: Cinematic, Fresh, CC Film, Leica Natural, Leica Chrome, Leica Vivid, Pos Film, Neg Film, NC Film.

## Processing and low light

- Dual AI Chip: "A dedicated imaging chip delivers impeccable low-light performance, while a 4nm flagship chip provides immense processing power for everything else."
- 4K60fps PureVideo Mode reduces noise and enhances detail; "Mini Fill Light keeps portraits bright in extra-dark scenes" ("Mini Fill Light sold separately").

## Screen, tracking and stabilization

- Detachable 2" OLED touchscreen with "HD image transmission up to 20m" and a built-in microphone. (20 m measured with the screen removed and connected via Wi-Fi in an open, unobstructed, interference-free environment.)
- 3-axis stabilization.
- Deep Track 5.0: Auto Tracking, Group Tracking, Smart Framing.
- POV Head Tracker for head-controlled POV footage, with Neck Mount or Backpack Mount ("POV Head Tracker and Neck Mount sold separately. Backpack Mount will be released soon.").
- Sliding Protective Case: "a single pull powers the camera on" (sold separately; listed as "Coming Soon" under accessories).

## Audio

- Pre-installed wind guard; audio modes: Wind Reduction, Voice Enhancement, Original Audio; format 48 kHz, 32-bit, AAC.
- 4 mics (3 on the main gimbal, 1 on the detachable touchscreen).
- Direct wireless connection to two Insta360 Mic Air or Mic Pro transmitters for dual-person recording.

## Post-production and workflow

- 10-bit I-Log, "compatible with ACES workflow"; DaVinci Resolve "natively supports Insta360 I-Log" (requires DaVinci Resolve 21 or later).
- Built-in timecode, "Compatible with Final Cut Pro and Adobe Premiere Pro".
- Instant App Access via NFC; QR Color Share (save looks as QR codes for other Luna users to scan).
- 360 Panorama, Barrel Roll, Timelapse modes; AI-powered auto editing in the Insta360 app.

## Battery and storage

- "The 1550mAh battery supports up to 4 hours of shooting" (run time 240 mins, tested at 77°F/25°C at 1080p24fps with screen and Wi-Fi off).
- Detachable touchscreen battery: 210mAh.
- Charging: "80% in 23 mins, 100% in 35 minutes (15V 3A)" with a PD3.0 PPS certified 45W USB-C charger.
- "47GB of internal storage"; supports microSD cards up to 2TB.

## Key specs

- Gimbal controllable range: Pan -57° to 235°, Tilt -57° to 120°, Roll -50° to 50°; max control speed 210.0°/s; angular vibration range ±0.005°.
- Video: 8K (16:9) 7680x4320@30/25/24fps; 8K (2.35:1) 7680x3264@30/25/24fps; 4K up to 120fps; 1080p up to 240fps.
- Photo: UltraPhoto 37MP (7040x5288, 6144x6144) and 33MP (7680x4320); Standard 9MP/8MP.
- Video coding H.265; max bitrate 120Mbps; color depth video 10-bit, DNG 16-bit; ISO 100-6400; shutter photo 1/8000-30s; white balance 2000-10000K; EV ±4.
- Weight: Cosmic Black 215g (7.6oz), Stellar White 218g (7.7oz). Dimensions 52.8x155.7x38.5mm.
- Colors: Cosmic Black, Stellar White. Operating temperature 32°F to 104°F (0°C to 40°C).
- Wi-Fi 6.0 on the main gimbal, Wi-Fi 4.0 on the touchscreen; Bluetooth BR/EDR/BLE; USB Type-C USB 3.0.

## In the box

- Protective Gimbal Cover, Carry Bag, Insta360 Luna Pro (with Wind Guard), 1/4" Thread Handle, Wrist Strap.

## Accessories listed

- Black Mist Filter, Mini Fill Light, Battery Handle, POV Head Tracker, Neck Mount for Luna Series, Sliding Protective Case (Coming Soon).

## Comparison shown on the page

- A dual-lens sibling model is compared: it adds a "Pro-Grade Telephoto Lens with 1/1.3\" Sensor", "Up to 12x Zoom with 6x lossless zoom", "Dual Pro Imaging Chips + 4nm AI Chip" (Triple AI Chip) and "200MP Scenic Panorama", weighs Cosmic Black 233g (8.2oz) / Stellar White 235g (8.3oz), and lacks the 4K30fps Vertical Video Mode and 4K60fps Portrait Videos.

## Service plans mentioned

- Insta360 FlexiCare: "up to four low-cost replacements over two years, plus free shipping and global coverage".
- Insta360 Extended Warranty: "one extra year of protection against quality defects on top of your official warranty".

wikis.title: Insta360 X6 360 camera announced with larger sensors, native 8K and Dolby Vision
wikis.summary: DPReview's announcement coverage of the Insta360 X6 flagship 360 camera, with its sensors, video modes, design, battery, AI editing tools, accessories, price and on-sale date.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- Insta360 has announced the X6, its latest flagship 360 camera.
- Updates include Type 1/1.1 (101 mm2) square sensors, native 8K/50 with 10-bit color, in-camera Dolby Vision and a new body design.
- "The camera also marks 10 years of 360-degree cameras for the company."

## Sensors and processing

- Two custom square Type 1/1.1 (101 mm2) Sony sensors, one per lens; Insta360 says they are 33% larger than the Type 1/1.28 (76 mm2) sensors in the X5.
- Lenses keep the same F2.0 aperture as the predecessor; Insta360 says the larger sensors mean better performance "in challenging lighting situations, such as low light and backlight".
- Insta360 says the camera has 500% more computing power than the X5 while using 35% less power, thanks to a new 8-core processor; each sensor has a dedicated image processing chip.
- In-camera Dolby Vision, which Insta360 says is a first on a 360 camera; 10-bit I-Log profile also available.

## Video and stills

- Framed as a "3-in-1 device".
- Native 8K/50 capture allows in-camera reframing and subject-tracking to flat 4K after the fact.
- Single-lens mode: up to 5K/60, or 4K/120 for slow motion.
- Stills: 120MP 360 photos at 2:1 aspect ratio, or 42MP flat photos with a square aspect ratio.

## Design and durability

- Noticeably shorter body than previous X-series cameras, "though it's still not as squat as the DJI Osmo 360 or GoPro Max2 360"; buttons at the bottom of the camera removed.
- 2.32" OLED display with 1200 nits peak brightness.
- Fast charge from empty to 80% in 24 minutes; records 140 minutes of 8K/30 footage on a charge, "47 more than the X5 at equivalent settings".
- IP68 rating; waterproof to 20m (66') without a case, 5m (16') more than its predecessor; up to 60m (197') with the company's dive housing.
- Replaceable lenses "now even more scratch-resistant and 60% cheaper to replace than the previous generation".
- Rated for -20C to 40C (-4F to 104F).
- Ships with 64GB of storage, "though only 47GB of that is usable".

## AI editing and cloud tools

- AI modes powered by PanoMind, which Insta360 says is "the first 360-native AI model", trained on 10,000 hours of footage across more than 30 scenarios.
- AI Director builds a highlight edit on the camera itself rather than the cloud when it is plugged in to charge; footage then goes to the Insta360 app.
- Moments Pro, a cloud-side tool built with Google Gemini, lets users describe the edit they want by setting subject, mood, style and timeframe.

## Accessories

- Works with more than 100 accessories; shares the magnetic mounting ecosystem with the X5, X4 and Ace series.
- Accessories named: Power Selfie Stick (adds a promised 180 minutes of runtime), Foldable Selfie Stick Remote with a joystick, a dedicated motorcycle mount, a charging case.
- Activity features: holographic speed overlay and automatic license plate blur for motorcyclists; cycling stats overlays from Garmin and Apple Watch.

## Price and availability

- "The Insta360 X6 goes on sale August 12 at the Insta360 official store, Amazon and authorized retailers for a starting price of $700 for the standard bundle."

## Page data

- By Abby Ferguson, published August 12, 2026.

wikis.title: DJI Mic Mini 2S global launch on August 4, 2026
wikis.summary: Imaging Resource report on DJI teasing the worldwide launch of the Mic Mini 2S wireless microphone on August 4, 2026, with internal 32-bit float recording and four-transmitter support.
wikis.body:
## Launch

- "DJI has officially teased the global launch of the **Mic Mini 2S**, confirming that its latest compact wireless microphone system will debut worldwide on **August 4, 2026**."
- "DJI has scheduled the global announcement for **August 4 at 12:00 PM GMT**."
- The microphone "was first introduced in China earlier this month and now appears ready for international markets".
- The teaser is captioned "Capture Every Detail" and shows the Mic Mini 2S with its new multi-color magnetic front cover.

## Internal recording

- Each transmitter includes **14.5GB of internal memory**, allowing it to record "even if the connection to the receiver is interrupted".
- Onboard storage supports both **24-bit** and **32-bit float** recording.
- "DJI says each transmitter can store up to **28 hours** of audio when recording in the default 24-bit format."
- 32-bit float "provides substantially greater dynamic range", at the trade-off of larger file sizes.

## Four transmitters

- Support for **up to four transmitters** connected to a single receiver simultaneously; "Previously, this capability was exclusive to the more expensive **DJI Mic 3**".
- The receiver has **four status indicator lights**, versus two on the original Mic Mini 2 receiver.
- Backward compatibility: the new Mic Mini 2S transmitters work with the original Mic Mini receiver.

## Design

- Each transmitter weighs **under 12 grams**.
- Redesigned magnetic front covers, "which are not interchangeable with those from the base Mic Mini 2".
- Added **haptic feedback** confirming when recording starts.

## Price and availability

- Priced at **HK$1,299 (approximately $165 USD at current exchange rates)**.
- "Availability in the United States remains uncertain, as the original Mic Mini 2 was never officially released in the U.S. market."
