wikis.title: Costed proposals published for restoring the Palace of Westminster
wikis.summary: UK Parliament news item announcing the R&R Client Board's costed proposals report, recommending seven years of phase one works capped at GBP 3bn and narrowing long-term delivery options to two.
wikis.body:
## The publication

- "Today, Parliament's Restoration and Renewal (R&R) Client Board has published its report 'Delivering restoration and renewal of the Palace of Westminster: the costed proposals', with recommendations on the way forward."
- Dated 5 February 2026.
- "The report, including alternative formats, and summary versions (including large print and audio) are available to read online."

## Case for acting

- The Palace of Westminster is "a place of work for thousands of people and a destination for more than a million visitors every year".
- "Most of the building dates from the Victorian era and some parts are much older. Over the decades, its fabric and its services have deteriorated and require substantial repair or replacement. We are beyond the point where putting off these major works is sustainable."
- "A decision is needed now on starting restoration work."
- The Board notes "the very high costs involved in an infrastructure programme of this scale, complexity and duration" and says the Programme "will continue to have due regard to any advice from the National Audit Office, Public Accounts Committee, and HM Treasury."
- It says the work "will bring significant economic benefits, supporting thousands of jobs and apprenticeships, and unlocking opportunities for businesses, from modern construction specialists to traditional craftspeople, in every nation and every region of the UK."

## Phase one works

- Recommendation "to both Houses to agree initial phase one works over seven years, capped at GBP 3bn."
- "This work would commence this year" and includes:
  - building temporary Chamber(s) and office space to support future moves
  - preparations for the restoration of the medieval Cloister Court
  - interior refurbishment of Victoria Tower
  - starting underground construction
  - building a river jetty for construction deliveries
- Purpose: "to build momentum and provide a strong foundation for later phases of the Programme"; described as "a pragmatic way forward in line with emerging best practice."

## Reducing the delivery options

- The Client Board "recommends that now is the time to reduce the number of long-term delivery options to two to bear down on costs and enable further focused development of the 'full decant' and 'enhanced maintenance and improvement+ (EMI+)' options while the phase one works get underway."
- Members of both Houses will be asked to make a final decision on the preferred model "no later than 2030".

## Signatories

- Judith Cummins MP and Lord McFall of Alcluith, Co-chairs of the R&R Client Board.
- Footnote: "Lord McFall, as the former Lord Speaker, was co-Chair of the Client Board until 03.02.26, with the report approved during his tenure."

wikis.title: Restoration and Renewal of the Palace of Westminster: strategic case and costed proposals
wikis.summary: House of Commons Library briefing on the Restoration and Renewal Programme, setting out the Client Board's February 2026 costed proposals, the two shortlisted approaches, costs, timescales and governance history.
wikis.body:
## The briefing

- Research Briefing "Restoration and Renewal: Developing the strategic case and costed proposals", House of Commons Library, by Richard Kelly. "Published Tuesday, 28 April, 2026". Full report is a 964KB PDF.
- Summary line: "The Client Board has proposed preparatory building works before a decision on how to proceed with restoration and renewal of the Palace of Westminster in 2030."

## The costed proposals (February 2026)

- The Client Board's report "Delivering restoration and renewal of the Palace of Westminster: the costed proposals" "was published on 5 February 2026" and "set out the costs and timescale of four approaches".
- The Client Board recommended both Houses be asked to approve a package of "phase one" preparatory works and to reduce the approaches for the "phase two" works to two.
- "The Client Board said the preparatory work was expected to take seven years and cost GBP 3 billion."
- The two approaches to be developed further:
  - "a full decant of the Palace - both Houses move out of the Palace of Westminster to allow the works to be undertaken"
  - "an enhanced maintenance and improvement approach (EMI+), which would allow the House of Commons to remain in the Palace throughout the works. The House of Lords would be decanted and MPs would be decanted to the House of Lords Chamber for two years while work was undertaken on the Commons Chamber."
- If agreed, that "would require a subsequent and final decision on a single preferred option once more detailed design, cost, timescale and risk information is available, no later than mid-2030. Under this approach, the earliest the Houses would begin to be decanted from the Palace is 2032".

## Costs and timescales of the two recommended approaches

| | Full decant | EMI+ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Total cost** | GBP 8.4-11.5 bn | GBP 11.8-18.7 bn |
| Total duration | 19-24 years | 38-61 years |
| HC decant period | 8-10 years | up to two years* |
| HL decant period | 12-15 years | 8-13 years |

\* to the House of Lords Chamber. \*\* Total programme costs (including optimism bias and risk but excluding inflation and opportunities).

- "Not making a decision on the R&R Programme has its own costs": the estimated cost of delaying the start of the delivery phase is "around GBP 70m per year at current prices", plus "GBP 250m to GBP 350m in the inflationary impact on construction costs across the whole of the Programme for each year a decision is not made".

## Governance history

- "In 2019 legislation established the Parliamentary Works Sponsor Body to oversee the Programme."
- January 2022: initial estimates presented by the Sponsor Body of "GBP 7 billion to GBP 13 billion, taking 19 to 28 years, with a decant lasting 12 to 20 years".
- 2022: the Commissions proposed a new approach in a joint report "Restoration and Renewal of the Palace of Westminster - a new mandate" (June 2022); "Both Houses endorsed the recommendations in July 2022." The Sponsor Body was abolished and its functions transferred to the Corporate Officers (the Clerks) of the two Houses; staff moved to the Restoration and Renewal Client Team.
- "The Parliamentary Works Sponsor Body (Abolition) Regulations 2022 came into force on 1 January 2023."
- The Commissions, meeting as a Client Board, are "responsible for making critical strategic choices and recommendations relating to the restoration and renewal of the Palace of Westminster", advised by a separate Programme Board.

## Developing and shortlisting options

- The Delivery Authority developed "Six outcome levels for the scope of works (the 'what') ... alongside six representative construction scenarios (the 'how')", producing "thirty-six delivery options".
- At its meeting on 20 June 2023 the Programme Board agreed a shortlist of "a full decant and phased return (Construction Scenario C)" and "a continuous presence option, 'under which the House of Commons Chamber would remain within the Palace, but may temporarily be required to sit in the Lords Chamber (subject to the Lords agreement)' (Construction Scenario F)", both delivering "Outcome Level 4" (agreed 5 June 2023).
- Nigel Evans, Chair of the Programme Board, wrote that "we unanimously agreed to shortlist one outcome level with delivery through two potential construction scenarios", considering "speed, safety, and value for money".
- July 2023: the Client Board endorsed the shortlist and "requested that a fallback option of enhanced maintenance and improvement forms part of further detailed design work". In November 2023 it asked for a more comprehensive description of the EMI option.
- The "Restoration and Renewal Client Board: Strategic Case" was "published on 19 March 2024" without costed proposals, concluding "further detailed work should be undertaken on the shortlisted scope for R&R, and the continued presence and full decant options identified for achieving this".
- In December 2025 Sir Alan Campbell, Leader of the House of Commons, confirmed a report would come "early in the new year (2026)" and said "We will bring forward a motion on the report".

## Temporary accommodation

- On 20 June 2023 the Programme Board "provisionally agreed that the QEII Conference Centre remains the preferred decant location for the House of Lords"; it is on Broad Sanctuary, close to the Palace of Westminster.
- On 24 October 2023 it agreed Richmond House "should be recommended to the Client Board as the preferred location for any House of Commons temporary Chamber for the full decant delivery option", with temporary accommodation at Richmond House and the Norman Shaw buildings considered for a contingency Commons Chamber under continued presence.
- The costed proposals confirmed these proposals and that "a Commons Chamber would be built in Richmond House": under full decant MPs would meet there; under EMI+ "it would provide resilience and could be used for an unplanned decant of the current Commons Chamber".

wikis.title: 520 Fifth Avenue supertall tops out in Midtown Manhattan
wikis.summary: New York YIMBY construction update reporting that the 88-story, 1,002-foot 520 Fifth Avenue by KPF and Rabina has topped out, with its program, interiors, sales and completion date.
wikis.body:
## Topping out

- "Construction has topped out on 520 Fifth Avenue, an 88-story residential supertall in Midtown, Manhattan."
- Designed by Kohn Pedersen Fox, developed by Rabina; the 1,002-foot-tall structure "will span 415,000 square feet".
- Program: 100 condominium units, a residents-only amenity floor on level 88, 25 boutique office floors, a private members-only club called Moss, and four cellar levels.
- Suffolk is the general contractor. Located at the corner of Fifth Avenue and West 43rd Street, one block north of Bryant Park.
- "The final stories and bulkhead of the reinforced concrete superstructure were formed since our last update in July, when the building was roughly 70 percent built."
- Recent photos show wooden formwork being disassembled from the stepped crown, and the terracotta facade and "signature grid of arched windows steadily climbing up all four sides". Some terracotta panels have begun installation around the lower arched windows at the base.

## Quote

- Josh Rabina, president and CEO of Rabina: "We are thrilled to celebrate the topping out of 520 Fifth Avenue, which is a remarkable achievement not only for our team at Rabina, but for all of the enormously talented and dedicated individuals involved and hopefully also for New York City... This tower will stand as a symbol of the continual renaissance of Midtown, Manhattan, honoring its past and offer a new blueprint for how we as New Yorkers live, work, and enjoy life in the center of one of the world's most iconic neighborhoods."

## Residences

- Condominium units start on the 42nd floor, in one- to four-bedroom layouts.
- Charles & Co. is interior designer; ceiling heights between 10 to 14 feet and white oak wide-plank floors.
- Kitchens: brand-name appliances, ribbed walnut islands, white lacquer cabinetry, luminous quartzite slab countertops and backsplashes.
- Baths: custom vanities with marble countertops, herringbone marble flooring, polished nickel fixtures by Waterworks.
- Penthouse residences offer full-floor layouts with 360-degree views.
- Corcoran Sunshine Marketing Group is managing sales, "which launched in April with prices starting at $1.7 million".
- The sales gallery is in the Art Deco crown of 500 Fifth Avenue, across West 43rd Street from the project.

## Amenities and offices

- The Penthouse 88 amenity suite on the 88th floor will include a glass-walled solarium, lounge, dining room, billiards table, library, game room and 360-degree views.
- The 25 full-floor office spaces will have ceiling spans of over 12 feet, arched 10-foot-square operable windows, and large private terraces or loggias on most floors; floor plates "are expected to range from 6,000 to 12,000 square feet". JLL handles leasing and marketing for the commercial space.
- A two-story portico at the base will have three separate lobbies for the residences, office space and the Moss private members club.

## Transit

- Nearest subways: B, D, F, M and 7 trains at 42nd Street-Bryant Park/Fifth Avenue; also close to Grand Central-42nd Street (4, 5, 6, 7 and Shuttle) plus Metro-North and Long Island Rail Road at Grand Central Terminal and Grand Central Madison.

## Completion

- "520 Fifth Avenue's completion date is posted on the construction board for June 1, 2026."

## Byline

- By Michael Young and Matt Pruznick, 8:00 AM on October 25, 2024; photos by Michael Young, renderings courtesy of Binyan Studios.

wikis.title: Chongqing East Railway Station, described as the world's largest railway station
wikis.summary: FTNnews report on Chongqing East Railway Station, which China says is the world's largest railway station, covering 1.22 million square metres and opened to passengers in 2025.
wikis.body:
## The station
- "China has opened what it says is the world's largest railway station, a vast new hub in the city of Chongqing that covers 1.22 million square metres, or about 170 football fields."
- "Chongqing East Railway Station began full operations on 27 June 2025 after about seven years of construction."
- Designed to handle 300,000 passengers a day; built as both a transport interchange and a business centre.
- 15 platforms and 29 tracks, with direct metro links to the wider city.
- The footprint "is said to be twice the size of the Vatican and larger than 170 football fields".
- It sits on the outskirts of the 10 million population metropolis of Chongqing.

## Timeline
- Planning began in 2011, when China Railway carried out logistics analysis for the site.
- Construction started in 2018; main works were completed in spring 2024; the station opened to passengers in 2025.

## Materials
- 2 million cubic metres of concrete and 366,000 tonnes of steel.

## Design and services
- Designed to resemble an airport terminal rather than a traditional train station.
- Intended for high-speed rail services only, "a choice that officials say should help improve efficiency despite a smaller number of platforms than some older intercity stations".
- Journey times expected from the hub: Beijing and Shanghai about 6 hours, Wuhan 3 hours, Wanzhou and Qianjiang about 1 hour.

## Context the article gives
- "Officials say the site reflects China's continued investment in high-speed rail as an alternative to short-haul flights."

## Byline
- By Vedat Ozgur Tore, May 12, 2026.

wikis.title: First runway of San Miguel's New Manila International Airport seen ready in 2028
wikis.summary: Inquirer report on San Miguel Corp. saying the first runway of the New Manila International Airport in Bulacan stays on track for 2028 while the passenger terminal and logistics center slip.
wikis.body:
## Runway schedule

- San Miguel Corp. (SMC) said the first runway of its New Manila International Airport (NMIA) project in Bulacan "could be completed ahead of schedule."
- SMC chair and CEO Ramon Ang, speaking at the company's annual stockholders' meeting on Tuesday: "We are on track to finish the first runway for 2028. In fact, it can even be earlier."
- Ang said SMC expects the first runway to be ready "by at least the second quarter of 2028," allowing airport operations to commence even if other components are still being completed.
- The runway is currently undergoing surcharging, "a process used to prepare reclaimed land before major infrastructure is built on it."

## Terminal and logistics center delays

- Ang: "What will delay us a bit is the passenger terminal and the logistics center."
- The logistics center sits in Phase 9 of the project, an area needing around 7 million cubic meters of sand for land development.
- That work was originally targeted for completion in 2025 but "is now expected to be finished by the end of 2026."

## Funding

- SMC sought to raise up to P30 billion through a preferred share offering, part of it earmarked for the Bulacan airport project.
- The company filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission a registration statement covering 266.67 million Series 2 preferred shares priced at P75 each, plus an oversubscription option of up to 133.33 million additional shares.
- Per the prospectus, as much as P5 billion of the base offer proceeds goes to SMC's infrastructure business within a year; the bulk of the funds will refinance existing obligations.

## Context given

- NMIA is "among the country's largest infrastructure developments" and is expected to help decongest the aging Ninoy Aquino International Airport.
- Once completed, NMIA "is expected to become one of the country's largest gateways," a hub for passenger and cargo traffic.
- By Emmanuel John B. Abris, Philippine Daily Inquirer.

wikis.title: MTA Board approves $68.4 billion 2025-2029 Capital Plan for resubmission
wikis.summary: Railway Age report that, after the New York State budget funded it, the MTA Board approved its $68.4 billion 2025-2029 Capital Plan on May 28 for resubmission to the Capital Program Review Board.
wikis.body:
## What happened

- "Following passage of funding for the Metropolitan Transportation Authority's 2025-2029 Capital Plan in the New York State budget, the MTA on May 28 reported that its Board has approved a proposed plan to be resubmitted to the MTA Capital Program Review Board in Albany."
- The $68.4 billion plan "continues to be 'a historic investment in state of good repair work'" and includes "targeted investments" to rebuild, improve and expand the MTA system of subways, buses, commuter railroads, bridges and tunnels.
- The plan was informed by the MTA's Twenty-Year Needs Assessment.

## Work already started

- MTA Construction & Development (MTA C&D) "is ready to hit the ground running and deliver this capital work better, faster, and cheaper following final approval of the capital plan".
- "Nearly half of work in the proposed plan has been initiated through internal processes at MTA C&D."
- Initial work already begun on: modern signaling along the Fulton and Liberty lines on the A and C; the preliminary design phase of the Interborough Express; resiliency efforts on Metro-North Railroad's Hudson Line.

## Other investments in the proposed plan

- An order of 2,000 railcars, including 1,500 for New York City Transit and 500 for Metro-North and Long Island Rail Road.
- Making 60 stations accessible.
- Modernizing 75 miles of signals.
- Installing modern fare gates at 150 stations.
- Overhauling the Grand Central Artery, "a four-mile stretch that carries 98% of all MNR service".
- Updating customer information screens, enhancing security elements, rebuilding more than 80 power stations, and upgrading train shops and yards.

## Quotes

- MTA Chair and CEO Janno Lieber: "Credit to everyone at the MTA who worked so hard to get us to this milestone."
- CFO Kevin Willens: "I'm thrilled to report to the Board that we have funding to move forward on the $68.4 billion 2025-2029 Capital Plan... Funding transit, whether operating or capital should be treated like a core government service like water, sanitation and healthcare."
- Co-CFO Jai Patel: "Today [May 28] marks a major milestone for the MTA. Having a fully funded capital plan protects the operating budget because it reduces the risk of additional borrowing."
- MTA C&D President Jamie Torres-Springer: "This is the most rigorously vetted capital plan in MTA history, and we're ready to deliver better, faster, and cheaper."

## In-house delivery and savings

- Since the Board approved an initial proposed plan, C&D "has revaluated which work can be moved in-house resulting in significant cost savings".
- The in-house team "has proven its capabilities by building out its platform barrier construction and installation work": MTA New York City Transit has installed barriers at 19 stations so far this year and "remains on track to install barriers at 100 stations by year's end".
- Additional in-house capital plan work includes "component work" at stations, substations, shops and yards.
- In MTA C&D's 2024 Year in Review and 2025 Strategic Plan, "the agency found it had saved $3 billion on capital project delivery in its first five years".
- Those savings let the proposed 2025-2029 plan "deliver far more for riders than previous capital plans, while costing 4% less in inflation-adjusted dollars than the current 2020-2024 Capital Plan".

## Byline

- Written by Marybeth Luczak, Executive Editor, Railway Age, May 29, 2025.

wikis.title: National Gas investment at Peterborough Compressor Station
wikis.summary: News report on National Gas's GBP 350 million UK investment in hydrogen-ready gas compressors, including new equipment at its Peterborough station creating 100 jobs.
wikis.body:
## The investment

- "New plans have been unveiled for a multi-million pound investment to upgrade and install new vital gas compressors at Peterborough's National Gas Compressor Station in a move that will create 100 jobs."
- "National Gas has announced a GBP 350 million investment in the UK with new equipment to be installed at its site in Gasworks Road, Peterborough, as well as at two others across the country."
- "The move will support 1,000 jobs in the UK."

## Suppliers and technology

- New equipment "will be manufactured by Siemens Energy, Baker Hughes and Solar Turbines, and installed by Murphy and United Living Infrastructure Services".
- "It is specifically designed to be hydrogen-ready"; the new compressors "will operate using natural gas today but are fully prepared for the transition to hydrogen and natural gas blends".

## The visit

- The announcement was made during a visit to the Peterborough site by Industry Minister Sarah Jones MP, who toured the facility with Peterborough MP Andrew Pakes, North West Cambridgeshire MP Sam Carling and Peterborough City Council Leader Cllr Dennis Jones.

## Local context

- "ARU Peterborough is already working on plans for a clean energy centre and Peterborough College has recently built its new Green Technology Centre to train the next generation in green skills and apprenticeships."

## Quotes

- Andrew Pakes MP: "Peterborough is fast becoming the King's Cross of hydrogen - a hub where innovation, infrastructure and ambition meet." and "National Gas's investment is a landmark moment for our constituency, laying the groundwork for a cleaner, greener energy network."
- Sam Carling MP: "This major investment by National Gas marks a vital step toward our clean energy future."
- Jon Butterworth, chief executive of National Gas: "Today's announcement is a major milestone for our business - signalling the end of the hard-working gas compressors that have given us over six decades' of service and ushering in a new dawn under those that will power our net zero future." He said the investment "will allow our world-class gas National Transmission System to maintain Great Britain's energy security, complementing our renewable energy mix to provide power to power stations, industries and businesses long after we achieve clean power in 2030".
- Industry Minister Sarah Jones: "National Gas' investment will support jobs while strengthening the resilience of our gas network, which will be crucial as we work towards achieving clean power by 2030." and "As part of our Plan for Change, gas will continue to play a role to ensure security of supply, alongside clean, homegrown power."

wikis.title: Nuuk Airport opens its new 2200m runway
wikis.summary: Flightradar24 report on the inauguration of Nuuk Airport's new 2200m runway in Greenland on 28 November 2024, the first Air Greenland arrival, and the new routes it enables.
wikis.body:
## The opening

- Bullets on the page: "Nuuk inaugurates new 2200m runway"; "The new runway will allow large jets to land for first time"; "Safety upgrades: new runway also includes ILS and AFIS".
- "Just months after Nuuk Airport (GOH | BGGH) unveiled its new terminal, Greenland's capital is inaugurating its new 2200m runway, a major shift in the country's aviation landscape."
- "The new, lengthened runway will enable large jets to land in Nuuk for the first time. Prior to this, all international jet flights operated out of Kangerlussuaq (SFJ | BGSF) to the north."
- The old 950m runway "did not allow large passenger aircraft to operate in Nuuk. The short length and lack of precision instrument guidance limited flights to aircraft like the Dash 8."

## First landing

- "When the new runway officially opens on 28 November, it will of course be Air Greenland's A330-800neo 'Tuukkaq' that will be the first to land."
- Flight GL781 is scheduled to depart Copenhagen at 10:45 local time (09:45 UTC), arriving in Nuuk at 12:35 local (14:35 UTC).
- The return flight to Copenhagen will depart Nuuk at 14:35 local time (16:35 UTC).

## New routes

- Icelandair "is set to increase service in 2025, upgauging its flights from Reykjavik to the Boeing 737-8 MAX for the summer season".
- SAS "will also offer service in the summer season between Nuuk and Copenhagen, scheduled for three flights per week".
- United Airlines "will become the first American carrier to operate flights to Nuuk when it launches service from Newark in June 2025".

## Construction

- Construction began in 2019; "one of the major challenges was keeping the airport operational for the duration of the project".
- The first phase focused on the southern portion of the new runway, opened at the same declared length as the old runway; work then shifted to the northern section to complete the expansion from 950m to 2200m.
- "In total, nearly 6 million cubic meters of rock were moved to support the airport's construction."

## Air Greenland

- CEO Jacob Nitter Sørensen: "Nuuk Airport will be the new hub for international and domestic flights to the entire country, where passengers will change planes depending on their final destination, just as we see today in Kangerlussuaq."
- The airline spent the days prior to 28 November moving staff and equipment from Kangerlussuaq to Nuuk after the final flight to Copenhagen departed.
- The article notes an earlier 2021 interview with Aviaaja Karlshøj Knudsen, Executive Project Director at Kalaallit Airports.

## Article details

- By Ian Petchenik. Published: November 28, 2024; Updated: November 29, 2024.

wikis.title: Queensland Premier says Paradise Dam will be rebuilt
wikis.summary: Bundaberg Today report (paywalled after the opening) that the Queensland State Government is holding to its promise to rebuild Paradise Dam, citing $59.8 million set aside.
wikis.body:
## What the accessible part says

- Headline: "Premier Says Paradise Dam Will Be Rebuilt", Bundaberg Today, 07/07/2026.
- Opening line: "The State Government is holding firm to their promise to rebuild Paradise Dam highlighting the 59.8 MIllion Dollars set aside" (text cut off at this point).
- Photo caption: "Premier David Crisafulli with Isis Mill Chair Shaun Tobin and Burnett MP Stephen Bennett discussing the rebuild of Paradise Dam. (Matt Gees)".

## Note

- The rest of the article is behind a subscriber wall ("Subscribe or Login to see the rest of the content"), so only the headline, date, caption and first line were available.

wikis.title: One Wall Street, New York City's largest office-to-condo conversion, prepares to open
wikis.summary: Bloomberg report that Harry Macklowe's 566-unit One Wall Street conversion in the Financial District will take its first residents in early March 2023.
wikis.body:
## The project

- One Wall Street is "the largest office-to-condo conversion in New York City history".
- Developer: Macklowe Properties, Harry Macklowe's firm.
- 566 units, in a landmarked Art Deco office tower.
- The building is the former Irving Trust headquarters at Broadway and Wall Street, constructed in 1931.
- It "spans a block along Broadway and is home to a Whole Foods Market".

## Timing

- "The first move-ins are scheduled for early March" — the building "will get its first residents next month".
- The conversion followed "five years of renovations".

## Finishes

- The tower is "now full of marble kitchens and baths, herringbone floors and — in a sign of how workplaces have changed — home offices".

## Context given

- The opening comes "just as developers and policymakers turn their attention to repurposing more commercial buildings".

## Byline

- By Jennifer Epstein, February 23, 2023, 4:00 PM UTC. Photographer: Colin Miller.

wikis.title: One Times Square completes its $500 million renovation
wikis.summary: New York YIMBY's report that One Times Square has finished its $500 million gut renovation, with a new observation deck and the new Waterford Constellation Ball used for the 2026 New Year's Eve drop.
wikis.body:
## The building

- "Last night, Times Square rang in the New Year with the dropping of a new ball above **One Times Square**, a **26-story** commercial tower that recently completed its **$500 million renovation** at **1475 Broadway**."
- Designed by **S9 Architecture**, developed by **Jamestown**; **SLCE Architects** was architect of record.
- The project "involved a full gut renovation and re-cladding of the **395-foot-tall** steel-framed structure, the addition of new LED displays, and the construction of an outdoor public observation deck".
- The site is a trapezoidal plot bounded by West 43rd Street (north), West 42nd Street (south), Broadway (east) and Seventh Avenue (west).
- "The remainder of the new LED billboards were installed since our last update in **late August**, including the modernized **Zipper** news ticker above the ground floor." A secondary digital ticker was added along the Broadway elevation above the Times Square-42nd Street subway entrance and the viewing deck access doors.

## The observation deck

- YIMBY attended a preview opening "last month" to tour the new public-facing spaces.
- Visitors enter along Broadway, climb to the second floor, then take an external glass elevator to the **19th floor**.
- That floor holds an installation of **7-foot numbers** from the previous New Year's Eve countdown and the mini crystal sphere used to launch the 60-second countdown.
- The outdoor viewing platform "cantilevers on all four sides and is lined with glass railings"; a **glass floor** at the southeastern corner lets visitors look straight down.

## The Waterford Constellation Ball

- The **ninth iteration** of the New Year's Eve ball.
- **12.5-foot diameter**, weighs **12,350 pounds**, covered in **5,280 handcrafted circular glass crystals** in three sizes: **Infinite Beginnings at 1.5 inches**, **Infinite Light at 3 inches**, **Infinite Joy at 4 inches** - each embedded with a distinct geometric pattern and attached to round metal "pucks" fitted with LED lights.
- Waterford used triangular crystals in previous years.
- "A subsequent visit on **December 30** brought multiple photographers and news outlets to the 26th-floor roof of One Times Square, where the ball was lit and tested several times."
- The year numerals "were also upgraded with **594 new LED light pucks**".
- New Years Eve 2026 "will build upon the birth of America and Waterford's Infinite Edition series with three new crystal designs called **Infinite Life, Infinite Liberty, and Infinite Happiness**", a nod to "life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness".

## America250 relighting

- **America250**, "a nonpartisan organization created by Congress, relit the ball shortly after midnight to recognize the upcoming semi-quincentennial celebration of America on **July 4, 2026**".
- "The post-midnight spectacle was the first of its kind for Times Square since the ball drop began in **1907**", marked by red, white and blue confetti, with the 2026 numbers and Waterford crystal ball illuminated in patriotic colors.

## Tickets and access

- Standard tickets start at **$37**, plus a **$3** online booking fee, giving access to the 360-degree viewing deck only.
- A **$220** experience adds an up-close view and photo opportunity with the Waterford Constellation Ball and includes commemorative 2025 crystals.
- Timed-entry ticket required, online only. Hours Monday to Sunday, **noon to 8:00PM**, "but can change seasonally and vary by ticket experience".
- One Times Square sits directly above the Times Square-42nd Street station, served by the 1, 2, 3, 7, N, Q, R, W and the Shuttle to Grand Central Terminal.

wikis.title: Sydney Metro City and Southwest line opens after two-week delay
wikis.summary: International Railway Journal report that Sydney's automated Metro City and Southwest line opened to passengers on August 19, two weeks later than planned, after a signalling failure on the Metro Northwest Line.
wikis.body:
## Opening

- Sydney's Metro City and Southwest automated metro line "opened to passengers on August 19, two weeks after the original opening date of August 4."
- A major signalling system failure in July on the Metro Northwest Line, which connects with the new line, "led to a thorough review of the new infrastructure and postponement of opening to passengers."

## Regulator

- The Office of the National Rail Safety Regulator (ONRSR) "had already voiced concerns about the time allocated for it to check the safety of the project, including a stretch of connecting line."
- ONRSR "has now signed off" the line.
- New South Wales transport minister Ms Jo Haylen welcomed the regulator's decision.

## The line

- Cost given as $A 21.6bn ($US 14.1bn).
- 15.5 km, connecting Chatswood with Sydenham via a city centre tunnel under Sydney Harbour.
- Six new stations, served by a fleet of 45 new trains.
- "The new line will move up to 17,000 passengers in each direction per hour in the morning peak."

## Article details

- Written by Tony Duboudin; dated August 16, 2024.
- Related earlier stories listed: "Sydney Metro City and Southwest metro line opening delayed" (August 2, 2024), "New South Wales commits funds to two major projects" (September 20, 2023), "Train testing begins on metro line under Sydney Harbour" (May 2, 2023).

wikis.title: Silvertown Tunnel planned to open on 7 April 2025
wikis.summary: TfL press release confirming the Silvertown Tunnel's planned 7 April 2025 opening, with the new bus and cycle-shuttle services, user charges, discounts and construction facts.
wikis.body:
## The announcement

- Transport for London (TfL) and Riverlinx Limited "have today (6 January 2025) confirmed that the Silvertown Tunnel is planned to open on 7 April 2025".
- Standfirst: "Construction works and rigorous testing of new modern tunnel linking Silvertown in east London to the Greenwich Peninsula now sufficiently complete to set out planned opening date."
- New bus routes serving the tunnel launch the same day and "will be free for at least the first year".

## The tunnel

- First announced in 2012; 1.4km long; links Newham to the Greenwich Peninsula.
- Journey time savings "expected to be up to 20 minutes at peak times".
- Located in the Ultra Low Emission Zone.
- Buses able to cross the river in the area increase "from six to 21 buses an hour in each direction during the busiest times - all of which will be zero emission at the tailpipe".

## Buses and cycle-shuttle

- New cross-river routes serve Greenwich, Newham and Tower Hamlets, including the Superloop SL4 from Grove Park to Canary Wharf; free for at least 12 months from 7 April 2025.
- Cycle-shuttle service: zero-emission, every 12 minutes, seven days a week from 06:30 to 21:30, two stops - the 'north' stop on Seagull Lane close to Royal Victoria DLR station and the 'south' stop on Millennium Way near the junction with Old School Close.
- The shuttle has bespoke shelters, cycle racks and branding; maps of local cycle routes will be displayed at shelters. "Further details of the branding will be revealed in the new year."
- Stagecoach London will operate the cycle-shuttle service.
- Free for at least one year: bus journeys on three cross-river routes serving Newham, Tower Hamlets and Greenwich, and DLR cross-river journeys from Cutty Sark to Island Gardens and from Woolwich Arsenal to King George V.

## User charge from 7 April 2025

- A user charge applies at both the Silvertown and Blackwall tunnels between 06:00 and 22:00, seven days a week.
- Off-peak rate of £1.50 "will apply the majority of the time, for vehicles registered for TfL Auto Pay".
- Peak charges add £1 for motorcycles, £2.50 for cars and small vans, £4 for large vans and £5 for HGVs; peak is four hours northbound in the morning (06:00-10:00) and three hours southbound in the evening (16:00-19:00), Monday to Friday, "or for anyone not using TfL Auto Pay".
- Penalty Charge Notice for non-payment: £180, reduced to £90 if paid within 14 days; only one per day per vehicle regardless of the number of unpaid trips.
- The charge is "a requirement of the Development Consent Order for the Silvertown Tunnel, made by the Secretary of State for Transport in 2018".

## Discounts and exemptions

- 50 per cent discount for low-income drivers in 12 east and south-east London boroughs (Barking & Dagenham, Bexley, Bromley, Greenwich, Hackney, Havering, Lewisham, Newham, Redbridge, Southwark, Tower Hamlets and Waltham Forest) and the City of London.
- £1 discount on the standard off-peak charge for at least one year for small businesses, sole traders and charities registered in Tower Hamlets, Newham and Greenwich.
- Automatic exemption for all buses, coaches and vehicles with nine seats or more registered with the DVLA.
- Not chargeable: all taxis, blue badge holders, wheelchair-accessible private hire vehicles registered with TfL, 'Zero-Emission Capable' PHVs licensed by TfL ("which currently make up at least 40 per cent of the 93,000 fleet"), and vehicles under the Accredited Breakdown / Recovery vehicle discount.
- Charges reimbursed to NHS staff and patients eligible through the NHS reimbursement scheme.
- Eligibility for the 50 per cent discount: people receiving Income Support, Income-related Employment & Support Allowance, Income-based Jobseekers Allowance, Universal Credit, Pension Credit, Child Tax Credit, Working Tax Credit, Carer's Allowance or Housing Benefit.

## Construction facts

- Construction began in 2021; "more than 1,860,000 tonnes of material have been transported to and from the site via river rather than using roads - helping to remove around 110,000 lorry trips from local roads".
- The tunnel boring machine, Jill (named after Jill Viner, London's first female bus driver), "was also innovatively turned around within the rotation chamber in Greenwich to then bore the second tunnel back towards Newham - a UK engineering first".
- The project "enabled more than 120 apprenticeships across the supply chain, as well as supported the hiring of more than 90 people who were previously unemployed and offered more than 1,500 days in placements".
- Work on Tidal Basin Roundabout and new walking and cycling routes around it and along Dock Road "has also recently been completed"; work improving Lower Lea Crossing is "currently underway and due to be complete by the end of spring 2025".

## Blackwall Tunnel context

- "East London residents and businesses currently face chronic traffic congestion in the area around the Blackwall Tunnel."
- The Victorian-era tunnel "suffers from frequent closures - more than 700 times a year - which result in large tailbacks, poor air quality and millions of hours lost".

## Quotes

- Stuart Harvey, Chief Capital Officer at TfL: "I'm pleased that we can now confirm that the Silvertown Tunnel will open on 7 April 2025, following years of hard work and close collaboration between ourselves and Riverlinx Limited. The tunnel is on track to open in the coming months and is a testament to brilliant and ground-breaking engineering."
- John Hagan, CEO, Riverlinx: "This represents the culmination of effort for the thousands of people that have worked on the project over the past five years."
- Borja Trashorras, Project Director, Riverlinx CJV: "the project will open on time and with the highest quality and safety standards."
- Paul Lynch, Stagecoach London Managing Director: "We're excited to be asked to operate the innovative and important Silvertown Tunnel cycle-shuttle service."

## Delivery structure

- Delivered by the Riverlinx consortium - abrdn, Invesis, Cintra and SK ecoplant - through a design, build, finance, operate and maintain contract; "the vast majority of the funding is coming from private finance which has been specifically raised for this scheme".
- Riverlinx CJV is a joint venture of BAM, Ferrovial Construction and SK ecoplant.
- TfL has launched a multi-channel marketing campaign about the tunnel, covering video on demand, online video, posters, press, radio, local leaflet drops, social media, digital advertising and emails.

## Page data

- Press release dated 06 January 2025.

wikis.title: Poland opens the Vistula Spit canal
wikis.summary: UPI report that Poland opened a new canal through the Vistula Spit on 17 September 2022, giving Elblag access to the Baltic without Russian permission.
wikis.body:
## What happened

- "Poland opened a new canal Saturday linking the **Vistula Lagoon** to the **Gdansk Bay**, allowing ships to visit the port of **Elblag** without needing Russian permission to use its **Baltiysk Strait**."
- Dateline: **Sept. 17 (UPI)**, filed WORLD NEWS SEPT. 17, 2022 / 10:55 PM, by Adam Schrader.
- A photo shows the new shipping canal through the Vistula Spit in **Skowronki village, northern Poland**.

## Timing

- Poland "timed the opening to occur on the 83rd anniversary of the invasion of Poland by the Soviet Union in World War II".

## Cost and completion

- "Construction of the **$420 million** canal, which has not been completed, began in **February 2019**."
- "Cargo ships will not be able to use the canal until it has been deepened another **16 feet**."

## Quotes

- Polish President **Andrzej Duda**: "A state that understands its potential, its history and its importance cannot afford to be a dependent state. It cannot allow someone else to decide about its important strategic matters."
- Duda: "This was the case throughout this extremely difficult period, from 1945, when it was impossible to influence the Vistula Lagoon here without the de facto consent of the Russian President, emphasized today."

## Reaction cited

- The Jamestown Foundation, "a conservative think tank based in Washington D.C.", said in an analysis at the time that Moscow commentators opposed the canal "because it would give NATO ships access to the Vistula Lagoon, which is also known as the Kaliningrad Bay".

wikis.title: First look inside the new U.S. Embassy at Nine Elms, London
wikis.summary: Londonist report on interior photos released of the new U.S. Embassy at 33 Nine Elms Lane, its reported cost and design, and the ambassador's announcement that it opens to the public on 16 January 2018.
wikis.body:
## The release

- "The U.S Embassy has shared photos from inside its new home at Nine Elms, giving the public a first look inside the building."
- Three images of the interior were released.

## The building

- Part of the redevelopment of Battersea and Nine Elms.
- "The building has reportedly cost £770million to build, having been planned as far back as 2008, with construction work beginning in 2013."
- Official address: 33 Nine Elms Lane.
- Described as a "giant spiky glass cube" that "has split opinions".
- "It's designed with security in mind, including a bombproof exterior and 'moat' partly surrounding it. It's also expected to be carbon-neutral."
- Interior image credited "Copyright Kieran Timberlake".

## Opening date

- U.S. Ambassador Woody Johnson announced on Twitter: "Big news - today I can announce that our new American Embassy in London will be open to the public from 16th January 2018! #33NineElmsLane" (@USAmbUK, December 13, 2017).
- The article asks whether this means a Trump visit around that time; "Johnson recently hinted that the new embassy will need to dedicated by an American president."

## The old embassy

- The current U.S. Embassy in Grosvenor Square "is being redeveloped into a 137 bedroom, 5-star hotel, at a reported cost of £1bn".

## Byline and dates

- By Laura Reynolds. "Last Updated 13 December 2017". The page carries a notice that the article is old and information may have changed.

wikis.title: Washington Monument and the National Mall (Britannica)
wikis.summary: Britannica's article on the Washington Monument - its dimensions, construction history and closures - followed by its article on the National Mall, its history, historic events and controversies.
wikis.body:
## Washington Monument

- Obelisk in Washington, D.C., honouring George Washington, the first president of the United States.
- "Constructed of granite faced with Maryland marble, the structure is 55 feet (16.8 metres) square at the base and 554 feet 7 inches (169 metres) high and weighs an estimated 91,000 tons."
- "At its completion in 1884 it was the world's tallest man-made structure, though it was supplanted by the Eiffel Tower just five years later. It remains the world's tallest masonry structure."

## National Mall

- "Often referred to as 'America's front yard'", spanning more than two miles from the Capitol building to the Lincoln Memorial.
- "the ever-evolving realization of Frenchman Pierre L'Enfant's vision for a 'grand avenue' through the nation's capital."

## News items shown on the page

- "National Park Service backs Trump's arch, despite its impact on Washington's sightline" - Aug. 28, 2026, 5:36 PM ET (AP).
- "Mile-long stretch of National Mall closed until 2027 for turf renovation" - Sep. 2, 2026, 10:39 PM ET (Washington Post).

## Authors

- Washington Monument article: B. Philip Bigler and Britannica Editors, Aug. 28, 2026.
- National Mall article: Tracy Grant and Britannica Editors.

wikis.title: Washington Monument: dimensions and construction
wikis.summary: The obelisk's measurements, the long stalled construction from 1783 to its 1885 dedication, and its later restorations and closures.
wikis.body:
### Dimensions

- 55 feet (16.8 metres) square at the base; 554 feet 7 inches (169 metres) high; estimated 91,000 tons.
- "The monument's height was previously measured as 555 feet 5 inches [169.3 metres], but a recalculation based on international standards in 2014 led to its revision."
- Load-bearing masonry walls are 15 feet (4.6 metres) thick at the base, "tapering to a thickness of only 18 inches (46 cm) at the top".

### Origins

- "A monument to Washington was first proposed in 1783, when the Continental Congress appropriated funds to erect a statue of the country's military commander on horseback."
- The site chosen was "the exact surveyed centre of the original District of Columbia, on direct axes with the White House (to the north) and the United States Capitol (to the west)", reserved by Pierre-Charles L'Enfant when he designed the city in 1791.
- "In 1804 President Thomas Jefferson drove a stone marker into the proposed site, though it later sank into the marsh." The project was soon abandoned "because of various problems, including bureaucratic inertia".
- In 1833 the Washington National Monument Society chose a plan by Robert Mills for "a 600-foot- (183-metre-) tall obelisk with a circular base complete with 30 Doric columns".
- The weight required moving the site "to a point 350 feet (110 metres) to the northeast, thereby slightly disrupting the axial relationship to the other buildings".
- It was hoped Washington's remains would be moved from Mount Vernon in Virginia and reinterred at the memorial.

### Construction

- "Construction did not begin until 1848, and the cornerstone was laid during ceremonies on the Fourth of July." Attendees included George Washington Parke Custis, Washington's step-grandson, President James K. Polk and Congressman Abraham Lincoln.
- Financial and political difficulties "led to major architectural modifications, including the abandonment of the structure's grandiose base".
- Pope Pius IX donated a stone from the Temple of Concord in Rome, "though in 1854 members of the anti-Catholic Know-Nothing party broke into the obelisk, stole the marker, and disposed of it in the Potomac River".
- "Construction was halted at the outbreak of the Civil War with the obelisk standing only 152 feet (46 metres) tall."
- Mark Twain wrote that the unfinished monument "has the aspect of a factory chimney with the top broken off...you can see cow-sheds about its base, and the contented sheep nibbling pebbles in the desert solitudes that surround it, and the tired pigs dozing in the holy calm of its protecting shadow."
- The Army Corps of Engineers took over completion; because matching marble could not be found, "the colour of the upper two-thirds of the monument is visibly different from that of the lower third".
- "Some 36 years after construction began, the 3,300-pound (1,500 kg) capstone was set on the structure (December 6, 1884), and the Washington Monument was officially dedicated by President Chester Arthur during ceremonies on February 21, 1885."
- It was "not opened to the public until October 9, 1888, following the installation of a steam elevator", which spared visitors the monument's 897 steps; the modern elevator makes the ascent in about 60 seconds.
- "Inserted in the interior walls are more than 190 carved stones presented by various individuals, cities, states, and foreign nations."

### Restorations and closures

- After a major restoration project in the 1990s, the monument reopened in 2001.
- "It closed again after an earthquake on August 23, 2011, struck some 85 miles (137 km) southwest of Washington, D.C., damaging the monument. It reopened in May 2014."

wikis.title: National Mall: early history and the McMillan plan
wikis.summary: How L'Enfant's 1791 'grand avenue' became a marred 19th-century expanse, and how the 1901 McMillan commission reshaped it.
wikis.body:
- "When L'Enfant was tapped by George Washington in 1791 to design a public space worthy of the new nation, he drew up plans for what he would call a 'place of general resort'", connecting the Capitol to the presidential mansion and ultimately a monument to Washington. "He called it a 'grand avenue.'"
- By the middle to late 19th century little of that vision had come about: the Mall "was marked (and marred) by railroad and streetcar crossings, a canal described by the Evening Star newspaper as a 'ditch and common sewer,' and a variety of ramshackle buildings".
- "By the 1860s only the Smithsonian Castle had been completed, sitting not far from the stalled-by-the-Civil-War stump of the Washington Monument."
- In 1901, during Pres. Theodore Roosevelt's administration ("who would officially change the name of the presidential home to the White House in 1901"), Sen. James McMillan, a Michigan Republican, headed a commission to reenvision the historic core, including architects Daniel Burnham and landscape architect Frederick Law Olmsted.
- Innovations included "the expansion of the Mall to the Lincoln Memorial, which would be completed in 1922". "The Washington Monument, once seen as the western bookend of the Mall, instead became its centerpiece."
- The Reflecting Pool by Lincoln Memorial architect Henry Bacon "was meant to create a mirror linking the Washington and Lincoln monuments".
- By mid-century, with the Jefferson Memorial completed, "the intersecting axes of the Capitol to the Washington Monument and the White House to the Jefferson Memorial defined the wide expanse of the National Mall".
- Smithsonian museums along the Mall include the National Museum of Natural History, the National Museum of American History, the National Museum of African American History and Culture, the Freer Gallery of Art, the National Air and Space Museum, the National Museum of the American Indian, and the Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden.

wikis.title: Historic moments on the National Mall
wikis.summary: Four public events Britannica lists as among the most famous on the Mall, with their dates and crowd figures.
wikis.body:
- **Marian Anderson concert**: In 1939, after the Daughters of the American Revolution refused to rent her Constitution Hall "because she was Black", and amid "an enormous backlash, including from first lady Eleanor Roosevelt", Anderson performed on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial on Easter Sunday. "Some 75,000 people attended."
- **March on Washington**: "In 1963 some 250,000 people attended the march to protest racial discrimination and to support civil rights legislation in Congress." From the steps of the Lincoln Memorial, Martin Luther King, Jr., delivered his "I Have a Dream" speech. King's own memorial, between the Lincoln and Jefferson memorials, was "dedicated on August 28, 2011, the 48th anniversary of the March on Washington".
- **AIDS Memorial Quilt**: "In October 1987 a 1,920-panel quilt was unfurled on the Mall to pay homage to those who had lost their lives to AIDS." The names of the dead were read. "The quilt returned to the Mall in 1996 with more than 39,000 panels." The Mall later hosted similar memorials for victims of gun violence and the COVID-19 pandemic.
- **Million Man March**: "In 1995 one of the single largest protests in U.S. history filled the Mall with crowds estimated at between 400,000 and more than 1,000,000 people." Organized by Louis Farrakhan to promote African American unity, it "was controversial, even among Black leaders at the time, but was credited with a surge in voter registration among Black men".

wikis.title: National Mall controversies
wikis.summary: Disputes over the Vietnam Veterans Memorial, the World War II Memorial, overbuilding, and the Reflecting Pool.
wikis.body:
- **Vietnam Veterans Memorial**: "Now known simply as 'the Wall,' the low-slung black granite memorial etched with the names of more than 58,000 who died as a result of the Vietnam War was widely disparaged when its design was unveiled." Tom Carhart, a Vietnam veteran who testified before the U.S. Commission of Fine Arts, called it an insult to veterans and "a black gash of shame and sorrow, hacked into the national visage that is the Mall". It was designed by Maya Lin, "then a student at Yale University".
- **World War II Memorial**: Situated between the Washington Monument and the Lincoln Memorial, "the memorial to the 400,000 who died in World War II and those who served was controversial during its construction in the early part of the 21st century exactly because of its positioning. The McMillan plan had called for nothing to be built to obstruct the sight lines between the two iconic structures."
- **Overbuilding**: "In 2003, in response to concerns that the Mall was becoming cluttered, Pres. George W. Bush signed an amendment to the Commemorative Works Act that declared the axes of the Mall 'a substantially completed work of civic art' that would bar future construction. That was part of the reason that a 2020 monument to Pres. Dwight D. Eisenhower was located a block off the Mall."
- **Reflecting Pool**: Completed in 1923 and envisioned by Bacon as a mirror between the Lincoln and Washington monuments. "Built basically on a swamp, the pool leaked immediately and has been the source of multiple attempts at reconstruction and restoration, including a 2011 plan to use more than 2,000 pilings to shore up the pool only to have an enormous algae bloom appear. In 2026 a plan supported by Pres. Donald Trump saw the bottom of the pool painted 'American flag blue.' Within days the algae was back and the paint was peeling."

wikis.title: MI6/SIS Building in London, and the Secret Intelligence Service
wikis.summary: Britannica entry describing the MI6/SIS headquarters at Vauxhall - its architect, design and security - together with a companion entry on MI6 itself.
wikis.body:
## The building

- MI6/SIS Building is the headquarters of Britain's Secret Intelligence Service (SIS) in London; also known as MI6 Headquarters.
- Designed by architect Terry Farrell and completed in 1994.
- Stands on the south bank of the River Thames in Vauxhall, on Albert Embankment; "one of London's most famous postmodern buildings".
- "Its distinctive green-and-cream facade, an homage to Art Deco, makes it stand out even on the grayest of London days."
- Security features: "walls and windows designed to withstand bullets and bombs, and a 'Faraday cage,' which prevents electronic eavesdropping from hackers"; two moats provide further protection.
- Farrell designed it as an "urban village" concept; it was adapted for MI6's high-security standards after being purchased by the government.
- "It is not one building but a group of three blocks interconnected by courtyards and atria, which are covered in panes of green-colored glass to coordinate with the decorated facade."
- Stepped outline stretches up to a height of nine stories and extends "downward deep beneath the London pavements to provide extra security".

## Why it was bought

- The SIS was created in 1909; the abbreviation MI6 (for "military intelligence, section six") was adopted at the start of World War II.
- "In the mid-1990s it was decided that MI6 should become more open, and the building on Vauxhall's Albert Embankment was purchased as a public statement of this new attitude."

## Reception and the 2000 attack

- "Since it opened, the building has excited controversy, becoming loved and loathed in equal amounts."
- "A rocket missile attack in 2000, believed to have been committed by the Real Irish Republican Army, seemed to prove such claims. Yet, despite the ferocity of the weapon used, the attack succeeded only in damaging an eighth-floor window."
- The building has appeared in several James Bond films.

## MI6 (companion entry)

- British government agency responsible for the collection, analysis, and appropriate dissemination of foreign intelligence, and for espionage activities outside British territory.
- "It has existed in various forms since the establishment of a secret service in 1569 by Sir Francis Walsingham, who became secretary of state to Queen Elizabeth I."
- Constituted in its present form in 1912 by Commander (later Sir) Mansfield Cumming.
- "In the 1930s and '40s it was considered the most effective intelligence service in the world"; after Hitler's rise it ran operations in Europe, Latin America and much of Asia.
- Helped train personnel of the U.S. Office of Strategic Services; has since cooperated with the CIA.
- Mid-1950s: British public reacted with consternation at revelations that MI6 had been penetrated by British double agents serving the Soviet Union since the 1930s.
- Details seldom appeared in the British press until the 1990s, "when the previously secretive organization publicly named its head for the first time".
- It can censor news accounts of its activities through "D" notices under the Official Secrets Act. MI6 reports to the Foreign Office.

## Authorship

- Building entry by Lucinda Hawksley; MI6 entry by The Editors of Encyclopaedia Britannica, "most recently revised and updated by Adam Augustyn".
- A news line on the page: "Former MI6 spy takes Trump to Scottish court for £800,000 legal payout - Sep. 17, 2026, 1:39 PM ET (BBC)".

wikis.summary: Britannica's entry on the agency's remit and history from 1569 through its 1912 founding in present form to its 1990s openness.

wikis.title: Gatwick completes partial resurfacing of its main runway
wikis.summary: Gatwick airport has finished resurfacing only the most trafficked parts of its main runway, saying the method halved the time and cost and cut asphalt use by 70 per cent.
wikis.body:
## What was done

- Gatwick airport has completed works to resurface its main runway, using what it called "a break from traditional methods" to reduce costs and save time.
- The resurfacing programme was originally intended for 2020 - the fifth "rehabilitation" of the runway since it was built in the 1950s - but was postponed as a result of Covid-19.
- Gatwick says the delay "acted as a catalyst to draw up new plans", delivering "a much more sustainable solution for the minimum practical budget".
- Instead of resurfacing the whole runway, the airport resurfaced "only the most 'trafficked' parts of its main runway" - where aircraft land and exit - as other sections were shown to still have seven to ten years of expected life.
- A resurfacing technique allowed the required two layers of asphalt to be laid in a single night, instead of the previous two-night approach.

## Figures

- The project was completed in just six months - half the normal time - and for half the cost.
- It used 70 per cent less asphalt than traditional resurfacing methods.
- All of the old asphalt material was recycled as aggregate in road construction.
- A temporary on-site asphalt batching plant reduced lorry travel distance and emissions.
- The runway "remains the world's busiest, with a current throughput of 55 movements per hour".
- Gatwick compared the work to "Performing open heart surgery while the patient is jogging".

## Quote

- Alasdair Scobie, capital delivery director, London Gatwick Airport: "The pandemic gave us the time and reason to rethink our original design. We think we have achieved the best balance possible between cost, operational constraints and durability, whilst reducing the environmental impact of construction." He added that "The cost savings can now also be reinvested in improvements across other parts of the airport."

## Byline

- Business Traveller, by Mark Caswell, published 11th October 2022.

wikis.title: GSA preserves Chicago's Century and Consumer Buildings instead of demolishing them
wikis.summary: Report that the U.S. General Services Administration chose adaptive reuse over a $52 million demolition plan for three historic buildings in the Chicago Loop.
wikis.body:
## The decision
- "Preservationists have staved off the demolition of three historic buildings in the Chicago Loop."
- The buildings: "The Consumer Building by Jenney, Mundie & Jensen (1913); Century Building by Holabird & Roche (1915); and 214 State Street by C.M. Palmer (1883) will not be torn down, contrary to a $52 million demolition plan that Congress issued last winter."
- All three are owned by the U.S. General Services Administration (GSA).
- "Previously, federal officials said they presented a security risk to the Dirksen Federal Building on Dearborn Street, and that they needed to be torn down and replaced."
- "Instead, GSA has opted for the 'viable adaptive reuse' of these iconic State Street structures."

## Reaction
- Elizabeth Blasius, cofounder of the Chicago office Preservation Futures: "There was a huge public outcry to save these buildings, and against the tremendous waste that their demolition would bring." "Now, it's no longer a question of if these buildings are going to be preserved, it's a matter of how."
- Preservation Futures "created informational videos about them to spread awareness"; Blasius "extensively reported on the Century & Consumer Buildings for MAS Context."
- Local nonprofit Preservation Chicago "listed the Century & Consumer Buildings on its endangered list in March" and "has since floated multiple potential uses for the towers, including a new home for the Chicago Collaborative Archive Center."
- Blasius: "I think housing is the obvious and natural choice here, an option which housing advocates have fought hard for. An archive center would also be a great use."

## Next steps
- "a series of public meetings will be held hosted by GSA to identify potential uses for the towers, and 'to avoid, minimize, or mitigate potential adverse effects on the historic buildings.'"
- "The public has until September 3 to weigh in."
- "Whatever new use the buildings accommodate, the retrofit will need to satisfy 'the security needs' of its neighbor, the Dirksen Courthouse, GSA said in a statement."

## Byline
- By Daniel Jonas Roche, August 5, 2024. Filed under Architecture, Midwest, News, Preservation.

wikis.title: Great Hall Program, Jeppesen Terminal, Denver International Airport
wikis.summary: Denver International Airport's page on the Great Hall Program renovating the Jeppesen Terminal, its three new Level 5 areas, phases, costs and completion dates.
wikis.body:
## The programme

- "As part of DEN's Great Hall Program, we are renovating the Terminal to make your journey more efficient and welcoming while being more authentic to the Culture of Colorado."
- The Great Hall sits under DEN's tents in the Jeppesen Terminal, holding airline ticket counters and security.
- "The Jeppesen Terminal was originally designed to accommodate 50 million passengers, but in 2024, DEN served over 82 million passengers. It's anticipated that DEN will reach 100 million passengers in the near future."
- Vision 100 is "DEN's strategic plan that will enable the airport to prepare for and reach 100 million annual passengers".

## Phases and money

- "The Great Hall Project consists of three phases. The first two phases were completed within the original $770 million budget" and focused on a new ticketing/check-in space for some airlines and one new security checkpoint in the northwest corner of Level 6.
- "This $1.3 billion Great Hall Completion phase began in late 2022 and is expected to be complete by the end of 2027 with sections opening along the way."
- "The entire Great Hall Program will be completed by the end of 2027 with segments opening along the way."
- Upgrades to restrooms, flooring, lighting, elevators/escalators "will save DEN approximately $200-250 million in maintenance costs over 10 years".
- Jobs: "Creating 6,500 direct jobs, 500 indirect jobs, 1,300 induced jobs and an estimated 54,000 additional apprenticeship hours."

## The renovated terminal

- The renovated Terminal "will consist of three main areas": the Global Gateway (North Level 5), Welcome Home Colorado (Center Level 5) and the Living Room (South Level 5).

## Site notice

- "South Level 6 terminal bridge and connected escalator are closed for construction until mid-November."
- DEN states it generates "more than $47.2 billion for the region annually"; address 8500 Pena Blvd, Denver, Colorado 80249.

wikis.title: The Global Gateway - North Level 5
wikis.summary: The north end of Level 5, where international passengers arrive and connect, gaining eight new security lanes.
wikis.body:
- "The north end of Level 5 will be known as the Global Gateway and will be where international passengers arrive and connect through Denver to easily transfer back through security for a flight to other cities."
- "Eight new security lanes will be added (four on the east and four on the west) to provide a seamless experience for international travelers connecting through DEN and to provide additional capacity for increasing passenger volumes."
- It sits on the level below the East and West Security Checkpoints.

wikis.title: Welcome Home Colorado - Center Level 5
wikis.summary: The central Level 5 arrivals area for domestic passengers, with seating, a flight information board and a centralised information booth.
wikis.body:
- "The center of Level 5 is where domestic travelers arrive and are greeted by their awaiting friends and family."
- "The area will have ample seating and a large flight information board as well as a new centralized information booth to provide support and information for arriving passengers."
- It is the level where domestic passengers arrive and come up from the train.

wikis.title: The Living Room - South Level 5
wikis.summary: The south end of Level 5, a seating and dining space with four security lanes for RTD A-Line travellers and a food court above.
wikis.body:
- "The south end of Level 5, known as the Living Room, will be a high-energy space filled with a variety of comfortable seating options and tables as well as numerous dining options."
- "This area includes four security lanes to serve travelers arriving via the RTD A-Line. These are enclosed in a structure that is flanked by a bar that will be an ideal place to sample Colorado craft beers."
- "Above the lanes, there will be a food court with ample seating and new places to eat and hang out."
- It is the level and space where the South Security Checkpoint is currently located.

wikis.title: Completion Phase
wikis.summary: The third and final phase of the Great Hall Project, now underway, including the East Security Checkpoint that opened 5 August 2025.
wikis.body:
- "The Great Hall Completion, the final phase of the project is now underway." It includes:
  - "Building the East Security Checkpoint on Level 6 in the northeast corner of the terminal, which includes extending the balcony 40 feet to match the west side and provide for additional circulation space"
  - "Renovating the airline check-in facilities on south end of Level 6"
  - "Creating a new meet/greet area for domestic and international arrivals"
  - "Constructing the Center for Equity and Excellence in Aviation"
- "The East Security Checkpoint opened Aug. 5, 2025. This second new state-of-the-art checkpoint consists of 17 new screening lanes with the same screening technology as the West Security Checkpoint."
- "Additionally, four new elevators will be constructed as well as additional elevators and stairs that will help move screened passengers from Level 6 to the train platform."
- With this second checkpoint complete, "both the checkpoints on Level 5 will be relocated to Level 6".
- Phase cost $1.3 billion, began in late 2022, "expected to be complete by the end of 2027".
- A new Center of Equity and Excellence in Aviation "will be constructed on Level 4 of the Westin Denver International Airport" to "engage, educate, empower, motivate and provide opportunities for under-represented students and young people who are interested and passionate about careers in aviation".
- Phase 2 "includes new security checkpoints, a widened balcony and a new triple escalator".
tags: center of equity and excellence in aviation

wikis.title: Tren Maya targeted for completion in December 2023
wikis.summary: Railway Age reports Mexico's president reaffirming that the 1,550-km, $10 billion Tren Maya will be finished in December 2023, with Alstom supplying 42 X'trapolis multiple-units.
wikis.body:
## Schedule

- Mexico President Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador "has reaffirmed his government's commitment to complete the 1,550-km (961-mile), $10 billion Tren Maya (Tren Maya) project next year."
- Lopez Obrador: "We are making progress in building Tren Maya, currently the largest railway project in the world."
- Lopez Obrador: "We will finish the [project] in December 2023."

## Rolling stock and depots

- Alstom is supplying 42 X'trapolis multiple-units for Tren Maya.
- Construction of rolling stock maintenance and storage facilities is "now under way" in Cancun, Merida, Hampolol and Escarcega.

## Note on the source

- The article is cut off after the opening section: "This content is for paid subscribers only."
- Written by Robert Preston, Associate Editor, International Railway Journal.

wikis.title: The Spiral opens at 66 Hudson Blvd, Manhattan
wikis.summary: CommercialCafe article on the completion and opening of The Spiral, a 66-story, 1,031-foot office tower at 66 Hudson Blvd. in Manhattan developed by Tishman Speyer and designed by Bjarke Ingels Group.
wikis.body:
## The building

- The Spiral, a 2.8-million-square-foot office skyscraper at 66 Hudson Blvd. in Manhattan, "has officially opened."
- Developed by Tishman Speyer; 66 stories; height 1,031 feet (314 meters).
- Described as "the first supertall skyscraper and commercial high-rise architecture project in New York City by Bjarke Ingels Group (BIG)."
- Project team: Turner Construction, Adamson Associates and structural engineer WSP Cantor Seinuk.

## Design

- Standout features are its "ziggurat silhouette" and a series of stepped terraces connecting indoor workspaces to exterior terraces on each floor.
- Terraces gradually cut into the floor plates as the tower ascends, reducing overall volume toward the top; "no two terraces are in the same place, and none is overlooked by any other."
- Cladding "showcases the innovative use of seven different metals," a nod to the industrial heritage of the surrounding Hudson Yards neighborhood.

## Amenities

- Zo Clubhouse, a private event space with city views; The Studio, a versatile events and work space.
- Dedicated parking spaces with charging stations for electric car owners.
- Bicycle room with private showers and changing rooms.

## Tenants

- 2018: Pfizer signed a 20-year lease for 800,000 square feet.
- AllianceBernstein committed to leasing 189,000 square feet.
- Turner Construction (75,000 square feet) and HSBC (265,000 square feet) are "set to relocate their headquarters to The Spiral."

## Recognition

- Won "Best Tall Building 300-399 Meters" at the 2023 Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat Awards.
- The team is "actively pursuing LEED Silver certification" for the building.
- By Matthew Preston.
