wikis.title: First flight lands at Red Sea International Airport and the RSI brand reveal
wikis.summary: Red Sea Global press release on the first flight touching down at Red Sea International Airport on 21 September 2023, the new twice-weekly SAUDIA service from Riyadh, the RSI brand reveal and wider Red Sea project progress.
wikis.body:
## The first flight

- "New twice-weekly service from Riyadh to Red Sea International Airport (RSI) starts today."
- Dateline: "Riyadh, 21 September, 2023". The first flight "touched down on the new runway earlier today (21 September 2023)".
- Red Sea Global (RSG) is "the multi-project developer behind the world's most ambitious regenerative tourism destinations, The Red Sea and Amaala".

## The schedule

- The SAUDIA flight departs King Khalid International Airport (RUH) in Riyadh each Thursday and Saturday and "takes under two hours"; flights return to Riyadh later the same day.
- Thursday: departs RUH at 10.50am; departs RSI for the capital at 13:35pm.
- Saturday: departs RUH at 12.50pm; return flight for RUH departs at 15:35pm.
- "Positioned within an eight-hour flight from 85 percent of the world's population, RSI will grow to welcome international flights from next year as additional phase one resorts open their doors."

## Quotes

- John Pagano, Group CEO of Red Sea Global: "We promised to make The Red Sea a place where people from all around the world would come to experience the best of Saudi culture, hospitality, and nature. Now, with the first flight touching down at Red Sea International Airport, and our first resorts receiving bookings, Saudi Arabia's position on the global tourism map is all but secured."

## Operator

- "Red Sea International Airport is operated by daa International, which has supported Red Sea Global with design validation and commissioning of RSI since 2020."
- "With the arrival of RSI's first commercial flight, daa International's operational responsibility commences."

## RSI brand reveal

- On the same day, RSG revealed the new brand for RSI, to be expressed "from the airport terminal and staff uniforms to the electric mobility vehicles that will transport passengers from air to land side".
- Pagano: "RSI is the gateway to The Red Sea destination. It is the first impression visitors have, and their parting memory when they leave. The brand echoes the qualities of the five-star hospitality guests will enjoy across the destination."
- "The brand icon is a representation of the Red Sea International Airport's unique architecture", its shape "inspired by the bird's eye view of the airport's exterior".

## Other infrastructure progress

- Five solar farms constructed so the first phase of The Red Sea can be off grid and "powered solely by sunlight, with more than 760,000 solar panels installed".
- Its Landscape Nursery, "the largest in the region", has grown "more than four million trees, plants, and shrubs".
- "In July, RSG also opened a state-of-the-art Mangrove Nursery, with the aim of planting 50 million mangroves by 2030."

## The destination at full completion

- "Upon full completion in 2030, the destination will comprise 50 resorts, offering up to 8,000 hotel rooms and more than 1,000 residential properties across 22 islands and six inland sites."
- Also luxury marinas, golf courses, entertainment, F&B and leisure facilities.

## About Red Sea Global (boilerplate on the page)

- RSG is "a vertically integrated real estate developer" across tourism, residential, experiences, infrastructure, transport, healthcare and services.
- The Red Sea "began welcoming guests in 2023"; AMAALA "welcomed its first guests in 2026"; Thuwal Private Retreat "opened in 2024".
- RSG was entrusted with refurbishment works at Al Wajh International Airport, upgrading the existing terminal and infrastructure and building a new international terminal; "The airport officially reopened in May 2026."

wikis.title: Chengdu Phoenix Hill Sports Park
wikis.summary: HKS Architects' project page for Chengdu Phoenix Hill Sports Park in Chengdu, Sichuan, China, describing its 60,000-seat stadium, 18,000-seat arena, mixed-use buildings, design features and awards.
wikis.body:
## The project
- Chengdu Phoenix Hill Sports Park, Chengdu, Sichuan, China. HKS practice: Sports & Entertainment; service: Architecture.
- Delivered on "an extremely tight schedule - just two and a half years from design to construction completion".
- HKS worked with a local design institute on its competition-winning design; the park is a "community anchor for the emerging Jinniu District".

## The challenge as stated
- "Many new sports venues in China sit inactive after big competitions." HKS "envisioned Chengdu Phoenix Hill Sports Park as both a state-of-the art venue for major global sporting events and a public place where the community can gather throughout the year."

## Venues
- A 60,000-seat FIFA standard stadium and an 18,000-seat NBA standard arena.
- The venues handle soccer (football), basketball, ice hockey, badminton, table tennis, handball and gymnastics, with retractable seating and stage options.
- "The sports park is set to host the 31st World University Games' basketball competition in 2022 and the 18th Asian Cup in 2023."

## Design features
- A public square or "urban living room" for outdoor events - parties, exhibitions, concerts and festivals.
- Mixed-use buildings comprising hotel, retail and training facilities, plus a network of public spaces.
- The stadium has general audience sections on the lower bowl and upper bowl, "a pioneering solution in China".
- "The country's first open cable dome structure with a massive single-layer cable system serves as the stadium's roof", enclosed with a translucent ETFE (ethylene tetrafluoroethylene) membrane that shades all seating while allowing natural light and ventilation and softening shadow casting on the field.
- A multi-use bridge structure with club rooms connects the two main venues across a wide public promenade.
- The exterior is "inspired by Shu Jin, or Imperial Embroidery, an art form that originated in Chengdu centuries ago"; layered materials and facade panels mimic silk threads.

## Project features (figures)
- 459,395 sqm (4,944,886 sf) development
- 60,000-seat stadium
- 18,000-seat arena
- 128,000 sqm (1,377,780 sf) retail + hotel complex

## Awards
- 2024 Architizer A+ Awards, Jury Winner & Popular Choice Winner
- 2022 Sichuan Province Excellent Engineering Survey and Design (Public) Architecture Awards, First Prize

wikis.title: Inauguration of the first phase of Mumbai's Coastal Road
wikis.summary: Report on Maharashtra Chief Minister Eknath Shinde opening the first phase of Mumbai's Coastal Road from Worli to Marine Drive, with travel-time claims, usage rules and project cost.
wikis.body:
## The inauguration

- "Maharashtra Chief Minister Eknath Shinde on Monday inaugurated the first phase of Mumbai's Coastal Road."
- Shinde, with deputies Devendra Fadnavis and Ajit Pawar, flagged off an electric bus ferrying women and a vintage car rally to mark the opening of the nine-kilometre-long corridor from Worli to Marine Drive.
- Published On: 11/03/2024 - 10:57 PM, by Indian Awaaz (AMN / Mumbai).

## What the Chief Minister said

- Calling the project "an engineering marvel", Shinde said the road is being built using advanced technology.
- He said Mumbai will get a world-class Central Park spread over around 300 acres, as 175 acres of green space is being developed as part of the coastal road project, besides 120 acres of racecourse land.
- The road is being renamed "Dharmaveer, Swarajya Rakshak Chhatrapati Sambhaji Maharaj Mumbai Coastal Road"; he said all safety measures are in place.
- He said projects like Atal Setu and Coastal Road will make travelling between parts of Mumbai easy and hassle-free, and that timely completion will help reduce pollution besides saving time and fuel.
- Taking a dig at the former Chief Minister for ignoring the demands of the Koli community, Shinde said his government got the necessary environmental approvals and agreed to the Koli community's demand to increase the span to 120 metres so fishing activity is not affected.

## Travel time and phasing

- Deputy Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said the partial opening is expected to bring down travel time between Marine Drive and Worli to less than 10 minutes, which usually takes 45-50 minutes during peak hours.
- Currently only the southbound arm has been opened; the northbound road "is likely to be opened in May this year" after completion of the connecting bridge between the Coastal Road and Bandra-Worli Sea Link.

## Usage rules and cost

- With construction work still on, heavy vehicles will not be allowed on the stretch.
- Small and light vehicles can use the toll-free road from 8 am to 8 pm.
- "The work on the ambitious Coastal Road project started in October 2018 at a projected cost of over fourteen thousand crore rupees."

wikis.title: Little Island, Barry Diller's $260 million park on the Hudson
wikis.summary: Bloomberg feature touring Little Island ahead of its public opening on Friday, May 21, covering its cost, construction, design, programming and funding.
wikis.body:
## Opening

- "When it opens to the public on Friday, May 21, visitors will be able to enter from 6 a.m. to 1 a.m. year-round via two, boardwalk-sized bridges that connect the structure to the Hudson River Greenway and roughly correspond to 14th and 13th streets."
- "It took five years to build, and now will open to everyone."
- Attendance will be capped "at least initially" at about 800 people. Trish Santini, executive director: "We'll do timed entry from noon until 8 p.m. every day, to help keep everybody safe and make sure people feel comfortable and not worried about overcrowding."
- Restrictions: "No dogs, (with the exception of service animals), bikes, or scooters are allowed."

## The structure

- "the 2.4-acre park - conceived and mostly paid for by billionaire Barry Diller through his Diller - von Furstenberg Family Foundation - is actually an undulating platform of grass, trees, and winding pathways mounted on concrete piles where Pier 54 used to be."
- Located on Manhattan's West Side, adjacent to the Meatpacking District.
- "the island's base is an undeniable showstopper: the 132 concrete 'tulips' that make up the park's structure." Each cast-concrete tulip "is made up of four to six 'petals,' none exactly alike."
- "Every concrete tulip is unique, fabricated by Fort Miller Co. in Greenwich, N.Y., trucked to a location on the Hudson River, assembled on land, 'and then each tulip was lifted by a crane onto a barge,' says Santini. 'We floated four at a time down the Hudson to come to the site. So that's just one example of how complex the work was.'"
- The layout was intended to evoke a "leaf floating on water."

## Origins and designers

- "The origins of the project date to 2013, when Diller, the chairman of IAC, became involved in fixing up Pier 54, which had fallen into disrepair."
- Diller and his wife, fashion designer Diane von Furstenberg, "commissioned architect Thomas Heatherwick - designer of the infamous Vessel in Manhattan's Hudson Yards - and the landscape architecture firm MNLA to design an entirely new structure."

## Spaces

- The Play Ground: "a large, oval area laid with tumbled concrete pavers" with outdoor seating and food vendors; "It's our central social space," says Santini. It can seat about 100 socially distanced people, "and around 230 at full capacity." Savory Hospitality will run the stalls, serving "coffee and baked goods in the morning, sandwiches and salads during the day, and shareable small bites, beer, and wine in the evening." Pop-up events there include "drag bingo, late-night DJs, and, 'cabaret-style performers,'" and "All programming at the Play Ground will be free."
- The amphitheater "seats 687 people with standing room for 50", with benches of black locust wood and "high-quality lighting and acoustics".
- The glade has a smaller stage and is "accessed via a trellis covered in white roses."
- From the Island's highest viewpoint, "1 World Trade Center and the Statue of Liberty can be viewed."

## Planting

- "More than 66,000 bulbs were planted on the island, which will be open all year."
- "There are 65 species of shrubs, and 290 varieties of grasses, vines, and perennials. Currently, the park has 114 trees, represented by 35 different species. (Some trees, organizers say, are anticipated to grow from 50 to 60 feet high.)"

## Programming and tickets

- Summer performances include Broadway Inspirational Voices and American Ballet Theater; "In August, New York Pops Up will hold 20 days of free programming on the island."
- "Rehearsals will always be free; for actual performances, 30% of the tickets will be free and distributed to nonprofits, including Hudson Guild, Westbeth, Greenwich House, The Door, PS 33 in Chelsea, and New York's Department of Youth and Community Development. A further 40% of the tickets will cost less than $25 and be distributed through the Theater Development Fund; the final 30% will be priced at $65 for adults and $25 for seniors and children under the age of 12."
- Four "artists in residence" take turns performing, directing events and curating festivals, and review submissions to Perform in the Park. "The first season's artists are actor, singer, and music director Michael McElroy; tap dancer and choreographer Ayodele Casel; playwright and director Tina Landau; and the theatrical group PigPen Theatre Co."

## Money

- "In addition to the $260 million that the Diller - von Furstenberg Family Foundation has already donated to the project, it committed an additional $120 million to the park's maintenance for the next 20 years. (New York City and New York state contributed a further $17 million and $4 million, respectively.)"
- The pledged funds "will go to pay for the Island's 110 full-time and part time employees" and help subsidize public programming.
- The article notes "criticism that the Little Island is a billionaire's folly".

## Setting

- "The far West Side of Manhattan... has already undergone a series of transformations over the last few years. The Whitney Museum, High Line, Hudson River Park, and tech giants including Google have moved in and wrought seismic demographic changes."
- "In the pre-AIDS era, the area's derelict warehouses and piers were a gathering place for the gay community, notably captured in the photography of the late artist Alvin Baltrop."
- "the thin, steel frame of David Hammons's permanent installation Day's End follows the precise dimensions of the now-demolished Pier 52."

## Byline

- By James Tarmy, May 20, 2021, 7:00 AM EDT. Photographs by Ashok Sinha for Bloomberg Pursuits.

wikis.title: Crown Sydney hotel opens in Barangaroo
wikis.summary: Business Traveller report that the 75-floor, 349-room Crown Sydney hotel has opened in Barangaroo while its casino licence remains on hold.
wikis.body:
## Opening

- "After seven years of planning and construction Sydney has finally welcomed the city's 75-floor Crown Sydney hotel."
- Described as the city's tallest building.
- "The 349-room property is located in the redeveloped Barangaroo district of central Sydney, at the southern end of Sydney Harbour Bridge."

## Restaurants and facilities

- Rooms opened alongside several of the tower's restaurants and bars: a Nobu outpost, Italian eatery A'Mare, Cantonese restaurant Silks, Japanese eatery Yoshii's Omakase, and Woodcut - "a unique dining experience that celebrates Australian produce and cooking with wood, charcoal and steam".
- Other features: an outdoor swimming pool and tennis court, fitness centre and spa facilities.

## Casino licence delayed

- "A casino had been due to open in conjunction with the hotel, but earlier this month Australia's Independent Liquor and Gaming Authority delayed the granting of a gaming licence, pending the results of an enquiry into the suitability of Crown and major shareholder James Packer to operate a casino at the venue."
- Crown "operates two existing resorts and casinos in the Australian cities of Melbourne and Perth."

## Quotes

- Crown Sydney CEO Peter Crinis: "Sydney is one of the world's great cities, and it deserves a great hotel. Crown Towers will deliver that and so much more. We have amazing bars and restaurants that will make this an incredible destination for Sydney. We are excited to open the doors and let Sydney experience it."
- Crinis: "A lot of time has been spent getting the offer right. Our chef line up reflects some of the most exciting names in the culinary food scene - we hope this becomes a destination people want to visit time and time again."

## Byline

- By Mark Caswell, published 29th December 2020.

wikis.title: OpenAI pauses $200 ChatGPT Pro sign-ups as Astra demand strains capacity
wikis.summary: News report that OpenAI has temporarily halted new sign-ups and upgrades to the $200-per-month ChatGPT Pro tier because demand for its new Astra model exceeds its compute capacity.
wikis.body:
## The pause
- "The company announced on Thursday it's pausing new sign-ups and upgrades to the most expensive plan on the Pro tier," the $200-per-month ChatGPT Pro plan where Astra is available.
- The Pro tier "provides 20 times the usage of the Plus tier below it."
- OpenAI's head of product Thibault Sottiaux wrote on X that the $200 plan "puts the most strain on the AI lab's systems": "We wanted to take the smallest step that allows us to continue giving the broadest access possible," adding that OpenAI is "working on adding more capacity" and that existing Pro accounts are unaffected.
- A day earlier, Sottiaux said demand for Astra was "unprecedented" and warned the company "might have to pause new Pro subscriptions for a bit" if it continued: "We're pulling all the levers possible to sustain the demand, but I've not seen anything like it until now and we went through very steep growth before."

## Astra
- OpenAI launched Astra "last week"; OpenAI president Greg Brockman called it the start of the "AGI era."
- At launch "it only gave a handful of enterprise customers access to give the company time to scale its compute capacity."
- Marquee feature, called "computer use," "allows it to interact with a desktop the way a human would, like filling out forms and navigating web pages at 'superhuman speed,' Brockman told reporters."
- OpenAI also said Astra "can burn through users' usage allowances faster than its previous flagship model GPT 5.6 Sol."

## Compute constraints
- Not the first such pause: in November 2023 OpenAI temporarily halted sign-ups to the $20-per-month ChatGPT Plus plan after its first developer conference led to a surge in demand. Sam Altman wrote on X at the time: "The surge in usage post devday has exceeded our capacity and we want to make sure everyone has a great experience."
- "OpenAI said its available compute rose from 0.2 gigawatts in 2023 to about 1.9 GW in 2025, a 9.5-fold increase over two years."
- The article notes concerns "that a potential bursting of the AI bubble could leave a glut of computing capacity behind," and that AI hardware like GPUs "can depreciate in a few years."

## Byline
- Mia Osmonbekov, September 11, 2026, 3 min read.

wikis.title: Big Ben returns to regular service after five years of restoration
wikis.summary: UK Parliament news page announcing that the Elizabeth Tower bells resumed regular striking in November 2022, with the state of the remaining restoration works and a tower-design competition for children.
wikis.body:
## The bells are back

- "After 5 years, the bells of the Elizabeth Tower have returned to regular service."
- Visitors to Westminster can now hear Big Ben striking the hour, "with the quarter bells sounding every 15 minutes".
- "The bells returned to service after 4 days of tests prior to Remembrance Sunday on the 13th November 2022."

## Remembrance Sunday display

- To mark Remembrance Sunday the Elizabeth Tower "was also lit up with a display of falling poppies".
- Commons Speaker Sir Lindsay Hoyle said the illumination to thank the Armed Forces for their service "was a fitting end to a 'Week of Remembrance' in Parliament in a particularly sad and poignant year".

## State of the works

- "Work to the exterior is now complete and the majority of works inside the Tower are close to conclusion."
- "The Ayrton Light has now been reconnected and is shining whenever either House is sitting."
- "Soon, power supplies will be activated and fire safety works completed."
- "The principal contractor will remain on site until December 2022" to ensure works meet a satisfactory standard and to support handover to the visitor-offer teams.
- "Parliament expects to welcome its first visitors back inside the Elizabeth Tower in 2023", following installation and testing of new exhibition spaces, workshops and tour routes.
- Campaign hashtag: #RestoringBigBen.

## Design-a-tower competition

- UK Parliament is asking UK residents aged 7 to 12 to "design their very own tower", in any medium - "matchsticks, building blocks, clay or even cake".
- Open to individuals and groups of up to 5, in age bands 7-9 and 10-12.
- Prizes include a VIP trip to the Houses of Parliament and the London Eye and a voucher for a family tour of the Elizabeth Tower.
- "The competition closes on the 30th January 2023."

wikis.title: Big Ben's chimes return full-time after Remembrance Sunday 2022
wikis.summary: Londonist report that Big Ben resumes striking around the clock from Remembrance Sunday, 13 November 2022, after five years of conservation work on the Elizabeth Tower.
wikis.body:
## What happens

- "Big Ben gets its bongs back full-time this November — after it strikes 11 on Remembrance Sunday."
- At 11am on Sunday 13 November the quarter bells will peal, followed by 11 strikes of the great bell, heralding the customary two-minute silence.
- "From then on, Big Ben will be back in action around the clock."

## Before that date

- On Tuesday 8 November from 3pm, people in the Westminster vicinity "should be able to hear the famous chimes intermittently" as the quarter bells and Big Ben are tested.
- On Friday 11 November — Armistice Day — Big Ben will also strike 11.

## The works

- Conservation work started in 2017; during it the chimes were silenced, "only returning on special occasions, such as New Year's Eve and the funeral of Queen Elizabeth II".
- The restoration of the Elizabeth Tower "has taken five years, and reportedly ran £80m over budget".

## Anniversary

- "13 November marks exactly 166 years since Big Ben was first struck."
- A Times reporter described the sound as "Like a potent poison, the vibration penetrates every vein in the body; it strikes every nerve, it attacks and tries every fibre in the muscle, it makes your bones rattle and your marrow creep."

## Byline

- By Will Noble. Last Updated 11 November 2022.

wikis.title: ICEHOTEL 365, the world's first year-round ice hotel, opens in Jukkasjarvi
wikis.summary: Forbes piece on the opening of ICEHOTEL 365 in Jukkasjarvi, Sweden, describing its size, construction, cooling system, suites and nightly rates.
wikis.body:
## The opening

- "Ever since the first ICEHOTEL opened in 1989, there have been roughly 50,000 people visiting annually to catch a glimpse of the northern lights."
- Because the frozen structure requires a sub-zero climate, the "original pop-up" (as CNN calls it) "had only been available for about four months between mid-December and mid-April every year".
- "Yet, earlier this month, the same location saw the opening of ICEHOTEL 365 - the world's first permanent ice and snow hotel."

## The building

- Situated "approximately 124 miles north of the Arctic Circle in Jukkasjarvi, Sweden".
- A 22,604 square-foot construction with 20 rooms, an icebar and an art gallery.
- "The idea came about a year ago primarily in response to people wishing to stay at the frozen structure during summer and autumn."
- Yngve Bergqvist, Founder of ICEHOTEL 365, on research showing winters will become shorter: "We want to create a sustainable product."
- "It took more than a hundred people over five months to build the permanent ice hotel": a steel construction with an inserted cooling system, then 30,000 liters of water from the Torne River turned into several tons of ice and snow covering walls, ceiling, ground and all the rooms.

## Climate control

- Steel pipes are drilled into the permafrost, at 16 feet below ground, to keep the building at 23 degrees Fahrenheit - "the ideal temperature for the preservation of the hotel plus its ice and snow sculptures, according to Bergqvist".
- Bergqvist: "That way, the building works like a thermos where it doesn't let the cold air out nor the heat in."
- Approximately 7,320 square feet of solar-powered refrigerating plants will be used to keep the hotel cool during the summer months.

## Guests

- Josefin Lindberg, Media & PR Representative of ICEHOTEL 365: "during the night we recommend them to only wear a base layer"; the hotel provides thermal sleeping bags (heated by body temperature) "tested to -40 degrees", with "Just thermal underwear, socks, long johns and long sleeve top, plus a hat" recommended.
- A separate warm building has 70 warm rooms, plus heated relaxation rooms with sauna, showers and bathroom.
- Activities include the ten-step Jukkasjarvi sauna ritual and a five-course ice menu made with local produce by Alexander Meier.

## Art and rates

- Each of the 26 Art Suites and nine Deluxe Suites has a distinctive theme that took the artists two weeks to create.
- Named works: "You Are My Type" by John Bark & Charli Kasselback (Art Suite 365), "Connect" by Edith Maria Van der Wetering and Wilfred Stijger (Ice Church), "Tribute" by Elin Julin, Marinus Vroom and Jens Thoms Ivarsson (ICEBAR), "Once upon a Time" by Luc Voisin & Mathieu Brison and "The Victorian Apartment" by Luca Roncoroni (Deluxe Suite 365), the Victorian-inspired apartment being by Norwegian-Italian architect Luca Roncoroni.
- An Art Suite costs "at least $470 per night".
- The general starting rate is $188 per night; an ice room at the seasonal ICEHOTEL starts at $350 per night.

## Seasonal hotel

- Next door, a seasonal ICEHOTEL of 15 art suites and 20 ice rooms plus an ice chapel for winter weddings "is opened right next door from December 16 through April 2017".
- During peak season the entire premise can accommodate up to 250 people at a time.

## Byline

- Forbes, Eustacia Huen, Contributor; the page notes "Opinions expressed by Forbes Contributors are their own."

wikis.title: One Piece (TV 1999) MyAnimeList entry
wikis.summary: MyAnimeList database page for the One Piece TV anime, with its airing information, studio and licensors, scores and member counts, synopsis, broadcast/release background and theme songs.
wikis.body:
## Information

- Title: One Piece. Japanese: ONE PIECE. English: One Piece. Synonyms: OP.
- Type: TV. Episodes: Unknown. Status: Currently Airing.
- Aired: Oct 20, 1999 to ? Premiered: Fall 1999.
- Broadcast: Sundays at 23:15 (JST).
- Producers: Fuji TV, TAP. Licensors: Funimation, 4Kids Entertainment. Studios: Toei Animation.
- Source: Manga. Genres: Action, Adventure, Fantasy. Demographic: Shounen.
- Duration: 24 min. Rating: PG-13 - Teens 13 or older.

## Statistics

- Score: 8.73 (weighted; scored by 1,558,044 users).
- Ranked: #55 (based on the top anime page). Popularity: #17.
- Members: 2,728,325. Favorites: 256,194.
- Reviews: 971 total - 738 Recommended, 117 Mixed Feelings, 116 Not Recommended.
- Streaming platforms listed: Crunchyroll, Netflix, Shahid. Official site and @OnePieceAnime listed under Available At.

## Synopsis (MAL Rewrite)

- "Barely surviving in a barrel after passing through a terrible whirlpool at sea, carefree Monkey D. Luffy ends up aboard a ship under attack by fearsome pirates... Luffy is a pirate himself who resolutely pursues the coveted One Piece treasure and the King of the Pirates title that comes with it."
- "The late King of the Pirates, Gol D. Roger, stirred up the world before his death by disclosing the whereabouts of his hoard of riches and daring everyone to obtain it."
- Luffy gathers companions to join him on the adventure.

## Background

- "The anime had a hiatus from October 13, 2024, to April 6, 2025. The anime switched to a seasonal release model starting from April 5, 2026."
- Airing times: Wednesdays 19:00 between October 20, 1999 - March 2001; Sundays 19:30 between April 2001 - December 2004; Sundays 9:30 between October 6, 2006 - October 13, 2024; changed again to Sundays 23:15 on April 6, 2025.
- Several anime-original arcs have been adapted into light novels, and the series has inspired 50+ video games as of 2023.
- In June 2004, One Piece was licensed in North America by 4Kids Entertainment, which partnered with Viz Media for home video distribution. 4Kids censored the show and in December 2006 stopped its production. In April 2007, Funimation took over the licensing, providing an uncut version.
- In Japan, the anime's first 574 episodes were released exclusively on DVD by Avex Pictures from February 21, 2001, to December 4, 2013; Blu-rays became available with the DVDs starting January 8, 2014.
- In North America, Viz Media released the anime on DVD between February 28, 2006, and June 26, 2007. Funimation has re-released and continued the series since May 27, 2008. From March 23, 2021, the DVDs were accompanied by Blu-rays.

## Main characters and voice actors

- Monkey D. Luffy - Tanaka, Mayumi; Roronoa, Zoro - Nakai, Kazuya; Sanji - Hirata, Hiroaki; Nico, Robin - Yamaguchi, Yuriko; Tony Tony, Chopper - Ootani, Ikue; Nami - Okamura, Akemi; Usopp - Yamaguchi, Kappei; Brook - Cho; Franky - Yao, Kazuki; Jinbe - Houki, Katsuhisa.
- Staff listed: Kobayashi, Miki (Producer, Publicity); Tokita, Hayato (Producer); Akahori, Tetsushi (Producer, Production Manager); Teramoto, Satoshi (Producer).

wikis.title: Caterpillar 797 mining truck
wikis.summary: Curbside Classic article on the Cat 797 ultra-class mining truck, its V24 and C175-20 engines, payload, tyres, assembly and price.
wikis.body:
## The 797 and its engine

- "In 1998, Caterpillar introduced the largest 'off highway' mining truck the world had seen to that point--the 797--which was powered by mating two V12 Cat 3512 HD engines together to create the 7,147 cubic inch V24 3524B HD quad-turbo intercooled diesel engine, capable of around 3,550 HP and 12,000 lb.-ft. of torque at an easy-going 1,750 rpm."
- "Fuel economy is a bit less than a Prius ... at 0.3 mpg."
- "The 797 was unique in that Caterpillar decided to stay with a fully mechanical drivetrain as opposed to the diesel-electric drivetrains more common on trucks of that size. It has a seven-speed planetary gear transmission, all controlled by numerous on-board computers."
- "The truck itself was also the first to be completely designed on computer."

## The 797F

- "The current 797F model, introduced in 2008, is powered by a Cat 175-20 twenty cylinder engine (single block) of 175 Liter displacement, which is rated at 4,000 HP."
- It carries "a load of about 400 short tons (equivalent to about 120 Ford Excursions) at a top speed of around 42 mph (loaded)".
- "With a 44/56 weight distribution, a gross weight of well over a million pounds and a live rear axle"; "0-30 times of about 27 seconds".

## Wheels and tyres

- "Each 12'-10\" tall wheel is attached by 47 lug nuts, each torqued to 2,300 lb.-ft."
- "Six Michelin tires are required per truck and they're the largest tires made on the planet--59/80R63 is the size ... and they'll run you about $42,500 each (as of 2009)."

## Manufacture and assembly

- "The 3524B (and current C-175-20) engines are manufactured at Caterpillar's Lafayette, Indiana engine plant and then shipped via flatbed semi to Decatur, Illinois for installation in the frame."
- "The final assembly of the 797 is done at or near the customer's site, and requires numerous semi loads to deliver. A team of seven mechanics will spend about twenty days working 24-7 to weld the dump body together and assemble the truck."

## Cost and operation

- "A new 797F will run you about $5,000,000, and can be completely rebuilt several times over its typical twenty year life."
- The author writes he "was in Canada a few years ago at an Oil Sands mining site, which had about 100 trucks in operation at that time", adding "Except for maintenance, these trucks are kept running 24/7 (time = money), and if you shut one down outside the shop in the winter, you're not going to get it started again until spring!"

By Ed Stembridge; the page is marked "UPDATED ON FEBRUARY 14, 2021".

wikis.title: Lufthansa takes delivery of its first A380
wikis.summary: Business Traveller report on the handover ceremony at Frankfurt Airport where Airbus delivered Lufthansa's first A380, and the aircraft's first scheduled service.
wikis.body:
## The handover

- "The first of Lufthansa's 15 A380 'superjumbos' was handed over to it by Airbus earlier this morning."
- The ceremony was broadcast live from Frankfurt Airport and attended by CEOs and chairmen from Lufthansa, Airbus and Rolls Royce, plus dignitaries and press.
- Published 19th May 2010, by Andrew Gough.

## What was said

- Lufthansa CEO Wolfgang Mayrhuber, "notably in high spirits", thanked Airbus and Rolls Royce, whose Trent 900s the A380 uses, for their work bringing the aircraft up to full-readiness. He outlined "technical solutions" that set Lufthansa's A380 apart, including its new in-flight entertainment system, first class cabin, low noise levels and fuel efficiency.
- Tom Enders, Airbus' president and CEO, described the years leading to the handover and the work to achieve flight certification as a "marathon", adding that after "some difficult years, the spirit is up again."
- Peter Hintze, parliamentary secretary to the German federal minister of economics and technology, spoke in German about the A380 in the context of the wider economy and welcomed its environmental benefits.

## The aircraft and first flight

- The new 526-seat A380 is named "Frankfurt am Main" and is to become Lufthansa's flagship aircraft.
- "Its first scheduled flight for paying passengers will commence on June 11, destined for Tokyo's Narita Airport."
- Passengers will experience Lufthansa's new First class cabin for the first time on that maiden voyage.

## Other A380 operators named

- Air France (described as a European rival already flying the A380), Qantas, Singapore Airlines and Emirates.

## Media

- Clips of the morning's webcast were to be downloadable later that day at a380.lufthansa.com.

wikis.title: Paris metro line 1: history, extensions, automation and stations
wikis.summary: RATP culture page telling the history of Paris metro line 1 from its 1900 opening through its suburban extensions, its automation, and its landmark stations.
wikis.body:
## Overview

- Metro line 1 connects Château de Vincennes station in the east to La Défense station in the west and "is the first line to have been commissioned on the Paris metropolitan railway network".
- After the extensions it runs "over a distance of 16.6 km".
- "Last modified on 28 November 2024".

## Origins

- Designed to connect the main sites serving the 1900 World Expo; part of "the 65-km network consisting of six lines".
- "The network was declared a service of public interest by a law that was enacted on 30 March 1898."
- The line follows the path of engineer Jean-Baptiste Berlier's 1887 underground electric tube tram project, which aimed to link Bois de Boulogne and Bois de Vincennes.
- "Metro line 1 was inaugurated at 1:00 p.m. on 19 July 1900, operating only eight stations, with the other stations being commissioned in phases between 6 August and 1 September of the same year."

## Extensions

- 24 March 1934: first extension to Château de Vincennes, removing the need for the reversing loop at Porte de Vincennes.
- 29 April 1937: extended to Pont de Neuilly; former terminus Porte Maillot reorganised and its loop phased out; the tunnel level was lowered to pass under the tracks of the now-defunct La Petite Ceinture railway.
- 1 April 1992: extended west to the foot of the Grande Arche, with La Défense as the new terminus, mainly to relieve RER line A ridership between Charles de Gaulle - Étoile and La Défense.

## Automation

- "Metro line 1 is the first line worldwide to have been automated without causing any disruption to operations."
- Works were conducted at night with service ending at 10:30 p.m.
- First automated shuttle trial on 8 July 2011, followed by commissioning of the first eight automated shuttles alongside driver-operated trains.
- "The transition to the full and permanent automation of metro line 1 was completed on 16 February 2013, with the deployment of new automated MP05 rolling stock."

## Iconic stations

- Champs-Élysées-Clémenceau: environment dedicated to the Palais de la Découverte museum.
- Tuileries: made over in a nod to the Tuileries garden above it.
- Palais Royal-Musée du Louvre: entrance through the Kiosque des Noctambules art installation.
- Louvre-Rivoli: paved with Burgundy limestone, similar to an antechamber in the Louvre Museum.
- Bastille: a mural harking back to major events in the French Revolution.

## Other

- The page also links a feature, "Behind the scenes of metro line 1 in 1965!".

wikis.title: Opening of metro line 1 and its suburban extensions
wikis.summary: How line 1 was conceived for the 1900 World Expo, when it opened, and the three extensions that took it from Porte de Vincennes and Porte Maillot to Château de Vincennes and La Défense.
wikis.body:
- Designed to connect the main sites serving the 1900 World Expo, as part of a 65-km network of six lines.
- The network "was declared a service of public interest by a law that was enacted on 30 March 1898".
- Follows the path of Jean-Baptiste Berlier's 1887 underground electric tube tram project linking Bois de Boulogne and Bois de Vincennes.
- Inaugurated "at 1:00 p.m. on 19 July 1900, operating only eight stations"; the rest were commissioned in phases "between 6 August and 1 September of the same year".
- 24 March 1934: first extension to Château de Vincennes, removing the reversing loop at Porte de Vincennes.
- 29 April 1937: extension to Pont de Neuilly; Porte Maillot reorganised and its loop phased out; the tunnel was lowered to pass under La Petite Ceinture.
- 1 April 1992: westward extension to the foot of the Grande Arche with La Défense as terminus, to relieve RER line A between Charles de Gaulle - Étoile and La Défense.
- The line now covers 16.6 km between Château de Vincennes and La Défense.

wikis.title: MSC Cruises takes delivery of MSC Euribia
wikis.summary: Cruise Hive report on the 31 May 2023 handover of MSC Euribia from Chantiers de l'Atlantique, its LNG propulsion and its planned net-zero voyage and naming ceremony.
wikis.body:
## Delivery

- "MSC Cruises has taken delivery of its newest cruise ship, **MSC Euribia**", the **fifth in MSC's Meraviglia-class series**.
- "After a **two-year build period**, MSC Cruises and **Chantiers de l'Atlantique** celebrated the official handing over... **today, May 31**."
- The ship "will depart from **Saint-Nazaire** later this week, with the official naming ceremony to be held in **Copenhagen on June 8**".
- Named after the Greek goddess **Eurybia**, "renowned for her mastery of the seas".

## Figures

- **181,541 gross tons**, accommodating **up to 6,334 guests** when fully booked.
- Over a dozen dining venues, five pools and the coral-themed **Ocean Cay Aquapark**.

## Environment

- "The ship is touted as the most energy-efficient cruise ship ever built", with advanced onboard wastewater treatment and waste management systems.
- Second MSC Cruises ship "to be powered entirely by **liquefied natural gas (LNG)**", following the line's flagship **MSC World Europa**.
- "MSC Euribia... is set to sail on the **first net zero greenhouse gas emissions voyage** in the history of the cruise industry", a journey "beginning on **June 3** and culminating in a naming ceremony in Copenhagen on **June 8**".

## Quotes

- Pierfrancesco Vago, Executive President of the MSC Group's Cruise Division: "With the delivery of MSC Euribia, we are taking a major step towards our goal of zero net greenhouse gas emissions."
- Vago: "The cleanest energy is the one we don't use, and MSC Euribia was built on this principle."
- Laurent Castaing, Managing Director of Chantiers de l'Atlantique: "This fifth and final ship in the Meraviglia class marks the culmination of an already highly successful series and the continuation of our innovative joint environmental projects."

## Onboard

- Kids' clubs including a play area for babies and toddlers and an educational lab; **Teens Club Extra Space** with PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and Nintendo Switch, foosball and table tennis.
- The **Carousel Lounge** "extends outdoors, providing guests with panoramic sea views".

## Also at the ceremony

- The event "marked the ceremonial laying-up of **hull number X34**, which will soon become **MSC World America**, the second ship in MSC's World Class series, **due for delivery in 2025**".

## Inaugural season

- Naming ceremony led by "Hollywood icon and Oscar-winning actress **Sophia Loren**".
- Then a **7-night roundtrip** sailing from **Kiel, Germany**, calling at Copenhagen and three ports in Norway - **Hellesylt, Alesund, Flam** - before returning to Kiel.
- "MSC Euribia will continue to offer northern European sailings through at least **October 2024**", cruising to Norway, Germany, Denmark, The Netherlands and more.

wikis.title: Bosch opens semiconductor factory in Dresden
wikis.summary: Express & Star motors report on Bosch opening its new Dresden chip plant, with the cost, jobs and the dates it starts making power-tool and automotive semiconductors.
wikis.body:
## The plant

- "Bosch has opened a new semiconductor factory in Germany with the goal of supplying the automotive industry with the much-needed components from September."
- "Costing EUR 1 billion (around GBP 860 million) to build, the facility in Dresden is set to create around 700 jobs."
- "Bosch's new site is expected to start producing semiconductors for its power tool this July before it begins creating chips for automotive customers in September."
- Standfirst: "Manufacturer will start creating components for the automotive industry this year."

## Why chips matter here

- "Semiconductors are used throughout a car and help to control certain aspects such as infotainment systems and mains screens as well as power steering and brake sensors. Many parts of a car simply wouldn't work without these important 'chips'."
- "a recent shortage has plunged the motoring industry into disarray with customers forced to endure long wait times as manufacturers suffer setbacks in production while awaiting fresh deliveries of semiconductors."

## Quotes

- Harald Kroeger, member of the board of management of Robert Bosch GmbH: "Chips for vehicles are the ultimate discipline in semiconductor technology. This is because in cars, these small building blocks have to be especially robust."
- Kroeger: "Semiconductors are the building blocks of progress. Electronic components equipped with chips from Dresden will make applications such as automated and resource-conserving driving possible, as well as the best possible occupant protection."
- Kroeger added that vehicle chips need to be robust as they are often exposed to "strong vibrations and extreme temperatures that range from far below freezing to far above the boiling point of water".

## Byline

- By Editorial Team, published 7th Jun 2021, 17:31 BST.

wikis.title: Rocky Mountaineer's 30th anniversary and company history
wikis.summary: Rocky Mountaineer blog post marking 30 years of its luxury rail journeys, recounting the first 1990 departure, the company's growth, routes and service levels, and introducing an anniversary story series.
wikis.body:
## The anniversary

- "2020 is a special year for Rocky Mountaineer: We're celebrating 30 years of being a leading travel experience in Canada and providing luxury train journeys between Vancouver and the Canadian Rockies."
- Date Published: 2020-01-29. Last Updated: 2025-05-30.

## The first journey

- "Our own story officially began on May 27, 1990, when we welcomed 200 excited guests onboard the first scheduled Rocky Mountaineer journey leaving Vancouver, British Columbia, bound for the Canadian Rockies."
- Founder: Peter Armstrong.
- "Rocky Mountaineer would only travel during the day, allowing guests to enjoy every moment of the ever-changing landscapes in daylight."

## Growth

- "Thousands of departures and more than two million guests later, our family-owned company has grown to become the largest privately held luxury tourist train company in the world."
- Four rail routes between Vancouver and Banff, Lake Louise, and Jasper, Alberta.
- "In 2021, we added our Rockies to the Red Rocks route which travels between Moab, Utah and Denver, Colorado."

## Service levels

- GoldLeaf Service, "Introduced in 1995", features bi-level, glass-dome coaches.
- SilverLeaf Service, "launched seventeen years later", offers single-level coaches with over-sized windows.

## The story series

- To celebrate the 30th anniversary the company will share "some of our favourite articles, photos, videos, social posts (and even a few surprises!)", added "all year long".
- Items featured on the page: "How Three Couples Celebrated Their Special Occasions"; "VIDEO: Hear from Two of Our Guests about Their Train Journey"; "Train Talk 101: Learn the Lingo and the Lore"; "5 Moments to Capture along Our Journey through the Clouds Rail Route" (Jasper, Alberta to Vancouver, British Columbia).

wikis.title: Gilmour Space test-fires Australia's largest rocket engine
wikis.summary: Report on Gilmour Space's 75-second full-throttle test fire of the engine intended to put its Eris rocket into orbit, with the company's launch plans and figures.
wikis.body:
## The test
- Gold Coast-based Gilmour Space "successfully test fired the largest and most powerful rocket engine ever developed in Australia."
- "The milestone was reached following a 75-second full throttle test, the motor performance required to propel the Eris rocket into orbit, which produced a force of over 100 kilonewtons (or 25,000 pounds) – enough force to lift four SUVs off the ground."
- CEO and co-founder Adam Gilmour: "We were really happy that we got this engine to run for greater than one minute which is getting into the zone that you need for an orbital flight and it was a great demonstration of a lot of technologies."
- After the test the team "opened a couple of bottles of champagne and had pizza"; Gilmour added "this is not the last big thing that we will do in the next few months."

## Launch plans
- Gilmour Space "is developing Australia's first capability for launching commercial, civil, and defence-related satellites into orbit and is now closer to obtaining a small orbital spaceport at the Abbot Point State Development Area in Bowen, North Queensland."
- Gilmour: "With timely assessments and approvals from relevant authorities, we hope to be able to launch Australia's first sovereign-made rocket from Queensland sometime in the latter half of 2022."
- The company has "set its sights on helping Australia become the 11th nation in the world to successfully launch a rocket into orbit."
- "The company's hybrid propulsion rockets are lower cost, greener and safer to operate than most traditional rockets and, if successful, Eris would become the world's first hybrid rocket to reach orbit."

## Company
- "Having secured $61 million in a Series C funding round in 2021."
- "currently employing more than 110 employees on the Gold Coast, Queensland but hopes to ramp up considerably after the first launch."
- Gilmour on hiring: "everything you've heard about a talent shortage in Australia, and around the world, is absolutely true."
- "Gilmour Space is Australia's largest sovereign space employer and manufacturer of orbital launch vehicles and spacecraft."
- Co-founder James Gilmour "was featured in the 2021 Australia's Top 100 Young Entrepreneurs list – coming in at number 27."
- "In March 2021... Gilmour Space announced a partnership with Sydney-based Space Machines Company and Fireball.International to launch a fire detection satellite into orbit which would be able to detect fires in real-time by analysing imagers and sensors' data."

## Figures given for orbit
- "space begins at the 100-kilometre altitude mark (also known as the Karman Line)"; sub-orbital space needs "speeds of around 3,000 km per hour - similar to Virgin Galactic and Blue Origin's human space flights."
- Orbit requires "about 27,000 km per hour; approximately nine times the speed and energy required for a suborbital flight."

## Byline
- By Neil Dorgan, 12 January 2022.

wikis.title: Gilmour Space Technologies completes first successful Eris rocket engine test
wikis.summary: Orbital Today reports Gilmour Space Technologies' first successful test of its Eris rocket engine in Queensland, a 75-second firing at 110 kilonewtons.
wikis.body:
## The test

- Engineers at Gilmour Space Technologies in Queensland, Australia "completed the first successful test of their rocket engine for the Eris project."
- On 11th January 2022 the engine was activated for 75 seconds, achieving 110 kilonewtons of force.
- The article says this thrust "is powerful enough to lift four cars" and "has met the aims of the project, which hopes to create a viable engine for a rocket launch."
- The test engine is described as "the largest and most powerful engine created by an Australian firm."

## Eris project plans

- The Eris project "hopes to send a small domestically built rocket into space in the latter half of 2022."
- "Over the course of the next five years, the project will expand to carry payloads weighing between 300 and 4,000 kilograms into orbit."
- With the test complete, the developmental process "can now move into its third and final stage."

## Launch site

- The company hopes to launch its rocket from a spaceport in the Abbot Point State Development Area in North Queensland.
- Gilmour Space Technologies "is currently in the process of applying for government and federal permission to make this spaceport a reality."

## People

- CEO Adam Gilmour "expressed his satisfaction with the recent engine test, recognising the moment as a big step forward for the Australian space sector."
- Published by Emma Thorpe; page states "Last Updated: 31st Jan 2022".

wikis.summary: 4C Offshore's vessel page describing the heavy-lift vessel Jumbo Fairplayer, its deep-water deployment systems and its work on the Arkona project (most spec fields are behind a subscription).
wikis.body:
## Vessel

- **Name:** Jumbo Fairplayer
- Category given on the page: **Heavy Maintenance and Construction**.
- Fairplayer "is fitted with DP and is suitable for installation of transition pieces and is a sister ship to Jumbo Javelin".
- "The integrated deep-water deployment systems allow direct lowering and accurate positioning of subsea structures in water depths up to **3,000m**."

## Equipment

- Jumbo has developed a **'fly jib'**, "which it claims can extend the vessel's lift and reach". The equipment is interchangeable between J-Class vessels.
- Fairplayer "has had an SMST gangway installed prior to working on the **Arkona** project where it installed the transition pieces".
- In **January 2018**, ELA Container Offshore delivered **two offshore living quarters** (Type All rounder) for installation on the MV Fairplayer.
