wikis.title: Windows Phone Central poll on the Windows Phone 8.1 Start screen
wikis.summary: Windows Phone Central article and reader poll of Mar 28, 2014 on the new Windows Phone 8.1 Start screen and its transparent-tile background images, ahead of the Build unveiling.
wikis.body:
## What the source is
- Windows Phone Central article "Let us know if you love or hate the new Start screen in Windows Phone 8.1", by Sam Sabri, "Friday, Mar 28, 2014 at 3:12 pm", with a reader poll and 644 comments.

## Key facts
- "We are now less than a week from officially seeing Windows Phone 8.1 for the first time." The unveiling "is happening next week at Microsoft's Build conference in San Francisco".
- "Nokia is expected to announce two new Windows Phone 8.1 devices - the Lumia 630 (Moneypenny) and the Lumia 930 (Martini)."
- "Microsoft is adding background image support, but in a way not a lot of people expected": the chosen image "will show through the various Live tiles that can be set to transparent", rather than sitting behind them as in Windows 8.1.
- "It also animates really nicely thanks to a parallax effect."
- The background image is "just an option".
- Previous Story: "New Windows Phone 8.1 video reveals Start screen backgrounds, parallax view".

## The rest of the page
- The remainder is reader comments, site navigation and the Mobile Nations footer ("Copyright 2014 Mobile Nations"), with no further article content.

wikis.title: Windows Phone Central poll: the new Start screen in Windows Phone 8.1
wikis.summary: Windows Phone Central article of Friday, Mar 28, 2014 asking readers to vote on the new Windows Phone 8.1 Start screen, explaining how its background-image support works ahead of the Build unveiling.
wikis.body:
## Article
- Headline: "Let us know if you love or hate the new Start screen in Windows Phone 8.1"
- By Sam Sabri, "Friday, Mar 28, 2014 at 3:12 pm", filed under "WPCentral News". Tags: "Start Screen, windows phone 8.1, poll".
- Sam Sabri is credited as Managing Editor.

## The upcoming unveiling
- "We are now less than a week from officially seeing Windows Phone 8.1 for the first time."
- "The unveiling is happening next week at Microsoft's Build conference in San Francisco."
- "Nokia is expected to announce two new Windows Phone 8.1 devices - the Lumia 630 (Moneypenny) and the Lumia 930 (Martini)."

## How the new Start screen works
- "Microsoft is adding background image support, but in a way not a lot of people expected."
- In Windows Phone 8 users "are able to select either a light theme or dark theme": the light theme gives a white background behind the Live tiles, the dark theme makes that space black. "A lot of folks had hoped to replace that black (or white) space with the image of their choice."
- "That's not exactly how the new Start screen works in Windows Phone 8.1. Instead, you'll be able to have your image on the Start screen, but it'll show through the various Live tiles that can be set to transparent."
- "It also animates really nicely thanks to a parallax effect."
- The article notes "this is just an option and not something you'll have to endure if you don't like it".

## The poll
- Readers are asked to vote in a poll and comment; app readers are told to "head to Internet Explorer to take the poll" at m.wpcentral.com/love-or-hate-new-start-screen-windows-phone-81.
- The page shows 644 comments.

## Adjacent stories listed
- Previous Story: "New Windows Phone 8.1 video reveals Start screen backgrounds, parallax view"
- Next Story: "Xbox Live puzzle game Hexic arrives on Windows Phone 8 and Windows 8 devices"

(The rest of this part is reader comments and site navigation, not article content.)

wikis.title: Trump plans to greet Xi at airport on arrival, officials say
wikis.summary: Reuters reports that Trump plans to greet Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews on his arrival for a White House state visit, and lists the visit's programme and the tech CEOs invited to the state dinner.
wikis.body:
## What is reported

- US President Donald Trump "plans to greet Chinese President Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews, at the airport of the military base just outside Washington, DC, on his arrival next week for a White House visit, a senior US official told reporters on Friday".
- "It is rare for the US president to greet visiting foreign leaders at the airport."
- The article gives no arrival time, and dates the arrival only as "next week".

## The visit's programme

Senior US officials who briefed reporters said the visit will include:

- an arrival ceremony **inside** the White House
- a Rose Garden military review
- a state dinner in the evening

## State dinner guests

"Among the guests for the dinner will be a number of tech CEOs", named as:

- Jeff Bezos of Amazon (AMZN.O)
- Sundar Pichai of Alphabet (GOOGL.O)
- Sam Altman of OpenAI
- Tim Cook of Apple (AAPL.O)
- Elon Musk of Tesla (TSLA.O)
- Jensen Huang of Nvidia (NVDA.O)
- Michael Dell of Dell Technologies (DELL.N)

## Agenda

"Issues such as trade, flow of rare earths to the global economy and AI are expected to be among the topics that will be discussed during the visit, officials said."

## Attribution

Reporting by Steve Holland and Humeyra Pamuk; editing by Chris Reese. Datelined "WASHINGTON, Sept 18 (Reuters)". Published September 18, 2026 3:36 PM PDT, updated September 18, 2026.

## The announcement

"Foreign Ministry Spokesperson announces:

At the invitation of President of the United States of America Donald J. Trump, President Xi Jinping will pay a state visit to the United States from September 23 to 25."

## Notes

wikis.title: First Lady Melania Trump Releases Details Ahead of Xi Jinping and Madame Peng Liyuan's Visit to The White House
wikis.summary: The White House Office of the First Lady's day-by-day programme for Xi Jinping's 23-25 September 2026 state visit, from the Joint Base Andrews greeting to the State Arrival Ceremony, the state dinner and the National Archives tour.
wikis.body:
## The visit

"President Donald J. Trump and First Lady Melania Trump will welcome His Excellency Xi Jinping, President of the People's Republic of China and Madame Peng Liyuan to the White House on Thursday, September 24, 2026, for an official state visit. This visit comes more than a decade since President Xi and Madame Peng's last visit to the White House, marking a significant milestone in the relationship between the two countries."

## Wednesday, September 23

"On Wednesday, September 23, the President will greet His Excellency, Xi Jinping, President of the People's Republic of China and Madame Peng Liyuan at Joint Base Andrews."

No time is given.

## Thursday, September 24 - State Arrival Ceremony

- Held on the South Lawn, State Floor and Rose Garden of the White House, featuring "479 military personnel, representing all branches of the United States Armed Forces".
- The South Drive is lined with the Armed Forces Full Honor Cordon leading to a national flag display of US and China flags; the United States Army Herald Trumpets present a fanfare on the South Portico.
- On the State Floor, "The President's Own" United States Marine Band plays the national anthems of the People's Republic of China and the United States, followed by remarks from both the President and Xi Jinping.
- A Presidential Salute from the United States Marine Silent Drill Platoon and United States Joint Forces Command on the South Lawn.
- A Military Review in the Rose Garden, with the United States Army Herald Trumpets lining the roof of the West and Oval Colonnades, and demonstrations by the United States Army Old Guard Fife and Drum Corps, the United States Marine Corps Silent Drill Platoon and "The Commandant's Own" United States Marine Drum and Bugle Corps.
- "The ceremony will conclude with a military flyover featuring a B-2 Spirit and four F-22 Raptors."

## Thursday, September 24 - afternoon and evening

- Mrs Trump and Madame Peng Liyuan visit the Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art "to explore works spanning centuries of artistic achievement and Sino-American cultural exchange".
- In the evening the President and First Lady greet the guests at the North Portico for a State Dinner in the East Room. "The Office of the First Lady will share additional details on the State Dinner on Wednesday, September 23."

## Friday, September 25

- The President and First Lady greet Xi Jinping and Madame Peng Liyuan on their arrival at the White House; tea in the Red Room at the South Portico.
- Both couples travel to the National Archives to view records and documents significant to the American and Chinese relationship, and the farewell is at the National Archives.

## Attribution

Issued by the Office of the First Lady, The White House, September 21, 2026.

wikis.title: Rare honour: Trump will greet Xi at Joint Base Andrews, not just White House
wikis.summary: South China Morning Post reports that Trump will greet Xi on the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews around 4pm on 23 September, and contrasts it with the reception Trump himself got in Beijing in May.
wikis.body:
## The airport welcome

- "US President Donald Trump will personally greet Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping on the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews when Xi lands in Washington next Wednesday, a rare airport reception, a US official confirmed on background."
- "Trump will attend Xi's arrival ceremony at Andrews, where the Chinese president's aircraft is **expected around 4pm local time on September 23**."
- "The president almost never meets visiting heads of state at the airfield. He typically waits at the White House."

## Contrast with Beijing, May 2026

- "The gesture is not a perfect mirror of what Trump received in Beijing a few months ago. When Air Force One landed at Beijing Capital International Airport on May 13, Xi did not come to the tarmac."
- "Vice-President Han Zheng led the reception, joined by ambassadors and senior foreign ministry officials, along with an honour guard, a band, and flag-waving youth."
- "Xi's formal welcome came the next day outside the Great Hall of the People, with a military review Trump later called 'incredible'."

## Attribution

By Khushboo Razdan. Published 11:13pm, 17 Sep 2026; updated 8:46am, 18 Sep 2026. Part of the SCMP series "Xi's 2026 trip to US" (20 of 22). The headline on the page itself reads "Xi to get what Trump didn't in Beijing: a presidential airport welcome".

wikis.title: Trump will be at the airport to greet Xi when China's leader arrives for his US state visit
wikis.summary: Associated Press report on Xi Jinping's 23-25 September state visit: the Joint Base Andrews welcome, the indoor arrival ceremony, the state dinner guest list and the prospect of easing some tariffs.
wikis.body:
## The arrival

- "The first state visit by the leader of China in more than a decade takes place next week when President Xi Jinping arrives in Washington for high-stakes talks - and a little schmoozing - at the White House with President Donald Trump."
- "When Xi's plan lands at Joint Base Andrews just outside Washington on Wednesday, Trump will be there to welcome Xi for the state visit, senior administration officials told reporters. That's unusual - Trump typically meets foreign leaders at the White House."

## Thursday

- "The heart of the visit comes Thursday when Trump and first lady Melania Trump welcome Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan at an arrival ceremony held indoors on the State Floor of the White House."
- "Trump and Xi will also participate in a review of troops in the Rose Garden before they retreat behind closed doors for their talks."
- The first lady and Peng Liyuan hold a separate engagement; details were not released on the Friday briefing call.
- A state dinner in the East Room on Thursday, with both leaders delivering remarks.

## The state dinner

Trump, speaking to reporters in the Oval Office on Friday: "Thousands of people would love to be at that dinner." He "appeared to lament that the 1,000-person ballroom he is adding onto the White House will not be available for the soiree because it is still under construction. 'This is a very tough ticket for me.'" He added: "I've told a lot of very good friends of mine, 'you just can't come.'"

Executives scheduled to attend, per the White House:

- Amazon founder Jeff Bezos
- Tesla and SpaceX's Elon Musk
- Sundar Pichai of Google
- Michael Dell, CEO of Dell Technologies
- Nvidia's Jensen Huang
- OpenAI's Sam Altman
- Jane Fraser, CEO of Citigroup
- Tim Cook, "who recently stepped down as the CEO of Apple"

## Friday

"Next Friday, Xi and Peng Liyuan are scheduled to return to the White House for a private tea with the Trumps, who will then take them on a tour of the National Archives, the home of some of the United States' most important founding documents as the nation celebrates its 250th anniversary. Xi will head for Joint Base Andrews after the tour."

## Substance

- "As for other substantive parts of the visit, U.S. officials said Washington and Beijing may be ready to ease some tariffs on some nonstrategic goods."
- "Senior U.S. officials said such a move might affect a narrow band of goods that would advantage both sides. The officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity under ground rules set by the White House, did not elaborate."

## Attribution

By Darlene Superville, Associated Press, carried by ABC News. September 18, 2026, 8:55 PM.

wikis.title: 2026 state visit by Xi Jinping to the United States
wikis.summary: Wikipedia's article on Xi Jinping's 23-25 September 2026 state visit to the United States, the reciprocal leg of the two leaders' mutual visits within six months.
wikis.body:
## The visit

- Xi Jinping is to pay a state visit to the United States from **23 to 25 September 2026**, at the invitation of President Donald Trump, with Washington, D.C. as the location.
- Xi travels with his wife, **Peng Liyuan**, and "a large business delegation".
- Trump invited Xi during his own May 2026 visit to China.
- It is Xi's first White House visit in eleven years, since the 2015 state visit.

## Framing

A Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson characterised the realisation of mutual visits between the two heads of state within half a year as having "historic, milestone significance".

## Note

The article is background and context rather than logistics: it carries no airport arrival time, no day-by-day itinerary, and no named agreements.
